I am not unhappy with this chili and am glad I have tried it. I will be buying more.

title: Excellent Cocoa Powder From a Trusted Brand
text:
I use King Arthur flour for most of my baking and have come to trust the brand. I was unaware that they made cocoa powder so I was surprised when I saw this. It's different than, and superior to, the cocoa I can find at my local grocery store. I will definitely buy more when this cocoa is gone.

This is Dutch-process cocoa and as a result it is less acidic than regular cocoa powder. Because of this, it is not exactly a 1-1 substitute in every scenario. Before swapping it in to a recipe where regular cocoa powder works, check to make sure (if you can) that Dutch-process cocoa powder will work. If not, adding baking powder may be needed.

This is a rich brown, fragrant cocoa that is fresh and really works well in the right recipes. It is especially good in a chocolate buttercream frosting which is good with regular cocoa but is elevated with this cocoa instead. This will be my new go-to when making frostings in particular.

I love the fact that there's close to a pound in the bag and it is resealable.

This is fine cocoa powder, good quality with a great flavor. I'll be buying more.

title: Fresh and Delicious
text:
We have a house full of cereal lovers so I was interested in trying this one out. We have had other Cascadia Farms cereals and they've been of good quality, so I expected more of the same. It did not disappoint.

Right out of the box this cereal is very fresh. It hasn't been exposed to moisture so it isn't soft (still has its crunch) and the flavors are fresh and unmuted. It had a distinct taste to it, almost like there's peanut butter in it, but there is no peanut butter at all in the ingredients list (peanuts are not listed as an ingredient either). There is an abundance of granola clusters, shaved almonds and cranberries. It has great flavor and great texture.

All of us in the house like this cereal and we're likely to buy more.

title: Good Spice Mix for Ribs
text:
I usually cook ribs on the grill, but I have seen a number of recipes online where people have found ways to make ribs in the pressure cooker. I have wanted to try this method and this mix gave me the motivation to try. There are a couple of things to say about this, partly relating to the method and partly relating to the spice mix itself.

I'll talk about the mix itself first as that is the main concern here. I like the flavor of the mix, and I will use all of it. It gives the ribs a pleasant, earthy flavor with a hint of smoke and not a lot of heat. It seems to be fresh and so far I have no complaints in that regard. I probably would have balanced the flavors a little differently, personally, but that's more in the realm of personal preference.

The method is another matter entirely. I like using the pressure cooker, though the spice mix includes a mention of using a slow cooker instead. The problem with either of these methods is that it still necessitates using the oven to finish the ribs under the broiler. There's certainly nothing wrong with that but there are enough people that want to use the pressure cooker for everything that will be disdappointed when the pressure cooker is not enough. Also, a proper mop is almost mandatory while finishing under the broiler.

This is a good spice mix that makes preparing ribs in the pressure cooker easier/faster/more convenient. It has a nice flavor and is fresh right out of the package. I'm still not sold on the method, but there's no reason this mix cannot be used on the grill too.

title: Cooks Up Beautifully
text:
We eat a lot of rice, though usually we eat regular long-grain rice. This was my first exposure to Basmati rice so I wasn't entirely sure what to expect. So far I am pleased with it. It cooks up beautifully and has a very nice flavor.

Following the basic instructions, this rice cooks up light and fluffy and doesn't stick together in clumps like long-grain rice typically does (or should). It holds together nicely (that is, it doesn't break) when it is cooked, yet it comes out tender. The flavor is subtle but distinct, different from other rice I have used.

As this comes in a 10-lb. bag, it is going to last me a good while. For a larger family that eats a lot of rice, this is probably a great size.

So far I'm very happy with this rice and am enjoying it. When it is gone, I will buy more (though it will take me a good while to use it all).

title: Fresh and Flavorful; I Like the Quantity Too
text:
I use tarragon quite a bit when cooking chicken in the pressure cooker. So, this six-pack of tarragon leaves is a good fit for me. This particular tarragon is flavorful and so far I am pleased with it.

Tarragon has a flavor that is well suited for chicken and I use it with a slightly heavy hand so I have to buy it periodically. A pack like this saves me time and a little money, and it I use it quickly enough to avoid it getting old and stale. That said, the individual jars are sealed so the contents should stay fresh for a good while.

Using this tarragon my chicken comes out with a nice flavor that is distinct. The flavor is fresh and clear without being overpowering. That's all I can really ask.

I'm happy with this six-pack. I will use it all before it goes stale or exceeds the recommended shelf life, and so far it has been fresh and flavorful. No complaints.

title: Good Flavor
text:
Pork butt in the slow cooker is something we have in the house often so this spice mix seemed like a good fit. I like Cholula hot sauce so I had high hopes for this mix as well. I have not been disappointed.

This is a simple mix to use - basically pour it on, rub into the pork roast and let it cook. It doesn't require much effort at all beyond that so to say this is simple and easy is plainly accurate.

Flavor-wise, this is good stuff. The flavors are earthy and bright and complement the pork very well. There were no complaints when this came out of the close cooker, from anyone in the house.

This is a lot easier than making my own rub and the flavor is good. I'll be getting more of this.

title: Bite Sized Treats
text:
One of my favorite things is Rice Krispies treats, so this box is a natural fit for me. I have mixed feelings about these, though.

There are three flavors of treats in this box - chocolate, vanilla (original) and strawberry. I love the vanilla ones and am very pleased with them. Not as good as homemade, but that's another discussion. The chocolate ones are all right though the chocolate flavor is very mild and could have been stronger. The strawberry ones, though - I am not a fan, and I am glad that they make up less than a quarter of the box. To me they taste artificial.

The portion sizes are small - only a couple of bites. If you are looking for a small snack that's just enough to curb a craving this box might just be the ticket. If you need something to stave off hunger in between meals, you may need a couple of these though.

Overall, this is a decent box. I really dislike the strawberry flavored ones, but these make up a small number of the whole and otherwise I would buy these again.

title: Sourdough or Soda Bread?
text:
I have been making breads for my family for 25 years and I have learned a lot about what works and what doesn't. I usually favor making things homemade, but I occasionally will use a mix like this one to save time when I want bread but don't have enough time to get it done. This isn't a bad mix but I can't say I'd buy it again - it did not quite meet my expectations.

This is a faily easy and straightforward mix and the instructions are printed right on the bag. It comes together easily enough and it does take time, though the main savings are in not having to maintain a sourdough culture and not having to measure everything. At the end of the process I had a decent-looking loaf.

However...

The first issue is the texture. It came out dense, a lot like a soda bread but not as dry, if that makes sense. I was hoping for something a little more airy and light and instead I got something closer to a brick though not quite that bad.

The second issue is that the sourdough flavor just wasn't there like I had hoped. There's a hint in there, yes, but it does not have the bite of a true sourdough loaf. If you are looking for something that has a real sourdough twang to it, this isn't quite it. The flavor is good, yes; it's just not quite right.

This is not a bad mix at all, but I think it's ambitious to think of it as a sourdough bread. It is more akin to a soda bread.

title: Fresh and Priced Reasonably Per Ounce
text:
McCormick is a well-known name in spices and I have had good fortune with their products. I do use paprika quite a bit and I was interested in this large container of it. So far it has met my expectations and I am happy with it.

The main concern is that this paprika is fresh and flavorful. Right out of the container it is very fresh and aromatic. There's not really anything else that matters. I have gotten containers of it in the past (different band) where the paprika has lost some of its freshness.

This is a larger container - a full pound. It will last a lot longer than the smaller bottles I find in the grocery store and per ounce it is less expensive.

I have no complaints with this paprika. It is priced well, it's in a large quantity, and it is fresh right out of the jar.

title: Quality Chocolates, Packaged to Stay Fresh
text:
I selected this tin of chocolates for my wife who needed a little encouragement. I was unfamiliar with the brand so I was not sure what to expect, though I was hopeful that the chocolates would be of good quality. This assortment exceeded expectations.

This tin has a nice assortment, from salted caramels, turtles, fudge truffles and more. Each is individually wrapped in plastic so they stay fresh much longer, and they come out tasting very fresh even after a week.

The metal box itself is attractive and is suitable for gifting. It is generic enough that it can be used for a variety of occasions, from birthday, Mother's Day, Valentine's Day and even Christmas. It's a solid tin, too, reasonably resistant to crush and drop damage.

This assortment is expensive but it is priced competitively with other higher-end assortments. This is not the kind of chocolates you'd find at the drug store or general department store but in a higher-caliber shop with quality goods.

These are much better than average average chocolates that are sure to please. They're not the cheap stuff you can find everywhere around the holidays but are of good quality and are packaged to stay fresh longer, in a decorative tin that's well-suited for gifting.

title: Versatile; Great Flavor
text:
I am new to chipotle-infused mayonnaise so this is new territory for me. I have no basis for comparison but I'm really liking this stuff. It has a good flavor to it and it works well as a spread as well as a dip. I have not yet tried this as a base for egg salad or other salads that require mayo but I think it would work very well.

I can't say this is the best ever simply because this is the only one I've had. But, it's definitely good stuff and I will buy again.

title: Decent Cinnamon, Priced Well
text:
I like cinnamon as an addition to oatmeal in the morning and it is one of the regular spices I use when making cookies, cakes and very occasionally coffee. I selected this cinnamon container because it has a lot (1 lb.), and so far I have no complaints. It isn't high-end cinnamon, but it isn't bad either.

Right out of the container this cinnamon powder is fresh-smelling and had a pungent cinnamon odor. It gives my oatmeal a good kick of flavor.

Looking at the different containers of cinnamon available here, it is difficult to find anything that sets this one apart. It is priced reasonably, on the lower end but not the cheapest available either. In a line-up I am not sure I would be able to distinguish this particular brand from another in a blind test unless it was being compared to a high-end cinnamon.

I am not unhappy with this cinnamon and likely will buy more when the container is empty. It is not the very best cinnamon I have used but neither is it bad by any means.

title: Good Cookie Bars but Overpriced
text:
I selected these cookie bars with my wife in mind who loves Twix bars and has been looking for ways to cut some sugar and fat from the household menu. To summarize quickly, these are excellent little cookie bars that compare well with the similar candy bar, but these are very expensive to the point of being cost prohibitive.

These are very similar to Twix bars in basic design - cookie in the middle, layer of caramel, all dipped in chocolate. There's no mystery there. There are some definite differences in formulation, though, with dark chocolate instead of milk chocolate and salted caramel instead of sweet. They are packaged better in little pouches and individually wrapped bars from there, making them very likely to stay fresh for a long time.

All that said, the cost of these is exorbitant. As I write this, the cost for the package is $19.99, at $5.88/ounce. Each little mini cookie bar works out to north of $0.80. That's a lot for a bar that's smaller than my finger. Is the price in line with the quality of the product? Some may believe so, but I think it's too high.

I likely will not buy more of these, as they are simply overpriced. They're very good mini bars and they're packaged well to make them last, but the unit pricing is simply higher than I am willing to pay.

title: Excellent but Expensive
text:
I selected these bars for my family as it seems we're always on the go and always in different directions. A snack like this can be grabbed on the way out the door and sufficient for hold one of us over until mealtime. These have proven to be a nice snack that doesn't give us a sugar crash afterward.

These bars have an almond butter base, and they're filled with good things like almonds, dried blueberries and more. They have a great texture and the flavor is better than any of us expected. They're not overly sweet which is a huge plus to me. It's nice having a decent-tasting bar snack that isn't loaded with sugar.

The one reservation I have with these is the price. At over $2/bar as I write this, these fall on the expensive side of things. While these are very good, the question is if these fit the household budget. For those who are on sugar-restricted diets or just want to cut as much refined sugar as possible, this may be a question that answers itself.

We all like these bars and have enjoyed them. I have mostly stayed out of them in favor of letting my family enjoy them, and at some point I likely will pick up another box. These have a higher price tag than many other snack bars available, though.

title: Decent Light Roast; A Little Expensive
text:
I am normally a medium roast kind of guy, but my office mate prefers light roast coffee. I took this bag of coffee to the office to share with him and to get his opinion on it as well. So far, we both like it.

My issue with light roast coffees is that they often have a “green” taste to them like they have been under-roasted. This is not the case with this coffee. It has a decent coffee flavor that is not dissimilar to many medium roasts, though it is not as strong in flavor. As is typical with other light roasts, it has a little more caffeine than medium roasts so it packs more of a kick.

The flavor is not super-deep, but it is rich enough to please me. It does have a subtle sour afternote, though, which is noticeable but not bad and is in line with some light roasts I have tried.

The only reservation I really have about this coffee is that it is slightly expensive. If it were $2-$3 less expensive for this bag I would be more likely to buy more.

This is a decent light roast coffee, with acceptable flavor that doesn’t taste under-roasted. It’s a little on the expensive side for me, but otherwise I have no reservations with recommending it if you like light roast coffee.

title: Very Fresh
text:
My family and I love nuts, so this was an easy choice for us. I specifically gave these to my wife as she was looking for a good snack that wasn't full of sugar. These greatly exceeded our expectations.

There are several different nut types in this assortment: pistachios, English walnuts, candied pecans, hazelnuts (filberts, if you prefer), macadamia nuts, cashews, and almonds. These are unsalted and with the exception of the pistachios, are unshelled.

These nuts are fresh! They came out of the package crunchy and with excellent flavor. There's not much else that one could ask, really. The package was sealed properly so these should last a little while before they're opened.

This is a great assortment to give as a gift, though my family (and my wife in particular) is enjoying this one right now. I will definitely be giving these as gifts to family and friends in the coming months.

title: Decent For Canned Chili!
text:
We like chili dogs in our house and we also have recipes that call for canned chili with no beans, Thinking this would be a good substitute for the chili and separate cheese we decided we’d try this chili with one of our favorite recipes. It worked out well for us and we’re happy with it.

Hormel makes good canned chili suitable for a variety of uses to include chili dogs, and this is no exception. What makes this different is that the cheese is incorporated already so there is no need to add cheese unless you really want even more cheese. The taste is good (if a bit salty) and it works excellently on straight hot dogs. However, it also works well in recipes, where a can of chili with no beans is needed.

I personally prefer a chili that is slightly more lumpy than this particular chili but that’s a personal preference, not a complaint. For most, this chili will be about the right texture for beanless chili to put on hot dogs.

For beanless canned chili, this is better than I expected and it works well on chili dogs as well as in recipes. It has the cheese already in it so there’s no need to add more - unless you really want to.

title: Good Quality and Priced Competitively
text:
I use semolina flour for one thing - making homemade pasta. The choices available to me at the local market are limited so I haven't had a lot of exposure to too many brands. I decided to try this brand and so far I am pleased with it.

This is a 2lb. bag which is a bit bigger than the other bags I have available to me. This is nice in that it will last longer. Better, though, is that the per-ounce price is competitive too, and so it will save me money in the long run. Already we're off to a good start.

Quality-wise this flour is good. It is ground fine and it makes good pasta doughs that are smooth and easy to work with. It seems to hold together well too which is a plus when working with this kind of dough - doughs that rip and require more work become tough and tedious.

So far I am happy with this flour. It is priced well, comes in a good-sized bag and it seems to be of good quality.

title: Excellent Flavor
text:
I have a son who works out frequently and is always hungry and looking for quick snacks. He happens to love coconut too, so this seemed like a good fit for him. These went over very well.

These are a low-sugar high-protein snack bar that taste a lot like toasted coconut. They're reminiscent of a Mounds bar but without the chocolate and having been put under a broiler until it starts to brown a little. In a word, the flavor is excellent. I got about two bites of one bar; my son ate all the rest.

These do a decent job of satisfying hunger when you have a craving too. One of these would hold my son over until the next meal.

I'm buying more of these!

title: Excellent
text:
I started cooking with sea salt years ago and have had good success with it. I recently used up my last box of flake salt so this was the replacement. So far I am pleased.

This is my first use of flake sea salt, and it has been an eye-opening experience. I have used granulated sea salt which is "less salty" than table salt, and I have used kosher flake salt out of a box and it has been fine for what I needed it for. This combines those two, and the result is a flaky, mild salt that doesn't overwhelm the palate and adds a pleasant flavor when used gently.

This is a perfect salt for sprinkling on loaves of bread, homemade biscuits, cheesecakes and more. It adds a small amount of crunch and the saltiness is just right. When baking breads, the same measure of this salt as compared to table salt produces a bread that rises better and doesn't seem to be appreciably impacted in flavor (though using this for making breads seems slightly wasteful to me).

This salt is the good stuff. It tastes better and is better for you than table salt, the texture is more interesting when used to sprinkle, and the quantity (3 lbs.) means it will last a long time.

title: Good, Complex Flavor - Not Overpowered by Vinegar
text:
NOTE: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the Piri Piri sauce.

This is my first exposure to Barnacle Foods sauces so I wasn't sure what I should expect. So far, though, I am pleased with this sauce.

My preference for hot sauces is very simple - I want a sauce that leaves me with a lingering burn for a few minutes after I eat it, and I don't want vinegar to be so dominant that I can barely taste anything else. Few off-the-shelf sauces meet these simple requirements - especially that part about vinegar. This sauce meets both - it gives me that pleasant, lingering burn and I can actually taste other flavors besides vinegar. The flavor is complex and it goes really well on seafoods in particular but it works on other things too like rice, pork, tacos and more.

I am not unhappy with this sauce and will buy more when it's gone. It has really good flavor and it has just the right amount of heat.

title: Complex Flavor
text:
NOTE: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the aged apple cider vinegar, 2-pack.

I use balsamic vinegar in cooking as well as in salad dressings so I do have a bottle of the [relatively] cheap stuff in my pantry. I had never used higher quality balsamic vinegar before so this was an eye-opening experience to me.

Balsamic vinegar and apple cider vinegar have always been two separate things to me, and I have a bottle of grocery-store brand of each. This is a new frontier for me, in that it combines the two into one and it is of higher quality than I would find at the local supermarket. Opening the bottle it smells fresh and good, which is a good sign.

This combines the best qualities of both balsamic and apple cider vinegars into one fusion. It's not just two vinegars mixed together (which just sounds horrible to me anyway), but rather has a depth of flavor that comes from being prepared from the ground up as a single product. In cooking it is far and away more flavorful than either type alone and it imparts the best of both to whatever you're cooking. In dishes that require balsamic as an ingredient it brings the added punch of apple cider as well which changes the dish (in a positive way). It's strong and I would hesitate to substitute this for straight apple cider vinegar though.

Price-wise, this is not inexpensive. However, when considering the price per ounce it is actually priced competitively with upscale brands.

This is a higher-end ingredient for those that like to cook with or season with balsamic vinegar. It has more complex flavor than either balsamic or apple cider vinegars, it is fresh right out of the bottle, and it is priced well.

title: Fresh and Good Flavor
text:
NOTE: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the variety pack.

I selected these nut bags before a trip with the intent of having them in the car along the way. Some of the flavors seems a little odd by description, but when actually sampling them they actually all turned out to be really good. I am quite happy with these.

This is a nice variety pack of nuts that sports some unusual flavor combinations. In addition to sea salt, there is a creole mix, white cheddar & black pepper, and Asian sesame. I had lower expectations on a couple of these, but all of these actually turned out to be far and away better than I expected. The nuts are fresh and crunchy, and the flavors are strong but not overwhelming. I was most concerned about the Asian sesame flavor which tends to be overwhelming in most other things I have tried with this type of seasoning, but these were balanced nicely and had good flavor without overwhelming my senses.

The bags have a ziploc seal so they can be enjoyed over a period of time without losing freshness.

These were better than expected and I will be buying more, to take to the office.

title: Flavor and Quantity is Good; Don't Like the Texture
text:
I will be blunt - my family and I didn't care too much for these.

The size and packaging are fine. There's a reasonable amount in each pouch to be just about right for a snack on the go.

The taste is all right. It reminds me of Thanksgiving sweet potato casserole, though the flavor is not as strong and it's served cold instead of hot.

Where this snack lost us was in the texture. It is firm but squshy at the same time and bears a vague resemblance to prunes in texture. We all were expecting these to be a bit more firm than that. They're moist and mildly sticky too, enough so that after eating a couple of these out of one pouch we needed to wash hands.

Perhaps these will work for other families, but they didn't work so well for us. There are some good things I can say about the flavor and the quantity in each pouch, but the texture is a complete turn-off for all of us in the house.

title: Finally, a Good-Tasting Energy Drink
text:
I will start by saying that I really do not like energy drinks. Every one I have tried in the past has had a bad taste, not unlike carbonated drink mixes with fake flavors and so much sugar that I feel worse after drinking one. I was not particularly optimistic about these energy drinks, and I was pleasantly surprised.

I have the grapefruit flavor, and these taste like, well, grapefruit. The Stevia used for sweetener isn't nasty like in other Stevia-sweetened things I have had, and the caffeine is enough to give me a modest jump start in the morning when I haven't slept well. The caffeine content in one of these cans it approximately equivalent to two cups of coffee.

I'm not unhappy with these energy drinks. They actually taste good and there's enough caffeine in them (without the sugar) to make them effective.

title: Cost Disproportionate to the Flavor
text:
I have developed a serious coffee habit over the last couple of years and I have definitely developed a palate for different coffees. I usually like Hawaiian coffee, though admittedly it is not my favorite. I was a little put off by the price of this coffee ($45 for a 12-oz. bag as I write this), but I assumed this would be some excellent coffee. I do not think the price matches the quality.

This isn't exactly a bad coffee, but I have had smoother and more pleasing Hawaiian brews. This particular coffee has a decent flavor but it has a distinct sour note to it that I find mildly off-putting. To be fair, I ground the coffee and used it immediately so it did not have time to go stale. I ground some and put it in the refrigerator for a couple of days, and this didn't fix anything (didn't expect it to, but it was worth a try). A shot of creamer did take some of the bite away, but not enough to make it work for me.

This is not bad coffee, but it is definitely far more expensive than most other coffees I have tried and the cost is disproportionate to the quality in my opinion. Perhaps others will like this coffee; I am mostly indifferent.

title: Cans Ruptured During Shipment
text:
I was looking forward to enjoying this drink mix, but unfortunately I received a product that was completely unusable. The two canisters were packed in an oversized box with no padding and as such, the cans were jostled hard enough that they both ruptured, spreading sugary pink powder everywhere in the box. Even worse, the contents were exposed to moisture along the way, so that even though there was a plastic liner in the box the powder was caked and sticky. Because of the poor packing and shipping, the entire package was completely ruined.

I know this is a good product, and I was very interested in the high quantity, but based on my experience I would strongly advise against purchasing unless you’re willing to chance a ruined shipment and dealing with returns.

title: Amazing Coffee; Great Aroma and Flavor
text:
I have gotten to a point in my coffee-drinking career that I have become a bit of a coffee snob of sorts. I know what I like – strong flavor that isn’t bitter, a good caffeine kick, and minimal stomach upset. A good aroma is a big plus as it makes the house smell nice as it’s brewing. This coffee checks all the boxes for me and I will absolutely be buying more when this bag is gone.

I had read other reviewers’ comments about the aroma before the bag arrived. When my bag arrived, I saw the mail carrier stuff it into my mailbox. It was in the box less than 5 minutes when I got to it, and when I opened my mailbox to take the bag out my whole mailbox smelled like fresh coffee. The claims that it has a good aroma are probably understated – this has a LOT of aroma and it smells outstanding.

This is a medium roast coffee which is exactly what I like. For me personally, dark roasts usually have an unpleasant flavor and light roasts lack depth. Medium roasts can be hit or miss, depending on how close to either end of the scale they are. This particular coffee is smooth with little bitterness, rich flavor and an aroma that wakes even the non-coffee-drinkers the house while it’s brewing.

So far, it has not upset my stomach or otherwise caused me any trouble. And, there’s enough caffeine in there to get me rolling in the morning.

This is excellent coffee. It has an amazing aroma and it is one of the better medium roasts I have tried. When the bag is empty, I will be buying more.

title: Mixed Reactions
text:
I selected these hot sauces for my son who absolutely loves hot sauces. I like hot sauces too but not ones that are overwhelmed by the taste of vinegar. We were both interested in these sauces and were eager to try them out. We had mixed reactions.

I’ll be blunt here - my son is not a fan, at all. I like them. This point of contention is the truffle oil, which comes through strong. As it turns out, he does not like truffle oil whereas I don’t have any issue with it.

Without the truffle oil, these sauces would be nothing remarkable, to be honest. The heat is mild at best and the flavor is decent but does not distinguish itself except for the truffle oil.

These are packaged nicely in a gift box.

We have mixed opinions about these sauces. I like them, my son does not. The truffle oil is actually the dominant flavor, and the spiciness is mild. At the price point, I was hoping for better.

title: High Quality, High Price
text:
Note: There are several products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the Mild single pouch of jerky.

My family and I love beef jerky, though we do not buy it often because we usually grab it when we’re traveling. I have had good beef jerky and bad beef jerky at different times, and I was hopeful that this should be among the better we’ve tried. It definitely is above average, and it quite possibly could be the best any of us have ever had, but it has one noticeable negative - it is very expensive.

This is not typical jerky in that it is more thoroughly dried and is cut thinner. The result is something with a lot more chew to it and it takes more effort to actually chew up than typical jerkies which still has some moisture in it. I was surprised initially when I worked on a piece of this stuff, but it actually is quite satisfying to chew on.

The flavor is nothing short of outstanding. It has a very definite peppery taste to it but it doesn’t have the “bite” that most pepper-coated jerky does, and as a result you can taste the other flavors more easily and without getting the typical mild spicy burn that comes with black pepper.

The one issue I have with it is the price. As I write this, the cost per bag for a single is approaching $16/bag. That’s very expensive, even when considering that this is higher-quality jerky than most. Buying a variety pack is a lot better, where you get $25/4 which is $6.25/bag. Unfortunately, if you want 4 of one flavor you have to buy them individually. Hopefully that will be changed in the future, as I would definitely buy more in that case.

This is excellent jerky, of better flavor and higher quality than most. It is held back only by the cost per bag and lack of packaging by flavors.

title: Fine Bittersweet Chocolate, but Very Expensive
text:
I selected these chocolate bars, knowing they'd be bittersweet chocolate and thinking they'd be suitable for baking. These are good bittersweet bars, with a very high price tag.

I received a box of 12 of these bars, and they are individually wrapped with a bendy closure not unlike a bag of coffee beans, only smaller. The ones we have opened so far have been fresh and haven't shown any signs of sitting on a shelf for any length of time or having been exposed to heat.

Taste-wise, these are not the kind of bar everyone will enjoy. Because there have only a small hint of sweetness, these are actually on the bitter side but avoid the bite that I have encountered with some other bittersweet chocolate bars. These are great in small doses and work well chopped and sprinkled on sweet things like a frosted cake or a heavily loaded sundae.

What gives me pause is the price tag. As I write this, the price on the box of 12 is north of $50 which is quite high, working out to over $4 per bar. That's steep and is the main factor that prevents me from buying more. If the cost dropped by $20 or more for the box, I'd find the price to be much more reasonable.

These are very good bittersweet chocolate bars. They are fresh and are wrapped carefully. The downside is the high price which is the main complaint I have with them.

title: Good Replacement for Dairy Chocolate Milk
text:
Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am writing this review specifically for the chocolate oat milk.

My wife has been on an almond milk kick, using that in place of dairy milk for a variety of things from breakfast cereal to coffee creamer. We were both interested in trying oat milk, and I was pleased to get the opportunity to try this particular chocolate oat milk. It’s not bad at all, but it’s not quite what I expected.

This stuff has a nice flavor, let’s make that clear right out of the gate. It is very similar to chocolate milk, but I would stop short of saying it tastes the same. If you like chocolate milk, then there is a much better-than-even chance you’ll like this.

Two things stand out about this oat milk that are worth mentioning. First, it has a strange texture, or “mouth feel” so to speak. What comes to mind is drinking liquid with a powder stirred it that didn’t quite dissolve and has a very slightly sandy texture to it. It’s not gritty or sandy, exactly, but it isn’t completely smooth either. Second, it has an aftertaste that is very comparable to the flavor of raw oats right out of the canister. Perhaps a closer comparison is that the aftertaste is similar to the smell of oats just when you open the canister for the first time and get a sniff of the oat dust that comes out.

This isn’t exactly low-calorie stuff either. It has a fair amount of sugar in it, and with the carbs that come with oats there’s a non-trivial amount of calories per serving. Keep this in mind.

What I did find puzzling when I read through the ingredient list – while made from plant products only I did not see vegan/vegetarian markings on the package anywhere. If the markings are there I missed them. According to the manufacturer everything in the package comes from vegan sources, so I do not understand why this point isn’t made a little more obvious.

So, while it may sound that I am being very critical of this oat milk, I do actually like it and I see it as a good option for people with lactose intolerance. It does have a nice flavor, it doesn’t have to be stored in the refrigerator until opened, and it is completely non-dairy. It is not identical to dairy milk but it is a good substitute.

title: Fresh and Priced Well
text:
I love Swedish Fish and I usually get a half-pound bag of them every year as a Christmas gift. A box of 12 half-pound bags is a dream come true for me!

The most important thing – these are fresh, not stale like they sometimes are when you buy them in the store. The next most important thing – this is a good price for these when broken down per unit. As I write this, the case is priced such that each individual bag inside would sell for $1.47 which is far better than I can find in most retail shops.

If you like Swedish Fish and you want a lot of them, or if you have several kids that like them, this is a good deal. The fish are fresh and the price is good.

title: Excellent Alternative to Other Available Mini Candies
text:
Everyone in my house loves Toblerone chocolate, so this was an easy choice for my household. So far, no complaints.

This is a perfect gift box of sorts. The outer container is a small, flat box that is tastefully designed, and inside there are three prism-shaped smaller boxes in which the candies are packed. My understanding, which was incorrect, is that there would be three separate boxes with one type of Toblerone candy each; instead, each box has a mix of all three types which is actually better.

There are three types: dark chocolate, milk chocolate, and white chocolate. Each bar is individually wrapped and is the approximate size of a Hershey’s mini chocolate bar. These can all remain in the Toblerone box for display, or they can be dumped out into a candy dish (which is what my wife has done).

The candies are fresh and taste as you’d expect, so there’s no storage issue or difference in quality from the full-sized bars.

These are not cost-prohibitive, either. They’re a little more than I would want to spend on a regular basis, but I will definitely purchase these for special occasions.

This is a fine alternative to other types of mini candies and these are of higher quality than many other brands. If you like Toblerone but don’t want a whole bar (or you want filler for the candy dish), this is a good option. I will be buying more of these.

title: Good Quality Cinnamon at a Reasonable Asking Price
text:
My previous experience with Happy Belly products was a huge bag of shelled pecans and they were of high quality. Based on that, I was hopeful that this cinnamon would be good and would be a good value for the asking price. I was right – this is another good-quality product, and it is priced nicely.

First, a word about the size. This is a big container, holding 15oz. of cinnamon. That’s a lot more than any other container I have seen (though I have since seen larger ones). If you work with cinnamon a lot (and around the holidays, who doesn’t), this is a container that will ensure you don’t run out anytime soon.

Upon opening the container and breaking the seal, I was greeted with the strong, distinct fragrance of fresh cinnamon, not stale cinnamon that’s been on a shelf for a year. I do not know how fresh it is, specifically, but it is definitely more fresh than any container I have gotten from the grocery store in recent memory. The fragrance translates to the flavor of things prepared with it and the cinnamon remains bright and unmistakable.

As I write this, the asking price on this container is $10.99 which is reasonable. There are less expensive options and those are fine if you don’t need “the good stuff” in what you’re preparing, but the cost is not unrealistic. In this case, you get what you pay for.

This is good-quality cinnamon at a good asking price. It’s fresh and aromatic, and the container is larger than average.

title: Another Vinegar-Based Sauce
text:
I will start by saying that this is a large jug of sauce, larger than is typically useful to a household unless doing a lot of barbecuing or cooking for a huge crowd like a family reunion. It requires some refrigerator real estate unless you use it quickly.

I’ll get right to the point – I do not care for sauces where the star ingredient is vinegar and I tend to make my own for this reason. I mean, I get it – the vinegar is important and it does have its place in just about every sauce, but the tendency is to be heavy-handed with vinegar to the point that it is the first thing you taste in many sauces. This one is better than some but still heavy enough with the vinegar that it’s the first flavor that hits my palette.

Fortunately the vinegar does not completely drown out everything else. There’s a good smoky flavor with tomato and molasses as well. There’s a good little kick to it too that gives a nice, slow burn for the finish. It’s not going to light your mouth on fire, but it does let you know it’s there.

I am not a huge fan because of the vinegar which is the first thing I taste in this sauce. It’s better than many sauces I have tried, though, in that it isn’t absolutely overwhelming with that specific flavor which is why I have given it 4/5 instead of 3/5. I’ve used it once so far; I will revisit after I have used it a few times if my perception changes for the better.

title: Good Flavor, but Weak
text:
My family and I use honey frequently, most often for cooking but also for spreading on toast and cornbread. We all like strawberry too, so we were all very interested in this strawberry honey. It’s a good flavor but a little on the weak side.

Spread on toast, the honey flavor and the strawberry flavors are distinct and mostly separable, but the strawberry is definitely the lesser of the flavors and is somewhat overpowered by the honey. Interestingly, the honey is very light, which says to me that a very light hand included the strawberry.

A heavier grade of honey and more strawberry would have made this even better.

title: Better than Most
text:
I use chili powder often so a large container like this is economical for me (and convenient too). I didn’t have any real idea what would set this apart as a “dark” chili powder from more generic chili powders, though I have usually had good experiences with McCormick spices. To summarize, this is a good chili spice blend that is a little better than most generic blends.

Looking at it sitting next to another chili powder canister I have, it is indeed slightly darker in color. That’s neither good nor bad unless you have a recipe where the appearance is impacted. The difference isn’t so much in the appearance but rather in the taste. This chili powder has a stronger (not necessarily hotter), fresher flavor than most other powders I have tried, and in my opinion that’s a very big plus. It adds a little deeper depth of flavor to chili and other southwestern dishes than more generic powders don’t.

The container is 20 oz., and unless you’re making food for a very large group, working a grilling circuit or working in a commercial environment, it will last a long time. Per ounce it is reasonably priced too.

This is good chili powder that is priced well and in good quantity. It has a little more flavor than many of the others I’ve tried, though it does not seem to add appreciably more heat.

title: Great Addition to Spice Rub Mixture
text:
I make my own spice rubs for grilling and two of the main ingredients I use are salt and smoked paprika. I wanted this salt for the purpose of making my spice rub, and it’s an outstanding addition to my spice mix.

I wasn’t sure how smoky this salt would be but I got the answer almost as soon as I opened the pouch. The smoke flavor is very strongly infused into the salt, and you can smell it and taste it very distinctly. As an ingredient in a rub, it imparts the same salty, smoky smell, even more so than the smoked paprika.

This is my new semi-secret ingredient in my spice rub mix.

title: Better Quality than Expected
text:
I usually do not mess with K-cups as I have found the emphasis in most K-cup products to be geared for convenience instead of quality. That said, I was eager to try these as I like maple pecan flavors, though I had some apprehension with their addition in coffee. It turns out these are better than I expected and the quality is better than average.

When brewing, the smell of the maple and pecan is strong enough to draw the attention of my coworkers. I was hopeful that the flavors would be stronger than that of other K-cup brews I have tried. They are, though the smell is still very definitely stronger than the flavor. I was pleased in that there was no bitterness in the cup either, which is a problem I have encountered numerous times with K-cups, usually when it was unclear how old the cups were.

I still found I prefer a small amount of half-and-half (just a splash), though I use even less sweetener than I have needed in other coffees. Green Mountain did a good job of producing a pod product that can stand on its own.

I still prefer plain coffee with little to no embellishment, but this is better than the average pod brew. If you like flavored coffee, in particular maple and pecan flavors, and you are fussy about the quality of the cup, this is a very good choice.

title: There are Better Choices Available for Less Money
text:
Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the variety pack of 4.

My wife is an absolute popcorn fanatic and she often has a small bowl of it close by wen she needs a snack. She does have a favorite brand on which she has settled, but that does not stop us from experimenting and looking for other brands and varieties. I had not seen Giada popcorn prior to this, so I took a chance on it.

My wife (the main consumer of popcorn in the house) summarized her opinion on this popcorn as simply: ok popcorn, nothing special.

There are three varieties in the 4-pack: sea salt, parmesan and butter. The fourth bag was another parmesan.

Trying each, the popcorn is relatively fresh. The flavor is not particularly strong though, so either you have to tweak them a touch or learn to deal with “light” flavors. In one of the bags we did notice a slight burned flavor (one of the reasons I usually do not eat popcorn is that burned popcorn is horrible).

Price-wise, this popcorn is on the expensive side. We have found better popcorn for less than half the price, at the local supermarket. For this reason alone we don’t plan to buy more.

While not terrible popcorn, it’s not especially good either. The flavor isn’t where it should be and the asking price is too high.

title: Outstanding!
text:
I love caramels and I have a friend who makes them on occasion. Homemade caramels are far and away better than most pre-packaged caramels, and at a glance these look hand made and hand rolled. Other than the freshly made and rolled caramels that my friend makes, these are some of the very best I have had.

These are very soft, chewy and sweet, with a creamy, smooth texture unlike most pre-packaged caramels. Right off the bat, that’s a good thing. I can get these hard and tough like the others, but it requires putting them in the refrigerator for a while...

Flavor-wise, these are outstanding. The description says that they’re made with butter and vanilla, and you can really taste those. What you cannot taste much is salt - and that’s ok because the salt would actually take away a little bit from these caramels. It’s there, but it is a minor flavor.

Unless you make caramels yourself or are fortunate enough to have a friend who makes them for you, you’re not likely to find caramels much better than these. The flavor and texture are far superior to the little square things we all know and put up with, and these are ready now without a big mess in the kitchen to clean up.

title: Just Ok - The Flavor Isn't There
text:
I like to have granola bars in my lunch and my son grabs them for breakfast since he gets to work early. I had not heard of Junkless granola bars, so I was excited to try these. I have to be honest, they’re not as good as I had hoped.

My first observation - these are on the small side. They’re a bit smaller than other other granola bars I have had, smaller enough that they’re not much of a substitute in terms of satisfying hunger. That said, they’re ok when I need a small snack.

Flavor-wise, these fall a bit short. The most flavorful, to me, are the cinnamon roll bars. In my opinion, though, something is just a bit off with them though I cannot quite pinpoint it. The others taste good, but the flavor is subdued at best. When my family tried them, they all agreed - these are lacking in taste.

I am not a huge fan and probably will not be buying more. They might be a healthy alternative to other chewy bars, but they are on the small side and they’re just not strongly flavored enough for us, though I suspect some others will disagree.

title: Trade-offs; Quality is Decent, Convenience is Great
text:
I selected these pods to go with my Nespresso maker. I like a good strong coffee though I usually do not consume espresso in its purest form, making cappuccino with it more often than not. That said, I like espresso on occasion, and this makes a decent cup for the convenience.

There are 20 pods in the box, working out to just over $1/cup. That’s a bit pricey per unit, but at the same time these are very convenient and it’s still cheaper than getting a cup of espresso in a typical restaurant or specialty coffee shop.

The espresso produced is not stellar, but decent. It’s strong and it has good flavor. Of course, it’s nice not having to clean up a huge mess afterward.

While not my personal preference in coffee, this is a good solution for making espresso on demand. The quality is decent and the convenience is great.

title: Love These!
text:
NOTE: There are several different products attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the coconut fudge dipped thins.

Oreo cookies are a favorite in our house and I was eager to try these Thin Bites. They have proven to be a huge hit with my family and I will definitely be buying more.

In the package there are 6 pouches of cookies. This doesn’t seem like a lot until you open then and realize that each thin is about as big around as a quarter and about twice as thick. This is a great snacking size – I can grab 3-4 little rounds and not feel like I am over-indulging. Each package lasts 2-4 days in our house and we all got into them.

The flavor is great. These are not overly sweet (a problem a lot of cookies and sweets have), and I can definitely taste the coconut flavor. It’s nice that they have a satisfying crunch too.

With my stash now gone, I have taken to buying them a bag at a time when I get the weekly groceries.

title: Best Caramel Syrup We've Tried
text:
NOTE: There are several products attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the Caramel flavor syrup.

I will be blunt – I do not like caramel flavored syrups in my coffee and I won’t touch them. However, my son is a coffee addict and he absolutely loves caramel syrup in his coffee. I selected this item for him to try and my feedback here is based on conversations with him.

To cut to the quick – he told me this is the very best caramel syrup he has tried.

The dispenser is a good one and is very functional. It is a pump-style bottle so you can meter out the amount easily without using measuring cups or spoons and without having to estimate the quantity. There are other brands that use a pump like this one, but this one is a bit larger and in our experience is a bit easier to handle because of the size.

The syrup itself is strong and definitely imparts a good caramel flavor (if that’s your thing). When my son makes his coffee, I can smell it from across the room. He says it tastes almost as strong as it smells which says quite a bit since I can smell the caramel in his coffee. The syrup gives a clean, rich caramel flavor without tasting like it’s burnt, a problem with some of the other available syrups.

Though I am not a fan, I will definitely buy more of this syrup for my son when the bottle is gone. It’s a little on the pricey side but it’s not outrageous.

title: On the Weak Side
text:
I enjoy my coffee, usually in the mornings. I usually go for a medium roast but I do have dark roasts on occasion, and espresso when I need the coffee hit. I hadn’t heard of Lavazza before receiving a bag for review so I was eager to dig in and find out what it’s all about. It’s good coffee, but not as strong as I would expect from an espresso.

It is definitely an espresso grind, being almost powdery right out of the bag. It’s fresh too - as soon as you open the bag you can smell the coffee and it smells great. So far, so good.

I measured some out and put it in the coffee maker and set about making a cup of espresso. It smelled right while it was brewing and when it was done I had a nice cup of espresso - except that it was not as strong as I was expecting (or as strong as other espressos I have tried). It’s good, but somewhat weak for espresso, and in that regard it’s a little disappointing. Subsequent cups yielded the same.

This is good espresso, but I would stop short of saying it’s great.

title: Very Good Coffee - and Very Expensive
text:
There are several coffee flavors attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the Dark Roast.

I am not a dark roast coffee person, I am a medium roast kind of guy. Most of the dark roast coffees I have tried have had either a very bitter taste or a burnt taste to them, and as such I have avoided dark roasts most of the time. I was interested in trying this dark roast, though, as I had not heard of the brand before and I am not shy about trying something new. I’m glad I did - I finally found a dark roast that I actually really like. It has excellent flavor, and it manages to avoid the bitterness and burnt flavor of other dark roasts I have tried.

I took this bag to the office with the intention of sharing with my office mates. I didn’t share. I brought the bag back home and I’m going to drink all of it myself.

The bag does not give any clues as to where the coffee beans were actually grown. This is a little unusual as most whole-bean bags tend to have some indication as to the origin. I don’t regard it as a big deal, but it’s a little on the unusual side.

My biggest concern is the price which is a little steep for a 1-lb. bag. For the dark roast the current price as I write this is $17.99 and the other flavors are higher (some close to double). That’s a hefty price tag on a 1-lb. bag of coffee, and though the coffee is quite delicious it’s difficult to justify the cost beyond the occasional special occasion. Will I buy more? Probably, but it will be a treat versus a regular occurrence.

title: Decent Flavor, but Very Overpriced
text:
I love peanut butter, especially natural peanut butters. I was intrigued by this particular peanut butter (Spicy Thai) and was willing to try it, but I had an even better idea - I took it to the office to share with my boss, who eats almost nothing but Asian cuisine (Thai in particular). I wanted to get his opinion on it, and together we tried it one afternoon. In summary - good stuff but it’s pricey.

Natural peanut butter is simply ground peanuts and salt - not a bunch of sugar and other stuff. As a result, oil separates and settles on top, so you have to stir it to get it to combine again. This peanut butter is no different. That’s not a bad thing, but be sure to stir down to the bottom of the jar or the peanut butter close to the bottom will get very dry and pasty. Also, it gets harder to stir and spread when you store it in the refrigerator. The jar doesn’t say to refrigerate after opening, but it’s probably not a bad idea to do so...

This particular peanut butter has been infused with lime and spicy pepper (cayenne), with a touch of sugar and a couple other ingredients. It isn’t overwhelmingly spicy, but it does have a twang to it that you won’t get with other peanut butters. If you like a spicy hit in everything you eat, this is an interesting choice that will work on celery, pretzels and other snacks.

The main issue I see with this peanut butter is the price. As I write this, the price is just north of $16/jar and that’s just crazy. I could see spending half that, perhaps, but I could spend half right now and get the ingredients to mix my own version.

It’s an interesting product with a good flavor and it is definitely for those who like a little zing in their foods, even their peanut butter. However, the pricing is outrageous.

title: Good Coffee; Very Finely Ground (a Little Too Fine)
text:
I enjoy a good cup of coffee in the mornings (especially on the weekends) and I love trying new blends and brands. I had never heard of Lavazza before now, so this was a grand experiment for me. In a nutshell, it makes a flavorful cup of coffee but it is ground so finely that it is more appropriate for espresso than a regular cup ‘o joe (if you use a French press this isn’t the best choice).

The coffee is very fresh and the aroma definitely is very good when the bag is opened. We used this coffee in our Ninja to make a couple of servings, and we agreed that it has a very good flavor (not bitter), on the strong side but not espresso strength. I can’t call it my favorite, but it is definitely a coffee I like and I will use up the whole bag.

The problem here is with the grind. It is powder fine and it if it was a dark roast I would label it as espresso. In a French press, this is ground too finely to be workable without getting grounds through the filter screen and into the coffee. I would recommend it only for drip-style coffee makers, for which is does well.

I can’t call this the perfect coffee, but I would describe it as good. It would be better if it were ground just a little less finely.

title: Tastes Good but Smells Better
text:
During the work week I almost always have a cup of oatmeal with cinnamon, sugar, pecans and some kind of fruit. It’s a good breakfast but variety is a good thing that keeps it more interesting. I was interested in trying this cinnamon apple spice mix, to liven up my breakfast a bit. It’s a good mix, but it’s not quite what I had hoped.

McCormick chose to use the small, square-ish container similar to their other spice offerings. This isn’t as much of a problem as the package is colorful and not easily confused with other spices on a spice rack. This particular package has 12 canisters, so it likely will last a long time unless used in a very large family setting or commercial setting. Consistency of the mix is a very fine powder, almost like espresso-grind coffee. It’s easy to shake, spoon or pour out of the container and so far I have not had problems with clumping.

It smells absolutely wonderful! That said, it smells a little better than it tastes and when I had some on my oatmeal I was mildly disappointed that the flavors were much more subdued. It doesn’t taste bad, don’t get me wrong, but it doesn’t quite taste as great as it smells to me. This may or may not be a function of my sense of smell, so I am hesitant to pan this until I get feedback from others. I have taken some to the office to share with coworkers to see what they think.

This is a good spice mix that adds some pizzazz to breakfast foods like oatmeal and cream of wheat. It does have a nice flavor and it is very easy to put into foods. It likely will make a great addition to sugar cookies, popovers, muffins and more. My one reservation is that while it tastes good, it smells so much better that it’s a bit of a letdown.

title: Cost Effective
text:
NOTE: I am writing this review for the 8-ounce bag of chopped walnuts which is what I received.

My wife loves walnuts and she has been known to steal my stash that I use for cooking. I was excited when I was given the opportunity to review this large bag (as it means I have a fair shot of being able to use more of them before she wipes them out). So far, it has met my expectations. It’s not the highest quality brand out there but it is widely available and it is very consistent in its quality. This larger bag is more of the same, at a better cost per ounce.

This is a pre-chopped bag and for the very large majority of cases the size of the pieces is fine. These work well in most cookie recipes, banana bread, muffins and more. There are occasions when I have needed to chop them a bit more, and because they’re already in fairly small pieces that’s an easy task.

The little pouches of nuts you usually find at the grocery stores are either 1-cup or 2-cup bags, which is ok but it means you have to buy several if you need to make something in quantity. It also means often not having any left over. With this 1/2 lb. bag, there’s enough to make most things that call for a cup (or two) of walnuts and still have more for later. And, at this size it is much more cost-effective per ounce than buying the smaller bags.

The one thing I have noticed about Fisher nuts, walnuts in particular, is that without properly storing them they will go rancid relatively quickly. The solution for us has been to store them in the freezer when we’re not using them. Other brands we have used have done the same so it’s not unique to Fisher, but some of the other brands have not gone rancid quite as quickly when stored in the pantry instead of the freezer. It’s just something to keep in mind.

I am pleased with this bag (well, my wife is more so). I really like the quantity and being chopped already has been a good time saver for me in the majority of cases. It’s priced well as compared to the smaller bags and with proper storage they stay fresh.

title: High Quality, High Price Tag
text:
I personally go through a lot of pecans, usually as an embellishment to oatmeal in the mornings but I also use them for making other dishes such as caramel rolls and pecan pie. My go-to has been the big bag that my local warehouse club store sells, as it’s cost effective and I don’t have to buy more every week. I was interested in trying this bag by Happy Belly; I have used their cinnamon and have been pleased with it so I has hopeful that the pecans would also be a high-quality product. They are, but they’re also quite expensive.

First things first - this is a big bag! 2.5 lbs. of pecans is a lot, and it will last a while unless you prepare things with pecans at almost every meal. I have had this bag for several weeks now and I’m still working on it. It’s a great size if you need a lot of shelled halves.

Speaking of halves, most of the time when I get a bag of halves, regardless of bag size, a good number of the halves within are broken and I get a lot of little pieces that settle in the bottom of the bag. That has not been so much of a problem with this bag. There are definitely some and that’s going to happen in shipping no matter how careful they’re handled, but it seems to be significantly less in this bag than I have seen with other brands.

A very important consideration is freshness. Most people who work with nuts frequently understand that you have to either use them quickly or keep them in the fridge or freezer to keep the oils in them from going rancid. However, many times I have had pecans that have gone past their freshness peak in the bag before the bag is even opened. When I opened this particular bag, I was immediately struck with how fresh they smelled. They do not have any bitterness at all, and they have not gone stale.

The catch is that this is a very expensive bag, approaching twice what I spend when I buy from the warehouse store. Yes, these are a lot better, but I question if the price (presently over $30 for the bag) is worth the difference.

I do really, really like these pecans. It’s a good quantity, they’re not broken in pieces on arrival and they come out of the bag very fresh. The question to ask is if the extra expense is worth it. For me, I will probably continue to buy from the warehouse store for most occasions but will buy these when I need to make something particularly special (like breakfast on Christmas morning).

title: Better Than I Expected - Not Bitter
text:
I am no coffee snob but I do know what I like and dislike. Most less expensive coffees I have tried have been very disappointing and have been either burnt or otherwise bitter so I did not have high expectations of this coffee given the price point. I was pleasantly surprised when I had some of this coffee - it’s smoother and not bitter at all.

I made a travel cup full of coffee for myself yesterday evening using this package. At night I do occasionally drink a little decaf for the taste and for the warmth, and I was in a mood for some. When I opened the package I took a deep whiff so see what I would be facing: it smells rich but not strong and there wasn’t any hint of burnt which is a good sign.

When I brewed it up and took a sip, I was even more encouraged - there’s little to no bitterness at all and I got a smooth, rich coffee flavor with no hint of burnt. Would I call it perfect? No. But as I write this it’s priced at $6.99 for a 12-oz. bag, and I really can’t find fault with it when most other quality coffees are selling for quite a bit more.

I do not drink decaf regularly so I likely would never have tried this coffee without having been given the opportunity to try some for review. I likely will buy more now that I know. For the price, it’s far better than I would have expected. I likely will also try some of the other varieties, too.

title: A Little Expensive, Susceptible to Heat, but Good
text:
I am always looking for quick snack ideas as I have a son who needs food on the go for work and school. I was interested in these as a potential idea. They’re a little pricey, and they are susceptible to heat, but the flavor is good and they meet the need.

I received a 12-count box of the Chocolate Marshmallow bars for review so that is specifically what I am reviewing here. Some of my comments may not apply to other flavors.

These come twelve in a box, and the price for these is approximately $1.20 each as I write this. That’s a little on the high side, as these are not dense and heavy like a traditional energy bar. They’re actually very light, which is both positive and negative when considering the intent. The energy comes from a caffeine infusion, though I have found these to be a little less effective than drinking a cup of coffee. Check the unit pricing when deciding between the 12- or 30-count boxes – as I write this, the 12-count box is more economical per bar.

Flavor-wise, these are great. They taste like a rich fudge brownie with a drizzle of frosting, and they are not overwhelmingly sweet. Another reviewer claimed that these are too sweet but I personally disagree. On this point, I suppose it comes down to personal preference. The drizzle is mild and represents the marshmallow flavoring.

These are very susceptible to heat. They arrived on a warm day and were in the mail box when I received them. When I opened the box and tried one of the bars, the frosting had melted off and the bar was hard to hold as it had gotten very soft. After allowing them to cool down to room temperature, they were much more stable and easy to work with.

These are nice bars that taste good and provide a modest boost of energy. They’re on the expensive side, and they melt/soften easily, but they are a good solution for a quick snack when there isn’t time for anything else or you’re on the go.

title: Fresh Out of the Bag, Diced Very Uniformly
text:
I use a small handful of pecans almost daily in the office, to toss into my morning oatmeal. I usually have pecan halves which I break up by hand and drop into my oats, which has worked wonderfully for a while. Chopped pecans are more convenient, so I was pleased to have the opportunity to try these. These are chopped almost perfectly for my oatmeal, but they work well in other things too like cookies, coffee cakes and more.

This is a nice, 1-pound bag which lasts for more than a single recipe.

There are really only two things I can share about these. First, as I mentioned above these are chopped very uniformly into small bits, though not ground, so these are ideal for cooking when you need chopped pecans. One thing that comes to mind is refrigerated pecan shortbread cookies which require chopped nuts, and these are ideal. They are also just right for my morning oatmeal.

Second, and more important, right out the bag these are fresh. Older nuts start to get rancid, and I looked for this when I opened the bag. It’s not a problem when the bag is first opened, though I do recommend either using them all up quickly or keeping them in the freezer.

I am very pleased with these pecans and will be buying more when this bag runs out.

title: High Quality but More Expensive than Most Organic Cinnamon Containers
text:
I cook with cinnamon a lot so a 1-lb. container is a good thing for my kitchen. I usually get it in large containers from the local club warehouse store due to cost, but I was interested in trying this cinnamon as it is a brand of which I had never heard prior. The cinnamon itself is good; the price, however, is quite high.

This is listed as organic cinnamon which is likely the cause for the high price tag. It is slightly higher than most organic cinnamon available here, though it is not outrageously so. That said, if you do not need strictly organic cinnamon, there are definitely less expensive alternatives.

Upon opening the container, you’re greeted with a very strong, almost flowery fragrance that suggests freshness and quality. It was startling to me when I opened the container because I was not expecting such a strong aroma, even though it is very pleasant. The smell is indicative of how well it flavors foods as well and it carries over when you’re cooking - expect it to have more impact than most cinnamon you buy off the shelf. This is one counterweight to the price tag.

This is very excellent cinnamon, with the one drawback of being very expensive. Unless you absolutely need organic, there are far less expensive alternatives. Even if you do need organic, there are several choices that will cost a little less.

title: Decent, but a Little Dry and a Little Bland
text:
I am always looking for good snack ideas for my family. I had the opportunity to try these organic cheese crackers and I decided I had nothing to lose, so I did try them with my family. They're good crackers, though they are a little dry and slightly lacking in flavor.

These are cheese crackers in the style of Ritz Bits crackers – two crackers with a little bit of cheese sandwiched in between them. I usually do not care for cheese crackers, but these are all right. We did notice that they are a little on the dry side and not as flavorful. That is, these were really bland and the crackers themselves could have used a little more fat to keep them from being so dry and almost powdery.

As with everything labeled “organic” these are a little on the pricey side. I question if being organic merits the price; I likely will opt for regular cheese sandwich crackers next time, based on the price and the flavor.

These are good crackers, but they are not the hit we had hoped. They are a little dry and a little bland, but if you are looking for something organic in particular, these are worth trying at least once.

title: Clean and Bright Flavor
text:
I am a relatively recent convert to coffee from soda and I have come to appreciate a good cup of coffee in the morning. It is one of the comforts in the office in the morning to have a hot cup of coffee as I settle in. Freshly ground coffee is almost magical compared to pre-ground bags of coffee and in most cases compared to pre-made single serving pods. I have had other Dancing Moon coffees so I was interested in trying the Kenya Kirinyaga. It is a very flavorful coffee and very enjoyable as my first cup of coffee in the morning.

Just opening the bag I'm greeted with the strong and pleasant aroma of fresh coffee beans. That is one of the most pleasant and distinctive smells and I could very easily sit and just smell the contents of the bag for a while. It is as enjoyable an experience as actually drinking the coffee.

I put some of the beans in a hand-held grinder and ground them to espresso fineness. Again, the fragrance was outstanding. I made my cup of coffee and enjoyed one of the most flavorful cups I have had in a long time. The flavor is bright and distinctive, very earthy and clean. I noticed an almost slightly sour afterbite which I personally like but did not expect.

This is not a dark roast and it lacks the bitterness that a lot of dark roast coffees have. I prefer medium roasts for that reason and this coffee is very much a medium roast.

This is a wonderfully aromatic and flavor-rich coffee. I look forward to my cup in the morning now than I did before trying this coffee. It is different than most other coffees I have tried and so far I am very, very pleased with it. When my bag is empty, I will be buying more.

title: Very Fresh and Pleasant; Doesn't Get Bitter
text:
Note: This review is for the Jiangxi Mountain Wild Harvest Tea.

I am relatively new to hot tea, having been a soda drinker for years. I have a brother who worked in a boutique tea shop for a while and he got me started on drinking hot teas and I have developed a taste for it since then. Most of my experience with green tea has been with matcha powder but I have had green tea leaves too. This is certainly a higher-grade product than other green leaf teas I have tried.

First things first. This tea is packaged beautifully, in a gold-colored pouch inside a fancy green and black box that makes opening this tea up the first time feel like you’re opening a gift. Most teas I have purchased come either in a sealed metallic pouch or in a little tin instead, so this is a pleasant surprise.

I cut open the bag and was greeted with a very pleasant fragrance. Other green tea leaves I have tried have had the distinct fragrance of freshly dried alfalfa hay, a smell with which I am quite familiar. Instead of alfalfa, this tea has a slightly sweet, very pleasant scent that is unlike any other tea I have tried. Though I don’t have a good way to describe it in terms of anything else, I can say this - it smells very fresh and very pleasant.

I put some in my tea cup and poured over the hot water and allowed it to steep. Again, I was met with a pleasant aroma as it steeped and after it reached the desired strength I removed the infuser. The cup of tea I made for myself was a pleasant shade and was not too strong or too weak, it had no bitterness and it retained the slight sweetness in the taste that it had in the initial smell. If all green teas were this pleasant and not quite so grassy, I likely would drink only green tea.

I discovered that if I steeped my tea for a longer time, to a point where most teas would start to get bitter, this tea did not get the same bitterness as with others I have tried (though I have not tried this with green tea before this one). So, I can make this tea as strong or as delicate as I want and not concern myself with it getting sharp and bitter.

This green tea has given me an eye-opening experience. I did not know that green teas could be pleasant and not taste or smell like the lawn. Between the beautiful packaging and the very fresh and pleasant flavor and aroma, I have found my green tea of choice and will be buying more when I have finished my first box.

title: Good Variety Pack of Coffee
text:
I am a fairly recent convert to coffee, having been a heavy soda drinker for a very long time. I like a couple of cups in the morning to start the work day and I have been enjoying this particular variety pack as part of my routine.

There are several different flavors in this pack, including a couple of breakfast blends, a couple of medium roasts, a dark roast, a cinnamon swirl, a mocha and a vanilla swirl. There is one decaf type included in the morning roasts but I have not yet tried it as I have been looking for the caffeine to get me rolling.

I have learned a few things from this pack. While I like the light roasts, they are weaker than that of a medium or dark roast which have much stronger flavors. When I made a travel mug size of one of the light roasts I was a little surprised when I tried it as it was not quite as I expected. The next cup I reduced to a large cup size and this worked much better.

I like the flavored blends - the vanilla swirl in particular but also the mocha. The cinnamon is an unusual flavor and it has taken some getting used to; it is a good cup but it is something that I need to be in the mood for before I am ready to brew a cup. The straight roasts give you an honest cup of coffee - good flavor and color, wonderful aroma. These are my go-to’s in the morning.

One thing I particularly like about this selection of coffees is that the coffee does not come out overwhelmingly bitter. Some coffees are more bitter than others and some are so bitter that they are just unpleasant to drink; that has not been a problem with any of the cups I have brewed from this pack and I have had a pleasant experience every morning as a result.

I like this variety pack. There are several very good flavors in this selection and they all have brewed up nicely for me so far. The light roasts are a little on the weak side and it has taken a slight adjustment to compensate, but overall I have been very satisfied with all of that I have tried. These have made my first hour at the office every morning a little more pleasant.
