title: My 3 Fave Flavors so far - Love em
text:
I can't drink typical soft drinks, so I drink a lot of water (kidney stones). I've flavored via lemon juice for many years, but I wanted something more. For whatever reason, the liquid (squirt bottle types) exacerbate my headaches, so I was left looking for another additive. Step in Torani. My typical drink is just water/ice + lemon/lime juice + a capful or so of Torani.

Recently for the heck of it, I tried to make an Italian Soda, using Canada Dry Lemonade (or Raspberry Lemonade) + Ice + Torani + Lemon/Lime Juice + Maraschino Cherries (w/some juice). Very tasty. I also add a hint of various Syrup flavors to change it up.

title: Can't, Stop, Devouring
text:
I originally tried the PB toffee, and loved it. So I decided to try the variety pack and I'm glad/yet upset that I did. I'm very happy b/c this is the, or one of the, best toffee's I've ever had (its different, but don't eat toffee enough to describe how). This isn't the hard caramelized sugar type of toffee, its very soft and melts in your mouth (but don't worry, doesn't crumble in your hands).

I do appreciate the focus on quality ingredients (see below). Oftentimes my favorite products come from that focus (eg, I love Talenti ice cream, which also uses simple ingredients, no artificial crap).

If I were to pick a fave, it'd be between the PB and the Coffee. I typically love Dark Chocolate, but the PB is just so much better.

If Dave's can ever read this, please introduce a PB & Coffee Flavor, its sounds odd but I think it could work.

My complaint? Its so bad for my waistline. I went thru all 5 jars in less than a week (tho I left a lone piece for 3 weeks, not wanting it to end). Its difficult to lose weight w/this amazing treat around (I'd hide it, but don't know how long it will last). Well, I guess I can complain about the cost. $60 for a treat that (for me) doesn't go far, is hard to make a regular thing. Too bad they don't offer Subscribe & Save, I'd add it to a 3 or 6 mo rotation.

If you even remotely enjoy toffee, try it. Maybe try a single jar of your usual fave flavor first, like I did, but I almost guarantee you'll be back for the variety pack!

I don't see this posted elsewhere, so I'll write what I see for the PB flavor:
Butter (milk, salt), Sugar, Almonds, Milk Chocolate (sugar, palm kernel oil whole milk powder, cocoa (processed w/alkali), reduced mineral whey powder, cocoa powder, soy lecithin (an emulsifier), salt and vanillin), Peanut Butter Chips (partially defatted peanuts, sugar, vegetable oil (palm kernel and soybean oil), corn syrup solids, dextrose, reduced mineral whey, salt, vanillin, and soy lecithin.

Hope that helps.

title: Why is this grape juice $13???
text:
I tried this wine because my little sister recommended it - yes, I realize that was my first mistake (and yes, she is of age). I generally enjoy Red blends that aren't overly sweet, but still fruit forward.

First things first, this wine is fizzy. I almost spit it out when I tasted the fermentation, I wasn't expecting it, so it was not a pleasant surprise. It's not as bubbly as a champagne or sparkling wine. It's almost like wine-beer. Secondly - this wine is quite sweet. Way too sweet for me. If you like sparkling Moscato or sweet Riesling's, you may enjoy this wine. I think if it was a super hot day and I was sitting at the beach or on a patio somewhere, I would like this. It would also be good with spicy foods. As a purely in the house sipping wine - not for me.

Finally, this wine costs like $13 - I think it's outrageous for the quality of the wine you're getting. This bottle should be 7 or 8 dollars, 9 at most.

title: Excellent Flavor and Mini Bag has as much actual popcorn as a regular sized bag!
text:
Way back in the day, Orville Redenbacher had a Lime & Salt flavored popcorn that I fell in love with that was discontinued. I was elated to find this flavor in the Skinny Girl line of popcorn and immediately ordered 6 boxes. I am happy I did.

First the flavor, if you like lime and salt tortilla chips, you will like this. The popcorn has a nice lime flavor along with the salt. It's not sweet, but it's also not sour. It definitely fulfills my craving for salty foods, with a little pop of lime.

Second, the serving size - these are the mini bags of popcorn. I was disappointed to not find this in a large (regular) size microwave bag. My disappointment disappeared after I popped this bag. I have found that regular bags of popcorn only ever pop to about 1/2 full before the popping slows down and you wander into burnt popcorn land. This means you have this big bag of popcorn that is only ever half full (BOO). This bag FULLY pops. Let me say that again - IT FULLY POPS. That means the whole bag is chock full of popcorn. When I poured the bag into my popcorn bowl, I found that I got as much actual popcorn from the fully popped mini bag as I did from my partially popped regular sized bag. This sealed the deal for me and it's now my favorite popcorn!

title: Expensive! Worth it if you are travelling with a small child and can't/won't have a cooler/fridge
text: So, this is much more expensive than comparable brands (Horizon) self stable milk. I paid almost $1.30 for a single carton (ouch). However, this milk tastes good, has a great flavor and consistency and is a must when travelling. I first purchased this when my little one was a little over a year old for our first flight. I was worried about keeping milk cold for the long trip and this was perfect. We were headed on a cruise and I wasn't sure what the milk situation would be, so I wanted to make sure I had enough. I got through TSA fine with this milk (after being super examined from head to toe) and used this during take-off and landing to keep her quiet and her ears from getting clogged. It was perfect and delicious. No screaming baby on a plane - priceless. I keep some of this on deck for long car rides and anytime when milk is needed and cooling is limited.

title: VERY Thin - You use 2-3x as much to get the same flavor...
text: Land O Lakes is kind of my baseline half-in-half. When utilizing Fat Free Half and Half, I expect it to be thinner than the regular Half-in-Half (like fat free milk) - it's just a given. However, if you have to use twice as much Half-in-Half to get the right flavor in your coffee, it really limits the benefit of using the Fat Free stuff. I found that I used 2-3x as much of this as I did any other Half-in-Half. It was pretty thin. The flavor is okay and the price is okay, but I would have purchased something more expensive for a bit more heft to it.

title: Beyond Meat Feisty Crumbles vs Gardein Crumbles review
text:
I bought the Beyond Meat Fiesta crumbles and the Gardein crumbles at the same time so this review is for both and a comparison review. I am trying to eat less meat so I had high hopes for both, particularly Beyond Meat as there is a lot of talk and buzz about this brand. FWIW I had not tried any other products from either company before this.

So I paid about $4 for 13.7 ounces of the Gardein crumbles and $5 for 11 ounces of the Beyond Meat crumbles.

The consistency of the Beyond crumbles aren’t real crumble but more pre-formed pieces of small meat about the size of a piece of cereal and they don’t really crumble. The Gardein crumbles however do have the consistency of crumbles and do in fact actually crumble when you cook and eat them.

So I cooked both to manufacturers specifications in a pan.

Now to the taste…..the Beyond crumbles just didn’t feel like I was eating crumbles… the small meat pieces were rubbery and the taste was not very good to be honest. I tried it initially in tacos and didn’t like them. Then I tried it with Mac and cheese thinking it might be better there but in both instances it just sadly wasn’t very good. It kind of reminds of of when they substitute turkey meat instead of beef in that there really wasn’t any taste of fat at all. When I tried it with Mac and Cheese I ended up with a bowl of uneaten crumbles at the end…that should tell you something.

The Gardein crumbles on the other hand had the taste and consistency of real beef crumbles. I honestly don’t think I could tell I wasn’t eating meat if I didn’t know it. And the fact that they resemble crumbles in texture and consistency made a big difference IMO. In comparison to Beyond Meat they did have the taste of fat and the chewing them felt like I was eating beef.

If I had to give a number grade I would give the Beyond Meat crumbles a 3/10 and the Gardein crumbles a 9/10. When you consider the prices per ounce this is a no brainer IMO (29c for Garden and 46c for beyond)

title: Convenient snack
text: Arrived on time. Well packaged. Pleasant taste. Quick convenient snack. Will buy more. Definitely recommend.

title: Delish
text: Arrived on time. Well packaged. I've never had anything from Ferrero but I'll definitely be having more after tasting these chocolates. I love dark chocolate & these are all delicious. Just the right size to indulge without going overboard. Giving this as s gift would be well received. Highly recommend.

title: Perfect
text: Arrived quickly. Well packaged. Candy rocks were unbroken & looked like real rocks. The taste is good. The size is very nice. They worked perfectly for my Halloween cake project. I've attached a photo showing the candy rocks which are blue/white around the base of the pumpkin cake. Definitely recommend.

title: Too runny
text: Arrived quickly. Well packaged. Color is NOT a true black; it's more of a really really dark gray. Too runny for my project. Won't use again.

title: First time
text: Arrived quickly. Well packaged. Worked exactly as I wanted. Made a black bundt cake for Halloween using THIS black cocoa powder & it was perfect. I'll be making more black cakes in the future. Definitely recommend.

title: It's fine
text: Arrived quickly after a shipping issue was resolved. Several containers were damaged but NOT opened so the product was fine. Recommend.

title: Too runny
text: Arrived quickly. Good color. Too runny so won't be using again. Disappointed.

title: As described
text: Replacement arrived quickly. Packaged okay. I used these as part of a cake made for Halloween & they worked nicely. Definitely recommend.

title: Cute but disappointing
text: Arrived in a timely manner. Every "rock" was chipped/cracked & the outer shell that chipped off was turned into dust. I can't use them in the way I intended so it's very disappointing. These would make a cute edible decoration if they arrived in whole pieces. Cannot recommend.

title: Addicted
text: Arrived late but worth the wait. I'm addicted to Spitz original salted sunflower seeds & this is the best price I've ever gotten on them. The shells are less "woody" so they don't splinter. The seeds are bigger/thicker. There are fewer empty shells when you crack them open. They're salted just right. I've been eating sunflower seeds for over 30 years & I've tried them all. I've changed brands several times & Spitz is my current favorite & has been for about 4-5 years. In a pinch, I also like the Spitz cracked pepper & I sometimes mix salted & cracked pepper together. I haven't tried any of the other flavors. Definitely recommend.

title: Good flavor
text: Arrived in a timely manner. Well packaged. Definitely recommend.

title: I'm addicted
text: Arrived a little early which made my day. It's well packaged. I've been addicted to iced tea my entire adult life & I've been drinking Pure Leaf Unsweetened Black Tea for years. This is a very good value because it's the larger size which in grocery stores is sold individually & costs more. I really like Pure Leaf's taste over other brands. I will keep buying it. Definitely recommend.

title: Yes, no peanuts
text: Arrived earlier than expected & I'm happy. Packaged fine with my other items. I ordered this because it has three nuts I really like & no peanuts. It has plenty of almonds & pistachios but I'm disappointed by the scant amount of cashews. Planters, please add more cashews. Great easy tasty snack. Highly recommend.

title: Quick & easy
text: Arrived earlier than expected which is nice. Packaged in sturdy box which is easy to open. I've purchased this exact brand in grocery stores but this is the best value. They store easily & keep for a long time. So many ways to use these & there's no mess or waiting for water to boil & then cook. Use with sauces, add to soups or just melt butter & you'll have a nice quick snack or meal. Definitely recommend.

title: Just enough sparkle
text: Arrived earlier than expected which was nice. Well packaged. Each bottle has a tamper-proof seal which I really like when giving it to other people so they know it hasn't been previously opened. I've never had VOSS flavored sparkling water so this was new for me & I love the Lime Mint flavor. It's not too bubbly which I really appreciate as some sparkling water is overly carbonated. The flavor is balanced & refreshing. The 11.15oz size is nice to carry on a walk or throw in my bag while running errands. The lid seals tightly so there's no leaking. Excellent value. Highly recommend.

title: Delish
text: Arrived earlier than expected which is always nice. KIND box was slightly damaged but items inside were fine. I've had this flavor bar before & really really like it. This is a good value for a healthy alternative to candy bars. Definitely recommend.

title: AWFUL
text: Smelled like play doh, tastes like play doh. Rice is soggy and gross

title: Good but very low in flavor
text: Good BUT it’s very low in heat and flavor. Like a kids version of tikka masala.

title: Delicious
text: Amazing

title: Stale
text: Stale when they arrived

text: The disgraceful advertising of MARS and their Uncle Bens products - on the labels - SAY CLEARLY "BIOENGINEERED INGREDIENTS"  - THAT'S GMO! - their cust serv will not disclose which of the ingredients ins BIO ENGINEERED! -  (but RICE may be the issue! ) I requested a list of all their products that are GMO (BIOENGINEERED) - THEY WILL NOT PROVIDE IT! - THIS IS NOT FOOD!

title: Not the best
text: Product is very easy to use. I recommend buying this simply as a last resort or emergency food for rations. They could have made a better tasting product but the fact you can make this quick is a trade off. I’ve tried two flavors and they’re just not that great. However, I will keep the rest of the packs for emergency in case of one!

title: Jordan Almond Connoisseurs Please Read:
text: These Jordan Almonds are very good but not the best I’ve had. There is just too much “confection” surrounding the almond.  They are of good value and have a nice vanilla flavor. They are crunchy and not hard on the teeth. Texture is good..  I just prefer a thinner crust around my almond and the Jordan Almonds I favor have more of a rose or floral taste. Do not let this deter you if you need a large amount for a party.  They will still be liked and they are very pretty!

title: Better than I can cook on a stove
text: Crazy about this brand.  All flavors are great. Just keep making!

title: Not enough of the precious “jellies”
text: Never found a company that is generous with those jelly pieces and this company is no exception.  Also this blend is missing “three stories” pieces. Tasty, soft, and satisfactory otherwise.

title: Addictive at a price
text: I love BodyArmor lyte.  My two favorite are the peach and tropical pineapple. Actually, I like watermelon too. The problem is that they are highly addictive and it gets costly to drink three or four of these a day.  No solution to this problem. I can say they hydrate better than any other drink in their league (whatever that means).  The coconut water base is the trick. I like them better than plain  water. I keep some by my bed at night. Please, if you know it causes any damage to teeth, do not share it with me.

title: I love when Jelly Belly creates giftable beans!
text: My sister is a Jelly Belly connoisseur.  The more unusual the better.  She also likes the beans  compartmentalized in order by flavor.  I like how Jelly Belly creates different  packaging. It is very novel. I hope they maintain their creativity.

title: Mochi heaven!
text: I lived downtown Los Angeles in Little Tokyo where all Japanese food is authentic.  There was a candy shop there that had red bean and yam filled mochi.  I moved so I went on a quest for my craving and found this brand to be THE BEST!!!!! It is gooey and just the tight texture and flavor.  I have bought three this month and will be stocking up on more.

title: Good mochi
text: I like this mochi but I have another favorite brand but this brand looked  bigger and prettier in presentation.  This is a little sweeter and more “marshmallowy” than my favorite brand which is gooey and not quite as sweet.  It is good to try since everone has their own preference in taste but it is up there with the top 5 mochis  out there

title: Return to my lover.
text: I grew up with Skippy living in San Francisco near the factory so my family is faithful to this brand.  I started wandering to other brands but when I tried this it was all over and I fell back in love.....

title: Mmmmm!
text: I am a rice connoisseur and this is so sweet and soft and sticky and fragrant it puts other brands to shame. Just try it!

title: Smoothest coffee!
text: I have run the gamut as far as trying different coffees.  While in waiting for one of my designer coffees to arrive I was forced to go to the supermarket to select a "flll-in" coffee, of  which most k-cups I had tried from he supermarket  ,obviously did not like since I  was searching designer brands.  Anyway, I saw the Gevalia K-Cups on the shelf and brought them home, not expecting too much.  So the first morning I brewed a cup I thought "this is so smooth." It was excellent, but as I would, started pulling out all my different K-Cups to compare to the flavor, thinking ONE would surely taste better, especially for all the money I poured out on all of these coffee companies.  It took me three days of three of my favorite coffee companies to make my choice between them or Gevalia.  Gevalia was the winner hands down.  I won't be going back to those other companies.  I love the price, availability, and mostly the smoothness of this coffee.

title: NO MIS-FIRES
text: All working as they should,. No misfires.  I will be reloading.

title: Five Stars
text: Jelly Belly elite!

title: Not my favorite West Rock
text: Not my favorite West Rock.  I got it by accident and wanted to return for my Muraho.  Amazon gave me a refund and I repurchased the right coffee. Now I have big boxes of Muraho and Meza that I love and find myself struggling through or passing up this particular blend. while really enjoying the others.  This one is just "not my cup".

title: Captured live..
text: And brer bear said to brer fox "There is nothing mo' tasty than  brer rabbit!"

title: It is slightly waxy and hard on the top but easily melts when you dip your spoon into it
text: This is a very mild honey that I grew fond of immediately.  It is slightly waxy and hard on the top but easily melts when you dip your spoon into it.  I am sure it may not be for everyone, but I am on my third jar and plan on ordering more. I put my bisquits on it. or anything else I can find to put on it, I will.

title: Awesome, love them hot.
text: Love hot peanuts. These hit the spot, not to hot that makes you be able to still taste the peanuts. Will be buying again, again and again.

title: Best . .
text: Best ketchup ever in my opinion, just enough spice to enjoy and still taste your food. But a little different than other catch-up’s which I really like, give it a try you might just love it like I do!

title: Really like. .  I buy it regularly
text: Good quality, and easy to make.

title: Yummy
text: Yummy

title: Good noodles
text: A little pricey but great product.

title: Great Deal!
text: Can not beat the price, and it comes straight to your door!

title: Best bottled dressing ever
text: I love this salad dressing.  It's not easy to find and hen you do, it's kinda pricey.  This was such a great value.  And just delicious.  My favorite with this is to make soba salad (cold soba (buckwheat) noodles on top of nice sharp salad greens, with tomato, shaved carrots, and a bit of diced apple.

title: He’s is the world's best salad dressing, but the price is insane
text: I love this dressing.  Like, seriously, it is insanely delicious.  My favorite is making a soba salad.  Cook up some soba noodles, ice them down, mixed with greens and such.  Amazing.  That said, the price is crazy. As I write ths, it's over $16 for an 8 1/2 a bottle.

title: This Soeos Black Vinegar is good stuff
text:
I'm in love. For those who wonder at what it tastes like, the closest I can say is, you know when you get hot and sour soup at a Chinese restaurant? This is the underlying flavor.

A super quickie ramen cheat. Toss out the flavor packet and use stock instead (canned is fine) with a shot of soy sauce and a shot of black vinegar. It is heaven.

title: It's gross, but it's not
text: I love this stuff.  It's a part of my childhood, slathered on squooshy white bread.  Love it.  That said, it is certainly not for everyone.  It looks disgusting, is really salty/fatty, and is not the least bit appetizing, unless you like this sort of thing.  And if you do, it's wonderful.  Once a year or so, I get massive cravings.  I grab a can and some cheap white bread, and am in heaven.  Think spam.  You either grow up with it and like it, or you don't.

title: This isn't the real Japanese Kewpie
text: This is the American version of Kewpie, which is not nearly as good as the original from Japan.  The Japanese stuff has MSG, which gives the umami that Kewpie is so loved for.  If you have a problem with MSG, then, I guess, go for it, but if not, buy the original.

title: I'm a big fan of this tea
text: I'm not a big tea fan.  There's the occasional herbal or earl grey I like, but regular tea?  Meh.  Barry's though, it's different.  Very full bodied, very flavorful.  It's almost like drinking coffee.  Like, I never understood people putting milk in tea.  Now I kind of get it.  And it is a wonder with a couple of biscuits.  I have a box at home and a box at the office.  It makes me happy.

title: This review is for the Rao's 12 pack
text:
Okay, first, Rao's makes the only bottled pasta sauce I will eat. I also have the Rao's cookbook and often make it from scratch but I'm kind of lazy, so... Anyhow, the quality of the sauce isn't really the question for me. Right now I'm dealing with the value and Use By date of the 12-pack. And it's good. The sauce for the 32 oz jars ends up considerably cheaper than buying it at the market and the use by date is well over a year and a half (like there's the slightest chance these won't be gone within a few months, tops).

So, if you are a fan, if you use Rao's Marinara Sauce often, or would do so if it were just a little bit cheaper/easier to find/whatever, get it. It's an excellent value, and is really well packed/padded to prevent breakage. The only problem I had was finding room for all the sauce in my teeny tiny kitchen cabinets.

title: Marmite is the best umami bomb ever
text: Marmite is one of those foods you either love (mostly having been brought up on this stuff), or hate.  Or maybe you just like the taste and you’re a fully grown person who’s having it for the first time.  That was me. A middle-aged person who tasted it and almost swooned at its goodness.  It is both salty and an umami bomb.  And it almost assaults you.  It is heaven.  There is no finer toast than a really good, dense, thick slice, slathered in butter with a slick of Marmite over it.  But not just toast.  Add a tablespoon to a beef stew, maybe a half teaspoon to a veg stir fry, or just a bit on buttered corn on the cob.  A little goes a long way, and that way is to pure awesomeness.  That said, if you don’t like umami/salt it’s not for you.  If you do, give it a shot.  It’s not that expensive and will totally change how you eat certain foods.

title: A great Keto stand in for a wrap - sort of
text: First, I don't buy these from Amazon.  Too expensive here.  Anyhow, the wraps are wonderful as long as you use them properly.  They do smell of coconut, which works great on a turkey or chicken wrap, not so much on pastrami.  One has to keep the flavor of the wrap in mind.  Also, these are not nearly as pliable as a regular wrap, so you have to be careful with them or they'll break.  I use these mainly for two things - almond butter wraps or chicken with mayo/greens/swiss or brie/hot sauce.  Both are really good.

title: It's not salt, don't expect it to taste like salt, great as a supplement
text: Maybe if a person hasn't had salt in forever, this is a great sub.  Entirely possible.  That said, I use this to add a little potassium to my diet. Just a dash or two a day because my potassium levels are low and I wanted to give them a small, safe boost.  For that, this is perfect and way cheaper than potassium supplements.  Also, this particular deal is a great price with an expiration date over two years from now.

title: Probably the most addictive snack ever
text: These are crack.  You start, you can’t stop.  They are delicious, crunchy, salty, sweet.  I break it up into servings because otherwise I could easily eat the bag in one sitting. That said, the price on Amazon is insane.  You can get these at Costco for $5.99.  That said, I live nowhere near a Costco, so I’ll pay the price.  They’re worth it.

title: Love Chomps!
text: Just like the sticks when I was a kid, only not loaded with lots of chemicals, etc. These are a treat and make Keto just a little bit better.  I’m a fan.

title: My favorite Dijon mustard
text: My favorite Dijon mustard.  Great for salad dressing, love it on cold roast beef, ham sandwiches, and mixed with olive oil as a dip for cold, lightly blanched vegetables.  I wish it was available at markets here, but at least I can get either here or through frenchfeast.

title: A great mayo, though not for all things
text: Kewpie is creamiy, an umami bomb of goodness.  Probably not the best choice for an egg salad sandwich, but amazing on a chicken sandwich.  It's a different taste profile.  It is excellent drizzled on steamed vegetables and with Japanese potato salad.  Texturally it is different than American mayo.  It's a little sharper, a little thinner, it's got MSG.  It is one of my favorite condiments.  As an aside, Kewpie now makes a version of this in America.  It is not the same and not worth your money.

title: Excellent ghee, excellent price
text: I love ghee, I do a lot of my cooking with it. Carrington Farms gives an excellent product at a very good price.  This will be my go to product from now on.

title: This is the best all around seasoning out there
text:
I use this stuff on everything. Seriously, from chicken to popcorn. Yes, there’s MSG in it, but I grew up on it, my family grew up on it. I have no issues with it.

So, for the uninitiated, a quick and easy way to understand its awesomeness - take one 16 oz can of Goya kidney beans, 1 8 oz can of tomato sauce, one medium low starch potato, one small green bell pepper. Dice the potato and the pepper, toss everything into a pot, covered, over med-low heat. Cook until the potatoes are cooked. Serve over rice. Ideally, this would be served with roasted chicken thighs, also Sazon-ed, but it’s not necessary.

title: These are absolutely delicious, very strongly flavored, a flavor bomb.
text: These are so good.  They are addictive.  Crunchy, salty, a little sulphuric, spicy.  If you don’t like Indian food you probably won’t like them, but if you do, you will not find a better crunch to go with a beer.  As an aside, they really are salty.  Saltier than they taste.  Like, you will wake up in the middle of the night with a mouth so dry you’ll drink a quart of water.  And still totally worth it.  Also, taking a few and chopping them up is so good on rice, with a squeeze of lime.

title: It is creak,  crack in a ginormous bag of goodness.
text: Totally addictive.salty, savory umami bombs, pretty much created to be a bar snack.  And, oh, does it work.  It's also'ptetty breat chopped a bit and tossed on rice.

title: Is this as good as freshly made rice?  No, don’t be ridiculous, but it’s good, quick, and easy.
text: I love the ready bags. They are definitely not as good as fresh made rice, but they are quick and easy and you’d never use them the same way.  You want to toss it into soup, drown it in chili, perfect.  It even makes a decent stir fry.  If you’re looking for the clean, beautiful, purity of rice, you wouldn’t even be looking at this page.  For the day to day, it's fine, certainly better than something awful like Minute Rice.  For the fancy, go elsewhere. Make proper rice.

title: My favorite mustard. Works with everything.
text: This is the best mustard.  Spicy, very mustardy, Great on a ham sandwich, in salad dressing, it’s my go-to.  Mixed with mayo, there is no better spread for a cheddar cheese sandwich, with sliced cucumber, tomatoes, and bean sprouts.  Add a little to your potato salad or coleslaw. I live on this

title: The best canned tuna on the market
text: I hate canned tuna, I really do.  It tastes like cat food to me.  But Wild Planet?  I have it on auto ship.  It is delicious.  Firm, tasty, not at all fishy.  I average 3 cans a week.  I know this may sound odd, but I open it, mostly drain the can, hit it with a shot of soy sauce, and dig in.  It makes a great quick meal.

title: Terrible seasoning, good quality meat.
text: I love Pat LaFrieda products, but these hot sausages were terrible.  Going by all the good reviews, maybe I just had a bad batch?  They were black pepper spicy, not red.  Totally different taste than what one would expect from a hot Italian sausage.  The quality of the meat was good, but the actual seasoning was awful.

title: Best mayo ever
text: OMG, Duke's is so good.  I've been hearing about it forever, but it's not available by me.  Finally broke down and ordered it.  Amazing.  Not like Hellman's, not like Miracle Whip.  It's got this wonderful tang and seems a bit lighter than Hellman's (my pre-Duke's favorite) and a bit less creamy.  Perfect for pretty much everything other than egg salad (Hellman's definitely wins on this one).  Great on sandwiches, potato salad, cole slaw, deviled eggs.  I love this mayo. I love this mayo way too much.

title: I do not get the product love
text:
It's not great. Sent to me with one week left on the sell by date. I contacted the company and they refunded the money, so while not thrilled, they do honor their customer regarding complaints which I appreciate.

Bought this because my sister raved about it. It's her favorite condiment ever. For me, all I got was this really strong soybean oil taste. Barely a hint of mustard or peppercorn. I tried it a few times quickly because it was so close to its sell by date, and honestly, it I was pretty bad no matter how I used it. So I decided, let me play with making a tasty version of what this was probably meant to be. Used Mayo (Duke's), added some Dijon mustard, added a bunch of mixed peppercorns on the roughest setting on my grinder, and just a touch of white wine vinegar, and it was absolutely amazing. Don't know whether this was so bad because it was so old, or whether this actually how it was supposed to taste, so am giving the actual product the benefit of doubt and giving it two stars instead of one,

title: They came stale
text: The whole box was stale.  The mentors closest to the edges of the packs rock hard, the centers just kind of stale.

title: Great nut mix and great price when one considers the quality and lack of peanuts
text: These are totally addictive.  Not heavily salted and really fresh tasting.  I'd have liked a bit more hazelnut and pecans, but still a much better mix than the standard nut mix which is usually half peanuts.  I love that there are none in there.

title: A truly great olive oil
text: Probably the best olive oil I've ever had.  It was given to me as a gift and I just can't say enough good things about it.  It's a finishing oil.  Great for dipping bread or drizzling on vegetables and fish or meat.  It has this wonderful, full, peppery taste.

title: Very tasty mayonnaise, but not for everything.
text: This mayo leans way more towards Miracle Whip than it does Hellmans/Best Food.  My personal preference is for a more Hellman's like mayo.  That said, this stuff is great for certain things.  It makes a killer turkey and whole wheat sandwich.  It's excellent with salmon.  I don't think it tastes of either chipotle or lime, but it still tastes great.  I think it would be awful in a tuna or egg or potato salad.  It's very, very thick, and a little goes a long way, so while it may be more expensive than plain old Hellman's, it'll probably last longer.  Regarding pricing - you can find it for as low as $6 a jar and much as $20, so shop carefully.

title: They should call it Black Bean Crack
text: I'm addicted to this stuff.  It improves almost anything I put it on, from plain old rice to vegetables of all kinds.  I've even used it to top hard boiled eggs.  The bottles are leaky though.  I mean, they came nicely sealed and but t seems I'm incapable of screwing the lid back on without a little oil running down the side.  This isn't very strongly flavored and has zero heat from the chili oil, but it works well with a lot of different things.

title: A good noodle soup, but not the best noodle soup
text: It's good, but not as great as I thought it would be.  When you first get it, you see these enormous cups and think yay!  What a nice, big serving, but the noodles are only about half way up and the water line is pretty low down, so one enters into this with a slight disappointment.  The noodles themselves are quite good.  The soup part has a nice body and kick to it and doesn't seem quite as salty.  Not quite as spicy as my two Shim faves, Spicy and Kimchi, but a good kick to it. If the lack of MSG is important to you, then these are definitely the way to go.  Not my favorite Nongshim, but pretty decent, and a slightly healthier choice.

title: So, so, so good.  Addictive.
text: I love these so much.  They are absolutely delicious.  Really spicy, pickly, really hard to stop eating.  Also, they make a great garnish for a Bloody Mary.  And add a bit of the liquid in.  Heaven.

title: The apples tasted okay, but a lot of them were bruised.
text: These were pretty banged up by the time I got them.  Lots of bruising, like the bag had been dropped a couple of times.  Don't think I would order these again.

title: Not sandwich bread, but great if that's not what you're looking for.
text: Okay, to use this bread as sandwich bread will make a pretty grim sandwich.  This is bread that you slather with butter and eat alongside a tasty soup.  It is a bread to toast and eat with peanut butter, to top with a nice sharp cheddar alongside your salad, or as a snack.  The one thing it most definitely is not, is a bread for sandwiches.  As long as you know that going in, you will love it.  Super dense, chewy, a bit dry, sour, it's excellent.

title: Best bottled dressing in the world
text: I do not like bottled salad dressing.  They taste gross.  But then there's Annie's Goddess dressing and I swear to god, it's so good I want to climb into the bottle and swim around in it.  I want to take shots of it.  It's amazing stuff.  Great as a salad dressing, great as a dip for veggies, great on falafel, great on a burger.  Seriously, this is the best bottled dressing I have ever tasted.

title: It's fine, I guess
text: It's fine, I guess.  So salty though that in order to get any other taste you really have to load it on which makes no sense to me.  I ended up giving all three bottles to friends who also weren't crazy about it.

title: So, let's pretend you're on a a diet...
text: Or, like me, going vegan for a couple of weeks.  And you're eating what?  Lots of veggies, I'll bet.  Lots of veggies with low calorie dippie things.  You know what makes said low calorie dipped veggies really good?  A little Loeb's Onion Crunch, that's what.  2 TBS is only 40 calories and it's really low in salt, low in fat, has no trans fats.  It's a lifesaver.  I love this stuff.  The only thing to be aware of though, is that the crunch doesn't last forever.  If you put them on your soup or something, they're not gonna stay crunchy.  Anyhow, I love the onion crunch.  I have one at my desk at work and one at home and it's my go-to when I want to pep things up.  Oh, also very nice sprinkled on a salad.

title: The Vanilla and Honey Flavor is Really Kind of Blah
text: I love McCann's instant oatmeal, but this particular flavor was a big disappointment. It has a slight honey/vanilla flavor and seems a little gummy compared to their other oatmeals.

title: This is delicious
text: If you're going to go with instant oatmeal, McCann's really is the way to go, and this particular flavor is awesome.  The texture is much closer to real oatmeal and the serving size a bit larger than one finds in standard instant oatmeal packs.  I have the Black Currant flavor on a monthly subscription.

title: No better soup to sit beside a grilled cheese sandwich
text: This is probably the best canned soup I've ever had.  Annoyingly, Amy's tomato soup is better than my own homemade tomato soup.  It's definitely a little pricey compared to other brands, but it's head and shoulders above their competition.  And seriously, best lunch/dinner ever - grilled cheese and Amy's Tomato Bisque.

title: My favorite vinegar
text:
It's a little less acidic and a little sweeter than regular vinegar. I think it's delicious and is my go-to for making a vinaigrette. Because it's less acidic than regular vinegar, you don't need to use nearly as much oil for a dressing, so it's also great for when one is dieting. It's sweet, it's sour, it's amazing in a non-mayo based potato salad. I use boiled new potatoes, minced red onion, slivered kalamata olives, feta cheese, Italian parsley and a dressing of Melfor and a light olive oil, though avocado oil also works great. I buy it six bottles a time, probably twice a year.

I've never bought it through Amazon though. I get it from this French food online shop that I buy from regularly.

title: An excellent product
text: I love Coombs Maple Sugar, and love its versatility.  Regular sugar is just sweet, maple sugar is maple-ey, so for me a clear winner when it comes to certain foods.  Broiling grapefruit halves?  Use maple sugar.  Baking (so much better than frying) bacon?  Sprinkle the bacon with a little hot pepper and maple syrup first.  You'll be hooked.  Oatmeal?  Of course.  I make an apple upside down pancake, swapping out the regular sugar with maple.  Amazing.  It's also great on yogurt.

title: Really good, but a little heavy on the salt
text:
I was involved in a food challenge using this product. It was not, however, a challenge set up by Slap Ya Mama, but rather a person in a foodie group that fell in love with the seasoning. We were provided free seasoning mixes of both regular and hot.

Being involved in said challenge meant using SYM in as many ways as we could. And let me tell you, there are lots of ways. This stuff is pretty great and very versatile. It works on meat, fish, stews, vegetables, sauces. It is killer with sweet potatoes. Chicken wings, dipped in butter then sprinkled with SYM and baked will rock your world.

Personally, I like a mix of half regular, half hot. This largely due to the saltiness of the regular blend, which is *really* salty.

I guess a good indicator of my enjoyment of the product is that even after being given freebie mixes, I actually came in here and bought a six-pack when I ran out.

title: This is my go-to order at Starbucks
text: Every single morning I get a trente (huge) Tazo Passion Iced Tea.  No sugar, no honey, no lemon, just plain. It is delicious.  I still get a kick out of the pretty color.  The price Amazon is selling the tea for is pretty great.  Were I not as lazy as I am, I would totally buy it here and save myself some bucks on the iced beverage front.

title: An excellent mustard, but the price is crazy
text: This is my favorite mustard, and always in my fridge.  I've been known to eat it like peanut butter, from the jar with a spoon.  It's amazing.  That said, the price is insane.  It is readily available in this size for half the price elsewhere.

title: Good stuff, man
text: Really high heating point, all the goodness of olive oil, but lighter flavor.  Makes a lovely mayonnaise, salad dressings, etc.  Plus, well, the container is damned attractive.  It looks so nice sitting on the kit hen counter.

title: My god, this stuff is good
text: I've tried making Indian food for years, grinding spices, closely following the directions in high end Indian cookbooks.  They just never worked.  The spices were too subtle, too refined.  The thing I love about Indian food is how it practically assaults your mouth (but in a good way).  While whinging about my failures to an Indian friend of mine, she suggested I use the seasonings that regular old Indian people actually used.  She brought me a bunch of MDH spice mixes.  My cooking world changed.  MDH spice blends are dirt cheap and absolutely delicious.  I have a few favorites, and at the top of the list is their Dal Mahkani, which, oh my god, it's amazing.  Buy it, buy it, buy it.  You will not believe how good this stuff is.  And if you go for the down and dirty, smack you in the face awesomeness that only Indian god can give you, grab a box of Chunky Chat while you're at it.  It will rock your world.

title: A wonderful addition to your pantry
text:
I love verjus and have been using it for years. It makes an excellent salad dressing, works well in stews, deglazes nicely, and can be used to make an awesome sorbet. The thing it does best though, at least for me, is to make water tastier. I add a bit to my drinking water. It gives a tart, refresing taste. Just use a little. I keep a 12 oz bottle of it at my office which lasts a full week of my refilling my water bottle a couple of times a day.

Also, for those people who do not wish to cook with wine, this is a good alternative. No, it doesn't taste like wine, it tastes like itself, but it sort of works the same way.

title: Is it the best chili in the known universe?  No, but it's darned close.
text:
I've rarely had better chili than Wick Fowler's, even by people who really know their stuff. It's a wonderful blend of spices, full-bodied, flavorful, warm but not hot. I usually swap out beer for the water, and I find that using a really rough grind on the hamburger makes a huge difference on its deliciousness. I also toss in a can of Goya kidney beans. Prepared exactly according to specs, it's a very good chili. With a little minor tweaking, it's epic.

It's much, much cheaper to buy this product at Amazon than it is by me, where the packages run about $4 each.

text:

title: Delicious!
text:
Living in Houston, Texas, we are challenged by the threat of hurricanes every year. Besides preparing in advance to meet the dangers of wind and water, we must prepare to face brutal heat, lack of electrical power, lack of clean water, and food shortages. What can we buy that will not spoil?

At the suggestion of a safety director, I first tried SeaBear Ready-To-Eat Smoked Sockeye Salmon this year, and I love it!

SeaBear Ready-to-Eat Sockeye Salmon was recommended to me as a "hurricane survival food" with a shelflife of about 4 years. Of course, it is routinely sold to the rest of the world as a delicacy -- and it is. I now eat this ready-to_eat salmon about once a month or so as a treat (with Triscuits or mixed with a little mayo and celery as a salad).

It should be mentioned that the salmon comes out of the packet looking pretty much like raw smoked fish -- not like the highly perishable, "sleek-looking" salmon that one sees at expensive breakfast buffets. (By the way, this kind of salmon can be bought at the SeaBear website.) It doesn't look like canned commercial salmon from the grocery store, either -- not pale pink. It is a moist, red or dark-red, rich, smoked salmon that looks very "authentic." The texture is firm, moderately oily, and perfectly seasoned with a smoky taste that is not overpowering. You should experiment with this salmon before serving to guests to be sure that you like the appearance.

Since eating too much smoked food is not recommended, I limit my portions when I am not concerned about storms. At the SeaBear site, you can buy different kinds of salmon and other products, and perhaps they offer salmon that hasn't been smoked, as well.

I am a picky eater "when it comes to fish," and I love this salmon!

text:

The flavor itself isn't bad, the smoke flavor might have been putting me off a little. Or was it the pineapple juice? Couldn't tell. The texture is flexible and chewy. I suspect the chicken is pre-cooked for inclusion into a wide variety of packaged foods, probably across several companies. Which is all a bit sad. The curry sauce is pretty good as is the rice. And no, you don't get much for the money: the portions are small and expensive. But, hey, it's better than most microwavable meals available in the USA. Which, also sadly, is not saying much.

However, if I was Indian and the original owner of this brand I think I'd be ashamed.

title: This is what *I* call Pumpernickel!
text:
Having recently moved to the US, I had been sorely disappointed by what is typically sold here as 'pumpernickel': i.e. vaguely brownish wheat bread, usually flavored and colored with molasses. After much searching online, I found this product and ordered 11 packs. It's exactly what I was looking for. Note: I partly identified it as the real thing after reading several horrified reviews by US customers who were clearly expecting the American-style 'pumpernickel', so this may not be to your taste.

If you enjoy proper European pumpernickel, this is the stuff. Mmmm, just thinking about it now, I'm going to pop downstairs and have some now, with a slice of extra tasty cheese, and maybe some onion. Delicious!

title: Fast delivery, yummy pepitas.
text: Delicious, with a freshly roasted taste. The bag was super-full, so beware when opening. Delivery was swift. I'm sure I'll be buying more of their products.

title: I use a lot of chives!
text:
I've purchased different spices, and herbs, in bulk before, but the size always seems to surprise me for some reason. This bag of one pound is huge! LOL For someone that uses a spoonful at a time, I guess this would be impractical, but I tend to use chives by the handful, and keep them in air tight containers. There's no way I'm going to pay the amount companies charge, per ounce, for those tiny bottles. This was the best price out there.

Unlike some brands that can be off color and pulverized into powder at the bottom of the bag, these were a nice green, still in tact, keeping their shape, and flavorful.

Highly recommended.

title: Surprising
text:
This is my first experience with this brand. I chose the Irish Cream because my regular flavored creamer has been harder and harder to find, not to mention the growing concern for health as I age. Sugar free options, with their chemical aftertaste, don't usually interest me.

Most products tell you the serving size, in this case 1 ounce, but never tell you how much coffee that's supposed to flavor. My guess was it would be less than my 16 ounce mugs. Liking things pretty sweet, my first try with this, I added extra. At 2 ounces, and 1 ounce of heavy cream, it was disgusting, an extreme chemical vat of sweetness! The second try, again, with a 16 ounce mug, I cut back to a 1/2 ounce, still with 1 ounce heavy cream, it was excellent. I was surprised!

With my serving size, at half their suggestion, the cost of $.18 a mug, also makes the value better for me. Everyone's taste is going to be different, but i'd definitely recommend this product. Just play with the serving size bit.

title: Love these!
text: Very rich butter cookies, crisp, lots of flavor. I don't know what another review was talking about saying these are soft. They're not. They're meant to be crisp and crumbly. Unfortunately, that does make them fragile, but after 3 orders, i've had maybe 4 broken cookies. The main problem seems to be getting the correct number of boxes because of the product's description. The first time I received 4. The next 2 times only received 1, but I was able to call both times to get the correct 4 boxes.

title: A bit finicky
text:
Unfortunately, I have to agree with the other review that said it doesn't melt well, especially since the description says it's "smooth melting."

The first thing I tried was loaded hashbrowns. Everything was put on top at the beginning of cooking. After crisping for about 20 minutes, I covered it and checked after 5 minutes. The cheese was barely melted. Gave it another 5 minutes and was maybe half melted. Any other cheese totally melts during the crisping stage.
The next thing I tried was a quesadilla. Same result as the potatoes. Added extra salsa for more moisture. It melted a bit better, but the tortilla was very brown by that point.
On burgers and eggs, even added at the start of cooking, and covered, were less than totally melted.
My best results were with slow cooking, cream soups, and mac and cheese.

The flavor is outstanding! That combined with the long freshness I've experienced, currently 9 weeks kept in the fridge in its own bags, have made me willing to overlook the less than perfect melting. If you're willing to work with it, as a bit more finicky cheese, i'd recommend it. It wouldn't be my regular go-to cheese, but it really punches up the flavor of many foods.

title: Odd product
text: I ordered this for the first time, thinking that it would be either like a sparkling water with a fruit essence flavor, or more like a sparkling juice. I'd like either of those. This is neither. When I first tried it, I thought it had gone "off," like the juice had started to ferment. Tried a second one, same thing. Ok, maybe it's just that case. Best by date was still 6 months out, so tried a second and third case, just to be sure. All the same. The only thing I can attribute it to is the ratio of juice to sparkling water and sugar. 15% juice, even with added sugar isn't enough to make a pleasant flavor, and is too much to keep it more like sparkling water. Just tasted nasty. I'll probably mix it with straight juice or lemonade so it's not wasted, but will never order again.

title: Never again
text:
I have had this shrimp before. The product is good, but they need to get better shipping. The first time it took 3 days. The shrimp was thawed, inside an insulated box, but still cool, so I used one right away. It was fine, so I froze the second.

This time, I ordered 2 shrimp and 2 scallops. It was picked up next day, but took 12 days to get here! 2 bags had exploded so the box was soaked and you can imagine the stench! UPS still delivered it that way! Too bad, I liked the shrimp, but never ordering again!

title: Love these!
text:
If you're used to a certain, common supermarket brand of English muffins, and think that's what all "real" English muffins are supposed to be, these are not those and you probably won't be happy. These are very thick and not split. They take a bit more care in toasting to get them right. I split them with a fork which made a few crumbs. Not wanting to burn them, I set my toaster on 4.5 with the bagel setting. They were lightly toasted, but not really done all the way through. I like them pretty dark and crunchy, so just put them down again. After the second time, they were nicely dark and crunchy while very tender and hot inside. They absorbed the butter beautifully and still maintained a good bite. I've had 2 of them now and both were delicious.

The 12 packages arrived in CA, cushioned and wrapped in dry ice, but most were room temp, with a few having a slight chill. There was no damage to any of the muffins. All still felt fresh. If you know there is more to English muffins than those others, give these a try, I'd highly recommend.

title: Won't buy again
text: Wanted to try this as a tepanade. Unlike other forms, this is smooth, but very oily. There is nothing in the ingredients list to explain it, but it has a distinct bite to it, and I can see tiny flakes, like red chili peppers that burn. Other than that, I didn't detect any vinegar and little salt. Not pleasant. Will use this as a mix in for pasta, with other things, but definately won't use it as a tepenade, or buy it again.

title: Prefer another brand
text: I never had Godiva before, but having heard about it most of my life, wanted to see what all the fuss was about. The package and product were intact, placed in its specialized packing and box with no cooling items. The chocolate shells were hard and were crushed just trying to take a bite. The centers were soft, smooth, and well flavored, but nothing outstanding. Overall, for the price and expectation, I wasn't impressed. I'd prefer the Lindt truffels. I wouldn't gift, or buy again.

title: Perfectly cooked rice
text: Definately a convenience item I can get used to. Not too soft, with a good bite.

title: Yum
text: I'm glad I took a chance on this. Looking at the negative reviews I was skeptical. Flavor is such a subjective thing. The bbq flavor is subtle, but it's definately there. It's not on the coverage level of potato chips or flavored tortilla chips, which many times is too much for me. I prefer this. They were fresh and crunchy, whole large pieces, no crushed dust, and no greasier than any other pork rinds. Will buy again.

title: Excellent
text: I've never eaten coconut as a snack, only the shredded, baking kind, but was curious about this. So glad I ordered! Nice large, fresh, crispy flakes, with a buttery, nutty flavor. No sugar. It will be a great addition to my morning oatmeal with fruit.

title: Not satisfied
text: First, the page description says, pack of six, I received one. When offered the option to refund or replace, I chose replace, thinking the next would be the right amount. Second time, same thing. This time it just kept saying no return, wouldn't correct. Grrr. So any way, I tried them. There was a distinct chemical flavor. Very off-putting. I love the flavor and texture of the regular strawberry, but in addition to the chemical flavor, these were much softer, and gummier. I would never order again.

Right up until the color leeches off and stains clothing, bedding or furniture. The flavor is good, not really any berry I've experienced in real life but a fun candy berry.

title: I Love Fig Newtons
text: These have been one of my favorite cookies since I was a wee lad. They're delicious without being overly sweet. The soft, crumbly cake like outer crust and fig filling set each other off nicely.  They're easy for me to eat though I have just a few teeth left.

title: Three Out of Four Ain't Bad
text: The Butterscotch was fantastic. The Caramel Apple was delicious although the green and brown color was a bit off putting. The Spiced Apple Cider was really good. And then there was the Pumpkin Spice. . . I really didn't care for the Pumpkln Spice. Though that may be a good thing in the end since I've eaten most of the other three, the Butterscotch is completely gone, the Pumpkin Spice got shoved into the back of my nightstand drawer. So when there's nothing sweet to eat and I'm dying for sugar I'll come across those drops in the back of the drawer and even though I'm not crazy about them they're better than nothing!

title: Nearly Inedible
text: I liked the texture. It was chewy but not soft. But that's where the good thing ends. There's no sugar. Maybe if you trained yourself to eat a bland diet something like this might feel like a treat but I didn't like these, my roommate didn't like them. Even my CNA who doesn't eat sweets didn't like these. You might,  everyone's taste varies.

title: Affordable Cookies
text:
Normally I avoid talking about cost but these are Amazon's Happy Belly store brand, generics if you will and they were, for the times, quite affordable.
They're a good cookie, fresh, crunchy, plenty of chips in each cookie, plenty of cookies in the pack and they taste great.

title: Delicious Cookie!
text: These taste awesome! There's just one problem that I forgot about. Never have chocolate shipped to Florida. The chocolate stuck all the cookies together and stuck the rows of cookies to the tray. The chocolate didn't separate but it's everywhere and your hands get a mess getting a couple cookies. I'll eat them but I'm not crazy about the product handling.

title: Awesome Soft Cookie
text: It's hard to find soft molasses cookies. All the stores carry are hard cookies which with my lack of teeth are really difficult to eat. These Archway soft molasses cookies are awesome, delicious, soft and chewy. I'm glad I bought multiple bags because we absolutely devoured the first one.

title: Tasty Chocolate
text:
I enjoyed the chocolate, maybe a little sooner than the calendar expected but I was hungry ;)
The chocolate was in many cases not much more than a bite for an adult but enough for a child. I did find some of the windows a little hard to open without tearing the calendar face which was festively pretty for the holiday.

title: Expired Product, New Labels
text: I tried these and found the flavor okay, then just laid up in bed I noticed the bag had a paper nutritional information label stuck over the bag (as well as two other paper labels on the bag. So I started picking away and using a wet cloth to remove the nutritional label and I found the printed on the bag expiration date was four months prior to the current date while one of the other labels they'd stuck to the bag was an expiration date three months into 2023. Eight months from the original expiration date. They tasted okay but I doubt I'll eat anymore.

title: Delicious!
text:
My roommates eyes lit up when he heard these were chocolate covered Oreos. We each had a couple, the coating chocolate is absolutely top quality the coating pieces are also quality my favorite were the white chocolate miniature kisses. I've had to defend them from my roommate with a stick. Luckily we're both wheelchair bound so it's hard for him to get away. 🤣
These were not shipped in/with a cold pack but happily there was only minimal melting of the product. Shipping to Florida, at least in cool weather, seems safe.

title: Hint of Blueberry Was Very Nice
text:
The squares had a nice essence of blueberries along with the chocolate which was a nice quality better than most American chocolate. I sometimes. . . most times really, had two pieces of chocolate due to their small size. They did have what appeared as a slight calming feeling from the different natural ingredients.
I liked these quite a lot.

title: Surprisingly Did Not Melt When Shipped to Florida
text:
These were delightful. Just enough of a snack, white & dark chocolate on one side of the egg along with two chrisp rice balls. Enough to fully satisfy a child and good enough to take the edge off an adults hunger. There was mild melting but nothing that affected the quality of the product which was very nice chocolate and white chocolate.
The toys, requiring minimal assembly were quite well made. In the eggs i opened I received two of the white and orange moon buggies and two of the purple and white moon buggies. Both of these vehicles have pull back and release spring loaded motors powerful enough to shoot the cars off my hospital tray. The third vehicle I received was a rover type that pops open to display two missile loaded wings, these do not fire. And a radar dish that pops forward. The other two toys i received were a space surfer in a white suit and a orange suited astronaut with a white jet-pack. They all seem quite sturdy and well made.

title: Medium Dark Roast?
text:
I'm a little confused. I've bought medium roast. I've bought (a lot of) dark roast. I've never heard of medium dark roast coffee. This is also called espresso but espresso is brewed with very finely ground coffee beans under pressure.
I know I sound like I'm being hard on this coffee. It's very good tasting, more dark than medium roast. But this is K-Cup coffee, not espresso. I like the flavor which I never have spoiled with sugar or milk.

TL:DR? I liked the coffee not the name.

title: Hit or Miss Sour Candy
text: This is a fairly nice assortment of candy. The description says "super sour" and some of them are like the Warheads Sour Booms. Those are very sour to start off but then go sweet. The Cry Baby Tears aren't quite as potent but they're sour all the way through. There was a pack of sour apple chews (my favorite sour flavor) that I had high hopes for and the were so not sour they almost didn't taste of green apple. This might be good for a kids party (do get some non sours for the kids that don't like sour candy) but i recommend an adult taste test and distribute the candy themselves. While there's a variety it's kinda hard to divvy up.

title: I'm Not Really a Fan
text:
As advertised, they're very thin. They're very crispy. The flavor is quite mild. They would go well with most dips, dill in particular seems very well suited to going with these cracker's flavor profile.
My only issue was I could only dip 5-10 crackers as the rest of the contents of the box was broken into pieces that ranged from quarter sized to dust. Eating these plain was kind of boring. I guess you could mix the shards and your dip of choice and eat them with a spoon. I thought they were okay when intact and dipped, boring on their own.

title: Love The Candy
text: I'm a huge fan of these soft puff mints. I'm missing a lot of my teeth so a candy that speedily dissolves when you eat it. Each individually wrapped candy has a Bible verse printed on them. I found quite a few duplicates but that can't be helped and doesn't matter.

title: Not My Cuppa. . . Coffee
text: The spice flavors completely overpower the coffee. I like a flavored coffee from time to time but you can hardly taste the coffee. You need the right size cup/mug for this to sit on and most of mine are too large as I enjoy a big cup of coffee. The filter doesn't flow all that well so you have to go slow and squeeze on occasion to get the water to pass through. Not really a fan.

title: Yummy Honey Candy
text: I have loved the taste of honey since I was a kid. These are great. The soft center is a delight every time I reach it. I've shared these with the staff at the hospital I was in and it was had keeping people's hands off them they were that popular. Very much recommend these candies.

title: Very Tasty Candy
text: I truly like cinnamon flavored candies. These have some heat but not painful heat like Fireballs. I really like these candies and so did everyone else who has tried them. Very highly recommend them.

title: Delicious "Fruit" Chews
text:
Yes, I air quoted around "fruit" because I don't think there's much natural fruit flavor involved. Also, along with the lemon, cherry, orange, lime flavors there's a vanilla flavored chew. . . Vanilla fruit chew. I mean I don't care. I love the orange, the cherry comes in a close second and the others are good, flavorful chews the vanilla being okay but my least favorite of the bunch. But my research says vanilla isn't a fruit.
Flavor and candy are long lasting, surprisingly so and very tasty. These were a favorite as a kid and it's nice to reconnect as an adult.

title: Freshens Breath. . .
text: Like Chiclets gums which has been around forever one piece will do to freshen your breath but isn't much in the way of chewing satisfaction. . . Then again neither is two or three. The flavor is okay and gets intense if you use a few. The Xylitol sweetener ads a distinct chemical after taste and the 'chew' doesn't last long. I guess if this meets your Keto friendly needs it will do. I wasn't a crazy fan.

title: Very Tasty Candy
text:
I get dry mouth quite often but I hate keeping sugary mints just up against my teeth all night or badly done sugar free candies that leave a horrible aftertaste 1/2 way through the candy.
These are fantastic candies. No sugar to rot your teeth and no horrible chemical aftertaste like so many have. They have a great flavor and last a good while. Will definitely be buying these again!

title: Went Over Amazingly Well
text: After the Easter basket and the small egg hunt the granddaughter was given these, shown how they worked and was given an area where she couldn't make too much of a mess. We actually had to go check on her because she was quiet for so long. She was just having a blast playing with these. She's going to run through them all in a short time but there's similar kits out there if she's still into these crafts

title: That Was Different
text: In all honesty I'll try any coffee K-cups that I come across just because you never know what nice novelty you'll come across. I can't say I'd want a steady diet of coconut coffee but sitting around on a cold day watching a movie or playing a boardgame with friends this coconut coffee really struts its stuff.

title: Very Versatile
text: The first time we tried this beef rub was on chicken breasts and they were devine. We then did a low and slow roast which worked out great. A little bit of this stuff even makes burgers taste better. Incredibly versatile, works on all meats ads flavor to everything.

title: Pretty Tasty!
text: I've tried this on crackers, Club, Saltine and for giggles the chicken flavored ones. Okay the chicken ones didn't go great but we did east them. I also mixed this into vanilla yogurt which was excellent and in a PB&J on potato bread which was good.

title: Not Bad Tasting
text:
Where do I start. . . Instructions say to add 12-14 oz. of ice water to a reusable bottle, I used a travel mug & 12 oz., then you seal the bottle well, I did the best I could, and shake well for three seconds, I got to shake. . . shake. . . then the lid popped off my travel mug and a great foaming mass of reddish pink foam poured out and over the lip of my travel mug. Having been a Boy Scout many, many decades ago, I was prepared and doing this over my sink. I made sure I got the lid reseated, rinsed all the foam and gack off the lid and mug exterior and let it sit for a while, which was also in the instructions.
Okay, so, what did this get us? I waited for my supper to finish cooking and grabbed this to sit down and watch YouTube videos to. It was cherry flavored and there was a smooth, silky cream mouth feel the likes of which you get from egg nog or Baileys. There was still some foam and a bit of carbonation. Not soda level of bubbles but maybe Alka Seltzer? I'm not sure. There's a little aftertaste but most of these low calorie mix-ins have some level of aftertaste. They're flavored with Stevia, have 10 calories per packet and a whopping load of Vitamin D (233% RDA) and 320mg of sodium. I'm not going to list the ingredients, they're in my pictures. These aren't bad. I'll be keeping them.

title: Yum!
text: I really like Rice Krispies treats. As I can't make them myself due to disability I am happy with the store bought ones. This 54-pack is a better price than buying the 8-packs at the grocery store. I like them, my roommate likes them. My friends like them. They're not going to last but we're going to enjoy them.

title: A Serious Disappointment
text: I ordered this bulk pack of snacks because we enjoy chips and this helps with portion control something I struggle with. Order placed on the 27th of December, delivered on the 29th of December and EVERY single package in this collection expires before the end of January. Some expire next WEEK. This is deplorable. I will never order bulk packs like this again.

title: If You Like Root Beer
text:
I've tried several mix in flavor enhancers. So far the two I like are sour green apple (different brand) and this. If you don't mind adjusting the flavor to suite your tastes and remembering you can ADD flavor but not subtract it you'll be golden. I like to use this in 1-liter seltzers and work the flavoring until I'm happy. I've written, in Sharpie, a good starting off amount. Each time I make a bottle my needs & wants change. I like something usually that's like a strong diet root beer.
Go slow, count your drops and I've found that the suggested drops per 8 fl. Oz. is on the low side. As mentioned you can eternally add flavor you can't take it out, use care. Still I broke down the liter bottle into the measurements from the product label and personally, your mileage may vary, I found myself using 33-50% more than the suggested addition.
Good luck!

title: Tolerable Energy Drink
text:
If i were thirsty and I was out of my favorite sodas and energy drinks I'd drink this. It isn't horrible. But honestly that's the best recommendation I can give this product. I'd drink it. . . If I was out of everything I prefer. Yeah I'll keep a couple in the fridge for emergencies.
The flavor is something akin to Sprite and 7-Up being mixed with a bit of extra sour added on top. My roommate hated it, his 20 something daughter liked it. You won't know until you try it.
Energy boost seems on par with most energy drinks.

title: Another Great Selection
text: My roommate and I love to grill out over chunk charcoal. Especially now that Florida is getting some cooler days mixed in with the seemingly endless summer. We've done BBQ chicken breasts, hot sauce in scrambled eggs. We've even spiced up macaroni and cheese and our favorite microwave popcorn. There's an endless variety of dishes, marinades and BBQ concoctions you can come up with for your cooking. I even liked the hot honey as a dip for chicken nuggets and fries. Yum.

title: Nice Selection
text: Beef, chicken we've had several cookouts using the products in this kit (no pork, nobody here is a big pork fan. Well, except for bacon of course) I especially liked the look, feel and tase of the black salt, something I've wanted to try for years. This would make your favorite grill master a great gift ot just treat yourself to a little something special.

title: Good Coffee
text: I like coffee. Just coffee. I don't add milk or sugar, black is the only way to drink it. This Columbian is quite nice. Smooth with very little of the bitter notes. Quite drinkable and very aromatic. I brew 10 ounce cups in my off-brand Keurig style coffee maker and they come out great. One of the better coffee's I've had recently. Would highly recommend.

title: Unfortunately Most Arrived Broken
text:
I tried these with a glass of milk and wasn't too impressed. They're mostly a cookie with the chocolate coating on the inside instead of outside. Milk being cold didn't do much at all to the coating. I did try it with a cup of hot cocoa which worked significantly better at melting the chocolate in the 'straw'.
As my title mentions the majority of these arrived in two or three pieces. Completely useless as a straw. There were a couple that were whole which I used with the milk and cocoa. The rest I ate like cookies straight from the package. They were okay but nothing Earth shaking.

title: Hit or Miss Snacks
text: Some of these were great, I loved the date balls, the fig balls were good as well. The dried berries were good, the dried strawberries were okay. I don't have a lot of teeth so the trail mix was mostly inedible for me. I did not care for the dried celery or carrots, they did nothing for me. I liked about a 3rd of the box, would eat a few others if I was hungry and there was nothing else and there's some I wouldn't touch again. Very hit or miss for me.

title: Delicious Snack
text: The only problem is these arrived in tiny small pieces. I don't think there was a whole crisp in the bag but that didn't matter to me. These were a delight. Crispy, vanilla flavor. The crisps were remarkably thin, like a potato chips but sweet like a cookie. I really enjoyed these and the bag didn't last long at all.

title: Hot! Hot! Hot!
text: Woah! I like the meat texture. It's softer than any other jerky I've ever had. Without a lot of teeth I don't do well with really tough jerkies. These were good. The Habanero was my favorite, it's got a kick but isn't deadly. I tried the Ghost pepper variety and wow. That was hot! Screaming hot. I liked it, I really did but in really small doses. I haven't yet tried the Carolina Reaper and I'm going to if I can work up the courage. If you like hot & spicy this is the box for you.

title: Pretty Good Gummies
text: For a low sugar, keto friendly snack these are really pretty darn good. Soft, chewy, flavorful. I've tried a lot of low sugar snack foods and this ranks up there with some of the best I've had. Each pack, a serving, contains just enough to satisfy that mid day or late night craving.

title: Not a Fan
text: All the flavor is on the outside of these bites. They appear to have no marinated the meat in the flavorings. They just stuck the meat (two pieces) into a pack, shot in some flavor and sealed things up. I'm lacking quite a few teeth so chewing things like this takes a while. After just a short time all the flavor was gone, completely. The meat alone is almost completely flavorless and has a weird texture to it. You might not notice if there's some flavor but that washes off in seconds. I am truly not a fan of these.

title: Yummy Lollipops!
text: The shapes make eating them a little funky, there's one with some bumps on it's side that can annoy the roof of your mouth and they are a bit large for kids. Kids are going to enjoy these but make a heck of a mess out of themselves with these. There doesn't seem to be any flavors beyond sweet. Still, fun for an afternoon in the backyard.

title: These Are Gross
text: These are small, fruit shaped plastic containers. It looks like you're supposed to twist or pry off the tops but I have scissors here so I quickly used scissors to rip the tops open. I tried three, a redish orange one I believe was to appear as a strawberry. A green one that looked something like a lime and a yellow one I'm guessing they want to appear as an orange. The contents of all three were mostly flavorless. It all tasted the same no matter what I tried. I had high hopes for these but that crashed. The contents  was like a poorly set  hospital Jell-O I can see how someone might have felt there was something inside but as far as I could tell it was weirdly set jell. Not sure how it's a partial solid after a week in the bottom of my fridge. I couldn't get over the consistency or the lack of flavor and the weird, lingering aftertaste.

title: Oily? Yuck. . .
text: I've had several of these muffins. The red velvet were the best tasting the other two, a blondie and a darker chocolate were edible but not thrilling. I did notice though that all of them were oily, my fingers were slick and I had to wipe them down before I touched anything. Not sure why, it's kinda gross especially since the muffins themselves are kinda dry tasting.

title: Good Tasting Coffee
text: I've had several cups of this, it's consistent, decently potent coffee that's got a good flavor and nice bite to it. I drink coffee black no sugar so I'm tasting just the beans. I like that the company helps dogs in need. That's a worthwhile cause.

title: Nice Snack Bars
text: I'm lacking more than a few teeth so things with nuts and seeds are a little hard to eat but these are soft enough that I can eat them. These are tasty and fairly soft. There's a bit of chocolate in the mix along with the rest which ads a good flavor to the bars. These aren't going to last long in this household.

title: There's a Problem Shipping Candy to Florida
text: This was a decent assortment of snacks and candies. The big problem was it spent time in a hot warehouse then in a hot truck before being left on my hot porch. All the things that could have melted, did. The fudge stripe cookies shed their chocolate. The Sweet Tart chews were all stuck to their wrappers. I ended up putting much of it in the freezer over night to harden up and most became reasonably edible. I've never had any luck getting things that could melt shipped to Florida.

title: Not Very Good
text: I'm not on Keto but I like pancakes and easy to make mixes intrigue me because being disabled I like easy to make things. This was hard to mix and took way longer than expected. The mix didn't spread like you'd expect pancake batter to do. They were hard to flip, cooked poorly and tasted grainy and weird like chalk but chalk with eggs. I did NOT like this product.

title: Good Salt
text: I got hooked on pink rock salt a while ago. I saw it on some cooking show and then on a show about how it was mined. I bought a bag and compared it to the plain table salt and a slightly better sea salt we had and I don't care what the detractors say, there's a taste difference. My usual go to which was a 2lb. bag shot up in price so I decided to give this a try. I completely cleaned the grinder before switching (I really wanted to be sure of the taste) and it's bang on. I got this 5lb. bag for less than the old company and the sizes of the grains are much more consistent in this product than the old which had a lot of dust and small bits.

title: This isn't bad. . .
text: I've used plain Polar seltzer liter bottles to make this so far and while it's almost impossible to get an exact 'this much to that much' ratio because the bottle goes from drops to spritzing at a moment's notice so measuring is near impossible but it takes a good double or triple dose to get a liter of seltzer to have a mild sour apple flavor. It's very similar to White Claw in taste just without the alcohol. I like it. Haven't tried it with anything else but I might with some vanilla pudding or something. We'll see.

title: Yuck!
text: Every mix-in I've ever tried has been a powder or crystal base and dissolved quite easily. This stuff is a gooey sludge that you seriously need to shake the mixing bottle like mad to get it into the water. The taste was. . . bad, like the tangerine's had gone bad, a weird chemical aftertaste. I've tried it twice, that's enough for this lifetime.

title: Nearly Identical
text: These are nearly identical to the product with MSG but with slightly less taste than the MSG variant. They still cook up fine and puffy. Quite a nice snack that's quick and easy to cook up.

title: These Are Neat
text: These cook up big and puffy, crisp and kinda tasty. They're a neat and fun snack that are so easy to cook up. Heat some oil just to the boiling point, use vegetable or safflower not olive oil. drop the discs in, wait a moment then drain. Eat right away.

title: Good But a Little Greasy
text: These have a nice bite of heat with the jalapeno pepper. The sticks are a bit greasier than sticks like Slim Jims but they are quite tasty, have a nice snap and make a nice snack any time of the day.

title: Yuck, No Thanks
text: I was not a fan. I like cranberries they're one of my favorite Thanksgiving dishes, my mom made them every year. I thought a spread made with them would be nice but these were tart to the point of being bitter. The chunks of cranberries were very large and kinda gritty. I really didn't like this, tried it a few times and just said no.

title: Weird. . .
