text: I like caramels, I truly do but the coconut aftertaste from these was too strong. It was practically chemical. They weren't chewy like normal they just kinda melted away. One thing I did like was they didn't stick to my teeth. I ate a bag because, sweets but that was enough for a lifetime. No thanks.

title: Not My Cup Of Tea
text: I have been a tea drinker since my early teens. . . So about 40 years thereabouts. And this had some  of the most bland and boring tea flavors I've come across. I take my tea black and no sugar. And this needed SOMETHING, ANYTHING to enhance its flavor because this had next to none.

title: Has A Weird Texture
text: These have a texture like coconut cookies, a stringy, crumbly mouth feel that I'm really not fond of. Maybe it's the tapioca fiber, I'm not sure. There's no coconut taste just that same feel you get with coconut cookies and the way they come apart when you eat them. I wasn't really a fan. I guess if you were sticking to a strick keto diet these would be okay but. . . not impressed.

title: A Good Cereal
text: The only thing I found about this cereal was it's kinda soft and stale feeling. I'm a fan of Cheerios which are fairly crunchy while these were a little on the soft side. Having never had this type of cereal so It could be exactly how the cereal is supposed to be. The flavor is very nice and mellow. Sweet without being overly sweet like a sugary cereal. The ingredient list is plain and simple; quinoa, purple corn, rice and panela (a type of unrefined cane sugar). I just finished the bag while typing this review.

title: I Love This Stuff
text: I enjoy spicy food and this salt is perfect for adding a bit of spice to all sorts of food, potatoes, chicken nuggets, chicken fried steak fingers. I think my favorite is putting this on popcorn. I love spicy popcorn and this has just the right amount of heat. You can put this on anything you'd put salt on. Five full stars!

title: These Were Good
text: I had planned on trying these in cereal or over ice cream and maybe even in a salad but then I realized while sitting there over several nights trying to come up with ideas for something to do with these. . . I'd eaten the entire bag as a snack. This stuff is delicious and addictive.

title: Delicious!
text: I had never had dried cherries until getting this. They're now my favorite dried fruit. All three, blueberry, cranberry and the cherries were good. The blueberries were my 2nd favorite and the cranberries were a little more bitter than I like so they come in third, still edible but not something I'm sad is gone like the other two. Quite a lot in the package. Makes a good gift and better for families rather than someone living alone. These went great over ice cream and in a bowl of corn flakes. Yum!

title: Surprisingly Tasty
text:
I haven't been one to look for vegetarian or vegan options when seeing out food. There's been a couple times when friends fed me non-meat 'meat' and at one outdoor concert festival the biggest, most filling, food for the money was an Indian dish which I completely forget what it was.
I like meat, I'm not proud of that fact nor am I ashamed. I grew up in a meat & potatoes household. This dish however wasn't bad at all. There was a nice mild heat, nothing scorching but there, the flavors of the curry were nice if slightly too salty (for most people but I like salt) once mixed with the rice it thickened up nicely. The rice on its own was a little. . . bland. Even for rice, this was boring on its own.
I enjoyed this.

title: They're Pork Rinds, Plain and Simple
text: There's really nothing artisanal about these rinds except the insane current price for two four-ounce bags. A few from each bag had a stale taste to them but the majority were decent eating. I've always like pork rinds and the flavors offered here; Smoky Black Pepper & Sea Salt in on bag and the other is BBQ & Zesty Chipotle. There's a nice heat in the Chipotle variety. Not super hot but a good crunchy warmth. The Black Pepper bag has it's own kick, not so much 'heat' but really peppery which I happen to enjoy (we used to go out to eat with a gaggle of people after a midnight movie and I learned to blacken my fries with pepper to keep sticky fingers out of my food). I like these, they're tasty but there's nothing whatsoever artisanal about these. I can't honestly recommend them.

title: Doesn't Really Taste Like Honey
text: This is a xylitol sweetener in a bottle that resembles a honey bottle, a liquid though much thinner than any honey I've ever tried, pours badly. There's really not a honey flavor anywhere and if you're sensitive to these artificial sweeteners you could spend the night in the bathroom if you over indulge. Not my favorite.

title: Not A Horrible Sugar Substitute
text: I think the hardest thing is remembering a half teaspoon of this is equal to two of table sugar. I've ruined a couple cups of coffee and a cake I was baking. Taste is okay, almost sugar but not quite perfect. Better in cooking than as a coffee sweetener. Not really Stevia but a mixture which is only disclosed in the fine print. Label needs to be changed.

title: Yummy Chips
text: Mellow spice, not screaming hot but warm enough to be delicious. Chip size is good though a little small for dipping they will hold up okay you just don't get a lot of dip on each chip. These were really popular with the couple people I shared them with.

title: Versatile, Tasty, Yummy
text: Adds a great flavor to pork loins, roasts, burgers, chicken and even mixed into meatloaf. This stuff is pretty good. Nice and thick with a great flavor. I like the addition of the coffee flavor which I found a really interesting addition. This is something I'm going to buy again.

title: Just a Beef Stick
text: After a lifetime of buying Slim-Jims, random flavored jerky and other meat in stick form products this just fell into line around the middle of the list. The texture of the pork products was really chewy, almost but not quite rubbery. The chicken was a little more tender but not much and tasted worse. Original was your everyday convenience store check-out counter product. The hot was just heat with no flavor profile. Garlic and fennel as well as the rosemary chicken I couldn't finish. Would not want again.

title: Nothing to Write Home About
text: Tried cooking this twice. First time in chicken stock alone, it was bland, a little chickeny, mostly boring. The next time I added some random spices I thought would go good with the chicken stock and it was slightly less boring than the first time. Edible but edible in the way that plain crackers and warm ginger ale are when you have a bad cold. Just didn't do it for me.

title: I Did Not Like These
text: Little hard pellets with little flavor. I lack quite a few teeth and was expecting something soft, squishy, etc. but these were golden rocks with purplish powder on them. Did not like what little flavor there was. Had a couple friends try them and they too disliked the product. Hard pass!

title: We Didn't Really Care For This Set
text: Received three bottle sampler; Classic, Mustard and Smoky Flavor. Took a while to get them all tested. The Classic just doesn't hold up as against other store bought "classic" barbecue sauces. It's a bit thin. A bit runny, Fairly bitter. Tried several ways and (as did the others) a marinade with other ingredients to boost or mask flavors was the best. The Smoky flavor was this with way too much smoke flavor added. No one cared for this one in any guise. The Mustard made a good marinade for chicken and pork chops but was also thin which helped the marinade work but doesn't give great expectations for barbecue sauces. Not recommended.

title: Very Nice
text: Perfect flavor for salad and we made an amazing marinade with this as a main ingredient. Overall a very good product. Labeled as organic and non-GMO if that's important to you, it isn't to me.

title: Hard as ROCK
text: Have you ever seen someone knapping flint to make arrow heads? That's how hard these cookies were. I really liked some of the flavors, the lemon-lime being my favorite followed by orange and apple cinnamon. The Passionfruit chia was by far my least favorite. Cookies are small, a little disappointing but the ones I liked were tasty. I found a little milk or soda softened them up nicely but lacking a majority of my teeth I had a lot of trouble eating them without any fluids. You seriously could knock these down for arrow heads but those lemon lime were really tasty.

title: Loved These
text: Just the right amount of heat. Your tongue wasn't left burning and they didn't upset your stomach. Perfect amount of crunch and the right size to snack on. I had to keep my friends from pilfering bags from my case. Everyone loved these and wanted some for their own to take home. I don't often give 5-stars to things but these were some darn tasty chips and I really wish I hadn't shared them because then I'd have had more for me. :)

title: Milk When You Need Milk
text: I don't drink a lot of milk. It doesn't bother me or anything I just don't like the way it kludges up my mouth and throat. Every now and then I don't mind a glass but I don't keep it on hand regularly. When I need it for cooking I quite often have to buy twice as much as I need and I either have to drink it or it sits in the fridge getting chunky. Enter whole milk powder. Not 2%, not Skim, Whole milk and there's one ingredient: Milk. That made me happy. Mixing is a breeze, 4 parts water to 1 part powder. You can make as much or as little as you need. It's supposed to be good for up to three days in the fridge after mixing. Taste is okay. It definitely tastes better the day after you make it. It's not great but personally I'm not mixing this up to have a glass of milk I'll make some if a recipe calls for it or if I have people over and they want coffee (I drink mine black). The expiration date was a year later than it arrived. This is handy to have around.

title: Scrubbed Clean, Light Scent
text: I had hoped, watermelon being a favorite of mine, that the scent would be stronger and linger longer but these cube are great at getting you feeling clean and refreshed. The scent reminds me more of watermelon candies than the fruit. They do tend to break down quickly but you can get a shower in before it's gone. A decent product.

title: Seriously Minty But. . .
text: The pieces of gum are quite small but at first chew they're insanely potent and minty. The flavor unfortunately doesn't last very long and then it's just chewing gum. Great for a blast of fresh breath but not all that long lasting.

title: Kind of Bland
text: No onion or garlic, not a lot of stand out flavors. The bottle I have is a little on the thin side, not quite watery but not thick and clingy getting and keeping a good amount on the salad mix. I tried this twice and I just couldn't get into it.

title: Fun Candy
text: About 95% intact, a few were broken, a couple had cracked and spilled their powder. One accidentally got blown into my eyes, that was unpleasant to say the least. For the most part these were fun candies. A sweet start with a reminder of Starburst candies and a sudden fizzy sour blast towards the end.

title: Not Something I Liked
text: I've had freeze dried watermelon before. It was airy, light and crisp. The watermelon in this pack was. . . Floppy, moist and just, honestly gross. Even if it was okay the look, the mouth feel, it was bad. The only part of these packages I found edible, not counting the 'rind' was the cocoanut which was properly dry and crunchy. I did not expect what I got when I chose this and I was very dissatisfied with the product.

title: Excellent Coffee
text: I love strong coffee. You can taste the quality when the coffee is strong not bitter. A lot of people make that mistake, over heating, poor quality coffee makers, water the wrong temperature. They get a bitter brew and call it strong. Coffee can be strong without being bitter and this Wandering Bear product is proof. I drink coffee, not milk water, or sugary water, coffee, black and hot. This is good coffee.

title: I Don't Understand This
text: Okay, the toasted sesame flavor on popcorn was odd enough though not horrible tasting but dusting them with blue seaweed dust just made it strange. There was a strange aftertaste that I can only attribute to the seaweed. The toasted sesame was okay but then the taste of the seaweed kicked in and I couldn't take more than a handful. A friend tried it and she said it was okay so it's personal preference that matters with this.

title: Good Basic Fruit Leather
text: I liked this fruit product, we called it fruit leather back when I was a kid. These appear to be fruit and nothing but the fruit. No added sugar, nothing. I like that. Each fairly large piece (approx. 5 inches x 1.25 inches) is only 31 calories! There's a nice chew and the flavors are good. I have to say the only thing I didn't like is the mascot, Bob Snail, snails are gross, leaving a trail of slime behind them wherever they go, I know because they're all over down here. I don't like looking at this piece of fruit and thinking of snail slime. But other than that I really enjoyed these.

title: Tasty Granola
text: I'm not on a Keto diet but I do enjoy trying new and interesting foods. The chocolate flavor was rich but not overly sweet. The granola had a good crunch but wasn't super crunchy or made of overly large granola boulders like some cereals are. The pieces were small, easy to eat and quite filling. I never did get around to trying this with milk. We ate it as a snack and it went rather quickly.

title: Okay Earl Grey
text: As Earl Grey teas go, I've drank a lot. There's probably a couple tea bags still stuffed into a far corner of my backpack. Earl Grey has been my go to tea for four decades at the very least. While this Bradford brand isn't quite up to Twinings tea quality is doesn't taste bad (maybe a smidge too much bergamot oil) and it comes in a kCup which makes my life a whole lot easier.

title: These New Chicken Snacks Confuse Me
text: Cinnamon, sugar, salt, pretzel. . . chicken? I don't get it but to be honest these tasted pretty good. No idea why the new thing is making snacks with chicken meat but if it tastes good and isn't bad for you, why not, right? The pieces are small, a couple dozen easily fit in the palm of your hand. They have a sweet, tangy, salty goodness and a hearty crunch. I finished the bag.

title: I Liked These Cookies
text: I'm ashamed to admit that these didn't last a week. I love raspberry and dark chocolate. Those two flavors are perfect together. The cookie was the weakest part of the product. It was a bit thin and didn't have a crispness you expect in a cookie. It was okay. The raspberry was something like a marshmallow creame spread. Different but I found it interesting. The dark chocolate was just the right flavor and thickness. I really liked these.

title: Really Like This Stuff
text: Kinda like caramel but different. Definitely has its own flavor. The product is very thick, even so I recommend keeping them in the fridge. They're good warm but much better cold. The best way I found to eat this, it is incredibly sweet, is to slice up a Granny Smith apple and dip the apple in the Dulce de Leche. It's fantastic. Goes great on ice cream and to be honest I'm quite happy to just eat a little plain, straight from the container.

title: Tasty Crackers
text: I liked these crackers. My favorite were the sweet corn then the roasted and lastly the seeded which I ate but wasn't really crazy about. The sweet and roasted went great with cheese, even the stuff in the can, peanut butter and lunch meats like pepperoni and salami. They were also enjoyable plain. The only problem I had with this was once or twice they'd soften and then adhere to the roof of my mouth like they'd been glued there! I would get these again.

title: A Very Odd Snack
text: These were strange. I don't understand the reason. Is there something inherently wrong with the potato chip? Why chicken? Who looked at a juicy, chicken part and thought "Grind that up, mash it flat, fry it and add some flavor!" I didn't mind them, The chicken and waffles chicken chips had an amusing pun like existence. The Sea Salt and Nashville Hot were the better of the varieties but even the chicken flavored chicken chips were okay. Not sure I'd buy them but as something to try and then review they were interesting and if I saw them at a party or something I'd have some.

title: Very Good Rice Cakes
text: These mini rice cakes were pretty good. There were some that were more rice and less flavor and then you'd get some just thick with the cinnamon, sugar and other flavors. I don't know about specifically tasting like an apple pie. . . That's asking a lot from rice and powdered flavorings but I can detect a hint of apple and the spices do remind me of homemade apple pie when I was a kid. I even liked getting the crumbs and extra flavoring left over after you finish the bag. I can't give a rice cake 5 stars but I'll give this 4 with a strong recommdation!

title: Delicious!
text: This was some of the best caramel popcorn I've ever had. The caramel coating was thick the flavor was dreamy, creamy and smooth. Popcorn was fluffy and popped large with very few duds in the bag. There's no GMOs, no artificial this or that. They use real butter. If you can afford it and you want some crazy good caramel corn, this stuff is the bomb.

title: Kinda Weird Flavor
text:
Somehow, like magic, I don't even know how, for easily a day anytime I burped I tasted this drink. I had coffee, pulled pork, many other things throughout the day and I could still, clearly, taste this. How?
I knew going in this wasn't carbonated but it still tasted. . . flat, my brain wanted bubbles. I like bubbles. Put bubbles in this and I might like it better. It wasn't bad. I've tasted far worse. But that day long aftertaste and lack of bubbles (yes, I know it doesn't have them by design!) just. . . there's a few cans in the fridge. I'm sure they'll eventually get consumed. Not something I'd get again.

title: Not Very Good
text: I tried this first with water and then with whole milk and it still had an unpleasant flavor. Not horrible but not really enjoyable. I'll likely keep this around in the hurricane supplies but I'm only going to use it in an emergency. Did not enjoy.

title: It's Just Water
text: This is purified water sourced from several municipal water sources. It's boiled and filtered until it's absolutely flavorless then they add back some minerals that might aid slightly in hydration but honestly the store bought naturally sourced spring water that may honestly be sourced from a spring in a city somewhere, tastes much better. This was bland and flat with little flavor like every purified water I've had to drink. I'll keep these around in my hurricane supplies. The water is palatable and also fine for cooking but as far as water goes, this isn't worth spending extra on.

title: Mild Not Bold
text: The flavor wasn't horrible but even using 25% or so more than we usually use to brew a pot of coffee it was never bold like they advertise. Smell was good and it doesn't taste bad but it's not bold. It's kinda mild. I'll use it up because it's coffee. But this isn't what I'm looking for in a 'bold' coffee.

title: Thin, Overly Sweet, NOT Fluffy
text:
Description says no preparation needed, several replies from the manufacturer/seller state that refrigeration for several hours will produce a better, more fluffy pancake. It doesn't, The spread less but still didn't fluff up like a real pancake.
I first tried this warm, the bottle taken from my pantry as it appears it's intended to be used. I would more call what I was able to produce with this product crepes rather than pancakes. The end results were uniformly super thin and though they browned up nicely the taste. . . very, sweet, like a cookie or dessert crepe, not a buttermilk pancake. The pour spout was next to useless, the batter ended up dripping down the bottle and making a mess no matter what I tried. They were edible, actually sweet enough to eat without syrup or for that matter the last couple I made I ate plain. I wouldn't get this again, not for camping or emergencies nor would I recommend this.

title: Not a Fan
text:
I tried one of these, grape I think, right out of the package when it arrived. After 10-15 minutes cleaning up the mess that made I realized my idea of "jelly" and the manufacturer's are drastically different. These are gels, even after days on the bottom shelf of my refrigerator these are liquid, not a jelly. I've tried another grape, orange, banana and strawberry and none of them have much flavor. It's more of a subtle hint of flavor and the texture wasn't one I really enjoyed. I'm a big guy, normally I would go nuts for sweet snacks but these just didn't do it for me.
A note on the packaging. The mesh bag they come in is an interesting idea. The treats themselves are thin plastic you either tear or cut the top off of opening a small tube to squeeze the gel through. This can't be resealed and as mentioned the contents are liquid. If you're giving these to small kids, that seems to be who they're aimed at with weird faces on each packet, do so outdoors or around furniture you don't like. These are a recipe for disaster.
There's also something in the product listing about watching the video, there isn't one, and taking the TikTok challenge. I'm on TikTok, I searched around. I found nine or so videos, some of people trying these and making a mess or trying to 'eat the most' (the challenge I guess) in 15 seconds, by biting the packet. . . and making a big mess. This TikTok challenge doesn't seem to be much of a thing and nothing I intend on doing.
I for one did not enjoy these; there's little flavor, they're very messy, I don't consider the contents to be jelly.

title: Yummy & Spicy
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect from these protein bars and I was pleasantly surprised. They did suffer some from shipping to Florida as do many chocolate and candy items. I was going to put them in the fridge for a while but overnight in the air conditioning seemed to firm the bars back up and reduce the sticking issue greatly.
The chocolate flavor is rich it doesn't come across as cheap. There's a mild hint of cinnamon which to me could have been stronger but I'm a fanatic when it comes to cinnamon. I felt the chili heat was mild, which is more what you'd want in a protein bar, some will like it, some won't. That's the way it is with most foods. The bars have decent sized chunks of almonds and cashews as well as there's almond butter in the mix so people with allergies please take note. I've enjoyed these bars. My box is almost empty and I have to protect it from my friends. . . Not really, I'm glad to share with friends but we're all maintaining social distancing and other factors.

title: Almost Overcooked But Delicious
text: My favorite thing in bags of Bugles and other chips was getting one or two in the bottom of the bag that had gone through the cooking process more than once. These chips are dark and extra super crunchy. Nearly overcooked these are great in small doses. I even like mixing these in with regular Utz potato chips to give it that special dark flavor at random. You get a whole LOT of chips in these packs. I got two, well sealed bags. The inside of the box and outside of the bag were greasy. Bags are easy to seal, I used a reusable zip tie. I really like these chips.

title: One of the Better Meal Replacement Shakes
text: I've tried numerous meal and nutrition shakes over the years from good to absolutely horrible. These are closer to the good end of the spectrum than the horrible. There's a slight aftertaste but it's not bad. My biggest problem is no matter the protein content 8oz. of fluid just doesn't fill me up. Something larger would be nicer but the flavor was decent and were nicely thick. They can be drunk warm but I much preferred them ice cold.

title: Good Flavor, Small Candies
text: These are nicely flavored candies though I haven't found a center 'full' of honey. I'm fairly sure they suffered some in shipping to Florida where they may have melted either in the truck on the way here or sitting in the mailbox. Still the flavors were good and all my friends who stopped over and tried them thought they were different and interesting. These are something I'd get again, though maybe in winter.

title: Not Crazy About These
text: I've had fig candies, fig cookies and real figs and there's something about these bars I just did not like. There was a bitter, almost chemical note to an all natural processed fig bar. You might love these, I did not and I'll be feeding them to guests and friends until they're gone.

title: Okay Drink Mix
text:
I mean, yeah, it's a little better than drinking plain water all the time. I wouldn't want this all the time either. As with most artificial sweeteners there's something of an aftertaste with this drink mix. The strawberry flavor is pretty strong, I tried full strength in a bottle of water I'd taken a good sized sip out of and it was potent. The next time I made it I left more water in the bottle and didn't use quite all of the packet. That got me a bottle with an essence of strawberry which I liked much better. The packets are nice, you can stuff a couple in your gym bag to give that after workout water a nice flavor addition. For me, this is a once in a while thing. If I had a variety pack I might drink more but all strawberry all the time gets a bit overwhelming.

TL:DR - Good flavor. Some aftertaste. Easy to carry. Easy to use.

title: Not a Fan of These
text: I don't get the thinking behind these flavors, I really don't. Blueberry, Yuzu? What's a yuzu? I had to Google them to find out what they are. This flavor was okay but the tart citrus with the blueberry was a little strange. Pineapple, Passionfruit. This was an okay flavor but the pairing just wasn't right. The worst though was Green Apple, Mango. I love sour green apple candies so why ruin it with mango? That just killed the tartness of the green apple. I was truly disappointed with all these flavor combinations it feels like they just drew them out of a hat and whatever two they go they made into candies. I even let my neighbor try them when she stopped over. Like me she was okay with the Pineapple, Passionfruit but also disliked the other two. I think I'll just put these in a bowl and offer them to people who stop by. . .  wait, no one does that these days. Ah well. I'm not a fan of these. Did not really like any of the flavors.

title: Delicious!
text: Using the smallest cup size on my K-Cup brewer this makes a perfect cup of hot chocolate. Sweet, creamy. Far better than the packets we used to use years ago. Better than using two packets to make one cup. You do have to run at least one possibly two cycles of plain water through after making the hot chocolate but that's a small price to pay for the perfect cup of hot chocolate. You could probably use the medium setting on your brewer if the small is too sweet.

title: Not Horrible, Not Great
text: It tastes mostly like the Italian dressing I'm used to. It has a little less twang and had a bit more oily mouth feel. It wasn't bad and if something like this was offered at a restaurant I might use it. I don't know that I'd buy it for use in my home though. The aftertaste has seriously lingered and my stomach's not feeling the best. I also want to note the cap disintegrated the moment I got the plastic protector off the bottle so I was able to use this once, had a nasty spill that took forever to clean up and ended up tossing the remainder because I had nothing to put it in.

title: Good as a Mixer
text: I've added roast chicken to this product and also a packet of ranch flavored tuna from Starkist. This brown rice has a good flavor and cooks easily in about 110 seconds (it calls for 90) in the packet it comes it. Simply squish the bag around to break up the rice, tear the packet corner and microwave away. It's so easy a kid could do it.

title: Meh. . .
text: In a time when getting pasta and other products was rather difficult I found this product available and bought a case of it. I've cooked it twice now and it's edible but both times it's been. . . chewy. I even cooked it longer the 2nd time for a softer feel to the tooth. This isn't bad and if you use a flavorful sauce it will be okay, not great but okay. In a quarantine situation when foodstuffs are hard to come by this will feed you and your family.

title: These are Good Pretzels
text: While I do prefer a sourdough pretzel I have no problem with regular old pretzels. These are crispy without being too hard to chew the flavor is good and there's a right amount of salt on the product. These are as good as any name brand pretzels out there.

title: Sweet!
text: Wow, made with no sugar and extra light vanilla creamer and this brews up super sweet. The coffee is decent but I didn't expect a total sugar bomb.  Not really a fan.

title: Yummy Honey!
text: Pooh would approve. Clover is one of my all time favorite honeys. My only complaint is this is sourced from several countries. Smooth, tangy, stored in a cute bear shaped bottle. This is just perfect for sweetening a cup of coffee or used in baking.

title: Delicious Peanut M&Ms
text: Great to snack on, use in decorating, kids crafts. If you like peanuts and chocolate you can't go wrong with these. Fresh and flavorful. Did have some issues with the resealable bag. The closure 'lines' were small, almost like something from a much smaller bag. It was also very stiff. Just a pain to close.

title: Coffee AND Chocolate!
text: The chocolate was deliciously creamy as was the coffee flavored caramel filling in the bars. High quality premium products. The coffee wasn't bitter but was very present. The packaging was kinda retro hearkening back to the 70s. These did not last long in our house. Absolutely delicious and something different.

title: Good Old M&Ms Originals
text:
You can't go wrong with M&Ms. They've been around forever because they know a good thing and don't mess with it. It's good chocolate (not Belgian but still good) and the bright colors can make a quick job of creating an edible decoration.
My only issue is with the resealable bag. The system they used is rather small and stiff making it a pain to open AND close. I found the easiest way was to open the bag only part way. That made resealing easier. In the end I just rolled the bag down and used a large paper clamp to hold things closed.

title: Pretty Good, Drink Cold
text:
These are filling, pretty okay tasting, I was able to discern the marshmallow flavor in the chocolate. It's not bad. I've had better and I've had worse. If I needed meal enhancement/replacement or was unable to eat solids I would most definitely consider this product. One thing I would note, they're FAR better when ice cold.
I wasn't crazy about the packaging. The soft sided cardboard box felt more like an oversized kid's juice box. They did open easy, even my 88 year old mother had no trouble with that, the spout was a little messy and too tight a grip is a disaster waiting to happen.

title: Neon? Nope!
text: Package says neon. Colors aren't. That could be my entire review right there. . . I expected bright, vibrant NEON colors and to be honest they're not as rich as the twenty plus year old bottle of blue food coloring I found in the back of the pantry. The pink is more of a washed out red, the purple and blue are anemic and require using an excessive amount to get decent color. The green was the only color that even vaguely hinted at being neon. At the price I paid and because I was only using these to amuse myself it just wasn't worth the hassle of seeking a refund. Not as advertised.

title: Extreme Mint Flavor
text:
I can get behind the potency of these mints because they're really strong, really, really strong. I'm okay with the mild sugar alcohols aftertaste I've dealt with that in sugar free products for year. My problem with these mints is they tend to disintegrate into powder in your mouth rather quickly. . . Often, not always. You can expect them to and that really increases the minty goodness to almost shortness of breath levels. I put three in my mouth when I started writing this review, one is gone already, the other two are acting normal. Nope, another fell apart. Inconsistent product.
Something else I'd like to point out is these mints are much larger than regular Tic-Tacs so there are literally half as many per container.
Another oddity. . . On one side of the product it clearly reads "Not a low calorie food" but on the other side it says "Serving size: 1 mint - 0 calories" . It's NOT a low calorie food BUT it's got no calories. . . I'm confused.
Still, I kinda like them. They don't get my mouth all gummy like sugary mints do.

title: Good Coffee Selections
text:
I like the Italian and Seattle roasts. Both are decently bold flavorful dark roasts that aren't bitter. I drink my coffee black, no sugar so I pay attention to these things. Good coffee.
My mom likes the caramel macchiato on occasion but says its a little odd tasting. Still, she asks for it so, there's that. She really enjoys the Kona blend. Says it reminds her of their vacations to Hawaii. I found it flavorful but a little weaker than I prefer.
My biggest complaint is all four flavors are just higgledy-piggledy thrown in one box. Even dividers would have been nice. It's a mild pain to dig through the box looking for a specific flavour especially when that one, Kona, is being used the most often. But, we enjoy all four flavors to varying degrees.

title: Good Mix of Flavors and Textures
text: An interesting bar with a good mix of flavors as well as textures. A little harder than I prefer but not granola crunchy. Spice was warm but not screaming hot. Decent heat, good sweet. All in all a good snack.

title: Good Basic Honey
text: While I prefer clover or orange blossom honey (and yes, you can taste the difference) over non-specific floral sourced honey this was good. Flows well, no added ingredients, 100% pure honey. Great for dipping chicken or making your own honey mustard sauce. Good for cooking or sweetening coffee or tea as well.

title: Needs to be Cold
text: I tried a bottle right out of the box and wasn't crazy about it but I put a couple in the fridge overnight and the next day, icy cold, this was delicious. Very nice caramel flavor with an exceptionally creamy base. Much thicker than most other nutritional shakes I've tried. We truly enjoyed these and they're actually good for you too.

title: Good in an Emergency
text: Lots, LOTS of shreds and small particles of chicken. Fully a quarter of the can was practically dust. Okay for making a soup or stew but not really appetizing. Also found it needed long, slow cooking, something you may not have time for or access to in an emergency. I would eat this, no matter how chewy, if there was nothing else to eat but I doubt I'd rely on this for camping or any other non emergency situation.

title: Very Small Containers
text: We're used to the refrigerator version of Coffee Mate and the flavor of the French Vanilla singles was very similar to each other. The regular flavor was okay and the Hazelnut was okay if slightly off. It just wasn't as pleasant as we expected. The biggest problem we encountered with these singles was how small they were. My mother likes her coffee light and sweet and it easily took three singles to get her coffee the way she liked it. It seems like it takes a lot of product to get to a desired outcome.  Nice to have around when there's no power or to take tent or trailer camping.

title: Tasty Snacks!
text: These snacks were quite tasty and chewy. They last quite a while. My favorite flavor was the clementine and my mother loved the Blackberry. Neither of us were excited by the mango but they were edible. The package didn't last long. Having resealable pouches would have been nice. They travel, even in Florida heat, well and don't melt. Very flavorful.

title: Tasty, Tasty Bars
text: These were sticky and yummy and I can't believe they were gone so quick. A little time in the fridge was required when they were delivered. Getting anything that can melt or become more sticky shipped to Florida is hit or miss. But we chilled them, then let them come to room temperature and devoured them. Delicious!

title: Absolutely Delicious
text: Wow these were delicious. Awesome flavor, texture was a little crumbly but we prefer that over very hard cookies. White chocolate and cranberry are a unique combination. My only complaint is there are only six cookies per pack! These didn't last long at all!

title: Butter Lovers?
text: The packaging and description call this product 'Butter Lovers' . I'd hate to see what they sold as 'butter haters' popcorn as I found next to no butter flavor in these bags. I like the mini size, it's perfect for a snack for one hungry person or two snacky feeling people.  Once I found the perfect time for my microwave it made good, plain popcorn. But as for loving butter, this product doesn't.

title: Truly Vile Tasting
text: I really like dark chocolate. I like bitter-sweet chocolate but this? It tastes like something made in a lab. Chemical tastes and scents. It won't melt even under extreme Florida heat. I gave it a fair and honest try and couldn't gag down more than half a bar before I ended up throwing everything away.

title: Surprisingly Good
text: If you like garlic you'll like this. Not overly potent but it's there in droves. I honestly like popping a pouch in the microwave, grabbing a spoon, a little salt and there's a quick meal. Have mixed with some Albacore tuna as well. I'm sure this would be a great base for many recipes. I'm disabled so I'm not really doing a lot of cooking, making this a great addition to our diet.

title: Yuck, Like Chewing Plastic
text: These arrived in a plastic ziploc bag with a cheap label. It made me think of a medical sample bag or a prescription from the pharmacy. The bag was either poorly made or not sealed as a large portion of the candies had spilled into the packaging. Everything was melted. I disposed of the mess put what remained in the fridge for about an hour to cool down. That done I tried these. . . the chocolate was good, nearly premium, sweet and creamy. The ginger was like chunks of plastic. I chewed one for a while, there was some heat and ginger flavor but in the end it was inedible. NOT recommended.

title: Not Very Appetizing
text: I've got to stop trying these healthy snacks. I keep hoping I'm going to come across one that's good for you and tastes. . . even okay would be acceptable now. Gluten-free, soy-free, dairy-free, stevia free. . . flavor free, texture free. It was like vaguely chocolate flavored clay. It didn't taste good and the mouth feel was not pleasant. Friends say "you get used to it!" I don't want to.

title: Adds an Interesting Flavor
text: Have used this three ways so far, all beef. On top of steak which was good and you can buy a cheaper cut and boost the experience. In a meatloaf which was 50/50, two of use loved it, one didn't like it and one really didn't like it. Then we sprinkled it on burgers while they cooked, they mixed with the grease and not only tasted great but dripped into the fire and made the whole patio smell heavenly and everyone likedd them.. So far the product has been pretty well received here.

title: Better Than Rice
text: A versatile product. Great as a base in the place of rice for dishes like General Tso's chicken, Orange Chicken, etc. or you can serve it as a side with butter and salt. Swapping the water for either beef or chicken broth adds another layer of flavors and ways to utilize this product. Personally I cook up a bunch (use caution; it can stick if the pan gets too hot as the liquid you use is absorbed) then slather it with butter, salt and a little garlic powder, it's delicious. Great product.

title: Flavored Raisins? Oh Boy!
text: Flavored raisins? I'd never heard of such a thing. These mixed berry sour raisins were quite good. The sour is tasty and not overpowering (do note, I like sour candies and such, you may differ from my tastes) then good old raisin under the sour. Unfortunately got a few stems in some of the packs but otherwise these were a definite hit around here.

title: All Pasta Is Not The Same
text: Maybe their grain is better. Maybe it's the spring water they purport to use. This is some seriously good pasta. I wish i were well enough to brew up a batch of my mom's secret recipe for sauce & meatballs. But even jarred stuff this stands out. Cooks just the same as you always have but there's something about the taste that's so much better than the big name brand stuff you normally get from the grocery store. Recommended!

title: Absolutely Terrible
text: Where do you start? It's not a hazelnut spread it's a hazelnut and almond spread with a bitter almond taste. Oh, calling it a spread or butter is a joke. Out of the jar this stuff bent a butter knife, I'm not kidding. It's dense like clay. The flavor is gross. Who cares if it's organic if it isn't worth eating.

title: Not For Warm Climates!
text: I had these delivered to Florida in February and we had a few warm days. The chocolate eggs are thin and melted in just 10-15 minutes in our mailbox (plus however long it was exposed to heat in the delivery vehicle). Two of the chocolates were melted into puddles, one had gotten out of the foil and the others were in various states of softness. I saved three out of six in decent shape by putting the package in the 'fridge for a few hours. Once resolidified the chocolate was pretty good. Out of six individual packs we got FOUR of the same character. All toys are serious choking hazards. They press fit together and the parts are small. Some parts didn't seem to go anywhere. Very confusing. Put two together, there were extra parts that had nowhere to go. Not for kids of an age to still put things in their mouths. Unimpressed.

title: Worst Diet Sodas Ever
text:
When I have soda it's diet. I really like diet soda. . . when they're good. Unfortunately these Dry brand diet sodas are awful, truly terrible beverages. I don't even want to keep these around as hurricane supplies. These would just make a bad situation worse;
Zero Sugar Cola - have you ever opened a can of diet soda, put it down, forgotten about it and picked it up a day, or more, later? That's what this cola tastes like the moment you open a can. It actually manages to taste like warm flat soda when it's ice cold and freshly opened. Oh and they've added the hint of some spices, because cola hasn't been a popular enough flavor. I'd rather drink warm, flat Diet Coke.
Mountain Berry - my mom hates diet sodas because of the way the sweetener has a before and after taste. I normally don't notice it because I've been drinking diet soda for decades. This stuff made me nearly spit the first sip out. The puckering overload of diet sweetener is overpowering. I can't even really describe the 'berry' flavor. Like the cola this tastes flat like they used the least carbonation allowed to call something a 'soda'. It's better than the cola but not much.
Island Fruit - Pineapple! Flat overly diet sweetenered pineapple soda with vague hints of other indistinguishable fruit flavors.
Sorry guys, this stuff was awful. Literally the worst diet sodas I have ever tasted.

title: OMG, So Delicious!
text: The only problem is how few caramels you get. They're so amazingly delicious and creamy. These come very well packed with two gorgeous decorated ceramic bowls that include fitted lids. There were three different flavors of caramels in the set; Vanilla, Sea Salt and Pecan. I don't think I can pick a favorite, they were all that good. Absolutely the best caramels I have ever had.

title: Like Chewing Rubber
text: The chocolate is the only reason these didn't get one star. It's a nicely rich dark chocolate but the 'banana' bits were like chewing clumps of rubber or pencil erasers with a bit of banana flavor misted onto them. I wasn't able to get a single piece to break up in my mouth. Loved the chocolate, spit out every piece of whatever the heck is in the middle. My mother also tried these with similar results but she's not really a fan of dark chocolate. Not for me.

title: Tasty Iced Coffee
text: When my coffee is hot I like it dark and as strong as I can get. I often make thermos flasks full of espresso forget those silly little cups I want a jug of it. I never put sugar or any sort of creamer in my hot coffee. But when it came to these iced coffees I much preferred the Mexican Vanilla can over the Double Espresso. The espresso is good but maybe because it's got sugar and a little milk which I would never put in coffee the taste is off, just a little. Oddly then the sweetened Mexican Vanilla cans are my favorite of the two. It's confusing but that's how it is. Both are good the vanilla is better.

title: Spicy But Lacking Depth
text: Sometimes people trying to create extra spicy foods will do so like it's a competition to just pack on the most Scoville Units possible but sacrificing or often completely forgetting flavor. Foods can be spicy even very spicy but still have a complex flavor note. The snacks in this variety pack are spicy and a couple, most notably the Funyuns Flamin' Hot and the Doritos Flamas with lime, having flavor and heat the rest just taste hot. There's some different textures but for the most part they taste the same, hot. I wasn't crazy about this collection of snacks.

title: Great Selection
text:
This was a great collection of chips, though I question the inclusion of the barbecue flavor potato chips. Everything else was white/plain, white cheddar Doritos and Cheetos puffs and lightly salted potato chips. Not really sure how the barbecue fits into the mix but everything was good. Though to be honest I'm unimpressed by claims of no artificial preservatives, flavors, or colors, etc. Because of those claims though these have a somewhat short shelf life of 60-90 days.
My favorite of the bunch were the Cheetos white cheddar cheese puffs then the sea salted Lays potato chips and then the Doritos and barbeque chips. I'll definitely keep my eyes open for the Cheetos when I go grocery shopping. I really liked those a lot.

title: Where's the Jasmine?
text: The rice cooks nice and fluffy. Simple and easy in the microwave but there was no flowery jasmine flavor. The rice was more tasty than regular rice but it just didn't have that jasmine flavor. We enjoyed the rice with a nice Chinese dish and I tried several spoonful's plain to test the flavor.  I doubt I'd buy this again over a regular rice unless the price were the same.

title: Boring
text: Honey? Lemon? No, chamomile. Barely noticed the lemon and honey, the reasons I picked this. It's mildly soothing if you've got a cold or sore throat but there's far better lemon teas out there. Neither my mother or I cared for this tea. I guess the organic nature and other ingredients are something if you're looking for that kind of thing. I was looking for a good honey & lemon tea and this isn't it.

title: Good Flavor, Great Size
text: Granted these are designed with kids in mind but I'm in my fifties and my mother whom I care for is in her eighties and these are great for those moments, usually later in the evening, when you really want to quench your thirst but you also don't want a large amount of anything which would keep you up and running all night long. One box is just enough to take the edge off. There's not that much sugar in a single box, the monster punch (fruit punch) has a nice flavor. The straw is easy to remove from the box and easy to remove from its wrapping. The straw is stiff enough to pierce the foil without a problem. If it's okay for two disabled adults it's not going to be a problem for your kids.

title: Good Candy
text: Often when a candy has a delivery vector like the sour shot from the coating on these candies the rest becomes bland and boring but although the sour, for me, doesn't last a long time the sweet side is almost creamy. This chewy candy is soft and doesn't have to be chewed forever like a piece of jerky. The sour apple flavor has a nice twang to it and a few will make you pucker some. They're not crazy strong and nowhere near joke candy range with their tartness. I actually have enjoyed sour candy meant to be a joke product so for me the sour is nice but not incredibly strong. Really do wish the sour lasted longer but they're enjoyable.

title: Thin & Slightly Bland
text:
I was a little skeptical about a shake snack drink that ships warm. I know they've had shelf stable milk for years now but I always thought that was some kind of voodoo magic or something. These snack drinks at a 170 calories per 8 fluid oz. aren't health food but they're not horrible for there are some ingredients I've never seen before, monk juice? And what the heck is fructooligosaccharide? Ah, Google tells me it's a low sugar carb used as a sweetener that doesn't cause sugar spikes. Beats me.
Any way, they call these rich, they're not. I found them a bit thin and watery. Like a really good chocolate milk diluted with water. I don't dislike them and my mom liked them saying they were okay and asked me to put a few more in the fridge for her. At the very least it's another item we can put in with the hurricane supplies.
Not great but not horrible.

title: Couldn't Be Saved
text: This honey arrived so well packed it could probably survive a fall off a five story building. And yet the cap was dented on the edge. I don't know if that contributed to the state the honey arrived in or not. The jar is quite large. Larger than what I normally see in the grocery store or small farmer's markets. Unfortunately when I unpacked this honey there was close to three quarters of an inch of crystallization at the bottom of the jar. I have tried twice, both times for quite a long time, soaking the jar in a pot of very warm water. I have not been able to save this honey. It's okay in coffee and tea where it dissolves but on waffles, biscuits and other foods it's gritty, crunchy honey which is disconcerting and not fun to eat. I've seen this happen but only on honey that's sat around in the cabinet for years. Very disappointed in this product.

title: We Didn't Enjoy These
text: These plantain chips are quite thick and if like the two of us you happen to be missing some teeth these chips become hard to eat and painful on the mouth. I had expected something a little thinner more on the line of a thick or kettle cooked potato chip. The flavor was a bit odd too. I've had plantains years ago, just plain fried chips and enjoyed them and I love salt and vinegar potato chips so I figured what could be better than plantains with salt and vinegar? Yeah. . . I don't think the two flavors go well together.

title: Vile!
text: I like watermelon, I like watermelon a lot. What I don't like is watermelon rind and that's all I tasted and tasted for an hour after drinking and eating stuff to get rid of this product's taste. There was also a weird chemical or metallic aftertaste that I attributed to possibly being from the can but could have been anything. Quite possibly the worst carbonated drink I've ever had.

title: Not Very Good, Bad Aftertaste
text: Wow what an aftertaste. Bitter, chemical. The overpowering sweetener just steps all over the lemonade & raspberry flavor. I'm a fan of diet sodas and enjoy almost all of them but they've gone overboard with the chemical taste. I guess, say after a hurricane and we were sitting around in the heat with no power one of these might be more interesting than plain water. Maybe. We'll see as the remaining packets, which in and of themselves are rather handy and easy to tote around, are going in with the hurricane supplies. I'll use them, maybe, during an emergency.

title: Okay Cold Coffee
text: Triple, three, shots of espresso in each can but oddly the claim is the equivalent of two and a half cups. . . either way, there's quite a lot of caffeine in each can, 175mg. Unfortunately, being a Latte there's milk, reduced fat, and sugar, sugar, sugar, 14 grams of sugar. I normally drink coffee and tea black, no sugar, so this was a change for me. Taste is a big odd. There's not a lot of weird chemicals in this so I don't know where it comes from but it fades or you become accustom to it. After that initial tasting weirdness it's not a bad drink. The 9oz can is a bit of a let down. Not even as much to drink as a can of soda for how much? I really disliked the stupid sip-through lid, it leaks, it's uncomfortable, strange and utterly unnecessary. Not bad but not spectacular.

title: Yummy Peanut Butter & Granola Bars
text: Good but a little small. One gives you energy and tastes really good but they're so small one leaves you wanting another. I could also do with more peanut butter and less peanuts but it's all good. These bars aren't health food but they're not horrible for you, as long as you can stick to one.

title: Delicious Maple Syrup
text: A good maple syrup. Nice and thick from the 'fridge. Dark amber color with a complex taste. I normally buy my pure maple syrup in glass bottles and I think being in a can, though a classic way of selling maple syrup does a disservice to an expensive product by imparting a slight metallic flavor to the syrup. I tasted the syrup upon delivery and then put it in the refrigerator which leads to one of the two issues I have with the packaging. Syrup will always get into the threads and unless you carefully and meticulously clean the inside of the cap and the spout on the can (and who does that?) then the sugars create a sticky glue and you have to run the top of the can under hot water to loosen the cap and that's going to happen every time you use. There's no way you're going to get everything perfectly clean. The pouring spout is short and syrup gets on the top of the can. Other than that this is a very good syrup and I'd highly recommend it.

title: One Awesome Candy
text: Love, love, love Necco Wafers and have for nearly fifty years. One of the first candies I can remember buying as a kid. while some like eating them one wafer at a time I love mixing and match the flavors in twos, threes and mores to make funky flavor combinations.

title: Quality Spices
text: Good every day sort of spices collection nothing exotic, things you'll use every day. We've bought McCormick spices for as long as I can remember. They claim to being organic which is nice. These spices, especially the garlic, have nice potent flavor and a good shelf life several years past the date I received them. A good product.

title: Paying Barilla for Water
text:
We're both disabled and use walkers to get around. Moving a pot of boiling water from the stove to the sink to drain is, not only dangerous but also terrifying. When I saw this product I thought it was going to be a life saver. I looked at the description and saw each bag was 8.5oz and we get a two full meals out of a pound of pasta from the grocery store so I thought, wrongly, we could easily get one meal per bag. Then I realized we were paying Barilla for their water. A full bag is just a little too much for a serving of pasta if all you're having is pasta (we're don't make elaborate meals) so we needed to use two bags to get a meal. That makes this too expensive even for the convenience. But read on to see why cost is irrelevant.

Then there's the product itself. First impression; this isn't penne, penne is much larger and what's with the color? This looks nothing like the pasta we cook on the stove. It's kinda scary and reminds me of pasta left out for a day or two. Taste wasn't great, there was a strange aftertaste and it was incredibly chewy like very undercooked pasta. And I have to say neither of our stomachs is happy now about an hour after eating this product. There's four more bags in the box, they're going in the trash.

This has nothing to do with my rating, the product deserves what's given, but it's worth mentioning: Check your expiration date. The product I received expires two weeks from the delivery date. But that's just a stocking issue. It's a wet product, I wouldn't trust it much past the expiration date. There's just two of us here, we aren't going to use an entire box in two weeks. I had hoped to get some time out of this product but now, that's irrelevant. We won't be buying more or even using the remaining bags.

title: Not Horrible
text: I've used this mix, using their directions, to make waffles a few times. I prefer them over pancakes, their easier to cook and the cleanup is about the same. I found the resulting food. . . edible? Somewhat bland, a little chewy and the chocolate had a funky aftertaste I didn't really care for. Maybe this is what 'organic' is supposed to taste like but I have the urge to doctor the instructions, you really can't call adding water and oil a recipe. Maybe I'll add some whole milk or an egg. See what happens. I'm not saying the product is horrible maybe my taste palate is just used to and likes preservatives and chemicals. Maybe this makes better pancakes than waffles. I'm really not sure. I'll probably use what was sent to review but I doubt I'd buy it if I came across it in the store.

title: A Tasty Snack
text: These are delicious. The cherries are just sweet enough to offset the bitterness of the dark chocolate. Each bag contains 8 smaller single serving bags of chocolate covered cherries. At only 120 calories per single pack there's no guilt. I'm used to cordials but these are a very nice change. There's also supposedly no GMOs or artificial ingredients which to me are no big deal but I felt it worth mentioning for those people who care about such things. Eat! Enjoy!

title: Brings Out the Kid in You!
text: It's been years since the last time we saw Necco Wafers. They've been one of my favorite candies since i was a kid. My 86 year old mother also remembers them from her childhood. These have been around a long time and the only thing that seems to have changed is the size of the wafers themselves. They gotten visibly, so we feel at least, smaller than they used to be. But other than that the flavors don't seem to have changed whatsoever. Open a package and a bad day gets better. Transported back to being a kid, camping with my family again. It's awesome. We're, to be honest, already on our second order. Very highly recommended!

title: Not Bad Coffee
text: The eight ounce bag I received is supposed to be used all at once in a restaurant for large containers which I found a bit disturbing. I thought restaurants brewed real coffee instead of very large containers of instant coffee. That aside the coffee came with instructions for single use cups of coffee in different sizes. Following their instructions this makes one very strong but good cup of coffee. It's not bitter it's just potent. I actually enjoy it. It reminds me of the coffee we used to brew when I was camping with the scouts. If you get the bag and don't like very strong coffee start off with a half to three quarters teaspoon of the grounds as opposed to a full teaspoon.

title: Yummy!
text: They're Fritos. The original Fritos. I mean you can't go wrong with these. They came out 85 years ago (seriously?) so they've been part of my life since I grew teeth and could chew them. Great with burger, sandwiches, hot dogs or just as a snack by themselves. You can't go wrong with these, you just can't. I'll take these over potato chips any day.

title: Not Really Worth Buying
text: I'm a fan of Oreos. Mint, Peanut Butter, you name it we've tried it and enjoyed them. . . until now. I noticed these after putting together a Prime Pantry box which was completely full so I looked for and found these at the local grocery store. For basically the same price of a regular bag of Oreos you get two thirds or less in this 'specialty pack' than in a regular package. If you're lucky and eat the filling off the cookies like we do you might, might mind you, notice one maybe two popping candies per cookie. Often there's not a single popping effect at all. They taste good, like regular Oreos but you pay way too much to get far too little.

title: Very Good Breakfast Bars!
text: We've tried both the peanut butter and strawberry bars. My mother likes the strawberry best. I find them a little bit tart but still not bad. Myself I personally think that the peanut butter bars are amazing. Either way you go (we've even bought the Apple Cinnamon from the grocery store to try we like the brand so much). Each bar is exceptionally filling. You really can't go wrong with any of the flavours just pick the one you like the most. For me it's the peanut butter all the way. Best breakfast bar, ever.

title: Great Way to Start the Morning
text: These are delicious and reasonably filling. Of all the flavors they make we've yet to find the cherry and don't want to risk a multi-pack purchase on a flavor we haven't tried. We regularly buy the strawberry from our local grocery store. Through Amazon they were slightly cheaper per unit and far more convenient to buy in bulk.

title: Best Cinnamon Ever
text: Rarely do I give a product five-stars and it's got nothing to do with this Happy Belly Cinnamon being organic or non-irradiated (I didn't even know there was such a thing as irradiated cinnamon). This gets five-stars because of the flavor, sharp but mellow, warm and spicy. We've bought probably every store brand of cinnamon there is and none of them came close to the flavors in this brand's cinnamon. We tried a sprinkle here and there, on waffles, in coffee, etc. but last night I made my special cinnamon crusted French toast. With the store brands even crusted you could barely taste their bland flavor, a couple were okay but nothing tasted this good. I was stuffed and I wanted more. I just couldn't believe how good this tasted, how flavorful it was. This deserves every one of those five stars.

title: Good Stuff
text: These are absolutely delicious. There's two of each flavor strawberry, orange, lemon and I think watermelon. Which makes these a fun treat to have around the house. They last quite a while too so the box will last quite a while.

title: Delicious Cinnamon Snacks
text: I'm stuck somewhere between three and four stars, the inclusion of cellulose fiber which is although considered safe for foods is still wood pulp and Fructooligosaccharide which in the US is considered  'Generally recognized as safe (GRAS).' [quote from Wikipedia]. That being said these are sweet almost, with a strong cinnamon flavoring with a nice hint of cream or vanilla flavoring. These are almost too sweet like a breakfast cereal but almost isn't exactly so these qualify as a very sweet, crunchy churro snack that is practically addictive. Once you start it's very hard to stop eating them. We've had them with vanilla ice cream which was a nice addition but to be honest straight out of the bag is, in my opinion, the best way to eat these. Just tear open a bag and have at it. These snacks are just delicious.

title: One Of The Worst Snacks I've Tasted
text: Too many nuts, weird chemical aftertaste, this repeats and stays with you for hours. I've eaten several breath mints and all I can still taste is the strange chemical and strawberry flavor along with dark chocolate that tastes nothing like dark chocolate. It was almost as sweet as milk chocolate. I ate one package and regret it. It's been over an hour and I keep burping up this horrible chemical strawberry taste. I won't eat another piece of this. I did not like them at all. I guess if you were starving and there was nothing else, okay, I'd eat them. Other than that I'd rather have dry toast.

title: Another Hazelnut & Chocolate Clone
text: Arrived like water. Seal on foil so poor it pulled away with the initial removal of the lit. Contents dribbled out staining (hope it comes out) a t-shirt, getting all over my desk and just barely missed my laptop. I took a sip, it honestly arrived in a completely liquid form. Wasn't bad. Really just another in the sudden hazelnut and chocolate 'spreads' that have hit the market. Not much taste difference between this and Nutella. Put it in the 'fridge to firm up for a few hours now it's an unspreadable rock. I don't know if defrosting it in the pantry is a good or safe idea or not. Wasn't impressed almost lost my laptop, had to scrub my desk clean and I hope the mess comes out of my shirt. Beware of this product if you have it shipped anywhere warm. It was just in the 80's in Florida when we received it but the delivery trucks get incredibly warm.

title: Delicious Easy to Prepare Rice (Edited)
text:
If you like sticky rice from the restaurant then this is the product for you. We even made a second order when, for a short time, this was only available as an add on item and since it comes in a pack of three we needed two so we could have two each available.
These packs are quite filling. You can add all sorts of meats and veggies to them if you want we find ourselves just adding butter and salt (pink Himalayan) and making a meal of just the rice. It's more than enough to fill you up.
As an add-on item this three pack sold for almost a third of the current price. 1-star removed for what feels like price gouging. We love the rice we just hate (and wont pay) the price.

title: Too Crunchy, Too Bland
text: We found these bland and boring, unless you got to a section with a lot of black pepper and then there was some heat. At best it tasted like the world's worst granola. It was missing something to bring out any special flavor. Very dry, very crunchy, very bland. I doubt we'll finish the box. Not something we'd ever buy.

title: Horribly Bland
text:
Bought these at the local grocery store instead of Amazon but felt the urge to leave a review of the product anyhow. Our reasons for buying these; firstly the grocer used to carry an off brand of peanut butter wafers that were very tasty but recently had stopped carrying them and couldn't explain why. Secondly we saw these and thought they'd just changed the standard peanut shaped Nutter Butter cookie we've known since I was a child. That, we found out later was untrue.
These wafers are terrible. Bland beyond belief. The outer casing is almost entirely flavorless, very dry and flaky. While there is some peanut butter filling inside the wafer within a few minutes of eating them there's no taste of peanut butter left to linger. They're filling but practically flavorless. We'll never buy these wafers again.

title: Apple Juice Is Good Stuff /  Cherry Apple Juice Mix Not So Much
text:
Just under seven ounces is good for a quick thirst quench, better for kids than, in my opinion, adults. There's really not enough juice in on box to satisfy me so I usually have two when I'm thirsty. They're also much better ice cold than war but they're drinkable warm just not as good as when cold. The flavor is rather good with little to no after taste. No added sugar is a plus so the sweetness is all from the apples. The ingredients are water, apple juice concentrate and vitamin C. The only thing I'm unsure of is where the apples are sourced as much of the apple crops used for juice comes from multiple countries which have different pesticide regulations and rules. But other than that the juice is quite tasty has no added sugar (at 23g of sugar per box these are not really diabetic friendly tough the 100 calories per box isn't too bad) or flavors. We both enjoyed these juice boxes quite a lot and had no trouble getting the straw into the box though sometimes we had a little trouble getting the straw out of its package. Enjoyable, thirst quenching (to a degree), somewhat healthy and all natural. we're quite happy with these.

{Edit:}
Amazon, as they often do, has combined two vaguely similar items from the same company into the same review.
So in addition to the juice boxes this review also covers the Mott's 100% Apple & Chery juice gallon bottle. I found the initial flavor to be good but there was a strange mixed up aftertaste which I might attribute to, on top of Apple & Cherry Juice Concentrates the addition of Vegetable and Fruit Juice Concentrates and 'Natural Flavors'. My mother on the other hand poured a glass of this and couldn't finish half of it. She said she couldn't stand the flavor. It's also a bit sugar heavy where an 8oz. serving contains 28g of sugar (29g total carbs) so this to is something diabetics need to be cautious with. I'm not to crazy about the vegetable juice concentrates and 'natural' flavors (which I have no idea what those are or what vegetables were used). I may slowly finish the bottle, I have small sips to quench my thirst. But I'm not crazy about the Apple Cherry Juice mix or the way all these products are bundled into one.

title: Absolutely Terrible
text: These were pretty terrible. Flavor was bitter and there was more. . . whatever that was kiwi-strawberry, than applesauce flavor to the packs. I'm glad I only got a four pack as I don't even want to finish the ones that are left. Neither I nor my mother could stand these. Bitter, and bland these were some of the worst food products we've tried. I can't understand how anyone can post four and five star reviews of these. Honestly, these were horrible, don't buy these.

title: Unimpressive Sampler
text: The cookies were okay, the Nana's gluten, and just about everything else 'free' cookies' were edible but not exceptional. The English shortbread and the two Oreos were, in our opinion, the best samples provided. I don't normally comment on shipping during a review but there was no protection whatsoever in the box and other than the Nana's cookies which couldn't possibly have broken everything else arrived in pieces, in some places crumbs we ate with spoons. I also forgot how bad an idea late Spring ad Summer are for mailing chocolate to Florida. Anything chocolate melted. I was very disappointed with this product and received a refund for the purchase.

title: Good Quality Himalayan Salt
text: Decent quality pink salt. Flavor is good. Size of the crystals are decent for our grinder. We enjoy the flavor and product very much. Honestly there's not a lot you can say in a review about salt. It appears to be honest pink unprocessed Himalayan salt. The price for two pounds was fantastic and I'm quite happy with the purchase. I'd buy this again.

title: A Good But Not Great Earl Grey
text: I was drinking Earl Grey long before Star Trek's Captain Pickard made it popular. This is good Earl Grey, a little flowery with a little less 'bite' or bitterness I'm used to getting with my old standby Twinings Earl Grey. I also like the Twinings better because each bag is individually wrapped. With these Nature's Guru tea bags all 25 bags are loose in one Mylar bag. The string on these bags is actually rather short. Not long enough to wrap around the mug handle and get the bag at least halfway down in the mug. They're also not well attached to the bags and pull off easily. I do like the shape of the bag, it exposes more of the tea to the water than typical flat bags. All in all, I don't think I'd buy this but I will finish drinking it. I honestly like my regular brand better. On the other hand my mother tasted the Nature's Guru Earl Grey and liked it better so it's really a matter of personal preference.

title: Delicious Breakfast Flats - Updated
text:
We love these and hope they become available locally soon we seriously want to buy more already but fifty nine or even forty two bucks for a case here on Amazon? That seems somewhat extreme. The taste is fantastic, a hint, maybe a little more than a hint, of cinnamon the actual taste of cranberries and almonds in three flat, very crisp bars in every individual package. Calories aren't bad at just 180 per package there's also 27g of carbs and 12g of sugar to deal with. We're not really fans of crisp/crunchy foods and worried about the nut content but they're easy to eat. These are going quick, they're really incredibly delicious as a breakfast replacement or afternoon snack. They're also quite filling. Surprisingly, I must say these are highly recommended.

Update - These have been available in bulk through Amazon for a while now and at a reasonable price. Very nice to have around the house.

title: Like Really Spicy Cat Food
text:
You know that look your cat gives you when you buy them some new food that supposed to make them get up and dance with happiness (when you're not looking of course) but what really happens is the cat takes a nibble maybe two and then finds a strategic place to sit and glare at you from? This was like extra spicy cat food. It managed to be wet and dry at the same time. The crackers were good, only one was broken. They were something like a water biscuit. The problem with the crackers is even if you filled them to beyond overflowing (and you really wouldn't want to!) there were only enough crackers for a third, perhaps half, of the can.
I have eaten several cookies, a handful of Tic-Tacs (cherry if you were interested) and four Butter Rum Life-Savers and I can still taste the Bumble Bee Sensation Chipotle Seasoned Tuna. If there were nothing to eat. If I were stranded in a raft at sea and this was all there was to eat. . . I'd lose a lot of weight. I'd eat some to keep up my strength but then I'd want to kick the inventor in the shins when the ordeal was over.
Have I gotten the point across that I didn't like this product at all? I'd like to think I at least tried to get that point across. I'd rather eat plain oatmeal or hospital 'special' eggs. This would keep you alive and that's the only way you could get me to eat this stuff again.

title: Yummmmm!
text: I don't care what anyone says, these are my favorite flavor M&M on the planet and I' glad they're only available once a year otherwise I'd have pails full of these in every corner around the house all year long. Plus, if they were available all the time they wouldn't be special anymore and I'd probably get tired of them. So, once a year as a special treat these things knock my socks off.

title: Not How My Cookie Crumbles. . .
text: If you made this only with the package, no add-ins and not reading far enough to add the suggested but not required, pinch (make it a big one!) of sea salt I think you'd be enjoying cardboard flavored things that somewhat resemble cookies. I added a really good dash of pink Himalayan sea salt and a full cup of Reese's peanut butter chips. The results were. . . edible, not even bad really but not Christmas cookie special and with the addition of half a cup of butter (required by the recipe) and a cup peanut butter chip the 'good' has gone completely out of the picture. The dry mix is the really only healthy part of the cookie. If you're going to add 814 calories in butter and (by my choice of course) over 1,200 calories in peanut butter chips there's really no reason for a healthy dry mix. But I guess if you've got actual gluten allergies this would be a good choice to try out. I really wasn't that impressed.

title: A Different Flavor of Tic Tac
text: Now that's different. The flavor definitely, sorta, somewhat remind you of Cherry Cola. The flavor makes a decided change about half-way through the mint.While it really isn't exactly Cherry Cola flavored it does have a distinct and interesting flavor. Comparatively we've tried several different flavors and these are far better than the Strawberry Fields, Orange and Apple flavors though we still prefer the Wild Cherry flavor best though those appear hard to come by lately. Still these are quite enjoyable.

title: Lots and Lots of LifeSavers!
text: These are the best LifeSavers flavor I've ever had and the best quick, more or less low calorie full sugar treat we've found. There's only approx. 15 calories per piece of candy. Buying them in bulk bag is even more economical than buying boxes of rolled Lifesavers candies and they'll last a whole lot longer.

title: Not As Pictured/Described
text: One look at the product images and the ones I'll upload with my review and you'll be asking yourself the same thing I did. "How come what was delivered looks nothing like what's advertised?" The advertised product shows large chunks of salt much closer to the 6mm size of the 3 - 6mm advertised. The salt I received is far closer to 1 - 3mm with very, very few larger pieces and maybe a scant handful that come close to 6mm in size. It still works in my grinder but it's not what I expected when I ordered this bag of salt. I understand this is a natural product and there are vagaries in size with such products but what I received looks nothing like what I ordered. I like the flavor of the product, it's a bit wetter than I'd like so it clumps in the grinder but my complaint is not being sold what I expected. I doubt I'll order from this brand again.

title: Our Favorite Flavor!
text: Just like I remembered from my childhood. Smooth and creamy. Absolutely delicious and incredibly addictive! I've had to start leaving the open roll on the other side of the house. When the open rolls were next to our chairs we'd have one and then, well one more won't hurt. They're not a lot of calories, right? Suddenly the roll's empty and hey, we bought a whole box, right? Next thing you know the box is half empty and you're sitting there feeling guilty, well a little, not too guilty for just one. . . two, more Butter Rum Lifesavers.

title: A One Star Pasta
text: Worst Barilla ever. We make a pasta dish with gravy, ground beef, spices and pasta. Normally we use shells but we wanted to try something different and picked this Orecchiette to try. Barilla has been our go to brand for years but this was awful. The domes stack together, stick together and come out undercooked. We stirred, vigorously, numerous times during the cooking process and they still stuck together in large numbers. The meal was edible but it wasn't great and we definitely won't buy this style pasta again. Very disappointed.

title: Yum
text: Delicious cookies that melt in your mouth. A little expensive but you get what you pay for and these are a quality cookie and worth the splurge from time to time.

title: Nice Mix of Chips
text: Great to have a variety of chips around for snacks and afternoon meals. Price was okay.

title: Scoooby Doooby Gooood!
text: These are really tasty and chewy snacks and at just 80 calories per pouch they're not bad for you. Well, at least not as bad as some super sugary snacks can be. Definitely something we'll buy again.

title: An Old Friend
text: I've been eating Barnum's Animals for going on fifty years. Nothing has changed in all that time except of course the price. They're a little bland but bring back memories out of my childhood. Great when you have a sour stomach or just want a light, quick, snack.

title: A Very Nice Treat
text: I'm torn between giving these bars three or four stars. My main complaint is the gritty component the roast coffee beans mixed into the chocolate add. Once you've done eating you're left with quite a bit of grit like after drinking a cup of badly filtered coffee. But one of our favorite treats years ago were chocolate covered coffee beans so I'm a bit understanding of the grit. The dark chocolate melts nicely and isn't overly bitter. So, all in all,  these are a nice occasional treat. Each four section bar weighs in at just one ounce.

title: Subpar Instant Coffee
text:
