title: New packaging and heating instructions result in a different experience
text:
The manufacturer has recently updated the container to be carbon neutral. While I do applaud this, the change has altered the experience of heating and eating this dish. The new container is paper-based, and the heating instructions have changed significantly, although the food inside does not seem to have changed. The old packaging required you to cut a slit in the film cover, and microwave for 3 1/2 minutes. This was perfect. The new (paper) bowl heating instructions require you to remove the plastic film from the top, and microwave it for five minutes. This produces a different meal. The old way produced a delicious meal. The new instructions dry it out - a lot.

I have now modified the way I warm this up, and instead of removing the plastic cover, I cut a slit in it and microwave it for four minutes. This seems about right. I suspect the paper packaging does not retain moisture the way the plastic bowl in the old one did, as this is still more dry than the previous version. Lost a star there. Still recommended, even though the portion size is definitely on the small side for the price. This should either be 4 oz larger or about a dollar cheaper. 2.5 stars, rounded to 3.

title: Not the coffee I was looking for
text:
Expectations were kind of high, given the reviews. While I absolutely love that these capsules are compostable, freshness does not seem to have been preserved. The capsules are not as pictured in the product listing, or on the Artizan website. They are covered with what seems to be a loosely-woven paper on both ends. There is no way this paper keeps air out and the coffee fresh - it looks very porous. I have attached a photo for reference.

Per the date on the box, the coffee was reportedly roasted less than a month before I got it, but tasted bland and flavorless - like stale coffee. Unless the coffee itself was not roasted on the date indicated on the package (I am sure it was), one can only blame the capsules for not preserving airtight integrity. One only has to see the capsule to know this design cannot possibly preserve freshness. I had high hopes for this coffee. A worthwhile experiment, with disappointing results. Will not be ordering these capsules again. :(

title: Definitely not Canadian, but a good substitute
text:
There is no substitute for proper Canadian grade B maple syrup, but this stuff will do in a pinch. And yes I know they have changed the grading convention; It used to be the lighter more delicately flavored syrup--you know, the GOOD stuff--was grade B. Now syrup is graded differently and the grading frankly doesn't make any sense at all. You just have to taste it to see what it really is. Thankfully Canada hasn't changed their grading system. Anyway, this is pretty good stuff. It'll do in a pinch if I run out of the (vastly superior) Canadian stuff.

By the way, as someone who truly does understand maple syrup, I need to throw some shade on the other reviewers who are complaining about this product needing to be refrigerated. Proper maple syrup always needs to be refrigerated. It spoils. It doesn't have crap in it like "table syrup". If you want to use some for your breakfast, you decant it from the bottle into a small pitcher (like what you would do with cream for coffee), and either let it come to room temperature or microwave it to warm it up. That's how you use *real* maple syrup. Period. Anyone complaining about having to refrigerate it doesn't know what maple syrup actually is. Give them a bottle of the artificially-flavored corn syrup and chemicals they are used to from IHOP. This stuff is for those who know (but can't get their hands on any good Canadian maple syrup). Of the American syrups, this is the best I've had. Four stars.

title: No Fun Jo Decaf = NO Fun ...at all
text: I am pretty sure this is not decaffeinated via the Swiss water method. I regularly drink coffee which has been - this just tastes like chemicals. Not the decaf I am looking for. In addition, this just is not good coffee. I am a pretty serious coffee drinker (James Hoffman subscriber), and I have a decent nose for coffee. This was supposed to be pretty decent according to a few reviews I read here and elsewhere (you know what I mean:  the eternal search for good decaf continues...). I can only conclude they were not drinking the same coffee I was. Not recommended at all. Gevalia decaf costs about the same and is *significantly* better than this drek. Tossed in the bin. :(

title: Whoa--is this ever awful...
text:
I am not a huge coffee snob or anything (maybe a little), but this is truly, epically bad coffee. I generally don't love flavored coffees, and this was in Subscribe & Save at a ridiculous price, so I (foolishly) tried a bag. I should have known better. In a word: awful. Of course it was. :(

I used 2.5 tbsp in a pour-over, as I usually would with any coffee (I like it strong). The result was extremely weak and tasted of nothing but chemicals. I could not believe how little it actually tasted like coffee - it just tasted like artificial cake flavoring (chemicals). Absolutely revolting. Maybe it will taste better in the bottom of the trash can? That's where it belongs. NOT recommended.

title: Didn't love it: no real flavor, over-roasted, and seemed stale
text:
*UPDATED REVIEW*
I returned it. This is the worst coffee I have ever had. Seriously. I made another cup today, had a sip and promptly called Amazon to return it. Awful. I wonder if what was in the bag might have been incorrect? This was very dark and sharp/bitter, not smooth at all. I used a normal amount of coffee (not too much), and the result was the same three day sin a row. Dumped the cup I had made, called Amazon and tossed the rest of it out.
---

Had high hopes for this, but found it harsh and unpleasant. The flavor is very one-dimensional, flat and strong. No hints of anything else here, just strong, dark roasted unremarkable coffee in a bag labeled medium roast. I found the roast incongruent with the labeling, definitely overdone for "medium". The lack of any meaningful flavor highlights the harshness of the roast. It just does not have any warmth, no pleasant robust feel or sweetness at all, no real body, just a source of caffeine. Also, it seemed a bit stale - not fresh. Will not be buying this again, and may not finish the bag.

title: This used to be my go-to coffee. Then it TRIPLED in price.
text: Love this stuff. Seriously delicious coffee. I was getting 20oz bags for between $7 and $8 all through the pandemic. I must have gone through 40 bags or more in the past few years. Suddenly, about a month ago I noticed it was ABSURDLY expensive. It is now $22 for that same 20 oz bag. Canceled that subscription. Starbucks is literally half the price. 100% Ridiculous. Shame, though. This was really good coffee, but they are are insane if they think anyone will buy it at this price.

title: Not great
text: Not sure what I was expecting here, but this was not it. Literally chicken nuggets and mac & cheese. Save your $.

title: Small, very small
text: Strombolis are decently sized. One should be a meal. Not the case here. You would easily need two of these for lunch. About the size of a hot pocket.

title: Very small
text: Literally a handmade hot pocket. Definitely not the stromboli I was looking for.

title: Mediocre gnocchi
text: These are decent, but nowhere near as good as the blurb on the back of the bags would have you hope for. Passable portion for one. Too tomato-y for me - sauce seem lacking flavor, just tastes like tomatoes. Needs some thyme and oregano! Adding grated parmesan cheese saved this dish. Likely will not buy again.

title: Say it with me ... FRESH LETTUCE?
text: The egg salad is mediocre. The bread is mediocre. The lettuce is awful. Seriously. Not only is it bitter green leaf lettuce, but it's as soggy and limp as a wet paper towel, every time. Ruins the sandwich.

title: FINALLY a superb brioche-style hot dog bun!
text: I cannot tell you how pleasantly surprised I am by this product. These are absolutely delicious and by far the best hotdog buns I have ever used. Definitely more expensive than other buns, but they made a hotdog a beautiful thing.

title: Unpleasant odor and flavor which does not dissipate
text: Uncle Ben's needs to spend some time with some people who can cook basmati rice properly. I have been looking for a good subscription replacement for the VeeTee basmati rice, which was decent but is no longer available. Unfortunately, this is *definitely* not it. While all packaged rice smells odd when first removed from the package after microwaving, the smell dissipates quickly in most cases. Not the case here. This rice has a lingering unpleasant odor and the flavor is simply not pleasant. Time to try a different brand.

title: Mediocre at best
text: These are the bottom of the barrel for store-bought croissants. Neither light nor flaky, these were far too dense and a bit stale, even though they had apparently been packed the day before. I've ordered croissants from Whole Foods (owned by Amazon) recently and these were not even in the same league. Or course, they also cost a lot less. You do get what you pay for here. These are very mediocre croissants. Oddly, Smart & FInal's store-brand croissants are much better, same with Ralph's.

title: Expired three days after on arrival
text: I should have checked the date when it arrived. :(

title: Good, but overpriced
text: Amy's products are mostly pretty good, and this is no exception. Tasty and relatively good for you, as far as frozen stuff goes. However, for the portion size (small), this is - like all Amy's products - very overpriced. A trip to TJs will yield higher quality frozen veg food for 1/2 the price.

title: Not as good as OR, and bags are smaller
text: These just do not produce as much popped popcorn per bag, about 2/3 the volume in cups. Feels like 3 of these = slightly more than 2 OR bags in terms of popped volume in a big party bowl. Also, make very sure you fully separate the ends before popping. If you do not, the bags will not inflate fully and you will have very crushed popcorn. While I like the flavor, the value equation is an issue. Going back to OR after this experiment.

title: Not the best havarti, no real flavor, spoiled very fast
text: This was disappointing. The flavor was too mild to taste anything but the dill, and it spoiled within a few days after opening. Also, no texture at all - just a solid brick. Havarti usually has small bubbles giving it a looser/less dense texture I typically really enjoy. This was not present at all here - just solid and soft. Not buying this again.

title: Mediocre quiche
text: Like everything else Fresh delivers, these are a celebration of mediocrity. Passable, but not "good" quiche. Also, these tend to repeatedly be crushed/bent in the delivery process because the people packing the bags are clueless. Conclusion: either make your own quiche or get it from TJ's.

title: Nothing like any old fashioned I've ever had
text: I guess I just do not get this recipe. Literally every old fashioned I have ever had has been better than this. Of course, I also prefer a quality scotch old fashioned, obviously. To me, bourbon just feels like what you drink if there wasn't a good single malt scotch or even a decent Irish whisky available. This also tasted not quite sweet enough, so adding a little simple syrup helped. Taste is so subjective, but for me this was definitely a miss.

title: I guess I just *really* don't like vermouth
text: Seriously, this was awful. I am learning how to make cocktails and I needed this for a Manhattan. Turns out I don't like Manhattans at all. I think really what's going on is I don't like vermouth. Seriously - it's gross. I have no use for this and I will be tossing the rest of it. Obviously this is a very subjective review based on my personal tastes, and as far as sweet vermouth goes this might be a good one. I have no idea, it was just disgusting to me.

title: This was terrible
text: I like pastrami. This was very disappointing - tasted artificial, and just not really like it was a natural food. Filled with preservatives, I guess. I tossed most of it. Moral of the story: if you want good pastrami, go to a deli. :/

title: Not tasty - skip this one
text: This company's other products are actually quite tasty, but this one just is not very good. It smelled a bit funny, and tasted odd. I don't think it was off, but it was not an enjoyable meal. I'll stick to their other products instead.

title: Tastes ...funny
text: This is really not good ice cream. I realized it after I bought it that it was actually a light ice cream, and I'm not sure what they're putting in it but it just tastes like chemicals. Gross, actually. This is just not a quality product. Did not finish it.

title: Something seems to have changed - smells rotten
text: I used to like this product. Something has changed and it now smells foul when you open it. And it tastes awful now. Threw it out. Nope.

title: Kind of expensive, easily damaged
text: This is a decent quiche - when it makes it to you in one piece. It is very likely to be crushed in the delivery process. I have had several arrive broken. The quiche itself is fine, not the greatest, but passable, but for the quality it is kind of pricey. This should be an $8 item, max. If they keep arriving crushed, I may stop ordering them.

title: This is revolting. Spend a few bucks more and get a quality Scotch
text: Tastes like an ashtray. Seriously. Anyone giving this 5 stars has obviously never had good whiskey or scotch. This swill is undrinkable - the kind of booze you would expect to find in a dumpy bar in Texas or something. Spend a little more on a bottle of Glenlivet 12 y.o. to try. You will never be able to drink anything this bad again.

title: Cork would *NOT* come out
text: I'd love to say this was great, but no matter what I tried (and I'm a big guy), the plastic stopper would not come out. I did everything short of getting my vice-grips. I was about to, and then thought, "This is a $6 bottle of cheap champagne. Hell with this--where's the Glenlivet?" Night turned out just fine.

title: A small bag full of crunchy chemicals
text: So, these are just not a quality wafer cookie. I've had good rolled wafers - these are not it. Honestly, the worst I have ever had. Tasted very much like food chemicals. Yuck. Hard pass.

title: Excellent flavor, ridiculously expensive
text: This is without a doubt one of the best-tasting frozen pizzas I have ever had. But at $10 for a tiny, individual frozen pizza, this is literally double the cost of a CPK frozen pizza - and its smaller. Very tasty, but like many AO products, grossly overpriced. 5 stars for flavor, 1 star for value = three stars.

title: Great, but pricey
text: Yes, this makes great M&C Spirals, but it is a lot more expensive than it should be. Seriously - it's double the price of boxed M&C, which makes three times the amount per box. Not worth it.

title: This isn't whiskey - it's cheap dessert liquor (and it's gross)
text:
As someone who appreciates quality scotch and whiskey, expectations were admittedly low going in. I usually avoid trendy frat-party booze (because it usually sucks - I mean have you tried birthday cake flavored vodka???), but people are raving about this stuff so I decided (against my better judgment) to pick up a bottle. This was mistake #1.

Mistake #2 was opening it and smelling it. I was hoping for something like a Reese's peanut butter cup, but sadly, nope. This stuff smells well, odd. The scent isn't really peanut butter or whiskey - just candy. Which brings us to mistake #3: drinking it. That weird smell is also how it tastes - like strange, gimmicky candy, maybe one of those weird, super-cheap holiday candies with the world's cheapest booze inside.

If I were to rate this the way you rate whiskeys, out of 100, this would be a 21 or 22 at the most. Yes, that bad. Ranking list sites on the internet generally don't even bother ranking anything below 60. This "whiskey" cannot be consumed neat, as the smell and aftertaste will make you lose your appetite for anything except toothpaste and mouthwash to get rid of it. It is as sweet as maple syrup. Yuck. The only way I can see this being palatable at all would be in a boozy adult milkshake. That's it.

Truly, monumentally bad. I cannot recommend this at all.

title: Nothing special - and the cap broke immediately :(
text: These dried chives are okay, not the greatest. They rehydrate quickly in liquid (eg. eggs), but the flavor is lacking. Fresh are obviously MUCH better, but other brands of dried chives are superior. These are also oddly expensive, especially for this quality. Sadly, in typical generic brand spices, the packaging is the cheapest possible bottle and cap. In this case the cap has a flip-top which broke the second time I opened it. I had to tape it shut, and resort to unscrewing the entire cap and pouring them out carefully. I will not buy these again. Overpriced, not great, and the ultra-cheap bottle broke.

title: Oddest Ranch ever
text: I am a fan of some other SK products (mayo, for example), and had high expectations for this. Sadly, the flavor is wonky. Tastes nothing like a traditional ranch, or even a commercial ranch. Just ...weird. Will not buy this again - and I only used it once. Tossed it.

title: Fine on the day after I ordered it. Rotted two days later.
text: Weird - this was not as fresh as one would hope. I used it the day after I got it, and it was fine, but a couple days later, it was browning and rotting, as though excess moisture had gotten inside the packaging - which it had not, at least not on my end. Disappointing.

title: Odd taste. Not like actual coffee...?
text: I do not know what to attribute this to, but this "coffee" has an odd flavor, definitely not like "normal" coffee. If you are looking for a clean, simple cold brew coffee, this is not it. I will not order this again. Not recommended. Yuck.

title: This ...did not end well.
text: Wow. I like other Quest products, and often have a Quest bar as a filling snack or after a workout for protein. I thought these cookies might be a smaller-serving alternative. While the size is right, the ingredients are not. Not only did I experience severe gastric distress after having one of these, but the taste, smell, and aftertaste was absolutely horrible. Truly unpleasant in every way. The after-effects lasted 12+ hours. I threw the rest away. Absolutely cannot recommend these. AVOID.

title: Decent pickles, very pricey
text: These are pretty decent. Not the best, but not bad. Certainly better than the mediocre kosher dill pickles you get from Vlassic, Claussen, etc. Still though, not what I was hoping for (trying to find something the equivalent of Strub's, which I cannot get here in the US). At this price, they had better be fantastic--and they were merely good, not great. Not worth 4x the price of Vlassic.

title: Moldy
text: There was already mold between several slices the first time I opened this package. Two days later I went back to have more and the entire thing was covered in mold. Threw it out. No bueno. :(

title: The #1 ingredient is maltitol
text: Caveat emptor: the #1 ingredient is these is maltitol. Do not consume these unless you are planning to remain within a ten-second sprint of a toilet for at least 4-6 hours. Seriously. I am not kidding. Google it. Maltitol should never have received FDA approval - it is that bad.

title: Good feta, overpriced
text: This is decent commercial feta (definitely not artisan-grade), but is good for salads. This tiny container is priced at about $1/oz. That's $16/lb--ridiculous.

title: Hit or miss
text: Most of the time these are pretty good, but the quality is definitely hit or miss. There have been times when the shallots I've received have been already old, and on occasion partially rotted. These are good about 70% of the time.

title: Seem to go soft very quickly.
text: Not sure what the deal is but these radishes seem to get soft very quickly. Much faster than other radishes I've purchased in the past. No idea why. It's odd. Going forwards I will wash them and place them in water to preserve them in the fridge.

title: Tasty, but watch out for expiration dates
text:
UPDATE: most recent order had only about 2 oz of tofu, still in pieces far too large for a salad.
---

This isn't bad. The tofu pieces are far too large, and I cut them in half. Plan to eat this within one day of receiving it though. I have ordered this a number of times, and twice I have received one which expired on the day it was delivered. Usually it is a day or two out, max. This does not keep well in the fridge, as the shelf life is extremely short. If I buy one, I now know I have to eat it within 24 hours or so. Once you get past this, it's pretty tasty. Bit of an identity confusion issue though in terms of the recipe: Vietnamese style noodle salad with thin vermicelli-style noodles (may be either egg or rice noodles, seems to randomly vary--depends on the day, apparently), shredded lettuce, carrots and daikon, a Thai satay dressing, and Chinese-style sesame snaps for crunch. I like it though.

title: Not enough strawberries or whipped cream
text: While this is a decent cake, it is lacking in both the strawberries and cream departments. There seems to be 2-3 thin slices of strawberry inside each slice, about the equivalent of one strawberry, plus the another 1/3 strawberry on top. That's it. There is a very thin layer of whipped cream between the layers and a thin layer on top. The cake itself is actually quite good. It just lacks sufficient toppings. When I make strawberry shortcake, there are LOTS of sliced strawberries and tons of whipped cream. Strawberry shortcake it is an indulgence, and should be served as such. This is simply a conservative interpretation. Also, I suggest ordering an extra slice or two - the slices I got were not the same size, and one was turned into parfait by being jostled in the process of getting here.

title: These taste like chemicals...
text: So, this is not really what I was hoping for. They just don't taste real at all--just a mixture of chemicals and artificial flavors. Disappointing.

title: Definitely NOT the real thing, and stupidly expensive
text:
I grew up within an hour or two of dairy farm country, and cheese curds were a fun snack growing up. Real cheese curds that is: chewy, rubbery, flavorful, fresh, and yes, "squeaky". These are literally none of these things, and mostly just taste like oddly shaped lumps of cheese. Very disappointing, especially for the absurdly high price of $6.99 for 6 oz. That's $1.17/oz, which = $18.72/lb. Um, what??

If you are looking for truly good cheese curds, keep looking.

title: One of the better MC entrees
text: MC has gone downhill in recent years. Once upon a time, you could count on MC for a delicious frozen meal. I ate my way through my first startup on their frozen meals in the 1990s. times have changed. Nothing they sell these days is anywhere near as good as the old days. This is one of the more palatable dishes, and it isn't great. Needs to have higher-quality meat (fewer chewy bits, please), and be about 30% larger. 3 stars.

title: Almost impossible to make without it falling apart in microwave
text: While these are certainly cost effective, they aren't great. A mass-produced frozen burrito = barely even meh in the best of circumstances. I have a 1000W microwave with a rotating turntable. The recommended 90 seconds on high results in a split burrito 9/10 times. a good way to prevent this is to remove it from the packaging, poke a couple small vent holes in it, and reinsert it in the package for microwaving. The package should recommend this, but it does not.

title: Almost, but not quite, entirely unlike real guacamole
text: This definitely isn't real guacamole. I ate a bit of it and then got very sick of it. Just not very good. Tastes processed. I guess I'm spoiled by having had plenty of fresh guacamole. If you like the real thing, don't bother.

title: Open bag. Threw them out.
text: Bag was open upon arrival. Tossed.

title: You know those soft, artist's pencil erasers you knead in your hand to clean? Like that, with sauce.
text:
Completely unpalatable. Would not serve this to a wild coyote (and they'll eat anything). You know those soft, light gray pencil erasers you knead in your hand to clean, and when you stretch them, they get light and airy? This is like that, with sauce. Not even kidding. If you buy this, think of that image while chewing on one of the chicken gumballs (for lack of a better word) for a while--and I assure you it will be a WHILE. The texture of these things falls somewhere between bubble gum, erasers and marshmallows. And they taste like, well, nothing really, with a faint hint of latex, perhaps (might be the bag you microwave it in--which melts!). Yes, this is that bad. Truly an extremely unpleasant thing to put in your mouth. As I chewed the first one up (took a few minutes--they do not break down the way actual FOOD does when you chew it), I could not help but wonder if this would digest properly. I felt like I was eating something from art class, and when I swallowed it, I felt like I had swallowed my chewing gum or something. Absolutely disgusting.

This is *not* food.

Make sure you read the instructions closely--there is a second bag within the outer bag. Unlike most entrees you heat up in right the packaging, you have to first remove the inner bag from the outer bag. Not sure why they go to the trouble of double-bagging, but this seems misleading (it looks like a larger portion than what is actually in the bag) is not environmentally friendly, and can be confusing--read the instructions closely if you still want to give this a try. Flavor: 0/10, texture: -1/10, packaging 0/10.

Oh, and please note the microwave instructions are simply wrong. This was delivered frozen from Whole Foods via Amazon, but I am not sure it is actually meant to be frozen. Following the microwave directions means you are giving this less than half the amount of time actually required to heat up properly. I had to put it in for another two minutes to get it hot enough to serve (it was still partially frozen after following the directions--and I have a 1100w microwave), which made part of the inner bag melt. Really not cool. Pretty sure the end result is a lot of free radicals in your dinner. I threw it out after 2 bites. I absolutely do NOT recommend this product. It was disappointing on every level--just terrible.

title: Inedible, and might have made me sick
text: I bought three frozen entrees from this brand. This was the first I tried. Absolutely disgusting. The sauce was really just not good at all, and the "chicken" was like eating erasers. Also, make sure you read the instructions closely: there is a bag *within* the bag. Unlike many entrees you heat up in the packaging, for this brand, you have to first remove the inner bag from the outer bag. Not sure why they go to the trouble of double-bagging (nobody else does), but this is not environmentally friendly, and can be confusing. Read the instructions closely. Cannot recommend--gross.

title: I might be spoiled but... meh
text: For a while now, I have been buying premium ice creams (HD, B&J, etc.). As I love Kit-Kat, this was intriguing, so I bought it. Disappointing on every level. Not only are there hardly any Kit-Kat bits in it, they don't really taste the same somehow, and the ice cream itself is totally sub-par ice cream. I will not buy this again. Back to Hagen Dazs. I go.

title: Tasteless - literally no flavor
text: These look like apple fritters. They kind of smell like apple fritters. But they really are not apple fritters. They are just  bland, plain fritters with a few bits of apple thrown in here and there. What really prompted me to write this review is the fact that, oddly, they have no real flavor--they are just very, very sweet. Tons of sugar, but no actual flavor. I won't be buying these again. They are also slightly too thick for proper apple fritters. This could be overlooked if they were tasty, but they just are not. Eating these just feels like eating a giant pile of dough and sugar. Gross.

title: Fish was spoiled. Threw it out. Made my house stink for hours.
text: Within 10 minutes of the start of cooking, my house started to smell like something died in it. This fish was bad. Rotten. Like it had been defrosted long ago, sat out for a day or two and refrozen. Rancid. I had to open all my windows and turn all the fans to get the smell out of my house. Not sure if it's the product or the logistics involved in getting it to me, but these were a total failure. I will absolutely not be buying them again.

title: Wow, this is *revolting*
text: I am trying to get away from dairy. This is proving to be surprisingly hard to do. There a lot of dairy-free alternative products out there claiming to be as good as or "better than" the dairy alternative. I am yet to find even one that lives up to the hype. This product certainly does not. It is only useful in one capacity: straight from the fridge (cold) on untoasted bread. That's it. As soon as you apply heat to this product (i.e. spread it on anything toasted, or cook with it), it reverts back into its liquid oil state and becomes completely unpalatable. Seriously--it is disgusting. I threw it out. I have had so little success with dairy-alternative products I am considering going back to having regular butters and cheeses, because the vegan alternatives are just so pathetic. I cannot imagine how anyone could give this product a 5-star rating. It is truly revolting.

title: Watch out: contains milk/butter (not vegan)
text: If you can't have dairy, avoid this. It is good soup, but it contains butter/milk.

title: Truly vile. Tastes nothing like eggs; literally made me sick to my stomach. Caveat emptor.
text:
Expectations were high for this product, based upon other's reviews and the videos in which they have people on the street tasting it and proclaiming it either indistinguishable from, or even better than normal eggs. Those videos are obviously works of fiction. This product is not even remotely close to eggs in anything but color.

Texture: cardboard boxes pureed with canola oil, tapioca, and preservatives. Flavor: somewhere between cardboard and a dish cloth. Yes, really--this was absolutely disgusting. There is no WAY those videos are real. Absolutely impossible. This product was revolting (a strong word, I know, but it is accurate).

I ordered two bottles. The first bottle seemed to cook up properly with onions and herbs de Provence, but it was barely palatable--truly gross. It also produced mild nausea which lasted about two hours. I figured I should use it up, so against my better judgment, I opened the second bottle a few days later. The second bottle was different - no matter how much I shook it, it seemed significantly thicker than the first, definitely not indicative of consistent product quality. This time, I added it to some cooked Soyrizo (soy-based chorizo; fantastic stuff which tastes just like chorizo), and the result was inedible (I have made Soyriozo and eggs countless times--one of my favorite breakfasts). I threw it away after eating about half of it. It tasted like wet cardboard with Soyrizo. Within 45 minutes, I was ill, throwing up. I think the JUST Egg had possibly spoiled, well before the best by date.

Conclusion: this was a failed experiment, and ultimately, a gastric nightmare. And no, it has nothing to do with mung beans--I know I can eat them. As for the videos, this feels like false advertising. Anyone who claims this is indistinguishable from eggs is lying. I also have some of the frozen pre-made stuff I bought at the same time, which I have not used. I will likely toss it. This was both a waste of money and a terrible gastric experience. I will never buy this again. Yuck. Caveat emptor.

title: Almost no flavor at all
text: Mediocreation Asian pear. Very juicy, but almost tasteless.

title: Some things just should not be attempted
text: I am in the process of going vegan. This is an attempt to make a plant-based meat alternative passable. Nope--total failure. Not appetizing in the least. Will not be buying this again.

title: Watch out for the sugar alcohols in these - nasty
text: These contain Maltitol, the sugar alcohol which I am told is the least-well tolerated. I must agree. I seem to be fine with other types, but these make my stomach hurt and feel gassy and terrible. This is the first time I have experienced this with a protein bar. Natural sugars are far better than this particularly nasty stuff. Would give this zero stars if I could for ruining my day, twice (I gave it another chance, thinking it might have been something else, but the second time I ate this and nothing else to check, and that was definitely not a good day).

title: This is passable --not bad considering it's vegan
text: I am new to vegan life and this is a passable alternative to traditional corn bread. Still has a lot of oil in it though. Need to find a way to reduce that...

title: A decent avocado, but overpriced
text: The price of avocados fluctuates seasonally. This purchase seemed to be higher than it should be.

title: Disappointing
text: This steak was far too thin to be useful. I understand is is a strip steak, but this one was only about 1cm thick, maybe 11mm, making it difficult to cook it properly. Also, at this price, I could have had a proper NY. Next time I will. Overpriced and disappointing.

title: Broken box seal
text: First of all, this tea is delicious. This is not an issue. However, the box was shipped in a paper envelope and was crushed. The box seal was broken when it arrived. Replacement was ordered, but the original order is apparently ineligible for a return. It was shipped and sold by Amazon, crushed in shipping, but a replacement has to come out of my pocket? Not cool.

title: Very expensive and very good
text: This is very good butter. It's also incredibly expensive. This company's milk is several dollars more than competitors, but absolutely worth it. I can't say the same for the butter. It's very good, but I don't believe it's worth $10/lb. I have also had better butter than this that costs slightly less.

title: Thick? Noooo.....
text: This is NOT thick cut at all. Literally paper-thin. I don't think they could have cut it thinner if they had tried to. There is nothing thick about this bacon--packaging and product name is very misleading. Flavor is also not great--very mild.

title: Very pale yolks, also overcooked and watch out for bits of shell
text: The yolks in these are so pale they are nearly white--the color of cheap butter. This means the chickens which laid these eggs were fed a mix of dead chickens and corn, a common practice in factory farming which produces unhealthy chickens who lay flavorless, pale eggs. Pick up some organic, vegetarian-fed, free range eggs and look at the color of the yolks. Healthy chickens lay eggs with dark yellow yolks. Why this costs more to the consumer is a mystery--chickens were eating natural vegetarian feed for centuries until factory farming came along. Those who still do lay great eggs. These are not the eggs you will find in this package. These are cheap factory-farmed eggs of the lowest grade, and are completely tasteless. Also, they were very overcooked and were hard and rubbery. Occasional bits of shell still on them, too. Not buying these again.

title: These taste like my childhood
text: Discovered these quite by accident a year ago. The grape side tastes just like a grape popsicle from the 70s & 80s. The other side is a soothing cool mint, which is nice, but I would be even happier if the whole thing was just the grape stuff. I love the little hockey puck packaging, but in this day and age it needs to not be plastic (i.e. not biodegradable).

title: Was not great at $10. Definitely not worth it at $13.
text:
Originally (2 months ago), this quiche was $9.99. It was semi-decent, definitely not great. The primary issue is the chopped ham: it is indiscriminately added, without regard for whether it is edible or not. LOTS of gristly/chewy/fatty pieces you have to pick out, as they are inedible. This is 100% unacceptable in a quiche. Lost two stars for this. Knocked off another star for the recent 30% price increase. At that price, it is definitely not worth it. I will not be buying this again until the price comes back down, and even then, if the ham is not higher quality next time, that would be the last time.

UPDATE 1-2022: They have changed something in this. It no longer cooks properly. Tried two different ovens, same thing.

title: A better cut than store brands
text: With Amazon Fresh, your choices for fresh chicken breasts are this, or the Amazon generic brand. I have tried the generic brand. This is a far superior chicken breast. The generic has that white piece of tendon running through the breast, meaning you either have to remove it yourself before cooking, or after. Either way, it's very unpleasant to encounter. Foster farms however, removes it. This is a go-to product for me now.

title: A great value for a decent Cajun spice
text: I have been using this seasoning for years. It's not as good as Emeril's essence, but it costs 75% less, and is still very good. Add a couple shakes of a good Louisiana hot sauce and you're good to go.

title: Absolutely delicious
text: This is an absolutely delicious, full flavored olive oil. Very robust. Makes excellent salads and goes well on anything. If you like a full-flavored olive oil, this is the stuff. This comes in a plastic bottle which can be recycled.

title: Overpriced, expires within 24 hours
text: I like this little side salad quite a bit. You could even add some protein and make it into a small lunch. Unfortunately, the expiration date is usually within a day of delivery through Amazon Fresh. I have also found the greens occasionally wilted before the expiration date. For what you get, this is overpriced. This should be a $3 salad, not a $5 salad. There's no protein here, just a tiny bit of cheese, dressing, pepitas, and greens. If this were at Trader Joe's it would be $3.50, (and would be higher quality).

title: This is the real deal. Your search is over.
text: This is the top rated Louisiana style hot sauce. It is so much better than anything else on the market, I don't see why anyone else even bothers trying to make a hot sauce to compete with this. Absolutely delicious. Unfortunately it's also more expensive on Amazon than it should be. Regardless, it's the only Louisiana-style hot sauce I use for everything Cajun.

title: Not a quality quiche
text: More care needs to go into the ingredients. In every other bite there are inedible bits of "ham" which should have never been included in the pie. You dice up quality cuts of thick bacon or ham to make a good quiche Lorraine. This is not the case here - the whole ham seems to have gone in, fat, gristle, and all. Yuck. This brand is clearly not interested in quality. Not recommended. (Also, make your own --it's super-easy if you use a frozen pie crust.)

title: Spoils the day it's opened
text:
Literally bad the day after I received it. Terrible. I won't be ordering this anymore. I will be going back to better brands. A disappointment. Amazon needs to rethink their vendor for this product.

Spoils immediately upon opening. I opened this up the day after I got it. 6 hours later, I went to have more, and it was already spoiled. Well before the date on the bottle. Terrible.

title: Not hot and just not tasty - DIY instead
text: Good bean dip is savory and delicious, typically made with pork and spices. This was just ...paste. Refried beans with some faint flavors added in, but just not something I wanted to eat. I had a small amount of it and threw it out. Do yourself a favor - make your own bean dip.  It's a snap: fry up some pork chorizo (recommended), and/or finely diced bacon. When fully cooked, add a can of refried beans in with some tapatio or cholula to taste, stirring the whole works together thoroughly. Let it cool and refrigerate what you don't eat. Delicious. VASTLY superior to this product.

title: Exploded in microwave
text: I followed the instructions to the letter, and this exploded in my microwave well before it was done. And no, I do not have a super-powerful microwave. It completely disassembled itself during cooking. I had a nice mess to clean up. Oh, and no lunch. I nuke a lot of burritos. Sometimes they split or crack. This was way beyond--a genuine explosion. Kaboom! Not recommended.

title: Not a substitute for the brand name peaches I would normally buy
text: There is nothing about these peaches which was tasty or good. They were sour, not sweet, and may even have been spoiled (although they smelled fine). Oddly, there were a few odd dark bits in the can, which seem to have been pieces of peach peel, and they tasted awful. Some pieces of peach were not peeled well, and had patches of peel/skin still attached. I will not be buying these again, and will likely avoid other canned fruit from the same brand. Definitely not the equivalent of the name brand canned fruit I would normally purchase.

text: I used to be able to buy a chili and corn bread entree form MC which was genuinely delicious. It had two bags of chili and a small loaf of corn bread. I cannot find it any more and have not been able to for some time. I got excited when I saw this item, and ordered it. Sadly, this is not even close. Not the same chili, not the same corn bread. This was mediocre, at best, and is reflective of the decline of MC products in recent years. They used to make the best frozen meals you could get. Not any more. :(

text: Most Indian places have their own version of basic chicken curry. This actually tasted a lot like what you might get from a moderately good Indian restaurant in California. I liked the saffron rice, which is a change from what you usually see with packaged Indian food (usually white jasmine). I would buy this again, and more often if it were priced reasonably at about $6, instead of $8. I wonder if it freezes well?

text: I love these. A decent high-protein snack. I wish they were a bit healthier (3g of sat fat, but that's what I get for eating meat, and a lot of sodium), but they are perfect to take with you instead of something with more sugar and less protein, such as a granola bar. This particular flavor (BBQ pork & pineapple) is awesome.

title: Sure would be nice if these were consistent
text: Buying bananas sight-unseen seems like a risky proposition at best, and rightly so. You have no way of knowing how ripe the bananas you get will be when you buy this item. I have bought these repeatedly, and have received bananas ranging from a dark avocado green (and VERY unripe) to speckled yellow and already fully ripe. Size varies a lot, and sometimes they are 5", and other times they are 8". I wish they were more consistent in both areas. Also, they sometimes arrive bruised, depending upon what else they put in the bag with the bananas. Once got a bag with bananas in the bottom and a half dozen yogurt cups, a jar of peanut butter, and a can of tomatoes on top of the bananas. You can imagine the result.

title: These seem to spoil very quickly
text: For some reason, these do not last long in the fridge--other bell peppers purchased elsewhere have typically lasted about twice as long. These are nothing special, merely a slightly-below-average bell pepper.

title: Very tasty most of the time
text: Once in a while I will get a pack of this which was cut from an unripe or male watermelon, and is not as sweet, but most of the time, this is delicious. I wish the pieces were slightly smaller and more consistent, but anyone who has cut watermelon knows this is no easy task to accomplish. Strangely, when I purchased the larger size of this same item, it went bad very quickly. These smaller ones are good until the best by date on the label, after which they do go south rapidly.

text: This was a pleasant surprise. I like trail mix, and while this one has a few too many peanuts for my taste, it is quite good. Real M&Ms too! A great value.

text: Amy's Organics products are usually quite good, and this is no exception. It is not the best vegetarian chili I've ever had (TJ's), but it is very good. 4 solid stars for flavor, although at "medium", I could barely feel any heat at all. The real problem here is that for the price of a can of this, you can get two cans of most other brands of vegetarian chili. And this is consistent with this brand's other products, which tend to be 30-50% more expensive than competing products. If this were $1.75 I would buy it all the time.

title: The perfect thing for a hot summer afternoon!
text: These are delicious! Very sweet and sticky though, so try not to spill. Strong authentic lemon flavor, and very cold. If you want to eat one straight out of the freezer, I suggest microwaving it for 10-15 seconds, which will help soften it up enough that it can be eaten more easily. title: Surprisingly tasty for the price
text: I fully expected this sauce to be terrible. I mean, it's $2. How good can it possibly be? I was pleasantly surprised, however, to find it was significantly better than other sauces costing double. I use it primarily for Hawaiian-style fried rice (bbq pork or ham fried rice + a small amount of bbq sauce), and for this it is good, if not authentic (actual Hawiian BBQ sauce is harder to find and a lot more expensive). It also works well on chicken. Again, a very good value for the money.

title: I don't know why I keep hoping Eggo waffles will one day be good
text:
I love waffles. I grew up with my dad making them on Sunday mornings every week like clockwork throughout my childhood. I have his recipe (unbeatable, and I've tried), and I have two fantastic waffle irons, one antique like his, and another modern, high-end one. Both truly make fantastic waffles. Thing is, it's a hassle and a mess to make proper waffles. You have to use multiple mixing bowls and measuring cops, get flour everywhere sifting, and then fold the egg whites in after beating them to soft peaks right before you pour the batter into the waffle iron. This works--well. I am just too lazy for it sometimes. Also, the racket of the mixer beating the egg whites is perhaps better enjoyed post-coffee.

Hence the foray into the world of frozen waffles. I've tried a lot of them, and none of them are anything like real waffles--seriously, not even close. Oddly those weird Kodiak Cakes seem to be the best frozen waffles out there to my taste, even though they are high-protein (6g/ea). I gave up on Eggo waffles long ago, as they really have nothing to do with actual waffles. They are almost a different food, definitely very Americanized. The US food industry (P&G, etc) seems to do that--take a good food and "Americanize" it into something ultra-cheap to produce which ends up being almost unrecognizable, far from authentic. Somehow I had a hope that this might be better as they were a specialty product. Nope, same batter, just poured (no doubt by the ton) into a slightly different machine designed to make a slightly taller waffle. Tossed them after the first two.

Good thing they are ultra-cheap. Lesson finally learned, perhaps.

text: Oops, I spelled expensive wrong. I meant this is very EXPENSIVE cheesecake. Yes, it is good, but at three normalish slices per cake, each slice costs almost $6. WAY too much for a frozen dessert. Lost 2 stars because this is a tiny cheesecake for $17.

title: And noooow I remember why I don't like pretzel sticks
text: These, like many pretzel sticks, don't really taste like pretzels at all, just tasteless sticks with salt. Only Rold Gold actually seem to have that "slightly sour" taste. These are just not good.

title: Packaging is terrible - the plastic bag tore when opening and the zip closure does not work
text: This is a decent rice--the flavor is fine, and it cooks well using the 2:1/10+20 method. That said, it is not the fantastic basmati rice I had hoped for after reading other's reviews; the grain is also not as long as expected. While the rice itself is decent, the packaging is another story: it is truly terrible. It is in a hard/inflexible plastic bag which tore while opening. The seal has to be cut to open the bag, which creates the the potential to cut/tear the bag due to the way it is (very thoroughly) sealed. I was very careful, and it did not tear in the initial opening, but the opening at the seal is so small you cannot even get a 1-cup scoop into it, so I (very gently) attempted to open it further. Unfortunately, at that point the bag did tear, despite my best effort to be careful. Also, the zip closure at the top of the bag simply will not stay on the bag--it is useless. I am now in search of some sort of non-ugly container to move the rice into as the bag is garbage. As well, the price ($26) was very high, but did include shipping. I am frustrated and disappointed with this purchase, and am not likely to buy this brand of rice again. I will instead look for basmati in the kind of packaging I have purchased many times before, one I know is more durable: a flexible plastic bag inside a burlap bag. It seems like this failure occurred because the company was trying to answer a question no one was actually asking. Why use such a strange package? Stick to what everyone else uses to package their rice--it works.

title: What happened to Marie Calendars?
text: This was a major disappointment. It was very small and while the mac and cheese was almost palatable, there was not enough of it, and the chicken definitely wasn't. It was like eating erasers--rubber (and there was not enough of that either). I guess I was spoiled by eating TJ's frozen food for a decade before the apocalypse. Now, I eat whatever I can get delivered. This was a zero-stars item. MC used to make good stuff (remember the chili and cornbread?). They have apparently lost their way.

title: Not entirely unlike cheesecake, but not quite cheesecake.
text: This sort of looks like cheesecake, and is a decent attempt for a purely vegan product, but is definitely not cheesecake. You know when you go to those cheesy buffet restaurants and they have those little cubes of "cheesecake" on the dessert table? You know how those are basically nothing like cheesecake? Yeah, this is like that. It's sort of a facsimile of cheesecake, which looks like cheesecake but is most definitely not cheesecake. As long as you don't expect cheesecake going in, you'll be fine. I was hoping for something a little more satisfying. Disappointing, and I will not buy this very synthetic-tasting product again. The texture was closer to Greek yogurt than cheesecake.

text: I keep wanting to like this company's food. It always sounds so good. And I keep regretting every purchase. I think I'm done with Hormel. This was gross--and SO much sodium. Never again.

text: These are tiny little packets. And I mean tiny. So small--you will need 3-4 of them for a decent snack. also, if you like thicker cuts of jerky, you won't generally find those in here. Small, thin bits only. I will not be buying these again. Not worth it.

title: A neat idea, but they really need to work on the chili...
text: I remember liking these years ago. What was I thinking? They are just gross. I warmed them up and slathered them with salsa and sour cream and still--not tasty. I suspect these need to be baked into a casserole with cheese and then covered in sour cream, salsa, and guacamole to make them palatable. In other words, why bother? I think it may be the chili which ruins them. Hormel chili is pretty revolting--the absolute bottom rung of the ladder of chilis--so just imagine that squeezed into skinny little mini tamales with a watery pseudo-ranchero sauce. These have little in common with actual tamales, which are delicious. These are a last-resort meal only. Kept in the cupboard for when you run out of literally everything else.

title: The right product, but smaller packets seem to contain less Splenda than others
text: At Starbucks or anywhere else I need only one packet of Splenda in my coffee. For some reason, I need two of these--they appear to contain about half as much as the Splenda packets you get elsewhere. It seems odd, I know, but these packets do seem to contain less sweetening ability than the Splenda packets you get at Costco for restaurant use. This means the price is not good at all--I am going through it twice as quickly.

title: Broke in shipping--not the kernels you're looking for.
text: OR popcorn has always been the gold standard. It costs more, but it has always been an excellent popping corn. I am a lifelong popcorn fanatic, and it has been my go-to snack of choice for over 40 years. OR is typically the bar against which I compare all other popcorns. This order was disappointing. There are two problems. First, it arrived broken in the box, with popcorn kernels everywhere. They just wasn't any packing material at all, so it rattled around inside the box and the container broke. Second, I'm not sure what the story is with this batch, but it was different from other OR popcorn I have had in the past. The flavor and crunchiness was actually right on, this was definitely the right product, but the kernels were significantly smaller than usual, and a much larger percentage remained unpopped. Like 10 times more than usual. Seriously. I think the smaller kernels made it more difficult for the hot air to move around between the kernels. I don't think this heated as well or as efficiently. For whatever reason, a lot of these just didn't pop. The flavor was excellent, but the higher volume of unpopped kernels makes me wonder. The price on this order was significantly lower than it has been in the past though, so that is oddly suspicious as well.

I’ve been buying Evian on Amazon and the prices have fluctuated greatly. The last carton I got was so wet because one of the bottles was punctured and it had to be done before they put it in the outer box because the outer box was fine.

title: A TASTY TREAT
text: I have always been a big fan of macadamia nuts  but the Mauna Loa brand is by far the best around.  They are always fresh, buttery tasting and salty..but not too much.  They possess that little crunch that turns into a melt in your mouth flavor and leads you to reach for one after another!  Beware..they are high in calories and they do cost somewhat dearly.  I have found that buying these 3 packs is quite cost effective and seem to last quite a while as I keep them hidden away.  For those of you that like to keep these lovely tasting nuts on hand, please know that placing them in freezer proof bags and storing them in the freezer will keep them fresh for at least a year if you wish to hold onto them for that long. text:

title: Rice is nice
text:
I learned a little bit about rice recently as I am learning to make sushi (I wouldn't use this to make sushi because it's not the right type of grain) but I started to check the grain quality and couldn't find issues with broken or rough grains of rice. This is a bit outside of the norm for a pour and go setup that rice normally is, BUT after learning the craft I figured I'd share that bit.
Jasmine rice is amazing and soft and is the perfect rice for a base for adding vegetables for a stir fry or just a little bit of butter and salt on top for a nice relaxing meal.

title: Lower calories, not lower flavor
text: These are awesome! So, my wife and I love morning coffee and I'd figure the majority of parents would say the same. We love having coffee time with the kids by using these and giving them to the kids for our morning coffee time. The reduced calories doesn't cause issues with reduced flavor. The kids love them and if you have issue with someone not thinking they are as sweet, you can always use the more concentrated flavor by selecting the smaller cup option on the Keurig. Really enjoyed these and yes I tried them and enjoyed it as well (though hot cocoa isn't really my thing, it's nice on occasion, especially to share time with the kids).

title: 1 out of 4?
text:

title: Carnation ftw!
text:
I remember using the packets as a kid and when I saw these in liquid form I had to pick them up for my kids. There is a decent bit of sugar per bottle, but there is also a decent helping of protein in the bottle. My kids love the flavor and are excited to drink it when offered. Due to the sugar, we try to make sure it's reserved as a treat rather than a daily habit. The flavor is smooth and rich and doesn't have the chalky aftertaste that would come from the packets. The amount of preservatives is expected given these products are on a shelf and don't require refrigeration. The cost would definitely increase if they were constantly needing refrigeration. We toss in a 6 pack a day before we want to give them to the kids so they are ice cold when ready.
Excellent!

title: Great salt!
text: I really enjoy this one being added to my dishes I'm making as it really helps further the healthy benefits of the food prepared. I am not overly conscious of my salt intake as I workout almost daily for around an hour and the salt becomes a bit more essential. However, that is not the case for all so I really like using this (plus sea salt has a much better taste in dishes) and it just adds the right pop of flavor. I would like it in a different container that has a spout as sealing the bag is somewhat difficult but I didn't think that was worth less stars.

title: Interesting
text:
These arrived yesterday and I had to dive in. Chicken breast chips? Yes.
The chips are in between a kettle chip and standard potato chip. They are a bit more stiff and flat so they don't have any air pocket spots you might see on a potato chip.
The concept just seems weird because it does look a bit odd and maybe because it's a newer concept.
The flavor is fantastic and it's similar to some of the crumbles that would fall off fried chicken (just without as much grease).
I thoroughly enjoyed these and found the bag size to be more than enough for one person. I am usually a big eater so the snack bags don't cut it. These are actually decent sized bags (like the bags of doritos in the store that would cost about $1.50).
Great work here!

title: The right amount of most
text:
I figured the right amount of most would be the best headline here because the product has the right blend of most ingredients. The goal is plant based and eggs aren't plants so the traditional way of making mayo was out the door. Usually avocado tends to have that replacement creaminess since it is also an item that is rich in fat content. That is really that slightly altered texture here that doesn't make this a miss, it's just slightly different than anticipated. The bonus is that it makes for a much better mix-in for adding softened cream cheese to make it a veggie dip OR a slight addition of cream cheese to make it a tortilla chip dip.
I do really enjoy this product, just had to note the above for reasonable expectations.

The nutrition profile is solid and it is very easy to drink. It is smooth enough that you could easily chug this to get in a quick meal replacement if you are on the go. Some ready to drink items are thick and hard to get down quick.

title: Tasty
text:

The added vitamin boost is a nice touch though I don’t know if heat would degrade those ingredients.

In any case I thoroughly enjoyed the smooth flavor and hopefully the vitamins help during these cold Michigan months.

title: Smooth taste
text:
There is going to be a big difference between coffee and tea coming from a pot or bag versus Keurig pods. That is very important to note for those that may be buying a Keurig and then their favorite cup of tea. All pods tend to be slightly more watery than their traditional brew method counterparts.

The flavor here was good overall with a smooth taste. I did notice some of the ground tea leaves did make it into my cup but not much at all. I do like that there was no issue with a bitter flavor which can occur when using single use bags since excess heat tends to extract a bitter flavor. This pour over/pass through style that is offered by a Keurig makes it just right.

title: These are the HOTTEST noodles for the Hottest Ramen Challenge
text:
[[VIDEOID:44f0a5913dd6c8326f0e42b28aa31bca]] The noodles are what does show up for the hottest ramen challenge and that's why I bought them. The flavor is pretty decent, and the sauce packet is actually sauce. Ramen seems to come with a dry flavor pack, which this one does have a dry flavor pack (it has nori bits and some sesame) however the sauce packet is liquid. It looks like a dark blood color which is representative of the feeling you have when you are about to eat spicy ramen.

In terms of the heat, it was hot, but not too hot. I'd put it in the "fire" category for a hot wings place (like B dubs). However, the heat wasn't tolerable and didn't kick in too much for the first few bites. It does get hotter though and overall I was still pleased with the flavor.

A lot of people seemed to mention the smell, but it wasn't too pungent and seemed to be a bit exaggerated in the videos I saw before I completed mine. Overall, it wasn't too bad, though instant noodles aren't something I'd recommend.

title: Great waffles
text:
[[VIDEOID:d700ff19c73e769906245343d0c43313]] The profile and ingredients really made me think these would be quite dry, but they were not. My only issue is that these did stick to my waffle maker on my first waffle. It did get MUCH better after that though as I knew I needed to cook them longer.

These do have more of a bread-like feel and texture versus the more crisp/fried-like taste that is more noticeable with a traditional waffle. The ingredient profile definitely flavors FlapJacked though and the carrot spice flavor was excellent.

I would definitely recommend these and have purchased again.

title: Hottest Beef Jerky Challenge
text:
[[VIDEOID:795c06b5f7d4da62b3949e8fb481db6a]] The beef jerky comes in solid pieces versus a bunch of little chunks. If you were to thinly slice beef to make a steak sandwich, you'd get pieces like that.

The flavor was good and the heat had a building effect. It wasn't incredibly apparent which made it tolerable at first. Toward the end it got hot and I could feel my eyes starting to turn a little red from the heat as well as the sweat starting to bead.

I got this for the Hottest Jerky Challenge (on my youtube channel and posted in video review above), so I was prepared for the worst but was pleasantly surprised in the end. It was definitely hot but nothing that consistent spoonfuls of ice cream didn't take care of after awhile.

My wife is not much of a protein bars/foods type person and she ate a few but wasn't interested in the whole bag.
I have purchased several of these now and have enjoyed them.
The sweeter flavors could use a bit more sweetness and flavoring overall.
The savory flavors do need a little more consistency with flavoring (some have a good deal of coating whereas others are light in coating).
Would I buy again? Yes I would and yes I have.
I've bought the savory flavors again, not the sweet flavor (cookies and cream was my specific sweet flavor I purchased before but not again). It just needs some tweaks and would be good to go again, in my opinion.

title: Short of beans this is perfect for my 20-bar espresso machine
text: The only thing better than this ground espresso would be grinding beans myself. Honestly, I tried that and cannot achieve the consistency of the grind in a repeatable fashion.  However, this is fresh, expertly roasted (to my taste) and products a perfect shot from my Gevi 20-bar machine. I do have a secret ingredient that makes this so perfect: I buy Aqua Panna bottled water by the case and use it exclusively for espresso making. That and correctly tamping down the ground and using a decent machine and you are guaranteed a perfect shot every time.

title: Packed with flavor
text:
I purchase mine locally. It has enough heat to keep you interested if you love spicing up your dishes. I would put this is the same class as most of the Caribbean sauces made from scotch bonnets. To be sure the flavor profile is different between those and this, but the heat factor is roughly the same.

For me this is much more flavorful than most of the Caribbean sauces, and this has a different texture since it's a paste. I use it mostly as a multi-purpose condiment for Thai and even Mexican dishes, as well as soups of any kind (canned or home made.) Oh, and for beans this adds an amazing punch and burst of flavor.

If you love spiciness and dishes that benefit from a squeeze of fresh lime (or any citrus actually) you will love this paste.

title: This is THE rice for risotto!
text: I switched from aborio rice to carnaroli about a year ago. This rice grain cooks faster, absorbs more and is much creamier. I've tried a few different brands and they all seem to be equal. I now decide which brand based on price - and I have not been disappointed with any brand that I have tried. One other thing - not only is the cooking time faster, but the tedious job of adding stock, stirring and adding some more is less tedious. I add a lot more stock, stir and wait until the grains have absorbed, then add more stock and repeat the process. The results are impressive!

title: The real thing
text: Mine arrived in time for a dinner party, so I served it with a baguette. I had an opportunity to taste it and it's every bit as authentic as the nduja I had in Italy. It's mildly spicy, and has a complex flavor profile, I loved the that it spreads easily, and the fact that my six guests gobbled one of these up in about fifteen minutes and asked for more speaks for the quality and taste. As for how long it will keep, I have no idea. I will probably be ordering another one in the near future solely for my consumption and will discover the answer to that.

title: Passed the ice cream test - excellent for a sub 25 year Modena
text:
This is not going to compete with a 25 (or more) year Modena Balsamic, but is also isn't going to set you back nearly as much. It does pass the vanilla ice cream and the strawberry tests, and that earns it five stars in my book. It's the real thing!

I purchased this to give my wife a taste of real Balsamic vinegar, and she was blown away. She said this was the first time she put balsamic vinegar on ice cream. I corrected her: it was the first time she ever tasted the real thing as well as trying in on ice cream.

Everything from the viscosity to the complex flavor make this worthwhile. I now have an excuse to purchase a 25 year old bottle (at a lot more, but life is short.) If you are on a budget, but still have expensive tastes this is a perfect Modena Balsamic. If this is your first exposure, it's the perfect gateway to the more expensive habits.

title: Nice bite and packed with flavor
text:
I am of Calabrese descent so I had to try this. I previously purchased a jar of this brand's crushed chili peppers and loved the flavor, although the bite was milder than I expected. This one has a much simpler flavor profile, a nice bite and rich flavor considering how few ingredients there are.

Although I am not wild about the price this has become something of an addiction for me. I mainly use it on non-Italian dishes such as rice and beans, gumbos, stews and the such. It adds a lot of interesting flavor with just a few drops when cooking (and I am careful to use just enough to add to the flavor profile without making dishes too spicy for my guests.) Of course, it also adds to some Italian dishes. I love it with polenta topped with a meaty stew, and a few drops as a finish on pasta ascuita is perfect. I have also used this as a finishing oil (along with red palm oil) on a Brazilian fish stew called moqueca. Perfect results. It's also great for curry dishes (both Caribbean and West Asian), and is one of my favorite condiments for tadka dal.

Basically, if you like hot sauces that feature a respectable bite and a lot of flavor this is worth checking out. It's pricey to be sure, but for me it's going to be one of my guilty pleasures in life.

title: Not as spicy as other Calabrese peppers that I've had, but delicious
text:
I sound these to be moderately spicy with the emphasis on flavor. They are definitely salty, so if you need to watch your sodium intake be careful.

The ingredients are simple, which is probably one reason why I found them to be so enjoyable. There are no flavors vying for your attention - the few ingredients fit into the flavor profile perfectly. I was actually unable to distinctly taste the basil that the ingredient list says is there, but it may be just enough to give it that umami boost, because umami was the first thing that came to mind when I opened the jar and tried them.

Based on a subtle flavor that resembles fried bell peppers it's pretty evident that the chili peppers in this mix were either fried, or initially sauteed, then pressure cooked. Either way, it had an unmistakable taste of Calabria (from where my grandfather immigrated to the US in 1898 and passed his love of this condiment to my father, then to me,)

I use mine as a condiment for soups and stews - adding it after the dish is served. My only complaint is cost. I can easily blast through one jar per week, but have been holding back because it can become an expensive habit. Regardless, it's delicious and has just enough spiciness to keep it interesting.

title: Very high quality!
text:
I make a few dishes that use this as a finishing oil. The main one (and one that is very popular with my friends) is moqueca, a Brazilian fish "stew". Some people use this as a cooking oil, but I don't. I have used it as an ingredient of salad dressings (use sparingly because a few drops goes a long way), and an additive to aioli (after it has been made - again, use sparingly.)

Normally I purchase Brazilian brands, and usually labeled as "dende" oil instead of red palm oil. Most of those brands are good quality. This one is very high quality, although two jars is probably more than I will use in the coming year. I have one jar stored in a pantry out of direct light, hoping that it will last. The other is going surprisingly fast.

Bottom line: this is a safe brand of red palm oil and a good value given its quality and price compared to others that I have purchased over the years.

title: Not too piquant. Amazing flavor
text:
I purchased mine at a local supermarket chain. It is not super piquant, although it has a bite and a slight after burn. What makes it special in my opinion is the flavor. Scotch bonnet peppers need to be aged to bring out their true flavors to provide an umami dimension to the flavor profile. It's obvious that the peppers used in this recipe were.

A note about the ingredients: the one I picked up off-the-shelf lists water as the first ingredient. I would not have bothered to look, but a number of reviews here complained about that. For me it is all about the flavor and how this adds to the food. As long as the ingredients or nutritional values are not high in harmful stuff like sodium I don't much concern myself. It's how it tastes that matter to me, and this one is flavorful. As an additional note, the ingredients also listed habanero peppers, which did surprise me. The reason is I usually don't care for the flavor of that pepper, but it sits beautifully in the flavor profile to my palate.

title: Almost identical to the hard to get Texas Pete Dust
text: I was recently introduced to Texas Pete Dust and wanted to get some for myself. Nowhere in my local area was any to be found. I spotted this on the shelf of one store, read the ingredients, and grabbed it. It's near identical, although the Texas Pete product has slightly more garlic in the flavor profile. Salt dominates both products. At any rate, I love them both equally and while my preference tends towards the Texas Pete product this is an acceptable substitute since this one is on a few local stores and Texas Pete is not.

title: Adds a lot of flavor
text:
A friend recently introduced me to this and while at first skeptical, I quickly fell in love with it. It's not overly spicy (which is a subjective statement because I normally love habaneros and other hotter than normal peppers.) However, it makes up for that with a clever mix of garlic and salt to enhance the cayenne. There are other, subtle flavors, but the main ones are cayenne, garlic and salt. I used it in some home made chili as a condiment and it took the flavor up a few notches. Not in a piquant way, but in a savory way. Almost umami.

The reason why I was so surprised is I normally use exotic spice and herb mixes and would have never taken this product seriously if I spotted it on a grocery shelf. By pure serendipity I was introduced to it by a friend and the rest is history - it gets it's own shaker on my dining table condiment tray. If you love really hot stuff it is not going to rock your world, but if you want a little bite with massive flavor give it a try.

title: High quality
text:
I purchased mine in March 2020, and by mid-April it was used up. Some reviews here cited mold and other issues. I experienced none of those, but the product may be sourced by different vendors, which would account for the inconsistency. I count myself as lucky.

For me this is absolutely perfect as a substitute for parmigiano reggiano grated over spaghetti. A little olive oil, perhaps some papers and this grated over a pasta it to me pure heaven.

Note the time frame that I mentioned: I know for a fact that this will keep at least a month if stored in a refrigerator in a sealed plastic container. Possibly longer. At any rate, do heed the negative reviews because there were enough of them to indicate there are quality issues with some shipments. I reduced my risk by ordering mine to be delivered by Prime, which meant that I could easily return it for a refund. I was more than pleased with the package I received and it's about time to order another!

title: Excellent quality
text: I ordered these in April 2020, and only recently got around to using them. A the time I paid a little less than twenty-five bucks, which was a bargain.  Fast forward to July 2021, over a year later: these were as fresh as the day that they were packed. That is impressive in itself. They roasted perfectly, and had that fragrance and flavor that quality pine nuts are known for. Easily five stars in my book!

title: Exceptional quality
text:
I routinely use saffron in various dishes - mainly risotto, stews and some soups. In fact I cook with it on a weekly basis, so I know quality when I smell, feel and taste it. This is the real thing. To be honest, this is not the only brand that I use, but it is among a handful of brands that I trust and this is one that I purchase when my other favorites are sold out locally.

Bottom line: if you use saffron this is light years ahead of that stuff you find in the spice section of local supermarkets, and even in some so-called gourmet stores. And it is definitely superior to the "Spanish saffron" that is more widely available.

title: You'll NEVER go back to arborio rice for risotto
text:
A half a package of this will easily feed six as the first serving after soup. In most other respects I prepared this the same way I would if I were using arborio rice (caramelizing onions in butter and toasting the rice before adding stock).

The key difference is this rice absorbed a good thirty or more percent of stock, and was fully cooked in two thirds the time of arborio rice. That surprised me - the cooking time and the amount of stock this rice grain type absorbed was unlike any other rice type I've ever used.

If you prepare risotto, this is the rice to use. It is a bit more expensive than arborio rice, but the creaminess and texture, and the faster preparation time truly set it apart.

title: Excellent quality and a staple of West African and Brazilian cuisine (among others)
text:
I managed to find this at a local Bravo Market. Since I did not play for shipping I am not going to address pricing and associated costs since I want to stick to the product itself.

The oil is high quality, and is listed as 100% natural and unrefined. It compares nicely to other high quality palm oils I have purchased from other sources, and has the distinctive flavor of a quality red palm oil. My primary use is using it as a finishing oil for moqueca (a Brazilian fish stew) as well as a finishing oil for Brazilian style rice.) I have also used a few drops per quart when making sopa de ajo (Spanish garlic soup) and it adds greatly to the flavor. In fact, if you have never used this oil before for cooking I will warn that a little goes a long way.

A few things to note if you have dietary restrictions. This is high in fat. Of the 130 calories per tablespoon, all are from fat (although it's unsaturated fat.) All other nutritional factors are zero: cholesterol, sodium, carbs, protein and dietary fiber.

If you cook West African or Brazilian dishes this oil is probably a required ingredient. This particular brand is authentic and the quality is there. It also lends itself to other cooking styles if you want to take some culinary risks - I have used it as a finishing oil on lamb, roasted vegetables (butternut squash, sweet potatoes and pumpkin), and soups like the aforementioned sopa de ajo, as well as lentil. All turned out wonderfully.

title: A touch of honey
text:
I purchase this locally. Indeed, this is the blended Scotch that opened my eyes (and palate) to the fact that blends deserve respect too. Until trying this I was a single-malt snob.

There are two dominating flavors to my palate: (1) honey (this reminds me a lot of Glenmorangie single-malt in that respect), and (2) salt (this reminds me of an Islay.) There are other nuances, but I have not detected them all since I have just opened my second 750ml bottle.

Another thing that is winning me over is the smoothness. This is totally different from the single-malts that I normally enjoy - those have a distinct personality whereas this one is more subtle. It's complex to be sure, but subtle nonetheless. I am sure some of the smoothness is due to the way gain and malt whiskeys are blended.

Bottom line: if you are a single-malt aficionado who does not take blends seriously, at least give this a shot (no pun intended.)

title: Nice heat, excellent flavor, but some ingredients are red flags
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review will focus on the product and not address variables such as price and shipping. I subtracted two stars because this contains HFCS (high fructose corn syrup.) It's a pity too, because the flavor is excellent and a refreshing change from many habanero-based sauces that tend to be heavy on habanero's natural flavor with no balance or complexity. Moreover, based on the flavor, it appears that this sauce uses aged habaneros that have a more mellow taste.

The flavor profile is nicely balanced with savory, salt, piquant, sour/tangy and sweet in that order. As another reviewer indicated, this is a medium hot sauce that I am guessing comes in around 20000 Scoville units (about ten times the heat of Tabasco).
