The flavor more than compensates for the moderate heat (to my palate).

There 5 calories per 100 gram serving, with nominal nutritional values for everything but sodium, which comes in at 530mg per serving. The high sodium is another reason why I down graded my rating. However, had this not contained HFCS (cane sugar is a better, healthier substitute) I would have given it 4.5 stars and a solid 5 had the sodium level been less than 300mg.

Still, if you don't care about HFCS or high sodium this is an otherwise wonderful how sauce for folks who like it a little on the hot side, but are not quite ready for scorching hot. The flavor is a treat as well.

title: High quality, aromatic pods
text:
I purchase this locally so am addressing the cardamom and not cost of shipping, which are variables and subject to change.

This is a high quality bag of cardamon, which I use when making coffee (I grind the pods with coffee beans), and these are both aromatic and, when brewed, delicious. Zero complaints in that respect.

Do bear in mind that a seven ounce pouch will last a long time, and once you open the bag these can lose their freshness very quickly. I seal mine in a container and refrigerate them after I open the bag, and recommend that you do the same.

A final note: I use a few brands besides this one, and these are easily the equal of any brand I use because I have always gotten fresh, aromatic pods from this brand. Of course, purchasing locally has something to do with it since I can visually see the pods before purchasing.

title: Excellent quality
text:
I purchase these at my local grocery chain, so this review will focus on the seeds and avoid variables like price and shipping.

Normally I purchase coriander seeds at an Indian market that I visit weekly. The reason I purchased these is I ran out and needed some seeds to complete a planned meal. Surprisingly, these proved to be a lot higher quality than I thought, and I also loved the convenience of a jar with a lid to reseal after use. I usually purchase seeds in a baggie, and store them separately.

These consistently pop when I prepare them in hot oil (or clarified butter), so the quality is evident. They release both flavors and aromas beautifully, which is further evidence of the quality. If you prepare Indian dishes you already know just how essential these seeds are. I am so impressed that I intend to continue using this brand.

title: Essential for bucatini all'Amatriciana and carbonara ... and perfect for much more
text:
I purchase this locally so am going to focus on this pasta and sidestep discussions about price and shipping. The shape of this pasta is perfect for bucatini all'Amatriciana because the mixture of egg, the renderings from the guanciale, and the pecorino and tomato seep into the tiny tubes to made each strand perfect. It is also near essential for making perfect carbonara, which is similar to the bucatini all'Amatriciana, except for the tomato. I've made carbonara with regular spaghetti and this particular shape makes a significant difference in flavor.

Before Barilla started offering this particular pasta I was using another brand that was high quality, but expensive and had to be ordered over the web. This one is as good - in my opinion - as the brand I was using, and I can purchase it at my local chain at a decent price. The key point is this is as good as the expensive stuff. What I truly love about this is I get identical results each time I cook it for the recommended time. More importantly, it's truly al dente when I follow the instructions (and DO NOT rinse it in cold water.)

If bucatini all'Amatriciana or carbonara are not on your menu, this shape is also perfect for pastas with cream sauces, garlic and oil (aglio e olio), and red sauces (it also works well with arribiata sauces).

Nutritionally this is typical for most pastas. A two ounce serving (of which there are six in a container) has 200 calories (of which 10 are from the 1 gram of fat), 42 grams of carbs and 7 grams of protein. The rest of the values are zero to nominal.

title: Works best with firm flesh white fish; nice blend
text:
I purchase this locally. This particular masala works best with coconut milk as part of the curry base, although it also works with tomato. I've prepared it using tilapia, monkfish and mahi mahi. Just about any firm flesh fish will work, although white is a not more suitable than red and darker fish.

A box will last about five curries assuming that you are using a pound or so of fish with each meal. If you are making larger portions, use about 20 grams per pound. A pound of fish will yield four servings.

Other basic ingredients you will need for your curry are turmeric (about 1/2 teaspoon per 20 grams of this masala), garlic paste (I also will use a garlic/ginger paste mix when I am using mahi mahi) and an onion.

Per 20 grams this mix contains 68 calories, 312mg of sodium and 8 grams of carbs. Divide those numbers by four for the values of this mix for each individual serving.

title: Nicely blended and aromatic spices and herbs, plus an easy recipe on the box
text:
I purchase this locally, so am not going to discuss price and shipping. This is a nice blend of herbs and spices that will allow you to quickly whip up a korma dish of your choosing. I use this exclusively for lamb (and use the cheaper shoulder cuts.)

You can use a home recipe or one you have found on the web, but I can tell you that following the simple one that is printed on the box will result in a delicious meal. I did double the cooking time with my lamb because I wanted it a lot more tender that the recipe on the box would have made it, but even had I gone strictly by the instructions I have a feeling it would have turned out alright. I will caution that if you are using this for goat, you definitely do need more cooking time. Note that the recipes on the outside of the box are in English and Spanish, and inside the box there are the same in French, Urdu, Hindi and Bangla.

Nutritionally, the box contains six 8 gram servings (a tbsp), each are 40 calories (ten of which are from 1 gram of fat per serving), 0 cholesterol, 730mg of sodium and 6 grams of carbs. While the sodium is extra high (4380mg total in the box!), you will be okay if you do not add more salt to the korma when preparing it.

I mentioned simple: all you need is some meat with a bone (ribs, lamb, etc.), onions, plain yogurt, ginger, oil or ghee and a box of this mix to make a delicious and authentic korma.

title: High quality and intense flavors - a little spicier than other brands, but not unduly so
text:
I purchase this locally at a greatly reduced price, so my review is going to focus on the product and not address variables like cost and shipping.

Normally the three brands of Indian meals in a pouch that I purchase are this brand, MTR and Tasty Bite. I have been using Tasty Bite for nearly two decades, but this brand is new to me. I have to admit that of the three, this one is my favorite. One reason is it's spicier from a pungent perspective. Medium Hot for this brand is about the equivalent of Hot for the other two.

Second, the flavors seem to be much more vivid. In the case of these two meals, the paneer used has a firmer texture and is a little larger than in the other two brands. The consistency of the curry meals in each box is about equal in other respects, but the flavors are more intense in this brand. I am especially pleased with the palak flavor, which is almost as good as fresh spinach.

Like most Indian quick meals in a pouch from all brands that I have tried, both of these have the same 140 gram serving size (two servings to a pouch) and both are extremely high in sodium. The matar paneer has 530mg of sodium per serving (1060mg per pouch) and the palak paneer has 470mg (940 per pouch.)

Here are the following nutrition facts:
Matar paneer: 215 calories (144 of which are from the 16 grams of fat), 30mg of cholesterol, and 11.5 grams of carbs.

Palak paneer: 190 calories (130 of which are from the 14 grams of fat), 30mg of cholesterol, and 9 grams of carbs.

The above are per serving, so double them for the entire pouch. For me both (and a few other meals from this brand) are convenience foods that I keep in my pantry for those days when I am too tired to cook. While the sodium content is high, treating myself to them only occasionally is not unduly harmful, but my cardiologist may disagree. I will say they either of the meals in this set are delicious and worth trying if you love Indian food.

title: Perfect paired with heavier meals or for just sipping
text:
I received this as a holiday gift in a collection called [[ASIN:B00UO36S40 Hedges Family Estate Balanced Reds Collection Mixed Wine Pack]]. This is a distinct wine, but is roughly consistent with the other wines from the vintner in that it's not fruity. The dominant fruit - to my palate - is slightly under ripe cherry with a touch of bitterness, raisins and berries. It's definitely not light, and will overpower lighter dishes (poultry and fish.)

If you love red meat, heavy stews, venison and wild rabbit this will pair nicely with some of them. The gamier the meat, the better this wine pairs. Surprisingly, it pairs best with lighter and creamier cheeses (brie, camembert, and even mozzarella), and if you like Mexican fare it's ideal with carnitas.

Another thing is this wine initially is a bit on the stringent side until it has had time to breathe. If you have an aerator, two passes through that works, otherwise give it at least forty-five minutes to settle and mellow.

In addition to pairing with some of the foods that I mentioned this is excellent as a sipping wine, and if you like Barolo or Amarone, you are probably going to like this one.

title: Would make a nice snack or soup for lunch, but there are nutritional factors
text:
I purchase this locally and will focus on the soup and not variables like price and shipping. This is loosely a 'Tuscan style' soup that has hints of Tuscany in the flavor. It's fairly enjoyable as a fast snack, but there are nutritional issues that caused me to subtract two stars.

The main reason is one 10.5 ounce can (plus another 10.5 ounces of water) is considered to be two and a half servings. Each full serving is 60 calories, so a can will contain a total of 150 calories. That is not bad. Where the problem comes in is the sodium content, which is a whopping 850mg per full serving. If you consume the full can as many adults will, the sodium is 2125mg, which would drive my cardiologist crazy (as well as spike my blood pressure.)

On the plus side this DOES NOT contain MSG like its companion, [[ASIN:B00Y95O55S Campbell's Asian Style Chicken Noodle Soup]], so if you do not have sodium restrictions this is probably no worse than other canned soups (and actually better nutritionally than some!)

You decide.

title: Tasty, but a nutritional disaster for some of us
text:
I purchased this locally, so will not address variables like price and shipping.

This has a distinct Asian-like flavor, but nutritionally is a nightmare in my opinion. I should have read the label, but was so intrigued with the 'new' recipe that I grabbed it. First, a 10.5 ounce can is 2.5 servings by Campbell's reckoning. If you poach three eggs in the soup while heating it that is closer to reality. The calorie count is not bad (70 per serving or 175 total for the can). It's the sodium that is off the charts: a whopping 850mg per serving, or 2125mg per can! That means that a whole can is well over 100% or daily intake for a healthy adult, and significantly more than a cardiologist would recommend.

There is also a major gotcha listed in the ingredients: this contains MSG. If you react to that (or soy) then this is NOT a soup you want to try.

Flavor wise this soup is tasty. It has peppers and short, Asian-style noodles, along with toasted sesame oil to impart a nice flavor. It's a pity that what could have been a convenient way to enjoy a quick soup on a cold day is such a nutritional disaster for those of us who do need to watch our intake (and for those who are now healthy, but will feel the effects at some point from such a high sodium food.)

title: A hot sauce that is actually hot
text:
I purchase this locally, so am not going to cover price or shipping, which both vary and fluctuate. I am going to focus on the sauce itself, which is not only hot (and I eat and cook with Scotch bonnets, ghost peppers and the like.)

Although this is hot it's also full of flavor, which is a critical aspect that is too often missing in true hot sauces. The Scotch bonnets do not dominate the flavor profile. You can actually taste the hint of sweetness that counterbalances the piquant aspects. In addition you can also taste the nuances of garlic, onions and thyme. There is a hint of sour and tang from the vinegar that actually flavors as well as preserves this sauce. So, not only is this an intriguing and delicious hot sauce, it's also one with a complete flavor profile. Nutritionally a teaspoon has a scant 45mg of sodium and despite the cane sugar the carbs do not even register.

This is a thick, viscous sauce, so a little goes a long way. Back to the heat. It builds instead of grabbing you by the throat, and grows very intense. Still, this did not scorch or have a sharp bite. If Tabasco sauce is your limit this will probably be far too hot for you, but if you do like it hot you'll enjoy it.

title: Quick way to make channa masala
text:
I purchase this locally and always keep some on hand for when I am in the mood for channa masala. The spices in this mix are pretty basic and not particularly 'spicy', although that is a relative term since I eat Scotch bonnets and other hot peppers.

This will not take the place of mixing your own masala, but it is still nicely and skillfully blended to impart a Punjabi style flavor.

When I prepare channa masala I use whole chickpeas, although on the rare occasions when I have split baby chickpeas I throw a handful of those in when I am cooking the chickpeas. Also, for a true Punjabi flavor, cook your chickpeas with a garni bouquet of tea leaves (in a pinch a teabag will do). Discard that after you drain the chickpeas and before you add them to the base.

Bottom line: this is about as authentic tasting as you are likely to get from a pre-blended, ground spice mix. However, you still need to pop them in hot oil before proceeding with the rest of the recipe.

title: Perfect substitute for some dishes requiring flour
text:
I received this as a free sample fourteen months ago and am just now using the last of it. Others have described this at great lengths, including health benefits (which I do not doubt.) My experience is a little different because I still enjoy pasta, rice and other grains that I probably should not (but probably will continue.)

My main two uses have been to thicken some dishes as well as make pick-me-up drinks. For the former I rarely use flour, preferring a starchy potato like a Russet, finely diced. This does an equally good job when I want a touch of flavor from Thailand or the Bikol region of the Philippines in my dishes. This is also interesting as a thickener in omelets in lieu of a pinch of flour.

For pick-me-ups I usually blend this, a little honey and a mix of whole cow milk and a raw egg. This gives it a thick consistency and subtle flavor. It's also the perfect breakfast and I did play around with almond milk, which also works.

After I opened this I kept it in my refrigerator, and in the past fourteen months have not noticed any degradation of flavor or other characteristics. I think from that it's safe to assume that a four pound bag will keep at least a year if properly sealed and refrigerated. As for how long it will last, I used it a few times a week for over a year and am just now finishing it up.

title: Perfect for cooking
text:
I received this as a free review sample. First, I want to address the 'extra virgin' claim. This oil was probably made by drying the coconut meat, then pressing it. That is a common method for making oil of the highest quality, but it is totally different from making olive oil. The EV designation can be confusing to cooks who are expecting a true grading system. There isn't one that is universally accepted for coconut oil. This does not detract from the quality of the oil, but I wanted to set expectations if you are new to it.

My testing was strictly in food preparation. I used this in lieu of olive oil to prepare sea bass, as well as to make a Filipino dish called binagoongang gatas (a dish from the Bikol region of southern Luzon.) In both cases this oil proved to be very high quality. On the sea bass it was a subtle difference. So subtle, in fact, that you probably would not be able to tell which was which if I were to identically prepare one using olive oil and one using this oil.

For the Filipino dish this is as real time saver. I typically boil coconut milk in a skillet until it flashes into oil, then continue with the rest of the recipe. Here I had oil to start with and it was just as good as the longer method I was accustomed to using. For me that is a big plus.

Note that once opened DO NOT refrigerate this oil. It will harden. It should actually last a good six months at room temperature if tightly sealed.

As for health benefits, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. Honestly, I do not know and even though I have been using coconut oil for cooking long before I tried this one, I would be lying if I said that made a difference. There are too many other variables in my diet.

Bottom line: this is a high quality coconut oil that is perfect for cooking. I think it's vastly superior to most vegetable oils, and while olive oil is my most used oil, this one is perfect for many dishes.

title: Amazingly good for olives from a jar
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review will be about the product and not variables like price and shipping. The first time I 'discovered' these was when I needed decent olives to make spaghetti alla puttanesca and the fresh olives at my local supermarket were sold out. I took a chance.

To be honest, these are not the same flavor, texture and quality of fresh olives - but they are very close. Since I needed to saute these in olive oil with anchovies, garlic, tomato and capers I was not too worried about the difference between these and fresh. The dish came out perfectly and I have been using this brand for that dish ever since.

In a pinch these will suffice in lieu of fresh olives for antipasti, salads and the such. However, I still prefer fresh olives for those dishes.

They are packed with distilled vinegars and water with some salt, and olive oil. When I cook with them I rinse them first because I do not want any extraneous flavoring. As an antipasti ingredient they can be served straight from the jar.

Nutritionally they contain the typical 4 grams of fat. What I love is there is zero cholesterol and only 240mg of sodium per four olives (much less if you rinse them).

title: Decent quality capers
text:
I purchase these locally, so am going to focus on the product and not variables like price and shipping.

While these are not the absolute best capers I've enjoyed, I love them because they are relatively inexpensive, easy to obtain in Central Florida and are truly high quality.

The sizes are not uniform like in gourmet quality capers, and some of the capers tend to be a little on the large side. However, these have an excellent balance of acidity and saltiness. More importantly, they are crunchy.

If you use capers often you probably have run across some brands that are overly salty and mushy. Compared to those this brand is superior. Also, despite the size aspect that I mentioned above these are nonpareil grade instead of the gigantic capers that litter many supermarket shelves.

title: Natural, not love at first sip
text:
First: I purchase this locally and am reviewing product, not variables like price and shipping. Frankly, it makes no sense to order this online.

However, if you spot this in a store and are curious, the essence of this is sparkling water (from CO2), natural orange flavor and zero sugar. If you are accustomed to soft drinks and juices you may not like this at first. It took me a few bottles before I started preferring it to bottled water. Do know that I never drink soda, and rarely do I indulge in juices. So this has become a treat and a refreshment.

As the product description claims, this is water, flavor and bubbles. I've discovered that as soon as I drink a bottle my appetite is suppressed to a degree, so I usually have a bottle about thirty minutes before meals to keep my food intake to a sane level. I am NOT claiming that this is a magic diet supplement, nor am I claiming that you will have the same results. It works that way for me, so I am mentioning it.

Bottom line: if you have a chance to try this, give it a shot. You may love it or you may feel as though something's missing. If you give it a chance you may find it to be a way to stay hydrated with a touch of flavor.

title: Interesting flavor and wonderful texture and consistency
text:
I purchased this on a whim at a local grocery chain and was taken in by the flavor versus the listed ingredients. Both the nutritional values and the ingredients are listed in the product photos of labels on this page so I will not repeat them. Nor will I address variables such as price and shipping.

What I love is the dominating sweetness with a touch of piquant. There is no real sour or tartness that characterizes many mustard types. And it's not especially salty. The surprise is the piquant quality, which probably comes from the turmeric. I am pretty sure that the amount of turmeric is nominal because there is no real bitterness that is also associated with it.

Regardless or the ingredients, they are all natural, and this particular blend is wonderfully sweet with a little fire to make it interesting. I tried mine on pumpernickel with salami, capicola, pepperoni and provolone and it was a perfect complement.

I also love the thick, coarse consistency that is perfect for sandwiches as well as a quick dressing made from this, a little olive oil, crushed garlic and fresh lemon juice.

title: Multi-purpose seasoning for a touch of Creole
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the seasoning and not variables like price and shipping.

This is a great seasoning or rub if you want a touch of Creaole flavor. It's a little high in sodium content at 290mg per 1/4 teaspoon, but a little does go a long way, so factor that into your recipes.

For me, a pinch added to a from-scratch tomato based vegetable soup, or rubbed into any meat adds an exotic flavor that is heavy on cayenne pepper, garlic and cumin (the other dominating flavors aside from salt). Another way that I use it is to sprinkle a little over red beans and rice before serving. It can also be used as a table condiment.

Although this has cayenne pepper it's not especially piquant to my taste. However, that is relative. I eat extremely spicy food so it could be very well too spicy for some folks. One final thing is this has no MSG, which is very important to me.

title: Affordable introduction
text:
This is not the best cut of Spanish ham, but it is affordable and works well for tapas. I purchase mine locally at a better price point, but know that this is the least expensive (and flavorful) cut from the 'black hoof' ham.

Although this is not strictly acorn fed like the premium [[ASIN:B002BL9ZQ6 Jamon Iberico de Bellota]], it is still an experience that will develop and refine your palate for Spanish black hoof style hams. It's a little thicker than prosciutto, and with a different texture. The flavor is what sets this apart from its distant Italian cousin. This one has a more pronounced flavor that is hard to describe. It's less salty to my palate.

A major difference between this and the Bellota (aside from price) is this one is made from grain fed pigs whereas the Bellota is from acorn fed ones. The flavor is totally different if you have a refined palate, and for me there is no real comparison. However, since I cannot afford Bellota more than once a year, this is a nice substitute for setting out a tapas and enjoying with queso Manchego and a glass of Tempranillo or Garnacha.

title: Healthier than most breakfast cereals but still has corn syrup
text:
I purchase this locally, so will focus on the actual product and not address variables like price and shipping.

Interestingly this cereal is the same concept as the competing Kellogg's Origins Ancient Grains. More interesting is both have near identical nutritional values. You can see the values for this particular cereal in the product photos, so I am not going to repeat them here.

What I love is this is not sugared down.There are natural sugars, as well as brown sugar among the ingredients, but this is nowhere near the levels in most breakfast cereals for adults.

More importantly, they need no sweetener. I will say that if you are accustomed to either sweet cereals or adding sweetener you may be tempted at first to add sugar, honey or an artificial sweetener. My advice: don't. After a few days of having this for breakfast you will begin to taste the natural flavors.

Why I subtracted stars is this has corn syrup among its ingredients. That substance undoes some of the health qualities, and there is no reason to use it given the other ingredients used to make this cereal.

Bottom line: this would be a five star, head-to-head competitor to Kellogg's Origins Ancient Grains had corn syrup not been included. Still, it's vastly superior to most other cereals on the market from a health perspective, including some 'natural' ones.

title: Simply amazed
text:
First, I purchase these locally, so am not going to address price, shipping or other variables. The focus is on the peanuts and their quality.

What amazes me is these are as good as the roadside boiled peanuts that I can purchase most of the time locally. More importantly, these keep in the can until I want to use them. The product images on this page contain nutritional values, so check those for that information. I am guessing that the only real variable between these and the roadside ones is sodium content, and I suspect that it's much higher in the roadside ones. There is a color enhancer in these that fresh boiled peanuts do not have, but the trade-off is the convenience of having these 'fresh' until you are ready to consume them.

Normally I only occasionally enjoy boiled peanuts, but lately have been substituting them for garbanzo beans to make an interesting variant of hummus. A friend introduced me to that and I've become fond of it. In fact, these with the normal quantity of tahini and other ingredients make a hummus that is to die for. But I digress. These peanuts are - to my palate - every bit as delicious as locally sold ones, and are far more convenient.

title: A healthier granola
text:
I purchase this locally so am not going to cover variables like price and shipping.

Surprisingly, this is a decent granola given that the brand also makes cereals that are heavier on sugar and other additives. This one is a step in the right direction. It's also slightly sweeter than the [[ASIN:B00WBGINFA Kellogg's Origins Fruit and Seed Muesli]], which has slightly better nutritional values and more roughage.

Unsweetened this granola with skim or soy milk is a nice, quick breakfast. I prefer the muesli, but enjoy this once or twice a week. A half cup serving comes in at 200 calories, of which 30 are from the 3.5 grams of fat. Carbs come in at 38 grams, 8 of which are from sugars, and the protein is 6 grams. Cholesterol is zero, but sodium is 110mg (the muesli has zero sodium), and the serving with a half cup of skim milk comes in at 250 calories.

This is about 12 percent of a 2000 calorie per day diet, so is a good source of morning energy without eating into your allocated daily calorie budget.

If you like granola this is a safer choice than some on the market. It is not as sweet as most, but once you become accustomed to that you will be able to enjoy a nice mix of flavors that stand on their own merit.

title: Surprisingly healthy
text:
I purchase this locally so my review will be confined to the cereal and not variable factors like price and shipping.

Normally I distrust big-name cereals because many are laden with sugar and additives. This one is not. To be sure, there are some nutritional values that seem a little out of line, but compared to most of the cereals they are not egregious.

For me this is the perfect source of fiber and roughage. I'm in my mid 60s so any food that keeps things regular is worth adding to a diet. From a flavor perspective, the fruits and seeds are more than enough for me without adding sugar. If you are accustomed to big brand granola and other unhealthy, sugar laden foods that are disguised as healthy, you may be tempted to sweeten this cereal. That defeats the purpose. After a few bowlfuls of this one, over the course of a week you will be able to taste the natural sweetness and enjoy it with low fat or soy milk.

Nutritionally each half cup of dry cereal is 180 calories, of which 20 calories are from fat. There are 36 grams of carbs per serving (10 of which are from sugar and 5 from dietary fiber), and 6 grams of protein. While the calorie and sugar counts seem high, they are not compared to most breakfast cereals. Where the nutritional values start looking very good is the sodium and cholesterol numbers: both are zero! Also, there are 260mg of potassium, which is a good number for most of us.

If you are on a 2000 calorie a day diet a half cup of this, and a half cup of skim milk come in at just 220 calories, are about 12% of your total caloric intake. Add in the fiber and protein and this is actually a healthy meal (as long as you resist the urge to add sweeteners). To my palate this is delicious, but it may take time if you have a penchant for sweeter cereal.

title: There is nothing like it
text:
Compared to cinnamon sticks and the usual grocery store fare Saigon cinnamon is potent, more aromatic and literally explodes with flavor.

Use two thirds of what you would normally use or it will be bitter. In fact, like other brands I have tried this is fresh and potent enough to get by with a half of what you would normally use. You can always add a pinch more, but cannot remove it. Experiment if you have never used this Vietnamese spice because it's definitely like cinnamon on steroids. I use this mixed with either honey or unsweetened applesauce as a topping on baked sweet potatoes. I also add a pinch to coffee grounds before brewing when I want a special treat.

This does NOT come in sticks because the nature of the bark from which this comes is too delicate to harvest in stick form. On the other hand, I have never had a cinnamon stick that came close to flavor and fragrance as this stuff, so do not let the powdered form fool you into thinking that there is something better out there. There isn't.

If you cook or bake with cinnamon and have never experienced this variety it's definitely worth checking out.

title: Creamy, mild and perfect with wine, coffee or ...
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review is going to remain focused on the cheese. This has been one of my staples that I enjoy for breakfast, or when entertaining.

This cheese is very creamy with a mild mold that has only a hint of bitterness. In fact, part of the creaminess and mildness come from the triple-cream process and the cow milk base.

For me this is one of the cheeses I enjoy at breakfast (usually spread on a baguette or toasted pumpernickel bread), paired with espresso. It's buttery and has a touch of earthiness and tang, so it also pairs with most fruit except citrus. For wine, this pairs nicely with most reds and whites, but to my palate is best with a Beaujolais Villages for reds and a Cortese di Gavi for white.

Nutritionally each 200 gram wedge in the wheel contains two servings, each with 450 calories and 44 grams of fat. Sodium is fairly high at 680mg per serving, but is actually less than most blue cheeses, which can be over twice that.

title: Darn good and a bargain in its price range
text:
I came to this Cabernet via the Chardonnay, which opened my eyes to this vintner. Note that this needs to breath for at least fifteen minutes before the full bouquet blooms.

A first sip immediately reveals a rough finish and a taste that is more like prunes. After it has breathed the finish smooths out considerably (but there is still an edge to it), and the prunes take on the flavor characteristics of plums and raisins. There is a hint of vanilla, but not the slight pepper that I have come to expect from California Cabs. In fact, there is a slight lightness to this Cab that makes it a good second choice if you run out of Merlot. In that respect it's an 'in- between wine.'

Since I have wine with my dinners and I am more concerned about pairing this with food. It will go with the usual fare, like beef, red fish and most cheeses. I took a chance and tried it with a double creamed cheese with shaved truffles on a baguette and to my surprise it did not overwhelm the truffle. In fact this inexpensive wine complemented it better than some of my higher end whites and some reds. That alone is why I gave this five stars. It's well worth checking out.

title: Perfectly roasted
text:
I received this as a free review sample to try after criticizing the roast of the [[ASIN:B00TXMKZBA Dancing Moon Ethiopian Yirgacheffe]], which I thought was over roasted. This one is perfectly roasted for the bean type. It's dark (the Sumatra Mandheling is best that way), but not oily, which would indicate over roasting.

The flavor was typical Mandheling, with a full, rich body, low acidity and complex with earthy dominating, but a touch of sweet and - to my palate - an ineffable flavor that I cannot identify, but lingers in a pleasant way.

When I test coffee I have a specific process. I always grind with a manual, ceramic burr grinder so as to not burn or burnish the beans, and I use a bottled water ([[ASIN:B004AHBH38 Acqua Panna]]) when brewing because that water is totally neutral. Sadly that water is too expensive for daily brewing, but it contributes to a perfect cup of coffee. I also brew two ways: in a French Press and in a [[ASIN:B0000CF3Q6 Bialetti 6799 Moka Express 3-Cup Stovetop Espresso Maker]]. This particular bean and grind brewed perfectly in both. I had expected a better brew from the French press, but surprisingly the moka did an equally nice job. In fact that brewer brought out nuances that the French press did not.

My only complaint is there is no roast date on the bag. There is a 'use by' sticker, but that does not tell you how long ago it has been roasted - and is important to we coffee fanatics.

Bottom line: I loved this particular bean and roast so much that I will probably be ordering a bag every few months - it's that good.

title: Perfectly neutral
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the water itself and not price or shipping.

One of the reasons why I love this water is it's perfectly neutral. There is absolutely no no minerals, salts or even bubbles. For drinking it's a luxury. The true value of this water is when you use it to brew teas and coffees. That is not something I often do, but when I am evaluating those this is the water I use to ensure that there are no impurities introduced to the brew. Also, if you love baking this water contributes to the perfect dough. I have used it for pizza and focaccia and the difference when using this versus even bottled or distilled water is remarkable.

Another reason why I rated this so highly and recommend it is for those of us who are amateur chefs this is the perfect accompaniment to some dishes. Especially ones that have subtle flavors like a hint of truffle because this water is so neutral that the dish stands on its own merits. I have also served this at cheese tastings.

I'll admit that it's not for everybody, and you have to try it side-by-side with other waters to fully comprehend just how pure and neutral it is. If your palate can detect those, then you will probably love it.

title: A little over roasted, but high quality beans
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The beans are excellent quality and fresh, but the roast is a bit too dark for this variety of bean, and far more oily than I expected for a good Ethiopian bean. The oil is from the roasting process, which the reason why I subtracted a star. Note that there is a "use by" date on the pouch, but there is no roasting date, so if you are an aficionado you may want to subtract another star. For me, the quality of the beans earned it a full four stars.

To ensure my test of these beans did not add external flavors and impurities I used [[ASIN:B004AHBH38 Acqua Panna]] bottled water, which is totally neutral. I also used a ceramic burr hand grinder so I would not further burn or burnish the beans. For this particular bean I brewed in a French press.

The brewed coffee had the characteristic earthiness with a strong nuttiness. Because the roast was so dark (somewhere between full and dark), I was not able to taste the nuances that are also characteristic. Had this been medium light roasted I should have been able to detect some floral and even citrus, but could not.

I love the positive seal aspect of the pouch, which definitely keeps the beans fresh once you open it and reseal. Also, while I subtracted a star for the roast, this coffee may be perfect to your palate. I am a stickler for proper roasting of each bean variety, but many folks WANT a dark roasted bean. Those will probably love everything about these beans and the brew it produces. Factor that in when making a purchase decision.

title: Expensive, but worth it
text:
First taste makes you wonder why one would pay a premium price for what seems like plain water. Read on because it is worth it for some of us. Also note that I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the water itself and not price or shipping.

My first try of this water was non-eventful. I thought it would be like the Pelligrino I normally purchase, but while it's sold by the same company, it's nothing like it. What turned me was a friend who raved about it and insisted that I give it another try. She was right. It was so pure and neutral that it it hard to enjoy unless you know what you are looking for. In my case, a water with no minerals, salts or even bubbles. There is an ineffable quality to it that I could never put into words.

For those of us who are amateur chefs is this is the perfect accompaniment to some dishes. Especially ones that have subtle flavors like a hint of truffle because this water is so neutral that the dish stands on its own merits. It's also perfect for brewing a special cup of coffee (or tea) because this water is so neutral that it will not mask the flavors of the grind or leaves.

It's not for everybody, and you have to try it side-by-side with other waters to fully comprehend just how pure and neutral it is. If your palate can detect those, then you will probably love it.

title: Perfect for snacks, or with rice or pasta for a light meal
text:
I purchase these locally (just about every place where I shop carries them), so am not going to address variables like price and shipping. This review will focus on the octopus itself.

These are surprisingly tender for octopus. They are slightly chewy, but not terribly so. The flavor is mildly spicy, with a hint of acidity and salt in the flavor profile. For light meals I toss a can of these in a small bowl of cooked pasta or over hot rice, add red pepper flakes and a touch of olive oil and salt. Out of the can they are a nice snack that staves off my appetite.

Each can contains a single, 160 calorie serving of which 90 of those calories are from the 10 grams of fat. Cholesterol is low at 40mg, but sodium is fairly high at 320mg. Carbs are 1 gram and protein a very respectable 12 grams.

The ingredients are simple: octopus, soybean (and/or) sunflower oil, tomato, onion and unnamed spices. If you have soy allergies you will probably want to avoid these.

Bottom line: for folks like myself you dine alone, a can of these with a starch like pasta or rice is an inexpensive and fairly nutritious meal. I love the flavor and texture, and despite the slight chewiness, each morsel is more tender than octopus that I prepare fresh.

title: Excellent paired with red meats
text:
I purchase this locally. It's a perfect red for pairing with red meats, especially better cuts of aged beef. However, it's also a nice choice paired with barbeque and even burgers. Part of the reason why is this is especially complex for such an inexpensive table wine.

The tasting notes claim vanilla, cranberry, raspberry and herbs de provence aromas, with plum and a touch of chocolate. My palate detects more of a plum and cranberry with hard to identify herbs. In fact, I detect a slight peppery nuance, so my own experience differs from the tasting notes.

Also, this is at the mid range of alcohol by volume for a pinot noir, sitting at 13.5%. It's not particularly high, but sufficiently potent that if you are pairing this with a meal I recommend not pouring and serving until the meal is on the table because it can go to ones head quickly on an empty stomach.

It goes with most cheeses, but for me the best pairings are with cheeses along the lines of a decent Spanish manchego or an Italian provolone. I have tried this with sheep milk cheeses like pecorino romano and the tang of those types of cheese subdue the nuances of this wine, so the milder the cheese the better in my opinion.

For an inexpensive table wine this is a bargain. If you are serving heavier meals and want a decent table wine to accompany them this is a safe choice.

title: Superb flavor and perfect tapas
text:
I purchase these from a local chain grocery and love how well they pair with Iberico cheese and tempranillo wine as a tapas for before meals or just socializing. The flavor is ineffable because the spices and other ingredients seem to have a heavy North African influence, especially the nutmeg and black and white peppers.

This sausage has a high fat content, which I feel imparts both its unique flavor and texture. Each serving is an ounce (about seven cuts from an approximately 11.5 inch sausage.) Of the 140 calories per piece, 110 are from fat, which is 12 grams per 28 gram serving. Not the stuff that will please your cardiologist, but will definitely please your palate. In fact this is the perfect pairing with the Campo Viejo brand of tempranillo because the ripe cherry in that wine contrasts nicely with the flavor of this sausage. Add in the buttery and slightly piquant flavor of a good piece of Iberico cheese and you have the makings of a tapas that is fit for royalty. To my palate anyway.

The sausage is made from free ranging pigs that have a significant amount of acorn in their diets. This is another factor in the flavor of the sausage, and is unique to Spanish pork (and especially hams). Another factor that makes this addictive is the high sodium content, which is a heart stopping 470mg per serving. Not the stuff you want to consume in vast quantities if you have cardiac issues, but definitely addicting with a good cheese and wine.

Bottom line: if you do not have sodium or fat restrictions this is delicious and the perfect centerpiece to any tapas spread. Even with its high sodium content a small slice served with an egg or even a piece of cheese makes for a great seasoning as well as a snack.

title: Better than some fresh tomatoes, but a LOT of sodium
text:
I purchase these locally, so I am going to confine my review to the product and not price, shipping or other variables.

These are truly delicious and have a great texture and flavor. However I had to dock them a star because of the high sodium that comes in at 260mg per half cup serving, of which there are six servings per container. If you are on a sodium restricted diet a mix of half of these and chopped or crushed fresh tomatoes will work, but that defeats the purpose in my opinion. If sodium is not an issue for you, then these are truly five star for flavor.

For me these are a viable alternative to most fresh tomatoes, which in my neck of the woods taste like cardboard. I get lucky sometimes and get decent fresh ones, but I cannot depend on that and often turn to these as a substitute.

Other nutritional values are 30 calories per serving, and 6 grams of carbs (five of which are from natural sugars in the tomatoes). Aside from tomatoes and tomato byproducts (juice and paste) the only other ingredient listed on the box is sea salt.

title: Fast, fresh and delicious
text:
I received a box of these as a review sample. Normally discussing delivery is both irrelevant and subject to variation, but you are paying a premium for that as well as the muffins. They are expedited and the ones I received were as fresh as if I had baked them myself.

In fact, they were so moist and delicious that I probably could not have done a better job. The only thing I do not care for is the lack of ingredients and nutritional information. These did come with a sheet providing the nutritional values of all of the cakes and cookies offered by Dulcets, but muffins were not included. I checked their web site and that, too, did not include the information I was seeking. Since these are Kosher certified and the product description claims natural ingredients I am going to take their word that there are no questionable stuff like high fructose corn syrup. In fact, since the other products had high amounts of sugars in the nutritional values I am convinced.

These are as moist and absolutely delicious. I tried two from the batch - cranberry and banana - and both tasted like all of the ingredients were genuine and not artificially flavored. In fact, all artificially flavored baked goods leave a bitter aftertaste in my mouth and these did not, further convincing me of their quality.

Bottom line: these are best as corporate gifts because they arrive very quickly and are a safe bet since most folks love muffins. They are of the highest quality and I am serious in stating that you would have to be a great baker to do a better job. That is high praise coming from me.

title: Exceptional quality potatoes
text:
I received these as a review sample.Unlike the bags of potatoes I purchase in the store - all too often getting soft - these are firm and in perfect condition. My first test was to make skordalia, which is a Greek potato and garlic dip. The starchy russet potatoes in this batch were perfect for that. Two was all it took to make a batch and these had a wonderful consistency after they were boiled. More importantly, they had that creamy quality when I blended in garlic, olive oil and a little fresh lemon juice.

Since these were so firm I tried making another Greek recipe called Ellinikos lemoni patatas (literally Greek lemon potatoes). They were too starchy for that recipe, but I had to try. I did use two of the smaller red potatoes in the same batch for the lemon potatoes and their waxy texture was perfect. In fact, I used the remaining red potatoes in this batch to make rosemary and garlic roasted potatoes, which is one of my favorite potato dishes.

Bottom line: the russets are some of the highest quality ones I have seen in years, and are better than any I get in Florida chain markets and even farmer's markets. They are heavy, firm (dense is probably a better word), and have no outer flaws or blemishes. Same for the reds - they have unblemished skin and are firm and heavy as well.

If you take potatoes seriously and want a good mix of the starchy and the waxy types this is a great way to purchase both and be assured of getting very high quality potatoes. I purposely did not include recipes of what I made, but will be more than happy to include them in a comment to this review if anyone is interested.

title: Excellent quality
text:
I received this as a review sample. Note that at the time of this review this product is erroneously cross-linked to a different product, so know that I am reviewing [[ASIN:B00QT62QII Japanese Matcha Green Tea Powder by iMaccha]].

As a matter of routine I use matcha tea from various brands, so I have some experience with this type. As for the health benefits I am not going to attempt to discuss them because, frankly, I am not sure and certainly am not qualified to make claims. What I can do, though, is make a direct comparison to other brands I have used. I would have to say that this brand is at the least equal to others I have tried and use because I cannot tell the difference between this and the matcha I purchase from Asian markets and online.

If you are familiar with powered matcha you already know the basic characteristics. If not, know up front that this, like other high quality brands, will not completely dissolve, even in hot water. I recommend that you stir and let it settle, or consume it as is.

Another thing you need to know is it's bitter. For me this is one of the reasons why I love it. If you are accustomed to brewed tea you may not like the first sip.

It's not limited to traditional tea, especially when it comes to making confections and smoothies. Also, if you are a juicer this also has value. I use mine two ways (other than actually drinking it as a hot beverage). One is to mix a half teaspoon and an equal amount of honey into plain yogurt as a breakfast pick-me-up. The other is a bit more off the beaten path, I use it to balance the flavor profiles in some sauces I make to add a slight bitter component. That allows me to reduce sodium. For some strange reason this compensates for the diminished saltiness in some dishes.

Regardless of how of why you use this, the aroma, feel and taste indicate that this is a high quality matcha tea and merits consideration if you are shopping for the real thing.

title: Delicious, but some nutritional gotchas
text:
I purchase this locally so am not going to address price and related variables. The smoked herring in these tins is delicious and has a firm flesh that is consistent from can-to-can. I indulge in this fairly often and have never noticed any variation in quality or flavor each time I enjoy it.

The ingredients are simple: herring fillets, rapeseed oil, salt and smoke. It's the salt and oil that elevate the sodium and calorie levels.

Total calories per one of the two pieces that are in the can are 370, of which 310 are from the 34 grams of fat per serving. If you have sodium restrictions, the 430mg per filet is a red flag, as is the 75mg of cholesterol. Frankly, while each can contains two servings, I usually consume a whole can at one setting, so the numbers above are double (and not exactly healthy at that level.)

On the plus side, there are no carbs and a whopping 15 grams of protein in each of the two filets, as well as a little over 3 grams of omega-3 acids per serving. Also, this is Kosher as well as Halal, so there are no issues in those areas.

Bottom line: the nutritional values are not bad for smoked herring, but you do need to heed them if you have restrictions. The only problem is these are so delicious that it's difficult to NOT consume an entire can at one sitting.

title: Great flavor - questionable ingredients
text:
I am a fan of many of Bookbinder's products. especially their Dijon mustard. This one, though, has a major flaw in that it includes high fructose corn syrup - an ingredient that many other brands have discontinued using for health reasons. For that reason alone I subtracted two stars.

If you have no problems with that ingredient, I will concede that the flavor is near perfect. It has just enough aromatic horseradish to take your breath away (a good thing as far as I am concerned.) It also has a tanginess that other prepared horseradish sauces lack. Finally, the consistency is creamy as claimed on the label. This is the perfect dipping or smearing sauce for prime rib, and a touch to any salad dressing or mayo transforms those into gourmet quality spreads and dressings.

Nutritional values are not bad - 15 calories per serving, of which 10 are from the 1 gram of fat it contains. Other values are 40 grams of sodium, zero cholesterol and 1 gram of carbs.

This would be a five star product had the ingredients excluded the high fructose corn syrup, and I am frankly disappointed that Bookbinder's still uses it in this sauce.

title: Definitely for southern palates
text:
I purchase this locally so am going to avoid discussing price, shipping and other variables. This has been my preferred brand of mayonnaise my entire life (I was born in 1948 and it was an established brand even then.)

The flavor is more natural than other brands, and the only thing better is real homemade (which I also do). Note that the ingredients in this differs greatly from genuine mayo from France, but the pairings of this with food also differ and favor US southern palates.

Ingredients are Soybean oil, eggs, water, distilled and cider vinegar, salt, oleoresin paprika, natural flavors, calcium disodium EDTA added to protect flavor. The latter is necessary since this mayo is intended to be shipped and stored on market shelves. Contrast that with the traditional mayo that uses olive oil, eggs and lemon juice or vinegar (sometimes both), plus spices.

What I love is the consistency which is close to homemade, and the more natural ingredients (read any other major brand's and the ingredients are anything but!) The flavor is also purer and does not leave an unnatural after taste like some of the major brands. Bottom line here is this is about as good as you are going to get short of making it yourself or some boutique brand.

Nutritionally, this is typical of real mayo, with a tablespoon serving coming in at 100 calories (all from fat) that comprises 12 grams per serving. Cholesterol comes in at 10mg, and sodium at 75mg - both are impressive numbers if you compare this to other brands. Zero carbs, which marks this is healthier than many competitors.

While flavor is subjective, nutritional value isn't. I cannot promise you will like this more than any other brand (unless you are southern and then the chances are good that you will). I will say that if you want a healthier mayo that is not laden with chemicals this is one you should try.

title: High wow factor and better than a box of candy
text:
I received a box of these as a gift and although I am not supposed to indulge in sweets I just had to try one. this is not like any cookie of cake I have ever tasted. This is more in the class of fine candy.

Frankly I only sampled one of the cookies, but friends who tried the other types in the tin raved. These may be pricey, but they are worth every penny if you want to indulge yourself or give it as a much appreciated gift. If I had to describe them in a single word it would be 'luxurious'.

Nutritionally you pay a price for indulging because they come in at about 150 calories per cookie. Each also has approximately 7 grams of fat, 70mg of sodium and 20 grams of carbs, so keep those figures in mind as you indulge. I am serious when I say that after one taste it takes a lot of will power to not try another ... and another.

Bottom line: these are for special occasions (or that special person). Do not let the price deter you because you are in for a rare treat if you've never tasted these.

title: Great for nutrition and snacks
text:
Not only are there a wealth of excellent reviews, but nutritional information on this page that render moot much of what I wanted to say. Instead I will confine my comments to some observations and also how I use these.

First, this is not that sweet chocolate that one normally associates with candies and other forms of processed cacao. It's slightly bitter and definitely not processed. You can use it for savory dishes that require a bitter component in the flavor profile (a lot of Mexican cuisine use cacao for this very purpose.) For sweet - but healthier - drinks and confections I blend this into milk and honey. When I say blend, I mean using a blender because the nib are crunchy and need to be pulverized into a powdery form to mix into most drinks.

Second, this truly is a source of nutrients. There is a nutritional values label depicted in one of the product images on this page and I encourage you to read that because these nibs provide an impressive amount of minerals and other 'good' stuff that most chocolate based morsels or drinks do not.

Bottom line: no matter how you use these, including as a raw snack for an energy boost, the possibilities are nearly endless. I have actually experimented with non-sweetened baking using these as a topping along with olive oil, sea salt and herbs for an interesting and surprisingly complementary flavor. Pulverized, a pinch in coffee grounds has the same flavor effect as chicory, and when combined with a pinch of cardamom gives coffee a rich and exotic flavor. But the key point is this stuff is actually healthy!

title: Very high quality quinoa
text:
I received a bag of this as a review sample and had other quinoa in my pantry to which to compare against. The grains in this bag were dry, fresh and had a slightly grassy flavor when I tasted a few grains. In contrast, the other brand I have in my pantry was not as pleasant to the palate (raw). The grains in this bag were smaller and more uniform as well.

This one soaked and cooked about five minutes quicker as well, compared to the brand I had been using.

As for the claims that this is non-GMO I have no way to verify that, but it's an important feature for me. I endeavor to eat only natural foods that are as pure as possible.

Other reviewers have provided recipes and other information, so I will not repeat them. I will say that I've\ been eating quinoa for years because it is healthier on my system than most other grains. This is one of the higher quality bags that I have some across and I do know the difference. If you are exploring the health benefits there is plenty of information on the web. If you already consume quinoa this is truly a quality grain that is noticeably better than bulk bags (and even the giant plastic jars that some brands use).

title: Intense aroma and flavor
text:
I received a bag of this mix as a review sample. As a morning tea it is not my cup of tea to use a cliche. I prefer regular back tea with a touch of milk and sugar. However, as a treat or even a sun tea this is superb.

The flavor is intense in that you can taste the tea and the apricot that is used to infuse it. The blend is perfect and this one practically begs for honey as a sweetener. I made it with an infusing ball first, and the second go I used a French press because I wanted to share it with a friend. I also made a half gallon of 'sun' tea that I served as iced. That, perhaps, was the best of all (sweetened with sugar).

As for the antioxidant qualities, I confess to being unwilling to make claims one way or the other for a few reasons. Foremost is I have not used this long enough to discern any benefits, and second, because I take claims at face value.

One final note about this mix: I got a nice caffeine buzz from a single cup. I read a review here that claimed the contrary, which means we all react differently. Depending on the brew strength and your own reaction to caffeine you may get a little wired from this tea.

Bottom line: if you drink black tea for health reasons by all means try this because the tea leaves are of the highest quality as is the brewed tea. The addition of apricot is a major plus for me for afternoon drinking.

title: Nice texture and flavor, but a little over the top with sodium
text:
Note that I purchase these locally, so my review is going to address the product and not price, shipping or other variables.

The reason for only four stars first: high sodium. If you are on a sodium restricted diet a mix of half of these and chopped or crushed fresh tomatoes will work, but out of the box this has a very high sodium content that comes in at 260mg per half cup serving or which there are six servings per container.

On the plus side, if you do not have restrictions this is delicious with an excellent texture and consistency. It's truly rustic and adds a lot to the presentation as well as the flavor of a meal.

Other nutritional values are 30 calories per serving, and 6 grams of carbs (five of which are from natural sugars in the tomatoes). Aside from tomatoes and tomato byproducts (juice and paste) the only other ingredient listed on the box is sea salt. No other preservatives, so I would actually rate these at four and a half stars if I could.

title: Light and neutral
text:
Since I found this oil locally and at a bargain price I am going to confine my review to the product and leave variables like price alone.

I have some favorite brands of olive oils, and also have preferences regarding their origin. For example I love Spanish oils even more than Greek or Italian ones. What sets this one apart, though, is its near neutral flavor. For some uses that is a detriment, but for others it's a major plus. It has the prized bitterness of a good Italian or Greek oil, but the after burn is slight and there are no dominating flavors or aromas. For example, I often use oils from Liguria because I love the grassy flavor, but this one is more neutral. For some dishes where I want other flavors to rise this is the perfect oil.

Physically the color is a light amber and the subtle influences in the bouquet are hard to discern. That is yet another indication of the neutrality. Thus far I have used it in cooking (browning garlic), drizzling (over both gorgonzola cheese and feta), and dipping. It's best over gorgonzola where it allows the hay like nuances of that cheese to dominate, and for dipping as long as you infuse it with herbs. It also worked well with browning garlic because it did not interfere with the garlic itself. It was a little boring over feta until I chopped in some fresh oregano.

As I said, this is not for every dish, but when you want a good olive oil that does not get in the way of more nuanced ingredients this is worth checking out.

title: High quality
text:
I have used vanilla powder before, as well as genuine vanilla extract, so I had a good idea of that to expect when I accepted a review sample. This powder lived up to my expectations.

While I sometimes use this in baking, my main use is flavoring a concoction that I am fond of: vanilla, milk and honey (and sometimes with an egg dropped in). I blend it and the drink is a wonderful pick-me-up. It's also healthy and is a great substitute for a meal.

Note: this is pure vanilla, so do not expect it to be sweet. Like cacao, pure vanilla is not at all sweet and has a slight hint of bitter. I use honey, but just about any sweetener will work well with it. It dissolves fairly well in liquids. Not perfectly or completely unless you use a blender, but sufficiently so to make drinks like I mentioned above. It also adds a touch of flavor when sprinkled over pasties. I tried it on French toast with just butter and a slight touch of genuine maple syrup and it was delicious.

I am not going to delve into the health advantages of pure vanilla because - frankly - I have no evidence one way or the other. In that respect I made no effort to validate the antioxidant properties. I enjoy this solely for the flavor, so if you are interested in the health benefits some research may provide answers one way or the other. For me, this is one of the best ingredients for healthy energy drinks, as well as for both sweet and savory dishes. It's perfect for adding a touch of bitter to balance out a flavor profile of a savory dish, as well as making some wonderful cakes and cookies. And a little of this goes a long way.

title: A little high in sodium, but convenient
text:
I purchase this locally, so am not going to address variables like price, shipping and whether or not the cans arrive intact. Those factors are highly variable and are better suited to seller feedback. My review is about the product itself.

The clams in this can are of decent quality. They have a nice texture and the size is perfect for making white or red clam sauce when you are in a hurry or you local market's live clams are looking a little unsavory. The juice is relatively thick and works well as stock for risotto too.

Nutritionally these are a little off the mark. I subtracted a star because of the high sodium content from added salt, which comes in at 290mg. Since there are three servings per can, that is 970mg total. Add in the natural cholesterol that comes in at 70mg per serving and you start to see why this is a 'for convenience' only product. I prefer live, fresh clams when feasible, although those have the same cholesterol.

On the plus side, there are only 45 calories per serving, of which 10 are from the 1 gram or fat. Protein is an impressive 9 grams per serving.

As far as canned clams go, though, these are my favorite. As for the nutrition, that goes with any canned product, although I do think the sodium is a little too high for this one.

title: Excellent flavor
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review is going to focus solely on the soup and not address price or other variable factors. This is an occasional treat when I am too lazy to cook.

If you love simple meals, Mediterranean style, this, an olive plate and pita are perfect and quick.

For canned this is not bad. It has a distinct lemon taste that dominates, but is also complemented by spices and herbs (including turmeric). The pasta is a little on the skimpy side, but I prefer mine that way because it's actually more authentic. The chicken is just enough to flavor the broth, which is slightly thickened by the egg.

Nutritionally this has a little too much sodium. Each can contains 2.3 servings and each of those contains 830mg of sodium. If you get carried away and have two servings your cardiologist would have a fit. Ironically, it's the sodium content that adds to the flavor, so be careful. Otherwise, it's values are not terrible: 100 calories per serving, of which 15 are from the scant 2 grams of fat. Cholesterol is a reasonable 30mg, and carbs are 17 grams (the pasta is the culprit.) It also provides 5 grams of protein.

Overall, this is delicious for a canned soup and for some folks is even exotic. As long as you have no dietary restrictions for wheat, egg or soy, and only occasionally indulge in such high sodium soups, this is a real treat.

title: Medium body, but rich
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is focused on the coffee itself and not price, delivery or shipping.

If you are expecting a coffee similar to the rich and full bodied Cuban style coffees, this is not it. In fact, it's quite different. While this is rich like a quality Cuban roast, this coffee has a medium body and very low acidity. To my palate it's the perfect balance of rich and smooth, with a hint of earthiness and a moderate depth. It's the depth that sets it apart from the much deeper Cubans.

This coffee has an extremely fine grind that brews best in a moka pot like the [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti Stovetop Espresso Maker]]. I tried it with a French press and it did not turn out as good. Ditto a conventional cone type brewer.

Bottom line: if you are accustomed to Cuban (or even Puerto Rican) style coffee roasts this is a new experience. It's a little lighter in body, but is still full flavored and rich, and is a dream come true if you value smoothness in a cup of coffee.

title: Excellent quality for a fairly neutral profile
text:
I found this - at a bargain price - at a local Walmart and purchased it on impulse. I was very surprised by the quality.

This oil is more along the lines of a good Spanish olive oil than many of the Italian and Greek ones. It has the prized bitterness, but the after burn is slight and there are no dominating flavors or aromas. For example, I often use oils from Liguria because I love the grassy flavor, but this one is more neutral. For some dishes where I want other flavors to rise this is the perfect oil.

Color is a light amber and the bouquet is difficult to discern the subtle influences - yet another indication of the neutrality. Thus far I have used it in cooking (browning garlic), drizzling (over both gorgonzola cheese and feta), and dipping. It's best over gorgonzola where it allows the hay like nuances of that cheese to dominate, and for dipping as long as you infuse it with herbs. It also worked well with browning garlic because it did not interfere with the garlic itself. It was a little boring over feta until I chopped in some fresh oregano.

Bottom line: if you come across this locally at a bargain price you will be pleasantly surprised by the quality. To be sure, it is a premium olive oil and safe choice, but lacks 'character'. That can be a good thing for some cooking and serving situations.

title: Delicious, but hard to define flavor profile
text:
When this arrived as a review sample I put off tasting it until I had the time and occasion.

My first test was plain. I had a hard time separating the flavor profile components. Sour seems to dominate, but with good reason. Lime juice is one of the main ingredients, and is backed with citric acid. The ginger seems to accentuate the tang. Piquant seems to come in a close second. While this is mild, some folks may find it a bit spicy. Salty ranks third, with savory and a ever-so-slight hint of sweet.

This salsa needs to be stirred because if it sits it separates. I tried it over a piece of grilled haddock wrapped in a flour tortilla with cilantro and chopped tomatoes and minced onion. It would not compete with authentic Baja California recipes, but it was not intended to. This stands on its own as an interesting flavor that may not be traditional, but is delicious.

Nutritionally this is low calorie and comes in at a scant 25 calories per two tablespoon serving. When you consider that mist salsas and sauces are single tablespoon servings, this is - in essence a 12.5 calorie salsa when compared to those. I love the fact that the fat and cholesterol are zero. Sodium is a bit on the high side at 140mg (or 70 if you compare it to single tablespoon servings of other salsas). And carbs are only 1 gram.

Overall this is a great salsa that is healthy without compromising flavor. Like the other two salsas offered by this brand, the flavor is not exactly traditional, but seems to go well with a variety of foods.

title: Tangy and goes well with grilled veggies
text:
I received this as a review sample. The first taste was dominated by a tangy/sour component of the flavor profile, followed by salty, then piquant and finally savory. To my palate the only component missing is sweet, so the flavor profile seems to be skewed towards tangy/salty.

Next I tried this on grilled eggplant and it was a perfect complement, It also went well with zucchini and even roasted peppers. One final taste experiment was to use a little of this over cannelloni beans and I loved the flavor of that too.

Some folks will find this to be good as a dipping sauce. I was not as enamored with it that way, but a friend loved it with a baguette.

Nutritionally this is relatively low in calories. A 32 gram serving (two tablespoons) is only 25 calories, with zero fat or cholesterol and only 5 grams of carbs. It is a little high in sodium at 140mg, but since there are only ten servings per jar is manageable if you are sharing with others.

The flavor is interesting to be sure and not particularly Tuscan. However, it sure goes well with some Tuscan dishes and I doubt I have scratched the surface of possible food pairings.

title: Transforms mundane meals into exotic (and delicious)
text:
When I was offered a review sample I was skeptical because I dislike store bought salsa. It arrived and the first thing I noticed is the sodium content is a very heart friendly 95mg per two tablespoon serving. That serving size was more than enough to garnish a half pound cut of salmon that I broiled with a rare center. The salsa perfectly complemented the cut of fish.

To be perfectly frank, as much as I pride myself on being able to make some great salsas from scratch I doubt if I could do better than this one. I love the savory balanced flavors that have a touch of sour from the citrus, some saltiness despite the low sodium, and even a slight piquant aspect from the curry and cayenne pepper. A very slight bitterness is imparted by the kale. Any sweetness is masked by the curry, citrus and cayenne. Lest I forget, the savory component is definitely there, but the dominating flavors in the profile are the curry itself and the citrus.

Another thing that I love is the consistency. The combination of lentils and sweet potato provide a lot of fiber, a respectable amount of potassium (75mg) and a full gram of protein per serving. If you are on strict diets note that this has zero cholesterol and only 4 grams of carbs.

The cayenne is a little on the mild side, but if you were to mix in some [[ASIN:B009QMEX0G Harissa]] this takes on a distinct North African flavor. I used a ghost pepper, finely minced, in the two tablespoon serving that I enjoyed over my salmon and it kicked the piquant component into high gear. Most folks will want something milder. I will forewarn against adding Tabasco because the sour component from that will completely change the flavor profile - and not for the better. I tried it out of curiosity and will not do that again.

If you love curry and want a dip or garnish that will enhance most foods this one is worth a try. I personally love it, but not everyone will. It depends on your palate. For me the most important thing is it's natural, healthy and along the same lines as something I would concoct in my own kitchen.

title: If you love tea this is a treat (and experience)
text:
At one time I spend a lot of time with a true tea aficionado who exposed me to some truly great teas and sharpened my palate. When I accepted a review sample of this one I was not prepared for either the flavor or the brewing process.

Although the tea that I received is the raw variety that is classified as lighter and milder, the taste was far richer than most of the other teas that I have experienced. Attempting to describe something as ineffable as the flavor of a tea is beyond my writing skills. The best I can do is attempt to compare some of the nuances to the grassy/hay nuances in gorgonzola cheese. Yes, I know that trying to make such an analogy is nonsensical, but it's the best I can do. This one did pique my interest in the ripe variety though.

If you are to enjoy this tea you need to understand the brewing process, which includes warming the tea pot, rinsing the leaves twice, then two separate brewing steps. It's not rocket science, but it is tedious. I recommend following the process to the letter, which will actually heighten the enjoyment when you take your first taste. I was provided with a link to a Youtube video, but found that confusing. I did some additional searching and came across one titled rewing Technique of Ripe Pu-erh Tea by Akira Hojo. It's ironic that the best video of brewing this special Chinese tea was done by a Japanese, but he definitely knows the process and clearly explained it.

I've enjoyed this on three different days so far and am still tasting nuances that I didn't before when I had my first and second servings. Moreover, I thought my palate was educated from past experience, but apparently I was not prepared for this flavor. If you are a tea aficionado and have never tried this I suggest starting with the raw and moving to the ripe. If you've had this, then there is nothing I can tell you that you don't already know - except, this is nicely packaged and according to a friend top quality.

One final note: The person from this company who contacted me sent me an MP3 file of music that was claimed to enhance the pleasure of this tea. In my opinion it's absolutely true and I wish I knew the title of the composition because I would share it here.

title: Pure delight
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the water itself and not price or shipping. My first try of this water was non-eventful. I thought it would be like the Pelligrino I normally purchase, but while it's sold by the same company, it's nothing like it.

First taste makes you wonder why one would pay a premium price for what seems like plain water. What turned me was a friend who raved about it and insisted that I give it another try. She was right. It was so pure and neutral that it it hard to enjoy unless you know what you are looking for. In my case, a water with no minerals, salts or even bubbles. There is an ineffable quality to it that I could never put into words.

What makes this special for those of us who are amateur chefs is this is the perfect accompaniment to some dishes. Especially ones that have subtle flavors like a hint of truffle because this water is so neutral that the dish stands on its own merits. I have also served this at cheese tastings.

It's not for everybody, and you have to try it side-by-side with other waters to fully comprehend just how pure and neutral it is. If your palate can detect those, then you will probably love it.

title: Excellent quality and perfect for taramosalata
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review is going to focus on the product and not price or shipping.

This is a decent quality tarama for making taramosalata. I have tried it with the potato and the bread recipes and it's equally as good with either. It has a nice consistency, but be forewarned that this needs to be refrigerated after opening if you do not use the entire jar at once. Moreover, it does not keep well, either in the jar or after being mixed into taramosalata.

While there are other brands (some equally as good) this one seems easiest to come by, and I have come to trust it.

There are some nutritional facts, though, of which you should be aware. This jar contains 30 one-tablespoon servings, and each contains 700mg of sodium and 50mg of cholesterol. Considering all tarama is made from roe and salt, this is not a surprise and certainly does not indicate low quality. I am mentioning it because it's so delicious that it's easy to forget that moderation is important if you have dietary restrictions. Of course, a properly made taramosalata with this roe is hard to resist.

Bottom line: this is readily available in many metropolitan areas, but if you cannot get it locally, it's well worth ordering here. Especially if you are like me and get cravings for taramosalata.

title: Very neutral and perfect for cheese and wine
text:
Because these are so neutral they are perfect for informal cheese and wine tastings. I love them because they allow the flavors and nuances of what you top them with to dominate the flavor profile.

Do be aware that these have a surprisingly high calorie count for a water cracker: 60 per four cracker serving. Fat is a very nominal 1 gram (and probably a little less), with carbs coming in at an unsurprising 10 grams. There is zero cholesterol, but 80mg of sodium per serving.

I love this with some of the softer cheeses like mascarpone or brie topped with roe.
