They are slightly brittle and require some care when spreading soft cheeses, but a thin slice of mozzarella topped with a basil leaf and a drizzle of olive oil is perfect. Or a soft cream cheese and lox with some capers.

The possibilities are endless, but the important thing about these is the neutral flavor that will not mask or interfere with what you use to spread or top them. They also work well for an informal cleansing between wines at informal tastings.

I always have these in my pantry for indulgences, guests and parties.

title: Great flavor without overpowering cheeses and spreads
text:
I purchase these locally and while this is not the only brand I serve, it's one that I love for savory spreads and some cheeses.

What I love is they are firm and will not crack when you spread a heavier cheese like brie, and the flavor tends towards the neutral side. What I mean by that is while there is a flavor, it's light and stays out of the way of flavors of the ingredients that you top them with. For example, when I serve these with a slice of thin, fresh mozzarella with a basil leaf and a touch of olive oil, I can taste the ingredients on top and the actual cracker's flavor does not dominate at all.

The nutrition information and ingredients are in the images at the top of this page (at the time of this review) so I will not repeat them. Do read those, however, if you care about such things. I do and have to admit that I am careful about how many of these I consume considering the calorie and carb content. Those are not terrible when compared to other crackers, but still a warning towards moderation.

These are perfect for parties or elaborate meals when you are putting out appetizers, meze, etc.

title: Not especially great caviar, but perfect for meze or antipasti
text:
This is a relatively low grade caviar, but is a perfect garnish for appetizers, meze and antipasti. I serve it on [[ASIN:B000FF96OQ Dare Breton Crackers, Original]] or [[ASIN:B0005Z7N2S Carr's Table Water Crackers]] with brie, mascarpone or a similar cheese (even plain cream cheese works). In that respect it's a great way to introduce roe to friends and guests who would not otherwise consider it.

Since I get this and the [[ASIN:B0005ZUEFQ Romanoff Caviar Black Lumpfish]] locally I am going to directly compare the two. This one is slightly less salty than the black roe, and is a little milder. The sodium is still pretty high at 340mg per tablespoon, but that is still manageable since a little of this goes a long way towards flavoring appetizers.

Aside from the sodium, nutritionally a jar contains four single tablespoon servings that are 100 calories each. Each serving contains zero fat, 2 carbs and 30mg of cholesterol. There are also additives that premium caviar does not contain, so this is best relegated to a garnish as I described above.

Although I gave this three stars that does not mean it's junk. I am grading it using decent caviar as a reference. As a garnish or topping this roe is not only worth the price, but is a good war to introduce friends to the joys of roe and caviar as a delicacy. I love it for what it is, but am grading it for what it isn't. If you like salty appetizers with a slightly fishy taste these will please.

title: Good garnish, but not for the trained palate
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review is about the product and not price or shipping. Basically this is caviar with training wheels. It's relatively inexpensive, and will please the uneducated palate in the same way as other gateway substances, but is not a caviar that someone who has developed a taste would appreciate.

That is not necessarily a bad thing. It has a slight caviar flavor that is adulterated by lemon, vinegar and - of all things - dextrose. On the other hand, someone who would not normally try a quality caviar would be able to appreciate this. And it does make a wonderful appetizer on a layer of brie spread on a quality cracker like [[ASIN:B0011CVP1O Carr's Table Water Crackers]] (or cream cheese or even mascarpone if you are truly adventurous.

Nutritionally a jar of these contains four single tablespoon servings that are 100 calories each. Each serving contains zero fat, 2 carbs, 30mg of cholesterol and 340mg of sodium. Where this falls short of a quality caviafr is the additives. Real caviar contains roe and salt. This contains, in order of percentage, roe, dextrose, salt, xanthan gum, lemon juice, caramel color, rice vinegar, and coloring.

As I said, this is caviar with training wheels. It will disappoint a connoisseur (or even someone who has an educated palate), but may also pique the interest in others who would not otherwise consider caviar. In that respect it has value, if not a flavor worthy of a good caviar.

title: Delicious, but watch the sodium
text:
I purchase this locally and surprisingly for about the same price as mail order when you buy in the twelve packs on this page. My review, though, will focus on the soup and not variables like price and shipping.

This is an occasional treat when I am too lazy to cook and want a simple meal of soup, a vegetable and olive plate and pita. For canned this is not bad. It has a distinct lemon taste that dominates, but is also complemented by spices and herbs (including turmeric). The pasta is a little on the skimpy side, but I prefer mine that way because it's actually more authentic. The chicken is just enough to flavor the broth, which is slightly thickened by the egg.

Nutritionally this has a little too much sodium. Each can contains 2.3 servings and each of those contains 830mg of sodium. If you get carried away and have two servings your cardiologist would have a fit. Ironically, it's the sodium content that adds to the flavor, so be careful. Otherwise, it's values are not terrible: 100 calories per serving, of which 15 are from the scant 2 grams of fat. Cholesterol is a reasonable 30mg, and carbs are 17 grams (the pasta is the culprit.) It also provides 5 grams of protein.

Overall, this is delicious for a canned soup and for some folks is even exotic. As long as you have no dietary restrictions for wheat, egg or soy, and only occasionally indulge in such high sodium soups, this is a real treat.

title: Exceptional quality
text:
When I was offered a review sample of this syrup I was curious to taste how it differed from a brand that I have used for a long time (Spring Tree). Both are Canadian products and both are Grade B.

To my palate there a slight difference between the two. This one was slightly less viscous and a little more subtle in flavor. However, the Spring Tree bottle had been opened previously, so the flavor difference may have been due to that.

I am familiar with various grades of Canadian and Vermont syrups, and they all come down to color and, to some degree, flavor. Frankly I find the differences so subtle and variable that as long as it's a Grade A or B from a known brand you cannot go wrong. To my palate this one is as good as my long time brand mentioned above. Not necessarily better, although I have to admit that this one is priced well below the Spring Tree brand and that makes it a value.

This is a high quality brand. it's labeled as GMO free and that alone is a compelling reason to consider it. Add in the price (less than twenty bucks for 16.9 ounces at the time of this review) and it becomes more attractive.

Bottom line: the real reason I awarded it five stars is there is a nominal difference - at best - between this and a brand that I have been using for years. The quality is definitely there and the price is right. You cannot go wrong.

title: Holy mole!
text:
When I received this as a review sample I just had to try a little on my finger. It had that rich, slightly bitter taste of an excellent grade of cacao. I stirred a little into a cup of coffee and it complemented it perfectly. I was impressed by how easily it dissolved into the brew as though it were sugar. But know that it's anything but sweet (no quality cacao is).

I know that this is supposed to have health benefits, some of which I know first hand from using cacao for quite some time. I have not had this long enough to say one way or the other. What I can say, though, is I have tried a lot of cacao in my life and this one is everything the product description claims as far as quality goes. In fact, if you make mole poblano from scratch, you'll appreciate this because it has a richness that you will not find in grocery store cacao or cocoa.

The reason why I awarded this five stars are it is genuine Criollo, it's non GMO (a big deal for me), and the intense flavor and characteristic bitter aftertaste. If you do a lot of gourmet cooking using cacao this is worth every penny. If you are looking for the health benefits, I am not going to make claims other than to say that this is an exceptionally high quality grade. For me it's going to be a cooking ingredient, something to enrich after dinner coffee for me and guests, and as a sprinkle over confections made with mascapone cheese. I am sure I'll think of other uses, but when this runs out I am purchasing another bag.

title: Great pick-me-up and refreshing
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is only going to address the drink and not variables like price or shipping costs.

There are a few brands of this sold locally and the reason why I love this one is it's made from GMO-free, natural ingredients. The flavor can be an acquired taste if you are trying it for the first time. To me it has the mellow/sweet flavor similar to putting a lime and a lemon lifesaver on your tongue.

It gives me a slight boost in energy, but the main reason why I consume it daily is it's soothing on the stomach. I've always used ginger when I have an upset stomach, but this is second best and very close. And for me it prevents reflux when I tend to overeat spicy food.

An eight ounce serving contains 85 calories and 22 grams of carbs (19 of which are from sugars). The only other nutritional value above nominal is sodium, which is a scant 17mg. When you compare this to most sodas the values are significantly healthier.

This contains mineral water as the main ingredient, followed by aloe vera powder (dissolved in the mixture) and aloe vera gel, which is suspended in the drink like pulp. So this is not some diluted concoction with a tiny amount of aloe vera - it has a significant amount of it. Other ingredients are organic cane sugar, aloe vera juice, honey, calcium lactate, citric acid, natural grape flavor, sodium citrate and gellan gum.

I use this more than fruit juices as a refreshing drink, and for me it's vastly superior to soda from a health perspective. If you find yourself addicted to sugar drinks that contain high-fructose corn syrup, caffeine, or a lot of artificial ingredients this is a wonderful substitute.

title: Popular with company
text:
I purchase these locally, so my review will be confined to the cakes and not price or shipping costs. The latter are always subject to change.

The reasons I gave these five stars include flavor, realistic serving size and sane nutritional values. These are delicious with coffee, tea or milk, and have a light inner cake with a cream layer, and a thick outer frosting.

Serving size is two cakes per individually sealed package. I was pleasantly surprised at that because similar brands have a tendency to claim ridiculously small serving sizes so that the nutritional values do not look so bad at a glance. Those, too, are better than most at 300 calories per pack (or 150 per cake, each of which is a generous two inches square and one inch thick). Fat for a two-cake pack is 120 calories weighing in at 13 grams, and carbs are 44 grams, of which 29 are sugar. The sodium is a little on the high side at 130mg per two-cake pack, which surprisingly has 1 gram of protein.

There are a big hit when I have guests, and make for a small desert when served with a half ounce of ice cream or frozen yogurt. I usually will have a single cake at a time when I am indulging myself, and store the other in a plastic, sealed container for a future indulgence. They stay fresh like that for at least a week (if they last that long.)

title: Excellent texture and flavor
text:
I purchase these locally so am going to focus on the product and not variables like price and shipping (which constantly change anyway.)

The trout in this can has a firm texture. The flesh has a slight reddish (or pinkish) tint, but you can clearly see the rainbow markings on the skin side of the filets. What I especially love is the smoke flavor is natural. Some smoked fish has a chemical taste, but these are as good as if you smoked them yourself. Another thing I love is there are no additives - the contents are only trout, olive oil and sea salt.

Nutritionally the sodium content is somewhat low at only 38mg per can, but the cholesterol is a little on the high side at 80mg. This should not be a problem with any but the strictest diets, though and those numbers are offset by nearly pure protein (about 23 grams). Calories are 173 per can, and fat (from both the trout and olive oil) is 11 grams, 3 of which are from saturated fats.

This is a delicious snack as well as a perfect tapas or antipasti when entertaining. The best part is the flavor, but the quality of the trout itself is exceptional for a smoked, canned fish.

title: Very good quality
text:
I purchase this at a local chain store and the price here is about on par. However, regardless of price this is one of the only canned pulpo a la marinara that I will buy because other brands typically have very chewy octopus. The ones in this can are surprisingly tender.

There is a slight piquant flavor that I further enhance with a few drops of [[ASIN:B003TRY4PI Peri Peri Portuguese Hot Sauce]]. Even without the sauce the flavor of this out of the can is savory, with a slight touch of saltiness. That comes from the 250mg of sodium that is in a can. The calorie count is not terrible at 110, and the fat is a scant 5 grams.

If you are watching your cholesterol this has 40mg, which is not bad. On the plus side, there is a whopping 13 grams of protein, so if you are on a high protein diet this is a delicious way to augment that. Do be aware that this is packed in soybean oil, so if you have issues with soy you may want to consider alternative brands.

I use this as a topping over rice, or as a snack. A can with a quarter cup of rice, some fresh or steamed vegetables and a little peri peri sauce make an excellent and surprisingly filling meal.

title: Guilt free and delicious
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review will focus on the product and not address pricing or shipping. This is guilt-free because even though it still runs a little high in sodium the calories and fat content are very low. Note up front that as a part of the process this tuna may contain traces of soy, eggs and wheat. I believe this has more to do with the facilities than any additives because the listed ingredients are simply tuna, water and salt.

The tuna is firm with excellent texture. The flavor is perfect to my palate and this makes a great antipasto or tapas. I enjoy mine with just a touch of freshly ground black pepper and a squeeze of lemon. In the past I had been enjoying the brand's sibling product - [[ASIN:B000YMFVQC Tonnino Yellowfin Tuna Fillets in Olive Oil]] - but this one is so much healthier and as delicious without the olive oil. Nutritionally this jar contains four 50 calorie servings, although more realistically it is two servings so I am going to call it 100 calories per 3.2 ounces - about half of the jar - twenty of which are from fat.

Fat content is very low at 2 grams per 3.2 ounces, but sodium is relatively high at 400mg. cholesterol is 16mg so that is well within acceptable limits. Protein is a whopping 28 grams per half jar, so it gives a nice boost of high nutritional value as long as you go not smother the tuna with mayonnaise or olive oil.

If you love premium cuts of tuna, but want to watch your caloric and fat intakes this is a perfect way to enjoy it. I have completely switched over to this one from the companion product mentioned above and rate it as a solid five stars.

title: It's all in the grind
text:
This is not pure coffee - there are additives like cocoa and other 'spices' - but it is authentic. I purchase mine locally and it comes in a bag. The key to this coffee is the grind, which is perfect for the filter in a [[ASIN:B008A0932S Vietnamese Traditional Coffee Phin Filter]].

In addition to the grind, the way you brew your coffee is going to make a big difference in taste. Unlike a single-cup Melita method the phin filter works best when you bring the water to boiling. If you are a coffee connoisseur this is the opposite of the just below boiling way you make other coffees. Also, you start with a small amount of water to saturate the grounds and start the drip before increasing the flow. If you try using the Melita method of pouring in all of the water, the grounds will not properly brew and this stuff will taste rather horrible.

Although I usually prefer coffee hot, this is best for ca phe sua da, which is iced coffee and condensed sweet milk. To be honest, I have tried this as regular hot coffee and do not much care for it. However, with enough condensed milk to get a cafe au lait color this is excellent when the mixture is poured over ice in a tall iced tea glass and stirred until it's truly cold.

If you love iced coffee this is well worth trying as long as you have the patience to make it correctly. If you try to take shortcuts you will be disappointed. Done right and you will become an addict

title: Perfect for Southern palates
text:
Note that this is a very coarse grind, so do not try brewing it in a paper filter type maker, and definitely not in Keurig or espresso type makers. The grind is all wrong for those. Use with a French press or a percolator (I use a [[ASIN:B00005NCWQ Farberware Classic Stainless Steel Percolator]] specifically for this coffee.

Because the chicory in this blend is fairly prominent, I usually make my coffee au lait style. Actually, I make it more like cafe Cubano with scalded or steamed milk, but that is a personal preference. If you have never tried a chicory blended coffee you may want to at least use a little cream or milk and a touch of sugar, even if you normally take your coffee black. Once you grow accustomed to the chicory you can cut back on the additives until you can enjoy it straight up. I'll forewarn you, though, that once you develop a taste for this you will get cravings at the oddest times.

Chicory in coffee was practically the de facto blend when I was growing up in Virginia. It's a traditional flavor throughout the south and especially New Orleans. I do not often drink this coffee, but when I have a craving this is the only brand that I trust.

If you are from New Orleans I am guessing that you associate this with beignets. I prefer mine with a palmier or one of my favorites, [[ASIN:B003H2IDXE Stella D'oro Original Breakfast Treats]].

title: For those who prefer less fishy
text:
I am giving this five stars for the quality of the sardines and the fact that it is mild enough in flavor for folks who would normally eschew sardines. To my palate, though, they were not as interesting. However that is subjective and does not warrant downgrading the rating.

From a flavor perspective these are close to kippered snacks minus the saltiness and smoke. I love the thick cuts of the sardines, which are almost pink. The texture is also firm. In fact I had to read the ingredients to make sure these were sardines because of the larger size and the flavor.

Nutritional values are relatively low in sodium at 260mg per serving (each can is a single serving), and these sardines are not particularly salty. Cholesterol is 13mg and fat (mainly from the olive oil) is 15 grams, three of which are saturated). The key is the protein, which is a healthy 20 grams, making a full can serving significant source. Since a can is a scant 210 calories (130 of which are from fat), this is a relatively healthy snack, or with soup and salad, a light meal that is packed with protein.

While I mentioned that this is not to my palate, I still keel a few cans handy for snacks. These are a lot healthier than most mid day (or night) fare, and I made mine a little more interesting with a few drops of [[ASIN:B0001590P0 Nando's Hot Peri-Peri Sauce]].

title: High quality tuna, but some caveats
text:
This is a cut above most canned tuna from the name brands, but there are a few gotchas. First, though I want to disclose that I purchase this locally so my review will not address variables like price and shipping.

The tuna is wild caught from Costa Rica and is firm, flavorful and slightly pink in color. I love the texture and it makes a great antipasto or tapas. The olive oil is just enough to pack it, so it's not especially oily. The oil is also decent quality considering it is used as a packing agent.

Caveats that I mentioned in the title are: it may contain trace amounts of egg or soy per the label. If you have allergic reactions to either you will want to take that into account. Each jar contains four servings, each of which is 90 calories (20 of which are from fat.) Sodium is a little on the high side at 200mg per serving, as is cholesterol at 26mg. Those numbers are not terrible, but worth noting if you have restrictions. Protein, though, is a respectable 16 grams per serving.

While this is a cut above most caned tuna, it's still a medium high quality tuna. If you want a better cut of tuna I recommend [[ASIN:B003AKJPEY Tonnino Ventrescas In Olive Oil, 6.7-Ounce]]. However, for what this is, it's excellent and worthy of five stars on my rating scale.

title: Superior roast and grind
text:
I purchase this locally so my review will focus on the coffee and not discuss pricing or shipping costs. One of my passions is coffee and this brand is exceptional to my palate. The beans from which this is ground are premium Arabica.

If you love Colombian coffee then you will enjoy the full body and slightly bright acidity of this one. The aroma is the first thing that hits you when you open the bag, and after brewing it adds to the richness of the coffee itself.

The grind is very fine, but not completely powdery like some Cuban and European grinds that I enjoy. This will brew perfectly in a [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti 6800 Moka Express 6-Cup Stovetop Espresso Maker]] or an electric espresso maker, but will also brew in a French press due to the slightly grainier grind. I have also brewed this in a paper filter style electric coffee maker and the resulting cup retained its body and slight acidity.

Although I test a lot of brands and cultivars of coffee I only have a handful of favorites. This one is so uniformly excellent that it's one of the few brands that qualify as my house coffee. If you love Colombian coffees this is one to try.

title: Delicious but with some caveats
text:
I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the soup and not address pricing or shipping. I purchased this and a few other flavors on a whim and was pleasantly surprised by the complex flavors, which are balanced and delicious.

It's easy to detect the ginger and lemongrass - just enough to make it interesting - and the slightly piquant chilis. Those lend authenticity to the flavor, and the different types of rice make it surprisingly hearty. This and a salad make a quick and relatively light lunch. This is not authentically Thai, but is inspired by flavors from Southeast Asia.

The caveat is the extremely high sodium content, which is a whopping 770mg per seven ounce serving. If you have restrictions a single serving will push you near your daily limit. Each serving is also 250 calories, which makes for a light meal, but over half of those (130) are from fat, which comes in at 14 grams. Cholesterol is 25mg, and carbs are 21 grams, nine of which are from sugars.

While the above nutritional values look a little bleak at first glance they are not terrible when compared to other processed or fast foods. Indeed, aside from the sodium they are better than most.

Personally, I have to watch my dietary intake so this soup is an infrequent guilty pleasure. It's also fast to prepare 90 seconds in a microwave), and delicious.

title: Slightly exotic flavor and decent nutritional values
text:
I purchased this locally so this review will stick to the actual product. This goes perfectly heated over basmati rice, or even cold as the main ingredient tossed into a salad.

What I love is the slight tang, the dense texture of the tilapia pieces and their delicate flavor that you can taste through the tomato sauce base and the chutney. There is sufficient saltiness that you do not have to add any to a dish, which is a plus if you have sodium restrictions. Another thing I love is Bumble Bee is generous with tilipia, which has the largest percentage in the ingredient list. And although this is a canned, prepared product it's heart-healthy and has impressive nutritional values considering how delicious it is.

Nutritionally these are high in protein at 13 grams per 100 gram serving. There is also 240mg of potassium per serving, which is good for my personal diet. Each serving is 160 calories or which 60 are from fat (which comes in at 7 grams.) Carbs are a little on the high side at 12 grams, and nine of those are from sugars. Cholesterol is a manageable 30mg and sodium is relatively low at 280mg.

I will put a complete list of ingredients in a comment to this review so that you can see exactly what is in the can. If you love tilapia, and especially prepared with a flavorful recipe, you will probably love this.

title: Rich and medium body
text:
I purchased a bag of this coffee on a whim at a local market. I was expecting something along the lines of a rich and full bodied Cuban style coffee, but found this to be markedly different.

While this is rich like a quality Cuban roast, this coffee has a medium body and very low acidity. To my palate it's the perfect balance of rich and smooth, with a hint of earthiness and a moderate depth. It's the depth that sets it apart from the much deeper Cubans.

This is an extremely fine grind that brews best in a moka pot like the [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti Stovetop Espresso Maker]]. I tried it with a French press and it did not turn out as good. Ditto a conventional cone type brewer.

Overall this is a little off the beaten path if you are accustomed to Cuban (or even Puerto Rican) style coffee roasts. It's a little lighter in body, but is still full flavored and rich, and is a dream come true if you value smoothness in a cup of coffee.

title: Among the best I have ever tasted
text:
I love kippered snacks, but quit eating them when most companies started using artificial enhancers and preservatives. These are made the traditional way and contain only the herring, canola oil, salt and smoke. The latter is important because I have tried brands that had a funny aftertaste as though the smoke was more artificial flavor than the actual smoking process.

You get two pieces of herring that have been split, yielding two filets per piece. Each piece is about 4.5 inches long, so there is a lot of smoked fish per can. Please see my uploaded photos for what these actually look like.

Another thing I love is the lack of any dye or other color agents like annato. I have uploaded two customer-supplied images to show that the flesh is natural colored. The lack of additives makes the flavor truly delicious. More importantly, the skin has been uniformly smoked, and the texture of the herring filets is firm. In other words, a high quality kippered herring.

Nutritionally these are about on par with other brands: there are 3.5 140 calorie servings per can, of which 100 of those calories are from fat. I round this to a simple three servings. The filets are packed with a copious amount of their own juices and canola oil. I thoroughly drain mine and pat the filets with a paper towel to cut out some of the fat from the oil. Total fat is eleven grams, with 25mg of cholesterol. Sodium - as expected - is a relatively high 280mg per serving (or 840mg per can), so be careful if you have restrictions. Each can contains 36 grams of protein - twelve grams per serving - which is a major plus.

Bottom line: if you love kippered snacks these are among the best I have tried. I purchase mine locally, but if I could not get them that way I would order them here because of the quality and flavor.

title: Interesting twist on hot sauce
text:
What is interesting to me about this sauce is it comes from Costa Rica, which is not known for extremely hot sauces. If I were blindfolded I would swear this was from Trinidad/Tobago based on the heat and flavor profile.

The piquant quality is typical of Scotch bonnets: mellow - but intense - burn that slowly spreads. There is no real bite to this like in many Mezoamerican sauces. It's more typical of Caribbean sauces that have the heat, but it builds. Heat is on par with medium hot sauces from Jamaica or Trinidad.

It's the flavor that sets this apart. The citrus from the lime juice and citric acid give it dominating tartness, and the tropical fruit (papayas and passion fruit) provide a hint of sweetness. I love the subtle effect that is a nice change from the cane sugar that is used in many Jamaican sauces. The savory component of the flavor profile comes from the carrots, garlic and onion, which also thicken the sauce. Finally there is a touch of saltiness from the 115mg of sodium per teaspoon serving. That is somewhat high, but not quite a red flag if you have sodium restrictions. All other nutritional values are so nominal that they register zero.

If you love a decent amount of heat and a lot of flavor you will probably love this sauce. It's definitely a 'must try' if you are starting to get bored with Scotch bonnet sauces from the northern Caribbean and you want to explore other favors.

title: A wonderful way to start or end a day
text:
I became a fan of this brand when a friend brought me back a bag from Costa Rica. The grind is fine and perfect for a moka pot like my [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti 6800 Moka Espresso Maker]]. If you correctly brew it in such a put you are practically guaranteed a great cup of coffee.

I want to note that this is more than just coffee grounds - it contains about ten percent sugar. If you are a coffee aficionado you may think this is akin to flavored coffee. It's not. There isn't a sweetness as much as a caramel taste that some pure coffees exhibit in their flavor profile.

The basic characteristics is it's strong, but with the richness and smoothness of a Cuban or other Latin style coffee. That makes it significantly different from the slightly bitter European blends. In those coffees the slight bitter taste is prized and I, too, enjoy it. But I am particularly fond of the Cuban coffees because of their richness and this Costa Rican coffee is every bit the equal of the best Cuban grinds to my palate.

While the grind is perfect for moka style brewing that I mentioned above this also brews well in a French press and even normal coffee makers.

title: Moderate heat and heavy flavor
text:
While I usually prefer hotter sauces this one has a focused flavor profile that appeals to my palate.

The piquant aspect is relatively mild compared to Jamaican and Trinidad/Tobago sauces that are also made from habaneros. The dominating component of the flavor profile is sour/tart from the lime and vinegar. That makes this sauce perfect for adding a kick to salsas, and it's excellent on salmon. I rarely eat meat, but I suspect that it would also enhance a burger.

There is a slight savory component that comes from the base of carrots, onions and garlic, but it is subtle. Plus this is not salty, so if you are accustomed to sauces that are heavy in sodium you may find this one lacking in that area. For me it's perfect because I have to watch my sodium intake. This comes in at a mere 55mg of sodium, which is half to a third of other habanero sauces I have tried.

If you love a touch of heat and maximum flavor this is an outstanding sauce. It is not XXXXtra hot, but it's extra delicious. If you want something with some real heat and a slightly fuller flavor profile try [[ASIN:B002ATCFX4 Melinda's Naga Jolokia Hot Sauce]].

title: A delicious snack with some nutritional red flags
text:
Two things: (1) I purchase this locally so my review is going to focus on the smoked trout and not address price of shipping costs. (2) When reading my comments about nutrition factor in that nearly all canned fish have high sodium and all that are packed in oil are high in fat. That is the nature of the product.

The reason I gave this five stars is the flavor is absolutely delicious and the texture of the trout indicates that it is of the highest quality.

One thing that I love is the 'smoked' flavor is natural. Some smoked fish taste as though they were dipped in a chemical. This product tastes like cold smoked fish should.

Another thing I love is the pieces have been deboned. There is skin on one side, which is easy to remove if you prefer completely skinless, but is also delicious to those of us who prefer it on the fish.

The nutritional red flags are high fat, sodium and cholesterol. A can is 260 calories of which 140 are from the 16 grams of fat. Sodium is 600mg, which is pretty high if you have restrictions. Cholesterol comes in at 90mg per can.

On the plus side there is a whopping 28 grams of protein per can, so this makes for a protein rich snack or light lunch. In fact, the nutritional gotchas can be be offset if you enjoy a can with a simple salad.

Despite the issues I cited I enjoy these on occasion because in moderation they are not harmful and they are irresistibly delicious to my palate.

title: Best of old and new world coffee
text:
I purchased this at a local chain called Fresh Fruit and Produce and fell immediately in love. I vacillate between European grinds that have a slightly bitter after taste and the Cuban coffees that are rich and smooth. This one is the best of both worlds.

This coffee has a subtle acidity that gives it the slight and highly desirable (to Italian palates) bitterness. But it has the body and richness of a great Cuban coffee. For folks like myself who love both this is a perfect bean. If you are more of a Cuban or Puerto Rican coffee aficionado you may find this to be a little rough. However, if you love European espresso, but have always wished for a deeper and richer cup this is pure heaven.

One thing I love is the aroma when this is brewing. Itn fills my house. The grind is perfect for my [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti 6800 Moka Espresso Maker]], as well as Melita style brewing. It's just a little too fine for French Press pots in my opinion.

In fact I am enjoying a cup as I write this review and it's fantastic to my palate.

title: Piquent and brimming with flavor
text:
I purchased this at a local World Market so this review will not address price or shipping.

What I love is not only the balance of heat and flavor, but how complete the flavor profile is. Aside from the dominating piquant qualities, this sauce has a pronounced sour/tart flavor that comes from the lime and vinegar. It is a little strong on the vinegar, but that is balanced out with papaya, carrots, onions and garlic that gives the savory component. There is a touch of saltiness too.

The pepper has a nice bite to it and the heat persists. I have been eating very hot sauces for decades, so I did not find this to be unbearably piquant like some pepper extracts that are all heat and no flavor. I use about a teaspoon in a five ounce serving of beans, but some friends have a much lower tolerance so start with a few drops and work your way up the first time you try this. If you love extremely hot sauces you will probably not be disappointed.

While the flavor profile is complete across the spectrum the nutrition profile is one dimensional. Everything but sodium is nominal and is listed as zero, including calories per serving. Sodium is 150mg per teaspoon (5 ml), which is not terrible considering the heat this packs.

If you are accustomed to Scotch bonnets and habaneros this one is going to be an eye-opener because the first taste will figuratively grab you by the throat. The flavor, though, is reason enough to award five stars.

title: Delicious and reasonably healthy in moderation
text:
I purchase these locally so this review will focus solely on the nuts and nutritional values and not address price or shipping.

What I love is these are premium nuts - cashews, almonds, Brazil nuts, pecans and pistachios in that order. While I love peanuts, sometimes I need to take a break from them and this mix is perfect for me. However, if you have allergies to peanuts note that there may be some contamination from those because they same equipment processes a variety of ground and tree nuts. Also the oil used in the roasting process can be either peanut oil or cottonseed oil or both.

For me the fact that these nuts are roasted with very little oil is a big plus because I need to watch my fat intake. The sodium comes in at 80mg per ounce. That is not terrible, but does mean that you need to consume these in moderation if you have sodium restrictions.

Nutritionally an ounce is 170 calories, of which 130 are from the 14 grams of fat. There is no cholesterol and only 7 grams of carbs per serving. Despite some of the values these are a healthy between-meals snack that suppresses my appetite. Of course you may react differently, but regardless of the nutritional values these nuts are a cut above most mixed nuts that use peanuts for a filler, with a lot more salt and oil.

title: Amazing flavor
text:
I was given a can of these by a friend so am not going to address price or shipping. If you love spicy sardines these are the gold standard in my opinion.

Here are the reasons why these immediately became my favorite. First, the quality of the sardines is the best I have ever seen or tasted. They are firm with a perfect texture. In fact they are literally plump and it's obvious that the brand uses only the highest quality fish. A plus for me is they are also boned.

The pili-pili in which the sardines are packed is authentic. There are interesting nuances that come from ingredients such as carrots and pickle and unspecified spices. The heart, though is the chilis that are very piquant. I have tried other brands of sardines and chili peppers and they were good, but not as piquant or as delicious as this.

Another indication of the quality is that the olive oil is extra virgin. Again, other brands that I have tried sometimes cut corners here, but you can tell from the flavor that these are the gold standard for sardines.

If you are a sardine lover you owe it to yourself to try these. The only downside is you may become addicted and they carry a premium price from every place that sells them. To me they are well worth it.

title: Nice spice but a little high in sodium
text:
If you are watching your sodium these will have to be an occasional treat because these come in at 250mg. Not horrible or a show stopper, but still a little on the high side.

I love the slight spiciness. These are not blazing hot. The chilis give the sardines a little bite without overdoing it. The fish are very high quality with a nice, firm texture. But it's the flavor that makes this a pleasure. Part comes from the high quality olive oil used in packing, and part from the fact that there are no chemicals of preservatives. Aside from the five sardines per can you are getting hot peppers, olive oil and salt. Simple and delicious.

Aside from the sodium these contain 180 calories, 5 grams of fat and 35mg of cholesterol. On the plus side there are fifteen grams of protein.

If you love sardines these are a cut above most brands and have been perfectly prepared and packed. I purchase mine locally so I am not going to address variable factors such as price or shipping. I will say that they are premium quality.

title: A seasoning and a condiment
text:
They should have named it 'pinakamasarap' because this is perfect for adding a wonderful flavor to soups, rice or any other dish. I have used it on ramen instead of the flavor packets that come with them and it make them the perfect fast snack. I have also used it as a condiment on pancit and it added a wonderful flavor.

My favorite way to use this is to season ginisang gulay when I am preparing it. I love sitaw at kalabasa, but this also works well with ampalaya and other vegetables.

Of course this has some ingredients that may put some folks off. For one thing it contains MSG, which many people are cutting out of their diets. It also contains salt, so if you are also using patis as a condiment this could spike your sodium intake. Other ingredients are sugar, chicken fat, garlic, onion, egg and meat powder.

The mix manages to capture the true flavors of the Philippines and add them to any food on which you sprinkle a little of this (or add when cooking.) I do not use this all of the time because of the sodium content, but when I do it's truly pinakamasarap.

title: Not healthy, but delicious and an energy boost
text:
Note: I purchase these locally so my review is not going to address price or shipping.

If you are active this is a quick and delicious way to boost your energy. Do not be fooled, however, into thinking that this is good for weight loss or overall healthy eating. It's not, although it's a cut above candy, donuts and other treats that we use for quick energy. Also, this is not terrible when taken in moderation. One for breakfast will kickstart you, and if you have a fast metabolism these are wonderful.

If you love cashews and walnuts mixed with apple flavor cranberries and cinnamon you are going to love the taste. Note that these are chewy instead of crunchy, so they are more like a fruit bar than a granola one.

The reason I mentioned the health aspects is the nutritional values get low marks. Each bar contains 160 calories, of which 50 are from fat. It also contains 25 grams of carbs, of which 14 are from sugar, so if you are restricting carb intake this is a fairly high number. It is also moderately high in sodium at 80mg.

Don't let the nutritional picture I painted deter you because if you are active, have no dietary restrictions and/or enjoy these in moderation (like one a day) they are a nice treat. I have found them to be a perfect way to start the day when I am low on energy, but I consume about one a week.

title: Delicious agua fesca, but contains aspartame
text:
I am not knocking aspartame, but some folks will not consume any product made with it, so I want to get the fact that this mix contains it out in the open. I also want to disclose that I purchase this locally, so am not going to address price or shipping - those are variables.

What I love about this particular mix is it makes a perfect blend of both the sweet and the tart. It's simple to make: I add a tablespoon of this mix per eight ounces of water and it dissolves completely with minimal stirring. The directions call for three quarters of a tablespoon, but I found that to be a little weak. Experiment and find your own ratio. I have also used fresh quarters of meyer lemons to add more citrus and tartness to the flavor. I think that is a perfect combination to go with a drink made from this mix.

Aside from the aspartame, the main ingredients include sugar and dextrose, and other ingredients that I will include in a comment to this review so you can see exactly what this mix contains. Nutritionally this comes in at a reasonable 45 calories if you use the three quarters of a tablespoon to eight ounces of water ratio. The carbs for that ratio come in at 11 grams, of of which are from sugars.

If the values above are acceptable to your personal dietary habits you will find this to be a delicious and refreshing drink - especially if you love tart citrus. It's simple and quick to make, and hits the spot on humid days.

title: Tart, refreshing and even has pulp!
text:
I purchase this locally at WalMart so my review will only focus on the mix and not address price or shipping.

This is delicious, especially if you love the tart/sour flavor of tamarinds. I acquired a taste for tamarinds when I lived in the Philippines and through many visits to Thailand. In those places they were used for cooking, but this agua fresca from Mexico uses them in a refreshing drink.

What I love is the relatively low calorie count for such a sweet drink: 60 per a single tablespoon that is mixed in eight ounces of water. The contrast of sweet from the thirteen grams of sugar (cane sugar and dextrose) against the tart/sour taste of the tamarind is interesting. In fact it's a perfect balance to two main elements of the flavor profile to my palate. Nutritionally there are no other numbers of concern - everything is so nominal that they register as zero (sodium, cholesterol, etc.); a plus is a serving contains ten percent of recommended daily values for vitamin C.

Another thing I love is this drink, once mixed, actually has pulp. And mixing it is easy because it dissolves and blends into water with little effort. If you like a touch of sour this is a perfect drink and one of the more refreshing aguas frescas I have tried on a hot and humid day.

title: A delicious agua fresca, but watch the calories!
text:
I purchase this at my local WalMart, so this review will discuss only the mix and not price or shipping costs.

Pluses include this is one of my personal favorites among all of the agua frescas, and it is easy to mix. The combination rice flour and cinnamon for some reason appeals to my palate, and I find this to be refreshing and even rich tasting. I have never tried making this from scratch, but I suspect it is not easy.

The cinnamon is strong without being overpowering. The actual mixing is easy because this easily and quickly dissolves into the water (a tablespoon per eight ounces.) I use a heaping tablespoon because it adds a touch of richness to the flavor without compromising the refreshing taste.

As much as I love this I have to watch my intake because this is relatively high in calories and carbs. There is also more fat and cholesterol than I would like. An 8 ounce glass mixed per directions comes in at 135 calories, of which 18 are from the two grams of fat. Cholesterol is 10mg, which isn't terrible but still something I need to watch at my age. Sodium is a negligible 30mg, but carbs are 26 grams, all of which are from sugar.

If you are active and nor saddled with dietary restrictions this is a wonderful and refreshing drink - especially on a hot, humid day. However, if you have to watch calories and carbs you can still enjoy this, but moderation is recommended.

title: Not only healthy, but also delicious
text:
I purchased a bottle of this on a whim at my local Publix (a Central Florida grocery chain) and was simply amazed. I expected the flavor to be lacking, but it was the opposite. Despite it being unsweetened, the natural sweetness from the tomatoes was near the top of the flavor profile.

Compared to regular ketchup this actually enhances the flavors of just about anything you would use ketchup on. There is a slight tartness from the cider vinegar that balances out the sweetness, and there is sufficient salt to add that element to the flavor profile as well. The savory part of the taste experience will come from whatever you are using this on.

Nutritionally this is a great substitute from other processed condiments. A tablespoon - 15 grams - contains only give calories, a single gram of carbs and only 70mg of sodium. I had cut regular ketchup from my diet because of the nutritional nightmare most brands turn out to be. This has allowed me to enjoy ketchup again and I will continue purchasing and using it. If you think that just because it's healthy that you have to sacrifice flavor you are in for a very pleasant surprise - it's actually better tasting.

title: Love the flavor, but there is much more to this gum
text:
I am a recent convert to gum. My dental hygienist gave me a sample and told me of the way it promoted good dental hygiene. I loved the flavor and subsequently tried most of the Orbit gums until I settled on Wintermint.

According to a card enclosed with my sample this gum works by causing increased saliva, which in turn neutralizes acids. Another point made by the card is that the increased saliva can also help prevent early tooth damage and decay. While I am sure most chewing gums will trigger an increase in saliva, this one is sugar free.

Nutritionally a stick of this is less than five calories, contains no sodium, and only a single gram of carbs. It's sugar-free (otherwise I doubt it would have the ringing endorsements of the American Dental Association), and it leaves my mouth fresh. I typically chew a piece between meals to keep my mouth fresh and to add one more layer to my dental hygiene regimen. It's too early to tell how effective it is in the long term, but my mouth feels cleaner.

title: Delicious, but needs to be consumed in moderation
text:
I purchase these nuts locally, so this review will focus on the nut mix and not price or shipping.

The mix itself is a wonderful blend of nuts that complement one another in both taste and texture. I was surprised at how the pistachios seemed to not only dominate the flavor of the mix, but to also enhance the flavors of the other five nut types. That's a revelation considering that the pistachios are third on the list of ingredients. Peanuts are the number one ingredient, and since I love that nut I was naturally drawn to this blend of nuts.

The implied warning in my title is based on the fact that this mix is not especially heart healthy. Consider that of the 170 calories per serving, 140 are from fat. Worse, of the 15 grams of fat, 1.5 grams are saturated, and the sodium count is 45mg. Not exactly heart healthy - at least according to my cardiologist. Of course, the recommended daily amount to consume is 1.5 ounces. That sounds great in theory, but try holding yourself to that piddling amount after tasting the masterful blend.

If you are not constrained by diet or sodium restrictions this is a sinfully delicious mix (assuming that you love peanuts and have no allergies to them.) I have managed to control my intake and they are one of my occasional self-rewards.

title: For those of us who insist on ingredient purity
text:
I was drawn to this because it contains the herbs and spices and nothing else - including salt. I was not disappointed. The mix is aromatic, which indicates both high quality ingredients and freshness. To be honest, I purchased this to experiment.

Traditional pickles do not interest me. I like them just fine, but the sodium that is required to make them well exceeds what my dietary restrictions allow. However, I do pickle garlic and Thai peppers in white vinegar to season my food and wanted to see if this mix would complement that. To a point it does. The dill is a little strong, but I knew that beforehand. And since this mix is designed for pickling cucumbers, the way the dill is placed in the flavor profile is perfect for that use.

The other flavors perfectly complemented the garlic and peppers, though. Since I am using pure vinegar instead of dilluting it with water a little of this mix goes a long way. I am guessing that one .4 ounce packet will easily pickle a gallon or more of pickles. At some point I may try pickling cucumbers with this mix - minus the salt - and see how that works out. For now, though, I like the flavor it imparts to my garlic and peppers, even if the strong dill flavor is not a perfect complement.

title: Actually promotes good dental hygiene
text:
To be honest I am not a gum chewer - or wasn't until a recent visit to my dentist. After a cleaning the hygienist gave me a 'goodie' bag with samples of products that she recommended to promote good hygiene. Among them was this gum.

I love the flavor (I have tried them all), but what I truly love is the fact that it's sugar free. According to a card enclosed with my sample this gum works by causing increased saliva, which in turn neutralizes acids. Another point made by the card is that the increased saliva can also help prevent early tooth damage and decay. While I am sure most chewing gums will trigger an increase in saliva, this one is sugar free.

Nutritionally a stick of this is less than five calories, contains no sodium, and only a single gram of carbs. It's rare to find something that tastes good and is good for you as well. The intense blast of flavor makes this a pleasure to chew. The fact that it is endorsed by the American Dental Association as a valid part of good dental hygiene is a big plus to me and reason enough to use this after every meal - which I now do.

title: A nice alternative to Tabasco sauce
text:
Disclaimer: I purchase this locally so my review will focus on the sauce and not price or shipping.

I have found this to be an excellent substitute for the Tabasco style sauces on the market. To my palate it's a more exotic alternative to Tabasco, but is more piquant. I would say that this is about twice as hot as Tabasco, but mild compared to most of the Caribbean sauces on the market. Do bear in mind that 'hot' is a relative term. What one person finds hot another may find mild. I am using Tabasco as a reference because US buyers are usually most familiar with that brand and style.

This sauce stands out in the flavor and the blend of peppers. Ingredients simply list unspecified spices, but I can detect what may be tamarind because there is a tang that you cannot get with just vinegar. There is also a little sweetness that I am guessing is cane sugar since nearly all Jamaican hot sauces contain it. It is salty with 80mg of sodium per serving, which is almost triple that of Tabasco, as well as most other Jamaican hot sauces.

The bite this sauce exhibits is probably from the habanero peppers that are blended with the Scotch bonnet peppers. Once the initial bite subsides the piquant component has the characteristic build and spread glow of the Scotch bonnet peppers. For me that is the best of both worlds because I love the initial bite of North American hot sauces, but also enjoy the slow burn and spread of the Caribbean ones.

Bottom line: If you love Tabasco sauce, but want to try something a little bolder in heat with an exotic flavor this is a perfect place to start.

title: Tart with moderate heat
text:
First let me disclose that I purchase this locally for less than three bucks, so my review will stick to the hot sauce and not the price or shipping.

This is a delightful sauce for folks who like moderate heat and a touch of tartness. By 'moderate heat' I mean that this is definitely hotter than Tabasco, which is at the low end of the scale, but nowhere near as hot as some sauces. It has the typical slow burn and spread characteristic of Scotch bonnet peppers and practically no bite. I am guessing that the peppers have been aged because they are particularly slow acting and somewhat mellow.

The flavor profile is heavily biased towards piquant and tart, but the sugar adds to the flavor as do the spices. I cannot pick out which spices, but can taste a touch of what seems like ginger and perhaps cumin. While this is salty the actual sodium is only 15mg per teaspoon, which is perfect for my sodium-restricted diet.

I love the pulp and seeds that are suspended in the sauce when you shake it. While this it not the thickest sauce on the market it does have medium viscosity for a Jamaican sauce. I use it strictly as a condiment because the one time I trued cooking with it (making red beans) it made the dish too sour. Otherwise, this goes perfectly on eggs, pizza, or anything else on or in which you normally use hot sauce.

title: Pure and delicious
text:
Disclaimer: I purchase this locally so my review will only address these strained tomatoes and not price or shipping.

This is the real thing if you are seeking an authentic Italian tomato puree. First, this is the best quality passata di pomodoro I have come across, including making my own from canned San Marzano tomatoes imported from Italy. That says a lot. And quite frankly, these are better than most vine ripened tomatoes I get here in Central Florida. There are exceptions, but for the most part this passata beats anything I can make from scratch.

Enough raving. What I love about these is you get tomatoes and nothing but. They have been perfectly strained with a consistency of a quality puree. It's sweet the way a sun drenched tomato should be, and there are absolutely no additives or preservatives. There is a touch of natural sodium, which comes in at 10mg per half cup serving. The tomatoes are free of any genetically modified organisms (GMO). In other words, this is a puree that you would have enjoyed before genetic modifications entered the picture and chemicals and additives became a way of life.

Do not let the box throw you - we are not discussing fine wines, but tomatoes and the packaging is one of the reasons the tomatoes are so pure because even the box is pure being certified as BPA free.

title: Some heat, but a very simple flavor profile (and weird color)
text:
This sauce has a simple and straightforward flavor profile - piquant and salty with a touch of sour - that makes it excellent for adding zing to some dishes. I have to admit that the bright green color put me off. When I tried it on scrambled eggs I could not get the Dr. Seuss phare, 'I do not like green eggs and ham' put of my head.

Color aside, this has the slow burn and spread heat that is characteristic of Scotch bonnet peppers. It is smooth and I would call the heat medium, but that is a subjective description because I have a high tolerance for spicy sauces. What seems to be missing - to my palate - is the typical fruitiness of Scotch bonnets. That lack is also part of the reason for the simple flavor profile.

The sauce is relatively thin and pours easily. It's smooth in consistency and pulp-free. The sodium level at 40mg per teaspoon is at the lower end of the scale for hot sauces, so that is a big plus for me since I have sodium restrictions. All other nutritional values are so nominal that they register as zero on the label (except carbs, which is 1 gram.)

Because this is simple and straightforward it works well with eggs and adds zing to salsas and soups. Sometimes the more complex and piquant sauces from Jamaica are too heavy for some dishes whereas this one is perfect for lighter fare where you do not want the sauce to compete with the food.

title: Pure. Tomatoes and nothing but!
text:
Disclaimer: I purchase these locally so will not be addressing price or shipping in this review. My focus is on the tomatoes and these are my favorites when I need to whip up a sugo or salsa, or even tomato soup.

The reason I love them is this box contains nothing but tomatoes. No preservatives, added sodium or anything else that would detract from the pure, sweet flavor of high quality tomatoes. In fact you can almost taste the Italian sun in the flavor. I also love the consistency that makes this perfect for salsas.

In all honesty I prefer these to locally [in central Florida] grown fresh tomatoes most of the time. Sometimes I will find local, fresh tomatoes that rival these, but most of the time they do not come close. Not to mention the price of premium fresh tomatoes compared to these.

Nutritionally a 750ml box contains six servings, each coming in at a scant 28 calories. More importantly, there is only a trace amount of naturally occurring sodium that is only 5mg. The tomatoes are free of genetically modified organisms (GMO), and the container is BPA free.

The essence of Italian cuisine is to keep it simple and use only the freshest, highest quality ingredients. These tomatoes are perfectly consistent with those goals.

title: Relatively mild, but with a little bite and great flavor
text:
I purchase this locally, so my review will focus on the hot sauce and not address price or any shipping costs.

This sauce is in the same general class as Tabasco against which I will compare it. Both are relatively mild when it comes to the piquant qualities, and both are thin with low viscosity.

The key differences are this sauce does not have the sour, overpowering vinegar taste, and while it is mild compared to most Jamaican sauces it has a bite and is a little more piquant than Tabasco.

One aspect where Tabasco beats this is the sodium content. This sauce has 80mg per teaspoon, which is almost three times Tabasco's 30mg. However, since this one has more salt you can eliminate or dramatically cut down on adding salt to dishes which you flavor with this sauce. It does perfectly with eggs and adds some zing to red beans and other dishes.

While I personally prefer a sauce with more kick, this has a flavor that many of the hotter ones do not. Plus it's perfect for some of my guests who are a little less adventurous than I when it comes to spicy foods.

title: Somewhat mild and very flavorful
text:
Two disclaimers: (1) I purchase this locally so I will not address price or shipping, and (2) I have a high tolerance for extremely hot sauces, so mild to me may be very hot to others.

On the heat scale I would say that this is at the lower end for Jamaican hot sauces. Part of that may be due to the complex flavor profile that masks some of the piquant qualities of the peppers. Plus, like most Jamaican sauces this one has a slow burn and spread kind of heat that is typical of Scotch bonnet peppers versus the immediate bite of habanero peppers that are used in Mexico and Trinidad/Tobago.

The flavor profile seems to be a balance of both piquant and sour (from the vinegar). There is also a hint of sweetness that I suspect comes from cane sugar, and a very little touch of saltiness. The sodium content is only 40mg per one teaspoon serving. For folks like myself who have to watch their sodium intake this sauce is a good choice. All other nutritional values are so nominal that they are listed as zero on the label.

I keep this handy for guests who like a little heat, but not the fiery sauces that I normally use. I also use this for some dishes where I want a little spiciness and maximum flavor.

title: Perfect for vinaigrette
text:
Note: I purchase this locally, so this review will not address anything bur the infused vinegar. Factors such as price and shipping are variables that differ by seller and time.

Nutritionally this is a simple and healthy product: each 15ml serving contains a scant 20 calories. There is zero cholesterol, no sodium and only 5 grams of carbs of which 4 grams are sugars. The flavor is delicate, but unmistakably raspberry. TO me it's the perfect balance of flavor and sour, and it mixes well with oil.

Although this infused vinegar is called 'balsamic' it's really a white vinegar plus grape must (the same stuff that gets distilled into grappa). It's less viscous than true balsamic vinegars, and actually has a more delicate flavor that does not overwhelm a vinaigrette.

I love the fact that there is no additives like sodium or anything else artificial - it's vinegar, grape must and real raspberry. The product description says that this can be used as a marinate, but I cannot think of many vegetables, meats or fish that I would want to have a raspberry flavor. Of course that is my personal taste. A touch of this with salt on a green mango is delicious, and, of course on ripe strawberries (true, aged balsamic vinegar is perfect on those too.)

title: Lots of sugar and spice
text:
At the risk of sounding like a nursery rhyme this is sugar and spice and everything nice. In fact, it is brimming with sugar, which is the top ingredient after the nuts.

Think of this is a guilty pleasure or as candy. The nuts taste just like the enticing aroma of a typical Cinnabon concession that seems to be in every mall food court in the US. Heavenly to be sure and the nuts taste just like that aroma. The cinnamon is intense and the sugar only seems to intensify it. I am sure there is a secret formula because I could not duplicate it at home. And if you truly want to make this sinfully delicious follow the suggestion on the can's lid and heat them to 325 degrees (F) for five minutes. I will forewarn you that if you do that you will probably wolf down the entire can yourself and be on a sugar high for hours.

Each eight ounce can contains eight servings that come in at 150 calories, of which 90 of those calories are from fat. Sodium (from sea salt) is a manageable 65mg per serving, but the carbs are 14 grams per serving. The nuts are mainly almonds, cashews and pecans, but the label warns that it may also contain other tree nuts as well as peanuts. For folks with restrictions, the mix that coats the nuts also contains soy, milk and wheat.

If eaten in moderation these are a wonderful treat. If you are on a diet, though, they can quickly wreck it - especially if you serve them hot as described above.

title: My guests love these
text:
A few things up front: I purchase these locally and will keep my review focused on the olives and not pricing, which differs significantly from what I pay at the time of this review. Second, these are not my favorite olives, but my guests seem to prefer them to most others I serve.

The flavor is delicate and more of a fleshy, savory fruit than an olive to my taste. The olives are packed in a brine made from just water and sea salt with lactic and ascorbic acids, both of which are natural ingredients. The lactic acid is used to reduce tannins and make the olives even milder. The ascorbic acid is an antioxidant. The simple packing and preserving allows the true flavors of this type of olive to be close to what you would expect of fresh Castelvetrano olives, which I can also purchase locally when they are carried by my store. There is some difference between these and fresh, but these are remarkably close.

Serving size is about one olive (perhaps 1.5 or 12 grams). Each serving is 20 calories, 18 or which are from fat. There are no carbs, but sodium is a whopping 240mg per serving, which is pretty high.

Overall, if you are putting out a spread of antipasti (or meze or tapas) these olives will probably be a hit judging from my own guests. If you personally like a stronger 'olive' flavor you may find these to be totally different and perhaps an acquired taste.

title: Truly delicious but a nutritional disaster
text:
These nuts get five stars for flavor and plain pleasure, but come with a price for those of us who have to watch our diets. Since I purchase these locally this review is going to focus solely on the product and not price or shipping, both of which can vary.

Describing the flavor is simple: it tastes just like the aroma wafting from any Cinnabon in any mall food court. These nuts have the same intense cinnamon flavor and sweetness. For a more intense experience follow the suggestion printed on the lid of the container and heat them at 325 degrees for five minutes.

The nuts used are as premium as the cinnamon: almonds, cashews and pecans. The can warns that it may also contain other tree nuts as well as peanuts. For folks with restrictions, the mix that coats the nuts also contains soy, milk and wheat.

Nutritionally these nuts are flavored with a lot of sugar, which is the main ingredient after the nuts themselves. Each 8 ounce can contains eight servings that come in at 150 calories, of which 90 of those calories are from fat. Sodium (from sea salt) is a manageable 65mg per serving, but the carbs are 14 grams per serving.

I view these as a guilty pleasure in which I only occasionally indulge. If I had one complaint it's that they are so delicious that it's hard to exercise self control. As an aside these are excellent with a cup of strong coffee or espresso.

title: Top quality and better than Badia's other cinnamon stick product
text:
This is the real thing and an order of magnitude better than [[ASIN:B001SATY7G Badia Cinnamon Sticks]] (that link will take you to sticks for the US market that are nowhere near the quality or flavor of these.)

What I love is the intense aroma and the slightly sweet taste that ranks up there with 'Saigon cinnamon' (which is actually my preferred type.) However, there are some dishes that require sticks and the Saigon type is crumbly and not harvested in a manner that would allow sticks.

In addition to the fragrance and flavor, these sticks are somewhat flaky. You can crumble them or use them whole. Unlike the other Badia sticks I mentioned above these are not tough as wood dowels. I use these to infuse a beverage I make from cinnamon and fresh apple slices. However, these can be used in any dish that calls for cinnamon, whole or ground. And because these sticks are not hard they are relatively easy to grind by hand (I use a [[ASIN:B003O1L7AY Beech Wood Mortar and Pestle]] for that.)

If you have never tried this style of cinnamon you are in for a treat. In fact I will wager that you will never go back to the US style after trying it.

title: Surprisingly good
text:
I purchased this on a whim while shopping locally. Note that this review will focus on the coffee and not address pricing or shipping costs, both of which vary and often change.

The reason I purchased it was it was on sale at a steep discount. I did not have high expectations, but when I brewed my first put I was impressed. This coffee is ground perfectly for my [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti Stovetop Espresso Maker]], so that is an immediate plus. The aroma when you first open the can is intense and is indicative of quality coffee. But the proof is in the taste.

Flavor is of the deeper, richer and smoother Cuban coffees that I normally brew. There is none of the bite and hint of bitterness for which European coffees are prized. Since I enjoy both styles I can quickly taste nuances, and this one was roasted and ground more like a Cuban coffee.

Out of curiosity I brewed a pot in my electric coffee maker that I use on occasion. This grind worked well with the cone filters in that maker and the resulting coffee was merely OK. That is more a reflection of the maker than this coffee. The key point is it will work in a filter-type coffee maker as well as in a moka pot.

Bottom line: this is a surprisingly good coffee. I am not going to switch from my favorite brands (Bustelo and Pilon), but I also would not hesitate to purchase it again if or when it goes on sale.

title: Diasppointing
text:
I purchase this locally so will not address variables like pricing in this review.

My disappointed is because these cinnamon sticks turned out to be as hard as wood - literally - and lacked the aroma of freshly ground cinnamon when I did grind them. To the taste these sticks were almost bitter and certainly lacked the characteristic sweetness of a high quality cinnamon.

In fact, I purchased a second jar from a different store to see if it was a problem with the first jar or a representative sample of the product. The second jar was the same. The other source of disappointment stems from the fact that I am loyal to the Badia brand. I usually purchase their products and have - until now - been one hundred percent satisfied.

Ironically the sticks with which I replaced them are also from Badia and are superb in every way: [[ASIN:B001SAU1F0 Badia Cinnamon Sticks Mexican]]. Those are what I will be buying from now on.

title: Absolutely delicious and a family tradition
text:
What I love aside from the tradition is the balance of crystallized fruits and the flavor of the baked cake itself. It has the slightly burnt outside with the light, almost fluffy inside that makes it such a treat. I have yet to get a bad cake from this company, and am fortunate that most of the time these are readily available locally. Even when I have to order one it's worth it because this is truly a treat that goes well with an espresso, ice cream or even milk.

Christmas is approaching and I immediately think of this particular brand of panettone that I have been buying for close to two decades. This brand has somewhat evolved in minor ways like emphasizing the fact that they use Sun Maid raisins in the traditional recipe (this product), plus their newer offerings with Hershey's chocolate. I stick with the tried and true and will once again be purchasing this in time for the holidays.

The downside is the nutritional values. In this 750 gram cake are six 280 calorie servings, each of which contains 40 grams of carbs and 10 grams of fat. These are not terrible figures, especially for a confection, but when you add in the 125mg of sodium and 40mg of cholesterol more than a single serving can tip the balance for those of us who are on strict cardiac diets. For me it's a temptation to have just one more piece, which is why I never open and serve this unless I have friends and family around to help eat it. I've never had a problem coaxing them to have a piece, and it is one of my guilty pleasures that I enjoy each year.

I have tried other brands of this panettone and have had inconsistent results. I keep coming back to this brand and have never been disappointed.

title: Meets every quality test I put it through
text:
I normally use another brand of Saigon cinnamon so imagine my surprise when I spotted this at a local WalMart. My normal testing is to first taste it to determine if it has the characteristic natural sweetness of a true Saigon variety. It does. Second, I rolled a little between my thumb and forefinger to detect any moisture. None. Third, is the whiff test. This is aromatic and passed with flying colors. If I have a single complaint, this one is ground a little too fine for my liking, but that is personal preference and no reflection of product quality.

If you have never tried Saigon cinnamon you are in for a pleasant surprise. First, this is never sold in sticks because of the nature of the bark, which is crumbly when this is harvested. In the past I ground my own sticks of regular cinnamon, but this - in its powdered form - is far more potent than any stick I have ever ground. That disproves the adage that pre-ground spices lose their potency. True, most do, but this stuff does not.

It would have been nice had the jar been darker to protect the contents from premature loss of potency. Store it in a dark place and you will be fine. Also, the holes in the shaker-style top are just the right size for the fine grind. The top is also hinged and seals the contents airtight.

The rule-of-thumb with Saigon cinnamon is to only use 2/3 of what you would use for regular cinnamon. However, I have found that you can get by with half of normal use in most cases. Experiment and let your own taste buds decide. I use this mixed with either honey or unsweetened applesauce as a topping on baked sweet potatoes. It adds a pleasurable flavor that allows me to get by without butter. It is also a pleasure when I add a pinch to coffee grounds before brewing.

One final note: I normally do not comment on prices because those are variables that change from seller-to-seller as well as market conditions. In the case of this spice anything less than seven bucks for this 1.8 ounce jar is a fair price.

title: Fresh and aromatic
text:
I purchase this locally (at a fraction of the price), so this review is going to focus solely on the product. Price and shipping information are always subject to change, but product characteristics are usually more constant.

The reason I awarded this five stars is the blend of garlic and rosemary is near perfect. But the important part is the fresh, aromatic qualities when you grind this over food. This can be used in food preparation or as a condiment. For preparation I will coat lamb with a little olive oil, grind some of this blend and hand rub it into the meat and allow the flavors to marry before cooking. As a condiment, this goes perfectly with boiled red potatoes with butter or drizzled olive oil or a number of other dishes. I have even used this to top hummus. Experiment and you may discover innovative uses that appeal to your palate.

The grinder is supposed to be adjustable and it is - to a degree. I seem to either get the grind too coarse or too fine. That is a problem on my part because the mechanism does allow you to adjust. I will forewarn that on the coarse a two ounce jar of this goes quickly. Fortunately at my local Publix they are three bucks, but even that can get expensive the way I go through this stuff.

Bottom line is this is a high quality blend of dried garlic that is potent and dried rosemary that is equally so. It will enhance many foods and is best when used with a decent extra virgin olive oil.

title: Convenient for when you don't have time to make it from scratch
text:
I love the convenience of being able to make a delicious Mexican style rice in practically no time at all. However, what makes this special (to my palate) is the flavor is not particularly heavy of artificial tasting. This is perfect for adding your own touch.

Actually, I was a little surprised that despite this having a whopping 750mg of sodium for each half cup serving that it was not salty to the taste. The flavors of the individual vegetables used in this rice are subtle and skillfully blended into the rice to give it nice body and an authentic flavor. The package claims that there is artificial chicken flavoring, but I could not detect that. One final note on flavor: even though tomato is the dominate ingredient after rice and water, there is zero acidity.

Nutritionally, aside from the sodium I mentioned, this is reasonably healthy. Each serving is 255 calories, of which 30 are from fat. Carbs come in at 52 grams per serving with an overall three grams of fat. Not bad numbers to be honest, and these are probably lower than if you were to make it (properly) from scratch. In fact the low fat content indicates that there is relatively little oil in the blend.

This cooks up in a microwave in just 90 seconds, but you need to make sure that the top of the pouch is torn back about a half inch or the bag will literally explode. One final point: this bag is tall. My microwave measures 8 inches from the rotating platter to the top inside and this pouch needs to be slightly folded over or it will get knocked down while rotating during cooking. Needless to say that this can lead to a minor mess.

Overall this is a convenient, relatively nutritious and delicious way to enjoy arroz a la Mexicana. It's not as good as home made, but it's also not as labor intensive to prepare. Heat, add your own touch with seasonings and serve.

title: Healthier than most traditional recipes and authentic flavor
text:
I purchase this product locally so this review will focus on the refried beans and not address price or shipping. I will note that a package purchased at my local store on the date of this review has an expiration date of May 2014, so I am assuming that this has an eighteen month shelf life.

The flavor is authentic based on my long experience with Mexican cuisine from Baja California, Northern Mexico along Arizona and Texas, and a brief time in Mexico City. Granted the recipes for this will vary by region and even state, but the key for refried black beans in my opinion is the flavor of the beans with a hint of seasoning.
