I have also used it in lentil soups, as an interesting substitute for sumac in Lebanese and Persian dishes, and even in pasta sauces. However, my favorite use is with hot chilis, especially when I saute bird's eye chili, garlic and tomatoes in olive oil a pinch of this in the oil before adding the other ingredients imparts a remarkable flavor. Also, add this in scampi dishes for a real treat.

As I gain more experience I will update this review to reflect recipes and other discoveries. Just do not let the fact that this is a Szechuan spice deter you from using it in other dishes.

title: High quality mint
text:
I purchase this locally so my review will focus on the mint and not price or shipping.

The mint is dry and highly aromatic, which indicate high quality. A container has a two year shelf life, but I use this so frequently that it does not lose its potency before the jar is empty.

Among my many uses are infusing it in hot olive oil as a topping on strews and thick soups. I also mix it with a teaspoon of of pomegranate molasses whisked into three tablespoons of olive oil that I pour over cucumbers, feta cheese and fresh tomatoes for a real treat. And, of course, this is a perfect herb for seasoning lamb (especially when combined with rosemary.)

I purchase other brands too. The brand I select depends on which store I shop when I need to replenish my mint and my past experience with its quality. This one is on my 'A list' of brands that I trust.

title: Delicious in salads
text:
I purchase these locally, so my review will focus strictly on the product and not on variable issues like pricing and other costs.

This is a low-calorie, healthy ingredient for salads that is not only delicious, but perfect on a hot day. I like the convenience of having these pre-cut into morsel sized pieces, as well as the firmness and texture that indicates quality.

Nutritionally, a whole can of these is 120 calories with a total of 1060mg of sodium - that is per can and not per serving. The sodium can be greatly reduced by rinsing these before serving. That will not interfere with the flavor, but the diminished saltiness will make them somewhat bland.

A typical salad that I make is a bed of arugula or spinach, some red onion and diced tomatoes, diced bell peppers and these. I drizzle olive oil and squeeze of lemon, a touch of sea salt and fresh ground black pepper, and serve. Sometimes I will add cubes of feta cheese to give it some body. These hearts also make a great garnish, or even a perfect morsel when laying out a tapas or meze spread (they also go perfectly with olives.)

One final use I have is when I babysit my friend's African Gray parrot the bird loves these.

title: A quality source of these hard-to-find seeds
text:
I have a few sources for obtaining these, but this is the most convenient because I can purchase this brand locally. I have come to depend on Zamouri for freshness and these are no exception. They are fresh and aromatic, and impart the flavor I look for with these seeds.

While the main uses of this are in baking and even flavoring some cheeses, my main use is in novel ways of blending za'atar or in making manaqish,, which is a flatbread with a drizzled olive oil mixed with za'atar. I normally use both oregano and thyme, sumac and toasted sesame seeds. These seeds, however, are a perfect substitute for oregano and add an ineffable flavor to my za'atar. I have also used this as a topping for home-baked focaccia, pushing it into the indents on the top of the dough and drizzling olive oil before baking. In fact, a mix of nigella and rosemary are a perfect combination.

If you are purchasing these for a specific baking recipe know that they have many interesting uses beyond baking. If you have never cooked with them try substituting this for oregano, and definitely give my za'atar recipe a try.

title: I'm a believer!
text:
When one of my nieces mentioned this product I was secretly shocked that she would make sinigang from a mix. However, I tried it and this mix made a believer out of me.

Before I proceed I want to get one caveat out of the way: this mix contains MSG, which many folks avoid these days. Also, while the 420mg of sodium per serving is not horribly high, the total sodium in a serving of sinigang made with this mix skyrockets after you add patis, which will more than double the per serving sodium count.

On the back of the pouch is a recipe for sinigang na sugpo, which I tried and it turned out excellent. I also used the same recipe to make sinigang na isda by substituting snapper for the prawns with equally delicious results.

The bottom line is this makes cooking sinigang a lot simpler than doing it from scratch. It has almost the same tartness and taste as homemade, and the sampalok flavor is superb.

title: Actually makes authentic kaldereta
text:
I was introduced to this brand when a niece recommended that I try the [[ASIN:B003JJTAX2 Mama Sita Tamarind Soup Base Mix]]. I was so impressed that I tried this.

Like the sinigang mix above this is authentic. I wanted to make kalderetang kambing, but had to substitute lamb for goat. The results were not only impressive, but quick and easy to make. You can follow your own recipe or use the one on the back of the pouch. Frankly, I prefer my own, simpler recipe.

While this is inexpensive and a major convenience, you need to be aware of some nutritional values. First is one of the main ingredients is MSG - monosodium glutamate - which was an essential ingredient when I was in the Philippines years ago, but has fallen out of favor in the US. Second, there are ten 1 teaspoon servings per pouch (a pouch will make a 10 serving kaldereta meal). Each serving is a mere 15 calories, but also contains 360mg of sodium. This is not horribly high, but adds up. If you have sodium restrictions you need to be aware of it.

title: An interesting substitute for fresh mint
text:
I found this at a local grocery store when I was disappointed in the quality of their fresh mint I needed for a recipe. I grabbed a bottle of this and a few drops worked beautifully as a substitute.

Since I make a lot of Persian and Mediterranean dishes that call for mint I began experimenting and found the flavor that this imparts to work. To be sure, it is different than with fresh mint or dried mint infused with hot olive oil, but that difference has become my secret ingredient.

The major difference is the sweetness that dominates the flavor profile. There is also a slight amount of sourness in the profile that comes from the malt vinegar, which is one of the main ingredients. The mint flavor is intense, but not overpowering.

Nutritionally a teaspoon is only 5 calories with zero sodium and 1 gram of carbs from the sugar in the blend.

This needs to be refrigerated after opening, but should last at least three months afterwards. Mine have the same intense flavor after that length of time as when first opened.

title: High quality and a perfect substitute for patis
text:
This is identical to the the top brands of the Philippine version called patis. It has the same purity and flavor, and can easily compete with my other favorite brand made by Tiparos. I switched to this brand mainly for convenience when I discovered it on a shelf at my local grocery store. That was a shock in itself, but a pleasant one.

I use this - sparingly - on grilled eggplant and zucchini, and to make a hot dipping sauce called nam pra prik. That sauce can be easily made by finely chopping hot peppers (bird's eye chillies are the best) and adding them to this fish sauce.

Although I haven't eaten pork in decades this was a perfect condiment for it when I did. The flavor of mixed grilled or fried vegetables is also greatly enhanced by using a few drops of this in lieu of salt or soy sauce.

Do be aware that this, like patis or other Thai brands, is extremely high in sodium. A single gram of this sauce contains 890mg. That means that a teaspoon contains a whopping 4450mg, so use it very sparingly if you have sodium restrictions.

title: Not bad, but lacking
text:
This one is not as spicy as I expected, so am slightly disappointed. The name, bisi bele bhat, translates into hot lentil rice, so I was expecting a more authentic entree.

On the other hand, I can understand why MTR made it tame: to make it palatable to a larger customer base. After all, one can always add spicy peppers, but cannot remove them. And it does taste delicious after seasoned to taste. Actually, it has a wonderful flavor out of the pouch. Compared to another of my favorite Indian lentil dishes - dal tadka - this one has a richer, more complex flavor.

The reason I subtracted a star is not because I was personally disappointed with the lack of spiciness, but in the nutritional values. A pouch contains two 173 calorie servings of which almost half of those calories are from the 9 grams of fat per serving. Both the calorie count and fat content are higher than other brands and dishes of Indian entrees. My real complaint is the 573mg of sodium. That is one of the highest counts I have seen in any prepared meal.

My complaints aside, I will admit that this is a tasty entree that is perfect for many folks right out of the pouch, and can be tweaked by adding chili peppers if you want more heat. Do heed the nutritional caveats, though, if you are on a diet or have sodium restrictions.

title: Authentic harissa
text:
Although this is made in France it has an authentic Tunisian flavor and is one of two brands I routinely purchase.

One of the characteristics of this particular blend that I love is that it does not gave a sharp 'bite'. Instead the heat from the chili peppers spreads and intensifies over your palate. That is the hallmark of a great harissa paste, and this one has it. Still, it is hot. Much more so than Tabasco or jalapenos. I would put it on par with habaneros without the extreme bite.

I also love the flavor. The label claims that in addition to peppers it contains carrots, turnips, tomatoes, coriander and caraway seeds. While I do not doubt that, the flavors become almost ineffable when blended with the dish in which it's used, and as spicy as it is, that aspect does not overpower the flavor. If anything it enhances it. It certainly teases and pleases your palate.

This is essential for North African cuisine, but will also work well in other dishes, including on omelets, in stews or even as a spread.

title: Fast, convenient and delicious
text:
This particular entree was my introduction to this brand nearly fifteen years ago, and I have continued to purchase this and a few other entrees that I particularly love.

A few disclaimers: I purchase these locally, so I am going to focus on the product and not the price or other unrelated factors. I also make this dish from scratch, so the only time I open a pouch these days is when I am too lazy or tired to cook, or unexpected guests drop by.

The flavor is authentic. Not as good as home made, of course, not as good as what I enjoyed during a few brief visits to India, but still better than anything in the ethic frozen food section of my local grocery. Health wise, review the nutritional values that are displayed at the top of this product page. The only red flag for me is the sodium level, but the rest is relatively (compared to other convenience foods) low calories, fats and carbs.

It's the convenience plus the flavor that has made me a loyal customer to this brand. It takes less than fifteen minutes to steam basmasti rice and heat a pouch, and most of that time is waiting for the rice to steam. In fact, since the potatoes are starchy I often do not pair this with rice. It also makes an excellent appetizer when entertaining. I set out a bowl of this, a bowl of [[ASIN:B0031YIN7O Tasty Bite Punjab Eggplant]] and some quartered naan or flatbread, raita and papadum, and my guests love it.

This is one of a few Tasty Bite entrees I keep in my pantry and am always delighted to spot them when I am rummaging through looking for a quick and easy meal.

title: Makes truly authentic chai
text:
A friend from Hyderabad used to make chai for me and I never could get it quite right when I tried on my own. This blend has enabled me to get close to the nectar I enjoyed in the past.

I am no newcomer to this brand, and like their other spices and blends this one is highly aromatic and fresh. And the blend itself is perfect. It has the dominating cardamom flavor that is a hallmark of an authentic chai. It also has the ginger that my friend would use, plus cinnamon that is a perfect complement to the spices and flavor. Understand that this blend is not a substitute from making chai by hand, including crushing cardamom pods to get the best flavor, but it's a convenient alternative. It allows you to enjoy chai they way it was meant to be.

For best results I recommend black tea (the stronger the better), half and half or even full cream, and do not be shy with the sugar. Add in a half teaspoon of this blend and sit back and enjoy one of India's many gifts to the world.

title: Convenience food in my household
text:
I normally cook this or palak paneer from scratch. However there are days when I am too lazy or tired, so I keep a dozen or so pouches of this and a few other Tasty Bite quick meals in my pantry.

This may not come close to homemade, but it is fairly delicious and is a snap to prepare. In less than fifteen minutes and very little effort I can steam basmati rice and heat a pouch of this for a quick and reasonably healthy meal.

What I mean by 'reasonably healthy' is although this two-serving pouch is low in calories at 100 per serving, it does contain 400mg of sodium, which is about one fifth of a normal adults recommended intake. If you have sodium restrictions that is a high number, and especially if you consume the entire pouch yourself.

On the plus side, nutritionally, there is only 3 grams of fat (which accounts for 25 of the 100 calories) and zero cholesterol. Carbs are only 13 grams and there is 3 grams of protein. A serving also is rich in vitamin A (24% of daily recommendations for an adult) and 10% iron.

As far as convenience foods go this is tastier than most (if you like spinach as much as I), and significantly healthier than most items in my pantry, including some other Tasty Bite entrees that compare poorly to this from nutritional and health perspectives.

I love it because I can purchase it locally and it's appeals to my palate. If you like Indian food and are willing to occasionally lower your culinary standards this beats a can or soup of cup of noodles for a fast meal.

title: Convenient and fast
text:
I normally make this dish (known as Punjabi baingan bartha) from scratch, but there are times when I am too tired to cook or company drops in unexpectedly. For those reasons I keep a dozen or so of these pouches and other Tasty Bite quick meals on hand.

While this is certainly not as good as home-cooked, it is tasty enough to please guests who drop by. It's quick to make, and steaming up some basmati rice results in a quick meal that takes less than fifteen minutes.

There are some caveats you need to heed if you are counting calories nor have dietary restrictions. First, a pouch contains two servings. That is about right because when you factor in the rice or naan that you will probably serve with it, a pouch will feed two people. Each serving is 150 calories, 80 of which are from the 9 grams of fat per serving. Carbs come in at 13 grams. Those numbers are not bad because we are talking about a meal. It's the sodium that you need to watch if you have restrictions because each serving contains 560mg. That is a quarter of a normal adult's daily recommended intake in a single meal.

In addition to quick and convenient meals this is perfect as an appetizer. Set it out with quarter pieces of flatbread and it will probably be a big hit - it has proven to be at my house.

Bottom line is this is an inexpensive meal to stock in your pantry for those days when you just don't feel like cooking, or a guest unexpectedly drops by during meal time.

title: The real thing!
text:
There are two major reasons why I gave this five stars: (1) the spices are fresh and fragrant, and (2) the blend is perfect.

Because this is especially blended as advieh polo (more about that below), the cinnamon and cardamom that dominate the spice profile is perfect for the rice dishes for which this is used. When I mentioned that the blend is perfect I think the proportions of the spices give this blend a true Persian flavor.

Also unlike some brands that leave out essential ingredients, this contains rose pedals that add to the authenticity and spice profile. This will also go perfectly with traditional American dishes like rice pudding and sweet potatoes, and even as a 'secret ingredient' in barbeque sauces or stews.

There is a different blend of advieh that is mainly for stews and similar dishes called advieh-e khoresh. This can be transformed into the khoresh style blend by adding black pepper, cumin, turmeric and saffron. If you are looking for one of the most authentic advieh blends this is the one I recommend. Short of making your own this is the best value (and quality) that I have found.

title: One of the more authentic blends on the market
text:
I have tried numerous advieh blends from varous brands and this is one of the best. First, it's more authentic than some, and second, this one is sodium-free (a plus for me because I am on a restricted diet.)

What I love is the fresh spices and the aroma that characterize a well blended advieh (also called adwiya). This one has a sweeter spice profile with cinnamon and cardamom dominating the blend. Unlike some brands that leave out essential ingredients, this contains rose pedals that add to the authenticity and spice profile.

Above I mentioned that this has a sweet profile. I do not mean to imply that it has sugars or sweeteners of any kind. It's just that the dominant spices are usually associated with sweeter foods. This particular blend falls more on the advieh-e polo side of advieh blends. That one is used to flavor rice, and can turn a simple plate of basmati rice into manna with just a pinch of this sprinkled as a condiment.

There is a companion blend that is mainly for stews and similar dishes called advieh-e khoresh. This can be transformed into the khoresh style blend by adding black pepper, cumin, turmeric and saffron.

This will also go perfectly with traditional American dishes like rice pudding and sweet potatoes, and even as a 'secret ingredient' in barbeque sauces or stews.

If you are looking for one of the most authentic advieh blends this is the one I recommend. Short of making your own this is the best value (and quality) that I have found.

title: Excellent flavor and nice heat
text:
There are a few things that I love about this particular sauce. First, it is mainly chilies preserved with vinegar and some salt. You get the base and can add any flavors you want like garlic, shallots, etc. Second, this is medium low heat, so you can use it when making meals for guests or family members who may not tolerate super spicy dishes. You can always add heat, but you cannot remove it. Finally, the nutrition profile is excellent.

It's the basic ingredients that I most love because this is more of a base than a sauce. I usually saute garlic and shallots in a little olive oil, then add a handful of nuts like cashews, and continue sauteing with this paste. If I am making this for myself or friends who love spicy food I will also shop some fresh bird's eye peppers to kick up the heat a few notches. The finishing touch is some fresh, chopped cilantro and I have a topping that works with everything from eggs to fish.

Nutritionally this sauce is a dieter's dream come true. A serving is a teaspoon and it has only a nominal calorie count. In fact, it's so nominal that two nutritional databases I checked claimed zero calories. The only value that does register is sodium, which is 110mg per teaspoon. That can add up quickly, so if you have sodium restrictions do that that into account.

Overall, this is a flavorful paste that is a little hotter than a jalapeno, but nowhere near as spicy as a habanero. It makes a great base for sauces (and soups), and even works well as a condiment right out of the jar.

title: Amazing as a condiment
text:
Although many folks cook with this oil I use it as a condiment. I love the way the spicy heat builds and spreads, and the subtle and not-so-subtle flavors that you can taste. Also, it is salty enough to use as a substitute for salt the same way you would with soy sauce or a fish sauce.

A little goes a long way, and especially if you are counting calories, fat or sodium intake. A serving is about a teaspoon - more than enough to mix into rice or drizzle over other dishes - and it comes in at 90 calories. That same serving contains 9 grams of fat and 440mg of sodium. So, do use sparingly if you are watching any of those nutritional factors.

Another thing that I personally love is this is unfiltered. There are pieces of peppers and other ingredients that will suspend in the oil if you vigorously shake the jar before serving. Those add a lot to the flavor profile, which is predominately salty and piquant (and there is also a distinct element of umami).

If you love spicy sauces and oils and want to 'spice' up your meal (pun intended) this is an excellent infused oil that will do the trick. I wish I could elaborate on how it works for sir frying, but I do not use it that way. I can say that it is an excellent condiment.

title: Almost perfect
text:
Sometimes Zamouri creates blends that are perfection, but on rare occasions this brand falls short. This is one of those rare occasions.

On the positive side, this blend is made from fresh, fragrant ingredients. The aroma is powerful and hits you the minute you open the jar. However, this blend is missing one critical ingredient that I've come to expect in advieh: rose petals.

I have purchased this type of blend from many different brands, and while they all vary there is one constant. The blend for rice and the blend for savory dishes invariably have rose pedals. I was able to rectify the lacking flavor by adding some from my stash of [[ASIN:B007IVDDU8 Ajika Rose Buds]].

Now back to the positive. I am more of a purist when it comes to spices, so you may find this blend to be a five star delight despite my complaint. It certainly works well with traditional American cuisine, and especially in rice pudding, or mixed with honey and dabbed over sweet potatoes. It's also surprisingly wonderful flavor enhancer sprinkled over butternut squash.

While the black pepper comes through in the spice profile, it's the cardamom and cumin balancing one another that makes this interesting. Both are dominant flavors, but the other spices add a nice flavor dimension. The hint of nutmeg imparts a little bitterness in a good way and the lemon peel seems to be the magic ingredient. You do not taste that right away because it's overpowered by the cinnamon, but it is there.

So while I am slightly disappointed, this is still a blend that will delight cooks who are new to Persian spices. Take a chance and try it in a few dishes. Start subtle and work your way to bolder uses. I do recommend adding rose petals for a more authentic experience.

title: Expect the unexpected
text:
This is like tasting cinnamon for the first time. The intensity is unlike any cinnamon flavor (or fragrance) you've ever tasted.

I am used to purchasing my cinnamon in sticks and grinding them myself. This is far more potent that any stick I have ever ground, and it disproves the adage that pre-ground spices lose their potency.

Use this as you would any cinnamon, but use less. Zamouri recommends using only 2/3 what you would normally use, but actually you can safely get by with half. To my palate anyway. I use this mixed with either honey or unsweetened applesauce as a topping on baked sweet potatoes. It adds a pleasurable flavor that allows me to get by without butter. It is also a pleasure when I add a pinch to coffee grounds before brewing.

The bottom line is if you have never tasted Saigon cinnamon you are in for not only a treat, but a completely different flavor experience with this. It's packaged fresh and fragrant, so I do not think you will be disappointed.

title: Interesting addition to my za'atar mix
text:
When I make za'atar - a blend that is mixed with olive oil on flatbread - I normally use both oregano and thyme, sumac and toasted sesame seeds. These seeds, however, are a perfect substitute for oregano and add an ineffable flavor to my za'atar.

I love the freshness of these seeds, and there is a nice aromatic quality to them as well. While the main uses of this are in backing and even flavoring some cheeses, my main use is in novel ways of blending za'atar or in making manaqish,, which is a flatbread with a drizzled olive oil mixed with za'atar. I have also used this as a topping for home-baked focaccia, pushing it into the indents on the top of the dough and drizzling olive oil before baking. In fact, a mix of nigella and rosemary are a perfect combination.

One other way I have used these is when I am making a base for lentils I will start by bringing olive oil to a medium high temperature, adding a half teaspoon and after the seeds pop and release their fragrance I add in the garlic, onion, carrots and celery. The flavor just a small amount of these add is remarkable.

Bottom line: these have many interesting uses beyond baking. If you have never cooked with them (and you like a flavor that is similar to oregano) these are well worth a try.

title: Healthy AND delicious
text:
It's rare when you find food that is both healthy and delicious, but these beans are both. I purchase mine locally and love the texture and taste (and price to be honest.)

One reviewer mentioned that these work well in pasta e fagioli and I agree. They are also wonderful as side dishes. I often make a soffrito by sauteing garlic, shallot and sweet peppers in olive oil, adding the beans and using that as a side dish.

With respect to my claim of healthy, there are four servings per can. Each is a scant 53 calories (only 9 of which are from fat), zero cholesterol, only 6 grams of carbs and 62mg of sodium. The sodium comes from the light brine in which these beans are packed, and can be reduced to practically zero if you drain and rinse the beans before heating them. In addition to the low calories, sodium and carbs, each serving contains 4 grams of protein.

Even if you can eat anything you want with impunity or do not have to worry about dietary restrictions these are still delicious. Even more so than other brands that are canned with high fructose corn syrup and a ton of sodium. The beauty of these, though, is that they are priced the same as the lower quality and less healthy brands.

title: Not spectacular
text:
Most of the time Zamouri knocks them out of the park with their blends, but this is one of their rare ones that fall a little short.

The ingredients are of the same high quality that I have come to expect from this brand, but the za'atar blend is a little too bland. I normally make mine from scratch, but purchased this locally on a whim to see if I could improve my own blends. In this case, what I make at home is better.

The thyme is the dominate flavor, and the amount of sesame used is generous. I do not think the sesame was sufficiently toasted, which is why I subtracted stars and probably why this blend is less than spectacular. If you are using this to make manaqish - flatbread with za'atar and olive oil- then when you toaste the flatbread with the za'atar and oil the seeds will toast a little.

However, on the plus side this blend does have a nice proportion of sumac to the thyme and sesame seeds. And I can 'improve' this blend by adding a half ounce of dried oregano to the two ounces of this blend, plus a pinch of sea salt. Then mixed with some quality olive oil and spread over a flatbread, this works out well. But those are to my personal tastes. In fairness, if you have never tasted za'atar this one is OK. Not great, but not horrible either.

Overall, of you know how to make za'atar pass this one by. If you have heard about it and are curious, this is probably as good as any to try as a sample. Just know that it's not the best there is.

title: My favorite brand
text:
I purchase this locally so I am reviewing the actual product and not pricing, shipping or other factors not germane to the coffee itself.

First, the grind is absolutely perfect for brewing in a cezve.

Second, this is the real thing. I've tried many brands and more than a few locally blended grounds for Turkish coffee and this one stands out as the best.

However, grind is only one part of what it takes to make a great coffee. It's the quality of the coffee that makes this a personal favorite. The characteristic that I love the most is the aroma that is rich and almost earthy. Equally important - to me - is that it brews perfectly.

Of course the best coffee in the world will not taste the best if it's not properly brewed. Here is how to ensure that your brew is perfect: First, use good water. Filtered or bottled. Most tap water will ruin the flavor of the brewed coffee.

Second, DO NOT fill the maker more than half way. And when heating do not use any heat source or setting above medium low. As soon as it boils immediately remove it from the heat and let it settle down. Trust me, it can get quickly out of control, so pay close attention. You can do a second boil to increase the strength of the brew. I use a little ground cardamom and a small cube of sugar when I am brewing mine.

If you follow the above instructions your palate will be rewarded. This is one of life's true pleasures for coffee lovers.

title: A standout among ras el hanout blends!
text:
I've tried many brands and blends of this wonderful mix and this one stands out from the others in a few important ways. Unlike many blends where cardamom and cinnamon dominated the flavor this one goes in a different direction.

As soon as you open the container you are immediately hit with strong pepper that has a hint of citrus. This is followed by cinnamon and ginger with slight hints of cloves and nutmeg. The rest of the flavors are difficult to identify, but this blend does remind me of a common Persian blend called advieh. They are not the same by any means, but no other ras el hanout blend has ever caused me to make that connection.

The first stew I made in my tagine sealed the deal. It was not only delicious, but took my food to a new level. Zamouri sometimes misses the mark with proportions and ingredients, but hit a bullseye in this case. The blend smells and tastes authentic and has a perfectly balanced flavor profile for North African cuisine.

If you are constantly trying different ras el hanout blends like I do, give this one a try. I cannot guarantee that everyone will love it because tastes vary among people, but if you like spices in which pepper dominates you may be impressed. And it does have the signature aromatic spices that characterize authentic ras el hanout blends.

title: Adds wonderful nuances to any coffee
text:
This blend actually contains more than the commonly expected cardamom in Turkish coffee. Indeed, this is a wonderful blend that takes the basic ingredients of Moroccan coffee spices and changes the portions to arrive at a vastly different spice profile.

The main ingredients in both blends are cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and vanilla. This one has the cardamom most prominent while the Moroccan blends emphasize cinnamon and cloves.

I love the freshness of the spices and the aroma that hits you as soon as you open the container. More importantly, though, I am glad that Zamouri kept the cardamom as the dominant spice. Frankly I think they have takes some liberties with 'Turkish' style spices, but kept the flavor profile true to Turkish tastes. It may not be strictly authentic, but it sure is delicious. I think part of the reason I love it is the hint of vanilla imparts a richness to the flavor that complements the more aromatic spices in the blend.

Also, this works with espresso. Perfectly in fact, as it also does with just about any coffee because the spices add an exotic touch to any brew.

This is one of those indulgences that are actually healthy and delicious. We need more treats like this in life. If you want to wow guests use a little of this in your coffee - before you brew it for extra strength or as a flavoring for brewed coffee. I am betting it will be a big hit.

title: One excellent variation on a spice blend that has many variations
text:
This is one of my favorite spices and an essential one for my tagine cooking. Most of the ras el hanout blends that I have tried in the past had cardamom and cinnamon more prominent in the spice profile, and often those were accompanied by nutmeg. This one is different - and in a wonderful way.

The first flavors that hit you are a strong pepper with hint of citrus, along with the aromatic cinnamon and ginger with slight hints of cloves and nutmeg. The rest of the flavors are, well, ineffable. They are difficult to identify, but this blend does remind me of a common Persian blend called advieh. They are not the same by any means, but no other ras el hanout blend has ever caused me to make that connection.

As for the quality, like all Zamouri brand spices I have purchased (and that is a considerable number), this blend is highly aromatic and fresh. While I will admit that even with the best quality herbs and spices Zamouri sometimes misses the mark with proportions and ingredients. Not so in this case. The blend smells and tastes authentic and has a perfectly balanced flavor profile for North African cuisine.

I had been using a different brand as my preferred blend. Now that I have tried this one I am switching brands because this ras el hanout seems take my tagine cooking to a whole new level.

title: High quality
text:
I'll be honest and confess that I am new to this spice, so my initial thoughts were that it had spoiled because of the odor when I opened the jar. I've since learned that the pungent smell (I dare not use fragrance or aroma) is a sign of quality. It's when that diminishes that you need to be concerned.

Once added to some oil that odor does transform into the wonderful aroma of fried onions with a hint of garlic. It does not take much, and the aroma is especially compelling when fried in olive oil. It will transform any simple dish's flavor profile into a Mediterranean delight. In India it's used for dal dishes (lentils). By the same token it will also augment the expected flavors of Mediterranean style lentils, and will even take something as simple as fried bell peppers and turn it into the base of an omelet.

One final concoction that I have made with it is to cook a very small portion in extra virgin olive oil, then let it cool as the foundation of a spread that I use based on za'atar (toasted sesame seeds, oregano and thyme), then mixed with [[ASIN:B0050IKSBI Harissa Paste]] and the infused olive oil. It's a delight when spread on flatbread and toasted.

There are a number of ways to use this spice, including giving an onion flavor to foods served to folks who are allergic to onions. One thing to know about this is do not refrigerate it after opening. Seal the jar and it should keep for six months of longer.

title: Exceptional quality
text:
This is an authentic harissa of exceptional quality. It is both flavorful and has that perfect spiciness. What I mean by 'perfect' is the heat from the peppers do not have a sharp bite, but, instead build in intensity and spread. It's a subtle, but important aspect of a truly great harissa.

Although I prefer my harissa in a tube because I find it more convenient, these cans are sufficiently small at four and three quarters of an ounce to consume after opening without having to waste or refrigerate.

One more thing that makes this such an authentic harissa is it's made by a company called Ets Khemir Freres that is located in the ancient town of Korba that is renown for its peppers, tomatoes and other produce. In fact, it is nicknamed 'the red town' and this is one of the many high quality products that are made there.

If you want the true taste and burn of a premium Tunisian harissa this is one to get. Fortunately I can get mine locally, which avoids the shipping costs and possibility of receiving dented cans. However, it is one of the best I have tasted.

title: Nice flavor, but missing something
text:
I am a harissa addict who has to try every brand on the market. I look for two things, of which this particular brand has one, but not the other.

The first thing I look for is flavor. This has it. Zamouri's recipe seemed to focus on the best possible flavor, in fact.

Where this falls short is the second characteristic. A truly authentic harissa would have a slow, spreading spiciness that has no immediate bite, but accumulates heat. This one is plain mild. It's on par with some of the milder jalapenos, and the heat from the first taste does not intensify. Hence, I subtracted a star. If you were to compare this to another brand that I frequently enjoy (and recommend) - [[ASIN:B0050IKSBI Harissa Paste]] - the difference in authenticity would be immediately discernible.

Don't get me wrong - this is an excellent introduction to Tunisian and North African cuisine for folks who want to taste but have a low tolerance for the spiciness of a true harissa. For that reason I did give this four stars because you can still capture the essence of the cuisine with the flavor it imparts, and enjoy the meal without being overwhelmed by the spiciness of real harissa.

title: Sweet and refreshi
text:
Disclaimer: I get these locally, so am not going to delve into areas like how shipping costs make this expensive. My focus is on the product itself. Compared to the [[ASIN:B0075LIHUC San Pellegrino Aranciata Rossa (Blood Orange) Sparkling Water]], which is bitter (in a good way), this one is light and sweet. It's perfect on a hot humid day.

As noted by others this (and the rest of the juice flavored sparkling waters from San Pellegrino) have a high sugar and calorie content. At 140 calories and 32 grams of sugar this is not a drink you want to toss down one after another if you are watching your caloric or sugar intakes. Put another way, a 12 ounce can of Classic Coke contains less calories (90) and sugar (27 grams). I am saying this to show a stark comparison, not to promote Coke (which I do not drink at all.) Just be aware of the nutritional values and then enjoy a can when you want to treat yourself.

What I love is the flavors of Italy in the can. This has the sparkling mineral waters from Northern Italy's Lombardia region and the citrus of Sicily. To my palate it's a perfect combination.

See the photo that I uploaded at the top of this page and you will note the color. It's not artificially orange, but natural as though you used fresh oranges and a juicer to squeeze them. It's the natural look and flavor that keeps me addicted.

See the photo I uploaded at the top of this page for a visual of how the juice color is a natural, pale as though you extracted it from fresh oranges. No artificial orange coloring was used, which is a plus in my opinion.

title: Excellent harissa in convenient sizes
text:
At the time of this review a pack of twenty four tubes was less than nineteen bucks, making this a bargain that beat local prices.

The harissa is both flavorful and had a nice bite that was much stronger than jalapeno, but well short of habanero. It's difficult to be any more accurate in that part of the description because everyone perceives 'hot' differently. What it does have is the flavor I have come to expect from well made harissa. In fact, I would put this as equal to one of my other favorite brands: [[ASIN:B002L0IRQG Harissa Condiment in Tube - Spicy 120 Gr 3 Oz]].

However, for value and convenience this one is a bargain. You get two dozen tubes that are about 2.5 ounces each. Since you have to refrigerate most harissa after opening, these tubes are sized for a perfect single serving. That is where the convenience factor comes in.

It's the fact that you are getting close to .85 of a kilo of this delicious paste for less than twenty bucks is where the true value comes in. Compare the price per gram or ounce to any other harissa on this site to she the true value proposition.

A parting tip: try this with to mix it in with za'atar to make a devilishly hot spread for flat breads. Za'atar can be quickly and easily made by mixing equal parts of oregany, thyme, marjoram, toasted sesame seeds and summac. Add a pinch of sea sale and make a paste with olive oil. From there blend in a little of this harissa to your taste and you have a wonderful spread that will bring flat bread to life.

title: Love at first sip - and love comes with a cost
text:
This is my second favorite flavored sparkling water from San Pellegrino (the top of my list is [[ASIN:B0075LIHUC San Pellegrino Aranciata Rossa (Blood Orange) Sparkling Water]].) I love that one for its bitterness and this one for its tartness.

Note that this is readily available from a number of local stores where I live, including our biggest grocery chain and Wal-Mart. I am not going to address the value versus cost issues, which seem exorbitant when purchased online.

What I love is the tart and natural flavor, which is greatly enhanced by the sparkling mineral water. This is a perfect refreshment on a hot and humid day. I also love the caps over the cans, which ensure that the drinking surface will be clean if you consume directly from the can.

Love does come with a cost unfortunately - and it isn't money. For all the tartness each 11.15 ounce can contains an extraordinary amount of sugar. In fact, of the 35 grams of carbs per can, 33 of those grams are sugar. And a deceptively small can is 150 calories. Compared to a smaller, 10 ounce serving of Classic Coke, this has 2 grams more carbs and 30 more calories. I am not complaining about this beverage, nor am I implying that you should be drinking Coke instead. On the contrary, to me there is no comparison between the two beverages, but if you are watching sugar or caloric intake do not be deceived by the natural taste of this limonata into believing that it's simply flavored water.

Regardless of the nutritional values, I love this drink and always keep at least a six pack of this and the Aranciata Rossa flavor on hand. What I do, though, is enjoy them as a special treat and only occasionally. If you can obtain these locally give a six pack a try. If you like a tart lemonade you will probably love this.

title: A guilty pleasure
text:
I've become addicted to this slightly bitter mixture of the sparkling mineral water from Northern Italy's Lombardy region and the blood orange (aranciata rossa) from Sicily.

The problem is, at 140 calories per 11.15 ounce can (and a whopping 32 grams of sugar), I have to watch my intake. If you are watching either calorie and/or sugar values of what you consume this is one to occasionally enjoy. The real irony is I am attracted by the bitterness which is predominate despite the high sugar content.

I will admit that this is refreshing, and especially so on a humid Florida day. However, since it is a guilty pleasure I have a ritual in which I serve mine in a fancy flute to remind myself that enjoying one is a special occasion to be savored.

In a perfect world I could drink as many as I wanted with no adverse affects. Alas, I do not live in such a world - but mine is made a little brighter when I have one of these.

title: Refreshing for grapefruit lovers
text:
Unlike the tart limonata and bitter aranciata rosso flavors, this one is smooth and subdued. In fact, there is a more subtle grapefruit flavor that is significantly less acidic than straight juice. That makes this particular sparkling fruit drink both refreshing on a hot, humid day, and a wonderful mixer for drinks that you would normally mix with grapefruit juice.

Combining the sparkling mineral waters from Northern Italy's Lombardia region with the citrus of Sicily is a marriage made in heaven. This is one of a number of flavors from San Pellegrino that is based on that combination.

As much as I love this (and the other flavors) they are heavy in sugar and calories. So if you are controlling your sugar or caloric intake you need to be aware of the following: each 11.15 ounce can contains 150 calories and 35 grams of sugar. Considering that this is not an overly sweet drink the large amount of sugar is surprising. A 12 ounce can of Classic Coke contains less calories (90) and sugar (27 grams), but also contains sodium, which this sparkling juice does not. I am not advocating that you drink Classic Coke instead - I just want to graphically illustrate the nutritional values. One thing to remember is this product is all natural: juice and mineral water.

Despite the sugar content I still enjoy this and the other flavors offered by San Pellegrino - I just enjoy them sparingly. And there are always at least a dozen (or more) cans in my refrigerator to enjoy or serve to guests. It's one of my guilty pleasures.

title: The real thing!
text:
Disclaimer: I purchase this locally so I am reviewing the actual product and not pricing, shipping or other factors not germane to the coffee itself.

This is genuine Turkish coffee. I've tried many brands and more than a few locally blended grounds for Turkish coffee and this one stands out as the best. First, the grind is absolutely perfect for brewing in a cezve (I use a relatively cheap model: [[ASIN:B005G74ARQ Turkish Coffee Pot (cezve/ibrik) with wooden handle]]). However, grind is only one part of what it takes to make a great coffee.

It is the quality of the coffee is what I love the most. It has an aroma that is rich and almost earthy. More importantly, it brews perfectly too. I use a little ground cardamom and a small cube of sugar when I am brewing mine.

Of course the best coffee in the world will not taste the best if it's not properly brewed. Here is how to ensure that your brew is perfect: First, use good water. Filtered or bottled. Most tap water will ruin the flavor of the brewed coffee.

Second, DO NOT fill the maker more than half way. And when heating do not use any heat source or setting above medium low. As soon as it boils immediately remove it from the heat and let it settle down. Trust me, it can get quickly out of control, so pay close attention. You can do a second boil to increase the strength of the brew.

If you follow the above instructions your palate will be rewarded. This is one of life's true pleasures for coffee lovers.

title: Transforms even cheap cuts of lamb into delights
text:
I normally do not eat meat, but have always had lamb on Easter as a tradition. However, this mix has lamb on my table more frequently. Also note that this is definitely for the grill instead of tagine cooking.

First, let me get the reasons why I love this out of the way. Like all Zamouri spices I have purchased this one is fresh and aromatic. More importantly I love the way the spices and herbs are blended. The flavors are balanced and perfectly enhance lamb.

The flavor profile is dominated by cumin and cinnamon, which surprisingly complement one another. The sodium seems a little on the high side because this blend is salty. However, since this is a rub a little of this blend, mixed with olive oil, goes a long way. I was also intrigued by the other spices in the blend - I expected mint and clove, but the fennel threw me a bit. I associate that spice with sausage, so it added a nuance for which I was unprepared. Don't get me wrong - I loved it. I just did not expect it. The rest of the spices were quite expected, and I especially loved the mild kick that the cayenne provided.

What I truly love is the way this simple blend can transform a relatively cheap lamb shoulder cuts (neck, blade or arm) into succulent pieces of meat. This allows me to enjoy lamb on the cheap because some of the premium cuts are too expensive for my fixed income budget.

I am fairly sure this rub would work with other meats and especially beef. However I have no direct experience so can only hazard a guess based on the aroma and how it works with lamb. It's worth experimenting though.

title: Perfect on a number of levels
text:
I do not want to repeat the other reviews that are raving about the taste, texture and al dente firmness, but I definitely agree and think those are reasons to buy these beans.

Other reasons why I love these include the fact that they are relatively inexpensive and absolutely the healthiest canned beans that I have come across.

First, let me address value. While I get these locally from a large health food chain, even the online price here with shipping is a bargain. That said, prices change,of this review.

On the health benefits, a half cup serving of these is 52 calories and contains 99mg of sodium. Contrast those values with another quality canned cannellini bean product - [[ASIN:B005F1YF7I Progresso Cannellini Beans]] - which is 110 calories per half cup serving with 340mg of sodium and you can understand why I said these are the healthiest I have found.

Bottom line is these are delicious and healthy: two characteristics that rarely go together. Don't take my word for it - read the other reviews.

title: Focus on the flavor and value
text:
These are not only delicious, but healthy. The online price is actually better than some local shops, further increasing the value of these tomatoes.

I do need to disclose that I purchase these locally from a large chain that specializes in health foods. As such my review is going to be based on the product and not the shipping, pricing or other variable factors.

In addition to these being delicious the total lack of anything but tomatoes and tomato puree is a key reason I love them. In this day and age it's rare to find any canned product that does not have added preservatives or salt. Granted, the shelf life is two years, but that is a small price to pay for the next best thing to fresh, ripened tomatoes. And make no mistake, these canned tomatoes can compete with a lot of locally grown, vine ripened tomatoes in my area for flavor.

Nutritionally each half cup of these tomatoes contains a mere 25 calories with a very low 25mg of sodium. The health benefits are obvious. Compare these numbers to any other canned, chopped tomatoes and be prepared for a shock.

Like others I often make decisions of Italian foods and wines based on the DOP or DOC assurance. These are not DOP, but I can assure you that you probably cannot tell the difference in a blind test. Indeed, DOP and DOC can also be straightjackets because in order to receive the certification growers have to follow processes that are traditional, but do not make sense in this day and age. In some cases, like DOC Chianti wines, the product can be inferior to non-DOC Sangiovese that is produced for less alongside the strictly compliant one. What I am saying is try these before writing them off.

Frankly, after discovering these I will not use anything else. The price alone - even shipped - is a bargain.

title: Perfect in soups and stews
text:
This and a very different spice mix by the same name are two distinctly Yemeni blends. This one is for soups and stews and the other one called hawaj is for spicing coffee. Hawaj, by the way, simply means 'mix' in Arabic.

What I love about this blend is the interesting flavors that are unlike any other spice mixes from the region. The spices used are fairly common - pepper, caraway, cardamom, cumin, nigella, salt and turmeric - but the dominating flavors of pepper and cardamom are what set this apart. The cumin in this particular mix is also somewhat prominent in the flavor profile.

Another reason I love this blend is the spices are fresh with an intense aroma and flavor.

While the directions claim that this can be used as a meat rub, frankly I do not think that is a good use. It's perfect in soups - both heavy and clear styles - and stews. It also works well as a seasoning for various beans, and especially the darker ones. However, I have also used this to season cannellini with delicious results. In fact, please ignore my opinion that this would not make a good meat rub. To your palate it may. And this is a fun spice blend with which to experiment.

title: Delicious and not too hot or spicy
text:
There is nothing metallic or chemical about the taste of these. They have a great texture and are plump and delicious. There is some bite, but nothing more than a jalapeno pepper. The flavor and not-so-spicy bite make these ideal to serve to a range of guests as long as they are not totally averse to some spiciness.

Ingredients are 100 percent pure and organic: hot peppers, water, salt and acetic acid. The latter is a natural ingredient that is common in vinegar and accounts for the slightly sour taste that is pleasant in most pickled products.

Do be aware that the main pickling is the brine itself - the salt and water. These have about 8 calories per one ounce serving, and a scant 2 grams of carbs with no fat or cholesterol. Unfortunately, at 570mg per serving they are pretty high in sodium. If you are watching sodium intake you can rinse them before consuming or serving, but some of the flavor profile is lost. Considering that the saltiness of these is part of the attraction you need to balance nutrition and health against flavor.

I purchase mine locally, so my cost is less than ordering online as is the risk of receiving dented cans. Please factor that into your purchase decision. If the sodium content is not an issue then I think you will love these if you enjoy mild Meditteranean-style peppers. They are perfect for meze or antipasti and are also allowed for folks who adhere to Kosher or Halal guidelines and restrictions.

title: Sometimes rules can be broken
text:
I almost never buy canned pickles or olives, but taking a chance on these was a good move on my part. The pickles are crunchy and delicious.

Their wonderful balance of dill and garlic with a hint of lemon (not listed as an ingredient, but there nonetheless), and the mild bite of pepper are why I love them. My palate tells me something that is contrary to some claims there is no metallic or bitter taste. Perhaps the reviewer who made that claim had a bad can, although I have purchased and consumed a number of canned products from this company without receiving a single bad can.

Ingredients are simple and natural without any that raise a red flag: cucumbers, water, salt, acetic acid, dill, garlic, pepper and calcium chloride.

Sodium is somewhere in the 340mg per ounce range, so if your can contains the full 25 pickles that is about right for one and a quarter of these delights. Not bad, but not good either. You can rinse them before serving, which will dramatically reduce the sodium. Unfortunately it will also diminish the saltiness which is a component of the flavor profile. Even rinsed, though, I find them to be delicious. And since each pickle is approximately four or five calories they are negligible in that department. Plus, there is zero fat or cholesterol.

Overall these are high quality pickles with a true Mediterranean flavor. If your dietary needs call for Kosher or Halal these are safe and one more reason to consider them.

title: Positively delicious
text:
These pickles are crunchy and have a wonderful flavor. You can taste the dill and garlic right away, and the subtle hint of pepper adds to what I consider to be a delicious side with a meal or meze for when I am entertaining.

That these are in a can is incredible - normally I only buy fresh from a barrel or from jars, but these are as good as any I have tried. I will disclose that I purchase these locally, so shipping issues and dented cans do not factor into my experience. As for the product and chemical and metallic taste that others have claimed I disagree. Perhaps those complaints are based on a single bad experience because I have consumed more than a few cans of these pickles as well as other products by the same company and have never been disappointed.

What I love besides the flavor and texture of these pickles is the simple and natural ingredients, which are cucumbers, water, salt, acetic acid, dill, garlic, pepper and calcium chloride. Nothing in that list that raises a red flag.

Do be aware of the sodium content, though. Each pickle has 340ml of sodium per ounce (basically per pickle), which is somewhat high. You can rinse them before serving, which will dramatically reduce the sodium, but will also diminish the saltiness which is a component of the flavor profile. Even rinsed, though, I find them to be delicious. And since each pickle is only 5 calories they are one of the more guilt-free pleasures in a meze or antipasti spread.

If you love Mediterranean style pickles with their wonderful mix of garlic, dill and pepper flavors you will probably enjoy these.

title: Surprisingly good considering they are canned
text:
I love olives - they are a staple of my diet. I have had the pleasure of enjoying them all over Europe and the Middle East, and have always tried for fresh first, jars second and never from a can. So imagine my surprise when I broke the cardinal rule and purchased a can of these only to find them excellent.

They are tasty with the slightest hint of the brine in which they are packed. The only bitterness I experienced is from the natural flavors of high grade olives. There is no metalic taste whatsoever. I buy these locally, so have avoided the dented can issue experienced by another reviewer.

The olives are plump with a perfect flesh and taste that one expects from high quality olives. On the nutrition side, though, you do need to be aware that since these are packed in basically brine the sodium content is high. A serving size is five olives, which contain 160mg of sodium. Calories per serving is a manageable 25, with fat coming in at 2.5 grams and carbs at a half gram. Overall these are not horrible figures, although the sodium needs to be monitored if you have restrictions.

Overall, these are excellent olives that are as good as some fresh ones I have had and if purchased locally quite inexpensive as well. If you love good olives I think you will be pleasantly surprised by these.

title: Excellent quality
text:
This is one of the best dried mints I have come across. It's highly aromatic and when reconstituted in oil or hot water has close to the same potency as fresh mint (which I also use in some dishes.)

Compared to the many different brands of dried mint I used in the past this is richer in fragrance and flavor, priced about the same and is locally available.

My main use is to infuse these flakes in hot olive oil for stews, but I have also used it in tea when I want to relive my youth (mint tea was popular in my home when I was growing up.) We used fresh mint and this comes close to recreating that taste.

This makes a great dressing that goes perfectly over a light salad of feta cheese and cucumbers. Mix one part vinegar or lemon juice with two parts of olive oil, add a tablespoon of these flakes and mix with the cheese and cucumber. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Add chopped parsley as an option to contrast with the mint.

Bottom line: this is one of the highest quality jars of dried mint I have come across and I have used most brands. To my palate there is no comparison - this one is hands down the best.

title: An excellent dry blend
text:
I normally purchase my harissa as a paste, but am starting to love these dry blends of which this brand is one of the better ones that I have tried. The ingredients are highly aromatic and fresh. I also love the blend itself which adds flavors to the chilis with cumin, caraway and allspice, among other ingredients.

Since this is a dry blend you can control both the bite from the chilis and the consistency of the paste by varying the amount of olive oil you use to mix into it. The heat is not to the degree of one of my favorite pre-made pastes ([[ASIN:B0001HAF3O Dea Harissa Hot Sauce in tube]]), but it also stores in the sealed tin in my pantry instead of the refrigerator after you have opened it.

Another thing I love about this dry blend is the small amount of sodium. A single teaspoon serving (before mixing with oil) contains a scant 2mg of sodium. This is a major plus for me over some of the other harissa dry blends that have a much higher sodium content.

While this is slightly milder than other harissa dry and paste blends I have used, it has an amazing flavor and can be kicked up a few notches by adding cayenne pepper to the mix before blending with olive oil. In fact, that is actually another plus because you can use this in tagine cooking to make authentic meals for guests who prefer a little less heat in their dishes.

Bottom line: I am impressed with the quality and flavor of this mix, and am especially pleased with the convenience of a low-sodium dry blend.

title: Packed with flavor and has a decent bite
text:
This is hot, but not to the extent that it masks the wonderful flavors of the blended basil and other spices. And flavor it has! I am of Calabrese descent (my grandfather emigrated from Reggio di Calabria in 1898), so I guess my taste for this spread is in my genes.

What I love most of all is the flavor. I am sure that this sauce was probably inspired by the Tunisian paste called harissa that shares the spiciness with this one, but has a slightly different flavor profile. There is no basil that I can discern in harissa and I have tried many brands of that condiment before settling on [[ASIN:B0050IKSBI Harissa Paste]] as my favorite brand. Other similarities between harissa and this is the consistency is near the same, although the harissa is smooth in appearance and looks like tomato paste.

This is a perfect addition to any arrabiata or fra diavolo style pasta dish, or as a simple spread for bread when setting out antipasti. I use it as part of the base when I am making lentils on a cold day, or to add a little kick to a non-traditional recipe for pasta e fagioli. In fact, the possibilities are limited only by your imagination. This is one condiment that has a place right beside my harissa, and one that reminds me of my own heritage.

title: A warm glow with a lot of flavor
text:
This is not for folks who like a touch of Tabasco or jalapenos. This paste is up there with habeneros for heat, but imparts wonderful flavors that you would never obtain from anything made with that pepper. Even if you love your food super spicy a little of this goes a long way. It overpowered the first omelet until I figured out how much was enough (about an eighth of a teaspoon works well).

It's the flavors that make this such a delightful paste. The label claims that in addition to peppers it contains carrots, turnips, tomatoes, coriander and caraway seeds. While I do not doubt that, the flavors become almost ineffable when blended with the dish in which it's used, and as spicy as it is, that aspect does not overpower the flavor. If anything it enhances it.

Aside from this being a wonderful way to spice up just about any kind of meal, this is essential for North African cuisine. I especially love adding this to za'atar on flat bread.

I've used it in everything from lentils to omelets, and have been delighted with it. Plus, this is spicy enough to satiate my palate that is hooked on super spicy food. You can always tame it down by mixing a dab with some olive oil and diluting it into your meal. If you love heat, a bite and wonderful flavor give this a try.

title: Simply delicious - but there are caveats
text:
NOTE: At the time of this review there are multiple products on this page that you can select. This review is for Pintos a la Diabla.

I tried these with a friend and was instantly smitten by the bite of the skillfully blended peppers and the wonderful flavor. I immediately tracked down a local source and purchased a can. That is where the caveats come in.

First, if you are a vegetarian, or your diet is based on Kosher or Halal restrictions, this is one you will regretfully have to pass by. Among the ingredients are both pork and bacon fat (I realize that bacon is pork, but it's still listed that way on the label.)

The full list of ingredients - verbatim from the label - is: Prepared Pinto Beans, Water, Tomato, Contains Less Than 2% of: Tomato Paste, Onion, Pork Fat, Bacon Fat, Canola Oil, Corn Flour, Pinto Bean Flour, Natural Flavor, Autolyzed Yeast Extract, Modified Corn Starch, Salt, Spice, Serrano Pepper.

Among the 'spice' listed above include jalapeno and chile de arbol in addition to the listed serrano pepper. If you are not a vegetarian and have no restrictions against pork, these beans have impressive nutritional values: of the seven half cup servings per can each serving is 100 calories, of which only 20 are from fat (which is a scant 2 grams). Moreover there is no cholesterol. Carbs are 16 grams per serving - about on par with unseasoned canned beans - and sodium is 440mg. Protein is 4 grams per serving, and potassium is 210mg.

Overall, the flavor profile is spicy and rich. In fact this has an impressive amount of chilis in the sauce. The nutritional values - despite the pork and bacon fats - are a lot healthier than some brands of canned pinto beans what are unseasoned.

If you love pinto beans with a distinct Latino flavor and heat - and have no dietary restrictions - this is a surprisingly great product.

title: Created for chicken but works with much, much more
text:
I almost never eat chicken, but I was intrigued by the blend of spices in this mix. As expected the base of the flavor profile is cilantro, coriander, cumin and turmeric, with the cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg adding a taste of the exotic. The mustard is subtle, and the black pepper seems to be the bridge between the two dominate sets of flavors. Combined this is not only intriguing, but it inspired me to experiment.

Before proceeding, the single thing that I love about this mix - besides the blend itself - is the fresh, intensely aromatic ingredients.

The first dish I tried this on was tagine haddock. The dense white flesh of that fish literally absorbed the spices and the preserved lemon I used, and was transformed into one of the most delicious dishes I have enjoyed in a long time. Preparation was simple: I rubbed the filets with some olive oil, then with this spice blend and proceeded from there.

I also tried this with great success as a seasoning for lentils, garbanzo beans, and even on fried eggplant. In fact, on everything BUT chicken (I tend to avoid most meats.) I am betting, though, that if you do eat chicken this is a perfect spice.

Bottom line: a two ounce jar goes a long way. Regardless of whether you own a tagine or prepare your food on a grill or in an oven this spice may enhance it in ways that will surprise you. It's definitely one for adventurous cooks to try, and essential for North African cuisine.

title: Superb blend and excellent quality
text:
I love this blend because it has some herbs that other herbes de Provence blends leave out. Specifically, not all brands include rosemary or lavender (or both). In addition to that I consider to be the optimum ingredients in the right proportions, the herbs used are fresh and highly aromatic. I will concede that the blend and proportions are subjective, but the quality is indisputable.

The way I use this is only as a seasoning on dishes that I have already prepared and just before serving them. The reason is the lavender in the mix loses its aroma when cooked. For some dishes like lamb this is not necessarily bad since the flavor of the lamb will overpower the nuances of the lavender, but for steamed vegetables or omelets I want the ineffable flavor of that spice in the mix.

Among my favorite uses is to season various steamed vegetables, such as red potatoes and carrots in butter, and on omelets and seafood (especially white flesh fish like haddock). It can also be used on meats. although the only meat I eat is lamb on Easter as a family tradition, this mix over the lamb right before it is served greatly enhances the flavor.

I've used other brands with mixed results. Many other brands are aromatic, but in this one the aromas are almost explosive in their intensity. That - to me - indicates that Zamouri uses the highest quality dried herbs to create this mix, and why I awarded it five stars.

title: Packed with intense flavor
text:
First, I purchase this locally so my review will focus strictly on the product and not price or other factors.

This brand of orange blossom water is potent and has an intensity of both flavor and fragrance that all of the other brands I have tried pale in comparison. Make no mistake: this is the real thing from Lebanon and one by which I judge all other brands.

If you are purchasing this for a single recipe and do not know how versatile this condiment is, here are some uses that will quickly deplete your stock. My favorite use is to add a teaspoon of this to eight ounces or hot water, stir in a tablespoon or more (to your taste) and enjoy a caffeine free hot beverage that is refreshing and soothing. Or add it to tea. In fact, use it in place of lemon (a few drops of this will do in most cases). It is also a good home remedy for stomach problems that I have found to be as effective as ginger.

Try using this in lieu of orange zest when called for in recipes, and a few drops in any chocolate will work wonders. Finally, a touch in sauces will add an ineffable flavor that especially complements tomato-based sauces and stews.

I love this brand and the condiment itself. There are so many uses that you are only limited by your imagination. But the bottom line is if you are shopping for orange blossom water this is - in my opinion - the best brand on the market.

title: Favorful and high quality
text:
I love the intense flavor and perfect balance of tart and sweet this particular brand brings to the table (pun intended). I do want to disclose up front that I purchase mine locally so this review will focus on the product and not the price.

If you are purchasing this for a specific recipe, do not waste the remaining bottle. There are many uses that may not seem obvious at first. My favorite is to base a salad dressing on a teaspoon of this whisked into three tablespoons of olive oil and some dried mint. Pour that over cucumbers, feta cheese and fresh tomatoes for a real treat. This is also a perfect substitute for any recipe or dish that calls for lemon. In fact, use this in lieu of preserved lemon in any tagine dish for a fresh flavor on an ancient way of cooking.

If you are counting calories or carbs be aware that a tablespoon contains 40 calories, 8 grams of carbs (from sugar) and a gram of fat. If you are counting carbs using this does require close attention, but the fat content is manageable at a single gram, and there is no sodium or cholesterol. Overall, this is relatively healthy.

The quality of this, like other Cortas products, is exceptional. I also use their rosewater and orange blossom water and will use no other brand if I have a choice because of the intensity of flavor. This is no exception.

title: Exceptionally flavorful blend
text:
I normally eat meat less than three or four times a year, but when I do it's usually lamb. This spice brings out the flavor perfectly.

The blend itself is a marvel of balancing flavors and aromas. There is no way I could take the same ingredients and mix them to the perfection that this has. More importantly, the spices are both fresh and highly aromatic, which is a testament to the quality of ingredients.

While paprika is listed as one of the primary spices, it is somewhat subtle in the flavor profile compared to the cumin and turmeric. The ginger is also prominent in the flavor and aroma, and adds a lot to the overall flavor and aroma.

Despite the claim that this is mainly for meat, it works beautifully with eggplant dishes - grilled, baked, fried or made into a dipping sauce. It also enhances lentils, garbanzo beans and other dishes. Thus, this blend has a place in the spice cabinets of vegetarians who want to add an exotic touch to their meals.

title: Excellent brand - one of the best I have purchased
text:
I can easily get this or other brands of Turkish coffee locally, but this one stands out as the best. The grind is absolutely perfect for brewing in a cezve (I use a relatively cheap model: [[ASIN:B005G74ARQ Turkish Coffee Pot (cezve/ibrik) with wooden handle - Small 8 oz]]).

It's not only the grind that I love about this brand, but also the quality of the coffee itself. It has an aroma that is rich and almost earthy. More importantly, it brews perfectly too. I use a little ground cardamom and a small cube of sugar when I am brewing mine.

Of course the best coffee in the world will not taste the best if it's not properly brewed. Here is how to ensure that your brew is perfect: First, use good water. Filtered or bottled. Most tap water will ruin the flavor of the brewed coffee.

Second, DO NOT fill the maker more than half way. And when heating do not use any heat source or setting above medium low. As soon as it boils immediately remove it from the heat and let it settle down. Trust me, it can get quickly out of control, so pay close attention. You can do a second boil to increase the strength of the brew.

If you follow the above instructions you will taste why I love this brand and gave it five stars.

title: Wonderful for making faux meat dishes
text:
The key to this delightful Turkish version of b'harat is the fennel. It imparts a flavor that is somewhat unique. Perhaps that spice is inspired by raki, a licorice-flavored beverage that is popular in Turkey. Regardless, this blend is very fresh and highly aromatic. Those characteristics are ample evidence of the quality.

I've tried various regional blends of b'harat, but this one is what I use in dishes when I want to imply meat while remaining vegetarian. It works because the fennel does evoke flavors of some sausages. It also works well in lentil dishes, and I have used it to make fried eggplant dishes that were simply delicious.

This mix still retains the 'sweet' fragrances that make up the aroma of a b'harat blend, but in a different way than the various Arabic regional varieties. It is vastly different in both flavor and aroma profiles, though, so take that into consideration if you have never used it, but want to experiment.

Regarding the brand itself - I purchase a lot of Zamouri products and have grown to expect the highest quality. I have yet to receive a spice from them that is less than totally fresh, and all have been strongly aromatic. Those are hallmarks of a high quality spice. They also seem to have a magic touch when it comes to getting the blends and proportions of mixes right, and this one is no exception.

title: A pinch transforms many dishes into something special
text:
This is a wonderful variation on b'harat, but with a slightly different flavor profile and more complexity. I love this particular brand because - like every other product I have purchased from them - the spices are fresh and wonderfully aromatic.

I use this a little differently than its close cousin b'harat, so I have both spices in my spice cabinet. This one is more of a 'secret ingredient' that I add a pinch of to dishes like soups, stews and sauces. In fact I commonly add a pinch to red pasta sauces, which gives them an ineffable Sicilian flavor. But bear in mind that a little goes a long way. This is an easy spice to overdo. Too much and what should be a savory dish will have a confusing aroma and taste that could wreck it.

One of my favorite dishes to use a hint of this is lentil soup. Another is Sicilian caponata sauce. However, let your imagination run wild. One whiff of this aromatic blend will trigger ideas of how it will fit within your own recipes. I also recommend hat you check out [[ASIN:B000FVMQJC Baharat Spice 2.0 oz - Zamouri Spices]], which is a related blend of spices that has a very different flavor profile, but will also work as a substitute if you want to vary your recipes by just changing the spices.

title: A vegetarian's delight
text:
I have used this in a tagine, as well as to spice soups, sauces and even sauteed vegetables. What makes this special to me - aside from the flavor it imparts - is the spices in this blend are fresh and highly aromatic. As soon as you open the jar you know that you are in for a treat.

Another thing I love is the way the spices are blended into this mix. The proportions are perfect to my taste. Plus, the only source I have found for this ahtriya is this brand.

One thing struck me the first time I used this spice: the way the ginger and rosemary contrasted, yet added a wonderful foundation for the other spices in the mix.

When I mentioned that I use this in sauces, two ways I love this is to add a little to a red pasta sauce before serving, as well as to mix some into a caponata for dipping bread. This spice totally changes the flavor profile for each. This is also an excellent spice to sprinkle on fried eggplant, and is perfect in Mediterranean style lentil soup.

For tagine cooking a favorite recipe is to cook a carrot and garbanzo dish using those ingredients plus chapped onion and garlic, a little chopped flat leaf parsley, dried apricots and a touch of honey. This spice manages to harmonize the flavors and aroma of the ingredients as it slow cooks in the tagine.

title: More like a great Cuban blend than an European grind
text:
I use this in two very different coffee makers and get different results. However, the brew from both share some common characteristics: smooth, rich and nice crema!

Indeed, for an Italian coffee this one is closer to the rich and smooth Cuban grinds that the European coffees with the slightly bitter - in a pleasant way - bite. It's like having the best of both worlds for me because I love both types of coffee for different reasons.

It's the crema that makes this a treat in my [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti 6800 Moka Express 6-Cup Stovetop Espresso Maker]]. The grind is perfect for that maker, and this is one of the better coffees to brew using that pot. However, when brewed in my [[ASIN:B0001DJT7G Bialetti Brikka 4-Cup Stovetop Percolator]], the result is pure heaven. That pot is designed to produce a rich, thick crema, and this blend's own recipe that results in a crema come together to make a heavenly brew. This should be bundled with every Brikka pot sold!

I cannot comment on how well this grind works in automatic espresso machines since I only use stove top pots, but I can only surmise that it will product the same rich, smooth cup with a nice layer of crema.

If you are totally sold on European style espresso with its characteristic bitterness you may find this to be too smooth. Also, while it has a lot of Cuban characteristics, it is not quite as rich as most of the Cuban brands, although the crema is significantly better. If, on the other hand, you own the Bialetti Brikka pot I recommend that you try this even if you love the distinctive European bitterness. In fact, try it anyway.

title: Delightful and worth every penny
text:
