To be honest there are not a lot of servings per jar - about 12 - but this is such a treat that it's worth every penny to me. The spices used are both fresh and potent. There is no way I can describe in words the flavor, so I will not attempt it. I will say that while cinnamon is supposed to be the dominating spice, the other spices used contribute a lot to the overall flavor. The problem is I cannot figure out which one does what.

Aside from the freshness and potency of the spices in this blend, I love the way they are proportioned. I have tried in vain to make my own, but never seem to get the portions right.

This is best made in an cezve - a Turkish coffee pot - that is also known as an ibrik. If you want to experiment, start with an inexpensive one like the [[ASIN:B005G74ARQ Turkish Coffee Pot (cezve/ibrik) with wooden handle - Small 8 oz]]. For coffee I recommend [[ASIN:B0012TAEJK Loumidis Greek Ground Coffee]], which has the right grind and is dark and rich like Moroccan coffee.

During the brewing process start with a teaspoon of this per two tablespoons of coffee for each cup. Bear in mind that a traditional cup is only three ounces. So, when I said this is expensive you now know what I mean because this jar will make about 12 cups of used in the above ratio.

First, use good water. Filtered or bottled. Most tap water will ruin the flavor of the brewed coffee. Second, DO NOT fill the maker more than half way. And when heating do not use any heat source or setting above medium low. As soon as it boils immediately remove it from the heat and let it settle down. Trust me, it can get quickly out of control, so pay close attention. Do a second boil to increase the strength of the brew, let settle and serve.

It's tempting to use a moka pot like the [[ASIN:B000CNY6UK Bialetti 6800 Moka Express 6-Cup Stovetop Espresso Maker]]. I recommend against that unless you plan to use the pot exclusively for Moroccan coffee. The reason is the aluminum pots absorb and retain flavors. That is one of the benefits and banes of that style of pot. Used once with these spices and it will take many subsequent brews before your normal coffee tastes like it should again. Trust me - I know this from personal experience. Also, the grind of the Greek coffee I use is too fine for moka pots.

Regardless of how you brew your coffee or how true you remain to authentic Moroccan brewing methods, this spice blend is a genuine pleasure. I promise you that the experience will be delightful.

title: A guilty pleasure
text:
I always have a few boxes of these in my pantry because not only do I love them, so do guests. These go perfectly with either coffee or tea - and, of course, milk.

The taste is what makes this one of my favorite cookies. I love the not-so-sweet aftertaste that is infused with almond. Even the texture is perfect (and especially for dunking.)

Where the guilty pleasure comes in is the nutritional values. Each cookie is 80 calories, and over half - 45 calories - are from fat. The 5 grams of fat per cookie include 1 gram of saturated and 1.25 grams of trans fat. Not a pretty picture if you are on a diet, but at least there is no cholesterol. If you are watching your sodium intake each cookie contains 35mg.

While the above values are scary, they are no worse than many other cookies, and if consumed in moderation - as an occasional guilty pleasure - will not do harm to most folks.

The final thing I love about these is their shelf life. They are in a plastic tray that prevents breaking and crumbling, and are sealed to keep them fresh. I have opened boxes that were in my pantry for six months and they were fresh. Usually they do not last long once opened, so I cannot say how long they would stay fresh - but I suspect for a few weeks is sealed in a plastic container.

title: High quality and necessary for many Middle Eastern recipes
text:
I purchase mine locally, so this review is going to focus on this product and not the price. If you prepare Middle Eastern dishes, and especially Persian, this is an essential ingredient in many.

The quality of this, like other Cortas products, is exceptional. I also use their rosewater and orange blossom water and will use no other brand if I have a choice because of the intensity of flavor. This is no exception.

If you are purchasing this for a specific recipe, do not waste the remaining bottle. There are many uses that may not seem obvious at first. My favorite is to base a salad dressing on a teaspoon of this whisked into three tablespoons of olive oil and some dried mint. Pour that over cucumbers, feta cheese and fresh tomatoes for a real treat.

This is also a perfect substitute for any recipe or dish that calls for lemon. In fact, use this in lieu of preserved lemon in any tagine dish for a fresh flavor on an ancient way of cooking.

Do be aware that a tablespoon contains 40 calories, 8 grams of carbs (from sugar) and a gram of fat. If you are counting carbs using this does require close attention, but the fat content is manageable at a single gram, and there is no sodium or cholesterol. Overall, this is relatively healthy.

One final use - if you are cooking Asian dishes that call for tamarind (sampalok in Tagalog) this is a decent substitute.

A bottle is always in my pantry because I do use this to contrast sweetness with a touch of sour, or as an interesting replacement for lemon. You are only limited by your imagination and creativity.

title: Excellent mix of a firey paste
text:
I am going to sidestep pricing and other factors not relevant to this excellent product and focus on the harissa itself.

Like every condiment there are numerous recipes and mixes, and this one is no exception. I love it because it is spicier than other brands that I have tried, but most importantly, it has a wonderful flavor. Some brands are more biased towards heat with less though given to taste. This is a balance of both.

To be sure this is not for folks who like a touch of Tabasco or jalapenos. This paste is up there with habeneros for heat, but imparts wonderful flavors that you would never obtain from anything made with that pepper. Indeed, what sets this apart from every other hot sauce or paste I've tried is the interesting way it teases your palate. The label claims that in addition to peppers it contains carrots, turnips, tomatoes, coriander and caraway seeds. While I do not doubt that, the flavors become almost ineffable when blended with the dish in which it's used, and as spicy as it is, that aspect does not overpower the flavor. If anything it enhances it.

I've tried this in dishes like an omelet, beans and a fish stew. Believe me, even if you love your food super spicy a little of this goes a long way. It overpowered the first omelet until I figured out how much was enough (about an eighth of a teaspoon works well). A good rule of thumb that I have devised for my own personal taste is to use a tablespoon per 16 ounces of food. One final use I have discovered is to mix it in with za'atar to make a devilishly hot spread for flat breads. Za'atar can be quickly and easily made by mixing equal parts of oregany, thyme, marjoram, toasted sesame seeds and summac. Add a pinch of sea sale and make a paste with olive oil. From there blend in a little of this harissa to your taste and you have a wonderful spread that will bring flat bread to life.

title: So enticing that I broke my no meat rule
text:
Normally I only eat vegetables and fish, but as a tradition I do have lamb every Easter. This arrived long after Easter, but the aroma of the spices was irresistible and I could not get lamb out of my head. I succumbed and am glad I did.

I'm safely back on my meatless diet, but have found a plethora of uses for this spice blend. It goes beautifully with lentil dishes - Indian dal style or the many ones based on Mediterranean recipes. It also transforms red beans and rice into an exotic dish that has become a favorite quick meal.

I also love it sprinkled over rice as a subtle and ineffable flavor, although I have to admit that this company's [[ASIN:B0063J1PLU Persian Adwiya]] works better for that use. While this will probably enhance a variety of meats, I think that it would overpower most fish. I may experiment since fish is a large part of my diet, but the flavors are too intense for most fish.

If you do eat meat the Afghan Kofta Kebab recipe printed on the top of the can may be a good starting place for trying this blend in a recipe for which it seems perfect. If you are, like me, mainly vegetarian, a good place to start is with a hearty vegetable stew or eggplant dish.

title: As complex as a fine wine
text:
This spice blend is like a fine wine that exhibits layers of complexities. The analogy goes further in that, like a fine wine, the nuances are not immediately apparent.

Like all spice blends from this company this one is highly aromatic with a fragrance that practically wafts out of the can as soon as you open it. One of my initial tests when a new spice arrives is to sprinkle some over rice, which is neutral enough to allow the flavors and aroma to come through. The can had a Persian rice recipe printed on the lid. I did not completely follow it because I do not use broths in rice, but I did make basmati rice, then after it had steamed and I fluffed it, I mixed a little butter and sprinkled some of this blend. Pure heaven!

What I personally loved about the flavor is how the rose petals, cinnamon and lemon zest dominated the flavors, but also how the cumin and black pepper anchored them. This is truly a magical spice for folks who have discerning palates.

I eat a lot of beans and legumes, so the second test to which I put this was to saute a little garlic and red onion in olive oil, then simmer cannellini beans until they were completely cooked. I then added this spice and was rewarded with a delicious meal. I have not tried them in my lentil soup recipe yet, but based on what I have tasted thus far I am sure it will be a marriage of spices and ingredients that will be delicious.

One final idea is to mix a little in caponata. I am ashamed to admit that I purchased a pre-made caponata sauce instead of making one from scratch, but mixing in a little of this spice transformed it. The same with hummus.

Mark this as another staple in my spice cabinet. I absolutely love it.

title: One of life's pleasures
text:
Life's pleasures can be as simple as grated fish roe in a good oil.

Although I prefer the tuna roe (see [[ASIN:B00AQ3D2QU Bottarga Di Tuna (Tuna Roe)]]), this one has has a lot of merit as well. Especially when grated into salads or as a substitute for anchovies in some recipes like spaghetti alla puttanesca or spaghetti con aglio e olio (spaghetti with garlic and oil.) Especially in salads or in spaghetti alla puttanesca the tuna roe version does not marry well with the other ingredients and can mask flavors if you are not careful. This roe, on the other hand, seems to go perfectly with those dishes.

First rule of using this or any bottarga: do NOT cook with it. Instead grate it over a finished dish before serving in much the same way you would a fine, hard cheese. I learned the hard way that cooking it into a recipe guarantees you will have a salty, bitter dish that only a Klingon would enjoy.

When I was researching this product I learned that Cabras, Sardinia is renowned for their high quality bottarga, and it shows in the quality. In the process I also came across a recipe that proved to be delicious beyond my imagination and is now fare that I serve guests whom I really want to impress: brown shallots or onions in high quality olive oil, add fresh tuna and braise on all sides. Then add capers and chopped tomatoes. Salt to taste (I also use black and red pepper). Toss into an authentic Sardinia pasta like [[ASIN:B005R3Z1PO La Casa del Grano Pasta - Is Malloreddus]] (also known as gnocchetti Sardi), season with this grated bottarga di muggine and serve. This is not only authentic Sardinia fare, but it's fast and easy to make and delicious.

Compared to a slab of bottarga di muggine this jar is more convenient because you do not have to shave it since it's pre-grated. Since I do not use this all of the time the jar is perfect.

Experiment and add a dash over savory dishes and you may discover some recipe secrets that you can either share or jealously guard.

title: Easily lives up to its reputation
text:
Normally I eschew the boutique olive oils because some more common brands are good enough to be a well kept secret. This one, though, is an olive oil lover's dream come true.

It has the grassy notes that characterize Ligurian oils, and that back of the mouth burn is perfect. I'll admit that I rarely purchase this because I am on a fixed income, but there are times during the year when I absolutely have to treat myself to something nice, and this is it. Not my favorite wines or cheeses, but this.

What I love is the care taken to protect the oil. The foil wrapped bottles are not marketing hype (well, perhaps partly), but a means to completely block light and extend the life. I have purchased boutique oils in the past only to be disappointed because they were stale. I have never experienced that problem with this oil, and I purchase it at least once a year. Always fresh and always consistent. Believe it or not, but I first discovered this oil at a TJs in Tustin, CA in early 2001. It was priced at less than ten bucks and I took a chance. One taste and I was immediately sold. Fast forward to today. The price is higher, but this is still the gold standard for me.

I use this over a Caprese salad or to make bruschetta, and I happily drizzle it over arugula salads. Heaven, though, is mixing it with [[ASIN:B000C1U83Q Bottarga Di Muggine (Grey Mullet Roe) - Grated - From Cabras, Sardinia]]. If you love high quality olive oils and have not tried this, I recommend that you do. If all olive oils taste the same to you then, perhaps, you should save your money. Personally, I will continue to treat myself to a bottle every year. It's one of the things that make life worth living.

title: Relatively mild with an excellent flavor
text:
I first tried this at a Portuguese restaurant and loved how the flavor added to the meal. It even transformed rice and black beans into a treat.

In the title I claimed that this is relatively mild, but that is a subjective term. The closest familiar (in the US market) hot sauce that this comes to with respect to heat is Tabasco sauce. Use that comparison as a gauge because it is about on that level.

Where this dramatically differs from Tabasco is that sauce has a strong vinegar base that I personally dislike. This one, though, imparts a completely different flavor. To be sure, it is salty with a little over four grams of salt per serving. That is really a nominal amount of salt that should not conflict with any diets restricting sodium. The ingredients are 45% peppers, with water, salt and vegetable oil as the primary ingredients. The vegetable oil varies, but palm oil is often used in the recipe.

Although I love spicier sauces, the flavor of this one appeals to me and I have a bottle in my pantry because it does lend an authentic flavor to Portuguese cuisine.

title: High quality snack with good nutritional values
text:
These have a nice texture and easy-to-pop skin. I purchase mine locally and at a better price, but still love the brand.

Nutritionally these have only thirty calories per forty grams of drained beans. There is zero fat or cholesterol, and three grams of carbs that are balanced by three grams of protein. Each jar contains about six servings. Sodium is 195mg, but more about how to reduce that below.

The contents are simple: beans, water, salt and citric acid, with a nominal amount of a preservative called benzoate of soda (less than a tenth of a percent).

I am on a diet that requires that I carefully watch my sodium intake, so I thoroughly rinse these before I eat them. Indeed, washed and drizzled with high quality olive oil and a squeeze of a lemon and freshly ground black pepper is my preferred way to enjoy these. Some folks eat them, skin and all. I pop off the skin on mine. Either way, they are both delicious to my palate and nutritious (especially if rinsed.)

In addition to snacks, they are a perfect addition to any meze or antipasti spread. Your guest will love you for putting them out.

title: Absolutely top quality saffron
text:
Earlier I reviewed a smaller vial of this saffron after the manufacturer sent me a sample. I was thoroughly impressed with the quality and value and inspired to continue purchasing it. I frequently cook with saffron and know what to look for - and this one passes all of my tests for quality. Basically there are three main things I check to determine the quality of saffron: (1) color, (2) feel and texture, and (3) fragrance. This saffron easily passes all three checkpoints.

Color: of the three tests, color can be easily faked with dye. This comes in well above the minimum of 190 color units for Grade I saffron. In fact, it is closer to 150. The reason this particular brand is not altered with dye is it also tops the other two tests.

Feel and Texture: This saffron is both dry and brittle and will easily crumple between your fingers. Those are the hallmark of a quality saffron that has been properly stored.

Fragrance: There is no musty odor - the saffron smells fresh.

I've cooked with this (rice, as well as in stews and soups), and have infused tea with it. That is the main test - taste - and it passes that also with flying colors (no pun intended).

It's difficult to find a decent quality saffron at any price, but to find this high quality one priced more than reasonably is one reason why I quickly became loyal to the brand and will continue to use it. This vial is perfect for folks who are moderately heavy users of saffron. If you cook with saffron more than once a week it should last somewhere between six months to a year.

title: In a word: potent
text:
I've used different rosewater brands and none have come close to this one in potency. It has an intense fragrance and a very little is all that is needed to flavor foods.

The company that makes this is known for its quality rosewater and orange blossom water (which I also use). What I love is the intensity that seems to be an order of magnitude stronger than any other brand. I also love the shelf life - this stuff will last for months after opening if you refrigerate it.

My main use is to flavor sweet rice dishes, as well as to flavor tea by adding a few drops. Some Persian recipes that I cook require it, and it's also indispensable for many Lebanese dishes and desserts.

If you are looking for a high quality rosewater for cooking or adding a wonderful touch to some beverages this is the brand I recommend. I would not think of using anything else.

title: Good for quick & tasty meals, but don't expect miracles
text:
I keep a few boxes of this in my pantry for those days when I am too lazy to cook from scratch. This is more of a base for a paella than a complete one - even the directions on the box make recommendations for adding ingredients.

Out of the box and prepared per directions this is tasty and hearty. It is not, however, a true paella in the strictest sense of the word. Think of it as a seafood rice dish that will please the palate and you will enjoy it. Compare it to a true paella and you will be unhappy.

What you are getting is convenience. It takes less than 25 minutes from the time you open the box until you are eating. There are two sets of ingredients - a bag of rice with spices to approximate paella, and a can of seafood and vegetables to provide a base that flavors the rice.

Cooking is easy: you bring three cups of water to a boil, add the rice and stir for a minute, then add the contents of the can and reduce to simmer and cover for 20 minutes. I usually add mussels and whatever fish I have on hand to mine, and I also add some [[ASIN:B005F5K7YO Badia Paprika]]. When I really want to get fancy I purchase a bag of marisco - mixed shellfish - at my local supermarket.

Nutritionally there are some things you need to know. First, the rice mix contains monosodium glutamate. Second, this box makes eight servings, each of which is 250 calories. Of those, 80 are from fat which is 9 grams per serving. Sodium is a whopping 770mg per serving, and cholesterol is 20mg. Carms come in at 36 grams per serving. This is, indeed, fast food and you pay a price in nutrition in exchange for convenience. For an occasional fast meal this is not a deal breaker. I watch my intake and still keep these on hand. For more frequent use - like weekly - this is not exactly something I would add to my menu planning.

I awarded this five stars because it is fast and tasty, and can be easily modified to be even tastier. As an occasional meal this is a convenience that I keep in my pantry.

title: Many uses in cooking and beverages
text:
All orange blossom water brands are perfect for adding to sweet and savory recipes, among other uses, but this brand stands apart from the pack in my opinion.

First, this brand is potent and has an intensity of both flavor and fragrance that all of the other brands I have tried pale in comparison. Second, this is the real thing from Lebanon.

Some folks purchase a single bottle for a specific recipe, using a fraction and either toss the rest of allow it to take up space in a refrigerator. If you are among that group here are some uses that will not only quickly use up this bottle, but will have you purchasing it in larger quantities. My favorite use is to add a teaspoon of this to eight ounces or hot water, stir in a tablespoon or more (to your taste) and enjoy a caffeine free hot beverage that is refreshing and soothing. Or add it to tea. In fact, use it in place of lemon (a few drops of this will do in most cases). It is also a good home remedy for stomach problems that I have found to be as effective as ginger.

In fact the uses for this are limited by your imagination and willingness to think outside the box. Some obvious ones include using this in lieu of orange zest when called for in recipes, and a few drops in any chocolate will work wonders. Finally, a touch in sauces will add an ineffable flavor that especially complements tomato-based sauces and stews.

Suffice to say, I go through a lot of this water in general and this brand in particular. I am fortunate in that it is readily available locally, which means a better price, but it is so versatile that I always have a few bottles on hand.

title: Fresh and an excellent price
text:
I purchase mine locally, but at the time of this review the price here is actually lower than what I pay at my local supermarket.

However, one cannot put a price on high quality ingredients and these are just that. I love them because they are fresh, firm and are both fragrant and delicious. I insist on using nothing but the best quality ingredients when I prepare meals, which is why I prefer this brand. I have never been disappointed by Diamond and I have purchased literally dozens of these bags of pine nuts with consistently outstanding results. Never a stale bag!

I use these mainly for making pesto, and even when I am cooking for three or four I only use a half of a bag. I tend to emphasize fresh basil, so these nuts are more of a base, while the thickness comes from finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. I also use them as a garnish over steamed vegetables and in fresh salads, which they augment perfectly.

Regarding the reviews complaining about these coming from China - I fail to see the problem. I a solely interested in quality food stuffs, and these are as good as any pine nuts from any source of origin.

Do be aware that these are high in calories and fat. There are four two ounce servings per bag and each is 200 calories, 180 of which are from fat. There is no cholesterol or sodium, but each 30 gram serving contains 21 grams of fat and 4 grams of carbs. If you use these to make pesto and consider what the olive oil and Parmigiano-Reggiano add in calories, carbs and fat you will be surprised at how quickly they add up. I am not mentioning this to discourage your using these as an ingredient, but to promote an awareness of the nutritional values they contain. I still enjoy pesto over pasta, but in moderation.

The bottom line, though, is these are an excellent source of high quality pine nuts at a very reasonable price (at the time of this review). If you use pine nuts I wholeheartedly recommend these.

title: Totally unique ras el hanout blend
text:
Ten different masters will mix ten different blends of ras el hanout because each is as unique as a fingerprint. Usually there will be subtle differences depending on which spice is favored or emphasized. This blend, though, is unexpected.

It has the aroma of a well blended ras el hanout, but the rose pedals, nutmeg and ginger fool you into thinking that this is an exotic Persian or Lebanese spice mix. Then the turmeric, mace, clove, anise and cardamon point to India. The cardamom is the wildcard because it could have come from anywhere, but the lavender hints at Provence. Actually, the lavender makes sense because of the French influence. No, it all makes sense because it actually flavors any North African dish with authority and authenticity.

I am frankly not wild about the salt. Himalayan pink salt does have a signature flavor, but it's salt at the end of the day and I - like many others - watch my intake. In the case of this delightful (and highly skillful, if not imaginative) blend of spices and herbs I will put up with the salt.

The more I think about it, this fits more as a mix along the lines of a couscous blend than a true ras el hanout. Those blends are typically ras el hanout on steroids and that is exactly what this one is. If you love Moroccan or North African cuisine (or even Sicilian cooking) definitely give this a try.

title: Ras el hanout on steroids! Superb spice mix
text:
I agree with the previous two reviewers and especially the 22 April 2013 one regarding the versatility of this mix. It can be used in a multitude of dishes ranging from soups and stews to grains and legumes.

What I love is the solid ras el hanout base with peppery spices dominating, and aromatic ones such as ginger and nutmeg balancing out the peppercorns and cayenne. Indeed, think of this as a bare bones ras el hanout with a slight kick.

The main purpose of this mix is to flavor the bottom ingredients that are cooked in a [[ASIN:B001KZHDL8 Couscoussier]], which is a two chamber steaming pot in which a stew or other dish is cooked in the bottom chamber while the couscous is steamed in the top chamber. That is where the aromatic spices in this blend come in - they waft up in the steam and flavor the couscous in the upper chamber while permeating the ingredients in the lower one.

This also works magic is sprinkled over basmati rice regardless of the cuisine. A pinch in a red pasta sauce of ragu instantly transforms it into Sicilian even if it started out as inspired by Puglia.

title: Superior quality at a reasonable price
text:
I am always on the lookout for reliable sources of high quality saffron, so was gratified to find a US source that is also reasonably priced. I came across this brand when the company provided me with a review sample. I tried it out, posted a review and was sold. By the way, this is NOT the review of that sample - this review is my personal enthusiasm for the product.

When I evaluate saffron I look for three things: color, feel and freshness. The color easily exceeds the 190 color units that is required to call a saffron Grade I. In fact this one is probably closer to 250 (give or take).

Color is only one characteristic and can be faked. There is feel too. This has the feel of a high quality saffron - it's brittle enough to pulverize between your fingers, and it is dry. Of course the two characteristics are related. And, finally, if has a fresh fragrance. I am looking for whether or not the saffron was improperly handled or stored, which would make it give off a musty odor. This one does not.

I use a lot of saffron. I cook with it at least twice a week, so I can quickly tell if I have high quality or a lower grade. This is definitely high quality. If you are a moderate user of saffron; i.e., cooking with it about once every eight weeks or so, this is a year's supply. For me - a heavy user who cooks with it twice a week - it will last about two months. Use this information as a gauge as to whether this size is right for you because the company sells it in larger sizes.

One final note: this is Sargol saffron, which comes from a small area in Iran and is considered to be one of world's best. I have made more than a few dishes with various batches of this saffron and have been thoroughly pleased with it. When I do have to replenish my stash it will be with more of this brand, and probably this size too because it allows me to rotate my supply before it gets stale. It's the real thing and is worth every penny!

title: One of a few brands of harissa I routinely use
text:
I love the variations between and among brands of this wonderful paste, and this is one that pleases my palate.

What drew me to this is the flavor. It is a little different from the other brands of harissa I frequently use and each has its own flavor personality. This one has a distinct cardamom flavor that my other favorite brands lack. That balances the spiciness in an interesting way because my palate associates cardamom with sweets, while the heat and bite from the peppers counterbalance that effect.

Other aspects that I love about this harissa is the way the garlic is a little more dominate than in other brands, and the olive oil, which is exceptionally high quality.

Nutritionally, this particular brand of harissa comes in at a lower caloric content than others, and is has zero sodium, which is a major contrast with another of my favorite brands - [[ASIN:B0084L61OG Mediterranean Harissa (8.8 ounce)]] - that comes on at 298mg per serving. This one not only has zero sodium and cholesterol, but only 51 calories per 11 gram serving. Fat and carbs come in at 4 grams each. If you compare these values to other brands you will see that this is one of the most favorable for nutrition.

This is not only an excellent harissa for authentic Tunesian cuisine, but adds authenticity to some Sicilian dishes as well. It's slightly different in flavor from other brands, and middle-of-the-road in spiciness compared to others. I will confess that I often squeeze a little lemon into mine before I use it, but that is a personal preference. I definitely recommend this one if you are looking for harissa that is both flavorful and piquant.

title: Nice bite and full of flavor
text:
I love trying various brands of harissa as well as making my own using dry harissa, a little lemon and olive oil. This one is has become one of my favorites.

What I love is it is pre-mixed with very flavorful peppers that are complemented by the ras el hanout spice and olive oil. It also has a wonderful touch of lemon that is more a nuance than a dominating flavor.

The ras el hanout, too, is somewhat subtle in the mix. The blend used seems to be more on the aromatic side, but still does not overpower the peppers. There is a nice, spicy bite to this mix too. Not over-the-top spicy, but not wimpy either. It's difficult to describe flavors and piquant qualities,, so the best I can do is say that this falls about three quarters away from a jalapeno towards the spiciness of a halapeno. Pretty hot, but not so much that it's distracting.

Nutritionally this harissa has some values of which you need to be aware if you are watching calories or sodium. There are 16 servings per jar, each of which is 16 grams. Each serving is 77 calories (17 of which are from the 1.9 grams of fat per serving.) There is no cholesterol, but there are 11 grams of carbs. The number that I personally watch is sodium and this contains 298mg per serving. These are not terrible numbers since one typically uses small amount of harissa in a dish, but is useful to know for folks like me who do have dietary restrictions.

Overall this harissa has - to me - a perfect balance of spiciness and flavor, and is definitely authentic tasting. It's worth a try.

title: Yet anoither favorite blend of this essential mix
text:
I wish I had a penny for each variation of this blend because I'd be rich. I have made my own (and continue to do so), and have experimented with countless blends. This and a handful of others are among my favorites.

The reason I love this one is it is convenient and is also fresh and aromatic. The ingredients are sparser than some blends, which leaves me room to tailor this to whichever dish I am cooking. Basically this one contains coriander, green and black cardamon, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaves, nutmeg, ginger, pepper and cumin. The main ingredients are definitely aromatic, but the blend also leaves me the freedom to add turmeric, fennel, anise and other spices or combinations.

Indeed, the flexibility that this allows me is one of the reasons I selected it for my spice cabinet. That and the fact that every jar has been fresh (and reasonably priced) earn it my highest recommendation.

One final note: this is available from a number of local sources, so it's even more convenient. But if I were to order it here the fact that it is part of the 'Add-On' program (at the time of this review) in which it ships for free for qualifying Super Saver orders make this a good bargain as well as a great garam masala mix.

title: One of a near infinite number of variations - this is a decent one
text:
When it comes to garam masala blends I usually prefer to start with a simple base like [[ASIN:B003JO5TIW Ajika Organic Whole Garam Masala]], which contains whole cinnamon, cloves and cardamom. Nothing more and nothing less. I then add my own additional spices, usually in whole form too and I grind them in a coffee grinder.

However, when I am in a hurry this is a convenient and full bodied blend that I love. It is pre-ground and contains turmeric, red chile powder, ginger powder, mustard seeds, fennel, and star anise. While pre-ground spices and herbs are not as potent and aromatic as whole ingredients that you grind yourself, this blend is surprisingly fresh and pungent. I love how the aroma rushes out as soon as you unscrew the cap.

One key to getting the most out of this blend is to toast it in oil or clarified butter before adding the other ingredients for whatever dish you are cooking. That step will release the flavors and aromas immediately, and further intensifies this particular blend.

The best use for this is as a general purpose garam masala mix when you are pressed for time and also want to add a complexity of flavor without fuss and muss. There are other pre-ground blends that I also use, depending on what I am preparing. A less complex one which I also use is [[ASIN:B000GHJJVI Garam Masala Spice Blend]] (and especially when I want total control over the turmeric in the mix.)

If you are experimenting with Indian cooking and are looking for a single blend that will work in many basic recipes, this is a good blend to start with. If you already understand the nuances of regional Indian cuisine this one may be too single-purpose with its array of ingredients that does not leave room for tailoring.

If you do opt for this product you will get a nice blend of perfectly proportioned spices and herbs. This mix is wonderfully aromatic and very fresh. You will not be disappointed.

title: Quickly became my preferred brand
text:
I discovered this brand when I was provided with a small sample to review. I was so impressed with the quality and the price that I quickly decided that this would be my preferred source of saffron going forward.

This easily passes the three basic tests when you are evaluating saffron for quality. First, the color is the deep red that indicates a top grade. This saffron is from the Sargol area in Iran, which is a relatively small area that is renown for its saffron. I've come to expect any saffron from Sargol on the open market to pass the color test.

The other two tests have more to do with the storage and handling of the saffron. Even the highest grade can be ruined by carelessness. The of these tests is to make sure that the stigmas (threads) are dry and brittle. If you can easily crumple a stigma between your fingers then you can be reasonably sure that it is top quality. The final test is to sniff it (right from the container) to make sure there is no musty smell that would indicate that it had been exposed to moisture at some point.

This saffron passes all of the tests with flying colors (no pun intended). As important is the price. This brand is reasonably priced considering the quality. In fact, if you compare this brand to saffron you commonly find in the spice section of a supermarket, you will see the value here. Take this common brand as an example: [[ASIN:B0012ORCPY McCormick Gourmet Collection, Spanish Saffron, 0.06-Ounce Unit]]. It's a little over a half a gram at little less than half the price. This is ten grams. You can do the math.

Another reason I love this is it's a perfect size for me because I am a heavy user of saffron. I cook with it at least twice a week, so conservatively this will last four months (much longer if I do not entertain guests with meals.) In fact, this is easily a year's supply for households that are moderate users of saffron.

The bottom line is this is a brand that has earned my trust because each batch of saffron is consistently of the highest quality.

title: One of my guilty pleasures
text:
To say that these are delicious would be an understatement. They are well made chocolate with a wonderful finish and a rich flavor that indicate that the company knows a thing or two about the art of chocolate making.

I have to be honest and state up front that I do not indulge in chocolate often. When I do indulge it's with an espresso. These go perfectly with any coffee and are a touch of both luxury and decadence that we all need periodically.

This is a variety pack that consists of seven different styles: milk chocolate, Coffee and Cream, Hazelnut Almond, Hazelnut Cream, Dark Cream, Dark Mousse and Praline Cream. There are twenty pieces in a box.

If you have lactose issues or are a vegan know that each style contains milk products. Thankfully these do NOT contain high fructose corn syrup (something that cannot be said about some other premium, flavored chocolates). While the box claims a serving size of four pieces I am going to provide the nutritional values for a single one. Each contains 75 calories, of which 45 of those calories are from fat. There are 5 grams of fat per piece, of which 3 grams are saturated. There is less than 2mg of cholesterol in each one, and 7.5mg of sodium.

The above nutritional values are not terrible for flavored chocolates, and are actually better than competing chocolates. As long as you are aware of what you are consuming and do so in moderation this is a wonderful treat that is rich and creamy, and of the highest quality.

I keep these on hand mainly for guests, but to also to satisfy late night cravings that occasionally arise. They are expensive, but to me they are worth every penny.

title: I love this particular blend
text:
Za'atar blends vary - especially by region - and this one has a distinct Palestinian flavor.

The way that the thyme dominates appeals to my palate. I definitely love the summac too. That is one spice that I frequently use in a large number of dishes and the citrus nuance adds an interesting flavor that is a cross between Lebanese and Persian.

What I love, aside from the flavor of this blend, is the aroma of the herbs and spices used. They are intense. The sesame is perfectly toasted and the blend itself seems to have the right proportions of each ingredient.

The traditional way of using this is to dip bread in olive oil, then za'atar. Personally I rarely consume it that way. I'll confess that I use this more for making man'ousheh, which is nothing more than za'atar and olive oil spread over a piece of flat bread and baked. ANd when I do dip it I add this to a dish of olive oil much the same way as Italian dipping spices are used, and eat it that way.

Regardless of how you consume it, this is an excellent blend of za'atar that is a lot more convenient than making it from scratch.

title: High quality saffron in a perfect size for light use
text:
This is an exceptionally high quality saffron packaged in a quantity that will last you about six months if you cook with saffron about every seven or eight weeks. Please see the customer-supplied photo that I uploaded to the top of this page to see the size of this vial relative to a twenty-five cents coin.

Before proceeding I need to disclose that I received this product in exchange for an honest and candid review. I can honestly state that this is a five star product that is also a great value.

The first thing I did when I received this was to check it for texture. All high quality saffron is brittle and dry, and will easily crumple between your fingers. This passed that test with flying colors. I sniffed it to ensure that it had a nice fragrance instead of a musty odor that would indicate stale saffron. Again, it easily passed. As importantly, the color says a lot about the quality of saffron and this one had that intense, deep red that one looks for. Saffron is graded and the top grade requires the color to be 190 units or above on a color scale. This one was at least 40 points (and possibly more) higher.

However, the real test is flavor. I prepared some and made a simple basmati dish that only had a little sea salt to test the flavor. This had the nuances and fragrance of excellent saffron. I then added a little ras el hanout (a Moroccan spice blend) to see if the flavor would come through. It did in a subtle way that convinced me that this is truly a sargol saffron that has earned the reputation as being among the world's best.

When you take into account the price of a run of the mill saffron found in most grocery stores that sell for nearly the same price as this, then the value is apparent. Compare it to [[ASIN:B0000EWNHE Vigo Saffron 1/2 Gram]], which at the time of this review is two thirds the price for one sixth of the quantity and this one is a bargain. When you factor in that this is truly a top grade of safffron, then it is a bargain at any price if you are used to top quality saffron.

Frankly, this brand has become my favorite for a few reasons. First I trust the quality. Second, the price is among the best bargains around, and finally it ships from a US location so delivery is fast and no customs hassles.

title: Exquisite flavor
text:
This is specifically mixed for Indian-style pilafs, but is a lot more versatile if you use your imagination.

The ingredients are perfectly proportioned and the spices used to augment the raisins and nuts make this close to ambrosia. The mix itself is comprised of Cashews, pistachios, raisins, cinnamon, green cardamom, cumin seeds - all of which are fresh. It's the skillful blending of the green cardamon and cumin seeds that sets this apart. At least to my palate.

I have to admit that I usually take the spices up a notch by adding [[ASIN:B003JO7RU0 Ajika Organic Garam Masala]] to my dishes when I am preparing them. That is just me suiting my own personal taste and cooking style. This blend out of the bottle can easily stand alone as the sole spices in a dish, except for salt.

If you are using it to make a pilaf or biryani this jar's contents will suffice if you are serving six people and maybe eight. I live alone, so I can make it last for three meals, depending on what those meals are.

In addition to a pilaf, this can be used as a garnish. First, one of my pilaf recipes to illustrate how I use this mix. I will prepare a quarter of a teaspoon of saffron in a cup of boiling water and let sit while I am preparing the rest of the dish. Next I toast this mix and a tablespoon of garam masala in oil (I use olive oil, but you can use any oil you choose or clarified butter). Finally I add a finely chopped carrot, a minced garlic clove and shallots, and saute until the garlic has browned and the shallots begin to caramelize. I then add water and basmati rice, bring to a boil for two minutes uncovered, then cover, reduce the heat and let simmer for eleven more minutes. Midway through I fluff the rice. I salt to taste right before serving.

As a garnish for fish (I do not eat meat) I saute halved garlic cloves, a coarsely chopped shallot and deseeded and finely cut guajillo chilis in olive oil until the garlic is a golden brown, I then add this blend and continue until you can smell the aroma of the released spices. Finally I add chopped vine ripened tomatoes and chopped, fresh cilantro and use this as a topping on fish or as a garnish over couscous or rice. Sweet peppers can be substituted for the guajillo chilis if you or your guests prefer less spicy food.

The possibilities are endless and the price is more than reasonable. It's the skillful blending or ingredients and their freshness, though, that inspired me to award five stars.

title: Nice size for moderatte use
text:
