Be aware that there is sea salt in the mix, which means you need to be careful with respect to sodium if you or your guests have dietary restrictions. I always have a few of these around, both in my kitchen and on my table.

title: Convenient, but be careful
text:
I always have this and [[ASIN:B0019S5444 Alessi Whole Mix Peppercorns, 1.12-Ounce Grinder (Pack of 6)]] on my table and love the convenience. The caveat for this sea salt grinder is it produces relatively coarse pieces of salt when you grind a portion.

While the grinding process breaks the sea salt, releasing flavors that you will never get from iodized table salt, or even unground sea salt, you need to be very careful if you have sodium restrictions. Be aware that the grinder will deposit a lot more salt with one grind cycle than most people realize. By the way, I use a clockwise-counterclockwise motion on the cap to grind my salt - the Alessi disposable grinders seem to work better that way.

Another consequence of how much salt is dispensed is this particular grinder is quickly depleted, even if you do have sodium restrictions and use it sparingly. While the peppercorn dispenser I mentioned above will last me nearly six weeks, this sea salt grinder barely lasts three weeks, and sometimes two - and I only use it on the table (for the kitchen I use [[ASIN:B001SAUOMK Alessi Fine Sea Salt, 24-Ounce (Pack of 6)]]).

For convenience, though, this is hard to beat, even with the limitations I have discussed. However, do be aware of the possible implications if you or your guests have sodium restrictions because the grinder does dispense too much salt.

title: I always have one on my table!
text:
My table has this and an [[ASIN:B0019S714A Alessi Coarse Sea Salt, 2.83-Ounce Grinders (Pack of 6)]] at all times (I use bulk sea salt and a larger pepper grinder in the kitchen.)

Since I live alone, a single grinder can last me six plus weeks, so a pack of six of these is roughly a nine month supply. For families or couples, or for those who entertain often, how long it lasts will vary.

The peppercorns are fresh and when ground they immediately burst into a wonderful aroma. The mechanism is relatively easy to turn, and unlike some grinders, does not stick of easily clog.

Do be aware that the grinding mechanism tends to produce very coarse pepper, so if you prefer yours to be finer, a dedicated grinder may better suit your needs. Another possible issue is when you have just a few peppercorns left in the container they may not "catch" in the grinding mechanism and grind. I've learned through experience that it's best to just dispose of the grinder and use a new one from the pack. It will save you frustration.

For me this is a convenient way to make sure that my guests and I have fresh ground pepper during meals, and I always have a few on hand.

title: Missing a key herb in my opinion
text:
This has everything to make a great herbes de Provence mix except rosemary (in my experience and opinion anyway.) Still, the herbs in this mix have sufficient aroma and flavor, and the missing rosemary is easily added (which I do using [[ASIN:B005F5K8AM Badia Rosemary]].)

I use this mixture on omelets (added after it's cooked, not when making the omelet because I have found that the delicate fragrance and flavor of the lavender gets destroyed during cooking). Although I am a vegetarian 364 days of the year, I do eat lamb each Easter - it's a tradition. I have found that by rubbing the lamb with rosemary and olive oil before cooking, then using this herb mixture just before serving, it greatly enhances the flavor. I also use this on white fish, such as haddock, halibut, etc., and love the flavor it imparts. In the case of fish I almost always prepare mine "en papillote" and find that I can season the fish with this mix prior to cooking without any adverse effects on the aroma or flavor, especially the delicate lavender.

My complaint about the missing rosemary notwithstanding, this is an excellent mix of quality herbs, and the missing ingredient can easily be added to the mixture, as I described.

title: Great for dipping and marinating/basting
text:
This is an interesting product that is made from grape must (the same base for grappa!) and balsamic vinegar. I am a vegetarian, but also eat fish, so I keep this on hand mainly for friends for whom I cook or entertain. For personal use this is wonderful as a flavor enhancer for fresh strawberries. A drop on a fresh, ripe strawberry comes close to the same exquisite taste that a very old Acetaia Reale would draw out. Well, not close, but in the same ballpark.

For friends, especially those who insist on mixing balsamic vinegar, olive oil and spices such as [[ASIN:B001SAWHPM Alessi Dipping Spice Grinder, 0.76-Ounce (Pack of 6)]] as a bread dip, I use this instead. First, it actually mixes with the olive oil, giving a more uniform dipping sauce, and second, it has the balsamic vinegar flavor. Personally, I do not understand the need to mask the nuances of a good extra virgin olive oil with the heavier flavor of a balsamic vinegar, but I do endeavor to be a good host so I accommodate.

Many of my friends prefer their fish to not taste fishy. To me that defeats the purpose, but since nobody elected me to dictate how fish should taste I use a little of this (along with lemon juice) as a marinate before cooking the fish. Apparently it does the job because even friends who normally dislike fish seem to enjoy it when prepared that way.

For basting, this is ideal with vegetables such as zucchini, peppers, eggplant and similar to be grilled over a charcoal fire. I usually mix a little of this with some olive oil, which as I stated above, it blends with perfectly, and a little crushed garlic. Baste, grill and enjoy. Conversely, you can grill the vegetables plain and use the mixture as a dipping sauce ... or just a few drops of this balsamic glaze as a flavor enhancer directly on the vegetables when they are served.

I have not explored all of the possibilities with this product, but am glad I stumbled across it at my local market was was curious enough to give it a try. I am on my third bottle! One final use is to make gift baskets consisting of this, [[ASIN:B001HTR41G Gia Russa Olive, Extra Virgin, 17-Ounce (Pack of 12)]] (a high quality olive oil), and [[ASIN:B00759NNKI Balsamic Vinegar of Modena]].

title: One of my guilty pleasures
text:
I can get this locally, but for nowhere near the amazingly low price I get it from here. This a is the real deal when it comes to tuna, and I try to have a serving 4-6 times a month.

In the past I have used it in paella, but have grown to love it as a part of a cold plate consisting of the tuna on the side, with a bed of arugula topped with chopped fire-roasted red peppers, chopped red onion, sliced vine-ripened tomatoes and fresh black olives - drizzled with [[ASIN:B00451SCUU Badia Olive Oil Extra Virgin, 33.81-Ounce (Pack of 3)]] and seasoned with ground black pepper and sea salt. But I digress ... this is high quality tuna and nothing like the typical fare found on US supermarket shelves. If you love tuna you will love this, and the price is incredible.

title: One of my three favorite brands of couscous
text:
Couscous is a staple to me and the size of this package - about enough to serve five - is perfect since I live alone and fend for myself.

This, and most other brands without flavorings (which contain too much sodium in my opinion) are heart- and lifestyle-healthy. Not only is the plain couscous itself fat free, but at 190 calories per serving it provides 7 grams of protein (pretty impressive for a gain-based dish.) But that does not distinguish this specific brand from the others. What I most like about Vigo's couscous is that consistent in preparation. What I mean by that is if you follow the instructions to the letter each serving of couscous is going to be identical to past ones. I have used brands that I will not name that are not as consistent or as repeatable when preparing it.

Plus the size is perfect for families that don't often eat couscous, meaning no waste and for most families the 10 ounce package can be used in its entirety in a single meal without having to worry about storing it and keeping it fresh.

title: This is my favorite pizza sauce
text:
My daughter introduced me to this pizza sauce and it has become my favorite. We have recently started to buy the smaller 8-inch Boboli pizza crusts, but that size does not come with the sauce like their other crust sizes.

Lately this sauce in the boxes has been hard to find…what’s going on Boboli?

Even though this was a bit pricey, I was happy to buy this set of five boxes with the usual 3 bags of sauce in each box.

They arrived today and the expirations dates are a month of so far out, so I decided I would freeze three of the boxes. I did a bit of research and found pizza sauce can be frozen.

For the small pizzas I use half of a packet of sauce on each 8-inch pizza. We found our store brand (Pavilions) turkey pepperoni to be good and then we add shredded Italian cheese. Pop it into the toaster oven for 7 1/2 minutes on 450 degrees (no preheating) and it’s perfect for me. Fast and easy.

title: This may be my new go-to beef gravy
text:
My daughter ordered this and, when I saw it was called “au jus,” I was afraid it was going to be too thin of a gravy.

I actually love the consistency. Some other bottled gravies are just too thick for my preference. (I suppose you could thin them out a little with water or milk…that’s always an option.)

This gravy has a nice full beef flavor. It’s perfect over mashed potatoes or open-faced sandwiches. If you wanted to use it as a sandwich dip, I would thin it out a bit more.

No fat listed which is an added bonus.

I will keep this on my grocery list and continue to purchase. So happy my daughter had us try this out!

title: Who doesn’t love French’s Crispy Onions?
text:
These onion pieces have been around forever. My mother used to send me a can in my “care package” when I was in college. And that was many years ago.

I recently was trying to make a tuna noodle cheese casserole (with canned chicken instead of tuna) and had trouble finding these onions pieces to go on top of it. I was very happy to find them on Amazon and in such a generous package.

The taste and texture are exactly like I remember them. This package should last quite a while…if I don’t stop snacking on them.

There are many uses for them on a variety of casseroles, potatoes, meats, salads.

The price is good and I received quickly. Needless to say, I can recommend and will be buying again.

title: We buy extras of these French toast sticks
text:
We consider this Farm Rich brand of French toast sticks to be the best out there. No more buying from Carl’s Jr…which saves me money.

We pop these in the toaster oven and we’re good to go. I actually prefer this brand over any others I have tried.

The price is certainly a good value and you get a generous amount in the box.

Great with sides for breakfast or by themselves as a snack. I prefer the regular version but they do have a cinnamon kind.

I highly recommend and will continue to purchase…as long as I can find them. Not all stores have them!

title: Our favorite bottled water
text:
I live in Southern California and the tap water here is really awful. Not necessarily unhealthy but does not taste great to drink or cook with.

We even have water purification tanks on the whole house and, while that helps, we still don’t want to drink this water.

My daughter introduced me to a couple brands of bottled water out there. FIJI is the best for us. Can water taste “smooth?” That’s how it feels to me….It is so refreshing.

So far I’m still comfortable with the 16.9 ounce bottles. I tried getting larger bottles and putting in glass water bottles, but that is just too time-consuming for me. Also, this bottle fits my hand nicely. When working, I don’t want to think about it when grabbing for the bottle on my desk.

I work from home full-time and keep a drink fridge in my upstairs home office. We keep bottles in all fridges, including the one in the garage. It certainly helps make it more convenient to get our healthy water intake each day and cuts down on sodas.

And, who doesn’t love that pretty pink flower on the label? Dresses up my refrigerators.

So far this is a decent value (which I carefully watch) and we recycle our bottles. It’s hard to beat having this 24-pack delivered to our door. It’s well-packaged and always arrives in good shape. (Another brand we use to order always came half-opened. Fiji knows what they’re doing.)

A small thing, I know, but the slightly rectangular shape actually helps them stack nicely in my fridge.

I do recommend.

Recently I see it’s “not available” to buy, so I’m hoping that is temporary. I prefer the turkey (they also have beef) and I also like the wider roll versus the small sticks. (We cut part of a stick up for our dog’s treat ball…just a few but he loves them.)

title: Our favorite Ben’s 90-second rice flavor

You can literally wait until the last minute to heat this up in the microwave, toss it in a bowl and stir up with a fork to fluff it up…and you’re good to go.

I highly recommend this rice and will continue to keep purchasing. This pack of six pouches helps me keep stocked up.

title: TOO SPICY!!!!
text:
I'm not a fan of commercially made vegetable juice, but I drink it because I don't have to prepare it and it's supposed to be good for me. When my hands were not crippled with arthritis, I used to make my own delicious vegetable juice each morning with carrots, broccoli, cabbage, and cucumber(s). After the arthritis ruined my hands, I used to water down the low sodium V-8 from Campbell's (half H2O, half juice), warm it up, and drink it as a broth. It's OK plain or with a sandwich, but by comparison to homemade juice, V-8 tastes awful. Then while surfing the net I discovered that the other "natural" ingredients in V-8 are milk, poultry, fish, and beef. If I were vegan or followed a kosher diet, adding ingredients that aren't disclosed up front or on the back label, for that matter, could be disappointing. Anyway, learning about the deception motivated me to find an alternative. I happen to love Lakewood pineapple juice so I decided to give their Super Veggie a try.

It tastes pretty bad and has the added negative of being too spicy/hot for me. If Lakewood had omitted or substituted those hot peppers with a more palatable vegetable I probably would have given it three or four stars, but it has to be content with the two b/c I still don't think that processed vegetable juice tastes good. However, Lakewood Organic Super Veggie is truly low in sodium, so I warm it up without diluting it and add whole milk to neutralize the taste of the spicy, stinging hot peppers. Next I'll try low fat or no fat milk and see if it has the same effect. For people who like hot peppers, enjoy!

title: Airy and delicious
text:
Taskin Bakery Turkish Round Pita Bread
Ingredients: flour, water, yeast, sesame seeds, and salt. It doesn’t have butter, as listed on the Amazon website.
Nutritional information:
Serving size: 1 oz. (28 grams); Servings per pack: 16; Calories: 77
Fat, cholesterol, and sugar are 0% of the daily value; Iron: 10%
Sodium: 150 mg.; Carbohydrate: 16 g.; Protein: 3 g.

Review:
This bread doesn't resemble any pita bread that I've had, which open up into pockets and are great for making grilled cheddar cheese pockets and for stuffing with omelets or tuna salad. It's also not 100% whole wheat, but that doesn't reduce this product's excellence. The shape and size of each of the three loaves that come in the pack reminds me of a seven or nine inch pizza dough before it’s flattened to form the pizza’s base. The diameter of each loaf varies, depending on how flat the baker chose to make it, but each loaf can be sliced across to form a top and a bottom of a big sandwich. One loaf can feed four to eight people, depending on the serving size preference and on whether you’re preparing an open or closed sandwich. I’m a little person who seldom gains weight so two servings of this bread is good for me. Depending on how I complement a loaf, I can get as many as twelve servings out of a single pack or as few as six when I have a ravenous appetite (that would be like eating half of a medium pizza by myself).

The texture is similar, but airier than a Thomas’s English muffin. As a matter of fact, the bottom of these loaves have the same corn-like flour coating (probably coarsely ground semolina) that’s on the Thomas’s English muffins, but this Turkish bread is nicer than a Thomas’s. The Turkish loaves have a small sprinkling of light and dark sesame seeds. A sesame Kaiser roll or bagel normally has more seeds per serving.

I don’t know anything about Turkish bread or food and I was anxious to taste this new product. As soon as the bread arrived today, I cut and enjoyed a plain serving after brunch. It was delicious and I can think of a lot that can be done with this bread. Simple recipes include coatings of butter, fruit spreads, and peanut butter or you can slice it for a favorite sandwich. It’s a nice bagel substitute so I will be enjoying it with cream cheese and/or smoked salmon. The consistency is also strong enough for baked dishes: top it off with veggies, cheeses, and sauce to create an exiting pizza or other flavorful dish. I hope you enjoy any combination with your favorite beverage! I also suggest that you visit their website, where they feature 44 different products, including dessert items (www.taskinbakery.com).

Storage suggestions: A reviewer complained that this nice bread became moldy too soon. I have successfully stored bread in the freezer for months by slicing it in portions, making it easy to thaw and enjoy. This particular bread shipped from Jersey City to my New York home and it arrived in excellent condition. I’ve also ordered breads from Indiana and have never had a problem because I convert large portions into smaller servings and store them in the freezer.

title: Fantastic Juice!!!!
text:
I was never a fan of pineapple juice because the brands that they sell at the supermarket are usually acidic tasting, but Lakewood is a fantastic combination of organic pineapple juice and puree: the consistency is just right, the sweetness is perfect, and it's potential to become addictive is way up there. I love it so much that I'm neglecting the orange juice and drinking as many as three bottles a day, which I suspect is way too much.

Amazon sells the case for $33.48, which comes out to $2.79 a bottle. My local diner charges $4.00 for a freshly squeezed 12 ounce cup, so $2.79 is a bargain. The glass bottles are a plus for most people (they're nice and reusable), but a downside for me because with my arthritic hands I would have preferred something lighter, but that's just me.

Health News: Years ago a doctor recommended pineapple juice to me in order to counteract constipation. My reaction was, it ain't happening because I didn't like the stuff. After a recent bad case of "a medicine ball gut" I remembered the doctor's words and quickly got a hold of Dole pineapple refrigerated juice (the type that comes in a large bottle that looks like a Tropicana jug). The taste was good, but not as great as the Lakewood that I later discovered. The good news was that two 12 ounce cups of the juice did send me to the bathroom. Since then I have read about pineapple juice's other health benefits: it's anti-inflammatory and because of it's vitamin B content, it allegedly regulates blood sugar. I've become a believer.

UPDATE on May 2, 2015: I was drinking way too much of this delicious juice and one morning and for nearly 3 weeks after that I was barely able to lift my feet off the ground and the right knee hurt. Granted, I had a similar problem a few years ago because I have serious arthritis, but after taking good care of myself with over the counter supplements I was doing well. I concluded that the problem was probably due to the excess consumption of the juice and enjoying one or two Dole pineapple fruit cups daily. Maybe I was getting too much acid, bromelain, or potassium. I stopped drinking the juice after putting up with the heavy legs for about a week or so and the problem eventually subsided. Now I drink 6 ounces once or twice a week and I'm reintroducing the fruit cups slowly.

title: Terrific for Your Health and Desserts
text:
Knox unsweetened natural gelatin is a great product whether you use it as a health supplement, in soups and broths, or as a dessert. Years ago, I used to consume it religiously and as I sometimes do with other food items, I slowly eliminated it as a food staple and that was a big mistake. As the winter progressed through 2013-2014, my feet were getting rougher and flakier to the point that I felt them scrape on the bedcovers each night. I had two large boxes of Knox on the kitchen shelf that I had purchased perhaps two years ago and luckily they hadn’t expired. I started mixing two packs daily (morning and evening) into about 3 ounces of cold water and then mixing it into my Ghirardelli unsweetened hot cocoa with milk. In less than a week, my feet looked and felt smoother. For further foot therapy, I recently sent away for organic shea butter and cocoa butter creams. If I’m not feeling overly lazy, I’ll apply either moisturizer at night and cover my feet with cotton Peds. That will most likely give me the smooth feet that I had a few years ago.

In the past, I’ve added Knox gelatin to homemade soups. I’ve also mixed it with Kedem or Welch’s Concord grape juices and water to make a wonderful “Jello” without any artificial flavors or too much sugar. By watering down the gelatin, I control its consistency, which I like really wiggly. I also enjoy apple and cranberry Jello. Any of the three flavors are excellent alone or with ice cream. There are other recipes on the packets or you can Google them.

Gelatin is supposed to help our joints, hair, nails, and other connective tissues. So I recommend this product if you’re having any such problems, or to avoid them.

title: Not for Weak Stomachs
text:
Awful: that’s the word that sums up this Keystone beef (details below). I recommend the Costco Kirkland beef (available through Amazon), which tastes and smells better and is also low in salt.

So, commentators say that the Keystone brand cooks up in its own juices. The truth is that these carelessly slaughtered slabs and massive chunks of meat are cooked up in their own smelly blood. The terrible odor hit me as soon as I opened the can. I did try the Keystone pork and while it too had a very gamey odor and taste, I was able to doctor it for passable eating with Newman’s Own Cabarnet marinara sauce. I tried the same thing with the Keystone beef, but I masked the odor and not the nauseating taste. I suspect that nothing can kill this meat’s gamey taste, except perhaps soaking it in vinegar for a week, which I’m not going to do. So, it’s been a sad waste of ten bucks. Lesson learned: I’ll never buy any of their meats again. And, even in a dire life threatening emergency, it’s not for anyone with a weak stomach.

I’ve tried several canned protein sources, especially after I read that the victims of Hurricane Sandy received prepared processed foods that were terrible and too high in salt. To date, Kirkland is the only canned beef that I can recommend for emergencies and for other lazy people like me. Other protein sources that I’ve enjoyed are Crown Prince Salmon, Progresso Tuna, and Bar Harbor herring in tomato sauce. My niece likes the Hormel chicken because it has both dark and white meat, but I haven’t tried it yet.

title: Great Taste and Healthy
text:
When I first started having serious arthritic problems decades ago, my sister introduced me to Osteo-Biflex (aka Glucosamine/Chondroitin complex). I mention the product on this coconut oil review page because little was known about Glucosamine/Chondroitin at the time, except that it was given to horses. Well, as time progressed, patients were recommending the product to their doctors and today it’s a popular anti-arthritic supplement that is used with other nutrients that benefit joints and cartilage. Based on what I’ve read and seen about coconut oil, this short chain fatty acid might be the next wonder product that consumers have discovered and are now sharing its role against dementia and other related problems with their medical practitioners. You can judge for yourself by viewing a few of the videos on You Tube (I’ve included the URL links below. If you can’t link on, highlight the address, copy it, and paste it onto your browser’s Search bar).

As for coconut oil’s other attributes: It’s delicious on or in many foods, including for making pancakes, cakes, pie crusts, and rice and meat dishes. A contractor that was working in my apartment uses it on his bread as a substitute for butter. In my opinion, it’s more flavorful than extra virgin olive oil. Because it’s a short chain fatty acid, it doesn’t behave like the other saturated long chain oils (animal fats and butter). It decomposes quickly and won’t clog your arteries as long chain fatty acids and hydrogenated oils such as margarine tend to do.

As mentioned in other reviews, coconut oil is excellent for skin and hair. Author Bruce Fife also says it’s good for teeth and gums.

Suggestions: Unless you can store it in ice cube trays (with Saran Wrap) so they’ll be easy to remove, don’t refrigerate coconut oil. Although cooling it might prevent it from spoiling quicker, the colder coconut oil gets the harder and more difficult it is to spoon out. In warm temperatures it behaves as any other oil and will flow easily.

Recommended reading: The Coconut Oil Miracle by Bruce Fife

title: Ruined a Nice Candy
text:
The ingredients for these squares are as long as my arm:
Sugar, cocoa butter, whole milk powder, unsweetened chocolate, hazelnuts AND, here it goes: palm and palm kernel oil, milk fat, crisp rice (rice flour, barley malt extract, salt, distilled monoglycerides, partially hydrogenated vegetable oils - cottonseed and soybean extract), nonfat dry milk, sunflower oil, soy lecithin - as an emulsifier, salt, vanilla, TBHQ - a preservative. Sugar content: 22g/serving, sodium: 40 mg, saturated fat: 9g, cholesterol 10mg, Protein 3g, Calories 240.

I sent for these after I failed to take a good look at the picture; my fault and shame on me. Until last year, Ghirardelli used to make an excellent milk chocolate hazelnut square and bar in a white pack. The white packs contained few ingredients: milk chocolate (sugar, whole milk powder, cocoa butter, unsweetened chocolate, milk fat, soy lecithin - as an emulsifier, vanilla) and hazelnuts. Sugar content: 21g/serving, sodium: 25 mg, saturated fat 8g, cholesterol 10mg, Protein 3g; Calories 230.

If you happen to be allergic to any of those extra ingredients, beware. I hope Ghirardelli will reintroduce the better candy.

12 ounces; recommended serving size: 2 ounces; servings per can: about 4 (that recommendation probably takes the presence of the liquid into account); calories: 80; calories from fat: 15.

Distributed by Costco Wholesale Corporation; 1-800-774-2678; [...]

I pronounce this product good and low in salt. The only drawback might be the phosphate content, but if that doesn't kill me, something else most definitely will.

I'm a skinny person, but whatever food providers claim to be a serving never works for me. The most I'll get out of this can is two servings; a larger person might have to eat the entire can's content, which contains a lot of broth. I had my serving with mashed potatoes and peas, and it was good after I doctored the meat with curry, onion, Tobasco sauce, sesame oil, and garlic. Although olive oil makes a lot of things taste delicious, my body behaves better when I feed it sesame seed oil. Next time, I'll try the beef in spaghetti sauce or tomato sauce with vegetable puree. However, I'm okay eating insipid stuff, so I could have easily eaten the meat as a sandwich with just lettuce and tomatoes. For people who can't eat anything without flavor, you will need to add whatever you prefer; think of it as plain beef because that's pretty much what it is, with plenty of beef broth that you can use as a stock for stew, gravy, or any other concoction. I used a portion of the broth over my potatoes; it made them smoother.

The meat comes in stew-size cubes that were apparently pressure cooked to tenderness, since they flake apart with a fork - I like tender meat. The meat has almost zero fat; much of which was solid and stuck to the lid, so I guess my apartment is comfortably cold. The pack comes with three Mexican-style recipes, but you can definitely do your own style of cooking; a beef stroganoff would be nice.

When I used to drive along the east coast and stay at the Days Inn, I always carried my own canned goods with me that I warmed up at the motel because a can of Health Valley soup, Del Monte vegetables, Progresso tuna fish, or Crown Prince salmon is always healthier than eating at one of those fast food chains. I suspect that eating this Kirkland roast beef is also healthier, despite the sodium phosphate. As the daughter of a cook, I can prepare fine fresh food, but I choose not to because I don't like kitchen duty. So, whenever I don't order take out, canned or frozen items and baked potato work fine for me. Conclusion: I recommend this product and will buy it again.

title: Excellent, Nutritious Soup
text: I love both the 14 Garden Vegetable Soup and the plain Vegetable Soups (no salt and low salt varieties) that Health Valley produces because they are truly vegetarian, without pasta or rice or any other non-leafy product.  Best of all, they don't contain MSG or any other chemicals.  They don't require any doctoring, but you might like a pinch of salt or Tobasco sauce. I sometimes add hamburger meat to them or crush Inka plantain chips to give them a crunchy cracker texture without the gluten.  I have taken Health Valley soups and a can opener with me when I do road trips in order to avoid the awful roadside garbage that franchise restaurants call food.  You can heat them in a glass or plastic bowl in a motel room's microwave oven or eat them right out of the can.  Either way, they're not overly delicious, but good.

title: Good Gluten-Free Cracker Substitute
text:
The 4 ounce Inka Plantain Chips countains 4 servings of 140 calories each (60 calories from fat). Sodium 60 mg., Potassium 220 mg, Total Fat 6g (9%), Saturated Fat 2.5 g (13%), 0 Trans Fat, Carbohydrates 20g (0 sugar), Protein 1g, Fiber 1g, Vitamin A (6%), Vitamin C (15%). The good news about the fat is that it is a plant based saturated short chain fatty acid, so your body can digest it efficiently.

For anyone who isn't familiar with plantain, it is an Asian fruit, which like it's cousin, the banana, was introduced to the new world by 15th and 16th century explorers, such as the Portuguese and Spanish sailors, so calling them Inka Chips is interesting. For more than a year, I was looking for a good gluten-free cracker and I never considered a plantain chip as an excellent substitute until now, and shame on me, because I discovered them about twenty years ago. As a matter of fact, instead of making dumplings out of wheat flour, Puerto Ricans make them out of ground green plantains or bananas. I never ate plantain chips as a kid, but I did enjoy the plantain dumplings in soup; they were delicious and low in fat. Puerto Ricans also combine the ground plantain with other tropical tubers and stewed meats to make a huge dumpling that they boil in parchment paper in order to keep it intact while it cooks in a light brine; it's delicious and filling. At the West Indian markets in NYC, they sell plantain, banana, casava, and peanut flour. So, if you like to cook and experiment, you may want to make dumplings from such flours; I'm not a cook.

The Inka chips are thicker than the plantain chips that I ate years ago, making them a suitable cracker substitute. I cover them with peanut butter or fruit preserves and enjoy them as a snack. I also crush them and add them to my bowl of soup in order to give the soup a nice crunch; these chips hold up well in liquid, better than Saltine crackers, with less salt.

title: Made excellent fried mozzarella sticks
text: I purchased these specifically to make homemade mozz sticks as I was pretty unhappy with some of the frozen products out there.  These turned out great.  Will share recipe.  Put how many sticks you want in a batch in the freezer.  I would say at least overnight but it can go longer w/o harm. Mozz freezes well.  When you are ready to make, take out and peel from pkg to "sweat" a little.  This will help the starch to stick.  Use corn starch or flour or mix of both.  Beat one egg per 2 sticks you are making (a lot will get soaked up in double dipping).  After shaking/coating in starch, dip in egg, then into breadcrumbs (I used a combo of panko/bread crumbs).  Use a seasoned product if you wish.  Then repeat with egg wash and another coating.  Back to freezer for just a few while you clean up and heat your oil.  I used a combo of light olive oil and veggie oil.  Do just a few sticks at a time.  Rest on paper towels for a few an enjoy.  With the second half of pkg I will experiment with an air fryer version.

title: Can stand up to gravy
text: On their own, with say just salt/ketchup, these are not that great.  A little hard dry and bland from an air fryer. But they lend themselves to gravy and can stand up to poutine for sure, they won't get soggy in a heartbeat like shoestrings do.  I think my next go at them will be in poutine actually.

title: Very sweet
text: Like just about every prepared drink or drink mix I found these too sweet.  I think the mango flavor makes it even  more so in this version.  I could easily use just half or even a third of a tube.  If you are going to get more than one serving out of it, don't forget to shake your tube first.

title: Watch them closely
text: All I can say is they cremated in about 5-7 minutes in my convection oven at 350 deg. My convection is very strong so I always take off 25-50 deg what convention oven says.  So many of these were thin with a barely there onion.  Flavor is fine, although a bit mild but since the paper thin onion in many of them had turned carbon, not sure.  My bag had many thin more like "onion straws" in them.  Out of the first half of bag I got three whole rings, two with a pretty decent thickness of onion and one with a vaporized ring of onion inside.  I prefer battered onion rings to be honest, I find a lot of these breaded brands put in a tissue thin  bit of onion and probably shaken up in crumbs like a shake and bake chicken.  YMMV especially using an air fryer, lower it down, way down and check at half the time.

title: Made great meat sauce
text:
Update: not changing my score at all from what you see below. I just got around to making the burger I prepared and put in freezer from my original purchase. As I said this is seriously ground and something like that generally doesn't make a good burger texturally. I only patted it into a round shape and vacuum sealed straight out of package into freezer. The burger was prepared about medium-medium well. Flavor excellent but as expected, texture not up to a coarser grind of beef. I will be purchasing again and wish I was still up to grinding my own as I would also purchase a cut and grind myself not so fine. But definitely getting more to use for meatloaf and meatballs.

I don't often eat real meat (75% lactoveggie here) But when I do I try to get it ethically sourced. I wanted to make my meat sauce and was disappointed in all the faux beef crumbles I tried previously so I figured I would give bison a go. It is lean. It is also, this ground product, a little on the mushy side. Since I bought this for meat sauce for maybe my meatballs or meatloaf it was not terribly off-putting. I reserved about a 1/4 pound of it and gently patted into a patty to freeze for a burger sometime. Will review when I get to it - it is probably a bit too lean and a bit too finely ground for a good meat burger. But I do go lean for meat sauce, meatloaf and meatballs (if your tomato sauce turns orange, there is too much fat!) I was pleasantly surprised this does have a mild flavor (beefish but not beefy) and it did not turn my passata orange. I would purchase again. Since I can no longer find a butcher where I can point to a chuck or round steak and say "grind that up for me" this fit the bill. For years, maybe two decades I was grinding myself steaks/cuts I bought whole. Too much work both grinding and cleanup so I have been missing my meatballs and meatloaf. And this is certainly better than faux beef crumble in a meat sauce. YMMV of course but if you need lean beefish - this should do the trick.

title: Dry, tough and tasteless
text: Not sure why I am being generous with two stars. I only picked these up because WF has been out of plain old hamburger buns for weeks (why WF, why?)  I figured they couldn't be any worse than the brioche ones I was forced to get last shopping list (those are like trying to eat a veggie burger on a donut). I was wrong.  They did not arrive with my frozen foods, they were dated 4 days ahead but I heeded the warnings of other reviewers and kept out just one to use immediately after slicing in half.  Which wasn't easy- these are tough to saw through even with a good bread knife. I debated whether or not to try toasting for the sandwich.  I opted to toast for just a minute even though I was worried about the already very hard bottoms (you can tap it and it is like a rock) but I was afraid this dry creation would sop up all the ketchup if I didn't at least toast the interior surfaces.  I have real pretzel salt in the cupboard but couldn't be bothered, don't see how  salt could have stuck to the burnt exterior anyway.  Well veggie burger was almost done and I put these under the broiler for just a minute.  I didn't even let it really toast, put some ketchup on it  and threw on the veggie burger.  No thank you.  I kept peeling away the tough dry bun (which isn't easy) trying to get to my burger. Since it had stuck to the burger (the ketchup might as well been glue) I tossed without finishing and got a drink to wash what I did try to chew down.  Now, my veggie burgers are not the  fake bleeding type of veggie patties (I don't want blood, that is why I consume a veggie burger). This was a bad match.  Maybe a real meat burger like medium rare would juice this bun up a bit.  I doubt it.  And I am not going to waste my expensive bison burger meat putting it on this. They are just overcooked, overmixed dry and tasteless.  I will resort to making my own hamburger buns and oh, I can make homemade pretzels too - a thousand times better than these.

title: Disappointed
text: I usually like OV products and although this was OK I was shocked to see it looked/felt exactly like the less pricier 365 and Target brands mozz.  It is good for shredding as it is firmer than the mushier mozzarellas (even ones claiming to be low moisture). Since it is so firm (think brick) it also will slice well.  Just don't expect the kind of creaminess you get from even a low moisture part skim commercial mozz. This is a brick.

title: Too hard, too small
text: Kettle chips are known to be crisper so I knew what I was getting into. These chips are so small and so irregularly shaped, though.  I have to wonder just what kind of potatoes they are using?  You could use these for a garnish even or just half the bag that is bits, crush up just a bit more and use for a breading. The flavor is fine, unlike some national brands it won't make your tongue sore if you eat just - you aren't going to choke on the vinegar or salt.  They are mild.  I just wish I could get one the size of say the usual from a russet?

title: Just a little too buttery?

title: fine for pizza will try pasta next
text: Ok, first of all I accidentally ordered two containers.  One was more than enough and I have the rest of the first one now in freezer.  I ordered this to try on my own pizza.  I prefer making my own sauce from tomatoes, scratch but circumstances don't really allow that now.  I wanted a nice, seed free tomato product without anything added to it. title: Hard to rate - it takes on what you add to it
text: I only got around to trying this brand of faux beef crumble today. I am around a 70% lacto-vegetarian for most of my adult life. Having found that the ethically-sourced bison meat I had purchased a while ago was expired and wanting a comforting childhood dish requiring ground beef, I had this in the freezer. I put in a generous amount of olive oil into the pan, dumped half a package in and was greeted with no aroma whatsoever (not necessarily bad) Oh my did this soak up that oil.  Added more oil.  Added more oil before I said enough and just dumped in tomato paste and water and stirred like crazy.  I can say i did add my own seasoning just garlic and onion and only finishing salt.  My there is definitely pepper in this.  But otherwise it is totally neutral like tofu.  No real flavor of its own and should certainly absorb any flavored liquid. I can see how it could fool strictly carnivore types in a dish requiring ground meat (lasagna?) Not bad and not terribly expensive considering costs today of especially meat and quality vegetarian product. Be prepared for it to need a lot of liquid seasoning.  Keyword: liquid for it to absorb flavor. It is very dry.

title: Torn betwen 3 or 4 stars

title: Wonderful flavor but texture/baking method not good
text:
First the positive: These have a wonderful flavor perhaps even better than my homemade scratch ones.
Now: All I have available to me in current situation is a countertop convection oven. I have adapted my own recipes as best I could over the years to that appliance and carefully read directions on convenience when they give convection oven (read a big air fryer in glass where you can see the food cooking). I had high hopes for these after reading reviews/advice on how to get them cooked in the middle. I was close. So close. Now these babies must be somewhat dense (like my scratch made ones) they supposed to fill you up. I tried so hard but there was an obvious raw spot in the middle. I can't believe people are advising not to thaw first? How can something this dense get cooked through to middle without cremating the outside? I did follow advice, lowered to 375 and when I saw outside getting too brown I lowered to 350. I have 5 biscuits left to experiment on. Wish I had a real oven to try them in, taste is quite good! Updated before this was published even. I had to knock off another star. I had a 2nd go at baking one. Worse than the 1st. It was not as crispy on outside but was much more raw on inside. Someone in reviews has said that is the result of thawing/refreezing. These arrived rock hard frozen in a cold climate. I keep frozen until baking. I give up. A very nice taste but baking through to center just impossible at least with the pkg I got.

title: They are fine

title: Giving same rating as their excellent tenders
text:
Mostly vegetarian person here. Currently limiting meat to about twice a week (mostly ethical reasons).

I recently tried their tenders (see that review) and was quite impressed. They have nailed the texture of processed white meat chicken. These do that as well. Very happy with the texture. Coating is also spot on. They only fail a bit in the flavor department. The tenders, while sodium loaded had no real flavor at all. These, the flavor was a bit peppery (although they are possibly a dietary sodium bomb as well). I feel they are equals and the absolute best faux chicken I have ever had (and I have been doing faux meats since I was a teenager, eons ago). Many possibilities when preparing both. I would recommend to all although with caveat due to sodium content (which you may or may not taste) it is there.

I might try their nuggets next or not. Not a fan of real chicken nuggets (mechanically separated gristle chunks in grease) at all. For now, I want to try enhancing these two products for flavor without adding any more sodium.

I would recommend to both vegetarians and meat eaters. Not a bad value and unlike with real chicken you don't have to power wash your kitchen with boiling bleach after preparing :) Go veggie.

title: Taste I remember
text:
I don't have ice cream often. Especially in winter. I am lactose intolerant so it is a rare treat which I love and am willing to have a little bit of once in a while despite discomfort. Ice cream yummy. I always try to keep to small amount. I remember this flavor from years ago and it seems to me about the same (yay! so many things are not).

I limited my first serving and had minimal distress. I do want to add some chocolate syrup to it the next time. It is perhaps not as chocoheavy as it used to be. Now I want some today :) Seriously thinking about two days in a row, I survived my intolerance but must still be an adult and try not to eat the rest of the container.

title: Not gamey - could be more tender/juicy
text:
It is probably more than ten years since I have had any lamb. I am 70% more vegetarian at this time but have learned in my 64 years, I need some meat in my diet. So I have it maybe twice a week.

I ordered one pound, received 3 chops. Not huge thick but what seems normal for this cut. I prepared in an air fryer after dry rubbing with a few spices (NOT rosemary, I hate eating xmas tree). These cooked up in about 20 mins to a tad over med-rare, I would call it a solid medium. A little more done than I was shooting for but not bad like cooked too much. I didn't get much aroma except for the few spices I used (onion, garlic, smoked paprika with a splash of olive oil). All in all I was surprised at the total lack of what some call "gameyness" These were surprisingly tasteless actually, if blindfolded it would have been difficult for me to discern just what meat they were. They did not exude much fat unlike what I remember from lamb chops. On the fence about these. Just not as flavorful as I was expecting. I may have goofed with a slight overcooking. I have the third chop in the freezer now and will maybe look at a few recipes that might bring out more flavor. If you don't normally care for lamb because of its strong flavor, these could be an option for you. Very very mild flavor.

title: Five star texture - three star flavor
text: Quite happy with these and am going to try next the fillets.  Until these I had not found in years a suitable veggie or vegan substitute chicken.  I am seriously impressed with how these pass for (processed) chicken texture.  Now, the flavor hmm unlike many faux meats these were not overly peppery (good! I don't want food to hurt).  But like many faux meats they had no umami flavor.  Which is odd since faux meats are notorious for the high sodium mgs that I cannot usually taste.  I didn't bother adding a flavored salt or even just pink salt to them.  I used a little ketchup on the bun. Hmm or maybe a dipping sauce with a base of dark soy or HP brown sauce next time. Passable and have to get those fillets now - if one fits a bun rather than having two on a bun that would be great and I am also thinking chicken parm.  A teeny bit of garlic and onion powder wouldn't hurt in the sauce.  Cheese should more than ramp up the flavor.  But yes, the salt is there even if you don't taste it so take care in that area if you are restricting sodium.

title: Defective
text: Although I am no stranger to making my own biscuits this is one of those convenience foods that you hope is a trade off.  This tube was garbage, I know how to open "pressurized" refrigerated biscuits/dough.  Made quite a few times in my long life.  This was defective for sure.  No pop.  At all.  Checked exp date - still two weeks left.  I had to literally saw a seam on the tube to get to the non-popping contents.  Not good.  Checked exp date again.  Not expired. Dug out the dough.  The obviously not "popping" dough.  Supposedly 8 biscuits I had over ten (I had to pry them apart, just totally flat dough).  There must have been a small hole in the tube, the only thing I can think of.  I made three and put the rest in the freezer on a plate.  They did rise a bit baking, but not much. Taste bland, texture not a biscuit by any stretch of the imagination.  I am going to copy this review and look up mfr customer service too.  I am so disappointed and angry. Obviously defective.

title: This is a big heavy cannister
text: This I do believe is the best value for making your own gatorade with your own water.  Down points is it is a big heavy canister that may or may not arrive damaged.  I have ordered three times with one disaster in the middle where although the outer box was fine, inside was a crushed leaking all over (and out of the box) mess.  For someone who frequently needs electrolyte/hydration due to health issue this is the best value for your money, water it a bit more down from directions and it is practically as good as pedialyte.  I haven't seen the powder form of the original (with real sugar!) in stores in ages.  This is a great value but to have delivered you are gambling with a powdery sugar mass disaster.  I will order again, excellent value and hoping for intact canister.

title: uhmmm, good but pricey

Anyhow this reminds me of the flavor of those fake chocolate oranges that I do love. If not for the price point and maybe, just maybe, it could be a little more orangey this could be a five star.

title: Yum but where the toffee?
text: Chocolate with salt is a yummy thing and I think any chocolate fan should give it a try.  We got crunchy salt here and a nice chocolate...still wondering about the toffee part.  I don't regret this purchase but probably won't again.

title: Didn't realize these are WHOLE WHEAT, my bad
text:
I am someone with health issues that cannot generally consume high fiber products. My fault I did not investigate enough to realize these are whole wheat.

I applaud all of you who can handle fiber, but I am not one of you. Due to intestinal adhesions, fiber means agony for me. I know, all of you out there it is so much healthier. Me, no, not so much.
