title: wow - watch out for the seeds
text: well no doubt these have some form of raspberry but most of the fruit content is seeds.  I bit into a square of this one in the dark (I bought a variety of bars in different flavors) not knowing which it was.  Chocolate I think is fine.  But my first bite had such a note of not only "rottenish" fruit it was also so crunchy that I thought it might be something like a crisped rice bar.  Except for the past its prime fruit taste.  I used to pick wild blackberries, raspberries, strawberries and blueberries, etc as a kid but do shun them now in my old age because seeds.  Especially raspberries. Blueberries the seeds are not so abundant.  I still have a stubborn one stuck that will need specialty floss to get it out.  I think other varieties with this chocolate may be fine, or even just the chocolate itself.  I am going to be put off berries for a while now.  Got to get this out of between my teeth before I go mad.

title: Better than their 4-cheese
text:
Granted, that is not saying much as the 4-cheese poppers/rolls/whatever are indescribably bad. But these can be a solid three for me. If they allowed half stars the flavor could be a 3.5.

They come in a cute (microwavable I think) tray I didn't use because this was going into an air fryer. I made about half the package. Plopped them on the non-stick (I know, I know but it has its place). In retrospect the dough may have benefited from a non-aerosol spritz of some oil. About half of them leaked (to be expected with such products) and the leakage didn't look particularly cheesy but stuck like it was. The dough a bit soft, definitely oil might have helped. But the dough tasted okay and the filling was miles better than the garbage in the 4 cheese version (which as far as I am concerned doesn't have any cheese in that ketchup pocket). The sauce was mild but did not taste like cheap ketchup. If not for the price point I might be tempted to buy these again. Actually I am going to cook the other half now. Will try a spritz of a neutral oil.

title: Where do i start? Peppery, uncookable crust
text:
Not a frozen pizza fan. Back in the days of yore and old Tombstone and Red baron (they have both changed) I basically shun frozen pizza. Unless it is (mine, the best homemade frozen after making) or commercial pizzeria joint (frozen after delivery). Frozen pizza is simply a convenience food you don't have to pay a delivery/tip and can make in the middle of the night or a blizzard. When I buy frozen pizza these days it is like an emergency ration and I purchase smallest, cheapest and just use as a base for my own toppings.

Somewhere I remember some national review of frozen pizza where 365 did pretty good in rankings. So when doing an online shop I threw this in my cart. I don't care for meat additions as I am 50-80% vegetarian. Finally gotten around to try this today. As a single, I break these "full" size pizzas in half or thirds and keep the rest of it frozen. I wound up with about 50-60% whole piece and prepared according to directions in a strong convection oven, directly on rack. My oven is strong convection so I usually knock back the temp 20-25 degrees per mfr. Well, the top was starting to get a bit burnt on the point end and the rest of cheese pretty melted. Was worrying about the crust, I let it go for the full 18 minutes. Cheese was definitely well done (not black but getting there). The crust, oh my. In my eyes and fingers I was like is this raw still? How could it survive the circling vortex of hot air? I toyed with the idea of plopping it into a cast iron to crisp up the crust but decided I didn't want to dirty a pan until I tasted this.

Taste: Cheese not bad. I couldn't discern any distinct different ones let alone 4 but coverage was adequate. (I did not doctor up with any additions of my own) BUT there was an overwhelming 'pepperiness" in what i was assuming was the sauce. No garlic, no onion, no oregano, no basil. The tomato note was OK but that pepper was pretty strong (white or black or both?). Did get some off-flavor from something that I can't pin down what components.

The crust: as I said, it did not brown or crisp at all but was not raw. Before the pepper and off flavor turned me off I thought I good way to finish this might actually be fold it and stick in the cast iron for a few, flip. Might make it something calzone-y even.

But the overall taste of this just put me off too much (I did also hit something "hard" wasn't a peppercorn didn't burst pepper - maybe a tomato seed?), the other third (in pieces, I got an uneven break is stored in freezer in a zip for some day I am truly truly desperate. I will doctor, fold and flip brown it in a cast iron pan. Hard pass to buy again. I really have to go back to making my own. Or at worst, freezing up most of a pizzeria delivery pie.

title: Too sweet
text:
I fork split these pretty evenly. Proud of self. Happy with the nooks and crannies (except one drawback, get into it later) but after toasting and putting on some salted butter I found these just too sweet. It was jarring and not complimentary to my pretty good butter. Speaking of butter, the generously sized nooks and crannies, you have to careful buttering them, not only can you lose a good chunk of butter in there, when you bite into a particularly deep well you can get a "gusher". A similar issue might happen with jam or jelly. Bite into them carefully or make sure you are still in your jammies and not a work outfit you just put on.

Texture-wise they were OK. I kind of miss the cornmeal on the bottom of the "traditional" brand which BTW is no longer cornmeal. Turns out it is very tiny wheat balls because it doesn't go rancid as fast as cornmeal and is not as attractive to vermin. I live near where the traditional brand use to be mfr'd and we did get superfresh ones. No longer mfr'd nearby, not as fresh by a long shot, and pretty expensive.

My quest continues for a good english muffin - there is a gourmet brand I will try next. But I do have some canadian bacon that might be good on this sweet brand. Otherwise, the sweetness is just putting me off. It won't clash with jam, that is another way to use them up.

title: Second time trying this - not a lot of difference in dark roast
text: I originally purchased years ago based on some reviews and the fact I love peanuts that have been roasted a tad longer.  Was hard to find then (not much easier now)  I remember it being firmer than other natural peanut butters (which I eventually gave up on with the torture of trying to stir them in the confines of the jars) I see people say it doesn't require much more stirring than normal conventional PB because they do add some other oil that is less likely to separate.  Frankly though considering price/availability and that I don't taste much difference in the dark roast or their regular roast or  a dozen or so other PBs out there.  Your tastes may vary.

title: My favorite apple variety usually
text: My picker picked two nice ones for me.  No bruises or cuts.  I eat almost all of my fruits and veggies raw and with skin so I lean towards organic when available and not prohibitive expensive.  I am guilty of eating apples (and skin) that are conventional.  I am old, what's a few more pesticides to me? Wax I am not crazy about, so organic is the way to go otherwise I have to scrub like crazy with a produce wash. Honeycrisp are not as cloying sweet or often mushy like red delicious, my second favorite.  And I have been known to use them for baking too.

title: Used to use the conventional non-organic
text: I buy organic in produce and try when I get the once-a-week meat to go for humane/etc. and most of  all my produce I prefer organic.  This stuff organic is not that important for me.  No taste difference.  Hopefully no longevity difference.  This stuff is salty as conventional - a little bit goes a loooooong way and you need to be aware of other things you might add that have saltiness.  Probably why they say an opened jar will last 18 months in the fridge.  I tend to toss it though when I can't remember what year I purchased it in LOL YMMV check mfr website for keeping/exp instructions.

title: Smooth and minty but waxy
text: Not bad.  I prefer an andes myself.  I found the chocolate to have a definite waxiness.  A refreshing little treat to break off a square.  Don't know if I would buy again, have to check out some others.

title: A fine pick
text:
I prefer to do my own choosing of produce and meats but lately have been getting WF delivery. Overall have been happy with the pickers choices.

I was in a cucumber salad mood and decided to go with a conventional rather than organic since I was not doing the choosing myself, felt the picker would have more to choose from and I am Happy with this firm, not moldy, not wrinkled not mushy cuke.

Now the packer (if different from the picker) I am not happy with. My only big gripe with having someone (ANY one else) do my packing/bagging is they might commit the deadly sin of putting fresh raw meat in the same bag as fresh raw produce that is meant to be consumed raw or bakery products that weren't going to be baked any further. Boy was I ticked off this packer decided to drop steak on TOP of my cuke and baby carrots. Very ticked. If you never hear from me again I died of ecoli or salmonella. I do not cook my cukes or my baby carrots.

Back to cuke. It was in a produce baggie and since it is a conventional with wax/pesticides I knew I will be peeling it anyway I didn't call up to complain. Cucumber peel is nutritious but I will only eat if it is organic. So happy with what is basically an out of season conventional cuke here, don't know origin.

title: Chocolate OK - Almonds not OK
text: I could lick the chocolate off of the almonds bits.  Yes, I think that is what I will do with the rest of this.  The almonds are truly awful.  Not roasted, not toasted are they boiled?  They taste like wood.  Seriously like wood.

title: A good sauteeing oil
text: Nice value.  Not as strong as EVOO but I don't want EVOO since that cannot really tolerate heat at all.  I also used it like half and half with coconut oil for a little deep frying (combo foams like you wouldn't believe but things brown beautifully and not greasy).  Good value, very mild taste.

title: Just have to go down the middle rating these
text:
These were not bad at all. They did brown in the expected time in my air fryer (they use apple juice to promote browning, really?) Didn't stick on a nonstick *had already used for a veggie burger which is the most stickalicious you can imagine.

Two thoughts: 1) quite tasteless. I rarely have to salt tots since they already generally are too salty for my tastes. These are something I can believe would benefit from a flavored or finishing salt. I used plain old ketchup. 2) They were oddly "moist" inside. Not greasy but there was more moisture than I expected. Perhaps a side effect from the apple juice?

If not for the value/price point I could see these in my regular rotation. They are organic and I do like that as potatoes are supposedly some of the most heavily pesticide hit crops. So, YMMV. These were good enough and I actually appreciated their blandness in a way since you can doctor them without worrying about conflicting flavors or them getting too salty (as far as taste goes, not really looking at the sodium content not tastable). Oh, and I noticed no off flavor notes in the oil (canola) they use.

title: Soft - not too sweet
text: After a disaster on the regular white hot dog buns with home delivery (they were overcooked, next to last day of sale and dry as the sahara, crumbling) I went with these for my next hot dog bun order figuring if they were too sweet this style lends itself for sandwiches even, like ham. Or PB&J even. Well I popped them into the freezer first thing since they weren't dated too far out but didn't want to take a chance.  I prefer to grill my dogs but if my buns are getting dry I boil them so I can steam the buns to softness.  I didn't need to boil or steam this bun.  I just opened opened it a bit after being out of freezer for a few, placed it open over the grilling hot dog and it was great.  Not too sweet.  Not a big fan of brioche except buttered or for something needing sweetness like ham.  But these are good.  Soft.  And New england top slice style.  I wouldn't use brioche for a burger but for a dog, nice.

title: Not bad, good taste something odd in texture
text: I am a person who prefers a crisp cookie.  These were crisp, they were tasty, adequate chocolate chips present.  My only complaint is something that lingers in the mouth after eating them.  Almost like coconut bits?  I love flavor of coconut but not the texture and avoid coconut meat like the plague.  I have to check the ingredients again.  Otherwise these are a fine cookie for people who like them crisp.

title: Update: second order Yummy
text:
see my original review of pork chops way below - I ate one immediately and froze the other two. In a week or two placed a second order, follows.

I placed a second order of same PC a week or two later. The first order I chose two pounds (received 3 lovely chops w/o tenderloin attached - they were great), scroll down. This order I placed for one pound (hoping to receive two chops of a medium to thick-cut). What a received was one mastodon chop. Really. Straight out of the Flintstones. One single humongous (with tenderloin portion attached) chop that really should be called a roast for two/or 3. Not having a bandsaw I was stuck with either cooking this like a roast or deboning it so I could halve its thickness (keep tenderloin separate). I decided to roast. Mistake. While the tenderloin was tender it had an off-taste (no idea why) but it was all I could eat at first serving. Refrigerated, reheated in air fryer the next day. Darn it was dry. Like the sahara. Ate about half the chop, diced the leftover, soaked in tamari in fridge to throw in rice tonight While I am still a fan of this, my advice is go for a 2lb order. You will probably get 3 chops. You need 4 chops? well go for 3lbs and put some in fridge. Don't chance with a 1lb order (unless you have a bandsaw)

Second meat order for delivery and very happy with it (the first was truly wonderful beef ribeye). My only point off was this didn't seem terribly fresh. Not gone over at all but not firm enough, lost a lot of water in package, just a whiff here or there a little off. I had tried to get a qty of 2 chops so guessed at what that might weigh since you order by pound. Ended up with three chops. I can only eat one for a serving (and these were big) so I froze the other two and prepared the one with some good old shakenbake. It cooked up nice, still juicy, no off flavor and quite tender. Would buy again. Will probably try one of the other two prepared differently. I think just some simply seasoning, a good sear in a pan and then into the air fryer to finish off and serve with the au jus from searing and a little worcestshire. The one i had definitely was not dried out so I don't think the s&b is really necessary. Will update how that one goes when I get to making it.

title: Eh - ate them over a few days - just blah
text: Pringles tend to be too greasy for me.  Lays stax I prefer.  I thought I would give these a shot.  Nah.  Tasteless really.  Not very salty, not too greasy but just not tasty.  A little cardboard undertones and also a sweet note (these are just the regular).  Maybe the salt n vinegar might be a little better.  Willing to give them a try but won't buy the regular again.

title: so mushy I checked the expiration date
text: Wow.  I cannot believe the good reviews here.  Seriously.  My experience quite different.  I am an olive fanatic, hardly ever meet a variety or brand I don't like (except pimento).  This is my second poor olive experience with what WF has to offer.  My first  try was the 365 brand ripe green olive (not be confused with this preparation of olive).  They were uniformly mushy.  These were shockingly mushy.  I mean I went and got a magnifying glass to check the date and these are no where near expired.  The taste was just OK, the price pretty ridiculous but again, so mushy there were like only two that needed any type of chewing.  The rest you could just mash with your tongue and swallow.  I am not sure how they remained "intact" in transit.  How could anything this soft not dissolve when shaken?  Never again.

title: Good manufactured ghee
text:
I prefer to make my own like many people. Much better value, you can control how "toasty" you want it to taste, etc. But despite what some people tell you and happy helpful folks on youtube showing how easy it is... it is not.

Sometimes it goes great. My first attempt was a resounding success. My second time messy disaster. And all the times since, one never knows. Flip a coin. So I did purchase a nice organic brand locally. Even before covid and supply issues I started having trouble finding it a store, and online the price rose drastically.

I gave this a shot when I put my expired unsalted butter into the freezer (you have to be careful with unsalted butter, it goes bad faster than salted) and I thought let's try some other already made brand. I had found this at a good price point and I find it just as good as my old pricier favorite.

It is still expensive compared to making your own. If you are up to babysitting bubbling butter, pouring it out through various straining mechanisms into ball jars and cleaning it ALL up afterwards you will save money. Otherwise, give this us a try.

title: Disappeared from my local store and they were better
text:
Whether these are a victim of local "supply chain" issues or not I do not know. They just became impossible to find in my local markets since this spring/summer.

These have a slightly different package, the seeds are smaller and the salt coating thinner - almost non existent in places.

The seeds themselves also seem tougher and not as nutty. I will finish them up eventually.

title: Tiny not resealable package, difficult blending
text:
Disappointed. I have had powdered scrambled egg products at buffets, etc. I never really minded them as much as some people. I only eat eggs scrambled and the occasional omelet. My other use is exclusively baking, adding to stirfrys and for coating purposes. I have had trouble finding smaller sized packaging of whole pasteurized egg products in the stores. Even though a dozen fresh eggs last a decent time - with my occasional use so many end up bad so I prefer the pasteurized liquid ones. And certainly less messy.

These did not blend as easily as I hoped and also, I would have been hard pressed to get a decent serving size of scrambled eggs or an omelet. For camping, emergency use, etc. I guess these have a place. I won't purchase this particular one again though.

title: Quality varies too much
text:
Much like regular uncooked bacon the quality of the meat varies. My first two purchases were quite good quality. Mostly whole slices, even thickness, cooked evenly. The next two purchases not so good. Both had a big problem with breakages (many little broken pieces), unevenly cooked (some parts looked almost raw, uneven thickness and the taste not so great.

Not sure if I would purchase again to TBH. Precooked is a great time saver, both cooking and cleanup time. But these last two were very disappointing.

title: Nice packaging but I supposed it is a bit indulgent
text: Love these cookies.  I saw this container of snack size portable portions and was not disappointed.  I don't think there was a single broken cookie.  The canister is reusable.  Once you figure out the secret of the clasp on it.  It would be a lot more reusable if it was a simple snap on closure. But there is plenty of ways for me to re-use now that I know the secret (that still doesn't make it easy).  Somebody should put out a video of how to get that thing open, maybe they have.

title: Not as good as the major brand
text:
Firstly, from some of the reviews it seems like people don't know their olive varieties. Green ripe olives are normally a bit buttery, a bit oily (very much like good EVOO) and firm. These are not the briney vinegary type (which I also love) I am an olive fan, all types of olives.

This particular type was banned in US for quite awhile because of its freckles (google) when they came back I no longer saw the "california" brand on the shelves but "pearls". Pearls were just fine. I actually picked up a case online once and finished them off pretty quickly (I love olives).

With my WF order I thought I would see what they had and picked up a few cans of 365. A bit disappointed when I tried for the first time last night. They seemed about a size smaller than the pearls and unfortunately many of them were mushy. Most of them actually. Taste is still good but the mushiness left me wanting and considering price, I would rather order the pearls instead if only I could get them without ordering by the case. My local market stopped carrying this variety and online is my only option.

title: Believe the sticking tales
text:
I long for the days of the original introduction to vegginess that was morningstar. I grew up on all their stuff. Over the years MS changed. They tried to emulate meat. When I have a burger I am not looking for "meat' (or I would just make a meat burger!) I am looking for flavor, value and err, ease of cooking. While cutting down on meats for a variety of reasons.

Well MS is no longer an option since they went a ridiculous chemical route to get to "meatiness" so I tried these. I should of remembered in the days of yore when such became mainstream - a certain amount of stickiness was part of the ordeal. Wow, these took me back to those days prep wise. In a well seasoned cast iron pan with a squirt of nonaerosol avocado spray these stuck like the devil

Taste? meh. Learned my lesson, will dig out a teflon pan next time to finish up the last 3 whenever I can. What has become of the classic veggie burger? It wasn't meat but it was GOOD. There are recipes for making your own and I am just about at that point.

title: I love this stuff - nostalgia
text:
This was my go to along with the healthy O cereal for work. Yeah, it is wasteful in these single serving containers but really the only way to keep it fresh at work. At home I would dump most of my cereals into vacuum canisters. I only have a few canisters left, they tend to crack and one box takes a couple of glass jars for cereal so I have now purchased these for at home consumption too. It is what it is. Not great environmentally, my bad, but letting food get stale isn't such a great idea either.

As for my crunchberries, I loved them since I was a kid and since when I was working it was often an awful place in awful conditions for awful money and these things would cheer me up with their colorfulness. Seriously. They were therapeutic and do alternate with the healthy O type cereal. These are my secret comfort food. Gotta go, gonna cry.

title: Update to include avocado nice neutral oil spray safe for non-stick
text:
Update: I purchased both the grapeseed and avocado versions. See my addition of avocado below as I can't seem to separate them for review purposes

Grapeseed: I use this in both my cast iron and ceramic cookware. Also the rare times I use non-stick cookware. without the propellants and I believe the lecithin, you supposedly won't turn your nonstick into a sticky gummy mess. I also will use it on foil or aluminum baking sheets but often just hit those up with the traditional propellanty mess of the old style spray. I most certainly am happy to ditch the propellants. No matter how careful and doing it over the sink that stuff got everywhere and also choked me. It is not a very good buy economy wise. The best is what I used to do, quality oils in a refillable spray container (tried 3 or 4 different types). But they were so problematic with clogging, pumping, disassembling and difficulty cleaning to find they would still retain a stink of rancid oil in their plastic pump parts that I have abandoned the use of manual sprayers.

Avocado: To me this has a more neutral taste than the grapeseed. It is also supposedly a higher smokepoint by a bit. I used it to cook a beyond burger (ugh see my beyond review) in a seasoned cast iron pan. Taste of the beyond burger remained same as the grapeseed-cooked patty but my pan...another story. Where there was overspray (I tried to only get it the size of the burger going in but my poor pan developed an awful sticky ring that was not able to be gently scrubbed off using a detergent as well. Was it an interaction with whatever chemicals they create those burgers with? I did not have that issue with the grapeseed version. I don't know. Going to hit it next with some baking soda and if that doesn't remove the ring I will have to resort to steel wool on the sticky ring and and do some reseasoning. I have used the avocado with some other pans (non-stick and aluminum) with no issue. But I didn't cook a dreaded beyond patty. Some fries and I think a normal veggie burger. I don't believe this is the fault of the avocado oil. And I do find it more neutral taste wise than grapeseed. It will be my go to between the two. And no more beyond things for me.

title: Not sure what I think about these - different
text:
I was expecting a small bag and was not disappointed LOL But what I was not expecting was the chips themselves are quite small. Not broken, they are unbroken tiny chips. Trying to dip most of these would be impossible. Made me wonder what variety of potatoes they are using. A lot of irregularly shaped small chips. The taste was interesting too. While they definitely were vinegar flavored they were so sweet I double checked that they weren't actually BBQ flavor. It was not unpleasant and thankfully I didn't note any nauseating off-taste from the seed oils used.

There are other brands in vinegar flavor I want to explore but I may purchase these again. For chips, these so far have not caused any gastric disturbance. I eat them rarely because the seed oils can cause me much misery not to mention taste yuck. But these seem digestible so far. Just a wicked high price for them though. But it was a nice treat and I was able to contain myself to about a third of the bag.

title: Eww
text:
Annie's has always been hit or miss for me. Maybe half the things I have tried are good but don't repurchase because of the price. These are a notable exception as I won't eat them again even free.

I cooked according to directions in an air fryer. Minimal leakage. Odd aroma. I thought maybe I had overcooked because the shell was tough, chewy and also tasteless. The filling, this is when I actually got to the filling the source of aroma was unmistakable to me - ketchup. Cheap ketchup. For something that is supposedly three varieties of cheese, it had no cheese aroma or taste at all. Just ketchup. Cheap ketchup. I only made 4, have probably more than half a bag left and can't think of a way of making them palatable. That will be a challenge. I can't believe I chewed my way through that crust to hit - ketchup. Cheap ketchup.

title: Great flavor - packaging/spout could use improvement
text:
I was very happy to find a reasonable priced bottle of dark soy sauce online. Had been a few years since I could find locally and had been using various tamari.

The product taste is quite good. I am very happy with it. Packaging is another story. Unlike some people I don't mind that it is a plastic bottle. I figured less chance of breakage in shipping. But the pouring spout needs work. Much work. I have yet to find a technique which does not result in a lot of spillage down the side of bottle, my hand, work surface etc. My last use I used a spoon over the sink. Managed to keep it off the side of the bottle and my hand though the sink did get some overflow. I have to finish a bottle of tamari and then I will transfer as much as I can into that. That bottle has your traditional "shaker" spout.

This type of soy sauce is most often used in a quantity into a sauce, etc I think and maybe that is the reason for the inferior spout. I use it both in cooking and add a little to finished dishes. I don't refrigerate it. I suppose I should check online but this unheated kitchen is so cold in winter you cannot even get butter soft on the counter so I think it will be fine. YMMV

title: Did pistachios have a poor crop?
text:
I am a nut nut. Many different varieties of nuts I like. Pistachios and cashews are probably tied for favorite. Well, nuts don't like me and I do have to limit to once in awhile. It is a treat, a healthy treat but must limit for sake of GI comfort these days. I was introduced as a child to them in their artificial red shell. The red fingers were well the price you had to pay. Found un-dyed shells when I got older and didn't look back. I could still put away a good amount back in those days. This brand I think is the first shelled variety I tried. I think I got them originally when I had an idea I was going to make my own pistachio butter (still haven't gotten around to that)
Purchased them and in shell variety over the years. This big bag seemed like a good value, the zip closure seems to work well so far , I still probably have half the bag (can't eat many these days at all) I probably will transfer to a jar and vacuum seal soon unless I do get out the ninja and decide to make pistachio butter.

But I have noticed with these and cashews, the quality seems to be not what it was. You get more "hard" or "rotten" tasting ones I think than in the old days. Being an agricrop product nuts tend to vary, climate changes, crop diseases, etc. It is what it is. This bag was a good convenient value but at this point I do want to transfer to a vacuum sealed glass jar. If you have a large family, can indulge often or might make some butter, I would recommend - the zipper has held a few months now. Myself now, I can probably get away with purchasing a small bag in shells when I get the urge.

title: Keeps your portions in control
text: Although I was a hydrox fan, well, they are gone and for years have gotten my cookie fix with various Oreos.  I like the little cookies, not as many stray crumbs and the little pouches are good for portion control and freshness.  What's not to like?  Well, they ain't hydrox but :(  It is probably more expensive purchasing this way but again, the freshness keeping is probably worth it.  I don't snack a lot on such things and I don't have to worry about the rest of my cookies going stale.  To me, it is worth the trade off.

title: Not as good as they used to be but so few things are
text: Was happy with the purchase.  Decent price point.  Like so many things involving oils, the flavor is not what it used to be before they started switching to various government-mandated preparation oils I guess.  And cashews and many other nuts have suffered due to trade issues and poor growing seasons etc. Some pricier brands may be bigger, slightly better tasting but if you get these at a good price they suffice.

title: My favorite variety of olive
text:
I am an olive lover and pretty much can't hate on any variety. These (although not this brand) were always my favorite when I could find them. A few decades ago they disappeared (were banned actually) in this country and I mourned them. Had something to do with this variety and having a natural (and AFAIK harmless) fungus on them that gives them freckles. Our government banned them for awhile.

When I saw them return under this new brand I was so happy (TBH not sure if they still have freckles? will check next purchase) They are one of the few things that taste as good as when I was a kid. Hard to find in tiny town tiny grocery and I don't often (OK never now) go to civilization and the big stores. Decided to go to good ol Amazon and sure enough they had them. Had to buy a case :( That was my only issue. Not that I had any problem finishing it but getting it into the apartment was less than easy. I see WF section has another brand available singly in my orders and will try that. TBH, I never even look at the price. I love them that much.

title: Your usual Ritz crackers
text: Though a much larger purchase than usual I have had trouble getting these in the stores since "supply chain problems".  Item arrived fresh, intact,  nothing to complain about.  If you can't find them in the store consider an online purchase.  Value depends on quantity but these were dated far enough ahead that I am not too worried.  Maybe you can even freeze them to extend that.  I should check.  Also reminds me to see if I can find saltines online.  Geesh, supply chain issues who would of thought years ago?

title: UGH what is the off flavor in precooked rice?
text:
Thought I had already reviewed this. Guess not. I have been trying various pre-cooked rices for convenience over the years. Several brands, several varieties and was always disappointed with particulary an off-flavor much like cardboard. No matter how it is packaged, whether plain white or jasmine or now bismati. It tastes to me like strong cardboard flavor.

I gave this Uncle Ben's bismati a try. Bismati is the rice I use most often when cooking it from scratch. It has a kind of buttery, popcorny flavor - when cooked from scratch with nothing else added even but a little ghee goes a long way to make it yummier.

Well I figured I would try this, add a little ghee and voila, convenience. Nope. It was cardboard. My pretty strong ghee couldn't mask that off note. What is that flavor? An oil? A preservative? Both?

I have five more packages which I will try to use up in a main dish like stir fry or a soup or something strongly flavored to mask it. After this, no more precooked rice for me. I have a small (incredibly cheap) rice cooker that works just great for my needs. A little inconvenient to dig it out, wait and clean up but so much better tasting and cheaper to make. If convenience doesn't taste good, why bother?

title: Need to pay attention when cooking
text:
I have tried these three times now (and once ages ago when I first saw at supermarket). I remembered from the first time that these DO NOT BROWN. If you get them to brown and can consume them I salute your dental health and taste buds.

So my first try cooking this purchase I did pull them quicker than I normally would and they were just fine. Not too hard, a little greasy, no off flavors. Added a little finishing salt and they they got some au jus run off from the steak and they were good if not for the price. Second time I cooked them too long, my bad, they were browned. Knew I was in trouble. Well, some parts of some of them could be bitten. They had developed an off-oil flavor from the olive oil getting burned. Tossed probably half the serving or more.

Third time the charm? Well I watched them like a hawk. Turned my back once and almost lost them. Most all could be bitten and no off flavor. But these are more work then making from scratch. If only I could find loose yukon gold potatoes in the store. They make the best fries. Unfortunately I can only find bags of yukons that I cannot finish off before they start sprouting.

Have a decent serving still in the bag. Will make when I can devote my constant attention to make sure they don't get to the browned stage. Not worth the price either. If only there were more frozen brands not using seed oils with off flavors or drenching in unwanted seasonings. The olive oil on these is a step up but you cannot let it go too long. Olive oil is delicate. My go to brand is the nathan's in peanut oil.

title: Stale - such is having someone else do your shopping
text:
These were awful but I realize they were on their last day of sale and that is on the shopper/picker, not necessarily the product. However, they were also overly baked to begin with. Color wise you could see that and when I saw the date I was scared to go into the bag. But I had picked up packages of both meat and veggie dogs and I needed those buns! Grilled up a dog and plopped a little ghee into the pan to try and toast my dead bun back to life. Forget it. It's dead, Jim. Shame it kind of ruined my first meat dog experience in a while. I could barely open it to grill it face down without it crumbling in my hands.

My next (and last) try at these buns was boiling the dog so I could steam the bun back to life (see previous, resuscitation attempt futile).

I would really prefer to pick out my own bread products (as well as produce and meat) for just this reason. I don't buy too dark or last day of sale processed bread products. But I was overall quite satisfied with what was picked for me except for these. Probably the cheapest of the items, too, so the experience is what it is.

title: They are hamburger buns
text: I picked up some beyond burgers (another review, very disappointed) so picked these in my online order naturally.  They are just plain white burger buns.  Nothing special.  They did arrive fresh (hot dog buns another story).  I can say they were the best part of the three beyond burgers.  Won't hesitate to buy again unless something fancier catches my eye.  But you are gambling with what freshness level package your shopper picks up (see hot dog bun review).

title: Good brined green olives
text: I used to pick up goya brand pitted ones.  Store either discontinued or has supply chain issues and I was reduced to getting little stuffed ones I would pick or squeeze the pimentos out of (hate hate pimentos) for my frequent olive fix. I figured why not try these in an amazon order of a couple of things?  Jar arrived sealed in a box with my other items, not sure if it was bubblewrapped itself or not.  They are tasty, they are large and what more can I say?  They have pits which of course one has to work around and dispose of.  Not much more work than having to be careful with pitted olives that sometimes retain some pit (should have sued that restaurant where my first bite of my first course salad broke a tooth?)  I am a big olive fan and love almost every variety of olive.  I will probably just go back to removing the pimentos from pitted ones for a better price point though if I don't see regular pitted olives in the store.

title: Pleasantly suprised & changed my mind about instant
text:
I knocked off my regular coffee habit years ago due to advancing age, not wanting the heart "rushes" and interference with sleep. When my keurig died I did not bother replacing (before that I used a senseo for the crema effect - I was a bit of a coffee snob). I went out and purchased an inexpensive "pour through" mug and after using up the cups by dumping them out into a filter I went and picked up a tub of usual supermarket coffee to get my occasional fix of coffee. The taste was so-so (supermarket coffee) and it was a pain to keep dragging out my vacuum sealer to keep it from getting stale. So I saw this instant and figured why not give it a shot.

Wasn't expecting much but it is pretty good. I wish it came in packets for traveling and fresher keeping. I could vacuum seal this each time in a ball jar to keep fresh but I am using it frequently enough I don't think I need to. It is getting my toward a few cups a week I think. Worth a try if you are not a regular user or coffee snob. Will buy again.

title: Just meh
text: Prepared according to directions in an air fryer.  In ten minutes they looked done with just some slight oozing.  I am a big mozz stick fan and I can say I have had very few that didn't ooze a little at least.  They were okay enough crisp wise though the coating kind of freely crumbed.  The coating so bland that I was getting an off-note of either stale bread crumb or cardboard undertones.  They are wrapped in an inner package of plastic so I don't think that off taste is the result of paper taste transfer.  The cheese itself is equally bland.  The cheese is also oddly unfirm, very mushy.  I have never had the urge to put seasoned salt, my flavored salt or ANY salt on a mozz stick.  I didn't bother getting up to do so, I had only made 3 as a light warm snack.  I will finish the other four sometime, but will prepare a little bit of sauce, or in a pinch ketchup and SALT.  I won't purchase again needing to doctor them up so much.  Homemade is not that much of a trouble to make and well, there are quite a few better brands out there that don't need enhancement.

title: Liked better than the dark version
text: I purchased these once they came out in the store, in the dark version because I generally loved darker pretzels and chips.  I was not impressed as they were TOO dark.  It made them bitter rather than more flavorful.  I looked for the regular version in the store but they were always sold out so when I saw them online I threw two in the cart.  I liked them better than the dark ones.  Warning:  they are very hard .  Good teeth, much care needed eating them.  One of my favorite low calorie treats is a hard pretzel or two dunked in flavored seltzer (orange is good) or a diet root beer.  Had nothing for dunking but did managed to out away the two bags within a week or so.  They are good, just the right amount of salt and not terribly pricey.  Will purchase again but make sure I have something carbonated.

title: Too fragile for shipping?
text: I had longed for the taste of the OG and happily put these into my online order rather than picking up one of the numerous "knock offs" found in the store.  Immediately disappointed by the amount of breakage and mediocre taste.  It arrived in a decently packed box with other items but I found almost half of the cookies broken.  The taste was not the rich buttery one I had remembered.  Won't purchase online to be shipped again and unlikely to pick them out in store over those less expensive knock offs.

title: UPDATE: my 2nd order not so...Excellent - one of the best I have ever had
text:
UPDATE: ordered for a second time. See original review below. This time was not so wonderful just took off a star. After my first five star experience I figured the only was to go from there was probably down. But still not too far. As with my first order I asked for a pound. Since the first one was almost TOO think I figured I would slice thickness and get two steaks out of it and have one suitable for a steak n eggs breakfast. This steak was thinner. Not as marbled and gorgeous as the first. I did debate whether to halve it (I probably shouldn't have but did anyway because I am stupid like that) Got well two thin steaks. Froze one, cooked the other. I figured a quick sear even on cast iron and it should be a perfect medium. Eh, I messed up was more a medium well but it definitely didn't have the marbling or flavor (fat is flavor!) of that first purchase. A few days later and I decide to pull out the frozen half and try steak and eggs. I normally don't cook from frozen but since this was thin I did hoping it would save interior. My, that baby while a perfect sear also ended up well done (UGH). However, regardless of temp I can say my second serve of second order did not have the marbling or flavor of that first ordered single. Still on the fence as to what "meat" I will order for xmas. Maybe will go off to the brick n mortar butcher even and pick something out. Still kicking myself for not taking the first steak and saving it for the holiday in the freezer. I still dream about. Beautiful. These two, your average supermarket steak.

What can I say? I am old and this has to rank as one of the best I have ever had whether prepared myself or at a steak house. For a steak that is choice grade, this was truly a great value even at what many would consider a high price point. I have seen ribeyes at the supermarket going for more than this per pound. Was it on sale maybe?

I had this instead of turkey for Thanksgiving. Actually I made it today on Black Friday as I just wasn't feeling like an indulgent meal yesterday. Did not disappoint. Unwrapped and sprinkled with seasalt on both sides while it got the chill off and dropped it into my biggest cast iron skillet I had preheated. Initially considered slicing it in half thinner as I was concerned if I could get a nice medium (no more no less for me) on the stove top but kept it as it was. Perfect. Made some au jus with the drippings and a spoonful of dark soy sauce. Didn't even need the A1 I had already poured onto a warm plate.

I wouldn't hesitate to buy again. Especially at that price. Meat is always a gamble, even when I pick it out myself in person you never really know until you prepare and eat it. Looking forward to it I think I will get it again for Christmas but just get a ham slice in case this was a one-off.

At least give it a try. Never would have guessed it is probably only Choice grade, so tender.

title: Update- What did I just eat? Not talking about the burger
text:
Firstly, although the listing said (frozen) they arrived thawed. Rather disappointed in that as I bought two packs of 2 and wanted to keep one frozen for another time. Next time, I will order the frozen box of 8 (if I chose to purchase again) which leads me to the 2nd issue: The packaging. For a product that some consume for the greater good of the planet that is a mighty big piece of plastic packaging. This leads me point number 3:

What is stuck to the bottom of the patties in the package? I didn't notice because I picked one of them out of package with a spatula and placed on preheated cast iron griddle. I didn't notice any off smell while cooking but when I scraped and flipped it over (and this cast iron is well seasoned and can even do eggs) I said OMG. It looks exactly like plastic! It was wrinkled in the middle and charred around the edges. I poked it. Definitely not something errr edible? I came to the conclusion it must have been some kind of "diaper". Why does a veggie burger need a diaper? I have had one mishap where I did a similar thing with a steak (real beef) picking it up with tongs and plopping it onto a hot griddle - not realizing there was a darn diaper on the bottom of it. Never made that mistake again I tell you. Was afraid that pan was a goner. But it served well the rest of its non-stick life (I don't use those kinds of pans anymore BTW)

Anyway, I peeled it away from the patty - is it waxed paper? It's transparent to a point. I don't know. Intend to send a question to the Beyond meat people and ask how dangerous is what I just ate?

That said, yeah I ate it. It had an odd "petrochemical" kind of taste. The closest I can come to describing it - like food that has been cooked on charcoal with lighter fluid (don't do that - use a charcoal chimney with lump hardwood charcoal!) I can't pick up any smell on the "diaper" so it leads me to believe it is a flavoring that they add to make it seem like a real grilled hamburger.

i will update this review with the unadulterated taste when I try the other one maybe tonight after thoroughly cleaning my antique cast iron pan with soap and water and a scrubber. Also will update any response I get from Beyond company customer service.

They use diapers on real meat to absorb the hemoglobin that leaks out to make meat appear fresher and well less messy and disgusting (if you ask me, they shouldn't bother the packaging always leaks and it is so hard to keep contamination of non-meat products to a minimum). Yes, I am back to eating meat in old age after years of veggie. Just what my body needs to function properly. But I keep meat products to a minimum and I thought these were a good alternative.

I have tried two more of these patties (sans wax paper) and can definitely say the petrochemical taste I am getting is surely an intentional flavoring part of the burger. Perhaps to make it taste like the backyard BBQs of the 70s with charcoal drenched in started fluid? Why? Not finishing the last of the 4, if I could've refroze it maybe I would have a time where I could try and drown out that petrol flavoring. But can't so it is going into the garbage.

Although I am no longer veggie and do eat some meat, I still prefer a good tasting veggie burger to something trying to imitate meat. Especially with that petrol flavoring it is a no-go for me. Maybe the bulk ground product doesn't have that flavoring? (anyone want a charcoal starter fluid meat sauce or lasagna? no) But with the lack of storage options, etc. Just not worth it for me. Off to soy and black bean patties then.

title: Seriously good noodle
text: Very happy with this product.  Closest I have had to fresh/homemade in years.  Can't find locally so I suppose it is pricey this way but worth it.

title: listen to those who received damaged product
text:
I am in process of transferring product to another container. Because as you can see from the pic, product container was extremely damaged, to the point you can't get the plastic lid on it due to the bent up seam. Unlike the other damage pics I saw here, this one took a hit right to the seam near the top.

The product itself is just OK. How long it has been in this crushed state, how long it will last I don't know? I will put it in a mason jar in the fridge to hopefully keep it fresh as long as possible.

The whole reason I chose this product was because of what looked like "sturdy" "resealable" packaging so I wouldn't have to bother with transferring it like I have to do with the envelope/zip type products. Coming this damaged it defeated the purpose, is not returnable and all I could do was send comment to mfr and write this review. Beware and believe, you are likely going to get a destroyed can.

title: Very good product in good packaging
text: What can you say about pretzel salt?  It's salt.  But I do like the zip seal packaging which has not failed in all this time.  So I would buy again if I ever have to.  It's salt, if sealed lasts a long long time.

title: Very nice just a little pricey
text: it doesn't have a very strong maple flavor but for the price I think it is quite a fair value. No complaints, just not as mapley as I like.

title: Like I remember it
text: Yeah, I know they are fake blueberry bits.  And they are weirdly "capsule shaped" now.  This disappeared from my local stores a couple of years ago.  I decided to bite the bullet to purchase online at considerable more cost but it is good and easy.  If you want a real treat replace the water or part of the water with a berry flavored seltzer.  Krusteez still is the champion of easy fluffy pancakes. Even if the artificial blueberry bits are a little weird and maybe a tad crunchy.

title: agree with ALL those people that say they are not the same
text:
UPDATE - production code XPG2. I was reading other bad experiences people have had. They had varying different production codes. Just want to put my bad can code out there for other folks. If you see them locally, can look at the code before purchase. Avoid this one.

I was almost addicted to these things I guess it was around 1983 or so. Incredible melt in your mouth cheesiness I had never experienced in like a snack before.

I see things like that you have to check the plant code or something because some plants are good and some bad. Not about to get out the magnifying glass to check such code on this. there is only one flavor note and it is SALT. I have no idea how these new ones compare to the old ones in actual sodium content in taste, this is a salt block like I used to give to horses. Serious. No cheese flavor. In the "old" days, these blew cheetos out of the water. For awhile I would buy the cheetos when these disappeared. Today's cheetos too, are nothing but salt. But, at least texture and sodium concentration don't tear up your mouth and tongue after just a handful. Cheetos are at least edible. This canister of salt, not.

I was lucky enough to get them locally today, retail, didn't buy a case or anything which is a good thing. I ate about 5 or 6 ballz before the pain and revulsion were too much.

Seriously, even dollar store cheez balls are better than this.

title: good product, packaging just so
text: Well I have had this brand purchased locally and felt it good but over priced.  My opinion is the same.  Nothing wrong with the product but a little more effort into the packing would be appreciated.  They really need a resealable zipper kind of thing on this.  It is a large amount that you are not going to be going through quickly (although I managed at a pretty scary rate).  I put them in canning jars with my vacuum seal lids though I shouldn't have bothered as I did go through it pretty quickly.  At this price point I think either a resealable bag or a jar would be appropriate

title: disappointed - no expiry date
text:
I was kind of taken aback when I got these out of the box to check for an expiration date and could not find it. All the ones purchased in store have the date stamped (not too clearly now mind you) on the back on the bottom border. I searched with a magnifying glass but nothing.

That said, the first packet I used the powder did seem a little bit hard in the pack but finally came out fine. Now the one thing I have noticed about this having had a second one to compare - it is really thicker than those I have bought previously (in store). This stuff will turn to pudding if you turn your back on it for a minute. Not sure if they have changed the formula or it might be I have some old stuff since I can't tell because of no expiry date. Your mileage may vary. I hope to find it in local stores soon and see about the difference.

Update: I did check out the outer carton in the pantry and while the individual packets had no expire date the carton did have one stamped on it - about six months out. I continue to use these although I do still feel as though they thicken up too much too quickly. I have to wonder if there has been a formula change.

title: very nice fine grind
text:
I previously used Bob's for my pasta and pizza dough. Not wanting to buy a case, I opted for this product and am very happy with it. It is a finer mill than Bob's. It doesn't scratch my bread pan (you can actually hear how much smoother it is) when I use it to knead the pizza dough. Also it not noticeably grainy when eating like Bob's. I can't differentiate in taste.

One word - do not sprinkle cornmeal for pizza crust. It burns. You should use a dusting of this on the stone/paddle/pan for authentic result. Use this for a third of your flour in pizza dough recipe as well and you won't be disappointed.

title: excellent zipper package
text:
This I think is the first time I wrote a review for a products packaging (not to be confused with the mailing packaging)

These people have a quality zip lock on their product. We have all been there with so many products nowadays having a zip seal which does not seal.

But here, this one does. I am still reluctant to trust and use a binder clip after folding the zipped portion over but it does not seem to be necessary with this package. This thing zips up and stays sealed. I only have so many canisters/etc. and did not have one to dedicate to this product and I am so happy with this zip bag.

As for product, it seems to be fine I purchased initially to make soft pretzels but have not got around to doing them yet but I have added it twice to my homemade pizza dough which was already pretty awesome - it does add another textural element to the crust. I am sure it is going to make the best pretzels ever. And I won't have to worry about the bag having been sitting open. Great job on keeping your product fresh!

title: Could they please screw the lid securely at factory?
text:
I have been using Nutiva for as long as I have been using coconut oil. I have had a hard time finding it locally in supermarkets and don't frequent that many vitamin/health food stores. So I have mostly gotten it online. This is the largest single jar I have purchased. Normally I pick up two smaller ones.

The reason for a star off is something has to be done about the top. Like others have said, mine was nearly completely unscrewed when received and on it's side in box. It is winter. I am in the northeast. So, no harm no foul this stuff is solid. In the summer I would have had a mess possibly unless somehow the inner seal held up. With my past experiences with purchases in summer, the inner seal does not hold up. This would have been a big tidal wave of coconut oil goodness into the box.

This is a mfr issue. They need to secure the lid. They can't expect shippers to do that. Would be nice if they did...

title: Take your pizza game up a few notches
text: Do not use cornmeal for flouring surfaces, peels or stones for pizza. You should use semolina. Does not burn.  Also use this 1 part to 2 parts of bread flour for my pizza crust recipe. My only fault with it is that is is a little coarser than I care for to use in the bread or pasta dough. But it is more economical than fancy fine milled imported semolina. When necessary there are one or two stores within driving distance that carry this also. I picked this up at Amazon because the price was not too bad and I am handicapped and the less driving I have to do the happier I am. I especially don't want to drive to a store far away and find they are out of it or I just can't find it wherever they moved it since the last time I was there. This will last me the winter. I make my own pizza every two weeks or so and pasta once a month maybe.

title: The best ghee you pay a lot for
text:
This is the best of the several ghees I have tried over the years, hands down. Great taste, great texture. However, as it became more popular (perhaps because of paleo thing) it has gotten pricey and limited availability. This was available and also seemed to be the best price per ounce.

My only other gripe with the product besides price/availability is the packaging. While it is admirable that it comes in a glass container without a BPA liner and has a plastic overwrap, in shipping it is not quite adequate to prevent leaking. Two of mine arrived leaking, one barely and the other more severely. The lids just weren't screwed down all the way tight or had come looser on shipping. The plastic overwrap cannot contain the liquid ghee becomes when subjected to the merciless heat we have been experiencing these weeks so I had some slippery heavy glass jars to deal with. Cleaned them up, ghee is fine. From the looks of it they may have spent some time upside down too, which again, in this heat, ghee is a liquid so you are going to have spillage in this kind of container.

If they would find a way to make an inner seal without BPA that would be great. Or maybe they can tape down the lid to not loosen up. They also need to ramp up production/distribution. This is not kobe beef but is getting as expensive.

title: Grainy with a capital G and that rhymes with ghee...
text:
Oh well, anyway. I am a devotee of another particular brand of organic (maybe grassfed too, not sure) ghee for awhile. Maybe I am spoiled. That other has become obnoxiously expensive and back ordered for awhile now to make matters worse. OK, so tried this one.

Sadly, not only is it quite expensive, the jar itself has a seal that is really nothing more than to annoy you. It doesn't really seem to be a good seal of plastic as there was no "pop" on the metal jar lid. I actually unscrewed it off after slitting the rigid plastic. And I found GRAINY. Very disappointed. The taste is innocuous, nothing is giving me ghee vibes there. I don't get the really deep ghee smell like I do with my old favorite and am just so put off by the graininess. Trader Joe's I have never tried because of the reports of it being so grainy - I would bet that this is what the TJ brand is.

Will not buy again. Just not worth it. I am so close to making my own again, if it wasn't for the incredible mess. I really probably need to because where I am at, good ghee is just too darn hard to find.

title: Please stabilize the sizing
text:
Dear Purity - please stop messing with sizing. I was a devotee of this stuff years ago when it was available at my local wally world in the Indian food section. Wally inexplicably stopped carry it even in areas with a heavy population of people using it. So I found it on amazon. A little expensive but worth it. Then the next time I ordered it I found the price rose and when I got it found the jar had shrunk to something that looked sample sized. I was pretty upset. Same great ghee but more expensive than probably kobe beef per pound. I emailed Purity to try a find some other place local so I could see what I was ghetting (typo and it stays, heh). But they just told me to go to amazon. Long story short now I saw this new size with the new label and ordered. Again, same great ghee. The size might even be larger than my original, still pricey.

I have tried other ghees both from specialty stores and here on Amazon. This is the most shelf stable consistent quality but for goodness sake it is still darn expensive, especially if you need to go with a vendor that charges shipping. I just can't make my own after the mess I had to clean up when I did make my own. After cleaning that you don't want to look at ghee for a long time. But if you have nice big easy to clean kitchen/stove give it a try. It is not hard. Just messy. And smelly (good smell but still a lot of smell)>

title: Much smaller size than previously available
text:
Need to emphasize this is actually the same great ghee I had gotten for a year or two or three. Used to be able to get it in my local wally world, they stopped carrying and the Purity Farms people were ZERO helpful in locating anything other than Amazon as a distributor for me. But now, what has happened? Nearly half the size for more than the old price? I don't know if it is an Amazon issue or a Purity Farms issue but it means I won't be buying it anymore.

I couldn't believe the teeny tiny jar that arrived. I have tried other brands, both here and other sites and other brick and mortar. This is the absolute most wonderful brand. But what kind of game they are playing with their customers I don't know.

No other ghee comes close except for my own homemade which because of UNBELIEVABLE MESS I will never do again. And I am a foodie. And go to great lengths. Ghee making is not one of them - I have to draw the line somewhere. I continue to look for a good local source and mourn the loss of this excellent brand/value.

title: Great rice just not so much great price
text:
I have been purchasing this rice off and on for a few years now. When I first tried it about 4 or 5 years ago it was much less expensive. Then, for whatever reason, the price really got up there not just here on Amazon but you could see the increase on Asian food sites too. For those of us without easy access to Asian markets that may carry locally this type of rice, a lot depends on how much a vendor will charge for shipping since hey, it is a couple of pounds we are talking about here. So I don't order it as much as I would like and during times without I use basmati or more likely, Calrose. I prefer a stickier medium grain like these since they hold sauce, etc. so much better than fussy polished long grain like basmati. Don't mention Jasmine. I do not want my sauces to compete with that fragrance. Jasmine=parfum. Basmati=popcorn. Popcorn better if you must have something.

Back to this rice. Not understanding the comments about this "spoiling" so fast. I am a family of one that has frequently purchased this five pounds and do not eat rice daily, sometimes not even weekly! Once I open the bag I do shift to a vacuum canister and well, vacuum seal it. I do that with any rice, pasta, baking mix, etc. I don't know what spoiled rice would taste like but I guess I can sleep easy I have not tasted it yet :-) Yay.

Anyway, if you have the room in the fridge or a vacuum sealing system like I, don't hesitate to purchase this. Even at current prices it is better than the pricier premium Basmatis and better tasting, better sauce clinging and better for you with that germ business intact. Oh, tastes good too. P.S. I never soaked. Usually use my cheapo ten dollar rice cooker which makes a mess of all types of rice on bottom, this no exception but the rest is quite yum!

title: Great rice, why has haiga doubled in price?
text:
This is a nice compromise between white and brown rice. Some people call it brown and it isn't. It is white with a little bran left, actually the germ.

I think it might be a little better than consuming totally white rice and the taste is fine so I like using it. However, the price doubled from the last time I got it (not just here, it is hard to find on net and I don't have a lot of asian stores here to look into)

It is grown in California and if Calrose, etc, hasn't experienced some price doubling disaster I don't know why this has.

But the rice itself is perfectly fine and perhaps a little better than straight white.

title: The latest plastic container is a number 2 HDPE
text:
I had to chime in here. I have the 29oz and have looked all over the web (including the Nutiva site) to see if they mention what plastic this container is. Nowhere is it to be found. There are a handful of mentions of no. 1 plastic (when it was in a clear jar). But nothing about these white plastic jars that now seem to be the norm for most sizes. So when I got home today I turned mine over and found a "2". HDPE. Don't have to worry about BPA but I don't know much about HDPE.

If they carried this in a glass jar I would be happier though I would need to find at local brick and mortar stores because I am sure shipping would be a lot. Like others on account of the container, I give it a 4 star rating.

This is the BEST EVCO I have had to date and I will continue to use it. As for transferring it to another container: I have many Ball jars because I use a foodsaver vacuum sealer to keep things. However, the lining of the jar lids is apparently BPA rich. So, I will keep it in the white plastic number 2 and hope for the best.

Again, this is a great quality EVCO and I haven't heard a single bad word about it except for the plastic jar so wanted to add what information I could for those making a decision.

title: loving my Senseo more than ever
text:
I started having trouble finding my favorite Senseo pod, Sumatra locally. I did not want to spend even more money with shipping online. I couldn't find another pod strong enough to make an 8oz mug with one pod so I thought I would get my own beans, grind them and make my own pods. The first try was ecopad. Horrible - way too messy to empty and an awful awful tasting result. Then I got the Melitta pods with flaps. Not bad but could only get enough coffee in them for tiny cup. Then I bought the perfect pod sealer on an auction site and was so pleased I immediately looked around for more pods to buy.

I hope they don't stop making these. I will have to resort to using tea bag material and a heat sealer if they do. You can fit enough coffee in them for a mug. I haven't had any disasters. Yes, more expensive than any other options other than the Senseo pods which are most expensive. But worth it. I only drink one cup (BIG cup) of coffee a day and it has to be a GOOD cup. This does.

Hoping my pod maker holds up and the filters are available for a long long time.

title: Easy and quick addition to your meal!
text: 2 Thumbs up!

title: I love Ritz crackers
text: They are just rich enough in flavor to enjoy without a spread of any kind. The price compares favorably, and I like the way they are packed. I especially like that the box opens like a pizza box rather than the same as most crackers. I'll be buying them again.

title: These crackers are all right
text: These don't have a lot of flavor when eaten alone. I guess they'd be OK with a dip or spread, but I don't usually bother with those.

title: The flavor wasn't particularly good
text: I won't buy this item again. It was fresh enough, but there was barely any cinnamon flavor and the base flavor was just OK.

title: These cookies are as good as the ones from my grocery store
text: I like the flavor and must set myself a limit or I'll eat them all at once. There are plenty of pecans in the cookies. I've already ordered and opened a second box.

title: Very soothing tea
text: I had an extremely sore throat, so much so that I couldn't swallow water. This tea would go down, probably in part because it was warm,  but also because it eased my sore throat some. I used it for at least 3 days. I will use it again just for the flavor and relaxation it provided me.  I will definitely buy it again when I run out.

title: Could be a bit more cinnamony
text: I like the gummy bears format. I often share my snacks with others, and this form is very convenient. The taste was good if a little milder than I prefer. The cost is a little higher than I was hoping to pay, but the Jelly Belly brand is worth it. All in all,  I am quite pleased with the purchase and will order again.

title: The flavors are average
text: I mainly wanted these candies for the cinnamon ones. They do taste like cinnamon, but very mildly. I was looking for a little more spiciness. Other than that, they were good enough to satisfy my sweet tooth.

title: Great applesauce
text: I have always been a fan of Mott's applesauce. These small cups eliminate the waste I faced when a jar needed to be trashed. They're a good quick snack and I can recycle the cups.

title: I love this rice
text: It tastes good and is convenient. I use it as a base for baked beans, canned meats, soups, veggies, and often by itself with a little butter. The price is comparable to my local grocery.

title: Bought these as stocking stuffers
text: The recipient really liked them, which is a good reaction for a friend who doesn't like hot drinks. I will try them when I go there for a visit.

title: Good sausage
text: This summer sausage tastes good, but is not as good as another brand I've had in the past. I would buy it again for appetizers.

title: Love the stew over rice
text: I like this canned stew for a quick meal. I put it over rice and plan to put it over noodles as well. It tastes good and is satisfying.

title: Good mac and cheese in better packaging
text: I like Kraft Mac and Cheese but I didn't like having to trash the container. I'm trying to minimize my trash, especially foam type products like the lining of the previous kind of container. These packets were a pleasant surprise. Now I can enjoy my mac and cheese with less guilt.

title: Hard to find in store
text: I'm not crazy about the frosted PopTarts. That's too much sweetness for me. These are my favorite, but they're hard to find in stores. This 16 pack is a good value. They toast just fine.

title: This gift hit the spot!
text: I sent this as a gift to my sister. She called to tell me it was delicious. I also liked the quantity available.

title: Comes in fresh
text: Well packed, fresh, tasty.

title: Fresh and tasty

I haven't had any swelling, and the flavor was NOT salty.... which was my initial concern. We are happy and sad too that we went so many year without trying a smoked turkey before. I plan on ordering another for Christmas when our daughter is here, so she doesn't miss out throughout her life as we did. Last note is I spoke to one of the owners asking for the turkey to be shipped at a date later than Amazon listed, and he personally saw to it that the turkey was delivered a few days before Thanksgiving, and was so nice and helful as to my questions and even offered some extra tips to use the turkey for and in!! Will be ordering for Christmas and in future holiday times as well! By the way order more than you'll need so you can enjoy and share more!!

title: Clover's limerick
text:
There once was a rabbit named Clover
Sold by Amazon, over and over
When they said he was fresh
They did NOT mean his flesh
Which would make a coyote* keel over

When I saw he was missing his head
I surmised that old Clover was dead
So I took out some cheese
Which I melted with ease
And served some Welsh rarebit instead

*pronounced kahy-OH-tee

Note: This item does not come with Amazon's easy-open packaging.
It took me quite a while to find it hidden inside the shiny black top hat, even though the instructions stated quite clearly that it was a riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma. In the end, I used the knife, in the kitchen.

Amanda Richards, August 31, 2010

title: 90 seconds

Rice for one
Swiftly done
Squeeze, tear
Zap.
There!

Skillet, pot
Worry not
Ready rice
Quick
Nice!

Plump grains
Time gains
Kinda pasty
But
Tasty

All alone?

The takeout
Just
Break out

To
Make

title: Have I got something in my teeth?
text:
When you've dined but cannot brush
Just chew a piece of gum
It'll help you clean the debris off
And hide the smell of rum

This brand says it's got Xylitol
Whatever that may mean
It claims to fight your cavities
And keep your toothies clean

It'll clear away the Cheeto crumbs
You won't regret the loss
But stringy bits of gristle? Well
Just don't forget to floss

No substitute for brushing
But for when you're on the spot
It won't remove the spinach
But you'd better chew than not

Amanda Richards, January 31, 2009

title: The Cheeto Dilemma
text:
When empty crunches
Replace bunches
Of lunches

You get:

Bigger hips
Orange lips
And finger tips

But:

Though conflicted
And restricted
I'm addicted

Amanda Richards, January 31, 2009

title: Goodness gracious! Great balls of chocolate!
text:
Dear chocolate lovers, big or small
Try this scrumptious little ball
You'll swear off chocolate that's in bars
Once you try Maltesers by Mars

Creamy outside
Crunchy filling
Sweetened malt
That gets top billing

Bite right in
Or suck a while
Eat a handful
With a smile

One thing's for sure
That once you try it
You'll have no choice
But to go and buy it

An open bag's too quickly empty
You'll have to make sure you buy plenty
You'll need a bag or two to spare
That is, if you intend to share

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2009

title: For someone who deserves a treat
text:
Chocolates and caramels
And toffee supreme-y
Twelve different types
So deliciously creamy

Caramel cups
And slim toffee fingers
Milk chocolate blocks
For a sweetness that lingers

Orange that's creamy
Plus orange that crunches
Chocolate noisettes
That taste great after lunches

Strawberry and Coconut
Hazelnuts too
Chocolate fudge
Plus two toffees to chew

Give this for a gift
That you'll never regret
The person receiving
Will never forget

I bought two this Christmas
And wrapped them with glee
Then gave them to someone
Deserving them - ME!

Conclusion:

Candy is dandy
When you have it handy
But for a real treat
Try Quality Street

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2009

title: Some things need to be taken with a grain of salt
text:
Although it's not one of my usual topics
Humidity's killing us down in the tropics
Our cereals get cold and our icy drinks hot
Spaghetti resembles a Gordian knot

But the point of this verse is the seasoning I dump
When I go to the bottle and find one big clump
And I cry every time that I shell out more cash
For flavor full off-er-ings from Mrs. Dash

When I know fully well that I'll open the seal
And into the bottle the moisture will steal
So it's either I go on a diet that's bland
Or grab me a bottle of this well known brand

And although the crystals become intertwined
I'll upturn the bottle and proceed to grind
For freshly ground flavor, my taste buds exalt
All hail to the taste of McCormick's sea salt!

Amanda Richards, October 8, 2008

title: It'll take a village
text:
According to an old story, a beggar comes to a village, carrying an empty pot. He fills the pot with water, drops a large stone in it, and starts cooking in the square.

One of the villagers asks what he's doing, to which he replies that he is making "stone soup", which tastes wonderful, although it still needs a little "something something" to improve the taste. The villager (although rather stingy) doesn't mind parting with a few vegetables, so these get added to the soup. Another villager walks by, inquiring about the pot, and the beggar gives him the "stone soup" spiel once again. The villager gives him a little bit of celery to help out.

As word gets around (like it does in small villages) more and more people walk by, each adding another ingredient. Finally, a delicious pot of stone soup is bubbling on the fire, and is more than enough to share with everyone.

Now, back to our regular review:

If Healthy Choice
Had a voice
This tasteless phony
Minestrone
Would be begging to be put out of its misery

Potatoes, dried
Lurk inside
And the puny pasta
Spells disasta
For this unappetizing bowl of goopy stew

I see dead peas
And celeries
And other odd stuff
But not enough
To give this soup a flavor that could be considered "natural"

I would suggest
For the best
That it would be wise
To economize
And try a stone instead of shelling out your hard earned bread for this

Amanda Richards, October 2, 2008

title: Less Moore please
text:
I hate to judge
This load of sludge
That's just oodles
Of ugly noodles
But I must

Carrots and peas
Appear at ease
But the chicken
Seems to be stricken
With something

The bland brown sauce
Just comes across
As food for pets
So with no regrets
I'll just pass

Amanda Richards, May 21, 2008

title: Delicious!
text: I use an entire can of these tomatoes  (Op.  chop them).  When I make shakshuka,  Shakshuka is a poached egg dish.  Here is my recipe:  Pour the entire can in a medium size frying pan (about 12 inch), add two tablespoons of butter, 1/4 tsp. basil and white pepper. Bring to a boil.  Crack open three whole eggs into a small bowl and slide them on top of the tomato mixture. Poach the eggs until opaque on top then turn them to cook for a few seconds.  They'll be a soft or runny yolk. Serve them on microwaved corn tortillas (10 sec. for each tortilla).  You can also use noodles or rice or whatever.  These tomatoes are great!
