title: Just...blah
text: These are blah in a strange way, because sugar cookies are a bland type inherently. However, I felt these just didn't work. The frosting is sticky and a bit messy and didn't seem to add much to the overall flavor. The cookies are definitely soft, but don't come off as a classic sugar cookie to me.

title: The mix is appealing
text:
It's cheap mass-market chocolate, so I am reviewing it based at that level, since we all know that is what it is.

My review mainly is to say that the mix of flavors in this bag is a nice option. Besides the standard, you also get dark chocolate, and white chocolate mini-cups. Those two get the flavor combo down well for low end candy. Having the variety is nice, because these three options really do suit different moods.

title: Better options out there
text:
I usually avoid buying American chocolates anymore since they all have gotten just plain awful. But I remembered Dove chocolates used to be okay for cheap American mass marketed candy.

These are in that category. I wouldn't buy them again, but they weren't as bad as say something like a Hershey's bar. To me, one of the keys of making candy is getting the flavor blend combined with contrast down just right. These didn't have that magic. There is dark chocolate, and poor quality salted caramel, which should come together nicely, but it doesn't. The chocolate bitterness is off in relation to the salty flavor, and the caramel lacks punch.

title: Great for what they are
text:
I rated these highly based upon what they are, not how they compare to, say, actual real ramen.

These couldn't be easier to prepare; just pour in hot water (I use a little less than recommended).

You get a blandish, very basic ramen which is surprisingly filling, and great if you are having problems eating foods (such as dealing with cancer or chemotherapy). When I can't stomach anything, but want something to eat with my medications to prevent nausea, these work well. They also help late at night if I haven't been able to eat, and feel I should have something in my stomach to help me sleep.

No, it's not the most nutritious thing out there; but if you've been in such situations, you understand what I'm talking about here.

title: Doesn't taste close to the typical Hormel mix; too sweet and very runny
text: I thought this would taste like the regular Hormel pretty much, but just have more meaty chunks in it. It tastes quite different, and unpleasant to me; a weird overly sweet, unmeaty flavor. I'm not sure there is actually more meat in this; it seems like the can is at least half runny sauce, and very few chunks, but they are larger in size than the typical Hormal meat chili. I definitely wouldn't purchase this again and I will give away what remains of the batch I ordered.

And I was a long-time tree hugging vegetarian used to eating a wide variety of alternative type products and foods so I'm not put off by that generally.

title: Unpleasant taste and kinda greasy
text: There really wasn't anything I liked about these. The texture was somewhat like crumbly cardboard. They had a sort of greasy quality. The flavor was disappointing. They didn't go that great with anything I tried them with. I ended up just tossing them out actually. I offered to others who didn't like them either. They certainly sounded like they would be good, I'm not sure even how you could not end up with a decent cracker based on the organic selection of ingredients.

title: Not horrible but sort of meh; good emergency backup
text: I bought this for emergency storage use. I think these sausage ones taste better than the regular ones. Obviously canned ravioli, so don't expect anything else. A can is very filling and the nutritional label seems okay. Remember canned tomato sauce is healthy. For your emergency food storage, variety is wise, and canned ravioli is also something many people will eat. You don't technically need to heat it either, so if you don't have power or a heat source during an emergency, not a problem as long as you have a manual can opener.

title: Best Canned Mushroom Soup
text: Not much else needs to be said. Lots of mushrooms, excellent creamy bisque, great complex flavor, doesn't have the typical canned-soup disappointment. I wouldn't waste time with any other canned mushroom soup.

title: It's yer basic affordable olive oil
text: Many of us tend to keep a few different oils around, including several types of olive oil, for different uses. There's always a need in my kitchen for an affordable basic all-around sort of olive oil. This met that need conveniently, and I would purchase this product again. No, it's not the best olive oil I've ever had. But it's great for basic cooking needs, as well as cosmetic uses, if you make any of your own skincare or similar items yourself. I've also used it to make skin treatments etc. for my pet, which my vet said was good.

title: Really good, similar to home-made quality
text: These little cookies are addictive. This brand reliably produces great shortbread cookies in several riffs, all of which are excellent and come pretty close to home-made taste. They are crumbly/crunchy/sandy, buttery, just the right amount of saltiness and, depending on the type you get, the extras like chocolate chips are of good quality and well balanced with the cookie flavors. The mini-chocolate-chip cookies are really wonderful. The bags have a nice peel-back recloseable top that actually works, so the cookies stay fresh. You can dunk them, but you don't need to. They are excellent with milk, tea, coffee, or really whatever you like. Because of the quality of this brand, these little cookies are satiating, and you won't feel that you want to eat a lot of them to get your cookie fix, which is another plus with these.

title: wasn't interested in purchasing these again
text: Graham crackers are such a basic item that the flavor really does have to be right. These had a sort of flat, cardboard like hint and even the texture was a bit unappealing. Obviously they're just graham crackers so they are okay for whatever, but I think other brands I've tried are much better.

title: good for a lot of things, the same basically as collagen
text: Collagen is an uncooked gelatin. It costs a lot more, and research I've read indicates that cooking (i.e., gelatin) provides better nutrition and beneficial substances than collagen. It's just that collagen is a fad right now, and plain gelatin reminds everyone of great-granny's wiggly weird salads. But this product is good for a lot of culinary uses, and I personally use it by adding a spoon to plain bone broth with herbs etc. for the health benefits. You can also add it to smoothies and other things, and it makes a good egg replacer if you are out of eggs.

Needs doctoring but that's what this kind of white gravy is for.

title: Potent Fresh Cherry Flavor

text: Made as recommended, it seemed to stay watery with the oats not absorbing the fluid very well, and they seemed downright tough. It reminded me of the type of oats I'd see fed to horses when I was a kid, just sort of harsh looking. I guess that means the product is high in fiber. I don't want mushy oatmeal, but tough oat flakes in murky water with inspid apple flavoring isn't really the kind of breakfast I look forward to.

title: Not bad for bottled juice
text: The convenience factor and affordability were nice with this product. I enjoyed the flavor. FYI I always dilute fruit juice pretty heavily with water, it's otherwise just too sweet and intense for me. This particular one didn't dilute that effectively in terms of keeping the flavor from going bland, but still I feel better drinking diluted juice; easier for me than drinking plain water. I felt good drinking this juice.

title: Delicious; nicely balanced complex flavors for mass produced American chocolate
text: We all know that most mass produced American chocolate is garbage, but this was pretty good. The flavor combination had some complexity, such as the bitterness of the darker chocolate playing off the sweet minty crunch of the candy bits. Texture qualities are also pretty good. In my opinion, these need to be chilled for best effect. One piece is pretty satisfying, so that's nice for portion control.

title: Okay, I guess I'm spoiled by homemade
text:
All these pre-made products are disappointing to me honestly, because I've been a long-time homemade soup maker and (finally!) mastered the art.

But there are issues with home made including storing it all once you make it! I have been hunting for a really good convenient pre-made option.

This beef one is better than the same brand's chicken option by far. But still it's basically meh. If you are going to doctor it up, like adding medicinal herbs as I do, then it gets better. But overall it just seems not very nutritionally worth it, based on the flavor. I mean, our tastebuds and sense of smell are designed to detect nutritional qualities of our food, and this doesn't have that effect.

I guess it depends on what you want it for, and whether you have kitchen and fridge space, as well as the budget and skills, to make your own. There's a real learning curve to making different stocks etc. properly, because you tend to think certain steps aren't necessary (like pre-roasting the bones, and cooking the stock over low heat for a minimum of 3 days). So considering that hassle, this could be easier for your needs but may disappoint.

title: A rather uninteresting product
text: To me, this lacks much flavor when I expected more, based on past ramen experiences, both fancy restaurant style or cheapo packages. Also the flavor just seems "wrong" somehow. Crushed they make a nice topping as well, or added to something like scrambled eggs. I do think they offer a somewhat different option to more typical types of croutons, and I like having both types in my pantry, as these lean a bit more to the sweeter side than typical savory croutons, so you can use them in different ways.

title: Surprisingly good
text:

I was surprised at the nice, soft, fresh tasting rice. The rice kernels are whole and don't clump together. I do add about 1 Tablespoon of water into the packet before I microwave it, because I want very soft rice. That works great for me microwaving for 90 seconds.

title: Good but potent
text: I was a bit surprised at how good these are. However, they are quite potent, and for me, I believe they greatly benefit from the addition of some whipped cream. That makes them quite delicious. There is a lot of nice, fresh lemon flavor in this pudding.

title: Delicious and thirst quenching in convenient small but sturdy bottles
text:
This apple juice has a nice, strong, classic sweet apple juice flavor that is thirst quenching.

The small bottle fits in the can rack in my mini-fridge.

Also, these small bottles are not flimsy like a lot of beverages. They are nice and sturdy, and aren't going to flex and crumple on you. I would not be worried about carrying one even in my purse. If you had a use for them, I believe they would recycle well for various uses at home or for an art studio etc.

title: Chips in small bags seem to stay unbroken better
text:
I don't eat chips often, so the small bags are a good choice for me.

I've noticed too that the chips in the small bags are in better condition (less broken chips) than the ones in the large bags. If you are tired of buying a large bag of chips that is half or more broken bits, you might want to try these. These particular ones are 1-1/2 ounces, but the 1-ounce bags also have mostly whole chips in them.

title: Frontier is the place to buy fresh bulk herbs and spices
text: This company is really reliable as well as being ethical. The rosemary I received is excellent on all points.

title: Convenient and good quality
text: I was surprised at the quality of this product. It has a real, freshly cooked, nice bacon taste and texture. The pieces are well sized without being too large or small overall. It looks like bacon, smells like bacon, and tastes like bacon. Unopened bags do not require refrigeration; an open bag should be refrigerated, but the package is small so easy to stash in the fridge. Even so, there is a generous quantity of bacon. Because the bacon pieces are well flavored, you don't need much to use as a seasoning or added touch to your dish.

title: Tastes like sink water that washed a dish a chicken was cooked in
text:
Okay I've actually never tasted sink water used to wash a dish that a chicken was cooked in. But I'm pretty sure this product comes close to that.

It is really awful. It is, without a doubt, the worst thing I've consumed in years. I'm just warning you....

It is watery, extremely bland, and doesn't come close to resembling any stock or broth I've ever had, home made or store bought. It's so bad that I have doubts that it is even bone broth. I have made bone broth and I can't imagine what it would take to remove the distinctive body and flavor of bone broth to result in this product's disappointing characteristics.

title: Excellent protein snack that's filling and easy to eat
text: Convenient, easy, filling, and everything works well together between the salmon salad and the crackers; or you can use the salmon salad on bread and save the crackers for something else. Tastes fresh, you feel healthy after eating, a great late night snack for protein cravings. Very good with some nice olives on the side.

title: Okay but I think it's too thick for this format

title: Okay but flavors don't really gel well
text: This cereal just doesn't quite mesh. It's not horrible but between the flavors and the slightly over-hard texture, I just wasn't into it enough to want to buy it again.

title: Seems dumbed down and most of the time the can is dented
text:
Initially I was happy with the cookies and felt they made a great staple to keep around the house. I did find that more times than not the cans arrived dented with some broken cookies inside. I kept telling myself, that is just a fluke and won't be the norm. But it has been the norm frankly.

The tin I just got was once again dented with a lot of broken cookies, and I mean crumbled not just snapped in half etc.

I didn't even bother trying to refund this time, I simply don't plan to continue buying this product.

Something has changed, and I suspect that's part of the reason the tins all all now arriving dented; they dumbed down the tin quality for one thing; and the cookies are different, which is probably why a lot of them now arrive broken.

The cookies look different, have a different texture, smell different, and taste different. You can see they look flatter, more spread out during the baking process, and even the bottoms of the cookies are an entirely new and different shade from where they contacted the baking pan.

My initial impression is that the flavor has taken on that cheapo corn syrupy flavor, lowered quality flavorings and flour etc. even though the ingredients list still reads the same. I read some reviews that stated they believed some of these products are made in China but my tin didn't state this.

Yet another classic product that has been dumbed down to the point where I doubt most people are going to want to keep buying them for much longer. Old fans will recall what they are missing, and new potential customers likely aren't going to be that interested in "granny cookie" products like this.

title: Excellent staple product to keep on hand
text: I use a lot of milk and due to various health issues, I may not be able to make it to the store all the time when needed. This product enables me to reliably have good quality milk on hand. It is very easy to mix, tastes good cold, room temp, or hot, and you get a generously sized container that keeps well.

title: Fun and good variety; small bags keep things fresh

title: Not sure how you can ruin grits but these aren't very good

title: My preferred mass market tuna option

This one so far has held up to be passably good although I will say over time it seems like it is very slowly dropping quality, less actual fish quantity in the cans, etc. Eh, these food companies just are going to try that no matter what. When it gets lame enough I'll move on to something else. But for now this works for me as a budget option to keep tuna on hand for occasional use. I grew up eating a lot of fresh Pacific seafood including yellowtail so I happen to like this type. The quantity is generous for several sandwiches and it gets the job done.

title: Just somehow doesn't come together
text: Not sure really what the flaw is, but these just aren't that great. The textures aren't that great and don't mesh well. The flavors aren't that great and also don't mesh well. They aren't horrible and I bet children would enjoy them in their lunches etc., but for adults I think a bit disappointing.

title: Tasty and convenient but a bit sloshy in the making
text: Nothing's perfect. Yes, trying to remove the metal lid to nuke this is going to result in spillage which is annoying. After that though it's okay, and the soup itself is delicious and makes you feel pretty good when you consume it, so I believe it is healthy.

title: Weird gritty texture and unblended flavors that don't gel properly
text: This type of soup, when made from scratch, is utterly smooth and has a perfectly blended complexity of flavors even for the simplicity of it's overall character. So this product is a real let-down by comparison. The texture is sort of gritty, and the flavors don't mesh. It's off-putting to eat it, frankly, if you are accustomed to and expecting a more traditional soup of this type.

title: Not the worse cheap coffee but for desperate budget shoppers mainly
text: Going from coffee perfection years to a place where I have to struggle to find something drinkable that I can afford is depressing. I don't do fast food generally but a while back a relative wanted to go to McDonald's a few times and I was with him so tried the coffee. It was surprisingly good. I hear that this product now is not that same coffee and it didn't taste the same to me, but it's definitely not the worst cheap coffee I've been subjected to either. I wouldn't buy it again if I can get one of the other few cheap ones that I think are better, but this is on my list as an option when there isn't much else. I do add a LOT of cinnamon to my coffee press both for flavor and health benefits, and I also use a lot of milk in my coffee, so that of course enters into the equation. If you drink it straight, I'm not sure this will be right for you.

title: A masterpiece that isn't that bad ingredient wise for junk food
text: These are light, crispy little rings that aren't too hard or crunchy, with a pronounced but not overbearing onion flavoring. The ingredients list is not really at all scary and is quite short compared to many junk food type items; it's basically corn meal and onion flavoring. They stay very fresh in these individual serving sized bags. Due to the flavoring, these make a great side to a lot of different dishes, as well as being a nice solo snack. Also I like that they are savory without seeming to be overly salty like many chips can be. They also make great croutons for things like soup, salad, and chili, or even try them crumbled on scrambled eggs, hash, and other things. A surprisingly versatile little snack product.

title: I admit I am surprised at how good these are
text: Yes they are junk food, but they are not-very-seemingly-junky-junk-food. I was truly surprised actually at how nicely balanced these are in the cheese-to-cracker ratio. They have a great texture with a light crispy flaky cracker and a well done canned cheese sort of filling with a decent sharp cheese bite that isn't too over-bearing but neither is it wimpy and difficult to detect. One packet is filling, and for late night protein snack type cravings these are pretty good.

title: Absolutely delicious, healthy, nutritious, and good for ahem regularity
text: Having trouble finding affordable dried fruit (when did THAT become an issue?) I gave up and decided hey, these are dried fruit, I'll get them, they were actually cheaper than buying plain dried fruit. I wanted this combo with dried cherries and dates both for nutritional purposes and hoping it would help with regularity. These are absolutely delicious, very filling with half a bar being typically plenty, and they work great for the regularity issue as well. The almond bits add a nice texture and flavor. Very appealing soft texture, I would say these reminded me a bit of classic Turkish Delight type candies but with a softer quality and of course much more fruity flavor. The fruit flavor seems quite fresh and the cherry flavor definitely predominates in an excellent way. Very good product.

title: Nice basic to have on hand
text: Perrier in small cans that fit well in a mini-fridge and have a nice hint of flavor that isn't overwhelming, so you can add these to other things like juice, or just enjoy as-is. Great carbonation level. The can size offers a nice quantity, not too much or too little. Very refreshing and many people like them so your guests will probably be happy if offered one of these.

title: Might as well just drink some vinegar for a lot less expense
text: These are downright awful to the point of being inedible. The "flavor" is just plain vinegar. The "cheese" has no flavor and seems devoted to disintegrating as rapidly as possible into the jar liquid. The olives themselves have no flavor, and somehow achieve a weird interaction of being both too squishy/mushy and too hard in parts. I have to say after trying several Mario products, they all completely suck, seriously so. I would stay away. I also bought the feta option and, as with this one, the lids are so barely able to be screwed securely that the feta one arrived opened and drained all over the shipping packaging. The jars for these are terribly designed.

title: Not what I remember
text: I bought this as a sort of backup quick meal option for when I am not feeling well. I remember this being a good product with a nice, real soup type flavor and texture. However, this is pretty nasty to be honest. The texture is downright weird; the barley texture and flavor is also weird and seems sort of hard and just off, and the "meat" and other flavors seem very chemically and fake. I will stash this for emergency use but I was quite disappointed.

title: Excellent combo that others will eat before you get any of them....
text: I thought this was a perfect mix with a suitable variety for someone like me who doesn't eat a lot of these kinds of foods but it's nice to have small bags that stay fresh with this variety of options on hand. The problem is that others in your household are going to scarf them all before you do. I recommend you hide some of them for when you want them.

title: Fine for what it is
text: These are of course little bags of mass market produced junk food, so taking that into consideration, these are great for what they are. The combination here is good, the quality and freshness were good, and the package sizing is good. I think if you don't eat a lot of chips buying these smaller packages is the way to go, since each package stays much fresher than if you open a larger bag and try to store it. I also found that the unbroken chip ratio seemed much better in these smaller packages than in the larger ones.

title: Milanos used to be awesome but now aren't even worth bothering with
text: Milanos used to be THE mass market cookie that everyone adored, and for good reason. Over time though they have continually dumbed down this product until it is just plain depressing to eat them now. They taste just of corn syrup and bland flour and where they used to have a very thick double layer of the flavored icings in the center, now it is a stingy scraping which not only ruins the taste but the formerly great textural appeal of this cookie. No point really in wasting your time or money on these.

title: Consistent reliable quality and flavor
text: These are great for refreshing real fruit juice and sparkling water beverage use. The size is great for me as I am stuck with a mini-fridge at the moment, but I think the quantity per can is good; I can have two cans if I want, or just one. The flavors are always great, there is no flavor of Izze that I haven't liked, and the carbonation level is appealingly strong as well. Also a popular favorite so your guests will probably be happy if they come over and you can offer them these.

title: Seem a tad on the raw side
text: If you want raw nuts that's cool. If you want roasted nuts, you don't want them to have a sort of raw taste. These don't seem properly cooked to me, and that is kind of off-putting and disappointing when you are after that nice roasty flavor and crispiness. They're okay and not horrible, but I will probably further roast the remainder myself.

title: Fun junk food that tastes food for what it is
text: The entertainment factor in the giant tub is part of the charm of this product, but the cheese balls do have a nice flavor that seems a bit more complex to me than some of the other similar products, and also the texture of these seems a bit lighter and more appealing. You will have cheese balls for a long, long time, and they do seem to hold up okay; I live in humid conditions and they hold up okay in that container. After you finish the cheese balls, you are left with a giant plastic jar with a nice lid for various other useful purposes around the house, so you are being a tree-hugging recycling responsible person there as well for eating cheese balls. Feel good about it.  :)

title: I buy these for my cat....
text: and I wish I had thought of training my cats to eat this stuff years ago. When you have a sick cat, getting them to eat anything is a major hassle. This product (or the chicken or beef version) are just plain meat and works great for sick cats. I however typically use it daily to conceal my cat's medication. It works great for that; the cat considered it a treat. The little jars are easy to re-close and stash in the fridge, and when empty these make good little glass jars to hang onto at home for various other uses. It's gotten hard to find good glass jars used for products that are worth keeping at home and I think a lot of us want to get away from using plastic-everything especially for storing our food, spices, vitamins and etc. This product is I believe probably a lot healthier, cleaner, and cheaper than other products marketed for cats to be used to help them to eat medications. As long as one's cat is eating a properly prepared/balanced cat food of some type as the main food, you don't have to be concerned about the cat not getting certain critical nutrients. But if the cat isn't eating at all, this will ensure that the cat can stomach something that is safe and nutritious and easy to eat with enough calories to get by on. FYI if that situation presents itself, it often helps to either hold the dish while the cat eats or even hand feed it on your finger; for some reason that will make a sick cat eat when it won't otherwise just eat from the dish itself.

title: Really surprisingly good; filling; and versatile
text: You'd think this would be nasty but it's quite good for a protein type snack when you want something that is convenient. The chicken salad and the crackers taste good and fresh, and they function well together with the crackers being sturdy enough for the job without being too hard, crumbly, or breaking into weird bits as you try to eat the snack. The chicken salad quantity is plenty to put a generous amount on each cracker. One of the things I like about this thing is that I can just use the can of chicken salad to whip up a quick basic sandwich on bread, and save the crackers for something else another time.  It looks small but this is a very filling, satisfying snack meal, and definitely satisfies protein cravings. Great portability or for stashing in a desk etc. at work. Easy to open and use with the included nano-spoon. Not messy if you are reasonably careful.

title: Mainly giving this to my cat for pain relief
text: I'm not a turmeric-ologist but as far as I know, this product seems great. Affordable, well and properly ground to a useful powdery consistency, seems strong and definitely stains stuff if given the chance which means it's probably not adulterated etc. Container is convenient and generous size with nicely designed basic functional lid with a side for shaking and a side for measuring out etc. All good.

title: Very pleased; basic mayo flavor that doesn't make me feel sorta sick like most store brands do
text: I'd given up on standard mayo because all of them seemed to make me feel a bit sick when I'd eat them, even though I don't use mayo frequently at all. But for a couple of things, like yer classic tuna sandwich, I do like to use mayo. I also am currently relying on just a mini fridge, so my condiment space allotment is severely curtailed and I need only tiny-ish containers. I decided to try this brand as it came in a reasonably small and functionally designed container, had what sounded like a good ingredient profile, and I could store one of the two out of the mini-fridge until needed. So far, I am completely happy with this product. It has the basic mayo flavor I like for general use purposes, the texture etc. is excellent, not overly runny or gummy, blends well, and best of all it doesn't make me feel lodgy or sick when I eat it. The container functions perfectly as well with no splattering, and releasing a nice, even flow when squeezed, without then leaving a residue mess on the dispenser area of the lid. Just everything is right for a nice basic condiment you can rely upon.

title: Excellent peanut butter alternative
text: This product comes either plain, or sweetened with a little sugar. They are both great, but I prefer the unsweetened. Not only am I sensitive to legumes and want to avoid peanut butter for that reason, but I also am just plain tired of finding peanut-butter-flavored EVERYTHING EVERYWHERE. Almond butter is okay although some of those don't seem well prepared and make me feel a bit icky. However, this sunflower butter has been consistently awesome. It is delicious, very easy to use (it sort of separates a little but not really a hassle to stir it up, unlike natural peanut butters, that require some serious effort to remix in the oils). This product is runnier than a typical peanut butter, but I haven't found it to be a problem in any way, it doesn't end up dripping out of the sandwich or anything like that. It tastes great with various preserves (I particularly like it with ginger marmalade) and just by itself, and is good so far on every kind of bread I've tried it with. It would also make a great cooking ingredient although I haven't been using it for that, just for snacks. Compared to some peanut butters it is pricier, but I find it lasts a long time (I don't eat it frequently) and I feel the more interesting, pleasant taste and how I feel when I eat this product are definitely worth it.

title: Excellent basic veg juice to keep on hand
text: This type of product was entirely off my radar until I had emergency surgery and was on a fluid diet. The hospital started giving me these veg juices, and I was really surprised at how appealing they were and how good I felt consuming them.  Since I have continuing issues with fibrous foods making the consumption of many vegetables difficult, I decided to start adding these to my diet to help counterbalance that problem. These are a perfect size, and you can have them straight, diluted, hot, cold, doctored with herbs or whatever into a sort of soup; they are extremely versatile. My understanding is that they are predominantly tomato juice made from fully ripened specially grown tomatoes right at the source where this product is made, which I think you can taste; and the rest is a mixture of other vegetables. They appear to offer a lot of good nutrition in a small quantity, and are very low in calories. Easy to carry too nor does a can take up much desk "real estate". On top of that they are affordable and seem to hold up well in storage. Overall I think this is a great product.

title: Not worth consuming unless desperate. Really desperate.
text: It's been ages since I bought this kind of product and I thought it might be good to have on hand for quick doctoring of stuff like omelets or hot dogs etc. I felt that this was essentially downright obnoxious tasting. Very runny, very fake/chemically/artificial tasting, badly spiced/seasoned such that the flavors don't come together really as "chili" should. Really I would recommend you avoid this. I put it in my emergency stash and hope things never get that bad.

title: Great I wish they weren't so expensive and over-packaged
text: Due to extremely limited fridge and kitchen space I tried this product to help add some nutritional variety to my diet. I like these a lot, they are great basic daily use type green olives, and the packaging does make things very easy; they are not "dry" but they aren't doused in fluid, so you can just open and dump the little packet onto your plate or salad etc. no problem. The quantity per serving seems exactly perfect for me. If you wanted more you could have two packets, no big deal. Packets are very well made so great for travel, I think it would take a lot of abuse to make one of these burst and even then there really is no fluid to leak out, and the olives aren't going to spoil, as they are pickled/marinated, even if they did end up exposed for a while. Just truthfully there is a guilt factor in both the over-packaging and price for these, for just using at home, even though I have had legit reasons for it. But I would say these are a great option for certain applications. Far better than the awful Mario brand products, none of which have been any good so far as I have tried.

title: On the oily runny side but pretty good
text: This has a good flavor for being pre-fab bruschetta/tapenade type topping. It's not mind-blowing but makes a nice basic to have around for various doctoring of other stuff. There is a pretty good amount of mushrooms in the mix but note it is on the oily, runny side. Flavor is definitely "mushroom" and not "mushroom and Parmesan" or "mushroom and garlic" etc., which I think is a good thing. It doesn't taste totally bland but I like being able to alter it to suit my needs of the moment.

title: Rather bland and too sweet at the same time
text: Chex cereals are known for being sort of neutral but still with a good bland flavor suitable for when you want a mild meal easy on the stomach, or to add fruit etc. to.  This combo however just didn't gel for me. The honey-nut flavoring was not really noticeable, the main effect was just being a bit overly sweet. I wouldn't buy them again. I've tried other honey-nut flavored cereals that were much tastier. I will say these did hold up for a long time in milk, but if they don't taste very appealing, so what?

title: Fantastic but maybe not if you aren't use to the hint of muskiness in prickly pear
text:
It's refreshing and satisfying, sweet but on the light side.

I just want to note that prickly pear juice combined with this orange does have a slight bitter-musky quality, really more in the aroma than the flavor.

While the beverage tastes nothing like mushrooms or melons, just as an example, many people like mushrooms and muskmelons like cantaloupes, which also tend to have a hint of muskiness. So if you like that quality in other plant foods, you would probably enjoy this.

I appreciate that the can lids are well covered with a foil cap. You might not realize it, but any products in the grocery store were subjected to exposure from manufacturing all the way to your shopping cart by things like rats and roaches. Many people don't think to wash off the tops of their cans but YOU SHOULD because these critters were quite likely running around on them at some point and, as you probably know, rats in particular leave urine trails as they go. Yep. So with this product, the tops are safely protected.

title: Cheaper for my bunged up cat than the $400 vet treatment
text:
My poor bunged up little kitty required over $400 vet treatment (that was basically just an enema, but with all the obligatory "tests" they always want to charge for). They even tried to get me to take her home before she went, encouraging me that she'd go in the car on the way home, as if that would have been a good thing for either of us....I'm getting a new vet, by the way....

When that didn't solve the problem, and having tried various solutions already, I went with what struck me as a dubious recommendation found on cat lady forums, and bought this baby food pumpkin product.

To my amazement, it not only works perfectly, but my cat likes it. I mix a small amount (don't measure as it doesn't seem to matter, but probably around 1/2 teaspoon?) with a little meat baby food like chicken (I use this to conceal her pain medication powder), and she eats it enthusiastically. No more issues for her being unable to "go", and her health otherwise seems great.

Is this product good for babies? I don't know. Probably.

title: It's real Ceylon species cinnamon, not the most potent but good
text:
I would buy this again no problem. The product is good, and the company is a well respected, reliable one. I mainly use it daily in my coffee both for flavor and health reasons (and it seems to be working wonderfully for that). Buying the absolutely finest (and most expensive) Ceylon cinnamon would be a waste for that kind of use; you want that for baked goods and the like.

This does seem a bit blander than Ceylon grown in the original regions etc., but that of course is how anything produced from plants is going to be. It will vary based on location, annual environmental conditions, etc., just like wine. But that's not to say this is bad at all. It's very good especially for the price because in reality, buying the best quality real cinnamon is going to be expensive, just like other plant products such as the best coffee or teas. There are levels of affordability related to the quality levels of all these kinds of products. Due to global demand, it can be difficult to get this level of popular plant foods at all even if you have the money anyway. I've had that problem with obtaining decent coffee once everyone became faddish about drinking coffee. They can only grow so much of the prime stuff, it gets snapped up rapidly. I'm therefore grateful when businesses come up with ways for me to get good quality products at an affordable price by branching out with techniques such as developing alternate growing regions.

This is classic cinnamon, which is quite a different flavor than cassia bark. This is the type that you'd possibly most recognize from European style baked treats. It has a more complex flavor and aroma than the simpler, harsher, hotter cassia bark. That can be good too, depending on what you are using it for. But they are definitely quite different. FYI for health purposes, the Ceylon species is considered much safer than the cassia bark. Unlikely to be an issue with normal levels used to spice foods, but if you are taking a lot, apparently the cassia bark contains some deleterious substances.

title: Plump, well flavored, generous bag of traditional buttermints
text:
I would definitely buy these again, although the bag is huge so it could be a while before I need more.

These have a nice sort of generous rounded shape with no pointy corners like some buttermints have. Flavor is excellent, fresh, authentic, with a nice strong mint hit.

I find that a few of these settles an upset stomach very well; that's a good sign that the peppermint oil used in these is of good quality and generously included. Medicinal candy, yay!

I keep these in a sealed glass container and so far they have stayed fresh. They aren't smooshy or too soft although of course they start to melt in your mouth as you eat them. Very nice texture.

The sweetness is classic, but not overdone, with a notable but subtle butter hint that lets the nice fresh mint flavor play center stage. A simple candy that is much more than the sum of its parts.

title: Taste Great and Stomach Soothing
text:
I tried these mainly due to GI health issues I've been suffering from. I wanted something with a good kick of ginger that was otherwise sort of simple, like a graham cracker that was spiced up. These are awesome. They taste great in a way that is just plain classical, and have a lovely very light, thin, crispy but delicate but somehow homey texture all rolled into one. The spice flavors are nicely potent without being like a bomb on the tongue. Not overly sweetened. For as thin as they are, they ship very well, I've only ever had less than 5 broken cookies in an entire shipment of 12 boxes, and those were just snapped in half, nothing serious.

You get a lot in each box, but the box is still compact and easy to store or stash in your office desk or car etc. Inside the box the cookies are wrapped in a cellophane like cylinder and you open that by pulling the red strip around one end. Probably best to transfer to another airtight container after opening to keep them crispy and fresh. I have a desk bento box I use for snacks like this; works great.

Besides just being great for their tastiness as a cookie (and I think these would also be awesome baking ingredients for things like pie crusts and fruit crisp crumbs etc.), they really are nice and soothing for tummy discomfort. Definitely better than graham crackers or saltines.

I think they taste great with many different types of beverages, which makes them even more adaptable. Milk, coffee, regular or herb teas, sparkling waters, and juices etc.; I haven't found something yet they don't taste good with.

Finally, the ingredients list is definitely sane and really does contain the helpful digestive spices.

title: Astonished how good these are; good option for calorie counters
text:
Honestly I sort of hate mass produced American chocolate. It doesn't taste like chocolate to me and has some rather unpleasant/weird hints and elements. I decided to try these Brownie M&Ms because they were offered at a deep discount, I was sick and not wanting to try to go to the store myself, and I figured they could withstand the heat during shipping (which they did perfectly). Boy have I been surprised at how great these are as an option to have some chocolate around the house that you won't over-eat and that will hold up in your pantry or fridge well.

First, these are a bit larger than a typical M&M; they are round shaped and probably about the same size as the peanut versions? Maybe even a bit larger than those. Inside each does appear to contain a genuine chunk of a brownie. A very tasty, rich, and normal tasting brownie. These are so nicely chocolately and satisfying that I, a chocoholic, find that eating JUST ONE often genuinely cures my chocolate craving. I rarely eat more than 3; at most I've had 5 in one sitting and that makes me feel over-satiated. I know it's hard to believe. As a chocoholic I can't believe it, but it's true (for me anyway).

These are so good, so effective at handling chocolate cravings with a minimum of hassle, and doing so with minimal calorie investment, that I really do recommend them if you like brownies and maybe are looking to cut back on your chocolate intake without feeling like you are being deprived.

title: A new favorite; different and yet comforting classic vibe
text: These are something I think you have to try to understand just how great they really are. They have a rather magical combination of elements. Richly chocolate but still light...thin and crispy but not hard or unpleasant in texture at all...simple but rather sophisticated. They come in cardboard tubes containing plastic tray sleeves which keeps the cookies in good shape. You get a lot in each tin and, because they are flavorful and texturally appealing and interesting, with the genius touch of crunchy sugar on top, they are satisfying so you don't over-eat them.

title: Delicious and makes me feel good
text: I'm an agua jamaica fan so hibiscus teas are of particular interest to me. I wasn't sure what to expect with this one but I wanted to try adding tulsi to my diet. This tea is delicious; to me it tastes very much like a classic agua jamaica (unsweetened of course; you sweeten it yourself as desired), and has a very nicely balanced flavor overall. I appreciated that as so many tea blends anymore are just mishmash concoctions that don't actually taste good but I guess include marketable ingredients or whatever. Anyway, this has that nice floral/fruity refreshing quality from the hibiscus and the tulsi seems to add a very nice touch. The quality of the product and packaging etc. is all good and seems authentically treehuggy.

title: Meh
text:
I'm surprised that these weren't more appealing, as the idea sounds reasonable.

Something about the texture combination seems off, and didn't like that, more so than disliking the flavor. The texture is softish overall, but with just a couple peanut halves here and there. I believe these would be better with no peanuts, or possibly a lot more peanuts. Also, the peanuts were really hard, so it was rather like finding little pebbles in the candy. The peanuts didn't have any flavor either.

Otherwise, really, there are so many great candies one can buy, that these fall low on the list. While the flavor isn't bad, it's not great.

title: Worst instant gravy product I've tried
text: The container was only about 1/3 full, of grayish granules that resembled fish food.  While quick and easy to make, I wasn't fond of the gravy, a shellacked looking dark brown stuff with an odd flavor.  It reminded me of gravies I was subjected to in school cafeterias.  It doesn't taste horrible but, as one is hoping for gravy, the product disappoints, even taking into account that it is a packaged gravy mix.

title: Now I'm Depressed Because ....
text: I wish I could afford to hand these out for Halloween to all of the little trick-or-treaters....

title: The Best Candy Bar Ever Made
text: Still the best candy bar ever created.  Unlike so many others, it hasn't been dumbed down over time.  I can't believe so many people have never heard of these.  It's a little difficult to describe, but the closest I can get is to imagine a firmish chocolate mousse with teensy bits of almonds, covered in a thin layer of milk chocolate.  It's not hard, soft, chewy, or crunchy; it's fluffy, but not like marshmallow-fluffy.  Melts in your mouth, light, excellent flavor and texture.  Best if chilled; these will definitely melt in heat.  Bars are generously sized and rich, so one (or even one-half) is satisfying.

title: Low quality chocolate
text:
Strangely these larger bars don't taste as good as the smaller ones.

American chocolate has really been tanking over the past several years, I've noted especially with Hershey's products. Most of them are to the point where they don't even taste like actual chocolate. I think that might have been more noticeable here due to the thicker bar size with these.

title: Fit Torani bottles
text: I always keep a bottle of the Torani Peppermint and one of the Torani Vanilla syrups for coffee year round. And I keep extra pumps on hand in case one is damaged or just wears out. These pumps fit the bottles perfectly and seal completely.

title: Love the peppermint
text: This is a must have for me year round. I make a daily latte macchiato with my Dolce Gusto machine and add 2 pumps of the peppermint syrup to an oversized mug. It's sweet without being too sweet and the peppermint is strong and clear.

title: Perfect fall flavor, not too sweet
text: I love this syrup in a latte or cafe au lait. It's a classic pumpkin pie flavor, but it isn't overwhelming. I add two pumps and it's just sweet enough.

title: Surprisingly good
text: I really love this pumpkin pie syrup. It's thick, but still blends perfectly into a latte. The flavor is very much pumpkin pie and I don't get a weird aftertaste. There's no fake sweetener taste and this is soy free.

title: Stevia fake sweetener taste is strong
text: I'm not sure why they added Stevia to this mix since sugar is the first ingredient anyway. The end result winds up being as sweet as a soft drink or more so if you use less than 16 ounces of water to mix it. I much prefer Gatorade to this stuff at the end of the day. My friend tried this and she thought it was better than Gatorade, but she also thought the stevia left an undesirable aftertaste.

title: Mild coffee, rich flavor
text: I love my Dolce Gusto and the various coffees that go with it. My absolute favorite is the Vanilla Machiatto, but that's getting harder to find since Covid messed up the world. My backup is this simple latte. It has a mild flavor without any bitterness at all and the milk pod adds depth and richness. Mix in a bit of peppermint syrup and you've got something really special that no kcup can equal.

title: Good, but pricey
text:
None of the three blends were bad. All are good on pork or chicken, but they aren't outstanding by any means. Excellent seasoning is what turns dinner from ok to great.

Compared to Penzys or even Watkins spices, these are definitely twice the cost they should be based on the quality for similar sized containers.

title: Not great.
text: Meh. These give you a definite caffeine boost, but the flavor is off. It's almost like the drinks are too sweet and there's a fake sweetener type of aftertaste. Three of us tried these twice - I dislike them totally. The other 2 said the drinks are ok, but they wouldn't seek it out.

title: Fit the Torani bottles
text:
I always have a bottle of the Torani Peppermint syrup and one of the mocha in my office so I can offer guests a decent coffee experience at meetings. More than once the pumps that come with the syrups have broken or failed before the bottle was empty.

These pumps are a nice backup option. They fit the bottles correctly and pump smoothly without getting gunked up or sticky.

title: Almost as good as the Vanilla Latte
text: I like the Cafe Aulait better than I expected to considering it's just a single combo capsule rather a separate capsule for milk. The flavor is soft and no bitterness at all. The entire coffee is creamy, but not foamy like you get with the dual capsule flavors from the Dolce Gustos. I add a splash of peppermint syrup to this and it's pretty darn good - almost as good as my favorite Vanilla Latte Gusto flavor.

title: Excellent for a curry
text: This is good rice that cooks correctly in a rice cooker. I've paired it with a Japanese style curry and it was excellent in texture and flavor. We've also used it to make a quick Mexican style side dish and everyone liked it. I'll keep using this basmati.

title: Decent flavor, but pods leak
text: I thought I would try the generic Dolce Gusto pods for my office machine when offering coffee to guests or clients. Alas, while people like the flavor of this coffee, every single pod in the first box leaked. The second box was better, but almost half still leaked or brewed very, very slowly. These literally take twice as long to brew and fill a mug as the name brand pods. I'll stick to the original Dolce Gusto brand and flavors from now on.

title: Delicious bites
text: I love that each candy is individually wrapped and labeled! No more sample bites and waste to discover the pieces I don't like. The chocolate is fresh and rich tasting. The nut cluster pieces have big nuts and none were stale or too dry. We especially like the various pretzels and peanut butter. I've been able to share these with others due to the more sanitary wraps.

title: Jalapeno sauce is excellent
text:
We like heat on food, but it needs a clean flavor as well. The jalapeno sauce in this set is not terribly hot, but it adds a clean, strong flavor that both of us loved. I just mixed it in and cooked it with ground meat and diced potatoes for lunch burritos.

The other two sauces are quite good as well - we tried both with grilled pork chops and pork ribs. Everything had a slightly sweet, rich bbq taste. I'm surprised and happy - I'll definitely consider this brand again.

title: Fun, delicious flavors
text:
We aren't really nut eaters normally, but these flavors were intriguing. The peppermint is my favorite for sure. There's a definite mint taste and the almonds are fresh and the entire combination just works.

The gingerbread toffee is more toffee than ginger, but still a bit of spice comes through. All three bags were a hit. These aren't really meant for snacking on the go - not like the nut mixes in a hiking bag due to the chocolate. These are more like a desert option.

title: It's good, but not amazing
text:
Admittedly, we are not honey experts, but we are accustomed to local honey from desert hives. We don't eat the mass produced garbage at the box stores. Our honey is locally produced and tastes very light and airy.

This is much heavier and thicker than our usual stuff. This tastes fine, but it's not blowing us away. My husband says he prefers our local desert flower honey on pancakes and biscuits. I like this mixed in hot tea, but I don't love it.

title: Adds flavor, no real heat
text:
If you're a chili-head looking for a hit of heat, this isn't your salt. If you're just looking to add a hint of Sriracha flavor then this will work just fine.

The salt has a hint of heat and different taste and it adds a bit of a red chili color to food. I've used it in the water while boiling potatoes and that was very nice. The potatoes came out with a little flavor and were quite good in breakfast burritos.

title: Ok, but not great
text: This is ok and not bad at all. However, it's not as rich or thick as the Dolce Gusto cappuccino or vanilla latte. I end up adding milk to this.

title: Salt grinder broke 2nd use
text:
The salt is a course ground and is quite potent flavor wise - a little goes a long way. Unfortunately, the grinder failed and cracked after the second use. I have another grinder so we can continue to use the salt.

Kampot pepper corns are from Cambodia and the green ones have a fabulous, very distance taste. We were hooked after spending 2 weeks all over Cambodia. These are a different variety and while still good pepper, not quite what I expected.

title: Subtle flavor
text: This pepper is plenty "peppery", but has a lighter, more subtle flavor profile than ground black pepper. I use this with pork and chicken rather than beef or a heavy red sauce based meal. The pepper corns grind nicely in our hand grinder.

title: Expensive fast bread mix
text: I'm not thrilled. The mix is certainly easy enough to make - it's a fast bread. But the flavor is dull and bland. My husband liked it and ate a couple of sandwiches using this bread, but I much prefer my from scratch buttermilk bread. It's ok bread in the end, bit not something we would purchase.

title: Stale and full of soy
text:
I would never have expected a "small batch" maker to add soy to something as simple as cheese and Carmel popcorn. But they did and those who are soy allergic should avoid this as I had to.

Instead, my husband tried it. He said it was all stale and very dry. The expiration date on the bag was 43 days away, so perhaps they need better bags. He also felt that we have definitely had better flavor from other brands for the cheese, but the carmel was ok.

title: Nasty fake sweetener aftertaste
text:
There are several reasons to avoid these "cookies". The inclusion of erythritol is first for us. It leaves a distinct, sour, chemical type after taste that just stays and stays.

Second is the fact that there's only 2 miniature cookies to a serving and only 4 servings per bag. These are just stupidly overpriced for what you get.

We found the cookies dry and crumbly and barely sweet. Combined with that gross after taste makes these inedible in our house. Even my coworkers didn't like them when I sought additional opinions.

title: Soy free!
text:
This is really good on chicken and pork. I used it with basic chicken thighs on the grill and everything had a nice slightly smoky flavor and got a pretty chat color.

However, this shines on pork with jalapeno powder diced into tacos. We just marinated the diced pork in lime juice, added this and the jalapeno powder to the whole mess. Stir fried it and mixed with cilantro/lime rice. Excellent quick lunch.

title: Lighter flavor than some coffee
text:
I only drink the vanilla cappuccino for my Dolce Gusto machine, but my husband prefers regular old ground coffee.

He says this is nice. It has a solid flavor without any burnt or bitter sort of aftertaste. It blends well with milk also. The donut shop type of coffee tends to be milder and have a lighter overall flavor and this lives up to that.

title: Husband likes it
text:
I only drink the vanilla cappuccino for my Dolce Gusto machine, but my husband prefers regular old ground coffee.

He says this is nice. It has a solid flavor without any burnt or bitter sort of aftertaste. It blends well with milk also.

title: Super easy, tastes good
text: I love this rice  2 minutes in the microwave and it's ready to go. We use it for Frito Pie, as a quick side for enchiladas with refried beans, and with curry. The rice is tasty and fully done, but not mushy or lumpy. It also travels well in the RV.

title: Decent flavor
text: This is a little sweet, but not super sweet. In milk it tends to get soggy very fast, so not really a breakfast"cereal" type of granola. As a hand snack, it's fine. There's some crunch, but it's not like chips or little pebbles.

title: Nice flavor on chicken
text: This is a decent rub for grilling. It doesn't clump up or get gummy. The flavor doesn't overwhelm you with a fake smokiness that some other rubs use. It is a a teensy bit sweet compared to what we normally use, but that's fine for pork and chicken.

title: Add peppermint syrup for a kick
text:
I don't drink a lot of coffee, but I do love a peppermint cappuccino. Our Dolce Gusto machine makes the best coffee over all the other types we've tried.

My actual favorite is their vanilla macchiato, but it can be hard to come by this year. The cappuccino is a close second. It has a slightly nutty undertaste with no burnt bitterness. The milk tastes like milk and not like chemicals. I add 2 pumps of peppermint syrup and it's amazing in the mornings year round.

title: Soy free!! Great in sauces
text:
I use grated, jarred parmesan in my pasta sauce while it's simmering. It thickens the sauce and adds another flavor dimension....I imagine it would improve those bottled sauces as well if you're not making it from scratch.

I like this. It has a mild, non intrusive taste and worked well in my spaghetti sauce the other night. Just like the name brand. It was also good on pizza and in a salad. (We've been on an Italian theme for a week) . Most importantly, this is soy free so I can eat it without an allergic reaction.

title: Nice after dinner option
text: My favorite Dolce Gusto is the vanilla latte macchiato, but in the evenings, I don't need the added caffeine. I use the Lungo Decaf with fresh milk and two pumps of peppermint syrup as an after dinner coffee or late night treat. This coffee is smooth with almost no bitter or sharp taste.

title: Almost too sweet
text:
I like a little coffee in my hot milk and sugar, so I don't mind a sweet cup at all. I tend to add peppermint syrup to my cappuccino daily and thought a little chocolate would be nice too.

This syrup has a nice flavor, maybe a smidge to that bitterness of dark chocolate, but just a smidge. Alone or combined with the peppermint, this is a nice improvement over regular, plain coffee. However, I've found 3 pumps is way too sweet and two pumps is better no matter what size cup/mug I'm making. Once you get the balance right, this makes a pretty good peppermint mocha latte at home for a fraction of the coffee shop prices.

title: Yuck.
text:
Nope. I don't understand what this is actually supposed to be. It's not a hand snack unless you like eating dry, tasteless grit. It's not cereal with milk because it's still gritty and absolutely not sweet.

I expected a sort of Chocolate Rice Krispie type of breakfast cereal. This smells chocolatey, but is such a disappointment to actually eat. It's a shame because we have enjoyed the other foods from this brand like their Mac & Cheese and the breakfast scramble.

title: Nice overall flavor, but not hot
text: We tried this spice mix on both chicken and burgers. It's a nice flavor mix with a bit of tang to it and no one spice overwhelms. However, there's zero heat in this mix. If you're looking for hot, this isn't it. There's a hint of heat after a couple of bites, but that's all.

title: Full flavor and not too sweet
text: We really like this bbq sauce. Its sweet without being cloying and still has a bit of a twang. The flavor is milder than other bbq sauces so it doesn't overwhelm the food. We've tried it on chicken leg quarters and steak and burgers so far. Its been good with everything.

title: Solid peppermint flavor, soy free
text:
I absolutely love peppermint year round and especially in a cafe latte. What I don't like is paying six bucks each for a peppermint latte at coffee shops.

So I bought a Dolce Gusto machine and three varieties of their pods - the Latte Macchiato, Cappuccino and Vanilla Macchiato. This peppermint syrup is amazing in the vanilla macchiato. It blends perfectly and doesn't overwhelm the coffee flavors at all. It adds sweetness without needing additional sugar and the peppermint taste comes through in every sip. Most importantly, this syrup is soy free and hasn't caused me any allergic reactions.

title: No drips, pump action is smooth
text: These pumps fit our Torani syrup bottles exactly right. They don't drip either. I do three pumps of peppermint syrup in a latte almost every morning and the pump just works.  It doesn't stick or stutter and each serving is consistently the same size.

title: No complete allergy warnings! Contain SOY
text:
These are not labeled for food ALLERGY ingredients!!! Incredibly dangerous and illegal to not include the allergens in EACH flavor on each box. Look, I'm not a moron and as an adult, I'm fully capable of reading the entire ingredient list to be sure a food product won't kill me. My 8 year old niece doesn't always remember to read the full label or even comprehend some of the different verbiage used to identify a life threatening ingredient.

All three of the flavors - Peanut butter, chocolate chip, and lemon - include multiple forms of SOY. That's an Epipen episode if I'm lucky. However, these packages should all include the allergy ingredient listing as a separate line.

Using trendy phrases like "vegan butter" instead of saying soybean and corn oil is just not ok. It means a child could be at risk because how will she know what "vegan butter" is actually made of?

title: Mild flavor
text: I love the mild flavor of the Cool Blue Gatorade. Its not as salty or strong as the regular Gatorade and not too sweet. These 12 ounce bottles fit easily in a hiking pack or saddle bags while riding horses. The bottles are thick and sturdy so you can refill them with water multiple times and they don't bend or crackle.

title: Slightly bitter with an aftertaste. Almost no peppermint flavor
text: Meh. I'm at a loss as to why on Earth this powdered hot chocolate mix is nearly seventeen bucks a bag. I love peppermint and add peppermint syrup to my morning cappuccino daily and to hot tea. This cocoa has a very light, almost invisible peppermint flavor under the chocolate. The chocolate is ok, but definitely not great. My husband and I both noticed a distinct bitter flavor that leaves a sort of burnt aftertaste. This happened with water and when made with just real milk. We will keep looking for a truly excellent hot chocolate mix.

title: Hot, roasted flavor and delicious
text:
We love heat in our food, but it must be heat with actual flavor. I've tried some other brands recently, but the Fiesta Texas TNT is the best.

It adds serious heat and still has a subtle roasted flavor behind the heat. I boil diced potatoes, season them with this jalepeno powder and add them to breakfast burritos with sausage and egg - huge hit. This also works great in pork carne asada, tacos and just to improve plain old hamburger helper.

title: Fresh, crisp taste
text:
We are pepper lovers and a good ground black pepper is actually hard to find. We want the convenience of pre-ground pepper, but the taste of fresh pepper corns.

Watkins delivers on both taste and quality. It smells fresh and tart and a little bit livens up every dish instantly. It's worth the extra cost for great black pepper.

title: Way too sweet, sticky texture
text: Well, this was a potentially good idea that got lost in translation. Apple cake is something that can be awesome, unfortunately, this isn't. This is like a weird cross between bread and sponge cake, but it isn't either one. Its very soft and very chewy and very, very sticky to the touch and the palate. The apple taste is actually quite good and tastes natural to me. I found it to be much too sweet - 3 of us ate it and we all agreed it was like sugar over apples. Of the three of us, only one liked it enough to eat a second piece.

title: Carrot cake was devine
text:
This is definitely a box of good stuff. We liked almost everything in this collection. The only thing we agreed was bad, was the strawberry flavored marshmallow ball. It was way too sweet and left a fake, chemical type aftertaste.

The little Poti carrot cake was awesome. I would totally buy a box of just those if I could find them. Dense, soft, intense cinnamon smell and absolutely delicious. The bread sticks and pretzels were pretty good too.

title: Filling for a winter breakfast
text: We don't eat this often because of the high salt content,  but we do like it. You definitely need to pan fry it and get it fully crisp and dry before you eat it. We typically eat it with Texas toast pan fried in real butter. Not so healthy,  but fast, filling and delicious.  I usually find single cans for around a buck each at the local discount stores. It's very handy in the RV.

title: Mild flavor
text: I'm a Dr Pepper and water drinker normally. But I also work outside, year round with horses every day. Dr Pepper and water aren't enough to prevent dehydration in the West Texas deserts. So I supplement with Gatorade twice a day regardless of the weather. Most of the flavors are too strong for me, but the fruit punch is fine. It's mild and doesn't taste as salty as the original version. I can drink this warm or cool and there's no bite.

title: Staple item in our pantry
text: This powdered tea mix is really good. It has enough sugar to satisfy my husband's  Texas Sweet Tea addiction without adding more. We use clean  old Gatorade bottles  and 5 scoops of this powder to take hiking or just to drink at home. The bottles chill well and are easy to carry and seal. The tea tastes fine and has just a hint of lemon tartness.

title: Delicious,  zero bitterness
text: I love my Dolce Gusto machine and most of the different coffees for it. The vanilla  macchiato is by far the best. It has a light vanilla taste that smells great as it brews. I add some sugar and its better than any version from a chain shop. There is no aftertaste or bitterness whatsoever and each batch is smooth. I  try to keep the vanilla in our pantry at all times.

title: Handy in a hiking kit
text: We are beef jerky eaters and always keep some in our RV, cars and backpacks. This is plain jerky without any flavors added or spice. These are tiny, snack size bags - a single, small serving. The meat is chewy without being tough, but slightly bland. We definitely prefer the peppered version.

title: Nice texture,  not dry or mushy
text: We eat refried beans often around here and we've tried every brand we can get our hands on over the years. Our absolute favorite is the Rosarita Spicy with jalapeno. I bought the traditional instead of spicy by mistake, but these are almost as good. The texture is good - creamy with a few whole beans scattered throughout the can. One thing I like about Rosarita is the moisture level.  These aren't dry or mushy wet and they stay that way after cooking. I have been adding dry jalapeno powder to the traditional for that spicy kick we like and its been fine.

title: Great for cooking meats or even in a bread dough
text: OMG! Why haven't I discovered powdered jalapeno before??? So much easier than cutting my owner peppers. This stuff tastes great and definitely packs a bit of heat. We've used it on boiled potatoes for breakfast tacos, chicken on the grill, enchiladas and in a buttermilk/cheese/beer bread just knock it up a notch. My husband was sprinkling a dash on his popcorn last night. Honestly,  there's very little we Texans won't put some jalapeno or chili powder on.

title: Jumbled mess
text: My husband is a K-Cup drinker. As a rule, I avoid them all and only drink the cappuccino and vanilla latte from Dolce Gusto. I find kcups watery and flavorless. My husband doesn't care at all, as long as its hot, black and unflavored, he's happy. This variety box has several good blends and he has liked all of them. Our issue is they came in a jumbled box all loose. In these days of Covid, it seems like these would be prepped with more attention to contagion safety. I don't think we'll order this again.

title: Tasty, no dry or rubbery texture
text: We LOVE rice and eat it often with lots of stuff. I have a fancy rice cooker that does a great job, but sometimes you just want a quick meal without drama or extra effort. This microwaves in 2 minutes and its always consistent. No dry or rubbery clumps and every piece is edible. One package is enough for two people  - single serving each. The flavor is mild and doesn't interfere with other sauces you serve it with.

title: Soy allergy alert
text: Well, another basic product with unnecessary soy added. If you're allergic, as I am, you'll want to pass on this. My husband is drinking these instead. He says the flavor is what he expected from the Cafe Mocha label. There's a bit of a chalky aftertaste for him that he's not a fan of though. He does lije them enough to swig one down on the mornings he has no time for real food.

title: Nice overall flavor without being bitter
text: I like these caramel pods better than I thought I would. They are more a hint of caramel rather than an overwhelming amount like you get with the Dolce Gusto pods. The coffee itself is smooth and not bitter. I do detect a trace of a chemical type aftertaste, but my husband says he didn't get that at all.

title: Lots of price for rather little product
text:
Everyone in this house loved chili heat and we add peppers in dry, powdered, fresh or chili oil to almost every recipe. So were pretty excited to find honey habanero nuts.

For the most part, these are good. Nice mix of different nuts and some seeds. The flavor is definitely hot, you can taste that chili pepper. But....about a 1/4 of each bag had no seasoning. Plus, these are small bags and super pricey for what you get.

title: Tastes the same as regular salt to me
text: Personally,  i cannot taste any difference at all between pink salt and regular salt. My husband says he can tell the difference, but its nothing worth paying extra for pink salt. I sed this salt in a regular meal and everything tasted fine. The pepper here is finely ground and tastes exactly like any mass produced pepper  - a bit of heat, but nothing like the fresh ground pepper we make at home from four different types of peppercorns. This set will work nicely in the RV though.

title: Very strong with bitterness
text: My first impression of this coffee was "Bitter" and that hasn't changed after trying 3 cups. Its just really strong with a bitter undertone that i can't shake. My husband likes it ok, but its not his favorite coffee. He doesn't taste the bitterness as severely as I do, but he did say it's too strong without adding extra water.

title: Chewy casings
text:
We love jerky and meat sticks and always have some in the house, cars and hiking gear. These are different in good and bad ways when compared to the usual brands we buy. The overall texture is chewier and harder than we normally care for - if you have delicate dental work, these may not be a great choice.

The original sticks gave a good flavor with a hint of beefy smoke. The Hatch chili sticks were ok, but reminded us of those off brand canned chilis - it was just off a bit with no real heat. The one thing with both flavors is the casing. Its really chewy, almost rubbery and neither of us likes it. These aren't bad by any means, but they aren't our favorites.

title: Best refried beans in the grocery section
text: We only buy Rosarita refried beans in the spicy version. I typically stickup on them every time we're at the grocery store. They are reasonably smooth and cook very well in  Tex-Mex casserole as well as a simple side dish for taco night. These spread nicely for tostadas or nachos - not too thick or thin. The flavor has a bit of heat without overpowering the other foods.

title: Taste like pea in flavored coatings.  Pretty gross
text:
Literally four of four people here hated these pea snacks. Using the word "pork" is definitely misleading. These are a pea based vegetarian crisp snack in a rind like style. No reason to pretend these are something they are not.

All that aside, the taste is just awful. The nacho cheese flavor was weird with a chemical aftertaste. The plain ones were crisp and crunchy, but tasted like salted peas. The BBQ were awful. Like peas covered in bbq sauce type coating. Our neighbors tried these after both of us hated them- they both concur, these just taste like dry, crunchy peas with a bizarre aftertaste.

title: Stevia leaves a weird aftertaste
text:
I realize that this is supposed to be a healthy option for folks and the ingredients reflect that. Unfortunately, if something tastes bad, it doesn't matter how healthy it might be, folks won't drink it.

My husband refused to drink another after the first one. He said there's none of that chalkiness most other brands get. But....he got a chemical aftertaste - that's the Stevia weirdness. My 9 year old neice drank one and said it was ok, but it isn't sweet enough. She thought it would be like chocolate milk from the bottle.

title: Flavorful,  but no real heat
text: We eat salsa daily on everything from just dipping chips, to eggs and casseroles. These three salsas are nice for flavor without any real heat. I do appreciate that there's no junk ingredients like soy added. There's a distinct smokey flavor profile with the orange label bottle and the blue label, but not so much on the green salsa. None of them are hot, they add a hint of heat, but if you're  a "chili head" these will be too mild for you. They do cook up well in a quick casserole though.

title: Soy free and surprisingly good
text: As a rule,  I'm not a fan of Ruffles chips. However, I love lime and jalapeno, so I had to try these. I'm surprised by how much I like these chips. I can get the lime flavor after a couple of chips and the jalapeno is evident from the first bite. The heat builds a bit after eating several in a row. I finally found a chip better than plain cheetos. And SOY FREE!

title: Very salty. Soy allergen warning
text:
I am a fan of shelf stable foods for emergencies and camping in the West Texas desert mountains. I had high hopes for this Turkey Schwarma, but it's not for me.

First is the inclusion of soy - if, like me, you're allergic to soy, you'll need to avoid this meal. My husband are it instead. He microwaved it and it cooked/heated up just fine. His first impression was salt. He felt the texture of the turkey and the chickpeas was fine and the flavor under the salt was pretty good. But he only finished half of the meal because it was just so salty.

title: Nice garlic tones with a little heat
text: We like chili heat in everything from stir fry to spaghetti sauce. This garlic chili oil is interesting.  It has a good base flavor overall. The garlic is detectable and there's a slight heat kick a few seconds later. We like this with a quick pork fry up and rice. You don't need much of any other seasonings. If you want the red pepper flakes in the bottle,  you're better off using dried flakes because these never come out of the bottle.

title: Excellent pepper hit in every bite
text: Like all beef jerky, the Prevail is expensive. However, it is soy free and doesn't have any other junk added. The flavor is excellent in the spicy version. You get a definite peppery kick in every piece and it's a good , tasty pepper. Each piece in every bag was soft and chewable instead of being hard or like rubber. We scarfed all three bags on hikes in the Chisos Mountains last week and the jerky was perfect for that.

title: Very tasty, not greasy
text:
I took these on a couple of hikes in Big Bend National Park this week. They pack super easily in nooks and crannies of a backpack. The wrapper is easy to pull apart while walking.

I love that there's no gross grease with every bite. The sticks are soft and chewy, but not mushy. They have a clean taste with a spicy after kick that's really good. I'll buy these again in the future.

title: Taste great
text:
We love seasoned salts and this is a nice collection. The little jars are magnetic do they stick to the fridge and don't take up any cabinet space.

We've used these on steaks and pirk chops so far. Every one tasted great and cooked we'll both in a pan and on the grill.

title: Molasses and vinegar are predominant flavors
text: Meh. If you're just looking for heat and no nuances of flavor,  then definitely try this. It is certainly hotter than most grocery store offerings. For us though, this is bland and very vinegary. We've been eating homemade hot sauces from both sides of the Rio Grande all of our lives and we're accustomed to a flavor beyond just heat. The first impression is molasses followed by heat and vinegar.  That's it. No depth here. No distinction between jalapeno,  perri,  habanero or anything else, just that overwhelming vinegar.

title: Easy way to make dinner
text: I love these ready to eat rice varieties.  We like rice, but hate cooking it - even the rice cooker is a hassle when you just want a quick meal. These pop in the microwave in the bag and then onto the plate. Zero mess and no drama. The rice tastes fine and has a normal texture.  Add a pork chop, some asparagus and a little aujus from the chop pan and you're golden. Works well with curry too.

title: Interesting selections of snack size snacks,  but way over valued
text: This a cute gift box with a slight masculine tone. It comes in a plastic toy tool box, setting the theme. The snacks included are single serving or snack size and they are pretty basic. A chocolate Rice Krispie bar, a small can of nuts, Chex mix and some other odds and ends. The microwave poke rinds were pretty bad actually. They do include a screwdriver set that's useful.  However,  if I paid more than fifteen bucks for this, I would definitely feel cheated.

title: Excellent taste and soy free!
text:
I'm severely allergic to soy in all forms and this is the first jerky product I've found that is soy free and isn't rubbery.
