The flavor here is very good - I can taste the sesame oil and ginger and the red pepper is nice finish note to each bite. Mostly though, the pieces are chewy without being rubbery, dry and difficult to eat. This is way too pricey for us to keep as a regular item, but it's a good treat now and then.

title: Fresh, clean taste and texture
text: These are soft and chewy - not dry and hard like jerky. More like a Slim Jim stick, but without all the grease and extra salt. These are much bigger as well  so you get a real snack. The beef and beef with jalapeno are our favorites, though the pork sticks are pretty good too. I'm happy to take these with hiking in Big Bend National Park next week.  My only complaint is the current pricing of two bucks or so per stick...that's a deal breaker for me in the future.

title: Comfort food
text: Sometimes I just need a basic, simple, tasty curry and that is exactly what I get from the S&B Golden curry. I love the hot version and literally have at least one box of it in our pantry all the time. This is so easy to make and serve. I add baby carrots and potatoes with either boneless chicken or beef and serve over rice. It freezes was leftovers to be reheated in the microwave.

title: Salty, fatty goodness
text: Theres something about a roadtrip that compels me to eat Slim Jims. I keep them in the car on the road for snacking. There is nothing healthy or nutritious about Slim Jim sticks, don't kid yourself.  They are just fatty, greasy, salty meat sticks that taste good and go anywhere.  Sometimes,  life just requires junk food and these things are a good solution.

title: Tastes great
text: Sometimes you need something more than plain water, but not a sweet soft drink or tea. I love Cran-Grape for the tartness and just enough sweet to make it delicious.  Other brands are ok in a pinch, but Ocean Spray is always the best.

title: 4 of 7 dogs don't like these
text: Meh. We have seven dogs and they are all about treats.  These have a simple ingredient list without any items I find objectionable. However, 4 out 7 dogs here don't like these. They take them because they are polite dogs, but quietly drop the piece in another room. The 3 dogs who like them, eat them happily and appreciate the chewy factor.

title: Light kick and flavor boost to lots of recipes
text: We really like this chipotle chile and we've used it in several meals recently.  It adds a tiny kick with a smokey background that is really good on grilled chicken as part of a dry rub. I also used it in a simple Tex-Mex casserole and it was awesome. This is going to become a pantry staple seasoning around here.

title: Pepper tastes fine and salt is good too
text: Salt and pepper is just a mandatory staple. This set is fine. The salt tastes like normal salt and dissolves for cooking like it should.  The black pepper has a regular peppery bite, but its mild. The bottle lids close completely to keep air and humidity out - that's not always the case with spice bottles.

title: Great for chicken or pork dry rub
text: We are huge fans of paprika, chili powder and all types of pepper. This dry rub mix has all of those ingredients and no soy added. We used it on chicken leg quarters for the grill as a dry rub. Everything came out great and very tasty. I think we'll use it for pork ribs next time because the paprika brings a bit of smokey tang to the flavors.

title: Fruit Punch is good with no aftertaste
text: I've been sick for 2 weeks now and Gatorade has been a lifesaver for me. Its kept me hydrated and less miserable. The Fruit punch flavor is lighter than others and doesn't have any sort of weird aftertaste. I like it both cold and at room temperature.

title: Rich scent. No bitter after taste
text: This has a lovely, rich scent that invites you to drink it. The taste is nice and not bitter or overbearing. My husband likes it, but it's a budget killer for us on a regular basis.

title: Soy free and tastes good too
text: We typically don't buy ranch dressing because all the big brands use soybean oil and I don't want to die that way. This one has no soy! I did not have any allergic reactions at all. Yay!! It tastes like ranch should so we're happy.

title: Soy allergy alert. Salty
text: Soybean oil. Why??? There's just no reason to use soy in a soup. Since this has soy, I wasn't able to eat the chicken and rice recipe we used the soup in. My husband ate it and said he felt it was saltier than usual  - I don't add salt to casserole dishes because the cream soups are always loaded with it. The overall flavor was chicken and tasted fine to my husband.

title: Bottle caps bend and don't reattach fully every time
text: Ok....I'm not sure why anyone would spend something close to forty bucks for this water. The water tastes fine and completely neutral with zero after taste. The aluminum bottles are attractive and light weight, but the tops are not quite as reusable as they say. The tops twist off, but unlike plastic, these can bend and dent. Once they are bent, they do not reattach correctly. That means the bottle can leak if you refill them or even wash the bottle and cap for a future use.  Nice idea, but not really ready for the real world.

title: This made my husband physically ill in minutes. Avoid!
text:
Avoid, avoid, avoid! This stuff is wrong on several levels. First is the inclusion of chemical, fake sweeteners. Then the inclusion of soy for no reason. Third is the nasty, chemical flavor. And finally, the stomach upset after just a half bottle.

My husband tried this since the soy and fake sweeteners makes it off limits for me. I feel bad for asking him to drink it. He said the first swallow was gross with a chalky under current, but tried more anyway. He barely reached half a bottle before being fully grossed out. About 20 minutes later he had fast pains and threw up. We threw out the remaining 3 bottles.

title: Soybean allergy warning.
text: What a shame. This stuff has soybeans. Why? Its beef jerky. A top 8 allergen should not be a primary ingredient.  Since I can't eat it, my husband has been.  He says it tastes good, but several pieces in two bags so far, have been way too tough to actually eat. That's a lot of waste in a very small baggie. Especially at this price point - this stuff is a budget killer.

title: Crunchy without an overload of salt
text: This is a giant bag of chips. They are your basic corn chips and offer a solid crunch. The flavor is pretty good - sort of cross between plain Tositos and plain corn Santitos chips. These hold up well for dips and salsa and they aren't terribly salty.

title: Buttery,  crumbly and delicious  despite the soy added
text: I used to love Chicken in a Biskit crackers. They have that buttery flavor and slightly softer crack that is perfect with dips or bits of cheese. Unfortunately, these include soy and I can't eat them anymore. Why must everything use cheap soy? Since my allergy won't allow me to eat these, my husband is instead. He says the crackers are still good and still break apart at the slightest bump. He likes them with a tiny bit of ranch dip.

title: Nice middle ground quality for basic cooking
text: Red pepper is a staple in our home. We use it on everything  - spaghetti,  pizza, Tex-Mex, steaks, etc. There's a definite difference between high end red pepper, middle ground and low end pepper.  The cheap stuff tends to have lots of seeds and little heat. The good stuff smells great and hot when you open the bottle and has more flakes and few seeds. This is a decent middle ground option. It smells fresh and the flakes are not too big or so small that you need to use extra. Its not loaded with seeds and adds a nice flavor and heat to food.

title: Bland, hard and not real rice
text: Yeah....no. This is a rice like product, but not actually rice. Sort of like that almond "milk" nonsense....looks like milk, but is not at all actual milk. The Harvest Pilaf style tastes really bland and needing serious seasoning to be somewhat edible. The directions said add hot water for 12 minutes and that's just weird. Everything came out crunchy and nearly inedible - it definitely requires cooking instead of some instant noodle treatment.  We won't buy this in the future.

title: Contains soy. Salted almond bar had too much salt
text: Unfortunately, Toblerone is yet another company using soy in their candy. That means that I can't eat it due to a soy allergy. My husband and our house guest have been enjoying these instead. They both like the original, the white chocolate and the dark chocolate bars. But both said the salted almond was much too salty and left a slight, bitter after taste.

title: Soy allergen warning.
text: Holy Oreo Overload! My husband is ecstatic at having a huge stockpile of original Oreos. He loves these like a 4 year old loves Oreos. The cookies are the classic chocolate with cream filling and taste like they always have. My only complaint is they use of soy products.  With a soy allergy, I can't eat them at all.

title: Double stuffed. Contains soy
text: My husband is an Oreo nut. Unfortunately, because they use soy to make the cookies and an adult onset soy allergy, I can't even try one anymore. So he gets all the Oreos. These are very handy sealed, travel packs of double stuffed vanilla Oreos. He keeps them in the truck when he's on the road as a snack option. He really likes these, but feels the original chocolate cookies are the best.

title: Safe soy free snack. Tastes great
text: Soy free! Finally! A healthy and tasty snack that does not include soy of any kind.  The cranberries are chewy and sweet without being like candy.  The cashews aren't rock hard and have a hint of salt - delicious. The almonds outnumber the cashews and cranberries significantly though. I really like that these are packed in little individual packets so I can keep some in my car and the house. Love this trail mix.

title: A little bland, but not bad.
text: I love Indian food and will happily try anything once.  This was not great, but it wasn't terrible either.  It's a small serving - like a small TV dinner,  so you'll need to add a side of rice and maybe a veggie for a full meal.  The flavor Inca little bland for my palate, but there's some flavor. My biggest issue is the measurements are metric and you have to convert them to standard - to get it exactly.  If you're going to mass market a product in the US,  you need to make the effort to convert the directions.

title: Sucralose chemical,fake flavor is way too strong
text:
That gross, fake, chemical taste from fake sweeteners is all I can taste in these. It just overwhelms and nothing else is discernible. Sucralose. Of course. So I won't touch these again.

My husband drank two and said they are OK, but he prefers old school Ensure. He said these leave a thick, chalky aftertaste and weird sort of film on the tongue. The sucralose doesn't gross him out like it does me, but he agrees that simple, natural sugar would be far better.

title: Nice, smooth coffee with no bitterness
text: I am a light coffee drinker and typically best described as someone who likes a little coffee in my hot milk. My husband is a heavy duty coffee drinker and he tends to prefer dark, strong coffee straight up with no cream or sugar. The fact that we both like this Rosewood blend is surprising. It's not bitter or overwhelming. It has almost a creamy texture and taste without any bitter, strident aftertaste.

title: Husband likes this coffee
text: I'm not really a fan of the dark roast coffees unless it's New Orleans style with chicory added and that's what I hoped this would be. Unfortunately, it isn't and it's just too strong for me. My husband does like it and he doesn't get the same slightly bitter aftertaste that my palate detects.

title: Something for everyone and real, original M&Ms are always welcome
text: Full size M&Ms!! This box has a decent variety so there's something for everyone in our home. There are several of each candy, so no-one really felt shorted. I do think it needs fewer Skittles and more plain M&Ms, but that's just me. Actually, the Dove pieces could just be entirely deleted. Those are actually just four little bite size chunks in the package and they aren't great.

title: Husband really likes this - strong, but not bitter
text: I tend to prefer light blend coffee and my husband likes the dark roasted blends better. This coffee is a bit too much for me, but he really likes it. It's strong, but smooth. There's no bitter after taste and it does blend well with milk.

title: Thin, easily broken chocolate, oozy filling. Mixed opinions in our household
text:
Well out of four people here, only one of us really liked the Mocha Cream bars. One person said they are ok in the event nothing better is on offer. The other two refused to eat more than one square - I was in that group.

I had hoped to find these were along the same lines of the classic Ritter Sport with fillings. Alas, the quality is not equal and the flavor really falls short. The chocolate is very thin and breaks apart with the least pressure, allowing the filling to ooze out. The chocolate is less sweet than say...Hershey bars and two of the four of us liked that aspect, the other two didn't care for it.

The cream filling is supposed to taste like coffee and none of us detected that at all. It was nothing special. My sister says 1 star and I rate this candy at two stars at best. One gave it four and my husband says three stars. We all agreed that any pricing over a dollar a bar is excessive.

title: Adds a nice peppery background to steaks or chops
text:
The first thing I noticed when opening this bottle was the scent of ancho chili and garlic. Off to a great start. It's a course grind for all the ingredients so it really is noticable with every bite.

We coated bone in ribeye steaks and grilled them on an open fire. The seasoning stuck to the meat and seared in as the meat cooked. It was really excellent - every bite had a slight smokey, peppery flavor. No steak sauce needed. We also used this stuff on pan grilled pork chops with equally nice results.

title: Includes soy. Husband likes thm as well as original Oreos
text: My husband is like a 6 year old when it comes to cookies and especially Oreos. He would eat half a bag in one sitting if I let him. These single serve packs are a great compromise - he gets cookies in a more reasonable way and I pretend not to notice he's eaten two bags in a row. My one star deduction is for the unnecessary inclusion of soy that means I can't eat Oreos at all due to an allergy.

title: Peppermint is light, no bitterness.
text: I love peppermint n lots of circumstances, but especially in coffee. This is a very mild peppermint taste - it's definitely there, but softer than I really like. The coffee smells awesome as it's making. This is a light brew so it's not bitter or terribly strong and that's always good. I had to add sugar and a dash of peppermint flavored creamer to enhance the flavor for my tastes, but this is a good coffee.

title: Soy free! Tastes as good as the coffee shop
text:
I stumbled on the Peppermint Mocha in the grocery store the other day and I had to try it. The peppermint mocha from the coffee shops is delicious, but I am not interested in paying five bucks a cup.

This goes in the fridge and is added cold. I use it with our fancy-schmancy espresso machine and it is amazingly good. I add this cold to my cup first. Then do the steamed milk froth and the espresso double shot. Stir and drink - done over ice makes essentially a frappucino.

There's no weird chemical aftertaste and the Peppermint comes through loud and clear, but doesn't overwhelm. This is already sweet, so no need to add sugar at all.

title: Unsafe for dogs with certain health issues
text: Well, because of the cautions list, I cannot give this to two of our seven dogs. You can't use these with dogs taking prednisolone or who have a cardiac issue - like a heart murmur. The caution list wasn't visible when I chose this stuff or I wouldn't have. For the other dogs in our pack, they will eat these mushed up onto their food, but won't touch them otherwise. I'm just tossing the whole tub out.

title: Nice mix of flavors - the Cheese Nips are the best
text: My husband and I are terrible about snacking late night while caught up in a good book. Ritz crackers are a huge favorite of his and Cheese Nips are my weakness. These little packets are a nice way for us to have our favorites in a controlled serving size, but still feel satisfied. There are actually a lot of crackers in the pouches. They are fresh and have the expected crunch and flavor of the big boxes. I'll keep these in the pantry on a regular basis.

title: Surprisingly tasty pepper for processed, commercial pepper
text:
We're black pepper snobs. To the point of importing four different kinds of peppercorns that my husband mixes into his own proportional blend and grinds as needed. We don't buy canned, grocery store pepper because it has no flavor in comparison. I wasn't expecting anything different from this either.

I've used this pepper in a homemade stroganoff, grilled burgers and on pork chops with an au jus. There's a very nice, clean taste here and a little heat, but not much. This pepper is noticable and definitely better than grocery store stuff. It's a slightly course grind and that brings out the flavors. It's pretty good pepper.

title: Tastes like regular coffee to us
text: Honestly, I can't taste any difference between this coffee and the Starbucks regular old medium blend Kcups. It's ok coffee and there's no burnt taste with this. My husband says it's fine with a donut, but so are Maxwell House and Folgers Kcups.

title: Two of three people like these. Weird chemical aftertaste for me
text:
We have mixed results here for these creamer flavors. Three people in our house this week and we all tried each flavor multiple times - vanilla, hazelnut, and original. My house guest liked all three and especially the hazelnut. My husband felt like the original was a reasonable substitute for real milk in a pinch or when we're down at the ranch in the backcountry.

And then there's me....the oddball. I just did not like any of these. I get a very strong chemical type aftertaste. It reminds me of those nasty fake, chemical sweeteners. The hazelnut was the strongest one with this effect for me - no clue what the "artificial flavorings" actually are, but I can't tolerate them.

title: SOY ALLERGEN ALERT
text: I'm just disgusted and disappointed with this tea. It has added soy lecithin...WHY? What possible reason is there to add soy to tea? Since soy triggers an anaphylactic reaction for me, I can't make this tea, much less actually drink it. My husband tried a gallon of it and he said it tastes ok, but it's not as good as just plain sweet tea. He says he can't see ever making this instead of regular tea with the cold brew bags. You have to use boiling water for these....twice as long as cold brew bags.

title: Tastes like the coffee n the stores. Little bit bitter without milk
text:
We mostly use kcups or beans for the espresso machine, but my husband does like to brew a regular old school pot of coffee when we have company. This medium roast ground coffee is fine for a quick cup, but it's not a delicious concoction like fresh beans from the espresso machine - that's ok.

All three varieties taste more like a dark roast from any other coffee brand instead of a milder, medium roast. There's no burnt flavor, but definitely more bitter than we expected. I add milk and it evens out. Basically, this tastes like what we get from Starbucks when we're traveling.

title: Seems to take less than regular salt for seasoning
text: I try to use as little salt as possible when cooking, but salt is a must even when making bread. This is pretty potent compared to traditional table salt. I think it takes less of this than regular table salt for most things to achieve the same effect. I set our grinder to fine and it grinds nicely enough to use on the table as well as when cooking.

title: Sweet and just a little tart
text: I love the Cran-Grape. It's not quite as tart as the Cranberry alone or even the Cran-apple versions. These little bottles are exactly the right size first thing in the morning or in the heat of the afternoon. I'm trying to drink less Dr Pepper every day and these are the first satisfying substitute I've found.

title: Nice light flavor and no weird burned or bitter undertones
text: I'm not a coffee fanatic and I only drink it when I have time to make a cappuccino or latte in our big espresso machine. These beans smell delicious and fresh every time I open the bag. They grind correctly and I haven't noticed an oily residue in the cup. The flavor is light and doesn't overwhelm my taste buds- no residual bitterness or burnt flavor. It's good coffee

title: One cat says no and second cat likes it
text: Our cat really likes the Purina One True Instinct dry food so I assumed he would like this too. But because he's a cat, he has decided that this simply isn't for him. He ate a little of it on day one and refuses to even sniff it now. I'm not sure what his objection is. Meanwhile, I offered some to a feral cat we see in the woods sometimes and he ate it without drama.

title: Soy free! Dry, crumbly and not sweet enough
text: First impression.. these cookies need some real sugar as well as honey. They are just a little too unsweet and don't taste quite right. Each cookie is 110 calories and frankly, for that many calories, they ought to be sweeter like a regular snickerdoodle. The texture is dryer than regular cookies and crumbly, so you need a napkin for sure. I doubt we'll but these in the future, there are better options out there.

title: Decent coffee without a bitter after taste
text: There are several varieties of coffee in this box - a little something for almost everyone. The light roast is definitely my favorite and the coconut is a good option as well with sugar and milk. My husband prefers the dark roast and says it doesn't taste burned or over roasted to him. None of these have an oily residue or bitter flavor.

title: Lime is the strongest flavor. Nice on a high humidity day
text: As a rule, I normally don't like these flavored waters. I keep trying them, hoping for one I like and this Raspberry Lime came through. It's a light, fresh, crisp taste without too much carbonation. The raspberry is barely there and that's ok with me. Lime is the predominant flavor and I love lime any time, anywhere. These are too pricey to drink every day though so in this house, they are just a treat.

title: Vanilla and chocolate mixed in a bigger cup... awesome
text: My husband is like a little kid when it comes to pudding - loves it and we keep some around all the time. This combo of vanilla and chocolate scored high on his happy meter. Plus the cups are bigger than usual so he's extra happy with extra pudding. These are very smooth and creamy and make a tasty quick snack on the go or you know, wallowing in front of the television.

title: Bland. Requires same steps as making a can of soup
text:
I get why this exists, but it's not really camping food and it's not good enough to be at home food for us either. You have to boil water and add that to the pouch, which can be...sloppy and dangerous if you don't have rock steady hands. The microwave option is easier, but requires a different container....might as well heat a can of soup.

The taste isn't bad, but I don't like it enough to eat a second pouch of Spicy Southwest Skillet. It's pretty bland and no heat. The meat pieces are tender and not rubbery so that's good. I may try another flavor at some point in the future.

title: Dry, bland birdseed chunks
text: My husband loves several of the CLIF bars, so we were excited to try these bites. Neither of us were happy. These are made with soy so I have to avoid these due to a soy allergy. My husband said they were bland and dry. Like eating bird seed held together with salt and rice cakes. He refused to eat a second pouch.

title: Tastes decent, salty so don't add any
text: I used this in a quick casserole and it was pretty good. The smoke flavor is readily detectable and it mixed well with a bit of honey mustard. The ham is salty though, so you don't want to add any. I can see taking a can of this ham in my survival gear pack when I'm out in deep West Texas hiking.

title: Chemical type after taste, too salty and weird texture
text: Refrigerated or room temp, these just taste wrong. There's a nasty after taste that reminds me of those fake sweeteners even though the ingredients don't show anything like that. The texture is both chewy and crunchy at the same time and then it dissolves into a weird paste as you chew. The Price here per bar is way too much. My final straw was the salt. The first flavor I noticed was salt and it stayed salty through half a bar. I couldn't eat a whole one and my husband didn't get past the second bite. It's a shame because I love coconut.

title: Too much raspberry overwhelmed the lemon for me
text: I love lemon and lime flavors and I like raspberry. These drinks are light and fresh. The initial lemon taste is delicious and bubbly. Unfortunately, the raspberry hits and it's just too much. I would love these without that second raspberry flavor - just lemon and you got me. My husband likes these though - enough so that he took eight cans on the road with him.

title: Excellent flavor, no bitterness and smells wonderful
text:
I'm no coffee snob and I typically find all coffee bitter to some degree, but I love a cappuccino....well, hot, sweet milk with a hit of coffee added. This is the first decaf coffee I've ever tried and I used our espresso machine to make a 4pm cappuccino.

I'm, frankly, amazed at how good this is. It's one of only two coffees that didn't strike me with that bitter flavor. It smells delicious and left no oily residue behind in my machine. The taste is very soft and mild with an earthy undertone. I am making a second cup as I type this.

title: Mellow flavor without any burned or bitter after taste
text: I'm certainly no coffee expert. I basically like a little coffee with my milk and sugar. As such, I am sensitive to bitterness or burned tasting beans. These are nice with a reasonably mellow flavor and no bitterness. I use these beans in our espresso machine for cappuccino and lattes daily.

title: 6 too sweet, undercooked cookies with soy
text:
These are just ridiculous on so many levels. The cookies are marketed as something high end and super special and priced like it too. They are not high end or super special than anything else on a regular grocery store shelf. The ingredients include soy - why?

The cookies themselves are about the size of a Chips Ahoy. These are soft and on the gooey side and covered in some sort of icing. The overall texture is like an unfinished or half baked cookie. These are so sweet that none of could eat a whole one...which is just as well since you only get 6 cookies in a package. You're just better off buying Pepperidge Farm cookies than these.

title: Hint of sweet and tangy.
text: I was expecting a watery mess from this, but it's actually delicious. It's not as thick as regular mustard or BBQ sauce though. There's a hint of both sweet and tangy here. I've used it as a dipping sauce for chicken nuggets and on a roast chicken sandwich and it was really good.

title: Chewy, made with soy
text:
Three of us had pretty similar opinions about these. First - I'm very disappointed to see they contain soy.... Since I didn't feel like experimenting and possibly needing my EpiPen, I wasn't able to eat one.

The other two folks did eat one bar each. These are very chewy and take awhile to finish. The consensus was that the bars aren't as sweet as a candy bar, but sweeter than sweet tea. The chocolate flavor is pretty weak, but overall, the bar is not bad and not great. None of us feel like we would choose these over something else though.

title: Helped tenderize beef ribs
text: I rarely use meat tenderizer, but some cheap cuts just require it. We did fajitas the other day and some ribs and this stuff did work. The fajitas weren't so gristly and we're easy to cut and to chew. The beef ribs were noticably more tender than usual.

title: Better than expected. Good for breakfast burritos
text:
I swear that I've eaten this chorizo hash at Denny's before. I'll be honest, this smells just awful when you first open the can and it looks pretty sketchy as well. Don't let that turn you off though. I put this in the Crock-Pot for three hours while we went about our business.

Once it was fully heated and ready to eat, the scent was more palatable and the texture reminded us of a sort of chili with potatoes instead of beans. There's a fair amount of grease here - I patted it off before serving. The taste is surprisingly good. It has a tiny bit of heat that slowly builds as you eat, but may need a dash of salt to bring out the full flavors. The leftovers make pretty good breakfast burritos in fresh tortillas with a smear of refried beans and cheese.

title: May contain soy. Overly chewy and very sweet
text:
Three of us had pretty similar opinions about these. First - I'm very disappointed to see they may or may not contain soy....as a top 8 allergen, that's important. How can a brand that makes grandiose claims about knowing every organic ingredient, not be sure if soy is in there or not? Since I didn't feel like experimenting and possibly needing my EpiPen, I wasn't able to eat one.

The other two folks did eat one bar each. These are very chewy and take awhile to finish. The consensus was that the bars aren't as sweet as a candy bar, but sweeter than sweet tea. The coconut flavor is very strong. None of us feel like we would choose these over something else though.

title: I noticed that extra caffeine immediately
text: If you have a morning where you're just dragging, this will put some pep in your step. The coffee itself has a smooth flavor without any bitterness or burned after taste. I definitely noticed that extra caffeine this morning. I can't drink this every day, but some mornings, it's exactly what I need.

title: Not sweet enough, dry texture and weird after taste
text: Yeah....these are just off. The bars are enormous, but the texture is dry and crumbly, so they don't hold together well. It's like there's not enough marshmallow in the mix. But our real issue is with the taste. These are not sweet enough to be a Rice Crispy Treat and there's a weird, almost chemical type after taste. Neither of us could eat more than a few bites.

title: Makes a nice side dish
text: I'm old school and I love the original orange Kraft Mac and cheese. This stuff is an ok substitute and possibly better for you, I don't know. What I do know is that these noodles are chewier than the others and take the same time to cook. The flavor here is fine, but it's missing that specific tang of the Kraft cheese powder. Served as a side dish with pork chops and green beans, this mac and cheese does round out the meal competently.

title: Makes a very good pumpkin spice cappuccino
text: No more coffee shop pumpkin spice latte! I added three sprinkles of this to my cappuccino after the steamed milk, but before the coffee. Stirring it up blended the spices and it was delicious. It seems heavy on nutmeg compared to McCormick's pumpkin pie spice mix. I really like this and it's certainly affordable.

title: Makes a good cappuccino or latte
text: I'm certainly no coffee aficionado or expert. I tend to find 90% of all coffee bitter and I drown it in steamed milk and sugar in the form a latte. This has a pretty strong flavor profile for my palate, but the bitterness is significantly toned down compared to other beans we've used. This is nice in our espresso machine with steamed milk and a dousing of pumpkin spice mix and sugar.

title: Makes a really nice baked ziti type dish
text: We eat a fair amount of pasta around here so I'm always interested in a new brand or type. These are thick, dense noodles and you get more per bite. I used this for a simple baked ziti type dish with cheese and a red sauce. Because of the density, I had to cook these about 14 minutes to get the soft texture we prefer before putting everything in the oven. The flavor is good and the noodles don't get lost under a thick sauce - they hold up well.

title: Tastes fresh and good on baked chicken
text:
Paprika brings a little extra..."oomph" to most anything its added to. We love it in chili, a dash in spaghetti sauce, on baked chicken and even grilled pork chops.

This version has a true paprika flavor and scent. It is fresh and was very good on baked chicken and potatoes the other night.

title: Spicy with a definite lime kick
text: Lawrys has been a staple in our house for years. It's just a solid, consistently good seasoning. This one with the red chili and like is excellent. Of course you can use it for fajitas, but it's also very good on grilled pork chops and a slow cooked brisket. I can distinctly taste the line in this and our next baked chicken will have this on it.

title: Clean, simple flavor - cooks fast
text:
In Texas, Skinner has been a household staple for most folks for decades. My grandmother and my mother just never bought anything else and I buy it now. The ingredients are exactly the same as Barilla spaghetti - perhaps in different quantities, but the same items.

Skinner tastes clean and simple to me without bringing any sort of external flavors or after taste to compete with your own seasoning or sauces. This is thin spaghetti and it cooks quickly and is excellent in a simple carbonara style or with a traditional red sauce.

title: Bitter, weak and generally weird taste
text: We had three flavors of these coffee pods and 9 people over the holidays trying them over four days. Only one person liked any of these after tasting them. The resounding opinion from 8 of us was bitter, weak and tastes like bad tea. Nobody wanted a second cup of any flavors except my sister in-law and she had to add milk to the probiotic version to make it more palatable. This stuff is just not for us.

title: Convienent for fresh coffee in a semi truck on the road
text: What a clever idea. My husband has taken several of these premeasured packets with him on the road and he's happy. He uses them in his coffee maker in the semi truck when he's on the road. Fresh coffee on demand in the truck is big deal for quality of life and these packets are less expensive than buying truck stop coffee.  He said he likes the flavor - it's robust without tasting burned or too strong.

title: Tastes good and soy free!
text:
I eat a lot of peanut butter, it's always been one of favorite go-to snacks and a peanut butter and jelly sandwich will suffice for a fast meal any day. Due to a soy allergy, I have to be very careful with the brands we buy because most are made with soybean oil and that's just a death sentence.

Fortunately, this has no soy listed and I did not have any allergic reactions to it - yay! The flavor is good and there's none of that burnt, over roasted taste that so many generic peanut butter have. This makes nice cookies too.

title: Very close to the delicious Nutterbutter cookies.
text: I cannot overstate how much I love the original Nutterbutter cookies and I compare all other peanut butter cookies to the Nutterbutter cookies. Rarely do any measure up - not even the Girl Scout version. These are surprisingly tasty and really good. The creme isn't too sweet and the cookie parts are sweet without being cloying. My one complaint is that the cookie pieces are really hard - not crunchy, just hard.

title: Nice little kick and easy to eat too much of.
text: We don't do a lot of dips, usually choosing to make question with the extra hot Rotel and jalepeno. However, this was a nice change mixed with sour cream. It's got a little kick to it, but less than our usual quest. I think it tastes a lot like buffalo wings which isn't my favorite. My husband and a friend really like this and think I'm wrong. So I'll make it again for the boys.

title: Works well to enhance a chili recipe. Not overly salty
text: I made chili from scratch yesterday and my key ingrediente are thin sliced steak and beef broth in addition to all the regular chili fixings. This broth has a nice caramalized color and smells fresh. It's thinner than what you might make from scratch, but no thinner than you get with any other store bought brand in a can. The flavor is clean and beefy rather than salty or watery. My chili came out exactly as it should have and our guests literally ate all of it! No leftovers.

title: No bitterness or weird aftertaste. Doesn't froth or foam at all
text:
Meh. I'm not impressed with this and I certainly won't replace real milk with this ever. It's very thin and it absolutely does not froth for cappuccino. I have a four figure pro style espresso machine that steams and froths milk under tremendous pressure - we never buy coffee out anymore. Even with this machine, the almond "milk" just gets hot, but not froth or foamy. It's flat like any cream you might pour into a cup of coffee.

The flavor is actually pretty good considering that it's just almond juice. There's no added sweetness and no bitterness either and it hasn't been contaminated with soy additives. If you physically can't consume real milk, this stuff is a reasonable substitute, but it isn't budget friendly at all. My personal peeve is the use of the word milk rather than "milk like substitute" on these types of things.

title: Very, very bitter with a sour after taste
text: I'm not sure what coffee these folks were drinking before they made this because they clearly don't understand what "BITTER" actually is. This stuff is really, bitingly bitter. Both the Double Espresso and Mexican Vanilla are bitter and leave a sour after taste. Neither my husband or I could finish an entire can of either flavor.

title: Nice well rounded flavor - good on a burger or as a dipping sauce
text: I haven't eaten honey mustard in years and forgot how good it can be. This is the high quality we expect from a French's product. It's not as tart as plain mustard and yet not sugary sweet like the generic honey mustard can be. I've eaten this with chicken fingers, on a burger and a chef's salad. It tastes great on all three without overwhelming the flavor of the food.

title: These grind well both coarse and fine, nice flavor on meats
text: We are a peppercorn family here. We only use whole peppercorns for cooking and meals. My husband has three different grinders and he orders four different types of peppercorns from Penzys to blend at home. I thought this giant bag of simple black pepper would be a good way to have just a black pepper grind for certain dishes. The pepper smells fresh and the corns grind very nicely. This has a good peppery bite, but doesn't overwhelm your food. I like it on hamburgers and a simple quick broiled fish.

title: Needed a bit of extra water. Nice flavor, makes a good side dish
text: This is the first time I've tried couscous at home and it's a nice change from rice or potatoes as a simple side dish. The first batch was a little dry for our taste, but adding a bit of extra water the second time was just right. The pieces are puffy balls and have a nice flavor by themselves. We ate this with a hot Japanese curry sauce and it was excellent.

title: Soy free! Nice, balanced taste and no oily separation
text:
I love peanut butter - always have and I am perfectly happy to eat a peanut butter and jelly sandwich for dinner. However, because I have a soy allergy that's gotten worse with age, I've been limited to just a few brands. My go-to is always Peter Pan because it's made without any soy oil.

This Skippy Natural is free of soy and safe for me to eat. It's very smooth and soft in texture and easy to spread. Unlike other "natural" peanut butters, this isn't oily with that creepy separation that requires mixing it before you can eat it. The taste is good and a bit mild - none of the overcooked taste that some generic brands have. I'm glad to have a second peanut butter option that's budget friendly.

title: Love that they included Cheetos Puffs
text: This is my favorite combination variety pack from Frito Lay. Between my husband and I, we like every flavor in this box. The inclusion of the snack size Cheetos Puffs is great - those are my favorite chips. I also really like the cheddar popcorn - wish I could find this locally. This box is just a well thought out collection of classic flavors with popcorn and little pretzels thrown in.

title: Weak flavor - bland.
text: I don't drink tea often, but when I do, my preference is a solid chai tea. This is ok, but it's not something I would buy in the future. None of the tea bags are individually sealed, so once you open the box, these will get stale unless you store them in a Ziploc bag.  The flavor is ok. It's very mild and I barely recognize it as a spiced chai tea - it's just weak even using two bags in one cup.

title: Nice mix of classic chip flavors
text: We are chip lovers and eat a wide variety of flavors. This combo pack has the classics that everyone likes - Doritos in Cool Ranch & Nacho Cheese, BBQ Lays, Cheetos and more. I like the little bags because they are enough for a snack without overdoing things.

title: Cat likes it, but doesn't love it. Sort of a mix of mush and flaked pieces
text: Our Siamese, Free Cat, is particular about food texture more than flavor - he will not touch a pate mush, only cuts or flakes when it comes to wet food. I'm particular about ingredients and try to avoid any food with soy added. He likes the salmon and likes the tuna a bit more in the Simply Perfection food. The cans are labeled as flaked, but it's sort of a mix between flakes and mush. The food is very wet, but it spreads out to reveal pieces which was good enough for Free Cat. He is happy to eat these cans.

title: Doritos Flamas are worth buying in big bags - so good
text: Ok the Doritos Flamas are the best of the bunch here. The red pepper heat is definitely turned up, but you can still taste the like mixed in - these are great with bean dip. The Cheetos are hot, but still cheesy though I think the puffs are better as regular Cheetos Puffs. We both dislike regular Funyuns anyway and the hot version was really gross - neither of us could eat more than one piece.

title: No soy!!! Tastes fine and is good with fries
text:
We don't eat a lot of ketchup and I usually just buy whatever is on sale at the moment, plus we literally don't care whatsoever about high fructose corn syrup. I realize that other people think it's a questionable ingredient, but our concern is actually about soy because of a real life threatening allergy. So as long as the ketchup is soy free, we don't care about the other unimportant stuff.

This stuff is soy free and has honey instead of a different sweetener. I can't tell the difference taste wise between this ketchup and any other brand to be honest. It's good and it perks up fries. I am very happy that it's soy free and I can actually eat it safely and that alone is worth the five stars in our home.

title: Contains aspartame. Chemical flavor and after taste with every swallow
text: I wanted to like these because we are lemonade drinkers, but there's a problem. You mix these little packets into a bottle of water and have instant lemonade on the go and that's a good idea. However, these contain aspartame instead of real sugar. I cannot consume any of the fake, chemical sweeteners and must avoid at all times. My husband trued these and said all he got was a nasty chemical flavor and after taste with every swallow. He doesn't want another bottle of this at all.

title: Smells amazing and tastes pretty good with sugar added
text:
I'm not a serious coffee drinker and I actually find most Kcups bitter. Usually, I will make a cappuccino from fresh beans in our espresso machine or just avoid coffee all together. These pods are liquid and can be used in the Kuerig or as cold coffee with water - I ran them through the brewer.

The macadamia vanilla smells amazing. I added sugar and it became a delicious flavored coffee like one you get from a coffee shop. It's smooth without the bitterness of most other coffees for me. However, you only get 6 pods in the box and that makes these really expensive compared to our other pods or just buying beans.

title: Two of four people liked this juice, but two of us really disliked it
text:
This had mixed reactions in my home with four different people over the weekend. The glass bottles are nicely shaped and easy to hold - that was the one thing we all agreed on. As to the pear juice, well.... I've learned that I may not actually like pears as much as I thought I did.

I just absolutely hated this juice. It's thick and the flavor was overwhelming for me. My husband said it was tolerable to drink once in awhile, but he would prefer not to buy it. My mother and sister both liked it and they loved it mixed into a smoothie with pineapple juice. I tried those smoothies and it wasn't any better for my taste buds.

title: Nice bottle design, but a hint of bitterness in the oil itself
text: We don't use a lot of oil of any type here, but sometimes you have to have some. Primarily when cooking pasta or as a pan coating for seafood. This is pretty standard olive oil, but there's a hint of very slight bitterness that I don't normally taste in other brands. It might just be me, hard to say.  I do like the bottle - it has a no drip top that definitely makes adding just a tiny bit possible.

title: Cup of fresh, flakey, good tuna with its own fork. NO SOY
text:
I'm funny about tuna - I hate the stuff in oil and most canned tuna is coated in soy for some reason which means I avoid it due to a severe soy allergy. Fortunately, there's no soy in the Basil cups - I didn't need Benadryl or my EpiPen, so that's a win.

These cups are just the right size for a quick snack on the go or a protein boost when I'm exercising horses. Since they are self contained, all you need is a napkin. The Basil smells stronger than it tastes, but it's really good. The fish is flakey and not the usual wet mush from a can. The flavor is actually bright and fresh. I really like these cups.

title: Really bland flavor unless you add real cheese and pepper. Quinoa is tiny and gets lost in draining
text:
We love Mac and cheese in all versions - home-made, in a restaurant, Kraft box, or frozen. Trying this was a no brainier. It's a wheat pasta with the quinoa in the form of little pieces of grain. This quinoa is a problem when you drain the pasta - it will either vanish with a big colander or clog up the tiny holes in a fine colander.

The actual flavor is ok, but really bland. The cheese powder used is just too mild and almost flavorless. We added black pepper to the first batch and extra real cheese and pepper to the second box and that definitely helped. One thing I do appreciate is that they didn't add soy to this so it's allergy safe for me.

title: No oily residue, big strong flavor in espresso. Better as a cappuccino
text: I'm not a coffee snob in the least. To be honest, I like a little coffee with my hot milk and sugar. My husband though is all about coffee flavor and balance and what not. He loves this Westrock brand in all varieties - ground, whole beans and Kcups. I like these beans in my cappuccino through the espresso machine with frothed milk. However, as straight espresso, they are a bit too strong for me.

title: Bold, but not bitter and doesn't overwhelm when milk is added
text: I'm not a coffee drinker, I'm a hot milk and sugar with some coffee splashed in drinker. My husband drinks coffee throughout the day and he can get picky about the Kcups. These Community Dark Roast pods are really good. They have a distinct, bold flavor, but aren't bitter or too strong and there's no after taste. I like them in my milk and sugar and he likes them straight. There's no oily residue on top of a fresh cup either which has happened with some of the no name kcups before.

title: Fresh smell and taste. The roasted garlic powder is really good
text: I have tried the generic garlic powder and garlic salt over the years, but it's never quite as good as McCormick for some reason. This variety pack just reinforces that for me. These bottles smell like fresh, real garlic and the flavor is distinct and strong - you can definitely use less and get the taste effect you want. I particularly like the roasted garlic powder on simple steamed boneless chicken thighs  with a dash of black pepper and salt over rice. That roasted garlic adds a smokey scent and taste that is very good. Spices are one of the few things where you really do get exactly what you pay for.

title: Seriously the best surprise I've had in months. Wildflower Honey is perfection
text:
Holy Honey Heaven! I don't think that I've ever tasted honey like this before - not even from our local farmer's market guy. I have the Wildflower Honey and it's light, crisp and delicious. It's sweet, but not cloying. I've used this in hot tea, coffee and on a peanut butter and honey sandwich (OMG Do that!)

Eating this honey after the cheap stuff in the plastic bottles from the grocery store is like driving a Porsche after a 1972 Pinto with duct taped bumpers. I've always thought the price of fancy honey was just a rip-off and now I get it. This stuff is amazing and now we can't have the cheap stuff in the house anymore.

title: Super easy in the rice cooker, good flavor and zero drama.
text: I love rice in all its variations, but I can't make it well on the stove top to save my life. Thankfully, I have an excellent rice cooker and this Della Jasmine rice works perfectly in it. Light, fluffy and delicious. I just served it with simple marinated, grilled chicken and asparagus for dinner and we ate everything - no leftovers at all.

title: No watermelon taste, slightly bitter
text:
Umm....no. Of four people in our home who tried the watermelon water, only one sort of liked it, the other three were United in a vote of "Yuck". The cans burst open with the traditional whoosh like all carbonated cans should and you get lots of bubbles with every sip - if sparkling, bubbly water is your thing, this is good.

However, the watermelon flavor was pretty awful. It just doesn't taste anything like watermelon and it's not sweet like watermelon. It just tastes like slightly bitter mineral water to us. Looking at the ingredients list shows no watermelon, it just says "natural flavor" which could be literally anything. As to the caffeine, since we didn't finish the cans, we don't know if there's enough caffeine to give you a boost or not. We usually drink Avitae caffeinated flat water often for a simple boost without any flavor and we'll just keep doing that.

title: Allergy alert for soy. No fake sweeteners, tastes decent with cold milk
text:
Allergen Warning! For crying out loud!!! Contains SOY. Why??? Meanwhile, since my husband doesn't have a food allergy to soy, he uses these packets when he's on the road. On the plus side, these don't contain any of the fake, chemical sweeteners - just simple sugar, so no unpleasant digestive system upset.

He likes these because it's a simple, fast on the go breakfast when he's in the semi truck on the highway. Mix with milk, drink and keep moving down the road. It's a healthier option to truck stop breakfast sandwiches or burritos and he gets a dose of protein and calcium without grease etc. He says the flavor is fine - like chocolate milk only less sweet and as long as you mix it well, there's no powdery or chalky after taste.

title: Soy free!!! Decent flavor, little bland for adults
text:
I'm a reformed Slim Jim eater due to the soy since I developed an adult onset food allergy to soy in all forms. I've been missing having a neat quick snack on the go at the barn or in my truck. I'm glad to see this one is available without any soy.

These taste ok, not great, but okay. They definitely are bland and need some spice or pepper added for an adult palate - however, as a kid's snack, these are probably just right. The texture is a bit chewy around the skin, but not rubbery. I like these, but I have to say, they aren't terribly budget friendly, which is apparently true of anything without soy added.

title: Makes great sugared bacon
text:
There's something almost hypnotic about the smell of fresh brown sugar... The heavy molasses scent just warms the heart and makes you think of cookies, pie and hot toddies. This bag smells fresh and delicious even before opening it. The sugar is soft, slightly moist and flexible - not dried out, hard or stale. I made sugared bacon this morning and it was excellent.

Just melt the brown sugar in a pan over low heat til it turns a caramel brown. Don't scorch it. Dredge fresh cooked bacon through it and let it set up a minute. Serve warm to adoring family who now thinks you're a freaking genius.

title: If you're sensitive to bitter, this is too much. Other palates like it fine
text: Well, two of the three people in my house like this well enough to drink it and one of us really dislikes it. My mother and husband both think it's a reasonably decent, strong coffee to get their morning going, but neither of them love the coffee. They aren't rushing back for a second cup of this. I actually really dislike the Revv No Surrender - I found it very bitter for my palate. I tried adding sugar and milk and it was still too much for me.

title: No soy!! Allergy safe, delicious snack that I can take everywhere
text: I'm allergic to soy and it's really hard to find snacks that are soy free and delicious. Fortunately, Goldfish crackers are both! I absolutely love these things. They are somehow both crispy and crunchy at the same time. The Xtra Cheddar flavor is tart and a little sharp without going overboard. I keep some in the house and at the horse barn all the time for a safe snack. Plus they are a fun treat to toss at the dogs.

title: Not bitter or oily. Decent drip brew coffee option
text:
I prefer fresh ground beans for cappuccino from my espresso machine and my husband is all about the Kcups or the drip machine. This is ground coffee and works fine in the old drip coffee maker, but it never works right when used in the kcup container for loose coffee.

The coffee smells nice and fresh when you open the bag. There's no oily residue in the bag, coffee filters or the cup of brewed coffee. The coffee itself isn't bitter and mixes well with milk and sugar for a balanced flavor.

title: Allergy warning! Contains SOY as the very last ingredient
text:
I'm seriously disappointed with these caramels. I had looked forward to trying them and was happy to see that each piece is very soft and individually wrapped in paper. They smell wonderful and slide off the paper without sticking. Exactly what a great caramel should do.

Unfortunately, the last ingredient is soy lecithin. Why??? Why does an otherwise natural and simple candy need soy added to it? I'm very allergic to soy and I don't dare taste these. What a waste. Yet another brand to avoid if you're allergic to soy.

title: Tastes like mocha & creamy. Same calories and sugar as a soft drink
text:
I am one of those folks who likes a little coffee with my milk and sugar rather than an actual cup of coffee. These drinks meet that requirement and are very similar to the Starbucks bottled versions. The cookies and cream flavor is mostly just a mocha flavor - very little cookies to me. That being said, it's a good drink. Smooth, creamy and easy to drink ice cold.

My one star deduction is for the high calories and high sugar content. I'm very happy with the actual ingredients - no soy and no fake, chemical sweeteners. However, this is strictly a dessert or breakfast replacement rather than a snack or regular drink. With 290 calories and 41 grams of sugar, this is the equivalent of a 12 ounce Dr Pepper. That's definitely something you don't want more than once a day.

title: Tiny bit softer than non-sprouted almonds. Hint of heat with a good overall flavor
text:
I had never heard of "sprouted," anything other than potatoes gone feral in the back of the fridge. Apparently, the nuts are soaked in water until they literally sprout and the process makes the nuts a little softer. These almonds still have plenty of crunch, but they are a bit softer.

The flavor is really good. You immediately notice the black pepper and then the red pepper heat lingers after you swallow. These have just a hint of heat, but I don't consider them hot. These are a nice snack on a roadtrip for sure.

title: Full flavor without bitterness or acidity
text: My husband discovered the Westrock coffee at a rest area in Little Rock, Arkansas and called to tell me how good it was. It has a good flavor without being bitter or over roasted. The kcups work fine in our four years old Kuerig and taste the same at home as they do on the road.

title: Good, but way more expensive than it should be
text:
Let me say first that I am in no way a coffee bean snob or even very experienced with the different types out there. I had always avoided coffee until we got a fancy automatic espresso machine that creates the most amazing cappuccino. Suddenly, I'm educating myself about coffee beans, roasts, and strengths. And I'm trying a multitude of coffee beans from various sources to find out what I like and can tolerate.

The Espresso roast beans here are lighter in color and aroma than another brand we tried. They grind up easily in our espresso machine and have a nice scent while brewing/pulling. I like the taste here too - no bitterness or unpleasant mouth taste after you swallow. My issue is the price point compared to almost everything else out there....this little 12 ounce bag is two and a half times the cost of a 16 ounce bag from multiple other brands. In my house, that means we're just never going to buy more of this coffee when it's gone.

title: Flavorful, but mild taste. No bitterness
text:
My husband and mother are both serious, straight coffee drinkers - I tend to prefer a cappuccino or macchiato. Since we had a whole house full of company this week, I put out these KCups and the regular Maxwell House morning blend KCups.

Four days later, I have a full box of the Maxwell House left and we're down to just 10 of the 40 Lucky Cup pods remaining. Everyone preferred this coffee. It's mild, but flavorful and doesn't leave any bitter after taste behind. I mixed it with whole milk and sugar and it was pretty good - I didn't feel overwhelmed by the strength of the coffee.

title: Utterly flavorless, bland and too thick to enjoy as a dip
text:
For the record - we are a family of bean dip lovers and we love the Bush's Original baked beans. So, of course I was excited to see Bush coming out with bean dip. Alas, this is really not good. It's too thick, too chunky and most importantly, this has almost no flavor and zero spice.

When compared to Frito Lay Bean dip, this stuff is like a bland, cold can of refried black beans. You know, the kind you heat up, add some red chili and jalapeno to before you serve it. The Frito Lay Bean dips are tasty, spicy and addictive. Bush needs to just stick with BBQ beans and baked beans - the things they do better than anyone else.

title: Incomplete allergen warning label! Contains multiple forms of soy
text:
INCOMPLETE ALLERGY WARNINGS ON THE BAGS. This is a potentially serious health risk for people with food allergies. The warning states these include tree nuts, but leaves out the SOY ingredients on the warning. The Hunter mix and Nomadic includes soy oil, soy flour, and soy protein concentrate listed in the tiny print ingredients list. Soy is as dangerous as milk, nuts and shellfish for people with food allergies - soy is one the top 8 food allergens listed by the CDC.

Fortunately, I read all ingredients before I try a food so I don't have an epi-pen episode from hidden soy. However, children may not be as vigilant and rely only on the allergy warning. Both flavors of these that we received are off limits for me. My husband is blessed with the ability to eat anything, so he tried them.

He likes the Hunter Mix - little bit cheesy and savory. He wasn't such a fan of the Nomadic mix. He felt like both raisins and cranberries lent a gummy texture to the whole bag.

title: Nice variety of flavors. Caramel is pretty good
text:
I don't drink much coffee as rule because I honestly hate the taste of plain black coffee. My husband though....coffee all day long. I thought I would try this collection since there are multiple flavors and the decaf works for my husband in the evenings.

The Hazelnut had a bit of an after taste for me, but my husband didn't notice it. The vanilla is quite nice, but for me, the caramel is the best one. My husband prefers the unflavored versions. Fortunately, there were 8 different versions of coffee in my box, so something for everyone.

title: Incredibly foul flavor - dried peas and bell peppers. Lingering after taste. Just yuck
text:
I can't begin to describe how absolutely foul this stuff tastes. It literally made my stomach turn and triggered a gag reflex with the first swallow. The flavor is an overwhelming mix of dried peas, bell peppers and something bitter that i just cannot identify. I tried with water and milk - milk was even worse. The powder is funky olive green color and it does get smooth and creamy with mixing.

The after taste lingers and lingers. Bottom line is that this stuff is just gross - I would lose weight simply by starving if I replaced actual edible food with two swallows of this witch's brew.

title: Working to help house-train a Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
text:
Two weeks ago, my husband rescued a dog left at a rest area on the interstate. We thought she was around 18 to 24 months old and reasonably close to grown. A trip to the vet disabused us of that notion quickly! Turns out, Beth is a 6 month old Greater Swiss Mountain Dog with enormous growth yet to come before maturity. She's a big, goofy puppy needing to learn to live in a civilized pack of house dogs - that means puppy pads and crate training.

Fortunately, Beth is super smart and already learning to follow the cues of our Plott Hound and Ridgebacks - the sit by the door when they need to go out. However, at night, we put a pad in her crate (it's a ridiculously big crate) so she has an option if she needs to potty while we're asleep. These pads hold up pretty well and don't shred with minor contact. So far, Beth has used the pads three times in a week without any drama or soaking through the bottom. Can't ask for more than that.

title: Flavorless on their own - add a bit of bacon and pepper and these perk right up
text: I like canned green beans for their simplicity and ease of use. We eat them often and I toss a can n with our dogs' kibble a couple of times a week. These don't really have any flavor on their own which is normal for canned green beans. I added a bit of bacon and black pepper to these and they were fine with pork chops and rice.

title: Contaminated with soy. Cookie dough flavor is good, soft chewy texture
text:
These bars don't have actual soy in the ingredients, but they are made in a facility that has soy, so they run the risk of cross contamination. I took one bite and had a reaction about 2 minutes later, so my batch of cookie dough bars are definitely contaminated with soy.

My husband likes these and he has no food allergies. The texture is soft and very chewy with a bit of crunch from the nuts throughout. There's no after taste and none of that chemical flavor you get with other bars that use fake sweeteners. They are a good between meals supplement and on the go snack for my husband. Sadly, I will never buy this brand again because I can't trust the products not to be contaminated with soy.

title: Soy allergy alert!! Bitter chocolate, lots of sugar and high calories
text:
Soy allergy alert! These contain soy lecithin which means that I can't eat them due a soy allergy. It's ridiculous because there's simply no reason to add soy here. My Mother is here for a couple of weeks, so she was very interested in trying these because of the implied "healthy" snack factor.

However, it turns out that a serving size is four of these little squares with 160 calories and 12 grams of sugar. It's so close to a Twinkie or half a Kit Kat's that the healthy snack idea is debunked immediately and a Twinkie or half a Kit Kat tastes better. The chocolate has a distinctly bitter undertone and the blueberry flavor overwhelms any other flavors. The cranberry squares are better. These are awfully pricey for what they really are.

title: Soy allergy alert! Contains soybeans
text: Crisco oil has always been a go to staple in our home and my Mother's and my Grandmother's kitchen. Fried chicken just tastes better with Crisco. Unfortunately, this generic term "vegetable oil" actually means soy oil. I have adult onset allergies to soy and that means Crisco can never be used again. It's unfortunate that a no name, generic soy free oil is my only option now.

title: Soy free!! Finally, good tasting mayo that's also safe for me to eat
text:
I have adult onset allergies to eggs and soy - soy exposure can cause an Epi-pen episode. Mayo has been off my safe list for years. When I saw this Chipotle mayo at the local grocery store this week, I snatched it up. Soy and egg free mayo is like a gift.

This tastes great with a distinguishable hint of chipotle. It's very thick and creamy and spreads smoothly. Put this on fresh bread with warm roasted chicken and sharp cheddar and you have a gourmet sandwich in your hands. The chipotle doesn't overwhelm the other flavors, just adds a but of enhancement. I'm just thrilled that I have had no allergic reactions eating this mayo.

title: Soy free and tasty. These are denser and take a little longer to cook than regular pancakes
text:
This review is for the Paleo pancake mix. We are a pancake house hold - breakfast for dinner is always popular here. We've even been known to serve heaps of pancakes with a variety of syrup flavors on game night with friends. While no one in our circle or family has a problem with gluten, I am severely allergic to soy and I was happy to see there's no soy in the Paleo mix.

This requires only water to make and it's a pretty dense batter. I had to add extra water to get it to the right consistency for pancakes. The batter makes fewer than it suggests, but still plenty of flapjacks for a single meal using just a third of the package - I got 7 medium size pancakes.

These need to cook longer than Bisquick batter and they do not bubble up when it's time to flip them. If you aren't paying attention, you can end up over cooking them or worse, flipping too soon and ending up with the inside not completely cooked. Once you get the timing right, these are good. They are dense and chewy with a good flavor. Syrup doesn't absorb as fast as with regular pancakes, but it's not a problem. We'll use this batter again.

title: Allergy alert - may be contaminated with soy. Mixes well with warm milk as a latte
text:
First make note that this may contain soy contamination from the factory, which means that I don't dare try it myself. If you're allergic to soy, avoid. We tried this matcha powder in lattes for family on Thanksgiving n lattes.

It blends well with water and with warm milk with just a small whisk - no lumps. My husband didn't like it and felt like it left an after taste even with simple sugar added. My mother likes it and says the taste is not overpowering and she could see drinking thus on a cold evening with a good book. I wish I could try it and I do not understand the need to add or expose every product to soy.

title: Smooth and no harsh or bitter back taste.
text:
I drink very little coffee because I can't stand the bitterness of most coffee, but my husband is a full on, multi cup a day coffee drinker. He and I both like the scent of these beans before and after grinding them. We are just using a tiny, very inexpensive grinder, nothing fancy here.

This donut cafe style blend is a medium strength and brew. It's still too strong for me black, but with sugar and cream, I can drink it. My husband says that I like a little coffee with my sweet milk. He, on the other hand, likes this coffee unadulterated. He says it's a smooth coffee with no bitter after taste and it's not a harsh blend. He likes it.

title: Several varieties of drinks we've never tried before.
text: This sample box is a great idea. There are two flavors of the Gold Peak tea in the box that we've never seen in local stores - the vanilla chai tea is surprisingly good. The Java Monster has a weird chemical flavor, so  we'll never buy it. I love the Illy Cappuccino can in particular. It's sweet and creamy with no bitter aftertaste and no unnecessary ingredients. I have already ordered that with the sample box credit.

title: Rich, strong blend with zero bitterness
text: We're pretty easy going when it comes to coffee and I usually just buy whatever K-Cups are on sale. These are definitely a different breed of coffee than the dollar store generic cups. The Adrenaline brew is a very dark coffee and certainly stronger than Folgers for example. Surprisingly, it's not bitter at all - it's pretty smooth and tastes good. We might buy these again, but they are a little bit more than I care to spend for every day K-Cups.

title: May contain soy. Dark chocolate is good, lots of almonds
text:
My husband loves this mix. I might love it too, but unfortunately, they use equipment contaminated by soy products and I am extremely allergic to soy. I don't dare try this stuff lest I risk an anaphylactic episode. Honestly, there is no reason to use any type of soy in a trail mix. (It's one of the top 8 food allergens)

There are tons of almonds in the bag and lots of crisp coconut slivers. The little chocolate cups look like miniature peanut butter cups. Looks is all they have in common though. These are made of dark chocolate and include a tiny bit of coconut in the middle. My husband said there is a slight bitter undertone from the dark chocolate, but it's offset by the toasted coconut. If you aren't afflicted by the soy allergy, this mix is tasty.

title: Definitely taste the lime. Cooks well in a rice cooker, great in burritos
text: I picked up a single box locally to try and we're hooked. It has a definite lime taste, but isn't overwhelming. I popped the whole thing in our rice cooker and it came out perfectly - fluffy, loose grains and smelled so good. We made burritos with this rice, refried beans, grilled steak and it was delicious. We'll totally keep a box or two in the pantry.

title: Very cheesy flavor and nice crunch factor
text: I picked up a big bag of the cheddar cheese flavor at a local store and now I wish I had bought a case. These taste great - very cheesy and with a hint of salt. They don't taste like rice. There's a definite crunch with each bite, but it's lighter than eating corn chips. Even my husband likes these and he normally turns up his nose at anything resembling rice cakes.

title: Weird looking mush that actually tastes great and is easy to eat.
text:
My initial reaction to reading the directions was essentially... This is going to be gross. Nonetheless, I dutifully put whole milk in the container, stirred until everything was thoroughly mixed, closed the lid and left it in the fridge for 7 hours. All the while dreading a cup of weird, coconut mush in the morning.

At 6am this morning, I removed the cold cup and looked at it with suspicion. It had a texture that reminded me of both oatmeal and granola. There was still some liquid milk in it and after stirring it again everything mixed nicely. The mouth feel is soft oatmeal with those slightly crisp almond slivers, but not mushy or porridge like.

It actually tastes great and the almond slivers still had a bit of crisp to them. The flavor is excellent and it's just sweet enough to not feel like you've eaten a donut. I can taste the coconut easily. I am very pleased that the ingredients are so simple as well. I think the key here is definitely mixing it really well before chilling. Now I just need to remember to make one before bed each night.

title: Tastes good - not too sweet or salty. Nice shape bottles
text:
This took me by surprise in a good way. I work with horses in the heat and high humidity every day so electrolyte replacement is a constant thing for me. I drink Gatorade, but I hate their lemon flavor and Gatorade can get gross if it's not ice cold. I'm not always in the position to have it cold when I need to drink it.

First thing with the Honest Sport Lemon is that it has a very mild taste. Not too tart, not too salty, not too sweet and it's easy to drink straight without watering it down. Personally, I don't really care if the ingredients are "organic" or not - most "organic" products are way over hyped and over priced. All I care about is palatablity and if it keeps me from becoming dehydrated. These drinks taste good and help me stay on track with a heat index of 109 degrees for two days.

It tastes fine at room temperature as well as cold. However, you definitely don't want to leave an open bottle sitting around in high temperatures for long. The organic component means this can spoil - say if it's left in a hot car or outside unfinished for a couple of hours. I also appreciate that the bottles are shaped to fit in my truck cup holders - helps with portability.

title: Excellent for legs, elbows and feet
text:
This is very thick and creamy. I'm using this on my legs after shaving each night (I can't stand a stubbly leg) It goes on thicker than a regular lotion and needs a minute to fully absorb into the skin.

After a week, I have to say that my legs are incredibly smooth, soft and silky looking. I've also taken to using this cream on my elbows and heels with the same results. I won't use this on my very sensitive face - I tried once and it just felt way too heavy. The next morning I noticed a little redness so I will reserve the coconut oil cream for my legs from now on.

title: Makes burger patties more moist, but it's flavorless and boring
text:
Meh. We cooked 12 burgers on the grill today and did half with this added to the meat and half the old fashioned way. The Wicked Juicy is very much a liquid, just a bit thicker than regular broth.

The burgers with this added were juicier and didn't get that crispy char on the charcoal grill. The other burgers were fine, but a dash drier and they all got a bit of that char.

The flavor on the Wicked Juicy burgers was bland and we had to add steak sauce to them. These were salted and peppered before cooking. The regular burgers had the usual pepper, celery salt and a tiny bit of Worcester sauce added before cooking and definitely had more flavor. In the future, if I use this again, I'll know that it just adds moisture without any seasoning or flavor.

title: Slow cook over pork for green chili carnitas
text: This sauce is delicious. Hot chilies and the tang of citrus makes it balanced and perfect for pork. I use this to cook chunks of pork in the slow cooker for green chili carnitas. Add rice, refried beans and corn tortillas for a Tex-Mex comfort food.

title: Light flavor that goes well with curry
text: I picked up several different flavors of the Ready Rice locally and I really like them. The Jasmine rice has a good flavor and has been really good with a homemade curry. The rice comes out of the microwave light and moist without any overcooked or rubbery chunks - make sure you loosen it up in the pouch before cooking it though.

title: Tastes good, goes well with a quick grilled chicken breast for a fast dinner
text: I picked up several of the different flavors of these Ready Rice pouches locally and I am happy with them. 90 seconds in the microwave and you have soft, moist, tasty rice without the hassle. This chicken flavor is very good and goes nicely as a side with simple pork chops or grilled chicken breasts.

title: Light, crisp, very summer flavor. Delicious ice cold with & without alcohol
text:
Ok...I'm not normally a peach fan, but this mocktail is sooooo good! By itself, it totally tastes like Bellini and with a splash of champagne added, it's wonderful. Definitely serve cold.

This has a very summery feel. It's light, airy, just sweet enough and has no artificial sweeteners. The color is a pretty pink that just invites tasting. I like this so much, but that I added four bottles to my shopping list for our annual July 4th gathering. I love that I can offer our non-alcohol friends something different than tea and colas. And the drinkers can add a splash of champagne without over consuming.

title: Thick enough for dips and strong enough for nachos. Taste fresh
text: I don't understand paying double the price for corn chips from Tostitos etc. These are crunchy, lightly salted and taste great. The chips are just the right thickness for dipping in queso, bean dip or guacamole. We like them in nachos especially because they don't get soggy and drop the toppings as you eat.

title: Excellent base for a one dish family meal - just add sausage
text:
I love this as a base for a sort of jambalaya type group dinner. I toss it in the rice cooker with water then add smoked sausage. Set the rice cooker and walk away. An hour later...voila! Easiest, tasty meal for a group or just two people. I do two boxes with two big sausage links for 4 to 6 people plus salad and a veggie side.

This can be a little salty with sausage added, so it's not a regular meal for us. But in the winter, it's a great comfort food to enjoy by the fire on game night.

title: Contains SOY and sucralose. Has a chemical aftertaste, but the milk chocolate is tolerable
text:
My husband drinks the Instant Breakfast milk chocolate daily and I drink one maybe twice a year. We tried the cafe mocha flavor recently in this lower calorie version and it had a distinct chemical aftertaste.

This one is a little better for overall flavor, very similar to the regular milk chocolate version. However, there's still the artificial, chemical aftertaste of the sucralose. Due to the inclusion of soy and fake sweetener, I can't drink this again. If you're sensitive to the sucralose or allergic to soy, be cautious.

title: Just not for me. Nice crispy bite, smell good, but...an aftertaste that bothers me
text:
I want to love these pea crisp things. They are very simple, relatively healthy snack that has lots of satisfying crunch and a bit of salt. The texture is good - crispy like a Pringles chip, but not as salty or complicated. But there's just something I don't care for with these.

The color is fine, a light, yellow-green. They smell nice and appetizing when you open the bag. The flavor is just so-so for my palate. There's a undeniable aftertaste of peas that can turn sort of sour pretty quickly. I shared the second bag with my husband, thinking that I would get used to them, but he experienced the same aftertaste. I would eat these on a desert island, but not as an every day snack.

title: Exactly the right size for single servings of queso or a baked potato topper
text:
I indulge once a week in queso and chips on movie night, but the big block of Velveeta is a bit much. I end up having to stuff it in Ziploc bags and hoping it doesn't go bad before I can use all of it.
