These mini blocks are exactly right. Each one mixed with a quarter can of Rotel Hot makes the perfect serving size for two people just having a snack. We've also melted a mini block to pour over baked potatoes - that is actually really good. Be sure to scrutinize the prices from various sources - these are only three or four bucks at the grocery stores.

title: Chalky aftertaste and the mocha is not as good as the Carnation Chocolate version
text:
My husband drinks the original version of these in the full chocolate flavor every morning and I had hoped that this might be a second choice he could rotate with. He said the texture is the same, but they seem...."off" compared the regular drinks.

I tried them and agree that they aren't as good. The mocha flavor is reminiscent of a diet chocolate - slightly bland and boring. There's a distinct chalky aftertaste with every sip that erases the mocha and takes a glass of water to get past. These do include a significant vitamin count, so they are helpful if you skip actual food in the morning. I think for us, the original chocolate version is the one we're going to continue to buy.

title: Tastes and smells right when used in spaghetti sauce and chili.
text:
Holy Onion Powder, Cook-Man! This is just an enormous jug of onion powder. Fortunately, it has a clean, clear flavor. This is easy to cook with, especially since I don't cook with actual onions unless forced.

None of us likes the texture or overwhelming taste of whole onions. Most of my recipes that require onion can be substituted with good quality onion powder. I've used this in a huge batch of homemade spaghetti sauce and chili so far. The powder smells and tastes fresh, but doesn't consume your tastebuds with onion over the other spices.

title: Tastes much better than the generic, random sage I had been buying. Great on pork
text:
Much stronger flavor than we've become used to. We've been using a generic version of sage from the grocery store forever and I guess I had forgotten what it should really taste like. This smells very good and it doesn't take much at all to season a dish - well compared to the cheap sage we were using previously.

I've added this to a homemade stew and to pork chops so far. I mixed the sage with fresh ground pepper, a bit of rosemary and a dash of Worcestershire sauce to make a rub for the pork chops. Very simple and a nice, peppery flavor.

title: Still the best tasting caramel popcorn. A nostalgic bit of joy
text: I had forgotten how delicious the original Cracker Jacks are. I used to eat these as a kid (didn't we all?), but I haven't had a box in years. My husband snagged a couple at the grocery store on a whim. The popcorn pieces are large and intact and coated in the traditional caramel. The taste is exactly like we remember from our childhoods. I just wish they had a peanut free version.

title: Thicker and more tender than traditional jerky for sure. I'm looking for a pepper version now
text:
Jerky that doesn't fight back! This is still jerky, but it is more tender and definitely easier to chew than traditional beef jerky. It's more like actual pieces of meat rather than very thin, dried strips.

The flavor is good, consistent throughout the entire bag. It is a little bit bland for me. I prefer the peppered jerky, it has a little more....ooomph. My husband really likes this which means that we'll buy more of it.

title: Taste like normal cookies, but hard as rocks. Allergy alert contains SOY.
text:
At first glance, these look like great ingredients, but.... these contain soy. Why? A top 8 food allergen that isn't even necessary to the recipe - when's the last time you ever added soy to home made cookies? Never. Nonetheless, the gluten free aspect doesn't affect the taste.

We tried the Chocolate chip and macadamia nuts and the Oatmeal with chocolate chips. Both have a nice overall flavor that makes you want to eat a second cookie. Both are also hard as bricks. I mean these are rock hard, not merely crunchy, but reminiscent of jaw breaker candy. Additionally, a single cookie is a whopping 60 calories, but these are so hard, I don't want a second one anyway. That's a shame because I really liked the oatmeal cookies.

title: Soft version of Butterfinger. Thick and really sweet
text:
We tried these on a whim at our local grocery store yesterday. I love Butterfinger candy and I love Reeses Peanut Butter Cups, so these seemed like the best of two worlds.

These are basically a Butterfinger bar in a square cup shape. The filling is just a soft, not crunchy version of the original Butterfinger candy and coated in a thick chocolate. It's not crunchy, but there are little hard textured bits mixed in that feel like the real candy bar. I can't eat more than a single cup in a day because these are extra sweet, bordering on almost too sugary for my palate.

title: Very rich and really sweet milk chocolate. One piece gives a distinct energy bump
text:
So...candy that has added caffeine, who knew? I don't know what I was expecting, but good chocolate was a surprise. The milk chocolate is really rich and very sweet - I actually think it's a bit sweeter than a traditional Hershey bar. I couldn't eat more than a little of this at a single sitting, it's just too rich for me.

Each bar is divided into four "bites" so you can gauge the amount of caffeine you're ingesting. You will need a Ziploc bag to keep the rest of the bar fresh after you open it. The bites are thick and taste really good, it's definitely a milk chocolate candy bar. I ate one bite piece after lunch and it was enough. I noticed a bump in energy - the combination of sugar and caffeine will do that. I won't be eating any of this chocolate as an after dinner treat, no desire to stay up all night! This is an interesting product that could really come in handy without being a hassle to obtain or make.

title: Smells and tastes like fresh fall apples. I can't detect the blueberries at all
text:
The very first thing that I noticed when this was brewing is the fruity scent of apples. Drinking it absolutely was all about apples. I barely taste the blueberries or currants.

The tea itself is very smooth and has a clean, fruity aftertaste. Again, I taste only apple here during the cup and afterwards. There's no bitterness and it steeps quickly. Like the chai tea version, each of these bags are individually wrapped to stay fresh until you use them. I like this Rose Berry (apple!) tea, but I prefer the chai version.

title: Fresh tasting peanuts, but they could use just a bit more honey
text:
I like honey roasted peanuts...way more than I should actually. There's a specific pleasure in the combination of sweet, salty and peanutty flavors all in one bite.

This is a nice sized, resealable, plastic bottle which means I can keep it safely in my truck for a snack on the go. The nuts taste fresh and there's none of the bitterness from over roasted peanuts. There is just enough salt. However, I wish these had more honey. They aren't quite as sweet as they should be for my tastes.

title: Smells great and tastes better. Each bag is individually sealed to stay fresh
text:
While I love Chai Tea, I don't have it at home simply because I have not found a really nice tasting home use version. This one is actually very good. It smells wonderful just dry in the bag and steeping is even better.

I can definitely taste the ginger in each cup and I love it. There's no bitterness or weird aftertaste at all, just a bold spice flavor. Since this is decaf, I have been enjoying a cup in the evenings before bed. Each tea bag is individually sealed in its own plastic bag. This keeps them fresh and free of moisture until you're ready to use them.

title: Smells great and tastes better. Each bag is individually sealed
text:
While I love Chai Tea, I don't really have it at home simply because I have not found a really nice tasting home use version. This one is actually very good. It smells wonderful just dry in the bag and steeping is even better.

I can definitely taste the ginger in each cup and I love it. There's no bitterness or weird aftertaste at all. Since this is decaf, I have been enjoying a cup in the evenings before bed. Each tea bag is individually sealed in its own plastic bag. This keeps them fresh and free of moisture until you're ready to use them.

title: Addictive bite size cookies.
text: I love Nutter Butter cookie and they are completely addictive. The cookie part is crisp and sweet, but not overwhelmingly sugary. The peanut butter filling is the perfect blend of peanut butter and sweet. These snack sacks are re-sealable, unlike the full size packages. The smaller, bite size cookies are a nice way to get my fix with a few less calories. Just pay attention to the sales prices here.... they can really be outrageous compared to local options.

title: Great base for a quick casserole
text:
I keep a box of these au gratin potatoes in the pantry all the time. They taste great with lots of cheesy sauce as a side dish, but even better is using this mix as a casserole base.

Add cooked ground beef, corn, spices, and a layer of shredded sharp cheddar. You have a filling, one dish meal in under 45minutes. This is very popular around here on cold winter days. Plus, any leftovers freeze and microwave well.

title: Much too sweet for me to eat more than one. A single serving is just 2 cookies with 190 calories
text:
Tim Tam isn't new to me, but it's easily been 5 years since I have eaten one of these cookies. My husband picks them up when he's traveling because he absolutely loves them. Me....not so much.

The chocolate coating reminds me of European Kit Kats - it's good, but not the same as American Kit Kats. The flavor is different and the milk chocolate is very creamy and smooth. And sooooo much sweeter than our milk chocolate.

These Tim Tam cookies are really two thin cookies sitting on a layer of chocolate cream in the middle - forming one thick cookie. It's a good thing that you sort of get two for one because just two cookies are a whole serving and those two count for 190 calories. There are only 11 cookies in each package, so the high calories won't be a problem for long. I can't eat more than one cookie a day though simply because these are much too sweet and too rich for my palate. I prefer a Milano or Thin Mint because those are decadent, but don't give me a sugar overload with one piece.

title: Soy allergy alert. Real, simple sugar makes it taste great & no chemical aftertaste
text:
I have avoided all gum for many years because of the artificial sweeteners and chemicals, so trying this "new" gum with just real, legitimate sugar was a pleasure. The only flavor you notice is the mint and sweet. No fake chemical aftertaste or weirdness that hides the mint. The flavor lasts about 20 minutes before it is time to discard it.

I do wish this didn't contain soy lecithin - I'm allergic to soy and while I didn't have a reaction to a single piece on two different days, I would not dare chew multiple pieces per day.

title: Iced Tea variety tea bags - weak flavors, requires boiling then cooling. Cold brew bags are easier
text:
I'm a pretty big fan of the Pure Leaf bottled sweet tea because it is very simple & doesn't include any extra ingredients - tea, water and sugar. I do make iced tea at home, but I use the old stand by Lipton Cold Brew tea bags. I was open to trying Pure Leaf bags at home because the pre-made bottles are so good.

This just doesn't quite live up to either the Pure Leaf bottles or the Lipton cold brew bags in either taste or simplicity. The Peach flavor is ok, but I really couldn't detect any peach flavor at all. Honestly, I suspect that the act of boiling diluted the peach entirely. The regular tea is fine, but nothing special. The green tea is very weak and almost flavorless when served as iced tea - I tried it as just hot tea and that was definitely better.

Compared to using the Lipton cold brew tea bags, these are time consuming, old fashioned, and a hassle. I am no longer interested in boiling water, steeping and then diluting/cooling over ice before I can drink a glass of simple iced tea. Making a half gallon at a time requires using 6 or more tea bags at once. I'll just stick to the simplicity of the cold brew bags - toss them in a glass or jug of cold water and like magic....tea. For me, Pure Leaf bottled sweet tea is their sweet spot.

title: Delicious, decadent gift after a hard day - rich chocolate between two scrumptious cookies
text:
Rich, decadent, thick and full of chocolate between the absolute best sugar cookies ever. The chocolate Pepperidge Farm uses isn't actually my favorite, it's a tiny bit too dark for my taste, but the genius here is the two perfect cookies. They are just sweet enough to make everything work in harmony.

There are only 15 cookies in each bag, which seems like a small amount for the price at first glance. However, these are so rich that I can rarely eat more than three in a single day. I regard the original Milanos as a delicious, small gift at the end of a particularly hard day rather than a daily snack. The double chocolate version is definitely a reward.

title: Oreos are excellent at curing cranky husbands and kids alike
text:
Take a grumpy man in his 50s, add one cold, rainy winter day and a list of unpleasant Honey-Do chores and you get more whining & muttering than a pair of four year olds forced to eat all the Brussels sprouts on their dinner plates. Fortunately, the cure is the same for both.... a pile of fresh, original Oreos and a glass of milk.

This big family size package is a bit larger than a regular pack of Oreos, but not enormous. I typically transfer the cookies to Ziploc bags immediately after opening so they stay fresh. The releasable sticky thing on the package is not really intended to work more than a few days at best.

title: Palm oil is not eco-friendly. Soy free, tastes good. Oily & needs stirring
text:
I love peanut butter and I especially love finding peanut butter that doesn't contain any form of soy added. The Skippy Natural line is one of the few national brands that is safe for me to eat due to my soy allergy. This singles pod version is interesting for the convenience factor, but it isn't quite as good as the jar version of the Skippy Natural.

Each pod has to be stirred - a lot - before it can be eaten, spread or dipped. The oil is on top and sort of a gloopy mess and the peanut butter is a hard pasty clump on the bottom of each pod. If I am out on horseback riding trails with this in my saddle pack, I still need a spoon to eat it - I can't just dip apple slices in it on the go. Frankly, it's easier to stick to carrying a pre-made peanut butter and jelly sandwich in a bag with me.

The taste is clean and definitely like fresh roasted peanuts. There's no burnt or bitter undertone or aftertaste. Nor is this "stick to the roof of your mouth" thick. I do like that each pod contains Vitamin E and Niacin - my regular brand, Peter Pan, doesn't. The trade off is that the Skippy pods have a bit more sodium, more sugar, more calories and more fat than a similar serving size of the Peter Pan.

Also.... just for clarity's sake, the Skippy natural ingredients are : Roasted Peanuts, sugar, Palm oil and salt. The Peter Pan ingredients are: Roasted Peanuts, sugar, less than 2% of cotton seed and rapeseed oil, and salt.
I literally see no reason to pay more for the word "natural" on the jar. Especially since palm oil is one of the most destructive products/crops for the rain forests and absolutely non essential & not eco-friendly.

title: SOY allergy contamination warning. Cranberries are tasty & plentiful
text:
Warning - potential SOY contamination from both the processing equipment and the oil used in this mix. If, like me, you are allergic to soy, this is a health hazard. My husband and mother are here and not allergic to soy, so they are enjoying this trail mix instead of me.

The cranberries are plentiful and tasty without being dry or rubbery. The cashews have a sweet, meaty texture and fresh flavor. None of the almonds have been bitter and nothing is too salty. Both of them like this enough that they polished off half the bag in two days. So one star deduction for unnecessary ambiguity about what specific oils are being used in the processing here - is it canola or peanut or soybean oil? Why doesn't Happy Belly actually know exactly what they are putting on their food products?

title: Allergy alert for Soy contamination. Mix of nuts is good & they are fresh
text:
First things first - ALLERGY WARNING for potential SOY contamination due to processing with soybean oil. The ingredients list says may contain one or more of the following - peanut, canola, sunflower and/or soybean oil. Soy allergy can be as dangerous as a milk or shellfish allergy, so avoid these to be safe if, like me, you are severely allergic. Why on earth can't these companies just be specific and honest about what exactly they are using? Either you processed these nuts with soybean oil or you didn't.

As to the quality of the actual nuts.... I am impressed with the fact that almost all of them are intact and the bag smells delicious and fresh when opened. There are way more almonds than we typically care for, but loads of cashews, and the pecans & Brazil nuts are plentiful. Since I am unable to eat these due to the safety risk of possible soy contamination, my husband has had the "duty" of taste tester. He says the cashews are fresh and none of the pecans have had a bitter undertone so far, but a few of the almonds are a little close to bitter. He also feels like they could use a bit more salt. He does like them enough to continue snacking on them without adding any extra salt though.

title: Got a velociraptor in need of a snack? Enormous box of delicious extra cheesy goldfish
text:
ROFLMAO!! I didn't really comprehend the size of this box of Goldfish when I ordered it. Pulling it out of the Prime Pantry box today had me laughing out loud with delight. I could stock a lake with this many Goldfish....or you know stuff my face for weeks.

I love these Flavor Blast Xtra Cheddar fish. The taste is bold and really satisfies that snack urge while reading or watching a movie. The irony of this Godzilla size box is that because of the strong flavor, I actually eat less goldfish in a sitting. I kind of love this enormous cartoonish carton o'fish.

title: Bitter aftertaste from the chicory.
text:
I rarely eat Nutella to begin with, but I bought a jar specifically to compare with this copy cat version from Peanut Butter & Co - Chocmeister. I love hazelnuts and chocolate together - nothing beats the classic Rittersport hazelnut chocolate bar - and I do like the original Nutella spread now and again on a slice of toast in winter.

This stuff though.....not so much. First problem is that you do get the nice flavor of hazelnut, immediately followed by a bitter aftertaste of chicory. This might be less pronounced if there were more sugar or more chocolate or maybe no chicory in the first place. Second problem is because of the bitter hint from that chicory, it makes the milk chocolate taste like semi-sweet chocolate which I really dislike to begin with. I assume they used chicory in order to avoid copying the original Nutella recipe completely. Though.... The design & shape of the jar, look of the label and size is a deliberate replica of the Nutella look.

Third problem is my jar of Chocmeister arrived as a gloopy, oily separated mess. The paper seal was soaked with oil and pealing off when I opened the lid the first time. I stirred everything well and it was edible. It hasn't separated again after 5 days, so I suspect the trauma of being jostled in trucks was the problem. I think that if you're looking for a lower sugar option, this may be a choice to consider - it has the same 200 calories & only 1 less carb for two tablespoons as original Nutella, so the trade isn't entirely sin free.

title: More calories, more fat, more sugar than national brands. Hard & clumpy with separated oil
text:
The idea here is cute and could be handy if only it were better executed. Little, single serving dipping cups of creamy peanut butter that you can take anywhere - like I said, cute. The problem is that the oil and peanut butter are separated in all of the cups in my box. I have a nasty oil slick on top and a dry clump of peanut butter on the bottom. I had to get a stainless spoon to stir/whip it all together in order to eat it - never mind trying to dip anything. There's no way this could be eaten while on horses, on a trail ride in the woods with pretzels or apples.

I ended up just spreading it on bread with jam. The overall flavor is ok. A little bland frankly when compared to Peter Pan and that surprised me. I love peanut butter and eat it at least 4 days a week, but I don't understand what makes this brand so expensive to be honest. I compared the ingredients and nutrition information to that on the Peter Pan jar and frankly, found that a little shocking too considering the price point.

This has 240 calories, 20 grams of fat with 3.5 gram of saturated fat, 130 mg of sodium, 4 grams of sugar and 9 grams of protein per cup.

Simple Peter Pan peanut butter (which is what I happen to have in my pantry this week) 210 calories, 17 grams of fat with only 3 grams of saturated fat, 140mg of sodium, 3 grams of sugar, and 8 grams of protein. That is a serving size the same as the cup. I'm not seeing any reason to buy the Peanut Butter & Co. version over traditional Peter Pan. Both are soy free and made without high fructose corn syrup (Peter Pan has regular sugar) and it is affordable for regular families and doesn't require extra mixing before you can eat it or dip into it.

title: Literally compared to simple peanut butter, this is not as good taste or health wise.
text:
At first glance the package on this stuff would have you believe that it's something amazing and better than good peanut butter, healthier than simple peanut butter even. It is not. Looking more closely at the full nutritional information on the Probar Almond label and comparing it directly to the nutritional information on a new jar of Peter Pan creamy peanut butter reveals that this is no "Superfood" at all.

This is a very expensive pouch of spreadable almond & cashew butter with coconut oil and strawberry flavor, chia, acai, dates and some grasses and gluten removed wheat. It smells very much like strawberries when opened and it spreads pretty well - see the photo. The taste is ok, very thick and pasty with a distinct date aftertaste. I added some strawberry jam and ate it like and sandwich and it is fine that way.

My real problem here is that this so called superfood has only 5 grams of protein compared to a similar serving size of peanut butter - 8 grams. Probar also has 4 grams of sugar - peanut butter...3 grams. Neither of them have any actual vitamins, but the Peter Pan peanut butter at least has 2% of our DV of iron and 190mg of potassium (5% DV) - Probar...0 of both. The Probar is lower in calories (190 to 210) and significantly lower in sodium (25mg to 140mg). Yet the Peter Pan peanut butter has 3grams of saturated fat & 17 grams total fat to the Superfood Almond Butter's 3.5 grams saturated fat and 16 grams total fat. Fewer calories, but almost the same total fat & more saturated fat.

Additionally, the ingredients are awfully complicated and expensive to provide less overall nutrition and protein than an everyday peanut butter with just 4 ingredients. I think this stuff tastes ok, but it's in no way superior to simple peanut butter. Organic ingredients are nice, but if you're paying more, but not getting more then why do it?

title: Allergy alert - contains soy. Tastes great before the hives.
text:
I was falling in love with this popcorn mix. Delicious, distinct cheese bite on the orange cheesy pieces with no weird fake aftertaste. The caramel pieces are sweet and almost have a warm, smoky undertone. The caramel popcorn is very crunchy and a few pieces were actually a bit too hard at first - more like candy.

My problem started after about the 6th handful. The distinctive throat itch and urge to cough. The allergy symptoms indicating soy. Sure enough....soy lecithin in the list. Why? Why on earth does a flavored popcorn made with natural ingredients require soy added?? Soy is one of the top 8 food allergens - right there with milk and shellfish - and soy is not a requirement for cheese, popcorn or caramel. It's just cheap filler and a big disappointment.

So -5 stars for a great tasting snack in a family sizes bag,.but minus 2 for including an unnecessary and dangerous filler like soy. Additionally,.for other allergy suffers.... This.is made in a factory that may be contaminated by tree nuts.

title: Grain, soy & corn free. Smells like fresh fish. No flatulence
text:
I really like the Wellness line of dog treats and canned food. Trying the dry food seemed reasonable. I'm looking for a substitute dry food to keep on hand as a mix in with our regular kibble anyway. (In a situation where our regular food isn't available for some reason, we need an alternative that the pack is accustomed to eating)

The whitefish and sweet potato version definitely smells a little fishy when you first open the bag - not bad, it smells fresh, but there's no doubt this food contains fish. Three of the five dogs were glued to my side as I scooped this food. Very interested in the scent and they all liked it as dry kibble piece treats.

Everyone ate it fine with water, mixed in with the usual food. Only one dog seemed to eat his regular kibble first and ate this last. He's not a big fan of the sweet potatoes in anything actually. None of them have had any flatulence after adding this to three meals. We'll try the grain free chicken next.

title: Real sugar, soy free deliciousness. Shop around for the best deal from Amazon direct
text: I am wholly addicted to the Mocha frappuccino in these glass bottles. It's creamy, chocolatey, smooth with no bitter aftertaste and just the right sweetness. Plus there's only real sugar - no fake sweetener and no soy added!  Word of warning though, never buy these from the random offers here! If you can't find them locally for under six bucks a four pack, then the only reasonable value is the 15 count pack on the Subscribe and Save directly from Amazon.

title: Easiest sweet tea ever - so much better than colas. A snap for unexpected company
text: I've been using the single size cold brew bags and really like them, but switching to these is so much easier. I keep two big half gallon bottles of cold water on rotation in the fridge so I always have one ready to go. I've figured out the best results for perfect sweet tea is to start with a jug of water, leaving some space at the top rather than filling it to the brim, add the sugar, shake it up, and chill in the fridge for several hours. Then add the tea bags. Screw the lid back on the bottle, shake mightily and put it back in the fridge for 20-40 minutes. Perfection.

title: Soy free for the allergic!! Tastes good, spreads easily. Palm oil use is eco-UNfriendly
text:
I'm seriously allergic to soy and finding peanut butter without soy has been surprisingly difficult. Most common brands add soy and a lot of the supposed organic brands do as well - this is entirely unnecessary, soy is considered one of the top eight most serious food allergies, like milk and shellfish. So far, Peter Pan has been reliably safe for me to eat and tastes great, but I am glad to find this Skippy Natural is soy free and provides another option.

My initial impression is very good. The peanut butter is creamy and smells good as soon as the jar is opened and there's no oily skin on the surface. It spreads easily on a slice of bread like it should. The flavor is good - peanutty with a little sweetness, but no burned or scorched aftertaste. It makes a perfectly fine sandwich with grape jelly.

The ingredients comparison between this Skippy and Peter Pan are pretty simple as well. Personally, I could care less about the type of oil because the absence of soy is a life threatening issue. Though the use of palm oil is absolutely not ecologically friendly and is the number one reason for destruction of the Asian rain forests.

Skippy: Roasted Peanuts, sugar, Palm oil, salt.
Peter Pan: Roasted Peanuts, sugar, less than 2%hydrogenated oils (rapeseed and cottonseed), salt.

title: Best treat on a hot day - creamy, smooth pick me up. Subscribe and Save is awesome
text:
This dual flavor 15 pack on Subscribe and Save is the best value for these bottled frappuccinos that I've found yet. For me they work out to about fifty cents less per bottle than the four packs at the grocery store and a dollar less each than the convenience store on the run.

The six vanillas are not my favorite, I drink them because they are in the pack, but my preference would be a Mocha only case. The vanilla has a bit of an aftertaste to me. The Mocha is sweeter and definitely chocolatey. Both are creamy and smooth and are excellent ice cold on a hot afternoon.

title: Shop around and watch the listings for the best prices. Vanilla has a bit of an aftertaste
text: I'm not a fan of the Vanilla flavor - the have a bit of an aftertaste to me, but my husband loves them. The mocha is my favorite of the bottled frappuccinos. However, definitely shop around and check these different listings carefully because the prices are all over the place. The Subscribe and Save variety pack with both the Mocha and Vanilla is the best value.

title: Shop around for the best value - coffee flavor is less sweet than Mocha, but better than Vanilla
text: Be careful about purchasing these and check ever single listing carefully. The prices and quantities vary tremendously from listing to listing on Amazon! The 15 count on Subscribe and Save is a much better value. The Coffee flavor version of these frappuccinos is not quite as sweet as the Mocha and definitely tastes better than the Vanilla.

title: Soy & Egg free if you're allergic. Mild cheese flavor with nice crunch.
text:
Pea flour based snacks are a new thing for me, but I love cheese flavored snacks. Plus I have a serious soy allergy, so anything that's soy and egg free is something that I have to try. These are in a reasonably large bag - 3.5 ounces and it says each bag is actually 3 1/2 servings with 120 calories per serving. That's comparable to the Simply Cheetos Puffs White Cheddar that I love, so we're off to a good start.

The actual snack is a puffy, slightly crunchy greenish color, extruded tube shape. Again, very similar to the Simply Cheetos Puffs White Cheddar. The initial taste sensation is mild cheese, sunflower oil and an aftertaste of green peas. These have a good mouth feel with reasonable crunch and no pasty melting while you chew. I like them, but I'm not loving them.

In looking at the ingredients and nutrition label, I pulled out the bag of Simply Cheetos Puffs to really compare the two side by side. The Peas Please have 120 calories per 1 ounce serving, 190mg of sodium, 1g of sugar and 5g of protein. The Simply Cheetos have 150 calories per 1 ounce serving, 290mg of sodium, 1g of sugar and 2g of protein. Both are soy free and both are free of artificial ingredients. For me, the cheetos have a stronger cheese flavor. The Peas Please are a little better for you overall for sure. It's a toss up that really hinges on your priorities - taste or the lower sodium & higher protein value.

title: Bitter, very dry with a sour aftertaste. Stick to the Cinnamon and Cherry flavors. Allergy safe.
text:
I'm viciously allergic to soy and fairly allergic to eggs. Finding safe, truly soy & egg free commercial snacks is that are also edible is really difficult. I LOVE several of the Enjoy Life products - their soft baked snickerdoodle cookies are awesome and their Cinnamon Bun & Cherry bars are staples in our house. I bought one box of these Cocoa Loco bars locally to sample before committing to a case - thank goodness. Unfortunately, this Cocoa Loco bar is one I won't buy again.

Like all the Enjoy Life products, these are very small and they are expensive. It's just the way of the world with allergy safe foods apparently. The texture is similar to a very dry stale Fig Newton type cookie. The taste is weird with a bitter undertone and a slightly sour aftertaste. I had no negative reactions after eating this other than my palate being offended.

title: Great flavor and soy free.
text: These are a limited edition flavor from Lays, but one I hope they keep around. The taste is absolutely like a bowl of tzatziki dip and it's totally addictive. These are soy free so allergy safe. One note - shop around and do not pay more than a couple of bucks per bag, these are available at the grocery store.

title: The Cherry is a tolerable flavor with a bit more medicine than the Citrus version
text:
I caught a vicious head cold and sore throat on the last day of our vacation. Which meant a 12 hour drive home coughing, sneezing and generally being and making my husband miserable the entire way. We picked up a bag of these cherry drops at a local dollar store (for under two bucks a bag BTW) and they definitely helped. Shop around for the best value.

The flavor is tolerable and better than the regular menthol blue or honey versions, but not as good as the tropical and citrus versions. I did notice when we got home that the Cherry has a tiny more of the active ingredient than the Citrus triple action drops.

title: No weird chemical aftertaste - ingredients you can actually recognize.
text: Surprisingly good! A fresh tomato flavor with no weird chemical aftertaste and no sugar under tones. I've avoided Prego sauces for years because they are so sweet and have a bitter aftertaste from all the preservatives added, but the ingredients on this bottle are simple and straightforward. This is not an overpowering sauce either - I used it with sausage & cheese stuffed ravioli and all the other flavors came through just fine.

title: Holds sauce in the ridges and lends itself well to a variety of recipes
text: Perfection in a quick summer dinner with a bit of ham, black olives, parmesan cheese, black pepper and olive oil. I have really become a Barilla pasta fan after trying the bow ties last year and discovering that plain pasta actually has a real flavor of its own. This penne pasta has little ridges and cooks exactly in about 12 minutes. It's pretty good with chicken and the Barilla bottled Alfredo sauce on an extra rushed night also.

title: Crispy traditional Ritz crackers and creamy peanut butter - excellent combination
text: These are pretty good. They have that traditional crisp buttery flavor we all know and love of the Ritz crackers and a nice creamy peanut butter filling. They don't have that over roasted flavor some of the generic peanut butter crackers get either. My husband has become such a fan of these that he doesn't want the other brands at all anymore. I prefer the Ritz cheese crackers.

title: It's a popcorn chip - genius! Easy to eat and Kettle is loaded with flavor & no kernels
text: I discovered the Kettle flavor of these by accident in a gift basket from a friend and now I am addicted! These have the traditional slightly sweet, faintly fall caramel taste of kettle corn with a bit of salt popcorn. The trick is the flat chip shape that is easy to hold and eat. It gives this popcorn a crisp bite without the obnoxious kernel waste of regular popcorn. I haven't been able to find these locally, so I am delighted to see the variety of sizes and other flavors on Amazon.

title: 9 grams of sugar per serving, soy & gluten free! Tastes good & super easy to make
text:
I love instant oatmeal in general because to be honest, I am lazy and busy in the mornings and I know I need to eat something, but I do not want to cook and I am not going to eat fast food. My recent problem has been adult onset food allergies (soy and egg primarily) so finding convenience foods that are also safe to eat and tasty has been a jigsaw puzzle. I have been eating the Simple Truth Organic brand maple & brown sugar oatmeal until now and frankly, I'm more than a little aggravated that I've been paying a lot more for something that is almost equal and doesn't taste as good.

First - this oatmeal tastes lighter than the original Quaker Maple & Brown Sugar. The flavor is still there, but it's not as strong. Second - this version tastes good and it is far less sweet that both the original Quaker and the Simple Truth Organic. And to me the Quaker Gluten free tastes better than the Simple Truth. Third - here's a little comparison from the back of the two boxes.

Quaker Gluten Free - 9 grams of sugar Simple Truth - 12 grams of sugar
Quaker Gluten Free - 2.5g Total Fat Simple Truth - 2 grams Total Fat
Quaker Gluten Free - 180mg Sodium Simple Truth - 140mg of Sodium
Quaker Gluten Free - 4g Protein Simple Truth - 4g Protein

Quaker Gluten Free ingredients - Whole grain rolled oats, brown sugar, salt, natural flavor, caramel color.
Simple Truth Organic - Organic rolled oats, Organic dried cane syrup, natural flavor, sea salt.
They are pretty similar and the Quaker costs less and tastes better.

title: Simply delicious. Broken up in coffee creates a hazelnut mocha. Nice light crispy sweet snack
text: I tried these in my cookie sample box from Amazon last week and was hooked immediately! I ordered this twelve box multi pack first thing. They are crisp, but not hard and don't have the waxy sort of coating that the Pepperidge Farm version has. The chocolate filling is smooth and seems to just melt away on your tongue. These are sweet without overwhelming like a candy bar. If you find some have crumbled in shipping just dump the broken pieces in your coffee cup - instant hazelnut mocha.

title: Decisions...Decisions....Decisions....so many delicious cookies & just one lonely credit to use.
text: I bought three of the different Sample boxes from Amazon and the cookie box has been the most fun! The standards are included - Oreos and Milanos and classic Walker butter shortbread. Any of those alone are certainly worth the box price for the coupon credit on a future purchase. Then the new to me samples appeared in my line of sight and now I can't make up my mind.  Hazelnut Piourlines or gluten free chocolate chip chip softbake? Or the Belvita breakfast cookies? Or double chocolate softbake individually wrapped gluten free? Decisions....decisions....

title: Relatively mess free fudgy, sweet snack
text: My husband has never let go of his childhood love of Pop Tarts in any flavor, but the Chocolate Fudge are his favorite. They are chocolate, sweet and they don't melt or make a mess. He will grab these as a snack on the go and a desert choice watching tv. Pop Tarts are not a health food, but I guess they are a tiny bit better than a big slice of chocolate cake. I do like the availability of getting these in the Pantry Box - our local store doesn't always have a full selection of flavors on the shelves.

title: Super sweet and delicious occasional treat. Does contain soy if you're allergic.
text: You're not eating a Moon Pie for health food, so let's just get that out of the way up front. This is a chocolate covered cookie covering a layer of marshmallow cream. It's a big ol' gooey, chewy, delicious sugar bomb. The minis are a little bit less sugar per pie and fewer calories so you can eat one now and then without feeling too terrible. These are made with soy so if you're allergic be aware.

title: Soy free and taste free. High sodium and high cholesterol compared to other soups.
text:
Just blech. I am allergic to soy in all forms and my hunt for soy free foods led me to this soup in my grocery store. I am not impressed. It's very bland and frankly, boring. I had to add black pepper and garlic to make it remotely palatable and still the taste was overwhelmingly onion. I will give them credit for having lots of noodles, carrots, peas and little chunks of real chicken though.

What stops me from buying it again is a comparison with Campbell's Bean with Bacon Soup which is also soy free and delicious. I try to eat it rarely because it's high in sodium....well surprise! This Pacific Chicken Noodle is no slouch in the high sodium club. Pacific - 710 mg per serving. Campbell's - 870 mg per serving. That's only 160 mg difference between a heavily processed, mass produced, very inexpensive and delicious soup and an organic, fancy packaged, very expensive, not delicious soup. The cholesterol was surprising too - Campbell's 5mg per serving. Pacific 15mg per serving. The Campbell's is a Bacon soup. Pacific will have to do much, much better to make a repeat customer out of me.

title: No soy, no gluten, no salt! Allergy safe and easy to cook with
text:
I love chicken bouillon added to lots of things for an extra bump of flavor - gravy, mashed potatoes, pasta, soups and stews, and even in the crock pot to dress up a slow cooking chicken & vegetables meal. The problem has always been two fold around here - excessive salt and MSG in most bouillon cubes or powders. Some brands even contain added soybean oil & soy protein- I'm highly allergic to soy in all forms, so finding the Herb-Ox has no soy and no sodium is a double blessing. I can cook with bouillon again.

These packets dissolve in boiling water easily and I had no allergic reaction to sipping a simple cup of broth today with some homemade bread. It needed a tiny bit of salt, but that is just fine - I am aware of adding a sprinkle vs drinking a mug o sodium. For comparison purposes, I looked at a jar of Wylers Chicken bouillon cubes still sitting in my pantry and I am shocked at the difference!

Herb-Ox : 0 sodium. Wylers : 800mg sodium per cube
Herb-Ox : 1 g protein. Wylers : 0 g protein per cube
Herb-Ox : 1 g sugar. Wylers : 0 sugar
Herb-Ox : no soy Wylers : 4 types of soy

title: Amazing taste, safe for soy allergy folks like me. Moist & no artificial sweeteners
text:
I have a severe adult onset soy allergy and a pretty unpleasant allergy to eggs - finding commercial cookies that I can safely eat and taste good enough to want to eat is a little like searching for diamonds in a fig tree. I discovered the Enjoy Life soft baked varieties at our local grocery store and I've been trying each flavor with suspicion. Thus far, I've been utterly delighted!

These chocolate brownie cookies taste amazing. They are moist, chocolately, sweet and have a texture very much like a traditional brownie. There's no weird fake sweetener aftertaste which makes me especially happy. My husband has no food allergies and is a serious chocolate addict, he likes these and had no clue they were dairy, soy, and egg free until I told him. He actually thought I was making it up until I showed him the box. (Just note that these cookies are high in calories despite the small size) Finding the cases on subscribe & save from Amazon has been a bonus as well - the subscription price works out to about 2 dollars a box less than the local grocery store price.

title: Excellent for use in a base model bread machine - shop around for the best value
text: I recently purchased my first bread machine and I remember my Grandmother swearing by King Arthur bread flour, so that is what I bought. It just never occurred to me to even try a different flour actually. I even used the recipe for basic white bread right on the back of the King Arthur bag - it's simple, basic and worked out nicely in my simple Sunbeam bread maker. My first loaf was dense enough for sandwiches, but light and fluffy enough to just eat alone. You should definitely price shop this item though.

title: Soy free with actual meat balls & good overall flavor and texture. Very filling
text: I am severely allergic to soy and this Italian Style Wedding Soup is soy free and safe to eat. I've been on a search for soy free foods that are edible and tasty. This is a little like hunting for diamonds at the local dog park. I discovered Imagine Soups recently at our local grocery store. I think it will become a welcome addition to my no soy collection from now on. I had zero allergic reaction after eating it - though it does contain eggs if you are allergic to those, be aware. The little meatballs are tasty and the barley & navy beans are soft, but taste like what they are. This is lower in salt than most store bought soups and to be honest, it is a bit bland overall. I added a dash of black pepper and it was an instant improvement.

title: Tastes fine - contains Soy and Sucralose. Lots of protein & low sugar
text:
After two major intestinal surgeries last year, my husband supplements his diet daily with a liquid nutritional drink to be sure he's getting all of the protein and nutrients he needs. He varies between the Boost, Ensure and Kroger brands in chocolate and I used to drink one now and then until I developed an adult onset allergy to soy. (All of these include soy and are now off limits to me - including this new Boost Glucose Control version)

I did taste this and we both agree, this is less sweet than regular Boost, but it tastes fine. With only 4 grams of sugar per bottle, the term Blood Glucose Control is pretty accurate. There is sucralose added, so if your digestive tract is sensitive to fake sweeteners, take note. The 16 grams of protein per bottle is a definite plus for getting you going and feeling powered up for the day. I am just disappointed to learn that yet another product is made with unnecessary soy protein isolates and soy lecithin (an emulsifier).

title: Generic berry taste - good starter base for a fruit smoothie
text:
I like these squeeze puree things as starters for smoothies. Just drinking - slurping? - them straight from the pouch is pretty disgusting actually. The other flavor options are Mango/Orange & Strawberry/Pineapple and both of those taste distinctly like mango and strawberry to me. This one is more of a generic berry mix with a slight tartness underneath.

All three of the flavors have whey protein (milk based) and are soy free, but these are pretty high in sugar for a "healthy" snack. I use one as a base in a smoothie, add fresh berries, cherries, some spinach and ice and blend. No need for anything else. It's too sweet for breakfast for my palate, but makes a nice mid afternoon pick me up.

title: Soy free and no seeds. Tastes great on a sandwich
text: I'm on the hunt for jams that are soy free and seedless. The Smuckers versions have all been good so far and this strawberry jam meets my requirements - no allergic reactions and there are no secret soy protein additives in the ingredient list and I haven't run into a pesky seeds after several sandwiches and mornings of biscuits with jam. The flavor is fine - no doubt that this is strawberry and it's not so sweet that you think you're eating a dessert topping. I do think the Smuckers Blackberry is the best flavor of this brand though.

title: Taste great, no allergy symptoms. The puffs are a staple around here
text: I always keep Cheetos Puffs in the house. I love these things despite that distinct orange coating of Cheetos evidence left on my fingers afterwards. I love them even more after recently being diagnosed with a soy allergy - Cheetos are one of the few snacks out there that don't cause me to have allergic symptoms AND taste awesome. I can live with the orange finger tips.

title: No soy! The cheese flavor is milder than other brands, but these are good crackers
text:
Having recently developed a serious adult onset Soy allergy, I am on the hunt for new snack foods that are soy free and still palatable. Those two requirements don't seem to go together often - soy free and tastes good. I bought the Back to Nature Cheddar cheese crackers at our local grocery store this week in place of my usual Cheese Nips.

These are soy free and I have not had any allergic reaction eating them - hallelujah. The crackers are very crispy and the sea salt gives a nice bump without being "salty" like potato chips. My one complaint is that these don't seem to have that super cheesy flavor the Cheese Nips do - perhaps the Nips are chemically enhanced, I don't know, but these are a milder taste. I'm getting used to it and I can always eat actual cheese. I will buy these again simply because I can eat them safely.

title: Tastes fine with pasta & chicken, not quite as thick as the original
text: I love the original version of this alfredo sauce and this light version is almost as good. I'm trying to cut some of the fat and calories from our diet in various places and this is a reasonable place to do so. This sauce has a decent flavor, but isn't quite as thick or full flavored as the original. I added a bit of black pepper and it was fine. It mixes well with pasta and a little grilled chicken.

title: No soy if you're allergic! Tastes great and spreads easily on fresh bread
text: I love peanut butter. It's one of my favorite pleasures in life. What I didn't know was lots of the generic brands and major name brands contain soy! Recently I've been diagnosed with an adult onset soy allergy requiring avoidance of it in all forms. I have been delighted to discover that Peter Pan creamy peanut butter has no soy and it tastes great. I bought a small jar at the grocery store a week ago and have eaten it four times with zero reactions,  so Peter Pan will now be a staple in my pantry.

title: No pineapple anywhere in the ingredients!! 36 grams of sweetener per BOTTLE. Cough syrup aftertaste
text:
I was excited to try this Coconut Pineapple flavored water for a couple of reasons. First this is specifically Soy Free (I'm seriously allergic to soy) and it's all natural. Second I love pineapple and that is a naturally sweet juice, so combined with Bai's shrieks of "no artificial sweeteners" & the "1 gram of sugar" plastered all over the bottle, I was expecting an actual pineapple drink. That is not what this is. At. All.

Bai has added Stevia and Erythritol sugar alcohol to sweeten this drink. 16 grams of the erythritol per serving - 32 grams per bottle. For me that's enough to cause the same digestive upset that sorbitol causes - cramps, flatulence and worse. If you are sensitive to these ingredients, avoid this stuff. Additionally, this combination of stevia, erythritol and sugar has a distinct aftertaste with every swallow that reminded me and a friend of the original, blue Nyquil.

But my biggest reason for the one star rating is because nowhere on the bottle or on the Bai website is Pineapple actually listed as an ingredient in this Coconut Pineapple water with the picture of a pineapple and a coconut on the label. The bottle says "6% Juice".... what sort of juice? It's not pineapple juice. All the label says is filtered water, Bai proprietary sweetener blend, coconut water concentrate, natural flavors, potassium citrate, citric acid, ascorbic acid, coffeefruit extract, white tea extract, sea salt.

title: Easy if you use pre-chilled water, tastes smooth with no bitterness or chemical additives
text:
This is an interesting product. I drink iced tea through the day (instead of colas), but I don't have the patience to boil water, steep a bunch of tea then chill it an hour before I can have a glass. I've tried these bags a couple of ways now and what works best for me is to keep a pitcher of cold water in the fridge, ready to pour.

Cool tap water doesn't work well and water with ice cubes doesn't really work with these bags either. A tall (16 ounce) glass of really cold water, two tea bags, some dunking, sugar to taste, and 8 minutes later produces a medium strength glass of ice tea. There's no bitter undertones, no weird chemical aftertaste and the tea is smooth and simple. My issue is that the tea bags are all open in a sleeve of 25 bags - once you open the sleeve, the rest are exposed to the air and fingers reaching in. Not a great hygiene situation if you have multiple people using these.

title: Easy one dish meal with chicken & veggie add ins.
text: This makes a good, super fast meal with very little real effort. The noodles cook fast and the sauce is light without a heavy,overbearing taste. It lends itself well to the addition of chicken and a little asparagus mixed in. Inexpensive one dish hot meal in 20 minutes - what's not to like?

title: Cake like consistency, tasty and easy to make.
text: After baking 3 dozen of the 4 dozen brownies I need for Thanksgiving day, I realized I didn't get enough of my usual mix, so I grabbed a box of the Duncan Hines chewy fudge to finish with. The mix is simple enough, but requires more eggs and water & less oil than the Betty Crocker version. In my brownies maker these came out taller than the Betty Crocker and these have a more cake like consistency. The Betty Crocker brownies are much denser and have a richer flavor. I like both brands, but the Betty Crocker fudge brownie mix is a bit better.

title: With very hot water & whipped cream these are excellent. Shop around though.
text: These VIA instant mixes are darn near the same as the lattes in the store. The trick to getting a true peppermint and full mocha flavor is to use very hot water and exactly one cup (8 ounces). If you run the water through your Keurig machine, do it at 192 degrees. I add a bit of whipped cream and settle in with a good book. However,shop around on Amazon for the best value on these boxes as the prices vary hugely.

title: Definitely a good flavor - just need a bit more bacon. Wish they were sold locally.
text: I tried the Bacon Mac and Cheese chips at a friend's house today for the first time. The bacon flavor is almost not there,but the cheese flavor stands out. I would buy these if they were available locally. I would like a little stronger bacon taste....of course these are still good enough to snack on while watching the sadness that is the latest season of Doctor Who.

title: Helps me stop eating quite so many cookies in a single sitting.
text: I have a serious Milano weakness. I stopped buying them in the regular packages because the temptation to just eat half the bag while watching a movie was more than I could resist. Rather than listening to the cookies call my name, I stopped eating them. This tub O'Milanos is a sort of compromise. The little packs make you think about what you're doing before you open another one,but they are also very easy to toss in the car and take with you. Or in your purse.... The tub is handy later for other snack size products.

title: Our choice for a small dessert without the big guilt.
text: Great quick snack on the go or small dessert. Lots of chocolate taste and while these pudding cups are sweet, I don't feel like I just had a sugar bomb afterwards. And....you can pretend they are a little bit healthy because they have a bit of calcium and milk.

title: Tastes the same as always, good consistency & upside down cap is easier to use
text: I'm not sure what is really "new" about this recipe. It tastes like pretty much any other yellow mustard on the market today. Unless you're eating a brown mustard or a hot mustard,  there just isn't a lot of difference between the big brand names once it's on a burger or ham sandwich. The main reason we buy this or Frenchs instead of the generic stuff is the consistency of the mustard. This is nice and thick - no watering it down so you use more per serving like some of the off brand versions. I do like the cap on the bottom too.

title: Chewy, not tough. Excellent black pepper bite & not too salty.
text:
My husband and I eat jerky around here as a snack pretty often and we're pretty easy to please when it comes to beef jerky. It needs to be relatively easy to chew. It needs to be peppered and have a hot kick. It needs to never, ever be sweet - sweet is for candy and cokes, not meat. It needs to not be overly salty. (For example, the Jack Links buffalo chicken jerky bites are much too salty, but easy to chew)

This Peppered beef jerky is really good and checks all of our boxes. The flavor has a smokey background and a definite hit from the bits of cracked black pepper on each piece. There's a bit of the soy sauce taste without that sugary sweetness some other brands have and this jerky hasn't been salted to survive the zombie apocalypse. It's chewy, but not tough. The pieces in our jumbo bag are almost all reasonably bite size, a few need to be split in half, but none are tiny left over crumbs or filler.

My one star deduction is just the smell. It smells so strong that my entire car smells like jerky! This isn't a good, yummy steak scent either. I thought it was just me being weird, but my husband and our friends all noticed it too. The jerky tastes better than it smells and Febreeze got it out of the car.

title: Tastes bitter & slightly burnt. Pure Leaf and Gold Peak are better choices
text:
I love bottled sweet tea. This should be a great choice, but it falls very short of both the Pure Leaf and Gold Peak brands of bottled sweet tea. The organic claims mean nothing when the taste is bad. This stuff has an almost burnt, slightly bitter overtone to every sip in every bottle of the twelve bottles in the case we ordered. At first we thought it was flavored with something deliberately, but there's nothing on the ingredients list. It's just bad tasting tea.

The positive points are twenty fewer calories than Gold Peak and Pure Leaf and the Sweet Leaf Organic has no sodium at all. The sugar count is 6 grams less than Pure Leaf and Gold Peak per bottle, but again....it tastes burnt, so we're going back to the other brands.

title: Great cheese taste, but way more crunchy than the regular Lays
text: These have the same excellent cheddar cheese flavor as the regular Lays chips. Each chip is pretty evenly coated, son you never get one that is bland. But...The wavy thing makes these way more crunchy than the regular Lays and for me that's a deal breaker. I like Lays for the light, crisp crunch and distinct flavors. If I want a serious crunch, I'll eat Fritos Scoops with dip.

title: Cheese flavor on every chip without the need for dip - totally addictive. Soy free!
text:
These are really good chips. A nice balance between the slight tang of the sour cream and the cheesy cheddar on every chip. These don't taste quite as salty to me as the regular Lays - that's good and bad.... I am certain that I eat way more of these than I mean to! I think the trick to getting them intact in your Pantry box is to limit soft or fragile things to a single box order and the heavy stuff separately.

Update March 2016

I have an adult onset severe soy allergy and to my delight, these chips are soy free. I have been eating them with no problems.

title: Stays fresher & better flavor than generic versions
text: I use a lot of black pepper in everyday cooking and usually we do a custom blend of fresh ground pepper corns - because my husband took a class and got persnickety about pepper. That's a good thing for the most part, but sometimes you just want a quick dash of pre-prepped plain black pepper over a burger or fries. I've tried the generic versions, but McCormick has the best flavor, even heat and it doesn't clog up in the can if you don't use it daily.

title: Waxy coating on your tongue and funky aftertaste.
text: Meh. Something is missing here compared to the powdered sugar donuts from Mrs Bairds. These are heavier and leave a sort of waxy film on the back of your tongue. The donut texture is dense and more cake like than the Mrs Bairds also. The one good thing about these is the dogs love them and I can easily hide pills in a donut, hand it to a dog and no drama.

title: Surprisingly fluffy, tastes like buckwheat pancakes. Not a great value for your money.
text:
I am not on the gluten free train - I don't have Celiac Disease, so no reason to avoid something that makes food taste great. However, my dear friend does legitimately have the disease and is always searching for products that she can eat safely and don't taste like sawdust or require a fifty percent increase in her grocery budget for the lack of ingredients. Enter this Bona Dea Gluten Free pancake mix. Since she was visiting this morning, we whipped these up to try.

The batter processes normally with an egg, milk and bit of oil. Just like Bisquick, maybe a bit thicker (see the photo), but it stirs easily and cooks fine. The cakes themselves are a tad thicker than I normally like, but again, this batter is a bit thick - if I use it again, I think I will add a dash of water next time. I was actually surprised at how fluffy the pancakes turned out (again, see the photo). They are tender and cut easily and they absorb syrup just as you expect a pancake to. These have a definite buckwheat taste to them. You won't mistake 'em for your granny's light buttermilk pancakes, but they are fine and perfectly edible with a side of bacon in the morning. My one star deduction is for the price/value. We got a total of 7 pancakes out of one entire bag and if you have a family of four to feed, you're going to need both bags of this mix. That's going to get very expensive very fast as my friend pointed out this morning.

title: Too sweet and a little chewy. Not as good as a Ding Dong or the powdered sugar version.
text: Meh. I love the Hostess powdered sugar donuts and I love the Ding Dongs, so these should be a happy marriage of the two. Not so much. The icing is the same as you find on the Ding Dong and the inside texture is a cakey type of donut. But the taste of the two together is sort of...off. They aren't stale ~ they just taste a little too sweet and sort of chewy. I think I will stick with the powdered sugar variety in the future.

title: Old faithful friend after a long, hard day.
text: I admit it. I love Kraft orange Mac and cheese. All the trendy food stuff with gluten free, no carbs, organic whatnot etc etc I simply do not care. When I have a cold, the flu or just a rough day I want comfort food that doesn't require fancy ingredients or any actual effort to prepare. That is what Kraft Mac & cheese is - straight up, creamy, tasty, easy to make and inexpensive comfort food. You can dress it up if you want with tomato sauce or meat or extra real cheese or even cheese and tuna for a lazy bachelor's type of tuna noodle casserole if you're so inclined,but plain straight from the pan into my bowl is just fine too.

title: Light & Airy flavor, no weird after taste
text: I had this for the first time, on a plane yesterday and it's really good. Very crisp,, clean taste with no after taste or chemical undertones. It's a real gingerale taste and much lighter than regular, boring sodas.

title: The lime flavor is fresh and perfect in homemade salsa
text: This is the best version of Rotel out there. Distinct twang of lime with the little bit of the cilantro and the traditional spice of original Rotel. I use the Lime version in a Tex-Mex casserole, when I make my own salsa and when we make old school refried beans from scratch. It adds a bright, fresh flavor.

title: We add Rotel to loads off different recipes. A staple in our kitchen
text: It's hard to imagine a more versatile add in for recipes than a can of Rotel. I use this for the traditional queso dip (Velveeta, Rotel, microwave and serve) and.... mix a can into chili, a quarter can added to refried beans, a can mixed into meat for enchilada filling, half a can in the slow cooker to spice up home made spaghetti sauce, stirred in to King Ranch Chicken, or added to rice and ground pork as stuffed pepper filling.

title: Can be very. dry - add extra milk. Six muffins per pouch, fast & easy snack quality
text: The Martha White wild berry muffins are ok in a pinch, but they can end up drier than expected. I have to add extra milk or my husband won't touch them. These pouches only make six muffins per bag. Normally, I only use the Martha White if I am doing muffins with kids because they are very easy and fast. I won't serve these to house guests or take them as a get well gift type of thing, these are strictly snack quality.

title: Tend to be dry compared to other brands, only 6  out of each bag
text: The Martha White blue berry muffins are ok in a pinch, but they can end up drier than the Betty Crocker mix and these pouches only make six muffins per bag. I only use the Martha White if I am doing muffins with kids because they are very easy and fast. I won't serve these to house guests or take them as a get well gift type of thing.

title: Old school comfort food of. the best kind
text: This one of the few condensed soups we eat. Most are way too salty. The Bean and Bacon is salty, but in a good, cold weather, comfort food sort of way. This has definite bacon and smoked taste that just makes you feel better when you have a cold or life isn't being fair. I actually only add a little over a half a can of water - this makes a thicker, tastier soup. Serve with Clubb crackers and sharp cheese.

title: Like a warm butterscotch candy. No chemical aftertaste,  light roast coffee.
text: LOVE this Butterscotch flavored coffee! Smells like the best memories of fall while it's brewing and tastes even better. No chemical aftertaste, no bitterness at all. This is a light, smooth coffee with just enough Butterscotch flavor to make you think about the old fashioned hard candy, but not so much that you feel like you drank a dessert. Add a bit of real milk and it's sort of a decadent treat that can't quite be replicated at the over priced coffee houses.

title: The jalapeno adds an extra bit of flavor, no heat. Great for burritos
text: I love the original Rosarita refried beans, but the Jalapeno flavor adds just a bit of extra flavor. There's not any real heat or spice that I can detect, but then again our family adds fresh jalapeno peppers to as a side to spaghetti sauce....so we're essentially immune. These beans cook smoothly without being dry. They are easy to spread on tortillas for burritos and with a little melted cheese on top, they are a great side dish.

title: Excellent flavor - mixes with grilled chicken perfectly. Compatible with a rice cooker
text:
I have been buying single bags of the various Vigo flavored rices as they come on sale at our local grocery store - trying each variety to see what we like. This Black Bean & Cuban Rice is really good. It is a tad high in sodium, so keep that in mind. The spices are very good overall, though if you're looking for pepper heat, you won't find it here. The ratio of black beans to rice is just right.

I put the whole bag in our fuzzy logic rice cooker with a bit of olive oil and let the machine do its thing. In the last 7 minutes of the cycle, I added two cups of cooked, cubed grilled chicken and served with a simple green salad. A nice, very simple summer meal that took almost no effort. I'll buy this from Vigo again for sure.

title: Simple, not fancy or trendy. Just comfort food that's easy to make
text: I admit it. I love Kraft orange Mac and cheese. All the trendy food stuff with gluten free, no carbs, organic whatnot etc etc I simply do not care. When I have a cold, the flu or just a rough day I want comfort food that doesn't require fancy ingredients or any actual effort to prepare. That is what Kraft Mac & cheese is - straight up, creamy, tasty, easy to make and inexpensive comfort food. You can dress it up if you want with tomato sauce or meat or extra real cheese or even cheese and tuna for a lazy bachelor's type of tuna noodle casserole if you're so inclined.

title: Nice compromise for a Coke treat without loading up on sugar. Diet drinks are not for me.
text: I love Coca-Cola. I detest diet colas of any kind for any reason. Period. I don't need all the sugar of a full size Coke and I know it. So these little mini cans are a decent compromise. I get my coke fix and don't torpedo my diet. Plus they fit nicely in a small lunch size soft cooler when I know I need to be out at the barn all day.

title: Two full meals for two people in one box - great with red sauce & mini meatballs
text: This mezze penne pasta is exactly right for a quick dinner for two. The box has enough for two full meals. I boil it up and add tiny meat balls and a vodka red sauce. Serve with rolls and a salad and dinner is done. Reheats easily in the microwave the next day as well without being rubbery.

title: Nice mix of flavors and tastes for everyone in the house
text: This is an excellent variety pack with four of the toast & peanut butter,two of the club crackers & cheese, and two of the cheese crackers with peanut butter. The crackers are all fresh and crisp, but not overly crunchy. I can't find the club crackers with cheese locally, so I love being able to get the variety pack in Subscribe and Save. Great snacks and I always keep a couple of packages in the car for emergencies.

title: Excellent sharp cheddar cheese flavor with buttery Ritz crackers - great combination
text: I love the Ritz Cheese cracker sandwiches. We eat cheese crackers and peanut butter crackers almost daily as a go to snack or side with a sandwich lunch. The Keebler version with cheese crackers & cheese had been a mainstay item in our pantry for years, but the Ritz is definitely a better tasting option. The buttery smoothness of a classic Ritz cracker and a very good, slightly sharp cheddar cheese flavor. The trade off is a slightly higher price and ten more calories per package than the Keeblers....it's worth it!

title: Buttery golden goodness - perfect for cheese, soup or dips
text: Simply the best crackers. These are light, buttery, and crisp without being crunchy. They are strong enough to stand up to dipping in soup, chili, or actual dip yet they soften exactly right as you bite into them, adding a subtle flavor of their own. We like them with slices of sharp cheddar cheese and thin slices of apple as an evening TV snack.

title: Nice medium coffee, not bitter or too strong, works fine in an older Keurig
text: These KCups work fine in our three year old Keurig brewer and there's none that DRM drama.  It's a medium brew coffee - not too strong and not bitter and smells great in the mornings. We usually get it at the local grocery store,  but it's nice to see this available through Amazon for those days when it's out of stock locally.

title: Exactly the right mix of the best chips in snack size bags
text: Finally! The perfect mix and combination of chips. 6 each of the Cool Ranch and Nacho Cheese Doritos, 5 of the regular Cheetos and 3 bags of the Cheetos Puffs. These are the little lunch box size snack bags running 130 to 150 calories per bag. I will keep these on my Pantry list since our local stores don't carry this particular mix.

title: Fake chemical flavor and unpleasant aftertaste that lingers
text: These are just not right. At first bite they taste like regular classic Ritz crackers. Then you chew and the very fake bacon-esque flavor seeps through. It's faint and barely noticeable, so you eat the rest of the cracker and the flavor does build. This is unfortunate. There is a distinct chemical fake aftertaste when you swallow and it lingers. My husband said he noticed the aftertaste as well and would prefer either regular Ritz or plain Clubb butter style crackers in the future.

title: Smells and tastes great, easy to do in the rice cooker
text: This is incredibly easy to fix in the rice cooker and the kitchen smells amazing while it's cooking. The saffron and other spices waft through the air and you know something delicious is waiting. I serve this rice with a lightly seasoned roast chicken - just olive oil, rosemary and sea salt. I add baby carrots to the chicken pan in the oven and serve with the Vigo rice. Perfect family meal.

title: Classic American favorite. None of the generics live up to the original
text: My husband LOVES Frosted Flakes and has since he was a child. That classic sweet corn taste is a standard in our pantry. These do get soggy in milk faster than I care for, but apparently that is part of the charm for Frosted Flakes aficiondos. The generic versions of this cereal don't have quite the same taste, so this one of those things where only the brand name will do.

title: Not too sweet, spreads smoothly and tastes like black berries
text: I love blackberry jam above all other flavors, but I don't care for the seeds found in most varieties. I tend to always come back to the Smuckers seedless version because it spreads smoothly, has a consistently good flavor and isn't too sweet or too tart. This works great on biscuits, toast, bagels or an old fashioned peanut butter and jam sandwich.

title: Served like a stew with beef & potatoes - best comfort food around in winter
text: I have been using the S&B Golden Curry mix for many years with great response from dinner guests every time. The hot has enough heat to make it taste awesome and give it a bit of zing, but not so much to make you sweat or tear up. Might still be too hot for kids, but I have never served curry to children, so I don't know. I typically make this with thin slices of beef, carrots and potatoes and serve over rice or noodles in the winter. Absolutely the best, warm up, make you happy, curl up with a good book sort of comfort food. Not diet food, but life is meant to enjoyed.

title: Almost perfect mix....Sun Chips are just filler, but the rest are classic junk food goodness
text: Almost the perfect mix bag. The right quantity of salty with the classic Lays. The perfect straight corn chip with the Fritos. The exact blend between nacho cheese and cool ranch Doritos. Just right cheesy goodness with the old school crunchy Cheetos. And then you reach in to discover all that's left are two sad, flavorless bags of Sun Chips. No one wants those. To be honest, we just crumble the Sun Chips up and toss them out to the squirrels because even our dogs prefer the Cheetos.

title: Insistent flavor, lots of berries, luxury item pricing
text: I like this, but it's not my favorite. There is a very strong bitey, currant flavor and plenty of berries in it,  but it doesn't spread easily. It sort of clumps a bit and that can be difficult in a sandwich. I like the addition of the sloe gin flavor with the black currants, very nice against a mild peanut butter actually. At this price point, I will consider this a luxury and certainly not a regular or daily use jam.

title: Easy to spread on tortillas, taste great
text: I am a fan of Rosarita brand canned refried beans, but these are equally good. I was expecting the fat free version to be lacking in flavor or drier, but the difference is barely noticeable. These microwave easily and spread smoothly on a flour tortilla for burritos. Adding a bit of Rotel with Lime & Cilantro spices them up enough to serve as a stand alone side dish with tamales or enchiladas.

title: Tastes like pure water and nothing else, provides a simple boost with no sugar or weird chemicals
text: I love the Avitae caffeinated water and I keep it on my subscribe and save list every month so I always have a case or two in the house. It tastes that clean, pure water with no bitter aftertaste or hint of any other flavor. I can drink this cold or at room temperature, just like regular water and still get my  caffeine kick - can't do that with energy drinks or coffee. Plus no carbonation - I am not a fan of anything carbonated, so that's a definite plus.

title: Perfect size for a burrito, no need to heat first - soft and ready to serve
text: These are ok tortillas - I actually prefer the Mission brand for flavor and softness, but if you can't them locally, then Old El Paso is a reasonably decent substitution. They are the right size for a beef & bean burrito and if you like a big soft taco, then these work too. They can be used right out of the bag, no need to heat first.

title: Smaller snack size serving, still delicious guilty pleasure food
text: This is a snack size Slim Jim rather than the bigger version you might be used to. That's just as well, if you like these, you already know that they are seriously addictive! And, sadly, so very high in sodium and fat. This smaller size let's me get my salty, greasy, meaty, utter junk food craving met without a complete overdose in one serving. Plus they fit in the glove box of the car, so I can pretend they are "emergency" food.

title: Tastes better than most otger brands, no chemical aftertaste, no stomach upset
text: My husband has been trying all the various breakfast and nutritional supplement drinks on the market for several weeks and he keeps coming back to the old stand by...Carnation Breakfast Essentials. It tastes good, no chalky back flavor, has a reasonable consistency - not too thick and not watery either and there's no weird after taste. The pre-made bottles are more expensive than the old school powder mix, but very handy.

title: Tastes almost as good as home made, very creamy & rich, perfect for a hearty meal
text: I typically don't use any sort of bottled or pre made pasta sauces - way too much salt and sugar in most of them. But...Bertolli Alfredo is my Achilles Heel. It's just so good! It has a real cream base and you can see & taste that. It's very thick with a rich texture that works well over traditional fettuccine noodles and butterfly pasta and stands up to sliced chicken.

title: Almost as good as in the Starbucks store if you use VERY hot water
text: I got addicted to the peppermint mocha lattes and frappaccinos over the fall after spending several weeks with a sick family member in the hospital. The Starbucks in the lobby was just too easy to get to.  However, at over four dollars each, every day, that habit had stop and fast. These VIA instant mixes are darn near the same as the lattes in the store.  The trick to getting a true peppermint and full mocha flavor is to use very hot water and exactly one cup (8 ounces).

title: Tastes good, but Pure Leaf brand has more natural ingredients
text: I cannot make a decent home brewed iced tea to save my life. Thus, I am forced to rely on bottled teas or the kindness of my neighbor. This Gold Peak sweet tea really is pretty good. It has a lighter flavor than the Pure Leaf and both taste more natural than the Arizona. The Gold Peak is just sweet enough without feeling like you had a cola. My one star deduction is because water is first ingredient and there are other additives. Compared to the Pure Leaf which has tea as the first of only three ingredients total. Given the choice, I'll take the Pure Leaf first and this stuff second every time.

title: Love Bush's Original - great with brisket inside a baked potato
text: Nothing is better than Bush's Original Baked Beans if you are going to eat pork & beans out of a can! These are a staple in our pantry and have been for years. They have a sweet, smokey flavor that adds a bit of zing to plain mashed potatoes and can hide the taste of bad potato salad at a family pot luck dinner. (Thank goodness!)

title: Tastes like a peanut butter cookie, lots of iron, do not eat cold!
text: These taste great and travel well in a pocket or saddle bag working horses in the mornings. They don't melt or get messy and in the Texas summer heat they don't make me feel heavy or full afterward - I can eat this and continue riding two more horses and clean saddles. My one complaint is they are almost impossible to eat if they get cold - like chipping off pieces of an ice block with your teeth! I do like the fact that these have a high iron content compared to other similar products. The peanut butter and oatmeal raisin are my favorite flavors and I keep them in the barn and the house constantly.
