They are super easy to prepare - just pop them in the microwave. One pouch made a generous portion to split between the two of us. I also shared a bag with my son.

Everyone thought they tasted great. The rice has a very good flavor. It could not be easier to prepare. I do wish there was a little more moisture though.

I do think this is overpriced, given it is still just rice. You could do your own minute rice in bone broth for a fraction of the price. But we liked not having to stand at a stove, and no complaints at all about the flavor.

title: No one liked these
text:
Well, this one was a fail at our house. My son, who loves pumpkin seeds, did not like these at all. He tried them right out of the package, and then also tried roasting a handful. It was a nope all the way around.

We just did not care for this brand of pumpkin seeds.
However, the neighboring squirrels and a few birds were happy with them.

title: Not a strong lemon taste
text:
This smells great. I have only had the chance to use it once so far. I added a generous amount to a batch of blueberry muffins. Honestly, once baked, I couldn't taste it or smell it. So, I am not sure of what the best use of this item might be.

I also did not care for the suggestion of storing it in the refrigerator after opening. We have a small fridge and I don't have a place for little emulsion bottles.

I would not repurchase this one.

title: There are no words for this one
text:
Well, what can I say about this product? It was a total fail with almost everyone in the house.

Upon opening a bag, my daughter said it smelled a lot like the penguin room at the zoo. She does not like salmon, so I wasn't expecting a good opinion. She hated them.

My son loves salmon, so he was my next victim, er, test subject. My salmon-loving son hated these.

I braved it and tried a bite, despite two other rejections. Yuck. I spit it out.

There were two guys who were interested in them and liked them - my cats. Both were intently interested in them and had to have a piece. Maybe the company is missing an opportunity to market these as cat treats.

So, this was a smelly failure for us, and I'd never buy them or try them again.

title: Has a horseradish aftertaste. Can't refill bottles
text:
I had high hopes for this one. I really did.
We love mayonnaise at our house. We are not vegans, but were willing to give this a try. If you are a vegan, the ingredients probably matter more to you than they did to us. Just a dietary choice.

The bottle design is nice. It uses good ol' gravity to keep the product available to squeeze right away. It was nice to not need a spoon to put some mayo on a sandwich.

The mayonnaise itself was not something I would personally buy again. It had a sharper taste to me, closer to mild horseradish than to mayonnaise. It was acceptable, but I wasn't a fan.

It was a bit disappointing that I could not re-use the bottle. I really liked the bottle design, and had hoped to just wash it up and refill with my preferred mayo. But you can't - the design with the plastic collar is no removable. So, the whole empty container went into the trash.

Overall, it isn't a bad product, just not a taste we cared for. We won't be repeat customers.

title: Tastes good, but not our favorite
text: So far, I am pretty happy with this seasoning. It is for burgers, but we also used it on chicken thighs with good results. I am not sure I would buy it again, but it definitely has a good flavor.

title: Quality product, reliable company
text:
These look really great. They are UNCOOKED black beans, so remember to allow soaking time before cooking.

These come in a very nice resealable bag. But honestly, I would just cook the whole bag at once and freeze whatever you didn't need.

Another quality product from Perez.

title: Really cute packaging, but that's all
text:
Well, this one is more show than substance. You receive a fairly large, colorful cardboard container shaped like a lunch sack. The Cat in the Hat is front and center on the package.

What you actually receive fits in your hand. There is a very small bag of cookie mix (6 ounces), to which you add one egg and 3-1/2 teaspoons of butter. It says to use a small scoop and form into balls.

While it does not say to, you would use the stamp at this time, before baking.

Our stamp arrived with the handle broken off. We'll try to reglue it and see if it will stay. The stamp itself was disappointing. It is a very lightweight wood with just a thin silicone coating over it. I am not sure if the molding is even deep enough to make a decent impression on the cookie ball.

The entire thing is packaged in China. The cookie mix says "made in the USA" and packaged in China. That seems confusing. So do they mean just the cookie mix was made in the USA and shipped to be packaged in China, or was the mix also packaged here and shipped over to be included in the overall package? Given how it is the heaviest part of this package, it doesn't make any sense to do that.

Overall, I did not like this kit.
My suggestion is to buy a quality cookie stamp that you like that will make a deeper impression in the dough. And use your own cookie recipe so you know exactly what you are eating.

Cute packaging, but hard pass.

title: Disgusting!  Hard pass
text:
What would you like to know as a review reader? The idea behind these is okay, but the execution needs work. Please note that ALL food tastes are subjective, so your experience could be different from ours.

When we first opened the package, the first thing that hits you is a rank odor. Kinda like it is past time to get the garbage out. It didn't make us in a hurry to actually taste them.

The tasting was not much better. Out of three of us trying them, including two peanut lovers, NONE of us liked these. They had a bitter taste that matched the smell. I don't know if we got a bad batch, or this is how these are all the time. However, the rest of the bag got tossed directly to the trash, where I am sure they felt right at home.

These were a huge fail on both smell and taste. I cannot recommend them and definitely will not buy these again.

title: Very fresh
text:
Note that I have never had chamomile tea before. Therefore, I have nothing to compare these to. They were packaged well, and should stay fresh well.

I decided to get these just to have on hand, as I have read more and more about the health benefits of chamomile. This is a nice item to keep on hand.

title: Smells good, not much cookie flavor
text:
First impressions. Smells pretty good.

There was a hard chunk on the side that would not mix back in. The taste is not bad. Mostly like peanuts in regular peanut butter, but thinner texture with a weird flavor aftertaste. I would not have guessed cookie dough ever. I tried it with crackers. It left my tongue feeling fuzzy.

Not thrilled with the ingredients, using allulose as a thickener. Perhaps that is why mine has that hard chunk that would not mix back in.

Overall, not horrible. Just nothing special either. I would not repurchase this one.

title: Different from "regular" cinnamon. Great for Thai dishes
text:
Now, I've been cooking most of my life, but there is always something new to learn. I never knew there were different kinds of cinnamon before today! I really never thought about it at all.

As it turns out, the majority of cinnamon most Americans are used to using is Ceylon cinnamon. It has a nice warmth and a flavor we are all used to.

Saigon cinnamon, by contrast, comes from a totally different tree, a cassia tree. By nature, it contains more cinnamaldehyde, the compound that makes the "heat" of cinnamon, than the Ceylon type does. It also contains higher amounts of coumarin, which is a chemical naturally found in cinnamons that can have toxic effects when used in excess. Who knew?
Not me until today! These differences make Saigon cinnamon a little bitter if used in excess, so be sure to measure when using this. (I have always just eyeballed the amount of cinnamon I used in recipes by sprinkling generously, but don't do that with this cinnamon.)

I've also read that the two types of cinnamon cannot be used interchangeably, or it will cause a difference in recipes for certain types of cuisines. Mexican foods most often need Ceylon, while Thai or Vietnamese dishes use the Saigon variety.

I hope this review has helped someone out. I never knew about the different types, but have never really had Thai food much, if at all.

I have not tried this cinnamon out in any recipes yet...it is still too hot here to mess with the stove! But now that I know about the different types, it looks like I'll be looking up dinner recipes to use the Saigon type, rather than just adding it to cookies or pie.
I'll update my review on the taste (which is subjective) once I actually put it in a recipe.

UPDATE: All I can say is YUMMMM!!
I love the flavor of this Saigon cinnamon! It is close to the taste of red hot candies to me. I have been adding a dash (or two, or maybe three) to various dishes and have not found one I dislike yet. It is even tasty on good ol' buttered toast. I highly recommend this. I will definitely be a repeat customer for this item.

title: Surprised by how good it is
text:
I was not sure what to expect with this product. Canned hamburger?? But, the quality of hamburger had tanked where we live - it was like they got bonus points if they added more hooves. We'd end up wasting it, so I had stopped buying hamburger entirely.

So, I decided to try this. They make 14 oz cans and 28 oz cans, with the big ones being the better deal. (If your family size doesn't need the big can in one meal, you can freeze the rest.)

I was pleasantly surprised by how good it was! Note that there is NO additional seasonings - only a salt cube added while processing - nothing else. So, it is ready to season to your own tastes.

We just drained the can and heated the meat up in a small skillet. It allows any leftover fats you might not like to melt away. Add your seasoning, and you are ready to go. We added cumin and chili powder for great tacos.

I added a photo of the last thing we made with this meat...nachos! Perfect for quick nacho snacking. (Note, I can't chew tortilla chips, so I made mine with Ritz crackers. Yum!) We used steak seasoning on the meat instead of taco. It was so good!

For the reviews complaining about fat and liquid...I am guessing they have never cooked ground beef at home before?? Or they have a magical skillet where liquids disappear. Just silly to gripe about fat being in a can of beef!! It is less fat and liquid than if you cooked a pkg of raw ground beef at home.

Note that you do have to watch for price gouging online. This is often available at WM as well for a very reasonable price.

If you have never done so before, please take 5 minutes to watch the video on how they process and can their meats. No water is added, and the meat is cooked in the can.

Anyway, we love the Keystone products. They are great quality, and have a great shelf life. We keep them on hand now, since we can only get to a store about once a month. Very hard to keep unfrozen meat on hand.

title: Smells great!
text:
I love the smell of allspice. It screams "autumn" to me. However, we are still in an incredibly hot summer, and no baking is being done here for quite a while yet.

So, I cannot comment on the taste of the Cerez Ground Allspice yet, but it smells great! I don't forsee any problems.

title: Nice quantity
text:
It is always nice to have a tube of frosting on hand for quick projects. This brand is a larger tube than what I have seen in local stores. It is easy to knead.

It does need to be refrigerated after opening if you don't use it all. I cannot comment on the taste, as we have not yet opened the tube, and I do not want to waste it

Also of note to some, this brand does use some GMO ingredients. Definitely not something I would prefer.

title: Fresh and fragrant
text:
This is a large container of a very popular seasoning. Made by "It's Delish", this is a blend of roasted minced garlic, roasted minced onion, coarse sea salt, poppy seeds, black sesame seeds and white sesame seeds.

I personally can do completely without the poppy seeds. Not a fan. But everything else is good.

When you pop the sealed top, it smells SO good! We are looking forward to trying this on all kinds of foods.

title: Not for us, but still quality ingredients
text:
Well, this item is very easy to prepare.
But I don't have a lot to really say about it. I am one of those people for whom cilantro tastes like soap. So, that kinda makes this rice unappetizing to me.

However, I gave a packet to my son, who prepared it the next time he had tacos. He really liked it, and said it was a great side dish for tacos.

So, this will depend on your love of cilantro, but definitely good quality, nice packaging and easy to prepare.

title: Yummm! Perfect for crusting meats or topping sauces
text:
I tasted no difference in the Happy Belly brand from any we have previously used. If anything, it is a little better, with a sharper taste that is closer to shredding your own cheese than many brands.

We love parmesan cheese, and use it often for mixing with panko to coat foods, or shaking on to pasta or pizza.

I would have no problem buying the Happy Belly brand again. It tastes good, and I like the easy-grip container.

title: Smells SO good! Rich flavor
text:
Oh, this smells so good!
We have not had the chance to use it in a cooked dish yet, but we did use it in a lap salad (a cold cabbage salad dish). It added a wonderful flavor depth, and seemed much richer than the sesame oil I usually use.

Very nice. I would buy this roast again.

title: Very tasty
text:
We love parmesan and romano cheese, and use it often for mixing with panko to coat foods, or shaking on to pasta or pizza.

I tasted no difference in the Happy Belly brand from any we have previously used. If anything, it is a little better, with a sharper taste that is closer to shredding your own cheese than many brands.

I would have no problem buying Happy Belly again.

title: Good white gravy
text:
Happy Belly is proving to be a reliable brand in the food offerings.

This country gravy was very easy to make. While it might not taste like Grandma's homemade gravy, it is certainly a tasty option for today's busy families.

title: Great for low carb, keto or gluten sensitive people
text:
This is a very large bag of arrowroot powder. For those who don't know what to do with it, you can use it in place of corn starch, so this is good for those doing low carb. To keep it fresher, I would break it down into smaller portions and vacuum seal it.

Generous amount, and everything looks good and clean.

title: Great to keep on hand
text:
I had never tried Keystone meats before, but several people in a group I belong to had recommended them. We seem to have a hard time getting decent hamburger where we live, and it either cooks up rubbery, or dies way too quickly. If you freeze it and thaw it out, it just makes it worse. So I was looking for a better way to keep ground beef on hand.

We tried this tonight for the first time. I had read reviews and expected all kinds of nasty. But the truth is, there was nothing wrong with it.

These are packaged with only beef and sea salt. No extra water, no extra spices, just ground beef, cooked in the can at the processing plant.

So when people say it is bland, it is - they leave it up to YOU as to how you want it seasoned.

Yes, there is fat in the can. It is beef, cooked in the can. It will have naturally occuring fat. No fat is added.

What we did was put the entire contents of the can in a glass dish (easier to clean greasy stuff off glass) and microwaved it o power level 7 until it was reheated.
It was a little more soupy than I wanted,
so - hold on - we drained it in a metal colander. Easy peasy.

We were making tacos, so tried the meat as is first. Yes, it is plain. I added some cumin, and boom - taco meat. (I could have added a little chili powder too, but couldn't find it.) We had delicious, filling tacos. The can has a lot of meat in it. One can made 8 tacos for us.

I will DEFINITELY be buying this again. I look forward to trying all the Keystone products.

title: Adorable collection of five Halloween themed Peeps
text:
Peeps - you either love them or you hate them. There seems to be no middle ground! Ha!

This is a packaged set of Halloween themed Peeps. We happen to like Peeps, so our household was happy to see them.

You get one small package each of green Frankenstein heads, black cats, multi-colored Day of the Dead skulls, white ghosts and orange pumpkins. There were designs I had not seen in our local stores before.

They all taste like regular Peeps...marshmallows covered in colored sugar. (I mention that, be ause a year or so ago, the black cats had a black licorice taste that was disgusting.)

These are so cute. They would be perfect for a Halloween party, decorating a cake or topping cupcakes. Adorable, fresh and tasty.

title: Not a fan
text:
I am willing to give this brand a try. I have not been a fan of ground vanillas in the past...they just do not seem to have the oomph needed to boost vanilla flavor.

This is a very small jar. It is 1 ounce of ground vanilla beans (Madagascar beans, should that matter to someone). There are approximately six teaspoons in one ounce. The jar claims a substitution rate of 1/2 a teaspoon of the ground vanilla to be equivalent to one teaspoon of liquid vanilla extract. I have not tried that out.

So, you only get the equivalent of six teaspoons of extract in this jar. That just is not enough to make me want to buy this again. I will not be a repeat customer.

title: Another great Big G spice
text:
We have not tried anything from Big G's that was not top notch quality. They do things right.

The basil leaves are very fresh, strong and fragrant. The size of the jar is very manageable...you won't end up with stale leaves before you can use them.

I just love this one, and would definitely buy it again.

title: Fragrant, generous quantity
text:
This is a LOT of whole cloves!
The bag can be resealed once opened. However, since we don't use whole cloves super often, I chose to vacuum-seal the remainder of the bag.

Everything was very fresh and very pungent. My whole kitchen smelled like cloves! It reminded me of how much I love autumn. My mom used to poke whole cloves into an orange, then sit it in a dish to make the house smell good. My grandma used to poke whole cloves into a ham to add a little bit of spice flavor to them. This bag is generous enough that you can make a LOT of hams with them.

Wonderful smell and generous amount.

title: Great mix
text:
I really love the packaging this company (The Spice Way, Van Nuys CA) uses - strong, sealed mylar bags with a clear window on the back to see exactly what you are getting.

The ingredients are: yellow mustard seeds, coriander seeds, allspice, black pepper, cloves, chili and bay leaves.

I can't comment on the flavor of this blend, as I currently have nothing to pickle! But I forsee no problems with what appears to be a very fresh, varied and tasty blend of spices.

title: Stays fresh much longer in the jar
text:
This is not my usual brand for this type of item. In case you were wondering, arrowroot is basically a form of corn starch from a different plant.

I like it being in a plastic bottle instead of a box. It is much easier to store, and should stay fresh much longer.

title: I just can't get past the visual here
text:
You know, I like to try new foods.
But I have not been able to bring myself to actually eat these. It is a visual thing for me. Sorry, but they visually present as a bag of tapeworms. I know they aren't, but I have not been able to move past that point.

title: Tastes just fine. Great for iced tea
text:
I like this product.
I know artificial sweeteners are a subject of debate, but a lot of folks still need them. Sucralose tastes the best to me.

I use this to put a few drops in iced tea. This is a convenient way to have a few easy drops of sweet in either coffee or tea. I've had a different brand before, but this tastes just as good to me.

title: Pretty good. Super easy to use
text: We love turkey gravy, but only get it when we cook a whole turkey, so once or twice a year. These packets make it easy to get a decent turkey flavored gravy to pour over mashed potatoes any time of year.

title: Very healthy product
text:
These are just lovely little whole flaxseeds. You can use them right out of the package as is, or grind them up for a finer powder. Flaxseed is very good for you. I sprinkle a generous amount into meatloaf, lettuce salads, potato salad and pasta salads. You can also add them to smoothies if desired.
Good quality, happy with this product.

title: Nice to have whole nutmegs to grate as an accent
text:
I was very happy to get a chance to try these. I have long used pre-ground nutmeg in cookie and pie recipes, but have never had the chance to grate some fresh.
You get a generous amount in a resealable bag. I would definitely keep these sealed tight. I have not really noticed any huge difference in using this form though, so perhaps I am just not as sensitive to the spice as others might be.

title: YUMMMMM!  Great on chicken
text:
Growing up in a family where both parents had gall bladder troubles, we were not adventurous eaters and had few spices beyond the most basic.

I was happy to see this sauce and give it a try. I'd never had any Thai food before and wasn't sure what to expect.

This sauce is DELICIOUS!!

I used chicken tenders and cut them up into bite sized pieces, then cooked them in a skillet until they were opaque. I did not temp them, because I knew they'd be cooking longer in the sauce.

After adding the entire bottle, the kitchen smelled so good!! We love peanut butter chicken from an area Chinese restaurant, but could never get it right at home. This sauce comes very close.

It was not super spicy, so I was glad about that. I never developed a love of spice heat. The flavor was so good...definitely peanut-buttery, but you still know it isn't just peanut butter.

We all loved this sauce, and I'd definitely eat this on a regular basis. The only thing stopping me is the online cost, which I feel is pretty high. I've not found it in any area stores, so will probably give in and buy another bottle soon. Yum!!!!

title: Excellent. Perfect for dishes where you want the flavor, but not black specks
text:
I have become a pepper convert over the last several years. I never ate it before, with my only real encounter was my dad over-shaking the pepper container and me getting the overspray! Haha!

But, I have since come to appreciate pepper in many varieties. I actually prefer to use whole peppercorns and a grinder, but there are times you just need a quick sprinkle, so ground is great.

This is WHITE pepper. The taste, at least to me, is no different from black pepper. The reason to use white pepper is esthetic... with some recipes, you just don't want black speckles in it, so the white looks better.

This is flavorful, and has a decent shelf life.

title: Beautiful little onions
text:
These are beautiful jars of cocktail onions. Small bulbs, just right for cocktails or quick stir-fries.
You get two glass jars (which arrived intact, with lots of cushioning), enough to last for quite a while. The onions themselves are just the right bite-size. Very fresh. Very nice.

title: Nice quality and generous amount
text:
I have been searching for the kind of peppers I find in my Chinese food. These seem to be the ones!

I loved this product. You get a generous amount of dried chili peppers. They were very fresh.
There were so many, it would be hard to use them all before they might go bad, so I divided the package up and vacuum-sealed the majority of them in sizes our family can use.

Over all, I am very happy with this product, and will definitely buy them again when I run out.

title: No thank you
text:
Well, I am not sure how this item tastes, because I am not going to use it .
This product was made in India, which has different production restrictions and/or requirements than the USA. It even claims to be "certified organic", but it must be by India standards, because the USA still has no legal description of what constitutes "organic" - the word can be put on anything without legal troubles.

This particular package was made in Aug 2020, nearly a year ago, during the cv shutdowns worldwide.
No thank you!

title: Hard pass. Just make your own mac n cheese
text:
This review is for the Four Cheese flavor. Well, this has cute packaging, and leans heavily on trying to be clever.

It toots its horn about being "organic", but as of this review, there is NO legal definition of the term organic, and food manufacturers have zero accountability when using the term. In other words, you could slap the word "organic" on a box of cookies, flour, green beans, you name it, with no FDA legal requirements. So don't pay more for an unregulated word.

We made two boxes of it.
The macaroni is traditional elbow mac. The sauce was a huge disappointment. Huge. It claims to be "four cheese", so I guess it set our expectations higher. The box suggests things like adding chicken, veggies or panko breadcrumbs to the mac. We could see why...nearly zero flavor on its own!

All we could taste was parmesan. So, if you bought a dollar bag of elbow mac, cooked it, added a little butter and sprinkled it with parmesan cheese, it would be the same (only likely more flavorful) than this stuff. Neither of us could discern any hint of the other cheeses it advertised on its box. This stuff is over three dollars per box. Don't bother, at least with the Four Cheese (which should say "parmesan and three invisible cheeses").

Overall, this was all hype, cute box but no substance. We didn't even eat the whole batch, and tossed it in the trash. Yuck.
Hard pass. Four thumbs down. Even our cats wouldn't lick the bowls on this one.

title: Nutrient and fiber packed little gems
text:
I have to admit, I never thought about eating chia seeds before. In my head, I'd hear "Cha-cha-cha-chia" and visualize them being spread around some terra cotta form.

But these little guys are surprisingly packed with nutrition! They are tiny little powerhouses. I don't personally think they have much flavor, but adding them to other foods boosts your nutrition.

My favorite way to eat them is as pudding. It is simple overnight refrigerator pudding. You can use nearly any flavoring with them. The basic ratio is 1/2 cup of any milk you like (whole, skim, almond, etc) to 2 tablespooons of chia seed. Add the sweetener of your choice to taste, or just used crushed fruits. Mix well, divide into at least two containers, and they will be ready for a snack that offers some protein, high fiber, and great flavors. I sometimes just use extracts to add flavors. (The only thing that I haven't really liked was making it with heavy cream...it created a fluffy texture that I didn't really care for.)

Visually, I think I prefer the white chia seeds, but these black seeds offer the same nutrients and neutral flavor. I would not be able to eat this many fast enough, so I vacuum-sealed the extra to keep the maximum freshness.

title: Good quality, easy to use
text:
Coconut flour is a good alternative flour for those who either cannot have wheat, or do not want it for carb or gmo reasons.

Coconut flour is much more absorbant than regular flour. If you try to substitute 1:1 for regular flour, your baked goods will be very dry. You need to add more moisture, either via a spoon of oil or perhaps an extra egg.

Other than that, this is a nice flour and one that you need to try at least once. We keep it on hand all the time now.

title: What a wonderful, fresh smell!!
text:
I have never used this particular seasoning before, so cannot really compare this brand to others.

What I CAN say, is that you get a generous amount, and this smells WONDERFUL! The ingredients are listed as basil, oregano, thyme, marjoram, lavender and rosemary.
I have never tried lavender as a food ingredient before, so this will be new and different for me. I have included a photo of the mix with the lid off...interesting.

I am going to have to look up some recipes that call specifically for this seasoning!

title: Smells wonderful
text:
Smells GREAT

The first impression of this product was great. I've never personally seen a grinder bottle for anything but pepper or salt.

Second impression was the labeling. It is designed well, and clearly lets you know of the source.

Third impression was pure yum - I opened the inner liner on the bottle, and was hit with the unmistakable smoky barbeque scent. I also tried a sniff with my eyes closed...it was like I had just popped open a bag of smokey barbeque chips, and not in a bad way.

I did not care for the insert materials promoting their cause, as I prefer to judge and/or buy based on the quality of the product, not on attempts to pull heartstrings. But the one product I have tried from their line was very good.

title: Great for low-carb cooks
text:
If you are doing low carb or keto, xanthan gum can be super helpful.
This powder is a non-carb thickener. You can use it to thicken gravies, sauces, pies, soups, etc. Where you might use flour or corn starch, you can use a little xanthan gum.

It doesn't take very much and doesn't really go bad, so this will last most of us a pretty long time. Happy with this product.

title: Ok, but nothing unusual. Basic snackage, no chips
text:
This pack looks like someone went to a big box store and just made mixes of various individual snack items, or perhaps it was repackaged from broken multi packs of other snack boxes.
Nothing really wrong with that. This would still be a nice box to send to a kid in college, or a hungry friend. It could work for school lunches too if your kiddo isn't picky about their snacks.

I'll list the actual count of what we got below. Another thing to note is that twenty (20) of the items were just DumDum suckers, so 13% of the total snacks were inexpensive DumDums.
Everything was name brands.
But I think for most people, especially if you wanted to send snack packages more than once, you should just buy the boxes of your favorites and make your own mixes.

Here is the count, in random order by the way we sorted for the count:
Veggie straws - 2 bags
Chewy Choc Chip granola bars - 10 bars
Fudge Stripes Cookies - 3 bags
Keebler cookies - 2 bags
Takis - 4 bags
Snyders pretzels - 4 bags
Cheez Its - 8 bags
Lance cheese crackers - 10 packs
Famous Amos Chocolate Chip
Cookies - 3 bags
Pirates Booty Popcorn - 4 bags
Chips ahoy - 4 pks of two cookies
Golden oreos - 3 pks of two cookies
Reg oreos - 3 pks of two cookies
Sour patch kids - 10 packs
Swedish fish - 10 packs
Motts fruit bites - 10 packs
Laffy Taffy bites - 10 packs
Twizzlers indiv sticks- 10 small sticks
Dum dum suckers - 20 suckers
Jolly rancher hard candy bites - 5 bites
Jolly rancher sucker - 1 sucker
Airheads - 10 strips ass't flavors
Odd twizzers pkgs - 4

150 pcs, with the following breakdown:

Salty - 22
Candy - 80
Crackers - 10
Cookies - 18
Other - 20
(No potato chips.)

title: Nice quality and generous quantity
text:
Now, this is a BIG package of baking soda! I did not realize HOW big...it is FIVE POUNDS of baking soda!

It comes very well packaged and heat sealed. Once you open it, it can be resealed with a zipper-style strip on the package.

The quality seems very high. If you use a lot of baking soda, either for baking or cleaning (or both), this might be a perfect way for you to buy it. I appreciate that you support a family business with this purchase.

title: Great nutrition in a tiny little seed
text:
It took me a while to get on board the chia seed train. Like many, my only experience with them has been those various terra cotta head shapes. I really never thought about eating them before.

I have become a fan of chia seeds over the last few months. My dental issues don't allow crunchy, but I add them to overnight puddings, mayo salads, etc.

What I have learned, in case you are like me and knew nearly nothing about chia, is that they pack a lot of nutrition for their size. (I have also learned that for purely esthetic reasons, I prefer the white seeds. The black ones can sometimes look like little bugs have invaded your food! Haha!) But either color seed is nutritious.

These are great and great for you. I hope everyone will try them at least once.

title: Okay, would not buy these again
text:
These seem overly dry to me, but I confess that I have never previously used the whole vanilla bean before.

I broke open the package, and vacuum-sealed them by the bean 8n pint sized sealer bags to make them last longer.

They are not super fragrant, but I could see these being soaked in a jar to make vanilla flavored liquids.

title: Nutritious little guys. The white ones look better in recipes
text:
I have become a fan of chia seeds over the last few months. My dental issues don't allow crunchy, but I add them to overnight puddings, mayo salads, etc.

What I have learned, in case you are like me and knew nearly nothing about chia, other than the terra cotta head shapes, is that they pack a lot of nutrition for their size. I have also learned that for purely esthetic reasons, I prefer the white seeds. The black ones can sometimes look like little bugs have invaded your food! Haha!

These are great and great for you. I hope everyone will try them at least once.

title: Yummmmm
text:
We love to make Chinese food, and use a lot of sesame seeds.
This is a great container of sesame seeds. Note these are NOT toasted. We prefer toasted, but it is so easy to toss some in a pan yourself.

I hope Happy Belly offers the same container in toasted some day. But until then, these are great!

title: Not a great one
text: We like the Pili nuts a lot. However, none of us really cared for this flavor/version. The nuts themselves were just fine and a good quality. We just did not care for the seasoning combo.

title: Not one of my favorites
text:
I have tried a few manuka honies. I have to say that this was my least favorite.
I didn't care for the flavor. I am keeping it for potential wound care, but that would be it. Kind of disappointing.

title: Smells great, tastes great!
text:
I love this one!
It has become our go-to for all our mexican dishes. Fragrant and flavorful, we love it!

I made roasted sweet potato and black bean tacos a couple days ago. The kids said you could smell the cumin as soon as you opened the door.

Yummmmmm

title: Oily, not a pleasant mouth feel or aftertaste. Yuck
text:
I had to cut the bag open...I couldn't do it with my hands alone.

First impressions:
The scent is reminiscent of red licorice, but not of the real thing. The first piece felt oily in my mouth...not a great impression. It has a similar texture to licorice. The taste is so-so at best. It leaves a coating on your mouth and tongue that I don't like.

If you have ANY grain allergies, beware! This has a host of ingredients in various incarnations that could be problematic: corn, wheat, sunflower, coconut and made in a factory that produces soy. 😑 They left corn off their warning list, despite corn being a huge allergen. The vegetables and fruits claimed used for coloring are not identified.

I get it that they were trying to get a sugar free version of red licorice. But this is not it. It has a high carb count (whether you subtract fiber grams or not). Better to have a couple bites of the real thing than a bag of this lab concoction.
Hard pass. Maybe project #8 will be better.

title: Another great spice from Big G's
text:
Another hit from Big G's!

We seriously have never had a bad product from Big G's, and this cumin is no exception.

Fragrant and tasty, I actually keep this bottle in the bedroom! I've been on a hummus kick, and we buy a box of plain individually-packaged hummus cups, so everyone can do their own thing. I have been adding Big G's cumin sprinkled over mine for a tasty snack.

Well done, Big G!

title: Looks great
text:
I don't have a lot to say about this product, as I've never tried dried chickpeas. I've always bought canned.

These look great, and I don't anticipate any issues at all. My plan is an overnight soak, then trying them in the air fryer for a crunchy snack.

title: Super fresh, great scent and flavor
text:
These smell so good!!

I have to say that there has not been one thing from Big G's that hasn't been a very good quality and tasty.
They have become a brand I trust.

Another great spice from Big G's, my newest kitchen buddy.

title: Nope!  Not worth it
text:
Well, I have nothing good to say about these. Out of three people trying them, all three disliked them and tossed the rest of the packets out.

The idea behind these is good, but the mouth feel is HORRIBLE. If you like eating greasy sand, then this is the product for you. We all passed! The flavors were just okay, and we could not get past the disgusting texture.

Hard pass.

title: Tastes good, pricey
text:
Mustard all over the bubble wrap, label soaked. Gross.

This item is a premium, stone-ground mustard that comes in a small, ceramic crock of its own. There are a lot of great mustards out there. Honestly, I think this is overpriced.

The mustard smells great, and the taste is ok. There was a lot of leaking and a mess to clean up, so they need to work on their seal.

title: Looks like a nice quality rice
text:
This is a 2-pound bag of jasmine rice.

The packaging is attractive and designed well. You can see the actual product through a clear spot on the front of the bag, which I always appreciate.

The only thing I found odd was the suggestion to store uncooked rice in the refrigerator after opening. I have never put uncooked rice in the fridge (although I have heard of freezing it for a few days to ensure any critters die off). I can't comment on the taste, as we have not had the chance to cook any yet. But the rice looks to be a nice quality product.

Personally, I did not like the "woman-owned company" schtick on the bag. So what? Lots of women own lots of companies - this is not unique, nor does it make your product better. Provide a good product at a reasonable price, and I'll be your customer - simple as that.

title: Tastes great, less sweet, nice sparkle
text:
Coconut sugar is a good alternative to white sugar. It has a lower glycemic impact and tastes a little less sweet. The flavor is a little bit like brown sugar.

The added bonus is that it looks so nice as a topping, alone or in a crumble, for cupcakes and muffins.

title: Another winner from Big G's
text:
Truly, there has not been even one product from Big G's that hasn't been great.

The paprika is another winner, with a wonderful depth of flavor, perfect for any rub or add-in on your egg salad. They do spices right!

title: Very weak raspberry presence
text:
This bottle has a lot of space at the top, so it must be sold by weight, not volume.

I love all things raspberry, so when I popped open the inner seal, I expected to have a burst of wonderful raspberry scent.
Nope.
There is more of a raspberry scent from the syrup I add to my tea than from this item. This smells like a lone raspberry floating in a bottle of water.

Now, I have not tried baking with it yet. Maybe it gets a more pronounced flavor when heated. But based on first impressions I am definitely NOT impressed. I would not buy this one again.

title: Very nice, very fragrant
text:
There is something very satisfying about a large, fresh jar of a spice. These bay leaves are no exception.

The timing was perfect, as I had run out of bay leaves, and despite trips to two stores, I had still forgotten to get some.

I anxiously popped open the plastic seal, and removed the inner seal, then had a wonderful, deep sniff of quality bay leaves.

Looking forward to the next dish to which add them. Very nice.

title: Will experiment with this. Haven't previously used emulsions
text:
This one arrived properly sealed up.
It looked a little cloudly, but not sure if that is the emulsion itself or just shipping conditions/temps. I used a Roku remote in my pictures for bottle size reference.

The part I don't like right up front is how the label suggests refrigerating after opening. I really don't need one more little bottle in our already-tiny refrigerator. That is a drawback for me. I guess it is because there is no alcohol in this blend, but annoying all the same.

I am going to try adding some of this to some orange/cranberry muffins and see how it does.

title: Missing outer seal.
text:
This item arrived without an outer seal, which makes me a little suspicious about using it. The inner seal seems to be okay, but not sure why the outer bottle seal (as is on other flavors of this brand) was missing.

The part I don't like right up front is how the label suggests refrigerating after opening. I really don't need one more little bottle in our already-tiny refrigerator. That is a drawback for me. I guess it is because there is no alcohol in this blend, but annoying all the same.

You get a generous amount in the bottle. I have not used emulsions before, so this will be an experimenting item for me. I will update my review after I have tried it in a few recipes.

title: Pretty good, but I prefer the fine grind salt over the flakes
text:
Himalayan salt is very good for you. It is loaded with extra minerals. We have Himalayan salt lamps in our house, and a Himalayan salt grinder, so was happy to get the chance to try these.

They add a nice, mild saltiness to what you sprinkle them on. But note that you really should have an extra empty, clean container in which to put the rest of the flakes. These come in a bag that is not resealable, so you'll want to keep the rest of it fresh.

title: Ten star product. SO good!!
text:
If you have not tried Mike's Naturals yet, you are missing out!

It might seem expensive up front, but they use amazing ingredients with no junk additives or hfcs in them - just tasty, real food.

This is the second Mike's we've tried.
Both are so good, I just came back and ordered a third flavor. Yes, they ARE that tasty.

These do take a lot of stirring from the bottom up, as the oils rise to the top. It takes a few minutes, as they are super thick. Keep stirring until everything is one consistency... patience needed.

This flavor tastes like you are spreading a gooey cinnamon roll topped in pecans on whatever you are eating it on. So far, we have only done ritz crackers and celery sticks. The ingredients are very filling and satisfying. You enjoy the entire experience. This has a lovely aftertaste of vanilla...no weird chemical flavors.

We seriously love Mike's. They have done this right with great ingredients. If you love cinnamon rolls, please try a jar of this.

title: Not super strong, but will add a nice flavor
text:
These smell wonderful!
I have not yet had a recipe where I needed the whole bean yet.

I cut these open, and vacuum-sealed them in sets of two beans, so I wouldn't waste them.

title: Smells wonderful
text:
Well, this item smells wonderful!
I bet it would be perfect with grilled chicken or pork. I had planned to use it with a crock pot pork roast.

However, it arrived with the lid and seal broken, and goo leaking out. Sadly, we never got to actually use the product.

title: Very tasty with chicken nuggets
text:
Wow. We don't eat a lot of salads here, as our ability to get fresh veggies is limited to about once a month. So, I can't comment on how good it is on salads.
But, I CAN say this tastes great for dipping chicken nuggets in or putting on a corn dog. Yum!

title: Yummmmm!
text:
This one hits the bullseye on every target. It looks great, it smells great and tastes great!
We haven't had any steak to try it on, but it was wonderful on hamburgers.
Excellent blend.

title: Just enjoy a glass of tea. That's the caffeine source, and you don't need the veggie dyes
text:
This comes in a flat envelope. I was expecting a box of packets, like most water additives come in these days.

Upon opening, I was surprised to see little packets of LIQUID. You have to snip the corner off with scissors. If you try to just tear it open, you will lose most of the product.

It goes into the water in a very unappetizing way, blobbing down to the bottom like blood droplets in an iron test. Ew.

Giving the bottle of water several good shakes does manage to dissipate nearly all of the product. (There were still a few tiny droplets that did not really blend in.)

The resulting bottle in your hand is now a very unappetizing shade of mauve (dusty pink). The smell was much like tea that had been left in the container for several days without the benefit of refrigeration. Based on the packaging, I had expected a much more fruity scent and taste.

The taste. Taste is subjective, so take this as you will. I had again expected a berry flavor. This is NOT a berry flavor. Old tea is the first and lasting taste. Perhaps if my water had been cold, it would have helped. Room temperature water enhances nothing about this product. A big ol' "meh" from me. The sweetener is monkfruit, so use your judgement accordingly.

The packaging also misses the mark. By trying so hard to look like cool graffiti, they stuck any possible benefits to their product in tiny print on the back bottom of the paper container. The front is loud hypehypehype, in-your-face, with the important info in tiny print on the back. Really?! And be sure to notice the way they did their neato backwards "S" in their name - an innovation no one has seen since Toys-R-Us in the 1970's! WoopWoop!

Oh yeah. In trying to squeeze the rest of the packet into my drink, a little bit got on my finger - the "natural dyes" in here stained my skin around my finger. *eye roll* In the ingredients list, it uses the word "organic" FIVE TIMES. Spare me. In the USA, there is no legal definition and no legal requirements for a manufacturer to be able to use that word - repeating it endlessly (instead of saying "100% organic") felt like I was being keyword spammed. They tried to be funny in some of their wording, but that missed the mark as well. Not sure who their target audience really is, because it sure isn't me.

Overall, I would pass on this product. It talks big, but doesn't deliver, either in actual benefits or taste. Its only redeeming quality is that there is no aspartame or propylene glycol in it.

Also, I would NOT just toss these packets in a gym bag or purse - if it gets poked by anything sharp, your contents will likely be stained by their "all natural" dyes, just like my finger was. I don't want to carry liquid packets in my purse!

In the time it took me to write this review, all the tea had settled to the bottom on the bottle, while the dyes kept the water mauve. So, be sure to shake this often, because it separates.

Sorry, there just isn't anything redeeming enough about this product to buy it again (or in the first place). Their antioxidant and caffeine claims can be had from nearly any cup of plain tea, without the dye nonsense and mess.

Hard pass.

title: Has the standard mix, plus coriander and caraway
text:
This smells wonderful!
But, it has a couple ingredients that I've never used when making pumpkin pies. The listed ingredients are as follows:
Cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg, coriander, ginger, cloves and caraway.

It isn't pumpkin pie time, so I'll likely give this a try in pumpkin muffins.
We got this in April 2021, and the "best by" date is November 2022 - not horrible, but not as long as I would have expected.

title: Smells great, but I don't have much experience with jerk seasoning
text:
I've heard of jerk chicken, but never had it. I decided to try this seasoning out to see how spicy it might be.

The initial scent that hits you is pepper, like black pepper. The ingredients are sugar, black pepper, coriander, allspice, thyme, red pepper, cinnamon, salt, turmeric and onion.
I guess the heat level will depend on how much red pepper there really is in this one.

We'll give it a try on some chicken.

title: Good, NOT low carb, a bit dry
text:
I wasn't sure quite what to expect with these. But a cookie is a cookie, right? My daughter made them the same day we received them.

She used a cookie scoop to put them on the tray. As it turns out, they do NOT flatten much, so we had haystack-style cookies! I would suggest taking water-dampened fingers and press them down a bit.

The final product is pretty good. If you are expecting a toll house taste, you'll be disappointed. These are much less sweet and not as gooey. My daughter did not care for these at all. However, I liked them. The lack of sweetness made them better, in my opinion (but I don't like toll house cookies, so...). There is a bit of a funky aftertaste that I could do without, but not a deal breaker. Note these say keto cookies...these are NOT low carb.

Overall, I'd give them a 7 out of 10. If the aftertaste wasn't so prevalent, they'd be a solid 8.

title: Dinky amount
text: For some reason, I thought there would be a lot more product than I actually got. Don't waste your time on this one.

title: Dry, dry, dry
text:
Let me say up front that I love chickpeas. I love to just eat them as peas, love them in dips, love chickpea flour with which to cook. I am a chickpea fan.

But I am NOT a fan of this spread. The idea is great. But our jar was so very dry! We tried mixing it up in case oils had settled. Nope, dry as day-old toast. But we gave it a try on round crackers anyway. Ew. Double nope. It broke the crackers as well.

Not only was this incredibly dry, it left three out of three of us with a metallic aftertaste. We all agreed that the closest description we could think of was if you had licked an old, dirty penny - very coppery aftertaste and not very pleasant.

So, although I had high hopes for this one, I just cannot recommend it.

title: Great to keep on hand
text:
Powdered peanut butter is a great item to keep in your food pantry.

Regular peanut butter has oils that will eventually spoil. Powdered peanut butter has had those oils removed...think dehydrated food...so has a nearly infinite storage life if properly stored.

This is one of those items every food prepper should keep in their supplies. Easily rehydrated with water, and a good source of protein.

title: Pretty good, but not one we'll get again
text:
We were anxious to try this one, as it sounded so good.

I would recommend eating this as a side dish to chicken. If you are vegan, maybe a side salad with it. This was very tasty! There are bits of veggies and pineapple with the rice. It was super easy to prepare in the microwave. It wasn't dry like so many rice dishes - I dare say it was just right!

The taste was very good, and we loved all the extra veggies thrown in. But, neither of us could taste any pineapple. It tasted more like a bowl of chili using rice instead of beans.

Overall, good enough taste. However, we will not be repeat customers, mainly due to the price.

title: Two thumbs up from our salmon lovers
text: I wasn't sure what to expect with this one as I had never heard of this brand, but it is actually very good. My son loves salmon, and said it is his second favorite brand now. So overall, all thumbs up!

title: Very nice quality
text:
I started using almond flour for cooking when we did low carb a couple years ago. I grew to really enjoy it.

This looks like great almond flour, and is very finely ground. I really like that they have a clear bottom on the bag so you can see the contents before you buy (in person, of course).

Overall, looks like a great quality product with nice packaging too.

title: Ok for basic snack
text:
Well, I thought these were actually flavored almonds of some kind. They are not.

These are small bags of plain, chopped almonds. I guess if you like to snack on chopped almonds better than whole ones, this is for you. As for me, I'll save these for topping cakes or brownies. The flavor is fine, just nothing I would buy again.

title: Generous amount, great
text:
This is a generous box of pink packets, which are generic for Sweet-n-Low.

This is saccharine. I know a lot of peope have a bad image of saccharine, but that is false. It is no worse than any artificial sweetener, and much better than the one who did the smear job on saccharine to begin with - aspartame. It was cleared as safe only a few months later, but the media damage had been done.

This is safe to use, a nice sugar-free option, and plenty to last a while.

title: Good ingredients. Needs a spice boost
text:
These look positively tasty!!
This is a risotto-style dish made by using vegetable and rice flour which has spices added to it, and extracted to look like rice.

These are the "creamy parmesan" style. The ingredients mostly sound great: lentil flour, chickpea flour, pea fiber, rice flour, sunflower oil, sea salt, dehydrated garlic and onion, parsley, natural flavors (?), lactic acid and lemon juice powder. Not sure what "natural flavors" actually encompasses.

This is also non-GMO, gluten free, vegan, kosher, and has a low glycemic impact. Awesome on all counts.

I really like the packaging design as well. It is designed and laid out very well, with legible fonts and colors used, while displaying the tasty-looking product. The only thing I didn't like was the company name! "Betterer Foods". Really? Funny in the same way you might think saying "pasghetti" is funny, but it was an eye roll from me.

We are making this tonight, and I'll update what we thought of the taste later.
*three hours later*
Ok. This looks good. It smells like chicken noodle soup. Alone, it tastes like pasta with no seasoning. The garlic is very faint and I taste no parmesan at all. This is definitely not bad tasting, just totally neutral, awaiting some sort of seasoning. Not a huge fan of this alone. It would be really tasty in soup or stew. But it needs a flavor boost.

title: Would not buy again
text:
For some reason, I expected this to be lighter than it is. The color is a muddy light gray, and not very appetizing.
I think this was only my misconception, and not a problem with the product.

While there is nothing technically wrong with the product, I just did not care for it and will not repurchase it.

title: A good way to get ACV in your system
text:
So many people like the benefits of taking apple cider vinegar. For many, myself included, the taste is so off-putting, we just don't take it.

Enter a supplement! These are medium sized capsules that nearly anyone should be able to swallow. They are vegetable capsules, for those who do not want gelatin capsules.

Each capsule contains 650 mg of apple cider vinegar. The recommended dosage is two capsules, or 1300 mg a day.

The brand is VitaMountain, but there is no real data as to where these come from or are packaged...it only says "distributed by" Market Raven in Plano, Texas. The bottle I received had a good shelf life of about 2-1/2 years out from now.

So, this seems to be a good way to get your vinegar if you don't care for the taste of the vinegar directly.

title: Mega nasty. Did NOT like them, or the mess they create
text:
We got one of these to try just for fun.

Cover your work surfaces, because this stuff gets everywhere fast. I don't know if it makes a permanent stain, because we threw our towels in the wash right away.

The mix is definitely blue! It does not cook up that way though. It just looks like mud with some blue tint.

I added some vanilla when mixing, because I like to do that in my own mixes. It did not help. These are bland, blue cardboard. Butter and syrup made them tolerable, but still not good.

I will never buy these again in any color. Messy, didn't hold the bright color, and flavorless. Ugh.

title: Yummm!!  This will be a repeat-buy item
text:
I love to try new foods or new brands, so was happy to get to try the Esme brand of shredded coconut.

First off, know this is unsweetened, and not toasted. Toasting is pretty simple in a pan on the stove.

We made mini banana muffins, and I topped them with the coconut. It has a very fine shred on it. They baked up beautifully and tasted great! Next time, I am going to add this coconut to the batter as well. I don't normally add shredded coconut into my baked goods, because I don't like the texture it creates. This one was very fine shreds, and didn't create a gummy texture or chewy weirdness.

I definitely liked this brand and would very gladly buy it again.

title: Not my first choice, but ok. Too powdery
text:
We are long-time nutritional yeast users. It adds a flavor similar to parmesan cheese to foods without adding any dairy.
(And nutritional yeast is not the same as the yeast used in breads. It is grown as a separate item.)

We usually buy flaked yeast, so maybe that is why it looks so different from the brand we normally buy (not sure if I should mention other brands here). This one has a more powdery appearance, similar to ground mustard.

The ingredients are also different from what I've ever used...most just have nutritional yeast. This one says "inactive yeast and vitamin D yeast". I personally find this very odd. The designation of "inactive" could mislead people into thinking this was a form of bread/cooking yeast, which it is NOT. Also, why the addition of something I have NEVER heard of, "Vitamin D yeast"?? Weird.

Overall, to choose this one would be solely for brand name loyalty. I would not recommend this one. I don't like the extra/vague ingredients, nor the powdery texture. I think I'll stick to my preferred brand, which only has ONE ingredient and a flaked texture.

title: Nice, colorful, tastes good
text:
I am not a huge pasta fan, but when I do eat it, I like to use colored pastas.

This farfalla (bow tie) pasta is so cute! There are stripes of red and green throughout. Instead of a pasta salad (which we will do later on), we substituted the rainbow farfalla for the regular pasta in a quick skillet stroganoff. It turned out very nicely! We should have added just a little more liquid to the skillet though, because the very middle of the bow ties were just a little too "al dente" for my preference.

Overall, a nice change of pace. I would buy these again.

title: Very nice
text: This is a nice, large jar of fragrant oregano. If you like to cook, you'll enjoy having this container on hand. Since it is a generous amount, you can make all kinds of sauces, lasagna, chicken, etc. It had a nice, long shelf life as well.

title: Grab a straw!  This stuff is so good!!
text:
Ok, where has this been all my life?

I am not a huge mustard fan, but this sauce is AMAZING. I love it. The entire family loves it.

The Big G sauces have mastered the ability to have a very tasty sauce with a wonderful undertone of smokey flavor. This has no fake, liquidy smoke type flavor, but like it spent hours and hours is a big ol' wood-burning structure.
We've tried it on chicken and meatballs so far, and it is excellent on both.

Whatever they do and however they do it, Big G has turned our entire family into fans of ALL their products. YUMMM

title: Really short life after opening
text:
I am really looking forward to using this powder. I love dragonfruit, but I've never seen it in the area in which we currently live.

BUT, I was surprised by the extremely short use life. Once you open it, it has to be refrigerated and use it within ONE WEEK. Wow, why so short for a powder form? Maybe they just don't have preservatives in them, but a week is just way too short for me to use it up. I haven't even tasted the product yet, because I don't want to open the package yet! I'll update my review regarding the taste once I open it.

title: These taste very good, a little sweet
text:
We had no idea how these would actually taste. I love green tea, but not a big fan of matcha in general.

These are roasted cashews with matcha coating. They are vegan, gmo-free and gluten-free. They come in small, colorful snack-sized bags.

The cashews taste really good. I was expecting a little bitterness from the matcha, but it was actually sweet. It had a slight aftertaste/reminder of cereal, but in a good way.

I personally think the price point is too high. But, I cannot deny that these are a very tasty snack.

title: Big bags, decent value, good product
text:
The very first thing you should know, is that these are much larger bags if flour than I had expected! They are a full five pounds of flour. I took a photo next to a soda can. I had expected a much smaller bag.

Everything looks fresh and wonderful. I'm so glad we are able to try some new foods. The bags have a zip-style closure so your flour stays fresh. Very nice indeed.

title: Good substitute for sugar
text:
I am trying to get back off of sugar. I had succeeded, but several big life events sent me back into the arms of cookies and candies.

I am also careful with which artificial sweeteners I use. Note this is not a debate about whether to use artificial sweeteners...some folks need them.

I am allergic to aspartame. I have found sucralose, while not being the best one for you, tastes the closest to real sugar to me. However, monk fruit is what the sweetener is in a few of my favorite sugar-free foods. Gotta say, it isn't my first choice, because I find the texture to be less-than-desireable...it can be a little gritty.
But I am determined to learn to substitute monk fruit for real sugar in recipes. It will be a learning curve, but this bag has enough to experiment with fairly easily.

title: Tastes musty, did not like it
text:
Well, I've never had macademia nut oil before, so this was a totally new experience for me.

First off, the bottle is beautiful. Someone spent a lot of time designing it, and it shows. It is like they wanted it to look like a bottle of wine. Very pretty design and a push-style lid. BUT, the design also creates some storage concerns.

The bottle has an unnecessarily-long neck. That is wasted space, and it affects storage. The long neck of wasted empty space meant it was too tall to fit in my kitchen cupboards. Even tipped first to get past the cupboard frame, it is too tall. The lid does not securely screw on, so I would never trust laying the bottle on its side. This is a problem. So unless you have the space in your kitchen to keep this out on your counter somewhere, or you have a pantry with tall shelves, this is going to be an awkward bottle to even store.

Now on to the taste. Having never had macademia nut oil before, I'm not the best judge on quality or taste. But I can share that I found the flavor to come off as musty to me. Even though I opened a sealed, new bottle, it tasted like it was so far past it's prime, it was ready to be tossed out. I have no idea about their processes, but I did not like the oil.

So in summary, esthetically-pleasing bottle with poor storage practicality, and a musty-tasting oil. I cannot recommend this item.

title: Dry, barely any sweetness
text:
Would you believe, I am one of the few people to exist that has never had a popular hazelnut brand called Nutella. I mention that, because I have nothing to compare this hazelnut spread to, so will simply share my impression of it.

The spread is very dry. Very. It is thick like peanut butter, but without the oils or moisture. It was hard to spread. Perhaps it was just my jar, or maybe this is normal for this kind of spread. I really don't know.

Along with being very dry, I just did not care for the flavor. It is not very sweet, and definitely not what I was expecting. I thought it would be more chocolately, given the appearance. They use cacao, and apparently didn't choose to counter-balance with monk fruit, stevia or anything.

So this one is a big "nope" from me. I didn't like the texture or the flavor. Yuck.

title: Very tasty
text:
I am not a fan of pasta in general, but thought maybe one made of kale would be good. I am a fan of kale.

Since I don't hardly ever eat pasta, I gave a box to my son. He loves it, loves kale, all veggies, etc. He made up the entire box, then split it into two bowls; one he used an alfredo sauce, and the other, a cauliflower pesto sauce.

I can't describe the taste for you, because I didn't even get one bite! He loved this pasta, and ate all of it himself. Ha! I still have a box left, so will eventually give it a try. But he gave it two thumbs up, and loved it equally with both sauces.

(The photo in a bowl is my son's concoction of the kale pasta, chopped chicken, and cauliflower pesto sauce.)

title: Tasty sauce
text:
I had never heard of a pesto madecwith cauliflower, but was certainly up for trying it.

My son made up a batch of kale pasta and used this pesto sauce on it. Guess what - I didn't even get a bite! It was history! He said it was delicious and he'd buy it again. I guess I need to let him make it again so I can get a bite!
So, this is apparently pretty tasty sauce!

title: Very mild tasting honey
text:
I love honey, and definitely wanted to give this one a try.

I'm still fairly new to manuka honies. I do know the color and taste varies by the region.

This came beautifully packaged in a white and gold cardboard circular tube, and is definitely gift-giving worthy.

The honey itself is much lighter in color than previous manukas I have tried. It is a caramel-like color and texture. The taste is very, very mild.
I can see this being a good honey for teas. I prefer a little stronger honey flavor myself, but there is certainly nothing wrong with this one - just know it is very mild.

title: We all loved this bbq sauce!  😋😋
text:
I had never heard of this brand before, but we love to try new foods and brands, so why not.

I am happy to report that this sauce is DELICIOUS! We've eaten it two days in a row now...with cocktail weenies one day, and as a dip for a pork roast another day.

This has a nice balance on everything. There is some sweetness to it, but not overly so, like some of the mainstream brands of bbq sauce. This has a great aftertaste as well, and no heartburn.

My favorite part is the great smokiness it offers. Not overwhelming, but it doesn't hide either. It has just a really great balance. I'm looking forward to a burger with this sauce on it. And yes, I would definitely buy this one again. Yummmm

title: Very tasty, cost per packet too steep
text:
Well, we definitely have our favorites. When I ordered this one, I was on my phone and thought it was a couple new flavors. It was not. So, I'll share our opinions on these two flavors.

Chicken and Mushroom:
This one visually looks the worst of all of them in the pouch. Smell is ok, but doesnt draw me to it. There is a generous amount of mushrooms in here, fairly large pieces as well. There are little pieces of chicken meat as well. The taste is good. It tastes like a beef boullion base, but has chicken meat in it. This was the only soup flavor that I chose to add crackers to. Closest thing to flavor is like the gravy over a salisbury steak.

Red Pepper and Meatballs:
This one was really yummy! I don't care for overwhelming tomato in soups. This one is a great creamy vegetable soup flavor. Lots of parsley, little bitty meatball bites, and overall very good flavor. This is my favorite so far. 😋 smells great. I would definitely repeat purchase this one.

These are very good quality soups. But their price point is a stumbling stone to me. If they could perhaps pare down the excessive packaging and inserts, they could lower their costs. The heavy cardboard soup pouch toppers are visually attractive, but don't really add value to the product.
But, very tasty soups.

title: Heavy duty, no clean-up, easy to use
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect with these, but you never know until you try one out, right?

These are very THICK bags. They WILL hold that big turkey! We had more than enough room for our 16-lb turkey.

These work much like clothing storage bags. There is a slider closure at the top of the bag, with a little white thing to slide across, to be sure it is sealed (just like clothing bags). The bag itself is very heavy duty. It also comes with strings for tying off the bag, and two clamps to help keep everything inside the bag.

We threw in our turkey, about a gallon of brining liquid, an onion and orange (why not) inside the carcass for a little extra zing. My son used the zip closure, but also tied it shut lower on the bag with the included string.

When it was oven time, we put the bag in the sink. Since we did not want to reuse the brining liquid, of course, we cut a small corner tip off the bag at a bottom corner and let all the liquid drain out. Then we cut the brining bag open just below the string to get the turkey out and transferred to a cooking bag, ready to pop into the oven.

The turkey turned out great, very tender, very moist. The whole process was so much easier than my husband's method of brining the turkey in a 5-gallon bucket! The bags were super convenient, made for a tasty turkey and easy clean-up. I would buy them again.

title: Very tasty
text:
This smells SO good! I have not used a lot of Happy Belly products before, so wasn't sure how good they might be.

We cut up some veggies, tossed them in the HB toasted sesame oil, and into the air fryer. It turned out really good. So good, that batch of veggies never made it to the intended next-day dinner - we scarfed them then and there. Yum!

I am happy to report that this was really good! The smell was great, and the taste was excellent too. I would definitely repurchase.

title: Xylitol - be cautious. Super runny.
text:
[[VIDEOID:335e25184dd5a6584c79c02fa613c8bb]] I love honey. So when I was given the option to try a sugar-free honey, I thought it would be good.

Right up front, know that the sweetener is xylitol. So much xylitol, it is the first ingredient. Why should you care?
1. Xylitol can give a lot of folks loose bowel movements. Very loose.
2. If you have dogs, xylitol can be poisonous to them. If your dog licked your plate after breakfast, it could make him/her very ill.

That being said, let's move on to other factors. The taste was not bad. But it did not taste like honey to me - it tastes like sugar free pancake syrup. I ate it directly, and put it in my tea. It dissipated in the tea so much, I could not taste it at all.
The texture is off as well. It has to be viscous to come out of the bottle. But mine was almost as runny as water. I want my honey thick and wonderful, not watery pancake syrup.

Once opened, it has to be refrigerated. Real honey doesn't need to be, and is shelf stable. Maybe getting cold will help it not be so runny. But then, I'd want it at least room temperature, so we are back to square one.

Overall, not thrilled with the ingredients, the taste is lacking any honey flavor, and the xylitol could cause problems for some people. I would not recommend this brand nor will I be a repeat customer.

title: Only two flavors in the bag
text:
Well, I thought I would try a big bag of gummy worms, since for whatever reason, they are hard to find in our area.

This was kind of a disappointment. The worms tasted fresh enough, but the bag only had two flavors, not three.
There were only orange & yellow worms, and clear&reddish pink ones. There were no green & red worms in the bag at all.

Seems odd. Maybe these are "oops" bags. I'm okay with that, but would have liked to know that upfront.

I probably won't buy these again.

title: Great juice, but hard to find
text:
This is one of the very few fruit juices we drink. The flavor is fantastic. Have it over ice, and it is like a fresh tropical drink.

For some reason, the flavor with the banana is VERY hard to find, and priced pretty high. No idea why, since bananas are plentiful.

We also love the small cans. We keep a drink mini fridge in the bedroom, and these fit perfectly.

title: Great water - watch the bottle size when you order
text:
I love Fiji water.
It sounds weird, but most water gives me raging heartburn. I have tried nearly every brand (including tap) with similar results.
It must be the mineral content that helps it stay in the tummy, not crawl up the throat.

It has a good mouth feel and tastes great too.
One thing to watch when buying online is the SIZE of the bottles. I recently ordered what I thought was my regular sized (500ml) bottles based on the photo, only to receive tiny 330ml bottles. Disappointed, because I would not have paid that much. But still love Fiji. It is hard to find locally.

title: Love Premiere Protein but hate the bottles
text:
I've been using Premiere Protein shakes for about two years now, since a friend suggested trying them. They are great for folks on low carb diets, and help keep the protein grams up for a reasonable calorie count.

I love the aseptic box packaging. They fit perfectly in my mini fridge and easy to handle.

I've tried vanilla (meh), chocolate (my fav), cookies-n-cream (no! Has texture from the "cookie" part that is like sand in your mouth! Nasty!!), caramel (not bad but not my fav), and strawberry (yuck).

So, when they came out with a coffee flavor, I had to try them of course!
I am pleased to say that they taste GREAT. Like an iced cup of coffee with cream. They claim to have caffeine in them as well, but I noticed no boost from them. I still avoid them at night, just in case.

The worst part is the packaging! WHY did they go to these tall plastic bottles like a few other brands use?? They are too tall to go in my mini fridge now, and have to be laid on their side. Hate that!!

Plus, they are way too expensive for what you get. I got them on a special deal, but despite enjoying the flavor, I will not be repurchasing. The cost is out of whack for what you get.

So, Premiere Protein, you made a great new flavor, but the bottles are a bad choice and you've priced them out of reach for a lot of people.

title: Save your money. Not worth the price
text:
Ok, so these taste good. They have Velveeta cheese. It would be hard to not have a decent flavor.

But the amount!! What a joke.
We tried them with the amount of water listed on the cup, and had Velveeta soup. It never did solidify, despite letting it sit for quite a while.
Then tonight, we tried them again with a little less water. That worked MUCH better. But it showed what a minuscule portion you actually get! Ridiculously tiny.

I liked the idea of a shelf-stable quick snack cup. But seriously, at a dollar a cup, save your money. Buy a bag of pasta shells and a small brick of Velveeta at the store and make a batch that way. I use RediTainers for portion control, but you don't have to.

These have a good flavor, just not worth the price for what you get. If these were 3/$1, I might be ok with it. At $1 EACH, would not buy these again.

Where I circled it in the photo is the level of food after cooking that was in our cups. TINY amount!

title: Not one I would buy again
text:
Taste is subjective, of course.
I like trying new teas and coffees.

I love tea, I love caramel. I don't love this tea. I tried it plain first. The caramel is nothing but a light aftertaste. I tried adding sweetener...that helped a little, but not a lot.

I would not buy this one again.

title: Sour swill with a light candy watermelon additive
text:
This was my first time trying the strawberry watermelon flavor. It will be my last.

I looked forward to it. It sounded great. Reality is, it is sour. The watermelon part is more like liquid Jolly Rancher watermelon candy. Okay. The strawberry part... oh my gosh. SOUR. As in, mouth-puckering. Bitter. Right next door to rotten. Not sure if I got a bad batch, or if this is the norm.
Now I'm stuck with 7 more bottles of vile swill. Ugh.

Cannot recommend this flavor at all.

title: Flavor ok. Amount WAY too tiny, what a joke.
text:
Well, I hadn't tried this brand and wanted to give them a shot.

They don't look particularly appetizing, but freeze dried foods can sometimes take on altered appearances.

These taste just fine.
My issue is with the TINY amount of actual food you get. Inside the small bag is a much smaller amount of food. A jokingly small amount.

These are okay, but for the price, the amount you get is like a practical joke played on your wallet.

title: Guess matcha isn't for everyone
text:
I love green tea. I'm not a huge hot tea fan, but love green iced tea with a little sweetener.

I'd heard about matcha, but had never tried it myself. During Prime Days, there was a good deal on this tea, so I thought I would try it.

The bag was very easy to open and to reseal. The tea is bright green. The scent that hit me was like a field of mowed alfalfa! Not really pleasant.

I'd read in other reviews about needing a little more than the bag suggests to taste good. I saw a scoop mentioned, but there was no scoop in my bag. So, I used a plastic spoon and did around 1-1/4 spoonsful. I dissolved it in a small amount of very hot water, and stirred until I couldn't see any individual crystals. I then added cold water to the top and stirred it all again. Then I poured it over a full cup of ice.

First off, the sweetness has a nice balance. While I wanted it just a little bit sweeter, I could have lived without adding any more.

Then came the taste.
If you have ever cleaned off the cutting blades of a lawn mower with water, imagine catching the runoff cleaning water. Got that in your head? Good. Now drink it. That is how this tea tastes to me. (And taste is, of course, subjective.) I had a hard time getting the taste out of my mouth. It hung on for a long time. Yuck.

I'll experiment with this, using different strenghs. Maybe I used too much tea.
But if this is how matcha regularly tastes, then this is not for me. I really don't want to drink boiled lawn clippings.

title: Very pleased, easy to fit in fridge, great portion control
text:
I cannot say enough nice things about this juice.
Cran-grape is one of our favorite flavors in juices anyway. I tried the little boxes on a whim. I am happy to say that these for great into my mini fridge, and provide easy portion control...no more big bottles open for some undetermined length of time, or taking up fridge room.

I truly love them.
Now, dear Ocean Spray, PLEASE start making these aseptic boxes with DIET Cran-Grape for those of us who could use the sugar reduction.

Great product.

title: It's a big "meh" from me
text:
Well, this product certainly has the hype downpat, and feeds into people's mental games that this is awesome, and you are doing your body a favor.

Well, it is just bottled water folks. I can't find a legitimate description of what actually makes up the "essence" portion. Could be just flavoring like Lorann drops.

I have only tried the watermelon, as it seemed to be such a popular flavor. Glad I didn't order a case! You get the faint scent of watermelon when you sniff the open bottle or your glass. There is the TINIEST hint of taste of watermelon when you drink it. They chose their brand name very well.

In my opinion, just buy less per-bottle water, and float a piece of your favorite fruit in it. They even make infusers for water jugs to hold fruits or veggies.

This was my first and last purchase of Hint. Nice concept, but in reality, just more over-priced bottles of water. Disappointing.

title: Great tea, online costs very high
text:
This is a very tasty iced tea. If you are watching carbs or sugar, you will probably want to pass on this one.
It is high carb.

Just a note - watch the prices online. This is available at another Club for about $8/case on sale, around $11 regular price.
