title: This one is NOT all that good
text:
We were happy to see a flavor of instant tea from Lipton that didn't have aspartame in it.
Mind you, this tea has THREE sweeteners in it - really? Did it really need so much?
I vote a resounding NO. Lipton at least didn't load this one up with aspartame, which is a shocker,
but they did use plenty of other sweeteners, then added SUCRALOSE too. Too much. Way too much.

The honey adds a really pleasant smooth taste to the tea. Most of us at our house like pomegranate and
love blackberries, so thought how bad could it really be? Answer - BAD.

This tea is more like kool-aid than flavored tea.
The color is a medium pinkish red, not anything like tea and more like kool-aid.
The taste is overly fruity, with hardly any tea taste at all. We tried adding some
other instant plain tea to it, and it helped somewhat so the box was not a total loss.

Would we buy it again? Nope, not this one.
What could have been a healthy, refreshing tea drink ended up being more of a glass of kool-aid
instead. We'll pass.

title: They lose a star for having so many types of sweeteners...
text:
We tried this recently. I have to say I was pleasantly surprised.

First off, I am allergic to aspartame, so most of the great flavors of drink mixes out there are already off my radar. After living in a place with nasty ol' well water for a few years, I developed a soda habit that I am trying to break. I've tried plain tea, don't care much for it, so looked for a decent flavored tea that I didn't have to boil water for.

Last time at the store, I saw these. The package is a little deceptive, so be aware!
That "five calories" is not even for one whole bottle of water - it is for HALF of a bottle of water with ONE packet mixed in! I guess they didn't want to post double-digits of a whopping ten calories, but that's what it is for one packet.

The sweeteners are THREE KINDS - Honey, Sugar AND Sucralose. Why they needed three kinds, I do not know. It actually ends up being a little too sweet. I make it, them dilute it with more water than it technically needs.

Not sure why Lipton can't just make something ALL natural, or use stevia, which has no effect on blood glucose. They seem to be hesitant to use it for some reason, but I don't know why. They have no problems loading up the other drinks with chemical sweeteners, but avoid stevia! Weird...

I have had a lot of problems with my throat swelling up this week, but I have been sick. I am not sure if it is related to the illness, or because I've been drinking this tea almost exclusively for the last few days. Aspartame makes my mouth, tongue and throat swell up, which is why I read every label now.
Not sure if the sucralose is doing anything or not - I would tend to think not, because my lips are not numb nor is my tongue swollen.

The flavor is really sweet, but I like it. It is refreshing and tasty. Again, a little too sweet for mypersonal tastes, so I "water" it down with lots of ice, and it makes it very good! It's worth trying. This is the only flavor we've tried so far, but will definitely give the others a shot as well. If it helps me give up soda, then that's even better! : )

UPDATE JULY 9, 2012:
Well, it has been incredibly hot here in the midwest, with a heat wave that broke all kinds of records.Of course, I was drinking a lot of tea. These packets are 10 calories each (that "5 calories" on the box refers to HALF of one packet!), and I had either one or two packets each day for the last month, perhaps. We also tried the peach flavor now, and I don't care for it, but my husband and son like it better than this one.

I had to come back and add to the review because of something kind of odd. Now, I am hypoglycemic, so maybe that is part of it, but I have to mention it in case others have this problem. I
I got this tea originally to help me get away from my Pepsi habit. The 24-oz bottles of Pepsi that I buy have 300 calories in the bottle. I make the tea kind of weak, so one packet actually makes closer to 32 ounces of liquid for me - I like the flavor better that way (just personal preference), so by comparison, I am getting just 10 calories for 32 oz, vs the 300 in the 24-oz Pepsi. Savings of about 97% of the calories, which should be a good thing!
Here's the kicker - I have been GAINING WEIGHT since I changed over to the tea! Nothing else has changed. I didn't suddenly
take up eating endlessly, etc, and in fact, have eaten a little less during this heat wave. I put on almost five pounds in the last few weeks of changing over to this tea. Now, from a caloric standpoint, it doesn't seem possible. However, I am one of those people who does much better on high-protein, low-carb. If you have a similar type of metabolism/body, then be aware of these little packets! I think it might be the honey in them creating a non-stop (because I sip tea all day long to keep cool) assault on my blood sugars. I've noticed that I feel hungry more often as well too. I normally don't get all that hungry - just have a few hungry days once in a while. With this tea, it almost gives you the munchies. I haven't indulged, so it isn't from extra food. It has to be the tea.

Again, I have to say that I don't think that everyone will experience this effect, but wanted to bring it up. I think the combo of the THREE sugars Lipton has chosen to use for reasons unknown are having a negative effect for me personally.
I still like the tea, but have now been cutting it down even more, to see if I can lessen the effects of the sweeteners.

I find it odd to think that I could cut out 590 calories a day (I usually drank two of those 24-oz pepsis! Yes, I was bad...) and GAIN weight. It has to be the way all those sugars are interacting with my system.

So, if you are one of those folks who do really well on a low-carb diet, be aware that this tea could cause you to lose progress, or even cause you to gain weight. I have also warned my husband, who tends towards higher blood glucose, to only drink it with meals, never alone like I do. Just an important heads-up on what could have been the best thing to happen to tea in a long, long time.

Lipton - please try making something with stevia, which has no impact on blood glucose levels and has no calories. Why put sucralose into your items, when stevia is so much better? I don't get it - it can't be that much cheaper to use! And I'd pay more for an item that used stevia... what a shame!

UPDATE 06/27/13:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
We have recently tried the latest flavor - Dragonfruit Peach. I have to say that it is very tasty. I love dragonfruit in almost anything. I think the addition of peach was a mistake. It tends to overwhelm all other
flavors. However, this is my favorite one so far of the Tea & Honey line. I think that's because it is green tea which I prefer over black teas. They are still using multiple sweeteners though, so you still have to be aware of your blood sugar with this one.

title: Don't expect great tea... this is kool aid!

title: Powdered peanut butter??  YES!!
text:
Well, I have to say that I thought this would be pretty bad. I admit it.
Deconstituted peanuts - wow. Dry, tasteless, useless, but less fat.

I have to say that I was wrong!
It smells pretty darned good when you open the jar up. It is powder, so
I used a knife to only cut half the lid off. That way, if my fumble fingers
dropped the jar, I would not spill as much of this - it is pretty pricey.

I like peanut butters, but don't eat enough of it to really use it up before
it separates into oil/goo. This is the answer for me. You just mix up what you need!

Basically, this is just powder that mixes with water. While directions say two Tbls of powder
to one Tbl of water, who wants to really measure peanut butter? Best eyeball judging that I could
say for advice, is to get a small bowl, and put enough water in it to be about the amount
that you want to have of peanut butter. Use a spoon or fork, either one. Sprinkle the
powder over the water generously and mix, mix, mix. If it is too runny for your desired use,
sprinkle a little more powder and mix again. Repeat until it is just like you want it. I did find
that I had to mix it more than I thought I would to get the desired consistency/texture. If you
don't mix it enough, it will feel grainy to the tongue.

The freedom to have it slightly runny for dipping, or thicker for spreading, is so nice!
While I honestly thought I wouldn't like it, I really do. I made a small batch up, intending to
dip my finger in it for taste testing. This is how I learned about not putting so much water in the bowl.
I had more peanut butter than I really wanted. So, son and I whipped out a package of Ritz crackers
and thoroughly enjoyed dipping/spreading it on the crackers. There was only the color of the bowl
left when we were through!

If you've been on the fence about it, especially since it is a little costly, just jump in.
I can't see any waste in this product (except maybe spilling it). If you are trying to watch your
fat intake, this is the PB to eat.

I have ordered a jar of the PB2 Chocolate tonight. I simply have to try it too. I hope it is as good
as this one! YUM! Now, I wonder if the same company might want to make this in almond or cashew
versions?! *HINT TO THE COMPANY*

title: They taste okay (some aftertaste), but the ingredients...EW!
text:
Well, like most foods that someone brings to the market and tries to convince
you it is a great substitute for the real thing... the fake is worse than the real.
Add this bar to the list!

We tried this just yesterday.
Admittedly, they are not horrible to the taste. Of course, sweet taste overrides most
other tastes on the tongue, so anything sweet will taste okay upfront.
They taste like one of those sugar wafers (the ones you can get in vanilla, strawberry
or chocolate really cheaply in the stores) dipped in chocolate flavored coating.
It had an odd aftertaste I could not pinpoint.

Then I decided to look at the ingredients. That made the decision that I wouldn't be buying
these again. Why do mfgs continue to make chemical cocktails for us, shape it like a treat
and tell us how great it will be for us? I guess because we keep buying them. I'll pass!

INGREDIENTS OF THE SKINNY COW HEAVENLY CRISP 110 CAL BAR:

SUGAR, whole wheat flour, hydrogenated palm kernel oil, nonfat milk, cocoa processed with alkali,
high oleic canola and/or sunflower oil, chicory root fiber, partially hydrogenated palm oil,
maltodextrin, milk, baking soda, corn syrup, partially hydrogenated palm kernel oil,
vegetable emulsifiers (soy lecithin, sorbitol tristearate), salt, natural and artificial flavor,
TBHQ (?) to protect flavor, ground peanuts.

Wow - what a cocktail of garbage!
anything partially hydrogenated are the artery cloggers and should always be avoided.
I checked the wrapper and did not see peanuts mentioned anywhere except the ingredients list,
so if you have a peanut allergy, you should not eat these bars, but saw no warnings on the label.
Sugars, oils, salts and junk, made to look like a candy bar.

All in all, have a real chocolate bar. Those have sugar too, but they'll taste good
and not be nearly as bad for you as these things.
I'll never buy them again.

title: Very tasty rice - highly recommended.
text:
First off, we all love rice at our house. I also love wild rice and rice pilaf,
although the others are not all that big on those dishes.

So, when I read the descriptions on this, I thought it sounded really tasty, but
had some real hesitations about buying six packs of the rice. I wondered how we'd actually
manage to use six bags before it went bad.

Well, the bags are not all that huge. Each bag is one pound of rice. I guess I had a hard
time visualizing it, but the bags are fairly small. I don't have one in front of me, but they
are maybe 6" square.

Anyway, we made the first bag this weekend, putting it in a crock pot and letting it cook
on low for 2 or 3 hours. Hubby is the chef in our house, and he used beef broth with the rice.
We had it with some sausage for dinner. Let me say - WOW!
This is really tasty rice! Between the four of us, we managed to wipe out the entire pound
of rice (yes, it was that good!), and were figuring out what the next meal with the rice would be!

Watch your prices on this - they vary widely, even across Amazon.
Try to stay under $3 a bag.
Seriously, this stuff tastes great! It was tasty, filling and actually easier to
chew than I thought it might be (I have troubles with crunchy foods).

Thank you Lundberg for a really great blend of rice. You've converted us!

tasty, filling and actually easier to chew than I thought it might be (I have troubles with crunchy foods).

title: Yummy bars!  Very happy with them.
text:
I recently tried the Gnu Fiber bars in Banana and Walnut for the first time.
I have some dental troubles, so I am always concerned as to whether or not I
can even chew some of these fiber bars. Some are so hard, I can't bite them at all.
Others are expensive, and taste like cardboard.

These bars are very tasty! They are soft enough that they are enjoyable to eat.
There is one little seed in the bars that I have a hard time with - guessing it is
the millet. Other than that - they are easy for me to eat too.

I didn't have troubles with them crumbling like another reviewer said. Mine were
very fresh and tasty.

I am going to be buying these from here on out, and plan on trying some other flavors
as well. I wish the cost was a little better, but watch for sales - they are out there
from time to time. If you like banana walnut flavored items, then you'll like this bar.
It tastes almost like a banana walnut muffin. Well worth trying.

title: This will be a real help ...
text:
Wow - I just tried this this morning.
I love both vanilla and caramel, so thought how bad could this be?
I am not normally a fan of warm drinks, but I am trying to break my soda habit.
This tea will go a long way in helping me break this habit!

I have tried it plain, with sweetener and with sweetener/milk combo.
I like just the sweetener the best, but of course, everyone has different tastes.

I don't really taste a whole lot of vanilla, but there is a definite caramel taste,
which is why I loved it so much. This one will be on my regular list to buy from here on out!

Great job, Bigelow! You have converted me from Celestial Seasonings!

title: Wow - can't wait to try the recipe on the label
text:
Well, I have to admit that I love the Bases for cooking.
They do have forms of MSG in them, so those who are allergic need to be aware.
They can say no ADDED MSG, because they add it in a different form than pure MSG
(which you can actually buy - it is a salty powder). If a product has "hydrolyzed __ protein",
then it has a form of MSG, which is created in the hydrolyzing process.

Anyway -
There is a recipe on the label that I look forward to trying, and plan on making
seafood enchiladas with this as well.

Since Amazon sellers almost never list ingredients for their food products, here is
what the jar says on the lobster base:

INGREDIENTS:
Cooked Lobster, Salt, Maltodextrin (a sugar), Hydrolyzed Soy Protein (form of MSG),
dried onion & garlic, potato flour, corn oil, natural flavors (?), xanthan gum,
disodium inosinate and guanylate, soy lecithin, oleoresin of paprika.
(As they'd say on HeeHaw,Yum Yum!)

NUTRITION:
serving size 1 teaspoon.
Calories - 10
Sodium - 680mg
Total fat - 0
Carbs - 2g
Protein - 1g

If you eat out much, you probably are already eating these bases. They are highly concentrated,
so you don't need to use much. You "reconstitute" the base in boiling or very hot liquid and add
it to your recipe. Very easy to use.
The product should be refrigerated after opening.

I'll update my review once I've made something with it.

title: Could make me love movie popcorn again!
text:
Check the dates on the boxes when you buy them if possible.
If you get fresh, Cousin Willie's Popcorns are absolutely delicious!
We buy ours locally, and just tried the Explosion Move Theater Butter flavor.
WOW!

If you like your popcorn a little bit on the greasy side because of the amount of
butter, then you'll love this one! If I am getting buttery corn, then give me lots of butter!
This one requires napkins folks, and it is SO good!

Cousin Willie's has a lot less nasty ol' hulls than most microwave corns.
The kernels pop up nice and big and crunchy.
This is a big hit at our house.
Thank you Cousin Willie - you're the best cousin yet! ; )

title: Very tasty and smokey!
text:
I'd never heard of this type of base before my husband was in culinary school. They used a different
brand, and a beef base had given a certain dish a flavor I'd had in restaurants that was missing in home cooking.

One thing to note - while these bases all say "no added MSG" it does NOT mean they are MSG-free!
It means they didn't ADD any straight MSG. They still have hydrolyzed items in them, which are a form of MSG.
If you are sensitive to it or allergic to MSG, then heads-up, you might be careful about base products.

That being said...

I'd never personally used it before, so was not really familiar with it. I had a great soup recipe that I wanted
to try, but it called for vegetable stock. There was not a drop of stock in the house of ANY kind, so I thought
about my new ham base. I stirred several spoonfuls up in a separate bowl with very hot water, but I probably didn't
have to do it that way. I then added it to my soup, which had lentils, sweet potatoes, apples, regular potatoes, onions
and carrots. I figured ham would work with any of those items individually, so should be okay together.
Wow! The soup was SO GOOD! The ham base gave it a nice, smokey flavor. You'd have thought I put a ham bone with meat
in there with the other ingredients!

The base does have to be refrigerated once it is opened. I put the date on ours with a sharpie, but of course,
that isn't super necessary.

All in all, this was very tasty. I'll be trying it with soup beans and cornbread next.
As long as you watch out for the salt/MSG content, you'll be okay. If you are not sensitive to such things,
then it'll be okay. I can tell you that both my husband and I have problems with MSG, but did not seem to have
any effects from this base.

title: What a great way to package this fruit!
text:
I absolutely love these!
Each canister is filled with individually wrapped prunes.

I am the only one in our house who eats these. I've tried buying the bags,
and buying another type of canister, but they always get dried out before I
can finish them all. This is just right - allows me to eat them when I want to,
and I always get a fresh product.

While they could do better on the cost in my opinion, I have not had a bad one
from this canister from Sunsweet yet. Is it the best value for your money?
Depends on how you look at it - it costs more per prune, but in my case, I have a lot
less waste. So, it is a flip of the coin.

The fruit, however, is fresh, soft and tasty. Don't let an "old person" image of prunes
keep you from trying this yummy fruit!

title: YUMMMMMM!!  Great gummy!
text:
My son and I are both big fans of gummy candies. He had proclaimed his favorite as
the blue sharks, such as these. I'd had them before too, and while I loved the blue
raspberry flavor (yes, in my 50's, blue raspberry is still one of my favorite flavors!),
I'd always found the sharks to be TOO gummy - more stiff, thick and not very easy to chew,
sort of like chewing on a thumb-sized eraser.

He wanted these anyway, so we ordered a 5 lb bag. How big a risk could it really be, after all?
If they were horrible, we'd just never order them from here again.

Well, they were GREAT!!
Without a doubt, we received the freshest gummy candy we'd ever had! The smell alone when opening
the bag was wonderful. Then the taste... super fruity and easy to bite. Each shark was super soft,
super fresh and tasty. I am almost ashamed that the four of us went through this 5 lb bag in a fairly
short amount of time! They were so much better than expected that we "foundered" on them. It was hard
to stop eating them.

Fresh, fruity, tasty - sharks have moved up the scale to be one of my favorite gummies now too.
As long as the sellers keep providing such fresh snacks, we'll keep buying!

title: Great - very tasty
text:
I was pleasantly surprised when I received my order. Honestly, I thought maybe I'd get something that was
stale or very old when ordering online. However, the price at the time was a good deal, so I tried it anyway.

I also received the type of pop tarts that you could sell retail on a counter somewhere.
Rather than the ones in a thin, silver, foil-like packaging, these come with a thick printed plastic
packaging.

The pop tarts themselves are a little bit thicker than the ones you get off the store shelves in the
boxes of 8 or 12. I love that, because the crust part is really the only part I like. This flavor is
good, because it isn't as sickeningly sweet (despite being brown sugar) as some of the jelly-like flavors.

All in all, I received a fresh product that was very tasty. I'll be happy to order them again as
sales pop up.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Update Nov 9, 2011:
Well, I placed a second order.
This one was not nearly as fresh, and contained one box less than the last order.
So, be sure to read the listing carefully to see how many you are getting. I thought I had
notice of a sale, but it was really a count decrease.

This batch came with a couple of the boxes' perforations already popped (not clear open)
and nothing was as fresh as the previous order. Not sure why, but I didn't like the
quality swings of this item. I'm dinging a star for lack of consistently fresh product.

title: So good!
text:
These are really incredible. I am not a huge fan of cheetos in general,
but I do love white cheddar, and had to give them a try.
They taste great!
I don't recommend buying them online here unless you are totally desperate though,
because the cost with shipping works out to over $6 a bag. That's a very pricey snack.
But, look for it in your stores - both Cheetos and Lays make very good natural
white cheddar puffs.

title: Well, so far so good - first order very good
text:
This was my first time ordering these cherries.
My husband has gout, so I thought this might be a good snack to help him ward off attacks.
(Cherries are known gout helpers.)

I wasn't thrilled with the price, but when it got down to a more reasonable cost (under $25), I
ordered one to try. I was not sure I really wanted to, with all the mixed reviews of some orders
being moist and great and some being nasty and dry.

The box we got arrived quickly and in good shape.
I'll post photos later, but wanted to get the review going.
I must say that I had a much bigger box in the picture in my head.
Yes, you get this box, but it is SMALL! I know they list the weight, but it was a little
hard for me to visualize four lbs of dried cherries. I'm probably not the only one.

Upon opening the box, all the cherries are in one sealed blue bag. I guess the blue
color helps with keeping the condition of the fruit from deteriorating.
I cut it open very carefully, and decided to bag them up in snack-size zipper bags.
(I was originally going to use our vacuum sealer to make smaller bags, but the quantity
was less than I had visualized. Zip top snack size worked great. I used a spoon to fill them
to not touch any of the other cherries.

Then came the big mistake - I ate a pinch of them.
I say mistake, because my husband is going to have to be quick to get some!
These were a little more tart than I thought they'd be, but they are delicious.
The bag we got had reasonable-sized cherries, around a fat raisin size. They were
very moist. As I let some sit in my mouth, they seemed to plump even more. Upon
chewing, they released a wonderful flavor that made my mouth water a little bit.

I can see using these in muffins and cookies, in your cereal, snack mixes and just eating.
So far, I've had more of the cherries than my husband. (Hey, you snooze, you lose!)
They are wonderful.

Not sure a second order would be the same quality though. I am a bit concerned with all the mixed
reviews about getting a consistent quality for the second order. They are too expensive to have
something dry and tasteless arrive at the door.

All in all, happy with this purchase.

title: Very tasty spread - would definitely get it again.
text:
We ordered two jars of the Amish spreads, which arrived today.
The seller packs carefully, and the jars arrived quickly and in fine shape.

We anxiously opened them both with spoons in hand to enjoy.
Both spreads were very tasty.
The apple blueberry is a definite keeper and I would buy it again without a blink.
The cinnamon was a little heavy, but it was still very tasty.

The cherry was a little too spicy in my opinion - it seemed again like there was
too much cinnamon in it, to the point of overriding any cherry flavor.
If I was tasting that one blindfolded, I am not sure I could tell it was cherry!
It was still very good, just not as "cherry-ful" as other fruit butters I've had.
The spread looked lovely - you could see the cherries, but the taste was obscured
by the spices. Note that I love cinnamon in all forms - in cookies, on toast,
in spreads, in candy, in gum. So, I am not picking on it - it just seemed to be out of balance.

Now, I do want to mention one thing that bothered me a little bit.
I saw no place or way that these jars were sanitarily sealed.
In other words, there was no lid to pop up, no inner seal, no plastic seal on the edges.
I am guessing that the jars are filled as orders come in, but it still
bugged me that the screw-on lids didn't seem to have any real seals.

I would have liked to at least see those plastic heat-shrink seals around
the lids so I could have at least felt I was the first person dipping in the jar!
I did deduct one star for the lack of a visible sanitation process.
The jar does say to refrigerate after opening. Since there is no seal inside or out,
I would refrigerate immediately upon receipt no matter what.

So, I would recommend the apple blueberry butter.
The cherry butter - well, I am going to keep trying other kinds.

title: Very tasty milk in a great packaging
text:
Just had my first Horizon vanilla milk. It had been chilled in the fridge, so cold enough.

First off, I love the packaging. I love the design, I love the straw that doesn't
fall down into the packaging because of good design.

The taste was very good and fresh. My first impression was that it was like a melted
vanilla milk shake. It did not taste artificial or overpowering. It wasn't quite thick/creamy
enough to make me think of homemade ice cream, but still a great taste.

I like the hormone-free aspect of this product as well.

I would not hesitate to buy it again!

title: Very tasty!  I like it so far
text:
I was very pleasantly surprised to see a Crystal Light product that wasn't loaded with aspartame!

I hope they get on the stevia bandwagon (or even go back to saccharine since it has long since been proven
to be perfectly safe) and start making more flavors.

I love the drink mix packets anyway, and I'm always happy when there's a really tasty flavor.
This one had my attention as soon as I opened it - it smells like cotton candy when in the powder form!
(It made me wish I had some!) I had to cut the packet open - the little corners don't always tear
too well.

It dissolved fairly easily, and makes your water a shade of pink.
It tastes really good, even though I had room temp water, not cold water.
It is a little bit strong in the 16.9 oz bottle (since I took a drink out of it before
adding the powder), but nothing outrageous or overwhelming.

All in all, I'd buy it again.

Crystal Light - I hope you'll start making more flavors in the Pure Fitness line.
I'd buy your products all the time if you didn't have them stuffed with aspartame.

title: Very good taste
text:
We finally had the chance to try these in our area.
(I didn't want to buy a big load of them online when we had not even tried them yet!)

We had the original flavor.
If there are people older than 40 out there who remember the Munchos chips (still being made, but
often hard to find), then you'll know what these taste like - very similar to Munchos.

Very crunchy, so satisfying in that way.
I look forward to trying many of the other flavors.

title: Not Spirutein's best flavor - try a different one!
text:
Well, I tried this because it sounded good.
We really like the Spiru-Tein shakes. They are highly nutritious, and
they fill you up, stomping on hunger for several hours.

So, I thought I'd try the Pina Colada flavor. After all, I love Spiru-Tein,
like pina coladas, so sounds like a great match, right? Right?

Well, SOUNDS like one. In reality, this shake is very off-putting!
First off, I would expect a pina colada flavor to be either white, off white
or some shade of yellow from the pineapple. Not this shake.
It is GREEN. Yes, GREEN.

Then let's talk texture. This is a big downfall of Spiru-tein, in my opinion.
If I am drinking a protein shake, I really don't want chunks of things if I didn't
put them in there. I want a healthy base, and I'll add fruits if I want chunks.
This drink has chunks of something in there - I think it is supposed to be like
little pineapple chunks, but it doesn't come across that way.

Best analogy that I can make about the experience of drinking the pina colada flavor?
It is like drinking a glass of milk that has soured and gotten chunky.
The color is nauseating and the texture just adds to it.

Spiru-Tein, I love your shakes, but this one needs to go back to the lab and be re-worked
into something more palatable and pleasing to the eye. Some of us look at what we drink!
This would be marked a fail in my book.

title: It's okay, but they need to work on texture.
text:
I bought this, because I am trying to get a variety of protein shakes for
meal replacements to help me lose some weight. I'm not an athlete looking to bulk up,
or a weight lifter trying to pack in protein.

I liked that this was a low glycemic index item. That is very important.
But honestly - why is the drink so thin Aria?
The taste is very similar to a plain glass of chocolate milk, with similar consistency.
I mixed mine with water, as I prefer, due to lactose sensitivity.
About half way through my serving, I added some Sweetleaf Stevia Chocolate flavored drops
to try and help it on the flavor boost. It didn't do all that much, but did add a little
sweetness to what is a pretty bland flavor.
Of course, flavor is subjective, so that's just adding my two cents on that part.

It was gone too soon, and I never felt like I really had anything to eat.
It is NOT filling in any way, and not really satisfying.
Most likely, it is better for you than some breakfasts you could be eating.
If you had a gastric bypass, this might be okay too.

Other than that, I think they could do a whole lot better.
I hope they find a thickener for the product. It results in a shake that is
just too runny to be satisfying. This is the second item from Designer Whey that
has been disappointing, so I think I'lll keep looking for a good protein shake.

title: Overall, not a bad flavor for a protein shake
text:
I haven't tried this one from a bulk can, only the packets.
I would suspect that the packets keep it a little fresher.

This was actually pretty good. I judge all my shake mixes based on water,
because I don't want to use milk for weight loss and lactose-sensitive purposes.
I had this one this morning with very cold water. I used my blender ball cup (also from
here on Amazon) and very cold water. The shake mixed up very easily.

Spiru-tein does sometimes tend to settle to the bottom of the shaker cup,
so be sure to shake it before each drink (if you let them sit). I did leave this
one sit quite often this morning as I was doing something else while snacking on
the shake. What I found was that the flavor grew on me. The first sip was a shrug
and not impressed. However, the other sips grew more enjoyable. The shake also
got THICKER as it sat, which I considered a bonus with this flavor! It might be why
it tasted better too.

I've heard other people recommend adding a squirt of sugar-free chocolate syrup to
these shakes to make them more chocolately. I didn't try that, but would certainly
not rule it out.

Overall, not a bad flavor, but I sure wish these were more cost-effective.
It is, however, one of the better brands out there if you want to use these shakes
for weight loss and not for workout bulking up. They have a lot of nutrition in them
without a lot of sugars and junk.

title: Bleah!  Don't bother...
text:
I like munchies.
I like bite-sized snacks.
I like cookie dough items.
I even like peanut butter.

But, these things should be stripped of their name!
They are like regular malted milk ball size, very soft (which is good), but the flavor sort of
defies description. They don't taste like chocolate balls, don't taste like peanut butter (although
they are the color of peanut butter on the inside), and don't taste like cookie dough.

All in all, pretty junky, even for junk food!
Don't bother with these at all. Four of us tried it and none of us liked them.
The rest of the box went into the trash, which was the best thing about them.
Seriously - why does the manufacturer even bother to make these? : P

title: Not your best bet if you want smoky paprika - try another brand
text:
Well, I ordered three tins of smoked paprika, one each of sweet, bittersweet and hot.
I love the smokiness and flavor it imparts to dishes, and wanted to try some other
strengths.

We received the cans today. It was well-packaged and everything arrived in great shape.
The seller was also quick to ship the order out. I have no problems at all with the seller.
One tin expires in 2012, and the other two are 2013, so guess I got an older tin of one strength.

This review is for the MILD (or sweet) paprika from Chiquilin.
What a disappointment!
This has NO smoky aroma at all, despite it supposedly being a smoked product.
I have not cooked with it yet, but I surely hope that it adds more flavor than it does aroma.
Otherwise, I could have just bought plain paprika in the grocery store for a lot less.
(The actual smoky paprika ([[ASIN:B000NO943C Smoked Paprika Tin]]) DOES have a wonderful smoky aroma and was what I expected from all the versions.)

I read a lot of different information about the brands, and while this was not my #1 choice on brands,
it was affordable and the seller did combined shipping, which was why I chose it. I guess you get what
you pay for? I was under the assumption that all of the Spanish paprikas were smoked paprikas, and you just got
different strengths of the roast. This does not seem to be the case with this brand.
We are going to keep the mild/sweet and the smoked, but returning the hot without opening it.

I hope it tastes better than it smells. I am admittedly disappointed in the aromatic qualities
(or lack of them) of this particular mild paprika. You can probably do better with another brand.

title: LOVE it!  They did a great job on the assortment
text:
We got our suckers today! Hooray!
Of course, almost everyone loves Yummy Earth lollies.
I won't bother with reviews on the flavors, because they are fantastic.
These suckers are not tooth-curlingly sweet, but very pleasant, very fruity
and definitely worth the wait.

Our previous purchases have been a very uneven assortment, like so many others have mentioned.
We'd get an abundance of sour apple and grape, but very few (if any) blueberry or mango tango.

I'd never ordered the counter container before, as we do not have a retail location.

a try so I didn't have to keep slapping my husband's hand for taking my customer's suckers.

I read that Yummy Earth was working on a better package for Amazon customers, and I think they
made it. Now, for date references, I ordered in Oct 2010. This assortment was more than fair,
with truly a very decent distribution of flavors. We even had a decent count on our
personal favorites, the mango! Thank you Yummy Earth, for working so hard to get this assortment
package more evenly distributed for your customers!

Now, if they'd only tuck a chili lime in there too, we'd be over the top! Ha! (We still want to try
that flavor, but no one in our area carries them. I didn't want to get a whole package in case we
didn't care for them.)

So, hats off to Yummy Earth for a great product. The suckers all arrived intact, nothing broken.
Amazon packaged them very well, and we will definitely be reordering from here!

title: Nice variety ...
text:
I'm at an age where several health conditions have led to my having to monitor my salt intake. I've never used a huge amount of salt anyway, so the new restrictions haven't been too cumbersome. What has helped the most is exploring various salt-free herb/spice blends, and there are a LOT of them out there!

This is a rather nice set -- you get 5 bottles for a very reasonable price -- and they're flavor combinations that are versatile. My favorite way to use them is to coat skinless/boneless chicken thighs or a salmon filet with one of the blends, and then bake it in my toaster oven (I'm single and cook only for myself, so ...). I use the Southwest Chipotle blend on chicken and then dice the cooked chicken to use in a Southwest-flavored salad -- combined with romaine lettuce, diced tomato, maybe a little spicy salsa, and topped with ranch dressing and grated cheese. Yum! The "Original" and "Table Blend" seem to be identical with the Table Blend a finer "grind" -- but that's OK -- it's one of my favorites in the bunch.

Will happily purchase again when needed as long as the price is reasonable.

title: Many uses for these ...
text:
I'm a cherry fanatic. It's one of my favorite flavors of all, so I tend to use it as often as I can. And these dried cherries are definitely useful!

My favorite use: I make bran muffins, but instead of raisins I load them with dried cherries. I also toss them in salads (along with chopped hazelnuts), oatmeal, and cherry pie (I use canned tart cherries with sugar and corn starch, and add a handful of these to the cherries before dumping them into the pie shell -- adds an extra layer of cherry flavor to the pie filling!).

Definitely will continue purchasing these as needed in the future. They're excellent quality and reasonably priced.

title: Excellent dried cranberries ...
text:
I use dried cranberries mostly with cereal (Frosted Mini Wheats plus a small handful of dried cranberries = breakfast bliss). But I also toss them into salads, into homemade apple pie prior to baking, and cookies (mix up some chocolate cookie dough but instead of chocolate chips, try cranberries, pistachios, and white chocolate chips). So I kinda know my way around dried cranberries.

These are excellent -- not too sweet, just the right amount of sour/tartness. Good price, too. Will purchase again when needed.

title: One of my favorite Mrs. Dash blends ...
text:
I've been using Mrs. Dash seasoning blends for years, long before I reached an age when I need to monitor sodium intake. These salt-free blends work so well with so many dishes -- I usually coat salmon fillets with one of the blends and then bake it until just done and still flaky. Each blend has a distinctive flavor profile, and this Southwest Chipotle is one of my favorites.

I've used it on salmon, chicken, and pork chops. I've also sprinkled it on simple quesadillas (flour tortilla loaded with cheese, refried beans, and maybe some shredded poached chicken). It works great and the flavor is amazing! Smoky chipotle with other subtle southwest flavors (cumin, garlic, etc.).

If you're looking to minimize sodium in your diet, this is a good way to add flavor without added salt. And even if you're not, it's still a great seasoning blend.

title: Not a good replacement for the original "On-The-Go Peach Iced Tea" packets ...
text:
Crystal Light seems to have discontinued the original On-the-Go Peach Iced Tea packets (the packets that you mix with 16 oz of water), which I have had on Subscribe & Save for years. Amazon suggested the Crystal Light Pure version, so I tried it. Sadly, it is NOT the same. Not even close.

The Pure version tastes more like lemon-flavored iced tea with a very very slight subtle hint of "peach" flavor. It's also not nearly as economical: the original On-the-Go Peach Iced Tea boxes contained 10 packets; the Pure version contains only 7.

I'm going to have to figure out some way to use the larger-size Crystal Light Iced Tea products (the ones that make an entire pitcher). The flavor of this just isn't that good. Perhaps if you've never had the original Peach Iced Tea mix, this might work for you. But if you're expecting a similar taste, you'll likely be disappointed.

title: Another yummy flavor from Pioneer Valley ...
text:
I've been purchasing Pioneer Valley preserves and jams for years, but just got around to trying this strawberry-rhubarb variety. I'll definitely be purchasing this again.

There's a perfect balance of sweetness from the strawberries and tartness from the rhubarb. I use it mostly on English muffins for breakfast and it's perfect for that. But I'm planning to use it in a glaze for a pork roast this weekend, combined with some dijon mustard -- it should work perfectly with the pork.

No problems or issues at all. Very happy with this purchase.

title: Will be purchasing this again ...
text:
What a nice find! I had gotten away from using a Keurig until recently when I started noticing more companies offering recyclable k-cups. I finally purchased a new Keurig K-Slim coffee maker and purchased a variety of new recyclable k-cup offerings from different companies. This Maud's Breakfast Blend was one of them and it's one of my favorites!

I don't like overly "charred"-tasting coffee, so usually go for a "light" or "medium" roast blend. Although this is "light," it's not without flavor! Smooth but robust, no burnt taste at all, great by itself but also stands up to flavored creamers (hazelnut or vanilla are my favorites). Obviously, taste in coffee is subjective, but if you're like me and want coffee to taste like coffee and not ashes, this might work for you, too.

Will definitely be purchasing more of this! It's just about the perfect morning cup. Solid 5 stars!

title: Great for those times when the supermarket is out of reach ...
text:
I like to keep food items like this on hand for those times when I can't get to the store for whatever reason (weather, illness, etc.). I'm single and at an age where "cooking" has become more of a process of "assembling" a meal from a combination of convenience products and fresh produce/etc.

And so -- this.

This is actually better than I expected. It doesn't look like much when you remove it from the package, but after it's heated, it is rather tasty. It is LOW SODIUM -- this surprised me as I was expecting a salt bomb. But it works well for those of us who have to watch our sodium intake.

I usually get two meals from each pouch. I like it best just heated and served over mashed potatoes with lots of pepper (yeah, I know -- sounds boring, but it works for me and it's fast). I've also used it with a good barbecue sauce to make sandwiches, and with taco seasoning for burritos.

Best of all, it's shelf stable -- I just keep it in the pantry and pull it out when I need it.

It's a little on the pricey side, but getting two meals from each pouch helps defray the "per meal" cost. I have it on Subscribe and Save so I can keep it in the pantry.

title: Just like the "other" pink packaged saccharin sweetener ...

title: Tasty, but sodium content is rather high ...
text:
I love a good vegetarian chili, and this harvest black bean is excellent -- a great combination of ingredients, nice consistency, etc. My only quibble is the sodium content -- to get the maximum protein and fiber content, you have to consume the entire can (not a problem -- 17 oz is a good serving size), and in so doing, you also consume 1240mg of sodium -- 54% of the daily recommended value.

Those of us who have to watch sodium (high blood pressure/etc.) have to weigh the pros/cons of high-sodium meals and adjust the day's meal plan to accommodate something like this. For example, if I wanted to have this for lunch, I would likely limit my breakfast to yogurt/berries/granola (low sodium) and my supper to a salad topped with some diced grilled chicken with a low-sodium dressing.

Something to consider. Yes, I'll purchase this again -- it's really a good veggie chili -- but I'll also be careful to plan to offset the high sodium content.

title: Nice quality, good flavor ...
text:
I hate chopping onions and don't use them that often except in soups, stews, and casseroles. So having dried minced onion on hand works great for me. I'm single and cook only for myself, and most of my recipes make only 1 or 2 servings. This way, I can add just the right amount to flavor a stock, sauce, or soup.

The flavor is excellent, and they reconstitute into recognizable bits of onion texture-wise. Will happily purchase again.

title: Works great in stews and casseroles ...
text:
I'm single, live alone, and cook only for myself. And I DO love to cook. Unless I want a ton of leftovers, I usually size recipes down to make 1 or 2 servings, And that can pose a problem with certain ingredients.

Using dried versions of common ingredients has worked great. This way, I can use exactly what I need and not worry about a bunch of celery going bad in the fridge before I can use it up.

The flavor and texture seem to be just fine -- you get recognizable bits of real celery. One of my favorite ways to use this is as an addition to a turkey/dressing casserole that I prepare in a small pan -- enough for one serving. I toss in a teaspoon of this and a teaspoon of dried onion in the stock I use to make the stuffing (usually a combination of a cornbread muffin and a handful of croutons). It reconstitutes nicey and fills out the flavor. Add in some diced turkey, mix, then toss in the toaster oven just until brown. Top with some turkey gravy and serve with cranberry sauce. Serious yum!

Will purchase again when needed. This is a good brand and I'm quite happy with the quality and results.

title: Bean Dip:  A throwback to the 1960s ...
text:
Still a favorite! And I'm happy to say my 4 cans of bean dip arrived in perfect condition (no dents).

The perfect accompaniment for Fritos Scoops chips. Think a very slightly spicy version of refried beans but blended into a smooth dip. Will continue to purchase as long as the price makes sense.

title: My favorite granola for yogurt parfaits ...
text:
Excellent vanilla flavor with the crunch of almonds and rolled oats. I use this most often layered with peach yogurt and chopped fresh peaches and/or raspberries -- the perfect breakfast yogurt parfait! Adds that bit of crunch that really wakes me up in the morning.

It's not bad by itself, either, with some low-fat milk.

Amazon's price is better than my local supermarket, so I'll keep purchasing here as long as that holds true. Really delicious!

title: Versatile and tasty...
text:
I use this not only for quick soup, but also added to eggs (scrambled, frittata, etc.) and ramen noodles along with some diced chicken for a quick chicken and noodles. I’m single and having shelf-stable products helps me reduce waste and still prepare reasonably healthy meals. I usually soak these dried veggies in boiling water for a few minutes to soften before adding them to the eggs, but I just toss them in with the dried noodles straight out of the package and let them soften as the noodles cook.

You get a nice balanced assortment of veggies, and they rehydrate into full flavored bits of cooked veggies. I usually add 1 tablespoon of dried veggies per egg for scrambled or frittata, or 2 tablespoons per ramen “block.” That amount seems to provide just the right ratio and flavor.

Will definitely purchase this brand again when needed.

title: The label says it all...
text:
When they say “intense,” they mean “intense”! I’m a big fan of Bonne Maman preserves, so when I saw these “intense” fruit spreads, I knew I had to try them.

I got the apricot flavor first, and liked it so much that I knew I had to try the strawberry. My favorite way to used it is on a bagel with cream cheese. The intense flavor is the perfect balance with the tangy cream cheese so I don’t have to use much. The texture is more like a fairly loose jam with some chunks of berry. Really lovely!

Will purchase again if available when needed.

title: No complaints at all...
text:
i’ve purchased double-dipped chocolate-covered peanuts from several different brands here, and these are my favorites. The chocolate has the best flavor and it’s “creamier” than the others. Yes, there are some smaller peanuts in the mix, but the majority in my bag are “normal” size. My bag has an expiration date 9.5 months from today and taste fresh.

Overall, this is a good value. I like to have a small handful as a treat a few times a week, and these fit the bill perfectly. Will happily purchase again.

title: Excellent salted caramel flavor ...
text:
I like the hint of salt in this caramel sauce. It's not too much -- just the right amount to let you know that this is, indeed salted caramel.

I use this almost exclusively on ice cream. The texture is absolutely smooth and it becomes firmer when chilled -- perfect for a caramel sundae. I purchased the two-bottle set with the measuring spoon and consider it a good value.

Solid 5 stars! Value, flavor, etc. - everything is good.

title: Decent crisp cookies -- Ginger is the star ...
text:
I purchased these after hearing a friend rave about them. The lemon were good; the chocolate were sort of "blah." The winner was the ginger package.

They say "triple ginger," and they mean it! There are visible bits of candied ginger throughout, plus the added dried ginger and fresh ginger flavors. The best ginger cookies I've ever had.

There was some breakage, but not as much as I had feared after reading the reviews here.

Will definitely purchase the ginger flavor again (and again!).

title: Works for certain recipes ... not so much for others ...
text:
I find this works great for chicken salad, adding to ramen noodles along with some veggies, etc. The size is perfect for a single serving. I'm single and live alone -- in an apartment in an assisted living facility with almost no kitchen facilities at all, so finding "convenience" versions of things is important.

The flavor is OK -- obviously not as good a rotisserie or freshly poached or grilled chicken, but it works when used along with other flavors, veggies, etc. I've used it several times for adding to ramen noodles with some mixed frozen veggies and a low-salt stir-fry sauce. Not fancy, but tasty. And this chicken tasted like it's supposed to (chicken), so I'm OK with that.

Shelf stable, good price, etc. I'll purchase again.

title: Love this stuff ...
text:
This is hard to find in my local supermarkets -- rarely in stock, and when it is, it runs a lot more expensive than this.

Happy to find this here and at a fair price. The squeeze bottle is a nice convenient touch, too. I use this for hot dogs, in various salads (chicken salad, tuna salad, macaroni salad, etc.). It's just the right consistency, too. Will continue to purchase from Amazon as needed.

title: Excellent honey mustard -- not too sweet, not too hot ...
text:
Honey mustard is one of my go-to condiments for sandwiches, for dipping chicken tenders or nuggets, for bratwurst -- so many things! I love the combination of sweet and mildly hot.

Beaver is my #1 choice (I think I've tried probably 8 or 10 brands). It strikes the perfect balance, has exactly the right consistency, and the price point is reasonable. Adds just the right amount of "oomph!" to an otherwise bland turkey sandwich.

It's almost impossible to find locally, so ordering from Amazon is almost my only way of getting this. Will continue to order as needed.

title: Just beef - no fillers/preservatives/etc. ...
text:
I purchased this when the facility I live in was under a "hard" COVID lockdown (it's an assisted living facility, so it's filled with really vulnerable people). We were told not to leave our apartments unless there was a fire or we had a medical emergency. I prefer cooking my own meals rather than relying on the stuff they were delivering during this lockdown. Grocery shopping was out of the question. So .. Amazon to the rescue.

I ordered this on the off chance that it would be an acceptable substitute for my usual pulled beef (a chuck roast, slow-cooked, then shredded). Really pleasantly surprised at how good this is!

I portioned the contents into 10 air-tight storage containers and put them in the freezer. You're advised not to freeze it in the bag (for obvious reasons), but removing the contents to freeze works just fine.

I love the fact that this is JUST beef plus a little broth and a slight amount of salt. The flavor is quite good. I've used it so far for 1) barbecued beef sandwiches (just mix the shredded beef with a little barbecue sauce); 2) enchiladas (mixed with some red enchilada sauce, rolled in corn tortillas, topped with more sauce and cheese, then baked); and 3) heated with some onion & garlic salt-free seasoning and served on top of mashed potatoes. Each dish turned out very tasty. The beef is lean -- really almost no fat -- and quite tender.

I plan to purchase this again to have on hand for times when I just can't get to the store. It's a tad pricey, but the convenience, flavor, and versatility make up for that.

title: I use this a LOT…
text:
I live in an assisted living apartment with what is euphemistically referred to as a “kitchenette” — basically, I have a 2-burner electric cooktop, a microwave, and a decent sized refrigerator with no counter space at all. So I use pre-cooked packaged products that I can reheat in the microwave a lot.

This is my favorite of the pre-cooked rice varieties. It’s a long grain white rice with a good flavor that pairs well with a lot of things. I use it as a base for a creole black beans and rice dish (with sliced andouille sausage), topped with chili and cheese, and with curries. It takes only 90 seconds to heat up. Easy to use and versatile. I keep it on hand all the time (I have it on subscribe and save). Good stuff!

title: Excellent in a pinch…
text:
These are my favorite “instant” mashed potatoes. No, they won’t replace freshly made mashed potatoes that take at least an hour or so, but they’ll do when you need something quick.

You get 8 packages in this box. The flavor is really exceptional for an instant product. I usually dress mine up with butter and various herb mixes, then top with sliced grilled steak. A nice quick meal that serves 2. I always keep these on hand for a quick meal. No issues at all.

title: Absolutely delicious…
text:
Apricot pineapple preserves are almost impossible to find. They were a favorite from my childhood (1950s-1960s), and I always look for them in the local supermarkets, but I’d given up finding them. I finally found them on another website that features bread mixes and ordered several times there, but they’ve been out of stock for a couple of months. On a whim, I did a search here on Amazon, and… Surprise! Here they are! Same brand and everything!

These are NOT overly sweet. Packed with fruit — tart apricots and just the right amount of pineapple. I use this with the big oversized English muffins from a company based in my hometown Kansas City. Really makes my breakfast something special.

I’ve also used this in a glaze for salmon: 1 Tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1/3 Cup white wine, 1 Tablespoon of the apricot pineapple preserves - blend well. Makes enough for one large (~6-7 oz) or two small (~3-4 oz) salmon filets. I do mine in the air fryer, brushing the glaze onto the fish a couple of times during cooking. Pair with some steamed veggies and coconut rice, and you’ve got a meal!

Mine came well protected with no issues in terms of breakage. Will gladly order again!

title: Still my all-time favorite ...
text:
Being an unrepentant chocoholic, I've tried dozens of varieties and brands of fudge over my 70+ years. THIS is absolutely my all-time favorite.

Perfect taste, perfect texture (not grainy!), perfect consistency (not too soft, not too hard), and a decent price all things considered. I've tried all of the variations of this brand and they're ALL excellent. My favorites are the chocolate raspberry, maple walnut, and Belgian chocolate.

Very happy to have found this on Amazon -- will continue to order as long as it's available.

title: Excellent cookies -- but a lot of broken bits ...
text:
I first had these at a "happy hour" in the retirement home where I live, one of the better "packaged" cookies I've had. The shortbread flavor was excellent and there was just the right amount of strawberry jam. I whipped out my smartphone, found them on Amazon, and ordered a box for myself.

The flavor and quality are exactly as I experienced a few days earlier. However, they really need to do something about the packaging as every bag I've opened so far (about 5 or so) has about 1/3 of the bag filled with cookie "bits." Don't get me wrong, they're still delicious, but there's something happening in the packaging/shipping process that seems to be causing a lot of breakage (a lot of reviews here mention it).

I'm still giving them 4 stars -- for a packaged cookie, they're really great. Wonderful flavor, etc. They just need to tweak the delivery process (manufacturer to Amazon, then Amazon to customer). Will absolutely purchase again.

title: Just say "no" ...
text:
I'll admit it: I'm an unrepentant chocoholic. So I had high hopes for a large oatmeal chocolate chip cookie that I could mix up and bake in the microwave.

I did everything according to the directions. It smelled more like an oatmeal raisin cookie with a lot of vanilla added than a chocolate chip cookie. I cut it in half and took a bite. All I could taste was sugar -- the texture/etc was just ... sugar crystals ... with a lot of vanilla and some cinnamon. There were a lot of what I presume to be chocolate chips in the cookie, but they didn't taste like chocolate. Kind of bitter, like burned cinnamon stick, maybe?

Anyway, it didn't work at all for me. Sorry -- not a good representation of any sort of chocolate chip cookie. Pass.

title: Works for me ...
text:
This stuff makes my life SO much easier (and tastier).

I'm currently living as an "independent resident" in an assisted living facility (I get housekeeping, laundry, and meals, but no medical supervision) due to some recent physical challenges (let's just say that late 2020 and early 2021 were not kind). While meals are provided, I prefer to cook for myself while I'm still able to do so. Although my apartment is nice, what they euphemistically call a "kitchenette" is really just a 2-burner electric cooktop, a microwave, and a decent-sized refrigerator with zero counter space. This makes cooking for myself a little tricky.

I tend to look for shortcuts wherever I can, but I still want things to be reasonably tasty and not totally "junk." I use this precooked bacon a LOT. It crisps up fine in the microwave, and I use it on sandwiches, crumbled into salads, in breakfast burritos, etc. The cost is actually considerably lower than my local supermarket (by about 20-25%), and I can store the packages in the closet (cool temp, no direct light) or if needed, in the freezer.

Will continue to purchase as long as Amazon carries it at a reasonable price point.

title: A bit of nostalgia ...
text:
I remember Archway cookies from my childhood -- many MANY years ago. They were always the "special" cookies, reserved for special occasions, and my favorite were the various molasses and ginger cookies.

So when I saw these on Amazon at a very decent price (<$3 / bag when I purchased them a couple of weeks ago), I had to see if they tasted the same.

Yes, they do. These are soft cookies, not too large, with a thin layer of white icing. Two or three of these after a meal with a cup of coffee -- perfection! Also, the expiration date is sufficiently in the future that I'll be able to finish these easily before the "Best by" date occurs (it's about 4 months from now).

I will purchase again for sure. Just a note: try to order these with other items so that they can be shipped in a box, rather than a "puffy" envelope. And even then, try not to order them with something heavy (like 6 cans of chili or whatever). They're soft cookies in a bag, and can easily be "squished" into oblivion. The cookies are excellent - Amazon's shipping not so much sometimes. Five stars for the cookies.

title: My favorite jarred salsa ...
text:
Great flavor, just the right amount of heat for the "medium" spiciness rating, smaller jars work great for me. I'm single and smaller jars mean I'll have a fighting chance of working my way through a jar before the contents go bad.

I use this on burritos (breakfast and lunch), tacos, and salads when I want a sort of "southwestern" spicy kick. Good stuff! Will order again for sure.

title: Great way to try some different sauces ...
text:
FIrst -- my four bottles arrived in perfect condition -- no breakage, carefully packed, etc. No issues there at all.

These sauces run about $7/bottle in my local supermarkets, so Amazon's price with prime shipping is excellent. I'm at a stage in life where I need to watch sodium intake, and these do have considerable sodium (300-500 mg per 2 Tbsp serving), but I use them judicially and sometimes thin with a little pineapple or apple juice or a little sherry. The flavor is really nice -- I use it for stir-fries, of course, but also ramen noodles. I take just the noodles and cook them with some extra veggies, then add diced cooked chicken or shrimp and a little sauce. Makes a quick and easy lunch.

I don't have a specific favorite as they're all good -- I just pick whichever one fits my mood at a particular time. Will definitely purchase these again.

title: Better than Special K Red Berries ...
text:
Never thought I'd say that -- I've been a long-time fan and consumer of Special K Red Berries, but after a recent "out of stock" situation, I decided to give this Happy Belly Strawberry Good Balance a try.

Holy smokes! SO much better than my former brand. Fresher tasting, berry chunks are bigger and there are more of them, not overly sweet, either. Just about perfect.

I now have this on subscribe and save -- don't want to run out! Seriously, just give it a try -- I think you may be surprised at how good it is.

title: Worth the price...
text:
I usually just buy the cheap store brand of refried beans, but I recently was in a situation where grocery shopping locally wasn’t possible.

Hello, Amazon! Ordered a couple of cans of these Amy’s Refried Beans, and was blown away by the flavor. Is this what refried beans are supposed to taste like? If so, I've been missing out for years. Definitely more “bean” flavor, so much so that I can use less in my burritos, nachos, etc. Really, there’s that much difference. Yes, the price is significantly higher that lesser brands, but in this case, you really do get what you pay for. The fact that I can use less and get more flavor justifies paying the price difference. These are really that good!

title: Great if you make things that don’t need a can of sliced olives...
text: Nice flavor, convenient packaging (I reuse the containers for craft storage).  The perfect size if you cook small quantities.  I use one “cup” in my baked ziti for 2 and it’s just the right amount of sliced ripe olives to go with Italian sausage, sliced mushrooms, sauce, and cheese.  Yum!

title: Tasty, nice size...
text:
I’ll admit it: I like Jello, and remember fondly the fruit-filled jello desserts my mother made for us.

This version -- mandarin orange segments suspended in orange gelatin -- is a little fancier than what my mother made. It’s quite good and fills the bill when I need something a little sweet. No “off” flavors, just nice mandarin orange taste. I have it on subscribe and save -- it’s that good!

title: Versatile, tasty...
text:
I’ve been using the “plain” version of these for years and find them the perfect vehicle for a lot of things besides tacos. I decided to try this cheese version as the others were out of stock.

They’re very similar to the others -- same shape/size -- but with a mild cheese flavor. I’ve used these for breakfast (sausage, scrambled eggs, a sprinkling of cheese), for pulled pork (pulled pork, barbecue sauce, a veggie [corn or beans]), for “open” burritos (refried beans, carnitas, spicy salsa), even chicken “pot pie” (diced poached chicken breast, mixed veggies, mushrooms, with a white wine/cream sauce). The cheese flavor adds an extra non-obtrusive taste that doesn't clash with other flavors.

Very happy I tried these. I’ll purchase again when I want to add some variety to my routine.

title: Arrived in perfect condition -- taste is wonderful!
text:
Reading some of the other reviews, I wasn't sure what to expect (dented can? inferior product?). The can arrived in great shape (even though it was shipped in a "puffy" bag). I opened it this evening, and I have to say it's in PERFECT condition.

So why buy butter in a can? In my case, mobility issues prevent me from grocery shopping in stores, and while I can get grocery deliveries under normal circumstances, at present my apartment building (housing for seniors, most of whom are an assisted living situation) is under lockdown due to the current health crisis (we had our first cases at the end of last month), so no one can leave the building, and no one except staff can enter unless it's an emergency. I try to keep an extra 8-16 ounces of butter in my freezer, but I'm running out and we're not going to open back up anytime soon. So, canned butter is something I can purchase and use now, and also keep a can or two on hand for other times when buying from local grocery stores isn't possible.

The butter in the can looked exactly like the photo above (some folks have received less-than-perfect product due to high temps or ??). Creamy, light yellow -- appearance was just what I was hoping for.

I just used it on some mashed potatoes -- super flavor! It's a little different from other kinds of butter I've had. I usually purchase either Irish or French butter, and I'm convinced that the flavor of good butter is largely dependent on what the cows eat and where it's grown (what type of soil). French butter to me always has a slightly "floral" almost slightly sweet taste; Irish has a more robust slightly earthy flavor with still a hint of sweetness. This has a very slight "tangy" taste -- not sour, not "off" -- just slightly different. VERY tasty, will be using it tomorrow on my morning English muffins.

With no added color, flavor, or preservatives, you're getting a 12-oz can of pure unadulterated butter, very lightly salted. This is a winner.

title: Great to add to ramen ...
text:
I purchased this to add to stuff -- not just soup, but scrambled eggs, rice, and ramen. It works best as a ramen additive. I use a microwave ramen cooker and put about 2 tablespoons of this mix in the bottom, add the dried ramen, and then water to just above the fill line (you need a little extra water to rehydrate the dried veggies). It actually works quite well, rehydrating the veggie bits perfectly. I then add m own sauce (those "flavor packets" that come with ramen are just too salty for me), and sometimes some diced grilled chicken. Perfect lunch!

For adding to scrambled eggs, I need to rehydrate the dried veggies first. I just put a couple of tablespoons in a small plastic container and add water, then leave overnight. In the morning, whisk up a couple of eggs, add to a nonstick pan, then toss in the rehydrated veggies. Scramble and top with cheese -- yum!

So versatile. Will reorder again when I need more.

title: The BEST orange slices I've found ...
text:
Orange slices are among my favorite varieties of candy. I'm a die-hard chocoholic, but these are my favorite non-chocolate treat.

Super flavorful -- intense tart orange taste, just the right amount of granulated sugar coating. My package purchased in early August 2021 has a "best by" date of December 2022. Of course, they won't last that long -- I'll be ordering more fairly soon. For the quality, the cost is reasonable.

Definitely a keeper ...

title: So much better than I expected ...
text:
I really wasn't sure what to expect with this I wanted something that was shelf-stable that would work for tacos, burritos, enchiladas, etc. I also have some health issues that pose some challenges for shopping and cooking, so I'm always looking for things that will simplify meal preparation but don't fall within the "junk food" category. I took a chance and I'm so glad I did. This fits the bill perfectly.

I like that the ingredients list is straightforward -- no extra preservatives. The seasoning is perfect -- lots of flavor without a lot of "heat." I can add my own salsas to give it as much spice as I want. I just heat it in the microwave in the pouch, then add it to whatever I'm making (today was burritos with refried beans, Mexican cheese blend, and a medium-spice salsa).

Initially, I purchased the 3-pack, but I like it so much I just ordered the 6-pack. This one's a keeper.

title: Lots of peach flavor ...
text:
I'm a lover of all things peach -- peach preserves, peach pie, peach ice cream, fresh peaches, and canned peaches (when fresh aren't available). During a recent hospital stay, I also rediscovered gelatin desserts (long story -- restricted diet -- LOTS of jello ... ).

Anyway, when I saw this product -- diced peaches in peach gelatin -- I knew I had to give it a try. Not disappointed at all.

Nice strong peach flavor, shelf-stable(!), good texture, lots of peach fruit bits. Definitely worth keeping on hand for a quick dessert.

title: Fresh, no breakage, yum!
text:
I usually get the powdered donettes, but decided to try the Crunch variety. Glad I did! These are super yummy. Mine arrived with about 4 months to go to the expiration date, so they were super fresh. The donut itself is identical to the powdered sugar variety, the difference is the coating. This one has finely grated coconut and some kind of caramel-y tasting crumbs that give it the slightly "crunch" texture. Really nice!

I like these enough to put them on subscribe and save. They're almost addictive! Very tasty.

title: Great convenience, excellent flavor ...
text:
I'm older and live alone, but I still enjoy cooking for myself. I don't like having a lot of leftovers, though. So I compromise by using a few "convenience" items, like this Uncle Ben's Basmati Ready Rice.

I use this as a base for easy quick stir-fries (beef, chicken, or shrimp, some frozen Asian veggies, a good-quality sauce). It's the perfect amount to make 2 servings -- one for now, one for this evening or tomorrow. I was a little skeptical about microwaved rice, but it really works. You really do need to kneed it before nuking -- it makes "fluffing" it up for serving so much easier.

I keep this on hand all the time -- also use it with chili, with southwestern dishes, etc. It's like the perfect rice for almost any cuisine. And getting it delivered by Amazon is the icing on the cake. Love it!

title: As far as instant coffees go, this is the clear winner for me ...
text:
After several major health issues in a short span of time (2020 was NOT kind healthwise), I had to resort to instant coffee as I simply didn't have the stamina to deal with anything else. I know that some people would rather do without than drink instant, but when that's the only option or do without coffee, I chose to at least give it a try.

I think I tried 5 or 6 different brands/varieties of instant coffee -- none of the flavored stuff, just plain black coffee. Included in the mix were well-known brands, "premium" brands, and more pedestrian varieties.

This was the clear winner. Hands down.

I don't like the charred/bitter flavor of a lot of coffees (even in my bean/ground coffees), so this light/medium roast fits the bill. It has robust flavor, and I can control how strong/weak I make it. The price here on Amazon definitely beats my local markets, too.

So until I'm back in pre-health-nonsense awesomeness, this will do just fine. No, it's no match for freshly ground premium beans, but it still produces an enjoyable cup first thing in the morning.

title: What a pleasant surprise! ...
text:
Decided to take a chance on these -- I like the serving size and the price was right. Anyway, I was VERY pleasantly surprised by the flavor of these. They have the strongest "potato" flavor of any chips I've tried in recent years -- really delicious! Not overly salty or greasy, either. Just about perfect! They say that beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and I don't find these "ugly" at all -- just perfectly golden brown. These are sliced with the peels on, so I'm sure that adds to the "potato-y" flavor.

Overall, I'm a huge fan now, and will purchase again for sure!

title: Nice strong lemon flavor ...
text: I'm almost addicted to these Pia white chocolate and lemon cookies.  VERY strong tart lemon flavor balanced nicely with the smooth white chocolate.  The cooking part is tender, not "crunchy." The perfect combination with tea or coffee.  So yummy!

title: My "go to" daily drink ...
text: I love peach tea, and this version is a tasty quick fix.  I try to drink at least 64 oz of water a day and this makes it easier to swallow.  I also like the crystal light raspberry lemonade, so I'll usually alternate between the two each month.

title: Some of the best I've had ...
text:
I've been around a while and being an unrepentant chocoholic, I've eaten my share of fudge over the years.

I can say with all honesty and seriousness that this is some of the best I've ever had -- anywhere.

Creamy, just the right consistency, not "grainy," just the right amount of add-ins, every flavor top notch.

I came back to this page today to order another box. It's really that good.

Highly recommended -- but beware: it's habit forming.

title: Super value for an excellent product...
text: Really good!  Nice chocolate flavor, great texture, good value, too.  You get a larger serving size with these.  Will happily purchase again.

title: Always a hit ...
text:
I've ordered these probably 6 or 7 times over the past several years, and I've never had a problem with freshness or quality. They're always the same yummy peach-flavored gummies that I know and love. I usually "repackage" them into 5 or 6 vacuum-sealed packages to retain freshness and never had a problem.

Will continue ordering these -- they're one of my favorite guilty pleasures!

title: Nice little treat ...
text:
I purchased several varieties of these -- this review is for the orange variety. These are rather reminiscent of the oh-so-British "Jaffa cake" but on a smaller scale. A light tender soft cake-like cookie base, a disk of orange jelly, and a thin topping of chocolate. Totally delicious, I like the individual packages of two cookies as that can serve as a nice evening treat with a cup of tea.

Will certainly purchase again!

title: My favorite Apricot preserves ...
text:
The perfect mix of tart and sweet. The flavor is intensely "apricot" -- perfect for my morning English Muffin breakfast, great to use as a glaze on chicken (I use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs). This stuff is really good, and a little goes a long way (another "plus").

I purchase these along with the Tiptree Morello Cherry preserves regularly -- both are suberb. Will continue to purchase as long as it's available on Amazon.

title: Seriously addictive ...
text:
Wow! I've had cashews coated with a lot of different stuff -- caramel (salted or not), chocolate, cinnamon, etc. But these "coconut toffee" cashews are seriously tasty. They're not *too* sweet, and the coconut is present but not "in your face" -- just the perfect blend of sweet and slightly salty.

I now have these on "subscribe and save" -- just too yummy to pass up. I do think they're a little overpriced for what you get, but it's a price I'm willing to pay for such a sweet delight.

title: Finally!  Nearly perfect orange marmalade ...
text: I think I've tried them all!  Expensive brands, store brands, at least 20 different varieties/brands.  This one is my favorite.  Not too sweet, plenty of orange peel, great on English muffins.  I can't stand overly sweet jams/preserves/marmalades, and I've found several orange marmalades that were too bitter (and one that was both too sweet and too bitter - go figure ...).  So I was thrilled to find this one.  I now have it on Subscribe & Save.  Good stuff!

title: Just like I remembered ...
text:
I've been using Melitta products for over 40 years starting with their cone coffee makers and their coffee. I kind of got away from it after trying new brands and switching over to a k-type machine. But I recently decided to go "smaller" -- and purchased a single-serve Hamilton pod coffee maker which takes up only a fraction of my previous coffee makers. And I saw this in the "purchased with ..." list and decided to try it again.

It's just as good as I remember. The pods make it very convenient to brew a single cup (I live alone), and I believe they're more eco-friendly than the k-cups. The flavor is robust but not too strong in any one flavor note -- no "charred" taste, just nice smooth medium-roast flavor.

I'll continue to purchase these pods as long as they're offered at a decent price. Very highly recommended.

title: Nice quality salt mill with good pink Himalayan salt ...
text:
So many of these individual salt mills are poor quality and they usually break before the salt is gone. I just finished the last of this salt and the mill is still in fine shape.

I don't use a lot of salt, but I do like it to be flavorful. I also use sel de mer, so I like having an alternative to that. This works nicely. A nice mild salt, with a good quality grinder. Can't get much better than that.

Solid five stars.

title: Great for baking ...
text:
I have mixed feelings about these. For eating right out of the bag, the caramel flavor is a bit mild. I get mostly "sweet" and chewy, but not a lot of caramel flavor. However, I added these to some chocolate chip cookies, and WOW! the flavor exploded. I think the additional heat made the difference.

Will use these for sure in cookies - better than toffee chips, plus they add a colorful touch. Four stars from me.

title: Yes, instant mashed potatoes CAN taste great!
text:
I’m single and 99% of the time I cook only for myself. I avoided instant mashed potatoes for decades thinking that none of the available products would be edible. Imagine my surprise when I tried these Idahoan Buttery Homestyle potatoes -- great texture and flavor, so easy to prepare. I just went through some dental work that landed me on a ”soft diet” for several weeks, and these mashed potatoes ended up a major part of my diet, usually topped with cheese and/or pulled pork or poached chicken.

It’s nice that I can put together mashed potatoes quickly without the multi-step process I usually use. These are good enough to keep on hand as a permanent option. They really are that good!

title: The perfect holiday ginger cookie, but great any time of the year...
text:
