I’ve ordered these several times -- they’re absolutely the best!

I started ordering these as a traditional holiday treat, but like them so much that I order them several times a year. Very thin but packed with sharp ginger flavor. My friend who lived in Sweden while on a Fullbright scholarship says they are the same cookies she bought there.

Will definitely keep a stock of these around this holiday season... and afterward. They’re that good.

title: Hellman’s Mayonnaise in shelf-stable packaging...
text:
I use Hellman’s mayonnaise regularly, usually purchasing the smallest jar available. I’m single, so I’m almost always preparing meals only for myself, and often face the problem of various condiments reaching expiration before I can use them completely. A product like these mayonnaise packets can be a real winner for someone like me.

Each packet contains one tablespoon of Hellman’s Real Mayonnaise and best of all it doesn’t need refrigeration. I use it mostly for wraps: usually some thinly sliced meat, a slice or two of cheese, some finely-shredded lettuce, thinly-sliced tomato, topped with mayo, good dijon mustard and some pickles of some sort. The perfect serving for my usual wrap us two packets of this mayo. Yum!

I also use it to make tuna salad using the 3 oz size can of water-packed tuna, 3 packets of mayo, a tablespoon of dijon, and some finely-chopped pickle (usually a single small sweet gherkin). Paired with multigrain crackers, it makes the perfect size lunch.

My only issue with this product is that I wish it was available in a smaller count for home use. The box contains 210 packets which probably works great for the food service industry. But it would also work extremely well for home use in a box of, say, 120-150 or so.

Still, I like this enough to give it five stars. It really us great mayonnaise and this shelf stable version definitely measures up to what I expect.

title: Surprising flavor, not too lemony, very nice on salmon
text:
I liked this more than I thought I would. The lemon flavor isn’t as pronounced as I thought it would be, but it’s still a tasty sauce.

I used the first packet with grilled salmon filets -- about 5 oz each. I warmed the sauce according to the directions and split it between the two servings. I ate one and stored the second serving in the fridge for a later meal. I liked it on the warm fish -- nice compliment for the salmon. I’m not sure it would work as well with a milder fish, but it pairs nicely with salmon. I used the second serving the next day with a salad. I wanted to see how it would hold up after chilling overnight and eaten cold. I used mixed greens, some grape tomatoes (halved) and a little sliced cucumber. I flaked the salmon with the sauce and served it over the greens, then squeezed a little lemon juice over the plate. This worked really nicely -- in fact, I liked it so much that I may purchase more of this sauce to use specifically for this salad in the future. It worked with both the fish and the salad veggies.

I used the second packet for chicken kabobs: I cubed skinless boneless chicken thighs, seasoned with a little salt & pepper and threaded them onto skewers. I also threaded some mushrooms, onion wedges, and red bell pepper chunks. I usually do meat kabibs separate from veggie kabobs since they cook at different rates. Anyway, grilled the skewers until everything was cooked through and heated the lemon dill sauce while the kabobs rested. Slid all the chicken & veggies into a bowl and tossed with the sauce. I liked this -- a different set if flavors but overall very tasty with the chicken & veggies.

Bottom line: I liked this best used on grilled salmon and then chilled overnight to use on a salad, and i’ll probably purchase more for just that purpose. I think a slightly stronger lemon flavor note would be a little better, but overall it’s a fairly well-balanced sauce. Four stars from me.

title: Great mixed berry flavor — perfect for pancakes & waffles ...
text:
I’ve been using Kodak Cakes Power Cakes Pancake Mix for several years and love the flavor and ease of use (just add water — really, what could be simpler?). When I was offered the chance to try their Mountain Berry Syrup, I jumped for the opportunity. After all, I usually mix in some frozen mixed berries into my pancake batter, so having that flavor in my syrup was a no-brainer.

I was not disappointed. Robust berry flavor, great consistency — I can see using this not just for pancakes and waffles, but as an ingredient in a glaze for chicken or pork tenderloin. Definitely will be purchasing more of this! Five stars well earned!

title: Surprisingly good for instant coffee! ...
text:
Yeah, I'm usually a "grind the beans and brew within 10 minutes" fresh ground coffee kinda person, but there are times and places where that just isn't possible. Instant coffee has always gotten a bad rap -- for understandable reasons -- but lately, more companies have been producing some very decent instant versions of their more popular brews.

Starbucks is one of those companies, and this VIA Instant line is their entry into the instant coffee market. I really like their Veranda Blonde Roast coffee (usually, their coffee tastes "burnt" and charred to me -- the Blonde Roast solves that issue). These little packets brew up an 8-oz cup of coffee, so I usually use 2 of them in my large 16-oz mug.

The taste is surprisingly close to fresh brewed -- clearly not as robust, but still not nearly as bad as one might expect for instant coffee.

I've also used these packets for iced coffee -- a lucky "test" I ran to see how they'd dissolve in cold water. Happy to report it works great!

The only downside is the economy of these -- a little too pricey at forty dollars for 50 packets. But if your overriding concern is convenience and you really like Starbucks, this might be a good solution.

title: Variety pack is a good way to try all the flavors ...
text:
I've been curious to try these new(er) Clif bars and was happy to have a chance to try them. The variety pack gave me a chance to check out all the flavors, and I definitely have my favorites.

First things first -- each bar is 240 calories with 10g of protein 13-14g of fat, and 24g of carbs. Gluten-free, they're made from dates, nuts, and seeds with different additions for flavor (chocolate, spices, peanuts, cherries, etc.). All varieties are the same size/shape and basically the same consistency and "mouth feel" (a few minor differences depending on the flavor/additional ingredients).

I liked them more than I thought I would. I've had similar products in the past that didn't work for me, either because of texture or flavor. Also, I have to avoid soy protein and so many "protein bars" rely heavily on soy protein to boost their protein count. These are a welcome change.

Overall, my favorite flavors of the four are the Tart Cherry Almond and the Spiced Almond Ginger. Although I'm an unrepentant chocoholic, I found the chocolate-flavored bars to have a kind of slightly bitter aftertaste. Not horrible, but enough to make me not want to purchase them individually.

In general, though, I like these -- four stars.

title: Liked these more than I thought I would, but ...
text:
I received the "Everything" sprouted seed crackers -- made with sunflower, hemp, chia, and flax seeds (the flax and sunflower seeds are sprouted) with a hint of onion and garlic (from powder). The small hexagon-shaped crackers are kind of "tough," but they're very thin so that's not too much of an issue.

Overall, the flavor was fine -- I've tried them so far with slices of aged cheddar cheese, spread with cream cheese topped with smoked salmon, and a thin slice of mozzarella topped with a slice of pepperoni. All good.

I'm lucky to not suffer from celiac disease or any other condition that requires a gluten-free diet, but if you do, these are "certified gluten-free."

Overall -- I do like these, but I'm not sure the economy of purchasing a "gluten-free" product when I don't need one makes sense since there are non-gluten-free alternatives that taste better and cost less. But if gluten-free is critical for you, these might be an excellent choice due to flavor alone. Four stars based on flavor.

title: Makes everything taste better ...
text:
I really lucked out: Both of my brothers married Filipinas, and I've had the pleasure of getting to know both these ladies and their culture/cuisine. On a 2-week holiday visit with one brother, I was introduced to Magic Sarap -- one of those rare spice blends that works on nearly everything. My sis-in-law and I worked shoulder to shoulder preparing meals -- learning from each other -- so we always had a nice mix of midwestern US fare plus some great Filipino dishes.

Since returning home to the Pacific NW, I've used Magic Sarap in meatloaf, sprinkled on chicken thighs before and after roasting, in scrambled eggs, in potato salad, in mashed potatoes along with some roasted garlic, and as a table seasoning to sprinkle on anything else (steak, grilled salmon, etc.). It just seems to enhance the flavor of everything it touches.

I like that it comes in the small packets -- keeps it fresher longer. I got a good deal here on Amazon and will continue to purchase as needed. Really great find! Solid 5 stars from me: I love it, and use it almost daily.

title: The best elderberry syrup ...
text:
This is my all-time favorite pancake syrup (maple is a close second). And Pioneer Valley makes a good one!

My earliest experience with elderberries came at my great-aunt's house in Okmulgee, OK, when I was a child. They had massive elderberry bushes on their property, and they always had elderberry preserves, jelly, syrup, and, yes, wine on hand when we visited. We weren't allowed to pick/eat raw elderberries - they're poisonous - but we often had vanilla ice cream with elderberry compote for dessert during the summer.

I rediscovered Elderberry Syrup again a few years ago when I found it on another website and ordered it just to see if it was as I remembered. It was -- and then some. Yes, it was this very same Pioneer Valley product and it has a slightly tart full flavor that is reminiscent of a cross between huckleberry and raspberry. It's perfect on buttermilk pancakes or waffles, and I've also used it in a glaze for roasted lamb. Just perfectly yummy!

I really do love this -- solid 5 stars!

title: My FAVORITE Cherry Preserves ...
text:
I've been trying a number of different Tiptree products, and this has been my favorite so far.

Spreads made from Morello cherries are a little different from other cherry preserves -- Morellos have a more intense "cherry" flavor and a darker almost black/red color. Most US-brand cherry preserves are made from Bing cherries and are always too sweet for my taste. Tiptree takes care to make the cherry flavor the star of the show, keeping the added sugar to the minimum needed to offset the tartness. The result in an intensely flavored cherry spread that isn't too sweet. The cherries are chopped relatively finely, so you get bits of real cherry goodness in every spoonful.

I use this mostly on English muffins or buttermilk biscuits with butter. I'll keep coming back for more as long as Amazon keeps carrying it -- I can't find it anywhere locally, and I'm now spoiled. No other brand will do!

title: More like orange/tangerine jelly ...
text:
I hesitated to write this review as I'm such a huge fan of Tiptree fruit spreads/preserves/etc. But I was expecting a marmalade with a lot more fruit peel bits. This was more like a jelly with a few (very few) shreds of peel, so almost no texture. The flavor is good -- sharp, not too sweet, etc. But the texture is just not what I would expect for marmalade.

If you prefer fewer bits of peel in your marmalade this would be a great choice for you as the flavor is good.

I give it 3 stars -- it's OK, but it's not something I'll purchase again, especially when there are so many great Tiptree flavors available (seriously, the Morello Cherry preserves are the best I've ever tasted anywhere ... ).

title: Great for casseroles or ham salad ...
text:
I've used Hormel canned chicken before and been happy with the product, so I was happy to try their canned ham.

First things first, just out of the can it's a little saltier than I like. Ham by its nature is always a little salty and the canning process seems to accentuate that. This is easily fixed, though: just drain the can of the excess liquid, toss the meat into a fine mesh strainer, rinse under cool water, then squeeze slightly to remove the rest of the water. It's ready to go.

I decided to try two different preparations -- one hot, and one cold. I'm single and tend to prepare smaller quantities, so using 1/2 of the can for each recipe worked fine for me.

The first dish was a breakfast/brunch "strata" (a combination of bread cubes, peppers, onions, eggs/cream, some seasonings, the ham, topped with some cheese). Used a 5" x 8" baking dish. Turned out really nice. I usually make this with some diced ham from a ham steak, but having the option of using something shelf-stable will give me a little more flexibility.

The next dish was ham salad (I love a good ham salad sandwich). A little mayo, a little dijon mustard, some finely-diced celery, and a little sweet pickle relish (yes, I used sweet pickle relish -- it balance the saltiness of the ham). Again, this worked nicely. Half of the can supplied enough ham for a generous amount of salad. Tasty!

This is definitely something I would consider having on hand in my pantry for those days when I need to fix a meal quickly and don't want to (or can't) drive to the store. Good stuff! Solid 4 stars: I like it.

title: I like these more than I thought I would, but ...
text:
I tried the Mango Coconut variety of these. I wasn't sure what to expect. Only two ingredients? OooKkkkk. I like that there's no added sugar -- the sweetness comes from just the mango.

I actually ended up liking them more than I thought I would. They're small "balls" of soft/chewy tart mango, not sticky at all (on residue on your hands), with just the right balance of coconut so that the flavor is there but not overpowering. It took a couple of bites to get used to the flavor, but I found that I really do like it. Not *too* sweet, either.

Not sure how economical these are, however. They seem rather pricey (two and a half dollars per small pouch) to me. I'm tempted to try the pineapple flavor but may wait awhile for either a sale or a price point that's more sensible.

I like the concept, and I like the flavor, so for me, that warrants 4 stars.

title: Nice hearty chili ...
text:
This is a decent "middle of the road" chili with red kidney beans. There is the barest subtle hint of "heat" -- but I wouldn't call this spicy at all. Just a satisfying savory chili with identifiable meat chunks and bell pepper.

My favorite way to eat chili is over rice (yeah, I know -- weird), so I need one that has enough flavor to stand up to the "neutral" flavor of steamed rice. For my test, I ate 1/2 the can by itself and 1/2 over rice with good results both times. I've been looking for a replacement of another brand that no longer comes in the size and flavor I like so this might end up being a good substitute.

Bottom line, I like it. Solid 4 stars.

title: A decent microwave cheese popcorn ...
text:
Orville Redenbacher's Cheddar Microwave Popcorn is definitely a cut above most competitors. Popcorn isn't my first choice for a salty snack (that honor belongs to the potato chip family), so when I decide "it's popcorn day," I want something that exhibits consistent quality. OR is my "go to" brand for other microwave popcorn flavors (especially their Movie Theater version) mostly because nearly every kernel pops -- you end up with very few "old maids" in the bottom of the bag.

So -- this is my first experience with the Cheddar Cheese flavor variety of OR. I've purchased pre-popped cheese popcorn from other sources, usually as part of a "sampler" package including cinnamon and caramel flavors in a tin canister. This microwave version is actually quite good.

The label says "natural flavor" -- and the flavor definitely tastes "cheesy." The fluorescent orange color is courtesy of paprika and beet juice. I like that it's not *too* salty (label says 400mg of sodium per serving, and there are 2.5 servings per bag) -- just enough to enhance the "cheesy-ness."

Overall, then, the same consistent quality found in my other OR favorites, a decent cheesy flavor, not too salty. Adding this to my list of "salty snacks to keep on hand" when I want to shake things up a bit. Solid 4 stars -- I like it!

title: Easy to prepare and super versatile! ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Zatarain's various rice dishes. Most follow the same model: easy-to-prepare with boiling water, a little butter, and the contents of the package. Within 20 minutes or so, I can have a delicious dinner.

This one is a great example. The flavors are excellent: roasted garlic, black beans, peppers, onion, lime, and spices. I usually add a grilled chicken breast, cut into strips. One package produces a substantial 2 meals (I'm single), so I prepare the rice per instructions, add the chicken, then put half in a storage container for a later meal. To the remainder, I add a squeeze of lime juice, some avocado, and a chopped Roma tomato. It makes a filling meal with the right amount of protein to help keep me satiated until my next meal.

I've also made this using skirt steak grilled and sliced thin, and another version using a boneless pork loin chop grilled and sliced thin.

I use the Zatarain's Spanish Rice variety quite often, and I'm adding this Roasted Garlic Adobo to my rice repertoire. It's super tasty and easy to customize.

title: Quality on a budget...
text:
I’m really liking this budget line of herbs, spices, and dried flavoring products. I’ve used this Minced Onion product in soup (multi bean & ham), mixed into hamburger patties, and in veggie dip, and it’s comparable with pricier sure and name brands. Since i’m single, I tend to prepare recipes with smaller yields to avoid tons of leftovers, so it’s definitely more convenient to use products like this to avoid waste (you can’t really purchase 1/4 of a medium onion, for example, so the rest has to be chopped and frozen which presents its own set of problems).

Once reconstituted, either by soaking in some liquid or use in a recipe that contains a lot of juice or liquid, you end with small recognizable onion bits as in a fine dice. The flavor is just fine -- not acidic but not sweet either. Just what I like especially in souos and stews.

I’ll definitely order this again -- economical and quality make it a good value. Solid 5 stars.

title: Just like the "other" pink-packet sweetener ...
text:
I've been using the pink packets to sweeten tea and coffee for years (decades, really), so I was curious to see how this would compare. Bottom line -- they're almost identical based on the list of ingredients, same size, etc. I couldn't taste any difference between the two products. So as far as I'm concerned, they're interchangeable.

Then it comes down to cost. You'll want to pay attention to the price and number of packets in the box to determine which is the better buy as it can change depending on seller/etc. The bottom line is that I now have another option for my preferred sweetener. Good stuff!

title: Nice all-round seasoning blend ...
text:
I use a lot of seasoning blends from a variety of manufacturers/brands (Mrs. Dash, Penzeys, etc.). This one contains some salt -- it's listed as the second ingredient after "dehydrated vegetables" (onion and garlic), and contains 140mg of salt per 1/4 tsp serving.

I'm not sure who Jackie is or where Jackie's Kitchen is located, but she (he?) puts out some good spices/blends. This one is well balanced in terms of herbs/spices and onion/garlic and seems to work on everything so far. I've used it on grilled chicken, mixed it with unsalted butter to make a seasoned butter for a steak, mixed it into mashed potatoes (particularly yummy with that!), included a couple of dashes in the eggs I used to make an omelet, and sprinkled it over roasted veggies. It really does go with everything.

I'll probably to continue to use it mostly on poultry and the occasional steak, and on mashed potatoes. You get a full 12-oz of this for a very reasonable cost (as of today), so it's a great value. A good all-purpose savory spice blend -- extreme versatility warrants 5 stars.

title: Beats the heck out of the competition ...
text:
I think I've finally found the perfect "kettle-cooked" chips. The Original Sea Salt chips are absolutely the best I've tasted so far (and I think I've tried virtually every chip available either online or in my local supermarkets.

These are crispy, perfect golden color, and, most important to me, NOT TOO SALTY! The perfect amount of sea salt makes these tasty but not "drying. There are only three ingredients used: potatoes, sea salt, and sunflower oil. That's it. No preservatives, nothing else. Yummy!

The case I purchased has a long expiration date -- 3.5 months from the date of purchase gives me enough time to consume these before they exceed their "best buy" date (yes, I know their consumable after that date, but it's nice that these are on the "fresh" side).

I also appreciate that they donate 10% of their profits to organizations that affect them directly.

Will definitely purchase these again! Really tasty, not too much salt -- solid 5 stars. I love them!

title: Less "hot & spicy" than you might expect ...
text:
I tend to make friends with most spicy food. No issues at all with it, and as long as the dish is well balanced in terms of flavors, everything is good. One of my favorite spicy dishes is vindaloo -- yummy!

I was expecting a product labeled "Hot & Spicy" to be ... well ... hot and spicy. This chili has some heat, but I'd call it "mild to moderate." There's no lingering burn, it doesn't make my eyes water or my face sweat. It's just a bit on the spicy side, but not objectionably so. AND it is well balanced by the blandness of the beans and the ground beef. So overall, I like it.

The individual smaller cans are convenient for putting together a quick lunch. I especially like this over rice -- about 1/2 to 3/4 C of brown rice, maybe topped with a little shredded cheese.

So if you're considering this but are not fond of really hot/spicy stuff, rest assured this isn't that hot & spicy. On the other hand, if you're really looking for something that makes your eyes sweat, this probably won't do it for you.

I really like it, and will continue to purchase as long as I can get a decent deal on it. Solid 4 stars.

title: A wonderful addition to the holiday cookie tray ...
text:
I LOVE having these around for Christmas as part of my holiday cookie tray. They're light and crispy with very strong pronounced ginger flavor, just like they should be. I've similar thin ginger cookies "homemade" by a Swedish friend, and these are VERY close to what she makes. They're wonderful with tea in the afternoon -- a real treat that's not a huge "hit" in terms of calories.

Will continue to order these as long as they're available at a reasonable cost. They're really SO good!

title: WARNING:  HIGHLY Addictive!
text:
I'll admit it: I'm a huge cheese puffs fan. I've been a huge cheese puffs fan all my life, even before they came out with the "crunchy" variant.

I read about these online, they sounded interesting (I find a lot of Canadian snacky things interesting), so I tried them.

Oh.my.gosh. They're so yummy. Imagine, if you will, that the crunchy cheese puffs and the regular cheese puffs had a love child. Voilà -- Hawkins Cheezies.

They're crunchy and vary in size from "jumbo puff" to tiny crunchy bit. I have to portion the out or I'll consume an entire "sleeve" of these. They're really that good.

Will continue to purchase from Amazon when I can't make the trek across the border to pick them up in British Columbia (I live 13 miles from the border). They're one of my top 5 snacks of all time.

title: Almost impossible to find ...
text:
I grew up with elderberry "stuff" -- my family used to visit relatives who had elderberry bushes flanking their front porch. Every year, they'd strip the bushes of the berries and make jam, syrup, and elderberry wine. I love the flavor, but it's nearly impossible to find

This is a very good elderberry jam. It's maybe a tad sweeter than I remember, but the elderberry flavor is definitely front and center. I love it on English muffins, but I've also used it in a glaze for chicken. Really yummy!

Will continue to purchase here as long as it's available at a reasonable price.

title: Easy way to get garlic flavor without the mess ...
text:
When garlic is minced and dried, it loses some of its "sharpness" -- which, for me, is a good thing. I'm single and don't use that much fresh garlic anyway, so having this on hand makes things so much easier, and I really do like the flavor. Just 1/4 tsp will provide as much flavor as an average clove of garlic. I add it to mashed potatoes along with the butter and cream, mix it into ground beef before I shape hamburgers, add it to meatloaf and meatballs. Adds just the right touch of mild garlic flavor -- definitely present, but not overpowering and "sharp."

Good stuff! I like it -- a lot!

title: My favorite of all the McCormick Grill Mates products ...
text:
Seriously, this stuff works on EVERYTHING. It's like a "magic powder" -- it seems to enhance the flavor of anything it touches. Deviled eggs, steamed veggies, garlic bread, pizza -- in addition to the usual grilled stuff (ribs -- mixed with some other goodies it makes a great dry rub; chicken; steak; salmon; shrimp).

You know that onion dip everyone makes with sour cream and dry soup mix? Mix a teaspoon or two of this into the mix for some added depth of flavor. Add it to cream cheese along with some finely shredded sharp cheddar cheese for a yummy cheese spread for crackers. You get the idea.

I love this stuff for its versatility and depth of flavor (the roasted garlic is what makes it different). Solid 5 stars.

title: Super tasty! ...
text:
I love red beans and rice, so when I saw these, I thought I'd broaden my horizons and try something new. I got the variety pack (6 different flavors) to sample some different flavors. So far, I've had 4 of the 6, and I couldn't be happier! Super flavorful, not too salty (that was my biggest concern when I initially ordered these), and perfect over rice. Easy to prepare in the microwave, too.

Will definitely order these again!

title: Perfect serving size for a quick lunch ...
text:
I love the convenience of this. On days when I'm just not feeling up to cooking an entire meal for myself or when I'm rushed for time, this is my "go to" lunch. I usually serve it over some heat-and-serve brown rice and add few pinches of shredded cheese. I found the texture and flavor to be fine -- not "OMG! That's amazing!" level, but certainly tasty. I prefer things a little spicy, so I'll be trying the "spicy" version of this soon.

Overall, this works well for me -- tasty, right size, super easy to prepare, filling. I'll purchase again for sure.

title: My new favorite tea ...
text:
I'll admit it: I like both coffee and tea and drink them in almost equal amounts. I've tried a number of different "premium" brands and found most of them ranging from "acceptable" to "very good." Then I tried this one on the basis of recommendations from friends.

I love this one! It has a bright flavor that only deepens as I let it steep. I drink it with just some sweetener (no milk), and like it brewed slightly "strong." It's smoother than other brands, but still has the robust flavor I crave in the morning. I'll keep purchasing this as long as I can get it on Prime. Really good stuff!

title: Strong tart lemon flavor ...
text: Liked these more than I thought I would - enough that I now have them on Subscribe and Save.  The cookies are soft-textured with a strong tart lemon flavor and just the right amount of sweet lemon glaze icing.  Definitely, a nice treat that isn't too sweet.  One or two after a meal is perfect for me.  Solid 5 stars!

title: Well-balanced flavors, crunchy and addictive ...
text:
These are definitely a new tasty addition to the "chips" family of snacks-- crispy/crunchy crackers with a nice strong Parmesan flavor. I don't taste much rosemary -- just a hint -- which is actually good since rosemary can easily overpower other flavors. The parmesan doesn't taste "fake," either. It's prominent but in a good way. And they're not overly salty -- a real risk whenever Parmesan is involved as it tends to be a really salty cheese.

The crackers themselves are crispy and tender. Just perfect for a snack. A handful of these and I'm good to go. The caloric hit isn't too bad, either: 140 kCal per 10 crackers. Perfect serving size.

My bags arrived with most crackers intact -- little breakage. Definitely will be ordering these as an alternative to chips. Solid 5 stars!

title: Surprisingly good! ...
text:
I'm not usually a fan of instant coffee and I've never been a huge fan of Starbuck's (most of it has a sort of "charred" taste that I find off-putting), but I had heard that the Via Instant coffees were pretty good, so decided to give this one a try (Medium Roast Colombia).

Very happy I did! So much better than I expected. It's nothing like the usual instant coffee I've had in the past -- much more robust in flavor. And there's none of the burnt flavor I disliked in the Starbuck's bean and ground coffees I've tried in the past.

I do still prefer my fresh ground coffee at home when I have the time to do it, but these Via Instant Coffee packs are great to take along on vacation and/or to have on hand when I just need a quick cup of coffee and don't want to mess with grinding and brewing from beans.

WIll definitely purchase again! I really do like it!

title: Nice for peanut lovers ...
text:
I've ordered from Oh Nuts a couple of times in the past, so I was curious about this peanut gift tray.

It's a nice assortment of peanut flavors -- including in-shell, chocolate covered, yogurt covered, etc. And mine arrived in decent shape -- the tray is sturdy and makes for a nice presentation. The nuts tasted fresh to me -- I'm a sucker for peanuts anyway, and the chocolate- and yogurt-covered ones here are especially good. The only thing I'd change is get rid of the peanuts in the shell, and substitute another flavor.

I liked this -- solid 4 stars.

title: Long-time favorite in a new package ...
text:
I've been a huge fan of Oreos since I was a child (MANY years ago), and I purchase them periodically when I feel the need to splurge a bit. I also crumble them as a topping for a brownie hot fudge sundae -- and I've used them crushed as a cheesecake crust. So many possibilities!

These are the same Oreos in a new presentation: Each sleeve contains 10 cookies, and there are 10 sleeves in the box. Cookies are fresh, the "best by ... " date is far enough in the future that I know I can finish these off before they reach expiration. Having the cookies packaged in 10-cookie sleeves helps to maintain freshness -- I'm single, and it's difficult to eat my way through an entire regular package of Oreos before they start going stale. With these smaller sleeves, I can open one and usually finish it off in 2-3 days.

I'm a happy camper! Nice to see a new approach -- one that works great for me. Solid 5 stars! Great cookies, intelligent packaging.

title: Great for a brownie hot fudge sundae ...
text:
I got these more for the convenience -- I've been a huge fan of Kodiak Cakes Power Cakes pancake mix and more recently the "muffin in a cup" mixes. I also have a not-insignificant attraction to brownies, especially when used in a brownie hot fudge sundae. So I really wanted to give these a try.

First things first -- VERY easy to prepare -- add water to the mix, stir, and microwave for a minute (I found that 57 seconds is perfect). This produces a moist fudgy brownie. No, it's not as good as homemade or even some box mixes, but it's certainly tasty and a good size.

Second -- it's a very nice base for my version of a brownie hot fudge sundae: I make one of these in the cup, drop in a scoop of good vanilla ice cream, and top with hot fudge sauce and a sprinkling of chopped pecans. If I happen to have whipped cream in a can handy, I might spritz on a blob of that, but it's not mandatory. The size means I don't over-indulge, and I get my BHFS fix.

I now have these on subscrie and save. They're nice to have on hand when I just need a little brownie "pick me up." Solid 4 stars.

title: No "best by ... " date, but a tasty blend of herbs ...
text:
Italian seasonings usually contain similar herbs/spices -- and although the blend ingredients for this Spice Classics blend aren't included on the label, tracking them down took less than 10 seconds -- Basil, Oregano, Thyme, Marjoram, Rosemary, Sage and Savory -- no salt. Very similar to other blends on the market.

I use a lot of this type of seasoning because the flavor profile works with a lot of proteins and vegetables. One of my favorite uses for Italian seasoning is on pizza -- I like to make my own pizza at home using store-bought pizza dough. I stretch out the dough, brush lightly with olive oil, then sprinkle with Italian seasoning blend. The oil keeps the crust form becoming soggy. I then top with pizza sauce (either home-made or a good storebought version) and toppings -- and sprinkle again with seasoning. This Spice Classics blend is not a finely-chopped as some, and I like that. The flavor is excellent -- as good as pricier options. I did find a few bits of stem in the mix -- not many, but the coarser grind makes them more obvious.

I've also used this in a quick marinara sauce that I made to go with meatballs and linguine -- again, very nice flavor and texture for this purpose. And I used it on a vegetable blend I like to make in the fall/winter: chunks of butternut squash, carrots, and parsnips. The flavors work great with this combination.

So why should you select this product over other similar ones? It's really a matter of personal taste. This particular blend I found to be very "oregano-forward" -- a more "Mediterranean" taste. Some other blends I've tried are more "basil-forward." It really just depends on what you like. From a cost standpoint, it's comparable to other upper-end mass-market blends.

For me, I'll continue to use this for my Italian seasoning needs and then decide if I want to replace it with Spice Classics. Based on my use so far, I suspect I will. Solid 4 stars (if the ingredients list and "best by" date were included in the labeling, it would be 5 stars).

title: Not *that* "hot and spicy" ...
text: I'd classify this as more of a "medium" spicy chili.  It's very good, with lots of meat and beans.  I'm single, and usually dish up 1/2 of a can of this over 1 Cup of steamed rice and topped with some finely-shredded colby-jack cheese, with a small green salad on the side.  Makes a good filling lunch.  A single can easily provides two servings, which makes it economical as well.  Will definitely purchase again -- even though I generally like things a bit spicier.  If you usually totally avoid anything that might be even remotely spicy, you'll probably want to skip this as it does have *some* head -- just not a lot.  Tasty, though!

title: Easy to prepare, tasty, but are they muffins?
text:
I've been using Kodiak Cakes Power Cakes pancake mix for a few years and love it! I knew they had branched out into other breakfast treats, so I finally decided to try their Minute Muffins.

I've tried two flavors of these: Blueberry and Apple Cinnamon, and I definitely prefer the taste and texture of the Apple Cinnamon. I've tried multiple cooking times and find that with my microwave, 55 seconds is perfect. Both perform about the same: they rise to near the top of the cup, then sink back down to about the 2/3 level (the Apple Cinnamon a little higher -- maybe 3/4). Neither looks like the photos showing the top of the muffin above the rim of the cup. So there's that.

I kind of hesitate to call these muffins. They don't come out of the cup easily (I still haven't figured out how to get one out without destroying it), so I have to eat it with a fork. That sort of takes it out of the realm of "muffin" in my book.

UPDATE! I figured out how to get one of these out of the cup intact. First, let it cool almost completely (wait 10-15 minutes or so). Then, using a fork, insert the tines between the muffin and the cup along the side and remove; move over a bit and insert tines again and remove (don't "slide" the fork around the cup and don't use a knife -- the muffin sticks to the knife); work your way around the cup twice -- this makes sure most of the side is separated from the cup. Now, flip the cup upside down onto a plate (paper or otherwise), and smack it a couple of times. The muffin should fall out of the cup. It's still kind of fragile, but at least you have a "muffin" rather than a "breakfast treat that you have to eat with a fork."

HOWEVER, they are both fluffy and tasty for sure. The blueberry is a little "gummy" -- not horrendously so, but enough that it's noticeable (tried increasing the cook time and that just made it dense and gummy instead of light/fluffy and gummy). The Apple Cinnamon, however, is near perfection, probably due to the inclusion of rolled oats which give it some texture. I find that adding a bit of butter just after taking it from the microwave gives it some extra flavor -- I've also sprinkled the Apple Cinnamon with a little cinnamon sugar.

I've just put the Apple Cinnamon on subscribe & save, so I really do like it. The blueberry is "just OK" due to the texture. Haven't tried the other flavors but I may give the chocolate Minute Muffins a go.

title: Just OK ...
text: Kind of soft and "mushy" -- not at all like the pepperoni I'm familiar with.  There's a slight pepperoni taste -- even a hint of heat -- but that's where it ends.  VERY salty tasting, too.  I think Hormel kind of missed the mark on these.  Sorry -- just not a fan.  They're OK, but I'd avoid them if other options were available.

title: Nice assortment of Frito-Lay products ...
text:
I'm single, but I do like a few chips with my sandwich at lunch. Having serving-size bags means I don't have to open a big bag and have it go stale before I finish it.

This assortment offers a nice variety of chip styles and flavors plus some other "salty" snacks. My package contained:
5 Doritos Nacho Cheese Flavored Tortilla Chips
3 Doritos Cool Ranch Flavored Tortilla Chips
3 Lay's Sour Cream and Onion Potato Chips
3 Rold Gold Tiny Twists Original Pretzels
3 Smartfood White Cheddar Cheese Flavored Popcorn
5 Cheetos Crunchy Cheese Flavored Snacks
3 Cheetos Puffs Cheese Flavored Snacks
3 SunChips Harvest Cheddar Flavored Sun Chips

Pretzels and popcorn aren't my favorites, but I'll use the pretzels for holiday candies (I make "turtles" by laying a few pecan halves on each pretzel, top each with a dollop of caramel, and then covering the whole thing with melted milk chocolate). And I'll probably use the popcorn as a munchie when I watch my favorite football team.

The rest are among my favorites (especially the Sour Cream and Onion Lays chips, the Harvest Cheddar Sun Chips, and the Cheetos Puffs). It's a good assortment, with something for everyone. I do wish it had more of the chips (Lays Classic Chips, Fritos, etc.), but for those that like non-chip treats, this might work really well. Four stars.

title: A superior classic Dijon mustard ...
text:
The Maille Dijon Originale is a classic dijon: creamy texture, subtle "kick" but not overpowering. The texture makes it easy to whisk into salad dressings or marinades, and the flavor is great for sandwiches, sausages like bratwurst or kielbasa, and combining with a little honey for a nice glaze on salmon or chicken. So versatile!

I definitely like this better than the more popular "name brand" dijon -- there are no extra overpowering flavor notes to muddy the clear mustard flavor. Bottom line: I really do love this stuff! Highly recommended.

title: Convenient, quick to prepare, great quality ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Success Boil-in-Bag rice. I've used it for years, starting with the white rice version and now the brown rice version. It's so easy to make -- put water and bag o' rice into a saucepan, bring to a boil and boil for 8-10 minutes, pull the bag of now-cooked rice out of the water, drain, cut the bag open and empty into a bowl. Done!

I also tried preparing this in the microwave (in the interest of complete analysis): put bag o' rice and water into a large bowl, nuke for 10 minutes on high, remove the bag and drain, cut the bag open and empty into a bowl. I was expecting there to be some differences between the stovetop and microwave preparation versions. Nope -- taste exactly the same: same texture, same flavor, etc. Using the microwave shortens the process by as long as it takes to bring the water to a boil on the stovetop (on my gas stove, that's about 8 minutes). So I intend to use the microwave preparation method in the future.

I use the rice in casseroles (chicken/broccoli/cheese/rice is one of my favorites), as a base for chili (a cup of rice topped with a cup of my homemade "knock-your-socks-off" chili topped with some shredded colby-jack cheese), and in salads (chicken, rice, chopped apricots, sliced almonds, sliced spring onions, and a raspberry/balsamic vinaigrette). Good stuff!

Parboiled rice offers great convenience and versatility. Success Rice is a super example -- highly recommended!

title: Seriously addictive! ...
text:
Took a chance on these. I love pecans, and I love cinnamon, so the combination is a winner in my book.

These are fresh and crunchy with just the right amount of sweet cinnamon-y coating -- but not *too* sweet. The balance between sweet and "spicy" is perfect. My biggest problem -- they're so tasty I can't keep the bag within arm's reach or I'll eat far too many. I've portioned them out into 2 oz "servings" stored in zipper snack-size bags and stored in the fridge. That way, I just pull out a bag and that's my limit (it's still a little "pricey" in terms of calorie hit, but I just work it into my overall daily intake).

The expiration date is 8 months from the date of delivery -- plenty of time to enjoy these before that date.

Will definitely purchase these again.

title: Excellent flavor, more like graham crackers from years ago ...
text:
Wow! I actually prefer these to the more famous brand -- the flavor of these is outstanding! Much more like the graham crackers I remember from my childhood.

I use these mostly for eating spread with Nutella OR to make a crust for cheesecake or an ice cream pie. The flavor compliments everything nicely. You get a large amount of as well. Really happy with these! They're close to the perfect graham cracker -- crisp, great flavor, works great for graham cracker crumb crust -- I can't find anything wrong with these. Solid 5 stars as far as I'm concerned ...

title: Not a fan, sorry ...
text:
I regularly drink another brand's raspberry lemonade drink mix -- it's my favorite "go-to" beverage year 'round. So I was looking forward to comparing this product with that product.

Bottom line: I'll stick to my tried-and-true drink mix. This one just has a seriously odd aftertaste and tastes of neither raspberry nor lemon - just a sort of sharp acidic flavor with an overpowering sweetness. I really wish I could like it more than I do but I've tried the whole box (each packet makes a pint or so -- I use two in a quart Nalgene bottle), hoping that it might grow on me, but ... no.

I rate it as "OK" since flavor preference is definite a personal thing, and I'm sure there are folks who might find this absolutely appealing. Me? I won't purchase more of it.

title: Nice round hazelnut flavor, "cream"y taste ...
text:
I usually use Coffee-mate French Vanilla powdered creamer, but I was interested in trying this Hazelnut liquid. I've used the Hazelnut powered creamer int he past and liked it, so I was interested to see how this compared.

Bottom line: much better! It has a "creamier" texture (natch -- it's a liquid) with just the right hint of hazelnut flavor. It's also shelf-stable until opened, which is a bit plus for me (I'm single, and don't go through this as fast as some folks).

This may just get me to break my "powder" Coffee-mate habit! Good stuff, for sure

title: Summer means salads, and salads need dressing ...
text:
I've been a fan of Hidden Valley Original Ranch ever since it first came on the scene as a mix that you mixed with buttermilk and some other items to get that distinctive flavor. Since then, they've gone on to offer a bottled version, and expanded the available flavors. Still good after all these years.

This package contains two "regular" Ranch dressing and an Avocado version. The biggest difference is the calories: 90 per serving for the Avocado version, 140 for the original. Since I'm already familiar with the original Ranch flavor, I decided to focus on the Avocado. Bottom line: very subtle avocado flavor, you still get the original Ranch "tang." Really not a huge difference between the two in flavor, but enough to be noticeable.

I like it, and I'm adding the new Avocado flavor into my salad dressing "rotation."

title: Great hazelnut flavor, dissolves quickly --
text: I've been using Coffe-Mate French Vanilla for years, so when the opportunity arose to try the Hazelnut flavor, I jumped at it.  I like the sugar free version -- it dissolves quickly and the flavor it excellent!  Color me surprised!  I thought it would have an artificial taste, but no.  Very nice clear hazelnut flavor that's not too strong, with a slightly "buttery" taste.  Good stuff!  I'll probably alternate between my old-time favorite French Vanilla and this Hazelnut variety.  Solid 5 stars: I love it.

title: Nice twist on almond bark ...
text:
Do you like dark chocolate? Do you like almond bark? If so, you'll probably like these, The almonds are chopped finer than you find in other almond barks, but I rather like that as you get an even distribution of almonds throughout the bark.

But it's the dark chocolate that really shines here. It's an intense dark chocolate and appears to be a very good quality. As the product name says, these are "thins" -- more like "chips" but still recognizable as almond bark. There's also a slight hint of sea salt. I was a little concerned that it would be too salty -- not no. It's really just about perfect -- just that little after taste of salty brightness.

Definitely would purchase these as a tasty after dinner snack. They're so intensely chocolaty that only a couple of chips is all it takes for a satisfying end-of-meal treat. Good stuff here!

title: Just about perfect caramels ...
text:
These are some of the best caramels I've tried. They're handmade in small batches, and each piece is individually wrapped in waxed paper, like old-fashioned candies I remember from my childhood (yes, I'm that old). The flavor is pure caramel goodness, rich and buttery with just a hint of salt. The pecan bits are tiny and there aren't a lot of them, but I can definitely taste them. They're soft caramels -- no risk of losing a filling due to excessively sticky/hard caramels.

I like these enough to try a few other flavors. I find that one of these can satisfy my sweet tooth - they're rather rich and creamy. Definitely a quality product with great caramel flavor. Love them!

title: Ready Rice: Whole Grain Brown Rice -- convenient, super simple to prepare, works great as a base for other stuff ...
text:
I like the convenience of "heat and eat" rice and am happy to see more companies coming out with their versions of it. I've been using Uncle Ben's rice products for years and yes, cooking from dry rice either on the stove or in a rice cooker yields a better end result. But when I'm under the weather and just want something fast, this helps me get a meal prepared in short order.

I use this a lot with stir fries. I keep "stir-fry packs" in the freezer with diced chicken or steak or shrimp in a small zip bag, and frozen stir-fry veggies in another small zip bag, then bundle them together in a large freezer bag. That way, I just grab a pack out of the freezer and a pack of this Ready Rice Whole Grain Brown Rice, start the stir fry, and when it's almost done, pop the rice into the microwave. I also like to top it with my home-made "Knock Your Socks Off!" chili for a quick meal.

Quality is fine for this use -- not the greatest rice I've eaten but when smothered with other goodies, it works great. Solid 4 stars.

title: "Mini-me" Oreos -- thinner, smaller, but same big flavor ...
text:
I got the "original" flavor - the one we all know and love. These are little miniature versions of the original: thinner, smaller in diameter, but packed with the same Oreo flavor I grew up with and love.

Thirteen of these little "mini"-Oreos has 140 calories, so they're still "high-octane" snacks, but really 13 of these can satisfy my sweet treat craving. So all is good.

Would definitely consider purchasing if the cost is economical. Tasty and flavorful -- good stuff!

title: Unexpectedly good flavor/texture for gluten-free pasta ...
text:
I liked these more than I thought I would. I've tried some varieties "gluten-free" pasta that were just plain nasty. Not these. If I didn't know beforehand, I could easily mistake this for "regular" pasta.

First -- I don't need to avoid gluten, but I have a friend with celiac disease who needs to follow a gluten-free diet, so I'm always on the lookout for new products that she might enjoy.

I've tried three of these so far: Creamy Garlic Herb, Parmesan Pesto, and Creamy Alfredo. I really liked all of them, but my favorite is probably the Creamy Alfredo due to its versatility. I can easily add some chicken, shrimp, or some chopped roasted veggies to this to add to serving size without adding too much in terms of calories. The box says you get 3 servings -- that serving size was fine for me.

Preparation is very easy, much like other similar "pasta side"-type products. You cook the noodles, then add a sauce mix with oil/butter and either milk or water. Nothing tricky, and everything is ready about 15 minutes after the water boils.

I like that these provide a good amount of protein per serving, too. They're a little high in sodium so if you're sodium-restricted, these might not work for you.

Overall, better than expected. I really do like them and will probably purchase more as soon as I figure out my favorite flavors. (I'm trying Sundried Tomato Basil today).

title: Sparkling water lightly flavored with orange and mango -- refreshing alternative to plain water ...
text:
I actually liked this a little more than I thought I would. I'm not much of a fan of flavored carbonated water, but this one actually works.

First things first -- this is NOT soda pop. It's not sweetened other than via the fruit juices that have been added. And the flavoring is very light. So if you're expecting something similar to Fanta Orange soda or the equivalent, you'll be disappointed.

That said, it is very refreshing over ice. I got the Orange Mango flavor, and mango is the predominant flavor by far. I could taste the orange but just barely. Not a problem for me as I like both mango and orange -- but just be aware that you'll likely taste more mango than orange.

I also got the16 ounce can version -- larger than the usual 12-oz soda cans.

I liked this enough that I may order more of the Orange Mango -- and maybe try one or two other flavors, too. I can see this being a "go to" alternative to water, especially during the summer.

Bottom line: I like it.

title: Ginger Sparkling Soda -- refreshing and not too sweet ...
text:
This review is for the Ginger variety of DRY Soda.

What a pleasant surprise! I generally like ginger ale but often find it too sweet or too insipid in ginger flavor. This is neither! The sweetness level is perfect, so it lets the bright ginger flavor shine through.

Each can holds 12 ounces -- the same as most canned soft drinks -- but these cans are taller and skinnier. So far, I've had it plain over ice, mixed with vodka and apple juice for an Apple Cider Surprise, and mixed with vodka, cranberry juice, and juice of a lemon (about 1 oz) for a Cedarwood. Yum! It plays well with other ingredients so that's a big "plus" in my book.

I had never tried this before and I'm impressed enough by it to try some of the other flavors -- especially the Rainier Cherry. Should be interesting!

title: Dove does it again ...
text:
Large bag of Dove dark chocolates, three varieties in three different color foil wrappers making for a very attractive collection when displayed in a candy dish.

If you're familiar with Dove's dark chocolate, you'll feel right at home with these. The flavors are plain solid dark chocolate, dark and white chocolate swirl, and dark chocolate surrounding a soft caramel filling. Yummy! As always, it's quite rich -- I find I'm perfectly satisfied after eating just a few of these.

This would be a nice addition to a Valentine's gift for the dark chocolate lover in your life. Really fine chocolate!

title: So many uses - not overly spicy -- just right!
text: I first had this sauce when a friend brought a bottle back from Belize over 20 years ago.  I know the company has changed hands since then, but the bottle I recently purchased from Amazon is very close to my first bottle of this.  The "Hot" is just right to add a little head with good flavor.  I use it to heat up red beans and rice, chicken soup, egg/hash browns/sausage casserole -- anything that could use a little "bump" in flavor.  Not *too* hot (some folks might disagree) -- I like that you can actually taste the ingredients even though it's spicy.  Good stuff!

title: Still tasty after all these years ...
text: A childhood favorite, these definitely measured up to my memory of them.  No quality issues at all; expiration date was far enough in the future that I didn't worry about them expiring before I finished them.  Prime Pantry makes it convenient to get these when I order my "monthly" pantry box.  I prefer these little 6-donut packs rather than the bags as it helps with "portion control."  :-)  Overall, good product, will order again.

title: Crispy thin "snickerdoodle" Cinnamon Sugar cookie chips ...
text: Got a sample of these in an Amazon Sweets Dash delivery and LOVED them.  I liked them so much I ordered more!  They taste just like snickerdoodle cookies flavor-wise, but the texture is crisp and thin ("chips" is a good description), and they're just a little more buttery in flavor.  Really nice to have a handful of these at the end of a meal as a little sweet treat.  Will definitely order again ...

title: Excellent quality "neutral" oil ...
text: I've been using La Tourangelle Grapeseed Oil for several years now and love it!  It has a high smoke point and is "neutral" -- doesn't add any distinctive flavor notes.  It works great for general sautéing (does a wonderful job browning chicken, for example).  I also use it for oven-roasted veggies (toss potatoes, sweet potatoes, broccoli, brussels sprouts, carrots, whatever I have on hand with a little oil and some herbs, then load onto a sheet pan and roast until tender).  Economical, too -- will continue to purchase this as long as it's available on Amazon.

title: Surprisingly excellent -- great flavor, unique snack ...
text:
What do you get when you combine the taste of a snickerdoodle and the thinness of a potato chip? You get spectacularly yummy cinnamon sugar cookie chips! I got these in a "Sweets" box a few months ago and liked them so much that I put them on subscribe and save. They're super tasty and not overly spendy in terms of calorie hit. Just go easy on them and savor the flavor.

Really good stuff here. Highly recommended!

title: Tasty, easy to prepare, the "best of breed" for dehydrated potato shreds ...
text:
What a treat! I love having the smaller containers of dehydrated shredded potatoes so I can cook up a smaller batch without opening a larger carton.

These are VERY good, indeed! I just use my countertop electric kettle to heat some water, then add it to the carton, seal it up, and go on to gather whatever else I need for dinner. By the time I have everything else assembled, the potato shreds are ready to crisp up in the skillet.

One thing, though -- the directions say to cook "3-4 minutes" over medium-high heat" to get them crispy. That has not been my experience. That might heat them through, but crisp? no. I've prepared 4 of the cartons so far and EVERY time it takes 10 minutes on the first side to get crispy/medium brown, and another 5-7 minutes on the other side. I usually add another 1 tsp of oil when I flip them (I like mine extra crispy, though, so your mileage might vary).

They also say each carton provides 7 servings. Not really, unless you are one of 7 children You'll get maybe 1 3/4 Cups of finished cripsy shredded potatoes, which will provide 4-5 servings at most, 3 if folks are really hungry. I can usually get 3 servings from each carton as a single -- I make these for breadfast and serve with 2 scrambled eggs, 2 sausage links, and some fresh fruit. That holds me until lunchtime.

Flavor is excellent, the best of any of the dehydrated potato shreds I've tried (and I've tried most of them). I'll continue to purchase these as long as I can get a good deal on them on Amazon. I really like them that much!

title: I may never make homemade turkey gravy again ...
text:
Really great turkey flavor and so easy to prepare! I love to cook from scratch and usually stay away from "mix and fix" items, but a series of health issues just before Thanksgiving left me with depleted energy and a meal to prepare (temporary setback, all better now). I read the reviews, read the ingredients, and decided to give this a try.

Honestly, I may never make homemade turkey gravy again. This stuff is that good! For Thanksgiving dinner, I made one change: instead of using boiling (plain) water, I used my own vegetable stock (that's how I use up odds and ends of veggies like celery, carrots, onions, potatoes, etc.: make a few gallons of stock and freeze it in 2 C containers). I made 2 cups of gravy (the instructions are on the package for smaller amounts), and it was a smash hit. I had leftovers of turkey and dressing (naturally), so I made another batch of this gravy using just water. Not quite the depth of flavor I got from using veggie stock, but still -- so much better than I expected!

I'm single, so I like the fact that I can make smaller amounts (I made 1 C of gravy using the 2-C measurements divided in half ... came out just fine). Less waste, fewer leftovers.

I like this enough that I'm tempted to try some of this brand's other gravy/sauce mixes. Solid 5 stars from me -- I really do love it!

title: Memories of my hometown Greek restaurant ...
text: These are the closest I've found to the stuffed grape leaves from my favorite hometown Greek restaurant.  Just the right combination of mint, garlic, rice, and packed in oil, but not overly "greasy," these are a nice change of pace from my usual hors-d'oeuvres.  Will definitely purchase again, but may get the larger 4.4 lb can (makes more sense from an economy standpoint).

title: Excellent quality, nice stocking stuffers!
text: Got these to use in some gift baskets I was putting together for a fundraiser.  Of course I had to try one pack before including them in the baskets and I was really impressed at how good the tea is.  No reservations about including some of the various flavors in my gift baskets.  The size is perfect for my use.  I packaged a nice porcelain mug, some hot cocoa mix, hot cider mix, cappuccino mix, and one of these little boxes of tea bags along with some cookies and small chocolates in a small basket, wrapped in cellophane and tied with a gold ribbon.  Perfect!!  Would recommend these without reservation for stocking stuffers for that tea lover on your list.  Solid 5 stars!

title: The same great quality in a single-serving packet ...
text: No issues at all.  Heinz is my "brand" of choice for all things "pickle" -- relish, sandwich dills, etc.  I'm single and rarely get through an entire bottle of relish before it goes bad.  Having individual serving packets solves that problem completely.  No waste, great flavor, always fresh.  Will purchase again if needed.

title: A childhood favorite ...
text: I've been a fan of these little powdered sugar donuts since I was a child.  The shipment I received was in decent shape -- some "breakage," a few donuts reduced to crumbs -- but less than I expected given the givens.  The expiration date was about 7 weeks out, so that's acceptable to me.  No issues, really.  Will order again.

title: Soooo good!  If you're a Baileys Irish Cream fan, you MUST try these ...
text:
OK, first things first: I'm an unrepentant chocoholic. I'm also a huge fan of Baileys Irish Cream -- it's my "after-dinner" liquid treat of choice. So pairing them both in a single bite makes for a real sensory treat.

These consist of a milk chocolate shell covering a smooth Baileys Irish Cream-flavored center. These are non-alcoholic, but the flavor of Baileys is strong and clear. The chocolate coating is the perfect thickness to create a real balance of flavors. The container I received held 54 individually-wrapped candies, so you do get quite a few. And with the intensity of flavor, I find I need to eat only a couple of these to get my chocolate fix. No binging on these -- they're very rich, creamy and luscious!

I can honestly say they're now among my favorite candies and I'm planning to keep them on hand over the holidays. They really are that good!

title: Really nice Irish Breakfast Tea ...
text: During the summer I'm usually a coffee girl, but in the winter, I love a good mug of hot tea to start off the morning.  This is the best Irish Breakfast Tea I've tried.  Robust flavor but not too "puckery."  I usually brew a large mug (around 22 oz), and a single bag is all I need to get a nice medium-strong mug of tea.  This is definitely my new favorite.  I now have it on "subscribe and save" -- never have to worry about running out!

title: Decent tart orange flavor -- not too sweet ...
text: Like this more than I thought I would.  The orange version has a very intense orange flavor; not too sweet, either.  Each package contains 3 servings (100cal per serving), so just remember that if you decide to consume the entire package in one sitting.  The primary ingredients are pineapple puree, papaya puree, peach puree, mandarin orange puree, and pear puree.  For me, this provides a little sweet "treat" at the end of a meal without overdoing things.  Will likely purchase again as long as it remains economically feasible.

title: BETTER than the more famous brand ...
text:
I would never have believed it! These are actually better than Oreos. It has to do with the filling -- it has a hint of vanilla and is not as sweet tasting as the more famous brand. It might have something to do with the use of cane sugar in this version rather than a mixture of sugar + high fructose corn syrup in the alternative. Whatever the reason, these just taste better! Not cloyingly sweet, nice rich chocolate flavor and that hint of vanilla.

I try to limit my treats, usually having 2-3 of these with dinner. It's the perfect sweet touch at the end of a meal, totally satisfying. Will purchase these again.

title: Super convenient, cooks nicely right in the package -- tasty and fast!
text:
I had tried another Barilla Ready Pasta and thought it was OK -- not great, not terrible, just ... OK.

I just tried this one. What a difference! The gumminess that I found with the earlier elbow version of this is mostly missing in this version. I prepared it according to package directions, then combined it with some homemade marinara and roasted summer veggies, topped with shaved parmesan. YUM! Next trial was alfredo sauce + shrimp + sundried tomatoes -- another winner. The shape of this pasta holds up well to things like meatballs and lots of cheese. Each package makes two small-ish servings or 1 generous serving. I usually load it up with sauce + veggies + other stuff, so I get 2 servings from each package. Perfect!

Honestly, I don't know what they did differently with this version, but the difference is remarkable. Definitely worth having on hand when I need a quick no-brainer supper.

title: Tasty snack -- not overly sweet ...
text:
This Fruit and Seed Blend offers a good combination of dried blueberries, dried cranberries, pepitas (pumpkin seeds) and sunflower seeds, in about equal parts. Nice flavor, no preservatives -- not as sweet as other dried fruit/seed blends. This is NOT low-calorie, however, so moderation will be necessary -- it's really good stuff and the tendency to overdo will be strong.

My favorite way to use this: 1/4 C mixed into plain Greek yogurt (about 4-6 oz). I've also added it to my favorite high-protein pancake mix -- yummy!

Bottom line: I like it. It has a nice "healthy" flavor, not *too* sweet (although the dried berries are sweetened), and plays well with other items.

title: A tasty blast from the past ...
text:
Wow! I didn't know this stuff was still around. It used to be my favorite cereal of all time, and then I sort of lost track of it. Saw it here on Amazon and ordered it from the Pantry.

It's just like I remember it! Great "oatmeal" taste with just the right amount of cinnamon and spice. Good right out of the box, too, as a snack. I usually have a "standard" serving (3/4 C) with about 1/3 C milk, along with some fresh fruit or small 1-egg veggie frittata -- the perfect size breakfast and a tasty beginning to my day.

Will continue purchasing this as long as Amazon carries (it's not available at my local supermarket).

title: Convenient and tasty!  Super Pizza sauce ...
text:
This is by far my favorite pizza sauce, and I've tried a lot of them! Not too sweet, lots of basil flavor, just the right amount of garlic & onion flavor, too. I love the squeeze bottle. I'm usually cooking for 1 person, so this lets me get just the right amount of sauce onto a 7" crust without having to worry about what to do with the rest of a can of sauce. Keeps great in the fridge for at least 2 weeks or more. I usually make 2-3 small pizzas a week with different toppings, so I go through a bottle of this every couple of weeks or so.

Will keep purchasing this as long as I can find it -- and so far, Amazon has been the most reliable source (my small-town local supermarket is hit-or-miss with specialty products like this). Solid 5 stars for sure!

title: The BEST "orange" soda I've had:  Sanpellegrino Clementine!  Wow!!
text:
I'm always on the look out for "off the beaten path" soft drinks -- unusual flavors, especially, or a different taste combo. I tried this Clementine flavor based on a couple of recommendations from friends.

Wow! This stuff is great!

It's not *too* sweet, and it doesn't have that weird metallic taste I get sometimes from artificial flavors. The flavor in this is all natural, with 17% juice (a combination of Mandarin, Orange, and Clementine juices). It does have 140 calories per can, though, so if you're watching calories or sugar intake, this might be a problem.

I figure it's all good in moderation -- a can of this after dinner or with lunch isn't going to kill me. The flavor really is superior. I love it!

title: A great fruit-flavored tea for those who don't like fruit-flavored teas ...
text: I was pleasantly surprised by this tea.  I'm not usually overly fond of "fruit"-flavored hot tea, but this is so nicely balanced that I'm planning to purchase more of it.  You get a nice hint of mango -- not too strong, and not overly sweet.  I did use just a tiny bit of sugar (maybe 1/2 tsp) just to brighten it up a bit.  It's perfect with English muffins (with butter and orange marmalade), with Welsh cakes, even with plain bagels and cream cheese.  Really nice flavor.

title: Wow!  Works great on steak, pork chops, and chicken ...
text:
What a pleasant surprise! I usually make my own marinades, but I saw this and decided to give it a try.

It's NOT "barbecue sauce," at least not in the traditional sense. It does have a nice slightly smoky flavor (but not too pronounced), and a tomato/molasses base, but there's a complex blend of other flavors that make this truly unique.

My first use was on a piece of skirt steak that I grilled to use in a salad. I put about 1/4 C of the marinade in a zipper bag with the steak and refrigerated it for about 4 hrs. Grilled just until medium rare, sliced thinly and tossed with lettuce, tomatoes, sweet onion, and cucumber. Yum!! Since then, I've also used it with boneless pork chops (grilled on the stovetop) and skin-on bone-in chicken thighs (baked). All equally good!

I like this enough that I'll definitely be purchasing again. Really great flavor! Solid 5 stars.

title: Excellent sandwich slices -- super on burgers!
text:
The best I've tried -- great on burgers and sandwiches. Just the right thickness, too. You get a lot per jar -- enough for a dozen burgers at least.
Flavor is not too sour -- really just perfect! Will definitely purchase again.

title: Great size for singles/couples -- makes 2-3 servings of yummy sauce
text:
I'm an experienced home cook but I'm usually cooking only for myself. The small package here works nicely for making a small batch of sauce -- a couple of servings or so.

I usually don't use "convenience" product like this do make my sauces -- I prefer to make things "from scratch" whenever possible -- so I was a little skeptical about how good it would be. I needn't have worried. I used it to make a mushroom/peppercorn sauce for grilled steak and garlic mashed potatoes. I started with the recipe included in the package and embellished it a little. The sauce calls for butter, shallots, fresh sliced mushrooms (I used a combination of cremini and oyster), red wine, cream, and the entire 1.5-oz cup of demi glace. I added a couple of tablespoons of mixed peppercorns (black, green, pink, etc.) slightly crushed with a mortar & pestle, to the sauce. Turned out VERY tasty and just the right complement to the steak and potatoes. Made enough for two generous servings, too.

This is the kind of convenience product I can like -- not overly processed, nice flavor, not overly salty, easy to use. Good stuff -- solid 5 stars. I'm putting it on subscribe and save.

title: Why haven't I tried this before??
text:
I consider myself an "experienced home cook." I've never had any training other than a little from my mother, and the rest from years of just doing it, experimenting, etc. I've used various forms of chicken broth and chicken stock, but never tried a demi-glace version. Now I wonder why I waited so long?

This stuff is gold. It's a highly concentrated -- you need only a couple of teaspoons per cup of water -- and the flavor is simply amazing. I've used it so far to make a yummy apple & squash soup, instead of water to make rice (seriously good!), and braised chicken thighs with a mushroom sauce.

One thing I often worry about with packaged stocks is salt -- many of them are seriously overly salty. This one is not. Sodium count for 2 tsp of demi-glace is 310mg (that would be equivalent to 1 C stock). Not bad at all.

I just keep mine in the fridge and use a little once or twice a week. Still can't believe it adds so much flavor to sauces and soups. Good stuff!

title: Surprise! Superb quality extra virgin olive oil ...
text:
Better than I expected! This is really nice olive oil, comparable to many mid-range offerings. I've used it so far for a balsamic vinaigrette salad dressing, as a dipping oil for fresh homemade bread (with some finely chopped fresh herbs), and for sautéing chicken breasts, scallops, and sea bass. No complaints at all. I also like that's it's offered in a dark-colored bottle. I keep mine in the pantry where it's generally cooler than the kitchen.

I have to admit, I was skeptical about trying olive oil with an Amazon label. But this is the real deal -- truly excellent quality. Solid 5 stars.

title: Not a fan of these ...
text:
I wish I liked these better. I'm a HUGE fan of Archway cookies and purchase them often. But these "frosty lemon" cookies fell short of my expectations.

The biggest disappointment: the lemon flavor. The ingredients list "natural and artificial flavors" -- and all I can taste is a highly acrid artificial "sour" lemon taste. I've made lemon cookies myself (with real lemon peel and freshly-squeezed lemon juice) -- and these are just not very good.

The texture is soft, yes, but VERY crumbly. The lemon glaze is OK, but I don't think it adds much except a touch of sweetness that helps (a little) to counter the incredibly sour artificial lemon taste.

Obviously, your mileage may vary. What I perceive as "acrid" you might taste as "tart." Just relaying my own experience.
Bottom line: sorry, I didn't like these. I LOVE Archway's Molasses cookies (both the iced ones as well as the plain ones), Windmills, Iced Oatmeal, and their Soft Dutch Cocoa -- I'll stick with those.

title: I like this, with some reservations ...
text:
I have somewhat mixed feelings about this product. Some aspects I like ... a LOT ... and others, not so much.

On the plus side, it's convenient and super easy to prepare in the microwave. Even if you're using it for a cold pasta salad you still need to cook it; otherwise, the flavor and texture will be "off." (I tasted one of the "elbows" before cooking ... yeah, it needs to be cooked.)
The pouch makes two smallish servings or one moderate-sized one. I used mine to make a macaroni salad with shrimp and managed to get two decent sized servings with the addition of veggies and shrimp. I just used my regular recipe -- mayo, mustard, vinegar, sugar, chopped celery, chopped green onion, and mini shrimp (sometimes called "salad shrimp"). Mixed it up and chilled it for a couple of hours. Tasty!

What I don't like -- the texture is a little odd even after cooking. Just a bit gummy -- not super bad, but enough that you'll notice. Most of that gumminess disappears with sauce or dressing. It's also heavier than dried pasta -- the walls of the elbows are thicker. Again, just a little odd. None of this affects the flavor, and I tend to use strong flavors in my sauces and dressings so it's not that big a deal for me.

Bottom line: I like it, with some reservations. It's not something I'd use every day -- I prefer Barilla's dried pasta and since I'm usually cooking for one, it doesn't take long to cook up a serving from dried product. But I might purchase this occasionally to have on hand for those times when I'm craving pasta and just want something quick (rotini with creamy pesto and crisp prosciutto for example).

title: Tasty and super easy to prepare ...
text:
I like to have some of these Zatarain's Big Easy rice packets on hand for those days when I'm rushed or not in the mood to cook much. This Red Beans & Rice is one of my two favorite flavors (the other is Dirty Rice). I usually grill a sausage of some kind (spicy chicken sausage, brautwurst, etc.). Prepare the rice in the microwave, slice the sausage and combine. Put together a quick side salad and ... lunch! I've also pan seared the sausage in a small skillet, add the rice from the pouch, a couple of tablespoons of water, cover, and heat 5 minutes or so, stirring once in awhile. Again, super tasty, super easy.

Will continue to purchase -- really excellent once-in-awhile quick-fix meal.

title: All the flavor of the original Oreos -- just "flatter" ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Oreos -- ever since I was a child (and I'm really old now). The biggest problem, though, is that I tend to eat too many. I tried a few "tricks" to mitigate that tendency with mixed results.

That's why I was interested in trying these, and I'm very glad I did.

I get all the flavor of Oreos, and they're the same diameter -- just thinner. Mine were perfectly crisp and fresh with the familiar white creamy icing in the middle. And they're pre-packaged into 4-cookie packs. Much easier to limit consumption.

I'm sure I could get them other places at lower cost, but I haven't seen them in any of the supermarkets around here. And I can get these delivered right to my door.

title: Canada's answer to Cheetos Crunchy snacks ...
text:
Someone on a Facebook group I frequent recommended these, so I decided to give them a try. I love all things "cheese" and "crunchy," so I figured I'd probably be happy with these.

And I am. They're VERY crunchy, closer to the Cheetos Crunchy variety than to the Cheetos Puffs version. They're not uniform in size (they range from tiny to thumb-size), which is fine with me. They're not overly salty, either -- a major complaint I have with some snacks like this. They're packaged in seven 5.6 oz packs, so they stay fresher longer than if this was just one big bag of snacks.

My only complaint is that they're not super cheesy. I think I'm just used to the US counterpart where the cheese flavor is predominant. Don't get me wrong -- they're GOOD, really good. Just ... different. I like them enough that I'll definitely be ordering again

title: Wonderful crispy snack ...
text:
Like others, I'm sure, I first tasted these in a "pub mix" blend of pretzel stix, cheese twists, and rice treats. It was love at first taste, and I spent some time trying to find a source for just these sesame chips. Tried a couple of other options, but this is the clear winner! It comes closest to the taste of the sesame treats in the pub mix -- a little salty, a little sweet, and a tender "crunch" that is ... well ... just about perfect.

I eat them "straight up," of course, but one of my favorite ways to use them is in my own savory trail mix: these crackers, mini pretzels, cheeze crackers (or goldfish crackers), honey roasted almonds, and corn chex cereal. I usually have a couple of bowls of this out for cocktail parties and it always goes over well.

Will continue to purchase these as long as they're still available. These OliveNation chips have the best flavor and definitely are the freshest tasting. Solid 5 stars!

title: Nice way to end a meal on a sweet spot ...
text: Nice tart cherry flavor with just the right amount of dark chocolate.  Chewy without being too "sticky," and large enough to keep hunger in check.  I usually use these as a part of my evening meal as a sort of "sweet ender."  Nuts are flavorful and fresh tasting (no stale nuts here).  Will likely keep these on hand -- I really like them!

title: My new favorite Pop-Tart ...
text: I was pleasantly surprised at how good these Frosted Cinnamon Roll Pop-Tarts are!  You get the flavor and aroma of a cinnamon roll, with a light vanilla-flavored icing.  They're not overly sweet, either.  These work for me as part of an overall breakfast when I'm in a rush (1 pop-tart, plain Greek yogurt topped with fruit, coffee).  I can't find them locally, so being able to have them delivered to my door is a major plus.  Will definitely purchase again (and again ... ) as long as they're available on Amazon.

title: Odd flavor, mostly "smoke" ...
text: Not as good as I hoped.  They're OK, but there's something odd about the flavor.
