You get a smoky hit, but not much "bacon" flavor -- and added to the flaky/buttery/sweetness of the traditional Ritz flavors, it just didn't work for me.  I may try one of the other flavors as I like the idea of a crispy "snack"-type treat that isn't some variation of potato chips.  But I won't be ordering this "bacon"-flavored variety again.

title: Better than expected -- easier to eat, low calorie ...
text:
I'm not a huge fan of beef jerky because it's usually tough and difficult to bite. So I was interested to see how this Jack Links "extra tender" product measured up.

Answer: quite nicely. I was impressed with both the tenderness and flavor. I'm familiar with several other Jack Links products (their Tender Bites are great as a snack on road trips), so I sort of knew what to expect in terms of flavor. Not overly salty, just the right amount of spice. Good stuff.

You get a substantial amount per package, too, and it's low calorie (if that's important). I definitely would consider purchasing this regularly.

title: Nice new entry into the "healthy" soup field ...
text:
I liked this more than I thought I would. It has a nice balance of ingredients: black beans, quinoa, corn, and red peppers with tomatoes. Not too spicy at all -- relatively mild, really. The consistency is quite good -- not too thick or thin. I added a little cheese before serving. Delish!

The entire can has 340 calories (2 servings, 170 calories each), so it's not *too* much of a calorie hit. "Well Yes!" seems to be a new Campbell's brand that showcases natural ingredients, no preservatives, and nutrient-dense soups. This is honestly good stuff. I'd give it five stars if it had a little more flavor (I'm a "spicy food" person, and to me, Black Bean soup needs to have some heat/spice/bold flavor). I like it enough, however, to order it regularly. I can always add a splash of hot sauce or some fresh chopped jalapeño.

title: Not a favorite ...
text:
I think children might like this better than I did. It's a pink-ish applesauce with small bits/chunks of cooked apple. I really didn't taste much strawberry flavor -- it was mostly just sweet. And the applesauce is a rather strange texture -- almost too smooth for applesauce.

Sorry -- I'm a huge fan of Dole fruit items (especially their grapefruit), but this didn't do much for me. I'll take regular applesauce with a little cinnamon added.

title: Regular peanut Snickers with a *hint* of hazelnut flavor ...
text:
Snickers has long been one of my favorite candy bars. So I was curious to see how hazelnuts would work with the basic "formula."

The bottom line: this is still the same basic Snickers bar: caramel, nougat, chocolate, and peanuts -- with the addition of some hazelnuts. I get the hazelnut flavor -- barely perceptible, but present. But if "Hazelnut" is going to be featured on the label, I would expect the flavor to be more pronounced.

On the plus side -- you get two "bars" in each large package: one for now, and one for later, so that's a nice packaging plus.

Don't get me wrong -- these are still very good as far as "Snickers" is concerned. But they need to increase the proportion of hazelnuts (eliminating some of the peanuts) to make it worth the prominence of labeling this as "SNICKERS Hazelnut."

If you want a traditional Snickers with just a hint of hazelnut flavor, these will work. But otherwise, just go for the regular Snickers.

title: Perfect size, great taste ...
text:
I'm single, and usually can't work my way through a large jar of this salsa before it goes bad. These small portions are the perfect size for when I make quesadillas or burritos (or even just with chips) just for myself. I store them in a cool place (the pantry is between the garage and the kitchen) and this way I use just what I need for each occasion.

And this is a very respectable salsa -- chunky texture (my favorite) with a little kick of spice. "Hot" is kind of subjective, but this is rated "medium" and I'd say it's on the "milder" side of "medium" compared to other brands. If I want more heat, I just add a few drops of hot sauce to the salsa.

Like someone else mentioned, I'd really like this better in a smaller carton (maybe 12 or 15 instead of 30 tubs), but this has a nice long shelf life, so I think we're OK.

Overall -- I love this stuff. It's really good salsa in a convenient package. Highly recommended!

title: Same great taste as the canned version, but in a smaller more convenient package ...
text:
This is the same Hunt's Tomato Paste that we know and love -- just packaged differently.

A lot of recipes call for only a couple of tablespoons of tomato paste, but it's usually sold in 6-oz cans. So what do you do with the rest? I've tried freezing it, but I usually forget that it's in the freezer. The bottom line is I end up wasting more than I like.

These 2-Tablespoon pouches are a nice solution. I use just what I need, no waste, no fuss. Quality is just fine, too. I've used this in Beef & Guinness Stew (for St. Patrick's day), pork & lentil stew, and butternut squash & ground turkey chili -- same great taste and texture.

The only downside is that I'm not sure the convenience outweighs the higher cost. I'll watch for deals on this, both here and at my local supermarket (they're not carrying this yet), as I do like it and would love to use it more often. So --- I like it -- 4 stars.

title: Super lower-fat version of a great snack cracker ...
text:
I've loved Cheez-Its ever since I first had them as a child a LONG time ago. This reduced fat version is stellar -- no loss of taste at all compared to the "full fat" version; just not as "greasy."

I try to keep these on hand for that quick salty/crunchy hit, usually with a meal (especially chili or Tex/Mex flavored soups). It doesn't take too many to satisfied that particular craving. Just about the perfect snack!

title: Seriously addictive! ...
text:
Wow, are these ever addictive! If you like the combined tastes of chocolate and peanut butter, this is for you.

M&M's Peanut has long been my Achilles heel in terms of snacks, but these may soon take that honor. Sooooo good! I purchase the larger bag and then repackage them into 1-oz "snack" servings -- otherwise, it's too easy for me to mindlessly overindulge.

Seriously, these are worth a try -- they're just heavenly. Will definitely purchase again.

title: Convenience with no waste ...
text:
I love these little packets of Kraft dressing! I'm single, and often can't get through an entire bottle before it "expires," which means I end up tossing about half the bottle (usually). These packets need no refrigeration, and mine have an expiration date over a year away which should mean no waste.

The taste is exactly the same as the Kraft bottled dressing. I use one packet for a large-ish side salad and two packets when I do a "whole meal" salad (usually greens, mushrooms, bell pepper, carrots, and grilled chicken or shrimp). No muss, no fuss, just perfect!

Will likely look at purchasing some of the other flavors, too. Really good stuff.

title: Chocolatey goodness in a nice assortment of favorites ...
text:
I grew up with Mars candy bars and M&Ms and they're still among my favorite sweet treats.

This box contains an assortment of tried-and-true favorites: Snickers, 3 Musketeers, Twix, M&M Peanut, and M&M Peanut Butter, all in one fairly sturdy box. The candy is fresh -- I've tried one of each so far and nothing has looked or tasted stale or "off." These are full-size candy bars/packages, too -- not mini or "fun" sized. I'm much less likely to overindulge when presented with a single full-size treat than a bagful of smaller servings, especially when it's a tasty treat like these bars.

Definitely a real winner -- solid 5 stars worthy.

title: Good size for a quick snack ...
text:
TWIX fun size cookie bars are buttery caramelly goodness -- very rich and, to my taste, just a tad too sweet. A little definitely goes a long way, which is probably a good thing. One or two is really all I need to tame the chocolate/sweet cravings I get sometimes in the evening. The individual wrap also slows down the tendency to overindulge, too.

No problems as far as freshness is concerned. Mine were in perfect condition.

I do like these one or two at a time.

title: Creamy dark chocolate goodness ...
text:
I'm an unrepentant chocoholic -- I love it in all its forms: milk, dark, filled, etc. Dove chocolates are a better quality chocolate than a lot of other popular brands, and I really like their dark chocolate probably the best of all their varieties.

Very creamy and smooth, but not overly sweet with a hint of dark chocolate "bite." These are perfect for satisfying my after-dinner chocolate craving. Just a couple and I'm good to go. Having to individually unwrap each piece slows me down so that I'm not prone to overindulge mindlessly.

My order contained 4 small-ish bags with about 30 pieces per bag. Each piece contains 42 calories, so a couple of pieces isn't a huge hit from a "diet" standpoint.

Overall, I really love this. For the price, it's excellent quality.

title: Long-term favorite ...
text:
These have been my favorite "all-purpose" crackers for years. They go with just about everything, but I use them mostly as an unobtrusive base for cheese, especially when I'm doing a cheese tasting for friends and family. Our last experience was trying out different cheddars from England, Wales, Scotland, Canada, and the US.

Triscuit comes in some variations -- different flavors, reduced fat, reduced sodium -- but the quality and basic shape is the same. My favorite is the "original," but they're all good -- just for different purposes.

Will continue to purchase as long as Amazon carries them at a good price.

title: Nice lemon + raspberry flavor -- and not too sweet ...
text:
I've been drinking this Crystal Light On-the-Go Raspberry Lemonade off and on for years. It has just the right tart-sweet taste. Yes, I know it's artificially sweetened, but I'm OK with that. I'm not fond of just "plain" water, so I use things like Crystal Light as well as decaf iced tea mix to help me stay well hydrated.

I usually prepare this in a 32-oz polycarbonate water bottle -- fill to about 28 oz with water, add 2 packets of this mix, stir well, then fill to the top with ice. I go through two of bottles a day (so 4 packets of mix). It works for me.

As long as Crystal Light doesn't change the formulation of this too much, I'll continue to include it my rotation of water additives. I really do like it that much -- solid 5 stars from me.

title: Versatile, slightly sweet cornbread mix, super easy to prepare ...
text:
I've been using Marie Callender's Original Corn Bread Mix for years and it's always good. I usually make corn muffins. They're just easier for me to deal with -- I'm single, so I can bake the muffins and freeze them, taking out a couple only when needed.

I also use it with chili -- I make a pot of my knock-you-socks-off chili, put some into a 9" cake pan, heat it in the oven until totally bubbly, top it with some cheese, and then with the cornbread mix prepared according to package instructions, back in the oven until the cornbread is cooked through and lightly browned around the edges. Yumm!!

I've never tried any of the other Marie Callender's varieties as I always have good luck with this. It is a "sweeter" cornbread, so if you don't like sweet cornbread, you probably won't like this. But to me, it tastes exactly like what I've had in Marie Callender restaurants. I like it!

title: Lifetime favorite, Skippy never disappoints ...
text:
I've been a Skippy fan since I was a child -- MANY years ago. My favorite "go-to" for a quick meal is a peanut butter sandwich, a small salad, and an apple or other fruit. It just hits the spot. They've changed the formulation over the years but retained the same basic flavor.

I use the creamy mostly for cooking/baking: peanut butter cookies, peanut sauce for satay or summer roll dip, etc. The Super Chunk is for eating -- sandwiches, peanut butter & celery, peanut butter and crackers, etc. All things in moderation -- this isn't low-cal, but it doesn't take much to satisfy the hunger pangs.

Excellent deal, too -- you get two 64-oz jars. I love the stuff -- a well-deserved 5 stars.

title: Heavy on the coconut, but a nice change of pace from ice tea or soda ...
text:
Very strong coconut flavor, but overall not bad. A serving contains 90 calories, and there are 4 servings per bottle, so that might be a little high for some people. I tried it both "straight," and also with rum. Good either way, fresh "tropical" taste. Not as much citrus as I expected given the name, but still refreshing.

Might purchase again, but I'll probably try another flavor (the peach bellini sounds good). Solid 4 stars: I like it.

title: Great for sandwiches and wraps ...
text:
I usually purchase these locally, but sometimes I'm unable to venture out (health reasons). Being able to get my favorite products online is a super convenience, and when the cost is similar to the local supermarket, it's even better.

These Stackers dill pickle slices are great on burgers, of course, but I use them with cold cut sandwiches and wraps. You get quite a lot per jar, too.

I like dill pickle chips, but these slices seem to cover better. Really tasty, too.

title: A tasty guilty pleasure ...
text:
Yeah, I'll admit it -- I really do like this stuff. People joke about it, but when push comes to shove, it's pretty tasty and easy to prepare for a quick lunch. I use 1/2 of the can, smash it into a skillet with about 1/2 tsp of oil and fry it until crispy on both sides. I usually eat it with a small salad on the side. Makes for a decent lunch with 21g of protein and only 12g of fat (total calories 290 per serving; 2 servings per can).

The only downside: this is the "reduced sodium" version and the sodium content is still rather high (660mg per serving). I now use 1/3 of the can + an egg so I can cut the sodium down to 440mg. I usually add a little cracked pepper for some added brightness. Yum!

title: Lightly salted, great freshness and flavor ...
text: Wow!  Definitely better than I expected.  Very lightly salted, very fresh tasting, no "oily" feel or taste, either.  A LOT of almonds, very few Brazil nuts, good amount of cashews, pecans, and hazelnuts - no peanuts (although the ingredient list includes the possibility of the use of peanut oil in processing).  I've been purchasing another brand of mixed nuts (sold at one of the membership big-box stores), but I'm actually going to switch to Happy Belly.  I like that they're not overly salty, and the flavor is excellent.

title: HUGE barrel of crunchy goodness ...
text:
Wow! The container for these is HUGE and filled to the top with crunchy yummy cheese balls. Seriously, this barrel will last me at least until Christmas. It's at least a 2-gallon barrel -- about twice as big as I thought it would be.

The quality is super, too. Very fresh, "use by" date far enough into the future to make it worthwhile. Will definitely order these again if I can manage to work my way through my first order of these. They're really REALLY good and priced well for the quantity. Solid 5 stars.

title: My favorite salad dressing -- great with grilled chicken and veggies ...
text:
Kraft's Southwest Ranch Dressing is my favorite salad dressing, bar none. It took me awhile to "land" on this one, and it had some great competition, but this is it.

It has just the right balance of spice and bold flavor. There's just a bit of heat -- I wouldn't call it "spicy," but you'll definitely get a hint of heat. I use this mostly with a green salad topped with grilled chicken breast. I grill a bunch of chicken breasts and then freeze them. I put together a classic green salad (lettuce, tomatoes, etc.), then slice some chicken breast. Toss with a couple of tablespoons of this dressing, and top with some shredded cheese. YUM! It's also great as a dip for veggie sticks/strips -- I use different bell peppers (orange, green, red, etc.), jicama, carrot sticks, celery sticks, etc.

I like it enough to have it on subscribe & save --

title: Crunchy and not *too* sweet --
text:
One of my all-time favorites, I have this for breakfast at least 3 times a week, usually with some dried cranberries added. This 70-oz box is reasonably economical -- equivalent to about 4 "regular"-size boxes. You get two sealed pouches (35 oz each), so it helps with freshness. I'm single, so I go through a single pouch in 3-4 weeks normally.

Filling and not *too* sweet -- for me, it's the perfect beginning to my day. I love it.

title: Not bad, but not that great, either ...
text:
Not terribly impressed by this. I really wanted to like it more than I did, but I found the flavor underwhelming and the consistency more like spackling compound -- very thick, chalky, and almost "gummy" or sticky. It sticks to the roof of my mouth and the back of my tongue -- not exactly what I expect from a sweet spreadable dip. The flavor is mostly peanut butter, which is to be expected, but with a name like "Dark Chocolate Dreams," I expected more chocolate flavor. It's almost nonexistent.

A single 1.5-oz cup is one serving and contains 235 calories, 147 from fat. This is mitigated by the 7g protein in each cup. But this isn't something I'll be purchasing in the future. It's just ... OK.

title: Just about the perfect cookie for so many things ...
text: I first discovered these little cookies in a local ethnic supermarket featuring Mexican/Central/South American products about 12 years ago.  They're light, both in terms of flavor and "calorie hit."  Great plain with tea or coffee, but I like them best as a foundation for Nutella!  Yeah, I know -- that kind of cancels out the low-calorie hit from the cookie, but it's so darned tasty!  Four or five of these with about 1/2 tsp of Nutella on each is a perfect light-ish treat at the end of a meal.  Amazon's deal on these (Prime Pantry) is excellent, too.  I'll keep purchasing these as long as Amazon continues to stock them.

title: Smooth but robust -- and no bitterness ...
text: I've been a fan of Caribou coffee ever since I received some in a "sampler" pack shortly after I purchased my first Keurig machine in 2012.  This Caribou blend is my favorite of this brand.  Robust flavor, but none of the bitterness or "charred" flavor that I get from other brands.  I keep this on hand and in my coffee "rotation" with a few other brands I really like as well.  It's good stuff!

title: Use your imagination -- fill with pizza toppings, steak & cheese, whatever ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of the Old El Paso "Stand N Stuff" flour tortillas in both sizes, but these minis are my favorite. Seriously, you can put ANYTHING in these. My usual serving size is 2 of these stuffed with ... stuff.

I use them for breakfast: two of these on a plate, add about 1-2 Tbsp of grated cheese in each, pop into the microwave for 15-20 seconds, then add some browned breakfast sausage (I make my own, but you could use the brown-n-serve sausage links for this) to each and split a couple of scrambled eggs between the two. Perfect size, tasty, and easy to eat.

Lunch: some grilled chicken, a little barbecue sauce, some sauteed peppers and onions. OR rice/black beans with a few steak slices, cheese and salsa. Really, the possibilities are endless.

I've even used these for dessert: brush with melted butter and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar, heat for 15 seconds or so, then add apple slices sauteed with a little brown sugar and apple cider, another sprinkling of cinnamon, and drizzle with caramel ice cream topping. Yum!

I'll keep purchasing these as long as Amazon keeps them in stock. Super handy and so versatile. Solid well-earned 5 stars: I love it!

title: Good flavor with microwavable convenience --
text:
I use pre-cooked microwavable rice fairly often primarily for the convenience. I use it mostly as a base for various stir fries or chili -- things with some flavorful sauce. Over the years I've tried a lot of different brands/varieties and have a few favorites that I purchase often. So I was curious to see how this Japanese product would stack up with the others.

This comes packaged 3 "trays" to the package. Instructions are in Japanese, but if you've ever used this type of product before, it's the same idea: vent the tray by peeling the top back about 1" or so, then microwave on high for 90 seconds or so (my microwave is 1100W, so 90 seconds is perfect; for a less-powerful microwave, you'll probably need to extend cooking time to one minute 45 seconds or 2 minutes). Each tray holds 3 servings, with 260 kcal per serving.

This is a short-grain rice and cooks up slightly sticky, but there's not a hint of the "plastic" taste that sometimes comes with products like this. It works fine with stir fry w/ sauce as well as homemade chili (made with ground beef and red beans). In comparison to some of the other products I've used, I'd say this falls somewhere in the middle of the pack: there are a couple that I like more but several that I like less. I would definitely consider purchasing this depending on how it compares in terms of cost.

So bottom line: I like it. Four stars.

title: Super convenience and excellent flavor/texture ...
text:
I've used a lot of pre-cooked packaged rice over the years. I'm single, and the convenience of being able to "heat and eat" is super attractive. I usually use it as a base for stir fry or other chicken/pork/beef saucy concoctions, and t's great with homemade chili. So I was curious to see how this Tilda Steamed Basmati would stack up.

Bottom line: it stacks up very nicely. Great flavor, microwave convenience, and a nice amount in the package (2 servings).

Preparation is similar to others of this type: squeeze the package to break up any chunks; tear a 1" opening near the top; nuke for a couple of minutes (my microwave is 1100W, so 1 1/2 minutes works best). Handle carefully (it's hot!), then open and use. Simple, no?

I like that the ingredients are few and simple: rice, rice bran oil, water, and a touch of salt. No artificial preservatives.

I will definitely purchase more of this. One of my favorite meals is stir fry: chicken, veggies, and sauce served over rice -- and this is perfect for that. Really really good stuff. Solid 5 stars.

title: Decent cookies, cute package, but nothing really special.
text:
For packaged chocolate chip cookies, these aren't bad at all. They're small and packaged nicely in a foil pouch inside a cute "milk carton"-shaped package. Some packaged chocolate chip cookies are tough and hard; these are not. They're kind of crumbly, but otherwise, the texture is fine. Overriding flavor is vanilla and you get a decent amount of chocolate chips. You don't get very many in the package: the serving size is 8 cookies, and there are 3 servings in the package.

Given the small amount in the package compared to the cost, I can't see myself purchasing these regularly. They're not really any better than other brands, and the primary distinguishing feature is the package. They're ... OK.

title: A little too sweet, but a nice treat with not a huge calorie hit ...
text:
I have been purchasing another similar product available on Amazon, so I was curious to see how these would stack up. My usual "bar" is cranberry, dark chocolate, and almond. These are cherry, dark chocolate, and cashew, so very similar.

I like these -- because of the nuts, they're reasonably filling, and of course ... chocolate! 180 calories (as opposed to the 150 in my current brand), isn't too much of a hit for something this tasty. They have the right amount of chocolate, and everything tastes fresh (crunchy nuts, etc.). Fairly intense cherry flavor, too -- ingredients list includes dried cranberries as well. The label says "Made in Canada" -- so I'm happy with that, too.

My only quibble is they're just a bit too sweet for me. Reduce the sweetness level a bit, and they'd earn 5 stars from me. For now, I'm comfortable with 4 stars -- I like them!

title: Handy to keep for emergencies; decent flavor, too ...
text:
This works nicely for most recipes that call for eggs, as well as working OK for scrambled eggs. Sure, I prefer fresh eggs, but there are times when it's difficult or nearly impossible for me to get out to the store. I keep this on hand for those times.

For cakes, cookies, etc. -- baked goods that call for eggs -- I mix 3 Tbsp mix with 3 Tbsp water (this makes the equivalent of a medium-large egg -- if the recipe calls for large/extra large eggs, I use 4 Tbsp of each). Once mixed, I treat it just like fresh eggs in the mix, and it works great.

For scrambled eggs, I usually mix 1/3 C egg mix with 1/3 C water, whisk, and add to the skillet with some roasted veggies (peppers, onions, sweet potatoes, mushrooms, etc.). Scramble until just cooked through and wrap in a flour tortilla with some cheddar or pepper jack cheese. Better than I expected, for sure. Good stuff.

I appreciate the smaller packages, too -- I'm single, and each package contains just the right amount so that it doesn't go stale before I finish it. I usually go through one of these over a several-week period, depending on how much baking I'm doing.

Will continue to purchase as the need arises. Solid 4 stars.

title: Tasty, easy prep, versatile ...
text:
Good, fast, easy to prepare. Probably not the healthiest choice out there, but certainly tasty.

I use this mostly to stuff flour tortillas for burritos, and top with cheese and salsa. I've also used them to make enchiladas (topped with enchilada sauce and cheese, then baked) as well as tacos. For those days when I just don't feel like cooking "from scratch," these are a nice simple alternative. The "heat" level is rather low -- not spicy to my taste, but I usually prefer my southwest flavors on the hot side. No problem -- I just use a spicier salsa and I'm good to go.

Will definitely purchase these again to have on hand as a back-up when I'm unable to get to the store.

title: Super with dips; great by themselves ...
text:
I've been a fan of Food Should Taste Good crackers and chips for awhile now. They're consistently high quality and the flavors are ... well ... different than the normal chip.

These multigrain tortilla chips are excellent by themselves just out of the bag or with all kinds of dips. I've had them with salsa and guacamole as well as onion dip and hot spinach/artichoke/cheese dip. The flavor just works with everything.

Will continue to purchase these -- they're that good.

title: Really good cashews -- and lots of them ...
text:
I'm a sucker for good cashews. They're my favorite nut to eat out of the bag, and I use them a lot in salads and Asian cooking. And these Happy Belly roasted and salted cashews are, indeed, good ones.

You got quite a lot in this 44-oz package: 2 3/4 lbs. Mine arrived mostly whole, with just a few halves. Other brands sell "whole cashews" at a premium and sell "cashew halves and pieces" for less. No worries here -- these are definitely premium nuts. Nice size, great flavor, too.

A word about the salt: I'm usually a little hesitant to purchase salted anything because unless it says "lightly salted," the amount of salt is just too much. That is not the case here -- the salt level is perfect for my taste. You know it's there, but it's not too much.

I like these enough to want to purchase other Happy Belly nut products (the mixed nuts look good, and the walnuts would be handy for upcoming holiday baking/cooking projects).

Solid 5 stars for these -- I love 'em.

title: Good on pizza -- decent flavor ...
text: Just a bit bland for my taste but still very nice pepperoni.  I use this mostly on pizza and in calzones.  It's not overly greasy, either -- some packaged pre-sliced pepperoni produces huge puddles of oil/grease; this doesn't. You get quite a lot in the package and for the price, it's a decent buy.  Will likely purchase again just to make sure I have some on hand.

title: The best of the Pirouline flavors ...
text:
Of all the flavors offered by Pirouline, this Dark Chocolate is my all-time favorite. Not too sweet, crispy exterior with a fudgy interior -- really nice!

Like others, my shipment of six 14-oz canisters arrived with some breakage and crumbling. So far, I've used 4 of the 6 cans, each containing 2 foil-wrapped sleeves (so I've opened 8 sleeves so far). I've had 3 sleeves with NO breakage at all -- every one completely intact with just a tiny bit of crumbling on an end here and there. The other 5 sleeves contained some broken cookies -- ranging from 20% to probably 60% of the contents. Since I purchased these for my own use, this isn't a problem. The broken ones taste as good as the unbroken ones. :-) So far, I've had no sleeves with total disintegration of the contents. But if you're looking for perfect presentation, bear in mind that you're probably going to have to deal with some breakage.

That said, I'll purchase these again. The price is comparable to my local supermarket, and having it delivered is a convenience I'm willing to pay a bit extra for. The dark chocolate flavor is divine -- definitely 5-star worthy in my book.

title: The PERFECT mayonnaise; don't even look at anything else ...
text:
OMG! I can't believe I found this mayo here! I lived for awhile in the deep South many years ago and was introduced to Blue Plate Mayonnaise there. I figured it was a regional thing since I couldn't find it anywhere after I moved away, and pretty much gave up on ever being able to purchase it again.

Many years (and many states) later, I'm living in the Pacific NW, and browsing Amazon in search of pantry items that I can add to my "Subscribe & Save" order and HERE IT IS! Goodbye, Hellman's -- come to mama, you gorgeous Blue Plate mayo!!

This stuff is seriously the best mayo available, hands down. Nothing else comes close -- the consistency, flavor, "creaminess," everything about it is perfect. I use it mostly for sandwiches and making dressing for pasta salads. Since I'm single, I don't go through it all that quickly, but that's OK -- the expiration date is far enough in the future that I'll be able to get through the 6 bottles before it reaches it's "best by... " date.

Just thrilled to find it here. Solid well-earned 5 stars.

title: Perfect for Cincinnati Chili!
text:
Barilla is my "go to" brand of dried pasta. The results are perfect every time -- taste, texture, appearance -- just great.

This thin spaghetti is what I use for my Cincinnati Chili. Regular spaghetti is too thick, and angel hair is too thin. This is somewhere in the middle, and it just works best. Cooks up super fast, too -- instructions are spot on at 6 minutes cooking time on the stove. I've also used this in my microwave pasta cooker and it works there, too.

This 4-pack makes it economical as well. It's about the same price as my supermarket, but I can have this delivered. Win-win!

Solid 5 star product as far as I'm concerned.

title: Better than my homemade -- a keeper for sure!
text:
I've been making my own spicy peanut sauce for summer rolls but thought I'd give this a try. VERY glad I did!

This is a seriously good sauce. Very nicely balanced -- you can taste the coconut and peanut flavors, and there's a hint of heat, too. It's not quite as spicy as I sometimes like, but I just add a squirt or two of sriracha when I'm feeling particularly spicy, and it's perfect. Reasonably priced, too (at the time I purchased it, under 4.00 per bottle, much cheaper than a comparable product in the local supermarket). Just ordered another bottle. The expiration date on the first bottle I purchased was 9 months out, so I feel confident that I won't get stuck with a short expiration date.

Great consistency, too -- not too thin, not too thick. Really, I can't think of a way to improve it. Solid 5 stars -- I love it!

title: Peach Almond is not very "peachy" --
text:
I usually eat oatmeal 2-3 days a week for breakfast, most often the Quaker Instant Oatmeal packets (dump into a bowl, add boiling water, let sit a couple of minutes -- breakfast). My favorite flavor for ANYTHING is 'each, so I was curious about these convenient oatmeal cups and how they might compare.

Ummm ... I think I'll stick to my instant oatmeal packets.

Nothing really wrong with these "Real Medleys" Peach Almond cups -- easy, convenient, fast, etc. -- but when I read "peach" on the label, I sort of expect to get a real hit of peach flavor. Yeah, not so much. It's there, but very VERY subtle -- even the chunks of rehydrated dehydrated peach don't taste all that peachy. Lots of almonds -- just don't let the cup steep with the hot water for too long or you'll lose the crunch of the almonds. Did that a couple of times. When they say let it sit for 3 minutes, they mean it -- any longer and it sort of turns into mush.

So -- these might be good for a "grab and go" type breakfast on the run, for taking to the office when you're running late. And they really are convenient -- self-contained​, just add water, etc.

But if you're looking for real peachy goodness in oatmeal, stick to the Quaker Instant Oatmeal peach flavor. 3 stars: "It's OK."

title: Dry, not overly sweet, good with tea ...
text:
I've purchased and enjoyed Walkers Shortbread cookies frequently in the past. I have a couple of varieties on subscribe & save, too -- so I'm really a fan.

These, however, were somewhat disappointing. I think I saw the name "Shortbread" and assumed they'd be another variant on that theme, like the [[ASIN:B0151CTXRC Walkers Shortbread Orange Viennese Cookies, 5.3 Ounce]] and [[ASIN:B00CJBR3BM Walkers Shortbread Chocolate Scottie Dogs Shortbread, 3.9 oz.]].

They are not. Instead, they're rather dry crumbly "basic" cookies with white chocolate chips and bits of dried raspberry. They're not bad -- in fact, with tea, they're quite nice. But they are NOT shortbread, so don't expect the buttery tender texture and flavor. They're not overly sweet, either -- which is a plus as far as I'm concerned.

I'm not sure I'll purchase these again -- there are just too many other Walkers products I like so much better. But if you're looking for a nice change of pace to pair with an afternoon cup of tea, this might just be what you're looking for.

title: Perfect to serve with after dinner coffee/tea or a glass of wine ...
text:
I've purchased a few Stella D'oro varieties over the years but haven't been a steady customer, so I really don't have much to compare these to as far as taste/quality over a period of time.

I do know that I like these. Probably not enough to put them on subscribe and save, but enough to purchase again occasionally.

First things first: these are not overly sweet and they're rather dry, so it's clear they're intended to be eaten with coffee or tea or even wine. The flavor is there -- vanilla in some, lemon in others, chocolate -- but it's very subtle. The icing and sprinkles really bring nothing to the party -- the icing is a thin "smear," without flavor. But flavor and "mouth feel" are overall pleasant. They're also quite "sturdy" -- mine survived transport in less than optimum exterior packaging without a single broken cookie. Seriously -- not a one broke. Even with that, they're still tender - not "hard" and crunchy at all. And you do get quite a lot of them -- they come in a plastic tray that is 9.5" x 5.5" x 2" that is filled full.

As I said, I'll likely order these sometime in the future, possibly adding them into my "cookie rotation" of brands/types that I like to purchase occasionally. Definitely worth 4 stars: I like them.

title: A favorite treat with built-in portion control! ...
text:
I've been a huge fan of Pringles ever since they first appeared in the late 1960s / early 1970s. Convenient, non-greasy, and yes, they taste good. The problem, though, is that unless I pay attention, I can easily consume an entire regular-size canister of them in one sitting. Not good.

These Small Stacks canisters solve that problem nicely. With just 210 calories per canister, even if I absent-mindedly indulge in the entire container, the caloric "hit" isn't too bad. And, of course, this Sour Cream & Onion flavor just happens to be my favorite Pringles flavor, so ... WIN! Add to that the small canisters can be cleaned and reused to store craft supplies, household items, etc., and this really becomes a perfect purchase.

I ordered these through Prime Pantry -- economical, for sure, and so far, I've had no issues with breakage (I've consumed about 6 of the 12 small cans).

Definitely will be purchasing these again.

title: A tasty & convenient breakfast treat ...
text:
Clearly not the most nutritious breakfast treat, but it's something I can grab with some fruit in the morning as I'm heading out the door and enjoy in the car on the commute. They've also come in handle when I've been under the weather and didn't feel like putting together a "real" breakfast.

This is not the usual "fruit"-filled pop tart ("fruit" always seems to be more of a suggestion than a reality). The flavor here is more like cinnamon toast in an easy-to-handle package. I don't indulge in these very often (maybe once every couple of weeks, if that), but it's nice to have options that taste good, even if they aren't the healthiest choice.

title: Good flavor, not greasy -- be careful how you slice it ...
text:
After reading about different types of pepperoni, and being a pepperoni pizza lover, I came to Amazon to see if I could find one of the brands that seemed to come out on or near the top of various taste tests. My first order was for this one, and I'm not disappointed at all.

Like a lot of things in life, tastes are very personal. What appeals to me may not appeal to someone else. Pepperoni is no different. I've eaten my share of the standard supermarket brands -- pre-sliced and not -- and find most of it extremely greasy, especially when baked on a pizza. This product is NOT like that -- it's much dryer, more "solid," chewier, and a little spicier.

I tried it first "straight up," as a part of a cheese & crackers quick lunch with some olives, fresh veggies, etc. I sliced it about the thickness of a nickel, and it delivered a nice bright flavor, chewy, for sure, but very tasty and no greasy mouth feel. A couple of days later, I ventured into pizza territory, whipping up my standard 7" "personal size" pie: crust, sauce, cheese (a combination of provolone & mozzarella), topped with very thinly sliced Fortuna pepperoni. Yes, I'd read a couple of the reviews cautioning about slicing thinly, so that's what I did. Oh. My. Yes, this is GOOD. No pools of orange grease, either. Just chewy spicy pepperoni goodness with lots of gooey cheese. Slicing thinly is absolutely critical. Otherwise, it will become very hard and tough. Remember, this is a DRY pepperoni.

Yes, I'll purchase this again. As long as I can get it for a reasonable cost here on Amazon, this will be a staple in my kitchen.

title: Almost perfect - a sweet but very tasty addition to your salad ...
text:
I've been using a vidalia onion "summer tomato" salad dressing occasionally for several years, but it's hard to find and super pricey. I've checked on Amazon periodically over the years to see if I could find a reasonable substitute with no success ... until now.

I took a chance ordering this since it didn't sound "exactly" like what I'd grown to love, but it sounded close enough to be worth a try.

Very happy I took a chance! I really do like this. No, it's not exactly the same as the more tomato-y version I used to purchase, but it IS tasty. It's very sweet, but there's almost enough acid to balance the honey sweetness -- almost. Hence, the 4 stars. With a little more tomato or lemon juice or some other acid, it would reach near perfection.

I get fresh veggies every 2 weeks from a local farm (a CSA - community-supported agriculture), and they always include at least one or two types of lettuce plus local tomatoes, so I almost always have salad "fixings" on hand, and this is the perfect pairing. I like variety, so I rotate this in my "salad line-up" with Honey Mustard, Balsamic Vinaigrette, and Spicy/Southwest Ranch. Yeah, I'm a sucker for a good salad.

Very happy I found this! Definitely worth 4 stars.

title: Versatile and super tasty -- my search is over ...
text:
I'm a sucker for honey mustard *anything*, and this product is one of the best I've found. In the past, I've purchased honey-mustard spread for sandwiches, honey-mustard salad dressing, honey-mustard dipping sauce -- all separate products from different manufacturers. Finding a single product that could do it all seemed impossible.

Not anymore ....

I've been using Sweet Baby Ray's barbecue sauces for several years and love them. I'm a Kansas City native, and Sweet Baby Ray's barbecue sauces come close to what I grew up with in Kansas City (yes, I know it's made in Chicago, but they got it right). When I saw this Honey Mustard sauce, I had to give it a try.

So far, I've used it as a salad dressing for a grilled chicken + mixed greens/tomato/peppers/etc. salad, a dipping sauce for baked chicken nuggets, a basting sauce for honey-mustard wings, a sandwich spread for a ham + swiss cheese sandwich, and mixed with mayonnaise to make a cole slaw dressing, and it works great for everything. Seriously -- the consistency and flavor just work in so many recipes. I don't know how they did it, but they got the balance of sweet with mustardy-hot just right.

This will have a permanent place in my pantry -- it's just what I was looking for. Solid 5 stars!

title: Larger bag of addictive deliciousness ... SCORE!!
text:
Oh, my. These are truly dangerous for me. Buying them in quantity makes sense economically, but I do have to be careful not to "binge" on my all-time favorite chocolaty-peanutty treat.

I distribute the contents of the large bag into smaller "snack size" zipper bags to help my portion-control issues, and store them in a cool place away from my normal roost, each bag containing about 1/2 C of the M&M'S. This way, I have to get up and retrieve a pack when I feel the urge to indulge. Works for me.

These are fresh, with the "best by" date 9 months into the future. If I'm going to take a "calorie hit" on something, I'd rather it be on something that tastes really good. These do.

Will continue to purchase these larger "Party Size" bags as long as they're offered at a reasonable cost on Amazon. Solid 5-star yum!

title: Small squares of goodness ...
text:
Wow! I ended up likely these more than I thought I would. The flavor I purchased as a "trial run" was the Cranberry/Almond/Dark Chocolate. Each package contains four little squares of "goodness," which doesn't sound like a lot, but they're so flavorful and rich-tasting that four is really sufficient for an after-meal treat.

You get twelve packages in the box, so these make sense to me from an economical standpoint. None of my local supermarkets carry these, so Amazon comes to the rescue here.

The only negative I can think of is that, like most chocolate, these probably won't travel as well during the warmer summer months. I live in the Pacific NW, so our summer temps aren't as bad as they are in other parts of the country, but it does occasionally reach high-80s / low-90s for a few days. I'll definitely order these again, and I'm getting ready to try another flavor or two.

Good stuff!

title: Perfectly portioned, travels well ...
text:
Special K Red Berries has been a favorite cereal of mine for a long time. I usually purchase it in the boxes (various sizes), but I sometimes have to do overnight trips where I have access to single-serving milk (cartons) but not to the cereal I know and love.

Enter these Cereal Cups -- the PERFECT single serving container, easy to pack, always fresh tasting. Yes, this is more expensive than the boxed version, but I'm willing to pay extra for the convenience of having this available when I have to travel.

I now have this on "subscribe & save" -- this way, I'll be able to keep it on hand without worrying about re-ordering. It's absolutely perfect for my needs.

title: Tasty chocolate shortbread puppies ...
text:
I bought these little chocolate Scottie dog shortbread cookies on a whim, and ended up putting them on "subscribe & save"! I really do like them. They're not *too* sweet, the chocolate flavor doesn't hit you over the head, and they still have the buttery taste I expect from shortbread cookies.

Others have mentioned issues with the cookies arriving broken. I've had two deliveries of these so far, and I've had only one broken cookie out of the bunch. Since they're for me (not gifts), I don't mind the occasional breakage. It all tastes the same.

I'll keep these on my "subscribe & save" subscription as long as they're offered as the cost is reasonable and I cannot get these at any local supermarkets.

title: Perfect for my Pacific Northwest-inspired recipes ...
text:
I live in the Pacific NW where hazelnuts are a staple. However, getting them already skinned and roasted isn't easy and is often really pricey, so these Turkish hazelnuts work when I'm in a hurry.

The flavor is excellent. I use these a lot in salads, in baking, and ground and mixed with panko as a breading for chicken, pork chops, and salmon. Super quality, reasonable cost, no complaints at all. Will continue to purchase to have on hand as a backup when I can't get local nuts.

title: Hard to find locally -- great chocolate chip cookie flavor ...
text:
​These are almost impossible to find in my local supermarkets. Other flavors, yes -- these, no. And they're one of my favorites! They really do taste like a soft chocolate chip cookie, no aftertaste, nicely loaded with chocolate chips. They're small, yes, but as an end to a meal, they're the perfect size. I like the portion control concept -- I'm not as likely to succumb to a "binge" with these.

I just put them on subscribe and save so I don't have to run out. I really do like them that much, and the current cost makes them economical (about three fifty per box).

title: Very mild cheddar flavor -- but still a tasty snack without too much of a nutritional hit ...
text:
​The cheddar flavor is very mild in these chips, which was a bit of a surprise. The other flavors of Sunchips are much stronger (the Garden Salsa, especially -- probably my favorite flavor). Sunchips are probably my favorite "snack chip" -- the calorie hit for these is 140cal per 15 chip serving, and I rarely eat more than 8 or 10 chips at a meal. They're also not as high in sodium as other "chip" alternatives.

My local supermarket doesn't carry all the flavors, so I rely on Amazon to replenish my "stash."

I like these, and will likely purchase again, but I do like a couple of the other flavors better (Garden Salsa and French Onion).

title: Not too sweet, just about perfect!
text:
I absolutely love these! I've been purchasing them for several years to use in baking (they're great in bran muffins), salads, in compotes/sauces, and to eat at the end of a meal with a glass of wine.

They're not too sweet. Instead, they have a really bright tart cherry flavor. I prefer getting them this way (8-oz packages) as they stay fresher longer that way.

Probably my favorite recipe for these is a variation on Waldorf salad:

PACIFIC NORTHWEST WALDORF SALAD
==========================
1 C finely chopped celery
3 apples (I use Granny Smith, but if you like sweeter, use Fuji or Gala) -- about 2.5 - 3 C chopped
3/4 C chopped dried cherries
1/3 C finely chopped toasted hazelnuts
1/3 C plain yogurt OR mayonnaise
1/4 C sour cream
1 1/2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
pinch salt

Combine first four ingredients in medium bowl. Combine yogurt, sour cream, juice, and salt in small bowl; stir well with whisk. Drizzle over celery mixture; toss gently. Cover and chill 1 hour.
Serves 4-6.

I've tripled this recipe successfully to take to a potluck dinner. These Traverse Bay cherries are absolutely perfect!

Will continue to purchase these as long as Amazon continues to carry them ...

title: Super flavor, easy to use -- makes super stir fry!
text:
Great texture, super flavor, and convenience -- definitely worth a try. I love stir fry and prepare it quite often, but I'm always looking for new sauces. I have problems sometimes with larger bottles of sauce since I'm single and don't use a lot of sauce. I saw these smaller packets that make 2 servings and thought I'd give it a try.

So far, I've used it with chicken, beef, and shrimp and an assortment of veggies (mostly carrots, red bell pepper, snow peas, onion, and some bok choy), and it's really good! This is the honey teriyaki sauce, so I was expecting it to be sweet. I'm happy to say it's not overly sweet -- really just about perfect for my taste. I make two servings, package one serving in a refrigerator container, eat the rest with rice, and have leftovers for the next day. Perfect!

Will definitely purchase this again, and I'll probably try other flavors in the Blue Dragon line. Highly recommended!

title: Great for making summer rolls ...
text:
I purchased these to make fresh summer rolls -- my first attempt at these. I'm a fairly experienced cook but had never tried working with these rice wrappers. I found a recipe for shrimp & veggie summer rolls (cooked shrimp, butter lettuce leaves, julienned carrots, celery root, and cucumber) with a spicy peanut dipping sauce. Didn't look too complicated, so I decided to give it a try.

I ordered these rice papers based on the reviews. It took a couple of tries to get the soaking step "right," but I managed to make 4 decent summer rolls in about 20 minutes -- and they were REALLY good! I'm happy enough with this process and the results to repeat it. I've made this recipe twice since, and I'm getting better at rolling -- still need some practice, but they're easy to make and tasty. The trick, for me, is to keep the temperature of the water at lukewarm to warm -- if it's too hot, the rice wrapper "disintegrates" really quickly.

You get 30 or so wrappers in each package, 2 packages per order and these appear to be shelf stable for an extended period of time. After opening, I just keep mine in a zip-top plastic bag in the pantry. Easy! Definitely will be purchasing these again, and I have plans to try other combinations of veggies/shrimp/chicken/etc. along with some different dipping sauces.

title: The perfect solution ...
text:
I'm single and don't use a lot of milk -- mostly for cooking and my breakfast cereal in the morning. My local supermarket no longer sells milk in a 1-quart carton, and I can't consume an entire 1/2-gallon carton before it spoils, so I looked for a shelf-stable solution: milk in a small enough carton that I could keep on hand without refrigeration and use as needed.

Saw this, and decided to give it a try.

I purchased the 2% "Reduced Fat Milk" -- six 32-ounce (1-quart) cartons. I'm extremely pleased with it so far. I've had it on "subscribe and save," and so far, I haven't had any problems with short expiration dates -- my last order is set to expire in about 9 months, and that's certainly enough time for me to use it. My intent and use might be different from some: I'm not looking for long-term (say, more than 3-6 months) shelf life, since I go through a carton each 7-10 days, so I have this delivered every 8 weeks, and that works out just fine.

So how does it compare in taste and texture to supermarket dairy case 2% milk? It's just a little less "full flavored," but it's perfectly fine for cereal and cooking. It's not "watery" -- no issues at all with taste or consistency. I've had no problems with spoilage, either -- it comes nicely sealed and keeps well in the fridge after it's opened. I usually put a new carton in the fridge the night before I need to use it so it's chilled in the morning.

I'm keeping this on Subscribe & Save for as long as Amazon offers it. It solves my particular problem perfectly. Solid 5 stars.

title: The BEST dried cranberries available on Amazon ...
text:
I've been purchasing these for several years for one basic reason: they're the best dried cranberries available. I think I've tried every brand available over the years, and these are hands down the best: best taste, best freshness. *Most* of the time, they're not overly sweet -- if I have one criticism, it's that there's some variability in the "sweetness" level, probably due to the cranberries themselves. Still, they're not nearly as sweet as other more "popular" brands.

I use these most often in morning cereal - especially Frosted Mini-Wheats (yes, really) -- and in baking (muffins, scones, etc.). I love getting the 6 "tubs," as they keep fresher longer that way.

I have these on subscribe and save for a reason: I use them a lot (I go through a tub every 3-4 weeks). Really first-rate dried cranberries, worth 5 stars.

title: Nice flavors, I use this a lot ...
text:
I absolutely love this stuff. My favorite way to use it is very simple: cook up some pasta (I like linguine or spaghetti), toss with just a little good-quality olive oil -- just enough to coat the strands -- and then sprinkle with this (I use about 1/2 - 3/4 tsp per serving -- I like a lot of flavor). Serve as a side dish with grilled salmon or chicken and a salad. Yum!

I also add it to homemade marinara for some added tastiness. For a salt-free seasoning mix, it really adds a boost of bold flavor. Really first-rate stuff, and I'm thrilled to find it on Amazon. Will continue to purchase here as long as they carry it.

title: Tasty source of protein!  ...
text:
I'm always looking for products that can do "double duty." I'm a sucker for pasta, but I don't like huge portions, and I prefer to do more veggie-based sauces/combos. This particular product is perfect!

I get 10g of protein in a single 2 oz. serving with this (if you like larger servings, you get 17g of protein with the 3.5 oz serving size). The protein is NOT soy -- a huge benefit for me (I'm not allergic, but for other reasons, I'm under orders to avoid it if at all possible). The texture when cooked is similar to "regular" pasta, maybe just a little more dense and "chewy." The flavor is exactly the same, in my opinion. In all, it's a good substitute for my usual pasta. I cook up a single serving of this and toss it with a roasted veggie/pesto combination that is super delicious and filling. In one meal, I get protein, veggies, and the right amount of fats and carbs for my particular situation.

This package includes 2 boxes of spaghetti and 2 boxes of angle hair pasta -- a nice collection to get started with this product. I'll be purchasing other Protein Plus products (rotini, farfalle, and elbows for sure). Solid 5 stars in my opinion.

title: Coconut/caramel/chocolate goodness --
text:
I've long been a huge fan of the coconut/caramel/fudgy-striped Girl Scout cookie, but they're available only at a certain time of the year. I've been hoping that Keebler would introduce a "year round" version of them, and so they did.

These aren't *quite* as good as the original GS Samoas, but they're awfully darned close. You have a basic vanilla/graham-type cookie topped with a thin layer of caramel, sprinkled with toasted sweetened coconut, laced with chocolate drizzled stripes. I can have 2 of these post-meal, and be perfectly happy with the sugar / chocolate fix.

I find, though, that if I don't take precautions, I'll end up mindlessly eating an entire sleeve. I solve this, I re-package the cookies into sealable "snack-sized" zipper bags, 2 per bag, and store them in the freezer in the garage. In order to indulge, I have to remember to take a bag out of the freezer and let it thaw for 20-30 minutes -- about the length of time it takes me to eat a meal. This way, I'm not tempted to graze through 1/3 of the package in one sitting.

Very happy with these ...

title: Rich chocolatey brownie goodness in a small size ...
text:
I've tried a number of these Fiber One 90-Calorie bars. Some have been really good (the lemon bars especially). Some have been ... well ... not to my taste (strawberry cheesecake). This one's a winner in my book.

First, they are SMALL. Like maybe 2" square small. But they do have decent flavor, and the texture is reminiscent of chewy fudgy brownie with the addition of semisweet chocolate chips. They're relatively low in fat, and each little bar contains 5g of fiber, so that's definitely a plus.

I use these at the end of a meal in place of a higher calorie/fat hit -- one little bar satisfies my "sweet tooth" and indulges my chocolate "addiction." Definitely a better option for my goals. I've also used one of these with a small scoop of vanilla frozen yogurt with a drizzle of chocolate sauce for a "fancier" treat.

Are they the healthiest option? of course not! But when I'm really craving something sweet and chocolatey, these really do work nicely. Solid 5-stars from me. I just put them on "Subscribe & Save" ...

title: New to Mrs. Dash? This is the bundle to try ...
text:
I've been using Mrs. Dash salt-free spice blends for years, and I think I've tried all of them. This particular bundle is ideal if you want to try some different varieties.

I use the Fiesta Lime on fish and chicken before grilling or roasting. The Southwest Chipotle is great on steak, chicken, or pork chops. I use the "Extra Spicy" whenever I just want to add a "kick" to roasted veggies, rice, or pasta. And the Garlic Herb is wonderful on *everything*. I usually mix a teaspoon or more into a pound of ground beef before forming into patties -- just the right amount of "special."

Honestly, if you're trying to reduce salt consumption, these are the way to go. Tons of flavor, excellent balanced combos, and in this bundle, economical, too. I pay way more per bottle at my local supermarket (obviously, your mileage may vary ... ). Highly recommended.

title: The keyword is "Orange" -- combined with Walkers usual great quality ...
text:
I've been purchasing these one box at a time in Prime Pantry, so I was thrilled to see them available on "subscribe and save." Yes, I like them that much!

SUPER orange flavor, you can even taste and feel the bits of orange peel in the cookie, along with the normal buttery shortbread flavor we know and love. The texture is more like a "spritz" cookie (that's what they were called when I was growing up in the midwest: a tender butter cookie pressed with a cookie press into festive shapes). They're a good size, too: 2.5" across. Nothing artificial about these: they're flavored with crystallized orange peel, and a lot of it (it's the 4th ingredient listed just after "sugar"). So yes, the orange flavor is quite intense. That's why I like them!

Will keep getting these as long as they're available. They're great with a cup of tea as a small dessert treat.

title: A tasty original ... still going strong ...
text:
Cheez-It has been my favorite snack cracker since ... well ... a very long time (I'd say over 50 years -- 1960s for sure). It now comes in a lot of different flavors and varieties (swiss, white cheddar, pepper jack, hot & spicy, etc.), but the original is still my favorite.

It has just the right combination of "crunch" and sharp cheddar cheese flavor. A handful of these always satisfies my craving for something a little salty and savory with big flavor. It really does help me keep my propensity to "binge"/snack under control.

I've purchased this a number of times through Prime Pantry, and I've had no issues at all with freshness or "too soon" expiration dates. Always fresh tasting without a lot of breakage. Definitely worth a repeat purchase, but keep an eye on the price; it can wildly fluctuate at times. I don't mind paying a few cents over my local supermarket price for these when I can have them delivered to my door. Super tasty!

title: Oh yum!!  Pesto heaven!
text:
I make my own pesto when I have fresh basil available, but I like to have a "back up" just in case I can't make my own. This is the 4th "off the shelf" pesto I've tried, and it is by far the winner.

It's just a good solid basic pesto: oil, basil, romano cheese, pine nuts, garlic, balsamic vinegar. Nothing fancy at all. But it has great flavor, and I absolutely LOVE the small jars. I'm single, and far too many choice condiments come only in larger jars/packages, so they end up going bad before I can manage to use them up. Not a problem here.

I've used this so far as a simple pasta mix-in with sautéd shrimp. I've used it to make a super "pizza" (I use Indian naan bread, smear on some pesto, top with slices of fresh mozzarella, maybe sprinkle some chopped sundried tomatoes or good cherry or grape tomatoes cut in half -- into the oven until the cheese is melty and the edges brown). I've mixed it with cream cheese, shredded romano, and finely diced prosciutto to make a spread for crackers or slices of baguette. It just works!

This now has a permanent place in my pantry -- super product, great taste, convenient. Solid 5 stars.

title: Makes wonderful apple crisp!
text:
I purchased the Country Apple pie filling to make quick apple crisp, and it works perfectly for that! I'm single, so I don't like to make a huge amount of desserts especially as I don't eat them quickly enough to finish before it gets stale or, worse, starts to spoil.

I can use 1 can of this apple filling to make 2 smallish single-serving apple crisps, and it's absolutely perfect! I make a crumb topping with 1/2 C flour, 1/2 C rolled oats, 1/2 C brown sugar, 1/2 tsp apple pie spice (a combination of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg & cloves) and 1/3 C melted butter; toss to blend, then divide between the two dishes. Bake until brown and bubbly. Top with vanilla ice cream for a real treat! I sometimes throw in about 1/3 C dried cranberries or golden raisins. Super flavor, really just perfect for my use.

Really first rate quality -- will continue to purchase on Amazon as long as it's available at a decent price.

title: My favorite "off the shelf" sauces ...
text:
These are probably my favorite "jarred" pasta sauces. Yes, they cost a little more than others, but the quality is exceptionally good. I especially like the "gift box" 4-variety package the best and have it on Subscribe & Save.

You get one jar each of puttanesca, arrabbiata, marinara, and vodka -- each has a distinctive flavor, all are excellent. I'm single, and I can usually get 3-4 meals out of each jar. I've used it to make lasagne, baked penne w/ mushrooms & sausage, even as a sauce for pizza and calzone.

The arrabbiata is slightly spicy -- not overly so, just enough so that you notice a bit of a "bite." The puttanesca is slightly briny with the taste of capers/olives; the vodka sauce is typically creamy (but not *too* much so) and the marinara is a good basic tomato-y marinara. I like them all, but my favorite is probably the puttanesca.

One other nice feature -- you can wash and reuse the plastic containers! They're heavy duty plastic, safe in microwave and dishwasher.

I've tried a lot of "off the shelf" pasta sauces and these are my favorites. Will continue to order as long as Amazon carries them.

title: Nice quality "everyday" crackers ...
text:
Nothing fancy here -- just good crisp crackers that pair well with cheese, pate, spinach/artichoke dip, etc. I received 5 boxes of crackers: 2 butter, 2 wheat, and 1 toasted sesame, each box has 2 sleeves of crackers which means they stay fresher longer. The "best by ... " dates are well into the future, too. The flavors are non-obtrusive, so that the taste of the cheese or whatever you put on top comes through.

I use these with soups, salads, and dips/spreads. They're a decent value, too -- my supermarket is definitely more expensive.

Will purchase again as the need arises.

title: Received 2 days AFTER expiration date ...
text:
I've always liked Hostess products -- I'm old enough to remember when Twinkies were filled with banana cream -- and they're not often easy to find in my local supermarket.

Amazon to the rescue! One of my all-time favorites, Zingers and at a decent price, too.

Unfortunately, the expiration date was 2 days before my delivery date. Received 1/24; expiration date 1/22. Yes, I know they will keep beyond that date, but they were already stale, somewhat dry, and the icing was hard as a rock. Really, someone needs to be keeping track of expiration dates before shipping product that will expire before it reaches the customer. I still like Zingers, and I stashed them in the freezer to try to prevent further product deterioration, but I shouldn't have to do that.

That said, they're as I remember (except for the stale part): nice chocolatey cake, creamy filling, thick layer of chocolate icing. What's not to love?

This is the 4th Hostess product I've ordered from Amazon (sold by was Amazon, not a 3rd party seller) that had this problem of the expiration date within days of receipt. I don't think I want to try again. I'll keep an eye out at my local supermarket and try to stock up next time they get them.

title: Surprisingly good for "off-the-shelf" vegetable stock ...
text:
I like to make my own stock (chicken, veggie, etc.), but I like having a packaged version available in case I run out of my own. I've tried a number of these Kitchen Basics stocks, and like them all, but this Unsalted Vegetable is one of my favorites due to its versatility.

I use it mostly for soups -- I make a lot of different soups during the chilly fall/winter seasons up here in the Pacific NW -- but also use it in sauces for pasta, for cooking rice or other grains -- anytime I need a flavorful liquid that allows for reduction without ending up overly salty.

I purchase the 32-oz cartons as one of those makes the perfect small batch of soup (I'm single). Lower in sodium, nice bright flavor. Really good stuff. It's *almost* good enough for me to abandon the time/effort of making my own. It's really that good. Solid 5 stars from me.

title: Not good -- serious quality issues ...
text:
What happened? This used to be a really good brand, but the bag I got had way too many stale bitter-tasting nuts. Also, I'd say at least 25% of the nuts weren't opened at all -- I had to use pliers to crack them like I would with other in-the-shell nuts, but I don't expect to have to do that with pistachios.

I was hoping these would be better than my local supermarket brand, but they didn't even come close. Just cancelled my subscribe and save order after 1 delivery.

title: Not perfect, but convenient and tasty ...
text:
I usually make my own stock but there are times when I'm out. I've been purchasing the 1-qt cartons, but saw this and decided to give it a try.

I have to say, I was impressed. It's SO much better than the cartons. Each tub makes almost a quart, so you're getting the equivalent of 4 qts of stock with a single package. It's still not quite as good as my own homemade, but it's the best commercial product I've found.

A word about salt. This is NOT low in salt (there's a reduced-sodium version of this available, but it's not that much lower). I didn't have a problem with it, but I don't salt soups or stews until the dish is nearly finished. So just be aware that you're dealing with seasoned stock and you may need to minimize other sources of salt in your recipe if sodium level matters to you.

I've made several batches of soup with this -- the latest a yummy chicken, vegetable, and wild rice soup today -- and the end result has been super every time​. I'll definitely keep this on hand especially during "soup season" (fall and winter here in the Pacific NW). I also have used the vegetable stock version of this and found it also quite good.

title: Good flavor, easy to work with ...
text:
I usually like the make my own chicken stock and freeze it, but occasionally, I need stock and the freezer is empty.

I purchased this more as a trial than anything -- how would it hold up from a taste standpoint to my homemade stock? The answer is: not too bad! Frankly, I was impressed.

Each carton contains 4 "tubs," and each tub makes about 1 quart of stock. I've used this so far for soups -- it's winter at the moment, and although we don't get a lot of snow in the Pacific NW, it's usually overcast, rainy, and chilly, so soups and stews seem a natural response.

My chicken/mushroom/wild rice soup turned out amazing with this! I also made a turkey & corn chowder with leftover turkey from Thanksgiving that was perfect.

So there it is -- I'm very pleased with the results. This is the lower sodium version -- still not super low but MUCH lower than other "boxed" or packaged stocks. I will definitely keep this in my pantry for those "just in case" times.

title: Not up to the usual Krusteaz high standard ...
text:
I've used Krusteaz products for years (since the 1980s), and this is my first disappointment.

I've made these twice now. The first time, precisely according to the recipe: 1 C mix and 2/3 C water. Mixed with a wire whisk until just barely blended (still lumpy), but I noticed that the mix was very thin and "watery." I let it sit for about 6 minutes while griddle heated to 375, lightly greased the griddle, and I ended up with .... crepes. Flat, apple crepes. That's what happens when the batter is too thin -- it spreads. OK flavor, but I wanted pancakes, not crepes.

The second time, I tried it with 1/2 C water instead of 2/3 C. Got a thicker batter, and the end result was a little better, but still not "light and fluffy." More dense and soggy. Nice cinnamon flavor, but not what I was hoping for.

I think I'll go back to the Krusteaz Pumpkin Spice mix -- it's really good, and I get perfect fluffy pancakes with a distinct pumpkin flavor and just enough spice. I may keep experimenting with this Apple Cinnamon mix to see if I can come up with a "formula" that works to produce actual apple PANCAKES comparable to other Krusteaz mixes. I'll update this if I find something that works.

title: Not too sweet, perfect fig/orange jam!
text:
Superb flavor! Seriously good stuff. I used this to make a glaze for a pork roast that I cooked for Christmas dinner. See recipe and photo below.

Obviously, this jam would be wonderful on toast, biscuits, on Brie cheese, any place you need a hit of flavor that isn't to sti​cky-sweet. The flavors of fig and orange are pronounced -- really first-rate jam. Will absolutely order this again. Solid and well-earned five stars from me.

For the Christmas roast pork w/ fig & orange glaze --
I used 8 oz of this (almost the whole jar), 2 Tbsp of dijon mustard, 2 Tbsp of whole grain mustard, and thinned it with a little orange juice to a thick glaze consistency. Used half of it to coat the pork roast (3.5 lb pork loin roast, excess fat trimmed), then covered and let it refrigerate overnight. Removed from fridge, let sit for an hour to get to room temperature, then wrap it in bacon strips overlapping a bit. Into a 375 oven for 30 minutes; then reduce oven temp to 300, baste bacon-wrapped roast with some of the remaining glaze, and bake for another hour or so until internal temp registers 145, basting occasionally with any glaze left. I'm telling you, this was absolutely DIVINE! The flavors of fig and orange just get better when heated, and worked perfectly with the mustard.

title: You want pumpkin? You've got pumpkin ...
text:
This is the best pumpkin flavored coffee I've tried, and I think I've managed to try all of the ones that are available as of winter 2015. I realize that coffee preferences are really subjective, but hear me out on this.

Caza Trail Pumpkin Spice has the perfect balance of flavors: coffee, pumpkin, and spice. Most pumpkin-flavored coffees just miss, usually on the pumpkin flavor. Not this one -- the warm pumpkin flavor comes through, with just the right blend of traditional pumpkin pie spice flavors and, of course, coffee. I've ordered two more boxes of it just so I'll have enough to last the winter. It's really that good.

Seriously, if you like the flavor of good pumpkin pie, you'll like this. Hands down, to my taste, it really is the best.

title: Tasty protein source ...
text: Just a bit salty, but a decent protein source.  It's also light in terms of calories.  I've used these on long road trips when I don't want to take the time to stop for a meal.  A few "cuts" plus an apple or some grapes, and I'm good to go.  I usually eat 1/3 of a bag (~ 2 oz) -- that's just enough to tide me over until I can stop for a "real" meal.  Nice seasoning on these, too.

title: First experience with cold brew tea -- I like it!
text:
This was my first experience with cold brew iced tea, and I'm really quite impressed with how nicely it works. The "formula" seems to be one tea bag per 8 oz of water. I use a quart-sized bottle, so I brewed 24 oz of water and then added ice to get 32 oz of ice tea. That means I use 3 bags in COLD water from the chilled water dispenser in my fridge, steep for 8-10 minutes dunking once in awhile, then add ice. I end up with a flavorful bottle of tea ready to add lemon and sweetener.

My only quibble is that it does take awhile to get to the strength I like. Since I always add ice, I brew it a little stronger do allow for dilution from the ice. Still, this was better than I expected. It's not "gourmet"-quality iced tea, but it's tasty and easy enough to prepare.

title: A lot better than I expected -- will order again!
text:
UPDATE Jan 8, 2016
I've now had three different varieties of this fudge. In addition to the Chocolate Walnut that I reviewed earlier, I've now had the layered Chocolate Peanut Butter and the Maple Walnut.

The Chocolate Peanut Butter was ... OK. Not as much flavor as I was expecting, though -- very little "peanut butter" taste at all, and the blandness of the peanut butter sort of canceled out the flavor of the chocolate layer. So .. 3 stars for this one (it's OK, but I wouldn't go out of my way to order again.)

The Maple Walnut -- OUTSTANDING! Really really good maple flavor and justs the right amount of walnuts evenly distributed. Not grainy, either -- very smooth and creamy, with the same sort of "buttery" aftertaste I experienced with the Chocolate Walnut. Solid 5 stars on this one -- by far my favorite.

So overall, I still stand by my 4-star​ rating -- although it's probably tracking a bit higher thanks to the Maple Walnut. Total yum there.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I really wasn't expecting this to be as good as it is. I've had "mass produced" fudge before that is waxy, flavorless, etc. I'm happy to say that this fudge is none of those things.

I got the chocolate walnut variety, and it was smooth, creamy, intensely chocolate, good amount of nuts but not too many, and a slightly buttery aftertaste that is really nice. I also like that it's already cut into bite size portions.

I love to cook, and I've made a lot of different fudge recipes over the years, from the more complicated powdered cocoa based ones to the chocolate chips + marshmallow cream ones to the super simple semi-sweet choco chips + sweetened condensed milk varieties -- and this ranks in the top 25% of the fudge I've tasted. It's a really nice addition to my holiday "spread" of sweet and savory snacks and at a reasonable cost, too.

Will definitely be ordering this again!

title: Great for salads and cooking ...
text:
I use these solely for cooking, and they're great for that. I use them on pizza, in casseroles, in salads. One of my favorites is a pasta salad with these sliced green olives, chopped marinated artichokes, chopped roasted peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, all tossed with a pesto dressing and topped with shredded parmesan cheese. Yum! There's an assertive brininess with these that adds a bit of a kick to my dishes. Not overly salty, either.

The can size is just about perfect for the kind and size of dishes I prepare, so I have no complaints there at all. I can't find sliced green olives in my local supermarket, so being able to get them here at a decent price delivered right to my door is a major plus for me.

title: Not sure what happened, but these were not good ...
text:
I had these some years ago and really liked them, so when I saw them here on Amazon, I didn't hesitate to order the assortment.

Not sure what happened but these really were NOT good. Slimy - sticky - gooey texture, and tough as leather. There's also a distinct chemical smell/taste, which may be the "sour" part but it's not at all how I remember it. Really not a pleasant experience. I tried one or two of each flavor and ended up tossing the rest. Life's too short to punish myself with something this bad. Sorry.

title: Great flavor and crispness for Pickled Asparagus ...
text:
Wow! This is seriously good pickled asparagus! There's just a hint of "spice," but it's not overly spicy. They've managed to keep the spears crispy, too -- a lot of pickled asparagus I've tried is limp and frankly a bit bland.

I realize that packaging isn't usually a part of a review like this, but I do want to mention that the packaging design used by Tillen Farms (the manufacturer) almost guarantees that your jars will arrive intact. It's ingenious, actually -- this is something I often worry about when I order items that are packaged in glass jars, but it would take a lot of damage (cyclone? overturned vehicle?) to cause any issues with these. I feel I can reorder with confidence that my jars will arrive with no breakage.

And I WILL reorder! This stuff is that good.

title: Tasty seasoning blend, strong on lime ...
text: Very strong lime flavor, moderate garlic, very mild cilantro flavor but it's easy to add cilantro if I want it.  I've been using this as a marinade for fish and chicken, and it works well for that.  It's also nice to sprinkle on after grilling shrimp or chicken.  I use a lot of salt-free seasoning blends (think Mrs. Dash's), and this is one of my favorites.

title: Just about perfect pumpkin pancakes ...
text:
Krusteaz is known for its easy-to-prepare baking mixes, and this is another winner. I've been using Krusteaz "original" pancake mix for years ​and decided to try this on a whim. I'm a sucker for anything pumpkin-spice, and this product delivers, especially on the "spice."

It's the typical Krusteaz pancake no-brainer/idiot-proof mix: just add water. I'm single, so I mix up a single substantial serving using 3/4C mix to just under 1/2C water, and it turns out perfect every time, 3 small-medium size pancakes. I love them just drizzled with pure maple syrup, but they're good with cranberry/orange compote, too. I sometimes mix some chopped pecans or walnuts into the batter before cooking or some dried cranberries. Really yummy. They cook up light and fluffy -- super texture. This is something Krusteaz *always* gets right.

The pumpkin flavor isn't terribly strong -- it's there, but subtle. I'd like it to be a bit more pronounced, but the lovely warm spices make up for it, and produce a really hearty flavorful pancake, really just about perfect.

Definitely recommend these!

title: Great flavor and versatility -- great possibilities!
text:
I've tried a number of different varieties of Betty Crocker Suddenly Pasta Salad and have decided that two of the flavors are my favorites: Caesar and Classic. It's impossible to find this in my local supermarkets, so I'm happy that Amazon carries it.

Both are good basic pasta salads and the seasoning packet used to make the dressing is very similar between the two in terms of flavor, the major difference being that the Caesar version contains breadcrumbs. Since this review is under the "Caesar" heading, I'll focus on that one.
