I've made this "plain" several times, and it's good. But it really shines as a base that you can tailor to your own tastes. I like to chop green olives and artichokes to add a little pungent "briny" flavor. One of my favorite combos is the salad made per instructions with shredded mozzarella cheese, capers, chopped sundried tomatoes, and olives. It makes a really nice chicken caesar salad, with chopped grilled chicken and parmesan cheese served over lettuce.

I like making this once a month or so -- it's a nice side with a good hearty minestrone, or by itself for a light lunch.

title: Excellent Licorice Allsorts ...
text:
I've been a fan of licorice Allsorts since I was a child. I've always liked licorice, and the addition of the colored/flavored fondant layers along with the sprinkle-covered nuggets just made it a lot more fun.

This is the 3rd brand I've tried from Amazon, and it's by far my favorite. The candy that arrived in the packages I received was fresh (the "best by" date is 9 months out), nicely packaged, and truly yummy. It's a nice treat to end a meal, and it takes only a couple of pieces to satisfy my "Allsorts" urge.

I initially ordered this as a "one-time" purchase. I just added it to my "subscribe & save" list to start next month. Compared to the other brands I've tried, this one is the keeper.

title: My opinion: the best pancake mix out there ...
text:
I think I've tried every pancake mix out there, and this is by far my favorite. It has added protein (14g per serving!) but doesn't do too much "damage" from a calorie standpoint (190kcal per serving). I mix 1/2 C mix with 1/2 C water and throw in about 1/2 C of fresh or frozen berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, or a mixture). I get 3 large pancakes, topped with a little butter and elderberry syrup (or maple) -- heaven!

I've also mixed in about 1/4-1/3C pumpkin puree, a small handful of chopped pecans, and 1/4 tsp each cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and vanilla. I usually need to add a tablespoon or two of extra water to get the right consistency, but they turn out moist and yummy every time.

How about 1/2 of a large peach, chopped plus a pinch of nutmeg, topped with warm maple syrup? The possibilities are endless. I've used orange juice instead of water and added chopped dried apricots for another variation.

I have these at least 3 times a week, and never get tired of them. Highly recommended!

(Photos show mixed berries version w/ elderberry syrup, and pumpkin-pecan version with maple syrup)

title: UPDATED:  A change for the better ...
text:
NEW REVIEW:
After having one of these from the supermarket, and having a craving for more, I decided to give these another try.

I'm not sure what Hostess did to these, but they are MUCH improved since the last time I purchased these. They are much closer to what I remember from my younger years; smaller, yes, but the filling is much nicer. The pastry is a little thicker and the glaze is thicker making these almost too sweet, but still quite good.

Also, the expiration date is far enough into the future that I won't have any problem finishing these off well before that date.

I will definitely order these again.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I've always liked Hostess Fruit Pies and hadn't had one is years. These are NOT what I remember. They're much smaller (I was sort of expecting that), and the taste isn't "right." Not sure what the problem is, but these were NOT good.

It was clear that the box had been dropped because every pie was squished on the same end, with the filling oozing out. They were almost "greasy," too. Very off-putting texture in the crust. I ended up tossing the entire box. Won't be buying these again.

title: Tender, and a decent source of protein -- but NOT "Flamin'"
text:
I was already familiar with Jack Link's Tender Bites products when I was offered the opportunity to try this "Flamin' Buffalo Chicken" flavor. I did a cross-country road trip about 13 yrs ago, and carried the [[ASIN:B00VB1Y3FK Jack Links Tender Bites Bag, Original Beef Steak, 2.85 Ounce]] in the car with me to help tide me over until I could stop for a proper meal. I like the consistency -- it didn't matter which truck stop I visited along the way, every package of Jack Link's bites tasted the same and were always tender. So I was already sold on the quality.

I was a bit disappointed in this version. Chicken -- no problem. But with a name like "Flamin' Buffalo Chicken" I was expecting something that would be spicy -- which is great because I like spicy! Yeah, these aren't that. They are VERY mild, just the barest hint of "heat," like someone maybe added the lightest sprinkling of cayenne to an entire vat of these, and each piece ended up with one or two grains of hot pepper. Don't get me wrong -- they're tasty in their own way, but definitely NOT "Flamin'."

They're also higher in sodium than I like: 610mg per serving. Each package contains about 3 servings, and each serving provides 9g of protein, so that's a plus -- the cost per serving isn't too bad, and that's a decent amount of protein, too.

But overall, these really are just chicken bites that are a little too salty for my taste, and very mild tasting.

title: Tasty hit of protein, but a bit salty
text:
I've been a fan of Jack Link's products for a long time. I did a cross-country road trip about 13 yrs ago, and had the [[ASIN:B00VB1Y3FK Jack Links Tender Bites Bag, Original Beef Steak, 2.85 Ounce]] in the car constantly to help tide me over until I could stop for a "real" meal. We're not talking gourmet stuff here, but it's tasty, filling, and supplies a hit of protein when you need it.

These Prime Rib Tender Cuts are similar in taste and texture to the Tender Bites, just a different shape. There really are tender, too -- not hard a dry like beef jerky; more chewy and "bite-able." They're a little higher in sodium that I would like (540mg per serving), but I wouldn't be eating them every day or in mass quantities. I look at these as more of an "emergency"-type snack or meal addition. And for that use, they're great.

Each pack gives you about 3 servings, so the per-serving cost isn't as bad as it could be. And each serving gives you 9g of protein. Not bad, really considering the size.

title: One of the best mixes available ...
text:
I first learned of Kodiak Cakes on a Facebook group I'm in, and it sounded like just what I needed. I'm not much of a "breakfast" person -- the simpler the better, and I don't like to eat a lot that early in the morning because I'm just not that hungry.

These are just about perfect for someone like me. Super easy to prepare: 1/2 C mix + 1/2 C water; mix until just blended (DON'T OVERMIX!!), and scoop onto a hot griddle. That is one serving, and will give you 14g of protein. Easy!

I would describe the taste as a cross between buttermilk pancakes and buckwheat pancakes -- a slightly "nutty" flavor, and the texture isn't quite as "fluffy" as your usual buttermilk variety. But beyond that, they're just plain good! They're great with just a little butter and maple syrup.

I love to dress mine up by adding 1/2 C of blueberries (fresh or frozen work equally well), or other berries (raspberries are wonderful), then topping them with some elderberry syrup. I've added 1/3 C of pumpkin purée, a little cinnamon and ginger, and some chopped pecans -- top with maple syrup. There's just so much you can do with these!

I started with the single 20-oz package, and like them enough to make these a part of my breakfast "rotation," so opted for this 4.5 lb "multi-pack" with 3 24-oz packages. Yeah, they're a little pricey, but for me, they're worth it. None of my local stores carries Kodiak Cakes, so Amazon it is. Yumm!

title: Oh yum!!  Sweet AND crunchy -- what's not to love?
text:
I tried these on a whim -- I love butter toffee peanuts, but saw these as a slight twist on that theme. I was right -- and these are excellent!

The Sweet 'N Crunchy peanuts are a lighter version of the traditional toffee peanuts: the coating isn't quite as heavy, and it's not as "dark" - it's a lighter color "caramel" coating. Since the coating isn't as heavy, these aren't quite as sweet as their heavier counterparts.

I have to be careful with these and portion out just enough for an end-of-meal treat -- otherwise, I'll eat half a can without even thinking about it!

If you're looking for a nice alternative to toffee peanuts, these would be a good choice.

title: Decent quality Hershey's chocolate ...
text:
I'm an unrepentant chocoholic, and I'm usually an equal-opportunity chocoholic, meaning I'll eat just about anything that isn't pure drek. Hershey's is a decent brand, with generally good products, not as good as some brands, but probably better than others. So I kind of knew what to expect with these almond chocolate bars.

You get 5 large-ish milk chocolate bars with just the right amount of crunchy almonds. Each bar breaks into 8 nuggets -- reminiscent of [[ASIN:B001FA1DZK Hershey's Nuggets, Milk Chocolate with Almonds, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)]]. Yes, the quality is consistent with Hershey's brand -- creamy, a bit sweet (it is, after all, milk chocolate), etc. The gift box is nice. But at the current price (twenty-five dollars) it's just not very economical, especially when you check out other options. If this were Scharffen Berger or Guittard quality, it might be worth the extra cost. But for Hershey's? You be the judge. Only you know if it's worth it to you. I'll pass.

title: Easy to prepare, great tasting ...
text:
This mix was recommended in a Facebook group as a great way to get added protein for breakfast without adding too much "bulk" (extra eggs, sausage, etc.). I was skeptical, but I'm now a believer.

These are REALLY good. And so easy to prepare! The "basic" recipe is 1 part mix to 1 part water (i.e., 1 C mix + 1 C water to make six 4" pancakes). I used 1/2 C mix and 1/2 C water, mixed it up, and then added 2/3 C of mixed frozen berries (raspberries, blueberries, and strawberries), which made 3 decent sized pancakes. A tiny bit of butter (about 1 tsp total for all three), and we're talking heaven on a plate. A splash of maple syrup wouldn't be out of line here, either.

I like this enough to use it probably once every week or so. It IS pricey, however. The convenience is great (delivered right to my door), but not sure it's worth the added cost.

Bottom line: tasty way to get additional protein in the morning; need to weigh the economical aspects.

Oct 5, 2015: ETA photo -- this is one serving made as described above: 1/2 C mix, 1/2 C water, 2/3 C frozen mixed berries = 3 decent sized pancakes. I use a 1/3 C "scoop" to get them on the griddle, and it makes exactly 3 pancakes.

title: One of my favorites ...
text:
I don't use a lot of bottled salad dressings (I really like to make my own vinaigrettes), but THIS one is different. It has a wonderful bright flavor, definitely classic vinaigrette but with a wonderful raspberry overtone. Don't let the "reduced fat" designation scare you: this is full flavored and rich tasting.

I live in a part of the country where fresh raspberries are a wonderful staple at the local farmers markets in the late summer. My favorite salad is fresh baby spinach, a handful of fresh raspberries, a chopped hard-boiled egg, and a few roughly chopped toasted hazelnuts -- topped with this dressing. Seriously, it doesn't get much better!

I've also used this to marinate chicken for grilling -- it gives it a bright flavor that pairs nicely with summer peas and crispy sweet potato fries.

Definitely one of the better bottled salad dressings available.

title: Still my favorite mustard ...
text:
What do you get when your cross a good yellow mustard with a good grainy dijon? Something that tastes a lot like Gulden's Spicy Brown Mustard.

I've been using this mustard for years. It's just perfect for everything: on sandwiches, as part of a good honey mustard salad dressing, part of a marinade for chicken or pork, dressing for potato salad -- anything that calls for mustard. It has a spicy bite, but not *too* spicy -- just a lot of good flavor. I've had no issues with the bottle; just store the bottle upside down (cap down) in the fridge door; then give it a couple of shakes, open cap carefully, and you're set to go.

I keep this on hand all the time -- I use it a few times a week in different dishes. Really good stuff!

title: My all-time favorite iced tea ...
text:
I discovered this a couple of years ago, and it was love at first taste. It's my "beverage of choice" during the warm summer months, and even during the winter when I want something chilled instead of soft drinks.

You get a perfect balance of traditional iced tea flavor and the sweetness of ripe peaches. Not overly sweet, though -- just enough to brighten the taste. I brew it on the 8-oz setting on my Keurig K45 Elite brewer. I usually make up enough for a 32-oz Nalgene bottle: fill the Nalgene bottle with ice, then brew 2 k-cups into a measuring cup, and pour immediately over the ice. Give it a quick stir, and I'm set.

I purchase this frequently so I won't run out. It's just that good! Five-stars for sure.

title: Something for everyone ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of iced tea and usually switch it up with lemonade a few times a week. This sampler pack from Two Rivers is a nice addition to the mix.

You'll get three flavors here: Lemon Iced Tea, Raspberry Iced Tea, and Strawberry Lemonade.

First the teas: I really enjoyed both of them. Not too sweet, the Lemon had just the right amount of tart lemon taste. And the Raspberry was as good as I've had anywhere (it's my current favorite).

The Strawberry Lemonade was just a bit too sweet for me. It's not bad -- I just like my lemonade a with a bit more "sour" punch.

I was curious about how these were sweetened since there's no nutritional info in the product listing here or on the box. I emailed the company (Two Rivers) and received the following info:

Per Serving:
Calories: 80
Total Fat: 0g
Cholesterol: 0g
Sodium: 0g
Total Carbohydrate: 21g
Dietary Fiber: 0g
Sugars: 20g
Protein: 0g
Ingredients: Pure Cane Sugar, instant tea, Citric Acid, natural and artificial flavor, Silicone Dioxide, Aspartame

So the primary sweetener is Pure Cane Sugar, and it looks like there's a very small amount of Aspartame used as well -- it's listed last in the list, which means that's the smallest amount of any of the ingredients. However, if you're sensitive to aspartame, even a little cane be a problem, so now you know.

That said, I really REALLY liked these drinks. I would absolutely purchase the Raspberry Tea flavor -- it's really that good.

(Sample supplied for an unbiased honest review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this item.)

title: Tasty, easy to use ...
text:
I wasn't sure I'd like these Stand n Stuff Flour Tortilla Taco Shell Boats -- so I tried a single package from the store, and ended up ordering this 32-count package. Yes, I really like them that much.

They can be filled with just about anything, really. Taco stuff, sure, but how about scrambled eggs + sausage + cheese? Shrimp stir-fry, with vegetables and sauce? They turn just about anything that isn't *too* "juicy" into a convenient manageable hand-held meal.

Preparation couldn't be easier: just wrap however many of these you need in microwavable wax paper, and zap according to the package (I usually prepare 2 at a time, and I usually set the timer for 20 seconds). Remove from microwave, unwrap, fill, and eat. It's really that simple.

This morning I loaded one up with 1 egg scrambed with some leftover roasted veggies (peppers, onion, mushrooms, artichokes, and a little broccoli), then topped it with a little shredded cheese. Perfect breakfast, lots of veggies, a little protein, fast!

I'm sold on these -- the price is decent, too, compared to my local supermarket. Will definitely order again!

title: Easy tasty meal ...
text:
So delicious! This definitely beats out Zatarain's (my favorite for years) in the flavor department.

Very easy to prepare, too: boil water, dump in the package contents, turn down the heat to simmer, cover, and just leave it alone for 22-25 minutes. Instructions say to add meat while water is boiling; since I almost always use meat that I've grilled or otherwise cooked ahead of time, I usually add it at about 20 minutes (2-5 minutes before it's done) just for it to heat up.

I usually make this with grilled chicken or pork, but I've also used shrimp w/ a little chopped andouille sausage for a more "authentic" flavor. I like this so much I now have it on Subscribe & Save. With the S&S discount, this works out to be extremely economical, as I can get 3 meals from one package.

I've also used the Vigo Red Beans and Rice blend and found it to be equally delicious. I think they're on to something there at Vigo!

title: One of my favorites for a LONG time ...
text:
I was thrilled to find this on Amazon in a 4-pack. It has been one of my favorite cereals for years, and is super pricey in my local supermarket. Amazon's current price (as of this writing, just over 4 dollars 50 cents per 16-oz box) is LOWER than the current "regular" price at the local store. So for me, this is a great deal, especially when I can have it delivered to my door.

I love the combination of chewy dates and raisins with the crunchy pecans and crispy flakes and clusters. This is a high-fiber cereal, non-GMO, and frankly, super tasty.

Nutrition info is not *too* bad: per 3/4 cup serving:
-- 210 calories (add 1/2 C non-fat milk and it's 250 calories)
-- total fat: 4g (no trans or saturated fat)
-- sodium: 135mg
-- potassium: 210mg
-- carbohydrate: 41g <---- yeah, this could be a problem for some people
-- dietary fiber: 5g
-- sugars: 13g
-- other carbohydrate: 23g

Anyway, this will remain in my "cereal rotation" for the foreseeable future, along with Mini-Wheats and Special K Red Berries. And I'll continue to purchase from Amazon as long as the price stays competitive.

title: Lovely hostess gift -- and delicious!
text:
German chocolatier Storck, the makers of these Merci chocolates, makes high-quality European-style candies -- maybe not to the level of Neuhaus, but certainly fine chocolates. That quality is apparent in this box of chocolate "bars" elegantly wrapped in gold foil and clear plastic. This selection has a mix of milk and dark chocolate candies, and both are creamy and super delicious.

I really liked the packaging: a smallish square box with a perforated "lid" that lifts to expose the selection inside. The gold foil wrapping on each bar has a colored band to indicate the flavor inside. My favorites were "Coffee and Cream" -- a coffee-flavored dark chocolate on a white chocolate base, and "Praline Cream" -- milk chocolate with a chocolate praline cream filling.

This would make a very nice hostess gift or something to have on hand for a special dinner party or event.

One caution: this is good quality chocolate that is not likely to stand up well in the heat, so if you live in a warmer area, this probably would not be a good choice to order in the summer or any other time when the temps are likely to exceed 65 degrees F or so, or if the package will sit in the sun for an extended period of time.

title: One of my all-time favorite indulgences ..
text:
I REALLY have to be careful with these -- it's all too easy to overindulge when they're perfect bite-size morsels of peanutty-chocolatey goodness!

I usually end up "repackaging" these into serving size snack bags, and store them in the freezer -- that helps to curb the temptation. They really haven't changed over the years, either -- same great peanut butter filling, same creamy milk chocolate coating. Just about perfect!

Will continue to keep these on hand as long as I can get them for a reasonable cost here on Amazon (I paid just under ten dollars for the 40-oz bag, which is a good deal as far as I'm concerned ... )

title: Tasty treat ...
text:
I used to work in the International District in Seattle within easy walking distance of Uwajimaya, the big Asian supermarket. Great store, and my weekly trips to stock up on great Asian delicacies always included a couple of packs of Pocky sticks.

I haven't worked in that area in years and had almost forgotten about Pocky until I saw it mentioned in a discussion. Amazon has Pocky?? Oh yeah!!

Placed my order for the Strawberry variety -- priced reasonably, quick delivery etc. etc. They're every bit as good as I remember. Thin pretzel-like sticks coated with a not-too-sweet strawberry-flavored coating, faintly reminiscent of strawberry yogurt -- crunchy creamy goodness. The key for me is these really aren't that sweet. I sometimes just want a slightly sweet treat, and these definitely fill the bill. The "biscuit stick" has almost no flavor at all; it's more a vehicle to carry the sweet creamy strawberry goodness.

There are quite a few of the sticks in each individual pack. I can usually get 2 servings from a pack -- which isn't a bad thing, given that the entire pack has a calorie count that would strike fear into most dieters' hearts (340 calories; for those on Weight Watchers, it's 9 points). A half package is a splurge, for sure, but if I limit it to only a few times a week and plan carefully, I can make it work.

I'll be back to order the chocolate ones as soon as I run out of strawberry.

title: Versatile and tasty ...
text:
I've been a big fan of Campbell's "Chunky" soups line for a long time. They're generally tasty, and if you're careful, you can find varieties that aren't a huge hit on the diet. I usually order the [[ASIN:B00IAE4O6E Chunky Roadhouse Beef and Bean Chili, 19 Oz]] -- great flavor, just the right about of spice.

Decided to try this "no-bean" edition, and basically I like it. Not as much as the Roadhouse version - the spice seems a bit off - but this one is absolutely fantastic for making chili dogs (I top mine with shredded cheddar cheese). I also serve this over rice for a quick meal. And I've also used it to make a queso dip using Velveeta (1 lb of Velvetta cubed, combine with one can of this chili, nuke until melted stirring occasionally). I also use it to make a sort of "Cincinnati"-style chili -- a can of this served over thin spaghetti topped with finely shredded cheddar and chopped sweet onions. Yum!

I have this on subscribe and save -- the price is actually better than my local supermarket when they carry it, which isn't very often.

Definitely will keep this on hand. Good stuff!

title: Surprisingly good ...
text:
I ordered these on a whim -- I wanted something that is shelf-stable for awhile, something that could be prepared quickly and easily. I really wasn't expecting much in the way of texture and flavor, but I was really surprised. These are actually REALLY good!

Super easy to prepare: peel back the cover to the dotted line and nuke for 1 minute. Remove cover, pour sauce over cooked noodles, and voilá! lunch!

The sauce contains REAL MEAT, too. None of that "soy protein" nonsense. The tomato meat sauce is just a tiny bit sweet for my taste, but it's definitely not off-putting. I can actually taste the garlic, basil, and onion, too. It's a good proportion of sauce to noodles. The pasta cooks slightly al dente -- not mushy at all. The serving size is perfect for lunch when combined with a salad.

Seriously, I was expecting something more along the lines of canned pasta, and this is anything but. No, it's not as good as homemade sauce and pasta, but for what it is, it's really impressive. Very tasty, will definitely order again.

title: Less bitter, more flavor ...
text:
I took a chance on this Soho Morning Mild Roast K-cup coffee, and it was a good move. This is another good one! I really don't care for the burnt over-roasted flavor of some of the more popular coffee brands, so I'm always on the look out for milder full-flavored varieties.

I'd heard of Chock Full o'Nuts, saw this, and figured "why not?" It's really good -- no rough charred flavor at all, just full-bodied richer coffee. I can't say yet that it's a new favorite, but it's definitely going into the "coffee rotation": I alternate my usual favorite with several other brands, swapping new coffees in and out as the mood strikes.

If you like a milder less "bitey" coffee, this might serve you well. I was impressed enough to order again.

title: Smooth rich flavor ...
text:
I have a couple of favorite coffees that I use with my Keurig, preferring to grind my own beans and use a reusable k-cup. I've noticed several brands appearing with these "recyclable cups" and decided to try several.

THIS one is my favorite so far. I love that the packaging is minimal -- a plastic ring around the top, the usual foil seal -- but the bottom, where normally you'd find a plastic cup, is a non-woven biodegradable mesh "pouch." The top fits exactly into the Keurig cup holder, and everything works the same way, but you end up with far less waste. This is a good thing.

Now, about the coffee itself. I'm not a fan of the over-roasted "charred" bitter flavor of a lot of the more popular brands (sorry, Starbucks!), and this Breakfast Blend suits me just fine. It has a bold rich flavor, slightly acidic (but not overly so), and takes well to additives like sweetener and/or cream -- but it just great black.

I'll definitely be purchasing more of this to rotate into my morning coffee routine. It really is quite good!

title: Why did I wait so long to try this??
text:
I remember seeing cans of B&M Brown Bread in the supermarket when I was growing up and wondering how in the world "bread from a can" would taste. Never thought much more about it until I was exploring on Amazon a few weeks ago, saw it at a decent price, and decided to give it a try.

Oh. My. Goodness! I was blown away, seriously. It's a molasses-based bread, definitely more "sweet" than "savory," nice texture, interesting flavor. I've tried it sliced with a bit of butter, then nuked for a few seconds to warm it up and melt the butter -- yumm!! And I've also sliced it and toasted it in the toaster, then topped with a little butter -- also yumm! The texture is slightly coarse -- kind of like a dense cornbread -- but with small crumb. It's definitely a different type of bread than my usual yeast/loaf varities.

It's canned, which means that it will keep awhile on the shelf. That's a good thing for me, as I'm a bit mobility challenged and sometimes getting out and about is a problem. I enjoy a slice or two along with a meal when I haven't any home-made "regular" loaf-style bread on hand. Traditionally, it's served with baked beans (it's a "Boston thing"), but I like it with just about everything.

This is now an integral part of my meal repertoire -- so much so that I have it on subscribe-and-save. Good stuff, this!

title: Tart and perfect!
text:
I love sour cherry candy, and over the years I've tried several brands. This, to me, is the best!

They have just the right amount of "sour" -- not exactly mouth-puckering, but it's definitely strong. And the cherry flavor is wonderful, without any artificial "medicine-y" taste that I sometimes detect in other brands.

These are smaller than some, but that's OK, too. I have to package these in single-serving pouches; otherwise, it's just too easy to over-indulge. Worth the investment; will definitely purchase again!

title: Crispy, OK snack ...
text:
These Almond Dark Chocolate Nut Crisp Bars aren't bad. They're very crispy with a decent amount of dark chocolate, not too "killer" for dieters (Weight Watchers points value for 1 bar: 4 pts; for 2 bars: 7 pts).

They not very big, and don't offer a lot of protein or fiber, but they ARE tasty, slightly sweet, slightly salty, crunchy. I didn't detect much almond flavor; I tasted more peanuts than anything.

Basically, I like these OK, but given a choice, I'd probably opt for something with more fiber than these, and more filling. These are just too much like "candy" for my taste.

title: Despite changes, still tasty ...
text:
I've been using Krusteaz since the early 1970s, when a friend brought back a bag from a trip to Oregon. I lived in the midwest, and it wasn't popular or even available in many places back then. I never realized pancakes could taste so good! It beat my mother's recipe all to heck, and that was a pretty darned good pancake recipe!

It has always been the best tasting of all the pancake mixes, and the easiest to prepare -- you just add water! Really, what could be easier? I change it up by adding fresh or dried fruit, different flavorings (cinnamon, pumpkin, etc.). It's like a blank canvas so you can add your own touches to it. Good stuff!

The recipe has changed over the years, and it's not quite as good now as it was when I first discovered it, but it's still the best-tasting in my opinion. I've never had an issue with the quality, and it has decent shelf life, too.

Will continue to purchase this as long as I can get it reasonably priced here on Amazon.

title: Oh, yum!  Spicy goodness in a can ....
text:
I first had Ro-tel tomatoes in the famous "queso" dip (1 lb of velveeta cheese, cubed; 1 can of Ro-tel, dump everything into a 2-qt bowl, and microwave until melted, stirring occasionally). It's the perfect spicy foil to the creamy cheese, and everyone seems to love it.

I use it often, too, in my chili -- especially good with beef (I use chuck, cubed into 1/2" cubes), black beans, onion, and a mixture of spices and herbs; in stews and other soups, even in pasta sauce! I love the spicy kick it gives. Not everyone will like the heat -- I consider it mild/medium; others find it "too hot."

Ordering through Amazon Pantry results in a price that is comparable to my local supermarket prices. Super convenient, too.

Definitely will order this again.

title: Surprisingly good!
text:
I've tried other brands of "powdered" eggs, and while OK, they weren't totally satisfactory. I decided to try these and ordered the 3-pack.

All I can say is "WOW!"

Each pack is 4.5 oz and makes the equivalent of 12 eggs. That means that 1.5 oz of powder ("crystals") is the equivalent of 4. I think the measurement is based on "small-medium" eggs, because the amount of egg I get from 1.5 oz is more like 2-3 large/extra large eggs, just enough for a nice omelet.

The liquid once mixed doesn't look like much until it hits the skillet or omelet pan when it magically transforms into what looks just like regular "fresh" scrambled eggs or omelet. Seriously, it behaves just like it -- turns fluffy yellow goodness, ready to be topped with fillings or cheese.

After going through the 3 packs, I came back to Amazon to order this 12-pack case. I'm single, and don't eat eggs all that often, so purchasing a dozen just doesn't make a lot of sense since I usually have to toss a few who stick around past their expiration dates. This is a great solution since I can have eggs whenever I want, and nothing goes to waste.

Definitely will keep purchasing these. Yes, they're a bit pricey, way more expensive than fresh eggs, but feel it's worth it for the convenience. Highly recommended!

title: My favorite cracker with cheese & salami ....
text:
These taste to me like a cross between a buttery Ritz cracker and a plain saltine, but with less salt. The size and shape make them ideal for pairing with cheese and salami -- my favorite things to eat with crackers! The slightly buttery flavor doesn't interfere with delicate cheese varieties, either. These always have a place on my cheese platters (along with water crackers and rice crackers).

This particular offer consists of 3 boxes of Club crackers, each 13.7 oz. I like this because it keeps them fresher longer -- I can open one box at a time while the rest stay sealed. Mine also have a good expiration date -- 9 months in the future -- so that's a good thing, too.

Pay attention to the price/shipping/seller. When I purchased mine, they were on Prime and a good deal. Today, there are no prime offers available, and the price plus shipping probably isn't worth it unless you're desperate. This is always a volatile situation on Amazon, so just watch it, and you'll likely score a good deal eventually.

title: Decent vanilla sandwich cookies ....
text:
I wasn't familiar with these before ordering, so I relied on the reviews. They're pretty good -- not the best I've ever had, but certainly a decent snack. The flavor has a slightly "artificial" taste, but it's not horrible. I like them -- don't love them.

Would I order again? Maybe -- I like the package size and the price (when I purchased them, they were quite reasonable but pay attention to the pricing as it can vary day to day).

title: Nice snack ...
text:
I was looking for a sweet snack to replace the cookies other sugary sweets that I usually enjoy, and found these. I'm glad I decided to give them a try.

They're not TOO sweet -- just a nice combination of raisins (both golden and "regular"), dried apricots, dried apples, dried peaches, and dried cranberries.
Dieters won't take a huge hit from these, either: a serving of about 1.5 oz is only 120 calories. It's just enough to satisfy my sweet tooth.

Am I going to totally avoid chocolate or cookies? Probably not -- but this will provide a tasty healthier alternative. Just pay attention to the price -- it fluctuates frequently (I've seen this pack of 6 packages for as little as about twelve dollars, and as much as 35).

title: Crunchy and salty + Nutella = delightful snack ....
text:
I'm a huge fan of Nutella -- I have to "ration" it due to the caloric hit, but it's one of my indulgences when I want a special snack. My favorite way to indulge is with graham crackers -- yum!

So I jumped at the chance to try one of my favorite snacks in a new way: a little packable pack complete with pretzel sticks. You get a dozen or so crispy pretzel sticks that work perfectly to scoop out the chocolate-y/hazel nutty goodness. The combination of the slightly salty pretzel sticks with the smooth creamy Nutella spread just works.

These are NOT terribly "diet friendly," though -- the small pack contains 270 calories, so it's not the kind of things I can enjoy too often. But for a planned special treat, it will work. At least I won't be tempted to overindulge since the portion is controlled by the packaging.

All in all, it's a nice snack, easy to pack in lunch or purse.

title: Hard-to-find flavor; pricey, but worth it ...
text:
Another winner from Mrs. Dash, this one is impossible to find in grocery stores in my area. I'm thrilled that I can get it online from Amazon. The price I paid (just under 12 dollars for the 2-pack) is a little high, but I personally think it's worth it. The flavor goes great with pork chops, veggies, seafood (I especially like it on seared scallops), and sprinkled onto a green salad to add a little extra "kick" of flavor.

As with all Mrs. Dash's blends, this one is salt-free, but that doesn't diminish the flavor at all. You won't miss the salt!

Will continue to purchase this as long as Amazon carries it.

title: Wonderful flavor ... and no salt!
text:
I'm a huge fan of Mrs. Dash blends -- and I've been using them since the 1980s. But this was a new one for me.

I love the blend of tomato, basil, and garlic -- and I really can taste each of the three flavors. This works really well on chicken, beef, and pork, and on stronger-flavored fish (I've used it on salmon and cod). As with all Mrs. Dash blends, it contains no salt -- just lots of great flavor.

Sprinkle on garlic bread for a change of pace -- or on a salad, on pasta, or veggies. Possibilities are endless, really.

Will definitely purchase this again. A note on pricing: watch carefully, as sometimes this is available with prime shipping at a lower cost. Mine cost less than six-fifty, with 2-day shipping included due to prime. I can't find this blend at my local supermarket, but other Mrs Dash blends cost only a little less than that. A lot of different suppliers offer this, so just pay attention and you might score a good deal.

Still a Mrs. Dash fan!

title: My new favorite ...
text:
I usually tend to go more for the medium-roast coffees, but it's difficult to find something that doesn't taste burnt. I've tried a few light-roast coffees, but usually find the flavor lacking.

So it was a GREAT surprise to try this Cafe 63 light roast coffee and find such robust flavor! I originally purchased it directly from Keurig just to try it, and immediately came here to Amazon to order a larger supply.

Cafe 63 seems to have that perfect balance: not too acidic, no charred aftertaste, just good strong clean coffee flavor.

This may become my new favorite! It's just that good.

title: Nice cheesy popcorn ...
text:
I grew up with Topsy's popcorn in Kansas City -- so that's my point of comparison.

This Cretors "Just The Cheese" corn is good -- no doubt about it. It's not *too* salty, and there's a definitely cheesy flavor about it. Topsy's is probably a little cheesier, but this is close.

It's not to damaging from a diet standpoint, either -- 2 C serving = 170 calories -- not fantastic, but not devastating, either.

Still on the fence about putting this on subscribe and save -- but it was definitely worth trying. It's better than I expected, so that's a good thing.

title: My favorite flavor of Mrs Dash ....
text:
I've been using Mrs Dash blends for over 25 years -- they just pack a huge amount of flavor, and are great on such a wide variety of foods. I also like the "original" flavor, but this garlic & herb is by far my favorite.

I use it on everything: chicken, vegetables, fish, pork chops, beef -- you name it. For fish, I just sprinkle it heavily on both sides of the fish filet and then bake it -- adds the perfect blend of flavors with no salt!

After going through the small bottles fairly quickly, I finally invested in the larger bottle -- I figure this will last me about 5-6 months, since I use it almost every day. REALLY good stuff!

title: Super convenient, decent flavor ...
text:
I'm a fan of Coffee-Mate products; have been for years. I regularly use the dry powder stuff because it's convenient, doesn't need refrigeration, and provides the taste I like (so sue me ... ). :-)

I was eager to try this new version -- and I wasn't disappointed. No refrigeration needed, portable, and flavor similar to the stuff I usually use. I found that a good "solid" squirt was sufficient to lighten my 16-oz mug of coffee -- so, probably about 1/2 - 3/4 tsp or so. I still had to use sweetener like I normally do, so I didn't find this any sweeter than the powdered stuff. Color and flavor were fine. This isn't fat-free, so there are extra calories to consider if that matters to you.

Bottom line: this is good if you need to use creamer and want to carry it with you. No refrigeration needed, etc. However, the cost at the moment is a little too high in my opinion to make up for the convenience (more than four dollars per bottle -- watch the pricing, though -- it may fluctuate in the future ... ). I probably won't be switching from my [[ASIN:B000STZS28 Coffee-Mate French Vanilla, Fat Free Powdered Coffee Creamer, 15-Ounce Packages (Pack of 6)]].

title: Good blend of tropical flavors ...
text:
I rather liked this trail mix -- great mix of tropical flavors. I love mango, and while not a fan of banana, the dried banana used in this mix is excellent and adds a nice mellow flavor. Add in the coconut, cashews, and peanuts, and it's a winner.

However, I didn't really like the inclusion of chocolate in this. And I'm a true unrepentant chocoholic! But I just don't think that flavor works in this blend. It adds a kind of weird "funky" flavor that just doesn't seem to work with the brighter fresh tropical flavors. Obviously, flavor preferences are a personal thing, so others may love this combo.

This seems to be marketed as an "upscale" trail mix -- and it is definitely high quality stuff. But I'm not sure it's that much better than other less-lofty mixes available. It's good -- but I'm not sure it's worth a premium price.

Would I purchase again? Probably not this specific blend, but I'm willing to try a couple of other blends from this manufacturer.

Bottom line: 4 stars, excellent quality, good flavors (minus the chocolate for me ... ).

title: My absolute favorite sauce ....
text:
I grew up in Kansas City, MO, the home of great midwestern barbecue. You can't drive 2 miles without seeing at least one or two good barbecue joints. I developed a taste for "KC-style" barbecue sauce: sweeter, tomato based, with a dark molasses quality to it.

Yes, I know Sweet Baby Ray's is a Chicago company, but they've nailed the flavors of my favorite KC-style sauce. There's a richness to this sauce that is missing from a lot of the "bigger" brands (Kraft, etc.). It's great as a dipping sauce, in addition to the more traditional basting sauce.

I also like the sweet and spicy version of this -- really, first rate sauce.

title: Surprisingly good! (Yes, really!)
text: These were much better than I thought they would be. They're not too sweet, and they're loaded with bits that are strongly flavored with natural lemon, giving them a tart freshness. From a diet standpoint, they're relatively harmless, with only 90 calories and 5 grams of fiber. Right now, these are my favorite snack when my favorite fruit isn't in season. Watch the prices, though -- there are a number of 3rd-party sellers with widely varying prices and shipping charges. Shop around for the best deal on Amazon.

title: Packs a punch for a "light roast" coffee ...
text:
I usually tend to go more for the medium-roast coffees, but it's difficult to find something that doesn't taste burnt. I've tried a few light-roast coffees, but usually find the flavor lacking.

So it was a GREAT surprise to try this Cafe 63 light roast coffee and find such robust flavor! I purchased it directly from Keurig just to try it, and immediately came here to Amazon to order a larger supply.

Cafe 63 seems to have that perfect balance: not too acidic, no charred aftertaste, just good strong clean coffee flavor.

This may become my new favorite! It's just that good.

title: My all-time favorite chocolate mint candy ...
text:
There seems to be a sort of rivalry between folks who love Junior Mints and those who favor York Peppermint Patties. Although I like both, I'm firmly in the Junior Mints camp.

These have the perfect balance between dark chocolate coating and creamy peppermint filling. These little 1.84-oz boxes provide a decent snack-size serving -- 220 calories per box, so it's a bit of a splurge, but totally satisfying. And there's no unwrapping.

I was very happy to find these on Amazon. The price is decent, too, but keep an eye on it -- it fluctuates from time to time. I got mine for about twenty dollars for the case of 24 individual boxes.

title: Garden Isle Medium Roast - k-cups ...
text:
I like trying different coffees in my Keurig machine, since I can make a single cup and not waste a lot of coffee making an entire pot only to find that I don't like it.

This is a decent coffee. I don't like the overly charred bitter flavor of most dark roast coffees, and this is a true medium roast. It has robust flavor, not acidic at all; in fact, it's probably just a bit too much the opposite -- just a little "funky" tasting to me, but not bad at all. I like it -- don't "love" it, but nice to try something different.

Would I purchase again? Probably not this specific variety, but I'll definitely try another Kauai Coffee offering sometime. They're doing something right over there. :-)

title: Nice little snack ...
text:
My favorite candy bar has been Snickers for a lot of years. I just love the combination of milk chocolate, nougat, creamy caramel, and crunchy peanuts. Yum!

This is that same yummy candy bar in an unwrapped bit-sized form. The serving size of 8 pieces is less than 200 calories -- not a *huge* diet hit. I repackage these into snack-size zipper bags and keep them in the freezer -- that way, I'm not tempted to overdo.

They're a bit pricey here on Amazon (I paid around twenty dollars for the 5 bags), but it's nice to have the convenience of ordering online.

Will definitely order again!

title: Convenience is worth it ...
text:
I don't use a lot of bacon, so I don't like purchasing the uncooked stuff from the supermarket because it usually "expires" before I can use it.

I discovered this pre-cooked bacon a couple of years ago, and determined that it was the way to go. This is a quality product -- excellent taste and texture -- and it's shelf stable until opened.

I keep mine in the freezer after opening -- it's super easy to pull it out and grab 2-3 pieces. The slices crisp up nicely in my microwave in about 20-25 seconds (cooking up to 4 at a time).

My *only* quibble is that they're sliced very thinly. I prefer bacon to be a little thicker cut - but this is a minor quibble.

The cost is a little higher than my supermarket (not much -- I paid just over twenty dollars for the package here; this would be the equivalent of 3 packages from my supermarket at just over six dollars each), but the convenience is more than worth it to me. There are times when I simply cannot get out to do grocery shopping, so this is a wonderful convenience, definitely worth the minimal extra cost. Keep an eye on the price; it does fluctuate occasionally.

Bottom line: I'll definitely order this again!

title: Small but filling ...
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect from these -- they never look the same as they do on television (things like this are usually smaller), so I was prepared for the diminutive size.

However, they do pack a punch! Each small bar has 5 grams of fiber, and for those of us on certain diets, that's an important number. I had one of these, and that's all I wanted -- my sweet tooth was satisfied, and I had no desire to binge. These have a lot of decent strawberry flavor, and the streusel topping is nice, too.

The price isn't terrible -- a little more than I would pay at my local supermarket -- but I have the convenience of having them delivered to my home.

Definitely will purchase again.

title: Raspberry-flavored "rice krispie treats" ...
text:
I've finally gotten serious (again) about dieting, and needed an alternative to my usual oreos or twix bars as snacks. Saw these, read some of the reviews, and decided to give them a try.

These remind me a lot of rice-krispie treats, although not as "gooey." They're small, but reasonably tasty. There are bits of dried raspberries that help with the flavor and texture a bit, and there's a white-chocolaty coating on the bottom that give it a slightly "cheesecake-y" taste. Flavor-wise, they're actually pretty good.

I like these OK. They're a snack food with a decent nutritional profile for those on diets (90 cals / bar, 3 gm fiber, low fat, etc.), and they're reasonable filling -- I never felt the urge to splurge on more than one as a snack. So that makes them worth the 4-point rating (it's closer to 3.5, but one can't give .5-point ratings ... )

Will I purchase again? Jury is still out. I'll try another flavor for comparison and then decide. The concept is a good one, so we'll see.

title: My favorite Sunchips flavor ...
text:
I love Sunchips. I've been a huge fan for as long as they've been available. And the Harvest Cheddar flavor is my favorite.

They're crisp, not too salty, with just the right amount of cheddar flavor. Ever so slightly sweet, these multi-grain chips are reasonably diet-friendly, too.

Great snack, excellent with sandwiches -- I'll continue purchasing from Amazon as long as I can get them at a reasonable price.

title: Super on ice cream ...
text:
I use this to make my version of a "brownie hot fudge sundae." I dispense with heating the chocolate, and just squeeze it out of the bottle over the ice cream. My favorite quick version uses [[ASIN:B000EMK4GO Betty Crocker Warm Delights, Hot Fudge Brownie, 3.1-Ounce Bowls (Pack of 8)]]. I top it with a scoop of whatever ice cream I have on hand (usually some kind of coffee/toffee/chocolate blend), and squeeze on a generous portion of this Double Chocolate syrup. It just works! OK, so not low-cal, but I only indulge a couple of times a month. I also use this with lower calorie frozen yogurt, for a more diet-friendly version.

Definitely will re-order this!

title: Best dried tortellini available ...
text:
This is a nice product to have on hand for a quick meal. I cook mine in the microwave in a [[ASIN:B000YT2XOI Microwave Pasta Cooker - The Original Fasta Pasta - No Mess, Sticking or Waiting For Boil]] -- it actually cooks better than I expected. This variety -- cheese and spinach -- pairs well with a lot of different sauces: marinara, alfredo, even just a little browned butter with sage and a little lemon. I can make as much or as little as I need, too.

Definitely a good buy -- the price for a pack of 4 puts each package at a price lower than my local supermarket charges. And I get it delivered right to my door.

Good buy, excellent quality and flavor -- what's not to love? Highly recommended!

title: Better than expected ...
text: I love these little single serving pouches!  The taste is better than canned, which has so much water that it dilutes the flavor.  I usually mix this up with a little mayo, mustard, celery, and sweet pickle relish to make a tuna salad that goes great with crackers or in a sandwich.  Yes, it's more expensive than canned, but it really is that much better.  Will keep on hand, for sure.

title: My favorite mustard ...
text:
I've been using Gulden's mustard since I first discovered it in the 1970s. It has the perfect combination of sharp "mustard" flavor with smooth richness, but it's not *too* sharp. I also like Grey Poupon, but find it a bit too "biting" for general use. Gulden's seems to strike that perfect balance for me.

Watch the price, as it fluctuates, When I purchased this, the price per bottle was about what my supermarket charges when it's NOT on sale. Getting it delivered to my door is worth the extra expense -- your mileage may vary. I also like the option of ordering 2 bottles rather than a case -- I'm single, so it takes me awhile to get through a bottle, and this way, I can consume it prior to the expiration date. Yay!

Overall, I'm very happy with this - it's good mustard at a decent price. Can't ask for more than that.

title: Nice alternative to other "healthy" cereals ...
text:
I usually have Special K Red Berries in my pantry, but wanted to try a couple of alternatives, just to shake things up.

Saw this on Amazon Pantry at a reasonable price, and decided to give it a try.

It's good. Great texture, nice blend of grains, definitely has a blueberry flavor. I like the "clusters," too -- really add to overall impact.

I'll probably purchase this again, but probably not as a "regular" addition to my cereal line-up.

title: Oh, YUMMM!!  Wonderful discovery ...
text:
I'm a sucker for hash browns. I order them whenever I have breakfast out, and make them often at home. Using fresh potatoes, it's labor intensive for sure, but so good!

Poking around Amazon, I noticed these, read the reviews, and decided to give them a try. I'm SO glad I did!

Super easy to prepare, and you can make whatever serving size you want using the simple 1:1 dried potatoes to hot water ratio. I'm single, so I can make just one serving at a time. Soak for 15 minutes, then into the skillet with a touch of oil, bacon grease, butter, or whatever. I occasionally add a little dried minced onion (this is the one I use: [[ASIN:B001VNGJ5K Frontier Chopped White Onion, Allium Cepa, 16 Ounce Bags (Pack of 2)]]) for some added flavor -- about 1 Tablespoon per serving -- with the dried potatoes, and then add the water.

Instructions say to cook on one side only, but I like mine really crispy, so I usually "flip" them to get a nice "crust" on both sides.

I was honestly surprised at how good these are. The price I paid -- just under fourteen dollars for the 33-oz box, or twenty-eight cents per serving -- was good, too. If the price holds, I'll definitely order again.

title: Pleasantly surprised!
text:
I was a bit skeptical about purchasing pepperoni online, but I'm happy to say I'm VERY pleased with this.

I love making my own pizzas, and my favorite is pepperoni. This works just fine for that. It has a nice spicy "kick" without being too spicy, Amazon's price at the time I purchased it was excellent, too -- actually better that the more "popular" brands in my supermarket.

I'll definitely be purchasing this again. It's convenient, tasty, and priced right.

title: Soooooo good!!
text:
These are quickly becoming my favorite cookie. They're packed with tart lemon flavor, and the "cookie" part is a crisp buttery near-shortbread type. So good! (and dangerous!)

Amazon's price at the time I purchased was great, too -- much better than I can get in the local supermarket. Will keep purchasing these, for sure.

title: Ugh! mostly peanuts ...
text:
What has happened to Planters quality? I used to buy these and get a really good mix of peanuts, almonds, brazil nuts, filberts, pecans, and cashews.

No more.

My can was well over half peanuts -- more like 75-80%. I got ** 4** brazil nuts, maybe 8 or 10 filberts, a few pecans (mostly small pieces), a healthy handful of almonds, and NO cashews that I could find, unless they were in pieces that look like peanuts. I certainly didn't taste any.

Overly salty, too. Just not worth it. Will purchase only "premium" nut blends at the supermarket in the future. Sorry.

title: Not perfect, but tasty ...
text:
I'm single and live alone, so cooking for myself usually means careful shopping so as to avoid too much in the way of leftovers. And usually I avoid "packaged" meals. But I saw these, read the reviews, and decided to give it a try.

I'm impressed. I found a nice balance among ingredients, with a hefty amount of chicken (surprise!). The spice is excellent with just the right amount of "heat" for my palate, and not overly salty. I used half of a package to make two small-ish "burritos" with 8" flour tortillas and a little shredded cheese ("Mexican" blend), and the other half is in the fridge for lunch in a day or so. Perfect!

I will absolutely purchase this again to have on hand for those times when I can't get out to the supermarket (I'm thinking this winter, when the roads are iced up ... ). It's a keeper!

title: Excellent buy, excellent quality ...
text:
I use these flour tortillas for quesadillas, enchiladas, and burritos, as well as sandwich "wraps" stuffed with sliced deli meats or chicken or tuna salad. I was skeptical about expiration dates, but my orders are consistently dated more than 6 months after my date of purchase, so there's no problem of reaching the expiration date before I finish them.

They're just like the ones I get at the supermarket -- no difference whatsoever. I'm thrilled that I can get them delivered, and at reasonable cost. Yes, they're a bit more than what I would pay at the store, but the extra few cents per package is worth it to me.

Definitely will keep these on hand -- they're so versatile and tasty!

title: Delicious!
text:
I order a couple of cans of this on Amazon Pantry every couple of weeks or so, and so far, I've not had a problem with dented cans. This was MUCH better than I expected. It's a thick, hearty chili, with great flavor. I combine it with cooked brown rice for a nice black beans and rice, sometimes adding some chicken sausage for extra protein and flavor.

Will definitely purchase this again.

title: Best cherry preserves I've found so far ...
text:
I'm a sucker for anything "cherry" - especially preserves! And good ones are hard to find. They're usually too sweet, or more like jam than preserves.

These Maury Island Tart Cherry Preserves are just about perfect. They taste like home made, not too sweet, just the right amount of fruit, including whole cherries (minus the pits, of course). Yes, these preserves are pricier than the standard supermarket brands, but they're Oh! so much better! I'll gladly pay a premium price for a premium product, and these preserves are premium, indeed.

I'm now tempted to try other flavors in the Maury Island brand. Marionberry, perhaps? We'll see ...

Highly recommended!

title: Just OK ...
text:
I tried the Vanilla and Caramel variety of these Lancaster candies, and frankly, I wasn't impressed.

It's OK -- but it has an odd texture, sort of like a combination of salt water taffy. They're really REALLY sweet, too, with not much flavor of either vanilla OR caramel -- just sugar in taffy form.

I think I'll just stick to "regular" caramels -- these are an over-priced poor substitute.

title: Bland -- what happened?
text:
This used to be one of my favorite dips. I haven't had it in awhile, saw it here on Amazon, and decided to try it again.

What happened? It's sooooo bland and nearly flavorless. I mean, yeah, you get a vague taste of beans, but where are the spices? Where's the flavor?

I'll finish using this with quesadillas combined with cheese, spicy grilled chicken, and salsa, but that's about all. Won't order again. I'll just order refried beans from now on. Cheaper and more flavor.

title: Still my favorite ...
text:
I've had my Keurig for 18 months, and Caribou Blend was one of the first coffees I tried. It's still my all-time favorite.

It had a nice rich flavor, full-bodied, but without the "charred" burned taste that other medium-roast coffees have (e.g., Starbucks). I brew it using the 8-oz (middle) setting, and it comes out perfect each time.

Will continue to purchase this as long as I can get a good price here on Amazon.

title: I like it -- but not over-the-moon "in love" with it ...
text:
I love the taste of peach -- cobbler, pie, ice cream, iced tea, etc. So I saw this, read the reviews specifically for this flavor, and decided to give it a try.

It's .... good. Definitely taste the peach and nectarine. Nice over ice on a hot day. But I keep picking up another flavor: watermelon! Maybe it's just how my "taster" works, but there's definitely a strong flavor accent of watermelon when I drink this.

It's not enough to deter me from drinking it -- but I have to say I was just a *bit* disappointed. Would I purchase again? Maybe. Jury's still out. If I stop thinking about it as "peach/nectarine," and start thinking of it as "fruit salad with peach, nectarine, and watermelon," I think I can get over it. But I still like my Snapple peach iced tea for my liquid peach fix.

title: Great taste!
text:
The more I try these Simply Organic spices and blends, the more I like them. I'm gradually switching out almost all my herbs and spices to Simply Organic due to the quality, price, and taste.

This taco seasoning is no different. It's better than any of the ones I get in the supermarket -- just more robust, a tad spicier but not overwhelming in that respect, and the price is comparable. AND it has NO MSG!

I use it with ground beef, yes, but also with chicken and pork. I dice the raw chicken into 1/2" cubes and brown in a skillet, then just follow the recipe on the package for beef and voila! I have chicken tacos. I do the same with boneless pork loin chops -- dice, brown, then do the taco seasoning thing. I also use the seasoned meat as filling for enchiladas, quesadillas, and burritos. It's the flavor that matters, and the flavor this adds is excellent.

I now have this on Subscribe and Save -- I use it that much. Great find! HIghly recommended!

title: My favorite "go-to" coffee ...
text:
I've been drinking this since I got a few cups of it in a "sampler" shortly after I got my Keurig machine 18 months ago. It has just the right combination of medium roast and the medium/robust flavor I like, with none of the "charred" burnt taste of other more popular brands.

I drink a few flavored coffees for variety once in awhile, but I always come back to this. It's like a warm comfortable sweater for me. Good stuff, and Amazon's price is very competitive with other K-cup sellers. I'll keep buying it here as long as the price remains competitive.

title: Creamy and SWEET ...
text:
I'm a big fan of Lindt Lindor Chocolate Truffles. These white chocolate ones are good, no question. But they're a tad sweet for my tastes.

Very creamy and smooth, the usual Lindt quality shows. They're a nice change from the usual milk or dark chocolate truffles -- I like them, but I didn't *love* them. Taste is a very individual thing, though, so if you like really creamy sweet truffles, these might work really well for you.

title: Love these simple cookies ...
text:
I first tried these over the holidays, and fell in love with their buttery flavor. They're reminiscent of shortbread, but not as heavy.

I've found these locally, but they're not stocked that often, and are priced higher. I was able to get 12 packages here on Amazon for less than my supermarket, and I haven't had any issues with broken or crushed cookies. I've gone through about 5 packages so far, and I think I found 3 broken cookies in the whole lot.

They work well with tea, coffee, even spread with Nutella. Just a couple in the afternoon can satisfy my sweet cravings -- just about perfect!

I would definitely purchase again, but it's going to take ma awhile to get through this bunch.

title: Nice mix of textures/flavors ...
text:
I rather liked this. There's a nice variety in here: milk chocolate- and yogurt-covered raisins and peanuts, and crunchy toffee peanuts. It makes a tasty snack, but I have to be careful to limit myself -- it's too easy to keep eating it! I've parceled the contents into small zipper snack bags to reduce temptation.

It's a bit sweet, but if you're in the mood for that, this is a nice option. I would purchase again.

title: These were just OK for me ...
text:
I'm usually a huge fan of Lindt Lindor Truffles, so I was really looking forward to trying these peanut butter ones.

They were a bit of a disappointment. They were ... OK ... but really too sweet compared to other less expensive products. Maybe if the chocolate had more flavor - more like a darker chocolate rather than a super-creamy milk chocolate, these would be better. I know that taste in things like this is an individual thing, so if you like super light and creamy milk chocolate surrounding a super creamy super SWEET vaguely peanut filling, you might really like these. I'll stick to Reese's.

title: The same tried and true classic ...
text:
I had none of the problems some of the other reviewers mentioned: my bottle has an expiration date in late 2014 (it's now early May 2014), and looks just like the nearly-empty bottle currently in my fridge.

I use this often: on sandwiches, in dressings, in marinades -- it just works in so many situations. I love the sharp slightly-acidic mustardy flavor that compliments everything: veggies, fish, chicken, pork, beef.

Will continue to purchase from Amazon as long as the price remains competitive with my local supermarket. I love the convenience of having it delivered, and it's worth a few cents extra for that luxury. (And it really is only a few cents difference in price ... )

Highly recommend this.

title: More goodness from Simply Organic ...
text:
I've been gradually replacing my "old" spice bottles with more of these Simply Organic versions, and I'm very pleased so far. The quality is excellent, and the price is better than my local supermarket.

This paprika is high quality and has the nice bright flavor I want. This would be considered "sweet" paprika -- it's not hot and spicy like the "hot" paprika you see in the red/green/white tin.

Definitely worth the money -- highly recommended.

title: Super quality for a reasonable price ...
text:
I've been purchasing quite a few of these Simply Organic herbs and spices here on Amazon. They're consistently high quality, and the prices are much better than similar products at my local supermarket.

This cilantro is no exception. I don't use enough cilantro to purchase fresh -- most of it gets thrown away. So having a high-quality dried substitute is wonderful. This has a nice bright flavor, and works well in my Asian and Mexican recipes that call for it. Most recently, I used it in a quinoa salad that turned out great! (Quinoa, dried apricots and golden raisins, almonds. lime juice/zest, cilantro, chopped jalapeno, etc.)

Very happy with this product ..

title: The best quality  ...
text:
I got these to use in cooking -- specifically, a quinoa salad that called for golden raisins -- and they're wonderful! Large size, plump, great flavor -- and no sugar added is a plus. They worked beautifully well in my salad, and I've used them in muffins and cupcakes since, also with super results.

I consider these a real find, and highly recommend them!

title: Excellent quality & flavor ...
text: These are super for snacking right out of the bag, but I use them most in cooking.  I add them to the batter for my yummy honey bran muffins, and toss in a couple handfuls when I make cherry pie or cobbler for that little "extra" flavor.  How about cherry-almond scones?  I make vanilla scones, and toss in about 1/2 - 3/4C of these cherries, along with a little almond extract, then top the iced scones with sliced almonds.  Perfection!  Watch the price -- it varies a lot, so try to get them when it's "down."  I've also purchased the 4-lb box of these, repackaged them into 1 lb portions, and frozen them for future use.  Definitely worth the effort!

title: Not my favorite ....
text:
I like Starbucks Veranda Blend in their Blonde line of lighter-roast coffees, so I decided to try this Bright Sky Blend.

I'm not a fan. It's OK, but is very acidic / "citrus-y" tasting. I don't know - it just has a very odd "sharp" element in the flavor that I really don't like. I'm also not fond of Starbucks "regular" line of coffees -- they all taste over-roasted to me, almost charred/burnt tasting. So I was happy to see them come out with a lighter roast line.

Like I said, I like the Veranda Blend, but this one? Sorry ... no. I'll be passing it along to my neighbors.

title: Nice assortment ...
text: I'm a huge fan of Sunchips, and my favorite flavor is Harvest Cheddar, so this assortment was almost tailor-made for me!  The expiration date is far enough in the future that it shouldn't be an issue.  You get 12 bags of Harvest Cheddar, and 6 each of the other 3 varieties.  At the time I purchased, the price made for an real value, too.  Definitely happy with this purchase!

title: Good quality, super flavor ...
text: I got these jalapeno flakes to use in a recipe that called for finely chopped fresh jalapenos -- I hate going to the store to purchase a single jalapeno pepper, so I thought I'd give these a try.  The recipe I was using also called for lime juice, so increased the amount of lime juice by a couple of tablespoons, and soaked these jalapeno flakes in the lime juice.  It worked perfectly!  They have quite a kick -- not overpowering, but more than I expected from dried jalapenos.  I'm planning to continue using these in any recipe when I don't have fresh jalapenos handy.  Good stuff, this.

title: Oh, YUM!! (I'm in trouble ... )
text:
These are just so good! I love all things maple, and I've purchased these on occasion at a local supermarket (I live near the Canadian border). I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon, and at a reasonable cost (I got twelve packages for thirty-four dollars). My problem is I have a tendency to eat too many! To solve that problem, I split up a package into 4-cookie "portions," each one in a ziploc plastic bag, which I keep in the freezer. That way, I just pull out a single package when I want a treat, and minimize the damage.

These have a nice fairly strong buttery maple flavor. The cookie is tender and slightly crunchy, with a buttery shortbread-like texture. The filling is creamy maple-y goodness, and just the right amount.

If you like maple, you'll like these. Definitely will be purchasing these again.

title: Built-in portion control!
text:
I'll admit it: I'm a sucker for Oreos. They're one of my favorite cookies, and it's all too easy for me to over indulge.

That's where these single-serve packs come in handy. Each one contains 6 cookies. I store them in my "auxiliary pantry" out of the way, and bring in only one pack at a time. I get my Oreo fix and I'm not tempted to overdo it.

I think the price I paid is decent -- a bit more than the supermarket, but I can have these delivered to my home, so there's that.

Definitely will purchase again as long as the price stays reasonable. They are, after all, Oreos!

title: Great for cooking and baking ...
text:
I got tired of buying fresh limes and grating off the rind, and unfortunately some of my knuckles, so I came to Amazon to see if I could find a suitable solution.

I did, and this is it. I've used this so far in salad dressings, cheesecake, cookies, and marinades, and it performs beautifully. Price when I purchased it was very reasonable for what I got, too.

Will definitely purchase again when I run out, which won't be any time soon because you get a LOT of this stuff!

title: I liked these, but ...
text:
... there's an overriding flavor of butter that I (surprisingly) find a bit off-putting. Don't get me wrong, I like the taste of butter. But when that's the first thing I taste in a chocolate cookie ("Triple Chocolate" no less), I get a bit disappointed.

They're good cookies, and I do like them -- just wish the balance between butter flavor and chocolate flavor skewed a bit more toward chocolate.

Will I purchase again? Maybe -- but I want to try some other alternatives before I decide.

title: Good quality ...
text:
I recently discovered quinoa, and I'm having fun finding ways to use it.

This particular version of it is good quality, it IS prewashed, and cooks up nicely in 12-15 minutes. The flavor of quinoa is subtle and a little nutty, allowing it to play well with savory and sweet ingredients. One of my favorite salads uses quinoa, dried apricots, golden raisins, slivered almonds, jalapeno pepper, and a little onion, with a dressing made of lime, cumin, oil, and some other stuff.

Be careful of the price, though -- it varies a LOT from day to day. The price I paid at the time I purchased it was good, but I've seen it MUCH higher.

Overall, a good product -- if you're new to quinoa and don't want to invest in a large quantity, this might be a good first step.

title: Excellent quality ...
text:
I recently discovered these Simply Organic herbs and spices, and I'm sold. This ground cumin seed is a great example.

I use quite a lot of cumin in soups, stews, even stir fries, so getting it so fresh and (at least when I purchased it here on Amazon) such a great price is wonderful, much less expensive than similar products at my local supermarket. I may even put it on subscribe and save and save even more.

Super product -- highly recommended!

title: One of my all-time favorites ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Lindt Lindor Truffles -- and this packaging gives me a variety of flavors.

You get a dozen or so in each package, and they seem fairly evenly divided among milk, dark, and white chocolate flavors. Price I paid was decent, so I consider it a good value.

Would purchase again if I can continue to get a good deal on it.

title: Slivered almonds in small packs - perfect for recipes!
text: I purchased these to use with various recipes that use small quantities of slivered almonds.  The small 2-oz packages allow me to use just what I need, keeping the rest fresh for future use.  My favorite recipe is a quinoa salad using dried apricots, golden raisins, slivered almonds, and a little green onion, with a lime-mirin-oil-spices dressing.  YUM!  The 12 packs will last awhile, too.  Very happy with this purchase.

title: Just what I was craving ...
text:
I really love Kit Kats, and this assortment gives me the variety that I crave.

My bags contained just a few more milk chocolate than white and dark chocolate minis, but that's OK -- I like them all!

My feeling is that the value for money was good -- for what I paid, I thought it was a good deal. I would gladly order again!

title: My favorite of the Triscuit flavors ...
text:
I really like these crackers -- they're lower in fat/calories than the "original" flavor, but the taste is nearly the same.

I've had trouble finding these in my supermarket, so finding them online (even at a higher price) is great. They work so well with nearly every kind of cheese. Yummy!

title: Good wafer cookie
text:
These are decent wafer cookies. The wafer layers are crisp and light, and they have a good amount of filling.

My only complaint is they just don't have enough chocolate flavor. They're good, but "knock your socks off" good.

title: Super quality ...
text:
I use this pineapple in the "weight watchers-friendly" angel food cake recipe (1 box angel food cake mix, 1 20-oz can crushed pineapple with juice; mix together; bake at 350F for 25 minutes until golden brown). I make it about every 3-4 weeks -- it's delicious and fits well with my diet program

This pineapple is consistently high quality: no hard "core" bits, consistent from can to can in terms of amount of juice, right amount of sweetness, etc. It bakes up perfectly every time.

It costs a bit more than the supermarket, but the convenience of home delivery makes up for that. Very happy with this!

title: Just about perfect ...
text:
I grew up in Kansas City, MO, so I know a little something about barbecue. Although this sauce is from Chicago, it's very close to the taste and texture of my favorite sauces.

I like all the Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauces, but this one is probably my favorite. It has a sweet smoky taste with a hint of "zing." It's not particularly spicy -- not to my taste, anyway -- but it has a hint of heat that gives it something special.

Be sure you watch the prices here. They can fluctuate wildly, with variations in shipping charges, basic prices, etc., making this more or less of a good deal. I usually check on it every couple of weeks or so, and get it when the price is a bargain.

title: My favorite candy bar in a bite-sized nugget ...
text:
Snickers has been my favorite candy bar since I was a child (and that's a LOT of years!). There's just something about the combination of salty peanuts, creamy caramel, soft nougat, swathed in milk chocolate. Yummm!

This new form -- small nuggets of Snickers -- is a welcome addition to the Snickers line. These are unwrapped -- yay! no wrappers to dispose of -- making them much easier to get to when you need to satisfy that Snickers craving.

They also work well in baking -- they're small enough to use in cookies in place of chocolate chips (OK, yes, they're bigger than chocolate chips, but still small enough that they will work), or toss on top of brownies.

Definitely a keeper in my pantry.

title: I remember these from my childhood ...
text:
... and they're every bit as good now as they were then!

The chocolate is just the right sweetness and texture; the pecans are crispy, but the BEST part of these is the caramel.

Buttery and creamy, it's not too "hard," and not too soft, either. Just the perfect consistency, and a delightful intense caramel-ly goodness.

These aren't cheap, but I like that they're packaged in 3-piece packages. Helps with portion control. :-) Otherwise, I'd be snacking on these constantly!

Very happy with these ...

title: The best ramen I've found (so far) ...
text:
Forget the popular supermarket ramens -- this one is head and shoulders above those.

The noodles are a nice consistency, and, best of all, it's not nearly as salty as other options. OK, so it's "artificial chicken flavor" -- and yes, there's a substantial amount of salt -- but the flavor is actually quite good.

Even better, however, is that this can serve as the starting point for a ton of flavorful additions: fresh veggies, some diced rotisserie chicken, etc. Nothing in the flavoring is too overpowering, so you can dress these up nicely to suit your own taste.

I don't eat ramen very often, but when I do, I like it to be decent quality. This stuff is.

title: Great for dieters ...
text:
I use this mix a lot, for both traditional angel food cake and the dieter's dream cake (a box of cake mix combined with a can of "light" pie filling baked in a 9" x 13" pan).

I use the traditional cake as a base for fresh berry or peach "shortcake," for a lower-calorie alternative. These Pillsbury mixes are consistently good, and you can't beat Amazon's price. Definitely a good buy!

title: What fun! Seasonal Kit-Kats!
text:
I'm a huge fan if Kit-Kat bars, and got these to add to our family's stash of holiday sweets. These are a bit different in shape. Instead of 4 segments, you get two that are twice as large as normal, with a "cut" that goes halfway down the center (hard to explain; the key point is really that you get two larger segments).

Each segment has a holiday character molded into it: reindeer, snowman Santa Claus, etc.

Same great Kit-Kat flavor. We liked them!

title: Super ginger flavor ...
text:
Got these to add to our family's "goodie stash" -- a collection of sweets and savories that enable our grazing tendencies.

Everyone LOVED them. The strong ginger flavor is the result of bits of candied ginger, but you also taste other spices as well: cinnamon, cloves, even a hint of nutmeg.

Amazon's price at the time I ordered these was wonderful -- just over two dollars a package. Great with tea or coffee.

title: Decent olive oil flavored crackers ...
text:
I purchased these to serve with a variety of tapenades and cheese spreads. I didn't want anything too big or too "flavored," and these worked well for my use. They're small-ish -- maybe 1.5" x 1.75" -- and mine were fresh tasting with just a hint of olive oil flavor.

These worked well with my spreads, but would also work well with hummus or even salsas of various kinds. They're relatively tender -- not hard and crunchy like pita chips -- with a crispness that I liked.

Very happy with these. Would purchase again.

title: A wonderful holiday family tradition ...
text:
I started purchasing Walkers shortbread several years ago, and it has turned into an annual event for my family.

This is really the best shortbread available outside of the British Isles, and being able to purchase here on Amazon is wonderful! We love the tin and the variety of shapes included. Lovely with tea, coffee, or cocoa. I've never been disappointed -- perhaps I've been lucky, but every time I've purchased these, they've arrived in great shape and not stale.

WIll continue to purchase as an annual holiday treat for my family.

title: Decent flavor ....
text:
I've tried a number of Ocean Spray drink packets, and although not my favorite (that honor belongs to the White Cranberry-Peach flavor), this one is quite good.

The lemonade flavor is pronounced, tart, not artificial tasting. The tangy cranberry is a secondary flavor -- you know it's there, but it's not overpowering, The color is a bit too red for my taste, but it's not too bad.

The sweetener used is aspartame, so if you have a philosophical objection to it, this isn't the drink for you. But if you're looking for something tasty to add to your water, this might be a nice choice.

title: MUCH better than I thought it would be ...
text:
