I purchased the Roadhouse Beef & Bean Chili based on the reviews here. I'm kind of finicky when it comes to chili -- I make a pretty good homemade chili myself, but I wanted the convenience of a canned chili that I could prepare in a few minutes when I needed a quick lunch.

I really wasn't expecting much, so I was very pleasantly surprised when I tried this for the first time yesterday. It has a spicy "kick" to it, but it's not overpowering. It also has a decent amount of meat in it, and a hearty robustness. Yesterday I ate it "plain," with a little cheese on top. Today, I served it over rice, and it was fabulous! It would definitely be good on hotdogs, too.

I just put this on Subscribe-and-Save -- at just under $2 a can, it's a great deal, and less than my supermarket charges. Very happy with this!

title: Best dried pasta -- chef recommended!
text:
I first learned about De Cecco pasta from a fairly famous restaurant chef in the San Francisco Bay area. He said it was the best dried pasta around (this was in the late 1980s), so I started purchasing it then.

Fast forward 25 yrs, and I'm still buying it. Oh, I've tried other brands over the years, but I always come back to De Cecco because it just tastes better. This fettuccine is no exception. It's just about perfect -- cooks fairly quickly to a nice al dente, and holds up well to any sauce decide to use with it. My favorite is alfredo sauce, with added sauteed mushrooms and shredded meat from a rotisserie chicken, topped with some shredded parmesan. Yum!

Yes, De Cecco costs more than some brands, but believe me, the quality is definitely worth it. Amazon's price (just under $2 a package on subscribe-and-save) is much better than my local supermarket. For me, this is a pantry staple. Good stuff!

title: Not the best I've ever had, but this is good ...
text:
I'm a sucker for licorice allsorts. I've ordered this twice now, and it's been great quality both times. The bags I've received were definitely NOT stale, with fairly even distribution of shapes/patterns/etc.

I can't help but compare it to the best I've ever had -- when I was in London on business -- but for moderately-priced allsorts, this is very very good!

Will definitely order again and again.

title: My favorite indulgent chocolate treat ....
text:
I first had these when I had neck surgery and wasn't allowed to eat anything "solid." After I recovered, I still remembered how good they tasted, but it wasn't until I saw them here on Amazon that I thought about ordering them.

Yes, they're just as good as I remember. Lots of chocolate flavor, very creamy consistency. But the BEST part is that they don't need refrigeration! I can store them in my pantry, and toss a pack in the fridge in the morning to chill for an afternoon snack. Super convenient! Each cup is 100 calories, so they're wonderful for those of us who need to "portion control" our snacks.

The price I paid -- less than twelve dollars for twelve four-packs -- is super, even less than my local supermarket. And the expiration date on mine is well into 2015 -- so these are nice and fresh.

I now have these on subscribe and save. Great deal, excellent product, super convenient!

title: Not quite what I expected ...
text:
With a name like "Cranberry Cherry Limeade," I was expecting more of a limeade-type drink, like you get when you order cherry limeade at a soda fountain: mostly limeade flavor, with the cranberry and cherry flavors as "add-ins."

This isn't like that. It's CHERRY, with a hint of cranberry, and virtually no "lime" flavor at all. The cherry is more like maraschino cherry juice -- very sweet and almost "cherry cough drop" tasting. It's definitely a RED color, too -- so just think sweet artificial cherry drink with a hint of tart cranberry flavor, and you'll have a pretty good idea of what this is about. Pay no attention to the "limeade" in the name. :-)

It's OK, but I will not be ordering this again. (Now, if they would just bring back the white cranberry peach flavor packets, I'd be a VERY happy camper!)

title: Decent medium-roast Colombian coffee ....
text:
Since receiving my [[ASIN:B00AWLBE6G Keurig K75 Single-Cup Home-Brewing System with Water Filter Kit, Platinum]] coffee maker last year, I've grown to really like a variety of different coffees. I've zeroed in on a few that are my favorites, but I'm always open to trying new ones.

So when offered an opportunity to try this Caza Trail Colombian Fair Trade, I jumped at the chance.

I'm glad I did -- I quite liked it!

I'm a "medium-roast" person -- dark roast always tastes burnt to me, with a bitterness I just don't like. Also, I use the middle cup-size setting - 8 oz. - as I've found that seems to give me the "strength" of flavor I like best. When I test coffee, I use that setting, and drink at least one cup plain black, and at least one with sweetener and creamer.

This one is a very nice medium roast, very similar to Caribou Blend [[ASIN:B007PA33KM Caribou Coffee Caribou Blend, K-Cups for Keurig Brewers, 50 count]], but with just a hint of "sharpness" to it. Describing coffee flavor/taste is such a subject thing -- so I'll do my best, but ultimately it's up to you. Caribou Blend is my all-time favorite, so if you like that, you'll find the taste of this very similar.

It has a rich flavor that really shines when served black, but it's robust enough to stand up to sweetener and creamer without losing anything.

Definitely thinking about adding this to my subscribe and save list -- it's an economical alternative to pricier similar K-cups.

title: Economical way to have milk in a pinch ...
text:
Usually when I purchase milk in the store, it ends up going bad before I can get through the carton. I just don't use it that much. But when I need it, it's nice to be able to mix it up fresh.

That's where this instant nonfat dry milk comes in handy. I can mix up 8 oz at a time to use on cereal, in recipes, etc. It does work better if I mix it up the night before I need it for cereal (it justs tastes better after sitting overnight in the fridge), but for cooking, I just mix up what I need when I need it.

This stuff keeps a LONG time on the shelf, and I like the resealable pouch. Very happy with this.

title: My favorite penne ....
text:
My local supermarket carries some of the De Cecco pastas, but they charge a premium (usually it's around three dollars a package). When I saw this on Amazon for just over a buck a package, I snapped it up!

This is by far my favorite penne pasta. It holds up well in casseroles, but it's also good just mixed with some sauce or pesto. The ridges (the "rigate" part of penne rigate) grab onto whatever topping you're using. The result is even coating, and better flavor.

I use it most often in mac and cheese (I make a killer bacon mac & cheese), and a casserole with Italian sausage, marinara sauce, green and red bell peppers, ripe olives, and lots of cheese.

I just wish Amazon would put this on subscribe and save. Definitely a great buy!

title: Another favorite from my childhood ....
text:
I remember getting these in my lunchbox when I was in elementary school -- a LONG time ago. They have several light crunchy wafer layers with creamy vanilla filling.

I really like this packaging option: the individual packages are perfect for a snack, although not super low in calories. Still, one small package is definitely enough to satisfy my sweet tooth, with none of the mindless snacking that might happen with a larger package. Portion control at its finest.

I paid around nineteen dollars for the box of 24 packs, so that's less than a dollar a pack -- not bad at all! I'll definitely be purchasing these again.

title: Decent side dish ....
text:
I'm a huge fan of Idahoan instant mashed potatoes, particularly the Golden Selects [[ASIN:B00D3J9F7O Idahoan Mashed Potatoes, Buttery Golden Selects, 4.1 Ounce (Pack of 10)]], so when I saw these on my "Recommendations" list, I decided to give them a try.

These are really very good, and super easy to prepare (water, milk, a little butter or margarine, mix in a baking dish, and bake uncovered for 20-25 minutes or so). I get 3 generous servings from a package -- label says 4 servings, but I like my servings a bit larger.

My *only* quibble is that these are just a bit on the salty side for my taste. I know everyone has their own idea of what "too salty" is, so you may find these perfectly fine. But for me, it's just a tiny bit too much salt, most likely from the bacon.

It's only a minor quibble, and I'll certainly continue preparing and eating these, but I might try one of the other varieties without bacon and see if that makes a difference.

title: Good snack ...
text:
I got these after trying them at a friend's house -- they're good straight out of the package, without heating.

The flavor is reminiscent of the chocolate-and-cream cookies we all know and love, but the chocolate isn't as "chocolate-y." The cream filling is decent, and the light coating of icing on the outside provide some texture without being too sweet.

Amazon's price is good, too, or it was when I purchased these, about 3 dollars per pack, which is a lot cheaper than in my local supermarket.

I'll likely purchase these again to have around as a handy snack. Good stuff!

title: Good coffee, but not enough cinnamon for me ...
text:
Nice medium-roast flavor. I would have preferred a bit more cinnamon flavor, but all in all, not bad. I added sweetener and a splash of vanilla creamer, and it was reminiscent of a "famous maker" cinnamon roll, but without a lot of cinnamon flavor.

I usually brew using the "middle" setting on my Keurig Platinum (I think it's 9 oz?) -- might try it at the "stronger" setting and see if I can squeeze more cinnamon flavor.

Bottom line: I like it, but I'm going to continue my search for the "perfect" cinnamon coffee K-cup experience.

title: What happened?? These USED to be good ....
text:
I grew up with Vienna Fingers. They were one of our "special" cookies: only brought out on special occasions (Lorna Doone was another). They always had a nice texture, and a lovely vanilla filling.

Not any more. These are really NOT good. The cookie part is almost tasteless -- no discernible flavor of any kind. The filling is grainy, with the tiniest hint of vanilla, but the overall taste is just "sickly sweet."

Something has happened to the recipe ... or something. Whatever, these aren't even a pale imitation of the ones I grew up with, except in shape.

Sorry, Keebler -- I won't be purchasing these again.

title: HOW do they do it?? This stuff is REALLY good!
text:
Well, you could knock me over with a feather. Good-tasting gravy from a POWDER? I would never have believed it if I hadn't tried it myself.

I'm single, and although I like to cook, I don't often make a big roast. So making gravy isn't something I do very often, although I really enjoy it with a small steak over mashed potatoes. Saw this, read some of the reviews, and decided it was worth a try.

As others have pointed out, the instructions are under a peel-down nutrition label on the back. My first test involved making approx 1 C of gravy using the microwave instructions: combine 3 Tbsp of powder with 1 C of hot water, whisk until smooth, then nuke for 2.5-3 min at full power, whisking after each minute (basically, I just hit the "1 minute express" button, whisked when it beeped, then hit the 1 minute express button again, etc.). This made just under 1 C of tasty brown beefy-tasting gravy, with no lumps, a nice silky texture, and seasoned just right (not too salty).

I used about 2/3 of it over my favorite instant mashed potatoes [[ASIN:B004UBNQTM Idahoan Buttery Golden Selects Flavored Mashed Potatoes (10 Pack)]] with a small steak from a local butcher, and a side of steamed fresh spinach. A quick balanced meal.

Based on this, I now know that I should be able to make a little less quantity using 2 Tbsp of powder and 2/3 C hot water. At this rate, this 21-oz container should last a decent amount of time.

VERY surprised at how good this is. Seriously. Highly recommended if you want decent brown gravy without the extra work.

title: Less sweet, VERY tasty!
text:
I cannot find these in my local supermarket, so I was thrilled to find them on Amazon. I love the taste of cinnamon at breakfast, and these are packed with cinnamon-y goodness.

They're not iced, so they're not as sweet, which I love! A couple of these with a cup of coffee, and I'm ready to face the day. A couple of these with a cup of tea makes a great afternoon snack.

Pricewise, I'm getting these for just over two dollars per box, which is about what I'd pay locally if I could find them. So it's a win-win for me. Great product, great price, delivered right to my door -- what's not to like?

title: Lower fat version of a tasty original ....
text:
OK, so these aren't a HUGE improvement calorie-wise over the original, but every little bit helps. The flavor and texture are very close to the original higher-fat version: crisp, slightly salty, just less "greasy."

I don't eat a lot of these -- maybe a bag every couple of weeks or so -- and I try to portion them out so that I'm not sabotaging my diet too much. But when you gotta have chips, these are a decent option.

title: Lime and White Chocolate! What's not to like??
text:
OH my! Why did I not try these before?

This is the PERFECT combination of tart lime flavor with the smoothness of white chocolate. The cookies are small, slightly dry (not soft and chewy), and packed with flavor.

Much better than I expected, for sure. I'll definitely be purchasing these again. They're excellent with a cup of hot tea in the afternoon as a snack. and the "caloric hit" isn't terrible, either, if you can limit yourself to just 2-3 cookies.

Great flavor, nice texture -- good stuff!

title: For canned stuff, this is pretty good ....
text:
I'm not a fan of canned food as a rule -- I just prefer to make things "from scratch" whenever I can.

But there are times when I just don't have the luxury of being able to spend a lot of time in the kitchen, so I like to have a variety of canned and frozen "entree"-type dishes on hand for those times.

This is one of those items. You get quite a lot in a can, which, when I purchased these, cost around a buck and a quarter per can. The pasta is not too thick, and the Italian sausage flavor definitely comes through. The sauce isn't the best, but add some grated or shredded parmesan on top, and it's not bad at all. It can be heated in the microwave or on the stovetop. It's one of those things to have around for those snowy days when I can't get out to the store, or when the power is out (my stove is gas, and I also have a small gas grill that can be used on my covered deck or in the garage with the door open part way).

OK, this isn't for serving to company, and it's certainly not upper-division gourmet fare, but for a quick rather tasty supper in a pinch, it's a decent choice.

title: Buttery Golden Selects - not your mama's instant mashed potatoes!
text:
I've tried several different brands of instant mashed potatoes over the years, and found none of them to be that great. I mean, they were an OK substitute when I didn't want to go to the trouble to make homemade mashed potatoes, but they weren't very satisfying, either. I'd come to the conclusion that no one could make really good instant mashed potatoes -- something about the processing required, etc.

Well, I've changed my mind. These Butter Golden Selects are the BEST instant mashed potatoes I've tried, and they're actually better than a lot of homemade mashed potatoes I've had, too. Each packet makes two generous servings, and they are truly "instant" mashed potatoes. Just add the packet to 2 cups of boiling water, stir, cover, let stand for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and you'll have amazingly good slightly "chunky" mashed potatoes.

I've made homemade mashed potatoes with Yukon Gold potatoes -- that's what these taste like. Rich potato flavor with just a hint of butteriness. I love that there are some small "chunks" of potato in the mix -- really makes them "feel" more like homemade.

I'm totally sold on these. I may never make homemade mashed potatoes again. They're really that good!

title: Not the best I've ever had, but good ...
text:
I really like licorice allsorts, and I've had several different varieties. These aren't the best I've ever had, but they're definitely better than some brands, and I liked them quite a lot.

They were securely sealed, and mine arrived fresh and soft. Each of the different "sorts" was well represented -- in other words, there wasn't a preponderance of one shape/type. Mine looked just like the photo above.

Would I purchase again? Yes. The price and quality are good, and I like them enough that I'd like to keep them on hand, especially in the fall/winter seasons. For some reason, I think of this as a "fall/winter" type of candy. :-) Good stuff.

title: Same great taste, in a can!
text:
I've eaten at several Skyline restaurants in Ohio (several times at the one in Dayton), and am a HUGE fan of their chili. It is NOTHING like the traditional southwest/Texas chili con carne, except that it contains beef (in this case, very finely ground) and spices (including cinnamon in this case). If you order this expecting some slight variation on the traditional chili, you will likely be disappointed. This is a very different animal.

But if you're already familiar with and are a fan of the soupy wonderfulness of Cincinnati-style chili, then you'll like this.

My favorite way to eat this is a 3-way: angel hair pasta topped with chili and finely-shredded cheddar cheese. Half of a 15-oz can of Skyline chili (heated) plus 3.5 oz dry pasta (weigh it dry, then cook to al dente) topped with a generous handful of shredded cheese = a decent-sized serving, filling and delicious. When you consider that you can get 2 servings from one can, the cost seems more reasonable.

I was surprised that the taste of the canned product is almost identical to the flavor of the chili you get in the restaurant. I couldn't taste any of the usual "canned" undertones you get sometimes. Very impressed they were able to get it this "right."

Still a huge fan, and will likely keep this in my pantry as long as I can get it for a reasonable cost. It's a wonderful warm weekend lunch to have while watching football!

title: Grade B = BEST flavor!
text:
Don't be fooled into thinking that "grade A" is the "best" maple syrup. Grade A is lighter, more "refined," and so has much less maple flavor than Grade B.

This stuff is SERIOUSLY good maple syrup. It's darker, richer, not overly sweet, either -- just a great hearty pure maple flavor. I use it on pancakes and waffles, sure -- but also as a flavoring in icings, cheesecake, and in my barbecue sauces and marinades.

I purchase it by the quart, and keep it on hand always. Highland Sugarworks is top quality, and an excellent value. Highly recommended!

title: My favorite Snapple flavor ...
text:
Really tastes like fresh peaches! I've long been a fan of Snapple drinks, so I was thrilled to find a version that allows me to brew it up using my Keurig machine.

I use the "middle" cup size setting on my Keurig Platinum [[ASIN:B00AWLBE6G Keurig K75 Single-Cup Home-Brewing System with Water Filter Kit, Platinum]], and a 16-oz mug. Fill the mug with ice, pop it under the Keurig's spigot, and in 3 minutes, I have a tasty mug of peachy goodness.

I've also tried the raspberry, and didn't like it nearly as much as this. With this, you definitely taste the TEA along with the peach flavor; the raspberry just tastes like raspberry kool-aid.

Will keep this on hand as long as the weather stays warm up here in the Pacific NW. Good stuff.

title: Captiva Dark Chocolate Brownie cookies ...
text:
Super intense dark chocolate flavor, soft/chewy texture, lots of chocolate chips: a perfect combination for chocoholics like me! I really like these fudgy brownie-like cookies, and really TRY to limit myself to only 2 at a time. I repackage them into 2-cookie zip-loc bags and toss them into the freezer. That way, I'm not so tempted to eat the entire package in one sitting!

Really really good -- if you're a chocolate lover, you'll definitely like these.

title: My favorite Milano flavor ...
text:
The buttery crisp cookie, dark chocolate, and thin layer of intense orange sweetness -- it really doesn't get any better than this. My local supermarket doesn't carry these very often -- almost never, really -- so I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon. Mine arrived with almost no breakage (in 2 packages opened so far, only one cookie, neatly broken in half).

These are just wonderful -- perfect for those who like orange and chocolate together.

title: One of my favorites in a nice portion-controlled pack ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Milano cookies -- all flavors of them. The buttery-crisp wafers sandwiching a thin layer of dark chocolate -- what's not to like?

These are nice because they're packaged in 4-cookie packs. No, they're not terribly low-calorie (230 calories per pack), but at least this way I can't do *too* much damage! I just toss a pack into my bag when I'm off for the day, and I have a nice tasty snack for later.

Good stuff!

title: One of my all-time favorites ...
text:
I've been a huge fan of this cereal for years. It has just the right combination of chewy dates and raisins, crunchy pecans, and crispy flakes. It's not overly sweet, either -- one of my biggest complaints with most breakfast cereal. It IS fairly high in carbs, though, so bear that in mind. I usually have 3/4 C with either 6 oz non-fat yogurt or 1/2 C of skim milk to minimize the "points" total (I do Weight Watchers, and that combination is 7 points). It's fairly filling, though, so I don't need much to feel full.

It's not something I have every day, but it's a great treat.

title: If you like "regular" Hershey's Milk Chocolate bars ...
text:
... you'll probably like these.

The flavor is almost the same -- although I find these to taste a bit "sweeter" for some reason.

The texture is ... interesting. Not crunchy, not "soft"; imagine "whipping" melted chocolate so that the consistency is similar to whipped cream, then letting it harden into a chocolate bar shape.

It melts the same as regular Hershey's milk chocolate (bar, kiss, whatever). The best thing about these is that you feel like you're getting more per serving, since the bars are about 1/2" thick, but the same width and length as a regular bar. Granted, that extra space is just air, but the overall feeling is that you're getting a larger serving for the same dietary damage.

I liked these OK -- not sure I'll purchase again, but definitely wanted to try them at least once.

title: Finally! A *really* good whole grain pasta!
text:
I've tried other whole grain pastas, and found them to be lacking in ... something. Most were either too chewy or two mushy, some had a "gritty" texture, some had too much "nutty" flavor, etc.

Not this Barilla Whole grain Spaghetti! It's nearly perfect in every way. Tastes very much like "regular" spaghetti, same consistency, same "bite," not at all mushy or chewy -- I was able to get it o the perfect "al dente" texture on the first try.

Even better, a 2-oz (dry) serving of this has a whopping 6 grams of fiber. This helps to mitigate the 200 calories per serving (those on Weight Watchers know what I mean ... ).

I'm switching from my old brand of spaghetti to this one. It has everything I look for in spaghetti, plus it's higher fiber. What's not to love?

title: Good idea; execution needs some tweaking ...
text:
UPDATE: 11/2014
I decided to give the Creamy Parmesan Chicken flavor of this sauce a try, and I LOVE it! Such a difference. Rich flavor, nice and "cheesy." I've added a star to my original review (based on the Toasted Sesame with Garlic and Ginger flavor).

Creamy Parmesan Chicken works well with chicken or shrimp. My most recent assemblage: half a package of [[ASIN:B00338BV68 Barilla Tortellini Pasta, Cheese & Spinach, 12 Ounce (Pack of 4)]], about 6 oz of medium shrimp, peeled/deveined, sauteed in a little butter, and this creamy sauce. Simple, fast, and YUM!

Will definitely be ordering this one again and again!

------------------------------

I tried the I like the idea of this sauce line from Campbell's, but this toasted sesame sauce just didn't "wow" me.

It's OK, but a little bland for my taste, and a little too salty. I used it with chicken tenders, and served it over whole wheat pasta. It's easy to prepare (just brown the chicken, add the sauce, simmer), so that's a good thing. And it's definitely edible.

I may try some of the other flavors, to see if they're any better.

Bottom line: if you want a very quick/easy meal that tastes vaguely Asian, this might be just the ticket. But if you're willing to spend even 2-3 minutes more, you could whip up a much better tasting sauce on your own.

title: Not bad ... too salty ...
text:
OK, so this isn't anything near "gourmet"-quality food, but for a quick and easy side dish, it's not *too* bad. My biggest complaint was that it's just too salty for my taste.

I've used several of the Knorr Pasta Sides over the years (I really like the Fettuccine Alfredo mixed with chicken, peas, and/or mushrooms), so I was looking forward to some new flavors. This one is close, but just not quite to my taste. Others might really like it.

title: Great for portion control ...
text:
I can't help it -- I love a snack once in awhile, even though I'm really trying to diet. I've been reasonably successful, and the biggest thing for me is portion control.

I can toss one of these six-cookie packs in my purse as I head out, and I have a decent snack that will last me all day. One or two cookies mid-morning, another cookie at lunch, a couple more during an afternoon break. And I'm totally satisfied.

At the time I purchased these, (Mar 2013), it was a good deal, much less expensive than the local supermarket. Expiration date is sufficiently in the future that I shouldn't have to worry about the product expiring before i finish it.

title: Who knew?
text:
I have to admit I'm a bit of a food "snob." I wouldn't have dreamed of using dried/powdery "cheese in a jar," let alone serving it to company. I was visiting friends, and this is what they offered to go on a casual spaghetti-and-marinara lunch. Hey, I'll try anything once, but I certainly wasn't expecting much.

I was totally surprised! This stuff is seriously good! It has the flavor of decent-quality fresh parmesan, the kind you can get in the little tubs in the deli section of most grocery stores. OK, so it's not as good as freshly grated parmesan from a wedge, but it's also not as expensive, either.

I'm a convert -- this is some seriously good cheese, perfect for pizza, pasta, and salads.

title: The BEST chocolate mints ...
text:
These are almost impossible to find in other than tiny packages at exorbitant prices. Finding them on Amazon in bulk was a dream come true. Yes, the price is high -- but these really are the best chocolate mints out there. The exterior is dark chocolate, not too thick, but not too thin, either. The filling is a strong minty cream -- smooth and silky -- but not "drippy" or runny.

I discovered these about 10 yrs ago, and it's been a constant treasure hunt to try to find them in stores or online. I'm thrilled I can get them through Amazon. And I'll pay a little extra to get high quality. These are definitely worth it.

title: Great way to try different flavors ...
text:
I'm a recent Keurig convert, so I've been trying a lot of different "samplers" to try to find my favorite K-cups so I can order them in bulk.

This sampler was wonderful. I ended up liking ALL the flavors, and ordered boxes of each flavor. I didn't expect to like the blueberry-flavored coffee, but it was wonderful! It tastes like eating a blueberry muffin while drinking a cup of really good coffee. And I've always liked French vanilla and hazelnut. These Green Mountain coffees are excellent.

I've found that I need to brew a smaller cup to get full flavor from any K-cup -- around 8 oz -- instead of my usual larger 12-oz cup. Larger cup = light flavor; smaller cup = bolder flavor.

Anyway, I had no issues with the coffees I received. They were all excellent.

title: Not "gourmet food," but still good ...
text:
This is one of my "go to" convenience foods, for those days when I'm under the weather, or just too busy to want to spend much time figuring out what to make for dinner (I'm single, so ... ).

Anyway, I use a package of this, a 9-oz can of chicken white meat chunks, and about 2/3 C of frozen peas to make a filling, FAST, tasty meal that isn't *too* out of line. Once it's cooked, I put half of it aside for another meal, and eat the other half. Add a quick fresh salad, and I've got a really decent meal, plus another meal for the next day. Economical, fast, convenient.

I've tried some of the other "Pasta Sides" varieties, but the Alfredo is the best as far as I'm concerned. Price here is decent, too, but keep an eye on it: it can vary wildly sometimes.

title: A very respectable cup of cocoa ...
text:
This is a good alternative for when you need that up of cocoa, and you want to use your Keurig machine. I've found that you have to use one of the "smaller" cup settings or the cocoa will taste watered-down. I have a B70 Platinum Keurig, and I set it on the next-to-the-smallest cup setting -- that makes for a creamy full-flavored cup of cocoa.

The flavor isn't too sweet -- my problem with most instant cocoa products. Just a lot of good chocolate flavor. I drink this a couple of times a week.

title: Not the best, but super convenient ...
text:
I like this variety pack -- it has the flavors I like best, and makes it really easy to prepare a hot bowl of oatmeal in a hurry.

I've been preparing and eating "instant" oatmeal for years, usually boiling the water in an electric kettle, and measuring it into a bowl with the dry powdered oats, not using the microwave at all.

With these, though, it makes it more convenient to cook these up in the microwave. Each packet is waterproof, and contains a measuring line, so all you have to do is empty the packet of dry oats into a bowl, fill the packet with water to the line, empty that into the bowl, and microwave. That's it.

My favorite flavor is the apple, but all of these are tasty. I actually prefer the Irish alternative to this (McCann's, also available on Amazon), but for the variety and the price, this is a very good deal.

title: Kettle corn flavor in chip form ...
text:
I'm a huge fan of Popchips, and regularly purchase them on Amazon (the barbecue and sour cream/onion flavors are my favorites), so I jumped at the chance to try these "Kettle Corn" chips.

They're like eating kettle corn, but without the hulls and tooth-shattering kernels. The consistency is like a light slightly puffy corn chip, with a slightly salty and sweet flavor essence.

I'm another Weight Watchers follower, and these are quite "points friendly." I open a bag, and parcel out the servings into snack-size zip-lock bags, ready for an evening snack. Makes it easier to control portion size that way.

These are definitely going on my "purchase regularly" list -- a nice alternative snack!

title: My favorite sea salt ...
text:
I don't use a lot of salt -- so when I do, I want it to be good stuff.

This is super. I don't have to use a lot to get the flavor I want -- just a pinch or two. The flakes are easy to "crush" and that seems to release the flavor.

Amazon's price for this is super, too. The 8.5-oz box lasts a long time for me. Definitely my first choice in salt.

title: Much better than the white rice variety ...
text:
I've been using the regular white rice version of this for about a year, and decided to try the brown rice version.

What a difference! This is SO much better! The flavor is great, and it cooks up nicely in the microwave. I use it for my stir fry lunches at home. I've found that, with my microwave (a GE built-in model), I microwave on high for 1 minute 20 seconds to keep it from drying/clumping too much. Also, I dump it into a serving dish, and then "fluff" it with a fork to get it ready to eat. Still, it takes only a few seconds, and I have a really tasty meal.

I now have this on "subscribe and save" so that I won't run out.

title: So far, my favorite non-flavored variety ...
text:
I was able to try this in a sampler that I purchased shortly after I got my Keurig. I really liked it: not bitter, not charred/burnt tasting, just a nice medium-roast full-flavored coffee.

I have a couple of other non-flavored k-cups that I like, but I go to this one most often. Very happy with this.

title: Good for those cutting down on caffeine ...
text:
I recently purchased a Keurig, and I've been experimenting with different k-cup varieties. One of the samplers I purchased included this Green Mountain Half Caff variety. Since I'm trying to limit caffeine consumption, it seemed like a match made in heaven.

I liked it better than I thought I would. I'm not fond of overly-roasted brews -- they seem to have a charred/burnt flavor that I really dislike. This one is pretty smooth, with only a tiny hint of bitterness. It's nothing that a splash of creamer can't smooth over.

I usually drink "high-octane" coffee in the morning, switch to this around noon, and end the day with decaf varieties. Seems to work.

I purchased the 50-count package, so this will last 4-6 weeks for me (1-2 cups per day). I'm happy with it.

title: I did NOT expect to like this ...
text:
... but I did! A k-cup of this showed up in a "sampler" pack I purchased. I honestly didn't expect to like it at all. I'm not usually wild about flavored coffees anyway, and the idea of coffee and blueberry flavor just didn't sound all that appealing.

I couldn't have been more wrong! This stuff is really REALLY good. Imagine taking a sip of coffee while eating a blueberry muffin. The blueberry flavor isn't overpowering -- just a hit of it, really -- combined with just a hint of vanilla flavor. The coffee itself is smooth, non-bitter, and full-flavored.

I liked it well enough to purchased the 24-count package. Very nice surprise, indeed!

title: Jamaica Me Crazy -- truly!
text:
One of my favorite K-cup flavors -- and I'm not usually a huge fan of flavored coffees.

This one has just a hint of rum flavor, along with a hint of coconut (very mild). The base is a medium roast Arabica coffee, with none of the bitter/charred taste I find in too many other coffees. Very nice, indeed!

I'm totally sold on this stuff -- it will definitely hold up well when summer comes (iced coffee!).

title: One of my favorites ...
text:
Found this in a "sampler" pack I purchased after I got my Keurig machine for Christmas, and decided I liked it enough to purchase an 18-count pack.

I'm not overly fond of the "dark" roast coffees -- they always taste burnt to me. This is a very nice non-bitter coffee with just a subtle hint of Kahlua flavor. The coffee has a rich full taste -- a medium roast flavor. And it seems to be perfectly balanced with the Kahlua flavor - neither overpowers the other.

I've discovered several "favorites" in that sampler pack that I'll be keeping on hand -- mostly non-flavored coffees. This will be one of the few flavored coffees I'll keep around. Very nice!

title: Interesting taste and texture ...
text:
I love the "potato"-chip variety of Popchips, so I jumped at the chance to try these tortilla chips. I chose the "nacho cheese" flavor (I'm a sucker for Doritos brand).

The cheese flavor could be a little stronger, but overall not bad. The texture is unlike anything I've had before -- not quite like the Popchips I'm used to, not like tortilla chips, either. Crunchy, yes. "Light" is the best description I can come up with. They're relatively low-calorie (120 per 1 oz. serving; 3 points if you're using Weight Watchers), and the 1-oz bag is filling.

I'm intrigued enough to try another flavor of these, but probably won't get more of the nacho flavor. They're OK -- nothing really wrong with them -- but I need a bit more flavor, more "oomph."

title: Tasty, but high in calories and carbs ...
text:
I was given the opportunity to try one of these Quaker Real Medleys, and chose the Cherry Pistachio.

Preparation was according to the directions -- added boiling water to the line inside the carton, stir, cover, let sit for 3 minutes, then stir again.

The result was quite good: good flavor, good combination of tart/sweet cherries and crunchy almonds and pistachios, nice texture. A bit on the sweet side, but overall not too bad.

However, if you are on a low-carb diet -- or any kind of weight-loss program -- this probably isn't the best choice for breakfast. It weighs in at 290 calories, 49g carbs (!), 8g fat, mitigated by 9g protein. On Weight Watchers, this will cost you 8 points. I can get a more filling breakfast with Special K Red Berries and 2% milk for 5 points (using skim milk brings that down to 4 points). Add some scrambled egg substitute (like egg beaters), 1/3 C with a little chopped bell pepper for 1 additional point, and you have a decent balanced start to the day for 5-6 points total. If you're in a hurry or looking for something similar for breakfast at the office, for example, there are other oatmeal products, including others by Quaker, that might work better for you

Obviously, with products like this, "likability" is a matter of individual taste. If you're looking for something quick, easy, shelf-stable, and tasty, and you don't particularly care about calories/carbs/etc., this might be a good choice. But if you're on a serious weight-loss program, you might want to look elsewhere.

title: Excellent balance ...
text:
I've been making my own pizza sauce, but it's a major hassle, and I just can't get it quite right (usually, it leaves the crust soggy).

I'd tried other "canned"/bottled sauces from the local supermarket, and found them far too sweet for my taste. One "high end" sauce was far too acid. I'd almost give up finding a sauce with a decent balance of sweet to acid.

Stumbled on this one on Amazon, read the reviews, and it seemed that most folks really liked it. Decided to give it a try, and BOY am I impressed!

This is the one for me. Perfect balance of sweetness and acid, with just a slight hint of heat/spiciness. Nice robust tomato flavor that is a perfect compliment to my sausage, peppers, olives, and mushrooms. A little part-skim mozzarella and I've got a very nice pizza. And no soggy crust!

If you like a really sweet sauce, this is NOT the sauce for you. But if you want a sauce with a good balance, a tiny hint of heat, and strong tomato-y flavor, this just might work for you.

title: Good price, good flavor ...
text:
Certain members of my family are mint+chocolate addicts. Peppermint bark, filled peppermint chocolates, chocolate mint cookies, anything that combines mint with chocolate.

This year, we got both the dark and milk chocolate varieties of these Ghirardelli peppermint bark squares. We liked both flavors, probably preferred the dark chocolate, but found both to have a nice balance of mint to chocolate. The crushed peppermint candy bits in the white chocolate top add a nice crunch, too.

The price here is very good, too. Definitely a keeper!

title: Excellent quality ...
text:
We've enjoyed a variety of these Hershey's Pot of Gold chocolates, but our favorite is this one.

They're not too big, not too sweet, either. There's a perfect balance of chocolate to caramel to nuts, too. Other similar products tend to have too much of one component or another -- usually too much chocolate -- so we try to purchase these when we can find them.

Amazon's price is not bad -- these tend to run six or seven dollars per box IF I can find them at all locally.

I may buy a few boxes to tuck away in the freezer to have on hand for later in the year.

title: Great chocolate, a tad pricey ...
text:
We're all big fans of dark chocolate in this family, and these special dark chocolate kisses are rarely available in our local stores. Finding them on Amazon was a real treat! They are a bit pricy here, but not terrible, and since this is the only place I can find them, I'm willing to bite the bullet.

Taste is wonderful. We had them on Christmas day after dinner with a bottle of good port -- heaven!

title: Excellent product, good price ...
text:
Purchased these for the family to go with our usual assortment of holiday goodies. We usually get these every year, and love the taste and texture of the chocolate. Amazon's price is very good, too.

We'll continue this tradition as long as we can get a great deal from Amazon. We also like the white chocolate and dark chocolate varieties, but these milk chocolate ones are our favorite flavor.

title: One of my guilty pleasures ...
text:
I'm a sucker for M&Ms, especially the peanut variety.

This is a great deal: two BIG bags of candy, over 2.5 lbs each (2 lbs 10 oz, to be precise). The product was fresh with an expiration date well beyond my usual eating pattern with these. Shared these with friends over the holidays -- all my friends love them, too.

Will definitely order again (but I'll probably re-"package" them into single-serving snack bags, to prevent over-indulging!)

title: Nice addition to our holiday snack table ...
text: Nice selection of Ghirardelli chocolate squares. We also got the peppermint bark squares. I'm a long-time fan of these filled squares, especially the mint and caramel ones.  Price was decent for the package, too. These are difficult to find in our local stores, so being able to order them on Amaon is great!

title: One of my favorites ....
text:
A crunchy cookie topped with caramel, all covered in milk chocolate. What's not to like? These make a nice snack in the afternoon with a cup of tea. They're more like a cookie than a candy bar (to me, anyway).

Amazon's price is pretty good, too, for 36 "regular sized" packages (2 cookie bars per package). Will order again, for sure.

title: Really yummy!
text:
Ghirardelli Chocolate produces consistently high-quality chocolate products, and these dark chocolate peppermint bark squares are no exception.

I LOVE peppermint bark, and I love dark chocolate, so this pairing is a match made in heaven. These delightful squares are just the right size for an afternoon snack with a cup of tea (or a glass of wine!). I like having them on hand for a quick chocolate "hit" during the holidays, or a small reward for finishing my holiday shopping early. (I tend to procrastinate ... )

The price here is OK -- not great, but getting them delivered to my home (or my relatives/friends) is worth a few cents more per package.

title: Better than I expected ...
text:
Maybe I'm just not that picky -- I mean, how could a microwaved brownie taste anything but revolting? But these are actually pretty good. Better than pretty good -- VERY good!

You might have to play a bit with the cook time to get it *just* right. But even if it's a tad off, it will still be edible.

I top mine with a scoop of low-fat vanilla yogurt, then use the enclosed packet of hot fudge sauce to make a hot fudge brownie sundae. I love it that there are no left overs, and the portion size is generous but not a total diet-killer.

Definitely keeping these on hand!

title: Sorry, not impressed ....
text:
These are OK, but not great. Not nearly as good as others I've had. The peanuts taste rather stale -- not much flavor. And the coating? Mostly sugar, no "butter" flavor at all. (Also not much salt -- virtually none.) Well over half the peanuts have no coating at all.

I really wanted to like these, but I'll be looking elsewhere for my holiday snacks.

title: Very tasty trail mix ...
text:
An excellent mix of nuts and dried fruit: lots of tender raisins (both dark and golden), date chunks, big walnut pieces, peanuts, and yogurt-covered almonds.

The raisins are very large, not hard dried out bits that show up in other trail mixes. There is just the right amount of peanuts -- some mixes have an overabundance of them, but not this one. The balance is really nice.

Definitely a keeper.

title: Delicious!
text:
I've been looking for a good cinnamon flavored coffee since last fall, when I had some "snickerdoodle"-flavored coffee at my brother's house. His came from a friend who roasted and flavored his own beans, so it wasn't really available. So, the search was on.

This is it.

I'm a huge fan of Coffee Masters anyway, so I was thrilled to find that they carry a couple of cinnamon-flavored coffees. I haven't tried the other one [[ASIN:B000I6O462 Coffee Masters Flavored Coffee, Cinnamon Nut Swirl, Whole Bean, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)]] , but I don't think I need to, now that I've found this.

The cinnamon flavor is just right -- not too strong, but assertive enough that you can tell it's there. There's just a hint of a slight vanilla taste, too, which I enhanced by adding some French vanilla creamer. A couple of packets of sweetener (we're talking an 18-oz mug here!), and the total package tastes like a liquid version of those wonderful cinnamon treats you can find at the mall (starts with "cinna-" and ends with "-bon").

One thing I like about all the Coffee Masters flavors I've tried is the lack of a bitter "charred" taste. What you get is a robust roasted flavor with no "burnt" overtones. We're talking super tasty coffee! Exactly what I was looking for!

Edited 3/22/13: I'm now using this with my Keurig machine using one of the [[ASIN:B0051SU0OW Ekobrew Cup, Refillable Cup for Keurig K-cup Brewers, Brown, 1-Count]], and I'm still loving this coffee. I find I need to grind it just a bit finer to get the flavor/strength I want. Wonderful stuff!

title: Packs a punch!
text:
I first had this in a litte sandwich shop in Laramie, WY, where all the sandwiches were named after Harry Potter characters. Loved it, asked for info, came home to the Pacific NW, and found it here on Amazon. Woohoo!

It has a bright flavor with a little heat, but not overpowering. I love it on turkey sandwiches, sure, but it really turns my deviled eggs into real standouts, flavor wise.

Glad I found it on Amazon!

title: The BEST!!!
text: This is a slightly darker maple syrup, and the flavor is fantastic! Seriously, once you've tried this stuff, you'll never want to go back to the artificially-flavored drek ("maple-flavored" syrup).  Yes, it's more expensive, but the taste is worth it. I use it on pancakes and waffles, and brush a little on chunks of sweet potato before roasting them to bring out the sweetness and flavor. Excellent product, good price.

title: An easy meal ...
text: This is VERY easy to prepare, and relatively fast. Seasonings are about perfect, too. I add about 6-7 oz of smoked sausage or andouille sausage to make it a bit more substantial. Add a salad, and you have a meal. I've tried several different brands of red beans and rice "mixes," and this is by far the best.

title: Best canned tomatoes I've had ...
text:
These are wonderful, and make the best marinara sauce! They are bursting with intense tomato flavor withou being too acidic or salty.

I use them all the time in chili, soups, baked pasta dishes -- anything that calls for canned tomatoes. The flavor really is worth the extra cost.

title: Love this oil ...
text:
I use this for everything now. With its high smoke point, it's perfect for stir frying. The light taste means you taste the food, not the oil. Amazon's price for this is fantastic compared to my local supermarket.

Will definitely keep this on hand.

title: I really liked this ...
text:
I've been using KOI butter chicken paste packets for awhile, so decided to give this a try.

I really liked it. I didn't find it too salty (and I'm usually pretty sensitive to salt), and the flavor was nice -- spicy withou being too hot.

I made it with boneless skinless chicken thighs, and added a sweet Walla Walla onion along with the chicken, served over saffron rice.

Butter Chicken from KOI is still my favorite, but this is a close second.

title: Another winner from the House of Tsang ...
text:
I got hooked on the House of Tsang Stir Fry Sauce years ago, and was happy to find it here on Amazon. I wanted an alternative, and decided to try their Korean Teriyaki sauce.

This is a very good teriyaki sauce. Not too salty, not too sweet, nice flavor that doesn't overpower the veggies and meat or chicken.

I can't find this brand near where I live, so finding it here on Amazon has even a real treat.

title: Decent flavor ...
text: I tried the "Sea Salt" variety crinkle-cut chips and they were pretty good. A little thicker than I'd anticipated, so harder to eat. But the flavor was good, with just the right amount of salt. Not sure I'll purchase this variety again, but I might try one of the others.

title: My new favorite pasta sauce ...
text:
This stuff is amazing! Just the right blend of mellow roasted garlic and perky tomatoes. It's not too sweet (my chief complaint with most packaged sauces), but also not too acidic. While it's great on its own served over ziti, penne, or linguine, it also players well with others: meatballs, add-ins like peppers, mushrooms, sausage, in casseroles, even as a pizza sauce.

I now have this on subscribe and save. I use it that much.

title: I really liked these ...
text: I'm just hoping Amazon gets these back again this year for the holidays. I found them perfectly delightful, especially with a cup of tea in the evening. The shortbread crust was buttery, and the filling was just about perfect. I bought them several times last holiday season, and every box was wonderful.

title: Almost impossible to find in stores ..
text:
... and when I do find it, the price is nearly double what I can get it for here on Amazon. I have it on "subscribe & save," so I save even more.

I have this once or twice a week for breakfast and occasionally for a snack. With only 140 cal per pack, it's a decent choice -- I usually have 2 packets for breakfast, and it's more filling than cereal with milk.

One of my two favorite flavors (the other is [[ASIN:B001M09BOS Quaker Instant Oatmeal Raisin, Date & Walnut, 10-Count Boxes (Pack of 4)]]). Really yummy stuff!

title: My favorite decaf ...
text:
OK, so I'm under Dr.'s orders to cut down on caffeine, so I've been looking for a good decaf that would match my favorite "high octane" coffee.

I think I've found it.

Although this stuff is a bit pricey, it delivers a LOT in terms of rich flavor and smoothness. Best of all, it doesn't have that burnt bitter aftertaste that too many popular coffees have. It offers a hearty robust flavor, and that's exactly what I want from a coffee.

Will keep this on hand for sure!

title: Good flavor
text: These are good, but a bit skimpy on the candy coating. The ones I get at my supermarket have a thicker layer of "yogurt" coating, but the store doesn't carry them that often. So I keep these on hand just in case the urge strikes and my local store is out.  I love the combination of crispy/salty pretzel with creamy yogurt-flavored candy coating.

title: My favorite Crystal Light flavor ...
text:
Nice tart lemonade flavor with just a hint of raspberry. I don't care for overly sweet drink mixes, and this one is just about perfect. I like it better than Crystal Light's lemonade or pink lemonade.

My local store carries this, but at nearly double the cost here on Amazon (although Amazon's prices vary widely from seller to seller). I need to drink more water, and this helps.

title: Super flavor ...
text:
The BEST frozen pops I've found, and I think I've tried all that Amazon has to offer plus all the brands carried in my local supermarket.

The flavors are bright and refreshing, not overly sweet, and totally recognizable. Too many pops end up tasting like frozen sugar water, with little or no fruit flavor. Not these. The lemon tastes like frozen lemonade; the strawberry tastes like frozen strawberries without the seeds.

I've looked for these locally, but no one has them. Glad they're offered on Amazon, even if they are pricey.

title: My favorite of all the Bear Naked flavors ...
text:
I've tried a few of the Bear Naked granola flavors, and this one is my favorite by far. It has the right amount of crunch and sweetness, is lower in fat and sugar, and has a good amount of fruit chunks. I mix about 1/3 cup of this granola with 8 oz. of strawberry or raspberry fat free yogurt for a yummy filling quick breakfast.

Amazon's price is excellent, especially if you opt for Subscribe and Save. Good product at a good price; what more could you want?

title: Nice peachy flavor ...
text: I love this stuff. I like anything peach -- ice cream, yogurt, pie -- and this has a really nice peach flavor. It's hard to find this variety in my local stores, and when I can find it, it's nearly as expensive as it is here at Amazon ($4.59 per box locally vs $4.62 from the least expensive seller here, including shipping), so I don't feel too guilty ordering here.  I mix up a quart at a time, and usually go through two of those per day. Very yummy!

title: Works much better dry as a snack
text:
OK, I'm an unrepentant chocoholic. I admit it. So I jumped at the opportunity to try a new chocolate cereal.

I tried this both with and without milk. With milk, it was just OK: not great, disintegrates rapidly, chocolate taste is good, but overall nothing that special.

Without milk, however, it was really nice: crispy/crunchy, great chocolate flavor. Very reminiscent of chocolate-coated graham crackers, but in miniature bite-sized form, and with the chocolate on the inside. Definitely a chocolate winner in my book.

title: Tasty snack ...
text:
These are pretty good. They're not as crispy as potato chips, but they have a decent sour cream and onion taste. Like someone else mentioned, these are VERY similar to Popchips, just a bit thinner.

The calorie count is low: 27 chips = 110 calories, and there are only about 3 servings per box, so even if you can't stop yourself, you're looking at only 330 calories or so for the entire box. Obviously, you wouldn't want to down an entire box every day, but if you do, the damage isn't *too* bad.

I'll probably purchase them once in awhile as an alternative snack.

title: Excellent basic cracker ....
text: If you want the topping to shine, this is the cracker you need.  I love these with flavored or layered toppings: cranberry goat cheese, garlic cream cheese topped with smoked trout; even basic westphalian ham and emmenthaler cheese.  These crackers don't add any distracting flavors, but maintain their crisp texture.  Really excellent as a choice on a cheese board.

title: Great shelf staple ...
text: I used this a lot for white bean / chicken chili, chicken salad, fettuccine alfredo with chicken and mushrooms.  The flavor is very good, it's low-fat, the sodium count isn't outrageous, and it works well with a lot of things.  Yes, I prefer using fresh chicken breast, but when I don't have any on hand or can't get to the store, this works very well.

title: A taste of home ...
text:
I grew up in the midwest, so Sauce Arturo was one of the "special" items I remember from my mother's kitchen. She used it for her version of goulash (a.k.a. Johnny Marzetti), and also for sloppy joes. I hadn't seen it in years, but saw listed in a recipe for Johnny Marzetti and decided to see if Amazon might have it.

And here it is! It's a tomato sauce with some special seasonings, including just a tiny bit of cinnamon. It adds a subtle exotic flavor to dishes that you just won't get with "plain" tomato sauce.

I've used it for that Johnny Marzetti recipe, of course, and also for a nice chicken dish that I threw together one night: 4 boneless/skinless chicken breasts, 3 cans of Sauce Arturo, 1/4 C sliced ripe olives, 1 1/2 C sliced pepper strips (I use frozen green/yellow/red bell pepper strips), and 1 small sweet onion (e.g. walla walla), sliced. Brown chicken, place in baking dish, top with peppers, onions, olives, and top with the sauce, spreading to coat evenly. Cover and bake for 45 minutes to 1 hr, or until chicken is cooked through. Serve with rice or pasta. Good stuff!

title: Good drink for peach lovers....
text:
This is the best of the Ocean Spray sugar free flavors, in my opinion. Of course, one of my all-time favorite flavors is peach, so this fits the bill perfectly. I usually make up a 32-oz Nalgene bottle of the stuff, using two of the sticks, and try to drink 2 or 3 bottles a day. It's not overly sweet, and has a strong peach flavor that doesn't taste chemical or phony.

Amazon's price varies, so keep an eye on it. So far, it has stayed a little below what I would pay in the local market for this, and since I can have it delivered (and with Amazon Prime, I can get it fast), it's worth it to me to purchase in bulk like this.

title: Nice assortment of flavors ...
text:
I purchased this tub as a way to try out some new Crystal Light flavors. I was told I had to cut back on caffeine, and I don't need the calories associated with sugared soft drinks. These work well, for the most part.

My favorite flavor is the raspberry lemonade. I like the hint of raspberry flavor, and find that I can drink quite a lot of it during the day without getting bored. I mix up a 32-oz water bottle of the stuff, using 2 packets of mix. This seems to work well, especially when i down 2-3 bottles of the stuff per day.

I also like the lemonade flavor, and the cherry pomegranate. The strawberry - not so much. It's their "energy" formulation, so it contains some "extras" that I think add to a slightly bitter "sharp" flavor - and it contains caffeine, which sort of defeats the purpose of my drinking Crystal Light in the first place.

I've managed to lose 23 pounds in a little over 3 months using this along with cooking everything from "scratch" - no processed foods, lots of fruits and veggies, fresh meats and fish. I do understand the controversy about aspartame, but given the choice between carrying WAY too much weight and consuming something that may or may not kill me eventually, I'll choose the latter. Plain water just doesn't do it for me, and this stuff IS tasty.

title: My all-'round favorite stir fry sauce ...
text:
I love stir fries! It's easy to put together a meal for one in a hurry, and you know what you're getting. I discovered the House of Tsang stir fry sauces several years ago, and got hooked on them. Then I moved, and the local stores around here don't carry this brand.

So, I was *thrilled* to find it here on Amazon. I've been using some other brands, but they just don't have the depth of flavor I get from House of Tsang. The other brands are more expensive, too: up to $8.00/bottle at the store.

This is a basic stir-fry sauce: not spicy, but with that slightly sweet / soy sauce / nutty sesame flavor, with hints of ginger and garlic. I've used it so far with beef, chicken, shrimp, and pork, and it works well with all of those. I usually use either frozen stir-fry veggies, or get a "stir fry mix" from the fresh produce aisle. My tools of choice are a small flat-bottom wok on an induction burner. In about 10 minutes, I have a meal.

Good stuff, this.

title: A blast from the past ...
text:
I used to get one of these each week before Youth Symphony rehearsal. Dad would drop me off early on his way to work, and I'd hit the vending machine for my pre-rehearsal Cherry Mash nugget of deliciousness. We're talking 1963-1965, Kansas City, MO.

I'd given up ever finding these again - then spotted them here. They're just as I remembered! Good price, too. If you like a creamy bright pink cherry filling combined with a thick nutty chocolate coating, you'll LOVE these.

title: One of my all-time favorite cereals ...
text:
I just put this on subscribe and save. It has been one of my all-time favorites for a lot of years, so I was thrilled to find it on Amazon and at a good price, especially with the "subscribe and save" option. Several folks have commented on the price; remember that there are a number of vendors selling this product on Amazon, and many of them do overcharge, both for the item as well as the shipping. Amazon's own price is EXCELLENT compared to my local supermarket.

This cereal is not too sweet, and quite filling. I'm on Weight Watchers, and the points value is quite reasonable. The added raisins, dates, and nuts contribute to the texture, which I find very satisfying (a little chewy, a little crunch ... ).

Really good stuff!

title: Not bad; not terrific ...
text:
I was interested in trying this low-acid coffee, as I sometimes have difficulties with "regular" coffee. Brewed up a pot in my drip coffee maker, and gave it a try.

It was OK -- decent flavor, comparable to my local grocer's "upscale" store brand. I tried a cup black, and a second cup like I usually drnk my coffee, with "pink packet" sweetener and a splash of creamer. I could tell it was low acid -- the negative effects I sometimes get didn't happen; not even a hint of stomach upset.

But I'm not sure it's good enough to warrant the much higher cost. I wanted to be wowed by it, and I wasn't. Your mileage may vary, of course, as coffee is a rather personal taste.

title: Nice flavor, a little dry ...
text: I liked these -- they're not too sweet, and you get lots of the graham flavor.  They're a bit on the dry side, probably because they're very low fat, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.  I'm not a huge graham cracker fan anyway, but these were quite nice.  I usually eat them with Nutella spread -- and these provide a great foundation for that particular treat.  They're a bit on the pricey side compared to other brands, but the extra health benefits and "nuttier" taste might be worth the extra expense to you.

title: Good - not very "spicy" ...
text: I liked this just fine.  The name is a little misleading:  It's really not very spicy at all.  It does have a lot of flavor, however.  I've tried it on sandwiches (very good), and on tacos of various types.  I liked it best on fish tacos, with shredded lettuce and chopped tomato.  It also works well on chicken tacos and burritos.  I also liked it as a salad dressing for a "southwestern" salad (romaine, corn/black bean salsa, chopped tomato, a few ounces of chopped cooked chicken, mixed colby/jack cheese (or pepper jack), a few sliced black olives, and a couple of tablespoons of this sauce.  Amazon's price is quite good compared to my local grocery stores.

title: I LOVE KitKat bars ...
text: ... and these "snack size" bars are perfect.  I can pack a few of them with me without taking up a lot of space, OR worrying *too* much about my perpetual diet.  I love the crispy wafers layered with smooth and creamy milk chocolate.  My favorite candy bar, bar none!

title: My favorite snack crackers ...
text:
I like these better than any chips around -- high-potency cheese flavor, crispy -- what's not to like? I have to package these up in "single-serve" packs or I WILL eat half a box at one sitting!

Mine arrived in great shape, too -- no more "crumbs" than I would expect to find in a box purchased at the supermarket. And these are MUCH cheaper than the local stores, too.

title: My FAVORITE shortbread cookies ...
text: These are almost too good: buttery, not *too* sweet, perfect with almost any beverage.  Like another reviewer, I often "fancy these up" by dipping in melted semisweet chocolate and dusting with chopped nuts (pecans, hazelnuts, etc.) or crushed Heath bars.  I've made shortbread myself, but why go to the trouble when I can get excellent ready-made?  Really exceptional stuff ...

title: Good basic pie cherries ...
text: One of my favorite pies is cherry, and my mother always made hers using canned sour pie cherries.  These cherries, from the same folks who bring you that yummy applesauce, bring back memories of those pies.  So far, I've used them for cobbler, cherry crisp, and, yes, cherry pie, always with good results.  I just add a little sugar (a couple of tablespoons, maybe as much as 1/4 C) and corn starch (my thickener of choice), then build the rest of the dessert around.  The flavor is intense and bright -- just what I wanted.

title: Chocoholics- this is for you!
text: Excellent snack for those of us who prefer our snacks chocolate.  It's not over-the-top in terms of calories, either.  Think of chex cereals and mini-pretzels coated with semi-sweet chocolate -- just a thin coat, mind you -- so it's not overpowering.  Very satisfying, indeed!

title: Super tasty!
text:
What could be better? Caramel corn drizzled with chocolate. YUM!

This comes packaged in individual servings each totaling 130 calories. If you can stick to just ONE pouch, you have more self control than I do. It satisfies my cravings for crunchy sweet and chocolate all in one snack.

Now, if I can just train myself to eat only one package!

title: The BEST marinara sauce ...
text:
I got a jar of this in a 4-pack "sampler" from Amazon [[ASIN:B000OCO76M Scarpetta Pasta Lovers Gift Box, 19.8-Ounce Jar (Pack of 4)]] , and finally got around to trying it this weekend. I used it with some home-made meatballs over linguine, and it was marvelous. (I make my own meatballs using ground turkey, spices, breadcrumbs, and egg, then bake them on a cookie sheet and freeze 'em in bags.)

WOW! It's packed with intense tomato flavor, with just a hint of garlic. I think I've tried 'em all, and this was so much better than any others (including some VERY expensive gourmet varieties). Nothing detracts from the tomato flavor. I find a lot of jarred marinara sauces to be too sweet, and that is definitely not the case here. You get that slight acidic "bite" from the tomatoes, and that subtle garlic flavor. Heaven!

I liked this so much I just set it up on a "subscribe and save" purchase. I'm planning to use it for lasagne, baked ziti, even pizza sauce. It's that good.

title: Nostalgia on a plate ...
text:
I grew up eating buckwheat pancakes about once a week for breakfast in the midwest. Until I was in my 20s, I didn't know there was any other kind!

This mix is VERY close to what I remember eating as a child. If you've never had buckwheat before, you're in for a treat. It has a distinctive "nutty" flavor that can't be duplicated. This mix is easy to prepare, and the pancakes cook up fluffy, although a bit more dense than buttermilk pancakes, and with plenty of good buckwheat flavor. I enjoy them with real maple syrup (which I also purchase here on Amazon), or with the wonderful huckleberry syrup I can now get here in the Pacific NW.

Bob's Red Mill products are available locally in grocery stores, but at much higher cost than Amazon. I plan to keep some of this mix around so i can treat friends and family to a these hearty tasty pancakes.

title: REALLY good -- almost addictive!
text:
These are very very good -- comparable to the ones sold in my local upscale supermarket, and less expensive per pound, too. I have to be careful and "parcel" these out into individual snack bags or I'll eat way too many! They have a nice vanilla yogurt flavor, with just enough crunch and salt from the pretzel.

The expiration date is far enough out (I purchased these in mid-August 2010; the expiration date is the end of June 2011) that I'll be able to finish these off before they expire, sometimes a concern when I purchase in quantity like this.

I'm very pleased with these, and I'll likely purchase them again.

title: Nice flavor ...
text: This is a very nice flavorful Columbian -- very smooth, no bitterness.  It's among the four or five coffees I try to have on hand, just for variety.  I like that it comes in a one-pound bag, instead of the usual 12-oz bags for other coffees, making it more economical, too.

title: Good with shrimp or chicken ...
text:
This is a very easy, tasty meal for two. It has a significant amount of "heat," so if you don't like "spicy," you probably want to skip this. For me, it was just about perfect.

It comes with rice noodles and stir-fry sauce. You add your own veggies and meat. My favorite combination is shrimp, carrots, red bell pepper, and either snow peas or just some frozen green peas (OK, I KNOW that's not "authentically" Asian, but it tastes good ... ). You soak the noodles for 3 minutes in hot water, stir fry the protein (shrimp, chicken, whatever) in the sauce for a minute or two, add the veggies and stir for another minute or two, then mix in the softened noodles. Divide onto two plates, and you're ready to eat.

This isn't too salty -- some Asian sauces taste like soy sauce with a hint of other flavorings, but not this one. It's full of citrus flavor (mostly orange), slightly sweet, with that punch of heat.

Will buy again!

title: Good for a snack --
text:
I can't really compare these to other similar products (Slim Jim,etc.), as I had never had jerky-type snacks before I got these. I decided to take a long road trip (4500 miles round trip), and I have a tendency to get drowsy if I don't get enough protein. I decided to carry these plus some string cheese in the car to tide me over between meal stops.

I really like these. The flavor is good, the texture is fine, and the "damage" from a diet standpoint is minimal (these are 60 cal apiece, based on the Jack Links site). They're not too salty, either. Having them on the trip from Bellingham, WA to St. Louis, MO and back was a huge help. One or two of these provided just the right amount of tasty protein. The size and packaging is handy, too, and easy to open when driving.

I now keep them on hand for when I need a little pick-me-up.

title: WOW!  Really good stuff here ...
text:
My quest for the perfect coffee may be over: this is some seriously good coffee. It's smooth -- no harshness or bitter "charred" aftertaste -- and full of rich coffee flavor. I've been trying various brands and varieties of coffee for the past few years, and have landed on a few that suit my taste. I don't like the burned flavor that too many coffees have (is it over-roasting?), or the rough acidic taste, so that rules out a lot of more popular brands (sorry, Starbucks).

Obviously, everyone's taste is different, but if you're like me, and just want a full-flavored coffee without the bitterness, you might want to give this a try. The price is very good, too.

title: My favorite Izze flavor ...
text:
So far, I've tried the Pomegranate and the Blackberry. Both are good, but I like the Pomegranate the best.

This stuff is best served chilled or over ice. Straight out of the can at room temperature, it has a sort of bitter/metallic after-taste but chilling seems to eliminate it. I like the fact that it has no added sugar, preservatives, or caffeine. It's a refreshing change from the usual carbonated stuff.

title: Absolutely delicious!
text:
Wow! Who knew you could get this kind of quality from a sauce in a jar?? This stuff works with just about anything: I've used it with shrimp, chicken, homemade meatballs, artichokes and mushrooms -- the flavor just blends beautifully. If you've never had "vodka sauce" before, it's sort of like a creamy marinara sauce with a splash of vodka (but you won't taste any alcohol -- it all burns off). This has chunks of tomato in it for some texture, too. I liked it so much I've set up a subscription, and will definitely be trying more of the Scarpetto line of sauces.

Preparation couldn't be simpler: just eat in the microwave right in the jar (loosen the lid first, of course); or you can heat it in a small saucepan on the stove. Piece of cake. Serve over the cooked pasta of your choice, or use it in a casserole with layers of cooked pasta and some chicken or Italian sausage. Top with cheese, and you've got a meal.

title: My favorite breakfast cereal ...
text:
This stuff is wonderful if you're on Weight Watchers: a 1-cup serving is only 2 pts, Add 2/3 C skim milk, and we're talking a total of 3 pts for a very filling and delicious breakfast. I've tried most of the Special K flavors, and this one is by far the best. The freeze-dried strawberries have a wonderful almost-fresh strawberry flavor, too.

Most of my diet (I'd say 90%) is unprocessed, consisting of meals I make "from scratch," using fresh ingredients from the produce and meat/fish aisles. I also make my own breads, biscuits, etc. I'm very much aware of the controversy surrounding high fructose corn syrup, the negative impact it can have especially on dieters, and I try to avoid it. That said, and given my overall diet, I don't have a problem with consuming a small amount of HFCS occasionally for breakfast. It would be lovely if Kelloggs didn't use HFCS, but they do -- it's fairly low on the list of ingredients (just ahead of salt), but it's there.

The bottom line is that I'm losing weight, keeping it off, and I feel great. If you're concerned about HFCS, you may decide this isn't for you.

title: Absolutely addictive!
text: Oh my. Well, there went the diet, big time. The milk chocolate is creamy goodness, and the toffee chips and finely chopped almonds add just the right amount of sweet slightly salty crunch. These are absolutely addictive, and I have to seriously limit my consumption if I have any hope of staying on track diet-wise. Will definitely keep these around -- despite the temptation. They're really THAT good.

title: I use this on EVERYTHING!!
text:
Well, *almost* everything.

I prefer using salt-free seasoning blends, since I like to control the amount of salt I consume. I also like to have a variety of blends from which to choose -- but this one I use more than all the others.

I especially like it on salmon. I sprinkle it liberally on a salmon fillet, and then bake it. The flavor is wonderful -- the blend of red and green bell peppers, garlic, citrus, and spices works great.

I also sprinkle it on baby red potatoes toward the end of roasting them in a little olive oil.

I make my own turkey burgers, and mix a pound of ground turkey breast with a teaspoon of this mix, then form patties and broil or grill. Super tasty!

Summer veggie kabobs: yellow squash, zucchini, onion, small pear tomatoes, mushrooms -- sprinkled with this blend, then grilled. Yum!

I was a little hesitant to purchase such a large bottle of this, but I use it on so many things that I'm glad I did! Also, although it's called "Asian Blend" seasoning, I don't find the combination of spices to be particularly strongly "Asian." It's just a very pleasant sprightly blend that seems to work well with most proteins and veggies.

title: My new favorite coffee ...
text:
I'm kind of picky when it comes to coffee. I find a lot of coffees to have a bitter taste, almost as if the beans have been scorched or burned on their way to my cup. Some folks like that; I don't.

So I've managed to collect a fairly large variety of ground coffees, always searching for one that yields the "perfect cup."

I may have found it with this one. Newman's Own organic Special Blend has a robust flavor, but with no bitterness at all. It's smooth and rich tasting, and provides a strong background for whatever other flavorings I choose to use with it (vanilla, hazel nut) or totally alone.

I've used it for my early morning wake-up cup, and I've also brewed it up to use in iced coffee. It works great in both settings.

The price here on Amazon is also very good, given the quality. I'll be purchasing more for sure!

title: I was skeptical ... but WOW!
text:
After reading some of the other reviews here, I decided to give Izze Pomegranate a try. I wasn't expecting too much -- I knew it would be relatively tasty, but I had tried another brand of "carbonated fruit juice drink" and found it too sweet.

My fears were unfounded. Izze Pomegranate has just the right balance of tartness and sweet, with a nice amount of carbonation. The flavor is crisp and bright, with a hint of cranberry.

Izze just feels like an "adult" drink -- and I'll definitely be trying some of the other flavors. This is seriously good stuff.

title: This is seriously good soup ...
text:
Thick and hearty, this soup is loaded with turkey, vegetables, and chunks of "crust" that *could* be sticky or gummy, but aren't. I'm not sure how they did it, but the "crust" bits really do taste like a good pot pie crust that's been broken up and mixed into the soup.

That said, this is NOT low-cal, and may not work for some diets. While the can indicates 2 servings, they would be VERY small servings. I usually consume the entire can. The damage: 400 cals, 16g total fat, 3g of it saturated fat, 1600mg sodium, 21g carb, 8g fiber, 22g protein (this is from the Campbell's website). That's 9 points if you're on Weight Watchers. Still, paired with a nice salad topped with fat-free or low-fat dressing, this would be a good and filling meal.

Sometimes, I find I have to "doctor" prepared soups to give them enough flavor; not so with this one. The only thing I add is a little freshly ground coarse pepper.

I keep this on hand for those days when I'm just too tired to do more than open a can and heat something in the microwave. Once in awhile, it's a wonderful alternative.

title: I LOVE this stuff ...
text:
This is my "go to" breakfast when I need something fast. I know -- you're thinking instant oatmeal can't possibly be *that* good. Well, I think you'll find that this is definitely the exception.

It has that wonderful nutty oatmeal flavor -- not pasty or dull at all. Add to that a LOT of chopped apples and just the right amount of cinnamon. Add hot water, leave it alone for a minute or two so that the dried apple bits can blossom fully into fruity apple goodness, and you've got a tasty and filling quick breakfast.

It also makes a great quick snack, too.

Amazon's price on this is excellent. Finding it in my local supermarket is hit or miss most of the time: they seem to have it in stock once out of ever 5 or 6 trips. Not good enough. I can order from Amazon (I have this on subscribe and save), pay less, and have a steady supply of it.

title: This makes INCREDIBLE chili!
text:
I've been using this Carroll Shelby chili mix for years, but finding it in local stores has been hit or miss. It had gotten to where I was buying several packages at a time whenever I could find it anywhere.

I was amazed to find it here on Amazon, and for considerably less than I've paid in stores in the past. I love chili, and usually make 1-2 batches per month during the winter, and at least a batch every couple of months during the summer.

There's a recipe on the package, but I don't know anyone who actually follows it to the letter. I suppose if you've never made chili before, it's a good starting place. You can then decide how you might want to modify it.

I usually use half ground beef and half ground turkey (approx. a pound of each), a chopped onion, a 28-oz can of "redi-cut" tomatoes, a small can of tomato paste, a small can of black beans, a small can of pinto beans; then, from the chili kit, I add the spice packet and the entire cayenne pepper packet. They used to include a tiny bottle of tabasco sauce; they discontinued that in favor of the cayenne. I like things a little spicy, and the amount of cayenne here makes for a low-medium "burn" level.

Only occasionally do I find I need to use the masa flour. Usually, my chili is thick enough without it.

Finally, I top it with shredded colby-jack cheese, and serve it with cornbred muffins. We're talking serious yum here.
