title: real ingredients, good flavor pairs nice w/ rice, or used in tacos/burritos, or make a quick dip
text:
Pretty good. I bought a couple of boxes as I assumed I would like them, and I do. I appreciate the real ingredients.

I love lentils, and will buy them in any format that looks good- dry bags, pre cooked, seasoned, unseasoned, canned. These are lightly season, precooked, and ready to eat. Either heat them up (stovetop or microwave) or eat them cold. Good flavor either way.

Because of the cumin and slight taco-esque flavoring, I prefer this Sofrito flavor profile paired with rice and or used in tacos or burritos. Would make for a nice quick "dip" by running a pack of these lentils through a food processor.

Ingredients: Water, lentils, tomatoes, onion, bell peppers, olive oil, sea salt, garlic, ground cumin, ground annatto seeds, natural cilantro flavor.

title: not freeze dried! Dehydrated. Soft & chewy, not dry & crisp. Taste is good, price is sketchy
text:
--Taste? is fine. Sweet and mildly tart. No added sugar. Just peach slices (4 stars)

--Appearance? is fine- soft peach color in slices of various sizes (4.5 stars)

--Texture? these would be fine if they were marketed as "dehydrated", but NOT as freeze dried. Freeze dried makes food crisp. These are chewy, leathery. Much more akin to dehydrated. Only now with bag in hand do I notice that there is no information regarding their drying process. (Combo of both: 1 star)

--Price? I don't rate on price, but I at first thought that the price was VERY reasonable per ounce. Then I noticed that what they have listed as price per ounce is WRONG. $20.99 for 3.5 ounces makes it $6.00 per ounce. THAT is very pricy. When I initially thought it to be $2.96 per ounce, I thought that very good. NOPE, shame on me for not double checking their math. Shame on them for even having it wrong. FOR THIS, I down rate. (1 star)

That being said, I have no problem eating them. The slices are all stuck together in one giant mass, but comes apart easily enough. Totally fine for eating as is, or tossing into other food. At least not a total loss. 4 stars

But if you want actual freeze dried texture, this isnt it. Either they were dehydrated, or these had been freeze dried but not long enough, or moisture has gotten into the pack.

Again-- taste is fine, and texture is doable so long as you are ok with a "dehydrated" product over a legit "freeze dried" product. I'll eat them up, but I wont order again.

Overall 2.5 stars

title: fresh, long lasting, versatile pantry item, great brand
text:
I suddenly had a hankering for grits. The polenta is versatile and is worth checking out Bobs Red Mill site for recipe ideas. Lots of ways to use this beyond basic grits, but also just using it for grits is a win. I like a basic butter, salt & grits, or a bowl of cheddar grits. Always seems easy on my stomach. I like it for a quick breakfast or snack.

Love the brand, been a long time fan for most of my pantry needs. Love being able to buy in bulk yet having it in regular sized bags. Would buy again when time comes.

title: 8 grams of fiber!  sweet but not too sweet, well balanced, easy to drink. Pleasant flavor
text:
The Cranberry tea is delicious. I normally don't go for sweetened tea because it can be way too sweet, but this is perfectly balanced. I can taste cranberry and tea, and it tastes good at room temp or direct from fridge. Not at all bitter. Just easy to drink. Has 8 grams of fiber too!!

I don't rate on price, you'll have to decide if $3 a can is in your budget (Cranberry is currently $35.99 for 12 cans).

title: fresh and tasty
text:
I love blanched almonds for baking. They are slightly softer, giving them a tad more chew than unblanched variety. I can slice the as needed, or easily chop them. I also like them for making a quick "milk" or for making a non breadcrumb coating for chicken. Lots of other options too, including just munching on.

Good quality almonds, fresh, no concerns. Tastes good, smells good.

title: gentle, easy flavor. Not too strong, not too sweet, no idea how much of each goodie is in it
text:
Mild flavor. Might be nice option for those that dont actually like the taste of matcha, but want the benefits that come with it. Very delicate flavor. I suppose how strong or weak it tastes will depend on amount of water used and overall preference. Directions on the bottle say to use 1 TBS with 8-10 ounces of water. In the written description here is mentions 2 TBS to 10-16 ounces of water, which I guess is same as what is on the bottle.

I think I used more like 12 ounces each time. Just makes a pleasant albeit kind of neutral tasting drink. I can taste the little kick of ginger, and mild grassiness. But that is about it. I am familiar with everything that is in this, and nothing really dominates. Use less water and/or more powder if you need more flavor.

For the price, and I dont rate on price.. but wow, More than $60 for this 24 serving tub? I would expect it to list the EXACT amounts of what you are getting for that price. I have no idea what the ratio of matcha to other ingredients are, how much mushroom, and how much collagen.

Fun fact: collagen is a near 1:1 ratio to protein. So while this doesnt list the collagen amount, it has to list protein amount, which is 6 grams. That means this contains 5-6 grams of collagen.

As for anything else? No idea. I do tend to like Kroma products, and yes they are a premium priced product. Would like to see a little more transparency. I was hoping for more info to come with the jar. Nada.

That being said, I like it, it is easy to drink, and it can drink it as directed or add other (or more) goodies to it. Kinda like the neutral flavor, but at same time kind of want a little more punch of flavor. Nice late morning, early afternoon drink to perk me up (not going to replace my coffee!).

title: delicate flavor, not too sweet, not too strong, loaded w/ fiber, vitamin C, and tea polyphenols
text:
Pleasant flavor, not too sweet. It is sweetened with erythritol, but it seems mild. The strawberry flavor is more of an essence. Very light tea taste. Gentle flavor. Not a strong tea taste at all. Overall I find it easy to drink. Nice when I want something more than water, but not a pop or other strong drink. This is delicate tasting and thirst quenching. I like it best at cool room temperature for best flavor.

Check out the fiber (8 grams), vitamin C (477 mg), and tea polyphenols (260 mg)

title: basic bare bones kit, good thick pvc lines and spiles.
text:
Maple season is coming up. The timing is not yet right to get these spiles tapped into place, but they seem like they should work. The blue tubing is stout- has a thick, firm but flexible feel to it. The black taps are a durable feeling plastic. Directions are to drill hole in tree in upward slant, then take a hammer to gently tap the spile into place.

Best if you already know what you are doing so you dont damage the tree. Need to use your own drill bit. Nothing more than a box of tubes and spiles. Very basic, bare bones kit. But it is enough if you know what you are doing. If brand new, you will also want filters and buckets.

title: great big bag for culinary use or for making drinks, perfectly fine for either
text:
I'm rather impressed. This 10 lb bag is comically huge. It is a great option for commercial use, or mega enthusiastic matcha households. Considering that it only takes a couple of teaspoons to make a cup of matcha, this is going to a last a very long time. I keep some portioned out in a container and currently have rest tucked in fridge. I may break it down into smaller mylar bags with 02 absorber just to ensure freshness.

As stated, it is culinary grade, which makes most sense for culinary use. Personally, I am fine with that for making hot or cold drinks. I have ceremonial, but I really don't care which I have. My tastes aren't discerning enough. I mean, I can usually tell the difference, but don't really mind either. I actually dont "like" matcha, but I have been drinking it regularly for 15+ years. It is loaded with antioxidants and it provides some really nice low key energy that is non jittery and long lasting. I still drink my coffee, but I will have some of this late morning or early afternoon to top me off. I like it iced or mixed into a smoothie best of all.

title: one of my favorite meals from Augason Farms. Use now or tuck away. Modify as desired
text:
I have pretty much all good experiences with Augason Farms products. I really like this chili mix, and I would buy it and use it for any time not just for emergency use. It has a pretty good flavor on its own. Good base flavor, and is doable as is. I can't help myself, so I doctor it up a bit. I will add more of my own seasonings, sometimes add TVP or real beef, or add in extra vegetables. Serve over rice, noodles, or have a side of bread with it. But as is, with nothing else under or over it.. I would have no problem with it either.

At this point I buy food on sale, and look for ways to stretch what I have to work with. When I can find sales on Augason Farms products, I usually buy a can or two. Some I use right away, some I tuck away. I find that the current global situation calls for using some of it now. Chili is nice way to fill the belly and is so easy to modify per person preference. I can make a little or a lot. I find that I spend less using this over buying all the ingredients to make a pot fresh. Or this can be used to stretch what I make. All the considerations, and this product this brand has a role in it.

My can was in good shape. I occasionally get dented cans from Augason (and other brands). There is rarely anything in them that cant take a dent. Those concerns are primarily for acid foods, like tomato or pineapple, and that is with it having liquid. Many products in emergency packaging have additional packaging inside (like a bag within the can). I just really haven't ever been concerned.

title: I like it a lot. Good flavor & texture, super quick to heat(or eat cold), convenience,emergency, etc
text:
I like it. I will buy it again.
I rarely eat Hormel Compleats as shelf stable meals in tiny portions don't really do it for me. But I bought these on a whim. I am looking to make a more robust pantry with a wider variety of items that include shelf stable meals like this. For ultra convenience, for emergency, for getting ahead of inflation and shortages. Just want something to eat. Heated is best, but could be consumed at room temp too.

I really expected the worst. I know I had one of their concoctions several years back and didnt care for it. But I gave this a go (impulse purchase), and was pleasantly surprised by the rather good taste, an overall good texture.

The stuffing is more of a gravy blob, but there are bits of celery or something that add to the texture. I really liked it. The turkey is a compressed patty that will flake apart or stay together depending on how you cut into it (no knife needed, very soft). Similar to canned turkey or chicken. At least is isnt a sponge loaf of unknown origin. I could tell it was turkey.

Can't beat the prep time. Just a minute give or take in the microwave. Stack these puppies high in the cupboard and you've got an easy meal anytime. If you have a big appetite like me then I would flesh it out with some noodles, mashed potatoes, rice or something bulky like that. Ooh maybe some toast or a good hunk of bread. Then maybe a vegetable if you have any. But if you are a light eater or someone who simply doesnt eat much yet wants the convenience and the variety (looking at you seniors!) then this is an option. No need to fuss.

I imagine perception of taste will vary. I cant say these are the new Holy Grail of shelf stable quick meals. But they have their place in my home and in my belly.

title: perfectly good tuna, refreshingly reasonable price (currently)
text: Perfectly good tuna fish. I get this brand in the store, but bought this here because it was a good priced multi pack. Reasonable price as a straight out purchase($10), and even better as a Subscribe and Save($8 something). I dont eat tuna often, but when I do I seem to go through a couple of cans at a time. I like to keep a lot on hand since shelf life is long, and it works in a pinch for convenient meal, emergency ration, etc.

title: good flavor, sprays evenly, no clogs so far, works well on popcorn to help make salt/spices stick
text:
Good tasting spray for use on popcorn and other foods where you want a buttery flavor. I bought this as part of a huge popcorn themed b-day gift for my husband. I figured a spray is easier to work with than melted butter. He likes using it to give the salt or other flavoring something to stick to.

Solid 4 stars. Works as intended, pretty good flavor. I think it could use a little more flavor, but husbands hasnt commented regarding that. I would possibly buy it again based on price (was $30 for 6 cans, which seemed pricy). I think if we used it a lot, then I would probably buy a container of liquid flavor oil then use a spray dispenser. But here, popcorn is an occasional treat, and most often during the winter.

title: eat as is or Dr it up w/ other spices, veg, proteins. Good flavor, potassium to balance sodium
text:
Nice shelf stable option for convenience or emergency. Eat cold, eat heated up in microwave, or over stove top. Pleasant taste, not too strong in flavor but doesnt taste like a shelf stable food. May depend on how it is prepared. I added it to a cast iron skillet with rice bran oil, a neutral tasting oil. The resulting taste and texture work for me.

While it is loaded with sodium (1000 mg for entire package), it is not outside the norm for shelf stable foods. It has a lot of potassium (490 mg) to help balance it out. None of this should come as a surprise as the picture clearly shows the nutritional panel.

It doesn't taste salty. It doesnt make me feel like I ate something salty. I didnt need to add anything to this to make it taste "better". I think it was fine as is. However, I think it could be doctored up a bit to suit individual taste preference and to further bulk it out. I like stronger flavors and a little more texture, so the next time I used sesame oil instead of rice bran oil. I added a little extra garlic and fresh ground black pepper.

I recommend adding in a side of vegetables or a protein of choice (chicken tofu, scrambled egg, seitan strips, pork, etc). I ate the package (considered 2 servings) as is- nothing added- and was satisfied. Next time I used it as a base for a bunch of vegetables and a little chicken. It felt much more satisfying.

I keep a variety of shelf stable foods on hand. I dont use them often, but once in awhile the sheer convenience makes it worth it. I also see the benefit for use in an emergency as little needs to be done to prepare it. Can eat at room temp in a pinch, or wont take long to heat up with other heating options, compared to a bag of rice (but I keep all options on hand).

title: minty freshness
text: 5 stars- all good. Not because it is necessarily better than others, just that it is as described and as expected. I often see my husband pick up this brand so I bought this as a stocking stuff of the sort for him. He seems pleased to have a multi pack, and I like it as well. Would buy again.

title: no flavor in the lychee-peach, cant taste either flavor, results in terrible bitter experience
text:
I have the variety pack. I bought it on sale. Glad I did, as I am not liking this all that much and I would have been more disappointed in a full price item. I have a high tolerance for unpleasant, but this actually turned me off, especially the Lychee Peach. Which is truly disappointing because that is the flavor that caught my interest. I love love love Lychee, and I figured peach would be a nice pairing. It tastes NOTHING like lychee or peach. I could not tell you what I was tasting other than spine shivering bitterness. It is almost like they didnt add any actual flavor to the bottle.

I dont need sweet, I dont need a lot of flavor, but I need to be able to tell what the flavor is and I need not to drink it and cringe. I shuddered with every sip until I finally just gave up. Energy drinks can be a bit unpleasant, and some taste best super cold, and some kind of grow on me. I tend to overlook some unpleasant for the benefit of lifting the mind fog and giving me a little pep.

This (the lychee peach) is so off putting that I ended up not finishing the can. I HATE WASTING food or drink. But this was so.. blegh. Maybe I can salvage it by mixing it with something. I gave the "Super Berry" a try, and that was much better--not great, but it is palatable. I can drink that. It has a berry flavor. I am very familiar with all ingredients and flavors here, so I know what to expect. I am hoping the yuzu (a citrus flavor) is good, and I have high hoped for the mango ginger. But I wont know for a couple more days. I haven't worked through the other 2 flavors yet. So far it is 50-50. Perhaps I will update.

I like that it has 100 mg of caffeine. Not too much. I have had some caffeinated drinks that are 200+ mg, and that is too much for me since I already drink coffee. I like an energy drink to top me off, for when I want something cold and bubbly, and for times I am about to start a chore or do a work out that will benefit from the added "motivation". I dont need a lot of caffeine, just usually a little bump. So this having 100 mg and being listed on the front of the bottle is a positive about this product.

Also has some vitamin C and some B vitamins.

RATING: I am going with middle of road rating of 3. I think it is "OK", and that is only because at least one flavor of the 4 has been good. The lychee peach is terribad (1 star). Super berry is decent (4 stars).

I like what they are trying to do here. I have had similar products (where the ingredients are much healthier than other energy drinks), but truly this has been the most disappointing. I doubt it would ever be a repurchase unless one of the flavors truly make me feel good and tastes good.

title: fun! Any fan of Franks will likely enjoy this marinade. Easy to use
text:
4.5 stars. I'm from Buffalo, and Franks is ubiquitous. We use their hot sauce on everything. Even love a bowl of rice with butter, Franks, and some fresh ground pepper. Just has a taste that I crave on occasion. We use other hot sauces too, but for me I love a few drips of Franks on just about anything. So yeh, this injectable marinade piqued my interest!

Not the exact same as the sauce, and taste isn't the exact same, but it sure adds moisture. I think taste will depend on how much is used, how well it is distributed. I used it on a pork tenderloin, and sort of just poked it all over. Just what I happened to have that I thought could benefit from a little added flavor. I followed directions then chose to cook this pork in the slow cooker. Good smell and taste. It wasn't hot hot or anything, though I will say I didnt use a lot. Despite my love for Franks, I am not one for excessive heat. I like a little flavor that it provides. It was a neat thing to try out. Easy to use. Just need to remember to not use directly from the bottle (you wont be using whole bottle). So be sure to pour some into a separate container to work from.

I'll try it on, er in, chicken next. I thinking of a reverse chicken finger. Get the hot sauce inside, then bread, air fry, and have a dip on the side. Maybe more Franks hot sauce!

I would get this again. Not necessarily a pantry staple, but it was fun to try and I find value it the taste experience it provided.

title: too weak to be worth it, barely any flavor when brewed at 2 ounces. Coffee in Mocha only
text:
3.5 stars. Needs more powder to make it taste like anything other than hot water with hint of flavor. Just not suitable in capsule form.

Variety pack has 3 flavor options: Cacao Ceremony, Mocha Ceremony and Ginger Ceremony. The ingredients are not listed on the product page (so much for transparency, hm?), but is listed on box.

Basically cacao, cacao butter for the cacao ceremony, then add in ginger for the ginger ceremony, and add in coffee for the mocha ceremony. So please take note that the Mocha Ceremony has coffee added to it, and the other two flavors not. I imagine it has very little since I can not taste it.

The flavor is very mild. I have brewed these at 4 ounces and 2 ounces, with little difference in flavor. Just sort of watery with a hint of flavor. No body. Just watery. I am not new to drinking cacao, and this is really quite weak and therefore quite expensive way to consume it. However, I dont rate on price. But I do comment especially as it applies to the ratio of water to cacao. This is very very weak. Cacao is weak, Mocha is weak, and Ginger is weak. That is brewed at both 2 ounces and 4 ounces. I didnt bother trying it at 6 ounces. I also tried it in another cup of coffee, but it is so weak that the flavor was entirely lost.

I love cacao, and I will just take a spoonful and stir it into liquid of my choice for better taste and better price.

This is an instant product, which I dont have a problem with. I keep some hot cocoa K-cups on hand for my husband, but I scoff at the idea of paying way more for what I could get from a kettle and a packet of powder. Now reduce it further in the nespresso capsule, form, and this is kind of crazy. Again, my rating does not reflect price (we all have different budgets, needs, interests, prices fluctuate and so on). I am strictly addressing the flavor to "brew" ratio on an instant product, and the result no matter how I brew it is just way to watery to be worth it. It will not be a repurchase for me, and I can't recommend it either.

If it had a stronger flavor-- nearly anything above a hint of flavor, then I would like it a whole lot more. What flavor is there is pleasant and fresh. But it begs for more of it. I think this would be better suited for the larger k-cup (be able to pack more product into a larger vessel), or one may need to brew one, then pour contents of another (dont brew it) into the mug. Or sold as a bag of powder, where one can just pour some water in an make it as strong or as weak as one wants.

Just a miss for me. I will drink it up though. If I come to any other revelations about my experience with this, I will be back to update. Still curious? I can say that it is fresh. The product itself is fine.

title: fresh tasting and smelling, slightly acidic, light leaning medium
text:
I happen to have their Instant Pod dual coffee maker, which has spots for nespresso capsules as well as for k-cups. This brews just fine in their machine (as to be expected). The flavor is good. I brewed it at 4 ounces.

Not my favorite, but it works for me. Coffee is a personal thing, so you may or may not like it. I find this medium roast to be a tad acidic to my liking. Oddly, I find their light roast to be very good, and prefer it over this medium. For reference, I totally prefer a deep dark chewy strong bold roast above all else. I nearly always avoid light roasts, and I am picky when it comes to a medium. However, the coffee smells fresh, tastes fresh, and I haven't had any problems with brewing. 5 stars for their light and 4 stars for their medium.

title: dynamic flavor, interesting flavor profile, has body, not too acidic, bright but bold
text:
I have tried this Leggero light roast, and their Lungo medium roast. I don't normally care for light roast, but the flavor of this impresses me. It has depth and layers of flavor. Not just a "one note bright citrus" that most light roasts have. This isn't bitter or too acidic. I can drink it at 4 ounces, plain, no problem. For reference, I normally prefer extra dark, chewy, strong, bold black coffee.

I will add a note about their medium roast Lungo (4 stars), in that I find that to be a tad more tangy and acidic over this light roast. Side by side, I prefer this light roast, which is saying a lot because I normally otherwise avoid the light side.

This is good, I like it, and would consider it again (hence 5 stars). Just something about it stands out over other light roast capsules. I also happen to have the Instant Pod brewer, which brews capsules like this (nespresso) as well as a spot for brewing k-cups.

title: 1/2 tsp per 8 ounces water (I use hot to start) makes a smooth cup of green tea
text:
I'm impressed! It tastes like brewed green tea! Mild, smooth, and the powder dissolves seamlessly in warm or hot water. Just stir, no blender or frother needed. I haven't tried it in cold water. I tend to use warm (or hot) water for stuff like this even if I intend to drink it iced. Anway, I was concerned this was going to be awful after reading some reviews. Did I get something different? Because this powder is exactly as it should be, and I am pleased.

An amber powder that makes for an amber drink, similar to when I brew some of my nicer green tea brands. Not a green color like some. Definitely not a matcha. Tastes like good ole green tea. Doesn't have that instant taste either. It simply tastes like brewed tea. All it is is 100% green tea.

Be mindful of following the directions. I use 1/2 tsp for 8 ounces of water, and that is plenty for me. Adjust to taste. I imagine as with any green tea, the more you use or the more unpleasantly robust it can taste. Green tea can easily go from smooth to bitter depending on amount, brew time (if steeping a bag) or temp of water.

I also have had Judees instant black tea with similar enjoyment. I am a fan of Judees products, and have been using a wide assortment for a couple of years now with no issues. Glad I can add this Green Tea to my list.

title: super smooth, no chewing required, use a little or a lot of liquid, nice warming gruel
text:
I haven't had this before, and I chose it because I wanted a warm gruel to eat when I am feeling chilled or I dont want to actually eat (masticate) food. This is where smoothies normally come into play, but I dont want a cold smoothie on a freezing day. So hot cereals and sipping broths are my go to thing. I have been using [[ASIN:B0BB7N5HNZ mushroom yam gruel powder]] and decided to try this Nestum for something different. I like Nestle products and since it was on sale at time of order, I decided to go for it.

Big pack of 12 canisters. Easy to make, just add water. Use as much or as little liquid as needed for your or your kiddo. I like it more like a slurry, but have made it thicker too. It is very smooth no matter what. No chewing required.

Has a slight caramel aroma and taste. I can taste the sweetness. It does remind me of honey wheat bread. I like to stir in a little peach, pumpkin, or apple butter. I think a fruit baby food puree would also very very nice. Just on its own is a little blah.

Overall, I like it. It will be a while before I get through it all. Not sure if it is a repurchase, but since I saw it very recently at local big box store, I may get it on occasion in a single can form.

title: good assortment of colors, vibrant enough
text:
Making macarons, and needed gel food coloring. Doesn't take much, and the colors work in macron making.

Normally I would prefer a known name brand, and one that knows to pair a picture of "icing" with some sort of frosting and not something that looks like ice cream, but I need more coloring for macrons that I wasnt sure if they would turn out or not, and the price was right.. so here I am. Not a bad product in terms of performance, just dont know enough about it for long term use in food. I would be fine with using it in craft needs.

title: Indulgent flavor (& calories), works nice in drinks alone or w/ other syrups, and in baking
text:
White chocolate is rather chocolatey. Like a mellow milk chocolate or nougat ish flavor. I like that I can tell that it has a chocolate vibe. I like white chocolate but rarely have it in drinks. This has an excellent pump, and it even has a little silicone cover for the tip to help keep it fresh, and to take care of any drippage.

Big big container. I will be trying out using this in some holiday baking. In the meantime I have made some white mocha drinks as per their recipe. I have even paired it with other syrups, and that has been fun. Adding it to hot chocolate is a nice way to add a level of sweetness and flavor.

title: pleasant level of sweetness, mixes well w/ frother, big container
text:
Big container of matcha with sweetener (erythritol and stevia). Blends up easy with my frother. I normally just buy plain matcha, but dont mind the pre sweetened stuff. The price per ounce is very low, much lower than expected for something make with ceremonial grade matcha. There is only so much sweetener used that can possibly offset it to such a low price. Not complaining :)

BTW I have been drinking matcha on and off for a couple of decades. It is not a flavor I particularly like, but I like the antioxidants, how it helps greatly reduce sugar cravings (discovered that on my own before it became a known thing), and the energy I get is low key and non jittery. It ONLY has less caffeine than coffee if you use a very small amount.

I tend to like NatureBell supplements, so it has been nice to try their matcha option. I tend to rate generously on matcha. Basically they are nearly all the same to me. So unless it sticks out as being something bad, I just go with 5 stars. I will add that the sweetener is actually well done (to me).

title: can actually taste grapefruit/basil/mint. Good amount of D3 & Zinc makes me feel better
text:
Taste: I can actually taste grapefruit, basil, and mint. It's interesting to be able to pick out those flavors. The taste isn't my favorite, but it hasn't stopped me from drinking it. I love fizzy drinks, and it has been a nice alternative to grabbing a bottle of pop.

If I were rating only on taste, I would have gone with 4 stars. But I noticed something.. and that is that it has been making me feel good. I was feeling a tad run down, wasn't sure if I was going to get a cold, I hadn't popped any supplements, and only was drinking this. Nothing ever developed and I just felt better. Then I remembered this is an "immunity" drink, and that it actually has helpful ingredients (D3 & Zinc) in a truly helpful amount. I normally take D3 but have been lazy on taking it for a couple months now. I guess returning to it (as well as zinc) has just sort of brought me back to normal. 5 stars

title: good flavor, use instead of a banana or to further boost banana flavor
text: Nice addition to recipes where I want to boost the banana flavor even if using bananas, or if I simply want a banana flavored frosting or something that I dont want to use an actual banana. I imagine will work to help reduce banana in a recipe. This has a good natural taste, so I am finding it really quite versatile as a flavoring agent.

title: For truly dark roast lovers. Great deep dark strong bold smooth flavor. SO GOOD
text:
I took a chance on this as some reviews were off putting. I've never had McCafe k-cups, but I decided to go ahead and give this French dark roast a try. WOW! I think it is fantastic, and would consider it again. I really like a deep dark bold strong dark roast, and this actually fits my preferred flavor profile.

Just.. YUM! I drink my coffee black, unsweetened, and really enjoy a super dark cup of coffee. I imagine it would hold up just fine with creamer too. Smells like coffee, tastes like coffee, and it makes me happy to drink this. SO GLAD I gave this a try. No issues so far with brewing, no grounds in the cup. Just perfect! YAY!

title: red pepper & parm flavor infusion makes nice flavor for drizzle and dipping
text:
Red pepper and parm in a very light oil. It is a nice drizzle or dipping oil. I have had it on pasta, used it to dip a fresh loaf of Italian bread (Mmmm!), and in other recipes for the oil, but also to add a little flavor. It definitely has a bite of heat (bit not hot hot), and I can taste the parmesan. I shake the bottle to distribute the pepper bits. Some may come out, but for the most part not much. But it is still very flavorful. Well infused flavor.

I dont notice a strong olive oil flavor. It is on the mild side to me. I tend to like a strong olive flavor, but this is still good to me. The flavor of the pepper and parm stand out, and it really is lovely for dipping bread. I am sure it would be nice over salads too, or vegetables.

Well sealed. Smooth cork like plug.

title: mild mint with sweet outer coating, melts away, smooth truffle texture, pleasant
text:
I think these are quite pleasant, and rather well packaged. What you get is a tray of 22 candies in a box with lift off lid (they should have gone with 24), with an outer sleeve and plastic wrapped. Ready for giving; would make a nice host/ess gift.

Pleasant little squares of minty goodness. Not overly minty. Nice balance of chocolate and mint. Some are chocolate coated, some are "pastel coated" which is basically a smooth sweet coating that is reminiscent of a white chocolate or sugar/vanilla. It's good. The coating is just that- a coating. It is not a hunk of chocolate that you have to bite through, it is a thin coating over a hunk of soft truffle like mint chocolate. Smooth inside and out.

Small bites, perfect for popping in mouth and allowing to melt away. Could easily be smaller for same effect.

I had my 70+ years old mom try these alongside me. They reminded her of a truffle, she thought both varieties were good.

I liked it enough to snoop around their other products and web page. The company has been around for several decades, and has a wide assortment of chocolates and other confections.

I think if you enjoy a GENTLE mint flavor, and want something that is just easy to enjoy (non cloying, no chewing needed, doesnt stick to teeth, nice for when wanting something sweet but dont want to eat the whole box--'cause who binges on mint? haha etc).

Solid 5 stars from me.

Ingredients
MILK CHOCOLATE (SUGAR, COCOA BUTTER, CHOCOLATE LIQUOR, MILK, SKIM MILK, SOY LECITHIN AS EMULSIFIER, VANILLA EXTRACT), SEMI-SWEET CHOCOLATE (SUGAR, CHOCOLATE LIQUOR PROCESSED WITH ALKALI, COCOA BUTTER, CHOCOLATE LIQUOR, MILK, BUTTEROIL, SOY LECITHIN AS EMULSIFIER, VANILLA EXTRACT), SUGAR-BASED COATING (SUGAR, PALM KERNEL OIL, SKIM MILK, MILK, HYDROGENATED PALM OIL, GLYCERYL-LACTO ESTERS OF FATTY ACIDS, SOY LECITHIN AS EMULSIFIER, VANILLA EXTRACT, SALT), PALM OIL, PEPPERMINT OIL, YELLOW 5, BLUE 1.

title: super silky smooth holiday blend, not exactly flavored, but it has a light comforting taste
text:
My coffee preference: as dark and bold as can be, usually drank black and unsweetened. Almost never get flavored coffee.

This is a medium roast, and I knew this going in. I am a bit of a sucker for holiday flavors though. Come cool weather, I am looking for a little added festive feel. So that is when pumpkin spice appeals to me, and as we edge closer to Christmas, I will want to try various holiday themed flavors of everything. It doesnt replace my preference for dark sludge, but it makes for a cozy festive addition.

So I bust out creamers, syrups, toppings, and all the different coffees and other snacks and goodies. This Community Christmas Blend was an impulse purchase. The description sounded nice, and so I decided to go for it.

I brewed it at 10 ounces, and it makes a decent cup of coffee. It is very smooth, like silky smooth. I was definitely missing the coffee bean taste, but it wasnt watery. Not at all acidic or bitter. I did use cream-- I find that flavored coffee does best with cream; brings out the nuance of flavor. I couldnt tell you what I was tasting. I could tell that it wasnt plain coffee, but it isnt exactly flavored either. It had a warm flavor profile. Gentle. Kind of begged to be consumed alongside some biscotti or other holiday treat.

If you want an ULTRA SMOOTH cup of coffee that pairs nice with a holiday treat, this is worth the try. I give it 5 stars because the quality is up there and it has a gentle flavor while also providing a caffeine kick. It is intriguing, and I would consider it again.

title: easy to use, mostly dissolves, just drink up. Bag within a pouch
text:
Slightly gritty, slightly bitter, but I find it pleasant. I use in water, in tea, hot cocoa, and the occasional smoothie. I may add to a sipping broth next. Don't need much. I aim for using in water on empty stomach in early part of day, then later i may take a little more in whatever I have and feel like drinking. I dont complicate it, I dont need to.

The product page lists some highlights to this food, but a quick search will tell you so much more. Dont need to be part of the target marketing to reap benefit from this. I am a big fan of health powders, and this has been an interesting addition. I may keep up with it through til my next doctor appointment. I am curious if there will be measurable benefits noted.

title: gloriously good decaf, smells divine, drink to your hearts content, so good tastes like regular
text:
I've recently gotten into the capsules. I have several brands, and use them in my [[ASIN:B096BJJ1FG Instant Pod coffee machine]]. I am enjoying the capsules so much that I have been having a major hankering for it well after my window of caffeine. I have not had the Nespresso brand yet (yeesh, SO expensive) but I figured I would go with the original brand for what I hoped to be a good DECAF. So I splurged on this 50 pack.

I must say... I am pleased. It doesnt taste like decaf. Has a gorgeous coffee taste, and it hits the spot when I want to keep on drinking coffee but really must stop the caffeine. Delightful! I usually brew it at 2 or 4 ounces for the deepest flavor.

I'll probably spring for the regular dark capsules by this brand given how pleased I am with the decaf. Wish it wasnt so pricey, but I dont rate on price anyway. We all have different budgets, needs, preferences, etc. I rarely get coffee out, but when I am at a place that has actual espresso, I usually buy a couple of shots, which sets me back much more than a couple of these. So I guess I am saving in some ways. That's what I am telling myself anyway, haha.

No coffee or basic home machine is going to create the same experience that a dedicated high end professional espresso machine is going to create, but it tastes good enough for my basic needs. Overall I would say that I very much like this Nespresso brand, and the decaf has been a worthwhile purchase, and I will likely keep on purchasing it. I imagine I will go through all 50 of these in a short time. I can't stop drinking it. YUM!!

title: "Fine" for stretching meat sauce, taco filling, stuffed peppers, meatballs, meat loaf, soups, cereal
text: I usually buy course bulgur for dishes where it is the main feature. I tried this FINE bulgur for something different. I figured it would be used as a hot mash or cereal like one would grits, or added to soup. But when I cooked it up, I determined that it would also be excellent for stretching ground beef-- either added as is to a sauce or taco filling, but definitely also for meatballs and meat loaf. Stuffed peppers!! So glad I had the opportunity to try the "fine" variety, as I am not sure I would have purchased it otherwise. Course is my go-to, but now the fine is equally useful.

title: budget friendly compared to other mushroom coffee, not sure how much caffeine per serving?
text: I love mushroom supplements, I happen to like instant coffee, I always have an instant coffee with mushrooms on hand, and I happen to really like this brand. Now I can add this product to the long list of products I have used and liked by Micro Ingredients. Huge bag, really a bargain. For that I will purchase again. My ONLY wish is that they would list the caffeine content. I'm sure it isnt that much different than a cup of instant, but I would like to know for sure. I sometimes like to add this into a brewed cup of coffee, or add plain instant coffee to it. I just want to know. I would also like to know how much mushroom is in this. For whatever reason many mushroom coffee hybrids dont list it. 5 stars if this listed the caffeine content!

title: budget friendly, good flavor, not too sweet, really nice in smoothies, smells good, good brand
text: I have been pleased with Micro Ingredients products. I have been using a wide variety for a few years now including their matcha. Truly budget friendly price (not that I rate on price) and pretty good quality. I normally don't go for a sweetened matcha powder, but this works out. Not too sweet. I go through a lot of matcha. I dont actually love the flavor, I simply enjoy the effects. I always get a healthy, low key non jittery boost of energy, and the high antioxidants makes it attractive for regular consumption. This is good hot, cold, or y favorite: added to smoothies. I am totally fine with this product, and would certainly consider it again. I am not too picky when it comes to matcha, so this is 5 stars for me

title: easy to make, good flavor, east as is, as a side, or add goodies into it, use as a soup base
text: I think I grabbed these on sale. I tend to keep a variety of Knorr products in my pantry for their convenience as well as their long shelf life. I like knowing that I have a variety of food on hand in case of emergency. Or simply to not have to go to the store all the time. I don't eat this kind of food all the time but it works in a pinch as needed. Not complicated to make, cooks up pretty quickly. Can eat as is, or add other goodies into it. Can even use it as a base for a quick soup. Get creative!

title: warm & comforting on a chilly afternoon, super easy to make, use miso pouch & garnish pouch
text:
I Love this Miko brand of instant miso soup. It is a slight change up from [[ASIN:B005HUVJYO my usual beloved instant freeze dried miso from the same brand]]. This one has a variety of flavor options, and I like them all. Nice to make cup at a time. Plenty of flavor. Use as much or as little of water as you want.

Be sure to use both the miso paste packet as well as the dry garnish packet. Put the two together with some hot water, and you have yourself a nice cup of miso. Delicious, warm, and comforting on a chilly afternoon

title: looooong term pantry, emergency prep, 25 year shelf life unopened, stacking calories
text:
Many products are sold based on weight, not volume. This contains 4 lbs of dehydrated potatoes. It will not be filled to the brim. It doesnt need to. It just needs to weigh 4 lbs, which is what you are paying for. In emergency food, the containers are typically chosen based on quantity and in keeping with uniformity. So with Augason Farms, you will find #10 (that reads, "number 10") sized cans for some weights and volume, and the buckets for larger quantities. Potato slices will initially take up some volume then settle. It is perfectly reasonable to have lots of space left over in a bucket. Why down rate for space left in the storage container when it is the weight of food you are buying? This product is fine. All is good. Go for it.

These potatoes are fine, and cook up well. I buy Augason products when they are on sale. Been doing this on and off for a few years now. Always been a bit of a "prepper", since I was a toddler it seems, haha (In my 40s now). It has served me well through power outages, sicknesses, unemployment, and even bigger stuff like the pandemic, and now... *vaguely gestures around* everything else that is going on. I've never been one to be without when anything has come up. I never did "emergency food" if only because I didnt have the budget. I would stick with typical foods and try to store them well. Well now I have a little more wiggle room in my budget, and with the on and off sales of long term storage (20+ years), I take advantage when I can. I remember buying some Augason eggs back in 2019 for $19. Today? $36-100 for same container, depending on the day. So buying when on sale is also an investment in future prices.

And so, I haven't opened this specific 4 lb bucket of potato slices.. sorry. I dont intend to any time soon, but I have used their slices from a #10 can, and have been perfectly happy. I bought these primarily for the extra long term storage, and I have other canned potatoes and fresh to use first, as well as hopefully grow my own. But I wanted to shore up my options. Having some soups and such just adds flavor to other options used. I can add more veg, or a protein, or beans, or simply have some bread to dip into it. Or I can use as way to flavor something. I have a slew of reviews to write on various Augason products, and so they will all be pretty much the same: Super long term storage (25+ years).

Everyone's SHTF scenario varies. It could be bad weather (tornadoes, hurricanes, blizzards, ice storms), could be illness, could be road trip gone wrong (you do keep supplies in your car too, right?!), could be unemployment, or power outage, or lack of transportation, or oven/fridge/other appliance break down, or bigger stuff like plagues, food shortages, supply chain issues, *cough WW3 cough*, etc. No matter the situation we all need some things to get by: we need is food, water, shelter, some hygiene and medical stuff, and so on. You don't have to stack "emergency supplies" but you do need to stack shelf stable food items. Buy a few extra things every single time you go to the store. If you get to a spot that you feel comfortable and have the budget, then grab the "emergency" items like Augason offers. I like adding it in and just forgetting about it.

I give 5 stars because the cans and buckets nearly always in perfect condition, they have regular sales, are good about shipping items as soon as they can, have lots of items to choose from, and so far seem to be of good quality.

Buy what you can, when you can. All this isnt just about inflation. There are global issues going on that will impact us severely.

title: Chai: gentle flavor, warm & comforting, reminds me of Christmas, hint of gingerbread, so creamy
text:
Definitely a treat, kinda pricey, but I find the CHAI Frothy cafe Latte to create a lovely, warm, comforting, drink, and for that I will be buying it again. It is sweet and creamy; just the right level of sweetness for me, and the creaminess is what makes this drink. I normally drink black, unsweetened coffee, but enjoy the occasional cafe latte. Your experience may vary.

Easy to make. Take your mug, and add the froth packet. Then set it under the Keurig to make the coffee pod portion. It recommends 8 ounces. As the coffee brews into the powder, the powder begins to dissolve and you see the creamy froth forming. At the end, you can keep it as is, or can quickly stir it to make sure it is all dissolved. Can add more sweetener as you prefer. The creamy froth stays, it doesn't disappear.

Taste is not entirely identifiable as "Chai" as I know it, but it is really pleasant. Mild gingerbread flavor. Really tastes like a Christmas flavor.

I first drank this after coming in from the cold (30s, overcast). I had been working a laborious chore (cutting wood, stacking wood, dragging bits of a fallen tree to other side of yard, and yes it truly did include a hill). 2.5 hours non stop (and 14,000 steps) later, I was done for the day. I wasn't "cold" until I got into the house. I hadn't been sweating that I knew of, but my layers were just damp enough to start giving me the chills. I wanted something to warm me up before hopping into shower. I kind of didn't want coffee, so I was thinking hot chocolate. Something creamy and sweet.. then I remembered that I had this Chai latte waiting to be tried out. So that is what I grabbed for. And it definitely hit the spot. Again, warm creamy, perfectly sweet, and... comforting. I think that last part is what makes this SO appealing to me.

Coffee sits in the background as any cafe latte creates. The emphasis is on the creamy froth. Dare I say I would make this as a straight "latte" and skip the cafe portion? It could be done. But if you want the coffee behind it, then make it as directed. If want a stronger punch of coffee flavor, then use more coffee, or stir in a little instant, or use less powder, etc.

I'll wrap it up by saying that the Keurig Gevalia Frothy Latte line is brand new to me. I'm pleased to have been able to try this Chai frothy latte. They have several flavor options, including some not on this page such as Peppermint Mocha and Pumpkin Spice (neither currently available--truly hope they are soon). I want to try them all! I would easily add this into drink/food themed gifts. Maybe pair it with a biscotti or other cookie.

title: pantry staple, often used in non cheese based "mac n' cheese", & other seasoning needs
text:
I'm not vegan or vegetarian, but I eat plenty of dishes that could be regarded as such. I simply love food, a wide array, and nutritional yeast just happens to be a pantry staple the past 20 years or so. It imparts a lightly cheesy taste. I use it as a seasoning, and I use it most often to make a quick "mac n cheese". I don't always want actual cheese. So this works really well for me. Just so you know, it isnt gooey, it doesnt melt, but it works well with a little oil or butter for my mac n cheese. It is dry flakes, and it is just a flavor I like. Different brands can taste a little different from each other. A review mentioned sweetness; I don't notice that here at all. Just tastes within norm of all the other brands I use.

Nooch is either fortified or not fortified. Really doesn't matter in terms of taste, and really only matters if you are a vegan and find it a challenge to get enough B vitamins. So "fortified" adds in B vitamins. 'Non-fortified nutritional yeast does not contain added vitamins. It only contains the nutrients that are found naturally in nutritional yeast flakes. Non-fortified nutritional yeast still contains protein and many B vitamins, but in smaller amounts'.

I dont rate on price, but with this I want to say that it is at a good price point at $0.69 an ounce. I dont always buy based on price, but when it comes to nutritional yeast, I will usually choose based on price because they tend to all be the same to me. I would buy this again. So far so good!

I like that they show all the same info on the product page that is on the bag. Country of Origin says USA (I didnt expect that). Bonus!
PS. I like putting some into a shaker jar, like a parm cheese container with the big holes. If the flakes are too big for your preference, then simply smash them up a bit.

title: Puts the sour in sour cream-- too much citric acid in this; fine for baking or dips, just not plain
text:
Mix 3 parts water to 5 parts powder. Basically add enough water to make it the consistency you want. Then keep stirring to give it time to fully dissolve and become creamy.

It smells good, but the added tang may be a turn off if using this strictly as plain sour cream. The addition of citric acid may have been heavy handed. If they scale back on that, then the extra tangy, extra sour flavor would likely be reduced. I like Hoosier Hill products, and I went ahead and bought the largest size of sour cream powder. I figured they couldnt possibly get it wrong. Well I was wrong, it is just too sour. Mixes up gorgeous though-- perfect consistency, but that is all about the water to powder ratio.

I think it will work for use in anything that has other flavors to help reduce the sour in this sour cream. If making a dip, then be sure to use some strong seasons to temper it. I have a very forgiving set of taste buds, and this extra tangy, kinda "bites back" level of sour is off putting. I wont be using it on baked potatoes or for use in burritos, etc, which was really my main reason for buying it. Some of these dishes are dead to me if I cant slather it with sour cream. Sometimes I forget to buy a tub, or my tub has turned green and fuzzy. Powered to the rescue.. or not. :(

For my quick and easy sour cream anytime powder, I really like [[ASIN:B08ZCF267K Judees Sour Cream powder]]. Pricier, but it tastes so much closer to a tub of sour cream. I will likely stick with that, unless I hear/read that there has been an improvement on this formula.

Edit to add: overall I am getting used to the extra tartness.

title: it's GOOD, not junk. Natural taste, good flavor texture, smell. Eat cold or hot, little broth& salt
text:
I have ordered this Shredded Beef in Broth a couple of times now. Twelve, 7 ounce packets make for good portion sizes. 1 pack provides plenty for a couple of hearty eaters. I'm surprised by all the negative reviews, but it appears that those are several months old. When I am reading reviews I often make sure to sort by "most recent" as sometimes recipes, formulas, or other pertinent info changes.

I am truly pleased with this Hereford product. It has a natural taste, smells good, and it tastes fine direct from pouch or heated up (my picture is of a portion of the pouch-- maybe 1/3 to 1/2 of contents). Appears like a thin block of meat at first, but it totally becomes a nice bowl of juicy shreds once heated. Not too salty, just enough to make it tasty direct from pouch. Do what you want with it. I tried it with crackers.

Great option for those that dont have time or interest to cook beef. Or want smaller portion sizes to work from. Shelf stable until opened, so that further lends to the convenience. Also good for those that want the beef but not the gravy. I really can't see any need for improvement. Not sure what else can be done (still thinking about some of the comments). It is only shredded beef, some broth (just a little, you are paying for beef here, yay!), and some salt.

Are you a prepper (proactive and ready for sudden food needs?) Super amazing for stacking up food for emergencies, mega inflation, shortages and such. Adds variety (only so much chicken and tuna one can eat), and it makes it easy. Dont even need a can opener. Can be shared with furry family members in a pinch too.

I would add this to my hiking bag for sure. Or even as an MRE to stash in my car or BOB or GHB (bug out bag, get home bag respectively).

I also buy their packets of [[ASIN:B096G7FZJZ meatballs in spaghetti sauce]] here, and their corned beef which I get elsewhere.

title: Crumbles. Use to replace meat crumbles (ie ground meat) or to stretch ground eat based dishes
text:
If you can spring for the bulk bag then you will be saving quite a bit per ounce. Super helpful if you go use it often or are looking to stock your pantry. I currently have it stored as is in the big bag, but may break it down into smaller bags or jars for easier use and freshness control. I have used Bob's Red Mill TVP before (and often use a wide assortment of other products over the years). I find it to be a high-quality brand.

TVP is versatile. This is in crumble form, and so I use it in dishes that benefit from the crumble texture. I love using TVP to stretch ground beef, chicken, turkey, or sausage. Basically, anything that is a crumble texture. Whether it is in tacos, chili, spaghetti and meat sauce, I will portion out some TVP and add it to the mix. That allows me to use less meat and not compromise taste or texture. Nice way to simply reduce meat consumption if that is of interest to you and your family. For me is is more about cost savings first followed by reduction in red meat consumption.

Naturally, can also simply use it as a total swap. For that, you will definitely want to use seasonings that help give it the flavor you are trying to replace. Texturized Vegetable Protein doesn't really have a flavor in and of itself. I use powdered broth (beef or chicken) and complimentary seasonings to achieve a close flavor.

Anyway, it is a pantry staple. I use it enough to warrant a bulk purchase. Pricy all up front, but price per ounce is very good, especially if looking to save on meat products.

As of 11/2022: $93.53 ($0.23 / Ounce)

title: fresh loose tea makes all the difference, comprehensive kit for boba lovers
text:
Perfect little boba tea kit at a refreshingly reasonable price (currently $34.95 w/ $5 off coupon, $30 to be reasonable). When it comes to Thai tea, I normally don't care for it in boba tea as most restaurant preparations (or online kits) use instant tea. But with this having loose-leaf tea, I find it to have a much better taste. I tend to prefer a brewed tea for use in my boba creations, so this set works well in my favor.

Brew the tea, cook the tapioca pearls, make a simple syrup or use any flavor syrup or milk tea base

Pearls cooks up nicely. Has a nice chew.

I really like the addition of metal straws with optional silicone tips, a straw brush, and a clip scoop combo as well as an extra clip.

It is sweet, mildly spicy, slightly earthy, and subtly floral—making for a blend reminiscent of Southeast Asian dishes like Pad Thai or Massman curry. Of course, the predominant flavor in Thai iced tea is that of the tea itself. Start the boba tea party.

Add sugar and cream to taste. Recipe Thai Ice Tea:
(1) Add 4 tablespoons of the Pantai Thai Tea to 1 cup of boiling water.
(2) Drain out Tea Mix with a strainer. Add 2-3 teaspoons of sugar or to your liking.
(3) Stir well and serve with ice. Add a slice of lemon for Lemon Ice Tea.
(4) Ice Tea with Milk: Add 4 tablespoons of the Thai Tea Mix to 1 cup of boiling water.
(5) Drain out Tea Mix with a strainer. Add 2-3 teaspoons of sugar and 1-2 teaspoons of condensed milk or to your liking.
(6) Stir well and serve with ice or prepared boba tapioca pearls

title: bold coffee, unique flavor, smells good, tastes good, no problems whatsoever
text:
Been buying nearly exclusively Peet's since first trying the brand a few months or so ago. I originally tried Peet's coffee (medium roast, Big Bang) via an influencer thing, and was impressed by how bold it was for a medium roast. I really enjoyed it. My preference is dark roast coffee, black, unsweetened.. the darker the better. I want it bold, smooth, and chewy. I figured if Peet's can make a gorgeous dark leaning medium, then I must try one of their actual dark roasts. So I came here to find some (this is my 2nd or 3rd box now).

This is good! It is strong for a K-cup. I usually brew k-cups at 8 ounces for best flavor, but this can be easily brewed at 10 ounces. Try 6 ounces for extra bite, or for pouring over ice. I intend to try their other dark roasts, and even their decaf (occasionally I still want coffee but don't want the caffeine). This Major Dickason's Blend has a little something I can't quite pinpoint. It has a hint of tang that I normally avoid, yet that deep undertone of dark roasts keeps it solidly in my favor. I really like this, but it is maybe #2 or 3 in my list of preferred coffee, but it has been a repurchase! I see that they also offer other dark roasts, so I will be sure to try them out. My usual dark roasts are:
San Fransisco Bay Extra Dark Italian Roast
Green Mountain Dark Magic or Diamond

As for others in my household, my husband drank some and he is more of a Caribou medium or light roast drinker (blegh). I had my mom over for coffee, and I made this for her. She never knows what I am making, but usually it is a medium or dark roast. She definitely noticed that this was different and very good. She thought it had a good strong coffee flavor. She added a little cream and sugar. I drink it black.

I'm pleased. My box of loose cups is exactly as expected. No problems, no issues, no concerns. Will continue to buy.

title: perfectly good powder for making pastes, mayos, dips, coating dry snacks (peas, popcorn etc)
text:
It's pretty good. In my familiarity of wasabi powder and pastes, unless a product states that it is 100% pure wasabi, nearly all of them are a blend of ingredients, including food color. Another telltale sign in price. Pure wasabi is several dollars per ounce. This is $1.56 per ounce.

It is the kind of wasabi powder that I like for making wasabi mayo, wasabi snacks (like the dried peas, pretzels, nuts, popcorn, etc), and for other applications that I don't want to sacrifice the pure, pricy stuff for. Basically, I only need pure wasabi for sushi and sashimi, and even then I find the blends to be pretty good, and usually just buy the blends (in powder form or pre made paste).

I don't recall all the ingredients, but it uses regular horseradish, mustard, wasabi, some food coloring, and a few other ingredients. They don't have any of that listed here. I will take a pic and add it to my review.

Pale yellow color, doesn't smell or look like wasabi until it is mixed with water. ,Then that lovely taste and aroma develops. I think it is pretty good, and would consider it again. I down rate for not including an ingredient list here, or the country of Origin. That info IS on the packaging though.

I made a wasabi mayo for dunking fried cheese sticks in, and to lightly coat a steak sandwich. Basically reminded me of any other wasabi may or dip I have purchased. Definitely reminded me of the powder coating on wasabi peas.

Product of Republic of Korea (south Korea), Made in China

title: flavorful, adds deeper level of flavor to broths and such. Pantry staple in my house
text:
Similar in use as miso, but prepared differently. It is a pantry staple for me. I like adding it to broths and dishes that can use a little added umami. I'll even add it to a miso soup. This has a robust flavor that I enjoy. It is fermented, so expect a punch of aroma. Good soybean paste. Tastes as expected: mashed soybeans with added tang from fermentation. Soybean paste always reminds me of the consistency of hot dog sauce. I have used soybean paste for adding a little salty umami flavor to broths. Plenty of recipes that include this ingredient. It is a basic staple that adds a good depth of flavor. Overall easy to work with, so I recommend it if you are looking to up your cooking game. Adds that "certain something" that elevates flavor. Some soybean pastes are better than others, this being one of them, but also price reflect it (I dont rate on price). This is a big container. I am still working though one of my smaller containers. I keep this is fridge. Lasts forever it seems.

I like it 4.5 stars. I gave my other container that I like 4 stars and I happen to like this CYCO paste a little ore, so I am going with 5 stars.

title: Dark roast w/ delicate tang, mild spice, develops w/ ore sips. Kinda reminds me of Pfeffernüsse
text:
I love Peet's coffee, have enjoyed everything I have tried. I was intrigued by this Holiday Blend and decided to splurge on it. I am partial to dark roasts, and this is described as a dark roast (yes and no). "Dark Roast. Candied peel, dark chocolate, Indonesian spice. A spirited winter blend - lush, spiced, and citrusy sweet - drawn from the best crops of spring, summer, and fall". I say yes and no because at first I coulde pick up on some brightness which should never be in a dark roast. It is a tad tangy, BUT it breaths out dark roast and chocolate. So it is a matter of the flavor profile rather than the roast level. I can taste the dark roast. I assume the tang is the citrus peel, and any spice is subtle, yet develops with more sips. Something like a delicate cinnamon and ginger. It reminds me a little of Pfeffernüsse. It is nuanced, and does not have a strong kick of "holiday" flavor. But it is there if you have discerning taste buds. At the very least the packaging and cups look festive. I'd say there it has a stronger holiday vibe over starbucks.

I like it, would consider it again. Not sure yet if it is 5 stars to me. I will update if I change my mind.

title: My new must have spice for butternut squash, acorn squash. Nice added to broths. Interesting!

text:
Good addition to my pantry. Happened to be a good price which is why I bought it. Been purchasing groceries based on price then making meals based on that. In my experience the freshness and quality lasts for years, well beyond any best by date. I like creamy chicken because it goes with everything, can be doctored up, or can have broth added to it to use toward a big pot of cheap soup. Can further stretch it by adding in plain rice. It has a plenty of flavor (to me). Love Knorr products. Grow up: if you dont find it flavorful enough, why toss it? Donate it, or use other spices and flavorings to make it work.

Currently $22! It has gone way up in price since buying this last month ($8.57 regular price, a buck less for Subscribe & Save, which is what I did), further reinforcing the need to "buy what you can while you can". When I saw these for around a $1 per packet, I figured that was the going price for a couple of years, and would soon go up. Sure did! Now if you are looking at this.. eh, it may be a matter of having something in your pantry while you can still buy something even if the price isn't ideal. As prices goes up, availability goes down, issues with crops around the world will catch up soon. We have food now because we are still working off of old harvests. Etc. Just get what you can while you can. Shop sales, shop regularly to take advantage of sales, prepare meals based on sales, and keep stacking your cupboards! (if no room, then take a storeage container and tuck away in a closet, underbed, or make a table out of it).

BTW, I DO NOT rate on price. We can all see the price before ordering, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, and prices fluctuate frequently.

title: Turmeric, ginger, licorice, cinnamon, blackpepper, cardamom and cocoa (licorice can raise BP)
text:
Couple of things as it factors into my rating. The written portion is different than the package information. I chose this based on it saying, "This cocoa turmeric mix contains Cocoa obtained from Auroville, Cinnamon, Coconut Sugar with Cardamom and Ashwagandha." (<--NO!)

Instead, it has these ingredients: Turmeric, ginger, licorice, cinnamon, blackpepper, cardamom and cocoa.

So, not inaccurate depending on where you look. Not accurate depending on where you look.

It happens to have ALL the spices I like (except for licorice). I dont care for the taste of licorice, but can usually handle the flavor as part of a blend. I AVOID it though because it can increase blood pressure which is not good for those among us with elevated blood pressure. I would have passed on this if I saw the info in the picture. Instead, I went by the title headline AND the exact sentence I copied & pasted above.

Definitely not sweetened. I made it according to direction, and overall it is fine. Turmeric leads the flavor, cocoa sits in the background. I like the spice of ginger and black pepper. And I adore cardamom, but it is barely noticeable here. Same can be said of licorice.

If you want more chocolatey flavor, then add more of your own cacao. It definitely benefits from a base of milk (I use non dairy). I dont often sweeten my drinks, but this needs a sweetener. I like that they didnt add any sweetening agents.

Bag is well packed to the brim.

Overall I think it is OK. I am used to products like this, and I can tell this is of quality and freshness. Flavor profile is not quite for me despite having everything in it that I like. The discrepancy between package and written portion of product description is off putting.

4.5 stars: quality
4 stars flavor
2 stars discrepancy

Going with middle of road rating of 3. To me that means that is is "OK". I know it wont be a repurchase (if it was then maybe I would go up to a 4)

title: Ultra delicate tea, 70% tamarind, 30% butterfly pea (as seen on product picture)
text:
Well packaged. A bag within a bag. Individual tea bags with no string. Smells good. I used 1 bag for 6-7 ounces of water. Let it steep (I usually dont remove my bag while drinking), and it really didnt produce much flavor. It did develop a very faint, delicate, lightly sweet tea. I know butterfly pea is light in flavor, and tamarind can be a little spicy. Both have a hint of sweet. Zero spice. So I really didnt know what to expect. Well.. turns out not much. I can barely make out any flavor. I mean, its there if you have it on its own and your tastebuds are working, and it isnt paired with strong food. VERY delicate.

I did get flavor develop by just letting it sit. At that point, I could taste the gentle sweetness of butterfly pea, and the mild tang of tamarind. It IS nice, just needs more time or more bags per cup.

I think I would pop this into another mug of tea for the benefit, or when I am not needing a strong flavor. It may develop more flavor with more tea bags.

title: smokey, sweet, not too thick, not too thin
text: Smokey! Hint of sweet, light teriyaki flavor. Not too thick, not too thin. I don't mind smoke, but too much can give me a headache. I felt fine with this, but I didn't use much. title: grassy, earthy, fine powder. Within realm of normal but too grassy for my taste
text:
Turkish coffee can come in different roast levels. I have learned that the default roast level is VERY light, and this makes for a GRASSY tasting cup of coffee. I prefer a DARK roast, and it can be found in Turkish branded coffee, just harder to find. Some use a medium roast. This says "medium roast", and I definitely think it is light. Blegh. I find that if the brand doesn't directly say the roast level, then it is likely the light, grassy tasting variety. That is what this is. This is light and grassy. Pungent. Earthy. Rather off putting. BUT, it is within the realm of normal for Turkish coffee. Just not for me.

I was first introduced to Turkish coffee a couple decades ago. I tried it at a restaurant and immediately fell in love. I drank it straight up as is. I was made with a dark roast, had it not I doubt I would have liked it. After that, any other restaurant/coffee shop that had it on their menu was always a deep dark roast. Never grassy.

It is often prepared then served with a side of hot water so it can be diluted to a preferred strength.

I made this in my Ibrik over a gas stove (sauce pan can work too, but it is the narrowing "sides" that make the foam). There is a basic sequence to make Turkish coffee, and I pretty much fail every time. I am never able to achieve a nice creamy foam. It isnt the coffee, it is me. Basically coffee and water in the little pot, bring to a gentle boil- allow the foam to form, then back of the heat. Bring up the heat again to encourage more foaming. Done. Pour into small cups. Serve with side of hot water, maybe sugar, cream, cardamom. Plenty of video and written tutorials out there.

In the end: I really don't care for this. The grassiness is too much. Best suited for those that like light roasts. Not a factor of quality, and it is fresh and it is totally within realm of what I have had before of this roast level. So really comes down to preference.

FYI: Turkish coffee can be used with other brewing methods; it just won't create the same dense coffee. It won't be "Turkish coffee". Also, you can use any brand of coffee in the Ibrik (or cezve), just be sure to use an ultra-fine grind- you want it to be powder. Some stores will have a Turkish grind option on their grinding machine. If grinding at home--good luck. Keep grinding until it is a powder. No granules! Keep this in mind if you decide to use this in something other than an Ibrik because the powder will be sludge, and not let water to pass through as well. A French press would be good secondary option. Pour over if you have patience, or a drip if you leave enough space for water to slowly drain. Wouldn't bother in a reusable kcup.

Going with 3 stars "OK". They designated this as a medium, and this tastes like all the grassy light roasts I have had from Turkish brands.

text: It's fondant! Not sure what else to say :) It is pink with a vanilla aroma and taste. I dont often use fondant to make super fancy creations, but more for accent pieces as I can cut as place as I want. Good pliability, so if you want to use it to cover a piece of cake, it will work for that. I think fondant as a flavor is kind of weird, so limiting it to small decorations work for me. I mean, who eats this stuff other than a few bits? It is really a decorative thing that happens to be edible. Glad to have been able to try another color and size (normally I get the smaller package)

title: fun flavor combinations, no bitterness, just easy fizzy carbonation with mild flavors
text:
Love love love. I am such a fan of carbonated water, totally unsweetened, hint of essence. These VOSS sparkling waters have flavor combinations that are different than what I usually find or would have a hankering for. But I tried them all and like them all, probably Cucumber Lemon and Lime Mint being my favorites. The taste is very smooth and light. Some carbonated waters kick up the citric acid too much making for a bitter drink. Not here.. very smooth and easy to drink. For that, 5 stars. Totally pleasant to me. "Sugar free, unsweetened and created with natural flavors, this fruit infused flavored sparkling water is also calorie-free."

title: refreshing non caffeinated afternoon pick-me-up
text:
Love this brand. I find to be of quality and consistent freshness. There have been several teas I have tried from Teavity that I have liked, and only didn't quite suit me. I am pleased with this energizing non caffeinated herbal blend consisting of: organic moringa, organic peppermint, organic tulsi (aka Holy Basil), and turmeric.

I am always up for trying new blends, and this "Mental Focus" tea piqued my curiosity. I enjoyed a cup brewed at 8 ounces while going through some paperwork. It was pleasant. A nice herbal blend that is not too complex in flavor. I would say that it is peppermint forward, but not peppermint dominant. There are other layers of flavor. Hint of turmeric, a nudge of tulsi, and a back end finish of moringa. It's nuanced and I like it. Although I tend to prefer my tea stronger, I am getting used to how it turns out from a Keurig. It light and refreshing.

It may not be my usual taste preference for tea, but it makes for a pleasant afternoon pick me up when anything caffeinated is out of the question. I drank it hot, but my last couple of sips were cold. All good, and soon I will try it ice (maybe brew a couple at 6 ounces). I didn't add anything else to it, but I imagine it would be nice with a little sweetener.

title: dark brown densely packed sugar (w/ potassium ascorbate as preservative)
text:
Very good, as expected. I recently had some of this sugar in a cup of Mexican mushroom coffee. It was extra tasty. The flavor profile of this style of sugar is just better over white cane sugar. Adds something special. It has become my go-to sweetener for Turkish coffee.

Deep brown densely packed cones (Piloncillo) is made by crushing sugar cane and collecting the juice. The sugar cane juice is then boiled and reduced to a thick syrup (similar to molasses).

This includes potassium sorbate in the ingredient list

Product of Columbia

title: mild tasting matcha with 6 mushrooms blend, 1.5 tsp serving provides 25 mg caffeine
text:
I don't rate on price, but I comment. Currently $20.99 for 2.54 ounces, which makes it $8.26 per ounce. At this time there is a 15% off coupon, as well as an additional 15% discount if order 4 of their products (Or 10% with 3, 5% with 2). The current max price is actually quite reasonable. Especially for ceremonial matcha. I tend to pay a bit more than that. This also includes a variety of mushrooms, which is not cheap. So I think it is a fair price for a blend of mushrooms and ceremonial matcha.

My container was well sealed. Aroma is quite pleasant- smooth matcha and mild mushroom. I made it as I usually do with 1-2 tsp whisked with kettle boiled water. Mix well as matcha has a tendency to settle otherwise. Deep green, rather than bright, which I attribute to the addition of mushrooms (which tends to be brown, beige, reddish). So yeh, deep green doesn't surprise me. Basically looks like culinary, but not harsh.

Mild taste. A balanced, tempered, gentle flavor. Easy to drink. I consume matcha regularly for the benefits (ceremonial and culinary, from Japan, or China--this one is from China). Frankly I don't love the taste of matcha, but I drink it so often I have become attuned to the nuances of it. I love the way it makes me feel, and the antioxidant level is amazing. I feel like I get a better bang for my buck drinking matcha over brewing a bag of green tea leaves. More versatile too (nice addition to a smoothie!).

25 g caffeine per 1.5 tsp serving

I'm impressed enough to recommend this. I think it would be a good one for those that are new to matcha, and for those that also want to supplement with mushrooms. This product takes care of both in a reasonably priced, mellow tasting way. Just be sure to blend well and not use too much to ratio of water.

I'd give it 4.5 if I could. I think I am appreciating it enough to give it 5 stars. I really see nothing bad about it.

title: bright, tangy, citrusy, acidic: very much reminds me more of a light roast
text:
Too "light" for me. Quality and freshness are very good. The headline describes this as "Notes of Chocolate & Bright Acidity", and this is accurate. Kinda missed that and just saw medium roast. I prefer a deep dark roast, or a medium that is balanced (even better if it leans dark, haha). Not tangy. This happens to be a tangy, bright, acidic medium roast.

Actually, it reminds me more of a light roast with all its bright notes. A vibrant coffee with bright acidity and citrus notes. It doesn't mean it is a bad thing, it just means it really isn't for me. Yet, I don't mind it with some cream (normally I drink my coffee black). Has a quality taste even if it isnt my preferred taste. My husband and I do not share coffee as he prefers a medium or light roast. This is more his style. we'll use this up, and maybe I will consider trying their dark roast.

title: creamy, sweet, with kick of ginger. Nice anytime, hot or cold. Lovely on chilly evening
text:
Ingredients are not great, but I really like their products. Warm, creamy, with a kick of ginger. Sweet but not overly so. It isn't a daily drinker for me. More of a thing when I am in the mood for a hot drink. I go through phases where I have a craving for ginger. So this is a perfect combo. I really like their [[ASIN:B00KC7J2QO Matcha latte with Ginger]]. Sometimes I drink that as is, sometimes I add more matcha, or more ginger. Been buying that for a couple of decades now. Well recently I was about to order more when I saw this Ginger Latte. I already use honey ginger crystals, and sometimes I add matcha to it. So I am thinking.. what if I just get the cheaper Ginger Latte and then I can add matcha to it if I want the matcha flavor and caffeine? If I dont like it, then I can always go back to their Matcha Ginger latte.

I like it!

So far that works. It is very similar in the strength of matcha, and has same ginger kick, and level of creaminess. Same ease of preparation. I have been able to enjoy it in the chilly evenings without worry of caffeine keeping me up.

title: nice deep dark roast, bold taste, so delicious
text:
I love dark roast coffee. I like it strong, dark, bold, smooth, chewy. I drink it black, unsweetened. But sometimes I will fancy it up with a little cream. This works well with cream as the lovely tastet of their coffee still comes through. Smells so good!

I have their medium roast which is very good for a medium, as well as this dark roast. Both smell and taste good and fresh. I have a preference for dark, but a good medium is always welcome. Mmmmm just inhale the scent!
