title: buy what you can while you can, todays prices are investment over tomorrows.
text:
I bought 2 cans and they arrived in perfect condition. No dents. But even if they were, the product would still be fine. It's a dry product, and I have never had a breach in quality or performance. Ever.

Buy what you can while you can. Look for sales. I keep emergency packed items for mostly tucking away and forgetting about, but more recently have dug into my supplies. For example, when eggs went way up in price, I dug out my can of Augason Eggs I bought like 5 years ago for $20 (now sitting at $100!!). So emergency food doesn't need to be just for use in an apocalypse. But since we seem to be in a precarious spot *gestures vaguely at everything around the world* the need is something to seriously take action on. Be prepared, be proactive, have a robust pantry and other personal needs.

If that doesn't feel real enough, then consider it an investment with inflation. Yesterday's prices saved me money today. And today's prices will help offset tomorrows. Pick up a little extra every time at store, shop sales, and when considering emergency packed items make sure to consider variety and the overall calories. Even comfort items. Also, some items are less expensive (when on sale) over non emergency equivalent. For example, this creamy wheat product (at $8.99) It happened to be less per ounce than just going to the store (or ordering online) a box of creamy wheat (or name brand). If I get around to eating it soon, great. If not, then I know it is going to be fine for many years to come.

For actual emergency: these things float, they are a standard size (#10 cans) for easy stacking, cans can be repurposed, just takes a regular can opener (might want to add a couple more openers into your collection).

Augason is my go-to brand for emergency supplies. Good sales, good price point, consistency across the years and across various food types.

title: smooth, easy to work with, good flavor and freshness
text:
Fine powder, good flavor. I've purchased this a couple of times now. No problems with effectiveness, flavor, freshness, etc.

Fiber is 1 gram per 5 gram serving. Some brands indicate 6 grams or 10 grams or 15 grams for their serving size, and so the fiber is based on that (ie 2 or more). This has 1 gram, possibly a hair more. Not as much as some, but fairly close. Again take note of the weight (grams), and not just volume (tablespoon). Use more if you need to. Price is very good.

title: GREAT "Coffee tasting coffee" w/ punch of pumpkin a/ a kick of caffeine. What is this sorcery???!!
text:
I love Peet's coffee. I have a few brands I really like, but Peets has become my new go-to brand. They have so many options, and the coffee is simply very good. I prefer dark roasts, as dark as can be, black, unsweetened. I was introduced to Peet's (via vine) Big Bang, which is a medium roast. When I first had that I was floored by how dark it tasted. So that prompted me to check out their dark roast options. Immediately bought Major Dickenson's and loved that so much that I keep on buying it. At this point, I will try anything and everything by Peet's.

I happen to be one of those that love all things pumpkin once the cool weather hits. IT's a simple pleasure, and is fun to me. Brings a feeling of coziness and celebration. I love the fall, and this gives me a taste of it. I have a brand I already like for my pumpkin coffee, but decided to give Peet's a try. WOW, this is GOOD. I didn't even notice that it is a LIGHT ROAST. That is a roast level I prefer to stay away from because it is usually bitter, tangy, green, acidic, and overall just totally unpleasant to me. It is only NOW that I am writing this review that I decided to double check the roast level. WOWSA, so good. Light roast tends to have a little more caffeine over dark roast. And I definitely a feeling it with this. WoOoOOoOoOo!

Coffee tasting coffee with punch of pumpkin and a kick of caffeine. Good black, but flavored coffee usually is amplified by cream. If you like pumpkin coffee, give this a try!

title: pleasant easy flavor, balanced creaminess & sweetness, light coffee taste (w/caffeine kick!)
text:
Lightly sweet, lightly creamy, light coffee flavor-- but packs a caffeine kick. I think it makes a lovely cup of coffee for times when I want something quick, easy, tasty, and a little different than my usual very strong totally black coffee. This will also dissolve with cold water when shaken. I have made it with warm (or hot) tap water just to be sure it dissolves easy, shaken it, then poured it over ice. Extra nice as a cold drink, as I like my cold coffee to be a little sweet and creamy.

Comes down to preference. Try it, you may like it or not. You may prefer it over something else, or you may not. I happen to like it, and I happen to like this brand. I have been buying their instant ginger lattes, and matcha ginger lattes for over a decade now. I just happened to see this coffee come up and did an impulse purchase. I saw some of the brands that others mentioned, and when I looked at those reviews, it was also a mixed bag. SO I just went with this. I like it and would consider buying it again.

title: Seitan! budget secret for making inexpensive dishes that either replace meat, or help stretch meat
text:
I like Anthony's products, never have any issues with this brand. I have purchased this vital wheat gluten a couple of times now. I don't go through a lot, but I do keep some in my baking cupboard for the occasional loaf of bread. My main use for it though is when I make Seitan. I am not vegan or vegetarian, but I like to eat, and I enjoy trying out a variety of recipes from all sorts of diets, cuisines, etc. I find that my stomach often growls the most when I am perusing plant-based recipes (take note that plant-based means only that-- that the focus in on plants, but does not necessarily omit other food sources). I like the creativity that people come up with in using foods. Mmm I love to eat.

When it comes to seitan, it just looks so good, and costs so much less than the equivalent in a piece of meat. I have made lovely gravies to go over seitan "steaks", have made strips to use in "beef" stroganoff, and so on. Taste and texture is amusingly impressive. I am not at all pushing any sort of diet or way of eating, but if you are a curious eater, give it a try. If you are planning for the future and trying to figure out ways to stretch your meat budget (either adding in seitan to pieced of meat, or fully skipping a meat-based meal) then this is a wonderful option. Stretch that budget, get creative!! I use regular feef or chicken stock or bouillon to make gravies and add meaty flavor! I also use texturized protein products for same purpose, but for those that don't want to take in too much soy then making seitan is a good option. Obviously (?) this is not for gluten sensitive folks. Seitan is not hard to make but definitely follow a recipe and get good at making one type of item. Let that be your go to option.

Seitan is high in protein and fairly low in calories, fat, and carbohydrates. It also contains a number of minerals. "Compared to beef loin, seitan contains fewer calories and less fat but nearly the same amount of protein"

title: tightly sealed so didn't open, buy what you can when you can, if there are bugs--so what
text:
My container, from Lot dated Sept 2022 (acquired 10/22), is very securely sealed. So much so, that I don't want to open it. I bought it to have if/when I need it. I have plenty of rice that I will use up first. I bought this specifically knowing that it should still be good 7 years from now. Brown rice does not have as long as of a shelf life due to its natural oils and such, so I simply don't add it to my long-term pantry supplies. But when I saw an emergency packed container at a reasonable price, I more or less made an impulse purchase. It was similar price or less than other regular stuff I'd buy off the shelf, and I don't need to pack it special for long term storage. This is done for me.

Since I did not open it, I cannot say if there are any bugs. I prefer not to have them, but in reality, I really don't care. There are always (always, always) bug eggs in grains, flours, and pasta (etc). Always. Sorry to say. Freezing will kill the eggs to keep them from hatching into bugs, but don't ever think that you don't eat bugs. Ya do. So, if there ends up being bugs, I will likely just pick them out. Or not. If this is opened when all else has dwindled away, the bugs will provide added protein. I'm not kidding. So, consider it a bonus feature?

Good luck all. Buy what you can while you still can.

title: good taste & texture, not too smokey, kinda salty, but overall pretty good
text:
Good flavor, good texture. Smoke isn't too strong. Once later in day I had a "smoky burp". But not a fishy one. I like this direct from can, or scooped out onto crackers and cheese. I keep it simple.

The cans aren't really all that great. They have a soft-ish top, and the tin is on the soft side. Mine were all dented but that is because they tossed my cans in with super heavy items (a gallon of molasses, a box of shelf stable almond milk, and huge laundry soap--so ridiculous). I wouldn't bank on this for extended storage (ie, prepping), but I would put it into rotation just for variety.

Money saving tip (if you can do it): Currently $2.24 on Subscribe & Save (at max 15% discount). If you order 12 of them single (well 10 at time is max, I think), it is cheaper than the 12 count Subscribe & Save option (at max 15% discount). title: 3.5 stars: chamomile forward, hint of flavor, need more than 1 bag for flavor development
text:
It is a pleasant tea, but it isn't strong on ginger which is what I am looking for. This is chamomile forward, with an ever so light lemongrass flavor. Ginger is in the background. I really could not tell you that it has peppermint, clove, cinnamon, black pepper, ginger. I made it with 5 ounces of water to 1 tea bag, and let it steep for 10 minutes. It was so light tasting that I double checked to see what I got. I thought maybe I got plain ginger instead of "chai" spice. Nope, it says Spice on it, and the ingredients match up. Just the flavor doesn't.

Again, it isn't bad. Just light, and mostly chamomile. I will likely need to use 2-3 tea bags to produce the flavor I am looking for. Or I will pair it with another more flavorful tea bag, or use it as base to add my strong [[ASIN:B09MVD36DK honey lemon ginger crystals]] . 3.5 stars

Ingredients:
Organic chamomile, organic lemongrass, organic ginger, organic cinnamon, organic black pepper and organic clove.

Country of Origan: Sri Lanka

title: INGREDIENTS: coffee, Cocoa, Piloncillo, cinnamon, cardamom, 6 mushrooms. Tasty, caffeine kick!
text:
It's the cardamom. I was trying to think of why this tastes so appealing to me, and I realized it is the cardamom. It pairs so well with coffee (often used in Turkish coffee), and it works so well here. YUM.

I use as assortment of mushroom powder daily. I like adding it to my coffee. I like my coffee black, unsweetened, yet the addition of mushroom (as well as collagen) doesn't impart any flavor. Minimal anyway. So same goes here. No distinctive mushroom flavor. Sweet. Light coffee flavor. Good caffeine kick. No idea how much mushroom is in it. So I wouldn't necessarily use this as my sole source of mushroom supplement.

I made it according to directions: 8 ounces (actually 8.45 oz) water to a packet. A little thin, and not a strong coffee flavor. Yet, I dont want to add anything to it. I find that is very pleasant as is. I haven't made it with less than 8 ounces. I still have a cup of regular coffee, but this just has an extra nice flavor. They also make a decaf version, as well as sweetened or unsweetened for both. This is the sweetened version which uses Piloncillo (an unrefined raw brown sugar). Very tasty to me. The deep sweet taste of Piloncillo intrigued me enough to look into buying that separately for drinks and baking.

I dont rate on price (we can see the price before ordering, we have different budgets, preferences, needs, prices fluctuate, etc). This is a cube of TEN packets for $12.99 (so, $1.29 per cup)- while a tad steep as a daily drinker, it isn't outside the norm of my shopping experience. I really like this, so it may be something that I add to my cart for the occasional treat.

Ingredients: Coffee, Cocoa, Piloncillo, cinnamon, cardamom, mushroom extract (reishi, shiitaki, lions mane, cordyceps, turkish tail)

title: Surprisingly strong, can easily halve the recommended amount
text:
I've used their Immune Support as well as their Energy blend. They are all strong and tasty. This Digestion blend is similarly good. I couldn't really taste any difference between them, but mushrooms are mild in taste and all that is different is the types of mushrooms used. All good.

I use more water than the recommended amount or use less powder, and still get a stout tasting cup of coffee. Using a full tablespoon to 8 ounces of water is really too much for me. Which is impressive since I like my coffee as dark and strong as can be; I like it to bite back. This made according to their directions is even too intense for me. Yet that actually works well in our favor. Can stretch this a bit!

I like it black, and I like it paired with cream. Fun with added syrups and such too.

I don't mind instant coffee, it is in my rotation. I like it for the simplicity, and dont even mind the taste. I have had instant coffee infused with mushroom before and they never seem to say how much mushroom is in it. But I still like keeping a tub of it on hand. I regularly use mushroom supplements.

I like that this dissolves easily, and can be dissolved even with cold water. So go ahead and make an easy iced coffee (or good to go in an emergency!)

title: Chai with benefits. Well balanced, warming & comforting. Chicory base, mildly sweet, very nice
text:
Lovely, spicy chai. Chai means tea, and while there are some standard chai formulas out there, Chai can embrace a variety of spices. But for the most part, the overall expectation from any chai is something with a lot of body, earthy, spicy, layers of flavor and comfort. I am most used to and tend to prefer the black tea based variety, but I am always open to trying something new. Rasa makes fantastic blends, so I was eager to give this option a try. The uniqueness of this Golden Chai is that it doesn't use black tea, but instead chicory. It gives it a more hearty mouth feel more akin to coffee. Quite nice. Here is the ingredient list:

Chicory*, Burdock*, Saigon Cinnamon*, Roasted Date Seed, Shatavari*, Codonopsis*, Ginger*, Dandelion*, Eleuthero*, Turmeric Extract (BCM-95®), Cardamom*, Vanilla*, Cloves*, Black Pepper*, Boswellia Extract (AquaLOX®), <1% maltodextrin & gum acacia
*Organic

Has a hint of natural swweetness, a gentle kick of spice, a mild tang of tumeric, and a gentle comforting aroma and flavor that is very nice on a chilly fall afternoon.

Be prepared to use a French Press or Moka pot. I use a French press. The tea is course and twiggy. It brews nicely within a few minutes. I prefer mine with some sort of creamer. I have used unsweetened macadamia milk, and have used their [[ASIN:B0BF2X14SD non dairy Premium Functional Oat & Coconut Powder creamer]] just be sure to froth before adding to your drink. I dont need it sweetened, but I imagine a spoonful of honey would also be very nice, especially if feeling run down.

The turmeric is evident but not over-powdering. It is a well balanced Chai, and one that I would consider again. I DO recommend the Rasa brand. I haven't tried anything I didnt like. The quality is there. Pricy, but the products offer a lot in terms of additional herbs, supplements.. making it a nutraceutical.

title: Typical texture of oat/coconut, added supplements, be sure to BLEND! Awesome result for coffee
text:
READ ON for CLARIFICATIONS!!
******Please follow directions, you will be sad if you don't. It states on the product page and on the bag to FROTH this, as in, prepare it with a blender, frother, or shaker cup. Whatever you have to make this mix with liquid. THIS IS THE NORM for oat powder and coconut powder. Use some water, your coffee, or RASA product (love their nooptropic and nutraceutical "teas"). Or add a splash of your drink to a cup, mix with this, then top of the rest of your cup. It DOES dissolve with a frother. It DOES NOT dissolve with a spoon, even with aggressive stirring. Again, it is all in the directions. I took a pic of what it looks like if you just dump it on top and stirred with spoon versus using a frother.

Probably asking yourself why bother then? That's up to you. This style of creamer is just how it seems to be across the board. So another brand of similar ingredients will just be the same way.

This isn't "just" a creamer. It is marketed as a creamer but it has so much more in it that it is also a considered a supplement. Mushroom, L-theanine, ginseng, amla, and MCT oil. Use at least 2 grams for benefit, though use 1 full TBS to get your coffee to lighten.

If you need just a "creamer" then go with liquid, or a milk solid or non dairy powdered creamer. If price is an issue, and need bare bones cheap, then definitely don't go with products that have additional supplements. Even plain oat & coconut powder can be pricy, and even those on their own (not formulated to be a "creamer") are even worse at dissolving unless care is taken to PRE blend it. RASA brand is pricy (to me) but I dont rate on price. Another good option of similar ilk is [[ASIN:B0971SFMZJ Laird Superfood Creamer]] which is a bit less and they have several options in their brand. Side by side, similar performance in terms of "creamer". Added supplements will vary.

Basically I am saying that this product is pretty much the norm. I like it.

Have you had powdered oat & coconut creamers before? Not liquid, but powdered from a bag? The texture, taste, and performance is all the same. Thick, clumpy, and with very little "creamy" mouthfeel. Any flavor is extremely mild, any taste is negligible. Smell is always nice. EVERY single time I try one, I ask myself why I bother, haha. BUT, and this is BIG REASON.. I find that I like them when I use 3x the amount (2-3 TBS). and BLENDED. Like, takes on a whole new vibe when run through a blender. Kind of gives my coffee extra body, and makes me feel full longer. Lights me up, sparks joy, whatever. But just added to a cup and hope it mixes? no, those are sad times, haha.

When I saw that this is from RASA brand (high quality brand to me, I have had a lot of products by this brand), I had to know what their version is like. It is exactly as expected from MY previous experience with multiple brands of "oat-coconut" powder creamers.

I like that they give nutritional information for the 3/4 tsp (2 gram) minimum, and then the info for the more likely to be used 1 TBS (8 grams). I also appreciate that they list both volume and weight designations.

I wish they listed how much of the supplement is in X amount of product. Hence, 4 stars.

I know I wrote a lot, but I had a lot to say. Happen to be drinking a cup of [[ASIN:B0BCX3S19X fresh coffee blueberry crisp]] BLENDED with this Rasa "creamer", and I feel chatty. Thanks for reading. Take care! :)

title: happy w/ popping performance, freshness, packaging, add to their other products as gift
text:
I'm not even a fan of popcorn, and I find this to be pretty good. My husband is a fan of popcorn and nearly exclusively makes microwaved popcorn. I think this tastes better than the prebagged types, smells better too. Just use your own bowl and lid, and add in some oil. Popping times will vary. I see that they have their own bowl and a variety of flavorings. That piqued my interest as an upcoming gift. Popcorn, bowl, flavor toppings all by same company. That would make a nice gift. I'm trying to get gifts figured out well ahead of time.

title: at 1 tsp per cup, this will make no more than 4 cups per tin (24 for box). Really nice tea though!
text:
"Approximately 10 cups of tea per tin". More like, per box. Excellent tea, just not much of it. Nice sampler.

The tea industry standard for measuring loose leaf tea is about 2-3 grams of tea per 6-8 ounces of water. My guideline is to use a little more at 1 tsp (4 grams) per 6 ounces of water. Following the standard, this 95 gram box, which is 15.8 grams per tin, makes for 5-8 servings per container. Going by my slightly greater amount, makes for just under 4 cups of tea. THIS happens to also be the amount that is indicated in the directions. Your experience may greatly vary based on your preferences.

Even so, this falls short of the "Approximately 10 cups of tea per tin". There would need to be at least 20 grams per container. I really dont mind as I see it as a sampler, and it keeps the tea fresh.

Attractively packaged inside and out. Smells good, tastes nice, no concerns regarding quality. Just dont expect 10 cups per tin (60 per box), more like 4 cups per tin for 24 servings per box.

title: super thick large bags w/ rope tie off, brining bags only (do not put in oven), no instructions
text:
Very thick bags. Definitely thickest I have used, largest too. Comes in super simple basic packaging, includes tie off string (more rope like!). Good sized bags. Use it for your turkey or any other brining (or marinading) needs with any other protein. Pack of 2!

There aren't any instructions. Not sure if it needs any? Put your protein in, put in your brining or marinade ingredients. Tie off, let sit for 12-24 hours in fridge.

Even so, I downrate, as the information on this page is potentially confusing (or dangerous). In one spot it says it can withstand heat up to 250*f, but then in another spot it says that it can " withstand high temperature cooking and low temperature refrigeration". NO!! As far as I know, a BRINING bag is not meant to be used to bake/roast/cook in. That is what a "roasting bag" is for. In fact, dont let brining bags come into contact with heat at all.

It would be good to have that info clarified here (and to make the two pieces of conflicting info cleared up), would hate for anyone to ruin their pricy thanksgiving dinner by thinking they could put this in oven.

title: easy flavor, even tastes good at room temp. Bigger cans compared to competition, very pleased!
text:
I know, it's simple.. it's their 5 hour energy formula with added carbonated water. Yet, it is so much better! The shots are neat to have on hand when you just need to grab some very quick caffeine and not take in additional fluid. Other times, I want a drink. Maybe I am thirsty, maybe I just want to sip on something over the course of an hour or so.

These are 16 oz cans! Three packs of 4 cans. 3 flavors. All good (to me). Currently $29.99 for pack of 12. I find this within range of many energy drinks, and a bargain compared to my beloved [[ASIN:B099V9Y63L GOAT Fuel energy drink 200mg 12 oz can]] which is solidly into the 30s. I dont rate on price.

What I like about this is that it doesn't have that energy drink taste. It doesn't bite back. I'm always hesitant with the first sip. But this is smooth, sweet (not too over the top sweet, but it is sweet) and nice bubbles. It is easy to drink. It is actually pleasant (to me). It even tastes great at room temp. Some brands aren't remotely palatable until refrigerated. These are totally fine just sitting out.

230 mg of caffeine per can. That's doable. I am not a fan of the ones that are much above that, because I do also drink coffee. My usual energy drink is 200 mg per can, but that is for a 12 ounce can. This is 16 ounce can. I dont drink energy drinks every day, but they are part of my life. I usually use an energy drink after I have factored all other caffeine sources in, then use it to power up a workout or a physical set of chores, or a super boring one that needs the added motivation, haha.

Great job 5-hour Energy! I recommend!

title: surprisingly good chili, tastes fresh, can even be eaten cold, no heat, cumin forward, tasty!
text:
Two bean beef and tomato chili. Very good flavor. Zero heat, so you will want to add your own or try their [[ASIN:B004S036DG spicy but not hot hot Stagg Dynamite chili]]. Has a strong cumin flavor. Overall tastes quite fresh, like something one would make at home (minus heat). For ingredient list, take a look at their product pictures. That image is accurate. Ignore the written portion as that is not the same as what is listed on my can. Also ignore that it says that it is "vegetarian" lol why?

All my cans look good, no dents. Can be eaten as is, or use it to flavor up other chili base, or use over rice, pasta, chips, etc. I normally dont just buy canned chili as use as a chili. For that, I prefer to make my own. But I can eat this as a bowl of chili. Or I would add this into a homemade chili. And I would use it on just about anything else. So yeh, pretty good on its own or over other stuff. But that's just me. Your experience may vary.. so take reviews as just that. I would look for comments pertaining to quality-- dented cans, weird taste beyond realm of reasonable, if anything looks off, etc. A simple "yuk" or "yum" is just an opinion. That being said, I find this to be "yum". haha

Tastes good at room temperature too. Just grab a spoon, peel back that lid, and eat up. There is no coagulated fat or gross bits. I'm rather impressed with this Brand, and this specific variety of chili.

Basically.. it is a good addition to long term pantry/emergency food. Has good amount of protein, fiber per serving. 2 servings per can, loaded with sodium as to be expected. Lends to a long shelf life. Not too shabby a price. I do not rate on price as I can clearly see the price before purchase. It isnt a mystery. Also, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, there are price fluctuations, price and demand, availability etc. So, if price looks good to you, then go for it. I try to buy canned meals like this when they are around $2 per can, but that is becoming more and more rare, unfortunately. But look for sales, or if you have the budget, please fill up your pantry NOW while you still can. Best to have extra.

Generous 5 stars as it pretty much meets my expectations all around. I would buy this again, and I do recommend it.

title: Do you like pina coladas? Tropical flavor, zero cinnamon, not how I know "horchata" to taste
text:
Not at all what I expected, but pleasantly surprised anyway. Read on to understand why I am going with 3 stars (though review headline pretty much says it all). Good price, good flavor, just not "horchata"

I have had Horchata in a variety of restaurants, and have had powder mixes to make at home. They all have tasted nearly all the same, so I figured that this Horchata would be the same. It is very very different than anything I have had. Does it mean it's bad? No, but it isnt what I think of when I see Horchata. So, now I wonder if this is supposed to be what a horchata is supposed to taste like (and everything I have had is wrong), or if this is just a fruity take on the drink. But I would not have guess "horchata" when I drank it.

I dont taste cinnamon, at all. That's the main thing. I strongly taste coconut and something fruity. It absolutely reminds me of a pina colada. Is it possible that my bag is filled with their coconut option? I'll never know. Funny thing is, is that it is rather good. The more I sipped, the more I liked it and found it hard to stop drinking it. I will drink this up, but not as a "horchata".

For a more creamy drink, use milk (or non dairy milk) instead of water. It is watery otherwise. Light. Most horchata I have had has been much creamier.

It dissolves well with assertive stirring.

If this wasn't labeled Rice & Cinnamon Horchata, I would just think this is a tropical drink. But it resembles nothing of horchata as I know it, and I cant even taste cinnamon. For THAT, 1 star.

BUT

The flavor is really good as a tropical drink. Has a pina colada vibe to it. Has a pleasing flavor. I will drink it up. For that, 4-5 stars.

YET, I am not going with a high rating. I will split the difference and go with 3 stars.

title: tasty gruel, make as thick or thin as you want. Lightly sweet, lightly savory, very comforting
text:
Fantastically comforting. Just perfect on a cold, dark, damp fall morning. I'm not new to this style of gruel, but something about this just really works for me. I think because I find it pleasant made simply as is. Can use as much or as little water as you want to get the consistency you prefer. I like making it into a thick sipping gruel. Bland with flavor, if that makes sense. It isn't a strong flavor, but it has good flavor. Lightly sweet, could be altered to be sweeter or more savory. Can add bits of food, spices, or simply just have as is. I absolutely adore this particular gruel. It really hits the spot. Downside, I tend to use too much which really bumps the calories up (100 cals per TBS). If looking to boost calories, this may be an easy to digest way to do it.

My stomach is easily irritated and I often skip breakfast, or I keep it simple with a smoothie. Now that the weather has turned chilly, I am not really feeling the smoothie. I tend to make simple soups, sipping broths, teas. I have added this into the mix, and it is here to stay. I love sipping it, but I also really enjoy it when I make it thick enough to use a spoon (actually tastes a bit different).

title: pleasant medium roast, fine black or with cream, dry matte beans, grinds to reddish hue
text:
Pretty good medium roast. I tend to prefer dark roast, but I can handle a well balanced medium. This is not too tangy, has a flavor that is doable for most drinkers. I can make a pot and share it, whereas if I make my preferred dark roast then no one else wants any. Wimps.

I normally drink my coffee black, unsweetened. I use creamer when the coffee is tangy, acidic, bright. This medium can be consumed black, but I prefer it with a splash of cream. For sake of review I usually will do a cup with cream so I can report if the coffee flavor itself is reduced any. The coffee flavor with this cuts through cream, leaving a coffee tasting coffee. Thats good.

Beans are matte brown, no oil, makes for a reddish hued grind. Smells good, seems fresh.

I probably wouldnt buy the medium again, but I like what I had enough to be curious about their dark roast offering.

title: syrup viscosity, floral-fruity taste (reminds me of lychee), natural, low glycemic, 4.5 stars
text:
Everything looks good on my end. 8.8 ounce jar of Yacon syrup. Typical size, taste, aroma.

Are you new to yacon syrup? It has a lightly fruity floral taste, and doesn't work with everything. I dont fault the brand, it really comes down to taste preference in sweeteners. It is viscous like Agave, or other syrups, with a hint of lychee fruit flavor. More mild than honey. Yacon sweetener is a pantry staple (syrup style or powder) for me because it has such a good nutritional profile. Because yacon products are not the most budget friendly, yet I still find great value in using it, I tend to use it more for the health benefits and low impact on sugar levels, than just as an anytime sweetener (but I really should use it more).

The slight fruity floral taste also limits my use, but there is plenty to do with it. I use it anywhere I would honey. So for me, I dont use it in coffee, but I use it in tea, matcha green tea, on hot oats, plain yogurt, in "protein powder balls" snacks, and even a little off the spoon. Not a strong sweetness, more low key. I imagine it can be used fine in baking, but unless it is a healthy recipe, I'd rather just use sugar or cheaper syrups. BUT I'm trying to reduce my sugar intake and this is an EXCELLENT product to use as it is low in sugar anyway, and it doesnt impact blood sugar levels like other sweeteners. It's good, and really worth the try.

Perfectly good yacon syrup. Price is same as an organic brand I buy. 4.5 stars

more infoDrAxe
"Yacon root syrup contains a high percentage of fructooligosaccharides, which are prebiotics that pass through the upper part of the gastrointestinal tract and remain undigested. When fructooligosaccharides reach the colon undigested, they are then fermented by gut microflora, increasing bowel mass and promoting the growth of beneficial bacteria. For these reasons, yacon root syrup can be helpful when it comes to digestive issues, such as providing natural constipation relief and treating traveler’s diarrhea"

title: Makes 4 cups, not oily, lots of flavor, tad salty, easy to make in a basic rice cooker
text:
One pouch makes up a lot of food. After it was done cooking, I transferred it into a 4 cup pyrex container, and it was filled to the brim. I had to pack it down some. Reheats well.

I cooked this in my [[ASIN:B0001XAG8W Cuisinart rice cooker]]. I did the usual 1 cup rice to 2 cups water ratio. Let it do its thing, and it cooked up very nicely. When in the packet, the rice and lentils are coated in oil and seasonings. I didnt change a thing. The end result was not oily at all. Just moist, yet fluffy. Plenty of flavor, but not overpowering. Spicy but not hot. Very nice as is. Good texture and flavor. I did find it a tad salty. Is the around of sodium off? because it seems to be really low for what is listed and the taste.

Having a convenient packet of rice AND lentils, and being perfectly flavored and cooks up really well. AND makes quite a bit, I think the price is reasonable. Currently $21.99 makes it $5.50 per pouch. I do not rate on price.

title: fresh, clean, well packaged, high-quality product from a high-quality company. No problems!
text:
Quality brand, quality product. Pricy yes, but if it looks good to you go for it.

I make a batch of amaranth on occasion. I keep a wide variety of grains/seeds/cereals on hand for nutritional variety and culinary intrigue. That being said, I don't use amaranth often, and so the smaller 8 ounce bag is perfect for me. Yes, it is at a much higher price point than larger bulk bags, that's how it works. But I would be tempted to spring for a larger bag given the great price difference. I do not rate on price as we can all see price before ordering, have different budgets, preferences, needs, prices fluctuate, etc. My focus is on quality, and this brand is of quality. I have had a few products now, and am very pleased with the quality, taste, freshness, clean appearance, lots of info, etc.

Amaranth is a pretty versatile grain as it works well both in savory and sweet applications.

title: warm up on cold days, easy to prepare, filled to the brim, nice flavor, easy on gut
text:
Good flavor, chicken-y, not too salty, easy to prepare, nice way to warm up on cold days. Belly filler when not wanting a meal. I didnt find the need to add anything to it. I like it as is. I would buy it again.

Take outer lid off, peel back inner lid very carefully as the container is truly filled to the brim, microwave uncovered for a minute or so, then put outer lid back on. I like taking this on the go and sipping it while driving to work, or as a quick light snack, etc.

title: perfectly sweet, feel warmth of ginger. So lovely on chilly fall day. I use 2tsp to 7oz water
text:
Oh, this is delightful. I tried it dry on the tip of my finger as was disappointed that I really only tasted sugar. Then I went ahead and proceeded to make a cup. I boiled some water in a kettle, then added around 7 ounces of water over 2 full teaspoons of this granulated ginger sugar. I was relieved when my first sip was noticeably sweet and gingery. The ginger gently kicks the back of the throat. I LOVE ginger, and I usually drink [[ASIN:B002SWB73C Prince of Peace Honey Ginger Crystal Packets]]. So this is a very nice change up. Easy to make it as strong or as weak as you like. I dont really intend to do anything with it other than drink it as a "tea", or added alongside a teabag. I drink it plain, or I have it with a little non dairy milk. I just had some with a [[ASIN:B092L9B97C splash of vanilla meal replacement drink]] which I typically drink one of those a day, but will sort of sip on it through the day or add it to coffee or tea. Anyway, OMG, it was so nice after coming home from work on a dark, chilly, fall afternoon to rest a little bit with a hot cup of sweet ginger drink. Not too sweet, just right. Good amount of ginger (but is there ever enough for us ginger lovers?)

Anyway, very pleased. BTW, 2 tsp is approximately 10 grams, which is the serving size. There are 300 grams in this container, making it a 30 serving item. Little pricier per serving than my usual brand, but I dont rate on price. This is good. Probably stick with Prince of Peace, but I would consider this again. Yum!

title: bold coffee with hint of flavor. I dont normally care for flavored, & this is perfect to me
text:
I have the Great Eight variety pack, which includes: hazelnut, caramel, vanilla, mocha, coconut, blueberry crisp, maple creme, Jamaican Me Crazy. The coffee is strong, and the flavors are mild. Those that like a punch of flavor won't find that here. This is subtle (at least all the ones I have tried so far). I brew it at 8 or 10 ounces, usually add some cream. I find flavored coffees are enhanced by the addition of cream. Otherwise black is my preference.

I don't care for Hazelnut in general, but that was the first I tried. I just sort of assumed it would be awful, haha, but I tried it because I was going to pass it on to my mom and her partner who like hazelnut if this was a strong enough tasting coffee. She says a lot of hazelnut coffees are very weak. Not the hazelnut flavoring, but the coffee itself. Says most taste like flavoring only. This Fresh Roasted hazelnut is coffee tasting FIRST (and robust at that), and a hint of flavor second. Not a punch of flavor. Hint. I can drink this. SO, that may be good or bad depending on what you are looking for in a coffee.

Caramel is smooth and light, with that bold coffee taste coming through. Vanilla is same. Jamaican Me Crazy has a low key rum-ish taste? Cant quite figure it out. I can drink this black (my preference for unflavored coffee). It is strong. I'm getting jitters trying all this coffee, haha

For reference, my preferred coffee is black, unsweetened, as dark as can be. Dark roast, maybe dark leaning medium. Can be brewed, poured over, French press, or even instant, but often K-cups. Very rare that I want a flavored coffee because the flavors are almost always so cloying and artificial tasting. I get a weird desire for flavored come fall/winter, so I do keep some on hand (I love "Wake the Hell Up" brand). I have had Fresh Roasted brand before and liked it so I figured I would give this flavored variety pack a try when the opportunity came up. I partly expected a big box of awful. But am really impressed-- because the coffee is bold and the flavoring is light. <<<---- this last part may make this not for you if you are used to and prefer the other way around-- strong flavor and weak coffee.

My star rating is specific: good bold coffee that has a hint of flavor. First time I ever liked hazelnut. Fresh, gives me energy, works fine in my Keurig

title: good ingredients, no artificial colors, good balanced flavor--sweet w/ mild tang. Nice simmer
text:
I like this better than many. I think because it isn't as cloying tasting, not as artificial. This is mellow and the flavors are balanced yet is clearly a teriyaki sauce (sweet with tang. Not a spicy sauce, teriyaki rarely has hot spice). I boosted the ginger with a little extra of my own. A dash of [[ASIN:B06Y2DMLQ8 the best sesame oil ever]] deepens the flavor further. I don't feel like (and it doesn't taste like) I ate a condiment as some known brands can impart. It is a simmer sauce, and maybe it is just phrasing or maybe it makes a difference.

States that it is an authentic Japanese recipe. This world cuisine brand has offerings inspired from other regions of the world. Their Indian options greatly pique my interest. Really like the ingredients, and that they dont use artificial colorings.

They have the price per ounce wrong on the listing. The current price is $26.99 for 8 packets containing 7 ounces each. At 56 ounces, that is $0.48 per ounce, not $3.86 (the smaller pack of 4 at 17.49 is $0.62 per ounce, not $2.50). $3.37 and $4.49 per packet respectively. Reasonable in my sphere of purchasing.

They have lots of other flavors, some at different price points, some with Subscribe and Save options.

title: sharp but not bitter, sour but not too tart. Citrus forward with pine finish. Intriguing flavor!
text:
I dont know all yet what I am going to do with this Yuzu juice. But I know it has cocktail, mocktail, and culinary uses that I have yet to explore. The taste is on point: has a grapefruit and lemon vibe with a light pine finish. Very interesting and appealing to me. Dry tasting. I sipped it off one of the included spoons. Pale yellow appearance. I see myself using in an aperitif or maybe digestif. I like a sightly sour, dry, hint of sweet flavor profile. The pine (or whatever it is) is interesting. It isnt a forward tasting note, more of a finishing note, breathing out note.

Seems that a little will go a long way. Half a spoonful is plenty for me--kind of like using straight lemon juice but without as much lip puckering tang.

Attractive little bottles, well-sealed. Two broth spoons (not sure of technical name).

I haven't had this before on its own, so I not sure if this is same or better than other product listings. But I like it, and it is right up my alley for taste preference. I'd consider it again, and I would recommend it.

title: healthy comforting soups, eat as is or doctor up. Variety pack nice way to try all flavors
text:
The variety pack is a great way to try 4 flavors before committing to any one flavor. All the flavors in this can be purchased separately in same quantity and price. I have liked them all, some more than others. None are overly strong in flavor, some may think too bland. Not too salty. Not a lot of texture, but not totally watery. All fresh tasting. All easy to heat, all could be eaten cold if need be. Eat as is, or doctor it up a bit. All low in calories (130-180), might be best paired with a sandwich or something to really fill belly. Other than the chickpea, none really require any chewing. Might be excellent choice if having dental issues, etc.

[[ASIN:B0BBSLMXYZ Lentil Curry]] : I love lentils, so my expectation was extra high. I find this falls a little short in the texture department. It could use more bits of food. Extra low calories make it nice for adding volume to stomach before a meal so as to not over eat on higher calorie items. 4 stars

[[ASIN:B0BBSMSKLR Tomato Chickpea]] : Mild flavor, good taste and texture. Has more substance than lentil option. Gives my mouth something to do since some chewing is involved. Really like this one. 5 stars

[[ASIN: B0BBSLLZMNCheesy Broccoli]]: I love the smell of this one. Has that nutritional yeast aroma and flavor. Comforting; might be my favorite for that reason. Even tasted good cold. Lots of broccoli bits, albeit doesnt add much texture (similar to other broccoli cheese soups). Some bits of potato. Would do well with added broccoli or served with rice or pasta if needing more textural substance. Experienced some broccoli burps later. Doesnt stop me from eating more. Tasty direct from pouch, but extra nice heated up. Could be poured over a potato or pasta for a healthy "mac n' (not)cheese". 4.5-5 stars

[[ASIN:B0BBSGM29Q Buffalo Cauliflower]] : Spicy but not too hot. Kind of creamy. Nice with crackers. I am tempted to take a packet and add in pureed cannellini beans or some Greek yogurt to make it into a healthy dip or sandwich spread. 4.5 stars

I'm not vegan or vegetarian, I simply like good tasting food. Plant based is bonus.

Currently $56.00 for 8 packets, which makes it $7 each. Even with some of them having a $4 coupon, that still only brings it down to $6.75. You decide if that is a doable price for you. I dont rate on price. I knew what this cost before ordering. Everyone has different needs, budgets, preferences, prices fluctuate, and so on.

Here is the crazy thing, it is highly competitively priced with other pouch or boxed soups of this ilk. Right in there with them. So if you are looking at this, then you are likely looking for healthy options that are outside of the usual sheap canned soup. If you have the budget, go for it.

I have been pleased with the 4 flavors I have tried, some I like more than others, and those get 5 stars from me. . I do comment on price though, and I will say that I find this wildly expensive for the amount. I'd keep it stacked in my pantry if it were a tad more friendly to my budget. Not sure what my price point is, but probably less than $7 per pouch. I'd eat this daily if I could afford to. Kettle & Fire (and Primal) has some good options (though not sure if any are offered in plant based). Similarly priced just to give you idea that Bare Bones does not stand alone in the price point. But still.. yeesh.

Overall: 5 stars. 4.5 if I could. I have been enjoying these, I love the ingredients, and for the most part taste and texture. I dont dislike any. My gut is sensitive, and never feels upset after eating one of these soups.

title: spicy but not too hot, light flavor, semi creamy, light texture, overall pleasant cup of soup
text:
I have tried 4 flavors, and liked them all, and my reviews are similar. I really like this brand. I use their bone broth pouches and sticks. Good stuff. They have a wide assortment of healthy soups, and I have liked them all. I am a huge fan of plant based soups and am already familiar with their bone broth products (I am not vegan or vegetarian, I just like good food). This Buffalo Cauliflower has a pleasant, easy flavor and texture. Makes me feel good to eat it. Very easy to make. Even tastes good cold. Not too salty. Spicy, but not too hot. Not exactly a cream soup, but it has a creamy mouth feel. Light texture from bits of cauliflower. Could be doctored up if need be. Might work blended with Greek yogurt (or chickpeas or cannellini beans) to make a dip. Not bland, but not overly flavorful. I had paired it with crackers, and found that pretty satisfying. Might be best paired with a sandwich to really fill the belly. I would also like it as a snack or means to get a head start on filling my belly before I delve into dinner. Maybe save a few calories. I've been eating one of their soups daily for the past week, and I have to say: I really like their stuff. My gut is sensitive, so if I can eat something without feeling ill, then it goes to top of my list for potential repurchase (that price though..:(

I dont rate on price. I knew what this cost before ordering. Everyone has different needs, budgets, preferences, prices fluctuate, and so on. Here is the crazy thing, it is highly competitively priced with other pouch or boxed soups of this ilk. Right in there with them. So if you are looking at this, then you are likely looking for healthy options that are outside of the usual canned soup. If you have the budget, go for it. I have been pleased with the 4 or 5 flavors I have tried, some I like more than others, and those get 5 stars from me. I happen to have their [[ASIN:B0BBSL5WTS Ready to Eat Plant Based Soup variety pack]] , which is nice way to try out 4 flavors before committing and includes this Buffalo Cauliflower option. I do comment on price though, and I will say that I find this wildly expensive for the amount. I'd keep it stacked in my pantry if it were a tad more friendly to my budget. Not sure what my price point is, but I prefer less than $7 per pouch. Kettle & Fire has some good options (though not sure if any are plant based). Similarly priced just to give you idea that Bare Bones does not stand alone in the price point. Hence, I prefer not to rate on price.

Overall I am very satisfied with the various Bare Bone plant based soups. All get at least 4 stars, but the overall mouth feel, flavor, and satiety I get from this makes it 5 stars.

Lentil Curry: 4 stars (little bland, could use more flavor and/or bits of food. Love lentils)
Tomato Chickpea: 5 stars (good balance of flavor and texture. Decent amount of food bits)
Cheesy Broccoli: 4.5 stars (very good flavor, kind of creamy, broccoli burps ensued)
Buffalo Cauliflower: 4.5 stars (mild spice, lightly creamy, bits of cauliflower)

title: nice quality pure vanilla extract, imparts lovely flavor to my cookie recipe. Love vanilla!
text:
I usually buy Madagascar vanilla, as well as imitation. No shame. Real vanilla for the win though, especially when wanting that delicate flavor to permeate a recipe. I use this in a basic chocolate chip cookie recipe. I know it made a difference, as the cookies just tasted extra good to me. All alcohol bakes off. I dont notice it anyway. Might be different in a frosting recipe. Might be extra nice when used that way. I've yet to use in a beverage or homemade icecream.

The jar style isn't my favorite as the mouth is wide open, but even my clumsy self never has issues pouring from it. I suppose a small enough measuring spoon dipped in would work too.

title: very good brand, nice fine flour for baking, cooking, coating, thickening (dont eat raw!)
text:
Really good brand. The amaranth flour is a fine powder. Use it for thickening, for adding into recipes by taking out a little of the usual flour. I haven't really worked with straight amaranth, I dont think it is meant to be used 100% in recipes. Kind of makes a dense crisp texture. Actually, just sitting here thinking about it I
vaguely recall making cookies with it. So I just did some digging through my notes, and there was a time I made a spice cookie. I just found the recipe (and easy to find in a search) that uses just amaranth. I'm going to make some this afternoon. Its a crisp fall day, and it begs for cookies and coffee.

But for most recipes, I recall the amount used is more like 25% of total recipe (unless using as a thickener). I usually use a mix of flours when baking. I simply like the fun and challenge of it, as well as the nutrient variety it adds over regular wheat flour. I buy amaranth puffs on occasion (works nice with oatmeal, yogurt, and adding textural & visual interest to homemade trail bars and protein balls, etc)

Note of caution: Because this is a grain, Amaranth flour is not to be consumed raw. It has oxalates and phytates which will bind to vitamins and minerals, essentially making it an "anti nutrient". If you are looking for a nutrient dense flour to add smoothies, give their [[ASIN:B0BBZN5QHH very lovely chickpea flour a try]]

title: adds fiber and protein, and other vitamins and minerals to dishes
text:
This chickpea flour is similar to the other brand I get, Bobs RedmIll. I like working with different flours for the fun of it, for the variety of it. I especially like the versatility and the additional nutrients over wheat flour. I love amping up the fiber to anything I use it in. Even as a basic thickener for gravies and sauces. I personally think it works better too. Healthy gravy? Yes please (heat up some broth powder or bouillon of any kind-meat or veg based, add water, whisk in the flour)

It is a fine powder that works well in nearly all wheat flour applications. I normally do a mix of flours. I think a little less chickpea can be used instead of white flour (3/4 swap from 1 cup). More often it is my go to coating for making crunchy chicken, or for added moisture (egg & flour dredge). Adds flavor, protein and other vitamins and minerals. Plenty of recipes out there if you are new to garbanzo bean flour. Can be consumed "raw", so even works to add bulk to smoothies.

title: fresh, pleasing aroma and taste. Non jittery energy
text: Lovely green color smells herbily-vegetal, and mildly grassy. Has the taste I am accustomed to. I drink matcha often and prefer ceremonial over culinary for simple teas and lattes. I like the smooth flavor. Doesn't take much to make a cup- just 1/2-1 tsp. Plenty of caffeine. I like the chill feeling I get from matcha- good boost of energy without the jitters. Main reason I drink it though is for the antioxidants and its ability to reduce sugar cravings. I dont rate on price, but price per ounce is within reason. I like the packaging- small tin with well-sealed interior. No problems with this matcha. Product of Japan :)

title: Soft, chewy, tasty. Hits the spot
text: Another nice Larabar option. I like their stuff. Some more than others. I am not much of a peanut butter bar fanatic, but I figured it would likely be good if it is done by Larabar (it is), and that my husband would like it too. Soft, chewy, tasty. Makes a nice snack, healthier "dessert", or as part of a meal. I dont do it so much with this flavor, but I have torn off bits of the fruit based bars and tossed it on oatmeal or yogurt. All good.

title: convenience, could be eaten cold or hot depending on situation
text: Good amount per pouch. Clear bottom, can see the rice before opening. Convenience and good flavor. Normally I will just make rice, then add coconut powder (or milk) to it. But this is a nice quick way to enjoy a similar taste. I keep stuff like this on hand more for times when I simply dont want to fuss in the kitchen, and for use in emergency situations- can be eaten hot or cold, no real preparation needed. Can open up a can of something else to make it stretch. I try to grab pouches of rice when on sale. The 8.5 ounce bag is larger than some offerings. I like it. I will buy it again if the price is right .

title: 24 boxes, each contain 8 packets (192 packets all together. Great taste, easy to use
text:
Long time consumer of Goya products, and I adore this beef bouillion. I have gotten other spices in similar packaging (stays fresh forever it seems!), but I dont think I had their bouillion. I normally go with a paste base, but in recent years I was having trouble finding my usual. Then when it became available the price was crazy. I switched to big jars of Knorr, which I like a lot. But I think side by side I may like this Goya option better. It really made my gravy stand out. I had made a beef stew, and at the end I took the liquid and made a gravy. Although the liquid had already been well seasoned, it just seemed to be missing something. That was when I grabbed a packet of this. It made all the difference and made me instantly love it. It's just.. tasty. I can taste the beefiness, and while it is salty it isn't overpowering. I could dip my finger in it for a quick taste test and not recoil. I think I could use some of it as a quick sipping broth on cold nights.

I prefer this over cubes any day. Way easier to work with, dissolves well, and I swear tastes better.

Currently $35.56 for 24 boxes, each contain 8 packets (192 packets all together. Share!)
$1.48 per box
$0.19 per packet
2.82 ounces per box, 68 ounces total for $0.52 per ounce

title: good quality addition to pantry & emergency supplies. Add cals/protein/nutrition w/ease
text:
Edit to add: it is AWESOME for use in cafe lattes. It froths up really well. Makes a sturdy froth that tops off my espresso gorgeously. I just use a [[ASIN:B0BBV3SLZH simple milk frother]] to make super quick easy foam.

If you order from the warehouse you have to know that it may have a short shelf life left on it (though should be a ways out if ordering from regular Amazon). Taking a chance on reduced pricing. I think this is a bargain at regular pricing. HUGE container. I normally don't care about the best by date, because it is only referencing the guaranteed quality, not the safety. So mine is 2 months out, and I doubt I will have this used by then. But it will be fine beyond that. I bought this more as a back up in case of scarcity or skyrocketing food prices. I normally just drink non dairy "milk", but will use stuff like this in recipes that call for dairy milk. I also dont mind it as a creamer.

One thing that is nice about powdered milk is being able to make it as rich and creamy or as light and bland as you want. Use more or less according to preferred taste. I think this has very good flavor.

I have used it directly in coffee with some effort to get lumps out. Best when use a little frother mixer. Nice for adding to smoothies and such if looking to boost protein and other vitamin and minerals. Might be helpful to those that can use the extra calories and nutrition boost without having to consume added volume (thinking ill or elderly).

I'd get this again. I have two big containers so it might be awhile. But I may buy extras and give away.

title: My favorite brand, always tastes good to me. Sumatra is bold yet medium, all around good
text:
San Francisco Bay coffee is my coffee. It is the brand I most often buy. I have been drinking their K-cups for many years now, and will pepper in the occasional bag of ground or bean. I also drink other brands, and always try other brands, but San Fran is my coffee. That being said, can't go wrong with any even ones that you may not think you will like, it might surprise you. They just do a good job (in my opinion, of course :))

Organic Sumatra is always a good one. Solidly medium with body, yet smooth and not acidic. It's bold, like a dark roast yet isnt exactly dark. A good "coffee tasting coffee" I am more for dark roasts, but Sumatra was one of those that always seemed to be offered at dark artsy coffee houses. Back in the day it always sounded exotic over anything offered in store. So I just have a soft spot for it.

I like my super dark bold coffee black, unsweetened. The lighter the coffee, the more apt I am to reach for creamer, usually to simmer down the acidity and tang. The flavor profile of this does not make me reach for the creamer. I can drink it black. But i have used creamer in it too to see how it holds up (sometimes the coffee isnt strong enough to overcome added cream), and this shines. It's a great option for those with different coffee preferences.

title: dark roast instant, good flavor, one of my favorite instant coffees
text:
I really like Waka Coffee, have had it a couple of times now. Best price is with their big bag. I have had that, and now I have the 3 boxes of single serve packets. I find that the single serve work well, and make a good cup of coffee for the amount that is in them. I feared that I would need two packets, making it extra pricy per cup. But this works well for me with exactly 7 ounces of hot water used. I like keeping packets of instant coffee tucked in my purse, as well as my bug out bag/get home bags. My review is for both the big bag and the packets since apparently my very old review for the big bag is what popped up when I went to review the single serve. I drink instant coffee often, and this tastes very good to me.

I drink all sorts of coffee, brewed in all sorts of ways. I often drink instant coffee, and as with other varieties of coffee no two are the same. This Waka freeze dried coffee is delicious. I tried it the second it arrived, haha. I especially love dark roast, and most instant coffee options are medium. So I am super stoked to have a good dark roast. I love instant for making iced coffee, or for making a quick cup using hot water from my electric water kettle. I can drink it black which is my preference for all coffee, but some instant needs some cream. I can drink this black or with cream. Occasionally I use instant for use in chocolate cake, or frosting.

title: ceremonial matcha in single serve packets, fresh, good color & aroma
text:
This matcha powder is good. Nice aroma, good smooth flavor. Lovely green color. It is mentioned all over the product description that this is USDA certified organic from China, AND they have it listed in the "Country of Origin" section. No mystery. I may prefer Japanese originated by far, but this listing is transparent. I liked reading through the description for the historical take. Well packaged, easy enough to open.

20 packs with about 1 tsp per packet. 1 tsp is standard amount. Using 2-3 ish ounces of water is standard (though use what works for you--but ceremonial prepared tea uses a small quantity of water). Enough to make a nice cup of tea, enough to flavor up an iced version. Can add to a big cup of water. It really all works. But for ceremonial level-- just a couple ounces of water. Nice addition to smoothies (though usually I use culinary for that). I think 1-2 tsp is the most I have seen a recommended amount section (.5-1 tsp is usual). So this is on par.

It's convenient, and I dont even think it is that pricy (not that I rate on price). When it comes to matcha I definitely look at price per ounce. All together this is 1.41 ounces making that $17.72 per ounce at current price of $24.99. There is a $5 coupon, so if that's still available, that brings it down to $14.18 per ounce for ceremonial. Quick glance at other offerings, and the pricing is reasonable, or within the norm anyway.

One thing I like about packets, is that I am not going to use too much. I seem to add too much when I am drawing from a container of loose powder. I have no discipline, haha. And since it is too easy to use to much (and therefore make caffeine content sky rocket), I rather appreciate the packets. I dont always get them, but I recognize the benefit. Of course, they are good for travel, office, other on the go situations. Stays fresh long time, etc.

title: when you want something other than water and dont want to spend a lot. Make into icecubes!
text:
I have the variety pack of Orange, Grape, Strawberry, and Peach. I think the first two are the winners of the bunch, but it could just be my preference for those flavors period. Basic flavored powder in a stick. Add to 16 ounces of water or so, and that's it. I've had these before and other drinks of similar nature. Fun taking some to make ice cubes with. Extra nice for hot days. I like peach added to iced tea. Strawberry is ok. Im not a fan of strawberry drinks, so it is likely more about my tastebuds.

Orange contains some caffeine. Not sure how much.

Basically it is as expected. Nice to find a big box, and I see they have boxes of single flavors as well as this variety pack. Price is as expected. No surprises. If you like this sort of drink, then it is similar to others out there. Not healthy, but cheaper than pop and many other drinks. Sometimes ya want something other than plain water. Try the ice cube thing, its fun.

title: good taste, texture, I find it filling. Good amount of veg chunks & whole chickpeas. Satisfying!
text:
I really like this brand. I use their bone broth pouches and sticks. Good stuff. They have a wide assortment of healthy soups, and I have liked them all. I am a huge fan of plant based soups and am already familiar with their bone broth products (I am not vegan or vegetarian, I just like good food). I am partial to this tomato and chickpea soup. It is heartier than their Lentil Curry by far (few more calories too 170 vs 130). It has a pleasant, easy flavor. Not too salty. Good amount of chickpeas. Could be doctored up if need be. Not bland, but not overly flavorful. I had pair it with half a sandwich and found that satisfying. I would also like it as a snack or means to get a head start on filling my belly before I delve into dinner. Maybe save a few calories.

I dont rate on price. I knew what this cost before ordering. Everyone has different needs, budgets, preferences, prices fluctuate, and so on. Here is the crazy thing, it is highly competitively priced with other pouch or boxed soups of this ilk. Right in there with them. So if you are looking at this, then you are likely looking for healthy options that are outside of the usual canned soup. If you have the budget, go for it. I have been pleased with the 4 or 5 flavors I have tried, some I like more than others, and those get 5 stars from me. I happen to have their [[ASIN:B0BBSL5WTS Ready to Eat Plant Based Soup variety pack]], which is nice way to try out 4 flavors before committing, which includes this option. I do comment on price though, and I will say that I find this wildly expensive for the amount. I'd keep it stacked in my pantry if it were a tad more friendly to my budget. Not sure what my price point is, but less than $7 per pouch. Kettle & Fire has some good options (though not sure if any are plant based). Similarly priced just to give you idea that Bare Bones does not stand alone in the price point.

Overall I am very satisfied with the various Bare Bone plant based soups. All get at least 4 stars, but the overall mouth feel, flavor, and satiety I get from this makes it 5 stars.

title: good brand, perfectly good matcha for hot or iced drinks and beyond
text: Good matcha, pleasant flavor and aroma. I go through matcha often. I usually enjoy it iced, but now that the weather is cooler I will be making it hot more often than not. Doesn't take much to make a good sized cup. One of the few things that I don't like made too strongly. 1 tsp is all that is needed. I actually prefer the smaller packet for best freshness. I like it, have no problems with it. 5 stars-- not necessarily because it is better, but because it meets my expectations of a good, fresh, ceremonial grade matcha. I don't rate on price.

title: really great brand, always pleased with their selections
text:
Bright, comforting peppermint. Pleasing for day or evening use. Alone or sweetened. I like it with a few drops of vanilla syrup or creamer. Peppermint feels settling on my stomach. Hence the comforting feeling. Great along, but play around with it. Peppermint is a neat option. Not my go to but i like it enough to keep it as an option in my bizarrely large tea collection.

I really like Teavity brand, and I would probably like anything by them. Good quality, good flavor, works fine in my Keurig. I used to scoff at k-cup tea, but I have come around to it and often reach for a k-cup over a tea bag (maybe 50-50). I am not exactly a tea drinker, but I drink my fair share once the weather turns cool. Something about drinking a hot cup of something all day long is just appealing to me. So after I have had my fill of coffee, I switch to tea. Caffeinated if I still need it, or decaffeinated if I dont. Love it for use in evening.

title: it's OK. Hemp, Cocoa, & raw sugar. Needs to be brewed. Gritty. Not chocolatey enough, kinda blah
text:
I dont like it as much as their Chai (which is actually spicy). This drinking chocolate actually needs to be brewed, which annoys me (but it DOES say it directly in description). I dont want to fuss when making a prefab hot chocolate otherwise I will just make my own with ingredients I have. I decided I would try it without brewing. It is passible. It is a fine grit, but it is definitely gritty. However, it worked for most of my mug. I added hot water over the powder. Used a frother to blend. Added a little creamer-- really needs something. Then just proceeded to drink it. I could see settling at the bottom. At some point I decided to swirl it. Not good, as it was all pulpy and gritty. Maybe I will try it in my french press. Maybe not.

"Easy Prep – Your hemp drinking chocolate is very easy to made and delicious. Add 1tbsp per person to plunger or teapot with infuser as hemp proteins can be gritty. Add boiling water, let stand for few minutes and pour. Sweeten to taste with Hemp Honey. Add milk if desired. You can also brewed with your favourite milk on stove."

Doesnt say how much water? I found that 1 TBS was not enough for the 6-8 ounces I used. I dont know why they dont include a picture of the nutritional information. If I were shopping for this normally, I would have passed on it based on not seeing the nutritional panel.

I'll (maybe) use this up, but it definitely wont be a repurchase. Not tasty enough, not chocolatey enough. Sort of just bland. I LOVE that it is just hemp protein, organic cocoa, and raw sugar. I am glad that they dont use other sweeteners. BUt I would really rather it just be unsweetened period. Very lightly sweet, but still quite a bit per tablespoon (12 grams). But it somehow falls short. Maybe not enough cocoa? I will have to use more (but that greatly boosts the calories as there are 80 calories per TBS), or add my own unsweetened cocoa (which would boost cocoa flavor and only add 10 or so calories). I'm just not sold on it. It isnt bad, it just isnt for me. Going with 3 stars. Middle of road rating. to mean "it's OK".

The DO have a money back guarantee, so if it still appealing to you then go for it. Food stuffs is just one of those things that comes down to preference. Hence all the differently rated reviews.

title: excellent brand, smells so good, melts easily, great mouth feel, can do so much with it!
text:
Cacao butter. Use it as you would white chocolate but know that it is unsweetened. Think of baking chocolate in that regard. Excellent for melting and using to drizzle over baked goods. Could sweeten it up if need be. Not something you will want to just nibble on, as tempting as it may smell. But go for it if that's your thing. Could be added to hot drinks for a creamier mouth feel. Or used IN baked goods. I was reading that it could be used fully or partially in replace of butter in recipes. Occasionally I make a scratch brownie recipe that might be interesting to do that with.

Excellent brand. One of the first brands that I came across 10+ years ago back when I first started making better food choices, and wanted healthier brands to choose from. I think the first time I used cacao was from Navitas Naturals. This is my first time trying their cacao butter disks.

I dropped on in my coffee so I could try it right away. I am rather liking how that turned out. I thought I may use this for some holiday cookies, but I know it will be used to make white hot chocolate, or white pumpkin spice chocolate because I am one of those that need all things pumpkin all October long.

title: long time quality brand, very good kit with fresh ingredients, just add milk if so desired
text:
Not my first time trying Locca brand boba tea products. It is to me a good quality brand, and if you are already familiar with their physical location offerings, then this is a nice way to enjoy it at home. Lovely, good looking kit. Definitely gift worthy. Classy clean look. Not an instant tea. This needs brewing. Fresh robust taste is wonderful paired with the deep brown sugar syrup. I drizzle in milk, and add healthy amount of tapioca pearls. Nice afternoon pick me up.

Includes a couple pouches of loose black tea (you will need a tea strainer), 2 bags of tapioca pearls, 2 bottles of brown sugar syrup, and 24 boba tea straws. Can supposedly make upward of 40 servings. Just have to include your own cup and decide if you want it to be milk based or not. Can swap out the brown sugar syrup for your own syrup of choice. Really nice pearls. Cook up nicely with excellent chew.

As a lover of Boba tea (aka bubble tea), I often make it myself. I've had the instant powder-based stuff which can be good enough, but it is the use of fresh brewed tea that takes it to another level. I cook the tapioca pearls, I make the tea, I make the simple syrup or buy specialty syrups. All very normal process, and boba tea lovers will likely already know how to make it. No special equipment required (unless you count a loose tea leaf strainer as special, haha). SO I find this kit lovely. And this kit is inspired from their physical location/cafe (located in California)! They have lots of kits! Check out their page to see the various offerings. I have never been disappointed.

Sure I could just go buy the occasional cup of boba tea, but for me.. that is an excursion, not making a special trip (gas prices, wear and tear, time= money), also those places often use the prefab powder stuff over fresh brewed tea. BIG difference. It is only very recently that some boba tea cafes have popped up in my area, and even "my area" is still at least a 30 minute drive (I live in rural area). Before that, I only got it when I was in a major city (like Toronto or NYC). Hence learning to make my own. Very very easy.

I can even share this with my husband. He is not into stuff like this, but one day he tried the brown sugar boba tea and liked it (with milk).

I'd love this as a gift! It comes in a gift worthy package, just clean and classy looking. Give as is or add in some side goodies (ideas: clear cup to see boba pearls, tea strainer, syrups, nibbles). Has an appealing classy aesthetic to it. They have a [[ASIN:B09JV6NJ4B Holiday Boba tea kit that is nice]] but will need syrup to go with it.

But I just want to say again, this product is fantastic as is. I always recommend Locca brand for gift giving.

title: excellent brand of chow mein and raman, Sriracha is savory, sweet, and hint of spicy. Good flavor!
text:
I love Sapporo Ichiban chow mein noodles and ramen noodles. What is the difference in the world of noodles? Not much! They are pretty much interchangeable. Same flavor, same ingredients goes into making each, but chow mein can be a tad thicker, while ramen has a more slip/slick texture for slurping. Forer is over a little more yellow, latter is more white/cream color. But really no difference. Unless having side by side, I imagine it wouldn't even be noticeable.

Way better than the cheapies in case you're wondering. Better yakisoba than some brands. Better taste, texture, and I never feel ill afterward. Hence my love for Sapporp Ichiban products. I am pleasantly surprised with the flavor of the Sriracha flavor packet. I like sriracha, but wasn't sure if I want the entire dish to taste like it. I thought it might be too spicy. But this isnt. I like that. It is actually a tad sweet, not too salty (to me)., and the spice is more of a back of the mouth thing that isnt fiery, nor lingers. If you are hoping for spicy hot, this wont cut it. You will want to add a few drops of additional sriracha, or some chili oil. I like it as is, personally.

I like my noodles a little brothy. I add in some sliced protein, and usually whatever vegetable or other toppers I may have on hand. I like stuff like this for a quick lunch/brunch. In my pics I used sliced pork, sliced brussles sprouts, and some pureed squash. Nothing else added. Not the traditional toppers, but I tend to work with what I have.

They list the nutrition assuming you will be eating one block. I appreciate that. Others will list it as 2 servings--yeh right. Loaded with sodium as per the usual- 1000 mg.

I dont recall what the actual directions are. I have been making them for so long, that I didnt pay attention. I put the block into a bowl, boil water in my counter water kettle, pour over top, then put a lid on. If need be, I may put in microwave for a minute to finish it off. Then add seasoning and toppers.

title: mojitos are my jam, this is surprisingly extra good. Use as is, halfsie, or N/A. YUM!
text:
Well packed glass bottle in a branded box. I have tried a few Proof Syrup and have enjoyed them all, but I am especially keen on the Mojito. I love mojitos, and I actually thought that this would be my least favorite because I am so familiar with the drink. BUT, WOW, I really like this. This will be a repurchase. Even if I found a brand half the price, I wouldnt risk it. I really like how this turns out-- made as directed, made as a halfsie, even made without alcohol (which I have been going for lately).

I am not much of a drinker, in fact more often than not I will make a N/A version or a halfsie. Sometimes I simply want the flavor but not the effect (more and more sensitive to alcohol these days, boo hiss). I dont keep a wide assortment of supplies on hand, so I rarely make drinks from scratch anymore. I will buy a mixer, then use it up in a short period of time (needs to be refrigerated). I will usually have a mixer with some club soda. Kind of used like I was making an Italian Soda, but with more complex flavors than a single note syrup. Maybe doctor it up further. Then if I feel like a little booze, then I usually do a splash of alcohol, not the 2 ounces in the directions. Really comes down to preference. How many actual servings you get will come down to your taste preference for booze to mixer ratio.

Pricy for my budget as there are other mixers like this that are half the price. But these tout real ingredients, and I have no problem with these products. Funny, I have thought about using these syrups in smoothies. Make it a fun tasting smoothie, and the ingredients are good enough to not junk it up.

I've had a few now, and fine them perfectly acceptable. I know all of their stuff is premium priced. All well packaged. Most all I have given 4 stars, but this mojito really impresses me. Speaks to me. 5 stars
