title: light roast, light flavor, no acidity, removes tang and brightness, might be too delicate
text:
Good cold brew. Not my favorite as it is a light roast. BUT light roasted coffee actually has more caffeine over my beloved ultra dark roasts, so it is still useful to me. I usually use cruddy coffee for cold brewing, as the cold brew method can make nearly any coffee taste better. Greatly reduces acidity and bitterness. So I am not sure if I want to sacrifice good coffee for cold brew method, haha. But it is good, and it could be brewed in a pinch. Just know that cold brew can be a tad more course ground than what is used in hot brewing methods. Really though it all works.

Light roast is not what I would normally use in cold brew as I think it would be too light tasting. Part of the flavor profile from light roasts is the tang and brightness (which I dont care for normally), and is missing out on the "coffee" taste. Since cold brewing further reduces acidity and nearly removes all tang and brightness, I am not sure what it left of a light roast when used in cold brewing. When I tried it, my suspicions were correct-- not a strong concentrated "coffee tasting coffee". It's not bad, but it is a little lacking. I am surprised that they use a light roast. I think this would be more coffee tasting if it used a medium roast.

I think next time I will give it a full 24 hours to "brew". That is what I normally do with my cold brews, and instead I did just 12 or so. Overall I think it will be fine.

BTW, San Francisco Bay coffee is my #1 brand of coffee. I have been drinking it for years, and while I totally have my favorites (Dark Italian Roast, Fog Chaser, and Vietnamese Style), I have liked everything by them. Never outright disliked anything. I even like their flavored stuff and I am not one for flavored coffee (other coffee brand I like for flavored variety is Wake the Hell Up)

title: bold, dark, smooth, delightful. Love this brand, love this Vietnamese Style
text: I love San Francisco Bay coffee. I have been drinking it for years and years. I am in love with dark roasts, and they are a company that offers a wide variety of all roasting level, including several dark roasts (and very dark leaning medium roasts). Ground, whole bean, K-cups. All of them. I love love love Fog Chaser and Dark Italian Roast most off all. I sometimes get French Roast. I have never outright disliked anything from this company. I even like their flavored options, and I am not one much for flavored coffee. Gimme strong, bold, dark, black unsweetened wake up juice. Mm. But yeh, I like it all, and have extra love for certain ones. THIS is now on my gotta have it list. MMM DARK

title: juicy blueberry aroma and taste
text:
Just right. Not too strong, but flavorful enough to tell it is blueberry. Only the second brand I have tried that actually is able to make blueberry work. [[ASIN:B08WPP3TSQ Wake the Hell Up the other brand I like]]. Really neat to smell blueberry brewing in the kitchen. Different but surprisingly good.

This is mellow and smooth. Light flavor that isnt artificial tasting. San Fransisco Bay coffee is my number 1 coffee brand for ground, whole bean, and K-cups (Italian Dark Roast, Fog Chaser are my ultimate faves). I buy it frequently, and I pretty much enjoy it all. I am not one for flavored coffee unless it is fall or winter. Then for whatever reason I start craving a little something different. Not so much for my first cup of coffee, but for sipping throughout day afterward. Or occasionally iced in summer and fall. I normally drink my coffee black, unsweetened, but when it comes to flavored coffee I find a little cream (and sometimes a little sweetener) makes the nuances of flavor stand out better. This tastes good black or with cream. Though cream enhances flavored coffee in my experience.

title: convenient tasty roast beef & gravy in a can. Good flavor hot or cold. Pantry staple
text:
It's quite good, not sure if 5 star good but I think its good enough to warrant full rating. I would buy it again. I usually buy [[ASIN: B001E4Q4BU Libby Roast Beef]], but the price has been all over the place. Currently $96 for a stack of 24 ($4 per can), or $81.60 with subscribe and save ($3.40). Not "bad" but not great. Falls in line with current prices in store. Originally was buying it for $60 for 24, which still makes this Hormel a better find. But finding this Hormel brand for $24 for a stack of 12 was a very good purchase. I see that it is no longer available, so I wonder if when it comes back it will be jacked up in price. I dont rate on price, but I do comment. Was really nice to add to my food supplies and not spend a fortune. If Libby and Hormel were same price, and I was choosing between the two, I would likely select Libby.

Taste wise, it is good. It tastes like roast beef with gravy. Lighter color gravy than Libby, but the taste is similar. Chunks of beef are big and tender. Heats up well, or if need be is not too shabby eaten direct from can. I like keeping food like this on hand for ultra convenience, but also as a means for having something on hand in case of emergency or whatever the situation may be. Food can be scarce in store, food may not look good, might not be able to get to store (weather, illness, car breakdown, etc). So I simply keep a wide assortment of foods readily available. I started with buying a few extra cans, jars, boxes, bags of whatever when doing a normal grocery run. Then I began pricing bulk items online, and really branched out. I never had roast beef in a can until recently, and am pleasantly surprised how delicious it is.

I have a big appetite and can easily eat a whole can along side some mashed potatoes and vegetables. I have split the can between two servings for ore reasonable portion size and to see if I can stretch it a bit (trying to figure out how much I need for two people).

Acquired 10/2022 with a BEST BY date of late 2025. For reals, I dont pay much attention to the date. It is NOT a safety date. Check govt sites, and all will say that it is not a safety date. It is JUST a "guaranteed" to be same consistent quality through that date if stored under proper conditions. That's it. For those that see the date and toss it, you are throwing away money (which they bank on ignorance). If cans are in good condition, then they are going to be fine for many many many years. If cans come dented, then plan to use them up soon. Only products that should be used in timely manner are acidic foods like tomatoes. All else will be fine. Might degrade in taste and nutrients, but safety is rarely in question.

Comically they have this listed as vegetarian. Uh, no. It's beef.

title: gorgeous color, lovely hot cup of evening comfort
text:
Pleasantly soothing chamomile. I have had several brands over the years both Kcup and regular tea bag. This is a good kcup to me, and works flawlessly in my keurig machine. I like the convenience. I make a 6 or 8 ounce mug. It results in a gorgeous yellow tea. I have been enjoying it an hour or so before bed, sometimes directly after dinner if I am feeling chilled. I tend to drink non caffeinated tea once the cold weather and early nights settle in. Nice warming drink.

I like it as is, or with a little local honey, or more often lately adding in some [[ASIN:B096WZBLK6 Honey Mint Collagen powder]]. Pairs well.

Nice looking box and K-cups. Organic. Good brand, I have liked everything by this brand thus far.

title: light, crisp, herbal. Notes of thyme and rosemary. Lovely alone, or w/club soda, other add-ins
text:
This is a pleasant aperitif. Light, crisp, doesn't overwhelm the tastebuds. Truly worthy of pre dinner enjoyment. I like the thyme and rosemary. Interesting taste paired with a hint of sweet. I have had it as is over ice, and have made it as a spritzer with a dash of club soda. I have gone further with it and used it as a base for non alcoholic cocktail by adding in ginger beer and a couple of cherries. That was fun, but I must say that I really liked it as is, or with the club soda. I may try tonic sometime soon. I prefer it a more dry taste, but it isnt overly sweet. Thinking a splash of grapefruit, or a lemon slice would pair very nicely. Ooh, a sprig of thyme or rosemary for garnish as well as a slice of lemon would look nice, smell nice, and enhance the taste. For those that prefer a little booze but not a lot of alcohol, I imagine this would do well as a halfsie.

Needs to be refrigerated after opening. Since I don't want it taking up space in my fridge, I will be drinking this daily until gone. For shame, haha.

Good experience. Piqued my interest in their other offerings. Really enjoying my new "drink" ritual. My body doesnt seem to tolerate alcohol, yet I enjoy the ritual of preparation.. so finding new and fun ways to enjoy a drink without all the fall out has been a pleasurable adventure. Very pleased to have tried this brand.

title: excellent brand, but cans should be better protected- many dented from warehouse
text:
Tired of smashed, crap products. I will take a small dent here and there but most were smashed. WTF. I dont rate on price. Everyone can see the price before order, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, prices fluctuate, there are sales, and right now.. prices have simply been rising on everything. If I can get good organic tomatoes at $2 or less per can, then I think that is reasonable (currently $25 with subscribe and save). DO I want to pay way less, yes (actually I got mine on sale at $12 so I did get a great deal, but at cost of mostly dented cans). Hence why my focus is on actual product.

Tomatoes are good and fresh tasting. No noticeable degrade with dented cans. I wont let the sit for long though.

title: perfect consistency for spreads, dips, sauces, drizzles or as usual on a sandwich.
text:
Online impulse purchase of a giant container of Reese's sauce. I mean, if it were a little container I would have probably looked past it. But I saw this giant container, and was adding to cart before really thinking it through. I received it quickly, seemed to have a slight leak, but not enough to be concerned. Opened it and stuck a spoon (mm, maybe finger) in and gave it a try. Has a sweet peanut buttery flavor. More syrupy/runny than regular peanut butter (hence "sauce") yet could be used in a sandwich. But this is begging to be used over ice cream, over pancakes, in satay, or other peanut based sauces and dips, Or simply by the spoonful.

Similar nutritional profile to peanut butter.

title: way easier, cheaper, convenient over fresh. Excellent looking flakes, rehydrate in oil for + flavor
text:
Packaged in USA. Product of Egypt. While not listed, I made direct contact with company and asked for country of origin for the cilantro. Would like to see the info listed somewhere.

Very pleased with this dehydrated cilantro. Really good looking flakes. I could use fresh, but unless I am planning ahead and if I can even find it in the grocery store (or it doesnt look gross or isnt mad expensive), I find this dried version plenty acceptable. I dont use cilantro enough to grow it. So having this dried version is a game changer for me. As with any dried herb, to get the most flavor out from it, cook it in a little oil. Dried herbs tend to be more potent than their fresh counterpart, but it takes some rehydrating to make that happen.

I have some pasta and rice recipes that call for cilantro and I am sure I will like this over fresh. I am more apt to make them now as I often will forget to look for cilantro in store. If making guacamole (and wanting cilantro in it), I dont know if it will impart same flavor unless dehydrating with oil first (maybe use a little avocado oil?).

title: smooth & strong as cold brew should be, can also be warmed up for no/low acid cuppa
text:
Cold brewing eliminates acidity, which is why cold brew is often quite smooth despite the concentrated flavor. I love strong coffee, and often times I dont dilute my concentrate. Either not at all (added over ice and let it naturally dilute) or just a little added water. Nearly always black, always unsweetened.

I have the vanilla option. I am not a fan of flavored coffee, and wish I had the option to try the original. Alas, I have the Vanilla, and figured I would give it a try (had it been any other flavor I would have simply passed on it). The vanilla flavor is as expected- stands out, can definitely taste vanilla. Yet not artificial tasting. Good on them for making a nice vanilla. Now that we are into the fall and all things pumpkin spice, my weakness for the season will override my usual preference for black unsweetened coffee as I delve into pumpkin spice creamers, pumpkin syrups (pumpkin caramel, pumpkin vanilla, pumpkin pecan, etc etc). That is what I have done with this, use it as base for all the pumpkin things. It works!

I took a large mason jar and followed directions. Basically, added one pouch to 16 ounces of water, and let sit. Says to let sit for 12-24 hours, but no more than 24 hours. This is typical. I prepped this in the early evening figuring it would be minimally ready by the next morning, with intent to use as my "go out the door" second cup of coffee. Well, I forgot. I even forgot to take the bag out. So when I initially tried it was at the 36 hour mark. OOPS. It was fine. Second time I made it, I made sure to keep it to 12-24 hours. Even better.

I scoffed at their "3 servings" per pouch. But, it has been making 3 servings for me. Big cups. I have to water it down some. Might be because of the robust vanilla flavor. Now I am really curious for the Original. I may have to spring for a box of it. I see they have a smaller bundle, which I may consider since I am less likely to drink cold brew in the cold months. This could be my new go-to brand for cold brew coffee if I like their original.

Here is why: the packs are really convenient. No big cold brew vessel needed, no filter needed. So very easy. I have been making cold brew for 15 years. I have a variety of means to make it. Early on, before it became a thing, I would just pack a jar with coffee, add water, let sit, then strain when done. That works. I have containers, special filters, etc.. It all works, but some means are simply easier than others. These pouches are easy, AND the coffee is actually strong enough (I have had some pouches that were weak, terribad tasting). This box is divided into 6 bundles (bags) of 4 pouches for 24 total pouches. Each provides 3 servings, for 72 servings. Price ($89.99) breakdown is $3.75 per pouch or $1.25 per serving (assuming 3 servings prepared as directed, will be more or less depending on how you use it/make it).

While I typically use the cold brew method for iced coffee, it absolutely can be warmed up for a low/no acidic coffee.

If you have cruddy coffee at home, I like using the cold brew method as it makes many bad coffees taste pretty good.

5 stars because I am impressed, it has clear easy directions, nicely packaged, can be shared, makes a stout cup of coffee, and flavor is good and fresh tasting. Super easy, and while pricy I dont mind paying for a product I can rely on. No hassle, good consistency. And I am already looking to try one of their other options (oh, and they also have decaf. mmmm cold brew day AND night. yeh, baby).

title: surprisingly very good, light cacao with cinnamon flavor, delicately sweetened, comforting taste
text:
I've only made it hot, and it is quite good. Dissolves well. Has a comforting taste. I don't so much see it as a coffee alternative. More like something I will have after my coffee, when I still want a little something. Especially now as the weather turns cooler and something hot to drink appeals to me all day.

It basically tastes like a mild hot cacao with cinnamon. I use a variety of mushroom powders in my coffee every day, and none really impart any taste. Same goes here. Lightly sweet, perfectly sweetened. I don't care for sweet hot drinks, and this is done really well in my opinion.

Use what is needed according to taste. 2 tsp tastes good enough (albeit watery), but a third brought to a level I really liked (little more body). Maybe 2.5 tsp to 8-10 ounces water will be the sweet spot for me. One thing to keep in mind, might be some delicious sludge toward the end of your mug. Do a few swirls once in awhile. Totally reminds me of hot cocoa with this. If I make this iced, I think will add a little hot water to dissolve it, then top off with more cold water or non dairy milk & ice.

Ingredients: Organic Cacao, Organic Tahl, Beyond Brew Mushroom Blend (Organic Lion's Mane Extract, Organic Reishi Extract, Organic Chaga Extract, Organic Cordyceps sinensis Extract, Organic Cordyceps militaris Extract, Organic Turkey Tail Extract), Organic Allulose, Bacillus coagulans, Organic Ginger, Contains Less Than 0.5% of Organic Stevia, Organic Ceylon Cinnamon, Malic Acid, Organic Monk Fruit

title: adorable, festive packaging. Power bottle necks a bit, no mess. 2 servings per bottle. Tasty!
text:
Directions say to use 3 TBS to 180 ml (approx 6 ounces) water. I did just that. I think it tastes pretty good! I think there are two servings per bottle? Seems like I used about half a bottle after measuring out "3 heaping TBS".

I have had had all but the gingerbread so far. The caramel is very nice. More please :) Water worked really well, but I think milk (non dairy or regular) would be great. I thought it was all perfectly sweet and creamy tasting. I added a little whipped cream and that brought it up a level.

Super cute presentation. Looks good just sitting out. Really festive and adorable. I dont think stuff like this is necessarily purchased for the actual cocoa, but for the overall vibe of it. But it IS perfectly good cocoa. Sure, I make my own, but I also find a lot of joy in making prefab stuff from adorable packaging. Simple pleasures.

The powder literally bottle necks, which makes the powder come out a little slow. It is doable, but just took a tad longer to tap the powder into a measuring spoon. No mess. Not a deal breaker, but if we could do half stars, I would knock a halfer off for that. SO, "4.5" stars. But going with 4 because this is a delightful little set. I have had other Thoughtfully products and have been pleased.

title: yummy, easy to make, breadcrumbs really make it work, hits the spot, nice w/ hot sauce/Franks
text:
Makes a decent sized portion, and I can eat a lot. Nice for quick lunch, but would likely use it as a side for dinner (love dinner time). After cooking, I scooped it all into a bowl then added the breadcrumbs. Made for a nice presentation.

Tastes good to me. Easy to make. The breadcrumb topping really makes this stand out. Adds a perfect texture that now makes me want to add breadcrumbs to any mac n cheese I ever have.

I made this EXACTLTY as described, and it couldnt have turned out any better. Add seasoning to noodles, fill with water to water line, do not use more or less. Fill exactly to waterline. Microwave X mount of time (I think it was 3 mins? its in the directions). Take out, there might be a little water. Thats fine, DO NOT DRAIN. Add in the cheese (like a velveeta packet). Stir. I let it sit for a minute. I decided to scoop it into a bowl for better presentation for myself. Then I sprinkled the crumbs on top. MMMM

Not a strong flavor. I could go for an extra sharp bite, but this is mild. Pleasant. I ate half of it as is. Then I decided to sprinkle a little hot sauce on top of the last few bites.

It's probably on par with velveeta mac n cheese, but a little less cloying and fake tasting. Breadcrumbs add a good texture. This has an easier flavor. It doesnt make me feel like I ate processed junk. Doesn't taste like homemade (zero expectation of that on my end, but people can be really weird with reviews & community questions). It is a shelf stable product, nice for quick meals. Convenience food.

I'll buy it again (in fact I just added it to my subscribe & save order)

title: tasty, dehydrated cheese bites, crunchy, no mess, delicious
text:
Do yourself a favor, portion some out before you start eating it. Once you begin, it is hard to stop. 170 calories per 1 ounce serving, 6 servings per bag. 13 grams protein, 2 grams fiber (can see rest of info in their products pics). Delicious!

I love the crunchy and creaminess of these cheese bites. All cheese flavor with a crunch, like having cheese and crackers! It's pretty much dehydrated cheese if you weren't aware. Very similar to Moon Cheese. Moisture removed and left with crunchy cheesy goodness. Smoked Gouda and cellulose. Small ball-ish shaped bites-- like size of cheese curd, a large marble, piece of popcorn. Easy to pop in mouth. Leaves nothing on fingers. Does not get stuck all up in teeth. Non complicated easy treat. No need to refrigerate. Just enjoy these bites.

I love dehydrated cheese, and buy it as a treat on occasion. I have even purchased packets for use in food/snack themed gifts. I immediately thought that about this.

title: gentle, mild flavor, pale green, hint of natural sweetness, versatile, easy to use
text:
I love Judees products, I order from them regularly as does my mom. She likes it because she can call them, haha. I like it because they offer a wide variety on Amazon, always of great quality, and I like the look, taste, and performance.

I buy vegetable powders. I do buy fresh, frozen, canned, and grow some of my own BUT these past couple of years have led me to add other storage styles to my long term pantry, emergency pantry. Sometimes I cant find certain foods, or it is low, out of stock, looks bad, price is too high. I decided that having some freeze dried vegetables and powders would help me to keep adding nutrition to my meals even when it is not available fresh in store. I havent been too concerned about cabbage, but it is a worthwhile addition.

I have used it in sipping broths, or simply added to food (soups, casseroles, sauces). I am sure there are a slew of other uses. Cabbage is naturally sweet, and i can see it being used in muffins. I will have to try that. So far I have kept the powder in the bag, but I may portion some out into mason jars and vac seal them.

I like it, I would buy it again.

title: easy to work with, plenty of flavor, nice for simmering, or making into noodle bowl broth
text:
Yay, I am so glad to have been able to try this Laksa paste. I really wanted to try it after having had their tasty [[ASIN:R1DZHRPKIHIR5D Rendang sauce]]. I find this Laksa to be easy to work with, makes a very nice simmer sauce OR used toward flavoring a broth for a noodle bowl.

I love the simple ingredients and the fresh taste makes this a worthwhile purchase. I rarely ever spend money at restaurants these days, and I dont have really any near me, especially nothing that offers food of this ilk. So over the years I have self taught to make dishes with flavor profiles like this. And yeh, sometimes I rely on a prefab spice blend. Even so, I'm not an experienced world cuisine cook. I sure do love dishes from all over the world. I will dabble in making some of my own stuff or follow a recipe, but if I can find a decent base sauce I am going to go for it. So TO Me this is very reasonable price. 3 large packets with two smaller packets (2 servings per packet) in each larger pack.

Yep, it is high in sodium. Can clearly see it in the product description. Not outside norm of stuff like this.

As with the Rendang, so easy to use, and really packs a punch of flavor. Saute protein of choice with this sauce, then add coconut milk. Simmer to marry, then spoon out over rice or noodles. Basically do what you want with it.

I like it better than powder packets, I like it better than jars (as I dont want to store any in fridge). I find it tastier than basic red or green curry. This has a more dynamic flavor. Similar but with more flavor and some heat. Just be mindful of sodium.

title: Fall crisp drink. Not too sweet, perfect level of spice, nice carbonation, lovely color
text:
I have Hibiscus Ginger Beer, and it is delightful. Sweet and spicy. Has a nice kick. Lovely as is over ice, or used with booze. I've yet to make a Mule, but its on my list when I want to imbibe a little.

Perfect little fall drink. I say fall because it was a chilly fall day when I decided to drink this, and it tasted rather refreshing, and the spiciness seemed fitting. Pretty color looks nice in a clear glass. I have this in cans, and it arrived in perfect condition.

title: fun flavors, extra caffeine (mix of Robusta & Arabica), I buy this brand often for Headless Horseman
text:
I love this brand. Love it!! It isnt my daily drinker (pricy and I usually go for non flavored coffee), but I buy it 2-3 times a year especially around the fall time when I need my fix of Headless Horseman (pumpkin!). Here's the thing. I dont even really like flavored coffee, but they do a great job of it. Not an artificial taste. The worst coffee in the world to me is Blueberry coffee, but I once tried Wake the Hell Up blueberry coffee (a sample) and loved it so much I bought more. Never thought that would be in my coffee drawer. They make it work. SO heck yeah I was down for a big seasonal assortment. So fun!

Totally stoked to give these a try. Haven't worked through them all, but I am enjoying each. I prefer to drink my coffee black, but I rather like these paired with a little cream. Seems to really bring out the nuances of flavor. The added caffeine is from robusta beans added to the mix, which is a coffee bean that is naturally higher in caffeine (upwards of 25%) than arabica or Columbian. This is a mix of Arabica and Robusta.

Country of Origin is USA, and more specifically Utica NY-- not too far off from my neck of the woods!

title: tasty options, love the extra dark roast, works fine in my original machine
text:
Pleasant assortment for office or for a household of different preferences. I personally enjoy extra dark coffee, and so that has been my go to capsule. It brews fine in my Nespresso machine (I have an older one that seems to work well with most standard capsules). I haven't head anyone in my house mention any issues with brewing. Everyone gives a thumbs up on whatever they brew.

6 boxes of 10 capsules (60 capsules total) are compatible with Nespresso OriginalLine machines like Essenza, CitiZ, Prodigio, U, Inissia, and Pixie. NOT COMPATIBLE WITH VERTUOLINE MACHINES .

Looks like they have a money back guarantee if for some reason they dont work. Looks like some of the reviews are from earlier in year, so perhaps they made some changes since then.

If they didnt work for me, I would harvest the coffee and make a pot.

title: flavorful, excellent size for smaller needs (quick saute, quick soup, sipping broth)
text:
Nice natural chicken flavor. Reduced sodium. Still salty but doesnt have as much as their regular. I didnt realize that Swanson carried small containers of broth. Normally I go with Kitchen Basics. I know that larger containers are the better deal, but the small ones rock my world for most uses. I sometimes just need a splash, or I just want a quick portion for use as a sipping broth (usually I will add some leftover bits of food and additional spices to add boost of flavor and belly satisfaction). I took a sip direct from bottle and instantly noted the nice chicken taste. I then proceeded to use it in a healthy sauté for some broccoli--very nice. The last portion I used to make a sipping broth (so nice and comforting on chilly afternoons). Another way that I use the mini containers is when I make some basmati rice. I like using a little broth, stirring in some coconut powder (or manna), add a little garlic, salt, and pepper.. then eat as it or add some vegetables on top.

I decided to see all what else Swanson has that I may not have been aware of, which brought me to making a couple of purchases, haha. I dont rate on price but these minis are pricy even in comparison to some of their fancier options (sipping bone broth for example, which would normally be marketed with higher price tag. Also a bit more than the Kitchen Basics). Hope they come out with a coupon, subscribe and save, or price change to be more competitive with their own offerings and among other brands.

title: enthusiastically adorable festive cocoa collection, flavors are unique, taste is adequate
text:
It's super cute, totally gift worthy, or for use as a display since it is so festive looking. Each container is a critter shaped box. Inside is a packet of cocoa. Really could get creative with this. As a single gift, it is well done because the box it all comes with is pleasant looking (just like in product pictures). Then that was wrapped in plastic. Could be opened and parted out among several mini gifts or maybe as stocking stuffers, or as part of a larger drink themed gift (add in some fancier, tastier cocoa, coffee, tea, mini booze bottles, snacks, peppermint sticks, etc). Each box is an adorable festive looking container of hot cocoa.

Different flavors, many well outside the norm of what I normally have. I haven't made many, will be a long while before I work through the entire box. But the flavor is fine. I really dont expect it to be amazing but it is within realm of acceptable. I never really have outstanding hot cocoa mixes. And I certainly wont compare it to homemade. Use water or milk, add as much or little as you want. Maybe add to coffee? Maybe add a spoonful of unsweetened cocoa or cacao powder to boost nutrients and chocolate flavor. Or keep it as is. It's fine. I would totally be stoked to receive this as a gift.

"locally sourced in the USA", but is product of China. The Thoughtfully brand has been pretty transparent with their info, which I am pleased with.

title: Fabula has fresh coffee, mild cocoa flavor, use with cream to tease out cocoa nuances
text:
Mild chocolate flavor that is teased out when paired with cream. Smooth, easy to drink. Makes a nice afternoon pick me up. Nice to have on hand to offer to others who enjoy flavored coffees. I prefer coffee as dark as can be, as strong as can be, black and unsweetened. So, flavored is not my "go to", but I like it on occasion for something different. Usually come fall I get the craving for a little sweet treat drink. If coffee is mild or flavored, then I usually want a little cream and sweetener. I will buy flavored coffee for use as a base to added flavoring like pumpkin spice seasoning, cinnamon seasoning, various syrups or specialty creamers. This chocolate is natural tasting, more like a light cocoa. I will be using this with some added hot cocoa mix, or added unsweetened cocoa powder to make it a caffeine laden cup of hot chocolate.

Individually wrapped (not plastic), paper cup bottom. Fresh.

I've had Fabula on various occasions. All fresh and smooth. Still, not my go-to coffee. But I like it enough to order when the opportunity comes up. I like their ground or whole bean best. The K-cups are good but are way outside my price range per cup. I dont rate on price. Currently there is a sizeable coupon offering which makes it more attractive.

title: all of their flavored coffees are mild and easy to drink, I use cream to bring out flavor

title: tasty fresh fig newtons, well packaged, loos good, tastes good, no problems whatsoever
text:
My packages of Fig Newtons are fresh and tasty. I got them through the warehouse so the best buy date is on the shorter side (month or so out), but i expected that. Will likely have longer date through regular grocery category purchase. I' not concerned. Totally good, well packaged, tastes great.

Have always loved fig cookies. I like the original, as well as flavored varieties. This is my favorite combo. Just hits the spot with a need to eat the whole package like I would with nearly any other sweet treat.

Usually eat as is, but i have warmed up a couple of cookies on occasion for an extra special treat. Can be nice crumbled over yogurt or ice cream.

title: pantry staple, excellent size for smaller cooking needs, add splash of flavor, healthy cooking
text:
These are 8.25 ounce mini containers of broth. While pricy in comparison to the large 32 ouncers that can be purchased, this is a size I greatly appreciate for many of my needs. I like it for making a quick soup, or a quick sipping broth. Just add some bits of left over food and spices. I use it when I just need a splash for flavor and/or healthy cooking. I can do that with the large containers too, but I simply dont want to buy/use the large containers all the time. There is NO mystery about what I am buying here, so for that reviewer that is crying over the size, I ask.. why did you buy it?

Currently $32.82 for a box of 12, which makes is $2.74 each. Competitive with local stores, if not cheaper. Obviously bigger containers are cheaper and therefor provide more bang for buck. But if you just want the occasional use item, a convenience item, this is perfectly good. I like the flavor just fine. I usually buy their low or no sodium option.

Works for convenient noodle bowls at the office. I will keep a couple bottles of this and some precooked noodles, rice or whatever (shelf stable kind that can sit in my drawer), then I just bring in some fresh bits of food to add to it all.

Best by date isnt a hard expiration date. If you bought from the warehouse, you may have a shorter date than a regular purchase. All fine, and all fine well beyond the date. It is not a safety date. Be smart, understand what the dates signify and save a few bucks by not tossing the moment the date rolls over. Plenty of good sites to confirm what the dates mean and why we have them.

title: leaked bottles made for messy unboxing, I otherwise like their products-style, flavor, presentation
text:
I have had a few items from Thoughtfully Store. Their listings usually include country of origin (China) but on this one, I don't see it anywhere on the page. I hadnt looked before ordering since I already knew, but I they really should have this highlighted.

I have had other syrups by them, similar flavors, and haven't had any issue with flavor. I haven't tried them all; I started with the fall flavors. I can taste the sweetness with a mild flavor when added to my coffee. It reminds of monin, torani, etc. Same ingredients, or very close to.

I see most of their stuff for use as a gifting item. Otherwise I normally just buy a bigger bottles of stuff I like.

The assortment of flavors is great. I love the different sizes and shapes. Visually appealing. I love how one of the reviewers placed them on a two-tiered tray. It is such a welcoming, homey sight to have a coffee corner with little syrups and such.

Use what you need to make the strength of flavor come through. I think 2 TBS is typical, but I prefer a lighter flavor so I go with half of that for 8 ounces of coffee. I'll also be using these in hot cocoa soon, or to flavor frosting.

Why the lower rating? Because the bottles leaked. My other syrups by them in similar packaging had no leaks. But this one? Lots of leaking. I couldnt even open the box as it was glued shut from the dried syrup. I had to tear into it. So that tells me it didnt happen in transit, but instead was sent in that condition. Boo/hiss. Though to be fair, I am not sure if anyone would have noticed it. It was more like glue in the corners, and didnt scream "syrup leak!".

Oddly, I could not find the bottle (or bottles) that leaked. There is one (vanilla) that appears to have less in it, so I surmise that is the one. Yet, they all have a wrapping around the cap, and the caps are well situated. I shook them to try to get them to leak, but none did. So I think the bottle laying on side just allowed a very slow leak that eventually got all over other bottles and box.

****** I CAN STILL USE ALL OF THEM**** so nothing lost here except overall presentation, and some extra clean up/wipe down of each bottle.

Box would have been nice. Gift worthy had it not been syrup ruined. It's a flip top box, and the inside has a list of the flavors and ways to use it. Since I had to tear into the box, most all of that was lost.

Had it been in perfect condition like all other Thoughtfully Store items have been, I likely would have gone with 4.5 stars (4 or 5, not sure. Kind of disappointed that they didnt include the country of origin in the product description, so probably 4 stars). I would have been ecstatic to receive this as a gift. Pair it with some coffee, maybe a couple of mugs, and it would make a stellar gift. But that's only if there aren't any leaks. Or for use for setting around the coffee area at the office.

3 stars (3,5 if I could)

title: a little light, but smells like tequila. Dont drink straight. Best to mix well & let flavors marry
text:
I may be the only one, but I dont mind it. The aroma is distinctly tequila like to me. I decided I needed to try it straight. The initial sip made me cough. I dont know what it is, but there is something peppery about it and tasted nothing like tequila. That sort of muddled the taste for me, but it didnt stop me from going further. Then I proceeded to make their spicy ginger margarita using their [[ASIN:B09WH78W5J Spiritless Horse's Kick Ginger Syrup]] which I am totally in love with. I followed the recipe included in the cocktail recipe booklet it comes with. Shook all the ingredients thoroughly with ice then strained. First sip was ok, but it was actually a couple minutes later that the flavors melded, and the tequila taste came through as it should. In the background, but not too far off. I found it rather pleasant. I actually began to wonder if this had a hint of alcohol because it was pretty close in taste at that point. Very odd how it changed. WHAT is this sorcery? haha

Not sure why such low opinions, but thats the thing with food and drink, it all comes down to personal preference. It is the exact same as booze? No, of course not. I can definitely see using this for a "halfsie". I dont do much alcohol these days, but I really enjoy the ritual of mixing a drink and enjoying at leisure.

Then I made a quick margarita [[ASIN:B0B7YHDT22 using a premade margarita cocktail mixer]]. Same deal. A little light on taste at first, but then seemed to settle into something that distinctly makes me think tequila.

Lovely bottle. Top notch. Worthy of sitting out. Cork top plug, well packaged, comes with recipe booklet. Only aspect about the bottle I dont care for is that I tend to get dribbles down the side when I pour. Maybe I'm just bad at pouring, maybe its the bottle.

title: light cinnamon tastes best with cream, brewed at 6-8 ounces
text:
I like Fabula coffee, but not in love. I like their whole bean or ground best, but I more often use K-cups, so I will give any of them a try for test/review. Their flavored coffees have a distinct flavor. This cinnamon really comes through when brewed at 6-8 ounces. I find flavored coffees to taste best when paired with creamer (non dairy or dairy). I otherwise drink my coffee black, unsweetened. I like to use flavored coffee as the base for some flavor syrups and creamers. I tend to get a little more adventurous come fall and winter. So this cinnamon was a great base for a pumpkin spice creamer. Or regular cream with a sprinkle of added spice. Stuff like that. Flavored coffee is never my first cup of the day. It is more like when I want something different late morning or early afternoon.

Individually wrapped in a non-plastic compostable pouch. They make a point to say that "I am not plastic". The cup itself is a thick paper cup. I have no problem using these in my Keurig. Maybe once I noticed some drips out the sides as it brewed.

Easy open

I tend to brew 8 ounces. So I imagine that the strength of the flavor will depend on how much water is used.

There is a huge coupon available which makes it nice for trying out. I dont rate on price, but this is pricy per pod. $1.87 per pod is insane to me. I recommend [[ASIN:B0B64CNV28 Envipods Fresh Roasted Coffee]] for similar style of pod and more budget friendly pricing. Try

title: easy to make, I made as is--pretty good. But begs to be doctored up, get creative. Leans sweet
text: I like corn pancakes, whether it is made with corn flour or mesa (this is a combo) or if I use buttermilk pancake base (or sourdough starter) and add in corn. kernals. While I prefer the latter, a corn mesa based pancake is nice. I did not doctor this up, but if I were to do so I would likely add in corn kernals for added texture, and then maybe add some hatch chili or jalapeno peppers to balance the sweetness. Could have shredded cheese add in, or added on top. Use a spicy honey. Could top with beans and sour cream. And the possibilities go on. For me, this is a base pancake mix, but I liked it for the most part made as is. PAN is a quality brand. I use a variety of products from them. I find their mixes to lean sweet, which I dont mind.

title: Chinese Vermicelli, glass/cellophane noodles, chewy/rubbery (softens w/broth,oils), great color
text:
Pro tip: allow noodle to soak up broth/sauce/ oil to make for normal texture; eliminate rubbery texture.

The are: Glass noodles. Or cellophane noodles. Noodles that work in specific application but not well generalized to other noodle or pasta needs. I took a look again at the description but I dont see it mentioning glass or cellophane noodles. That should be highlighted. I expected a potato/veg based pasta, not a glass noodle (I like glass noodles btw). I still would have tried them, but I would have been more prepared for their use.

If you are not familiar with glass noodles, but are familiar with shirataki noodles, the texture is similar: rubbery, chewy. Here is a hint to make it less rubbery. Let them absorb some water or sauce or whatever. They will soften to a more normal level of chew and texture. For example, I decided to use this with canned clam sauce. I made one whole package, drained, rinsed with cool water, then split between 2 bowls. I added some hot clam sauce on top (sounds gross but it was good). The bowl I ate right away was the typical weird rubbery chew. Good but, doesnt provide the mouth feel/texture that I want. I The other bowl had enough time to cool down and sit for a bit. When I went back to it, the noodles had absorbed a bit of the brothiness of the canned clam sauce. I took a bite. WOW so much better. Weird, since I have worked with glass noodles before, but this is first time I needed to put a little extra effort into it. Still, not too bad.

Sheer appearance. Cooks quickly. Doesnt stick when cool. Not a totally satisfying mouth feel but works well in some dishes (Asian inspired, mostly). Definitely allow it to soak up seasonings, oil, broth.

Neat purple color. Boiled water is blue.

Can be soaked or boiled Consumed hot, cold, or room temp. Nice in stir fries, and noodle bowls. Not at all my preferred way to incorporate noodles. It isnt all that filling to me, but on the plus side it doesnt weigh me down. I like it best paired with loads of vegetables and protein and then use this as an accent. If only because of the slightly annoying, sloppy chewy noodle (if not prepared with a little extra time).

3 packs, each pack contains 2 servings.

4stars. They are pretty much as expected once I realized they are cellophane noodles (aka glass noodles, aka Chinese Vermicelli) . I down rate for the lack of info clarifying what they are, and they should because people need to know. I think the price is pretty good, not that I rate on price. I just think it needs to highlight what kind of vermicelli so people know that they are definitely referring to cellophane noodles. I didnt know, and I am familiar. I can definitely tell others had no idea.

title: convenience, great for quick meal prep or emergencies
text: Looks good, tastes fine. Never as good as fresh cooked rice, but it works in a pinch.  I usually just cook my rice in a rice cooker, but I like having precooked options on hand for convenience and emergencies. Nice to have something I can just heat and eat, or skip heating. Nice to add to soups or other quick sides. Fills the belly. Tastes best when purchased on sale :)

title: tasty, convenient. Zero mess or damage. 5 trays of 20 cups
text:
I see a lot of comments on the condition it arrived. Mine arrived in a very sturdy branded box, and inside there are 5 trays of 20 cups. ZERO leaking, damage. No mess. Perfect. Love the trays. Good way to do it.

Taste is standard breakfast syrup flavor. Benefit over a big jug is that these offer portion control and convenience. Nice for packing in lunches, maybe even use in coffee if you like that sort of flavoring.

Easy peel back lid. Nice thick syrup. Really good flavor to me. Nothing off. It just has that pleasant flavor that I like with my pancakes.

title: good taste and texture
text:
For the most part I find tuna is tuna. I do prefer a firmer chunk over a tin of mush. This is the former. Nice for salads, wrapping, etc. Good taste and texture. A welcome addition to my pantry

Product of Thailand (fyi many are).

title: sweet, healthier candy bar. Mid day snack bar, or crumble over yogurt or oatmeal
text:
LaraBars tend to be sweet, but I like that they use real ingredients. I will eat a portion of it on its own, or sometimes I break it up and sprinkle over yogurt or oatmeal. Nice as a "healthier candy bar" too.

Super pricy, but I dont rate on price. We can see the price before ordering, and we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, prices fluctuate, and of course inflation. But yeh, I dont buy these unless they are on sale (closer to the older price).

Any that I have eaten from this box have been fresh. No problems, Love the variety.

title: yes, there are clams. Nice flavor in every bite that clings to pasta, doctor up or eat as is
text:
Soaks up into the pasta making for perfectly balanced bite. dont often eat clam sauce, really a rare thing. Not my go to flavor profile. But I dont mind it. So when I saw this on sale, I decided to buy a case as I figured it would help flesh out my longer term pantry. Gives it a little added variety for something different. Stock what you eat, but also add in variety (and buy on sale).

Works fine on pasta, or use as a base to chowder. Robust fishy clammy taste with chunks of clam, Layered flavor with garlic, parsley, black pepper, onion. You may prefer to add other seasonings. May want to add more clam if you need the added texture (tastes plenty clammy as is). Every clam sauce is different. What makes it good to you is subjective. To me, it's tasty. It is a bit brothy. As far as I know, clam sauce is supposed to be a bit brothy, not creamy or thick. The flavor clings well to the pasta.

I dont have broth sitting in the bowl. I simply warm this up, divide over pasta, grate some parmesan cheese on top, maybe add a chunk of bread. Definitely tastes liked clams.

I dont know what else to say.. I find it perfectly fine. Maybe if I had it more often then I would have more discerning tastes. But my knowledge and experience is limited regarding clam sauce. I can only just say that I personally liked it.

4.5 stars

title: mild, pleasant flavor, pair with rice and/or naan for more substance. Leans soup like
text:
Good flavor, very mild, a little soup like than what I expected. Not brothy, just a little thin. Tiny lentils dont add a lot of texture, hence my immediate thought that it needs something more. Needs something to go with it- rice, naan, something. More lentils?

I know this is convenience food. Of course it isnt going to be the same as what can be attained from a restaurant or from ones kitchen. I wish I lived closer to Indian restaurants (and/or could afford meals out). I have on my bucket list to learn a couple of my favorite Indian dishes, but I know it wont come close. SO I try stuff like this, and keep a slew of options in my pantry. Can it give me that taste that I want, when I want it? Sorta. It's passible. I think it could be doctored up a bit. But even as is I like it. Ingredients are good, and I would buy this again (on sale).

title: NO surprises, I can taste the flavors, use according to preference, nice little sampler/gift item
text:
These met or exceeded my expectation. 5 stars, and here is why:

--Product page, pictures, and information all match up. No surprises. I knew the ingredients, country of origin, flavors, and serving size and calories before hitting the order button. I dont rate on price, but I comment. I looked around and didnt really find better price; seems competitive for the size, flavor, style. Maybe outside of Amzn.

--Bottles arrives well intact, no leaking, well sealed, cute unmarred packaging. Has a little handle. Nice as a sampler, for tucking away in desk drawer at the office, or adding to a coffee/cocoa/tea themed gift

--Flavor. I am surprised that the flavors come through as well as they do. Perception of flavor will vary among users. What I like you may not, what you like I may not. You get the idea. I added 1 TBS to 10 ounces of dark roast coffee. That was enough flavor for me. Serving size is 2 tablespoons. So adjust according to preference. I find that coffee syrups taste best when used alongside creamer of some sort. Seems to highlight the flavor and carry it better. I would also use this in smoothies or tea (and add creamer there too)

--One minor flaw that works in our favor. The listing and container says that one bottle contains ONE 2 TBS serving (30 ml). But there is actually 45 ml in each bottle, providing 3 TBS (or 1.5 servings). Or more (or less) depending on how much you use. 1 TBS is the max for me for a regular sized mug, so 3 servings for me.

--Overall, it basically as expected. I dont know if it is necessarily better than others, but definitely (to me) not worse. AGAIN take a look at all the info listed in the description if ingredients or COO turn you off, then keep shopping. If all the information wasnt there then I would have down rated, as I prefer to know these things. They did well in terms of transparency.

I am just pleased that I can make out the taste of the flavors. My first use was with the Pumpkin Caramel. I could taste the deep caramel flavor first, and then as I continued to sip I was like, "oh there's the pumpkin". Pumpkin in and of itself is a mild tasting food or drink item. So if you are looking for the spice portion that is often paired with pumpkin, then sprinkle some spice on, or grab for their Pumpkin Spice Syrup (which is included as part of this set). Pumpkin Vanilla is nice (I add a sprinkle of spice). I haven't yet used the Chocolate Pumpkin. I am not a fan of chocolate in coffee, but I will gladly add it to a smoothie OR HOT CHOCOLATE. Ooh yeh!

I have a lazy susan cupboard full of syrups of this nature. Funny since I prefer my coffee black, unsweetened.
BUT I am a sucker for all things fall looking or tasting. So it's loaded with those flavors. I tend to go with Skinny syrups (this brand offers them too I think), but will certainly use regular syrups too since I dont need much to flavor it up. Syrups last forever, but they usually have a best by date. This one is dated a year out for end of September 2023.

4.5 stars (since we cant do halves, 5 it is as I like it better than 4 given all the bullet points above)

title: has that strong oaked taste & smell of bourbon, obviously no alochol, could add some in for halfsie
text:
I have liked all the Spiritless products. If you need the booze, then you probably wont like spiritless options. It's nice though to have on hand for others who may choose to not imbibe, or want to scale back yet still have the look and feel of drink in hand.

I dont drink much in the way of alcohol anymore. My body just sort of feels it too much, so I either skip it or look for ways to imbibe without all the alcohol. So I do a lot of "halfsies". I have tried their Kentucky 74, and found it just oaky/oaked enough to taste like bourbon to me. This Whiskey Sour uses Kentucky 74, and it definitely reminds me of a whiskey sour. It has that oaked smell and taste. Little tangy bite. It can be consumed as is, or spiritless bourbon can be added, or a little alcohol laden bourbon can be added for a halfsie. Or add red wine for a lower alcohol "New York Sour". Personally it makes for a very passible cocktail. Super pricy though.

I REALLY like it when poured over ice, with the addition of [[ASIN:B07KQ3JS31 Rex Whiskey Flavored Amarena Cherries in Syrup]]. I add a few cherries and stir in a spoonful of syrup. The Whiskey Sour maintains its flavor, yet is made better (to me) with this addition. It tastes like a cocktail, and I'm hard pressed to believe it isnt one. The smell and taste hits my nose and throat like a regular whiskey sour. But I dont feel weird from alcohol.

35 calories, 8 grams added sugar

Ingredients: Kentucky 74 Distilled Non-Alcoholic Spirit, Water, Sugar, Citric Acid, Natural Flavors, Natural Colors, Sodium Benzoate (preservative)

title: precooked corn flour/mesa for arepas, etc. Easy to make, quick. Fresh content!
text:
Good brand, easy to make. I like this over buying a big bag of mesa as I dont go through it quickly enough and end up tossing it before using it all up. This premeasured bag is so much better. Will stay fresh for a while, and makes just enough arepas for my needs. If you make a lot then grab their 5 lb bag of precooked corn flour for a few dollars more (or 2 lb bag for less than this packet). But I like the packet, and will likely buy it again.

Dont need to add anything-- just enough water to form dough balls, then cook in an oiled skilled. Press them down a little for a more flattened shape.

title: convenient, quick and easy
text:
This review is for Sesame Teriyaki Noodle Bowl. Convenience meal for when I dont want to do any cooking. I can eat as is, or add in some vegetables or proteins, or even added water to make a broth bowl.

Directions are for microwaving, as many convenience items make use of microwave. If you really need to, you can simply add the contents to a small sauce pan and heat it up that way. Directions are included in the product description so none of this should come as a surprise.

5 stars simply because *I* like it, and I buy a variety of this stuff to keep in hand.

title: sweet cornbread with undertones of vanilla
text:
It makes a SWEET cornbread. Sweet with undertone of vanilla. I prefer sweet, so this worked for me) not the best but was stilol pretty good made as directed). Usually I make my own or get Jiffy. I like to add creamed sweet corn to add moisture and sweetness. Then sometimes I balance it by adding hatch or jalapeno peppers. For sake of review I made this simply as instructed. I didnt doctor it up any. Only thing I did differently was to use an 8x8 inch pan rather than muffin tin.

I baked it in a large toaster oven, and didnt pay much attention to tie. I just checked it quickly on occasion. Took out when knife came clean. Baked up evenly, not too dry. Has a nice crumble. Paired it with a "taco pasta" I made. Was going to make chili with left over taco filling, but then at last minute while this was baking decided to out it over rotini pasta instead. Made for nice extra filling meal. I like corn bread to be more dessert like, and this really did remind me of a vanilla cake with grit (in a good way, from corn meal).

I'd consider this again. It made a good sized amount. I would probably play around with it a little to get the taste and texture I prefer. I am glad I made it as directed so I could report back what I experienced.

I have had other products by this company and have been pleased. Not wowed per say, but reasonably pleased.

title: it's so good its addicting, hard to stop taking swigs. Ugh, its so good. LOVE GINGER!!
text: I love this so much, wish it wasnt so pricy. It is so good straight up. I love ginger, and this packs that lovely heat of the spice. Little heat, little sweet, little tang, yet definitely has that perfect spicy kick that I desperately look for in ginger based products. I really like it as is, but will be adding it to club soda to make it feel like it lasts longer.

title: very tasty Lychee syrup--thick & sweet, works great in iced green tea Boba tea
text:
Thick and sweet. I adore all things LYCHEE. I use lychee syrup in my non milk green tea bubble/boba tea. It is my favorite way to have boba tea. My favorite brand is [[ASIN:B0147N45ME by Tea Zone]] but they only carry very large containers. I still have one I bought 5 years ago. I really need to toss it and start fresh. I am STOKED to find a smaller lychee syrup that has similar consistency. Pretty much same exact ingredients (btw this uses ACE-K as one of their sweeteners, thought I would point it out in case you are aiming to avoid. SHows on the label in the product pictures).

This is a thick, nearly gel like syrup (as is my other one). THAT is what I like. I have tried lychee syrup from popular brands that are often used in coffee and Italian soda, and those dont cut it in terms of flavor or viscosity. I'd say this Lychee by Fusion Select is very close to my Tea Zone. Smaller container, about twice as expensive in terms of price per ounce, but the other is such a large container that it is bulk pricing, and I just dont go through it in a reasonable amount of time. Takes up a lot of space too. This smaller size is easier to store. I had been using their [[ASIN: B0987Y4G4B Fusion Select MANGO syrup]] which is also quite tasty and worked well with boba tea (as well as ice cream topper). At the time I ordered it I did not see Lychee as an option. Pleased to have now tried the Lychee option.

For my needs, preferences, and how it tastes compared to the brand I normally use-- this totally works for me. 5 stars for that. Not because it is better or cheaper or whatever, but because it meets my expectations and is very similar to what I normally buy in a more reasonably sized container.

title: sweet tart flavor, can easily use more water, made me feel good- like an energy drink, motivated
text: Pretty good. Has that sweet tart taste. I tried it in a very full mason glass to get the 16.9 ounce recommendation. I could easily use more water or use half a packet. It did a good job of making me feel hydrated. I made up a cup before heading outside on a hot muggy day to work. I actually thought that maybe this was also an energy drink because I felt motivated to keep on working outside. I didnt feel run down. So for that, I give it 5 stars. I dont love love the flavor, but I could tell I felt good drinking this. Instead of grabbing another cup of coffee, once I hit submit for this review I am going to go make up a cup.

title: legit tangy lemon made from the entire lemon (skin, pulp, seeds, juice). Wonderful!
text:
Well this is sure lemony. Legit tart lemon. If you need a bright, tangy, truly lemon lemon powder then this is it. Little goes a long way. Definitely made my lips pucker when I tried it directly off fingertip. I LOVE lemon, so this made me very happy. I haven't always liked Orgfun, but most products have been very good. This is probably my favorite of their stuff, and all lemon powder options out there. It will be a repurchase.

SUPERFRUIT POWDER freeze-dries those whole lemons which include Skin, Pulp, Seeds, and Juice to make organic powder, retaining all of the valuable nutrients.

title: peanut butter mini bar is perfect sweet treat or on the go to stave off hunger
text:
Of course they are half the size of regular bars they are called MINI after all! I bought these specifically because they are smaller. I have a slew of Kind bars in my snack bar basket, and I like to carry a few on me throughout the day in case I get hungry. I dont always want a full bar, and I dont always want to wrap it up for later. My job isnt really conducive to sit down meals of any substance, so I just keep some small nibbles on hand in case I get hungry (normally I am not hungry until dinner time). Any of the minis are 100 calories or less per bar.

Small- just a few bites. Chewy? That depends on a few factors, primarily temperature. If the ambient temperature is on the cool side then these may seem a tad hard. They will become chewy in mouth, but you could stick in pocket for a couple of minutes to help it along.

This review is for the "Peanut Butter" flavor option. Simple, Sweet, peanuty. Lovely as a sweet treat or as means to stave off hunger.

Oats, tapioca syrup, sugar, canola oil, peanut butter (peanuts, sea salt), honey, brown rice, brown rice flour, palm kernel oil, peanut flour, chicory root fiber, millet, quinoa, nonfat milk powder, sea salt, peanut oil, soy lecithin, natural flavor, Vitamin E (tocopherols to maintain freshness).

title: perfectly tasty Herbs de Provence with Sea Salt, makes for nice finishing salt
text:
Pinch of flavor. Wide open jar made of "premium carton box with a cork lid". I really didnt notice that it is a carton container as it is sturdy, robust and feels super solid in hand. Attractive clean look. I dont have any problems uncorking the lid. Good snug seal. I keep it out on my counter primarily as a finishing salt.

I like Herbs de Provance, and I usually get it as herbs only, not blended with salt. This is a very nice finishing salt. I have been enjoying it over sliced garden cucumbers and later will be add it over baked chicken thighs. Just one of those herb blends that seems to go well with everything, No particular taste dominates which is the magic of Provence herbs.

A chuncky salt with Thyme, Rosemary, Marjoram, Green Oregano, Hyssop, Red and Oregano

I would add this into a food themed gift basket

Produced in France

title: no stir, smooth, creamy, lightly sweet, not strong PB taste but within realm of typical
text:
Skippy Natural peanut butter spread: Peanuts, sugar, palm oil, and salt.
Not sure why it is called a spread. I dont notice anything all that different from their other peanut butter or any peanut butter, really. I wonder if the amount of peanuts used is less.

Anyway, I think it tastes good, and this multi pack makes nice addition to my long term pantry. I've never had unopened peanut butter go bad in my life, so I didnt pay attention or care what their best by date is (you do know that that isnt an expiration date right?).

title: slug free, fresh natural peanut butter, knead well, just peanuts and a little salt
text:
In short: Unsweetened natural peanut butter with just a smidge of salt. Good fresh taste, and excellent option over others that add oils, sugars, and excess salt. Premium price but I dont rate on price (it comes from New Zealand, costly shipping, etc) . I'd be comfortable using this in treat toys (kongs, lickymats) for my dogs, and the ease of use makes me happy. Knead thorough to reincorporate oil.

I like that this comes in various quantities. This 150 pack is just on big box of peanut butter filled packets. The packets are thick, durable, and will likely keep the peanut butter fresh for a very very very long time. I have used Justin's brand years beyond the best by date and have it still taste great, and this packaging is much more robust. So if you are looking to add to long term prep supplies, this may be a contender.

Because the peanut butter does not have added oils, this will need a thorough kneading. You need to massage it long enough to reincorporate the separated oil from the peanut butter. Think of how jars of natural peanut butter will have a layer of oil on top and how it needs to be stirred back in. This is the same, but in a much easier format. Now that I think of it, I would rather pay more for these packets instead of a jar of natural peanut butter because I never ever manage to get a good mixing. Anyway.. knead it and knead it again. Really give it a good massage. Might be easier in warmer temps, but cooler temps will need extra kneading. If you open it and there is oil, then you didnt knead well enough.

Claims to have 25% more good fats than non high oleic peanut butter

Tear off to open, some packets have torn half way and I used scissors for remainder. Might be a little tricky for on the go use, but I havent had problem getting it out. Nice for squeezing directly into mouth or over some crackers, etc. I tend to pack snacks for on the go use as my job isnt conducive to a sit down full meal. Peanut butter is always part of the snack pack, and I always use packets. I also keep an air tight/critter tight container in my car with snacks like this for emergency use.

title: good strong coffee, daily use and emergency use. Use hot water or shake with cold
text:
I Like it. I use a variety of Nescafe products (love their Gold espresso). I really enjoy instant coffee. Funny, since I have all sorts of brewing systems- pour over, French press, drip, Keurig, Nespresso, but sometimes instant just really hits the spot. Love the convenience. Little goes a long way. Makes nice addition to chocolate desserts, gives a little added dimension to the flavor.

Good strong coffee taste, use as much or as little as you want to your liking. Tastes good black (I prefer black coffee) but I also like it with creamer- especially the Nestle coffeemate liquid creamer.

title: easy to drink, nice chocolate flavor, tad too sweet for me, but I would buy this again (4.5 stars)
text:
Rick milk chocolate is pretty good. So sweet though! I dont know why they need to add stevia as well as glucose syrup and sugar. Why do we need things to be so sweet? I normally dont care for chocolate drinks, but when it comes to Carnation, it is the flavor I associate it with (used the powder packets back in the day), so I went with chocolate (and it was on sale). Despite the sweetness, I dont mind drinking these. It has a pleasing flavor. Overall very easy to drink. I would consider this again.

I like stuff like this for use on the go, or as a base to a more hearty smoothie or "healthy" milkshake. Can use as creamer too. I keep stuff like this stacked in my pantry for emergency use. Works in a pinch to help fill the belly.

I like that it has some fiber (3 grams). The other options dont have any.

title: a little thicker and chewier, nice mouth feel, great flavor. Fresh. Yum!
text: I often purchase Bobs Red Mill products. I love being able to buy multi packs on Amazon. Convenient and good price. I love oats of all sorts, and usually just buy whatever looks good at the best price. I use oats often, so I love keeping my pantry stocked up. These have a good chew, good mouth feel. Nice flavor. Fresh!

title: sweet with mild heat, nice change up from usual sweet citrus margaritas. Love the kick of mild heat
text:
A little something extra special with the use of Hatch chilis, which range from mild to medium in heat. So if you are looking for hot hot then maybe go for a jalapeno mixer. Just the right amount of sweet, tang, and heat. Back of throat type of heat, not burning. Very nice. Add tequila and maybe some lime, and it makes a lovely drink. I love the sweet heat so much that I have made some N/A spritzers, or halfsies (my body doesnt handle alcohol these days it seems, but I still enjoy a little when I can) for times I want a drink but not deal with the full feels from booze.

I'm not a margarita aficionado. My thoughts are based on the occasional drink as one who really enjoys the sweet and spice combo. To me this has a nice clean taste and I would order this again

title: good assortment, fun pairing with Tajin (which is a kitchen spice staple),
text:
I have the kit that includes six, 2 ounce bottles of assorted mixers, 1 jigger, 1 bottle of Tajin seasoning. Packed in a basic, but festive looking packaging. Stick in a gift bag with tissue if gift giving.

Normally I see Margarita mixers being used at 1 ounce per drink, so with 6 small bottles I would say that it has 12 servings. Adjust based on your drink preference. Big drink? Use one full bottle.

This is a pleasant little set. I think it would make a nice little gift, especially if add in a bottle of tequila. The mixers work fine for N/A drinks too. Looking at the other stuff on this page, I think the "ultimate" option that includes 2 branded mason jars, large bottle of classic mixer, a jigger, and a bottle of Tajin is the best value. My little kit is nice for trying different margarita mixers.

If you dont care for Tajin to rim the glass, it is a tasty food spice. I buy it/see it at the grocery store. I like it on refried beans, potatoes, a little sprinkle on my burritos, stuff like that. Mmm. It isnt too spicy to me when use in or on foods, but it is a tad spicy when rimming a glass. I like this paired with the classic, skinny, or spicy mixers. Paired with the strawberry or watermelon is kinda weird but also kinda good. I havent tried it yet with the mango, I expect that to be extra good. Anyway, this has been fun to try. Glad I tried it. I didnt always use tequila, and I didnt always use the typical full amount of tequila. I also enjoy a nice N/A drink (because my body revolts against it not because I have any moral issue with it, haha). So I found some workarounds-- make a drink without the alcohol, or use a whole lot less.

The spice of the seasoning and the sweetness of any of the mixers is a fun change up from the usual. If I were to get this again and have it with friends, I may have the usual sugar rim option as well as the Tajin.

5 stars because it is cute, festive, and appears exactly like it does in pictures. I dont rate on price, extra hard to these days anyway. But I comment. I think it is a tad pricy for what it is, but its going to be a nice little gift or host gift for anyone who enjoys margaritas and enjoys trying something a little different (if they havent had tajin before)

title: high quality Rasa brand, intriguing assortment, this makes for pleasant cuppa, use French press!
text:
Rasa is a quality brand, really comes down to preference in taste. Over the past year I have acquainted myself with a few variations from Rasa and have been pleased with them all. I am a coffee drinker, but will also drink teas, tisanes, alternatives of any sort. I particularly love anything that is multi purpose-- a nice drink with added benefits, yes please!

Some of their selections have a more robust taste that is strongly [[ASIN:B09LJQ6MB9 reminiscent of coffee]] while others are more of a [[ASIN:B09NB9SSWL tea coffee hybrid]] taste. This is like a light coffee leaning toward tea. It is dynamic tasting and provides an experience as well as a good cuppa. It's pleasing to the tastebuds as well as to the sense of well being. I highly recommend this brand, and to try different ones (though pricy, I know). Would make for a nice coffee/tea themed gift. Though I would make sure recipient has a french press or moka pot (or buy one as part of gift!)

Please use a french press. I have never been able to successfully make it in a pour over style. It "kinda" worked, but I could tell I was doing a disservice to the product. I think French Press makes most sense because the particles are large (tea like) and they absorb a bit of water making any filter used get saturated quickly. That being said, I tried using a tea pot with strainer, and that wasn't any better. Go French Press.

title: for something different. Mild flavor, great texture, versatile. Soft peel back lid
text:
Goodness this exceeds my expectations. Season makes some excellent products, so I am not surprised that this mackerel is so good. So much better than other canned mackerel. I dont eat a lot of canned fish, but I try to keep a variety of foods in my pantry. I do enjoy the occasional sardine, and less often mackerel. I usually buy sardines from Season, so when I saw this mackerel in the warehouse I decided to give it a try. Glad I did, it is delicious.

Mild taste, pleasant mild aroma. Little less fishy than sardines. Really easy to eat. I added it on top of some [[ASIN:B0B8P7YQT1 healthy lupini bean pasta]] and just gobble it up. I just dump the contents fish and all right on top of the pasta. It's so good. Easy to eat direct from can, or add to salad, or mash up a little to make a sandwich (like a tuna sandwich).

Well packaged, and I was surprised to see such a long best by date (12/2024) for something i bought from the warehouse.

I'm happy, and wouldnt hesitate to buy it again.

title: easy to over cook, good flavor, leans toward too soft. Like it tho. PS: might experience GAS
text:
1 box each: Rotini, Elbows, and Penne. Be very careful of cook time. In fact, disregard the directions, and just stand there and watch. Try them every 30 seconds. They get soft quickly. I made mine in my [[ASIN:B09V85M4FJ well loved hot pot]] so it is possible it cooks quicker in that than over the stove. I also made about 1/3 of the box rather than whole box, so the time is affected there too.

I'm not over the moon, but I like it. I am used to pasta like this, and it has that odd tell-tale flavor that I rather like. It is no substitution for regular pasta, but when I want something pasta like but not take the heavy carb hit (still loaded with carbs, but there is more to it nutritionally), I turn to pastas like these. I really like [[ASIN:B08DVCDPJ6 Bentilia Zimmunity pasta]] as it has a firmer mouth feel and great taste (purchase history shows i have purchased it a few times in the past couple of years). I also like "purefit" pastas.

While this Lupini bean pasta has a good flavor (I can eat it plain, or with a little salt and olive oil), it is too tricky on the cooking time. It doesn't seem to withstand other ingredients without falling apart. I stirred in some avocado, kalamati olives, some seasonings, and topped with [[ASIN:B000HDMW9M Season Mackerel in olive oil]] and it began to just turn into much. Totally possible that I overcooked it, so next time I will take it out while still firm to that way if it continues to cook once drained, then it will perhaps hold up better. That was with the rotini.

I often make non tomato sauce toppings for pasta like this. I like making a quick ac n cheese using nutritional yeast, some oil (or reserve the pasta water--flavorful and thick), and seasonings. Stuff like that.

So overall, if you can get the cook time right it is tasty.

But..might get gassy later.

title: just freeze dried fruit in powder form, perfectly fine, little goes long way
text:
Basically: Freeze dried, nothing else. Not dried fruit juice. Freeze dried real raw fruit in powder form. Light powder, light peach taste, similar to freeze dried peach slices. Know that freeze dried takes out water content but leaves most nutrition intact. Yet can slightly alter flavor. Vegetables tend to be sweeter, fruits tends to me more mellow. This is on par as expected, and my 5 stars (4.5 if I could) is to reflect that it is what I anticipated in comparison to all the other freeze dried products I have had in my life. 5 stars not because it is better, but because it is perfectly good. Also, it is one of few companies that even have peach powder available. If you cant find it, or cant condone the price, then an alternative would be mango (this brand, or another brand-- other brands are less pricy even compared to their mango). That is readily available across many brands so it is easier to shop based on price. Also tends to have a little more flavor. Rest of review is ramble:

I am a huge fan of freeze-dried goods. I keep a wide variety tucked away in my long-term storage for times when food options are scarce and/or emergency purposes. I keep some on hand for basic day to day use (I dont get to store every day to buy fresh, nor is it always available, or look good when it is). Even when not in an "emergency" container, the product will not likely ever go bad. Most dates on containers indicate a frame of reference for "quality", not safety. Date on mine is a year out. It means nothing to me. Because there is nothing added to this, mild clumping is the norm. Breaks apart fine. (but this bag has been pure powder, no clumps)

I love freeze dried products as it is a nice way to add nutrition to meals in a pinch. Don't need much as 3.5 ounces equates to just under 2 lbs of fruit (28 ounces). Uses are endless. Flavor up some yogurt, smoothies, frostings, baked goods, making syrups, added to homemade energy bars/balls, etc. Freeze dried always tastes a little different to me than the fresh. For example broccoli and cauliflower always tastes sweet to me. This peach tastes like a slightly muted peach flavor. It is good and is as expected. Reminds me of the freeze dried peach slices I buy. Peach isnt my go-to freeze dried item. I usually focus on heavy hitters nutritionally and calorically, but variety is very important. Peach falls into 2nd or 3rd tier in terms of importance to me.

OK, so.. I dont rate on price but I comment. I'm hard pressed to find ANY peach powder, let alone cheap peach powder. Freeze dried anything is pricy, freeze dried fruit is especially high. You are paying for the process. Now add in supply and demand (and global concerns)? You've got a product with a high price tag. Now take a fruit that isn't often found in freeze dried powder form, and there will be a price tag that reflects it. Sucks, but it is what it is. I can see the price here before ordering, so I am not down rating. I'm not keen on the price of most freeze dried stuff (I try to get when on sale) but I find it valuable enough that I invest anyway. If a food item is scarce, I want to know I have access to it from my pantry. Prices fluctuate, so I prefer to focus on taste, quality, overall experience. Eco-Taste is a decent brand that is more budget friendly, but doesnt offer peach. I have some emergency cans for super long term storage that is around price of this, but its slices not powder. I have not found anything less expensive. I DO BUY peach slices, and one could grind it themselves to save a penny. But for real, you wont be saving much if anything.

title: easy to work with, plenty of flavor, high sodium
text:
I love Rendang. This paste by Homiah is very nice. I love the simple ingredients and the fresh taste makes this a worthwhile purchase (I will be coming back for their laksa). I rarely ever spend money at restaurants, and I dont have really any near me, especially nothing that offers food of this ilk. So over the years I have self taught to make dishes with flavor profiles like this. And yeh, sometimes I rely on a prefab spice blend.

A bit pricy. Yet not so bad per packet 2 packets per pack, 6 packets all together.

So easy to use, and really packs a punch of flavor. Saute protein of choice with this sauce, then add coconut milk. Simmer to marry, then spoon out over rice or noodles. Basically do what you want with it.

I like it better than powder packets, I like it better than jars (as I dont want to store any in fridge). I find it tastier than basic red or green curry. This has a more dynamic flavor. Similar but with more flavor and some heat.

I like it 4.5/5 stars

text:
Instant love! This course texture spice blend has FLAVOR!--little spicy, little sweet, little tangy. Zesty! Wakes up the taste buds.
