Anyway, I am delighted with this Chili & Lime seasoning

title: mild, light leaning medium roast, easy to use, stays on mug, great for travel
text:
Looks good, lovely easy to open packaging. The frame anchors well to mug. I have had some that slip easily. No problems here. Smells good. As for taste, it is a tad too light and mild. No tang like a light roast, but it edges close. So I would say this is a light leaning medium roast. Overall smooth, anyway. That's important to me. The coffee taste is too weak for my preference, I did not use much water at all. I normally dont "steep" with pour over coffee. Maybe this needs to be steeped a bit to bring out more flavor.

title: antibacterial properties, MGO rating is THEIR rating, and it is science backed
text:
I saw a review that got me curious. They more or less reduced this to a hack product by stating that the registered symbol is alluding to a fake product. My curiosity led me to snoop around. Good news: THIS IS THE ONLY BRAND that uses an "MGO" rating. MGO™ is a trademark of Manuka Health New Zealand Ltd, and this grade is seen only on their own products. This is why there is a (R) symbol next to the MGO number. Manuka Health isnt trying to bamboozle you. It is their property, and it actually IS meaningful. A quick search secures this info. The MGO™ Certification is scientific, precise, and transparent and leaves no room for misleading. It is also very easy to explain to consumers: MGO™ 100+ Manuka Honey means that in 1 kg of honey there are 100 mg of Methylglyoxal. And so on. If you look just at this product page, they will list their products on a a spectrum from "daily, culinary use" (table grade), to mid range "targeted use", to the rare "ultra care use" with its very high potency. An MGO rating falls in the mid range, antibacterial grade.

What is UMF? Unique Manuka Factor, a standard that tests the antibacterial property of a honey and compares it to phenol, a disinfectant. (The numbers following the letters UMF, refer to the percentage of phenol in water). Any producer must be regulated by the Unique Manuka Factor Association from New Zealand. UMF is more established and it is widely used. When UMF rating is more than 10, it is considered to be active. (Active Manuka Honey). You will ALWAYS see a UMF rating if the product is legit, as well as certifications. This is a standard expectation from New Zealand.

What is MGO? Methylglyoxal. it’s a toxic compound, found in high concentrations in manuka honey (up to 1000 times greater than in other honey, according to German researchers), and it is considered to give its antiseptic edge.

I dont think of it as normal honey. It is a different flavor and texture to me. Manuka is nearly always thick and creamy, with an odd taste. I like it for more medicinal uses. I keep manuka honey on hand for the occasional internal use. I will eat off the spoon or add to tea, usually as a means to sooth a sore throat or to help support my immune system. I have also used it topically with success. I think the latter is where manuka shines. It is not a daily use item for me. Manuka (or any honey) is nice for use as a facial mask too. Price point (especially as a subscribe and save item) is reasonable to me. I like it, I have no problems with it, and now that I have done further research into this company I feel that much more confident with this brand.

title: Must have moka pot. Smells good, not a powder, more course chopped tea
text:
"The freshly ground Téspresso is ideal for Moka pots or any tea espresso machine". I 100% missed this. It is buried in the 4th bullet point. Had I seen this, I would not have ordered it. I00% of the time when I see "black tea powder", it has been instant. I just assumed. That's on me. BUT had there been a full picture of the product, everyone would have seen this. They SHOULD NOT bury the most important aspect of this product down in a paragraph. TWO things would avoild accidental ordering: Show full picture of product (they only show front side), AND make a point to say "FOR USE IN MOKA POT". or if it can be successfully made in/with something else, add that.
I dont have a moka pot. This does not do well in just a filter pot, nor have I made it work in my espresso machine. I can't make it work. Too bad, because this smells really nice. Not a powder, but more like a ground tea. Has a course texture. I do have a French press tucked away somewhere, so I may get that out and give this a try again.

3 stars. Generous, as this is currently not usable. But it smells good, had a safety seal, and the actual quality seems fine.

title: very nice matcha, smooth and luscious
text: I use both ceremonial and culinary grade. Price point is higher on ceremonial. Really nice for those that enjoy the nuances of a cup of prepared hot tea. I usually save money with culinary when using it in smoothie and lattes, but seriously.. ceremonial is always better tasting to me. This matcha is quite pleasant, smooth, some finishing tastes can be altered depending on water temp. It is gorgeous as a latte or added to my smoothies. Love the low key steady energy I get from matcha. Now I have to make a cup :)

title: good strong variety
text:
Nice assortment, right up my ally for strength of taste. I love super strong coffee, and the 11 makes a real nice cuppa. The 9 is good for basic good coffee, leaning strong. I actually do drink decaf as well, usually in the afternoon or evening when I still want a nice warm cup of coffee but cant have caffeine. 20 each, 10 in each box, 60 capsules total.

5 stars just because I personally really like the coffee strengths used in this pack.

title: just plain instant black tea powder, good flavor, easy to use, easily a pantry staple
text:
I like instant tea. This is just instant black tea powder. I use it for making quick cups of iced tea, or to add oomph to other instant tea preparations I have tried but found too weak. This powder is great as I can just make up as little or as much as I want, as strong as I want. I prefer no crea, no sweetener, and this works well for that. I havent tried it hot, as would likely just use a tea bag. OOH but it would work well for when I am using a flavored tea bag and want the boost of flavor (and caffeine) from black tea. I can just add a little of this in. Hmm...

I like this tea, and will definitely consider it again.

title: perfectly sturdy for sushi rolls, hand rolls, poke bowls, noodle bowls, rice balls, etc
text: Love Annie Chun products. I simply call these sushi sheets as I predominantly use them for use in maki rolls and other sushi rolls. It will also take a sheet and make sushi rice balls, add to miso or other brothy noodle bowls and poke bowls. MMMmmm!. In case you are wondering, no these are not the snack style sheets. These (and any sushi sheet) have that robust, chewy, sturdy texture for being able to tightly roll up various goodies without disintegrating. Pricier than some but this is a good brand that I trust. Bulk pricing is nice. 108 sheets (12 packs of 9 sheets) From experience I have never had nori/sushi sheets go bad.

title: way too sweet, predominant cinnamon taste (which I like), easy mix, good taste if not so sweet
text:
Like licking the top of a cinnamon donut- very sweet with cinnamon.

Cinnamon forward, must really like cinnamon as that is the predominant taste next to sweetness. I expected cinnamon because it directly says on bag "Cinnamon Oat" with oat creamer. It pretty much is what I anticipated expect for the extreme sweetness. It is very sweet. To me, it is too sweet. Doesn't taste bad, I would just prefer a subtle sweetness over a dominating sweetness. Easier to add sweetener to taste, can't take it away. If I add more water then it becomes sweet brown water. It uses coconut palm sugar and stevia. I made it according to direction. Oof.

Nice hot as well as iced. Has a nice fall taste, rather nice for these last few days of summer. I'm not new to yerbe mate or other coffee alternatives. I drink everything, and have been for 20 years or so.

$1.92 per serving ($26.99/14). I dont rate on price, we can all see the price. Pricey to me so probably not a repurchase, but more so because of the intense sweetness. I wouldnt compare this to plain tea. This is not plain tea, it is an instant powder with other additions such as mushrooms, oat creamer, cinnamon, and sweetener. Just add water.

3.5 stars. Seriously, the sweetness is too much for me. I'd like it way more if I can get it to be less intensely sweet. I really dont want to have to add stuff to this to make it work. If they made an unsweetened version or used a lot less sweetener it would be way better to me. Often I uprate to 4 stars when I want to give 3.5 but here I will leave it at 3 stars.

title: when made as directed, it makes for brown water. Nearly no flavor. Hint of sweet (which I like)
text:
Concentrated liquid in a tear off packet (I needed scissors, and my there was leakage in my box upon opening).

I can of course make adjustment by using either less water or use a second packet. I have some instant black tea powder I thought about adding in. But why?

title: not powder but granules. Gritty. Hint of lemon. Best in smoothies. Mediocre for toast. NO guac
text:
People are scoffing at "freeze dried", This isn't freeze dried. It is low temp dried.

OK, so this isn't quite for me, but it isnt "bad". It's just avocado and lemon. Depending on what you are hoping to use it for, your expectation may be met or may fall short. Direct from bag, it is gritty with a mix of yellow and dark green. Do a 1:1 ratio of water and avocado powder. Well, actually it is granular, not at all powder like. Stir for a couple of minutes. I even let it sit. Remained gritty. Maybe a small mixer would help. The grit is going to be the turn off factor for a lot of people who want to use this beyond smoothies.

Taste is OK. Very mild avocado taste with hint of lemon. Kinda would prefer no lemon. I think that makes this taste off, especially depending on what it is being use in. Fine if using it in smoothies. Texture is probably best for smoothies, but I was hoping to use it as a topper for toast or coconut basmati rice.

I am finding that avocados in store have been sub par. I dont know.. was just hoping for something better here. No bad, but not what I want.

Again, I think it is fine for the nutrition and use it in smoothies. Can try it in other applications, just know that it wont quite make the same results. Because of the GRIT.

I dont think it is gross; I am not that dramatic. I'll use it up, but it likely wont be a repurchase. I will look for dehydrated or freeze dried avocado powder that can be reconstituted into a non gritty paste.

If this was smooth, and had less of a lemon taste (I love lemon by the way), I would like it more. Quality overall seems fine.

3.5 stars (4.5/5 stars overall quality, 1 stars for grit, 3.5 stars for taste). Since we can't do half stars, then I am going with middle of road rating of 3.

title: sweet and spicy, bit warm for me but doable. Not hot hot
text: Mmmm sweet and spicy! I wanted to try all of these as I love sauces. I went with Gangjung as the flavor profile made my tummy grumble. It has a sticky sweet base with a reasonable level of spicy. I am not one for hot hot, and this is reaching that. Yet it is doable, and of course simmers down when paired with a starch. I havent yet made fried chicken, but I have used it as a coating and dipped for grilled chicken. I plan to make some fried/breaded chicken soon. What I love is the container. Soft sided, with twist off cap spout. I can store it with ease in my fridge. I'll definitely get this again. MMMMMMM

title: pantry staple for wide host of applications
text: I use it exactly the same way as I do gelatin. It can add creaminess--that sense of fattiness., it can make vegan marshmallows, and gummies, and give structure to frostings, ice cream and whips. Nice to have a neutral taste, and it simply a pantry staple. Smells good, works well, no issues. I would buy this again.

title: no wheat, no preservatives, just squid ink powder. Long shelf life, but use up quickly?
text:
Does NOT contain wheat. Nowhere on my package does it say that it contains wheat. The image in the product description says it contains wheat. I default to the product in hand, but my curiosity (and concern for others who need to avoid wheat) got the better of me. I went to their web.page and directly contacted the company to inquire about this conflicting info. I was pleasantly surprised to receive a response the next business day. I am pasting the most relevant portion of the exchange:

"We are very sorry that our product page has showed wrong informations...
The listing that indicated the “product contains wheat” was a mistake in our listing designing process and will soon be fixed and reuploaded....We can promise you that our Squid Ink Powder contains NO wheat, "only contains" 100% natural squid ink. We also have certifications to prove this."

My packets say indicate an expiration date in 2024. Keep in cool dark place. The recommendation it to use it immediately upon opening. My order included THREE 1.76 ounce packets. Most recipes I have worked with only need maybe at most a tablespoon (usually a lot less!)-- really creates a rich dark color. Mildly salty. Mix with a little water, and/or add to whatever is being made. Not sure if I or anyone could use up all of it in one go. Here's the thing, this is just squid ink powder, and usually it lasts fine in the fridge for awhile. So I will probably get a few good uses out of each packet. But Im not sure. Doesnt contain preservatives or stabilizers. Curious how long it will last.

Personally, I like the powder over liquid. But liquid is much cheaper, and I never see an indication to use it up upon opening. I actually dont see that on other listings for powder either. This is the only one so far.

My rating is primarily on quality (its all good), and how much the product matches the description and pictures. The one doozy makes me drop it to 4 stars. I could reduce further for a few other mild snafu's I noted. But I do want to highlight that this powder works, and I otherwise have no issue with quality, performance, or taste.

title: sweet and spicy, not overwhelming, nice summer sipper, lovely heading into fall
text:
Ooh, I like this Spiced Pinarita better than their [[ASIN:B0B2YMWXLG Prickly Paloma]]. I like that (4 stars), but this one really speaks to me (hence, 5 stars). Just has more complex and interesting taste to me. I think it is the hint of spice in this one. I don't find it overwhelming at all. I don't even particularly like spicy foods or drinks. But I do like the occasional hot hot cocoa (the kind with a little cayenne pepper). This reminds me of that. It sits in the background.

I like non alcoholic cocktails. Nice for when I want something a little more interesting tasting above what a glass of pop can offer. I love fizzy drinks, and I usually go for the pricy [[ASIN:B09QFVNVWN minimally sweet De Soi]] but it's a rare treat for the price. Thiis kind of is too. But its not a daily drinker, and I love keeping stuff like this on hand for the occasional treat. Can keep it NA or add a little booze to it. I have even added a little extra club soda to it for more volume. It is on the sweet side to me, especially their Prickly Paloma, but not cloying.

I dont mind paying more for something that offers benefit above and beyond taste. I love drinks with added supplements or ingredients that offer health benefits. Makes it feel extra special, something to savor. I feel like I am doing something good for myself as I settle down with a cool summer beverage.

title: a healthy, natural tasting snack. Not too sweet, no artificial anything
text:
I like it, and it is better than I thought. I had splurged on some seemingly similar products, and found that they had an artificial taste. I saw that this just uses monk fruit, maple sugar, and coconut sugar, so the taste is natural, and not too sweet. Nice texture, easy to pair with other foods or even eat off spoon. I have been eating it with sliced apples. The ingredients make me happy as I feel like I am eating something good for me. It really is healthy snacking. Price is prohibitive to my budget. Definitely a splurge. I have spent upwards of $20 in recent times for similar, but $25 is pushing it for me. Good grief, I really just added one to my cart.

I just find it helpful in my quest to eat less and eat better. If I can control my sugar intake, I can control many other aspects to my diet. I mentioned apples, but I have also used it with another one of my go-to treats. I take a couple of medjool dates, and a few Brazil nuts. Paired together they taste like a candy bar to me. I have taken 1 serving (1 tbs), and lightly dipped my crunch sweet combo into it. Yum!

title: taste of autumn
text:
Masala Chai. As we finish up summer and head into fall the desire for spicy warm drinks grow (or iced, as the heat seems to be lingering). I LOVE chai tea, chai lattes, and all different types of spicy drinks. I am trying to drink more black tea, so this was a no brainer for me to try.

Ingredients: organic black tea, organic ginger root, organic cinnamon, organic cardamom, natural chai flavor

I prefer a stronger tea, so I used 2 bags to 10/12 ounces of water. I think I could go stronger, so I will make sure to steep longer, or maybe I will add a chai syrup or splash of [[ASIN:B0B4F8P79Y Maya Chai concentrate]].

When it comes to chai tea, I prefer it to be creamy and lightly sweet (normally I drink my tea and coffee straight/black unsweetened). Just seems to bring out the taste of the spices. I can pinpoint the flavor, I just recognize it as Chai.

I dont think it is the best I have ever had, but it is totally, absolutely acceptable. If I can get it to result in a stronger taste without adding half a box of tea bags, then I may come back to update. It is good, it is definitely a nice chai, very natural tasting.

I appreciate the look of the packaging and covers. I would add this into a tea themed gift basket.

title: 4/5 stars. Well packaged, great assortment, fun look, makes a great gift, from Australia
text:
Unique flavors, neat looking bottles, kinda weird packaging. Definitely gift worthy, or nice as a splurge for oneself. I really like the hot honey. They are all good to me. All very different from each other. Ketchup is like a thick hot sauce. Loaded with tomatoes, so definitely a ketchup yet has the taste and heat of a hot sauce. The salami sauce reminds me of hot dog or sausage sauces, which I am sure that is what they are going for. Green sauce has been enjoyed on eggs, potatoes. Hot honey has been licked off the spoon (and once stireed into a ginger drink--mmm). I haven't done anything ore with that yet, but I like it a lot. Mostly comes down to preference

Pricy, but I dont rate on price. Also, factor in that this is an Australian product.

Quality is good, presentation is good, flavor and experience have been good.

title: spicy, tasty, like thick hot sauce. I use it where hot sauce, not so much as a ketchup
text:
Update: excellent customer service, issue was resolved. Very pleased. Pretty sure it was just me. Original review follows. But in short: good spicy sauce, like a thick hot sauce.
-------------------------------------
I ordered the twin pack and got a single bottle. Sorry, that is a fail. We order and are expected to receive the exact same item as it is listed. Not ever going to be ok with a $27 bottle of thick hot sauce.

I like this stuff- 4.5/5 stars easily. It is well packaged, has a unique look, and the taste is more akin to a thick hot sauce than a spicy ketchup. But it has tomatoes (#1 ingredient) so it is indeed a ketchup. Spicy! (to me). But if you like heat, and like the idea of slathering on an extra spicy "ketchup" then I recommend it. Just be mindful that you may get half the order. Hopefully it is a one off and not something that others experience.

title: unique flavor, nice fizz, can stretch with added club soda, nice for summer evening
text:
I like non alcoholic cocktails. Nice for when I want something a little more interesting tasting above what a glass of pop can offer. I feel like I am doing something good for myself as I settle down with a cool summer beverage.

This Parch NA canned cocktail is a couple dollars cheaper (but still pricy), and the taste isnt as dynamic. It isn't bad, I just haven't quite figured out what I am tasting. I am always on search for drinks like this to enjoy in the evening when I just want something nice to drink, without alcohol (and if I needed some alcohol, I bet this would pair nice with some booze added in).

I like the look of the box and the cans. I think it would make for nice hostess gift, or added to a drink and snack themed gift basket.

title: tastes good to me. Country of origin is for each option is listed on product page & on container
text:
I have the pineapple and papaya option. I like canned and jarred fruit. I also like fresh and frozen, but I dont always find what I want in local stores, fresh isnt always available or look good, price can be too much for mediocre looking fresh fruit, or too expensive, etc. I find value in keeping shelf stable on hand. Works in a pinch as a snack, for use over hot oatmeal, in smoothies, or even in baking. If you like it, go for it. Firm and sweet, nice sized chunks. It is what it is.

I bought this set because they are pack in 100% fruit juice. The country of origin for this variety is the Philippines. Each listing states the country of origin, so no surprises. Hate seeing something downrated for that because the buyer didnt read the product description. I like the plastic containers over canned because it is easier to use. No need to put in separate container. Though for longer term storage I prefer actual cans.

Anway, I would buy this again if the price is right. I have no qualms about quality or quantity. Everything looks good, tastes good.

title: what a great assortment, gift worthy, use in anything, bitters enhance other flavors
text:
bitters accentuate the flavors of the cocktail by allowing the naturally sweet, tangy, and sour tastes to come out. Kind of like what salt does to food, not exactly a flavor in and of itself, but it enhances the taste of food greatly, brings out flavors. Some things need salt to taste right, just as an Old Fashioned needs bitters to taste right. I was definitely curious how these various flavors would enhance my drinks. In short: worthy purchase, and would make for an excellent gift.

I've really only ever worked with Angostura bitters. Having a wide selection of bitters to choose from, it has been fun to playing with them. Keep in mind that only a couple drops are needed. This is not a syrup, and not mean to exactly flavor a drink. Lends a hint, lends a little something extra but brings out other flavors. I like this set. Offers a nice change from the usual stuff I keep stocked in my cocktail pantry.

While typically used in cocktails, bitters can also be used in food preparations, marinades, non alcoholic drinks, and added to really anything you want.

Good sized bottles (looks like they also offer a mini kit), dark glass, dropper top. Good for controlling amount used.

I have ones I grab for more than others, but I'm really pleased with this set. I dont think I would have normally ever sought out bitters like this, again making it a contender for gift giving.

title: quickly has become my go-to brand for convenient on the go meal drinks
text:
Nice assortment of Soylent meal shake flavors. I've tried several flavors and styles and find that I like them all. I like that these provide enough nutrition to serve as a meal, hence being called a meal replacement drink. Keep that in mind. There are just enough calories to serve as a meal (320). This is perfect for when I dont want to eat breakfast, or days I dont have time for lunch. Good for anyone in need of extra nutrition or wanting to replace a meal with a liquid option for whatever reason (portion control, lack of food, resource reductions/food shortage, simple convenience, dont want to have to think about nutrition choices). Nice for on the go use, or tucked away for use in emergencies, for camping, hiking, every day use. Whatever. They also offer options that focus on protein, or they focus on energy. Calories are lower.

Loaded with protein, vitamins, minerals. No cholesterol. Plant based (soy), not too sweet.

Overall, I think all the flavors are good that I have ever tried. They have some interesting flavors! This pack has more traditional flavors: chocolate, vanilla, and mint chocolate. I find that they taste best cold, ice cold. Not too sweet, not too "protein" tasting, not bad. Not great. But totally doable. I have come to prefer Solyent over other options ever since I started drinking this brand a few months back. Not perfect, but I am now used to drinking it. 4-4.5 stars

Very creamy. Drink direct from bottle or use as a base. Blend with ice for a thick shake, or add in whatever you want and use as a smoothie base. Vanilla works nice with coffee. Chocolate is nice paired with a banana and a little instant coffee. Mint Chocolate is fun and mildly refreshing. Smooth flavors, not too strong. I recommend getting them as cold as possible for best flavor. But I have grabbed one from the box and consumed at room temp and had it taste ok enough.

I have had some meal powders and liquids that I liked a little more, but there is something to this that I find greatly appealing. This brand has become a regular purchase. I still use my other brands, but this has become a pantry staple of the sort.

Wish it had just a little more fiber. But I can chase it with a fiber drink as needed.

Anything you could possibly want to know about this product is available on their website.

title: fun kit for quick pickle making, exactly as described, easy to make
text:
Majority of my impression is based on the fact that this was so flippin' fun. It was just a pleasant experience. Grab your cucumbers, grab some vinegar, oh, and some spring water (I used tap). Directions are easy to follow. Fill included mason jars half way with hot water, add a packet of pickling spice, add your sliced cucumbers, then top off with vinegar. I didnt do anything else. Only difference is that I made spears for one jar, and slices for the other. Refrigerate for 24 hours, eat up within a couple of weeks.

It is packaged like a subscription box, and priced that way as well. The jars are nestled in paper, there is a thick glossy card with instructions. There are two sticker labels for use on the mason jars that make it look professional. Spot to jot down date. I kept one and passed the other to my mom (she had supplied the cucumbers from her garden).

Was just fun and cute. Makes for a different sort of gift. I'd like to see it have a second set of pickling spices for the price. I dont rate on price, and the product totally matches the description. So if this seems appealing to you, then go for it. It's perfectly fine.

title: pleasing variety of quality items, caramels are soft and easy on teeth
text:
Nice variety with quality look and feel. This is a well put together assortment, and the packing is top notch. Reusable ribbon tied box, tissue wrapped, paper nested. Just looks nice. Functional, useable items. The mug is in its own box. Basic, but there is something appealing to me about it. Beige cozy soft socks, a highly scented fragrance, mildly musky but not headache inducing (cashmere & plum), a little box of soft dark chocolate "caramels", 2 pouches of hot cocoa mix, and a long handled mini spoon. The card is one sided. Not a card that is opened, not mine anyway. It is of good thick card stock and the image is pleasing (flower hears with words "sending warm hugs").

Food items have a best by dates of: Caramels (02/2023) and Milk Chocolate Cocoa (10/2023), and Dark Chocolate Cocoa (12/2022). These will be consumed well before then, especially the caramels :) Those are soft, and easy on the teeth btw.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. Seems to be within range of other offerings of this ilk. I always think they are over priced, but I would feel comfortable/not embarrassed to send or give this to someone. It has a classy vibe to it.

I initially went with 4 stars, but upped to 5 because everything is as expected, and actually better. I have tried everything out, and I am pleased. Bonus? The candle can sit in the lid, and I can smell it without even lighting it. I had put it on a shelf, and found myself taking note of the aroma when I walk into the room.

title: good frothing barista blend, best for coffee & smoothies or baking. No a daily drinker style
text:
Italian Oats, sunflower oil and water. Creamy and sweet. Pretty good for use in coffee. I dont often add cream but once in awhile I get a craving for it. This would not suit me for just drinking. This CAN be a drinking milk, but it is a barista blend. I find those better for coffee, lattes, smoothies, and baking.

I like oat based non dairy milk over almond or coconut , but i dont like it (or any non dairy milk) to be sweet. Oat can be tricky because it has naturally occurring sweetness. This is the sweetest of the bunch. It says 8 added grams of sugar. If it were naturally occurring would it not just say the amount of sugar it contains, then below that for added it would say zero? Yet I dont see sugar in the list of ingredients. I am confused. Hmm

Even so, it works for coffee and frothing

title: quite tasty, eat it hot or direct from can, eat as is or use it as base for dip, big chili, pot pie
text:
Oddly satisfying. Divine eaten with crackers. I bought it on a whim as I thought the price was reasonable ($16 ish, any more I would have passed on it). I have been adding to my pantry a variety of easy to prepare items. The ingredients list looked good, and I was intrigued enough to want to give it a try. I will eat pretty much anything, so even if I didnt like it I figured I would still end up eating it, or doing something with it to make it better. Has a versatile vibe to it.

It's creamy, kind of gravy like. Doesn't have a lot of texture, but it does have a mild chili taste. I took a little out from the can and warmed it up, and I also had a couple of bites direct from can. It is good either way, which makes it a great addition to emergency pantry.

I had it with a tube of Ritz crackers, and that blew my mind. It super hit the spot. So I imagine a pack of saltines would be perfect too. Ate it like a loose dip. Made me think of blending with cream cheese or something to make a thicker legit quick dip. This stuff is really quite tasty.

If I wanted a hearty bowl of chili, then I would be inclined to add something to this. More beans, or more veg, or maybe some rice. More chili taste will need more seasoning. But perfectly fine as is. I had a hankering to put this in some dough to make a pot pie or a hand pie.

I would say 4 stars as a basic chili, but the decent ingredients and the fact that I have a craving for this stuff with crackers makes it 5 stars for me.

title: super duper crazy sweet, but it works
text:
J.F.C. this is sweet. Blech! I'm still drinking it all because...caffeine. I'm not a barbarian.

But why so sweet! I'm pretty sure the no sugar options are way sweeter than just using regular sweetener. Can't the sweetness be controlled better? I have had some that aren't too sweet, but once in a while I get one that is just excessively sweet. That is what this is. OOF.

That being said, I get past that and go for the gold. The caffeine, added vitamins and minerals, no sodium, no calories makes these doable. I catch a good boost of energy/ambition. Not my fave, not likely a repurchase, but it does work.

title: could not make them work, maybe baking powder is bad? very sweet, need 2 eggs per 2 pancakes
text:
Ugh, I could not get these to work for me. I made 1 serving according to directions: fail. I made 1 serving using powdered eggs (did not want to sacrifice 2 more eggs to the cause): extra fail. Then, I made 1 serving using banana instead of eggs. Not quite a fail, but not quite a win. At least the batter held together.

Taste is ok. Has that keto smell. Is way over sweetened as is usually the case with "keto" marketed items (why??). On the plus side, zero need for syrup.

I dont think I can make these work. Looks like some folks did just fine. I am not new to cooking/baking with keto marketed stuff.

I'm totally ok with something that isnt the same as the original. Ie; keto pancakes versus regular buttermilk pancakes. I have made and eaten a lot of different keto products. I am not keto, but I look for stuff that is lower in sugar and refined carbs. So my rating is based on Keto against Keto (not Keto against traditional/typical).

My thoughts that impact rating are:
--I think the use of 2 eggs for 2 pancakes is excessive.
--The flavor is very very sweet.
--The texture is weird. Has the typical gritty texture, but it impacts the how it turns out. It doesnt seem to cook right. I could not make the pancakes work anyway.
-- The one set that kind of kept some shape still get weirdly wet inside. Not a pleasant mouth feel. Might be doable if the shape was consistent then I could doctor it up with some yogurt and berries. But this looks bad, and just doesnt feel right in the mouth
--adding for emphasis: So very sweet

I thought taste was doable. If the texture was better and I could get it cooked up into something that resembled a pancake, then my rating would be much higher. Not sure how ya'll did it, but I failed. And while it could be user error, ... I am normally skilled enough to follow directions and have something turn out. Almost like the baking powder didnt add loft at all.

title: high quality organic arrowroot powder performs well. Bag within pressure zip pouch
text: Quality arrowroot powder exceeds my expectations. Bag within a bag. Have to cut interior bag to access powder. Outer pouch has pressure zip closure. Performs as expected. I used it immediately when I was making a pasta dish with roasted vegetables and a rotisserie chicken. Had some juices I didnt want to toss out so I added it to the gemelli pasta. It didnt absorb it, so I added this arrowroot powder. Figured it will turn into a sauce of the sort. It did. It didnt clump or impart any odd taste. Very clean. Very good. I recommend!

title: green plum reminds me of sweet tarts candy, love Dalamhari products, esp their instant kombucha
text:
I've liked everything I have tried by Dalamhari, whether it be various instant kombucha or tea bags. Quality products to me. This Green Plum is good. It is sweet, tart, and tangy. I dont mind it, but it reminds me of the candy "sweet tarts". Kind of funny to taste that in this. I like it, I really like this brand of instant "Kombucha"--whatever it is, whatever is in it-- I like it over others I have tried. Not sure exactly, but I just feel good when I drink it. This isnt my first try of this particular brand, and it is a repeat purchase (different flavor). At the very least, it is a really nice fizzy drink. I like the other flavors a little more, but this Green Plum is good too. I I like the red schisandra best, closely followed by the yellow citron yuzo. But I am also perfectly happy with the green plum.

Lightly sweet, though that will depend on how much water you use. This formula uses erythritol and sucralose. Ingredients are listed on box. More sodium than I expected, so I kind of need to rethink this. Each flavor has 320-350 mg of sodium. That makes this an occasional drink rather than a daily drinker for me. Might be best for me as part of an electrolyte replacement. Maye that is partially why I feel good when I drink it as i am sometimes dehydrated feeling., Interesting.

Easy to prepare. Just add to water, lightly stir. It gets fizzy. Kind of grows in my cup--so leave room for expansion! Lovely for times I want a cold drink, but dont want pop. Well, I always want pop, but I dont always need pop. haha. This is a nice alternative. Gives me a bit of that fizz I need.

I am highly familiar with kombucha. I go through phases where it is appealing to me. Despite all the health claims about any kombucha, I buy it primarily as a fizzy drink. Some make me feel good some feel neutral. When it comes to instant, I dont know exactly what makes it kombucha. I suspect that it has dehydrated kombucha in it, with all the naturally occurring vitamins and probiotics, then something added to give it the fizz. I am totally ok with that. In fact, I will nearly always grab for an instant packet rather than a pricey bottle or can. Just depends where my mood takes me.

OVERALL: 3.5 stars. They need to include the ingredients ON the product page. Maybe somehow reduce sodium. I do like it, so I am boosting to 4 stars.

INgredients:
Citric acid, Sodium bicarbonate, Omija extract powder 14%, Kombucha tea powder 10%, Omija flavor, Erythritol, Black tea extract powder, Fruit powder, Beet powder, Sucralose, Vitamin and mineral mix [Seaweed-derived calcium, ascorbic acid, Vitamin E (alpha-tocopheryl acetate), Iron (Ferrous fumarate), Niacinamide, Vitamin A (Retinyl acetate), Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine Hydrochloride), Vitamin B1 (Thiamine Hydrochloride), Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin), Folic acid], Probiotice blend [L. acidophilus, L. reuteri, L. lactis, S. thermophilus, B. longum, B. breve, B. bifidum, B. animalis subsp. Lactis, L. salivarius, L. casei, L. paracasei, L. bulgaricus, L. helveticus, L. plantarum, L. fermentum, L. rhamnosus, L. gasseri, E. faecium, E. faecalis]

title: unique flavor, stand out experience, drink as a soft drink/pop/soda, or use in mock/cocktails
text:
This is a variety from their "soft drink" line. They can be consumed as is, or used in a variety of cocktails or mocktails. The Fentimen's web page has recipes. They also have items directly considered mixers. I haven't worked through this whole pack. It will take me awhile. What I have had is unique tasting, and has piqued my interest in their other offerings. There is just a dimensional flavor that I find so intriguing. The cola kinda blows my mind. Not a flat brown sugar water flavor. This has been fun to try, and would consider it again or other flavors for the occasional treat.

I can see making a purchase like this as a gift. I would like to see nicer packaging or wrapping for it.

My 5 star rating is based on the quality of the actual Fentimen's soft drinks.

title: quite sweet, delicate chai, hint of warm spice, I like their low suagr option a little more
text:
I really like their [[ASIN:B0B4F8P79Y low sugar heritage Chai recipe]]. The two taste different from each other. I thought that the low sugar version tasted more like regular chai with perfect level of sweetness, where as this has a more delicate chai taste with a more cloying sweetness. I like it, but side by side I prefer the low sugar option. I see they have a regular heritage chai, and now I am curious about that. But your taste buds may be different than mine. Overall seems like a quality product and I will consider their products again. I do love chai!

What makes this "devi". I think an added spice level.

This is chai, but with a little something else. I taste a light chai to start along with the sweetness, then something spicy sits in the back of the throat. It is interesting flavor and effect. I can see drinking this more so on cold afternoons, hot, and curled up cozily with a book. I like the low sugar option for anytime, and I especially like it over ice.

Use 1 ounce (2 TBS) to 12 ounces of liquid (says 11 in description but 12 on bottle, you decide what works best for your preferences). I like my drinks strong, but I find this to be plenty. I dont rate on price. In fact, I think it is reasonable. I like it better than a lot of other concoctions, whether it be powdered, liquid, or even tea. THOUGH, I think I may use this Heritage recipe along side a chai tea bag to give it a little more oomph.

4 stars only because I do find myself grabbing for the low sugar one option more so over this. I do like it though!

title: pricy but very good. Grab the 7 pack bundle for better pricing. Crisp, yet creamy-ish, SO GOOD
text:
Really really really good. An open bag is an empty bag. Has a light delicate crunch, yet is also somehow creamy. Like, I know I am eating cheese. Oregano is just right. Not heavy handed. Well balanced. Might lean a little light if you are hoping for stronger oregano flavor.

Individual pouch purchase at $7 is way above price for my snack budget. If I saw this in store at that price, I'd pass it over. I see they offer a bundle of 7 for $30, which is $4.29 each. That is more reasonable, or at least more in line with similar offerings. It is VERY good. I thoroughly enjoyed these. I like the simple ingredients and the overall experience was delicious. I really couldnt stop eating them. At 150 calories for who bag, I didnt feel like I over did it any. I would consider these again.

title: great clean scorched rice flavor, very mild on the coconut, bag of broken pieces, crumbs though
text: Scorched rice :) Like ultra dense rice crisps. These are exactly as they should be in taste and crunch. I can smell the coconut but dont really taste it. Even so, has a fresh, clean taste. Pure. I wish my bag wasnt mostly crumbs though. My down rating is for having a bag of tiny pieces. Still doable as they are nice to snack on, sprinkle over salad, etc. But not working for use as a base for toppers and dips. Sad, because I had planned for using this with hummus. Ahh well. For perfectly formed crackers, I like [[ASIN:B09BN9BCJL try these individually wrapped crisps]].

title: natural citrus flavor, lightly cloying sweetness; simmers down w/alcohol. Try w/ClubSoda!
text:
Ingredients: non-gmo Cane sugar, water, lime juice, lemon juice, premium agave syrup, orange juice, citrus tincture, natural flavors

Acquired 08/2022 with Best By date of 04/2023

Sweet, citrusy. Mildly cloying sweetness, though I think that is partly affected by the ratio of liquid to syrup. Alcohol tempers it a bit, whereas making a non alcoholic drink will let more sweet come through.

I like that this has a natural citrus taste. I have had so many Margarita mixers that have a weird taste. So much so that I considered not ordering this. But, wow! Natural citrus that works well in margaritas, and other drinks that can benefit from a sweet citrus taste. It isnt margarita specific in taste. I have even used it as a refreshing summer evening drink paired with club soda.

Shake well, refrigerate after opening

title: smooth taste, I use 1 TBS to arund 12 ounces of water, not sure how much mushroom is in this?
text:
I've been enjoying this the past several mornings. I have had it hot, I have had it iced, usually black, but once I added some cream. All good. Has an easy balanced taste. Overall how it tastes will depend on your ratio of water to coffee. I find that the 1 tsp per 8 ounces to be "OK", and so I boost it with a little more powder. I Tend to use closer to 1 TBS to 12 ish ounces of water.

Just Columbian coffee with Lions Mane, Chaga, Reishi, Cordyceps, Maitake, Shitake, and Turkey Tail mushroom. Nice assortment!

Not sure how much mushroom I am getting though? 80-100 mg of caffeine per serving, but what abot the mushrooms? Thought maybe that would be made clear on the label, but I dont see anything anywhere. I would like to know more about that. I take mushroom supplements daily, and sometimes I pick up coffee mushroom combos like this for something quick and easy. I tend to like instant coffee (and mushrooms) so the overall flavor profile is as expected: coffee forward, with neutral mushroom flavor. I am always surprised by how little taste mushrooms impart when added to coffee.

Overall I like this for the pleasing taste of instant Columbian coffee, and the bonus mushrooms, even if I dotn know how much is in there. Has a pleasant, smooth taste. Makes for a quick, easy cup of coffee that I have enjoyed black, hot or iced.

The coffee itself is better than some instant I have had. This seems to only take on an "instant" taste if I use way too much. I find it pleasant to drink, easy to make, and I would give it 5 stars if there were any indication of how much mushroom is contained in this.

title: tastes like all things fall. Comforting, good level of spice. Great hot, cold, & in SMOOTHIES
text:
Makes a nice cup of chai. Nice natural flavor. I love their regular version, but I have extra love for this low sugar option. I'm stoked that they offer a low sugar option that uses natural sweetener. They still use cane sugar, but less. They add in pure monkfruit, which is one of my [[ASIN:B09DC4CPJB favorite sweeteners]], but is not cheap.

Delicious. Pleased with how this turned out. I made according to directions: 1 oz (2TBS) with 12 ounces of liquid. I used a mix of water and almond milk. I had it over ice. With first sip I knew this would be my go-to chai drink come fall. I love chai, and will usually make tea. But I dont always want a tea preparation, or I want a stronger flavor. I have some chai syrups which are OK. I have tried powdered chai concoctions, but they dont quite taste right. Basically... I have been wishing for a not too sweet chai concentrate. That's what this is! This allows me to decide what base I want to use and how much I want. So yeh, use more or less depending on your preference. Extra easy for cold preparation. I can see using it alone in hot use, but most likely will add it to my hot tea preparation to really amp up the flavor.

Try it in a smoothie. Ok, so I love all things fall, and anything chai or pumpkin is where my heart lays. I made a vanilla based smoothie (used a vanilla meal powder), added in a scoop of pumpkin puree, non dairy milk, and a splash of this concentrated chai. OH MY YUM! I think I will use this in "hot smoothies" too.

Personally I think it is a good price, but I dont rate on price. We all have different budgets, preferences, needs, prices fluctuate, and so on. It's a repurchase for me. 5 stars

I see no indication of how to store it, so I just keep it in with my coffee/smoothie syrup collection.

Ingredients: Tea infusion (water, black tea, spices), Organic Cane Sugar, Black Tea Concentrate, Natural Flavors, Sodium Bisulfate, Monk Fruit, Potassium Sorbate, Sodium Benzoate (To Protect Flavor).

title: very dark ,very rich, very sweet. Easy to make, pretty good texture
text:
Sweetened with Erythritol, Stevia, and Monk Fruit extract. To me, it is quite sweet and has that "keto" taste.

Calls for 2 eggs (or 3 if you want more cake like texture), 1/4c almond milk, 1 stick of butter. Very easy, and not too shabby in terms of added cost.

Very dark chocolate. Very dense. Very moist. I might try the cake like texture next time around by adding an extra egg. It has potential, but I dont love it. I DO love the use of Lupini flour- adds loads of fiber.

Butter was better than coconut oil, but I dont want to use a whole stick of butter. I will try my last bag with apple sauce. Really strong dark chocolate taste. Maybe I will add more lupini flour and baking soda to stretch the taste a bit.

I used an 8" x 8" pan and baked until I could touch it and it springs back. There is not much to the batter, so it results in a very thin brownie. Probably 1/3 of a regular brownie mix (I have lots of experience in that area, haha). Unlike a regular brownie, this isnt something I could eat much of at once, so it is good that it doesnt make much.

It isnt bad, but it doesnt make me excited to eat them. Maybe that's the benefit of keto marketed products. I've had worse, but I cant say I have had better.. so that means something. 4 stars

title: smooth, vibrant, lovely plain over ice
text:
Lovely hibiscus tea. Smooth and pretty. I like how this turns out each time I make it.

Hibiscus is naturally sweet with hint of bitterness. Makes for a juicy red color herbal tea. I use 2 tea bags with 16 ounces of kettle boiled water. I love drinking it as a cold drink, so I just leave it out and let it cool naturally. I usually keep my tea bags in it, so that likely contributed to the deep color. I usually drink it unsweetened, but sometimes I add some [[ASIN:B0B5L7ZRC9 kombucha powder]] for added sweetness. This tea pairs well with anything fruity. I have also taken hibiscus tea and added to another tea (flavored tisane or tea). I drink for taste, but also for health benefits especially pertaining to blood circulation and blood pressure.

There isnt much in each little tea bag, so I expected it to be weak. However, it made for a very smooth, perfectly strong glass of "tea".

title: overall good flavor, mouth feel, easy to make, tad sweet, hint of bitter but still good to me
text:
I tried this Chocolate chip mic and their [[ASIN:B09X97K6JW White chocolate macadamia]], at the same time. I figured I would discuss both in each review. In short: both are surprisingly good, however there is a slight bitterness. Cant pinpoint where it is coming from. Maybe the sweetener? Sweeteners used are monk fruit and sucralose (In the white choco macadamia), and this one uses erythritol, stgevia, and sucralose, none of which are normally bitter in the former. I can see Stevia making it bitter in these choco chips ones. But really, they both have same level of mild bitter. Nothing else in the ingredients would impart a bitterness. Oddly, it isnt bad, and I will finish them all off.. but it is there. If it werent for that, I for sure wouldnt be able to distinguish this from a regular cookie.

Very easy to make. They both require 1 stick of butter and 1 egg. That's it. Bake at 350*F for 10-15 minutes. Should be obvious that cooking times will vary. Also depends on how many cookies you make. These batters are meant to make 16 cookies. I made 14 with the chocolate chip, and 7 or 8 (large) cookies with the White chocolate macadamia. Made them in my convection toaster oven. Didnt pay attention to timing.

I made the chocolate chip batter first. Easy peasy. I made 14 cookies.

Good texture, very much just regular cookie like. Good mouth feel. Same as with the chocolate chip cookies. Even my husband ate them, and I expected him to dislike them. It can be a tough sell if you arent already reducing sugar. I'm not keto, but I rely on these products to keep me from binging, ad over doing the sugar intake.

All in all-- not too shabby 4.5/5 stars for a "keto" cookie.
3.5-4 stars as a cookie in general (the slight bitter isnt enough to turn me away).

Wish we could do half stars. I like them better than 3 stars, so I am going with 4, especially as they are (to me) better than other keto cookies I have tried, and a lot better than keto brownies or some keto cakes.

I dont rate on price. In the "rate features" section I put 2 stars for "value for money". All our budgets, needs, preferences vary. Prices fluctuate. Personally, $14 is way above my budget for something I have to add a whole stick of butter and an egg to. Makes for very pricy cookies. But they may be just what you are looking for, so I focus on other aspects instead.

title: baked up really well, surprisingly regular tasting but w/ hint of bitter (too sweet maybe?)
text:

3.5-4 stars as a cookie in general (the slight bitter isnt enough to turn me away).
