title: petite flakes, 8 grams protein per serving (up from 5)
text:
Just organic rolled outs. I noticed right away that these Oatsome flakes are smaller than typical rolled oats. They have similar fiber and other stats, but the protein is indeed higher at 8 grams versus 5 grams. I dont rate on price, but these are pricier per ounce compared to other brands. I like Oatsome products, and this is pretty good too.

I cooked them like I normally cook my oats, which is to boil water in a kettle, top with water, then cover and let sit. They cooked well, and perhaps I used a little too much water as they didnt absorb what I used. I then put it in microwave to help cook off water, but oddly it seemed to produce more fluid. It took on an oatmilk appearance. So I just left it. I am not too picky in my preparation. I drank off some of the liquid, and left the rest. Might be the oats, might be just me.

They worked well in meatloaf (instead of breadcrumbs).

Flavor? I found it to taste a little sweeter than my usual rolled oats. Just a natural sweetness came through. I could eat these totally plain no problem. However, I usually use hot oats as a vehicle for healthy toppers such as cut fruit and nuts. I didnt taste any bitterness. I like these a lot!

While I am still not sure if I would buy these again over my usual oats (price mostly), I think the small oat size would have its benefit in some applications- such as topping home made oat bread, overnight oats, cookies. Just might work better. I like the look of both the cooked product and uncooked product. If you are looking for the added protein, this is one way to get it.

They should add a picture of the back of the bag so people can see the nutritional panel. I'll likely add a pic, but really they should too. Hence 4 stars

title: smooth, balanced, and has a nice range of coffee notes. Very low acidity
text:
Makes for a pleasant cup of coffee. It is smooth, balanced, and I could immediately tell that it is low acidity. Brews nicely in my [[ASIN:B07PFLM2LK Ninja]] coffee maker. When I make a specialty brew, I note the gentle crema that forms.

While I prefer dark roast, I can enjoy a smooth, non tangy/bright medium roast. This fits that preference. It is smooth, balanced, and had a nice range of coffee notes.

title: good flavor, aroma, texture. Nice add on to long term preps (bought one to try, one to store)
text:
All good! Bought a couple of cans while on sale. I like maintaining a varied long term pantry. I'm at the spot where I am adding in more frivolous options (ie stuff not vital to emergency, survival, food shortages), but can make an impact in terms of flavor, calories, and comfort if need be.

In day to day use, I enjoy banana chips on occasion. I especially like to use banana chips in my oatmeal or added to a trail mix. Sometimes just hits the spot. I normally just buy a bag of banana chips as the emergency packaged stuff is really pricey. But emergency prepared stuff isnt going to go bad any time soon, and the packaging is usually quite robust, so the higher price is warranted. But best of both worlds is when you can find a sale. But if not, and you are now looking to buy add ons to your emergency preps, then a canister of banana chips can be a nice way to add sweetness, flavor, sugar, calories, comfort food.

When I buy the canisters, I normally don't get into them. They are simply tucked away and I hope for the best. I bought two, and decided to go ahead and open one of them. Well packaged, good looking, good smelling, and good tasting. ,,

title: good flavor chicken, plenty of chunks, shred it up to really see how much is there, great for lunch
text:
Small can = small amount of chicken. Similar to a can of tuna. I usually buy the big cans, but I wanted some smaller ones for quick lunches. Chicken is in chunks. If you break it up, it will kind of grow in volume. It is plenty for dumping over a salad, or for making a sandwich, a quick soup, or adding to a pasta dish. A quicky favorite of mine is to add mayo to drained chicken, finely cut up some vegetables, mix all together then eat with crackers.

There is water. Reserve for use in making gravy, or making/adding to soup. Or just drain it.

I like it more than anticipated. It didnt really have any of that canned/tinned taste that some chicken has, Nor was it swimming in blobs of fat. I didnt know that this is a BumbleBee brand. I'm impressed and will likely buy it again.

title: crazy easy to make (just add water), good taste, great nutrition, already buying more!
text:
Edit/update: I bought the variety pack. Really liking them all. Perfect pancakes every time!
-----------;
Chock full of veggies, these healthy pancakes that taste good as is, no need to add anything to them not even syrup. But of course, can go ahead and add whatever you want. I had no problem cooking these!

I intended to downrate for receiving the wrong order. I ordered Banana chocolate chip, and instead got chocolate. Chocolate really doesnt appeal to me as a pancake flavor, so I expected to not care for these. Funny how things work out because I am totally enamored with these chocolate pancakes. I think because they have more of a dessert like taste, with a natural chocolate flavor. It tastes quite good to me. And it has veggies, and natural sweetening (dates). I'm stoked to have tried this! MMMMMM so good!

So many things I love about this pancake mix that any negative just is minimal. I like the tin style container, but the lid worries me. If it isnt on just perfectly, it could pop off while picking it up, or if it tips over. Haven't actually experienced this yet.

What I do love: SO EASY TO MAKE. Basically, 1/4 c mix and 1/4 cup water. That's it. That is meant for 2 good sized pancakes. Use a little more (or less) water depending on preference for thick or thin. I added a little water and made 3 pancakes. I then made another batch, and made sure to distribute for 2 pancakes. Curious, I made another batch and really thinned it out,. IT MADE CREPES! SO EASY!

I didnt experience any sticking or other cooking issues. I used a plug in non stick deep skillet and used some organic coconut oil. I put it at a medium heat. I poured in my batter, and it cooked within typical time frame. They flipped fine. Zero sticking. Cooked evenly, cooked thoroughly. I dont know if it makes a difference or not, but I ALWAYS let my batters sit for a couple of minutes before pouring onto skillet.

I happened to make some of these on a "breakfast for dinner" night. I didnt think my husband would go for these so I also made regular buttermilk pancakes. And I wanted some too. I figured I would halve my portion od fluffy butter milk pancakes,and add in a couple of these pancakes to reduce calories and sugar. I rather liked that!

But for future use, I think I will just make up a couple at a time (again, SO EASY), or use it to make quick healthy "crepes". Or just simple pancakes and eat them like a soft slightly rubbery cookie. They roll up nice, and I think there is some creativity to be had with these pancake mixes. I have NOT tried them as a waffle.

Now I want more flavors, and if I do buy more I will update with my thoughts on the flavor I bought. I just added the variety pack to my cart. I just see the ingredients on all of them and I am sold.

title: lightly sweet, smells like cacao, tastes a little like carob.
text: Reminds me of cacao in scent, and a little like carob in flavor. It has a natural sweetness. It can be used as a sweetener or as a flour. Consumed as is (raw) or added into foods to be cooked/baked. It has a low glycemic index and is chock full of vitamins and minerals. It seems to compliment vanilla quite well. I had made buttermilk pancakes with vanilla almond milk, and added some of this to the mix. It gave it a gentle chocolate flavory as well as a hint of sweetness. I am still deciding what I want to do with it in terms of baking, or simply add it to a smoothie. I hadnt had a punch of mesquite flour to work with before, so this is new to me. Main thing to know is that it seems like a good product, and that it is sweet, with hint of cocoa or carob flavor.

title: Bugak: sweet & crispy. Though bag had a lot of tiny pieces.
text:
Taste: mostly sweet, minimally salty. Hint of seaweed. I like the taste, though I was expecting more salty and less sweet. But really, wasn't sure what to expect. It is as described "sweet and crisp". I enjoyed it, nice delicate crunch. I enjoyed these "chips". Good but quite pricy. I found a lot of smashed bits and powdery pieces. Takes a small amount and ends up feeling like even less when a portion of it is pretty much just flakes. Yet enough to feel satisfied with it. I really did like it.

3.5 stars

title: sweet, tastes like strawberry, similar to other known brands, no problems
text:
It's good, as expected in terms of sweetness and flavor. I can tell that it is strawberry. I buy certain flavors for certain uses. I like their Raspberry for use in Italian sodas. I keep strawberry syrup on hand for use in flavoring smoothies that need a little help (I make some off tasting smoothie/supplement concoctions that benefit from a flavoring to mask it/bring it all together. Strawberry is one of my go to for that reason). This strawberry is similar to other brands. It isnt real strawberry. Syrups of this ilk usually arent. I've dribbled a little over vanilla ice cream and liked it.

The only difference is that other brands usually dont use propylene glycol.

title: makes good Italian soda
text:
Raspberry flavored syrup, typical of other flavored syrups. This uses just cane sugar for the sweetener. Not sure why it needs to include propylene glycol. I know it is in foods and medicines and the such, but it just seems unnecessary. I simply failed to see it in the ingredient list, so that's on me. Wont stop me from using it.

Flavor is good, not real strong. But within realm of the likes of torani and monin. Adjust according to taste preference. I know there are endless uses this, but my go-to primary use is for a simple Italian Soda. I have a thing for club soda and raspberry syrup. One of my first discoveries at a coffee house back in the 90s, and it has just been sort of special to me ever since.

title: pantry staple, quick meal, eat alone, or add to other foods
text:
I keep convenience packets on hand for quick meals, for emergencies, for variety. I like this curry with vegetables a lot. I have their mild and this spice. I buy both whenever they are on sale. I am not one for hot spicy, but this isnt hot. But it has good flavor. Japanese curry tends to have a hint of sweet, and this has that little bit of sweet that I expected.

I like it at room temp direct from pouch, or warmed up and put over rice, or a potato, or chicken. Whatever. It is just good. :)

title: floral, earthy, deep color, PSC grade 1 Negin
text:
What an aroma! Saffron is a treat, and this is high quality Persian saffron. I have had fancier, pricier versions that I like to use carefully in foods where saffron is the star player. Other low end cheap forms are pseudo saffron, or are less preferred parts, and are best for adding in a layer of passable flavor. While this is not too pricey, it is a high quality saffron (in my experience). Wonderful aroma, possibly stronger than my preferred (but pricier) brand, lovely deep color, and the flavor definitely shines through. Floral and earthy.

Grade 1 (PSC-1) is considered the highest quality (Negin). No mention of organic or not

Well packaged, well sealed. It was tightly plastic wrapped, had a seal around the lid, then had a peel off lid on the opening. Comes contained in a pot like one would find their night cream in. I rather like that. My usual tin always scares me when opening as it is hard to open and is shallow. I feel very secure when opening and closing this.

title: sweet comfort drink
text:
Oh yay, so glad I tried this. I didn't recognize this for what it was when I first came across it. Then something about it triggered a memory. I have made something very similar before, using another type of nutritious "flour". In my experience, I use more "flour" to milk (or water) ratio. So I did that with this. Same outcome, similar taste. I used similar spices. Milk (of any sort) is nice to give it extra richness and comfort (think warm milk), the thickness combined with spices and sugar lends a comforting, sweet treat. I've only had it warm, and think of it as a fall winter drink.

It technically could be used as a thickener (my other "flour" is often used that way), but the price point makes this better used as a treat. Can make it as thick or thin as you want. Sweet or unsweet, spicy or not. I dont think it takes that long to prepare, but I am used to working with flours and such that take a little patience to thicken up as it cooks. Dont go too hot. Pretend you are making a gravy. Can be used to make an "ice cream" of the sorts.

Traditional egg-free Greek style ice cream (Kaimaki) Recipe

Ingredients
--3 cups kaimaki or heavy cream
--3 cups full-fat milk
--1 cup of sugar
--1 tsp mastic powder
--3 tsp salepi (sahlab)
Instructions:
--Dilute salep in ½ cup of milk.
--Heat the remaining milk until warm, then add some diluted salep & mastic powder.
--Stir this mixture until it thickens. After this, add the heavy cream and remaining sugar.
--Stir continuously and simmer for 20-25 min.
--Pour the cream in a bowl, let it cool and place in the freezer. Every 2 hours stir the cream and repeat 2-3 times. Keep in the fridge until served.
Serve with syrup (sour cherry ideal) and pistachios!

title: strong full bodied medium, hint of bright notes and tang, very fresh aroma
text:
It is definitely fresh and smells great. All else is a matter of preference.

This is medium roast, full bodied, with a hint of tang. Bright notes that I need to smooth out with cream. I usually otherwise drink my coffee black, unsweetened. I prefer very dark roasts, robust, and smooth. But I do enjoy a variety of medium roasts, especially if they lean dark and/or dont have any tang. I want my mediums balanced and smooth. The light tang of this is within the realm of normal, but it doesnt make me want to buy it again.

However, the fresh taste (and strength!) of brew piques me curiosity for a dark roast version if they have it.

I have only tried this in drip maker. I may give it a try as a cold brew.

title: coconut sugar is perfectly sweet, works so nice in coffee, sprinkles on oatmeal, used in baking
text:
I've been using coconut sugar on and off for about a decade. Lower glycemic level which means that it doesn't cause blood sugar to spike as quickly or as high as other sugars. Also has naturally occurring vitamins and minerals. There is NO coconut taste. It is really quite close to brown sugar tasting, but drier like white sugar granules. I think that is what makes it so easy to swap in- there isn't a big difference in taste. Not using something that is going to make anything taste weird. Just tastes like sugar, but better in so many ways.

I find it works with anything, as 1:1 swap for refined white sugar. I don't sweeten my coffee but rarely, but it works great in coffee, over hot oatmeal, etc. Can be a little trickier in baking but its workable (can be use as brown sugar or white sugar replacement). I usually do a combo. I always keep some coconut sugar on hand for guests for their coffee.

I like the smaller bags. I tend to buy 1 lb bags rather than larger. I either keep in in the bag, or I pour into a jar. Any clumping over time will easily break apart. It doesn't get hard like brown sugar can get.

Lasts forever. I ignore the expiration or best by date. It isnt going to go bad.

No bugs (be sure to sort reviews by newest to find info on product that is most relevant to your order)

title: just add your own oil, yeast is included, simple instructions, tasty chewy crust
text:
Yep, I am buying more of this. 5 stars. This simply makes a good, chewy, durable crust. Super easy. Loaded with fiber, healthier than other crusts, and you can worry not about it tasting like something "keto"; it really tastes like a regular crust. IN FACT, I made a regular dough alongside with it. While I liked both, and both tasted totally normal, I liked the mouth feel of this King Arthur crust mix better. Less fuss, too.

Simple instructions, includes yeast packet, and it actually makes two, 12" crusts. Add water, oil, yeast. Mix, let sit for an hour*, then press into the pan, let sit ten mins then proceed with baking.

* I initially didnt see that it needs to sit for an hour, and so I had prepped it thinking I could get right to it for making a quick dinner. So I instead let it sit for an hour, then I wrapped it up and put in fridge for use a couple days later. I took it out from fridge, let it come to room temp, then picked up where I left off. TOTALLY FINE. I didnt mess it up any. Phew! Figured I'd let you know in case you want to prep ahead. :)

I baked this in my convection toaster oven. I did not use a 12" round, I instead decided to make thicker, smaller rounds. I love how it turned out, but next time I will make a thin crust by using the 12" round I have. The thicker crust made for a really good mouth feel. I baked one longer than the other, and they both turned out fine, crispy on the bottom, nice air pockets throughout, and a satisfying chew. Very crust. I can tap it on top and it is solid, but inside has a nice fluff. I loaded it up with various toppings. Could pick it up no problem.

My regular pizza dough was similar, but a whole lot less healthy, way more carbs of course.

I really like the no fuss aspect of this. Think I may add it to my subscribe and save orders. That's how much I like it.

title: fun assortment, packaged for gifting, includes card, Nice set- quality powder & kernals
text:
5 packs of popcorn, 5 packs of different flavorings= "10 pack".

It's a nice set. I dont care much for popcorn, but my hubs likes it a lot. I dont mind it on occasion, especially if there are good flavorings. This has that, and I like what I have tried so far.

What drew me to this, and it should you too- are the different types of popcorn: blue (x1), ruby (x1), and classic (x3). I l also like that the flavoring packets are separate. You are not confined to a specific popcorn and popcorn flavoring. You can mix and match. These are all tucked into a gift worthy box. I dont rate on price, but $15 is a nice price point for a well put together "movie night" themed gift.

I had opted out from trying another popcorn flavoring set because the flavors were just too out there, too many, and way to crazy pricy. Maybe fun for kids, but not for me. This set has flavors that appeal to me, and most anyone. It has classic salted butter, garlic parm, cheddar, chive, and a not too spicy option.

And again, I find the price refreshingly reasonable. Includes a card for gifting.

title: brewed wit 6 ounces water: cocoa start with minty finish. Mild, easy to drink coffee
text:
I'm curious what others are brewing theirs at. For reference, I brewed at the 6 ounce water level. I would not go more than 8 ounces on one k-cup, unless you prefer more watered down taste. I can definitely detect cocoa, and it has a natural chocolatey taste. Not artificial. The peppermint is weak, just a hint. But here too a natural taste. I can detect it, it is just light. Cocoa start with peppermint finish.

Some flavored coffees taste really artificial to me. So this is rather nice. Albeit a bit weak. I could use a little more peppermint. I normally prefer my coffee as dark as can be, unflavored, and consumed black, unsweetened. With flavored coffees, I find they turn out better with added cream. Just brings out the nuances of flavor better. This tastes fine black, but definitely consider adding cream.

I dont mind this for something different. I tend to get into the mood for flavored coffee once fall arrives. We've had a lot of hot humid weather, and it just broke to pleasant cool morning temps, so this has been nice. It is smooth tasting, not tangy or bitter.

BTW, the box recommends starting with a descaled brewer, with a hot cycle ran through it, and using filtered water.

title: celery forward, simple ingredients, make as a shot, or as a drink
text: Make as a shot, or make as a drink. Drink alone, or add to a smoothie. I dont mind the flavor, but I happen to like the taste of celery juice. It has a hint of lemon that benefits from an extra squirt of lemon juice, or a packet of [[ASIN:B09MVD36DK ginger powder with lemon]]. It is sweet. Wish it was just monk fruit rather than monk fruit and erythritol. But its doable. I like Yae products. I like that they use simple ingredients. This just has celery, lemon, amla fruit, erythritol and monk fruit. That's it.  Little bit of fiber, goodly amount of vitamin C and potassium.

title: Just mango, erythritol, carrot, sea buckhorn, and amla
text:
Great combo of amla fruit and sea buckhorn, two heavy hitters in the skin care department inside and out. Chock full of antioxidants. Worth spending a little time looking up the benefits of both.

I like Yae products. They keep it simple. Ingredients are straight forward, clean.
Just mango, erythritol, carrot, sea buckhorn, and amla

Mix with water or add to smoothy. Nice flavor, good level of sweetness.

title: chocolatey, moist, good texture, easy to make. JUST NEED: 4 eggs, 1/2 c oil, 1 c milk or water
text:
Very good but very sweet.

I chose this specifically because it is from King Arthur. It is a brand I trust, often use, and very often refer to their wisdom (and recipes) when I am looking to make something (love their website). I figure, if anyone can create a good tasting, good texture cake (or muffin, or pizza crust--have tried them all recently) it will be King Arthur. So many are just bleh. This turned out well and I think will be fine for those that aren't even "doing keto". I think it is the best of all keto cakes I have made. I wish it were less sweet through. It is REALLY sweet. I wonder if the level of sweetness can be taken down a notch somehow.

This takes 4 eggs. I didnt try swapping out for anything (though I did with the muffin mix I tried). I had taken a quick look at the ingredients before ordering to make sure it was something I wanted to work with and that it wasnt too complicated or expensive above the basic mix price. This seemed doable. 4 eggs, veg oil, and almond milk OR water.

I made it in my large convection toaster oven. Some odd sized pan (8 or 9 by 11). I dont recall how long it took, I just checked on it until it felt done. Baked quicker than I anticipated.

I like the taste and texture. More moist than regular cake, which I like. Not eggy tasting. Has a rich chocolatey taste. I paired it with regular vanilla frosting (totally undoing the lower sugar effort, haha, but it was all I had). The already sweet cake did not need added sweetness!

Pricier than regular mixes, but less expensive than most all other keto marketed mixes

title: mild caramel flavor, good nutty flavor, cream brings out flavor nuances
text:
I dont mind it. My coffee preference is as dark as possible, and consumed black no sugar. But I dont mind a flavored coffee on occasion. Switch it up, ya know? I also keep a few varieties on hand for visitors. This "Caramel Nut" smells good. Caramel flavor is very mild, but the "nut" part is evident. I think the mild caramel flavor works for me in this because I dont like when the flavoring is very strong and artificial tasting. Something about this tastes more natural. Couldnt tell you what nut, but it has a nut vibe to it, kind of reminds me of an almond extract. I find flavored coffees best with cream. I did try a few sips black, and it was ok, but adding cream seems to bring out the nuance of flavor. Overall I found it pleasant. Not my daily drinker, but it has a stand out flavor over some flavored varieties. Your experience may vary :)

I brewed it at the 8 ounce water level

title: not too sweet, lovely strong hazelnut flavor, very oily (like a nautral PB) that needs to be stirred
text:
Very good. To me is is waaaaaay better than nutella. It is less sweet, has more hazelnut flavor, and tastes natural. It is more akin to a natural peanut butter than needs to be stirred, so expect it to be oily. I found it easy enough to stir. The little bit of effort it worth it. Resulting texture is still sei liquid, but it works. Totally works as a drizzle, dip, or enjoyed off the spoon. I havent tried spreading it on anything.

This is what a hazelnut spread should taste like (to me).

4.5 stars. The oily factor is a turn off, but it doesnt taste oily. And the fact that it blows away the stuff that we typically see as a hazelnut spread, I would buy this over that any day--so boosting to 5 stars rather than choosing 4. I dont use it enough to worry about price. It's a splurge, yet I like that there are two jars in the box.

title: light leaning medium with mild tang, mild hazelnut flavor, fresh, not my fave but good
text:
Light leaning medium with hazelnut flavoring. Coffee definitely comes down to personal preference and brew style. Hazelnut isnt a coffee I drink, so I had other tasters in on this with me. I tried it to suss out the freshness level and the overall flavor that comes through i a regular drip coffee maker.

The coffee smells good and fresh, the flavor of hazelnut comes through, albeit best with cream (I' usually strict black coffee drinker). I tried it hot, and over ice. I like it over ice best. No one had anything negative to say, but no one seemed wowed either. I think if it were more solidly in the medium roast level, then it would not have that bit of tang that I pick up on. Light roast does that. Good caffeine kick though!

3.5 stars (boosted to 4 for freshness and good caffeine kick)

title: good variety of tasty (but thin) sauces, some heat, sweet, tang. I like it.
text: They're all good, nice assortment of NOBLE MADE SAUCE by the New Primal. Sauces for anyone, not just those on a diet. Tasty mix of BBQ sauces and hot sauces. A little tangy, a lottle sweet, a little heat. They are thinner than many BBQ sauces, but they pack a lot of flavor. Hot sauces are done well with a clear distinction between the mild, medium, and hot options.  Super low cal, which can be nice when keeping track. I have used similar sauces, but I dont always find them in store. This is a nice pack, and worthwhile option for keeping in pantry.

title: fresh, very very fresh. Smells good, tastes, good, looks fresh gound. VERY pleased with this spice
text:
I tried this as soon as it was delivered. Spice Way has never disappointed me. I especially love their paprika. The thing I noticed right away about this cardamom is how it looks fresh ground. Not a fine powder, but a perfect course ground. I REALLY like that for my dessert breads and hot drinks (like chai and Turkish coffee) that I use cardamon in. Just looks, smells, and tastes like I had just ground the seeds myself, but without all the hassle.

Cardamom is one of those spices that just add a special something to a dish, dessert, or drink. Doesnt take much to pack a punch. I highly recommend it if you want to try something new, to find a new "secret ingredient". This brand is a sure winner. It is as close to grating your own as you can get.

title: great brand, but praline is best for pecans; makes almonds, cashews extra hard. Still GOOD
text:
Nuts on the Run make some of my favorite nuts. I absolutely love their [[ASIN:B09QW52HRF cinnamon pecan pralines]]. 5 stars over and over good. Pricy, but is a splurge. I have tried other brands, but I keep coming back to Nuts on the Run. So of course I had to try these Caramel Glazed nuts. MMmm tasty. Beware that you will easily eat the whole bag. But they aren't perfect.

Some are harder than others. In that I mean, I had a couple of cashews that took a little extra to bite through. If you are in your 20s, probably nothing to be concerned with. 40s and up, be mindful of stuff like this. Dental work? Probably should avoid all this stuff anyway. :)

Even so, it was far and few between. Didn't stop me from mowing through a bag in one sitting. I think some of the hardness is also attributed to the kind of nuts used. I realize now that a pecan is better for "praline" because the nature of the pecan is light and crisp. Adding on a coating doesnt make it harder to bite through. Gives it an extra snap. But a harder nut (even cashew), will be made harder with a sugar coating.

I like these fine, but my heart is with their praline pecans.

title: great for long term storage. Butter powder has 10 year "best by" date
text:
I sometimes wonder if those that think they received an expired can is actually only seeing the lot date? Acquired 08/2022, Mine says 07/2022, then a few lines over says 2032-- which is the lot date and expiration (or best by) date respectively. Butter and some mixes are good for 10 years, some stuff is good for 25. SO basically I got mine as fresh packed as can be. Also, that is BEST BY date, does not mean it is expiring that day. Best by is basically guaranteeing the best quality if used within that time. After that it can degrade in texture, taste, freshness, but not necessarily goes bad.

Mild denting in can. Would prefer no dents, but this does not appear to impact the integrity of the can. These cans are pretty much made to take a beating, and so I am not concerned. Still, would be better for them if they can ship off a pristine container.

Prices fluctuate, and we all have different budgets, needs, etc.. so I dont rate on price. I think it is a good brand, good product. I prefer to wait and buy when any of their stuff goes on sale. Better to buy when you dont yet need it rather than waiting until you are scrambling to find stuff. I buy non emergency packaging (ie bagged butter powder) for short term storage, for current use, camping, etc. I buy Augason farms #10 cans for long term storage. I only use them when the time draws near. Or if truly in need of it. These are mostly a tuck away and forget about it product. Hence why I look for sales. But I have certainly stocked up at full prices too. Just depends on where I am at with my food and budget needs.

title: nice assortment, I brew at 8 ounces for best depth of flavor
text:
I think it is pretty good, and the price is right. Bought the variety pack as I prefer dark roast, and my husband prefers anything but dark roast. I assumed this would be a weak-ish coffee, the reviews are terrible, but I went for it and so I figured the dark roast would be more like a medium. It isnt super strong, but it is a decent cup of coffee. And I recognize it as dark. I drink my coffee BLACK, no sugar. I brew at 8 ounces. This can handle 10 ounce, but for stronger brew go 8, or even 6. The taste is smooth and robust. Other reviews saying that they all taste the same? There is no way that this dark roast tastes like the morning blend, which is a light roast. The light roast tastes light- bright, mildly tangy. The medium and the donut house have a similar taste profile, but those are both mediums. Those have full body, overall balanced.

Not sure why the negative reviews, save for those that got in imbalance of quantity of each, or if they received less than 80. All good here.

No one who thinks they are a coffee aficionado drinks k-cups. But if you like the convenience, variety, and a decent cup of coffee, there are plenty of k-cups out there to choose from. I am always on a quest to find a super dark, super bold, chewy dark roast. I wont say that this dark roast totally achieves that, but I drank a couple back to back and enjoyed it enough to want a box of just dark, or to seek out one of their other dark options.

5 stars because there is nothing funky or off about this. 5 stars because I have been enjoying my cuppa. I would go 4.5, but since I like it better than 4, I am going with 5. Meets expecations.

title: creamy, sweet, as good as other manuka honey I buy.
text:
Creamy, tasty manuka honey. I always keep some on hand. I stir it in tea, or direct off the spoon. Nice for flavor, for soothing scratchy throat. Maybe one of the many benefits will pique your interest. I like regular honey for most uses, but I enjoy the unique flavor of manuka. Kinda hits the spot when you want a little something sweet. That's when I grab a tea spoon and savor it directly. Just different than other honey in that regard. Has a thicker, creamier mouth feel. Yet I wouldnt want to use it in place of other non manuka honey options. It is just a different taste. So I keep both in my cupboard.

This is in a dark plastic container. Best by is 22 months out, but keep in mind that honey doesnt actually expire. The best by date typically indicates a guarantee on expected flavor, texture. I normally use up this size within that time.

title: base mix for muffins or loaf, add own flavorings, add-ins. Takes 4-5 eggs, oil, & milk or water
text:
This makes a base for muffins (or loaf), just add your own flavoring or add-ins. As well as eggs, oil, and water or milk. I like it better than some mixes, and it happens to be less expensive than a few brands I had used when trying to reduce my sugar intake (i'm not keto by any means, but usually low sugar options are marketed as keto). It is also much easier than some mixes I have tried. The added ingredients are items that most people have, or can easily acquire. No special skills required. I have had some weird mixes.

I like how it is more muffin texture than biscuit texture. I made it as a loaf. It is sweet. One thing that annoys me to no end is that the low sugar stuff is over compensating by beefing up the amount of sweetener, in this case erythritol and stevia. Even so, I dont think it is bad. Overall, I would buy this again.

Takes 4 eggs for muffins, 5 eggs for making a loaf. That's precious given the current price of eggs. Could likely get away with chia or other egg replacer (unsweetned apple sauce could be a good one). But not sure. I ended up making a loaf. Since this uses coconut flour, I decided to add additional coconut flakes and banana powder, and totally reduced the "keto" aspect by swapping out 2 eggs for some mashed banana instead. I am thinking that if I get this again I will try it with applesauce to replace some or all eggs, then add cinnamon and maybe a sprinkle of walnuts or pecans. Maybe so a frosting style drizzle on top. Basically, it is a mix that takes to modification easily enough.

Yeh, I would buy this again. I like the added fiber and protein. That and calories will change depending on what is added to this.

title: best taste when simmered--more nuance, less liquid, more tomato flavor.
text:
Good, but not exceptional. I had to think about why. It isn't because it is watery (totally is), but more that the taste of tomato is pushed out of the way from the seasonings they use. As much as I love garlic, I think the beauty of the heirloom tomatoes is reduced. Let those shine through foremost, then let the use spice it up. It nearly reminds me of a base for bloody mary. I double checked to see if I was tasting celery seed or something. But no, they all just have tomato, vinegar, garlic, and salt. The last three overpowering the tomatoes. That's another thing, it really doesnt need the salt that it has. Again, this isnt presented as a run of the mill crushed tomato. It looks like, and is described like I am to expect something from off the vine. The added ingredients just take away from the tomatoes.

That being said, it is bad. Not at all. Just not.. what I was anticipating. It works fine with pasta. Just know that it is nearly liquid. Drinkable from jar if you want to give it a whirl. Or drink some, then add a splash of vodka, haha.

Also know, that cooking will reduce the liquid and bring out some added nuance of flavor. SO I recommend simmering it for best taste and performance. FOR THAT, I give it a solid 4 stars.

title: legal mooncakes, light matcha flavor with delicious red bean paste, matcha lava at core
text:
Delightful little moon cakes (no egg yolk to keep it legal, but does contain egg yolk powder), each individually packaged, well formed. I got 3-4 bites out of 1 little cake. Not too sweet, not too heavy on the matcha. Has lovely red bean taste. I love the individual serving size. Moon cakes are not something I can eat a lot of, so I find it precious that these are packaged individually to keep them fresh.

I think the intent is to take wee little slices and savor the little morsel with tea. I just gobbled mine up (just one, but could easily eat all 4).

Moist, soft, more gummy or doughy than cake like. Mochi-esque. They have the typical lava of mooncakes I am most familiar with.

Packaging is worthy of gift giving. Includes an envelope with printed information about the history of mooncakes. Each cake it nestled in its own tray with lid, contains a deoxidizer packet, and then sealed in an outer wrap.

Nutrional information is on back of box.

Acquired 08/2022 with best buy date of 01/2023

title: mild flavors, great ingredients, drink directly or use as smoothie base, or healthy treat drinks
text:
I instantly loved these bottled protein drinks. This will come down to preference. So I just want to say, take a close look at the ingredients for each. That will tell you a lot. They pack a lot of nutrition into this, making it more than a basic run of the mill protein drink. Vegetable proteins, greens blend, uses a combo of REAL sugar (not much!) and plain monk fruit. Ultra creamy mouth feel from sunflower oil and sunflower lecithin (both very good nutritionally), and 5 grams fiber!

I LOVE that it uses a variety of vegetable based proteins. Not because I am vegan, but because I dont usually care for the taste of whey. That tends to have an off taste. Nothing like that here. Also, whey is more apt to upset my stomach. I love love love that they use chia, pumpkin,

Overall flavoring is mild. I would rather have a muted tasting drink over a strongly flavored drink any day. These are not overbearing in any flavor. But I can taste each flavor. I happen to LOVE the "Cold Brew Coffee" option. I also very much like the vanilla, and the cookies and creamless has a light cocoa flavor. I have used their powdered version of [[ASIN:B09PTPR8WS Cookies and Creamless]] with similar good impression. If looking to save a little and dont mind powder, give that a look over. I like this brand, and have no issue with anything I have tried.

I can drink any of them as is, or I can use them as a base to a smoothie. I have added a little extra coffee to the coffee flavored one (either blending in some instant, or adding a little instant to the bottle and shaking). I have used the vanilla as a creamer and as a smoothie base, and I have used the cookies and creamless to make an icy thick "frosty" like treat by blending in a bunch of ice and a spoonful of cacao powder. Try the Cold Brew with a little extra coffee (instant) and a [[ASIN:B0198GOXWW little caramel syrup]] and ice to make an iced cappuccino similar to some donut chains.
[[ASIN:RTDTQNN7Y0QZE My review for the caramel syrup]]

Cheaper can be had by buying plain whey. Or a bucket of powder. But if you prefer an already made version (convenience, on the go use, etc), vegetable proteins, and like the simple ingredients, like having some fiber, and a greens blend (that doesnt taste like greens!) then I think this is very much worth the try. Again, they also carry some of these flavors in a bag of powder.

Personally, I rarely buy protein only products. I prefer a more well rounded product, and this fits what I happen to be looking for. I'd consider this again no problem.

title: flavorful, adds a pinch of flavor to dishes, even makes nice sipping broth
text:
This brand is good, always a bit pricy, but good. Main thing I like--which contributes to the cost, is the smaller packaging. I dont always need a lot of broth or stock at once, and so having a smaller container allows me to add a splash of flavor as needed. Of course, if I am going to be making a larger pot of something then I may reach for bouillon or a bigger carton of broth.

I really like that there is no added salt. There is still sodium, as there is naturally occurring sodium in bones and such, but it isnt added to this broth. 115 mg per serving, which is the whole container.

I like using it as a sipping broth, whether I warm it up and drink it alone, or I make a quick light soup using scraps of leftovers. Could be anything- vegetables, a protein, beans, lentils, spices, noodles. Usually I have something kicking around my fridge that I can add to my cup of hot broth. Or I use just a little to add flavor to something else. As I am writing this, I had JUST used some in a simple quick dish. I splashed some on top of freshe cooked delicious [[ASIN:B09N7V2DKZ brown basmati rice]] and [[ASIN:B06XCJ4C1N black beans]]. I chopped up some homegrown cherry tomatoes, stirred in some coconut powder (I love coconut rice), and added a little [[ASIN:B08HSKX5XX Purelife Himalayan Salt with Mixed Herbs & Spices on top]].

title: fresh, tasty, Happy Belly is quality brand, a go-to for my basic spice needs
text:
Good sesame seeds! Fresh, smells good, tastes good. I love being able to purchase a larger container of sesame seeds as I go through a lot of them it seems. I sprinkle seeds on a variety of dishes, and sometimes I just like adding that nutty taste and texture to bakes goods or oatmeal.

I've never had any issues with seeds going rancid. The container is pretty secure. Nice cap for pouring or shaking out. I use a lot of Happy Belly spices and have been pleased with them all. Nothing fancy, but all fresh and make great addition to my ever-growing spice drawer(s). I could have shopped around for a better price, but since my experience with Happy Belly has always been good, I figured I would go with a sure thing. I am pleased with my purchase! I think I did subscribe & save for the added savings.

I buy smaller containers as well as these bigger containers (especially on stuff I go through a lot of. I like the standard look of the larger containers. Something appealing seeing them all lined up. For stuff I use daily (like garlic), I use the larger container to fill smaller containers.

I'm pleased, and will continue to buy.

title: Seltzer w/flavor essence. Puts a little pep in the step, refreshing too.
text:
Energy drink without the jitters, though your experience may vary. 100 mg caffeine from Yerba mate, tea, & guarana. Lemon-Hibiscus has a light, mild flavor. I also very much like that it is not sweetened, at all. It's mostly fizzy water with hint of essence. Some carbonated drinks can take on an extra tart flavor from citric acid, but this is very smooth.

I know it works when my fatigue was lifted and I found the ambition to do some organizing projects on a hot day. I consumed most of this and just felt the urge to get some stuff done.

4.5 stars

title: in 10-13 oz of water: tame, mild, lightly sweet, fizzy, delicately flavored, ultra refreshing
text:
I like all of the Dalamhari super kombucha flavor options. Unique flavors, refreshing, and very easy to make.

I find this Schisandra Berry to be the sweetest of the bunch, but it isn't over sweet to me by any means. Ingredients are listed clearly in the product description, so choose wisely if you are picky regarding certain ingredients. (EDIT: or it used to have it listed:
Citric acid, Sodium bicarbonate, Omija extract powder 14%, Kombucha tea powder 10%, Omija flavor, Erythritol, Black tea extract powder, Fruit powder, Beet powder, Sucralose, Vitamin and mineral mix [Seaweed-derived calcium, ascorbic acid, Vitamin E (alpha-tocopheryl acetate), Iron (Ferrous fumarate), Niacinamide, Vitamin A (Retinyl acetate), Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine Hydrochloride), Vitamin B1 (Thiamine Hydrochloride), Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin), Folic acid], Probiotice blend [L. acidophilus, L. reuteri, L. lactis, S. thermophilus, B. longum, B. breve, B. bifidum, B. animalis subsp. Lactis, L. salivarius, L. casei, L. paracasei, L. bulgaricus, L. helveticus, L. plantarum, L. fermentum, L. rhamnosus, L. gasseri, E. faecium, E. faecalis]

I made it according to direction: use 10-13 ounces of water (I use 13-14 oz in a 16 ounce mason jar with ice). It is fizzy, so be sure to leave room for the fiizy expansion that will occur once the powder hits the water. Dissolves nearly instantly. I barely need to stir it. Then I load my cup with ice, and enjoy the refreshing, easy to drink glass of kombucha.

I have had other instant kombucha before, and I find myself really enjoying this brand the most. Just a tame, mild, lightly sweet, delicately flavored, ultra refreshing kombucha. I can drink it any time of day (I like it as a mid to late afternoon hot summer day cooler of the sorts). Zero stomach upset.

EDIT to ADD: I guess the Green Plum is also on this page, so it is either/or for review. I will add my thoughts on the green plum here. It is sweet, tart, and tangy. I dont mind it, but it reminds me of the candy "sweet tarts". Kind of funny to taste that in this. I like it, I really like this brand of instant Kombucha, it really is a nice fizzy drink. I think I like the other flavors a little more, but this Green Plum is good too. 3.5/4 stars

title: good brand, good flavor, good price. Fresh!
text: I go through a lot of cumin. It is always added to my homemade taco seasoning blend, or I add more cumin to store bought taco seasoning packets, and I always use it in bean or lentil dishes when I want to give it a bit if a "meaty" flavor. I just love cumin. Enough to warrant a larger container purchase. Happy Belly always has good basic spices, and I so I bought this one as it doesnt break the bank.

title: good taste, good flavor, good price
text: My go to chili powder for basic needs. It is balanced and can be added to depending on my needs. I use is as base for taco seasoning, and just add more cumin. I use it for chili, but tend to add more hot spices. I use it as a basic flavoring for potatoes and fries. It isnt fancy, but it is one I just use enough that I always keep it in my spice drawer. I like Happy Belly brand, so it was a no brainer to buy it.

title: Justins has great products but my batch arrived nearly 3 months PAST best by date. wTH?
text:
Come on. My package was loose in the packing envelope. The box was so smashed that it looked like it was just tossed in there in an already damaged state. I can almost overlook that, but then I took a look at the expiration date. I normally dont care, but since I bought this on the warehouse, I wanted to check to see how far out the best by or expiration is. It is normal for the warehouse items to be anywhere from a couple of weeks to a few months out. That is a trade off for the reduced cost. BUT, it is not supposed to be EXPIRED product. On the magnitude of nearly 3 months. Mine has best by date of late May 2022. GOOD GRIEF.

Now, I am going to eat this anyway, because I know most products dont go bad the day of the date. I happen to have eaten some Justins products a couple years old without degradation in smell or taste. But I dont want to knowingly buy old product. I do know that the Inspected food is supposed to at least have some time left on it before selling. What happened?

Between the smashed up box (again, didnt look like a box that got smashed in shipping, it was so torn apart that it didnt even look like it came in a product box. It was put in there all banged up), and the terribly over past expiry/best by date.. Im disappointed.

Product itself? I love Justin's products. Been buying the packets on and off for years. I prefer peanut butter but I gave the maple almond butter a try based on sale price. I like using the packets for on the go use. Can add to food, or eat direct from packet. I always have some tucked away in my car (in a critter proof container) as emergency food. Great for camping, hiking, bug out bags, etc.

title: smooth refreshing drink, lightly floral, hint of sweet, dissolves easily
text:
Refreshing instant kombucha. Has a lovely delicate floral taste, kind of reminds me of lavender. Hint of citrus. Just a really pleasant drink. Not too sweet! Just enough to make it smooth tasting.

Packets are full of air. Add to 10-13 ounces of water. It will fizz instantly and significantly. Mixes easily. I used a glass mason jar full of ice and partly filled with water, added this, did a quick stir, then topped with more ice and water. Really quite nice on a hot, humid mid summer day.

I have had instant Kombucha before, and this is the most pleasant I have had of the bunch.

title: good basic pilaf for side dishes and soups
text:
Good basic pilaf. Nice addition to pantry for convenience in coming up with something for dinner. Minimally seasoned- this is the style you use when you want the foundation; add your own additional flavors. Though tastes fine as is too. Just depends on your preferences. I make it as a side dish, or I use it as a base in a soup (or "stewp" as I tend to make thicker soups when using orzo or rice, and this has both!). Can be ade into a cold salad, too.

I bought from Amazon warehouse, so the expiry/best by date is real short (expected). But i am not concerned as stuff like this will last well beyond the date. I would expect a much longer date out if buying in a regular amazon order.

Ingredients: Parboiled Long Grain Rice, Orzo (Macaroni Product Made From Wheat Flour), Salt, Autolyzed Yeast Extract*, Onions*, Garlic*, Turmeric Spice Which Imparts Color. *Dried

title: caramel drizzle deliciousness
text:
Oh wow, so much yum. I opened one as soon as it arrived, and it was hard to stop eating it. The caramel is as expected, much like I would get drizzled through an iced Starbucks caramel macchiato. I rarely get out these days, and almost never buy coffee out anymore, so I make my own lovely creations at home. Usually I prefer black unsweetened coffee, but once in awhile I like a treat coffee. I'll also be drizzling this all over vanilla ice cream. Or directly into my mouth. Mmmmmm

I dont rate on price. We can all see the price before purchase, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, availability of products, convenience of buying online, prices fluctuate, etc etc. Currently as a subscribe and save, the pack of 4 is $16.93 ($0.26 per ounce), $4.23 per bottle. I find that reasonable.

Bottles were well packed, each bottle has safety seal in place, well sealed. After I took that off (I stuck with scissors then pulled back until totally off), then put lid back on. Flip cap squeeze bottle.

Good consistency. Thick enough to be decadent, thin enough to drizzle to hearts content.

title: versatile, fresh tasting blends, use on or in anything, glass wide mouth jars
text:
I like all the seasoning blends in this variety pack. Use any of them in anything; definitely not limited to steak, poultry, or seafood. I like them all.

The one aspect I greatly appreciate about these Villain Republic Spices is that the primary ingredients are clearly listed on the front of the container. It makes it easier to grab for a seasoning blend and know what the flavor profile will be. Some list the spices used on the back, or in tiny fine print, or on side of bottle sideways. This, I can just pick up and glance at the front and get know what's in it. I tell ya, I will grab for these any times over some other spice blends I try.

Packaged together in open faced box. Could be a contender as a food themed gift. I like the wide mouth amber glass bottles with twist off lid. Easy for grabbing a pinch, or using a measuring spoon.

Each blend is fresh tasting, and versatile. I like the packaging and overall presentation.

title: lactose free, just like skimmed, reconstitutes perfectly, great pantry or emergency staple
text:
14 ounces of non fat, lactose free milk powder. Laqita is easily one of my favorite brands for non fat or whole milk powder. I never buy lactose free, but it is a welcome addition to my pantry. I dont drink much dairy milk, but I use it for a variety of recipes. Reconstitutes well, has a creamy taste, and imparts added depth of flavor in baking.

I really dont go through much, and as much as I can save per ounce by going larger, the smaller size is going to keep longer. Even though I dont use it often, I always keep some on hand, as it makes a great emergency item. And so I also keep some tucked into my "long term pantry". Also some recipes call for milk, and when that time comes I can just make up what I need. I otherwise only keep non dairy milk in my fridge, so having powder to make up some milk for recipes is super idea. This mixes easily into water; adjust according to preference.

title: for pineapple lovers, very sweet, eat alone or crumble over oatmeal, yogurt, trail mix
text:
Dates, Almonds, Pineapple. That's it. It is very, very sweet but it tastes more or less as expected. The names are more of a label than a descriptor, so I didnt actually have expectations of it tasting like a cake. I really just wanted something that tasted primarily of pineapple. It does. Somehow, oddly, it reminds me of [[ASIN:B07DVTKTVV Solely organic pineapple jerky]]. That's just pineapple. Where as this has addition of dates and almonds. Similar texture, and since this has a strong pineapple taste, it ends up reminding me of soft jerky. I really like it. But it sure is sweet!

I enjoy it alone, or I break it up into pieces and toss on hot oatmeal or yogurt, or add it into a trail mix. Maybe one day I will cut into smaller pieces and dip it into warm molten chocolate.

I'd buy it again. Yum!

title: fresh, tasty, quality brand
text:
The COARSE ground corn meal is as fresh as expected. Pack of twelve 24 ounce bags come packed in a Goya brand box.

I usually buy Goya products, and when it comes to corn meal I often choose Goya. Just has a taste I like. I use their fine ground corn meal too (more like a masa). They are one of the few brands that I can find in the smaller size, as well as in a finer form (less granular, yet not a flour), and of course in this classic coarse grind. It's a pantry staple. Convenient polenta recipe on back, which is one of things I make with coarse ground corn meal. Mmm. Easy to make and significantly cheaper than a prefab polenta roll purchased in store.

Bagged up like this, I find it easier to store, as well as keep fresh. Also helps that the best by date is a few years from now.

title: light, crisp, delicious. Love waffles, and it is all about the base. This is very good.
text:
Finally got around to having breakfast for dinner. I dug out my [[ASIN:B00EQT6EBU Cuisinart Belgian Waffle Maker]] and made the batter according to directions. Batter thickens up, so let sit for a couple of minutes. I found that it can be thinned to make pancakes. It is a good mix, and I wouldn't hesitate to try it or anything else by Josies. 3 bags of 18 ounce waffle mix.

INGREDIENTS:
Brown Rice Flour, Potato Starch, Organic Cane Sugar, Arrowroot Starch, Baking Powder (sodium acid pyrophosphate, sodium bicarbonate, cornstarch, monocalcium phosphate) Salt, and Xanthan Gum

INSTRUCTIONS:
Mix all ingredients well. Batter should be smooth and may appear slightly thinner than conventional waffle mix. The batter will thicken as it stands! Heat waffle iron to desired temperature (medium cook preferred). Add batter to waffle iron and cook until golden brown.

Per 1 cup of dry mix add:
2 large eggs(or proportionate egg alternative)
¼ cup oil
¾ cup milk of choice
½ tsp vanilla (optional)

Per 2 cups of dry mix add:
3 large eggs(or proportionate egg alternative)
½ cup oil
1 ⅓ cup milk of choice
1 tsp vanilla (optional)

title: good looking bulbs, easy peel, mild sweet taste, eat on its own, or add to a recipe
text: Instant love! My container arrived intact. All good. Lovely looking black bulbs. Personally I dont use it for cooking to impart a garlic flavor. I use black garlic more like a supplement, and will add it into dishes where a robust garlic flavor isnt needed. See, black garlic is a tad sweet. Has a more carnalized flavor. It is mild enough to eat a clove all by itself. Very healthy, and I love having my container sit out on the counter.

title: good taste and texture, like kind out of cereal box
text:
Freeze dried marshmallows! Well packaged, good tasting fun treat. I haven't tried these in any other way than to just pop a couple in my mouth once in awhile. I keep the small container in my candy/snack bowl and it is just a fun little treat. I was looking up some options as to what to do with them. I may top some brownies if have any left the next time I make a batch.

I dont rate on price. I dont even know the going price of freeze dried candy. I like the taste, texture, and the container- better than a bag for my purpose.

title: 4.5 stars. Good flavor, well rounded nutrition, best consumed cold, but doable at room temp
text:
Nice assortment of Soylent meal shake flavors. I've tried several flavors and like them all. I like that these provide enough nutrition to serve as a meal. Good for anyone in need of extra nutrition or wanting to replace a meal with a liquid option for whatever reason (portion control, lack of food, resource reductions/food shortage, simple convenience, dont want to have to think about nutrition choices). Nice for on the go use, or tucked away for use in emergencies, for camping, hiking, every day use. Whatever.

Loaded with protein, vitamins, minerals. No cholesterol. Plant based (soy), not too sweet.

Overall, I think all the flavors are good that I have ever tried. I really like banana in general, so that was what made me want to try this variety pack. It tastes best cold, ice cold. Not too sweet, not too "protein" tasting, not bad. Not great. But totally doable. Very creamy. Blend with ice for a thick shake, or add in whatever you want and use as a smoothie base. Vanilla works nice with coffee. Chai has some caffeine in it. int Chocolate is fun. Smooth flavors, not too strong. I recommend getting them as cold as possible for best flavor. But I have grabbed one from the box and consumed at room temp and had it taste ok enough.

I have had some meal powders and liquids that I liked a little more, but there is something to this that I find greatly appealing. Its possible that it will become a regular purchase. Solid 4 stars. I would do 4.5 if I could.

Wish it had just a little more fiber. But I can chase it with a fiber drink as needed.

Anything you could possibly want to know about this product is available on their website.

title: spaghetti is pretty good. Neutral taste, very quick cook, I like the fettuccini better
text:
I like this, and I really like their black fettuccini and regular (beige) fettuccini. I like this spaghetti as well, but I like the other two a little more. The spaghetti is of course not directly like regular spaghetti, but it does a good job in terms of texture and neutral taste. Reminds me a little more of a whole wheat spaghetti texture.

It cooks very quickly- within just a few minutes. After that, just drain and do your thing. I made a quick dish using olive oil, mushroom powder, salt, and nutritional yeast for a slight cheesy, slightly umami comfort lunch.

I cooked it using a hot pot since I was only making one portion and since it cooks so quickly, the hot pot wasnt heating up my kitchen on a hot day. SInce these have loads of fiber per serving, I find this to be a very filling option. I have a huge appetite, and I was feeling full quickly.

If you dont want to boil it, it can be cooked just by pouring hot water on top. The quick cook of this noodle is just so nice for no fuss lunches and dinners. Might be good for camping, hiking, emergency food items.

Just organic soybean, and it is pretty good for being a pasta alternative. I have had many, some complete failures, and this is up there in terms of performance (taste, texture, high in fiber and protein, etc).

4 stars only because I like the fettuccini better.

title: good flavor and texture, eat warm or cold. Convenient, quick, hiking/camping/emergency too
text:
Eight, 8.5 ounces packets. Tasty, chewy, convenient, quick meal. Eat as is, or pair with other foods, hot or cold (use as salad topper!). Organic. 5 grams of protein and 5 grams of dietary fiber per serving. 450 g of sodium per serving. Has about 2 servings (1 cup serving size). Not too bad on sodium (have seen a lot worse). Super easy to warm up, also tastes fine at room temp.

Love the assortment of vegetables, and that is primarily why I keep coming back to purchase the Vegetable Medley blend. I feel like I am getting better nutrition over other convenience foods, and it works well for "on the go" use, camping, hiking, and emergencies. Just all around helpful to have on hand.

Ingredients: Water, Organic Quinoa, Organic Brown Rice, Organic Carrots, Organic Peas, Organic Corn, Organic Onions, Organic Celery, Organic Olive Oil, Organic Carrot Juice, Sea Salt, Organic Tomato Paste, Organic Garlic Powder, Organic Black Pepper

title: good flavor, nice chew, soak or just cook a long time
text:
I find myself reaching for this often. I have tried a couple other basmati rice varieties by Kitchen King, and they have all been good. My favorite is brown basmati as it has an added chew factor that I find pleasing. I keep a tub of it on my kitchen counter.

As far as my nutritional education goes, if I recall correctly brown basmati has a lower glycemic over other rice, even over brown rice. They are close though, so take a look at the nutritional profile of both to decide which is best suited for your needs. Despite being a whole grain product, brown basmati (of any brand) is low in fiber compared to brown rice. There are other trade offs but neither one losing/or winning out. More of a preference thing. I tend to enjoy the taste and texture of basmati, but I like both. In fact I eat everything. I keep an assortment of grains in my pantry, white, sushi, brown, wild, black, jasmine, basmati, etc. All good to me.

I rinse my rice. Once I learned about arsenic, it just became the norm for me. Though I went a few decades without having done so.. so who knows. Says to soak, which is the norm. Do it or dont do it. If you soak, then you can reduce cooking time. Will also help keep grains from breaking. Again, more of a preference thing.

I can buy basmati rice easily enough, but I dont often see brown basmati in my local stores so it is nice to get it here. I dont rate on price, but I will comment that it is pricier than some familiar brands. I like that this is a pack of six rather than one big bag. I dont have the ambition to break down a bag into smaller sizes, so having it already in a reasonable size makes it better for storing purposes. Organic too.

title: pantry staple, makes quick delicious dishes, I also recommend the green paste
text:
Lovely. I keep the green curry paste and the red curry paste as a pantry staple. I dont often find it in store, so I am pleased to be able to buy it in a pack of six for a reasonable price. From my experience the paste lasts forever unopened on a shelf, so I am not concerned with best by or expiration dates.

Packs a lot of flavor. I add this to a can of coconut milk, add some vegetables, sometimes a protein, then add over rice. Quick meal that tastes fancy.

title: ONE ingredient: organic shiitake mushroom powder. Use alone or add w/ other spices
text:
JUST 100% organic shiitake mushroom powder. Nothing else added. Imparts light shiitake flavor, mild umami vibe. BEST BY date of 08/25/2023 (printed directly on label). Inc USDA Organic icon.

"Whole dried mushrooms are harvested, cleaned, sliced, and freeze-dried being further finely ground into a fine powder."

I haven't liked everything I've tried by Orgfun, but this "Organic Umami Seasoning" is very good. Smells fresh, is packed to the brim in a nice durable container. Lid is twist off OR flip cap. All safety seals were intact. Add IN with other spices to enhance the umami vibe, or use alone to bring a hint of mushroom to a dish.

I made Miso with success, and I used it to make a quick mushroom sauce over pasta. It is same as other mushroom powders for cooking that I have used, and so 5 stars it is

title: 4.5 stars: tasty, smells good, dissolves easily w/water or oil, perfect pantry staple. Organic?
text:
Mmm, this is some tasty tomato powder. It is JUST tomato powder, nothing else, not even anti clumping agents. So yeh, it has some clumps--pretty much the same as what is shown in their product pictures. Does not impact flavor or performance. Dissolves well in warm water or oil. But a desiccant could help. Unless it is in there and I havent come across it yet. Doesn't stop e from enjoying this very much.

Tastes like tomato to me. Smells very good. I could eat this by the spoonful! Mild with a hint of sun dried tomato, I think the latter comes to mind because vegetable powders have a little more pop of flavor than their fresh counterpart.

Color: amber, orangey. Once some water or oil is added in, it takes on darker hue. It looks like most tomato powders I have.

I keep tomato powder in my pantry. It makes for an excellent staple since it is so versatile. Makes for excellent quick sauce (I like to use some water reserved from a pot of pasta, and/or mixed with a little olive oil), excellent for adding in flavor and nutrition to anything without the bright tang of paste.

I normally buy bags or packets of tomato powder, and I have to say I really like having it in a small tub like this. Way easier to store and get into and out of. Come with twist off lid. All security seals well in place.

Pricier than what I normally buy, but I don't rate on price.

BUT, I do rate on product description versus what I receive. While nowhere in the pictures does it show anything regarding this being organic, the title description does. There is nothing indicated on the container about this being organic (other than reference to not using pesticides). Further nothing is mentioned anywhere on their website. SO if you absolutely desire organic product, I would be suspect. IF you dont really care, then this is a perfectly good powder. I am enjoying it. I'd be inclined to try other products by this company. 4.5 stars

That Orzo recipe looks great, and I plan to make it using this.

title: this big gal w/ big appetite finds this filling, cooks quickly in my hot pot- quick, healthy meal
text:
I like it. I tend to be open minded toward new flavors and textures. I am not on any specific diet, I just like food and trying new stuff whatever it may be.

This is "pasta" made entirely from soybean. I have had pasta alternatives before, and they have come a log way over the past decade. I like how this turns out. By no means is it going to satisfy you if you really prefer semolina pasta. But if you want something different, something healthy, something that may fit into your diet (low carb), then give the alternatives such as this a try. Or do 50-50 (cooked separately as this cooks in a third of the time).

I love how quickly this cooks. It can be cooked like pasta or it can simply have hot water poured on top- either way, it takes just a few minutes. This is perfect for me for lunch. I dont eat breakfast, so I normally wait until mid day to eat something. I use my hot pot for noodles of this type (anything that tend to cook up within a few minutes). Then I just add whatever I want given my mood and ambition.

I can take any portion and cook up what I want real quick. While it is cooking I quickly assemble what I want to go with it. When it comes to trying a new food, I try to keep it as simple as possible so I can get a good handle on the taste, texture.

This has a neutral taste. Has a little something, but not enough to impart a taste over anything added to it. Texture is pasta like with a hint of added chew. Not rubbery. Though that will depend on how long you cook it. Try a noodle while it is cooking to get idea of what texture works for you.

Lightly ribboned. Initially looked weird, but I got over it.

I reserved some of the water for use in making a quick sauce using
delicious [[ASIN:B0B57RVY5Q dry box tomato powder]] and a
splash of [[ASIN:B09WRVBPNQ high polyphenol olive oil]],
sprinkled with [[ASIN:B083FHHMYQ mccormicks crushed red pepper with oregano and garlic blend]] and finish with some tasty [[ASIN:B08NFJC6WV fresh ground sea salt]]

I had tried another version first and made the above without anything else. Then when it came time to try the black soybean, I noticed it tastes same, so I decided to make it same way with additon of garden zucchini, onion, and some garlic.

That was delightful. It was surprisingly quite filling. I am a big gal with a huge appetite, and I was satisfied with 1 serving (2 ounces). Next time I may add in some vegetables or a protein. But I wanted to make a basic dish, and it did not disappoint.

There are other pasta alternatives that I like as much or better, all around same price. For me, I like it for the added convenience, how I dont feel weighed down and sleepy, and that I can get away with eating less because it is so filling. Cooks so quickly, love it!

I also have the beige soybean (which I made similarly but without addition of zucchini, garlic, & onion), and find it to taste and feel same (and review is therefore same). I also have the more spaghetti like style, and that reminds me more of whole wheat pasta. All good experience, but I think I like the thicker "fettuccini" style most.

title: quite spicy, typical shirataki texture, rinse and warm up, includes spork
text:
SPICY.
No surprises here. Typical konjac/shirataki noodles (rubbery). Thin like angel hair. Small portion in packet, and a packet of sauce. Says to put noodles in cup followed by sauce. No heating instructions. Frankly didnt care because I have made similar stuff for 20 years or so now. Except for one brand (see below), I always rinse the noodles well. Konjac in and of itself can have a slight "extra" taste, something akin to a fishy essence. Rinsing well helps that. Some products come pre rinsed, but I prefer the added rinsing. I always heat my shirataki. So after rinsing I put in my hot pot (quicker than microwave), and then added sauce. I added a splash of water as I found the sauce way too spicy for my preference. Then I poured all back into the cup. Comes with a folding spork.

OOF spicy. Hint of sweet. But predominantly spicy, and that warmth lingers. Great for those that adore extra spicy food.

The noodles are fine. They are konjac; they have a naturally rubbery texture. SO if new to these, then dont blame the brand. It is just how they are. Some are more so than others, but they are all kinda rubbery.

One of those foods that are hard to gorge on. Also, since some people dont digest konjac well, it can um.. come out the other end whole.

My all time favorite is [[ASIN:B08LW3T6XF Skinny Pasta]] which is a cup like this, has larger portion, excellent broth and spices, and somehow is not as rubbery. Similarly priced ($5 a cup, less if purchased in bulk).

Other brands (non flavor cups, just plain konjac/shirataki) vary a little. It's not for everyone, but it has been around for a very long time. In grocery stores, bags of the stuff can usually be found.

Overall: 3.5 stars. I like it a little more than 3 stars, so am going with 4 star rating

title: BACON! versatile, pre cooked, shelf stable (until opened), good price in bulk quantity
text:

Doesnt take long for it to crisp up all over. Then we normally add it to sandwiches. Dont usually use it as a side dish but certainly may do so. For that I bust out a package of raw bacon, but this works too. Mostly we like it for adding to sandwiches, burgers, salads, crinkling up over deviled eggs, stuff like that.. perfect.

I dont rate on price. We can all see price, and all have different budgets, needs, preferences, prices fluctuate, there are sales, etc.. But I do comment :)

I had seen that the price in store went up by a couple of bucks (or more) for 9-10 slice boxes. This "about 72 slices" packet (not a box) is about 7 or so of those boxes, which run $5-8, so $35-56 if you price it that way. Buy it while you can, makes good addition to long term storage. Refrigerate after opening

title: Columbian medium roast is balanced. Basic everyday bargain coffee that hits the spot

I tend to prefer a strong dark roast, but this Columbian is a balanced medium roast that appeals to me. I brew at 6 or 8 ounces and drink it black.

Comes down to preference. What I like you may dislike, and visa versa. I think it is one of those coffees that are easy to drink. Again, I have others I like more (and pay more for), but this bargain coffee works well too.

title: tasty, easy to make Udon for variety of noodle dishes

I like cooking it in my hot pot, then after I drain and rinse, I add back to pot then add whatever other ingredients I want. If I plan have a brothy dish, then I may reserve some water.

Good sized noodles. I dont often find udon in store, and I am not driving all over to find some. I can occasionally find the big fat noodles that are ready to go, but those are quite pricy. I like having an assortment, and I like Wel-pac products. Please with this purchase.
