title: very sweet..why??  Just..no. Maybe use for waffles and cakes, because it is so weirdly sweet
text:
Why are they SWEET and kind of caramel-like in taste? NO. no no no. I use dried whole egg before, from [[ASIN:B01G24Z06G Judees whole eggs]], Augason Farms (crazy pricy right now), and [[ASIN:B08R6JDZ8W Cinnamonster whole eggs]]. All are the exact same thing: just dried WHOLE egg. This package says, dried whole egg, price is similar to the others, and I figured it would be like the others. Nope.

1. There are NO directions. But since I am familiar with preparation I went with what I know (for a large egg 2 TBS to 2 TBS water, more or less). Their "serving size" says 2 TBS, so it lines up with "serving size" of other products. More of a play around to get right ratio.

2. Smells good. Hmm, why does it smell so good?? Very rich aroma and makes me think of pastries.
2a. Looks so nice too. Yellow with this moist powder appearance. Looks rich. Ok, lets prepare..

3. Whisked nicely with water. I let my eggs sit for no less than 2 minutes. Better to sit long than to not sit long enough. I gave it a good 10 minutes.

4. Heated up my hot pot, added a wee bit of oil. Then poured this in and began lightly stirring. Nothing. No formation of egg bits, nothing. Was in fact getting.. oily (not from the hint of oil I used). Still smelled good. Like funnel cake, or something from a bakery.

5. I then made a quick second batch, and let it sit for about a minute. Same results.

6. Then I simply just dumped in more powder-- why not?! Just powder clumps, not scrambled egg clumps.

7. Then I gave up. Not wanting to waste the 3-5 TBS I used, I decided that I would use it up to dunk some toast in. I dipped my finger in thinking it would taste like... egg. But IT TASTES LIKE CANDY. WTH?? Why in the world is it SWEET??

Why are they SWEET and kind of caramel-like in taste?

8. Then I let them sit. I just didnt know what to do with them. I figured maybe I would make a cake later, and the sweetness of these would pair well in that application. But as I look at it all amber orange and oily looking, it just... disgusts me. I have a high tolerance for weird, gross, off putting, and I hate to waste food. I am not sure what to do with this.

DO NOT buy this for "emergency" preparation. Anytime you are looking to stock a "long term" pantry, it is good to try it out a few brands to find the product that will suit your needs best. I am saving you a few bucks by recommending you skip over this. It is bizarrely sweet. If needing an emergency binder, keep some flax or chia on hand.

IF it was only meant to be used as a dry ingredient, it should say so. It only has whole egg powder, which is exact same as all the other products out there that only have that, and can be used dry in baking, or reconstituted for wet eggs for scrambling, omelets, etc.

But unless you are planning on using it in something sweet, I cant see using this for anything. It is really sweet. No wonder it smelled good. Maybe I will use it in waffle batter.

title: mild, gets stronger w/ brew time. Nearly identical to 2 others I tested against. Reasonable price!
text:
Strength depends on how many bags, how much water, temperature of water, and how long bags steeped.

I made this Handpick brand, and two other brands of green tea. In fact, I intentionally purchased (ok, impulse bought) a small box of green tea when I was at dollar general because it was $1 for 20 bags. I figured to add that into the side by side taste test.

I use this brand from India, Good & Smart (Dollar General) from Mexico, and name brand Bigelow Organic green tea from China.

I made each with 6 ounces of water. Let steep for 4-5 minutes.

All smelled good, though I would say this one has the nicest aroma. Leans more like something I would get from Japan in powder form.

See my notes on pricing below.

While all started with light color, they all darked to about the same. This one and dollar general/Good & Smart brand both resulted in the deepest amber, while the Bigelow was more golden yellow-green.

Taste? They all tasted nearly the same. This one having an ever so slightly more delicate taste (and from my next brewing can be made much stronger). This and the Dollar General one were very close, followed by a slightly more astringent Bigelow.

But really, I dont think I could tell them apart, none stood out as extra good or bad. I imagine longer steep times and water ratio will make for some differences. This is a perfectly fine tea. I DO NOT rate on price. The 20 bags for a $1 is an obvious bargain over this. I can get 300 bags for the $15 they ask of this. Bigelow is neck and neck with this HandPick brand. Even when compared to Lipton, it is competitive. Some Lipton options are "just" a little cheaper, and many are much more expensive (50% or more above this one per bag. Especially flavored options). Most other brands are this price per bag or more, some way more. It is only when I look at super cheapo dollar$ and dollar general brand that the price per bag is way less. And for that I have to travel to go get.

Shop around, or just know that this is a fine green tea smooth, and competitively priced.

The round tea bags impart a delicate, mild flavor. I found my initial cup to be almost too weak add directed. ie 1 bag per 200 ml of water. I then allowed the remainder to sit, and it simply got stronger the longer it steeped. Color was anywhere from faint yellow tint to deeper amber. So aim for 4-5 minute steep, longer if want a stronger brew.

I had wanted to make iced tea, so I used double the amount: 10 bags for 1000 ml water. I let steep for 20 minutes and the flavor was just barely there. But the color was evident. Might be good for those that want to drink green tea but not exactly taste it. Then I let it sit with the bags overnight.

WOAH, that made a robust green tea. Strong, and I needed to water it down, but it had flavor and deep color.

Overall I think it is fine. I would say this is a more mild tasting tea, but if need a strong tea then let it sit with the bag for awhile. It will do fine as a base to iced green tea. I like adding some lemon and a little sweetener. Or my favorite addition [[ASIN:B09MVD36DK Prince of Peace Honey Lemon Ginger sachets]] . Mmm green tea, add a packet of this, mix, then add over ice-- so nice!

I am giving this Handpick green tea 4 stars. I really see or taste nothing wrong in terms of quality. Rest comes down to preference.

title: not a daily drinker, good for those truly in need of electrolyte replacement (heavy sweat, medical)
text:
I like that there is no confusion as to what is in this, or how much per serving. Use roughly 1 TBS in 16 ounces of water. Try a kitchen scale to see what 15 grams look like in power dry weight, so you can use your volume measuring spoon.

Of course it is better than water, if you have an actual need for electrolyte replacement. Water may very well make things worse if you have nothing to replace it with (plain filtered water may not have enough naturally occurring minerals to do anything other than further dulite when in dire electrolyte shortage situation).

This is an actual electrolyte replacement drink, not a cute flavored drink marketed as electrolyte replacer. Those I think are fine for people who wont otherwise drink water, or may benefit from a little added something. Then there are mid range electrolyte replacement- has just enough minerals to be helpful but usually lacks on sodium (runs low) and sugar/glucose (doesnt use any). Good for mild dehydration, illness, basic workouts, etc.

SO when I see this product where I can SEE the ingredients before purchase, I take note of the electrolytes used. Look at that sodium! 600 mg per serving! THAT right there tells me that this is NOT for casual drinking, not for those that dont break a sweat or don't have a medical need for continual sodium resupply. How about as a water enhancer? oh definitely not.

But if you are laboring hard outside in noon day summer sun, if you work out intensely, if you sweat profusely and feel dragged down.. then you may benefit from this.

It has 600 mg of sodium, 8 grams added sugar (cane, not sure if dextrose counts), 46 mg calcium, 12 mg mag, 158 potassium. I am not entirely sure what the best ratios are for the ingredients. I will often see a 2:1 ratio sodium to potassium, and 2:1 for calcium to magnesium. I dont quite see it here, but it's good to see the ingredients that actual work toward replacing electrolytes.

Even so, that 600 mg is a lot, the most I have seen compared to any electrolyte drink I have purchased over the past ten years. 300-400 is the max. Very interesting. Keep that in mind.

After having said all that.. this is not a pleasant drink. I really dont mind it being a bit blegh (as its not a casual drink), but it is like drinking sweat. Gross. That is kinda what they are going for-- to replace minerals and such from sweat. It can be off putting., Yet, I would grab for this if I knew I would be in true need of replacement (intense hiking, my outdoor labor work when temps are super high with high humidity, etc). When a solution of "sweat" tastes good and refreshing, then you know you were dehydrated. That is my experience. I have not used this in any of those situations yet, so this is gross at the moment.

Cant really detect much flavor beyond the salt. Something lightly fruity, but muted.

OVERALL: I love that they use actual sugar as that is a beneficial ingredient in electrolyte replacement. Sodium is higher than my usual preferred brands, and may be a little tricky for those that are using this when they dont need such a "heavy hitter" in terms of electrolyte replacement. They market this a little too casually, and I personally would NOT use this as a daily drinker (unless situations truly called for it).

I definitely dont like the taste, but I dont really care when it comes to electrolyte replacement drinks, but this could use a little more "flavor". They use actual fruit powder which is less robust than synthetic flavors. Trade off. So I will take fruit powder over artificial options.

3.5 stars.

INGREDIENTS: Calcium, Magnesium, Sodium, Potassium, Organic Cane Sugar, Dextrose, Citric Acid, Organic Flavors, Fruit and Vegetable Juice (color), Organic Lemon Fruit Powder, Organic Strawberry Fruit Powder

title: made as directed: slimy, hard to dissolve. Tolerable, but weird
text:
Tolerable.
I like some of their soup packets, and have been wanting to try their shakes. I'm underwhelmed. I like that it is low calorie (90), has good amount of collagen (11 grams), has decent ingredients, and not overly sweetened. Whether mocha, chocolate, or vanilla, the "flavor" is natural and mild (I like vanilla best). It tastes good enough to drink them all up, but i am hard pressed to want more. I do not rate on price, at all.

It took some aggressive stirring to get it to mix up. I tried on in my personal cordless mixer/blender, and the first pass didnt get it to dissolve. Then I ran it a second time, and a few small clumps were still there.

Not thick, but it thickens up. But is more slimy than shake-like. I made it a couple of ways, the most slimy was when it was made with just water. Seemed to taste better and have better mouth feel with unsweetened almond milk. I used just 8 ounces as directed.

I put some of the prepared mix into my coffee, and it was ok, Made my lips a little sticky. So weird.

I imagine it would be fine is used as base to a smoothie, but even just as is.....is doable.

I dont exactly like it, but I dont straight out dislike it. I am giving it a middle of the road rating of 3. That means it is "OK".

title: coffee start, tea taste finish, interesting flavor, nice over ice (I drink it black).
text:
Definitely will come down to individual preference. It has an odd taste, but I kind of like it. Every time I take a sip, I think "hm, that's kind of weird", but I guess in a good way because I keep drinking it.

The aroma reminds me of beef bouillon. Maybe it is the mushrooms. I use mushroom powder supplements every single day, and this is the first that it smelled soup like. But once mixed with water and poured over ice (been hot and humid, so lots of iced drinks for me), it takes on a coffee-tea aroma, which is what it also tastes like. Has a coffee start, and a slight tea finish. Weird. But good.

I dont really measure. Use as much or as little for the size of drink you want. I like strong, so I go with 1-2 TBS for 16 ounces water, then poured over ice. I drink it BLACK, unsweetened. I imagine cream and/or sugar would be good too.

I prefer more coffee taste, and ore caffeine, period.. so I add in a little more plain instant coffee to make this work for me. I tend to do this with most instant mushroom coffee blends.

title: sweet treat, nice caramel flavor, clear instructions, comes with shaker cup
text:
Sweet, and very creamy. The caramel frappe flavor is pleasant; has a more natural taste. Some flavorings can come across off, and this is something I find acceptable. Contains a little coffee and cocoa. Gives some depth of flavor. Brown sugar taste. It's good (to me).

Very sweet, and creamy like whole milk. It clings. Not sure what exactly gives it that ultra thick and creamy feel, but its there. Which I would expect from a cafe frappe.

Use as little or as much as you want, but there are directions/guidelines for how much to use.

It can be used as a creamer.

I like it blended with a little added instant coffee over ice, or run through the blender with ice to create the thick cool frappe experience. I've used water, non dairy milk (currently I have unsweetened almond milk in my fridge), coffee, or some combination of. One of these days I may add in some vanilla ice cream.

My current jam is to take some strong coffee, add this frappe mix in, mix well, then pour over ice. Mmmm summer sweet drink!

Big bag makes 26 servings (and 1/3 cup of product used). Comes with a shaker cup, which I have yet to use for this, but it looks similar to most. Nice addition.

title: all purpose, salt & garlic forward, nice overall flavor and aroma
text: Salty but good. Seems to work on anything. Just have to like salt and garlic foremost, then other flavors seem to follow. Subtle or more robust depending on what it is paired with. title: fresh, robust, amazing smelling & tasting legit saffron presented in attractive tin
text:
Mm, wow. What a gorgeous, sensuous scent. I have had saffron, then I have had Organic Negin saffron. If you can, just go for it. Just wow.

Little goes a long way, super fresh and robust, open up and take a whiff worthy. Classy, exotic looking container. Adds to the mystery of upper echelon spices and other forbidden goodies. Their website specializes in such items such as saffron, truffles, caviar, pistachios, etc. You get the idea. If you have hard to buy for friends that are into foods and such, I imagine a tin of high end legit saffron would be appreciated.

PCS-I grade authentic Persian saffron

"With our patented grading system, we have identified and categorized four different types of Saffron. Ordered Negin, Sargol, & Pushal respectively. They’re most stringently categorized through the length of the stamen and its integrity, alongside their strength of core compounds Picrocine, Crocine and Safranal. These make up the main pillars of our PCS grading system. "

Negin has the highest price tag of them all. Organic, doubly so. Followed by Sargol, then Pushal.

Canadian company, the organic certificate for this Negin saffron is issued in Germany.

title: light sweet, good crunch, cute vibe to it with its light colors

title: Decent flavor, love unsweetened option, has grit at bottom of cup, overall "OK"
text:
I love that they have an unsweetened option. Totally unsweetened. Flavors are decent. I dont often like mocha or vanilla because the flavors can be weird. But these are tolerable. I like plain/original the best, followed by vanilla, then mocha. I like it best added in with a little extra instant coffee, or like adding it to a smoothie to give it a caffeine (100 mg?) boost. By itself is ok.

--Grit? I noticed when I prepare it cold (I do a quick blend with water and 1 packet), that toward the end of my cup there is some grit. I thought maybe it was from another supplement that I use, but I eventually figured out it was from this. Its a clear or light colored grit. No taste, and really only noticed at end of cup. Silicone Dioxide maybe? Other than that, I kind of like it. But not enough to buy again.

--It mentions vitamins, one of the graphics shows "K" then in smaller print, "potassium". The "K" for potassium is the chemical letter in table of elements, and is not used to indicate a vitamin or mineral in a nutritional panel. This is important to note because there is an actual "vitamin K" (which would be K, or K2 depending on source and function), and it has nothing to do with properties of potassium. So please note that this does NOT contain vitamin K.

--Why is sodium not listed? That is part of the standard nutritional panel profile of macro and micronutrients. Whether it is added or not, it should be listed.

--Caffein is not listed on bag (unless I missed it), but it is mentioned on this product page. I prefer info to line up. All this factors into my rating.

I poured this bag into another bag of instant coffee packs. I like having instant coffee on hand (and sometimes prefer it), and will often just make a random grab to make a quick cup (or add to smoothie). I like that this has added vitamins and minerals, and has a totally unsweetened option, but there is enough about it that likely wont lead to a repurchase.

Overall, "OK" Not great, not bad. Middle of road rating of 3

--Pricy, but I dont rate on price. Different needs, preferences, budgets.

title: refreshing, light, lovely fizz, bright & tangy, could use more layers of flavor
text:
Not perfect, but quite good (to me).

Fizzy unsweet "pop" with plenty of real flavor (albeit more tart and tangy). Something about it just really appeals to me, and I could drink this all day long.

I dont rate on price-- if you just want carbonated water with some lemon juice to save money, then go for it. I could also cook meals over a fire outside rather than buy a stove. Really comes down to our own budgets, values, preferences, interests, and perception of price. One of my favorite low sugar fizzy drinks is [[ASIN:B09QFVNVWN De Soi]], which I buy on occasion since trying it, and makes this Teonic a total bargain. I love carbonation, and I love trying it out in all sorts of different ways. If I were standing at a cooler at a store seeking to buy a fizzy drink, I will be spending $2 for a bottle of pop, and $2-5 for a can of just about anything else. Even plain fruity carbonated water. This falls into that expected price range at $3.25 per can. Do I want to spend less? definitely yes. If they have a coupon or other sale I will be all over this. I love keeping a variety in my fridge.

What I really like about this is that it is not sweet, at all. It has a nice amount of fizz and the flavor pops. Lemon forward, mere hint of ginger and cayenne. Has some dandelion and rooibos, though my tastebuds dont pick up on those so much. Some of the tang is amplified by the citric acid. When I say it isnt perfect, the area of improvement for me is the balance of flavor. Because of the tang (which I do like) it overpowers all else. Yet its good. Tastes refreshing on a hot summer day direct from can, or poured over ice.

Just wish there was more balance. I would love to pick up on the other flavors a little more, taste it in layers.

Even so, I would consider this again. 4 stars

B09SGLBSJ5

text:

title: brown/whole grain basmati naturally has lower GI than brown rice, good flavor
text:
It's good, no problems. Yum

I dont think this is made to be lower glycemic over other brown basmati rice, it is simply the rice style that is lowest in glycemic index, even over brown rice. They are close though, so take a look at the nutritional profile of both to decide which is best suited for your needs. Despite being a whole grain product, brown basmati (of any brand) is low in fiber compared to brown rice. There are other trade offs but neither one losing/or winning out. More of a preference thing. I tend to enjoy the taste and texture of basmati, but I like both. In fact I eat everything. I keep an assortment of grains in my pantry, white, sushi, brown, wild, black, jasmine, basmati, etc. All good to me.

I rinse my rice. Once I learned about arsenic, it just became the norm for me. Though I went a few decades without having done so.. so who knows. Says to soak, which is the norm. Do it or dont do it. If you soak, then you can reduce cooking time. Will also help keep grains from breaking. Again, more of a preference thing.

I can basmati rice easily enough, but I dont often see brown in my local stores so it is nice to get it here. I dont rate on price, but I will comment that it is pricier than some familiar brands. I like that this is a pack of six rather than one big bag. I dont have the ambition to break down a bag into smaller sizes, so having it already in a reasonable size makes it better for storing purposes.

My box was more than a little banged up and I had a couple of containers lightly smashed down. Not enough to impede use. The stand out thing to me is that my box had 5 brown and 1 white jar of rice. I think I got a return or something that sat on a cargo ship. Dusty too. No one else has mentioned anything off, so mine may be a one-off situation. Since everything else looked ok, and the product itself looked fine, I am eating it all.

title: limited info- how much of active ingredients are in this (ie calcium, zinc, potassium, creatine??)
text:
I normally like Kate Naturals products. This is one of those times that I did not take a close look at what I was ordering as I just assumed this brand would be on top of things. The label could use more information, specifically the nutritional portion. It lists the amounts for sodium, vitamin C, and some B vitamins, but fails to list any other. Ya know, the bulk of the actual electrolytes?! How much zinc, potassium, calcium? It has creatine? how much? If using this as an actual electrolyte replacement item, I want to know if it will help me. Fine for those that want flavored water. But those that are wanting a legit, effective product? lay out that info.

Use 1/3 TBS... in whatever amount of water you wish. No direction there, but even if there were that is how I would do it for "flavored water". If wanting electrolyte replacement, then yes it should have a guideline for how much powder to water ratio. More water does not mean more hydration. When actually in need of electrolyte replacement, more water can further dilute what you have left in your system. I'll never forget a ling challenging hike up a mountain on a humid hot day, and although I had lots of water, and ate well before hand, and was in good condition and had been training for this, at some point I just felt off. Something wasn't right. I sat down and it occurred to me that I might be low in electrolytes. I hadnt preloaded with them, and had only been drinking water. I added a packet (sqwincher) to just a little bit of water (normally would use a lot more) as I didnt want to dilute my body any further. Within a few minutes I felt this newfound balance and energy. I just felt "right" again. Shortly before, I had been scared. And so, now I judge all electrolyte drinks based on what I personally think they would be good for ie;
--just need encouragement to drink water/water flavor (I actually prefer plain water but there are those that would not otherwise drink enough water, or light illness
--light activity/workout,
--heavy activity/workout, more ill (think both ends- and no intake of water)
--extra hot environment + strenuous activity,
-- then super challenging, long duration activity/labor in hot temps

As is, I think Kate Naturals would be ok for the first two listed, and that is primarily because I have no idea how much of any of the other ingredients listed are contained in here. No idea what the sodium and potassium balance is. Crazy how this isnt included.

Taste is fine. I actually do not care what it tastes like when it comes to electrolyte drink. But bonus if it tastes ok. This is fine, not too salty- which again is indicative of a lower level hydration. Which is fine if that is all you need! Not good to have one that is loaded with sodium if you're not burning through electrolytes.

Overall, I am going with a generous 3 stars. It is ok. Had it provided a better nutrition label, then I could assess better. I like the addition of B vitamins, but I want to know how much of the other is in this as an electrolyte replacement. I did fail to see that, so some of it is on me. But the product description mentions those ingredients and it is only listed as ingredients rather than listing it with amounts like other electrolyte replacers do. For that it wont be a repurchase.

Price is reasonable at about a dollar per serving. I dont rate on price though.

title: pantry staple, easy to use, nice flavor
text:
I love Thai Kitchen curry pastes. I try to keep both red and green on hand for quick curry dishes. Really wish I had discovered a multi pack well before now. I dont always find this in store, and I am not driving all over to find it. When I use it, I tend to make a lot of food and go generous with the amount of paste I use.
