title: good balance of Monkfruit and Erythritol. Smells, tastes like brown sugar. Tasty
text:
Smells like brown sugar, tastes like brown sugar, works like brown sugar. Not as moist as brown sugar, but it makes do. Little more like brown coconut sugar in terms of moisture level. I really like monk fruit, but it cant be used as a one one replacement for use in baking. Pure monkfruit is awesome, but it is best lightly sprinkled on food, or in other small quantity needs where it wont impact the lack of volume. Enter Erythritol. That cuts into the intense sweetness of monkfruit, and adds the bulk/volume needed to be used as a sugar replacement in recipes.

Some blends lean too heavily on the erythritol making for an off tasting result (erythritol is very cheap compared to straight monkfruit). This blend tastes well balanced. Super mild "cooling" feel from the erythritol that quickly dissipates (its a chemical reaction). Very mild.

I'm not keto. I can attest to anything regarding that. I simply like having some options that dont mess with blood sugar levels. I am also a foodie and simply like trying anything and everything. I still use cane sugar. But if I can cut some out, then I feel like I am doing something better for myself. I have been using monkfruit for years, and have been trying blends. Some are better than others, and I think this is a good one because they have the balance of the two done well. I can always handle extra monkfruit, but it there is too much erythritol then it tastes weird. This is good.

title: sweet natural flavor, super quick cook pearls, nice chew, add your own tea, milk of choice
text:
It is very good with a nice natural flavor. The tapioca pearls cook very quickly (1 min or less), and have a mild sweet brown sugar flavor attached to them. Nice chew.

I wouldnt call it a "complete set". It includes quick cook tapioca pearls, a packet of brown sugar syrup, a measuring cup, and 6 paper wrapped paper straws. You will need to add your own tea and/or milk.

Brown sugar syrup has a good flavor. Some brands have a funny aftertaste, where with this I find it just tastes like brown sugar. Very nice. I find this to be true of other [[ASIN:B095XC9KHQ Apexy]] products'

enjoy as is, or add in tea of choice. Use milk of choice. Load up with ice. MMmm.

The ONLY down side, and it can be a big one, is that there is no real easy way to store the remaining once opened. It can be done, but I would use it up quickly. If you are on a Boba kick, then maybe just plan to use it up in a few days. Or if you are making a bunch at once, this is nice way to go. But if only an occasional boba consumer? This may not be best way to buy it. For I that I prefer the prefab single serve, or I prefer the components separate (dry tapioca pearls, Apexy's [[ASIN:B095XC9KHQ boba tea powder]] or syrup that can be easily stored. Downside is that it can take longer to prepare). But this is very good, and I have no qualms about it. In my observation, no matter what you get you will be saving a bunch over getting it at a boba tea shop ($7 give or take each). I only prepare my tapioca pearls as needed as they do not store well for me as a "left over".

2 boxes total. Each contain a big packet of syrup, and a big packet of wet tapioca balls in a little syrup. Also includes a measuring cup for use after the tapioca pearls and syrups have been combined. This is for use in doling out into glasses/cups being used.

Clear directions included on each box.

Comes with 6 wrapped thick PAPER boba tea straws. I personally cant handle that feel in my mouth, totally squicks me out, so they are a waste for me. But for those that prefer them, this is a nice change up from plastic.

Good flavor and quality.

title: bulk size, bulk packaging, packing intact but basic (excpected- just in a bag in a box). GOOD
text:
Stop. As yourself, is this for you: "Our 25 lb box is the right size for conveniently and efficiently breading fish and seafood in bulk batches"

It is 25 lbs of fish fry coating. Bulk amount, bulk packaging, same as restaurant suppliers and bulk store offerings. Nothing out of the ordinary here. I often see large quantity "fish fry", so I was not surprised by a cardboard box of coating. This is how I see it more often than not and the rest of my review is based on this. This size and style is usually packed in a bag, stuffed in a box. I am not sure why, but that is how it tends to be. So please know to expect what appears to be a garbage bag stuffed with fry mix, zip tied off, then stuffed into a branded box, Which also serves as the shipping box. When I buy it at stores that is how it looks. But if I wasnt expecting this, I would be weirded out. So I get it. Would be better to have at least slightly better presentation for those not used to fish fry bulk packaging. I remember seeing it sold in paper bags at some point in my life. So maybe plastic bag is an upgrade? haha

My bag and box were intact. If cooking in bulk isnt your thing, then pass on this. If you have the ambition, then simple break this down into smaller bags or jars. That's my plan.

Nice coating for anything. Anything Zatarains is good in my opinion. I dont often have fish (as much as I love it) but I do enjoy the occasional breaded chicken, which is what I used this for. Use in any capacity you normally would use a coating in. Then oil fry, air fry, or bake. It is just so light and flaky.

I'd like to see more product info included in the order. Even if just a print out. Full ingredients, nutrition, stuff like that. 4-4.5 stars

title: hot, iced, lassi, add spices to it, add to cup of tea, use in cooking, smoothies, or just as is
text:
Rich and creamy. Drink hot, drink iced, drink as is, or use as base for other spices (ie turmeric, cinnamon, or add a tea bag to it--or add some of this to a cup of hot tea). It tastes as expected: creamy coconut, lightly sweet, kick of ginger.

Keep in mind that this is a creamy coconut milk drink with sugar and ginger. If that appeals to you, or if you can imagine using it in different ways, then I think this is worth trying. I normally dont drink cups of milk (dairy or non dairy) but use it in various applications. While I enjoyed this iced, I will likely play around with it more to find best use. It is very very good though, and the quality is up there.

I am a fan of Prince of Peace products. I regularly consume their [[ASIN:B09MVD36DK instant ginger, lemon & honey drink packets]]. I just adore this brand, and so when this coconut ginger option came up, I had to go for it. I knew it would be authentic tasting. No BS. And, it does not disappoint.

It smells glorious. Beautiful coconut aroma. Perfectly sweetened with cane sugar. Kick of ginger. I love love love ginger. Just a dreamy drink. VERSATILE too. Like I mentioned, can be prepared in many ways. hot, cold, added to other drinks, other spices and such added to it. As I consumed it, I thought of how I could use it in food stuffs, such as smoothies, homemade ice cream, and in my curry dishes where some sugar is used anyway. Might be perfect for a quick lassi.

Use 7 ounces hot water for making a hot drink, or use 5 ounces hot water to make an iced drink. Pour over ice. Use more or less to taste.

I appreciate that they include all the information you could want in this product listing. Everything looks same on my package.

title: dark amber, sun dried apricots taste like ripe real fruit. Soft, moist texture. Use in recipes!
text:
Sun dried apricots. That's a new one for me. These taste much closer to the real thing than the bright orange ones I normally get. I like both, but there is something extra special about these. Slightly milder in flavor, yet slightly more sweet. Like an extra ripe apricot. Moist with a soft, delicate chew. Not a chomp down to chew through it. The brighter ones are usually more leathery, tough. Good but tough. Not these. This is really like something that could have come from my back yard if I grew apricots and had the ambition to dry them in the sun.

Product of Turkey, becuase.. Turkish apricots:)

I can see these being off putting to some, but I really am favoring these as far as apricots I would use in recipes. The other I like sliced up or kept whole and used in trail mixes. These taste like real fruit.

title: 3.5-4 stars. Good flavor, very sweet, added food coloring, product of Taiwan
text:
These are dried strawberries, similar to dried cranberries, and the like. So that means a lot of natural sugar is retained as well as having added sugar (yep, nearly all dried fruit has added sugar). Do NOT compare these to freeze dried. Different process, different result. Also, different price range.

That being said, they are really sweet. More candy like than most dried fruit I have had. Still, I find them tasty.

These are dried with added sugar. Also has citric acid, sulpher, and for whatever reason.. FD&C red 40.

Product of Taiwan.

Overall, they look and taste as expected. Definitely sweet. More sweet than berry tasting, yet I can tell they are strawberries. I think they are fine for noshing, for baking, and for adding into oatmeal and trail mixes. Moist, they DO Not just stick together; I can pour them out and they are loose.

Maybe I would buy these again, not sure yet. WHY the food coloring though?

title: pourable "paste" lends fantastic vanilla bean flavor and speckled appearance.
text:
The convenience wins me over. I have vanilla bean paste in jars, and I have actual vanilla beans. Once I added this into the mix, I 100% of the time grab for it. Actually, before this, I found myself grabbing for simple vanilla extract. I love vanilla bean paste, but even a few seconds of extra effort can turn me off from using it (I admit my laziness, or lack of care in some respects). This McCormicks vanilla bean paste in a tube is the best of both worlds for me. Has that vanilla bean taste but in the suprememe grab for ease of an extract. It is fantastically easier and quicker to use than doing my own scraping or trying to be measuring out from a jar. . I think it imparts a very robust vanilla flavor over some vanilla bean tastes.

Not exactly a paste though, but totally works. Has a slightly more liquid? gel-like? texture. And it is as described in the product description, "a pourable vanilla paste that will enhance all your desserts"

So whatever they are doing, it is working for me. I tend to trust McCormicks, and this is a no brainer for me in terms of repurchase.

title: all is good, works for me, nice to stack the pantry for use whenever I need some sauce
text: tasty addition to my pantry. I keep an assortment of tomato products on hand, and I often buy Contadina brand as it is smooth, fresh, with good flavor. I love the addition of herbs. Make for quick base for sauces, or even used as pizza sauce. Though I have and love their [[ASIN:B07GH72MD9 pizza sauce]] too.

title: not overly sweet, nice assortment of ingredients
text: Ingredient list is nice. Has lots in it and lots going for it. Mild keto vibe to it, but overall I think anyone could like it. Sweetened with erythritol and monkfruit. Small bits, not much in the way of clusters, so it made it harder to graze by the handful. I will use this on oats, or in my oatmeal. Price isnt too shabby for size and the quality of ingredients.

title: fresh & tasty hemp hearts
text:
Very good brand, one of two that I order from often for my mom and myself. High quality. We go through a lot of hemp hearts. Just a nice addition to smoothies, oatmeal, and yogurt. Sometimes I get more creative and add it to muffins, healthy cookies, and protein balls. Stuff like that. Fresh, and stays fresh for a long time.

For a fun, salty crunch try their [[ASIN: B07PGK5XVJ hemp SEEDS]] Great by the handful or sprinkled over potatoes, salads, soups, grits, oats, or homemade bread.

title: so good, fresh, tasty
text:
Not just for air frying. Go ahead and use this for use in oven or toaster oven. Basically anything you want to have a nice delicious coating. But yeh, absolutely perfect for "air frying". Because this is a "loaded" flavor, this begged to be used on french fries, that was my first use. Second was coating chicken with it. SO GOOD.

I really like the box of packets. It makes it easy to work with, and to keep fresh. McCormicks is trusted brands, so I didnt hesitate to give it a try.

title: took a sip, hard to stop. Fiery and Sweet, it has a bold presence that is divine tasting
text:
Fiery and Sweet, this ginger syrup definitely has kick. It is flippin' delicious! I adore ginger, and this has the intensity I desperately want from a ginger based product. On its own, it is very sweet. Mixed into something, and the sweetness simmers down. But the hot kick remains. Perfect for mules and apterifs (booze based or not).

I dont rate on price. I saw the $18,99 price tag and thought, ooh.. that's doable. Others will cringe. So because we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, etc, I simply take price out of the equation.

This is lovely. Use it in drinks (alcoholic or "spiritless"), desserts, foods, or as a sipper for those that love a little spicy sweet punch to the tastebuds. Ok, that person is me. I keep taking tiny little swigs of this stuff. It just makes me want more. MMMM.

title: it's ok. 100 mg caffeine, 100 mg sodium, inc calcium, A, C, & E. Yerba Mate. Ok taste
text:
yes, no, maybe? 3 stars. I think it is ok. Not bad, not great.. just Ok. The flavor sounds great, but it is more of a neutral fruity flavor. I have tried both flavor options. Both are OK.

Takes a little work to get a good dissolve. Use an electric stirrer, or I add to a shaker bottle and shake shake shake. It has 100 mg caffeine, some vitamins A, C, & E. Calcium. Yerba Mate. The 100 mg of sodium is crazy for an energy drink, but it totally reasonable as an electrolyte replacer.. though it is missing other components that would make me rely on this for that function.

So just a bunch of little things now that I have tried it and really took a look at it that just make it an OK product (overall). Some specific things are more of a con to me, some things are more in the pro side.

I'll use these up. I will keep some in my purse, in my hiking bag, at my desk. Nice little pick me up. Just not sure if it is a repurchase. Not bad, not great.. just Ok.

title: doesnt taste like a diet tea. Super duper sweet with black tea undertones. Actually works for me
text:
Super duper sweet with actual tea taste.

I made this as soon as it arrived. I was just so curious. It is meant to be a sugar free "Southern Sweet Tea", so I was slightly suspect. I really just expected a "diet" tasting tea, or a tea that had no tea flavor. That sort of thing. This uses Sucralose as its sweetener, and it is the one time I truly think Sucralose shines. It is a very sweet non sugar sweetener, and it doesnt impart much flavor other than super sweetness. In other applications it can be too much, as the sweetness dominates.. but here, it works as it is supposed to. You know where I am going with this.. well Southern style sweet tea is very, very sweet. Not just sweetened iced tea sweet, but syrupy sweet sugar packed iced tea. This Lipton version provides that.

This Instant non sugar Southern Sweet Tea by Lipton is quite good (to me). It has that super sweet taste as well as a black tea taste. This is good for being instant, and it is good for being a non sugar "Southern Sweet tea" dupe. I'm enjoying this a lot. Your experience may vary.

I like that it is super easy to make, and that the serving size is reasonable. 1 TBS for 12 ounces of water. It is in line with what people would make. I half expected to see something silly like 6 ounces of water. Nope, just 1 TBS for 12 ounces of water. Adjust as you see fit. I think this is a really good ratio.

75 servings per canister. 6 canisters in this set.

This could also be used to make "halfsies"- some regular sweet tea and some of this. Or add this in with some unsweetened sun tea. Basically do what ya want with it, but also know that it is pretty good just made as is.

I also appreciate that this product page lists all the info, so I knew what to expect. Only spot that is off is that it says "lemon" in the written portion. This does not have that, as seen on the pictures of the container, and in the ingredient list. This is pretty much just instant black tea and sucralose.

INGREDIENTS: MALTODEXTRIN, INSTANT TEA POWDER, SUCRALOSE (NON-NUTRITIVE SWEETENER)

title: the elusive mace; no more reaching for nutmeg because I dont have mace. Good stuff!
text:
Finally, I have some mace. This spice is hard to find in stores! At least around me. It is one of those ingredients that I dont often need, so when it comes up in a recipe, I find that I am looking for a flavor dupe (usually nutmeg-- similar side by side, but if you can get mace, get mace). So now I have mace. Let's cook! It is just a deep pungent flavor that layers in a special taste to a variety of foods such as curries, stews, baked goods. Now I will need to look up recipes that specifically call for it. McCormick's is a household brand, one that can be pricier than some but the quality is consistent. If I am getting a more obscure spice, nice to have it from a trusted brand.

15 ounce container will last a long time if stored well.

title: lovely mango taste, perfectly sweet, has refreshing taste, bits of aloe pulp
text:
Wow! SO GOOD! I'm not sure if I would have tried this, normally. I have had mixed experience with aloe containing products. Aloe can have a really weird taste. This is incredible. The mango is evident, and any aloe flavor is covered up. Yet, the bits of aloe (like pulp) are very nice. Perfect level of sweetness--not too sweet. Make no mistake, it is sweet. It just is at a level I can tolerate in small amounts. Sometimes I dilute it with water. I can drink this alone, and have played around with adding it to iced tea. It's quite refreshing any way I have tried it.

Simple ingredients. Used cane sugar (thank you). Just be mindful that there are 6 servings in this big bottle. I force myself to portion it out. But boy, is is yummy. Really pleased. I am already sniffing around buying more, maybe trying pineapple.

title: pleasantly surprised how nice this latte mix is
text:
An easy latte. It doesnt need much in the way of preparation. Sure it can be modified, yet it also stands very well on its own (to me). I just mix it up, and pour over ice. Dissolves well. Just so easy and nice. Smooth, rich, creamy, strong, slightly sweet, not full of junk. Pretty much better than what I can make.

I drink matcha daily, and this has been a very pleasant addition to my matcha recipe options.

title: This tastes NOTHING like Dunkin Donuts. Read on for explanation, skip to end for summary.
text:
5 stars! I dislike Dunkin Donuts coffee with the energy of a thousand suns. I never hit up their store even though it is the only coffee location near me. I'd rather do without than drink their awful coffee. I scoff at their $6 fancy coffees, and especially disappointed in their bitter plain old tasting coffees. So tart and bright, and they only offer dark roasts once in awhile as "seasonal" item. Really? So why did I order this? Because the little secret to crappy coffee is that it can be made into something wonderful by COLD BREWING it. That means, "brewing" using a COLD method. No heat. No hot brew. Not letting hot coffee get cold. But actually using cold water and soaking coffee until it turns into a gorgeous, smooth concentrate that is suitable for using over ice, or for sipping straight up if you enjoy ultra strong coffee (I do). So I am like, OK.. no matter how bad their coffee is, I am sure it can be made palatable as a cold brew (cold brew eliminated acidity). Or not. Trying it out allows me to report back to you. AND now here I am :)

Well, LMFAO when I saw that the bag says "COLD" and then in smaller letters says "brew HOT and pour over ice". JFC that is the opposite of "cold brew". I wondered if I had read the listing wrong, but nope.. the head line uses the term, "COLD BREW" coffee. It specifically says, "Dunkin' Cold Brew Ground Coffee".

Well, I am not a barbarian, so I tried it anyway. I made it EXACTLY as indicated: 24 ounces of water and 3/4 cup (12 TBS) of coffee. If you want to make it a 32 ounce pot (that is what a half pot is on my [[ASIN:B07PFLM2LK Ninja coffee maker]] ), then use 1 cup of ground coffee. All the while thinking that this is so lame. It is just taking coffee and using a whole lot more in order to make a stronger coffee that can be poured over ice (and not taste diluted). I continued to scoff at all this, and rambled on to all who would listen (my dogs mostly).

Once ready, I went for it. Says dont pour into glass, but I am a rebel, and went ahead and packed a glass mason jar with ice, then poured this over it. Left it BLACK. Bracing myself for the worst, I took a sip.

HUH. I am not too proud to overcome my bias against all things DUNKIN. I can admit when I am wrong. I can learn from my verbal transgressions. My first sip awakened my tastebuds, and nearly made me whimper in its strong, dark, bold, robust, NON ACIDIC, non bitter, non tart, absolute deliciousness. Did I accidentally make Starbucks instead?? hahahaha I am in heaven. SO GOOD.

I can actually taste coffee. Tastes close to the bean, like an espresso roast bean. It is glorious black, unsweetened, no cream. I even tried the coffee hot, straight up. I figured if it was just coffee made "extra" by using a whole lot more, then it would be too harsh. But this really simply reminds me of a shot of espresso.

It absolutely holds up to ice. Please, do not let the hot coffee get cool. Hot brewed coffee is always best asap. Letting it cool via just sitting out for a period of time great denatures the resulting taste. Sad taste. I still drink it, but best is right away. Pack your cup with ice. PACK IT to brim. Add some hot coffee. Swirl around to let that get cold, then add more ice if need be, and follow up with more coffee. If done right, it wont water down the coffee. Also, did you follow directions in the amount of coffee to use? it is meant to start off strong so it can handle mild watering down. If you start weak, well.. that's on you and your weak a$$ coffee.

And, if you want to go ahead with a true COLD brew, then go for it. There are no directions for cold brewing on this, so you will have to follow your own ways. I wouldnt use this in cold brew, as I prefer to use the crappiest of coffee, or cheapest of coffee, or coffee I tried but didnt like, for use in cold brew (because cold brew makes it taste very good, and a lot more coffee is used to make any amount, so mind as well use cheap or less desirable stuff).

And... I Can.Not. believe I am saying this, but this is not only the very best Dunkin coffee I have ever had (my opinion was really low though), but also comes out on top over many other brands of coffee, and especially brands that are actually meant to be used in the "cold brew" method.

Good grief, I actually like a Dunkin Donuts coffee. Shhhh

---------------------------------------------
SUMMARY: NOT a "cold brew". And is not the usual tangy, bright, acidic coffee that Dunkin puts out. If that's your thing, then you may not like this. Dark is my jam. This is a strong, bold, dark coffee that is meant to be brewed HOT, and then poured over ice. It results in a smooth coffee, robust, very dark. And DELICIOUS. Tastes better than just making "strong coffee".

It uses 3/4 (12 TBS) of coffee per 24 ounces of water. I use 1 cup for 32 ounces (half pot for me). It holds up perfectly to a cup (mason jar, or venti Starbucks disposable cup that I reuse) of ice, consumed black. Energized me all day. Best coffee I have had in awhile, and I hate Dunkin, normally.

Prepared as directed, I get 3-4 pots per bag.
Current price is $45.75 for 6 bags, which is $7.63 per bag. If you get 4 preparations made, then it is $1.91 per pot. I am only one who drinks this, and I have had quite a bit left over. I will be halving my creation to 6 TBS for 12 ounces of water (vs 12 TBS to 24 ounces). And that will bring it down to $0.95 per "pot". Which will give 2 good sized servings (like 2 iced venti sizes). Not too shabby!

(Subscribe and Save is $38.89 if have 15% unlocked--$6.48 per bag)

title: delightful, fruity, sweet mid day pick me up along side a glass of unsweetened iced tea.
text:
I do enjoy the sweet treat that is Turkish Delight. This is a no nut version. It is just a sweet, soft, smooth confection in lemon flavor. Soft and easy to eat. Does not stick to teeth. hard to stop eating. These pieces are cut in random sizes, and well coated in powdered sugar. Then set in a shallow tray and packaged up well. I also have their [[ASIN:B09TWVTVY6 Satsuma]] (green tangerine) option. Those were cut into similar cubes and places in same style tray. Both are excellent. And similar to other Turkish Delights of actual Turkey origin I have enjoyed over the years. Just a pleasant treat to me. I take a few cubes and enjoy. I will say I prefer pieces I can take a bit out of rather than popping into my mouth. For that, I prefer the other one I linked to. But I have no trouble enjoying these just as much :)

I have enjoyed these as a mid day pick me up along side a glass of unsweetened iced tea. Delish!

Both varieties were manufactured in 03/2022, with best by date of 3/2023

title: Not bold. Diluted mustard flavor, some heat, sweet, & tang. Runny yet clings to hotdogs, buns
text:
Not bold. Diluted mustard flavor, some heat, sweet, & tang. Runny yet clings to hotdogs, buns. And while not in love with it, I like it enough to use it up on all the hot dogs we seem to be eating this summer.

A company local to me (Weber's of Buffalo NY)) makes a variety of mustards. One of their more spicy options is their [[ASIN:B00A8I8GRS Hot Texan Sandwich Sauce]]. I can handle some spice, but that is just way too hot (even for my hubs who likes hot). So, I have been looking for a more toned down version, as I do like the bits of flavor but need something less fiery. I really have no need for it beyond hotdogs. My search was for something that compliments hotdogs first and foremost. This Zesti sauce looked similar and has some similar ingredients. I gave it a go, and used it on Sahlens Hot Dogs (another regional item). It is good but falls a little short on "bold" taste for us. It has some tang, some sweet, and a hint of heat. It is a little more runny than expected (will just pour out), but it managed to cling to the hot dog roll and hot dog itself without making any drips. I used plenty. My husband and I both like it, but not sure if it would be a repurchase. For two reasons, it is just a tad bland. I think the mustard aspect runs short, has a diluted taste. The flavors are balanced in such a way that nothing really sticks out. But it isnt bad! Just not $14 a bottle level of flavor for me (which is reason #2). I truly dont rate on price, my rating is based on simply my opinion of the product and overall taste.

I am kind of on the fence. I like it, but dont love it. I dont think I will use it on or with anything else. I really only see it for use on hotdogs. We'll use it up. But who knows, maybe it will grow on us.

3.5 stars
Overall quality would not keep me from trying other varieties. So with that, since we cant do half ratings, I will go with 4. But 3 was a consideration too.

title: Instant love- ACV with added spicy kick
text: I have the spicy option, and it is great. Apple cider vinegar with the mother, as well as ginger, turmeric, and habanero pepper. I just use ACV in a little bit of water and take it like a shot, or I add it to a good sized glass of water and ice, for a rather refreshing drink. I like this either way. Since I enjoy this more than plain ACV, I have been enjoying it mostly over ice with lots of water. I would get this again, and the other flavor option has also piqued my interest. I like stuff like this, and try to remember to take it on a regular basis. Makes me feel good. This brand instantly became my new ACV source.

title: I found I need longer than 5 minutes, but eventually makes a beautiful iced tea
text: Great taste is allowed to "brew" for much longer than the 5 minutes it suggests. I used 2 sachets in 16 ounces of cold water in a mason jar. After 5 minutes it had barely dispersed. I kind of forgot about it, but came back later and it was a lovely golden color. Light green tea taste (not a matcha taste), with mint. I love green tea and mint, over ice on a hot summer day. I drank this as is, and found it refreshing as anticipated. I think for a "5 minute brew", some hot water is going to be needed (which yes, negates the cold brew aspect). Other than that, my "set it and forget it" worked well. Not sure how long I gave it. Maybe an hour? Now if you are ok, with a hint of flavor, then 5 minutes is plenty. Personally, I would add this to a bottle of water and just drink all day, top off with water as needed. Slim tube style sachet makes it work well to be slid into a bottle.

title: mild vanilla flavor, unsweetened, long shelf life. Refrigerate once opened. Pantry staple!
text: Shelf stable! I dont get to the store often, nor do I want to pack my fridge with non dairy milk. I mean, I do buy the refrigerated containers from the store, but I like having back up in the form of something I can tuck away in my pantry. Unsweetened vanilla works really well for my smoothies. and that is pretty much all I use it for. I am not a fan of using almond milk in coffee, but I love it for smoothies. Light vanilla flavor. Unsweetened keeps calories low. Shake it, use it, then store in fridge. Unopened, they can store well for a long time on the shelf.

title: when you need pasta but dont want to make enough to feed an army
text:
I order the Rotini. All ready cooked, and ready to go. Eat it hot or cold. This is an item of convenience. I keep several tucked away in my pantry for emergency use as there is minimal to no preparation needed if the power goes out or if water isnt available. Works nice for camping, traveling, or simply as the ultra easy way to get a quick meal. Good for use on hot humid days when I dont want to heat up the kitchen.

I hate reviews that just day "gross", or "bad", or "good". Nothing else. Cant they provide a few more descriptors to make it helpful? And so I took a chance, and am pleased with this product. I like Barilla as a dry pasta product, the flavor and texture stand out over many brands. This is my first foray into precooked ready to eat pasta, and I am pleased with the taste and texture. I chose the rotini shape because it is going to hold spices, sauces, and bits of other food I add to it better than other shapes. I figured I would get something that would work for various applications. Otherwise I normally eat a lot of elbows and spaghetti.

This has a hint of olive oil and salt. Just enough to where if you had to eat it as is, it has some enhanced flavor. I like it, and had already purchased another pack before writing this review. Now I have it on subscribe & save.

Nice for portion control too. Not just for consuming, but for actually making. Who else makes enough pasta to feed an army, when just cooking for 1-2 people? *raises hand* :D

title: versatile flavor for iced drinks, Italian sodas, cocktails, etc
text: I have several flavors from Jordans. I like having a variety to choose from for flavoring up coffee, teas, iced drinks, smoothies, etc. I bought this raspberry for use in Italian sodas- just a quick mix of carbonated water and some raspberry syrup. Over ice, of course. Can take it a step further and make it a lightweight cocktail (wine, vodka, rum, champagne). I also like having a little flavor in my iced matcha. Lots of options with these syrups. Not always the best, but they are consistent enough and usually priced well enough that I just keep buying this brand.

title: for something a little different
text: Lovely little quick meal. Something different. Just the right sized portion for an easy lunch. Can be eaten as is, tossed over a salad, or scooped up with some bread or crackers. Peel back lids makes it convenient for on the go use. Already ordered some more. Yum!

title: try it in coffee, oatmeal, smoothies, muffin or pancake batter
text:
For something a little different in my smoothies. I've also added some to coffee, and to my hot oats. It all works. I imagine using it in a muffin mix or pancake mix would be great too. I am a big fan of warming spices, and I do love chai. This is labeled as protein powder, and it is. It is just yellow pea protein with assortment of spices as seen in their product picture. The headline mentions "meal replacement" but I would not go by that. I think it has more to do with triggering a search result than an accurate description of actual product.

That being said, I know it is a protein powder and I treat it as such. I like it, the ingredients, the overall flavor, and simply being something different.

title: balanced sweet and tart. Lemony goodness. I'm already back to buy more!
text:
All these positive reviews swayed me to buy a bottle. Now I am adding mine into the mix.

Very good. Sweet and tart. Lemony. Yet not too sweet. Some syrups can be overly sweet, cloying.. only made worse when the flavor is faint (then I end up using even more syrup, making it that much more sweet). This Monin Lemon syrup is balanced! I can taste lemony goodness.

It can be used to make a very quick cup of lemonade, or added to anything that you want a boost of sweet lemon. I have added it to iced matcha green tea, regular iced green tea, regular iced black tea, just plain with iced water, and added to a glass of iced lemon water (lemon juice concentrate or lemon extract, water, ice, then some of this to add lemony sweetness). All within the past few days, haha.

I think I will buy some more. I think this is going to be used a lot this summer. Just this week!

Cheers!

title: quality brand (usually), not at all effective on me, missing 1/2 of order
text:
In short: Good taste, good ingredients, didnt help me sleep at all. Received 1/2 the order. Buyer beware.

I like Cheribundi, but this one misses the mark for me in a few ways. I thought the combo of cherry juice, tart cherry juice concentrate, melatonin, and magnesium chloride would help me sleep. I already use magnesium (various chelates) every single night. Once in a great while I will add in melatonin to help the occasional restlessness. This past week I have had a few nights in a row where I was tossing and turning a lot. So, perfect timing to try this out.

--->>> Basically, I felt nothing. I eventually got sleepy like I normally do, and fell asleep fine. But then I was back to tossing and turning. I woke up fine; no grogginess. Normally I have some grogginess with melatonin. I am sensitive to melatonin supplements.

Even just a little melatonin will draw me quickly into sleep, and keep me there, and make it a challenge to wake up. So I normally go with 1-2 mg, 3 at most. Everyone is different in how they respond to melatonin. But with this being in liquid form at 3 mg, I expected it to work and to work quickly. Nada nothing. I'm not drinking 2 packets at bedtime. I dont need all that liquid, nor the cost.

And while magnesium also usually helps, I didnt find anything noticeable here either. Maybe a little.

Got some cherry juice in me anyway, so thats good. I do like their products usually. Love tart cherry juice, and this has a mix of juice and concentrate. Comes out of tear off packet easily enough. I drink it straight. But I'll stick with their bottles for same effect.

---->>>One spot says that each pouch is equivalent to 40 cherries, another says 30 cherries. Big difference. Which is it?

---->>>Another thing.. (and to me is a big thing as a prospective customer).. this is supposed to be a pack of TWELVE. This arrived as a pack of 6. This is not a vine thing, as it would have stated that we would get a reduced amount (which would be a rare thing). No, it states pack of 12 just like one would as they were ordering direct. Bringing from a lofty $3 per pack to a laughable $6 per packet serving. Buyer beware. This isnt the first time this has happened with this brand.

I'll work through the rest of the pack. If I find that it somehow seems to kick in then I will be back to update.

Taste, quality: 5 stars
Missing product: 1 star
Effectiveness: 1.5 stars
Going with 2 stars

title: sweet little treat, very good (no nut) Turkish Delight. 5 rows of 5 cubes
text:
No nut Turkish delights. Hard to stop at just a few. I do love me some Turkish Delights of all styles and flavors. I buy them on occasion as I find them to be such a neat little treat. This has a smooth citrusy lime like taste from Green Tangerine (Satsuma). Product description mentions no corn starch, but I am pretty sure it is a mix of powdered sugar and cornstarch, which doesn't bother me in the least. Corn starch is listed in the ingredients at least. It helps keep the confections from sticking, and I dont think powdered sugar alone would have enough oomph. These are well packed, but there will be some powdered sugar poofing out as you get closer to the tasty little blocks.

Cut in 5 rows of 5. Pressed toegther. All together in a tray, not separated like some. I try to stick to 3-5 pieces at a time, lest I get a sugar rush. I get two bites from each. I dont just pop into mouth. I like the feel of biting down. I first enjoyed them after a long day in a physical job. I got home on a hot day, grabbed my labs and a drink, and some treats for them, and these treats for me, and we all sat in a shady spot and enjoyed some num nums. Pre dinner refreshment.

Pricier than many I buy, but I have no problem with the quality, quantity, packaging, or overall taste/experience. Really lovely little treat. I'd get this brand again no hesitation.

Manufactured 03.2022, with best by date of 3.2023

title: good flavor, added pea protein for 10 grams per serving
text:
Shelf stable "milk". That is my primary reason for buying this. I keep an assortment of non dairy milk on my shelf, and in my fridge. I dont care for almond milk for my coffee, but for nearly any other application it is fine. I tried this, and it isnt too bad. Orgain tends to do a good job with the taste and mouth feel of their products, so I am not too surprised that this is better than some stuff I have tried from other brands.

I like having some shelf stable stuff on hand because I dont want often get to the store, and I dont want to have to buy a bunch of containers that need to go directly into the fridge. The shelf stable stuff is more costly, but it offers some much needed convenience and flexibility.

I normally only do unsweetened vanilla, but the lightly sweetened vanilla option was on sale, so I decided to go with that. It isnt too sweet, itsnt too strong in any flavor, which is fairly typical. It has a creamy vibe due primarily to sunflower lecithin. Slightly thicker than some from pea protein and guar gum. Also pea protein is what boosts this milk to a protein option. 10 grams per serving.

Includes added vitamins/minerals such as calcium and vitamin D, which is in the form of D2 (ergocalciferol). Too bad it isnt the healthier version D3 (cholecalciferol), which is more readily absorbed and used by the body.

title: oaky, hint of sweet and heat, pleasantly surprised by this, good looking bottle
text:
I dont mind this! After reading some reviews (and some giving me a good chuckle with the descriptions), I was expecting something terrible. I am almost disappointed to like this as I have no fun descriptors to toss into the mix. I actually find this pleasant. But I know that it isnt alcohol. It is not actually alcohol; it is not going to taste the same as actual alcohol. Dont expect it to. That is my experience with any alcohol free dupes. That being said, it has the oaked smell and taste, along with a hint of sweetness, and a gentle burn. Has a mild flavor that can be consumed straight, yet stands up when mixed with other liquids. I think most ideal scenario is when used as a halfsie--can double your consumption without filling up on alcohol too soon. Great for nice big drinks that are otherwise loaded with booze. Summer drinks, baby!

I wouldn't compare it side by side to actual bourbon straight. But the flavor profile is bourbon-esque. To me, surprisingly so, albeit watered down. If this were unlabeled and it was wafted under my nose, I would say, "that smells like bourbon". Mostly because of the oak.

I rarely drink bourbon. Mostly because I dont care for oaked flavors. But I enjoy some mixed drinks on occasion that call for it. Namely, an Old Fashioned. We have a variety of whiskey & bourbon on hand for that purpose. One thing I have noticed is that my tolerance for alcohol has plummeted. I was never a big drinker (on regular basis), but now I just feel weird with a little. I want a drink, but I dont want the bad feels. I am not a tee totaler. OI just dont want to feel like $hit.

So for me, I have been sniffing around "spiritless" options for some time now. Part of me was like, "why even bother?", but then I thought I could do half the amount of booze and boost it back up with flavor by using a non alcoholic version. In my experience with others, as with this.. it works. My brain thinks it is booze because every time I smell it I get slightly nauseated (there was this one time I drank way too much... ). Anwyay, I find it works in my Old Fashioned. I will be looking to make some summer drinks where volume appeals to me, yet dont want it all to be booze, yet dont want it entirely watered down tasting.

I really like the bottle. They did nice job on that. Has a classy look, and it looks like it belongs on a booze shelf.

title: Makes nice cuppa. Columbian w/Lions Mane, Chaga, Reishi, Cordyceps, Maitake, Shitake, & TurkeyTail
text:
I've been enjoying this the past several mornings. I have had it hot, I have had it iced, usually black, but once I added some cream. All good. Has an easy balanced taste. Overall how it tastes will depend on your ratio of water to coffee. I find that the 1 tsp per 8 ounces to be "OK", and so I boost it with a little more powder.

Just Columbian coffee with Lions Mane, Chaga, Reishi, Cordyceps, Maitake, Shitake, and Turkey Tail mushroom. Nice assortment!

Not sure how much mushroom I am getting though? Thought maybe that would be made clear on the label, but I dont see anything anywhere. I would like to know more about that. I take mushroom supplements daily, and sometimes I pick up coffee mushroom combos like this for something quick and easy. I tend to like instant coffee (and mushrooms) so the overall flavor profile is as expected: coffee forward, with neutral mushroom flavor. I am always surprised by how little taste mushrooms impart when added to coffee.

Overall I like this for the pleasing taste of instant Columbian coffee, and the bonus mushrooms, even if I dotn know how much is in there. Makes for a quick, easy cup of coffee that I have enjoyed black, hot or iced. I would consider getting this again as the price is not too far off from my preferred instant coffee.

The coffee itself is better than some instant I have had. This seems to only take on an "instant" taste if I use too much.

title: very sweet, I like it mixed in with iced tea or carbonated water, low key non jittery energy
text:
Very very very sweet, from Sucralose and fruit juice. The ingredients are clearly listed on the product page, so I knew what I was getting, but I wasnt sure what overall taste would be like. If you like sweet, then you will get sweet with the orange pineapple option.

I didnt feel much of any energy boost, but I will say that I was motivated to get some chores done, including mowing my grass (with push mower). Sometimes I can tell effectiveness of an energy drink based on that rather than strictly the amped up feeling. This is powered by tea, so the caffeine is more low key but effective. I like that better than other energy drinks that use stuff more likely to make me feel jittery.

While it is way too sweet for me, and I do find it refreshing because of that, I give it 3 stars. BUT, since I decided to add some to a cup of brewed iced tea, it added a perfect amount of sweetness and flavor that I now have a new found use for this. I will still drink it plain if need be, but I like it added to tea (or even carbonated water to make a peppy pop). And overall I like it enough to consider another flavor option (if the price is right). SO.,, 4 stars

title: balanced, sweet with hickory undertones, all around good, not fake tasting
text:
So good! I had no idea that this is by French's. I love all sorts of BBQ sauce, so this is really about preference, and you may or may not like it. It has mostly sweet flavor with an undertone of smoke. Not too smoky. Perfect tang. Love seeing tamarind in the ingredient list as that has a natural tangy sweetness with loads of depth. Additional sweetness sources include sugar, corn syrup (not HFCS), and honey. Some molasses. The usual BBQ sauce ingredients such as vinegar, tomato paste, smoke, & various spices. Whatever the combination, it just works. Lovely hickory sweet sauce, not to thick, not runny.

I hadnt yet seen this in stores, so I am not sure if it is new or just not available to me locally. As I love all sorts of BBQ sauce, and may not be the perfect candidate to offer up an opinion, I will say that this has a nearly home made taste. What I like it is that it doesnt taste artificial or too commercial. Not sure if I can explain that right. This tastes like some effort was put into creating it.

title: good quality, nice easy chew, easy to break off, nice assortment of non flavor flavors
text:
My review is for the meat loop variety pack. These pork based skinny dried sausage loops are pretty good. There is original, pepperoni, and chorizo. I like them best in that order, but I like them all. Soft, chewy, easy to snap off what I want, and store the rest. I prefer sticks, but the loops are a fun change up, and make it nice for finding the perfect portion in the moment. I love having meat sticks/loops on hand for hiking and for my busy work days of hands on labor work. I often have a variety of snack bars on hand as I dont take a lunch. When I have cheese sticks and/or meat sticks, I feel like I have gotten a "meal". Just nice over a dry cereal bar (or in addition to). Add in some sliced apples, and I feel well fed! The meat sticks make all the difference.

So yeh, overall I think these are good. Will you like them? No idea. It's food. A lot of this comes down to preference. I find the quality good, the packaging good, and overall experience good. The chorizo and pepperoni are a little more "fatty" tasting, but I think that is more of the spices used and the slightly extra moisture. I have to say, it is not unlike other brands I have had. I like that they are flavored beyond pepperoni/chorizo. I'm not one for extra flavors (fruity, vegetal, taco flavor, etc). Just want "plain" or close to.

Sometimes I just like some more than others, but all are kind of the same to me. Because of that, I will usually buy based on price, and I think the price is reasonable for this 3 pack of meat loops.

title: just brown rice, good texture, crunchy but not hard, seems versatile
text: 100% brown rice. Tastes exactly as that. Like a puffed rice cake, but the opposite in texture: flat, dense, compressed. Tasty. At first I thought they were bland, but then I sort of just kept working through a packet. Know that there are no other flavorings or salt added. It is pure rice. 5 crackers per packet, and 15 packets total. Some minor crumbling at edges but not enough to take away from overall appearance or function. Pretty good, if looking for a flat, plain, crunchy, easy to chomp through, textured cracker.

title: organic, fresh, scrumptious aroma makes me think of fall desserts
text:
Mmm nutmeg. So fresh, aromatic. Just lovely. I am impressed with Jai Ho products. I have tried several herbs and spices, as well as food staples (repurchased their black rice a few times). Just all good. Acquired 06/2022 with best by date of 12/2024.

Comes well packed in a plastic bag that is then tucked into a mylar lined pressure zip bag. I like this for a variety of reasons- likely lends to extra fresh product, maintaining freshness, allows me to open the bag without any powder poofing out. I can decide if I want to keep it packed as is, or transfer to another container with ease.

title: organic, aromatic, fresh, reasonable price, great quality brand/company
text:
Smells so good. Jai Ho has quality products, all organic, all as described. Packaging same as what is shown in pictures. Acquired 06/2022, with best by date of 12/2024. Packed in a plastic bag that is packed in a mylar lined pressure zip pouch. I like that for various reasons: extra fresh, allows me access to bag without poof of powder coming at me, and I can easily transfer it to another container if I dont want to use theirs.

1 lb! With cloves, a little goes a long way. I primarily use it in chai drinks, some Indian dishes and the occasional stove top aromatic simmer for freshening up house. Oh and the occasional fall time baking. What a flavor!

title: organic, fresh, really a step up from dry leaves, packs a punch of flavor, everyday spice!
text:
Bay leaves powder is fantastic. I have been using bay leaves for as long as I have been cooking, and never once thought to try powder, until recently. When I did, my mind was blown in how much better the flavor is. So after trying and loving other Jai Ho products, when the opportunity to try their bay leaf powder came available, I had to try it. Between another brand I recently bought, and this coming along so soon after, I am up to my ears with bay leaf powder.

This is organic, a product (and company) of India. Packed into a plastic bag that is then tucked into a mylar lined pressure zip bag. Smells good, tastes, good, and now I use it as an every day spice rather than limiting to use in stews and soups that I normally toss a few leaves in.

I figured if I didnt like it, I could use it as a bug deterrent. I also use bay leaves in food storage areas that I want to help keep critters away from. But I like it, and it will be used in everything I can think to add it to. Havent tried it in a smoothie.

title: fresh robust organic fenugreeek
text:
Divine flavor. Gives Indian dishes that extra something special. Havent tried it in a smoothie (or tea), but after reading up on benefits, taking it as a supplement has piqued my interest. Little goes a long way, and this 16 ounce bag will last me a good long time. I keep fenugreek seed on hand, and this powder is much easier to work with, and the flavor more intense. Very good. Nice when you want the fenugreek flavor to come through.

I have tried (and purchased again) a variety of Jai Ho products. All products of India, all organic. All fresh, and reasonably priced. Packaging is the same whether it be spices, herbs, or food staples (love their black rice). It is packed in a plastic bag then further packed into a mylar line pressure zip bag. I like that a lot. Helps keep it fresh, and also keeps the powder from poofing out upon opening. Can either be kept in that packaging, or easily transferred to another container.

title: fragrant, flavorful, and fresh. BBD of 12/2024. Organic!
text:
1 full pound of lemon grass powder! If you have a need for a lot of lemon grass, this is a great way to get it. It is quite a bit for my needs! I dont go through much, but I knew I what to expect in terms of amount. I also knew what to expect in terms of packaging. Jai Ho packages their product in a plastic bag that is then enshrouded in a mylar lined pressure zip bag. I like this as it helps further keep product fresh, and I am not opening the bag to only have it poof out. Then I can determine if I want to transfer the product or keep in in place.

Taste is good. Let me ramble for a moment, then I will round back to lemongrass. I rarely buy fresh parsley, and I can easily buy or grow that. Yet I keep a lot of parsley in my spice drawer. I always have fresh onions on hand, but I also have containers of onion powder within reach. Same with garlic. While I may prefer fresh lemongrass, I rarely ever have access to fresh lemon grass. Rare. And what I get often goes to waste because I only need a little. Mostly I have to go without unless I have powdered version. This is pretty much the only way I am getting lemon grass, and it totally works In the same way that powders work over fresh). I work with it a little differently than fresh--just like with other dry spices vs fresh herbs. Powder tastes different than fresh, powder is stronger than fresh because it is concentrated down since water is removed. So keep in mind that a little goes a long way with this lemongrass. It is all based on preference, need, availability, convenience, and targeted flavor.

I like it, and I decided to portion some out and put rest in our extra freezer. I think it would be fine in a cool dark place, but even the amount I took out will last me a long time. I may start expanding my use of lemon grass by working it into smoothies and broths. Normally I use it in Thai cooking, and thats about it.

Fantastic price for amount. Maybe share with someone?

title: like chopped garlic- fresh, aromatic. I like their packing practice (baggy inside a mylar lined bag)
text:
Good garlic, robust aroma and flavor. USDA organic. Reasonable pricing. Dry granules retain some moisture simply due to their size, but not enough to mold. That is my experience with chopped granules. Not a powder, but more akin to a jarred garlic (in terms of granule size). In fact, these would work well in an oil infusion if you didnt want to use fresh garlic. . I have tried other spices by this company with success. As for food, I am a big fan of their [[ASIN:B0B29CGZNZ Organic black rice]].

New to Jai Ho, but have tried (and purchased again) a variety of products from this company lately. I happen to like the packaging, and it is what has kept me coming back for more. I am keen on packaging that lends to longer term storage. If I dont get to it right away, then I am confident that it will be fresh for a long time. The best by date is 2 years out. They double bag their stuff. The product is in a plastic bag tucked into a mylar lined bag. I dont think there are 02 absorbers (I just dont recall at time of writing this). What I like is that I am not opening a bag and immediately having a poof of product come at me. I can then carefully open the interior bag, and either pour it into the outer bag, or transfer it with ease. I like options.

title: Gives flavor and warmth, not scalding heat. Balanced. flavor.
text:
I find that I can use 1-2 tablespoons of this in a dish, and it doest get too hot. More of an undertone of warmth, with the gentle flavor of paprika.

Once added to a dish, the resulting taste is warm not hot, though that may depend on how much is used and what other spices are used. I tried it plain off the tip of my finger, and it was spicy as expected. Don't do that, haha. I then proceeded to use it in a modified "Hungarian" goulash. I tend us copious amount of paprika, and I like to finish it with a sprinkle of something spicy, whether it be cayenne, red pepper flakes, or some other spice with a mildly hot profile. This Paprika and Red Pepper blend seemed like it would be a dream combo for my dish, and for others that benefit from this flavor and heat profile. I like it. My Asian dishes will benefit from a more low key heat. Happy to have this.

Giant container. Rather excited by this because I actually go through a lot of paprika, and to a lesser degree red pepper. I like that this isnt flaming hot, so this will likely be used nearly as much as the addition of red pepper just works really well with it. Paprika is one of those spices that I find work best in larger amounts.

I dont rate on price, and I know McCormick usually is a tad more costly over other brands (not always), but i am rather surprised that the price per ounce is as high as it is for a bulk sized 5 lb container. ($0.85 or $0.73 with S&S).

title: pure aroma and taste, true lemony flavor. Divine in frosting, or for amping up lemon drink flavors
text:
Lemon tasting lemon extract. Pure lemon aroma and taste. I have had some that fall short on smell and taste. This is very good. $3.75 an ounce good? Btw, they have the math wrong on the listing, $14.99 for 4 oz, not per ounce. Well, maybe so. I now know I am getting a sure thing with this But it is on higher end of many options out there, but not too outside of reason. Hence why I dont rate on price. I can see the price before ordering, and my review is based on if it lives up to its expectation of quality and performance. You can decide if price is worth the try or not.

The flavor, scent, and performance is very good. As with any extract, I just store in my baking cupboard. I may put it in with my coffee, drink, smoothie, tea supply cupboard because I think the lemon is so on point that I will use it to boost other lemon syrups and such.

My star reduction is in the design of the bottle. It has a wide mouth opening, which makes it more jar like than bottle like. It is large enough to put a measuring spoon in, rather than the more typical narrow neck where the extract is poured out. The difference is disconcerting. And while not a deal breaker, there was no safety film under the lid. Not all have that, but I do like to see it. This just had the plastic wrap around the lid. So be careful opening as it is totally open when lid comes off.

title: fresh smelling, fresh tasting, nice combo of hemp, chia, & flax
text:
Manitoba Harvest is a quality brand, really cant go wrong with anything by them. IThey've been my go to for hemp hearts or other blends for some time now. I always know what I am getting for the price. I appreciate that they include an image of the bag from every side so I can make an informed decision. Because of this, I knew I was getting seven, 3 TBS servings for $9.49 (as of 06/22). 7 ounces total (products like this are sold based on weight, not volume, and contents settle after initial pour). A mix of hemp hearts, flax, and chia. Hemp heavy.

Personally, I dont do a full serving as I find I dont want that much hemp hearts at once. I tend to use 1-2 TBS at a time at most. I like sprinkling it over my hot oats. Lots of other creative uses for it. I also dont use it daily, but for sure will use this up within a month given my usual application and frequency.

Good taste, good quality, and I like the all in one option. Love the pure, fresh aroma of all three combined. Makes it convenient, and I would consider this again for times I want that streamlined approach to making my morning smoothie or oatmeal. Less bags to get into. Or if I were travelling, stuff like that. OTHERWISE, I think I prefer to just buy separate hemp hearts, chia, and flax. If only so I can adjust the amount I want of each (I like a lot of chia), and save a little money. But price doesnt enter into my rating, as I can see the price before ordering, I can see what I am getting, prices fluctuate, we all have different needs, preferences, budgets, etc. Also this mix lends toward convenience, which may be reflected in price. I think this would be nice addition to a healthy foodie gift basket.

5 stars. It is a quality product, It is fresh, smells good, and it is exactly as described. 5 stars because it is a good product, quality brand, and they provide most of the info i am looking for.

title: nutrient dense, very similar to blueberry, reasonable price per ounce, organic and raw
text:
German company. This bilberry powder countries of origin are Bosnia and Hercegovina.
Acquired 06/2022 with best by of 01/2025
USDA Organic

Very similar in taste and nutritional profile as wild blueberries. This powder is very good, and dare I say a bargain per ounce (especially compared to blueberry powder but also in comparison to some bilberry powder). I saw the price for ONE FULL POUND, and thought this may be a sub par product. I dont always assume cheap=bad, or expensive=quality, but when it comes to whole fruit (or veggie, or herb) powders, I am likely to be more suspect (usually in terms of processing or country of origin). $49.99 for 16 ounces of air dried whole fruit powder is good. I have no concerns. However, I dont rate on price.

Good quality, and the product matches what is in the description. It says air dried. Normally I prefer freeze dried, but you cant go wrong with either. I think freeze dried keeps more nutritional integrity, but air dried keep more visual integrity. But the difference isnt enough for concern. This is very good, and use it like you would blueberry. Add to smoothies, to oatmeal, yogurt, muffins, frosting, etc. Benefits are worth checking out.

I keep an assortment of fruit and vegetable (and herbs) in my pantry as foods are sometime scarce, dont look good, are way over priced, or simply not available. Having shelf stable food items is not always as good as the fresh thing, but it is better than going without. Haven't been able to afford blueberries or raspberries lately, in any form, especially powder.. so finding a blueberry dupe for reasonable price makes me happy.

title: light, crisp, and refreshing, invigorating. Divine over ice for summer coffee drink
text:
This is why I dont rate on price. I am pretty sure price is wrong, or quantity is wrong. I received a box of 4 (22 each) for total of 88 cups, which is more standard for how Caribou sells their coffee, which brings it down to $0.72 per cup. Still pricier than some, but totally within range compared to the $2.89 it is set at for just a 22 cup box. Curious if that will change, and I imagine it will. No one will buy this for that. If it changes soon, and you are now seeing an updated price and/or quantity, then the rest of my review may be useful to you.

In short, I love it. My husbands likes it, and my mom really likes it- she came over to visit and I made her a cup of coffee as usual. Always something different. She made a point to ask about this coffee, and was surprised how good and strong it is for a light, and that it doesnt have bitterness. Basically my observation which is as follows:

Taste? Bou-Ya! is a light roast. To explain my thought on the taste, I need to say upfront that my preference is dark roast, as dark as can be. I can tolerate a medium if it is balanced. The one flavor profile I try to avoid is bright and tangy because those tend to also be acidic and cringingly tart. These types tend to be light roasts. (These are the offerings of most coffee establishments (dunkin donuts, tum hortons, etc). So I avoid them. So why would a dark roast loving, light roast despising viner order this? because my husband is a huge fan of Caribou, and I am regularly buying their medium roast k-cups. He also likes light roast, so I figured this was worth the try.

Well, I too decided to try it. I just assumed I would not like it. BUT, this is pretty darn good. I like it enough to want to continue to keep this in rotation (so long as it is indeed for the 4 boxes of 22, and not just 1). I have been willingly drinking it every day for the past few days, 1-3 cups!! Usually over ice as it has been wicked hot lately. Also, been drinking it BLACK. I prefer my coffee black, no sugar. But if I try a coffee that is acidic, then I will "doctor it up" with some cream and sweetener. I dont need that here. I am shocked.

I.. ME? I like this light roast, and I am floored. It is summery and light, yet provides a caffeine kick. Tastes like coffee, but not ruined by acidity/tang. My new summer coffee, as this is divine over ice.

So why do I like this light roast when I dont like any other? I dont know for sure! It is definitely a light roast. It has that bright taste, but there is no acidic tartness. I can taste coffee (very important, as many light roasts dont have that solid foundation of a "coffee" taste, if that makes sense?), and the brightness reminds me a little of grapefruit. A dry tang. Mellowed by a sweet finish. So odd, but so good. And now that I take closer look at description, "sweet and citrusy", I would say yes that is accurate. But in a good way. Like the roasters knew what they were doing! Not an acidic tartness from aging beans, or brutalized roasting. But nuances of flavor pulled out.

You know how with beer, particularly IPAs where there is a high hop factor that gives it tang? Some are just "too much" in that department, but then there are some that are more balanced, and have more nuance. Tastes of citrus come through, and the overall drink it light, crisp, and refreshing. THAT is what this reminds me of in terms of consideration (btw, like my coffee, when it comes to beer I also prefer super dark chewy beer, like Russian Imperial stouts and such, but will drink a well done hoppy IPA, much like this light roast).

Never ever thought I personally would consider a light roast something that is worthy of 5 stars. Your experience may vary.

Cheers!

title: reminds me of BBQ sauce. Sweet w/ Heat (non building)
text:
Not just for "vegans", but also for those keeping track of calories and sugars. Tastes like BBQ sauce to me. I rather like it. Upfront taste is sweet and honey like. Middle range has the tang of vinegar as it slides into finish line of heat from red pepper. All together is like a BBQ sauce flavor.

I was concerned that it would have a pronounced "stevia" taste, but it doesn't. It actually has a honey taste and mouth feel. Sweet with heat.

I like the bite of heat. Not hot, more like a tickle on the tongue. Doesn't build, simmers down quickly. But it's there. Like a spicy, slightly smokey and sweet BBQ flavor. If you wanted to go the distance, just add it into some tomato sauce or paste, and you are well on way to a BBQ sauce. I'm going to use this as a "honey" glaze on chicken. (I'm not vegan or vegetarian, I simply eat everything that tastes good). It would be mad good on chicken wings. I havent thought much beyond the hot sauce/BBQ sauce vibe about it, but i imagine there are some clever uses for it. Nothing about it makes me want to put it on pancakes. If it were just a hot syrup, maybe, but the addition of vinegar pushed it into hot sauce/BBQ sauce flavor profile territory.

Viscosity is more like a "bear" clover honey, or agave syrup, or any syrup.

4 stars for having more of a BBQ sauce flavor
5 stars for having more of a BBQ sauce flavor, lol.

title: quality brand, love this w/ water & ice, but 1/2 order is missing. Buyer beware!
text:
Taste, quality: 5 stars
Missing product: 1 star
Going with 3 stars, sorry.

Just want to say that this hits my maximum in terms of pricing. Yet, I dont rate on price. We can see the price before ordering, if price is too much for you why bother ordering it? I can see what is in this, so I am making an informed decision. No surprises. We all have different budgets, needs, preferences, prices fluctuate (currently $36 for 12 pouches), and if this looks good to you, go for it. Pricy for me at $3 a pouch, yet I really like it as a "drink" mixed with water over ice. So yeh, I'll leave the price feasibility up to you.

This supposedly contains the equivalent of 30 cherries per pouch. Cherries are crazy expensive right now, so this may be the only way I can get them in my system.

That being said, I rate on quality, experience, and factor in my perception of effectiveness. I also compare what I ordered against what I received, and further compare it to what is written in the product description. Does it all add up? Does it make sense? Did I get what I "paid" for?

In this case, a hard no for one factor alone, and its a doozy. This was an order for TWELVE, and I received 6. Making this a whopping $6 a pouch. This is not a vine thing, this is simply not being sent what was ordered. I am curious for others' experience. I would be turned off from buying more based on this. I have experienced this in my own orders for other things lately, as have others. Cheribundi is a great brand, so hopefully it is a glitch, a one off. But I am suspect.

Taste? Is as expected. Lovely tart cherry. Wasn't sure what it would taste like with the addition of other stuff, but it is pretty close to just tart cherry tasting. I like it. I buy bottles of local cranberry juice CONENTRATE, and this has similar taste and mouth feel, but more liquid. This also has a little added cranberry juice giving it the ability to flow from packet rather than stay stuck like syrup (which concentrate is more like). Includes ginger juice, and has added supplements (vitamin C, and B vitamins). Naturally occurring sugars.

If you just need/want cranberry juice or cranberry juice concentrate then find that- they have it in bottles and packets. If you want the added "immune support" supplements this is a pleasant option. I have had it direct from packet, and I have had it mixed with water over ice. Pleasant on a hot humid day and just want to get in some non sweet hydration. Contents pour out easily and entirely. Convenient for on the go use, or keeping in desk drawer, etc.

title: surprisingly bold, makes me happy that it leans dark. Stands up to ice. Confusing listing info
text:
Rather bold, smooth, coffee tasting coffee. Stands up well to being poured over ice. Perfect black.

I often have pour over coffee, usually using a filter and my own coffee. I have had this style before where it is a prefab filter loaded with coffee and it just hung over the mug. Normally I find that I dislike the coffee and like the style. And I got to the point where I wasnt going to try any more of this style because the coffee is usually bad (hence why I went for this one and passed over another they had for me to try). But here I am.

Surprisingly I really like the taste of this coffee, but the mechanism is finicky. No different than others except that it didnt stay on my mug very well. It was best used on a mug with more narrow opening, and I made to to hold it less it fall in. Worked fine on my 16 ounce mason jar (which I was using so I could turn it into iced coffee).

I prefer my coffee BLACK, no cream, no sugar, no added flavor. I prefer it as dark as can be, bold, strong, smooth, chewy. I can tolerate a medium roast if it is balanced, not tangy or acidic, and leans dark. Another reason I got away from these coffees is because they tend to use tangy acidic roasts. This has a good deep coffee tasting coffee flavor. I imagine the strength varies depending on how much water is used. But I can say that is shockingly held up to being watered down with ice.

Now the listing is confusing. There is info about being a pack of 5. This is a pack of 16, divided into 2 boxes of 8. Says a "can". Nope, a box of packets. Also, it mentioned "Just Black + Vanilla" ??? If this is supposed to have vanilla, I cant taste it. Or maybe it is part of the roasting flavor that comes through. But it is not vanilla (for which I am thankful. As much as I love vanilla, I do not like as a flavor added to my coffee). They do carry a vanilla option (the one I passed on). Says Vietnamese style, which my familiarity makes this a Robusta bean coffee? No clarification. I'm ok with that as I like robusta beans, and it naturally contains more caffeine than arabica or columbia.

There is really no info on the box. Directions are basic, and are easy enough to figure out. But that's really it.

Because I actually like the coffee, I would give it 5 stars for that.

Star reduction for the confusing product description and general lack of info. I dont put much emphasis on the pour over style, as it works fine depending on what mug I use, and totally works if I hold it, and also can be set into my pour over filter if need be. I have one that takes a paper filter, so this saves me a filter.

I DO NOT rate on price. I can see the price before ordering, we have different values, budgets, needs, preferences. Side by side with other pour overs of this exact style is with same price range, albeit on the high end. Not likely a repurchase for me based on that, but I think overall quality is fine, and is best pour over of this style I have had, taste wise.

title: no salt added! love black lentils, convenient item to have in pantry
text:
Dry lentils dont take long to cook, but I like having some canned lentils on hand for times I want extra quick and convenient preparation. These organic black lentils are just that, there is no added flavoring or sodium. Just packed with some water, and they arent swimming in it. So you are actually paying for lentils and not water.

I add them to whatever I feel like. Sometimes I make burgers with them, sometimes added to soup, sometimes over salads. I have added them to meatloaf/meatball/hamburger mix to boost fiber and stretch the protein source. I also toss in with vegetables or over rice. Again, just works in everything. I live lentils!

title: Salad beans: kidney, garbanzo, & pinto beans. No added sugar or salt
text:
This Salad bean assortment is simply comprised of (all organic) kidney, garbanzo, & pinto beans. No added sugar or salt. When I look for a "salad beans" in store, usually all I find are ones loaded with added salt and or sugar. I can buy a few separate cans and mix them together, but sometimes I just want a smaller amount to work with. This product from Westbrae is good and exactly what I was looking for.

Another thing that I like about this brand is that the cans are pretty well packed. Not just sitting in a bunch of water. I want to pay for beans, not water. SO I will consider this brand again when the time comes.

title: good grief this is good. Spicy, warm, hint of sweet. Complex flavors, try ICED, mega WOW
text:
Ahhh, I LOVE Yogi tea. Yogi has so many different varieties, and over the years I have liked them all.

I dont consider myself a tea drinker, but I always have some on hand. I go through phases where I just want some tea (never replaces my beloved coffee). I like it for warming during winter, and I like it for cooling (over ice) in summer.

The thing about Yogi tea (which I have been drinking for well over a decade, all sorts, love their bedtime variety) is that the flavors are complex. I think that is what appeals to me. There are other ingredients to make for a tasty experience.

This has a mix of black tea lead, green tea leaf extract, and guayusa leaf, as well as cinnamon, hibiscus, cayenne, and monkfruit. I love hibiscus in my tea for the health benefits, but it can be a tad too tart/tangy for my liking. It pretty much disappears in this. The overall taste is warm, spicy, and gentled with some sweetness.

This "Positive Energy" has a warm, spicy, mildly sweet, with no noticeable tang. It is lovely as a hot cup of tea, but then I put it over ice, and that upped the WOW factor. THIS levels up a cup of iced tea to something extra special. I think it is the warming spices used and the zip of heat from them. Yet over ice.. interesting juxtaposition. Love the addition of cayenne. So appealing!

Just a hint of sweet from monk fruit. Just enough to mellow the tea flavor, but not enough to make it taste like a sweetened tea. It is perfect for me.

It is strong enough that a sachet could be tossed into a big bottle of cold water to make a flavor essence.

6 boxes of 16, sachets are individually wrapped. I use 2-3 bags per big mug. Then I add over ice. Oh Em Gee.

title: aromatic, warm vanilla, caramel-esque. Fresh. Just 3 but that is all you will likely ever need!
text:
Fresh, aromatic, intriguing. 3 beans should last a very very very very long time.

I love food and trying anything new that comes my way. I had not heard of nor knowingly consumed Tonka beans. and as of writing this have still not consumed any. Before my order I did a quick dip into the online foodie world to find out what to expect, and what to do with them. Just like some spices, this is not meant to be used in large quantity, nor is a lot needed. Expect a vanilla like aroma, followed by notes of something else that is just intriguing and pleasant. Can be used to flavor anything, scent anything. I learned that Tonka is not approved for use in US because of its coumarin content, which is actually present in a multitude of foods (not to be confused with coumadin). I quickly learned that it would take significant amount to be harmful. Many citing the use of nutmeg in the same manner--fine for nearly application, but if taken in hugely inappropriate amounts, the myristica will be harmful. So that alleviated concern on my end. Also, that law is ridiculously outdated and unfounded.

So here we are with our contraband spice, and it is a delight. I'd say mostly it smells like vanilla, but I imagine it blooms other aromas depending on its application. I think it is one of those items that will taste like it smells. I read that a little goes a long way.

The Tonka beans are about an inch long (around size of medjool date pit), and come vac sealed in a tiny little pouch. So small it could have easily been overlooked, tossed out. Keep an eye out for it. I didnt just toss this in my cupboard. I kept them in their little pouch and stuffed it into a mini glass mason jar. I just wanted to have them be in something that gives a more physical presence.

I like this, I think the quality is good, and while the heat level turns me away, I think those who enjoy a kick of spice will enjoy this. I absolutely loved the texture & chew, as well as the sweetness.
