title: actually flavorful, true flavor, not a powder but not as granular as plain sugar
text:
I was most curious as to whether the flavor comes through or not. Some flavored sugars are weak, and it takes a lot of sugar to get the flavor. Not here. Whatever you use in sugar you get a good punch of flavor. Also, getting a true flavor can be tricky. These are full of flavor, and if you are looking for a flavored sugar that actually tastes like sweet vanilla, hazelnut, mocha, or caramel, then I think you will be pleased. I am.

I see these for at home or at office coffee stations, or use in baking. Sugar rim a glass or mug would be cute too. While not a powdered sugar, it isnt as coarse as regular sugar. Easy to work with for all those applications. This definitely helps the sugar to dissolve more quickly. And, because it is actually flavorful, you dont need to use an excessive amount to taste the flavor.

Run this through a blender real quick to make your own powdered sugar for making a quick, easy, flavorful frosting.

I try to rate as though I was shopping for this, and had an idea of what I wanted, and I knew how much I wanted to spend. So I dont rate on price, but I do rate on perceived quality and how much the product received matches the product description. This all lines up. So while I personally wouldnt usually go for a product like this, the quality and versatility and flavor is top notch. Enjoy!

title: good flavor and works quickly to wake me up. Quality brand. But how much mushoom, please?
text:
I might change this to 5 stars as I really like it.

Dark roast has a deep dark start, with a hint of brightness in the finishing taste. Breathes out a dark roast. Coffee bean flavor lingers on tongue. It's good. I wasn't so sure about the mild tang but it quickly disappears.

My first cup of coffee of the day is always a dark roast, always black, no sugar. This is also my preferred way to test and review a coffee. Says to brew 10 or 12 ounces for a medium strength coffee, or 8 ounces for a stronger brew. Typical for most kcups. I tried the 10 ounce option, and found it strong enough for a decent cup. 8 ounces is extra nice, and has been my go to brew amount (then I use 2 cups for 16 ounces. So good black!).

My second cup (usually also dark roast) is when I included supplements such as mushrooms and collagen. Sometimes I will add creamer, sometimes (but very rarely) a sweetener. Collagen usually adds no flavor, but sometimes mushrooms do. Very low key, never a strong taste, The description says, "tasty notes of Rhodiola and Coffee Cherry". So the hint of something is likely that. No matter, it is slight and does not get in my way of enjoying this coffee black.

I love adding mushrooms to my coffee, and because I use a separate product, I know how much I am getting. With this, I dont know. If it is mentioned on the bag, I cant tell as I cant read what is on the bag. Small white print against a light blue bag. Hpwever, the product listing says it has 100 mg coffee cherry per cup (that's the actual coffee right? anyway, it has additional coffee cherry powder). But I would like to know how much mushroom.

They need to clean up their listing, and add some helpful info. Such as take the term "capsule" out from "item form". This is a cup as in Kcup pod, not capsule which I attribute to being used in nespresso and the like. This is a soft sided K cup. They should add how much mushroom to expect

I am used to this style of packaging. Coffee pods are loose in a bag. In my experience, just keep the bag closed well and the coffee will be fresh for a long time. Might be an issue if you take a year to go through it, but if you drink regularly or even use this intermittently, I think it will be fine. I have used a few brands, and my favorite San Fransisco Bay is always packed like this. If you are familiar with that, then you know what to expect with this.

Lastly, I am well familiar with Laird products and find them to be of good quality, and the functional aspect seems to be on point. I want to trust that there is enough mushroom and rhodiola in this to warrant such a high price per cup. Btw, I dont rate on price, so my rating does not factor this in. I do happen to comment, and $1.46 per cup is well above my budget for price per cup. I do spend plenty on high quality mushroom supplements, so it isnt exactly about price. BUT I want to know how much is in my cup. And I dont, so 4 stars overall.

However, it is a good cup of coffee, and I feel GOOD as I drink it. Not sure what is kicking in, but I can feel the fog lift pretty quickly. Good WAKE UP coffee.

title: crickets are related to crustaceans, so be mindful if have shellfish allergy :)
text:
Neat. This is new to me. I haven't "knowingly" consumed bugs before. I have been curious about crickets after watching some program about food grade crickets some 10+ years ago. More recently I tried [[ASIN:B09BK4VWQ3 cricket flour]], which is really pretty good (all considered), and the easiest for me to try. Gave me a chuckle to make cricket muffins. Now I can add in some whole crickets. Can you imagine making a cricket cake or cookies, then decorating with these on top? haha.

Anyway, I am still weirded out, and I totally appreciate the opportunity to try it. Another bug/worm option came up and I passed on it because I just couldnt see myself trying it out. I'm not quite that adventurous yet. But a cricket? sure, why not.

It isnt bad. More about the appearance than anything. Really weirds me out. Taste is rather neutral, hint of fish? I cant pinpoint it. Slight crisp. I think chopping them up so they are less cricket looking is the way forward with these. Mixed in with other ingredients. I would prefer to see a nutritional panel, there is some helpful information on this page, but not directly on package. I am glad to see the allergy warning about crustaceans, as not everyone is aware that crickets are related to crustaceans (huh, shrimp really are the bugs of the sea!)

"A single 15 gram packet of crickets contains a whopping 10.5g of protein. They are also a good source of Vitamin B2 and iron."

Ingredients: Microwave dried crickets (Gryllus assimilis Sp), Salt.

Weight: 15g Net

Shelf life: 1 year from date of manufacture.

title: one of those hot sauces for use on anything

title: Cinnamon, Cloves, Cardamom, Black pepper, Grains of Paradise, Fenugreek
text:
Ingredients listed in community section is different than what is on actual website which is different than what I actually have. They need to get this sorted out. Here are the Ingredients that I have for this tasty Matafecha blend:

-Shai Kimem--cinnamon, cloves, cardamom
-Kunido beribere--black pepper
-Korerima--Grains of Paradise. They are the black (or sometimes brown) seed pods of a cardamom-like plant. Comes from same family as ginger
-Abish--Ethiopian Fenugreek

Smells nice, tastes even better. Awesome on potatoes, and pairs really well with chicken. I made a chicken stew of the sort, and used this to enhance the flavor. Very good.

title: they work! fits just fine on my Jordans syrup bottles
text: What can I saY/ They work! I dont mind pouring out from my syrup bottles, but I like the barista vibe I get from using a pump. It you have the room (head space), these make adding to a cup of coffee, tea, or smoothie real easy. Fits fine on my 25 ounce (750 ml) Jordans bottles.

title: a little bland but doesnt taste processed, could use a little more sauce, but otherwise good
text:
Pretty good but a little bland once I put over rice. Out of the packet it has a hint of spice, but it gets lost with carbohydrates. I think I would like it more if it had a little more sauce to work with, just seems a tad lacking. Plenty of soy beans and edamame.
I do appreciate the fresh flavor, and good texture. The flavor doesnt taste processed. Although has a goodly amount of sodium, it is offset by the high amount of potassium.

I really like having convenient items like this at the ready in my pantry. I would consider more products by this brand just given the real food taste.

Picture shows half the contents of the packet

title: fresh tasting, satisfying
text:
Smells good, tastes good. I dont drink a lot of tea, I go through spurts. I am always happy with Yogi tea as they seem to have these really interesting combinations that add to the flavor experience. Been drinking Yogi for a couple of decades now.

I brewed a mini cup using 1 tea bag to 5 ounces of water. Says to let steep for 7 minutes. For me, it made a mild cup of tea, easy to drink. Added nothing to it. Not overwhelming in any one particular flavor. My plan is to make lots of iced tea with it

6 small retail boxes (like you'd grab off a shelf) each containing 16 easy to open individually wrapped packets for total of 96 tea bags.

Organic Puerh Tea Leaf**, Organic Roasted Chicory Root, Organic Cinnamon Bark, Organic Ginger Root, Organic Reishi Mushroom Extract, Organic Green Tea Leaf Extract, Organic Chicory Root Extract.

title: good flavor but needs work. No actual matcha, uses artificial dyes, plastic hard to get off
text:
Taste: 4 stars, other considerations drop overall to 3/3.5

Not listing correct ingredients. If you look at the product picture where it shows the ingredients, know that that is wrong. The ingredients on my container say: Non gmo sugar, organic tapioca syrup, honey, natural and artificial flavors, blue 1, red 3, red 40, yellow 6, canola oil, soy lecithin.

This is supposed to be Honey and Matcha. I can taste the sweetness of honey, the texture of cane sugar, and oddly enough a light matcha taste despite no matcha being listed. If it falls under natural flavors then why not just list it as matcha. So I am doubting actual matcha is used, but a flavoring. If they had used matcha then they could have omitted the artificial dyes. The ingredient list on the fuzzy looking picture used to be natural colorings from food. Why the change? Makes me now question if the honey is actual honey. Hmm. (says real honey on front of canister, also says Made in USA).

I initially tried this like it was a lollipop, why not? Although I can taste a hint of "matcha" as a sucker, I really cant taste it when added to my cup of tea. The honey flavor comes through though. The overall amount per stirrer is a good amount. Thick, plenty for its purpose.

I like the overall look, but the packaging is obnoxious. The honey spoon stirrers are sealed in plastic, then wrapped in cellophane style bag with twist tie. Then all tucked into a plastic canister. The plastic that seals the stirrer is tricky to get off. It took a little effort to expose the edible part, and I never did get the rest off. It is just too tightly on the stirrer.

If that isnt bothersome to you, then sure I would have this among a coffee/tea bar, or as part of a gift, or parted out toward individual token tea gifts. There is an appealing look to it, and again I think the overall flavor is decent.

title: pretty good flavor, hearty, chunky, nice addition to pantry
text: Dont eat this kind of soup much, but I wanted to round out my long term pantry with various options beyond the typical canned soups (though I buy those too!). This is more for something "different". I like it with crackers. I can add noodles or rice to add substance, or whatever I have on hand. Just lends a different taste and texture that I find welcoming to my long term pantry.

title: good flavor for canned soup, hearty, eat as is or add to it, or add it over something
text: Pretty good! I dont eat a lot of canned soup, but I keep it on hand for convenience. I like that I can eat this as is or add more noodles, or rice, or whatever to it. Makes a good base, or flavoring agent. Works well for emergency food. Good to have options, and this provides an interesting taste profile over basic chicken noodle soup. Though, get that too :)

title: sweet, spicy, tangy, just all around delicious. Love it hot or iced, alone or mixed w/ green tea
text:
So good. I do love ginger, and so I always have ginger-honey-lemon sachets on hand. It all started when I wanted a strong ginger flavor to drink. Ginger tea didnt work (I know this is referred to as tea, but i mean ginger tea bags), pure ginger juice didnt cut it--close but doesnt keep real long in fridge, and real ginger root is just awkward. Cut to finding ginger cyrstals in these little sachets. Instant, easy, perfectly portioned convenience. And so, instantly in love.

Lots of brands, pretty much all the same. Though I am really loving the Prince of Peace product. Not as sweet as some, yet has all the spicy ginger taste I want. I LOVE drinking it as is Hot OR cold, alone, or added into other teas. Or right now, I am all about making up a cup of matcha green tea, stir this in, then put it all over ice. OMG, yum. Makes me happy to drink this.

Super great hot when you just need to settle the stomach as it is very comforting. Nice too for rough throat. It is just a must have for me as I find it endlessly useful. Also, I usually feel a little extra zippy when I have ginger crystals, how/why is that. I sure dont mind!

60 sachets-- I took them out and counted, all tucked into a large bag with pressure zip closure.

title: fresh, high quality, organic cacao. No issues or complaints--all good :)
text: Just powdered cacao! Pure, strong chocolate flavor that is loaded with nutrients (you;ll have to do separate search to see what all cacao contains).  Makes for great low cal hot chocolate, smoothies, added to oatmeal bowls, and anywhere else you can think of. I have been using cacao on and off for many years, and I find it a must have in my pantry. Judees is one of my favorite brands, so it was a no brainer to pick up a bag of cacao from this company. Fresh, high quality. And priced well for ORGANIC

title: balanced coffee, turmeric, pepper flavor profile, caffeine kick, smooth tasting
text:
Huh, this is pretty good. I already drink spicy concoctions like Chai tea, and "golden" tea or milk. I use turmeric often in my cooking, and so all around I am familiar with the taste. I have never used it in my coffee though. I didnt know what to expect, but I am pleasantly surprised by the gentle taste and overall caffeine kick. If you already like turmeric and black pepper, give this a try. Tang of turmeric, spicy gentle kick of pepper. Smooth coffee.

Nice hot or iced, black, or with cream, sweetened or not. I dont normally add cream or sugar, but it is even better with those added (imo). But I have been drinking it black just fine too (when I am too lazy to add stuff in)

I dont have a specific way to make it. It is really just to taste (I like strong!). Add some to a mug (or carafe), then add hot water. Stir. Done. Add creamer and sweetener, or not. I probably use more than what is called for, but I do that with all instant coffee. I like my coffee strong.

I drink all sorts of coffee, brewed in all sorts of ways. I go through these periods of time when I just want instant. My electric kettle is right there plugged in and ready to go. So I think I like the ease of making instant. But I have everything else to choose from too. Lately though, instant has been my jam.

I say all that because I think this is good not only for instant but overall as a coffee. It is robust but not bitter, the addition of turmeric and black pepper really works with coffee. Who knew. Now I do :)

Bonus experience: maybe it is the amount I use, but I am satisfied with one cup. Some days I can drink mug and after mug, but with this I was feeling all the good feels right away and found that I didnt want to keep on drinking it. Like I was saturated with coffee quicker than usual, which I think is a good thing. Though I am likely using more than I should, Oops :0

Been drinking this daily since i got it. Half expected to just drink it once in awhile, or have a need to add more coffee in (some blends are really weak), but this is solid. Im not sure if it is a repurchase, but who knows. I think the price is reasonable at $14.99 (less is always better, but overall seems fair).

Up to 35 mg of curcumin per serving

title: The only weird thing about this is that it is wickedly good, crave worthy, instant repurchase
text:
My new summer drink! Refreshing, tasty, fog-lfiting, all around pleasant (to me). Organic, no preservatives, sweetened w/ juice and cane sugar (very low, just right), and made in Texas, USA.

I did not expect this to be such a high quality tasting drink. I am on a search for a good canned tea, but most are ok, some are good, but none make me CRAVE it. This is what I was looking for and didnt know it. I really do love it.

The mint and green tea has a nice balanced flavor. Green tea forward with smooth light mint. Refreshing. Low key sweetness, which I am impressed with. I still taste plenty of fresh green tea, but it is gentled with a little apple juice and cane sugar. Not too much. Just right.

Also has a little lemon, spearmint, and rosemary.

Caffeine kick is perfect. It is that low key, non jittery, steady, "I feel alive" boost that is typical of green tea. It is a pleasant feeling. Like sun coming through on a cloudy day. 80 mg per can.

I appreciate the larger 16 ounce cans. So many products are in the 8-12 ounce range, with similar pricing. When it comes to tea, I want a big ole glass packed with ice to carry around with me. This makes me want to buy more, and in fact I am doing so right after I submit this review. Yum!

title: perfection! vac sealed brick, fresh, long shelf life, just all around fantasic.
text:
I like it so much I am already ordering more. This wonderful black rice comes vacuum sealed in a durable bag. It pops out as a brick, but is easily broken down into loose pieces. Clear instructions and other pertinent info on bag, and can all be seen in product description. Kudos to Jai'ho for the info! Hope to see more products by this brand.

I rarely have black rice, and every time I have it I always think that I need more of it in my life. So I added another one to my cart. I really like the packaging, so even if I dont get to it for awhile I know it will be fresh for a long long time.

title: excellent quality, fresh taste, nice container, all around good
text:
I've been using peanut butter powder forever it seems. Dont think I have met any bad ones. I think I initially got into PB powders for the low calorie aspect (take out oil, and caloric load is greatly reduced compared to regular peanut butter), but at the cost of that lovely peanut butter mouth feel. But it has its uses, and I have been using powders for 10+ years now. Just a pantry staple at this point.

Can be used as source of protein, and simply for flavor. Love it in smoothies, milkshakes, oatmeal, and for making peanut sauces. I have used it in making peanut butter flavored ice cream, and for the occasional "peanut butter" on toast. Though really I just go with regular peanut butter for that mostly.

I really like Sun Warrior products, and while they are more costly than some options out there, the quality is very good to me. Opaque, easy to open container. Good size to work with. A lot of their products come in this size and style of container which greatly appeals to my propensity toward a uniform appearance.

title: tasty, easy to prepare, convenient bone broth. Nice as is or used as base for quick soup
text:
I've tried a few flavors of bone broth by this company and I like them all. Delicious, healthy, convenient. Lemon and Ginger is a flavor combo I like, so having it highlighted in a bone broth flavor really appealed to me. I like it!

Makes a lovely mug of broth. Not so much now that we are on the cusp of summer, but all fall and winter I love having a cup of hot broth every day. Preferably bone broth, but usually any will do. I find this to be just warming, comforting, and tasty. I make a mug and drink alone, or I will add in some bits of left overs (maybe rice, or pasta, maybe some vegetable or protein..whatever is kicking around in the fridge) to make a quick little soup. Nice for filling the belly between meals.

title: 5 stars because it meets my needs for using in a cold blended/shaken drink/smoothie
text:
Bargain matcha; great value compared to other brands and even over their smaller 1 lb bag (which I bought about a year ago). Micro Ingredients has some decent supplements and other products. This culinary matcha is fine, and it works well in smoothies or even iced lattes. I never bake with matcha, but this is what this grade is for.

I do not have discerning tastes when it comes to matcha green tea powder. So long as it blends well enough to consume, and gives me that non jittery energy, I am happy. I go through a lot, and I usually just grab whatever looks good.. It works just fine for my smoothies. Any tangy green taste is masked once I blend it in with some flavorful protein powder or meal replacement powder. I tend to use a lot of matcha at a time. I think the serving size is 2 tsp? well, I tend to use 2-4 TBS. So no matter what brand I use, the taste can be a little harsh.

I will probably buy this again. Nice big bag will last me a few months or more of daily use.

5 stars because it meets my needs for using in a cold blended/shaken drink/smoothie

title: thick paste that can be thinned down, or made into broth. Full body, versatile, tasty
text: Thick, lightly textured paste. Holds up well on its own, or smoothed out into a sauce, or further stretched into a broth. I have used as flavoring for noodle bowls, and this did not disappoint. Good garlicky miso flavor that has body. I think the versatility of it makes it a contender for repurchase. Healthy too

title: good easy noodles for ramen bowls, pre seasoned, includes seaweed
text:
I love ramen bowls and all sorts of noodle styles. I bought this primarily on price and for adding to my long term pantry. They are well packaged and are nestled nicely into a sturdy box. The noodles are easily overcooked so by mindful of how much heat is applied. I tend to doctor these up with additional seasonings, veg, and protein. Not outside the norm for prefab "ramen". I like the flavor overall.

HInt of fishiness from addition of seaweed, which I like.

title: delicious, crunchy, perfectly salty
text:
Currently obsessed with dipping these crunchy salty rice crackers in [[ASIN:B00BEQEQJ0 Sunflower Butter]].

Typical texture and crunch of RICE crackers. I love the plain but salty taste. Another fave of mine is to use with hummus. I like these better than other options. I even like this alone just to grab a handful to snack on.

title: always fresh, perfect portion, nice hot or iced, mild mellow all very good
text:
It is actually very, very good. Splurge if your budget allows. I drink matcha all the time, for 15+ years. Benefits are great, so its one of my must have food/supplement items. Taste wise, that can vary and I prefer to bury the natural matcha flavor. But some are so mild and naturally sweet that it is easy to drink alone. Even so, I usually add stuff to it.

The packet/stick format is neat for on the go use, or simple quick convenient preparation. Also, this makes for a super fresh powder. My current obsession is to take a shaker cup, add a stick of this and a sachet of [[ASIN:B09VZLJCPR Honey Ginger Lemon]], add cold or room temp water (or even a little warm or hot--will always dissolve best in hot). Then shake until well mixed, then pour over a cup of ice. I get a great flavor and a great kick of long lasting energy. I haven't tried this hot, but I can tell it is a contender for hot preparation. Ooh, I bet my iced prep with the honey ginger lemon would be amazing added to hot matcha. mmmm. Writing this review is making me crave a cup, so off I go. My new summer drink.

Really nice product, easy to recommend.

title: Spicy, tart, & sweet! Love my honey ginger lemon sachets mixed in w/ iced matcha green tea
text:
I love stronger ginger drinks, and so I recommend this ginger "tea" if you like a strong kick of spicy ginger. I find that these sachets are way stronger than an actual tea formula. I just love them. I have the Honey Ginger with Lemon, which is always nice alone (hot or cold), or added to any lemonade, black tea, or my personal favorite: adding to matcha green tea (iced!). Nice tang of lemon, followed by kick of heat, and sweet. The levels of all that will depend on how much liquid you use. I'll add one sachet to a about 10 ounces of water (I'll add a bunch of ice to a grande starbucks cup, then pour the liquid over top).

Also good for after dinner tea, or when stomach is unsettled, or need a throat soother.

Addition of long handled spoon is nice :)

title: bold, smoky, divine. Totally added much needed oomph to rather blah canned baked beans
text: Smokey and delicious. I saw their recommondation on the bottle to add it to baked beans, and I was like sure why not. Took my blah beans to wow beans. That was just with regular canned beans. I will need this the next time I make home made beans. I love BBQ sauces, and I will find any reason to use some. Good on burgers! Now I want to try them all. If looking to create a food themed gift (best gifts!), add some of these sauces in.

title: nice pick me up, lovely coffee flavor, use more for stronger flavor (or add to coffee)
text: I like adding it to my brewed coffee, or adding extra instant coffee to this. Otherwise it is a tad weak. But overall I like the flavor, and the price is reasonable for however I decide to prepare it. I always add mushroom supplements to my coffee so this is nice to be an all in one combo. Since this is so easy to make, it could be easily taken for use on the fly. I can shake it up with cold water, room temp water, or hot water. Drink hot or add ice. Boost a smoothie, or simply enjoy as a regular cup of coffee. Has a little coconut powder for natural flavor, creaminess, and sweetness.

title: Matcha & Mushrooms! nice assortment of ingredients
text: I like this matcha mix! It includes an assortment of mushrooms that I normally use every day. Though I have no idea how much. Price is pretty decent for a matcha green tea powder and multi mushroom combo. Sweetened with agave powder. I mix this with my personal blender and then pour it over ice. Sometimes I add more matcha, sometimes I add other stuff. But as is is pretty good.

title: I can taste the mag glycinate a little, but otherwise good taste and excellent ingredients
text:
I love the ingredients. I prefer to run this through my personal blender to get it to really dissolve. I have had products like this before, so I am very much used to the taste and how it mixes. I like it as is, or with a little cream added to it. I have added extra cacao depending on how chocolatey I want my drink.

I can taste a hint of something. It is not mushrooms as they no matter what kind I use they tend to totally disappear. Ashwagandha can leave a hint of something earthy, but this is something different..and when I took a look at the ingredients it was then that I noticed that it has added magnesium in the form of glycinate. Reall a great form of magnesium, but straight up in powder form it has a weird taste, and I think my tastebuds are remembering my foray into powdered mag glycinate and that is what I am picking up on. So, the added cacao and cream helps mask it. You may not notice it.

title: fragrant, tasty dal, easy to make, makes good amount, nice for lunch
text:
I chose classic dal because I love lentils. I adore Indian spices, so this combo instantly appealed to me. I made it the same day I received it, and I found it easy to make and it resulted in a tasty dish. Makes 3 servings, or 2 for me and my big appetite. I made it exactly according to directions, but it seems like it is forgiving. I didnt pair it with anything, but certainly can add anything to it or anything added as a side.

Nice for anyone but might be extra appealing to those looking for quick way to enjoy an Indian spiced dish. If you keep an assortment of spices on hand and lentils, then the best bargain is to do it yourself. But this is a tidy, easy way to make a delicious dish without a lot of fuss.

title: nearly rock hard frosting (unusable), most broken, MOLDY, sprinkles good, taste ok
text:
This could have been great, but it is terribad. Maybe it was tucked into a shipping container for several months, and that is why the cookies are broken, MOLDY, and the frosting is both dried out and oily- all separated and it cant be mixed back together. It is like the packets of frosting sat in high temps and allowed to age.

The good: super cute packaging, colorful, fun, festive. If I were a kid whose parents presented this to me as something we will all make together, I would be excited. The egg shaped cookies (2) were whole, but all of the bunny shaped cookies were broken into 2, 3, 4 pieces. The sprinkle decorations look fine. The flavor of the cookie (yeh I tried it), and the flavor of the frosting (I am a risk taker), have a very sweet taste. Almost too sweet, but overall would have been good enough. About as expected taste wise.

The bad: broken cookies, like I said the bunny shapes were all totally broken.

The ugly: the frosting. The directions say to massage the packets to mix back together any separation. But there was no way that was happening. I tried, just in case. But it was evident upon first glance and feel that ALL the frosting is garbage. All dried out, with some oily drops. I even opened them all out to seeif any were workable. Nope. None would spread.

The box itself was intact. No denting, marring or other off look. So why the extensively broken cookies? They are also well packaged. There is a cardboard tray, with two large egg shaped cookies, unwrapped. Then next to it were individually wrapped bunny shaped cookies. Then the entire tray was wrapped. But just the bunnies were broken. All of them. Which left just the egg shaped cookies But then with the frosting being total garbage, it really left everything to be tossed. I admit that I nibbled on one of the egg shaped cookies. Good flavor. Hard, crunchy, and plenty of surface to work on for decorating.

Had it all just been how it should be.. I would have gone with 4-5 stars. But since this is a kit that simply can not be used (sprinkles seem ok), this makes it 1 star. Could have been super cute. Seriously though, did this sit in a hot humid warehouse or something? The expiry date is still over a year off.

title: Smooth, sweet flavor. Easy to prepare, includes everything packed into cup (straw too!)
text:
Fun, easy to prepare Boba tea kit. I normally dont do milk tea (my personal fave is green tea with lychee syrup), but I have come around once I started trying brown sugar flavors. So I chose the brown sugar with red beans and later tried the taro. I like both, but I prefer the brown sugar. It is sweet, and the caloric hit makes this a treat. It is within the realm of normal for sugar content, etc.

Mixes seamlessly. Use hot water. If wanting to have an iced drink, then add a little hot water to dissolve, wait a few minutes to allow tapioca to soften up (I waited maybe 2 mins max), then load it up with ice and then top off with cold water if you wish. The tapioca balls are much smaller than the norm, but they seem to work well enough. They cook up very quickly; no fuss. The sweet red beans are a neat addition. Usually I have those in bao buns, but in my boba tea? It works! Either add them in (I recommend you do, its neat), or munch on them separately.

The cups are sturdy, and have a good fitting lid. Includes a bendable, retractable straw (pull down and twist to lock). There are three packs tucked inside the cup. One each milk tea powder, tapioca pearls, and sweet red beans. Directions are clearly printed on the cup.

I liked how it turned out, and since I wanted to really load up my cup with ice above and beyond what this can hold, I transferred the contents to a big mason jar. I wiped out the cup and will reuse it for my coffee.

It is a delightful little kit, and I like how everything is all in the cup, and the directions are clear. Takes up some space over a bag or powder, bag of tapioca, but the convenience factor (and there is no down time cooking the tapioca pearls) makes this worthwhile. Pleasantly surprised how much I like this.

title: convenient for quick meals, or if power goes out and options are limited. Easy to warm up
text: Good for me. I keep some precooked food items on hand for ultra convenience and even for in case of emergency. Doesnt take much to prepare, shelf stable for awhile. Rice looks good, tastes fine. I buy when on sale for best value otherwise I dont bother.

title: fresh, pleasant taste. Nice boost of protein & magnesium
text: I can't imagine there being anything bad being said about this pumpkin protein powder. So I will toss in my 5 stars as well. Gorgeous organic pumpkin seeds ground down to a powder. That's it! Very good, lovely hint of nutty flavor, is super pleasant in a smoothy. I saved some for use in a healthy muffin recipe I am preparing.

title: works fine for me
text: Bread, biscuits, cookies, and cakes. Made them all with success. Just tastes like flour albeit gluten free-- never quite the same as regular flour, but it makes for perfectly good substitute. I am not gluten free but I tend to enjoy some of the added density that non wheat flours impart. So this also works with half of this, and half of regular flour if gluten free isnt the main objective.

title: perfectly good lentils, well packed, competitively priced, great protein & fiber source
text:
Nice lentils, nice packaging. I go through a lot of lentils. I wanted to top off my lentil supply as I havent been always finding it in stores. A little pricier than what I normally get it for, but still within reason. Even though I go through a lot, I like buying several pounds at once in smaller bags rather than several pounds at once in one big bag. Makes it easier to handle. When I am at the store I usually only get a few since I dont want to wipe out the shelves. Seeing a large amount in 1 lb bags worked out perfectly for my preferences.

This pack of twelve 16 ounce bags is currently $21.99 (as of o6/2022), which makes it $1.83 per bag, or $0.11 per ounce.

title: bold, strong, robust, chewy, super deep dark roast that tastes like liquid coffee beans. Dreamy!
text:
Midnight Express Columbia Supremo is my jam. I love a good, bold, strong, robust, chewy, super deep dark roast that tastes like liquid coffee beans. I knew the moment I peered into the bag of black, shiny, oily, whole beans that I was in for a treat. Smell is absolutely divine, too. I ground some up and made it in my pour over (one of these days I will use in my drip maker). Mmm so good. Smooth, zero acidity, zero bitter. Definitely dark. I drink my coffee black, and this is just so delicious to me.

If you like dark roasts, give this a whirl. I imagine it would hold up well over ice. I wont waste it on cold brew (I tend to use cheap coffee that i dont love for cold brew because cold brewing makes nearly any coffee taste good). But yeh, this would likely be extra amazing.

title: tasty popped potato makes for stout but crispy chip, spicy but not too hot
text:
For a 5 ounce bag, there are quite a few chips. Thin, crunchy and somehow different than a typical potato chip. I thought at first they were liked a puffed corn shaped into a "chip", but its made from potatoes. Rice cake esque but thin and dense. But it is in fact, puffed, popped potatoes. Neat texture.

Stout little chip that can handle heavy dips, yet is easy on the teeth. As someone from Buffalo, wings are life and spice is something I am greatly familiar with. While it is not my go-to flavor, these are pretty good. I know I would like other flavors even more. The spice on this seems just right. Has flavorful spice but is not hot hot. Will withstand flavored dips; in fact might make the flavors pop (haha). Thinking it would be an incredible chip for a buffalo wing dip. That would be amazing (*adds ingredients to grocery list*)

WHAT IS A POPCHIP? "we keep our potatoes out of the deep fryer. instead, we heat them in a pressurized chamber and then quickly release them. their first breath of fresh air is a... pop."

title: always a good brand for me
text:
Been awhile since I have seen Better Body coconut sugar anywhere, so I am pleased to see that they offer a big container online. Quality brand, quality taste. No problems at all. Ive been using coconut palm sugar for years, and this taste the same as my other batch. I love coconut sugar for everything, but it is a preference thing for sure. I think it works fine for use as white sugar or brown sugar. And while it imparts a deeper flavor, I dont think it is that far off from just plain sugar. Might be more noticeable in applications where the sweetener is the highlight of the flavoring (sweet drinks especially).

While I dont use sweetener in my coffee, I have friends and family who request it when they come over for coffee. For me, I use it in thai dishes, and baking (as white sugar or brown sugar). I've been using it for so long that I forgot why I began using it, haha. I simply like the flavor, but the fact that it is better on blood sugar is likely what originally piqued my interest. Stuff seems to last forever too. I always keep mine in a glass jar, but even bagged it never goes weird. I love that this is packaged in a solid container with twist off lid; I prefer it over bags just for ease of use.

I dont rate on price, but this large size is pricier than the smaller size (this is sold by BBF, and the other is sold by Amazon). Side by side I would rather find storage room for a couple of smaller containers than this big container. And then be able to save even more money? Huge difference in cost per ounce, especially with Sub & Save. Still, weird though, right?

title: organic, fresh, delicious, another good one from SFSC, small size with some smashed bits
text: San Fransico Salt Company makes some top notch spices. Always robust, fresh, and just have a little more flavor than other brands (to me). I love this pepper blend, but wish it had more to the pack (this will last us a week or two- seems we are constantly filling our pepper mill). Ok, maybe we wont go through it that quickly, but now that I can see what 1.5 ounces of whole peppercorn looks like, I'd rather pay more for more quantity. Some peppercorns are smashed which I think is a matter of it being in a packet, or maybe it is just so noticeable because of the small quantity. None of it makes it bad, just prefer to not see what had become some pre ground peppercorns. Organic, fresh, delicious. Just want more, and a few less smashed bits.

title: noodles for ramen dishes, add your own seasonings, veg, protein, etc
text:
Funny, there is "ramen noodles" the mainstay of those on serious budget, where it is a quick cooking processed brick of noodles accompanies by powder seasoning, then there are "noodles for ramen". Which is nearly any wheat noodle for use in "ramen" dishes (typically in a base of broth, then layered with veg and proteins, totally different, better than the other). This is for the latter (but doesnt contain wheat). Yet, it is packaged similarly to the bricks- basically for easy single serving use. I like it, bumps up the price over a box of buckwheat or bown rice, but it is a really nice blend that cooks up really well and makes a good sized portion (I typically make way too much, so this helps reign me in, and I actually save money by not having waste).

Just plan to add your own everything. These are just noodles, and it was expected as such (by me). But it occurred to me when I saw how they were packaged that they could be mistaken for "ramen noodles" rather than "noodles for ramen". Again, typical ramen is made using wheat noodles, so these are a NON wheat noodle using buckwheat and brown rice. Very nice option for those that want the wheat like texture and yet be able to avoid actual wheat. Takes typical time of cooking for other buckwheat or rice noodles- 6 mins or so. Not an instant item, but not anything that takes too long either.

I like them a lot. Really good flavor, texture, and portion size is perfect for a noodle bowl, ie "ramen".

title: pretty good, nice to have options in pantry, good emergency food too
text: Not too shabby. I know this Chili Mac soup is a popular one. It isnt my favorite, but I like keeping a variety of Chunky soups on hand just for the variety. They sure so have a lot of variety which makes it a great go-to emergency good. Can be eaten warmed up or cold, peel back lid is easy to get into, and can be eaten alone or added over more noodles, rice, proteins, etc. Price each for the case is a little better than what I find locally per can. So if you have budget to stock up, then I think this is a good way to go. Even better with subscribe and save.

title: perfect portion, excellent over vanilla ice cream, yogurt, etc
text:
Strawberry jam is good! Nice easy to use packets that travel well. Also nice for keeping portions in check, and for not taking up space in fridge with jars. Depends on how much you go through. I kind of go back and forth with my jam use, so I am liking just grabbing a couple of packets as needed. Is perfect texture and sweetness for use over ice cream. Dont buy special strawberry sauces marketed as ice cream sauce. Just grab a container of squeezable strawberry jam (or preserves). This is a very smooth jam that will squeeze out from the packet with ease for whatever application you want it for.

Date on box is when it was manufactured. Jams in packets dont really have expiry or best buy dates. But I imagine at least (ie no less than) 2 years from manufacturing date.

title: like a party in my mouth--sweet and sour, makes tastebuds sing
text: So good! Wish we had the fruit in the US. Having a freeze dried version is the next best thing. Pricy but kind of within reason for a freeze dried product. They sure are a treat. I am intrigued by the sweet and sour combo. It has a lovely sweet taste yet packs a sour punch. Fun, and kind of addicting. Not a daily snack, but an open bag will soon be an empty bag. Hard to stop eating!

title: good quality expeller pressed flax seed oil
text: Expeller pressed, meaning no chemical solvents used in the extraction process. This flax is perfectly good. I use hemp as well, but I prefer flax for the better nutritional profile. I either take it off the spoon, or drizzle over any food stuffs. Good smell, good taste, and as with any delicate oil it needs to be refrigerated after opening lest it goes rancid quicker than you can get through it. 5 stars because it is perfectly fine; meets expectations. No surprises :)

title: tasty representation of instant Japanese curry (mild, hint of sweet), Lovely over udon
text:
Probably more for those already familiar as it didnt even occur to me to think about how to prepare it or what to do with it, or how it might taste like. Reminds me of the packs of [[ASIN:B0043ZL0UW S & B Curry]] sauce I get, but with a little more oomp of flavor (complexity?), and less big pieces of vegetable. The one I tried has flecks of meat and veg. I like the deeper taste of this. If you are familiar with S&B you know what I mean (good taste but more processed vibe to it), and this is a step up. Price and size reflects this too. As anticipated, it has a mild overall flavor with hint of sweet. I dont know if any of these get more spicy, but it is a mainstay to expect a hint of sweet no matter the spice level.

Basically "Heat it and eat it". Heat it how you want (or not) as it is already cooked. Doesnt need to simmer as it is an instant food item. If rice or noodles are hot enough, then this may warm up enough just poured over. Or pour into a pan or dish to warm up. Or add the pack un opened to a pot of water to warm that way.

I had mine over Udon noodles. Use the whole packet. I am always looking for a good sauce for my noodle bowl nights. I really like this. I like my Japanese S&B for use over rice, and I like this "Japanese Curry Samari" for use over my udon noodles. I use it all up at once.

title: good looking nutmeg, smooth and mild
text:
Gorgeous container of whole nutmeg. Good looking nutmeg, a tad more mild than some. I think this makes for nice addition to drinks and when you want a more mild taste. I have some that are stronger, and a tad more bitter. That I like for baking. I think I will like this also for some dishes I make that take nutmeg where I want the depth of flavor but not the "nutmeg forward" flavor that some varieties produce.

SO get this if you want mild, smooth, hint of sweet, Think sprinkling over cookies, coffee, or in certain cuisine. The smooth flavor is conducive for use in DIY medicinal purposes.

title: fresh, tasty, and fun. The blocks can be stacked. Really hard on my teeth, best for kiddos
text:
Cambie candy is new to me, but recently have tried a few items and have been over the moon with the taste and quality. If you have the teeth of a 12 year old, then you will love these. A tad challenging on my middle aged teeth. They are big time reminiscent of the candy I enjoyed in my youth (circa 80s). Like a sweet tart maybe? Familiar taste anyway, and it is GOOD. But oh so bad on my teeth. I am careful with these, and given how much time it takes me to work through a block this 5 lb bag will last a long time. Cool thing though? It has a best by (or exp?) date a few years out or so.

Btw, the blocks are actually stackable, ya know like the name brand toy blocks. Different sizes, colors. SO FUN. Got a slew of bored kids? Drop this big bag in the center of the group and let them go to town on playing and getting hopped up on sugar. lol. I didnt say it was a good idea.

Would be super cute as cake, cupcake, or cookie decoration

Would be cute to divvy up into small see through containers and give out to kids as a b-day party favor, in a neat looking clear container and used as a decoration (that can be dipped into for the treats).

Approximately 130 pieces per pound. hahahaha omg that's a lot of candy.

Overall 5 stars. I can't think of anything wrong with these. If anything, I wish I could gnaw on these more easily. But that has more to do with my teeth rather than a defect in this product.

title: tasty, hard to stop eating.
text:
Tasty assortment of BBQ Honey Roasted nuts. Cashews, almonds, and pecans! Just a great texture combo. Once that bag is open, it sure is hard to stop eating. I especially love the pecans. Nice sweet and smoky flavor. I dont rate on price (we have different budgets, needs, preferences, and prices fluctuate. Oh, and inflation makes it hard to determine what is a deal these days). As a specialty treat, I say go for it. Would also make a nice addition to a food themed gift (my favorite type of gift!), especially with other Rufus Teague products.

If I can stop myself long enough from eating direct from bag, I think chopping these up and sprinkling over salad or chicken would be nice. Just a neat flavor that actually stands out.

title: sweet, crunchy. Eat as snack, topper, or rehydrate.
text:
Food to Live is one of my go to brands for freeze dried foods, and other foods stuffs like grains and seeds. This freeze dried corn is delicious. Seriously mega yum. Can be snacked on direct from bag, added dry as a topper, or will reconstitute to regular corn when added to liquid. I find freeze dried vegetables to have a sweeter taste than their starting state, and yet takes on their original taste once liquid is added back in. So for example, freeze dried broccoli taste sweet to me, then when I add it to a dish calling for broccoli it just tastes like broccoli again. I imagine the same will happen with this corn (as in its the same as other freeze dried corn I have used). So far, I have only been chomping on this Food to Live freeze dried corn a handful at a time.

Really nice for working pantry, and extended/long term pantry.

title: Pleasantly surprised, good texture, good portion, salty sauce
text:
Pleasantly surprised how tasty these are for a packet product. The texture is firm, there is nuance to the flavor; not just flat. The meatballs are just better than anticipated- 5 stars for that. The amount per packet is reasonable too. Each packet has some heft. More meatball than sauce, and the sauce that is there is thick. It is very very salty, though. That is where the slight tang comes from I think. Use this for what it is: convenience food, emergency food, DIY "MRE" option, shelf stable, or just because you like it.
Not as good as homemade (duh), but not as bad as canned spaghtettios&meatballs. More like the taste texture of a frozen meatball. "does the job". I am overall very glad I got these, as they make a great addition to my working pantry and longer term pantry.

I can eat it direct from packet if need be. Though I prefer to have it warmed up with extra sauce (no salt added) to take the salty taste down. Then put over pasta. If need be can be smashed up into a meat sauce, as a base to make sloppy joes, chili, tacos, etc. And of course, meatball subs.

If you are long distance hiker and need to replenish sodium, this will certainly do it, haha.

title: Fresh tasting. Potato like texture, mild w/ hint of natural sweet. Good portion. Versatile
text:
Roasted and fresh tasting, and taste look as anticipated. These are soft, and reminds me slightly of the texture of potatoes, or canned garbanzo beans (but 2-3x size), with a hint of sweet and meatiness. Maybe closer to a sweet potato. This texture is the norm! Any foodie site will state as such. For those expecting crunchy, that is not what how roasted chestnuts turn out.

This is just chestnuts, nothing added. I find them mild tasting, and make a decent little snack on the go. I enjoy the naturally lightly sweet taste of them.

I haven't really worked with chestnuts in dishes, but I will be experimenting. Good amount per bag, enough (to me) for adding to a recipe, yet not so much I have to worry about storage.

I think I will slice some for use over a pilaf. Or maybe get creative with something sweet. Or blend into a paste as dip or something. Just seem super versatile. These roasted chestnuts can go in either direction of savory or sweet.

title: clean, smooth, mild. Very nice tasting matcha green tea powder
text:
Smooth, gentle, clean tasting matcha green tea powder from the Shizuoka region of Japan. Their webapage(when translated) has a lot of information about their products, people, mission, etc. I like this matcha for use in my lattes. It is just so pure tasting that I like it as the front and center flavor. Temps are too hot and humid right now to enjoy it hot, but I am confident that this makes nice cuppa.

The .07 ounce packet is really just a tease, but it has been an enjoyable brand to work through. I would get this again, or I would buy it to add to tea themed gift basket. Just know that the packaging is entirely in Japanese. Preparation is like any other matcha.

5 stars simply because it is a quality tasting product. I was able to dip my finger in to the bright green powder and taste how smooth and lightly sweet it tastes. I knew I was in for a good drink, and sure enough I found this quite pleasant to consume.

title: Good flavor BUT says gluten free in listing, but nowhere on package (act says it contains wheat)
text:
Really quite tasty, and can be used on or in just about anything. Just a pouch, so use it all up at once, or good luck keeping it closed well enough to maintain freshness in fridge. Good tasting but not a repurchase.

The ingredient list is weird. They dont include the ingredient list on the product page (they should), so if I were shopping around normally (not testing/reviewing) I likely would not have purchased this. Or I would rely on reviews to tell me more about it. Which is why I mention all that I do. Here I am. The ingredient list is lengthy, small print (my poor eyes!). I will try to include a picture.

Basically starts off with: Water, Sugar, Soy (then long list of the ingredients included in that), then lots and lots and lots of preservatives, variety of spices (cassia, salt, black pepper, tomato, garlic), variety of oils (soybean, palm oil, palm kernal, coconut), some more preservatives.

THEN: it says it CONTAINS: soybeans, WHEAT, nut (coconut). (also says this in listing in one spot), yet in two spots it says Gluten Free. So only with product in hand can one determine what aspect is accurate. IT CONTAINS WHEAT, therefor it contains gluten. Sorry folks.

NO WHERE ON PACKAGE does it say that it is gluten free, BUT it says so on the product listing. That is a phrase that will make or break a purchase for someone. I am not even gluten free, so my pearl clutching is for others who look for information such as this. How awful to have it say gluten free in one spot then not mentioned on the container at all. THAT is much of what my rating is based on: whether the product received matches the product described. Then I add in perception of quality, etc.

Received 05/2022 with exp "2023.07.05"

Product of Taiwan

OVERALL: flavor is 4 stars, versatility 4-5 stars
BUT,
confusion, unclear, misrepresented info 1 star, especially for something as important relating to allergies.
0 stars.
Going with 2 stars. Safety is important. If they clean up their listing (take away phrase "gluten free", and extra highlight that it contains wheat. AND add a pic or written list of ingredients then I would have given it solid 4 stars simply for my taste preference).

title: extra protein pancake batter, nice flavor, versatile use as brekky or snack
text: The directions indicate that the batter will be thick, and it is. Either add a little water, or carefully spoon the batter onto the pan. I like to work small. The pancakes turn out nice. Good flavor. Versatile. It is a small bag kind of typical of other specialty/niche mixes. Price is about on point too. I find Judees to be a little pricier in general, but I often buy from this company because the quality is fantastic, and makes for a reassuring purchase. I love that they used Teff for this mix as it isnt something I see often. Very nice product if you are looking for extra protein.

title: tangy medium, weak taste when brewed at 8 ounces, I like Fabula but not this
text:
I like Fabula coffee; usually I get the ground or whole bean. This is the first time I tried their k-cups, and I am not sure if I like it much. I'll finish it off, but doubt it will be a repurchase. 3 stars.

I drink all sorts of coffee, all styles, roasts, including decaf. While I prefer dark roasts, I will drink a medium if it it smooth, balanced, and has no tang. And I think it is lightly acidic tasting. This medium is "ok". It falls in the realm of medium but it has a hint of tang that I dont care for. A lot of people do, so it is really about preference rather than a nod toward quality. Here is where a bulk of my rating comes from: I notice that it brews a tad weak. Decaf can be like that, but this is more so than my other brands. I brewed it at 8 ounces, and it was mediocre. Watery, tangy, blah. Again, preference thing.

I have used coffee packed like this. I have mixed thoughts on it as it takes up more space, yet it is an eco friendly option. It is an air filled wrapper, then the pod is a soft material with typical film top. It seems to brew well. Some I have used will spit, and this does not.

I know Fabula runs on the high end of the price spectrum, but this is over the top for a k-cup. I dont rate on price, but I comment. If I did rate on price, for me this would make for a further reduction in rating. The current $44.99 price for 24 cups makes it $1.87 PER CUP. Um, no.

title: looks good to me TWENTY FIVE YEAR shelf life
text:
If you sort reviews by most recent, one of the reviews says that their can is way over expiration. They included a pic, and I can see that they misinterpreted the info. Theirs says that the LOT (batch) date is Nov 2021 (09Nov21), but if you look over a little, the EXPIRATION date is still TWENTY FIVE years out! 2046! (09Nov46).

Many emergency food companies use #10 (as in, number 10, not 10 pound). So various weights of food will be packed in these standard containers whether it fills up or not. That means it is possible to have a full can of one style of food, and half a can of another style. Ultimately you are buying weight, not volume. You are not being gipped. You are only being gipped if the weight comes in lower than stated on package. Companies can give more, but they are not supposed to allow less (FYI, next time you go to the store you may be able to get more bang for buck by weighing a 2lb bag of carrots. It could be pushing 3 lbs depending on what you grab for. It just cant be less than 2 lbs, stuff like that.. )

Anway, I bought this as emergency food. I only buy emergency food when on sale, and am slowly amassing a stock. I normally stick to normal canned stuff, bagged stuff, and rotate through my short term and long term pantry. But when I see an emergency food item, I will pick it up if the price it right. When it comes to these onions, I figured I would grab a can since it was on sale, and happened to be less than cost of my usual bagged dehydrated onions. I have no intention to open it any time soon. Can looks good, weight seems spot on. No issues or concerns at this time.

title: smooth and lemony, not tart like regular lemons. Nice to find online for same as in store
text: Occasionally I can find this brand in a local store. Key West lemons are great, and the brand is fantastic for a really lovely lemon taste.  Price is on point for it in my region (NY), and for "Key West" lemons in general. If you need cheap, then go with the basic green bottles. But if you want a real lemon taste that can really make a drink or dessert, splurge for the Key West lemon. Side by side it really makes a difference to me. I love it most for simple lemon water, or lemonade. Smooth and lemony

title: versatile, add nutritional boost to anything and everything
text: Snagged a couple of bags when they were on sale. I gave one to my mom, and kept one for myself. I love adding hemp hearts to anything and everything. They dont really taste like much when added to something, making it easy to use with anything. Nice way to boost nutrition without having to put too much thought into it. Refridgerate after opening, or at least keep in cool place. Just depends on how quickly you go through a bag.

title: pleasantly surprised how delicious these drops are, nice for soothing throat too
text:
I got this more for use as a throat soother than as candy, and it does not disappoint. It has a pleasant light honey sweet flavor. I have medicated cough drops for more serious throat needs, but I keep basic throat drops on hand for other times (dry mouth, talk too much, etc). Buying a small bag simply for that purpose is crazy pricy since all of those are really just candy (ludens, etc). So why not buy candy instead? Thinking of it that way, this 4 lb bags with hundreds of pieces for just over $20 is a bargain. The soothing sweetness and honey vibe is delightful. I normally dont grab for hard candy, but after trying one I instantly poured some into a candy dish. Maybe the first time in my life I have put hard candy into a bowl.

The outer candy is hard, and I would say it is firm all the way throughout. I can tell there is a softer center. I think how soft or fluid that is depends on the temp, and if you are one to allow a piece of candy to dissolve, or if you are a cruncher like myself.

After taking some out, I placed rest in fridge. I may vacuum seal these into smaller bags. Good stuff. I would get this again, and would buy for others.

title: mega fiber, perfectly sweet, must have sweetener for everything
text:
I use various sweeteners, including date syrup, but more recently I began buying date sugar granules after learning how nutritious it is, and how it is essentially a 1:1 replacement to regular sugar. It is just so easy to work with. Just natural sweetness, nothing off tasting. Doesn't make me feel bad, has a very good taste. Date sugar is recommended in [[ASIN:B00Y7USB14 How Not to Die]] if you have read it or learn from nutritionfacts site.

Before trying sugar granules, I was sweetening some baked goods with pulverized dates. This is way easier. This bran "Just Date Sugar" is perfectly good. Nice deep flavor that I liken to brown sugar. I have a few brands in my pantry, and they are all similar. This brand has a recipe on the box.

Has 1 gram of fiber PER teaspoon. That's great! What a tasty way to add fiber to diet. I always add a little to my oats. I love hot steel cut oats or regular oats with chopped up apples, cinnamon, sometimes some pecans, then sprinkled with date sugar. Normally I would use coconut sugar (also lovely), but I am partial now to date sugar. YUM

title: flake like, small chop. Robust aroma and flavor. Well packaged
text:
I like and use various Huggiberries products. I keep my working pantry and long term pantry stocked with various dried, dehydrated or freeze dried foods. I use onion all the time, and keep fresh and frozen on hand, but the convenience of dry is a must have for me. I also sometimes like the added punch of flavor that dry provides.

These "granules" are good. Not quite what I think of when I normally buy granules. These are closer to small chopped. Little larger than granules, slightly smaller than fine chopped. They DO look like how they are represented in the pictures, so no down rating from me. I actually like it a lot. It is easy to work with, reconstitutes nicely, or can just add in to whatever dry. Has lovely onion aroma. Normally I buy Frontier, or huge restaurant sizes of McCormicks.

4.5/5 stars. Really just meets my expecations, no problems. Tastes good. Good packaging.

title: reminds me of dark cherries, robust flavor, sweet, little goes a long way
text: Small 3.5 ounce bottle of stingless honey which I havent had before. It is smooth tasting. Sweet with a hint of tart. It reminds me of a deep dark cherry juice concentrate, or biting into an extra juicy dark cherry. A little goes a long way because it has such a punch of flavor. Thin and syrupy, but is robust at the same time. Use it as you would regular honey or in place of sugar. Doesnt spike blood glucose levels. Pricy, but it is a worthwhile addition to my pantry. I am keen on that deep fruity sweetness with hint of tart. Very interesting to me.

title: not much to say other than they are as expected, excellent quality, no issues/concerns
text:
Whole, raw, unsalted, fresh smelling, fresh tasting almonds. That's it. Pleased with quality. 5 stars!

Store in fridge for extended freshness.

title: HOT but with flavor. Definitely an eye opener. Doesnt irritate or linger, really quite nice
text:
If the usual popular red sriracha isnt hot enough for you, then give this a whirl. All the flavor and some amped up heat. I initially tried it on my finger, and was like WOW OW, thats some hot stuff. But unlike a lot of hot sauces, this doesnt linger hot for long. Like it faded without leaving an irritated feeling. Very interesting. It exceeds my normal comfort range for heat, yet because that hotness doesnt build I can handle it. I like that it simmers down fairly quickly. And it doesnt reduce the flavor. So many hot sauces are just all about being as hot as can be, but have no real flavor to back it up. Hence why I like sriracha. But I know some dont think thats hot enough. Give this a whirl. Worth a try anyway.

Little goes a long way!

title: NO SALT added, but seaweed is naturally high in sodium. Light & crispy, airy.
text:
INGREDIENTS: seaweed (durvillaea incurvata), sesame, sesame oil. THAT'S IT. Seaweed has a fishy vibe, so please know these have a faint fishy essence to them. It is normal, natural, and should be anticipated. Like dulse, etc. I think it is pretty low key, but I am used to seaweed flavor.

I'm not in love with these, yet I dont mind them at all. I think I was hoping for a stronger kick of sesame. I have to say, you must like seaweed to enjoy these, and I do enjoy seaweed on occasion. It has naturally occurring sodium (none added) and iodine, so be mindful of intake (1140 mg sodium per bag, 120 mcg iodine per bag). Sodium is slightly offset by potassium (370 mg). I have thyroid issues that can be exacerbated by iodine, so I have to be careful. Even so, I always have seaweed products in my pantry. There is plenty in each bag to make it a several serving snack. I use dulse and other sea weed products on occasion, and I even buy sheets of roasted seaweed snacks. I rather expected these sticks to be more like that. These are crunchy, and airy. And salty as to be expected. Little more like the skin of a pretzel. Just sort of dissolves in the mouth. SO I guess similar to roasted seaweed snack wafers, but with no chew. There is a mild easy crunch that dissolves. Eat them as is, or toss on, or crumble them on Asian noodles.

Although it provides next to nothing in calories (35 for whole bag) the electrolytes may make it a contender for replenishment on an ultra hot and humid day. Followed by water, of course.

title: continually pleased with Pur360 freeze dried products, mega boost nutrition to soups, etc
text:
Yay for KALE powder. I have used a few different freeze dried powders from Pur360, and they all have been good. I love all the information the company provides, which makes me feel better about their products. This Kale is from Poland. Since nearly all the water is removed, 1 TBS is equal to 1 CUP of fresh. Really nice for long term pantry preps, a good way to get greens if for some reason fresh isnt available. I also just use it to boost my soups, stews, smoothies, add to breads, healthy muffins, whatever. Whether it is kale, collard greens, spinach, etc. Already love Kale, so I keep an assortment of kale powder and flakes on hand as my local grocery store doesnt always have fresh.

A word on freeze dried flavor- sometimes it taste a bit different than its fresh counterpart. I find sometimes a freeze dried product tastes a little extra sweet or just a little different. Yet once reconstituted it tastes the same as I would expect. Very odd, I dont know what this is, and I have noticed it across the board across the years across the brands. For example, freeze dried broccoli out of the bag tastes like a sweet snack to me. But once added to a dish and reconstituted, it tastes like regular broccoli. This Kale has a hint of dulsi- I think the naturally occurring sodium is amplified. But once added to anything, i just taste.. Kale. If concerned, I would recommend their collard greens or spinach. Those are always as similar to non freeze dried taste. OR find a dehydrated (low low heat moisture extraction).

title: moist, rich, flavorful. Wonky directions, see my notes on it
text:
The directions and nutritional info may be confusing. Allow me to clarify as best I can.

The nutritional info is for the DRY ingredients. It says, "Serving size 1 cup", with three servings per container. That just means that there are three cups of powder per container. You use all of the box (no no need to measure it out) to make a batch of brownies, which says is approximately 20 brownies. That depends on how you cut it, so you do you. I always use an 8"x8" and enjoy at most 8 brownies. That's the norm for me, your portion sizes will vary. So for entire box, not yet having added anything, is approximately 1500 calories in total. Approx 27 grams fiber in total, approx 30 grams protein in total, approx 36 grams fat in total, approx 900 grams sodium in total, and lastly approx 135 grams sugar in total. Says "includes 0g added sugar".

As for sugar, yes and no. A product can have sugar, but not have added sugar. It can have naturally occurring sugar. So if you have an apple, that has X amount of sugar, but no added sugar. With this product, there is an ingredient called PANELA, which is unrefined brown sugar cane. So yes, it has added sugar. It lends a deeper flavor, and also reduces needs for as much sugar like one would white cane. I have to knock them down a little for that. My overall will be 4 stars

As for the visual directions. There is an image of 3 cups that appear to have something inside. Usually we see this as an indication for liquid of some sort. IT IS NOT LIQUID. It represents the use of the powder in this box. There are 3 one cup "servings", and you need the entire box (3 cups) to make this. They could really just streamline it with standard brownie mixes where the entire box is always the norm. To confirm this, later in written portion it makes no mention of liquid. Then, use ONE egg (visual pic shows two so take note. ALSO-- 1 egg will product more gooey fudge like brownies, 2 eggs will produce a more dry result, more "cake like", So use based on your texture preference. They dont mention any of this), or can use egg replacement (ie, 1/4 cup applesauce, 1/4 c banana, or 1/4 pumpkin puree), and then 3/4 cup butter or coconut oil. Mix. Use a 20cm X 20cm pan, which is 8"x8" (what I normally use). 8x8 will produce thicker (obviously) brownies, larger pans thinner, and possibly more dry brownies. Choose wisely, adapt accordingly.

I line my non stick pans with parchment paper. I use a convection toaster oven. Any of the brownie mixes I use typically take closer to 45 minutes preheated. I just check in a couple of times starting at the 30 minute mark. Bakes times for this and any mix will vary depending on your location, type of stove, type of bake ware, even type of ingredients. So simply check in with a toothpick. Easy peasy.

Results: I used unsweetened apple sauce as I did not want to sacrifice an egg. I normally dont for much of my baked goods unless I happen to have too many eggs at the moment. Current egg prices are not conducive to me using in a brownie recipe. Works perfectly fine. I use refined coconut oil (zero coconut taste), as that is cheaper than butter right now. I would normally grab for my unrefined coconut oil to give it a boost of coconut flavor, but I didnt want to mask the flavor of this product since I hadnt had it before.

I love how they turned out. Moist, rich, flavorful.

I think some of the texture will depend on which ingredients were added, and how long it was baked, and how long you give it before cutting in. I find that the non standard brownie recipes do best with slightly shorter cook time, and then eaten the next day. For some reason I like how they taste given a day to sit. But when it comes to traditional brownie recipes/mixes, same day is best-- to me.

I love quinoa and I love their puffed quinoa. So what I did was take them up one of their suggested toppings of adding puffed quinoa on top. I did that on half, and it added a fun texture and appearance.

title: good light taste, not too sweet
text: Bought this on a whim, on sale. I like having a variety of beverages in our extra fridge, and so when I see something that sounds good and is reasonably priced I will just go and and pick it up. I like the flavor. It is light, refreshing, not too sweet. Nice drink to grab on the go, or pour into a cup, load with ice, and go sit outside with. If I dont want to use it all at once, then I can take what I want, cap it off, and put back in fridge. I also have used it to add a little flavor essence to water. I like my water plain, but sometimes a little added flavor is nice too. Options!

title: if you like carob and you like tahini, this blend makes for a nice treat. Apple dip for me!
text:
Those that will appreciate this most are likely already familiar with the taste of carobs and of tahini. I am a huge fan of tahini, so much so that I crave it and will eat it by the spoonful. Carob is special. Popular with those that do not consume chocolate. I like carob for its almost chocolaty taste, semi raisin-esque taste. It lends natural sweetness to whatever it is used in. I have used it as chips or in powder form (for cakes, hot "cocoa" etc), and while I dont use it often it still has a presence in my pantry.

Combined? Makes for a nice treat. When you take the deep sesame flavor of tahini and add the natural sweetness of carob, you have a lightly sweet mild tahini hybrid. Hint of chocolate. I like it. I tend to prefer those two flavors separate, but as a combo it is interesting. Thick and caramel like. Can be spread, or kind of drizzled (drizzles better if warmed). Add to coffee, or smoothies, over oats, just off the spoon, dip fruit, nuts, dates in it. Would likely pair well with a protein too. I havent done anything fancy with it. I like it off the spoon or for dipping my apple slices in.

title: good in lattes, iced or hot. Works well in my smoothies. Ceremonial/Culinary hybrid taste
text: Lower end ceremonial, higher end culinary. Tastes mellow enough for me. It works for my needs, and is at a reasonable price point for what I am used to. I usually dont drink it as tea. It is the one ingredient that I need to bury under other ingredients as matcha is a flavor I just havent come around to. Oddly, I have been drinking it nearly daily for 10+ years. It is all about the concentrated antioxidants and other benefits I seem to glean from it. So I add it to smoothies, or I will make a hot or iced latte. But never just plain tea, ceremonial or culinary. Pretty good overall. Solid 4 stars

title: another good one by Rasa. Lovely coffee vibe, intricate flavors, smooth, Nice hot or iced
text: I had tried another variety by Rasa, and was instantly impressed. Definitely use a French press as it was awkward trying to make it in a pour over, or tea filter. The particles are thick, and absorb a lot of liquid. French press works. It makes for a smooth, delicious cup of "coffee". I am taken by the coffee like vibe it has. It doesnt taste like an alternative or like a tea-- maybe if watered down-- but it other wise has a fully body mouth feel to it. Coffee like, yet not coffee. I can drink it black, I can drink it with cream. I like it hot, and l have enjoyed it iced. Really neat taste, to me.

title: plenty of flavor, but can add to it. Use instead of meat, or use it to stretch meat rations
text: I buy a lot of Augason Farms. Occasionally I receive a mildly dented can, and while not perfect, it doesnt bother me. The contents will be fine so long as the material hasnt been breached, and never have I had an issue. I buy when on sale, and the prices fluctuate wildly so if you are interested in building a supply then I recommend checking the list daily. Maybe add several to cart, then put them to "save to later" so you can see the current price in all in one spot. Or just go to individual pages. Of course, if you need it then get it while you can as there can be some unavailability or the occasional long time shipping (ie "usually ships in 1-2 months"). I like the black bean option as it provides a lot of calories, good amount of sodium, fiber, and protein. If you are suddenly increasing your fiber especially through beans, then you may want to start low and slow as you may experience temporary excess gas or bowel movements. It isnt a reflection of the product or brand. It is more about changing up diet to something you are not used to, in a form you may bot be used to. Soak well, and enjoy. Love the versatility of this product. A good one if you are someone who really needs the meat experience but may not have access (or funds) for it. This can be used to replace meat and still have a meaty vibe (esp if add some meaty seasonings like cumin, or mushroom powder, or soy, or worchestershire sauce, etc). OR can be used to make ground meat stretch, so you get best of both worlds.

title: Get your veggies! good assortment of ingredients, decent amount of calories for sale price,
text:
Weight is as expected. You do know that they use #10 cans as so most emergency suppliers. That means, NUMBER ten, not ten pound. The size is because it allows for continuity in storage, and allows for various volume amounts that also satisfy the weighted amounts (products are sold based on WEIGHT not volume, which means you can have a canister that appears half full, but it has the weight that is being sold). The #10 canisters are also reusable for other needs, and when still fully sealed will float and will take a lot of abuse all while maintaining integrity of the contents. I have not experienced these situations, but that is the idea across all emergency food. Next size up tends to be pails, then buckets, then simply multiples. Be smart.

I buy "emergency food" when it is on sale. That's it. The whole point of prepping is to accumulate well before it is needed. I buy regular food and store it well, and only then do I add in "emergency" food. It is great that it is available, but it is fantastically expensive. Even if you dont do any real food preserving, so long as it is away from light and rats, it all will be fine for a long long time. But added assurance is with emergency branded food, and it takes the knowledge and work out of it. But even then, pay attention to prices and buy when the prices dip low. You can amass more food for your buck that way. If and only if you are in a bind (you were late to the prepping game), then yes by all means get what you can.

This vegetable stew is not something I plan to open any time soon (I dont think). I buy similar dried vegetable assortments and soup blends for a fraction of a price, and just double bag it before I toss it in a dark cupboard, or with more motivation/ambition I could repackage in mylar or an air tight container. They are all the same, more or less. Difference is with the types of vegetables. I like having different brands for this reason. I use it for quick soups (just need enough hot water to rehydrate), for crock pot meals for simply adding vegetables anytime to anything whether I have fresh on hand or not. Since I was able to get this on sale at nearly same price as my non-emergency veg soup/stew products, I decided to pick up a couple of canisters to tuck away. I took a look at the ingredients and liked the assortment of vegetables (inc potato). The calories being purchased looked good too.

My canisters look good, no dents. I would not have been too concerned with mild dents anyway.

title: good ginger taste, pleasantly sweet to me. I like it hot or iced
text: Love ginger "tea". I have the original ginger and honey flavor. Not too sweet, plenty of ginger flavor. I love ginger! This is lovely hot or iced, or added to other teas. I adore the spoon it came with.

title: excellent water cracker for all toppings and smears, be mindful of shipping if that comes up
text: A yes, a classic water cracker. These exceeded my expectation because my boxes came fully intact and the crackers within all look good. Has the minimalist flavor that makes the water cracker great as a vehicle for all sorts of lovely toppings. Light easy snap crunch, plenty of working surface, holds a good smear. Well priced too (pleasantly shocked) for a pack of three. Although be mindful of shipping prices, which could make for an unfortunate price bump (currently not free/nor prime). I wont/dont factor this into my rating. I focus on quality and personal experience/perception. All good on my end.

title: smooth, easy to drink. Could use a little more "coffee" taste, but its still pretty good
text: I prefer a dark roast, extra bold coffee, consumed black, but am amenable to a good medium so long as it isn't bitter or acidic.
