This is very smooth, mild, easy to drink, and I can drink it black. Definitely a medium roast as described. Could use a little more oomph, a little more "coffee' flavor, but overall it's good. My husband drinks medium roast coffee, and usually only drinks Caribu. I let him know this was available to drink, and I noticed that a few of the cups were missing. So it seems to be a win for him.

title: good flavor, super convenient, great over a rice bowl or stuffed into tortilla, even just as is.
text:
I love pouch meals. I dont rely on them on a daily basis, but there are enough options out there that I could if need be. I stack them for convenience, for emergencies, for hiking trips, and for lazy days. I keep an assortment of rice, lentils, beans, and ethnic specific dishes. So cool what can be found in a packet. Truly a campers delight. This Cauliflower Tinga is delightful. Nice flavor, texture. I appreciate that they list the nutritional information for a single serving and for the whole packet. I know I could just do the math, but it is helpful when just wanting to do a quick glance to figure out what I am getting as I have a big appetite and will likely eat the whole thing.

This has a robust hearty taste that satisfies my taste buds. I have enjoyed it as part of a rice bowl, and I have used it tucked into flour tortillas with other fixings.

Sodium for whole packet is "high", but is is comparable to a can of soup. Also, has q goodly amount of potassium to help offset. Would help return electrolytes on sweaty outings. Their other offerings have significantly less. As for other aspects of nutrition, I like this cauliflower tinga as a flavoring more than use as a filling food. This comment is more for those looking to maximize calories for the money, and maximize "nutrient energy" for the weight of the product (preppers, hikers). There is a little protein and fiber in this one--moderate--, and is low calorie, but the best bang for the buck is with their bean options, where fiber and protein go way up (and costs a bit less), and has a good amount of calories for sustained energy. But this paired with extra beans, etc? Yum. Nice option, and flavor options are very important.

I dont rate on price, but it is just a little more than what I look to spend for a pouch of this size. Again, I keep a stacked pantry of foods like this, with prices in the $2-4 range. Though these days it is harder to find pouches in the lower range. I like this well enough, and would consider this again and anything else by this company.

title: mild, hint of sweet, good portion, eat as is or add in whatever you want, convenient
text:
I love noodles of all sorts, and I keep a wide assortment in my pantry. Then a portion of my pantry has a dedicated ramen area, including all sorts of fancy raman cups. This style is not the twenty cent packs. These tend to have a much more complex flavor, interesting textures, and still with all the ease of convenience. I almost always add stuff to them, not eat them alone. So with this jjanjang, I added some sliced soft boiled egg, pork slices, and chives. Sometimes I toss any vegetables I have on hand as well. Sometimes I add extra water to make it more brothy, or I use less for a thicker sauce like experience. This is not spicy, in fact it has a hint of sweet. Easy enough to spice it up a bit with hot herbs or sauces. Can be stretched with plain ramen.

I dont ratae on price, but I do comment. $5 is usually the max I pay for my "noodle experience", but this isnt too far outside the realm of reasonable, especially given the price increases all over. But at $7.50 pr cup, I am likely to shop around. I did enjoy these, and would circle back around to this if price is right (for my budget).

title: convenient packets, good on the go, and also good option if have no power, limited space
text: So far so good. Bought a couple of boxes to keep in my longer term storage. The packets should maintain freshness for some time, and I figured if power is out or if fridge space is limited, having the option to just use what I need will be preferable over keeping a large container fresh. Tuck into homemade MRE's. I also like the packets for on the go use, for packing into lunches alongside a sandwich, etc. Always been a fan of Hellmans, so I went with this brand over some of the cheaper brands because I wanted to make sure I got what I really enjoy.

title: 7 grams of protein per Tablespoon, neutral taste & texture, another high quality Judees product
text:
I am SO STOKED to try this. I have been curious about cricket flour for many years, but never went out of my way to try it. It isnt a new thing, but it is an emerging thing. Some conspiracy theorists are mad about bug products (Big Bug is taking away their Big Beef), and I think it is hilarious. Again, making use of bugs as a protein source is not new, and specifically the use of cricket is the most common presented for use in USA. I remember watching programs on how the crickets are processed and such. I was always like, I would try it.. why not? I will try anything. Even better if I can tell what it is, haha.

SO, this is just finely ground crickets. Not legs and eyeballs. And I JUMPED (hahaha) on the opportunity to try it as it is from JUDEES. I totally love and trust Judees products, have lots of Judees products in rotation, and it just seemed so fitting to try something I have been curious about by a company I really like. It was a no brainer for me. Doubt I would have tried it from another company I wasnt so familiar with.

However, my husband does not share my enthusiasm. I was so stinkin proud to hold up my bag of cricket flour. He's like, "that's all you". I'm like, really.. you dont want some CRICKET BISCUITS? Cricket pancakes? cricket waffles? cricket coated chicken cutlets? cricket cookies? yeesh. He said he'd try it.

I dont intend to have cricket flour as a mainstay, but to work it in, especially if in need of some really good protein? YES. 7 grams PER TABLESPOON! That's impressive!

As for shellfish.. they are being extra precautious in the allergy warning. Good on them. Crickets are related to shellfish, or maybe it is the other way around. When people joke about shrimp and such as being the bugs of the ocean, they aren't wrong.

I took the easy way out and tried it in a smoothie. For real, it doesnt have a taste or a look. I also made a small batch of my basic ultra cheap frugal level (prepping for depression era living) "lentil burgers", where it is just smashed up lentils, seasonings, and enough flour to make it hold together. Then once formed in patties, fry or bake. Add toppings of choice. Guess what? Now I have me a LENTIL & CRICKET burger recipe. omg.. lol.. I am giddy.

I do not rate on price. If you are familiar with my reviews, I nearly always mention that. We all have different budgets, needs, preferences, interests, prices fluctuate, etc. For me, if I am going to eat bugs, I am going with a company I trust, and this 1.5 lbs of cricket flour is pricy but worthwhile for me. I know I will use it up. They also have a tiny packet that can be purchased for those just wanting to try it out but not ready to commit to a larger bag.

It probably won't be popular anytime soon, but if you want a good quality product from a very good company, you cant beat Judees.

title: hint of flavor, lightly sweet from honey, no caffeine, no artificial sweeteners, pretty good!
text:
I like the taste. Low calories, lightly sweet from honey, not from artificial sweeteners. I love that. Has some D3 and zinc, which has been nice while I have been sick. No caffeine, so it makes it nice to enjoy any time day or night. I am a huge fan of carbonation, and this is really nice in the afternoon. I dont rate on price, but it is on the higher end for me. I would get this if it had a coupon, or was on sale.

Would like a little more flavor, but maybe my tastebuds are still broken. Even so, I like it, and it is lovely ice cold on a hot day

title: Non jittery energy that tastes good, if you like pina coladas!
text:
I like it, has a light coconut taste with hint of pineapple. Definitely a pina colada vibe. I tried this under a couple of circumstances. It took me awhile to getting around to writing the review because when I first tried this I was sick. I had zero taste and zero smell. I was quite tired, so I gave this a try anyway despite having no ability to taste. I could feel a light lift. Normally I dont do energy drinks unless I plan to be up and moving. But I was feeling so dragged down that I figured it would be worth the try. Oddly, the pep it gave me allowed me to get up and move around for awhile- get some basic chores done, take a shower, etc.. felt good to get something accomplished while ill. Then the next couple of times I had some were while I was still convalescing, but I could taste and smell again. Nice bit of fizz, excellent icy cold, not too sweet (to me), and gave me the light energy boost to carry out several tasks.

Non jittery energy that tastes good, if you like pina coladas!

Currently there is a coupon, and I am thinking of getting more.

title: beans, rice, and spam. Trifecta of survival food, haha. Pretty good, and versatile
text:
Pork with ham and mechanically separated chicken parts (and other flavorings, preservatives). The usual stuff these canned meats are made with. Just a little less sodium. I dont eat this, like ever (ok rarely), but I have no problem with it. I keep it on hand as an ultra convenience food item, and just as a food item period. Long shelf life (acquired 05/2022, and has 2025 date on it). Keep in mind shelf life is not an indication of safety (check out gov websites), but a matter of quality. It just means that if stored well it should maintain same level of quality as day one, after that there may be decline. But it is still good so long as can has not been breached.

Try it out in different ways. Frying is nice, or cubing up and adding to whatever is on hand. If you are using it as a food prep/food insurance item, then I imagine it wont matter what you do with it so long as you have it if needed. But it can sure add a lot of flavor to a casserole or one pot meal. If the price is right, go for it. Doesnt matter if it is low sodium or not, if it is being used in a more precarious situation when the added salt will be used up easily.

All my cans look great, no dents. Well packaged. I have them tucked away for future (likely near future use).

title: Eggs are gold these days, so a little chia can replace wasting eggs in recipes
text:
I love Judees products, and always recommend them. . I go through a lot of Chia seeds. I add it to smoothies nearly daily, and I use it as an egg free binder-- I am not vegan, or have any egg issues, but I like having the ability to not waste eggs in some recipes. Especially now with egg prices and issues.

Love chia seeds in homemade trail bars too, or snack balls. There is a neat taste and texture that I enjoy from Chia.

title: Tasty assortment of high quality olives, jumbo size, firm texture (Kals are softer), just SO GOOD
text:
Excellent quality olives. Firm, good size, flavorful. I love olives, all sorts, stuffed or seasoned. I just love olives. I usually just snack on them, and that is primarily what I have done with these. I use a fork to grab one, or a few. Really hits the spot, perfect for noshing or filling the void before a meal. Refrigerate after opening. These will also work on my "cheese and cracker" dinners, where I load up a cute tray with cheeses, some sliced meats, and my beloved olives.

6 bags, two of each flavor. Currently $29.99 ($2.50 per ounce). Pricier than many, but quality is way up there. I do not rate on price (prices fluctuate, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, and we can see the price before purchase. No mystery)

I am not super picky when it comes to olives, but these are above and beyond the usual quality I get. I'd probably give cruddy olives 4 stars, haha just because I love all olives, so definitely 5 stars here for me.

Casual looking bags, but luxury taste.

title: convenient, tasty, nice for on the go, or as a quick snack, simple lunch, etc
text: Nice pick-me-up. Simple ingredients, lightly sweet, good texture and chew. I keep a wide assortment of KIND bars stuffed into the kitchen snack basket. We often grab a Kind bar before heading out the door. I often dont bother with a lunch, so I keep some bars within reach. Usually when paired with a sliced apple I am good to go until dinner.

title: Beyond perfection! Has FLAVOR, texture, so easy to make, great nutritional profile
text:
Oh wow, I think this MEALET is amazing. It has become my most favorite food. It has everything I want, and seems really thoughtfully put together. Lovely assortment of grain, vegetables, and spices. I had taken the chance and bought 4 boxes (different flavors, including the variety pack), and they are all SO GOOD. I really love the Mediterranean. It has good FLAVOR and some SPICE. But not a building hot. Just a pleasant warmth. Really hits the spot. LOve em all.

JUST LOOK at the ingredient list! NUTRITIONAL GOLD! I love that it isnt loaded with sodium (JUST 5 mg?!!!). Great fiber (13 grams!!) and protein! (11 grams!)

As for rehydration.. I see a lot of negative comments. Have ya'll ever worked with dehydrated food? It doesnt always 100% soften up. I actually love this as it adds good texture. I wouldnt change a thing. I feel like I have eaten something, and therefore feel satisfied. Best bet it to use BOILING water, and then cover well (use plastic wrap), then allow to sit for 10 full minutes. Not soft enough? Then put in microwave for a minute or two. Be sure there is enough water. I use a little over a cup as I know that the grains will soak it up anyway. Can add even more if you want more of a broth style.

Comes packed in a small cube box. Then inside there are perfect little packets with all the info you need. If you are a camper, hiker, even traveler with access to a water kettle, this is an amazing option for good, nutritious calories that pack lightly. Long trail hikers-- you know what I mean. You want light weight nutrient dense calories. I am pretty sure this is something you will want to check out.

Now, I sure hope they get more in. At time of writing this review, they were out or had a long lead time in when it could be shipped.

$10 for 5 "mealet" packs. I can get some similar ish items for around $2 a pack, but a lot of that stuff is more processed, has a lot more sodium, and is not as healthy tastting/feeling. I could eat this every single day.. The appeal of this to me is the robust seasoning, the variety of vegetables, and how well it is packed. I love the little cube box (takes up very little room in my pantry), and I love the look of the packets- small, compact, and can tucked away anywhere. Nutritional gold!

title: mix with powdered sugar and get creative!
text: I've used this royal icing before. It is a pack of two (packaged together), and just needs the additon of powdered sugar. The flavor is vanilla. It works well. It is for making baked goods take on a more professional appearance. Gives that firm light sheen. Not my "go to" for frosting anything, but when I am feeling creative and want to spend time decorating sugar cookies (this is the only thing I use royal icing on. Great for other stuff too), a royal icing is the way to go. Pre-fab has been better for me over trying to figure out ratio of ingredients for DIY. Can be pricy, but can be worth it if you want to assure a good looking, easy to work with royal icing. Follow directions, but it is pretty much just add your own powdered sugar. And colorings, sprinkles, other edible decorations. And have fun!

title: just jalapeno pepper, flavorful, adds kick of heat, not too hot, just right for most applications
text: My new pantry must-have. This is just jalapeno pepper, granulated. I use fresh, but this is even better when I am looking for consistent flavoring--and the flavor comes through. Not too hot, not too mild. I can taste it, and it is easy to work with. 1 lb is a really good size, which will last me awhile. I'm a long time user of Judee's products, and have always been pleased with what I have used. I can add this to the list. I think I have no less than a dozen of Judees products in my pantry at any given time.

title: love taste and texture of Oats n Honey
text: I really like the Oats n Honey. It has a chew. Not as dry as Nature Trail granola bar.  But not quite as moist as some chewy bars. Somewhere in between in a good way. I like the taste and texture a lot. Not too sweet. Has a candy bar vibe yet isnt candy. Easy to eat on the go, nice paired with cup of coffee. I have even broken it up and sprinkled it over yogurt and fruit.

title: nice addition to grain pantry, good chew, flavor, nutrition
text:
My review is for the grain. I use it as one would in any application a grain is used. Nice to have an assortment on hand for various tastes, textures, nutrition. I have not tried it popped, as I got this for cooking and adding to stews, soups, and other hot dishes. It has a good flavor at room temp too. I like Anthony's products a lot, and this does not disappoint.

I normally dont eat popcorn, but maybe I will give this a try. If I do, I will report back my experience.

title: just black tea, extra nice for Boba tea base
text: Use 8 ounces water to 1/2tsp tea, adjust according to taste. It is a powder tea, an instant tea, no brewing required. I can brew a tea bag or I can grab a spoonful of instant. I will find myself grabbing for instant nearly 10/10 times, so long as it tastes like tea. This tastes like black tea.  I REALLY like it for BOBBA/Bubble tea. I also gave the recipe on back of package a try because I happen to have lemon powder and freeze dried strawberry powder on hand. Not my go to style of tea drink, but it was pleasant enough that I see myself making a pitcher on a hot afternoon. LOve Judees brand, always a quality product. Pleased with this.

title: summertime flavor, add to drinks, smoothies, iced matcha, anywhere you like Pina Colada!
text:
I have a slew of Skinny syrups. I prefer the keto version (not because it is "keto" but because the sweetener used is better), but I still buy and use the other regular versions, like this. And this is different than their usual syrups because it considered a mixer, and this uses sufar--just less than other mixers.

I love this Pina Colada for adding bit of flavor to smoothies. Often I make tasty smoothies, but sometimes they need a little help. I will use their banana, strawberry, or peach syrups. Now I have pina colada. I especially like it when I need a stronger flavor to mask a flavor profile. Such as when I make a smoothie or latte using Matcha green tea powder. I always use too much matcha which makes it taste too strong, but if I tone it down with a syrup that can mask that flavor a bit, all the better. I imagine it is great for skinny cocktails too.

I didnt realize I ordered a 32 ounce bottle, normally the bottles are 25 ounces. This is great! I am sure pina colada will be used a lot this summer. Perfect summer flavor!

title: best mixed fruit, could use more cherries, but it is still a tasty mix
text:
Bought this May 2022 with best by date of Nov 2022. Pretty good as this type of packaging isnt meant for super long term storage. For that, you want cans. However, the benefit of the cups is that I can grab one as I want, and not have extra left over. Good on the go, too. No waste (as I am prone to forgetting that I opened a can). Fruit cocktail is not something I normally care for, but the price was right and the mix of fruit seemed like a good addition to my pantry.

This mixed fruit is probably the best I have had. Fruit has good texture, good taste, and is packed in juice (not sugar, or sweetener alternative). Just so much better than the fruit cocktail of my youth. I am now a convert.

I also like their peaches and any other fruit offering so long as it is in real juice.

My box was totally intact, cups are in perfect condition, and nothing looks off, nothing tastes off. ALL good.

title: pleasant basic hot cocoa, creamy & sweet, comfort drink
text: I like it. Nice for making a quick mug of hot cocoa. I make it depending on what I am feeling like. Sometimes I make it with water, sometimes non dairy milk, sometimes I add a splash of vanilla or cayenne pepper, sometimes I boost the choco flavor with a little extra plain cacao. Sometimes hot, sometimes over ice. Somtimes add in some coffee. Whatever, sky is the limit. Just a nice product, at a reasonable price ((less than $6 for 50 oackets at time of review 05/2022). Has a 2024 best by date.

title: quality non fat powdered milk, pantry staple, excellent in baking
text: 16 ounces of non fat milk powder is the perfect size for me. I really dont go through much, and as much as I can save per ounce by going larger, the smaller size is going to keep longer. Even though I dont use it often, I always keep some on hand (several smaller bags like this), as it makes a great emergency item. Also some recipes call for milk. I really only keep non dairy milk, so having powder to make up some milk for recipes is super idea. This  mixes easily into water; adjust according to preference.

title: pantry staple, health up some soups, smoothies, home made pastas, add to sauces too
text: Adding a variety of dried vegetable and fruit powders to my pantry in case some fresh stuff becomes increasingly harder to attain. I also use it for adding to soups, smoothies, home made pasta dough, etc. I hadn't really worked with kale powder before, and it is a nice change up over my usual spinach powder. I prefer fresh when possible, but some applications are better suited with dehydrated. I like this.

title: comfort food/snack, pantry staple, easy to make, eat hot or cold
text:
Spaghettios with meatballs. This isnt exactly good food, but it is just one of those things I get a hankering for on occasion, and so I grab a few cans here and there. I nearly always regret it, haha. But boy it hits the spot, especially when paired with some buttered toast. Yum! Ive never purchased 12 at once, but with supply chain issues and other world events, I just want to m ake sure I have a few extra easy to make items in my pantry.

The 12 count case was a good deal for $12. Prices are going up, and cans of this size are normally closer to $1.20, give or take. I was able to get some on sale at a store recently for $1 per can, so this current case price is quite reasonable. Their original price at $30 lmao.. no. Spaghettios can be found at nearly every single store, and none charge more than $1.70 for a can.

Anway, my cans look good, and have a decent lead up time before so called best by date. These are great tuck away for emergencies style of food. Can be eaten hot or at room temp.

title: long term storage, insurance for future needs at todays prices
text: Container arrived in good condition. I have no intention of opening it any time soon; hopefully no need to open it anyway. Buy food now, folks. I buy Augason Farms when it is on sale, then I add it to my long term storage. I wouldnt buy at full price if I was only planning on using it for camping next weekend, ya know? I have this as insurance, and buying when on sale just adds more bang to my buck.

title: great little assortment, tasty, natural, good for snack or mini meal
text:
Nice assortment of KIND bars. I prefer the ones with a little chocolate drizzle, but I can say I pretty much like anything by Kind. I usually just buy when on sale. I keep a snack bar basket on my counter for anyone to grab a quick snack or mini meal. Great on the go, and usually will slice up an apple to have a long with it. Let me tell you, I am a big eater and the combo of both holds me all day.

I like that Kind products have a simple natural taste. I never feel bad/gross from eating anything by this brand. The variety box is great for exactly that- a little bit of a few different options.

title: tasty sweetener that works well in baked goods, hot oats, smoothies
text: Love Anthony's products. Love their date sugar. Their date sugar is not full of sand, lmao. I assume the person who said that isnt familiar with date sugar. It works best in baked goods, smoothies, or a bowl of oats as it takes longer to dissolve compared to cane sugar. So because of that, normally wouldnt use this in coffee/tea/cold liquids.

title: must have ingredient for all sorts of cooking, pantry staple, lasts good long time
text: Good price, good garlic. Go through enough to prefer a larger container like this. I keep it in the fridge once opened, and it should last a very long time. I have never had garlic go bad. Unlike fresh, which I tend to buy and forget about, haha.

title: good texture, taste. Nice snack or mini meal, regular repurchase for us
text: Light, natural taste. Mild chew. Works well as easy snack or quick mini meal. I keep a basket of snack bars for easy grab. Got lots of different KIND bars because they are the not fake tasting. I just like the simple ingredients and overall flavor. My husband seems especially keen on these peanut butter bars. I tend to see that spot empty out quickly, so I keep buying more. I like them too, but he is the one to devour these many times over.

title: love lentils, love Goya products, packed to brim with lentils. Good stuff
text: My cans are in excellent condition. I love lentils, and eat them as often as possible. I add them to everything, I make burgers with them, or I add them to stretch ground meat, soups, salads, and so on and so on. I usually just make them from a bag as lentils cook up real quick. Save a lot over buying canned. But I wanted some canned to round out my pantry, especially in case of emergency. But really for added convenience. I have to say, I am only getting canned lentils because they are from Goya. I find that Goya tends to pack their cans to the brim, without much left over liquid. Other brands (for beans, lentils) will be same weight, but there is a lot of liquid. Not with Goya.

title: pantry staple, good emergency food, comfort food, lasts forever
text: Just one of those odd comfort foods. I dont eat a lot of Chef Boyardee, but sometimes it is exactly what I want. I love it paired with some buttered toast. When I can get it for $1 or less per can, then I add a few to my pantry. They will last a long long time just sitting. Makes for a great emergency food too, in that there is no preparation needed. Can eat directly out of can if need be, or warm up over a tea light.

title: east to make, good flavor, versatile, good size. Excellent pantry staple
text:
Easy to make, good flavor, versatile, good size. Excellent pantry staple.

I like any of the packets of mashed potatoes. I may make mashed potatoes I keep mashed potato packets on hand because sometimes I just want a little mashed potato and dont want all the fuss, time, and expense of using regular potatoes. Also, I can never bring myself to waste potato skins, so usually I end up making "smashed potatoes". Having the packet version on hand just makes it all around easier for me. I also rarely bother with buying big boxes of dehydrated potatoes because I just dont go through enough. The packets are going to stay fresher longer.

While they recommend using butter, milk.. they can be made simply with water. Good if you are being extra careful with your budget.

title: pleasant taste, best for minor irritations, not for true coughing from cold
text:
Pleasant tasting lozenge for minor throat irritations. I dont talk much, so when I do engage in conversation for any length of time, my throat can get real scratchy. I grab for a non medicated lozenge like this Manuka Health Honey & Lemon to help alleviate the scratchiness. Does it work for a cough, like that associated with a burgeoning cold? No, not at all. I happened to receive this the day that a cough developed. It barely touched my cough. So I had to switch the gross true "cough drops" (non mentholated), as only that worked. All told, I tend to go through more throat lozenges like this as I rarely get colds. I like that it has some honey in it, tastes nice, seems to dissolve a bit quickly but that could just be me.

In short: Use this for basic scratchy throat, may not touch a true cough, but could be used in between coughing fits. I will use this today when my throat needs a break from the real cough drops, but still want to keep throat soothed. It has its place. If the price looks good to you then it may be worth the try.

Individually wrapped lozenges in small box. Nice size for tucking into purse, or desk, etc.

title: 5 stars for smoothness and freshness; comes with metal clamp/clip
text:
Smooth coffee. Highlander Grogs are not my go to coffee, but I certainly enjoy a cuppa on occasion. It is the one time I prefer my coffee with cream as it seems to round out the notes of rum and butterscotch. I dont need it sweetened. I am particularly impressed with how smooth and fresh this coffee tastes. I bag is well sealed, and comes with a very sturdy little jaw clamp to help keep it closed.

Makes for a nice treat coffee, or added to a coffee themed gift.

title: light natural taste, good snack or mini meal (esp when paired with some fruit). I like it
text: Pretty good, very light natural taste. Feel like I am eating something good for myself, haha. I usually prefer the ones with some chocolate, but this makes for a pleasant snack- fill the belly until dinner, or as a ultra quick lunch. I pair it with a sliced apple and i am good to go for most of the day.

title: really good brand, fresh, tasty addition to pantry.
text: Love quinoa of all colors. I wanted to get some darker colors to amp up the nutrition profile. When I searched for red quinoa, and black quinoa, and multi colored quinoa, this Food to Live brand came up for all of it. Since I already really like this brand, I just went and got all that I wanted at once. Makes great addition to all meals, and again the added color is a little more nutrition than the beige. But i use plenty of that too. I just like options. Good stuff.

title: fresh, well packed, very healthy grain
text: Good. Well packed, decent shelf life, makes nice addition to my grain options. Very healthy!

title: Oh WOW this is actually really good, even at room temp
text:
I want more of this but the price keeps bumping up. Maybe I will buy more when/if the price goes back to when I bought it ($60 something, now $80/90 something in a matter of a week). But since I dont rate on price, and I know everyone has their own budget, needs, etc, I will focus on my perception of quality, etc. See if it jives with what you are looking for.

I think it is spectacular. I did not expect this to be all that good. I got it because I keep an assortment of canned meats tucked into my pantry for convenience, or more so lately-- lack of food choices in store, or super pricey options. I usually stack chicken, tuna, salmon, ham, but was looking for a beef option. I did buy a few cans here and there of other brands, but when I saw this case (and thought the price reasonable), I went for it. Glad I did. I truly think this is some tasty stuff.

The cans are dense, and jam packed. I dont hear sloshing when I shake it. I open the can, and it is full to the brim with big chunks of roast beef, The texture is roast beef. The experience is clearly roast beef. There is some gravy which I think also has a nice flavor. They didnt cheap out, I feel like it has a very good ratio of beef to gravy. Here is the crazy thing, it actually tastes good at room temperature. All of it. I had opened it to take a peek, and decided to try some on the spot. I found it so tasty that it was kind of hard to stop myself. Extra amazing heated up.

So yeh, I think it is really good. And not just really good for a canned meat product. I think it is just really good.

Acquired 05/2022 with best by date of 03/2024

title: super fine freeze dried celery powder for use in anything, little goes long way
text: Nice addition to pantry for convenience. I try to use fresh celery more often than not, or I use my own dehydrated celery (slices). I dont often have a need for celery powder, but lately I have been stacking my extended pantry with extra long shelf life items. I'm looking for anything green. I have their collard greens which is great, and now this celery powder which is really wquite nice. All so pricy, but these days isnt everything? 1 tsp = 1/3 cup celery. That means when I am cooking with this, I will add 2-3 tsp to a big pot of soup, more or less. If I want extra boost of flavor, then I use dried celery seed powder. Freeze dried is different in that it brings out natural sweetness of a whole food product. Fine powder, a little seems to go a long way.

title: great blend by quality company. Will buy again
text:
I absolutely adore Food To Live products. I enjoy all sorts of grains and seeds, and this is one of many varieties that I keep on hand. I keep rice, millet, quinoa, lentils, freeka, sorghum, barley, lentils, wild rice, spelt, buckwheat, couscous, etc etc etc in my pantry. Variety of brands, but I can say that Food To Live is one I can rely on for quality. In fact, my most recent order included 3-4 other bags of various stuff. I like their dehydrated fruits and other offerings.

This is primarily a SEED blend, as millet and quinoa are technically seeds. But thats just being technical. It is always used as one would a grain. Adding in buckwheat is pretty neat, as I dont get enough of that in my diet. I love making up a batch, then pulling from it all week long for various meals. Whether it be a quick soup (just add some to broth, and whatever else in my fridge), adding to meatloaf/mealballs, adding to a bowl of veggies, etc. All good, YUM.

title: adds fiber and flavor, nice change up from wheat flour
text: Lovely flour blend. I use regular wheat flour for most baking needs, but I like other flours to health up other items. My two main used for this is to add to broths. I make simple quick soups--super simple and quick-- as in, I take a peek in my fridge, pull out some left over or other bits of food, warm up, add broth of choice, warm up some more, then I like to add a healthy "flour" to kind of thicken it up. Gives me a creamy vibe, or like a pot pie vibe. This has 3 grams of fiber per 2 tbs serving, which is comparable to my beloved [[ASIN:B09B64FJ3X Slimovina flour]] (15 grams per 1/2 cup) so makes it a nice alternative. It also works well for dredging. And, my newest quick recipe is to make ultra cheap lentil burgers. I was using regular flour to keep the price way down, but I also want to have option that is a bit more healthy. Loving this flour for that. Basically I take cooked lentils, and slightly mash them. Add seasonings (something beefy and/or umami is best), and then enough flour to make them hold together when formed into patties. Then bake or fry. Yum!

title: Robusta beans have more caffeine zing
text:
So... Slow Ride has been rebranded to Everly? I actually buy Slow Ride, and like it a lot. It takes me awhile to go through the 30 pack, so I still have some left from my latest box. I didnt expect it to be the exact same thing. Seeing the brand, "Everly" threw me off.

It uses ROBUSTA beans, which lends greater zip as robusta beans can a bit more caffeine than arabica. I happen to like it. It is better than some, but if I use too much, I find it can get a little bitter. I find it better to use a little more water than I normally do for instants. I just really like it, and while I normally need a little cream in my instant coffee, I can drink this black no problem. Which is great because I prefer my coffee black.

title: lightly spicy, little more zing than their mild version. Convenient pantry item
text: I like it. I have a couple boxes of their mild, and then I bought this box of hot. Like the mild, it has a good curry smell, a slightly spicy curry taste. Has a hint of sweetness, and is definitely salty. Decent portion for all the flavor it adds to rice or other vegetables. I really dont mind it as a convenience item. I tend to overstock my pantry in case of bad weather, illness, laziness, pandemics, WW3, food shortage, hyper-inflation. LOL. With this, it takes up little room, adds some good flavor to whatever I pair it with, and if need be it can consumed direct from pack (though it is best over something, or with something). It doesn't replace going to a restaurant or home made, just like Spaghettioos dont replace an Italian restaurant or homemade pasta, but its a convenience item that has its place in my life. I like it, its tasty enough, and I would buy more.

title: JUST freeze dried collard greens powder, little goes long way, add to whatever-- I like in broth
text:
freeze dried collard greens powder--that's it! NOTHING else added to it. It's food, in powdered form. I already use an assortment of freeze dried whole foods powders. Primarily fruits, and lately I have been adding freeze dried vegetable powders to my pantry. I want to make sure I have a good supply of nutrition at all times..because these times are precarious..
I find the powders easy to work with as I can add it to smoothies, simple broths, or wherever else I want. Though I mainly add it to homemade soups if I dont have collard greens, turnip greens, kale, or spinach on hand. Since it is a powder, a little goes a long way. Taste wise, it is mostly neutral with a hint of sweet. I tend to think freeze dried green vegetables to have a little sweet come through. Dehyrdated (non freeze) tend to taste more like the the fruit or veg. I do love freeze dried items as they really dont go bad, and the nutrition is retained.

title: tasty cans of peaches, no dents, arrived quickly, nice texture
text:
My cans of peaches arrived quickly and in great condition. They are packed in heavy syrup, which I knew before ordering and dont mind at all. When it comes to the liquid it sits in, I will often buy in heavy syrup (or light) because it is cheaper than 100% juice. I just rinse if I dont want the sugary cling. Sometimes I save the syrup for use in baked goods (use as part of the sweetener and as some liquid).

I have no idea what the difference is in these freestone peaches versus other peaches. There is a slight difference in appearance-- i can see where the pit had been. They are both firm and soft at same time. Some are more soft than others, some are larger pieces than others. I opened up a can to try and couldnt stop eating. I like these just fine!

title: fiber loaded sweet puree, just organic butternut squash, add to soups, pasta, smoothies, eat plain
text:
Love this brand, I am totally in love with their pumpkin (can eat direct from can, they use an extra sweet tasting pumpkin it seems), and so when I was looking to add squash to my pantry I went directly to this company. A bit pricy, but I wanted something I knew I would enjoy. I like it warmed up paired with other veggies, I like using it as a "sauce" for pasta, or adding it into soups (for added fiber, nutrients), as the star of the soup (ie squash soup), or even added to chili. LOVE with lentils. I have used it to bulk up my smoothies with fiber. I have added a little to oats. Basically use it same way as pumpkin. Light, sweet taste. Is it a replacement for cooking up some fresh winter squash (in this instance, butternut squash)? No. Just as canned green beans aren't the same as from the garden green beans. But they have their purpose (and not a fair comparison). Is it good as a convenience item (and healthy item to add to other foods stuffs)? YES. It is better or same as frozen bricks? yes/maybe. That's personal taste preference. I find this brand much easier to eat, has a smoother taste and naturally more sweet. I will grab for this many times over before the bricks (and I like the bricks ok enough).

Looking at some of the reviews, I want to add:
--It's a puree, folks. Butternut puree. That means its smooth. Nothing added.
--also, Its ORGANIC.
--Packed in BPA free can.
--A dented can isnt dangerous. Govt sites, and food sites will say this. Only one to be concerned over is tomatoes, and only if can appears breached. A little dent is fine, but better to use it sooner over later. But you do you. Overall, I prefer non dented cans and would easily down rate based on that. Mine are all fine, thankfully
-- best to sort reviews by "most recent" as that will give you more relevant info on the batch you are getting. Reading something from 2018, and it is mid 2022? Likely irrelevant.
--I personally dont taste the can. I am actually sitting here shoveling some into my mouth direct from can. It tastes like butternut squash.
--Acquired 04/2022 with expiry date of 01/2023. A lot of products a little short on best by dates. However this is reasonable, and I will likely have gone through this well before then. Also, stuff lasts in cans way longer than a date stamped on it.

title: pretty decent for a canned chili, nice over hot dogs, chips, potatoes, etc
text:
All my cans look good, has some decent flavor. Some spice but not hot hot. Can be eaten as is, or use it to flavor up other chili base, or use over rice, pasta, chips, etc. I normally dont just buy canned chili as use as a chili. For that, I prefer to make my own. But I would add this into a homemade chili if need be. And I would use it on just about anything else. So yeh, pretty good on its own or over other stuff. But that's just me. Your experience may vary.. so take reviews as just that. I would look for comments pertaining to quality-- dented cans, weird taste beyond realm of reasonable, if anything looks off, etc. A simple "yuk" or "yum" is just an opinion. That being said, I find this to be "yum". haha

Basically.. it is a good addition to long term pantry/emergency food. Has good amount of protein, fiber per serving. 2 servings per can, loaded with sodium as to be expected. Lends to a long shelf life. Not too shabby a price. I do not rate on price as I can clearly see the price before purchase. It isnt a mystery. Also, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, there are price fluctuations, price and demand, availability etc. So, if price looks good to you, then go for it. As of 04/2022, Currently around $25, or $22 if doing subscribe and save. I think stuff like this around $2 a can (especially with rising prices) is a fair deal. You do you.

Generous 5 stars as it pretty much meets my expectations all around

title: good mellow smooth ceremonial matcha
text:
I rate based on quality and overall experience, not on price. Prices fluctuate, we all have different budgets, needs, preferences, etc. But I comment, and I do think it is pricy per ounce even for ceremonial grade as there are very good ceremonial grades that are less per ounce. That being said, this is perfectly good ceremonial grade matcha. It's good, I have had better. 1 ounce can last awhile if abiding by 1tsp serving. Many ceremonial grades I purchase are in the 1-2 ounce range. Usually in tiny tubs like this. The difference here is the art work. It might make for a nice gift if the recipient is into this sort of look. I like the peel back protective lid.

I agree that ceremonial grade is nicer for lattes, teas, and other drinks where you dont want the grassy astringent flavor of culinary to poke through. Need less masking ingredients to enjoy. I use both, but yeh when I use culinary I have to add a bit of other ingredients to make a good drink. I go with what I can afford, and more often than not it is culinary. But once in awhile I am able to get a ceremonial, and all said this is a good one.

title: mix with powdered sugar and get creative
text:
For making baked goods take on a more professional appearance. Gives that firm light sheen. Not my go to for frosting anything, but when I am feeling creative and want to spend time decorating sugar cookies (this is the only thing I use royal icing on. Great for other stuff too), a royal icing is the way to go. Pre-fab has been better for me over trying to figure out ratio of ingredients for DIY. Can be pricy, but can be worth it if you want to assure a good looking, easy to work with royal icing. Just add your own powdered sugar. And colorings, sprinkles, other edible decorations. And have fun!

PS flavor is vanilla

title: pantry staple, nice option for any grain/seed dish.
text: Love millet, it isnt my go-to grain/seed as it doesnt have much fiber compared with other real grain options, but this is nice to circulate in my cooking. I enjoy all sorts of seeds and grains, and incorporate them whenever I can. I just use whatever grain (or seed) based on whim as so many are interchangeable. I often buy Bobs Red Mill products as the quality is always on point. I tend to buy more than what I need at any given time, but I am fine with that. All told I have never had anything go bad before "expiration date", nor long long long time after. Only stabilized rice bran (any brand) goes bad easily, but all else.. just store well and it will last a long time on shelf. This pack of 4 will last me a good long time. Yum yum

title: easy to use, way more convenient than single serve tear off packs, so versatile
text:
Brilliant. I love these squeeze containers of peanut butter. What I like is that I can take what I want and cap it off. Just has a twist off cap. Works really well for on the go snacks and lunches. I used to buy the single serve packets, but often I just wanted a smidge and not the whole thing. SO I either wouldnt use it, or I would use some and forget about the rest (waste), or I wold gobble it all up so as not to waste. THIS allows me to decide how much I want to use. I just need to be careful to not use the entire packet as it contains 5-6 servings (I think). Also, I can easily just squeeze some into my mouth while driving. Way easier than a tear off packet.

Just knead/massage the packet a little before dispensing.

GREAT for keeping in purse, bag, car, desk drawer, emergency food, on the go snack, etc etc.

title: good wholesome taste, convenient, but also good as healthy snack or dessert
text:
I happen to use mushrooms often, and I dont mind seeing it added to products. This uses cordyceps. This also includes maca, which I normally avoid as a regular supplement. Yet I find it fine as an occasional part of my breakfast or snack. I like their coconut oats, and I also like this maple option. I like it as a quick easy breakfast, as a healthy snack, or even as a healthy dessert. Has added sugar, but doesnt taste too sweet.

I dont rate on price, I can see the price before ordering. Prices fluctuate, everyone has different budgets, and so on. But I will comment. $2.99 per cup is competitive with other brands using ingredients of this ilk. Other than that, I focus on my experience and perception of quality. I have enjoyed this brand a lot, and I like it better than brand name oat cups that try to be "healthy". This seems to be pretty healthy (even with prop 65 warning). I dont intend to eat it every day, but I do like having it on hand as a quick meal, or as a tasty healthy snack/dessert. I'd buy it again.

title: not my daily oats, but incredible for healthy convenient oats, healthy snack/brekky/dessert
text:
Smells and tastes exactly as I imagined it would. Lovely coconut flavor from actual shreds of coconut, some flax seeds, lightly sweet from added cane sugar, some lions mane mushroom, and ginko biloba. Other than the natural coconut and oats, there is no stand out taste. Nothing odd or off to me. I like it, I would buy it again. Of course, your experience may vary.

LOW sodium (45 mg per cup, anything under 50 mg can be classified as low sodium), goodly amount of fiber (6 grams! yay!), 6 grams protein, and nice amount of potassium (210 mg). 250 cals.

I add kettle boiled water and put the lid on to allow it to soak into the oats. After a few minutes, I usually add some cut apples, then enjoy.

The product description says that "Each of these organic oat cups contains 1000mg of Lion's Mane and 120mg of ginkgo Biloba." I am pleased that this information is available, but I dont recall seeing it listed on the package. Also, no directions on package. Though have to ask, is there a need? I fill about 3/4 way up, and it turns out fine. Use more or less liquid depending on taste.

I like these cups a lot more than brand name organic oat cups.

Flax would be better if it were ground, but it wouldnt look as nice. I add in a little extra ground flax just so I am getting the benefit.

I have tried their maple version too, and both are good. I even like them as a snack, or dare I say "healthy dessert".

title: I enjoy Partake products, I buy their cookies regularly, never strong in flavor
text:
I like Partake products. I have been buying their cookies (and various mixes) somewhat regularly since first trying them sometime this past year. They aren't super loaded with sugar, nor sodium, or junk. Yet enough sugar and salt to be tasty to me. They dont have a cloying taste, nor chemically taste that other store cookies have (and hence I tend to avoid). I like keeping a little something on hand for when the mood strikes, and I am rather liking these single serving cookies in a bag. They are free from the top 12 allergens, so if this is important, then you may want to check this out.

I usually buy the boxes (which has a tray with a few rows of larger cookies), but these small packs are nice. Likely marketed more towards kids, but also good for those trying to not over indulge. Each pack has 7-8 little cookies, around the size of a quarter (see my pic). Just a nice little snack. I usually have Partake cookies alongside a cup of coffee and good company. I set out a little tray of num nums, and Partake is always a part of that. I happen to like that they are not strongly flavored.

I like them. I will probably stick with the boxes, but a big box of packets of mini cookies is always welcome. Taste just like I am used to from Partake.

I thought they tasted chocolatey enough, but I did think that they appeared to be a tad low on chips. My boxes arrived smashed up looking, but that did not impact the bags at all. The shipping box was totally fine, so this was packed like that. Not sure who is responsible for that, but it is unacceptable.

title: use it on and in everything and anything- meats, grains, roots, veg, plant based- just yum!
text: 1 full pound of seasoning in a pressure zip bag. Price per ounce is reasonable and competitive. This is the type of seasoning blend that I find to be quite versatile. This has all the typical "steak" seasoning, but with addition of a hint of citrus. I'm loving this on regular beef burgers, and for my ultra budget friendly lentil burgers (cook some lentils, smash them up a bit, add flour and seasonings, form patties- bake or lightly fry. Top with a little of this and other fresh toppings.. woah... mmmm). I tried in on chicken, and on the other end of the spectrum on some home made seitan "steaks". Just an all around good seasoning blend. I portion some out into a smaller shaker as I find this is a nice go-to spice for anything and everything.

title: perfectly good moringa powder, btw--whole food powders can be tricky to fully dissolve.
text:
It looks, smells, and tastes like a good quality moringa powder. I find that it has a slight tea taste, hint of citrus. It doesnt taste "green" to me. I have added it to matcha, but more often I add it to smoothies. I keep an assortment of food powders on hand to give me a healthy boost of nutrition. I stock up on whole food powders so I am assured of having something to work with when fresh options are low or are out.

Since they claim that it fully dissolves easily in water, I have to make a comment. Whole food powders never fully dissolve. Sometimes they can dissolve better with a little warm water to start. Better yet would have been to explain. If it did dissolve easily, 100%, then I would have been suspect. This moringa powder behaves as expected.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. The $12.99 price tag is reasonable price, and more budget friendly than some options.

title: moist, tasty assortment of dried fruit- great for trail mix, over oats, in baking
text: Phew! Mine came well packaged, and clearly labeled (same as in their product pics). Fruit is so "fresh"- moist, delicious smelling and tasting. I use it primarily for tossing on hot oats, and will likely give it a try in muffins or scones. I got this primarily for the variety. It contains plenty of everything. title: unsweetened has a vanilla taste, otherwise pretty good. Shelf stable. Great for smoothies
text:

For whatever reason, they do not include a picture of the nutritional profile. Lots of other pictures of the container, but not a single on of the important information??????!! Why?

The calories per 8 ounce serving is 40, not 50.
There are 4 servings per container.
Do not freeze
Refrigerate after opening (use within 7-10 days)

INGREDIENTS (for unsweetened option):
macadamia milk (filtered water, macadamias), calcium phosphate, natural flavors, pea protein, sunflower lecithin, locust bean gum, sea salt, gellan gum, D2

I would consider this again depending on the price. The unsweetened is currently $11.96 for a pack of 6, which is quite reasonable for about $2 per carton. I keep an eye out for sales, and never buy at full price.

title: looooong term pantry, emergency prep, hefty container, great for stacking calories
text:
I buy Augason products when they are on sale. Been doing this on and off for a few years now. Always been a bit of a "prepper", since I was a toddler it seems, haha (In my 40s now). I has served me well through power outages, sicknesses, unemployment, and even bigger stuff like the pandemic, and now... *vaguely gestures around* everything else that is going on. I've never been one to be without when anything has come up. I never did "emergency food" if only because I didnt have the budget. I would stick with typical foods and try to store them well. Well now I have a little more wiggle room in my budget, and with the on and off sales of long term storage (20+ years), I take advantage when I can. I remember buying some Augason eggs back in 2019 for $19. Today? $33-56 for same container, depending on the day.

And so, I haven't opened this 3lbs 4 ounces can of pancake mix.. sorry. I dont intend to any time soon. I have quite a bit of bagged stuff to get through first, and I will likely continue to top off from stuff I get to store, then simply know I have this as back up to the back up. We dont eat a lot of pancakes, but the mixes are super versatile (can make sweet or savory, thin or thick, etc). But I wanted to shore up my options. Having some soups and such just adds flavor to other options used. I can add more veg, or a protein, or beans, or simply have some bread to dip into it. Or I can use as way to flavor something. I have a slew of reviews to write on various Augason products, and so they will all be pretty much the same: Super long term storage (25+ years), no matter what the weight, it will be stuffed into a #10 can (that reads, "number ten", not ten pound. I see that mistake in reviews). They keep sizes uniform. Next size up is a round bucket, next size up gets into the rectangular buckets. This is for storage that can be uniform, etc. So yes, you may buy a 7 ounce item that is volume wise that takes up a smidge of space, but it will be packed into a large #10 container. Just remember, all food products are sold based on weight, not volume anyway. All of my containers have been in perfect condition. Maybe one day soon I will try one container out and see how the product actually is.

Everyone's SHTF scenario varies. It could be bad weather (tornadoes, hurricanes, blizzards, ice storms), could be illness, could be road trip gone wrong (you do keep supplies in your car too, right?!), could be unemployment, or power outage, or lack of transportation, or oven/fridge/other appliance break down, or bigger stuff like plagues, food shortages, supply chain issues, *cough WW3 cough*, etc. No matter the situation we all need some things to get by: we need is food, water, shelter, some hygeine and medical stuff, and so on. You dont have to stack "emergency supplies" but you do need to stack shelf stable food items. Buy a few extra things every single time you go to the store. If you get to a spot that you feel comfortable and have the budget, then grab the "emergency" items like Augason offers. I like adding it in and just forgetting about it.

I give 5 stars because the cans always are in perfect condition, they have regular sales, are good about shipping items as soon as they can, have lots of items to choose from, and so far seem to be of good quality.

title: crisp, yummy strawberries for long term storage, or daily use as snack, in hot oats, etc
text:
Freeze dried and Dehydrated are two entirely different processes for water extraction. I saw a review that mentioned that they expected a raisin style strawberry, and they expected it to be sweet. For that, one would want to look for dehydrated strawberries or just the search term "dried" (but making sure it isnt freeze dried). And they would need to know that nearly ALL "raisin" style dried fruits have added sugar, hence the perception of it being sweet (and this freeze dried being a tad tart). Hard to find them without added suagr. Why? 2 reasons. One, Dried (and freeze dried) fruit just aren't all that sweet. Two, added sugar adds weight. Sugar is very cheap compared to the fruit being used, so in essence you are paying for the weight of the sugar (and why the rare "no added anything" can be pricy). Freeze dried never has added sugar (at least that I have seen among the brands I buy).

These are freeze dried strawberries. So that means the texture is crisp, light, dry, has a light snap crunch when consumed direct from bag. No added anything. JUST STRAWBERRIES with water removed via freeze dry process. They reconstitute a bit when added to something moist or liquidy. Ie, they soften up when tossed in with hot oats, or used in baking. Can soak them with a little water and sugar to make an ice cream topping. For me, I like then as is or added onto yogurt or onto my hot oats. Since ALL liquid is extracted with freeze dried foods, the shelf life is indefinite. Makes for great long term pantry item without added fuss. Maintains a lot or all the nutrition, so good to have on hand if fruit options run low.

Good product, good brand, reasonable price. I have used Huggiberries products before and have been satisfied with all that I have tried.

title: great long term pantry staple, unflavored is great for flavoring it how I want to
text:

I buy the unflavored because in general I find that the flavored varieties can be lacking, and a lot of brands charge more for flavored and fancy packaging. I can flavor it up how I want to. I have found that Tova keeps it simple. Very simple packaging, and fair prices.

I like the shape of their TVP. It really comes down to what your main use is. I like crumbles for "ground meat" applications (sauces, chili, tacos), and I like the more waver style strips such as this for when I want a more meat like bite- soups, stir fry, rice bowls, etc. These bits are nice- good texture. As for flavor, they are neutral as expected. Just play around with it and flavor it up in any means you want.

I am not vegan or vegetarian. Those terms say more about what people dont eat. I am primarily plant based eater. I eat everything and hold back on nothing, but I prefer my meats centered around plants. I dont like consuming a lot of soy, so I dont do TVP daily. But it is worked into my rotation. I have been buying more as of late because of food issues-- ie food shortages, food availability, shipping issues, price fluctuations, etc. I prefer to keep a little extra food on hand so I dont have to rush to the store every time I want to eat. Having shelf stable options on hand helps a lot.

text:

Macadamia nuts are supremely easy to chop if need be for baking. I prefer that they come whole as they seem to stay fresher longer, also I prefer texture of popping a round macadamia nut in my mouth. LOve these so much I am already thinking of buying more.

text:

Usually just a few ingredients, if that. So if something from them is called coffee energy bar, I knew enough to expect a primarily coffee product. This does not disappoint. Well, save for one thing.. I dont pick up much vanilla, just a hint. Other than that, this has its place as an energy bar (95 mg caffeine from coffee beans). I dont use this to snack on like a treat, I use it more for a quick hit of energy. Like eating a cup of coffee. Like a fruit leather chew. Like their fruit chews but made with coffee and dates. I like it!

Ever eat coffee beans? They can be plain, or coated in chocolate. The bean is robust tasting and ya get a little kick from the caffeine. This very much reminds me of that, down to the taste. Expect not crunchy. A dense thick chew. Small bar, you wont want to eat much anyway. Great for keeping in a hiking pack, or on a long drive, or anytime you may need a caffeine kick and some healthy calories but not want a liquid form.

I'd like a little more vanilla taste to come through, but other than that I think these are fun. Mine are moist, dense, chewy. Not at all dry. Can be eaten direct from packet, or can be chunked up and tossed in with some trail mix. I am already a fan of "snacking" coffee beans, and this just reminds me of it so much that nothing about this product surprised me. I am also already familiar with "That's It" products.

I like. I may be the only one, haha. 4.5 stars. I like it better than 4. So 5 stars, but know that I want to know it a little for having too little vanilla taste coming through.

title: pretty good, loads of flavor, easy to make, good pantry (or long term/emergeny pantry) item
text: Pretty good, easy to make, little goes a long way. Make it as thick or as thin as you want. Can cut it into something else that's creamy to stretch it. I dont use this often, but I keep a pack or two on hand just as an option. This is first time I ever bought a case. Price was good, and I figured having excess during these questionable times is good. If I am going to eat a lot of beans and rice, I want a way to flavor it in all sorts of ways, haha. Or making a simple biscuit and having something to dunk it in. Not limited to austere times, it sure makes for an anytime comfort food.

title: add it anything, everything, a must have for pantry
text: Highly versatile must have for working pantry and long term pantry. Lends a lot of flavor used as a "spice", or can make a quick sauce for pasta or use as a base for soups. Just an all around great powder to keep on hand. Writing this in April 2022, the expiration on my bag is a few years out or more, which is amazing. So many products as of recent have been old or close to best by date. Of course products last a lot longer than that, but I want as much lead time as I can get.

title: pantry staple, convenient, tasty as is, doctor it up, add it over rice or veg, or add broth to it
text:
I have the regular "original" Madras Lentils. Comes as expected- pack of 6. I buy them when on sale, and S&S. They are great over rice or added to vegetable. Or just plain- warmed up or direct from the pouch. Can be used as base for making some quick chili, or as a topping for hot dogs. Doesnt really have a strong flavor, and it would take to any spices or other seasonings you can think of. Texture is kinda meaty.

title: versatile, pantry staple
text:
I keep coconut aminos in my pantry. I still use regular aminos, and I still use soy, but I love coconut aminos for its lower sodium health(er) vibe. title: easy to use, very much the same as making up a scrambled egg, buy now while still can
text:
Bought these powdered eggs for extra long term pantry use, ie, emergency supply. Prices have been going up (an up) , so while I still buy eggs at store there may be a time when they are totally unavailable as with other things. Be prepared people! I dont use eggs that much, but I know I will miss them if I dont have them. I just want options, and to have extra in case anyone needs some. This order was two, 2 lb bags for total of 4 lbs. Pricing and availability has fluctuate a lot over the past month or so. I ended up buying when price went up by $10 (initially 20). So $87. Crazy. title: smooth, easy flavor, nice hot or cold, anytime!
text: I love Necafe instant coffee. When I want caffeinated, I go with their ultra smooth Gold Espresso crema. Love being able to buy a big multi pack. I will keep on buying it. Yum!

title: a tad more greasy than their hot version, but very good for flavoring dishes. Dont need much!
text: Cooked, dried, ready to go. Great price too. I had initially tried (via Vine) and loved their HOT chorizo, so much so that I bought another and bought a couple of mild too. title: add to your pantry, super convenient

title: umami for that savory vibe, I use in making lentil burgers (described below)
text: This is comprised of one ingredient: Champignon Mushroom. It is a fine powder, and mixes seamlessly in anything I have added it to. The sense of Umami can come from a variety of sources, such as soy, msg, meats, seaweed, mushrooms, and the list goes on. Basically anything that enhances that special savory taste. It is not necessarily a taste in and of itself. So dont use it as a spice, use all your usual stuff then add this (or other source) to layer in that savory vibe. I used this in lentil burgers which I make from using slightly mashed lentils (I made 1 lbs. I half mashed, kept half whole for texture), then add up to 3/4 c flour (enough to bind, but not too dry), any assortment of seasonings, and umami source, made into patties then either baked or lightly fried. Since already cooked, this is a matter of crisping up the outside. Very forgiving "recipe".  Using a bag of lentils at $1.25 per pound (dollar$), this made 10 good sized patties that fit on burger roll--approx $0.13 per patty, negligible added amount for use of flour, spices. I am not vegan, nor vegetarian, but I eat a lot of fruits and vegetables. Love plant based meals. My husband is open to my creations but isnt as gung ho for meatless meals. But lentil burgers are so dang close ESPECIALLY IF USE UMAMI source (cumin is also "meaty"), that he has no qualms over eating this on regular basis. Sometimes I cook in a little bacon grease, haha. Top with onion, tomatoes, pickle, cheese (opt, or make a nooch paste), condiments.. yum. Long way of saying that the power of umami is real, and this mushroom powder by Judees is a healthy option. Love Judees products, so this was a no brainer choice. I'd buy this again.

title: good quality medical manuka in stout glass jar & packed in branded box
text:
All honey contains antimicrobial properties, but Manuka honey also contains non-hydrogen peroxide, which gives it an even greater antibacterial power. With Manuka honey ratings (whether UMF or MGO), the lower ratings are best for consumption and for non medicinal skin care, while the higher ratings are the ones you want if planning to use if for more intensive purposes (immune support, wound healing, o if planning to use diluted). These are usually labeled as "medical grade". If you didnt already know, manuka honey must come from New Zealand. Anything else, be suspect.

This New Zealand medical grade manuka honey comes in a glass jar, and has MGO rating of 360+. This is mid grade, or just a little lower, and likely has UMF of 12 (no less than 11 given the MGO rating).

Taste wise, the higher the rating the potent it tases (in my experience anyway). This has the distinct nearly medicinal taste of manuka honey that I am very familiar with. Manuka honey has a very different taste than "non manuka" honey. I dont dislike it, but in general manuka is not a pleasaing taste to me. Yet I always have a small jar available to me. I find great value in it for immune support as needed. I keep it for use to help sooth a sore throat (works better than local raw honey for me), and will use it in tea preparations when I am feeling down. I have used medical grade for helping to heal (and keep moistened) light burns. So long as you aren't sticking your fingers in the jar, or keeping it un capped, there should not be much concern for diluting/reducing the antibacterial properties.

So yeh, if you are looking for a good quality manuka honey in a glass jar, packaged nicely in a branded box, then this will be just fine. 5 stars- is as expected, no problems, concerns. Glad to have it.

title: comfort food paired w/buttered toast, emergency food, versatile uses, between broth&gravy
text:
The product pictures are pure BS, but anyone expecting anything coming out of a can shouldnt be gullible enough to think that is what this looks like.

I dont hate it, but I dont love it. Like it enough to keep stacking it. It's got it's purpose, especially these days and upcoming. It isn't bad, and I stack these on my shelf for a variety reasons. Now, anyone expecting a quality beef stew on par with homemade will severely disappointed. This is more like a chunky soup. I can say that is has lots of good sized bits of potato and carrot slices. The background flavor is indeed beef, and I dont find it weird tasting. The beef pieces are spongy, reminiscent of canned ground beef rather than chunks of roast. They list "beef", and so whatever that is, it is soft and spongy, and there is plenty of it. The liquid is thicker than a broth but not as thick as a gravy. Add a little flour to thicken it up if need be.

Loaded with sodium like most canned goods. Be careful, one can is ridiculously considered "2 servings". that will overblow your sodium content for the day.

Overall... for what I buy it for.. I am pleased. I dont eat this stuff often. It really isnt my go to. But I do have a robust pantry, and I keep stuff like this on hand for quick desperate meals, for using as a sort of flavor base (keep as is, or blend), for adding over rice, pasta, etc. Make up a bunch of buttered toast and dip it in this? Mmmm yes. Quick, easy comfort food. Got someone who cant chew real well? This stuff can be gummed. Or can be blended to make for a beefy smoothie (gross sounding, but people have issues that may benefit from this knowledge).

The price on this stuff has gone up a lot. Inflation, and food shortage combined. If you can get it for less than $3 per can (04/2022) then it is still holding at older pricing (I think $2.85 at DollarGeneral). If you are looking to stack your pantry, this is worthwhile to have. Gives some variety, convenience. Need a can opener. I know reviews are totally unfavorable, but this brand is reasonably (so far) priced, and has the most natural taste. I dont cringe eating it- no off taste, or after taste. Maybe grab a can from the store before committing to a case, or jump on getting the case and keeping it for emergency (or give away).

Know what you are getting this for, understand the limitations of taste and texture, and then proceed if you so desire. 4 stars from me. Not because it is necessarily better than others (in some cases yes), but because it fills a need, meets expectations (I set them low, haha), and the taste isnt too shabby. Also, my cans are all good. No dents. And, I bought another case.

title: perfect deep strong flavor for use in my Ibrik in making Turkish coffee
text: Super fine ground (like a powder) for use in my Ibrik when I make a cup of Turkish coffee. I am not good at making it, but I have nowhere around me that makes it. SO every once in awhile I give it a whirl.  I love a good bold cup of Turkish coffee. Some preparations use a more green bean, but I dont care for that taste at all. I need a darker powder for my preference, and this provides that. While this isnt limited to Turkish coffee preparations, if that is what you are going for then know that this works. Can also be used for baking (amp up the chocolate flavor with a little bit of coffee powder), or depending on your brewer this can work as regular coffee too, or for "cold brew" method (though I wouldnt waste it on that. I prefer cheap coffee for cold brewing). I have used it in pour overs with no issue. Love the aroma of the Fabula coffees, and the low acid makes it extra smooth tasting. Fabula is pricy, I dont rate on price-- everyone can make their own decision regarding this. I have noticed that low acid varieties have higher price tag than ones not marketed as low acid. I can tell the difference as I have had a few low acid brands as of late.

title: I've tried a few Fabula coffee options, all good, very smooth. Very pleased with this decaf

Low acid coffees are always (so far in my experience) priced well above those not processed to result in such a profile. So I am not rating on price. You can decide for yourself. I'm stoked that it holds up to ice. 4-5 stars for all their options. 4.5 if I could.

4.5 stars

title: liked it so much I went and bought another. Great pantry staple
text:
Wonderful assortment of mushrooms. I always use mushrooms- fresh, dried, powdered. title: when you want an olive oil you can taste. Nice for salads, bread dipping, veg drizzle

title: 3.5/4 stars. Good chew, some bits of soft, some more tough, interesting flavors
text: I've gotten so used to the soft jerky styles that I forgot that old school rough and chewy still exists. It isn't quite as hard on the teeth as some, but this is the kind you can take your time with. It reminds me of summers nibbling slowly on a strip of jerky. title: creamy smooth, lightly sweet, natural vanilla. This brand has lots of options!
text:
This brand has a lot of options; something for everyone. If I weren't trying it for Vine, I would have selected an unsweetened vanilla or unsweetened plain option or the lower sugar (7 grams) barista option. Alas, I went with the sweetened vanilla. It has 11 grams of added sugar and it is not too sweet tasting. Even so, I think it is a tad high per serving. I guess if you liken it to a "treat" like chocolate milk (but instead is vanilla), then it isnt bad.

I love keeping shelf stable non dairy milk in my pantry. I go through phases as to my consumption, so having something I dont need to keep in the fridge prior to opening is my go-to thing. Of course, product must be refrigerated after opening.

Taste is very smooth and creamy thanks to sunflower oil and sunflower lecithin. I am often too lazy to make my own non dairy milks, but when I do I always used sunflower lecithin to help boost the creamy factor. This is nicely done. I have tried this in coffee, and it is Ok. I normally dont want vanilla flavor in my coffee, but it has a decent natural taste (vanilla in general is one of my favorite flavors). I do however love it for use in my smoothies, again I would normally only buy unsweetened, but this is working for that for the most part (just have to watch that sugar!). For smoothies I much prefer unsweetened. For my matcha green tea preparations, I normally always need to sweeten it up and so this sweetened vanilla is actually most perfect for that use.

I would consider this brand again, just for me it would be a different option as the sugar is a little much for my needs and preferences.

title: best ACV w/ the mother. Great for use as a health supplement
text: Excellent ACV with the mother. In glass bottle, clearly has the bits of "mother", and is my go to apple cider vinegar for daily health use. I add some to water and drink up. Not a great taste, but it is doable. While there are lots of apple cider vinegar (with the mother) available, I find Braggs to be best of all. I'll use the others as back up, or for use in salads and such. but when looking to use ACV as a health supplement? Braggs it is.

title: Expired product, sweetened w/ STEVIA &MonkFruit, dull peach flavor, better IN food than alone
text:
I now officially despise the phrasing, "no sugar added". That just means a non cane sugar product has been added to sweeten something, OH, and higher price tag for such marketing. Really just prefer it to be packed in water. Peaches arent in season (and I have yet to learn to do my own canning of such items), so I buy some convenient packs of fruit as needed. Ok so I recognize my mistake, and I dont hold it against the product in terms of rating, but they could spell it out better-- other than trying to zoom in the tiny writing portion of the product pictures.

Overall, I find the peaches direct from cup to have a bland taste that is overtaken by Stevia. I dont mind the taste of monkfruit, and in many applications Stevia is ok, but the small cubes of peaches is too delicate to handle that level of sweetener. Makes for a dull peach flavor with hint of bitter.

I bought these on a whim, I wanted some chopped peaches for use on top of my oatmeal. I like the idea of single serve cups so I dont have to be concerned with using up a can of peaches. Usually I buy whatever is available- heavy syrup, light syrup,packed in fruit juice. But never packed in Stevia. I learned my lesson and will never do so again. At least with the other options I can drain the syrup and still have a pleasant peach flavor. But this? The stevia taste clings to it. I WILL SAY, that it tastes best mixed into something--so overall it works ok on my oats. The sweetness disperses and I pick up on the peach flavor better (sad that I am trying to taste peach among cut up peaches), but on its own? BLEGH. Dole does have other options (cheaper too--paying more for "no sugar added"), so I will just go back to the other stuff.

HERE's the kicker. I bought these APRIL 2022. These have expiration date of MARCH 2022!!!! I bought these on sale, and right now I expect and accept some short shelf life products. I know products are ok well past the date. BUT I EXPECT to NOT receive a product with a date that occurred BEFORE I even got my order. I would have been annoyed but overall ok even if it said "april 2022", but no. UGH. Maybe you will experience something else. I would hope.

So overall... my experience with this has not been favorable. 2-3 stars for taste, 0 stars for receiving an OLD product. 1-2 stars overall. Giving 1 star because this is unacceptable.

title: something for everyone, LOW SODIUM (30-40 mg), great assortment of flavors

title: wonderful assortment, lovely flavors, super convenient, nice addition to long term pantry
text: NIce assortment of precooked (and seasoned) rice. This set includes 2 pouches each of Coconut rise, Bombay Biryani, and Tikka Masala. I love them all. I am a big fan of precooked rice packets. I often make a quick broth, and then use some leftover vegetables and some rice from a packet to make an easy soup. It is one of my go to breakfast/brunch foods.
