title: surprisingly tasty, creamy, filling. Balanced flavor, not too salty. Nice for sipping or as base
text:
I am pleasantly surprised how tasty this is. I have been wanting to try some WonderFit/slim products for a while now, but was always turned off by negative reviews and price. This soup sounded really good to me, and so with the opportunity to try it, I made the jump. There is a little bit of powder in each packet. Reminds me of a tear off onion soup packet. I add it to a mug, then pour 6-8 ounces of kettle boiled (not full boil) water, and stir. There is mild clumping, but with extra stirring, it seems I get most of it smoothed out. There are visual bits of parsley (or some other green bits).

The smell is noticeably tortilla like. The taste is more like a cream of chicken. To me, not too salty. MIld balanced flavor. The creamy aspect is extra appealing to me. I am NOT keto, so I paired it with some toast. Haha. Just has 100 calories and has a decent nutritional profile (plus added vitamins and minerals). The later is what I was drawn to. I like having some "sipping broths" to help warm me up, or lightly fill my belly, or I like a simple broth or soup that I can use to bring together some left overs (veggies, maybe a spoonful of rice or quinoa, few bits of chicken, etc). The added vitamins and minerals makes this a "hot smoothy" to me. I would pack this in an emergency kit, or keep at the office, in the car, in my purse, for camping, or simply for anytime at home. Just an easy to prepare, shelf stable, nutritionally loaded simple soup.

It is much more filling than anticipated too. I'm a big eater, and this along with my rye toast just filled my gut. I like stacking my pantry, and this is a great addition for me. I am now comfortable trying other varieties, or maybe will just buy more of this. Again, I am not keto so I am not commenting on whether it adheres to some set of rules or not. But when I am watching my carbs (mostly from sugar) intake, I wouldn't hesitate to grab for this.

title: when you want a candy bar, but want it to be healthy
text: Good! One of my favorite KIND bars when I want something that tastes and feels like a candy bar, but has a significantly better nutritional profile. Lovely anytime- on the go, or on the couch. I like a lot of different KIND bars, and this is one of my "staple". Love the chewy, the perfect level of sweetness and chocolatey-ness.

title: delicious flavor, great of for on the go, portion control, and packs make for long freshness
text: So tasty. We love keeping packets of flavored almonds on hand. Although pricier than a big bag, I prefer the packets over a big bag for a couple of reasons. The freshness lasts. I go through spurts in eating this type of stuff. I dont want to reach for some almonds and have them be rancid. Next, portion control. Would be way to easy to keep on eating these if it werent for the built in stoppage point (empty packet!). Lastly, really makes for a great packed snack on the go. I will grab a few easy to pack, easy to eat snacks for use through the day. I dont often eat breakfast, and I dont pack a lunch, but I want to have something on me just in case. Almonds are often part of my snack pack. Usually I keep a sliced apple or other fruit, and maybe a Belvita or KIND bar. Almonds create good satiety.  I dont think I have met a flavor I dont like. This smokehouse flavor is delicious

title: Just powdered beets! healthy addition to smoothies, broths, etc
text: Just beetroot powder. I have been using beetroot powder on and off for many years. It's a whole food product, nothing added. I enjoy beets in all forms, but I rely on the powder for the times I can't find beets in my area, or they are way too pricy. It looks, smells, and performs like other powdered beets I have purchased over the years. I like the Sunwarrior brand because it comes in a tub with a twist off cap. Seems like a lot of stuff comes package in bags, and that is actually annoying when it comes to powders as powders are really easy to get caught up in the pressure zip area, increasing likelihood of freshness reduction. I have no worries with this container. I use it in smoothies, broths, stews, sometimes coffee, cocoa, or tea (depends on how creative I feel like getting).

title: Spicy and flavorful, little goes a long way. Yum way to spice up my peanut noodles
text: Ooh yeh, this is a nice condiment. Well packaged, attractive presentation, and definitely a contender for a food themed gift basket. This is a delightful tasting pepper relish. Has a brutal kick of heat for my delicate tastebuds, but I like it. Because of this, I dont need much. The container will last me a long time. Nice as a topper, or as a flavoring agent in noodles .I have successfully used this as a means to make some simple spicy peanut noodles--which is basically any noodle, peanut butter, and something spicy like sriracha- but this is incredible.

title: mild easy flavor that is lovely hot or cold
text: I'm pleased with the taste and smell of this stuff. I drink matcha daily (after my morning coffee), and have been doing so for 15 years or so. I typically use culinary because I prefer to use matcha in smoothies or masked with other flavors so choosing more spendy options isn't doable for me on a regular basis.  Also, I tend to use triple, quadruple the recommended amount so I tend to buy cheaper. BUT, I do love and appreciate a good ceremonial grade. I use that when I am going to make a hot drink or a drink that is focused more on the matcha taste. I find this to have a lovely sweet aroma, and it tastes pleasant--rather mild, gentle, easy to drink. When making a cold drink, I prefer to run it through a personal mixer/blender to guarantee a smooth finished drink. Each packet appears to be a teaspoon, so overall a little pricy per serving. But it is a convenience item, and I would certainly consider it again, especially a bag or jar.

title: Nutrition info for Blueberry Almond listed in my review
text:
Serving size: 2 bars (whole package)
Calories: 220
Fat: 9 grams (0 Saturated, 0 trans, 1.5 polyunsaturated, 6 monounsaturated)
Cholesterol: 0 mg
Sodium" 20 mg
Total Carb: 32 grams
Fiber: 5 grams
Total Sugars: 10 g (includes 7 grams added sugar)
Sugar Alcohol: 0

INGREDIENTS:
Oats, tapioca syrup, brown rice flour, canola oil, cane sugar, raisin paste, blueberries, cranberries, almonds, millet, buckwheat, honey, amaranth, quinoa, natural flavor, sea salt, Vitamin E (tocopherols to maintain freshness)
Allergen Information: Contains almonds. Made in a facility that processes peanuts, tree nuts, soy and sesame seeds.

The Blueberry Almond bars are lovely. Soft, chewy, not too sweet. Can eat the whole package, or just grab one bar. Can be consumed as is, or used as a crumble on oats, yogurt, etc. There are two small dense bars in each pack. One pack (both bars) is considered 1 serving.

I went to double check on that as I write this, and I see that the page doesnt show the nutritional panel nor an ingredient list. WHY?? Why is there no nutritional information listed on the page?? There is for some of the other options. I bought this without looking because KIND products are usually within my scope of nutritional interest. However, come on--add a pic page manager! I will try to grab a clear pic. I am an avid reviewer, and one of the things I look for it is completion and consistency of product information. And I look to make sure that the info lines up with what is in my hand. Now, again, I bought these without looking since I am familiar with KIND products, but not everyone is, and many folks want to see the same info as if they were looking at in in hand in the store. Not everyone will buy blindly. For shame. My rating drops a star, not that it likely matters. Anyway, I could get a good pic, so I typed out what is on my package. Hope that helps.

title: smells good, tastes pretty good, taste more like regular coffee than decaff, but its def decaf
text:
I think the decaf is pretty good. Tastes more like regular coffee, but I know it isnt caffeinated because I had no trouble getting tired (I tried this in the evening). I tend to find decaf to be weak, or have a funny taste, or simply no taste. So when I find a good brand, I tend to stick to it. Unless I have an opportunity to try another, such as in this case. I think this could pass for regular, and while not super dark, it has a darker deeper flavor that many. My favorite is [[ASIN:B006N3I2SK Dark Magic decaf]] for reference. I sometimes want a hot cup of coffee in the evening and no way can I have caffeinated, so keeping some decaf on hand nice.

The box says decaf, but the individual bag it is contained in does not say this. You will have to open the bag to see it on the cup itself. The word "knight" is mispelled on each bag/puff (Kight).

My Keurig gets a little mad with this cup. I find that cocoa cups tend to make my Keurig sputter water, and so my trick it so stab a couple of holes in the top. What I think happens is that this is very full of coffee, super packed. and it may need an extra hole to get the water through the coffee. I put cup in, press down, then pull back up and turn the cup, the close and continue. You may never have this issue. But if you do, give this a try.

title: tasty, versatile, use more or less water depending on your preference in consistency
text: I love Judees product- big fan, buy often. I even use their plain powdered sour cream. This is similar but has onion added. Makes for nice seasoning, or made up as a dip. Be sure to mix well, refrigerate. Use more or less water depending on your consistency, Yum yum!

title: large, durable plastic container, murky with mother (no noticeable bits), good even taste
text: Good apple cider vinegar on par with other ACV found in stores. Comparable in quality and price. This bottle is plastic, and the vinegar is murky (this is indicative of the "Mother", though I am used to more bits & floaters. I dont see any in this). I find that it is hard to compare to Braggs (chunky bits of mother, glass container), as I have yet to come across a true Braggs dupe. This ACV is more in line with ALL the other ACV with mother. I like this style (non Braggs) for use in salads and other light use applications. I still prefer Braggs for more medicinal like use. Both are good, this is perfectly fine. Would like to have it state what type of bottle is used.

title: love my nooch for quick, easy mac n' "cheese", gives cheesy flavor to anything- so versatile, tasty
text:
I love Judees products, and I love nutritional yeast. And so yes, I love this nooch from Judees. I am not vegan, not even vegetarian but I flirt with both. I love to eat.. everything. I tend to eat a lot of plant based stuff. I am a big fan of making a quick mac n' "cheese" using nutritional yeast (pasta of choice, butter of choice, nooch, salt, pepper, sometimes addins- vegetables, meat, or TVP). Often cheaper than dairy cheese, and I dont always want to consume dairy. Being shelf stable adds a lot of value to me. I know I will always have some on hand. It is a musy have pantry item.

And so because I am not vegan, I usually dont bother with fortified nooch (adds in B vitamins), and just go for plain. This product is fortified. I will keep this for use on vegetables or small application meals (anything that can benefit from a little "cheesy" fix). When I make my mac n' "cheese" I tend to use a lot, so I will stick with my regular unfortified nooch.

Competitively priced for the size.

title: just peas, cooks quickly, nice for hot or cold dishes, healths up a meal
text: The vegetable based pastas have come a long way. Once I discovered a couple of good brands, I have been splurging on them on occasion. I really like that this is quick cook pasta. I notice that the veg pastas can need more time over regular semolina, and so this feature is a bonus. Love the nutrition profile-- loaded with fiber. I have had this hot and cold. I made a mac and "cheese" using nutritional yeast (I am not vegetarian or vegan, I just love me some nooch), the other cold dish was simple oils, seasonings, and cut up veggies. Nice taste, texture, and convenient too. Certainly way more than a regular box of pasta, but I noticed the boxe size (12 ounces) is larger than some similar products and similar price. Even so, hence my "occasional" use, but I do love trying new things out and keeping an interesting assortment of food in my pantry.

title: nice flavor, texture. Easy to make. Love Judees products, nice addition to pantry
text:
I often add strawberries to my grits, or oats, or whatever hot cereal I am using and so this appealed to me. I also love Judees products, so it was a no brainer to give this a try. This has a lightly sweet., lightly fruity, lightly creamy taste and texture. I rather like everything about this, which is good because it is a big 2 lbs bag, haha.

Use more or less water depending on preference. Add other goodies, or just eat on its own. Easy to make, and tastes comforting. I'd buy it again, and other flavor. As for plain, while I am sure it is great I would likely shop around for best price. But if you want to be assured of a product coming from an allergen free facilility in the USA, then Judees is a great way to go.

title: Mix with a little water to get the flavor to burst, shelf stable, just horseradish powder!
text: This is the way to do horseradish if you dont use it often. I almost never go through a jar of it before it needs to be tossed out. I am loving this powder. Mix with a little water to get the flavor to burst, then add in whatever you want. Shelf stable, dont need much. It is wonderful.

title: nice on own, or over extra portion plain oats, sweet but not cloying. Overall pleasant
text:
I rather like it. It isnt perfect, but it is tasty and shelf stable. But food now while you still can, hm? Makes nice option among other oat products I use. Works as a quick snack, or as a "dessert". Add a little vanilla yogurt for extra tasty treat. Or if you are clever, figure out how to make it a cake. Or simply enjoy it as is. Just add hot water, or use microwave. Nice on the go convenience.

I was at first taken aback by the 17 grams of added sugar (22 total). Sugar is the second ingredient, but seeing that it isnt a daily item for me, I am simply enjoying it as something different. I keep a well stocked pantry, and I am looking to boost it a little further by peppering items with added appeal. I have the apple & walnut variety, and it has a pleasant flavor. Sweet but not cloying. I usually add in additional handful of chopped apples. I would even go with more walnuts, but at that point I should just make it "from scratch" using plain oats. Since this isnt a big portion (to me), I could easily eat 2. It is a regular portion, but I have also used it alongside a serving of plain oats.

I can taste the apples, cinnamon, cranberries, but I found the cups to be a little lacking in the walnuts. Even so, it is pretty good. I would consider more if the price is right (I dont rate on price- you do you).

Well packaged, I dont care what the expiry date is. Stuff like this lasts a very long time.

title: fantastic chorizo, already buying some more
text: Amazing, top notch chorizo. My links look fantastic- great shape, great color, nothing weird. Lovely spice, good overall flavor. Mmm.  I greatly appreciate this minimally processed chorizo, with no "added" nitrates or nitrites.  It is ready to eat. I buy chorizo for use in hot dishes, as a flavor additive rathe than the star of the show. But it is also wonderful as a tappas. I tried it with cheese and crackers, because I have a weakness for pepperoni, sausages, etc, and I just had to have some like that before I sectioned off a piece for use in a [[ASIN:B09V3FRJWT hominy]] based dish. Adds some nice spicy, but not too hot. Alone, the heat is more noticeable, but once paired with a carb it is more of a spice kick. So if I were doing tappas style treats, then I would likely use mild, but use the hot in dishes (dont need much!). Using it how I work with it, the pack will last me a while. I know it will store well in fridge (or even frozen). I dont rate on price, but I do comment. This Chorizo is currently best price out there at $1.43 an ounce (compared to other cured links. Raw is usually pennies per ounce). Anyway, I just added two more to my shopping cart, so I think 5 stars is fair, haha!. They have [[ASIN:B09TRYF3NH MILD]] too!!

title: lovely bag of hominy, excellent pantry staple, neutral taste pairs well with everything, adds bulk
text: Adding variety to my pantry is always a good thing. I have some cans of hominy that I keep on hand for a few recipes, so adding in a dry variety is nice too. Just soak, then do your thing. Funny, I have a love hate relationship with hominy. On its own, it is odd- trust that it does not taste like sweet corn. It has a neutral, grainy taste. Which is why it is used in making maize flour (different than corn meal), and to add bulk to various dishes. I prefer to chop it up small, or I mash it and add lots of other flavors for making patties, balls, loafs. I love it paired with bits of chorizo, which coincidentally I got this as at the same time I got [[ASIN:B09TRW7S2F Hot Chorizo]].  And so, I think you will be pleased with this 2 lb bag of hominy. It looks great, good flavor (I like it better than a brand name canned variety that I buy), giant pieces of hominy in a durable bag, truly nice addition to my pantry.

title: for extra umami above what basic soy sauce offers
text: The ingredients show that it is basically a salty powder, similar to soy but with additional layers of umami. Jazz it up with additonal flavors if need be, or enjoy it on its own. I like to have it on hand for simple addition to some udon noodles, or even fried rice. I dont get the flavor experience I want when I just want some mostly plain Udon noodles. This gives it the taste I am looking for. Sometimes I add a little toasted sesame oil and some broccoli. For less than $3, it is a worthwhile addition to my giant spice pantry

title: convenient, decent flavor, mild, a bit salty, has hint of sweet. Pantry item
text: I like it. Has a good curry smell, a mild curry taste. Has a hint of sweetness, and is definitely salty. Decent portion for all the flavor it adds to rice or other vegetables.  I really dont mind it as a convenience item. I tend to overstock my pantry in case of bad weather, illness, laziness, pandemics, WW3, food shortage, hyper-inflation. LOL.  With this, it takes up little room, adds some good flavor to whatever I pair it with, and if need be it can consumed direct from pack. It doesnt replace going to a restaruant or home made, just like Spaghettioos dont replace an Italian restaurant or homemade pasta, but its a convenience item that has its place in my life. I like it, its tasty enough, and I went ahead and ordered a second box.

title: actual slices, lightly seasoned, retains all the goodness of fresh avocados, totally love these
text:
Oh goodness, these are yummy. I absolutely adore avocado, and I was hoping that these freeze dried slices still maintained their avocado taste, and to a degree texture (I didnt want them mashed down and made into chips). They do look just like I hoped for, and with the light addition of spices, they make for a super delicious snack. Has a gentle crispness, not like some freeze dried fruits. This still has a creamy vibe to it despite being freeze dried. Good looking slices, taste like avocado, not drenched in flavor- they used a light hand in adding some spices. I can taste a little lime, a little salt (very low at 10mg for whole pack), and some garlic. I wouldnt be able to distinguish it as "everything" flavor. But whatever it is makes my taste buds sing. For that, I give it 5 stars. For those wanting it loaded more with the everything spices/seeds may be disappointed. Or maybe it varies per pack. These are so tasty to me though.

While freeze dried, and therefore less weight than a fresh avocado, there is a good amount in each pack. I dont know exactly how much fresh avocado this translates to? The calorie count makes it seem like 1/2 to one whole avocado. Like one small avocado. Still retains the fiber, protein, and fat. There is a good amount of potassium and very little salt.

I dont rate on price. However, I do comment. These are a splurge. I absolutely love these slices, and could eat them all day. And my beloved avocados are really really pricy right now (right?!!) making anything avocado related a budget buster for me. But I'll keep an eye on pricing and will likely buy more at some point. I'd love to add these to my long term storage. Would be great in a hiking bag, gym bag, on the go snack (planned or emergency). Just all around delicious!

title: adds variety to pantry and preps, add more goodies to it, add broth for quick broth bowl
text:
Not too shabby! Definitely more for convenience, to have something on hand. Not my go-to for a healthy meal (shelf stable is not going to be epitome of health food). But it adds a little variety to my pantry, and I love the fiber and protein content for each portion. Could use a little less sugar and sodium (from soy sauce) but it isnt terrible.

I added this to my longer term pantry, not exactly emergency food, but something that could be used as such since there is really no preparation needed. I can eat this alone, or use it to flavor something else. Add in more vegetables (fresh, canned, frozen, left overs), or a protein (beans, canned, fresh, frozen, left overs), or more grain (or pasta), or add in a bunch of broth to make a quick soup (my favorite application).

It is well packaged and the shelf life is going to be longer than the best buy date stamped on it (does not expire the day that is stamped in it- be smart).

title: great pantry item for quick easy noodle bowls
text: I stock a lot of noodles and pasta in my pantry. I dont wait until I want to make something to go to the store and buy it. I make according to what I have on hand more often than not. And every once in awhile I like a good Asian noodle bowl full of veggies and some delicious sauce. Usually includes toasted sesame oil. I love the texture of this brand, so it is a repurchase for sure. I bought this in a big pack, and will consider buying more sooner over later. Food shortages (and increased prices) are upon us, so I try to pick up a few extra goodies here and there on sale and/or in bulk. Stuff like this lasts a long time, so I am not at all concerned with expiration dates.

title: tasty base, very versatile, must have for working pantry, and great for long term pantry
text: Flavorful. Shelf stable. Once opened, store in fridge. Lasts a very long time. I keep a lot of bases, bouillon, and broths on hand. Works for so many applications that it is a must have for working pantry, and long term storage pantry needs. Sometimes the bases are hard to find in store, so I order online. Little more pricey per container than I am used to, but when availability is low I had to get what I could. This is good, and I would buy again.

title: looks good, tastes good, great addition to prepper pantry
text:
Nice pantry item; more for occasional or emergency use than regular use. Not something I eat regularly, but for the occasional quick meal it works fine. My main reason for buying stuff like this is simply to stock my pantry. If I cant get to store, or if grocery shelves are low, or whatever the reason, having some shelf stable food can make all the difference. So I buy a little here and there, and just add it to my personal stock. Then once in awhile it is used as needed.

My cans look good- no dents. Got the pack of four, and they are all bound together. No issues.

title: must have for my pantry, I keep a lot on hand as I use it in everything. Yum!
text:
The Knorr bouillon is really flavorful. I have the chicken, beef, and tomato. I use the chicken for everything it seems. Just goes well in everything; makes for a tasty "spice", as well as for use as making broth, etc.. I have purchased this a few times in recent months. Not so much because I go through it quickly, but because it is something I really want to make sure I have stocked in my pantry. I dont want to run out, and if I cant get to the store, or if things get low/unavailable, I want to have extra to pull from.

I am not at all worried about expiration date, as this stuff has a long shelf life open or not. I have gotten away from buying liquid broth, and while I still buy semi solid base, this powder is really flavorful. It has actually become my GO TO, rather than desperation bullion (normally I really dont like bullion, but I love this). Yum yum. I even use it to make a quick sipping broth. Sometimes a hot broth just hits the spot. Or I take some left overs and toss in some of this to make a quick broth/soup bowl.

title: decent caramel flavor, very sweet as usual
text:
I have a love hate relationship with Jordan's Skinny Syrups. They are really sweet and sometimes the flavor takes a backseat. Yet, I do rely on these syrups to flavor up some drinks and foods, so I find myself buying this brand regularly. I like being able to buy what I want as I need it from Amazon, over buying direct from their website (annoying expectation to buy lots of bottles at once to get shipping reduction, and sale prices or discounts dont count toward that, so I always spend too much at once, and get way too much at once). SO, I now always buy from Amazon.

Caramel is nice in coffee, hot cocoa, some teas, smoothies, even on ice cream (though a little liquidy), hot oats, etc. I prefer their Keto versions (different sweetener used, flavor often more pronounced) but their regular stuff is good too (it is sweetened with sucralose--very sweet).

title: good brand, good product, store open bag in fridge for freshness longevity
text: Good size container, I like the smaller bags. I prefer already ground flax but it has higher propensity to go rancid if not stored well. So once open, store this in fridge. Even try to use up unopened bags sooner over later. For longer term storage, whole seeds are better. Then just keep a grinder on hand (can even be a basic pepper grinder) for grinding them as needed. Big fan of Bob's Red Mill products, and I try to buy from this brand when the price is good.

title: excellent pantry staple for all sorts of cooking, baking needs
text: I go through a lot of oats. Whether it be oatmeal, or use in meatballs, meatload, non meat "loafs", muffins, cookies, and baked oatmeal bars. Bob's Redmill has good products, so I try to pick up this brand when the price is right. Always a good pantry staple.

title: big tub, great addition to pantry, longer term storage (even w/ shorter best buy date)
text: It's a big tub of peanut butter. I got it on sale, so I anticipated a short "best by" date. Also, I am noticing this on a lot of foods in general from any location. Anyway, I acquired this in 04/2022 with a late May 2022 date. Again, this was expected (from warehouse). Main thing is that it wasn't one of the recalled Skippy peanut butter lots. It isn't (phew). Will be put into rotation sooner over later, but it will be fine for a long time unopened. Glad to add it to my pantry.

title: go for it, nice garlic flavor, super fine powder for use in everything
text: This is garlic powder. I know the term "powder" is used to mean anything not in whole food form, but know that this is fine powder. If you like it chunkier, go with granulated. Sometimes that is called, granulated garlic powder (to add to confusion). But yeh, this is a fine powder. Really nice for all garlic needs, but especially so for dusting at the end of meal preparation (or for some applications like popcorn, etc), or for use on table. I love the garlicky taste, and I use garlic in everything.. so I go through a lot. This McCormicks is at a good price point for good quality.

title: good brand, good price, multi box makes nice quick addition to pantry staples
text: Good brand, cooks up well. Makes a great addition to pantry. Can't ever have too much pasta. 8 boxes of spaghetti packed into 1 larger branded box. Even though I find most spaghetti to be the same, I do notice that Barilla is a better brand. Though I really dont care when it comes down to it. I bought this because it was a good price, even relative to prices in store. Since food shortage is a thing, I figured I would impulse buy this just in case. Low price (and good brand) was a determining factor, otherwise I dont think I have ever purchased basic spaghetti online before.

title: well packaged, long shelf life, great addition to pantry for anyone, including (esp!) pets
text: I was able to get this on sale a little cheaper here than I normally can find in the store. It may sound odd,yet some of you may relate, but I use baby food myself. I like the fruits and vegetables for smoothies and baking (and oats, and over yogurt), I like some of the cereals to bulk up my oats and smoothies, and I adore many of the snacks as low cal healthy munching. As for the meats, I really dont use those myself, BUT I have 3 cats, 2 dogs, and the baby food comes in handy as meal toppers, treat puzzle goodie, and for some of my (prior-RIP) extra geriatric kitties, I could get them to eat by spooning out a little baby food for them. So it's just habit to keep an assortment of baby foods on hand. I go for turkey, chicken, or beef. (also makes a quick gravy, just saying). I guess I can even share if I knew someone who had littles.

title: excellent pantry staple, long shelf life, good flavor for cooking, no problems
text: Good ghee, good price. No problems. I think the little bit of added salt is nice. This sits out fine on my counter, or can be stored in fridge (but not needed). Ghee has a long shelf life, and so I always keep a couple containers on hand just in case. Makes a good long term pantry item. I always find ghee to have a slightly funny taste so I never just eat it, but I do use it in cooking and some baking. Keep in mind that ghee is solid at room temp- soft not hard. The warmer it is, the more soft it can become.

title: easy comfort food
text: Simple comfort food! Sometimes I just want some shells and cheese, and I I find velveeta tastes the best to me. I really dont care for the powder stuff, and I rarely bother to make my own, so the liquid cheesey stuff rocks my world. I may have it 2-3x a year. I just keep a few boxes on hand for when the mood strikes. Sometimes I stretch it by adding in extra pasta. Looks like an extra good deal can be had with a larger order, and subscribe and save.

title: good natural sweetness, doesnt spike blood sugar, use more to get same sweetness as sugar
text:
One of the few sugar alternatives that do not raise blood sugar levels (actually can be helpful to diabetics and those doing Keto diets). I see this being used more and more in sugar blends, and it is the first time I am trying it on its own. It isn't a 1:1 replacement. It is about 70% as sweet. Plan to use a little more of this than you normally would table sugar. The going adjustment seems to be 1 1/3 cup allulose for 1 cup table sugar. Adjust accordingly to your own preferences.

A natural sweetener; it is a rare sugar that can only be found in a few plant-based foods like jackfruit, figs, raisins, maple syrup and wheat. Even so, if totally new to it, start low and slow. People digest sugars and such differently, so too much at once may promote a little digestive distress. But that is temporary, and again usually only if in big quantity when first trying it. But that's just my two cents on it.

Big bag makes for good bulk pricing. Bargain if you go through a lot or intend to share.

title: easy to drink smooth, balanced medium (and I prefer extra dark, bold!), I am enjoying it.
text:
We all have different coffee preferences, so this is simply a matter of trying. I tend to prefer very strong, bold, dark roast coffee, but I am open to a smooth medium so long as it isnt acidic, bright, tart, green tasting (some mediums lean too light). If it is a dark leaning medium then I am more likely to enjoy it. This Butter-Nut coffee is an easy, middle of the road medium and I am enjoying it A LOT.

It is SMOOTH, balanced, and all around pleasant. I determine whether I really like it or not based on whether I can drink it black or not. I prefer my coffee black, but if the coffee is acidic/bright/tart/bitter then I find I can mellow it out with cream. I CAN drink this black, it is quite lovely as is. Yet, also holds up well to cream (oat milk); the coffee taste still comes through. I really think anyone could drink this, just depends on how much coffee to water you use, brewing style, etc. Does it remind me of grocery store stuff? I dont know. I normally buy various brands online. I either like it, or I dont. I like this. I'd buy again, I would recommend. It doesn't necessarily stand out above other coffees, I do have some brands I prefer, but I have ZERO problems with this. Also-- I noticed it powered up my day, and I may have had too much as I didnt sleep well. Sign of good coffee? haha

Love the metal can. That's a keeper.

title: good taste, pairs best with fruits, or vanilla base, gentle on stomach, makes me feel good all day
text:
After trying (and totally loving) the Living Essential Foods [[ASIN:B09SGTF2GW Cacao Immunity Smoothie powder]] I set out to try them all. While I still prefer any of their cacao based powders, this Superfood smoothie powder is pretty good too. I prefer it as a base to a fruit smoothie. I like adding in banana and blueberries, and/or strawberries. Just seems to pair best with fruits. I add in non dairy milk and sometimes a couple other supplements. I may or may not buy this one again, but I will (and have) purchased their cacao based powders (just really hits the spot).

What I like about any of them are the ingredients and overall nutritional profile. I always feel good when I have consumed any of them, and I don't know how to describe it.. it just feels right when I make myself a serving. My stomach is happy, my hunger is satisfied (or I pair it with a super healthy meal), I feel good through the day. Not many servings, but i dont need to drink it daily. Usually 2-3x per week, and I do other smoothies remainder of says. Seems to be working out well for me.

title: Essential Living Foods have such good powders, love them all especially cacao based powders
text:
I really like the Essential Living Foods products. I have tried 4 varieties, and I like them all. However, I like their chocolate based ones the best--tthis and their [[ASIN:B09SGTF2GW Cocao Immunity blend]]. Really makes me feel good when I drink it. I love making it with some frozen banana, non dairy milk, and then sometimes other supplements added in. Not many servings ( 9 in this, 4 in the other), but I realllllllly like these powders. So I buy them when I can. If I dont drink them daily, I usually drink them 2-3x per week. SO GOOD.

The other two kinds I have are the [[ASIN:B01I429HWC Superfood Immunity]] which is best mixed with fruit, or add in your own cacao. I also like their [[ASIN:B07WPX1P1M Matcha Vanilla powder]] for something different. I try to drink a lot of matcha, and I find I like it best as part of a smoothie. This is nice too. But it is the chocolate based ones that really rock my world. Love it.

title: love the soft texture, good mouth feel, surprisingly good taste (expected bad as per reviews)
text:
I got mine on sale, not sure if I would buy again at full price. I am pleasantly surprised by the taste and texture. A little thicker, heartier than a pop tart. More moist directly out from package. Good mouth feel. Not too strong on protein or sweetener taste. Ever so slight cooling effect from erythritol.

I am not keto, not really on any diet, but I do try to reduce my sugar. I look for items that are less likely to trigger a binge. Finding lower sugar items helps a lot. I dont want to totally avoid sweet foods, but I dont want to feel compelled to eat a whole box of something because the sugar triggered me. This tasty pastry is indeed tasty to me. I have had all sorts of keto/diabetic/no sugar snack foods and most fall short. Very few actually taste good to me. This Legendary Cake Style Brown Sugar Cinnamon pastry actually hits the spot, doesnt have too many calories, and actually has fiber. I dont necessarily need all that protein, but it contains both fast absorbing protein and medium absorption protein- so body has some quick access protein and has some that takes longer to burn through, helping us to feel fuller longer. Fiber sure helps too.

I have grabbed these to go with my morning coffee, as a mid day snack, and as an after dinner dessert (not all in same day!). Good direct from package or warmed up.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. I find these way pricy. We'll see. I kinda do want more, haha!

title: lifts the fog, SF BAY coffee always makes a good cuppa for me
text: My favorite coffees are SF Bay Dark Italian Blend and this Fog Chaser. I love strong dark, bold coffees (their Italian Blend) or a dark leaning medium which is what this Fog Chaser is. Smooth, tasty, gives me energy. Tastes great black, and also holds up well to some cream. I normally go for the Italian Roast, but the Fog Chaser was on sale, and since I knew I liked it already I figured I would get it. Does not disappoint.

title: trusty stand by for very healthy shelf stable bread, high protein is a little off tasting
text:
I have been a consumer of these German breads on and off since childhood. Definitely an acquired taste, or should I say texture. These shelf stable breads are dense, moist, and are best (to me) simply toasted and buttered (or dairy, non dairy, nut butters, etc). I like it for smashed avocado toast, but not so much as a regular sandwich bread. Does better as an open face sandwich bread. Once the package is opened, it is best if it is stored in fridge and used up soon.

As for this particular variety-- carrot, it has a nearly neutral carrot taste; hint of carrot. There is another flavor that comes through that is not bad, but makes me less likely to buy it again. I think it is the fact that this is one of their high protein varieties. I normally just go with the regular stuff, and this is my first time trying the high protein kind. I love all the ingredients, but there is a pronounced protein taste. I will definitely use these packages up, then next time I will simply choose one of my usual varieties. Very healthy bread that has been around forever.

title: strawberry, apple, and chia is perfect combo, great taste & texture, all around perfection MMM!
text:
Strawberry, Apple, & Chia instantly became my favorite pressed fruit bar. SO GOOD. Really exceeded my expectations, and I already think KIND bars are really good quality. Dense, chewy, sweet, natural. Appeals to my hunger as well as my appetite. My sweet tooth is happy too. I have enjoyed it direct from package in its entirety, or have nibbled on it over the course of day. I have also tried it broken up over hot oats. MMMM!

Pricey though :( But if they go on sale, I will sure to buy more.

title: Loose slop, reminds me of canned "corned beef hash" w/o potatoes. If you like that, then try this.
text:
Hmm, I took a chance on this despite what a lot of negative reviews shared. It really isnt so bad if you keep your expectations low. This isnt not a can full of sausages (they need to take that out of description), NOR is it a sausage that can be formed into anything, well maybe if carefully mixed with some eggs (and maybe bread crumbs or oats) to bind it and other goodies. Only then it can be made into a patty of the sort. BTW, this is already COOKED. That alone should tell you that is will not just form a patty, so stop expecting it to. It would have to be raw--before the fat had rendered. At best, it would only be crumbles.

Out of the can just heated up? It's loose meat. And you know what? What it 100% reminds me of is CORNED BEEF HASH, without the potato cubes. Or sausage hash (this uses chicken and pork). If you have had that, then you know that the consistency is just like slop. A bizarrely delicious slop. Not a go to item but it adds variety to a pantry, to camping supplies, to emergency pantry.

I really dont mind this at all. Great addition to my preps and for times I want to make add extra "meat" (lol) to a can of hash, or can grab a can of potatoes (or grab a potato) and make a quick hash. Or use it to flavor something. Just know it has a canned corned beef hash vibe. I'd even consider sharing this with my labs, but the sodium content is high. I will instead stick with their 100% pork that I keep in preps for them [[ASIN:B0769534WZ just pork cooked in can]]

Anyway, I wont stock pile this stuff, but it is a welcome addition to my pantry, and I plan to buy some more. It is really not that bad!

Edit to fix typos, and to say that I though this was worth it when it was around $13 for the pack (march & april 2022), even $15. But now it jumped to $34 in a matter of a couple of days? Unless desperate, no. I know canned meat has jumped significantly, but yeesh. Rating stays same because I dont rate on price.

title: Just peel, pulp, seeds and juice of organic Nordic apples. Excellent addition to pantry
text:
I use all sorts of freeze dried fruit and vegetable powders, but somehow I have never bothered with apple. Maybe because I eat fresh apples daily, they tend to be easy to come by, and are usually budget friendly. But still, I am surprised that I haven't at least tried it before. And so here I am. I have been extra diligent about adding to my panty, and making a point to have a wide variety of freeze dried foods and food powders. Not sure what the next couple of years will be like, and I dont want to worry about finding my usual food items or even basic food items.

What drew me to this is that it uses the WHOLE apple, and nutrition is greatly retained. I like having the assurance that if I cant get to store, or if supplies are low, that I can still reap the benefit of shelf stable options.

In my experience, and it is true of this as well, is that it does well when mixed with a little warm water. It helps the clumps to break down, and reduce grittiness. Then from there I use it in whatever- baking, oats, smoothies, yogurt. It is pleasant tasting- freeze dried can reduce some flavors, and enhance others. I find it plenty sweet with a hint of tart. Very good (to me).

ONLY ONE INGREDIENT: Organic apples – and nothing else. You’ll get all the nutrient-packed goodness of the peel, pulp, seeds and juice of organic Nordic apples. Nothing added, nothing artificial, organically grown

title: shelf stable protein for meatless dishes or to make meat dishes stretch (ie 50/50)
text:
I like Anthony's products, so when I was looking to add TVP to my pantry, I decided to just go with this brand--didnt even shop around. Textured protein crumbles take on other flavors, so it really makes for a nice "meaty" mouth feel if you want that vibe without actually using meat. I am not vegan or vegetarian, but I enjoy incorporating a lot of plant based options into my life, or even to cut into a meat dish (ie use a little ground meat, and use this to flesh it out, so to speak). I also like to make sure I have shelf stable options. I dont use soy products too often (thyroid issues), but I do incorporate them.

These crumbles work well in chili, "meat" sauces, and even work well as part of a non meat hamburger, meatball, meatloaf base.

Good amount of food from this bag. Get a good amount of protein and fiber. Main thing for me is the shelf stable aspect. No need to have something take up space in my fridge or freezer. With rising prices and lower availability, I want to make sure I still have options when I want them. Basic TVP such as this is a must have for me.

title: excellent quality, must have for working pantry, and long term pantry/preps
text:
I highly recommend Judees products. Might pay a little more than some companies, but I have always had top notch experience with this line of products from Ohio, USA. Also, you can be assured that the products are coming from DEDICATED nut free, gluten free facilities. That's a big deal for some folks, and I am glad that a quality company caters to these needs. I have no allergies or sensitives, thankfully. I just want a product I can rely on. So Judee's is my go-to for pantry items like this. I even have my mom on board.

The milk is really really good- tastes like milk, and not the usual powdered milk I use. I dont even drink cow milk, let alone whole milk, but I find great value in keeping powdered milk on hand for various cooking, baking, or SHTF needs. I try to stock whole milk powder because I can always water it down. Also whole milk works better in baking, cooking. Since I dont buy cow milk (but rarely) being able to have some cow milk on demand is fantastic. I can just make up what I need, at any consistency, and there is no waste.

When it comes to stuff like this, I buy the largest amount I can afford. Since much of it is shelf stable, I can either tuck it away, OR I can break it down into smaller storable sizes using simple mason jars, or mylar bags. I plan to share this bag with my mom (unless she has already put in an order, ha).

title: good color, taste, pliability
text:
I had great success with their red fondant, and now i have the black. Same quality, taste, durability, and pliability. I'll definitely buy more in other color offerings, especially since they carry various sizes.

This is some nice fondant. I see that they have two sizes. I have the smaller pack, and it is perfect for my creative needs. Once in awhile I want to make a good looking cupcake, mini cake, or cookie, and this is all the size I need. If working larger, they have larger size available. Small pack takes up nearly no space in my baking cupboard. The fondant is durable and pliable, and tasty. Love a nice vanilla flavor. This is good, color is good, no concerns.
