title: good brand that has been around a long time, traditional powder contains aluminum
text:
Good price, very effective. Must have addition to pantry staples, or just buy it for long term storage. Just so you know, this does contain aluminum. I usually use the aluminum free varieties, but as I was looking to shore up my long term food storage supplies, the price was right for this size and style, and I figured.. why not.

For those down rating because it contains aluminum.. you can see the ingredient list in the pictures. That is on you. Quick tip: all (as far as I know) aluminum free baking soda will specifically state that it is aluminum free.

title: great addition to pantry when juice or fruit aren't in stock
text:
Lime fruit powder is as expected- citrusy and lends limey flavor to drinks and dishes. Mix a little with water (I do warm) to get it to dissolve, then add it to whatever. Works nice in making a lime flavored simple syrup (that's the first thing i did with this). Mmm.

I dont often need lime juice for flavoring, so I either buy some and end up tossing a mostly unused container, or I dont have any on hand. Fresh fruit often looks sad in the store, or I totally forget to buy any. Not sure why I didnt think of trying lime powder before. I have lime leaf in my pantry, but that is totally different. But it didnt occur to me to buy lime fruit powder. Really a game changer.

title: tasty, chewy, delicious. Add to pantry, preps, hiking bag, on the go. So yummy
text: Really good, really expensive. Chewy, tasty, delicious. Totally love the pineapple- eat as is or chunk it up and add it to something. Nice pantry item or on the go item. Bought on sale, but a tad pricy for regular purchase. Curious to try other flavors. Looks good, and if the price looks good to you then I recommend this brand.

title: lovely oil for use in everything, so very versatile, will buy again
text:
Mild taste that works well with everything and anything. I even found that it makes an awesome base to homemade "sub oil". Lovely for use in salads, and just about anything else one needs oil for. I bought this after seeing it recommended along with sesame oil for healthy blood pressure. Its become my go to oil as of late.

Yes, it is refined and says so on the bottle in the picture .No surprises here.

title: blah flavor, but spectacular nutrition. Add as base to nutritious broth bowl/quick soup
text:
I have the Beef and Mushroom, it has a very bland taste. I love the nutritional profile though, so I do find value in it. Pricy though! It dissolves well in hot water. Just have to pop the gel disk out from the holder. Directions say to use 8 ounces of water. Has a luscious silky mouth feel, as all good bone broths have. So I dont doubt the quality. However, again this is bland, and at first I thought it had no salt added because I cant taste any, this does have 340 mg of sodium per cup.

So if you want a quick bland sipping broth, go for it. Feels good on stomach. I like to use it as a base to a quick soup/broth bowl. Often I grab some random ingredients from fridge and add it to broth. For example, I had some left over broccoli, some left over quinoa & kale mix, and some pumpkin puree that needed to be used up. I add all that in with this broth, added a little more water, some added spices (turmeric, black pepper, sea salt), and then proceeded to enjoy an extra nutritious broth bowl.

For the price, I wish there was more per pack. I do like this, I would consider more flavors, but the price is prohibitive at this time. I dont rate on price (we all have different budgets, needs, values, prices fluctuate--especially now--, and so on). $14.95 / 4= $3.74 per cup. Better price with the 12 pack ($3.32 per cup).

Quality: 5 stars
Taste: it's blah, 3 stars
Overall.. I do like it, like the way I feel, and I use this more for the nutrition.. which seems good. 4 stars

title: something for everyone, excellent quality, taste is pleasant enough, loaded w/ nutrition
text:
When it comes to taste, take a look at all the nutritional goodies contained in this formula and it is rather impressive that they pulled off a neutral, pleasant tasting nutrition drink. Light vanilla, lightly sweet. Best cold, works as a creamer in coffee, use it as a base to a smoothie (depending on your nutritional needs), or of course.. drink as is.

As I become more familiar with Kate Farms nutrition drinks, I become more impressed. The formulas have similar ingredients but in different amounts- as seen in the macro and micro nutrients. I think it is wonderful to have a product line that someone can choose from based on their situation. You are getting assurance if you have a condition you dont want to exacerbate, yet I see nothing that would be harmful if you dont have the condition/situation it targets. Just depends on your needs. Worth checking out!

I originally became aware of this brand when I was looking for a truly low sugar meal replacement option that did not use artificial sweeteners or even stevia. I found that with [[ASIN:B09QFP9BR7 Kate Farms Glucose Support]]. While the taste is "ok" on that one (I still recommend it), I think this Renal Support is a little better. More vanilla comes through, or it could be because it is a little sweeter (again no artificial sweeteners). Also love that it is plant based protein, no soy. Easy on the stomach.

--Taste: 4 stars (my tastes buds have changed or this is actually better to me than the glucose formula, which I rated 3 stars in taste-- 3 stars means its "ok". This tastes better to me)
--Formula: 5 stars lots of goodies, decent nutrition profile, normally I would down rate for that much sodium, but this is a renal formula and I am not sure what amount is good. I trust they know.
--Overall: 4.5/5 stars. While I may not get this particular formula for myself again, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this brand, and so I do.

title: my favorite blackstrap molasses, has deep caramel-like taste, super dark, intense
text:
My favorite blackstrap molasses for use in coffee, over ice cream, oatmeal, and for recipes when I want intense sweetness at the forefront. It has a deep dark caramel-like flavor, not a tangy flavor like some blackstrap (and all regular). This is special. Super black, super thick and slow flowing. Absolutely adore it by the spoonful. I cant do that with other molasses, which isnt to say those are bad. I happen to keep a variety of molasses on hand for different uses. Most are fine for use in basic recipes and sauces. I just like this specific one for off the spoon consumption (or as mentioned above, in coffee, oats, even on ice cream).

Came packaged really well!

title: versatile young jackfruit for meatless, low cal, high fiber options. Artichoke like taste plain
text:
I like jackfruit. I am not vegan or vegetarian, but I try to incorporate a lot of plant based meals into my life. I have been eating jackfruit on and off for years, just depends on pricing. I very recently bought this for $10, and I came back to buy more but saw that it has increased over 100% in price. Nope. I dont rate on price, so if this looks good to you go for it.

edit 08/2022: LMAO-- and I just saw it went up again--up 400% to nearly $50 HAHAHAH, nah, I'll wait. That's around $10 PER POUND. jfc..

Canned jackfruit is easier, stores longer. I may go back to that. This is a big pack that will need to be used up quickly or repackaged and stored. It will freeze fine. Or go ahead and do your own canning with it.

I soak it, then marinade it. The go to recipe for anyone new to using jackfruit is "pulled pork". It really works well in that manner as the mouth feel is nearly the same. These chunks are bigger and tougher than a lot of canned versions, so I will be trying this as a "stew". Can be tossed in slow cooker for "pulled pork" texture too.

Jackfruit is nice as a meat replacer, and/or as a means to take in volume without all the calories that go with it. Lots of fiber per serving, super low calories, modest amount of protein. I think jackfruit is worth trying at least once, and if you can find some good ways to use it you will then likely want to continue with it. BTW, young jackfruit is not sweet. That is what is used in meat replacement. Young jackfruit has a neutral, almost artichoke/olive taste. I like it, and it seems to take on other flavors very well.

I down rate only because my bag came with zero labeling. Just a bag of jackfruit. I hope this is accidental and not the norm.

title: love robust tasting olive oil, good price, good quality, will buy again
text: Got this at a good price. Makes nice addition to pantry. We go through a lot of olive oil, and I tend to like the more robust flavors when I can get them. Mild stuff is easy enough to find, but finding olive oil with some robust flavor (lightly peppery) can be tricky (or I spend a whole lot more). While perfect for salads and marinades (becuase of the flavor), it can be used in anything, for anything so long as you like the tase. I use it when I make my own vegetable/plant based "butter". I still use dairy butter, but I find I can get more bang for my buck making a creamy vegetable oil based butter (add in sunflower lecithin for added creaminess).

title: versatile condiment for anything & everything, nice tonkatsu style sauce
text: Versatile condiment. I figured it would closely resemble some Tonkatsu sauces we keep on hand, and I find that accurate. I think this has a little more punch in taste that I find to be very appealing. It can really be used on anything- just sort of a sweet, savory, spicy ketchup/BBQ-esque sauce. I plan to make okonomiyaki soon, which I expect this to be amazing on. And it will work as a topper for meatloaf, burgers, to dip fries, add to noodle bowls,

title: super sweet, low ginger taste, more ale than beer, blown out bottoms on 5 of 10
text:
Really sweet, likely best for use in alcoholic beverages where the added sweetness will be mellowed out. But as a simple sipping ginger beer, it is really quite cloying. If it were less sweet and had a stronger ginger taste I would like it a lot more. Really the sweetest and most mellow ginger beer I have had. For me, I taste sweet first, and too mellow of a ginger taste, then a lingering coating of sugar on my tongue well after. I want it more robust, and I can get that in other brands. All comes down to preference, as this might be just the thing for you. Small cans are perfect for home bar use. Moscow mules, baby.

5 out of 10 of my cans were blown out on the bottom. I assume it is from fluctuation in temperature conditions, with it freezing at some point. I dont know. It isnt bothersome enough to keep me from drinking it, but it keeps it from sitting upright. I have to set them upside down. I am drinking the blown out ones first. Taste fine.

Giftable if one could be assured that the cans were in good condition. I like the way the product looks.

title: gourmet spicy has slight kick of heat, nice texture, creative flavor profile. I really like it.
text: Just add water and oil. I love when I get a mix and not need to add a long list of extra ingredients. I'm always down for trying a new flavor profile, and this Gourmet Spicy pancake mix option really intrigued me. At first I was like, no way! Then I thought, well why not? I made up a serving, and was delighted by the overall taste and texture. That hint of spice really makes it for me. It got me thinking of uses well beyond that of a "pancake". Or of different pairings to go alongside it. But as they already did the creative part, I am also totally good with a plain pancake with a little butter. I think it is worth the try. Saw that this has a coupon at the moment, so I am buying another of the same.

title: smooth, very convenient, no fuss no waste, add more or less water to taste & preferred consistency
text:
This tastes like coconut as it is derived from coconut milk. How strong the flavor of coconut depends on water to powder ratio (more water, less coconut flavor, thinner consistency; or less water, more coconut flavor, thicker consistency). Coconut milk powder is a shelf stable product made from unsweetened coconut milk that’s been dehydrated. When the milk is dehydrated, what’s left is a concentrated powder. Makes for excellent pantry and preps staple.

This coconut milk powder appears to contain additional ingredients (organic acacia fiber, organic tapioca maltodextrin) that prevent the powder from clumping when stored, as well as to help the powder dissolve, thicken, or emulsify when mixed with water. Basically giving back the creamy mouth feel expected from coconut milk.

I use coconut milk all the time (the wonderful canned stuff, and the mediocre refrigerated carton stuff). I am most interested in using this powder in applications like I would use the canned stuff. If you use that already, then you know how pricy it is per can, and how most recipes dont call for a whole can so it is an added chore to use it up in something else quickly. This powder can help stretch my coconut milk budget by just making up what I need without fuss or waste.

I dont care for it as a creamer, but I am not a fan of coconut milk in my coffee anyway. I love coconut, just not in that. I like it as a light milk to drink, or as a thicker milk cream in recipes (so rich, so versatile, but must love coconut). Now that I think of it (mind blown), this is going to save me space in the fridge too. I use unsweetened almond or coconut milk in my daily smoothies. I dont get to the store regularly enough and I use it often enough that I usually keep 2-4 cartons on hand. Well, that's a lot of space! I dont even need to make this up before I add it to smoothy. I can just add some water and a scoop of this along with my other ingredients. Game changer.

I like it enough that I am already looking to buy more. I saw that there are a couple of brands that are a little cheaper, and some that are more pricy, but this seems to fall within a tight range of reasonable. Since I know i like it, I will likely just go with it again. I had tried a "creamer" of same ingredients that I found to be clumpy and gritty. This is not, I find it smooth. So for that 5 stars.

title: mmm coffee & chocolate- fun sampler, good size, nice treat for self or others
text: Really nice sampler of coffee and chocolate with description cards that I find appealing not only for myself, but also as a potential gift. The box is sturdy and well packed, but the weird sticker that says "this is a pretti box" is just confusing if you dont know that the brand is "Pretti & Luxe". Maybe rebox if you are gift giving. No problems to note. Quite a delight!

title: must have for working pantry, and prepper pantry, adds so much flavor, budget friendly
text:
This is really good! I took a chance on "tomato bouillon with chicken flavor" (3 big containers at that!) not really sure what to expect. I already love the KNORR chicken bouillon, and beef bouillon. So why not?! Also, its the end of the world and mind as go out with a flavorful bang. lol. Seriously though, this stuff (all varieties) are budget friendly, versatile, and super tasty. I sort of stumbled upon this brand of bouillon when my usual go-to doubled in price. I already have excess in my pantry (and good prepper does), but I was close to needing to get into that, so I started looking to repurchase. I saw the Knorr options, and as someone who already likes a lot of Knorr stuff I gave it all a try. I figured at worst, it was extra for emergency, or at best I found my new go to product. Suprise surprise, it is now my go to product. All are good, and the addition of this tomato variety is great. It is very versatile. I find myself using the chicken all the time, followed by this, then the beef. I have purchased them here on Amazon, as well as wallmarty. Pretty good price no matter where I find it.

How I use this tomato bouillon: my first use was when I made a simple cabbage and lentil dish. I cut up an onion and browned it with some bacon fat. Added garlic. Then added some chicken broth (left over water from simmering boneless chicken breasts, so kind of mild in taste), then added tomato paste. Got that simmering then added cut up cabbage, can of diced tomatoes, 2 cans stewed tomatoes, some uncooked rice and uncooked lentils. Added more water and a healthy spoonful of this bouillon. Got it to boil, then turned temp back and covered. Let it all similar until everything was tender. Added water as needed. Is a dish that can have less broth or more broth depending on preference. Added more bouillon to taste. Other spices to taste. Really just added a depth of flavor and saltiness that was perfect. Another time was used to make a simple pasta sauce (included tomato paste-- basically softned some onions, garlic, added some olive oil, tomatoe paste, water, this bouillon, and some other spices. Simmer. Done.). Lastly, as a sipping broth, or as a quick soup. Got some left overs? I love putting them all into a bowl (maybe a little grain, a little veg, little pasta or protein..) then add hot water and some of this bouillon and voila -- a quick soup or "broth bowl: that looks and tastes extra fancy.

So stop hemming and hawing, and just buy this. YUM.

title: unsweetened coconut & almond creamer. Coconut forward, almond settles into background
text:
Coconut forward, it will definitely make your coffee taste like coconut. Good balance though, as the almond simmers it down a bit, yet the almond doesn't poke through. I tend to find that almond milk ruins my coffee (even though I like it for everything else), so I took a chance on this because of my favorable impression of other Califia products. It's good. Just have to like coconut.

Thay being said, it isn't as creamy as their [[ASIN:B07PBFNYXV Unsweetened Barista Blend Oat Milk]], which is very creamy and has a neutral taste that works well in my coffee. I love it, maybe too much.. haha.. as I keep buying it. I prefer my coffee black, but when I have some of their oat milk in my fridge, I cant help but grab for that. In comparison, I am not grabbing for this coconut & almond blend. It isnt bad, it just isnt quite doing it for me. I use it when I make one of my weird, slightly off putting coffee blends (my 2nd coup of coffee is used as a vehicle for some supplements. If I dont want to make a real smoothie, I use my coffee to put it all into. That makes for some strange flavors. This creamer helps mask some of it, and helps give it some normal flavor).

I love that it is shelf stable until opened, so it is a welcome addition to my pantry and preps. Also works in a pinch for smoothies and other food preparations that could use some coconut/almond milk. Nothing bad that I can see. Really like this brand, so try some stuff out until you find a perfect match. For me, it is the barista blend I linked to.

title: BEST pumpkin puree I've ever had, & I've had a lot. Sweet, smooth, good to eat on its own!
text:
WOW! OUTSTANDING! Now this is pumpkin puree. Purely smooth, rich..really tastes like pumpkin. I normally just buy whatever is available. Sometimes it is super cheap stuff, sometimes mid priced. All pretty much taste the same to me. Some are more dry, some are more wet. The watery kinds can be great for smoothies. The more dry is better for baking. I wasn't sure what to expect with this brand because all the reviews had me thinking I would open a can of watery mess.

Opened the can, it looked.. moist. Not watery. The watery kinds look like pumpkin puree and water blended together. This has a deep color, very very smooth texture, and the puree is dense. Any liquid is clearly just pumpkin "juice". It is THE BEST pumpkin I have had. WHY IS IT SO GOOD???? I have had other organic brands too. It might come down to what kind of pumpkin is used? This is AMAZING. Like, i can eat it by the spoonful plain, amazing. It just has this natural sweetness that I dont ever notice in other brands (Aldi, Clover Valley, store brands, Libby, Full Circle Organic, other organics I cant recall). This is flippin' delicious! I really do wonder if it comes down to type of pumpkin variety used. This is just overly good.

All my cans look good (no dents), has plenty of time on it in terms of expiration. This is my new favorite pumpkin brand. I really didnt know that pumpkin puree could taste this good. Right now I have been using it on hot oats- adds a bit of sweetness on top of all the other good nutrtion it has to offer. Glad I finally came around to trying this brand. I originally wanted to get some canned squash puree and this was the brand I booked marked. I tried the pumpkin because it was on sale. Now that I know this is the best ever, I will try other products from them. All a tad pricy, but I dont rate on price anyway.

title: good enough oats for me, no problems concerns. I'd buy again
text:
I think they are fine. 5 stars not because they are better, but because they meet my expectations. I wanted a couple of smaller containers for my pantry. Figured time to stock up. Been going through an oats craving, so it was on my mind to buy more. I dont get to the store that often, so i thought this size and price was reasonable for not having to leave my couch. The two tubs I bought are fine, but one had its security wrap slipping off--likely during shipment. Another jostle and it would have been all over the box.

Taste and texture is yummy. I am not all that picky. I tend to load it up with some chopped apples, pecans, and a little vanilla yogurt.

Prices are fluctuating a lot, so my general approach in reviews is to not rate on price. We all have different budgets, needs, accessibility, and with current inflation and shortages it may be a matter of getting what you can based on what you have to work with.

title: cure for everything but death. Just take it and enjoy the benefits
text:
Black cumin seed oil is a must have for me for general health, and for times I need the extra boost. With its intense thyme taste, it is not a pleasant tasting oil, but it works so well. Tastes so strong that I will often forgo it, but once I turn to it again, I am reminded of how truly an amazing supplement this is. I add some to water and quickly chug. I imagine there are culinary uses, but I dont bother. I just take a couple of teaspoons and be done with it. Much easier to work with than actual black cumin seeds.

Black cumin seed oil is known as "The cure for everything but death". I believe it. Give it a try. I find most to be the same, and this brand has a very good look to it. Dark glass bottle, well sealed, 100% USDA organic, cold pressed, non GMO. Acquired in 03/2022 with expiry date of 03/01/2025

title: for the unfamiliar- less is more, wickedly putrid but lends magical taste when done right
text:
It's been a very long time since I worked with heeng (or hing), so long that it is like using it for the first time all over again. You dont forget your first time. If you are not familiar with this, then you may want to educate yourself first. It is not for the weak or wary. LOL. Read on for my description..

I think I used weaker stuff before because I do not remember it being quite this potent. The teeny weeny pack (maybe 1-1.5 tablespoons?) is robust, and not much is needed. The crystals are big, I think I used flakes before. Just use 1 or 2 crystals (size of coarse salt or so) to start. That is likely more than enough for whatever you are creating.

Definitely a spice that needs to be used with a light hand, and as a way to enhance other flavors NOT as means to create a flavor in and of itself. Trust me, you do not want this to be the forward flavor (omg no, lol). Because you know what it tastes like on its own? how I imagine dirty feet, armpits, butt, rotting garlic and onions all mixed together would taste. It's fetid. Nearly putrid. Makes you wonder how something like this was even first discovered as something one wants to eat. BUT done right, it does absolutely magical things when combined with other spices, oils, and foods. Definitely for savory applications.

Be mindful of trying it by itself, as that is not the resulting flavor (and it will be a taste that lingers all night, and you will wonder if you are rotting).

High quality. Small amount that is actually a lot. Try it dissolved in ghee, add it to lentils (I'm always trying to find new ways to have my beloved lentils.)

A MUST HAVE once you get to know it. Just.. be easy on how much you use. Trust me.

title: creamy, sweet treat, hot or cold, reminds me a lot of BOBA tea base
text:
I like that it is instant. It is creamy and sweet. Reminds me a strongly of the powdered "tea" base for bubble/boba tea. Has that cloying sweetness and extra creaminess that those bases have. If you know what I mean (and like that) then you may very well like this. Nice hot, but it really shines over ice. Maybe add in some tapioca balls.

When made as instructed, it is definitely sweet. I feel like my tongue is coated a little with too much sweetness. I tend to feel this way with sweet drinks anyway, so it isnt a matter of this being all that different than drinks of this ilk. It is pleasant hot, but I like it A LOT over ice. Consider it a creamy sweet treat more so than a cup of tea.

The amount of water to use is about 3/4 cup. That isn't much. I can load a star bucks grande cup with ice, pour this over (hot), and it will fill 80% of cup. Not bad as far as a sweet afternoon treat. Part of me wants a stronger black tea taste, but overall I like it as is. Oddly, I think it would pair well with a cup of coffee. It is one of those teas that have a hybrid taste (kind of like yerba mate in that sense).

I enjoy cardamom a lot, and I can taste it fine. It has a low key (to me) taste of it- light punch of floral/citrus, but not over done. I may try this mixed in with a little extra black tea, or maybe I would use this as a creamer for coffee (or extra tea). I like it. I may or may not get it again, but I like it.

They also carry UNSWEETENED options.

title: smells, looks, tastes like my fresh grated dried turmeric root. LOVE Judees products
text: I use a lot of Judees products. Ive never had any problem with quality, freshness, or packaging, so it one of a few "go to" brands for products of this ilk. I use turmeric regularly in cooking, and sometimes I make "golden milk". I keep powder on hand as well as turmeric root that I have to grate/grind myself. I imagine there are nuances in turmeric, but for the most part I think they are all the same. So long as it is similar to how it tastes and looks compared to when I grate it myself, I consider it a 5 star product. So 5 stars here. Not because it is better that others but because it is the same. Also, I love Judees.

title: high quality assortment. Bag each of actual coffee, guayusa "tea", & cocao nibs
text:
Pack of 3, high quality beautiful products. Great contender as a gift, or as a treat for yourself. This assortment includes COFFEE, loose TEA, and COCAO NIBS.

COFFEE: has a dark leaning medium taste, yet has a few brighter notes. Not acidic. While I usually drink my coffee black, I prefer this with a generous amount of [[ASIN:B07PBFNYXV Califia Farms barista blend oat milk]] . Really smooths out the taste and allows the hint of chocolate to come through. Definitely a FOG LIFTER. This is actual medium roast coffee that needs to be brewed. I use it in a pour over system. I use a generous amount and so will likely get 4-5 "brews" from this pack. Says that the 3.5oz pack is ideal for 5 moka pot loads or 12 cups in regular brewer. Your mileage will vary. "High altitude grown 100% arabica from world's renowned region of Zamora"

TEA: loose leaf herbs, so more of a tisane? The base is comprised of yerba mate Guayusa leaves, lemon, ginger, cinnamon, and cardamom. It is robust! Brews up dark, has (to me) a balanced taste. No particular flavor is overpowering. I can pick up on notes of lemon, and a hint of cardamom and cinnamon. The ginger is far in the background. I'm not a huge tea drinker, but I enjoy a cup on occasion. I am currently drinking this hot, but as soon as I tasted it I figured it would be an incredible contender for iced tea. It is delightful. Also, I am terrible at making tea- usually I make it too strong or too weak, and something about this turned out just right. "Guayusa is a native tree that played an important role as the source of leaves to prepare an energetic drink compared to coffee, tea, and mate. Mixed with original and healthy spices like cardamom, ginger, citric fruits it gives you the boost of natural energy without making you anxious."

COCAO NIBS: 100% fermented cocao. Interesting addition to this pack, as I wont be drinking the nibs unless I grind them into powder first. But I always have nibs on hand due to their incredible nutrition. I love adding some to "smoothie bowls" or hot oats. Can of course be used in baking, or ground into powder, etc. No issues with quality here. Small pieces, light and crunchy. Intense dark chocolate flavor. I find these easier to bite into compared to some brands I have purchased. Very pleased with these. "Cocoa Nibs right from Cacao motherland Zamora-Chinchipe, Ecuador. Keeps you awake naturally without the need of black coffee or espresso shot"

There is a bullet point in the description that says, "Alternative to coffee and tea. Makes you wake all day long without stressing your nerves system". Well, the coffee is actual coffee (not an alternative!!), and while there is tea, the "tea" is from guayusa. That has (according to internet) about 90mg caffeine. So I think they are referring to the cocao nibs, which has caffeine but very low amount, and can give a little zip to your day, naturally. Hence why it is a smoothie bowl favorite.

Overall, I am just tickled with this assortment. It has been joy to use all of these. That will come down to personal preference, of course. However, the quality is up there, no doubt. Well done packaging. Well done, period. I'd buy this again, I would buy it for someone else.

title: worth the try, love the shrimp garlic taste- simple but explosive. Little goes long way--UMAMI!
text: Different than what I normally go for, but I have very open minded taste buds and enjoy expanding my taste options. I am shoring up my spices, keeping a wide variety. Never know if we'll be eating beans and rice for days on end, so mind as well have different flavors to switching things up. I am really intrigued by the taste of shrimp and garlic powder. Try the taste on mentally for size, and imagine the possibilities. Adding some to a simple pasta, or pasta and egg dish makes it taste fancy. If you eat anything and everything like I do, try it to season extra firm fried tofu. I keep tofu (of various sorts) on hand because I can get shelf stable varieties that work well to bulk up dishes without a lot of calories.

title: good tasty nooch fortified with B vitamins.
text: I love nooch. I am not vegan so I dont need them to be fortified, which these are. Get your B vitamins here! I usually buy non fortified. These are perfectly good for those seeking out good quality nutritional yeast (fortified). Save for a few, I tend to find that they all taste the same. My favorite use for nooch is sprinkled generously over pasta (and oil or butter, salt, pepper), or sprinkled lightly over my vegetables. Mmm mm. Just had this today on my broccoli (brunched on broccoli, sweet potato, sunflower seeds, nooch, and some cottage cheese).  I have had other products from this company, and all have been fine. I give this 5 stars because it meets my expectations.

title: light crunch, hint of salt, excellent on salads, yogurt, oats, etc
text:
I have been buying the Go Raw sprouted seeds on and off for years. Know that they are not roasted (because they are raw). These have a lighter crunch and snap over dense roasted seeds. Raw also imparts a lighter, more neutral flavor. Very lightly salted. Really nice flavor. I especially love these sunflower seeds for use on oats and salads. I also love their spicy fiesta seeds. I've only had good experience with this brand. You do you though.

Sometimes I buy them in store, but the past couple of years I have done mostly online shopping, so it is nice to find them for a reasonable price here.

title: creamy, neutral flavor, great in coffee or other "milk" applications
text:
If I am not using cow creamer (Nestle coffee mate creamer or half n' half), my go to plant based is oat creamer. As much as I use almond milk, and as much as I love cashew milk, coconut milk.. none of them taste right in coffee. They are best left for smoothies, and everything else but coffee. I otherwise never use cow milk.

This Califia Farms Oat Barista Blend is quite good. Very creamy, thanks to sunflower oil. On the rare occasion I make my own oat milk, to get a creamy taste and mouth feel the use of sunflower lecithin or sunflower oil is the key.

I havent tried frothing this, I just use a health splash in my coffee. I will use this in a pinch for any other milk or cream needs. It has a neutral taste. I think oat milk is the best milk for anyone who prefers cow milk but are open to plant based milks. It just has the best taste and mouth feel.

I'd buy it again. I got this from the warehouse where the expiration date may be a tad short. This pack of 6 was acquired 03/2022 with exp of 05/2022. Regular orders should have longer date.

title: TOASTED-- just look at that deep color. Wonderful aroma and bold flavor. PERFECTION!
text:
Ok, you win. This IS the best sesame oil. I kept sniffing around this brand, and would buy something else for a little (or a lot) cheaper. Now to clarify.. this does not directly say "toasted". But look at that deep dark color! THAT is toasted, roasted whatever my friends. Ingredients: "sesame seed oil". Then it says, "Kadoya Pure Sesame Oils brings ROASTED flavor by sprinkling to your meal such as ramen , Yakitori, & BBQ marinade sauce"

title: delightfully sweet treat, lovely soft chewy texture, like a moon pie 3 musketeer caramelly hybrid

THANK YOU

title: confectioners makes for quick maple frosting, lovely sprinkled on hot oats
text:
Love Judee's products. It is my go to brand, since everything I have used has been consistently of good quality and freshness. Their products and facilities are gluten free, nut free. Helpful for those that need that assurance.

There are two options on this page, the granulated maple sugar and the powdered maple sugar. I keep granulated maple sugar in my pantry as it works so well in a variety of recipes. But the confectioners powder really rocks my world. I dont always like real maple syrup, but the granulated (and now powder) have a better taste to me. Besides adding to recipes, rubs, I love sprinkling some on hot oats, or added into an overnight oats recipe, or to add a little flavor and appeal to a cookie, muffin, or pancake top, smoothies, coffee, etc. Now with the confectioners, I can do all that and even make a nice frosting or drizzle. I could have run my granules through a blender to make confectioners, but I never ever do that. I love that the granules and the powder are same price and same size. Much appreciated.

Currently enjoying some sprinkled over a bowl of steel cut oats, vanilla yogurt, and chopped up apples. YUM!

I always recommend this brand, and I do so here as well.

title: need to add eggs, milk, oil, extract, sweetener. Versatile mix for sweet or savory preferences.
text:
Easy to make, modifiable. I like that it isnt loaded with sweeteners of any sort. If I want sweet, then I can add some in. If I want it for more savory applications, I can do so. If I want extra fluff, I can add more baking powder or baking soda. If I want more protein, I add in some protein powder. Etc. Just makes for a good foundation for various applications.
Yet, if i want to make it as is, as instructions go on back of package, that totally works too. Since the pancake recipe and muffin recipe is so close, I did half pancakes, half muffins. While it requires 4-5 eggs, it isnt eggy tasting or have an eggy texture.

Keep in mind, you will need to add your own stuff: eggs, milk, oil, extract. This gives you the foundation of almond flour blend. I have all sorts of pancake mixes, some are add water only, some require eggs, milk, oil, extact. This mix happens to require double the eggs that I normally need. Adds to overall price, and the base price of this is a little pricey (I dont rate on price though, I knew what the price was before adding it to shopping cart!). I have had other Good Dees products and have like them well enough.

title: fig powder for pop of flavor and sweetness, good in my oats, planning for use in cookie recipe
text:
I love Judees brand (gluten free, nut free facilities!), I have always had excellent experiences with Judees products. It is my go-to for everything, and often find myself just trying something new on occasion. I recommend this brand all the time.

The fig powder is brilliant, wish I knew of its existence before now. Adds a sweet pop of flavor and light sweetness to my steel cut oats. I just sprinkle it on. Or I could make a paste using a little water. For that, I will be using this in a couple of cookie recipes that I make around the holidays that has fig element to it. Mmm. I will be buying more when the time comes (if not before then!).

title: excellent quality brand, from gluten free/nut free facilities, works as well as expected
text: Judees is my go-to brand for everything. Often a little more pricey, but the quality and care is top notch. I recommend this brand for everything. title: works well, recipe included, gluten free and nut free brand (and facilities).

I'd buy it again, no hesitation. I definitely recommend it (and this brand).

title: 3.5 stars. A healthier version of "NOW & LATER" candy chews., 1 gram sugar per chew
text:
"Grape chews for your sour tooth". That alludes to these having a sour edge. I dont think they are sour, but I also dont think they are too sweet. Has a nice burst of grape flavor, smells undeniably grape-y too. Hard at first, then softens up. Does not stick to teeth.

I can see where some folks would liken this to starbursts, but have you ever had the candy, "Now & Later"? That is much closer in resemblance to me. If you like that then you may like this. Very similar, even down to how they are wrapped. Same size, hard squares. Put in your pocket (or mouth) and they will soften up. Also a "long lasting chew".

Side by side nutrition (to N&L), you take in a few less calories and HALF THE SUGAR with this Faves brand. The nutrition profile isnt totally bad or totally good for either, but I like the reduced sugar for a full sugar tasting treat.
--Serving size for the Now&Later is 26 grams, 100 calories, 23 grams carbs (15 grams added sugar), 1g fat (.5 saturdated), 35mg sodium, 0 fiber, 0 protein
--Serving size for this FAVES is 32 grams (here is 6 chews), 110 calories (18 cals per chew), 26 grams carbs (6g added sugars, 7g sugar alcohol---so 1 gram sugar per chew), 3 g fat (1.5 saturated), 60 mg sodium, 0 fiber, 0 protein
Also, Faves does not use artificial coloring, just food based ingredients to give it purple color.

Each pack has 12 chews. That is TWO servings as each serving is 6 chews. If you consume the whole pack, then you can say that you have had: 1 carrot, a slice of squash, 1/2 a beet, a slice of pumpkin, a slice of sweet potato.

I wouldnt eat these for ADDDED nutrition, but I would eat these as a treat knowing that the ingredients aren't entirely nutritionally devoid.

I liked the taste better after having one in my pocket versus just popping one into my mouth from bag. Not sure why it makes a different, but I swear the taste was different. More of an odd taste when I just popped it into my mouth, but more of a natural grape taste when I had it warmed up in my pocket.

I do not rate on price, but I comment. We all have different budgets, interests, values, needs, and so you decide if it is something you want to try. I dont eat stuff like this all the time, so price usually doesnt factor in for me. However, it is pricy to me not matter what it is made of. Current price is $21.99 for 6 bags, so that is 3.67 per bag. $1.67 per ounce. There are 72 chews all together, making them a whopping $0.31 per chew. That's crazy to me.

OVERALL: 3.5 stars. I like the taste, but definitely not in love. Not sure if I like them enough to go with 4 stars. So, I'm going with "3 star" as in, it's "OK". Not bad, not great, just OK. I will work through them but they wont be a repurchase. The reduced sugar and decent nutrition (and not using artificial colors) is 4 stars. I'd like to see less excess packaging by having these in 6 packs then placed in another pack. 72 chews arent that many that they cant just be in one bag.

title: Makes decent iced instant green tea, but falls short on orange citrus flavor; barely there
text:
I think this is ok. I can't really taste any orange. I have their [[ASIN:B09S6R54S2 green tea and lemon]] which is good, but doesn't wow me. Has a very light lemon taste but at least I can recognize it. This orange citrus is barely there. I do find it pretty easy to drink, so I will certainly drink it up. It doesnt taste too sweet to me. Basically tastes like instant green tea, which it is.

Mixes well in hot or cold water. Because I am used to preparing matcha green tea powder (yes, it is different. Matcha is made from early tea leaves, and has more strict standards to be classified as matcha, where as green tea powder is made from later crop tea leaves with more liberal designation), I dissolved it in a little kettle boiled water, then added cold water and ice cubes to make an iced drink.

I really dont mind it. I just dont love it. I dont know why I dont taste orange when others are saying they find it strong.

title: not fancy, comfort food level tasty, good addition to pantry, emergency food supplies
text:
Been shoring up my pantry and emergency food preps. Got much of the basics, but now I am working on adding variety. I really didnt know what this was. Price was right, trusted brand, figured I would give it a try.

Interesting and rather tasty. Like an extra thick cream of chicken soup. Good overall taste, but Minimal vegetables. Seems like it would best used as a base for something rather than just eating. However, I had mine with a pile of buttered toast (dipped it), and that was comfort food level tasty. Just one of those things.

I imagine it would add a load of flavor to a bowl of pasta, rice, or with additional vegetables. Or used as sort of a chunky gravy.

Cans arrived in good condition, expiration is a ways away. When it comes to canned stuff, so long as the can itself is in good condition, I really dont care what the expiration is. Like another review mentioned, canned goods last a very very very long time.

I'll likely buy more of this. 4.5 stars

title: performs exactly like regular confectioners, but it is super sweet. NO stevia
text:
This blend contains just Erythritol, cornstarch, and Sugarcane Reb M (rebaudioside M). Not to be confused with Stevia Reb M (rebaudioside M). There is NO stevia in this. This reb m is derived from the fermentation of sugar cane. So basically, you are getting the sweetness of sugar without the "sugar". NO stevia, and therefore NO stevia aftertaste.

It is very sweet, and because it uses erythritol it has the slight cooling effect (a chemical reaction). But it is faint. This effect can be reduced by including other sweeteners (in this case, sugarcane reb m). So not as intense as straight erythritol.

The powder is exactly like regular confectioners sugar, so it will work the same and have same texture/consistency. But boy is it sweet. I made a quick vanilla frosting, and initial taste really perked up my taste buds (yum), but then it was like.. woah, this is intense. I then turned it into a peanut butter frosting hoping to reduce the sweet assault. It was better-ish, but once on the cake I made, it just seemed like too much. I dont know.. the sweetness level wasnt pleasant. Didnt stop me from eating it, though!
The addition of peanut butter made me think this could work to sweeten peanut butter fudge recipes.

What I may do is cut it further with cornstarch or something non sweet. I want a reduced sugar frosting option, but the intensity of these non sugar sweeteners make it hard to be 1:1 swaps. I dont think there will be better brands unless they are able to cut in other non sweet powder. SO I really dont rate on that.

For the price i have considered just making my own confectioners sugar, but I am lazy, and I really liked just buying this bag for ultimate convenience.

Solid 4 stars.

(PS, why is current price for larger size bag more pricy per ounce than the smaller bag by quite a bit $1.13 per ounce for 24 ounce bag, versus $0.77 per ounce for smaller 12 ounce bag. Weird. Usually costs less to buy larger quantity. You'd be better off buying 2 of the smaller. Just keep eye on price per ounce).

title: YUM!! not just gluten free, but free from a lot of allergens (depending on how you prepare it)
text:
My cake turned out perfect- taste, texture, consistent from edges to center. Moist.

I am not much of a baker, but I can usually handle a "box mix". With this, just add the equivalent of 2 eggs (or use two eggs if allergen is not an issue), 1 cup milk of choice (they recommend rice milk as other options could pose allergen issue), 1/2 cup oil of choice. And vanilla.

I used eggs, unsweetened almond milk, canola oil, and vanilla (healthy splash).

I baked this in a convection toaster oven on regular bake option. Directions say to bake at 360*F for 20-25 minutes. I could choose 375* or 350*, so I started with the higher temp, then dropped it to lower half way through. I used a [[ASIN:B08GCVDMYW casaware baking pan]] that measures 9" x 11" x 2". I lined it with parchment paper.

I dont recall exactly how long this took to bake. I remember adding some time, but it wasn't that much more. End result was perfectly baked, totally consistent texture from edges to center.

Taste is good to me. Nice chocolate flavor. More of a milk chocolate flavor.
Texture is pleasing. This is really where gluten free can alter the experience. It really never changes the actual flavor. I happen to like some gluten free textures, with cake and brownies being one of them. Wasnt sure what to expect as the ingredients are created to eliminate known allergens. Of course, I added some back, but its brilliant that there is something for people who need to know they have a safe product.

This has more of a spongy texture. It doesn't have a crumble. I can pick this up and eat it without mess. If i press down on it, it springs back to life. Yet I can cut through with a fork no problem. It has a good mouth feel to me. I could eat this plain, like a "snacking cake", or slather it with frosting (I tried it both ways.. yum). I'm sure the more clever among us can come up with creative ways to prepare/present this. I kept it simple for testing purpose (ok, and I am not that motivated, haha)

Overall really quite pleased. I may skip eggs next time and use a banana or applesauce. Pricier than some options, but if you need a sure thing, then pricing may not matter. Follow the easy to read directions, pay attention to baking time, and check in with a toothpick.

title: Caramel Nut Clusters: good size, good taste, good chew.. just surprisingly good. I'd buy again
text: Chocolate Caramel Nut Clusters are my favorite of the bunch. I have tried a few types of their keto snacks (not listed here), that were ok. I bought these clusters on a whim, and I am glad I did. I really enjoyed mine. Reminds me of the sugar free clusters from Russel Stover but these are a little bigger. Good taste and mouth feel. title: nice emergency/pantry addition, 7 grams protein per serving, texture like hard boiled egg whites
text:
The main thing to know is... While is it is "extra firm", it is still SILKEN, which means no matter what it is not going to hold in little squares or strips (unless you put in a lot of effort). For that you want non-silken regular. This SILKEN tofu is good for "egg" scrambles, "egg" salad, for baking, for smoothies, for other creamy applications (sauces, "gravies", puddings, desserts). Directly out from box it is a firm block, but if you take off a chunk and it eat plain, ot very much has same texture as a hard boiled egg white.

Shelf stable makes for great Emergency option. Pantry option. I have always been one to keep a well packed pantry (not live close to stores, dont like to shop, dont want to have to buy something every time I want to make something), and especially in the past couple of years due to pandemic and current world affairs (supply chain issues, transportation issues, price inflation, availability, worldwar3?, etc)...I just want more on hand. Or have extra on hand in case someone close needs it. I can do up some care packages. During early days of pandemic, I was able to stay out of public and was able to help elderly folks by supplying them some stuff so they didnt have to put themselves at further risk. And so now, I am just shoring up and adding more variety. Buying a little of something here and there (not all at once!) helps build a nice supply.

I dont often use tofu, but it comes into play for some recipes and cooking/baking curiosities. I'm not vegan or vegetarian, but I love all sorts of food. I figured I would add this into my mix. Decent source of protein (7 grams per serving, there are 4 servings per box, so 28 grams if you ate the whole thing), shelf stable, and adds a creamy kick to sauces and smoothies.

title: makes lovely long grain fluffy rice, good smell/taste when cooked, read on for more info!!
text:
Ok, many of ya'll had me freaking out that I bought a 15 lb bag of plastic pieces. I gave the bag a sniff test, and couldnt pick up any aroma. Doesn't basmati rice emanate a luscious aroma? So I looked up other brands (well known) and saw similar comments about the rice not having an aroma. Then I decided that the only way I would know is just to cook some. First I added a little to a plain pan and proceeded to "toast" it on my gas top stove. I figured if there were plastic bits, I would see it, smell it right? Nothing unusual to be noted. Threw that out, and took fresh rice to add to my rice cooker (rinsed well first). I made according to my machines directions. As it cooked I could smell the aroma that I expected. When it was done, the pieces were perfect. Not sticky, totally fluffy. No gumminess. Tasted as it should.

Then I wanted to look over the plastic bag within the burlap sack. In order to pull it out I had to pour out some rice. Glad I did this because once in a bowl (2 quart size), I put my nose to it and could smell the rice just fine. There's that aroma! After I pulled out the plastic bag with remainder of rice, I looked it over for holes, bugs, and debris. No bugs, no debris. I did see some tiny holes. Very small, and I could tell that they were/are most likely puncture marks from the rice. Not many, but enough for me to double bag it with another plastic bag I had on hand. Then I slid it back into the burlap bag and put back what I took out. Really, no problems. I had this at 4 stars, but once I really worked with it and looked it over, I can say that I am pleased. Very happy that the rice is in a plastic bag and not just in burlap.

I would consider this again depending on price. I was able to get a 15lb bag for $20 (on sale). I can get 1lb bags at local $Tree for 1.25 per lb, so I didnt really save any buying this.. but it saved me a trip.

title: mild tasting instant green tea mix, with lemon & sugar. Dissolves well, lovely over ice.
text:
Instant green tea with sugar and lemon. Has a mild taste, hint of lemon, lightly sweet. Though your perception may vary. Mixes well in hot or cold water. Because I am used to preparing matcha green tea powder (yes, it is different. Matcha is made from early tea leaves, and has more strict standards to be classified as matcha, where as green tea powder is made from later crop tea leaves with more liberal designation), I dissolved it in a little kettle boiled water, then added cold water and ice cubes to make an iced drink. It didnt wow me (so 4 stars), but I have been enjoying it. Gives me a light boost of energy, and I like that it isnt too sweet. I could use more lemon, and for that I really love/prefer (the more budget friendly) [[ASIN:B07TDBYZSW Matcha Iced Tea Lemonade]] as it has a pronounced lemony flavor.

But this is good too. Good option for those that want to like matcha but find it too intense. This has a very mild green tea taste.

title: keep your coffee, but swap out a cup for this. Morning fog lifter!  Must like warm spices tho
text:
It is worth the try, especially if you like warm spices. Surprisingly effective at lifting the morning mental fog. Easy to make, don't need much (1 Tbs). Won't replace my coffee, but I can how it could.

Two main reasons why I chose to try this:
1. It is instant. Just add hot water. I didnt want a coffee alternative that I had to brew. If I am having something meant to replace my coffee (or use as my second cup after real coffee) it needs to be quick to prepare.
2. A glance at the ingredients told me that I already incorporate some of this stuff into my life, so there was a high chance that I would like it.

When I got it, I had pretty much forgotten all what is in it. So instead of looking it over before taking a sip, I decided to drink some to see what all I picked up on taste wise. I made according to direction (1 TBS to some amount of water. I used 6 ounces water, this makes a small mug).

FLAVOR: very cinnamon forward, then settles into an herbal and spicy profile (various mushrooms, licorice, yerba matte, ashwagandha, ginseng). Finishes with a gentle warmth, and a little tingle (ginger). I noticed that it has a slight natural sweetness. It was while writing this review that I figured out that is where the use of Lucuma powder comes in (a natural, nutrition low sugar sweetener).

Overall I like the flavor a lot. I'm not a fan of licorice, but it adds positively to the flavor profile. Adds to the depth of flavor. I liked it best with a little creamer, seemed to make the flavors all come together and mellow the cinnamon.

It isn't meant to taste like coffee, but it has more of a coffee vibe than a tea vibe. I think it is the mouth feel- simply reminds me of coffee, and because of that it allows me to enjoy this a lot. I have had Yerba Mate in the past and always thought that brewed up "thicker" than other teas.

I get a buzz. I dont know how much caffeine is in here (yerba mate), but I can feel the kick. I had it as my first cup on a dark rainy morning, and the mental fog lifted. I know mushrooms can add to the alertness, so if you are wondering if this can power your day, I will say yes. I am surprised. Unlike coffee, I dont think I could drink this all day. 1 cup for sure, maybe a second if I had nothing else. It is rather potent!

Yet, I'm not giving up my coffee. I simply like the taste. I also drink matcha for its long lasting no crash energy, and now I have this. I thought at best that I would low key like it, but I am rather impressed by it. All comes down to personal opinion/experience. I think it is important to really look over the ingredients (especially Yerba mate, and licorice) for any possible complications/concerns.

One note on how much I used. The 1 TBS to 6 ounces of water made a robust tasting cup of coffee (probably more tea like the more water that is used), however, slow to drink it, I noticed toward the end I had about a spoonful of sludge at the bottom. So I think either more water to start, or I can add more water to this sludge to get a few more sips. It can also be the nature of the ingredients. The bag says some residue is normal because they dont use chemical solvents. This reminds me of when I make my own "chai spice latte mix", and the components usually leave a little sludge after having been saturated with water. I assume same situation here.

Overall impression is really good. I do not rate on price, you will have to decide for yourself if current price is something that works for you. I rate more on perceived quality, how close product matches the product description, and if it is effective or not. I appreciate how detailed the product page is on all what is in this. I'd go with 4.5 stars if I could. I do like it more than 4. So 5 it is.

title: not overly sweet, good amount of collagen, subtle mild matcha flavor. Lovel iced
text:
Organic Matcha + Grass Fed, Pasture Raised Collagen, and sweetened with Monk Fruit? YES!

I've wanted to try Jade Leaf for quite some time now. I had my reservations previously over the sugary option, but this collagen with monk fruit piqued my interest. It has a good amount of collagen (8.5 grams), and I figured that the addition of monk fruit sweetener would keep it from tasting too cloy. It's good! Very smooth, not too sweet, mixes up nicely in my shaker bottle or mini blender. Lots of foam! I follow according to directions (1 heaping TBS with a little warm water to help dissolve, then add 8 ounces of milk and some ice). It makes for a VERY MILD drink. Lightly sweet, almost neutral tasting depending on if you use a little too much liquid. I used unsweetened almond milk. If you want a stronger matcha taste, then either use a little more, or add your own plain matcha.

I love how matcha makes me feel-- like the fog has lifted and sun has come out. No jitters. Packed with antioxidants. And this adds in collagen. Yet, I tend to not really care for the taste of matcha. So at first I was like, hm I dont really taste the matcha, but then I was thrilled that I cant really taste the matcha, haha. It's there.. it is just subtle.

15 servings as prepared according to directions. I love the idea of a quick all in one mix, but I will probably just continue with my own matcha+collagen+sweetener. Though I wouldnt hesitate to get this for something convenient (take to office, take on the go for whatever reason, use before a workout when collagen is best consumed, etc). Also, I know when I use this I am not going to be grossed out like I normally am when I make my own. Even so, matcha just makes me feel so good.

5 stars because my experience with it has been good, I am enjoying it, and would consider it again, and would happily reccommend it. There are reviews for various options on this page, and this review is for the "collagen sweetened"

title: yum, nice chocolatey flavor, makes nice addition to smoothies
text:

Buy these for the olives, and not necessarily for gift presentation.

title: just a nice natural snack, low sugar, chewy, nice alone or crumbled over yogurt, oatmeal
text:
Not too shabby. Love the ingredients. Nothing artificial, just real food stuffs. Soft baked, chewy. The banana nut is a tad bland. There are two boxes of that. I am not rating on that because I am learning the deep discount is likely attributed to older, excess, stock. The expiration for me is just a month away, the shortest I have experienced so far. If buying from regular page, then highly likely these have much longer shelf life. (warehouse is separate list to go into).

Anyway, I like these. I would definitely get the Spiced Carrot Cake again, and I would consider other flavors if any appeal to me. I really appreciate the good ingredients and low sugar.

title: very smooth, clean taste, slightly nutty, easy to drink
text:
Very smooth. I happen to like instant (brands vary), and I think this very easy to drink, and may even appeal to those that otherwise dislike instant (can be harsh). A good one to have on hand at the office, in RV, camping supplies, in purse/bag/hiking pack. Since I like instant, it is kept on my kitchen counter alongside my hot water kettle.

Kava has been around for a very long time, yet this is the first time I have tried it. I was curious if "low acidity", which is achieved by adding potassium hydroxide, is noticeable compared regular instant coffee.

With first sip I could tell the difference. Very smooth. Lightly nutty flavor, with ultra smooth taste. Doesn't have that slight bitter taste that other instant coffee (or regular ground coffee) can have. It's pleasant.. and easy to drink. I like all sorts off coffee and brewing styles. I regularly include instant coffee into my rotation (I dont know what it is, sometimes I just crave that sort of flavor and convenience), and this is pretty good to me. I normally prefer my coffee black, but when it comes to instant I have to add cream. Except this, this Kava low acidity instant coffee can be consumed black.

I like it for the taste, but I know others may benefit from the actual reduction in acidity ie heart burn, acid reflux issues

Directions say to use 1 packet per 6 ounces of water. I use 2 packs for my 12-14 ounce mug.

title: neutral taste, excellent performance for higher temp needs, good nutritional profile
text: Light aroma, but neutral taste. Creamy. I like it better than my usual ghee, which can impart some off flavor notes. This has that slightly granular texture at room temp, but is creamy when in mouth (I tried a little off the spoon to start). It melts easily in the pan. Works wonderfully for times I want to get a fry, or near fry, and not have to worry about damaging the oils like with other stuff. Bonus that it has a healthy nutritional profile. I've never been one to use ghee direct from jar. It isnt butter, and never has a taste I enjoy. But I like it for cooking. This camel ghee happens to have a nearly neutral taste which is extra appealing to me. Camel based products are pricy compared to cow products, yet I prefer this over cow based ghee. Taste, performance, nutritional profile is just better in my humble opinion. Glass jar, protective inner seal. I'll watch the price, but I would consider this again. Their informative website helped me learn more about them and their offerings.

title: lovely, sweet mild syrup with hint of lychee taste, use it on/in anything, low GI !
text:
Viscous like Agave, or other syrups, with a hint of lychee fruit flavor. More mild than honey. I always have yacon sweetener in my pantry (syrup style or powder). Because yacon products are not the most budget friendly, yet I still find great value in using it, I tend to use it more for the health benefits and low impact on sugar levels, than just as a anytime sweetener (but I really should use it more).

The slight fruity floral taste also limits my use, but there is plenty to do with it. I use it anywhere I would honey. So for me, I dont use it in coffee, but I use it in tea, matcha green tea, on hot oats, plain yogurt, in "protein powder balls" snacks, and even a little off the spoon. I imagine it can be used fine in baking, but unless it is a healthy recipe, I'd rather just use sugar or cheaper syrups. BUT I'm trying to reduce my sugar intake and this is an EXCELLENT product to use as it is low in sugar anyway, and it doesnt impact blood sugar levels like other sweeteners. It's good, and really worth the try.

Nice packaging, easy to use bottle. Lovely taste

title: mostly all dented cans, but the are so far filled to brim w/beans (not liquid), slightly firm
text:
Boy, I'm not the only one buying canned beans and such as emergency food, hm? Most recent reviews reflect this. Good thinking, best to have something on hand and not need it then need it and have nothing. Be safe my friends. Beans are great addition to a prepper pantry, and so long as cans aren't damaged will last indefinitely. (BTW, I acquired these March 2022, with "exp" of 09/2026)

That being said, I love Goya, and I love black beans but 19 out of 24 cans are banged up. Some significant, some just a little dent. Only 5 are perfect. One can had mouse poop on top. It was otherwise packaged well enough-- all in a large tray with plastic wrap around it. Then tucked into a shipping box with the protective wads of brown paper. Not sure where/when in the process the banged up cans came about. I wiped them all down with disinfectant wipes before storing in pantry.

I will heavily rate on the actual quality of the beans, but keep what I said about dented cans in mind. I haven't done anything about it (yet, but I doubt anything can be done. Some stuff is just buy at your own risk). I placed the worst of the dented cans at the forefront of my pantry for use first. I opened up the worst one to see how it fared. The contents actually appeared totally fine.

What I like about these beans from this brand, is that the cans are filled to brim with beans. Maybe that changes from can to can, size to size, style to style, but my experience so far is that I am paying for beans and not liquid. Drives me nuts to buy an off brand, a cheap brand only to open the can and have an 1/8 to a 1/4 of it be liquid. I took pics of an open can, and how it looks in a 2 cup pyrex container. It is FULL, and it fills the 2 cup container.

Beans are perfectly small, firm, not mushy. This may throw folks off that are used to bargain canned beans. Also with these being organic they hold their shape better than others, too. Then, in additon to that these are low sodium. Sodium packed beans tend to be mushier--even when rinsed off, the sodium has already had time to permeate and break down the insides. Fine for taste and texture if you prefer a softer texture.

I got these on sale, ($21, I think) and that helped a lot as I think they came to around $0.85 a can. Good for any brand, organic or not. I just wish the cans were't all banged up, Otherwise 5 stars.

4 stars for actual beans.
