title: like a robust holiday spice coffee blend, not bitter/tart/tangy, surprisingly good, caffeine kick
text:
Pleasantly surprised by this blend of coffee and herbs. Maybe shocked. I will give anything a try, and have very open minded tastebuds. So given that this is branded as a "Fitness Coffee" and is loaded with herbs.. it was really a toss up as to what this would taste like. Gotta say.. YUM. It reminds me of a holiday spice coffee, which I already have a tender spot for. I dare say, much better and more robust than holiday coffees I normally get. Like, next time I want a holiday spice coffee (I tend to get into mood for something a little different from October through December), I would get this. If someone I knew was looking for a spicy coffee, I would recommend this. Never mind the fitness aspect (though love me some antioxidants), get this for the spice! Green tea usually has more antioxidants than coffee, but this blend is purported to have more than green tea. Interesting!

I dont know what the roast level is, but I am partial to dark roasts-- darker the better, and since most blends are mediums I will assume the same of this. However, it doesnt have that tang that lighter roasts have, it isnt acidic or bright. I think it is a dark leaning medium. Overall balanced coffee taste with even amount of spicy herbs that work really well (to me) with coffee.

It definitely has caffeine. I tried it as my first cuppa of the day, and I could feel the fog lift. I normally drink my coffee black (first cup), but I decided to add some creamer to it (fat loaded coffee.. whatevs!). I just thought that the herbs/spices would benefit from cream. That is how I would normally do a spice coffee. It works.

I think it is really good! I can pick up on hint of licorice, something I normally despise, but it works so well here.

It can be prepared in any brewing fashion you want. I made it as a pour over. I tend to use a heavy hand when adding coffee to a paper filter for a single mug (12-14 ounces) of coffee (probably 3 TBS easily). The pour kettle boiled water on top.

I'm totally trying this ICED soon.

title: not much more effort than regular ice cream recipe, will need heavy cream and milk
text:
I made this in my [[ASIN:B07VVQ7XH4 Amazon Basics 1.5 quart ice cream maker]]. I used the whole packet. I make a basic vanilla ice cream that pretty much uses the same ingredients we are expected to add to this packet: iel Milk, and whipping/heavy cream. The sugar is in the packet, as is the vanilla flavoring (though I added extra splash of vanilla) Basically what this is doing is adding a rich, creamy texture. If you are comfortable making a gelato base on your own, using your own selected ingredients, then have it. This is for those that want the convenience, or to try something new with little know how needed. So whereas I would normally just mix the liquid ingredients cold, and keep in fridge for the day (if I prep in morning then I make late evening, or leave overnight), same here... but with this I am heating it on the stove (so the powder can fully dissolve and then thicken), and then just putting in fridge for minimum of 4 hours. Really no more effort than my usual vanilla ice cream recipe. Not complicated, and I didnt feel need to use a thermometer. Just made sure it was steamy but not scalding.

Following day, I added took my frozen vessel, placed it in machine, turned on, added this mixture, and let this do its thing. It was almost too much content, but it worked. I didnt think it tasted weird or off. But then I had added more vanilla, and a little added sugar. They have other flavors available, or you can probably add your own flavor to this vanilla. Overall I liked how this turned out. Creamy, sweet, vanilla yumminess. To each their own. Pricy (to me) for a one time item. I already thought my regular vanilla ice cream was pricy to make, now boost it by $10. Yikes. I dont rate on price though.

Typo in ingredient list.

title: good sized bag of a variety of tasty veggies, must have pantry item, use in everything
text:
This bag of dehydrated vegetables contains: Carrots, Potatoes, Celery, Onion, Bell Peppers, Tomatoes, Cabbage. It is a pretty good mix. I rely on dehydrated vegetables for use in quick soups (I'll make a mug of broth and add leftover whatever from my fridge, and add a spoonful of dehydrated veggies), boost up egg dishes, and longer simmering soups. Really a must have for any prepper, or anyone who wants to round out their pantry. Makes nice addition to meal prepping, particularly shelf stable stuff (think of camping meals, emergency meals that just require water, etc). Good way to get some vegetables if getting to the store is out of the question, or produce is low, or way too pricey.

This is a good mix, at a good price. I will likely buy it again. However, it is worth buying a few different brands to get the various varieties of vegetables. I like the inclusion of cabbage in this mix, where as my usual brand does not. So I am learning to take look at actual ingredients, then keeping a 2-3 brands on hand to choose from. I find that they stay "fresh" because there is really nothing to go bad. But when I have excess and have room in my spare fridge, then I will just store it in there. But any air tight container in a cool dark place should be more than adequate for a food item like this.

[[ASIN:B001VNKZQY Frontier Co-op dehydrated soup vegetables]] which has Peas, Carrots, Potatoes, Green Beans, Onion, Bell Peppers, Parsley, Tomatoes, Celery Flakes

title: have your brownies and eat them too. Really good sugar free mix, already bought another
text:
Pretty good! Different than regular brownies of course, but compared to other "sugar free" brownie mixes, I like this a whole lot more--doesnt have that odd sugar free taste that other brands have. Way better price too, and no need for addition super special ingredients, unless of course you want to do some swapping out. Someone else here had mentioned using pop/soda in lieu of eggs & oil. I forgot about that! I used to do that with cake mixes. Really works. I ended up buying another box of this stuff, so later today I am going to do it up with some pop. Mmm brownies! That will reduce calories by a bit. Another option is to use unsweetened apple sauce instead of oil. This sometimes makes the texture a little light, so I am not sure if I will try that with brownies. But yeh, this mix can be altered like any other mix. It is as close to regular as you can get. Add sugar free frosting for added deliciousness.

BTW, it uses malitol, which some people are super sensitve to (like other non sugar sweeteners), but most people may feel gassy if they eat too much of products containing malitol.. so be careful!

title: nearly no excess liquid, good looking chunks, nice addition to pantry staples, YUM!
text:
I'm pleased. The reviews vary greatly, so I figured I was taking a chance as I really didn't know what to expect. I am pleasantly surprised by how good these tins of white and dark turkey meat are. They are full of meat, with really no liquid (see my picture). It is more like a thick broth. I didn't bother straining any of it off because there simply isnt enough. Though I wonder if ambient house temp impacts this (currently winter, with cool house, with pantry in coldest part of house, so fats may thicken up)?

Good sized chunks, good taste- albeit similar to chicken. I mean, its meat in a can so for the most part expect it to taste, smell, appear as such. If you don't like tinned chicken then you wont like this. If you are expecting carved turkey breast, you wont like this. It is canned meat, so it is what it is. And for me, it is exactly as I was hoping for, and so it gets 5 stars from me. The main thing for me is that it wasn't a tin of mush, and it wasn't a tin of liquid. I wanted to pay for meat, not water, and this has been so far a very good purchase. I'll buy again so long as price stays reasonable. Currently $15.60 for 12 cans.

Very convenient. I dont rely on tinned meat for day to day living, but it comes in handy. I keep an assortment in my pantry- chicken, tuna, salmon, and now turkey. It makes for quick no fuss protein source for salads, crackers, sandwiches, and quick soups. But I also keep it on hand for emergency use. Good for SHTF as well as semi regular use. Not always able to get to the store, not always able to find foods in store, not always able to pay the prices, and so on. Also, I have two big dogs and 3 cats, so having extra meat on hand also reassures me that they will have nibbles in case there is food shortage for them. I just like having a variety of food available. I never bought tinned turkey before but now I plan to add it to my on going grocery/pantry list. Glad to have found something worthwhile to stock in my pantry. YUM!

title: quality culinary that is kissing up on ceremonial grade, very nice, I'd buy again
text:
Quality is very good, no problems or concerns. Has a fresh, mild taste- overall a smooth culinary matcha. Higher end for sure, though it might be a matter of region as I find the best tasting matcha comes from Japan.

I drink matcha daily (antioxidants, true non jittery energy, and reduction in craving for sweets) and go through quite a bit, so I am often buying it, and I try all different brands, regions, grades. Despite the copious amounts that I consume, I am not a fan of the taste of matcha. So usually I am burying it in a smoothie, or including other add-ins to reduce the flavor. And because of that, unless a matcha brand is really awful, I pretty much find them to all be within a typical/similar range of taste and performance. I can go super cheap and bitter, or ultra pricy and smooth- yet they still are similar enough (to me) that I can go with anything and be pleased. If I were to drink it totally plain, then yeh a super smooth culinary or ceremonial will be appreciated- the nuance of flavor is subtle but can make a huge difference. That being said, this high quality culinary is touching ceremonial grade. I think you will be pleased with this no matter your application.

I find that I can mix this into anything easily, and it whisks up nicely for hot or iced lattes. Serving size for all matcha is 1-2 tsp. I almost always used 1-2 TBS. I find that to be the sweet spot for me in terms of energy boost and reduction in cravings. My go to application is in smoothies (mask it with meal replacement powder or protein powder, etc), or as a hot/iced latte- cream, some sort of sweetener. Those I will usually use 2-3 tsp and then make a couple of drinks through day. I never bake with matcha as it really isnt a taste I want in my food.

Price is within reasonable range for quality matcha

title: perfect for sushi/maki rolls, no complaints, quite yummy
text:
Sushi sheets! Thick, pliable, chewy. As expected for making simple maki rolls. Or cutting into strips for adding to broth. But I nearly 100% use it for making quick maki rolls. I will make sushi rice, prepare an assortment of fillings (I love sashimi- raw fish, but I dont make that at home. I leave that to professionals). Then roll is up and cut. Usually I do carrot, cucumber, sometimes cream cheese and/or imitation crab meat. I dont make gorgeous rolls, but they always seem to turn out well enough for me to enjoy with a copious amount of soy and wasabi. Pretty sure I eat "sushi" for the soy & wasabi.

This multi pack is reasonable, and I wouldnt hesitate to buy again.

title: Love my Hotta products, esp this as it is not sweetened w/ anything. Just ginger, C, Zinc
text:
I always have an assortment of Hotta ginger products on hand. I just love a mug of hot ginger. I dont want ginger tea sachets as the ginger is never enough, though I have added hotta ginger to a mug of tea. I usually drink it plain. They make some with honey, some sweetened with non sugar sweeteners, and now there is this, which isnt sweetened at all.

It is totally plain, no sweetener of any sort which I love. I can add my own sweetener if I want, or simply enjoy the simple taste of spicy ginger. It has a strong, hot ginger taste made from ginger aged 11-12 month. The addition of vitamin c (32 mg, which is 35% DV) and Zinc (4.1 mg, which is 35% DV) makes it a nice immune support item. That's it!

Because it isn't sweetened, I would add this to a mug of sipping broth, or simple bowl of soup. Or added to tea, or just enjoyed alone (add to as little or as much as you want). Use hot water, or make it iced

title: tasty, versatile, two huge containers (mine "exp" in a few months, but I am fine with it)
text:
Good taste, balanced flavor, quick dissolve, versatile.

I dont rate on price (we all have different needs, values, budgets, preferences, prices fluctuate, etc) but I do comment. I know that this is pricier than what I can buy at my local walmart (32 ounce container for $5.16=$0.16 per ounce) , but considering that I rarely shop there (or anywhere as I prefer to shop online), I found that this PACK OF TWO was reasonable at $17.99 (81 ounces total, $0.22 per ounce). I'd buy this again at that price as a pack of 2.

Knorr makes good products. I go through a lot of bouillon. Just one of those things that can make all the difference in a dish. I find that the loose powder is easier to work with over the packets or foil wrapped cubed. Liquid is nice, but there is only so much room I want taken up in my cupboards or fridge. I love bouillon paste, but it can be tricky to find (and price of my usual--tones-- has more than doubled recently). I find this Knorr loose powder to be very tasty. Good natural flavor, hint of parsley. Dissolves well. It is super salty, so be mindful of how much you use.

I use it in soups, stews, for seasoning just about everything. I will even make up a mug mixed with hot water as a sipping broth. Really nice way to warm the belly, and to help fill it up before/in between meals. Or I will make a quick soup, by making my mug-full and adding in a little leftover vegetable, pasta, (or quinoa or lentils-- usually I have something like that precooked), etc.

Pantry staple. Also, I am a bit of a prepper, and am always looking for ways to maximize my pantry in case I cant get to the store- whether it be terrible weather, car is in shop, super tight budget, pandemic, gas prices, worldwar3. Spices and bouillon is vital. Can make anything taste good, taste different by swapping out the spices. Bouillon gives it a comforting depth of flavor. From flavor, to broths, to making gravies.. it is just a heavy hitter in the flavor department.

I can make a lot with this container, and its just so versatile. Despite receiving AGING containers (acquired 03/2022, with EXP date of 05/2022) I am not concerned with the overall freshness. This stuff will last a long time. But OMG-- no one is going through 81 ounces of this stuff in 2 months. Hopefully they get on top of this. At least when I buy it in a store I can look at the exp date and decide for myself. even so, I down rate one star for that.

title: convenient, yeast optional, chewy dense crust, roll thin or gently press out for thick
text:
Says yeast is optional. I happened to have some, so I went ahead and used it. I think my next batch will be made without it and see how it does. Add spices and such as you wish.

The packet makes one 10ish inch pizza. All that depends on how thin you roll it out. Instructions for pizza crust are included on bag. Come back here or find their website for other recipes (bread sticks, cinnamon sticks)

Not too challenging to make, just takes some time. Keep your hands oiled if it feels too sticky.

Overall quality is fine. Partake products are usually good tasting to me. I may be the odd one out, but as someone who does not need to be gluten free, I happen to enjoy a lot of gluten free products. Many years ago, before "gluten free" was a thing, I had a close friend with celiacs disease, and they could not be around anything gluten. I took to eating the same as them when around them, and I would buy (hard to find, ultra pricy) gluten free products. I remember liking the texture of gluten free brownies over regular, and that some pizza crusts were just chewier, had a better mouth feel than regular flour crusts. Now that gluten free products are the norm, the prices have come way down. I still pick up a few goodies once in awhile for my own enjoyment, but also to have items on hand when I have company who refrain from gluten. This pack of 3 is nice as they dont require me to dig out all the separate ingredients.

title: mild mayo with slight tang, more like Kraft than Hellmans for reference, worth the try
text:
This was an impulse purchase, kinda. I was going through my pantry making a list of items I was out of or getting low on. I dont get out to the store that often, so I rely on getting it all at once (and extra) and/or online shopping. Mayo was on my list. As I was poking around the grocery listings, I saw this mayo. Price wasn't too bad-- way less than Hellmans (my preference) but about the same or a little more than store brands. I bought one for $3.06 and figured if I liked it then it would be added to my subscribe and save for $2.61 which would be competitive to my store brand, which is pretty good.

I think it tastes a slightly tangier than Hellmans. It reminds me more of the Kraft brand of mayo. I like mayonnaise, not "salad dressing" (ie miracle whip) so I was a little put off by the mild tang, yet not so much to not continue to use (I waste nothing). Even though it isnt as eggy as Hellmans or other heavier mayos, I think it has a nice balance. Again more like Kraft for those familiar. Or if you were to take 85% mayo and and 15% miracle whip. For those that want a slightly more bright tasting mayo yet not a salad dressing/miracle whip may enjoy this.

Food stuff comes down to preference. So everyone could love it, but you may hate it. Only your tastebuds matter. Just as everyone could dislike it and you may love it. Only your perception matters. I like this, but dont love it. Yet, if the price is right I would keep it on hand in my pantry.

I didnt take note of the expiration date. This is one of those foods that I dont care what the exp date is.

title: easy to eat, good taste, not too sweet, not too much stevia, 3 net carbs per 1/4 cup
text:
I was sent [[ASIN:B09PT9697D Wonder Granola Original]], so my review is for that. Simple ingredients, good flavor, mildly sweet. The use of stevia seems minimal, I can detect it but it isnt overwhelming. Pleasant crunch, yet not hard on the teeth. Love the seeds. Overall flavor is good, overall texture is same throughout (no large chunks, all loose pieces). 1/4 cup serving has 150 calories, 14 grams fat (1 g saturated), 0 sodium, 4 grams fiber, 5 grams protein.

For "Keto friendly" this has 7g carbohydrates (no added sugar), but minus the fiber, I think that leaves 4 net carbs? I am not keto, nor on any special kind of diet, but I do best and feel best when I can reduce my sugar intake. The more sugar I eat, the more I want it (and I am a binge eater) so I can appreciate the use of stevia in this. They do a good job of not overloading it with stevia. I find a lot of keto marketed (or other "no sugar added") products use way too much sweetener, way above what is reasonable. THIS Wonder granola uses a light hand with the sweetener. (thank you!)

I never eat a bowl of granola (big calorie hit that doesnt fill me up), but I do add it to hot oats, yogurt, pancake topper, and ice cream.

Almonds, Sunflower Seeds, Pumpkin Seeds, Pecan Nuts, Chicory Root Fiber, Inulin, Canola Oil, Natural Flavors, Cinnamon, Rosemary Extract, and Stevia.

Acquired 03/2022 with exp date of 10/12/2022

distributed by General Nature (NY)
Product of CZ

title: decadent aroma, moist pods. Lovely in ice cream, great for making vanilla extract
text:
decadent aroma, moist pods. Lovely in ice cream, great for making vanilla extract

Moist, fragrant whole vanilla bean pods. They come tucked into a thick packet. All look good. I kept two for use in making homemade ice cream, and the others for use in making vanilla extract. I'll start them now, and they will be more than ready for use as gifts next years holiday season. No better, no worse than other MADAGASCAR vanilla bean pods I have purchased.

Second time I have gotten these- once in Nov 2021, and again March 2022, and the quality is the same-- soft, plump, lovely.

title: tangy, lemony, perfectly sweet, mild matcha taste but gives matcha buzz LOVE IT
text:
I think this is absolutely fantastic and I am super stroked to have tried it. I know it comes down to preference, so I will just say why it appeals to me so much. Basically it is a lemony, tangy-tart lemonade with mild matcha taste, and perfectly balanced sweetness. I absolutely adore lemon, and rarely are prefab lemonades tangy tart enough for me. Usually just overly sweet and blah. This is perfect to me. My opinion of course, but here are more details why I love it:

Matcha green tea- I drink it daily. I love the steady energy (matcha does better job than coffee, but I will never give it up), and the antioxidants. Also helps reduce sugar cravings. However, as much as I drink it, I dont care for the taste of matcha, so I am ALWAYS looking for ways to make it taste better. I tend to bury it in smoothies. I have even tried making a matcha green tea lemonade, with mediocre results. SO when I had opportunity to try this, I figured it would also be medicore.

BUT, WOW WOW WOW. I love it!!!! It has a mild matcha taste (its clearly there, but more in the background), with a bright, tangy, TART lemon. It really has that perfect (to me) lemonade taste. Truly lemon, just enough sweet (from cane sugar and stevia) and then the glorious aspects of matcha, without tasting too matcha-y. LOOKS like matcha in a cup.

I would say that it dissolves best in a shaker cup. Otherwise, there may be some bits that go undissolved, which isnt entirely bad because that just means you get some extra tangy pops of flavor, haha. But yeh, shake it for best results.

Says to use one TBS for 8 ounces of water. Like anything else, adjust accordingly. I used 2 scoops in a 16 ounce mason jar, added ice and a straw. SO GOOD. Its only March in NY, but the temps boosted to 60+ degrees which is a tease for good warm weather. Having this delightful lemonade has determined what my new summer drink will be.

I imagine this would also be pleasant as a "water essense"-- add some to a bigger bottle of water.

Again, uses a mix of cane sugar and stevia to sweeten. Before you make a purchase, take a look at the product description. The very first picture shows the ingredients, so none of this should be a surprise. I like it, as the combo of the two help make it sweet without overloading it with cane sugar, yet not totally stevia (or other sweetener) that would make it taste strictly of that. For me, it is a nice balance. Again, thats my observation/opinion/preference.

OH and I know it has enough matcha in it to be effective, because I got my usual glorious buzz off of it.

Totally a repurchase. 5 stars!

title: pretty good, play around w/ratio esp if new to it. Not always 1:1, but can replace some sugar
text:
I appreciate that this is clearly labeled as a blend, way too often I see a single source shown on the front of the package, only to turn over the package and see in small print that other sweeteners are added in. But while I am glad to see both listed on the front in large letters, I dont know how much of each is in this. On the front it lists Monk fruit first, then erythritol, but when listed in the ingredients, Erythritol is listed first then Monk fruit.

Anway, it tastes good. Monk fruit is amazing as a sweetener. I love it on its own, but I like it as part of a blend too. Usually when I see monkfruit in a prepared product, I am assured that it wont have a weird aftertaste. Not always, but often. Erythritol can be a little more tricky as it can impart a cooling effect sensation, but usually no weird taste.

This is said to be a 1:1 swap for regular cane sugar. Maybe, maybe not. Depends on what you are used to. I have greatly cut regular sugar from my diet, and so my taste buds are acclimated to less sweet. Despite a lot of these sugar alternatives being hundreds or thousands of times sweeter than cane sugar, the taste buds pick up on it differently, so if new to it, it may not be sweet enough. So my advice is to experiment. I think small scale, it works great as a swap. So try it straight in coffee, tea, or sprinkled over oats. For larger scale (ie baking), try it mixed with some regular sugar (my favorite, as I can greatly reduce sugar content, but still have the true taste of cane sugar-- aim for 1/2 cane, 1/2 blend). Then work from there.

Overall it is on par with other blends I have had, I have no problem with it, would consider it again.

title: nice addition to smoothies and oatmeal bowl, versatile powder/meal for baking, etc
text:
I have been using this Ground sunflower seed meal in my smoothies and the occasional oatmeal bowl. I have yet to bake with it, but I imagine it can be swapped in for something, or simply added in with minor liquid adjustments. Might be good as a veg burger binder or for making a pizza crust of the sort. Or as a coating for chicken or pork. But I am enjoying it in my smoothies too much at the moment to give it a go in anything else. I thought it would have a stronger taste, but it is kind of neutral tasting to me. Maybe my tastebuds are broken.

Meets my expectations. I would consider it again.

title: gorgeous thick simple syrup, so many applications, pails could use work
text:
Simple sugar syrup- thick, sticky, sweet. Just a neutral sugar syrup taste. Versatile use. Comes in little tubs/pails which are kinda cute but not easy to work with. The lids are going to be covered in syrup. Maybe you will be able to figure it out better than me, but I made a mess and decided it best to pour the contents into a jar. I think if I had made sure the lid was clear of syrup, and made sure to wipe the edges, then that would be fine. I'll try it with the next container. I imagine this stuff will last forever in storage.

Thicker than vegetable glycerin (and no weird taste), about the same as corn syrup in viscosity, but clearer and cleaner in taste. Really like a thick simple sugar. Good stuff.

The pails were really well packed. I dont know what more they could possibly do, but somehow it was all sticky- somehow the syrup leaked out a little. Just a little. Containers weren't open, no damage, and they were very well wrapped and packed. I suspect that it is simply the container itself when the syrup is on its side. I think the syrup just manages to drip a little. It wasn't a big mess, and certainly didnt impede my use of it-- I just ran the containers under warm water. I'll even but this again if it stays at same reasonable price.

I find good value in this product- 1 kg (2.2 lbs), 2 containers= 4.4 lbs for $17.99 makes is $0.25 per ounce. I really like that it is broken up into two smaller containers rather than one large one-- easier to store.

title: salty, smoky, tasty- yields enough for 10 lbs (all at once, or use a little multiple times)
text:
YUM! This Cholula seasoning packet is formulated for use with 10 lbs of pork. TEN POUNDS. So if you aren't working with that much pork at once, then use less powder accordingly. I love that I will get at least 4 uses from this pack. A whole lot more if I get it again and use it for flavoring tacos, beans, etc. Basically it is like getting 10 packets of taco seasoning in one large packet. No price savings, but this is a tasty blend, and I love this brand.

It is a tasty blend of spices, and it works extremely well with pork. Pleasant hint of smoke, not over done (to me). Salty, like most pre fab seasoning blends like this are. I think this would work on top of a home made blend-- just dont use salt then cut some of this in to round out the flavor with smokiness and saltiness.

I used it to make a pork carnitas soup. I slow cooked 4 lbs of pork with this, then I added in some broth, corn, green chilis, red peppers, diced tomatoes, onions, brown rice. Made it more like a stew, then served it with toasted tortillas. I think I will do regular chicken or pork burritos or tacos next.

Anyway, good stuff.

title: My go to instant coffee, smooth, strong robust coffee. Fine powder, lovely crema formation
text:
I really enjoy this Nescafe Gold Espresso. It is a fine powder that easily dissolves in hot or cold water. Has a smooth rich flavor and natural "crema" that forms on top. Lasts a short while then blends into cup.

TASTE is surprisingly smooth with a hint of sweet. It is just coffee- nothing added to it. It is not only good for an instant but it is pretty dang good as a coffee, period. It is robust and strong without being bitter.

I always have instant coffee on hand. I use it in baking to amp up the taste of chocolate, or to add a special coffee flavor. I also drinking it willingly, lol. I make brewed coffee, pour over coffee, K-cups, and the occasional cold brew. And sometimes I just want instant coffee. It just hits the spot sometimes, and once I tried this, it has become a regular repurchase for me. Definitely my go-to instant, but is often my go to for any time I want coffee.

Works real well blended into cold drinks, too.

The directions say to use 1-2 tsp in 50 ml (1/3 cup) of water for a shot of espresso, or 1-2 tsp in 250 ml (1 cup) of water for an Americano. I tried 1 tsp in 50 ML and was impressed with the robust taste. Definitely try it out following the directions, then work from there.

title: Brown & Red Rice w. chia & kale is super versatile, pantry must have, convenient, emergency too
text:
This review is for the 12 pack of "Brown & Red Rice With Chia & Kale". I acquired this 02/2022, and have been pleased with this purchase. I am familiar with Seeds of Change products, and strive to keep some in my pantry at all times. Just works really well for quick meals, emergency meals, meal on the go, and for adding texture and flavor to a dish. I like how the serving size is simple, with the information for half a packet or a whole packet included. Depending on what I am using it for, I will consume the whole packet. I am a big eater.

Last night a couple of these packets came in handy at dinner time. I really didnt have a dinner plan, but I had some boneless chicken to cook up. So what I did was cook that separately, then in a pan I added 2 packets of this Brown & Red rice along with a small pat of butter, a splash of chicken broth (cooking off the chicken breasts) and some frozen peas, and frozen onions. Added in some garlic & fresh ground pepper to season as this particular variety doesn't have additional seasonings in it other than salt. Chia and kale add a depth of flavor but not a punctuated flavor.

Cooked that on low until chicken was done. Then I shredded the chicken and added that in. Made for a hearty dinner "bowl". We even had left overs- so really only one packet was needed.

5 stars because I will buy again (just added more to cart).

title: delightful cookie biscuit for teas & coffees. Pretzel shape is crisp, others are more dense. Delish!
text:
I figured I would give these a try despite some of the scathing reviews. I simply didnt expect to see sugar free danish butter cookies. I get the regular ones at the holidays- small tin, usually $1 for 7-10 cookies. Ya know, hard, crispy-crunchy, mild flavor. Begs to be eaten along side a cup of tea or coffee. So how much different can these sugar free ones be? A mystery awaited..

I think they are fine! All of my cookies are/were intact (Ive nibbled through half the container). The flavor is similar, and even the texture is similar. Maybe a little more dense? I dont find it all that far off from the original that I buy. I can eat them alone, or paired with tea/coffee. They dont feel all that more crisp-hard-crunchy than my others. The pretzel shape is the more crispy and light, then the other shapes being a little tougher, but still good. Like, eat the pretzel shape one as in, then use the denser ones for tea/coffee.

And these have the added benefit (for me) of not having excess sugar. Maybe other brands of the regular are better than the brand I always buy, and so perhaps the difference would be greater. But my experience is that these are good, and I will buy them again. This time a pack of two, so I save a few bucks.

5 stars because I have been enjoying these enough to add more to my cart.

Its a food item, everyone has their preferences. I like them, glad I tried them, glad to have a sugar free option.

title: 3.5 stars. Good taste, formula, but no idea how much caffeine (or Nopal, green tea, mushrooms)??
text:
I like the taste, it is creamy and coconut forward. Nothing off tasting, overall quite pleasant. Sweet, but not overly so. I guess it depends on how much water you use, or if you use the whole serving size (6 TBS) or less. Contains 14 grams of added sugar (which is a hair over 1 TBS). Kind of nice to not have it loaded with super sweet artificial sweeteners, but I would be happier if this wasn't sweetened at all.

To make: add 6 TBS to 11 ounces hot water. Drink hot, iced, or add to smoothies.

I use about a third to half a serving, and I add in extra instant coffee. I have used the whole serving when I want it as part of a caffeinated smoothie or mini meal. Also works as a creamer.

No mention of how much caffeine, nor how much (or what kind) of mushroom, Nopal, or green tea. For as much as this costs, I would prefer to know more about what I am buying. As with any supplement or exercise, the main aspect of weight loss is what you eat, how much. Keep those calories in check! I like using "weight loss" supplements to help support my effort. I dont take them and then not do anything. Matcha/green tea is my favorite for all its benefits, so I am glad that is in here.

OVerall: 3 stars. I like it, but the lack of info down rates it in my opinion. Unless I missed it somewhere?

Taste though for me is solid 4 stars.

My go to "weight loss" support coffee is [[ASIN:B08WWFVQD1 anything by Fitne but especially this one]]

title: delicate flavor, reminds me of dark cherries, not cloyingly sweet, nice treat, upgrade!
text: These are a delightful change from the firm super sweet maraschino cherry that we usually keep on hand. These remind me of soft, dark cherries. Not too sweet, and has this delicate nuance that I find intriguing. I suppose that is the "whiskey flavor", but its so much better than I expected it to be.  Just a nice taste to and aroma to me. Natrual tasting, not cloyingly sweet like the other. Very interesting. Easy enough to eat direct from jar, or add to drink or desserts. Would make nice addition to a food or drink themed gift.

title: excellent addition to pantry, adds visual & textural appeal to various dishes
text:
Well packaged pack of 20 (7 ounces each). Takes up little space, and is a welcome addition to my pantry. I dont often find "stars" at the store, and even more rare to find Goya brand stars. Great for soups and other recipes where the shape and size adds visual and textural appeal. Would buy again.

Edit (after seeing other reviews): NO BUGS. All packages were/are perfect. All came shipped well in a Goya brand box.

title: delicate vanilla, not as robust as some, but it has a creamy natural vanilla taste
text:
It's good, little different than my usual vanilla syrup (not better or worse, just different). A lot of these syrups use the same type of ingredients, but somehow all taste different. This vanilla syrup has a very light, creamy, natural vanilla. But it is faint. I find that I am using a couple of generous pours (I dont have a pump) in my 14 ounce coffee cup. I prefer this added alongside creamer to carry the flavor. Although I need to use more than I normally do, somehow it doesnt make my coffee overly sweet. Some brands can make my drinks too sweet. The ingredients are clearly listed on product page and product pictures so should not be a surprise to see propylene glycol. Came dented as it was shipped in just a bubble mailer with no other protections.

Ingredients: Water, Natural Flavors, Propylene Glycol, Cellulose Gum, Sucralose, Citric Acid, Potassium Sorbate (Preservative).

Made in USA

Overall, I think it is ok. I will use it up, but not sure if it would be a repurchase. If we could do half ratings, I would do 3.5. Not sure if I like it enough to be 4 stars (I like the flavor, but it is so faint and I need to use a lot). So I am going with 3 stars. Doesnt mean it is bad, it is just "OK". But you may like it.

title: makes my tastebuds sing, perfectly balanced sour, sweet, gentle heat. Best tamarind candy
text:
Perfection! If you like tamarind candy, this is a great one to try. It has the most natural taste and texture that far outsees other tamarind candies. What I like about it is that it is just tamarind, sugar, and cayenne pepper, all rolled together in chewy bites. Nothing else. So natural, some of my bites had pieces of stem.

I LOVE how these awaken my tastebuds. Tart followed by sweet, then finishes with a little heat. Just because it says "spicy" doesn't mean that it is flaming hot. Think about hot chocolate (or solid chocolate) made with cayenne pepper. Does it ever set your mouth on fire? No, it just adds a hint of warmth/heat. When done well it plays with the other flavors and sits softly on the tongue but doesnt take over, doesnt linger. THIS has that balance. I get that punch of sour and sweet, with a gentle warmth nestling in.

Tamarind is sour and sweet, with a date like texture. I often use it in some Thai based dishes (ever see those reddish blocks of tamarind paste? yeh, that). So basically take some of that, add about equal amount of sugar, then add a pinch of cayenne, roll it up and you have spicy tamarind balls. I haven't actually done that, but that it what I imagine these are. Although these are balled up to be a hand to mouth snack, I suspect that these could be deconstructed if added to a dish.

There are 8 balls in a bag. 2 servings (so four balls) per container, 100 calories. 21 grams of sugar.

So thats 25 calories per ball, and 5 grams of sugar per ball (about same as taking a gummy supplement if needing some perspective, or a spoon of sugar in coffee). I personally can only eat 2 balls at a time. Can easily be satisfied with one ball. SO for me, it a reasonable treat when I just want a little something. Really makes my tastebuds sing!

I'd get these again in a heartbeat, as well as recommend them especially for those that are familiar with tamarind or those that like sweet/sour snacks. Or have open minded taste buds. These are excellent representation of a GOOD tamarind quality. SO GLAD I was able to try them.

Acquired 02/2022 with best by date of 07/25/2024

title: pretty smooth, barely there vanilla, makes nice latte (hot or iced)
text:
pretty smooth matcha with hint of vanilla. I can smell the vanilla more than taste it. The color of matcha is slightly dark dull green. I would not call this ceremonial, but more like a good culinary. It is priced competitively at $7.38 per ounce (current price is $12.99 for 1.76 ounces). Mixes well. I have made basic matcha latte using this, but the vanilla doesnt really poke through.

Container is cylindrical and made of cardboard, mine has a slight dent. Inside is the packet of matcha, either keep it in there or dump out into the container. I poured mine into the container. Fills it about half way.

title: true mango taste, sweet and savory, great w/ pork, noodles, spring rolls, gyoza, etc
text:
Ooh it was hard to decide which one I wanted, Original or Mango. I decided on the mango because I figured that flavor profile would be a little more complicated to get right. This mango option absolutely has a punch of mago flavor. Both sweet and savory, this is gorgeous as dip with spring rolls, gyoza/dumplings, anything with pork. Mmm. Little goes a long way.

I had made a spicy pork noddle bowl, and added a little bit of this to compliment the hotter spices I used. Really added some depth of flavor.

title: excellent 1:1 swap, worked fantastically in the included brownie recipe, Yum!
text:
This review is for the Ilya 1:1 gluten free WHEAT FLOUR swap. I use it to make the "extra fudgy gluten free brownie recipe" they have printed on the back of the bag. I followed it save for adding chocolate chips (I dont care for added texture in my brownies). I used [[ASIN:B0049IF5OU Hersheys unsweetened cocoa powder]]. I used an 8x8 pan, and baked it for an additional 10 minutes in my convection toaster oven. The end result was a thick, chocolately, fudgy brownies with evident homemade taste. Turned out really well. Though I may scale back on the cocoa as it was a bit intense. I may add a little milk instead of water (to boost a milk chocolate taste) and maybe add a little vanilla to smooth it out. Maybe top with a nice frosting to make it over the top good. But just as is, really good. So I am pleased I was able to use this in something that they provided a recipe for. That's how I a really like to test/try a product.

So because it worked out so well in that recipe, I imagine it will work as a good 1:1 swap for anything else I want to use it in.

title: fine oregano POWDER, pleasant aroma, taste, fresh & bright
text:
Neat. I have never used an Oregano POWDER. Usually it is the typical tiny leaves. I think I like the leaves for sprinkling on pizza or pasta as finishing spice, but this powder really packs a punch in soups, sauces, as a rub or other applications where it gets mixed in. The large bottle has a twist off cap, and the cap has two flip top tabs- one for spooning or pouring, the other side for sprinkling. Since it is a fine powder the holes on the sprinkle side might make too much come out. I may see if I have a small shaker jar to put this in. THEN I will find it easier to sprinkle on pizza, pasta, popcorn, etc.

Pack of two is going to last me a long time, so you may want to share a bottle with someone. I acquird this 02/2022, with a best by date of 12/2024

title: cashew cranberry is perfectly sweet w/ creamy crunch. No added sugar or sweeteners
text:
My review is for the CASHEW CRANBERRY, and I love it. This is probably the best granola I have had in a very long time. It is perfectly sweet, yet has NO ADDED SUGAR, and better yet???? NO added/artificial SWEETENERS. What I mean by that is that there aren't any sweeteners used that can cause digestive distress or add an off taste (or make it explosively sweet). Even natural stevia or monk fruit can be a little much for the taste buds and digestion. THIS doesnt use any of that. There is natural sweetness from date paste and cranberries. Sweet but not overly sweet.

There are loose bits, and small clusters. Light crunch, lightly sweet, has a creamy vibe. Really delish eaten by the handful. I may add it to yogurt or top some steel cut oats with it.

Really outshines many granolas i have had, even ones I really like. This is just extra perfect to me.

title: pleasant assortment, crunchy pairs well w/ coffee, definitely a repurchase
text:
I like these more than I thought I would. I have the pack of three, one each of Birthday Cake (crunchy), Chocolate Chip (crunchy), and Double Chocolate (soft baked). I find them to be sweet, but that makes them all the better to be paired with a strong cup of hot coffee. I'm especially enjoying the Birthday Cake, which is more like a sugar cookie. I like the others, but i am not a big fan of chocolate. I look forward to setting out some cookies next time my mom comes over for morning coffee (snow storms have hindered our visists recently). I think she will like them too.

I like the crunchy texture of the two, and I like the softer texture of the other. I see they have a carrot cake cookie, which I have go get like right now. lol.

3 cookies is a serving, one serving is 140/150 calories. 8-9 grams sugar. I think that is reasonable for a snack.

I'm not even in need of gluten free anything, I simply like the ingredients and the overall nutrition profile. I dont feel like I am eating junk. Yet it doesn't taste too healthy either, haha.

5 stars for me because I like the flavor, texture, level of sweetness, and the fact that I am adding more to my cart right now (come to me carrot cookies...!)

title: nice grind, nice container, good salt, no problems!
text:
Phew! The grinder is GOOD. It is a robust, sleek, attractive grinder that has a nice grind and easy to use. Grinder can be refilled. Salt is clean tasting, pleasant.

I have had some grinders that are terrible, so I am very pleased with both the grinder and the salt.

title: smooth dark with mild tang, maybe more like dark leaning tangy medium?
text:
Honduras Dark roast is indeed dark. Overall smooth BUT with a very slight tang, which is momentarily distracting as dark roasts normally do not provide that. I think I am picking up on a hint of molasses. I absolutely prefer dark roasts- I want it thick, chewy, bold, deep. I drink a dark roast black, because a good dark roast needs nothing else. If I am grabbing for the cream, then I am trying to dull a particular tasting note (usually green acidic, bitter, or tangy-- profiles found in lighter roasts). With this.. I grab for the cream. SO what is it that I am tasting? I can tell its dark roast, but the mild tang is confusing. Sometimes that comes with OLD coffee, but it doesn't smell old. Again, they either managed to lift a molasses taste from their roasting method, or they actually added molasses. I can't tell from the description. Is it actually flavored then?

Smells amazing in bag, brews well as a pour over. I am going to try it in my Ibrik as a Turkish brew.

I like it but dont love it.

title: Nice treat, crispy, perfectly salty, well packaged, grab their bigger bags for better price
text:
Well packaged, gift worthy even. Each small bag contains 1 ounce of chips- which is typical amount for 1 serving of regular potato chips. Has 140 calories (also similar). I find that they have a good crisp snap- like a smoother, more solid kettle chip. Definitely has a chip mouth feel. Pleasantly salty, but not overly so. I found that it made a good portion control snack. Overall quite tasty, fresh, and of quality.

I dont rate on price, and these are pricy to me, but taking a look around part of the price reflects convenience of small single serve bags. I see that other brands that are just in 1 big bag of chips the price range is $1.00- $2.00 per ounce. THIS BRAND also offers larger bags (the other option on this page 4.5 ounce bags in a pack of 6, for $29.99, bringing it to closer to the $1.00 range). So while $1.83 per single serve bag/ounce at "sale" price of $21.99 is steep to me (or $2.16 at regular $26 tag) it seems to be falling within typical market range at this point in time. Hence why I focus on quality, taste, packaging, and product received vs product description.

All looks good from my end.

title: great variety pack, use little H20 to make shot, or add to any water bottle to add light essence
text:
I had bought their Squeeze Dried Beetroot packets a few months back and loved it. Having the ability to try other flavors/formulas by this company though a variety pack is awesome. If the flavors sound good to you, then I recommend it. Neat option if you are looking for a convenient way to boost your nutrition. I say flavors, but really it is different formulas as the flavoring is part of what makes it have supplement benefits.

So even though a supplement, I think it is a GREAT way to add some flavor to a bottle of water. Use less water for more flavor (or even less to make it a "shot"), use more water for "flavor essence". I've never felt the need to use more than one packet at a time, but it is really all about preference. You do you!

All the flavors are good (to me). I'm used to strong flavors, and this is easy to drink. All simple ingredients, sweetened with stevia, yet not too sweet. Dissolves well in water- stirred or shaken.

I dont rate on price, we all have different budgets, values, needs. Prices fluctuate. But I do comment. These break down to $1 per packet, which in my extensive experience with "convenience" packets like this (whether it be mushroom, coffee, matcha, electrolyte, immune boosting supplements, supplement shots etc), this price range is within the norm of what I see. Of course I want to spend less, but it is what it is. Main thing is that quality is good, packets are easy to open, definitely convenient, and for me the variety of flavors are pleasant. I'd buy it again.

title: more brown, but not stems or other bits, breaks down to green, bright, tingly, citrusy
text:
Ideally these should be bright green but these are more brown. Not the first time I have encountered brown Sichuan peppercorns. They masticate to a bright green- I can see the oils press out green. The taste is as expected- pungent, bright, herbal, earthy, with a punch of citrus. Has the notable tingling and numbing sensation. I like these when cooked into something, not alone-- but I tried one to taste the "freshness" level. These seem fine. Not a taste that I can handle well by itself. Almost makes me feel ill- I think because the oils or whatever are really potent and lingers for a few minutes. It is an interesting assault on the taste buds. Add in a distinct tingle and numbing, and its a wild little spice to keep around.

Says to keep refrigerated. My experience is any cool, dry place like any other spice is fine. The best buy date printed on mine is for some time in 2023.

title: ZERO SODIUM! kick of heat, sweet, w/ layers of flavor. Thick, spicy, & delicious, but not hot hot
text:
I am not one for stupidly hot hot sauce, so I wasn't sure what to expect from this BLACK ("extremely hot") variety. It has heat with flavor, but not hot hot. That is what I like- give me some heat, but dont make it so hot that it numbs my mouth and I cant taste anything else. This has some true flavor. I was able to place a bit on my tongue and not have any ill "mouth on fire" feeling. I could feel the heat, but it didn't hurt/irritate.

For me, this is edible, and I find it really flavorful. It thick and robust, and just loaded with a mix of SWEET, SAVORY, and HEAT (punch of heat, but not building or irritating). I'd by this again, and I would buy it for someone else as part of a food themed gift.

I would love to have it in a bigger bottle, like a big squeeze sriracha bottle as this would easily be a go-to condiment for me. For use on everything.. eggs, potatoes, burgers, using as a flavoring ingredient in chilis, soups, etc. ((currently using in a bbq slow cooked country pork ribs recipe--choochin away as I trype this. Mmm)

5 stars overall flavor, texture
4 stars heat level (but works in my favor, so that brings us back to 5 stars)
5 (5 thousand stars) for NO SODIUM. Some of my go-to hot sauces happen to be loaded with sodium. This has none. What is this sorcery?

title: salty, sweet, smokey, spicy- versatile flavor combo that packs a lot of flavor
text: Everything I have tried by this company has been exceptional. Such clean, fresh, robust tastes. This CAJUN blend is really quite good. Multi layers of flavor. Initial punch of salt, followed by smokey heat (not too hot, and doesnt build), mixed with a hint of sweet, then it settles into a strong garlic flavor. I love this sprinkled on roasted potatoes. It works real nice mixed with a little mayo or yogurt as a spread or dip. Little goes a long way, so I find extra value in this 2.8 ounce pouch

title: crisp, light tasty flakes, better than most nooch BUT also much pricier, robust glass shaker bottle
text:
Love nutritional yeast, buy it regularly. I dont rate on price (we all have our own budgets, can clearly see the price before purchase, and prices fluctuate), BUT I do comment. At $6.99 for 1.4 ounces, this is phenomenally more expensive than nearly every other nooch option out there. Part of the price goes into the sturdy glass shaker bottle. I wonder if they carry refillable bags for better pricing?

Anyway, thinking this would be the same taste as my usual nooch, I find that this San Fransico Salt Company nutritional yeast has an elevated taste and texture. I dont know how they do it, but it has a slightly more crisp texture over any other brand I have had (and I have had many). Lovely naturally salty cheesy flavor, very clean tasting. Very good quality. Not fortified.

The shaker cap has large holes for effective shaking, or it can be popped off for pouring. I can eat this plain by the spoonful

Quality, taste: 5 stars. No issues

title: WOW!! Moist, dense, perfectly sweet, tastes like regular donut, no weird protein taste. IMPRESSED
text:
I bought these on a whim, well I had them in my saved items, and on a whim added them back to my cart. I have been ordering [[ASIN:B08W9GMY3V Elite Sweets low carb donuts]], which I find surprisingly good so I wasn't looking to try another (got a freezer full!). But I saw these Wow Protein donuts and decided to give them a try anyway. WOW is right. I like them a little more than the Elite (elite is good but has hint of something that is off, but not off enough to make me stop eating them), and I really like these WOW Protein donuts as a for real donut. What I mean is, I find them to be REALLY GOOD, and not just "better than other low carb donuts", and not "good for an alternative". NO, I like these as a REGULAR donut, but they are healthier, and dont make me feel dragged down gross. I would reach for these anytime. I just had one and want more.

I have the "Cake Batter" flavor, havent tried the other one- chocolate. They have an excellent mouth feel, really good natural taste- no weird protein taste, not too sweet, and the sweetness doesnt taste bitter or artificial. TO ME, they taste like a good basic cake donut and of same size. Hearty, firm but moist,. Kind of reminds me of boxed donuts like [[ASIN:B074SZDJ1N Entennmans]] plain cake donut but with a punch of vanilla instead (and heartier). Maybe closer to their individually wrapped pound cake square. Anyway, it reminds me of a regular donut, and I had to double check to make sure it was a low carb donut--thats how regular they taste to me. There are just 4 added grams of sugar, 130 calories. 11 grams protein. 2.5 grams fat. 250 mg sodium. Compared to Elite, which has 0 added sugar, 1 net carb, but has 170/180 cals. Also 11 grams protein. 10 grams fat. 140 sodium

I will buy these again. Pack of 4 is currently $11.99 making them $3 per donut (similar to Elite, depending on which quantity-- buy more save more, getting them closer to $2 per donut). I would love to see bigger packs or better pricing for these WOW Protein donuts.

I also like that they have a long shelf life (acquired 02/2022 with exp date of 09/2022). Not that I expect to keep them around that long (4 donuts? they'll be gone real soon), but it helps that I can just leave them sitting out on counter (Elite has no preservatives and must be refrigerated immediately or frozen lest they mold). The individual packaging is very robust. Donut sits in carboard tray, so totally intact perfectly round delicious donut.

I think they are worth the try, and I am super glad I did. It comes down to preference, so while I may think they are the best thing ever, you may have exact opposite impression. Such is life. Regardless, hope my review helps you make a decision. For what it is worth, I intend to buy more asap (currently unavailable, boo).

title: light, refreshing, not too sweet, not tart, just easy to drink.
text:
I have tried a few Tru varieties: Power (added caffeine), Rescue (added electrolytes), and now this Defend (immunity support). I find them all easy to drink, have a pleasant level of carbonation, and the taste is always light and refreshing. Never overly sweet. Never tart. I really like this pineapple variety.

As with all of the product listings, there are more pics of people drinking it over pictures of helpful information. Would like to see a nutritional profile. That being said, the stuff is good all around.

title: Robust, fragrant, tasty cumin. I highly recommend this brand
text: Tasty, fragrant, robust cumin. I have been impressed with other San Fransisco Salt Company products, especially their [[ASIN:B09HYVH1ML Organic Garlic]] which totally stands out over other garlic I have used in my life. I go through a lot of cumin so I wanted to try their brand. The anticipation for a high quality product has been met once again. It is very good (to me). I do not rate on price, we can all see the price going into it, and prices fluctuate, and we all have different budgets. While I use cumin regularly, really gives dishes a certain special something. However, not many dishes can handle a lot at once, so I dont use a lot at once, therefor this will last me awhile yet not so long that it loses potency., As for the garlic, I go through a lot of garlic and use enough of it each time I cook that the small pack is not conducive to my budget (though if they had bigger container I'd be on it). Even so, it is a 5 star product to me. As with this. So I used it in dishes where I wanted the garlic to really come through. And will buy it again as a side garlic. For this cumin, I will likely buy it again. While I am not a fan of packets of seasoning, I really like the quality enough to move past that. Pressure zip seems to stay closed and not get gunked up with powder. I do rubber band it just in case.

title: can't go wrong, this is a very nice culinary grade matcha, smooth, bright green, good price
text:
Very good, bright green, high quality culinary. I had double checked my bag to make sure it said culinary because this is borderline ceremonial. This is a very good representation of a quality matcha. Though I have to say, I haven't met a matcha that I didnt like, and I have been drinking all grades of matcha for probably 15 years now. That being said, I like it best in a smoothie, so overall grade doesnt matter. But when it comes to a hot tea or latte, the nuances of flavor stand out between brands, grades, regions. This happens to hit all the markers for a good matcha experience. It has a smooth taste with slight green finish, whisks well with hot water, mixes fine into my smoothies, is gentle enough in flavor to add a little to hot cocoa or even coffee. I really dont drink matcha for its taste, I drink it for all its benefits (low key energy, antioxidants, seems to decrease my taste for sweets).

I actually have two sizes of the same matcha from this brand, Somehow I thought I was trying a culinary cersion and a ceremonial. But they are both culinary, both same quality, so my reviews are the same.
