title: good flavor, very sweet, 5 grams fiber, easy to drink on the go
text:
I like the taste- I found it easy on my tastebuds. I like the watery jello-esque testure. I had no problem slurping it through the spout. I squeezed it into my mouth rather than suck it through the port. No noticeable vinegar taste. Mostly sweet, slightly chunky. Has a good amount of fiber per pouch. Low cals. Can be used as a mini meal, or a quick convenient snack.

I dont know whay erythritol and stevia are added to this, doesnt seem to need extra sweetener considering that it has plenty of sugar content from the fruits used. Some of those sweeteners can cause digestive issues for people, so I'd rather not see it

title: light airy puffed cheese, good taste, not too salty tasting, not messy but sticks to teeth
text:
Like a cheese puff, or cheese puff ball but in square shape. Little lighter, more airy than typical cheese puffs. Not as salty tasting. Perfectly cheesy, and I found them pretty tasty. Downside is that they stick to teeth. It has been awhile since I have had a cheese puff, so I dont remember if they stuck to the teeth as much as these do. But it sure is noticeable here. I chomped on these curled up on my couch, and found myself picking my teeth or swishing with water. I wouldnt want to pack these in a lunch box. I didnt find them messy, nor did I have much residue on my fingers.

Overall I do like them. I like the smaller bag, and that even though it has typical amount of sodium for cheese puffs, it doesn't make me excessively thirsty. Sticking to teeth is a tad annoying, but it wont stop me from devouring these.

title: another great flavor by Hypothermias
text:
Im a big fan of Hypothermias syrups. Definitely not limited to use in snowcones. I use any of them as a regular syrup in coffee, smoothies, drizzling over ice cream, yogurt, oatmeal, or mixed into club soda. I find that their flavors are "true", so I can always count on them to taste as described. Some come concentrated, some come premixed, some are sugar free, some are totally devoid of any sweetener. I dont normally go for full sugar syrups, but this uses actual sugar, not corn syrup AND the serving size is reasonable- nearly 2 TBS has 50 cals and 13 grams of sugar. I tend to not ever need more than 1 TBS for flavoring coffee, smoothies, tea, or Italian soda.

When it comes to this Dreamcicle flavor, it is extra awesome to me paied with vanilla ice cream, or added into a vanilla based smoothie. Yum yum

title: pea protein, 9 gr sugar from Agave & Brown Rice syrup, bland taste but palatable, low sweetness
text:
Not much flavor, rather neutral--but what I can taste isn't bad. Take a look at all the goodies contained in this formula and it is rather impressive that they pulled off a neutral tasting nutrition drink. Light vanilla, kinda thick, kinda chalky. But not "bad". I like that it has a faint sweet taste. 9 grams added sugar from low glycemic agave and brown rice syrup. The fact that they dont use artificial sweeteners may make this a huge hit for those that are looking for a diabetic friendly option (or anyone looking to reduce sugar) but dont do well with artificial sweeteners. For example, my 70+ years old mom who is totally healthy and fit, prefers lower sugar options but has digestive issues with all artificial sweeteners. She can handle this. Also, for someone like me, who wants less sugar, and has no issue with artificial sweeteners-- but finds products with the artificial stuff way too sweet, this works well for me. Lastly- PEA PROTEIN. I find whey protein hard to digest, and taste wise a lot of whey products are gross. I dont do soy for various reasons. So I dont mind having some pea protein.

I love a nutrition drink. I dont always eat well, so I rely on supplements to bridge the gap. I also tend to skip breakfast and lunch, yet I like having a smoothie that uses a meal replacement powder to help me power through my day. With this, I either drink it plain, or use it as a base for a smoothie. I also like tossing one in my bag as I head out the door as a "just in case" meal. I've even used it as a "coffee creamer" with success.

Taste: 3 stars. Though really, it is more bland than anything.
Formula: 4.5 stars- lots of goodies, decent nutrition profile, a tad high on sodium for my preference
Overall: 4 stars. I actually think I would consider this again if only for the overall formula and low sweetness taste.

I dont rate on price.

title: nice quality matcha, good one to try out if havent had matcha before
text: Very nice. Pleasantly surprised by the very reasonable price point ($9.50 for 3 ounces, $3.17 per ounce). Good taste, texture, color. Mixes well into my smoothies, or for making simple lattes. I would buy this again, and I may buy this for a friend who has not yet had matcha. Good price point to try it out. I am not a fan of the taste of matcha, but I love it for the non jittery energy it provides me. I am a die hard coffee drinker, but when I need to swipe the cob webs from my brain, it is matcha that clears it out.

title: pretty good for chili, may need to add more spices. Versatile use on other food use
text:
Pretty good as far as pre fab chili seasoning goes. It is a basic seasoning mix using organic spices. You may want to adjust according to taste preference. If you like it more spicy, then add your own hot pepper spices or sauces. If you look at the picture with the ingredients listed, there is no mention of anything spicy unless it falls under the generic term "spices".

Also, to figure out if this will be enough for your needs, take a look at the recipe they include on the packet (1 lb beef, one can tomatoes, 1 can beans). I usually make enough chili for my husband and I to feed an army. So I would need a lot more of this seasoning, or I would need to heavily add to it with my own spices. Which is fine, and is kinda what I did. I happened to have leftover taco meat-- usually I make chili after taco night since a lot of the seasonings are the same. I just add more seasonings, more beans, sauce, and whatever else looks good. When i do it this way (rather than making chili from the get go), I can usually make a more reasonable amount. This packet worked fine for the primary base of flavor on top of the already seasoned meat. I just sprinkled in some hot sauce to spice it up a little more.

This seasoning mix will thicken up your sauce. I like that it isnt overloaded with sodium per serving (380 mg, 4 servings per packet).

I imagine this seasoning packet would also be nice for use on non chili related items-- like potatoes, on eggs, added to dip base, on popcorn, etc.

title: perfectly good culinary matcha, priced well, no problems-- typical performance, taste
text:
Good quality matcha from China (PRC). I drink matcha daily, it is an often purchased item. Any region is fine for me, and while I prefer ceremonial, a good culinary is usually best bet for price and quality. I rarely drink it plain as I actually dont like the taste of matcha, but I drink it all the time because I love the true energy I get from it. I am a hard core coffee drinker, but if I want that fog to be lifted, and get a good non jittery energy buzz, matcha is always up for the job.

This matcha works. Has a slightly green vegetal taste, all within the norm of matcha. I like adding it to smoothies (mask that flavor), or made into a latte with additional flavoring added.

Serving size for this is 1/2 tsp for 3-5 ounces of water. That is about right. Most all matcha will say use 1 tsp per 6-8 ounces of water (more or less depending on taste preference). So this is 50-100 servings depending on how much you use. I tend to use closer to a tablespoon in my smoothies, and closer to just 2 tsp for lattes.

Price wise (not that I rate on it, but I do comment) is within reason for price per ounce for culinary matcha.

Unless a matcha brand stands out as particularly bad, I usually go with 4 or 5 stars. Not so much because it is better than others but because it is as expected. This meets my basic matcha needs, hence 5 stars

title: WAY TOO GOOD, very happy tastebuds. Waistline maybe not so much, haha
text:
3 packs of 4 ounce bags of super tasty cinnamon sugar coated pecans. OMG SO YUM.

Ok, I love that this is a pack of 3 for the weight that $14.95 buys. It helps me to not plow through all 12 ounces. Stout pressure zip bags help keep it all fresh. As is, the serving size for nuts is 1 ounce, and these are so good it is every easy to chomp through the whole bag. So I really like the way these are packaged. Even so, I have to force myself to sprinkle out a handful, and close off the bag and tuck away. They just taste so good.

What more can I say? Just delicious tasting big pecans, coated with cinnamon, sugar, with hint of vanilla. I cant see anyone being disappointed. Really makes my taste buds sing. I add them to my absolute favorite morning oatmeal:[[ASIN:B0917Z5GNH The Pinole Project - High Protein & Fiber Pinole Oatmeal]]

I'd buy these again, I would buy these for others- would make nice addition to a food themed gift bag.

title: like a mild, lightly sweet dark molasses, so many uses
text:
If you like carob, then I imagine you will like this. This is just carob and water in syrup form, and tastes as one would expect. If you aren't already familiar and are curious to try it, I would say that as a syrup, it very much reminds me of a mild molasses. Naturally sweet. Highly versatile use.

I am familiar with carob, having used it as a powder, and often encountering in various forms in health food products as a chocolate substitute, or natural sweetener. I never have a need for it, but I do usually keep some powder in my pantry. I rather like it. Mostly for the great nutritional profile and that it is naturally low in sugar (none added).

title: charming nice assortment, presentation. BUT NOT a usable tray, basket is meh
text:
overall, 3.5 to 4 stars. It's charming, even with its faults I would still consider this as a gift. Hence 4 stars.

Lovely product. Fresh, soft, chewy fruit. well wrapped, nice box. Nice presentation. GIFT WORTHY! The addition of the apple shaped "tray" (not a tray, read more) that can turn into a basket is rather charming and really makes this product an eye catcher. I bought this for myself, but I would consider this as a gift for anyone, anytime.

HOWEVER, know that the tray really doesnt work as a tray. I thought that if the apple shaped plastic tray was kept for use on top of the wood it would work as a tray. The wood itself doesnt really work because it isnt solid-- its all grooves. But when I fully unwrapped it (i hadmt at first), that is when I noticed that the "tray" doesnt stay solid, it immediately begins to turn into the basket. It doesnt lock into a tray. It can not be picked up for use as a tray. Too bad. (hence my edit, because I thought it would stay a tray).

As for use as a basket-- doable, but had potential to tip. Not as in fall over, but the basket is on a slight swivel, and I can easily angle it down. Yet, all told, its cute, and I think anyone would like it. I really have no use for a basket. Had this been a workable tray, I would have loved this item

The fruit: nice assortment, loads of apple rings. Some dry medjool dates. Would like to see pineapple. LOVE the mango. Pear is good. Lots of apricot. Couple items were hard to bite into. Still, for most part good.

I dont rate on price, as I know prices fluctuate and people have their own budgets. But I comment. I was able to get this when it was $30, and I thought that was reasonable. In fact it was an impulse purchase for myself. Now (a few days later) that it is pushing $40 I dont think I would buy this again for myself or as gift. I think some stuff just has a sweet spot for pricing, and closer to $30 is likely it (for me).

But that being said, I think it is a decent gift item. If buying for self, take note of what I said about using it as tray--wont happen.

title: really quite flavorful, but misses on heat level. I can eat direct from spoon. Good flavor though!
text:
Heat with flavor. But not "hot hot". I am not one for hot hot, and I can handle this. Directly off spoon, in fact! Initial warmth but it doesnt build. Not at all uncomfortable. Low key hot. Anyone hoping for hot hot will be disappointed for that. But flavor is good.

What I really like about this is that it has FLAVOR. It isn't just a "hot" product. That bores me, annoys me. This has the ability to add flavor to foods. A little chili like, a little sriracha like. Not runny or watery, but not thick. Is a pourable bottle, not a shaker. It is too thick for a shaker cap.

In terms of taste and texture I would say that it is more like if you took some Sriracha and mixed it with Franks Red hot. And added a dash of chili powder. Mild tang--not bright or distracting.

Good for me, as I dont like super hot. I figure this would be more for my husband as he likes hot hot. But I rather like it.

Taste preferences vary, and I find this sauce to be versatile as it has a good texture and flavor. While I am personally glad that it falls short on heat, I am sure those looking for XX Hot will be unimpressed. But if you can appreciate flavor with some warmth behind it, then give this a try.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. $13 is a bit steep for my budget as a regular purchase. Maybe on occasion or as part of a food themed gift basket.

title: quality matcha, mellow ceremonial grade, lovely non jittery energy boost
text:
I drink matcha all the time. I dont even like the taste of matcha green tea powder, but I love how it makes me feel. It will never replace my beloved coffee, but it is a great addition to my caffeinated needs. Big bonus? loaded with antioxidants. Matcha just gives me such a good long lasting thrum of energy. No jitters. I usually make a hot latte, or a iced latte, or my favorite: add to a smoothie. Then I am getting loads of nutrition and I cant taste the matcha, haha. Depending on how much is used, matcha can actually work well mixed into coffee (odd, I know, but give it a try), or hot cocoa. If I drink it plain, then I make it iced.

I prefer matcha green tea powder over green tea leaves because I am consuming the leaves rather than just having the left over from steeping. More bang for the buck.

This matcha is good quality, no issues. Ceremonial grade, which has a more mellow taste over culinary. Fine powder as expected. Whisk well. I have had dozens of brands over the years, and while there are differences- nuances- between grades, brands, regions, I am usually totally fine with any of them. Especially how I use the powder-- mixed well with other flavors. I have tried matcha on its own, and I just cant get past the taste. But it is a part of my daily life for the last 15 years.

Comes in small 1 ounce tin. I dont rate on price, but I do comment. Their coffee products and this matcha fall on higher end of pricing spectrum. Quality is there, which is most important to me.

OVERALL: 5 stars. Not because it is necessarily better than others, but because it falls directly into range of expectation for quality, taste, performance.

title: like an extra creamy deviled egg filling, minimal lemon pairs nice w/ savory applications
text:
Direct from jar, this is thick, more of a spread than a sauce. Once warmed up, it becomes a pourable sauce. It like that it has the initial thick texture- makes for nice dip or addition to a sandwich. Taste wise, it reminds me more of deviled egg filling. In fact, I may use this to make an egg salad sandwich or some deviled eggs with this. I had it mixed in with canned salmon & crackers.
I have had Hollandaise sauce many times through my life, and no two are the same. This has an aioli vibe, matte appearance. Some are liquid with a shiny look. All depends on what goes into it, and the amounts. This seems extra rich. I think it is nicer than many. I like this more than some because the lemon doesnt really come through. Which I find better for more savory applications. For me, it would be my preference for eggs benedict. The more lemony tart varieties are better for vegetables, or maybe chicken. Though I saw some reviews saying it was lemony. Not to me, and to me that is a good thing. Other reviews say not enough lemon-as a bad thing. I prefer less lemony varieties, more eggy. See, it is really a personal preference, so all I can do is describe it. In short, "like an extra creamy deviled egg filling" taste.

title: lightly sweet from cane sugar, gentle fizz, decaff tea w/ added juice/flavors. Pretty good!
text:
Ever so lightly sweet, gently fizzy, naturally flavored delicate tasting "sparkling tea". I love fizz, so this is right up my ally. They are all decaffeinated, so this is especially nice for later afternoon or evening consumption. PSA: peach option also contains ginger.

I am pleasantly surprised by the tase. It tastes like carbonated tea, with added flavor. The flavors are mild, and pair nicely with the teas used. I greatly appreciate that the citric acid is very low in taste. Some carbonated seltzers/beverages, especially the more delicately flavored varieties can be ruined by too tart/rough of citric acid taste coming through. I find this well done. I taste the "flavor" then the "tea", then the citric acid sitting nicely in the background. Some scream citric acid while any other flavor begs for attention. This is well balanced (to me).

--Ginger Limeade White Tea tastes like a mix of gingerale and tea. I taste lime, but there is no lime in this. I only see mango, passionfruit, and apple as far as juice goes. Has ginger.

--Peach Green Tea also has ginger. It should be called ginger peach. I often have ginger peach green tea, and this was immediately noticeable that it is ginger peach, not just peach. So if you like ginger peach, then you will like this. If you wanted peach only, then you will be disappointed. The ingredients can be seen in the product description pictures, but it would be easy to miss.

--Citrus Punch Hibiscus has the bite of natural hibiscus. I cant quite pinpoint the other fruity-ish flavors, and they aren't listed on the can. Mostly hibiscus forward.

I like that it is LIGHTLY sweetened with cane sugar, not at all cloying or syrupy- between 4g and 6g per 1 can serving (my gummy vitamins have that amount, for reference). 30 calories for 12 ounce can.

I'm a big fan of ginger, so finding out that the Peach is really GINGER peach is a bonus, but could very well be disappointing to some. I like them all, this is my style of drink. Just the type I would keep on hand to grab when I just want a simple non caffeinated not too sweet (but not artificially sweetened) bubbly drink. Really nice option for those that dont do well with non cane sugar sweeteners. I'd consider buying this again.

title: tastes best a day or two later, good alone or w/ frosting, coconut flavor from oil only
text:
When reading reviews, be sure to sort based on the variety you are interested in, and maybe sort to see the most recent. Things change, varieties differ. This review is for the YELLOW SNACKING CAKE.

Easy to make. This formula is in a base of almond flour, no coconut flour. So if you dont want a coconut flavor then omit the coconut oil and swap to something else or use refined coconut oil (no coconut flavor). Want more vanilla taste? add more vanilla.

Bakes up well. Kind of spongey, definitely moist. Has large crumb- reminds me more of cornbread in texture (but moist). Allow to cool completely before cutting. Directions say as such- this helps reduce crumbling, breaking apart.

Tastes fine on its own as a snacking cake. No frosting needed. But it holds up well with some added frosting. It is pretty sweet already. I dont know why all these baking mixes have to be over the top sweet. I'd like this more if it were less sweet (but I find this true of other brands I have tried too)

I think this cake tastes better a day or two later, and it seems to stay fresh and moist for several days.

I dont rate on price. We all have different budgets, values. Prices fluctuate. But I do comment. I tried this on a whim. I want to find a go-to dessert that isnt loaded with sugar. This is sweeter than I want, but it is pretty good overall. Not sure if it is a repurchase, but I do think it is worth the try.

I had also tried their [[ASIN:B01H298206 Brownie Mix]], which has a very chocolatey not too sweet flavor. I made that according to direction for "fudge like" brownies, and wish I hadnt because it actually tasted and had mouth feel of fudge (which I hate as a texture). It went uneaten. Most regular brownie mixes have a "fudge like" option, which simply makes it like a trypical brownie. Where the "cake like" option makes it more like a fluffy cake (which I dont want in a brownie). I went with what I know. For this, I didnt expect it to actually be like fudge.

title: coconut cake, better next day, super sweet & moist, no frosting needed, has Chicory fiber
text:
So sweet. I wish it was less sweet. I find a lot of these "no sugar" baking mixes are over the top way too sweet. WHY?! Simmer down on the sweeteners! Use frosting at your own risk. This is really more of a snacking cake that does not need frosting. That being said, it is within the realm of normal, taste & texture wise.

Texture is as expected for a coconut flour and almond flour base. You know, moist but kind of gritty and dense (like cornbread), not fluffy and airy like white flour cakes. Again, within realm of normal.

Because it uses coconut flour, this is going to have a coconut flour taste. You must like coconut. It calls for coconut oil, which will further boost the coconut flavor. If you want less coconut flavor, use refined coconut oil, or some other oil that fits your dietary needs. But coconut will still come through.

It cooks up moist. Definitely allow it to cool before cutting into it lest it falls apart. Holds together well, but is borderline crumbly.

Definitely tastes better the NEXT day. I dont know why, but I find that true of other keto cake mixes.

Definitely not a low calorie food, 10 servings. Happens to be the one thing I can not eat much of at once. If it were a normal cake, I would easily eat this as 1 or 2 pieces of cake. But this super intensely sweet cake is easily 6-8 servings of good size, 10 if just taking a few bites at a time (which is likely good enough).

Contains CHICORY, so if you eat too much or are not used to chicory, know that this is a form of fiber that may make you very gassy. That combined with the sweeteners (that can cause digestive distress) and this cake may be as painful as it is sweet. Again, within the realm of normal for products of this nature. lol

I DO NOT rate on price. Prices vary, and everyone can see the price when they buy it. Also prices fluctuate. And we all have different budgets, values. BUT I do comment. . Currently the price is $4.98. I thought that reasonable for a brand I know and trust. It was an impulse purchase because of the fair pricing. I have spent as much as $13 for a [[ASIN:B0764H5423 similar yellow snacking cake]], which I will never do again for any cake mix. However at <$5 I would say that it is worth the try. If you dont like this one, you likely wont like any of them. I'm at the spot where I am going to try to make my own from scratch.

Overall, it is "good" in that it meets expectations. I am not "keto" but I do try to reduce my sugar intake. I dont consume stuff like this with abandon. I count it like I was having a regular dessert. I dont indulge in regular desserts (or not often) because it is more likely to trigger a binge, or trigger a growing desire for me. I am not triggered by these sweeteners to eat more. If anything it works as an aversive. I dont know enough about the sweeteners to know if it still spikes blood sugar or not. I am assuming not since I am not craving more sweet when I eat this stuff.

If it was less sweet I would like it more. Not sure what I can do to it to make it less sweet. I dont know what order of magnitude of other ingredients would need to be added to make a sizeable adjustment to the level of sweetness.

title: use alone, or use as flavor base, not overloaded w/ sodium (100 mg per 1/4 tsp)
text:
KEEP IN MIND, that an "umami" blend isn't meant to add specific/notable pungent spice flavors. This isnt a spice blend per say, but a variety of spices that come together to help create an overall "umami" (Umami, being another one of the tastes our tongues recognize along with salt, sweet, bitter, and sour, it is generally described as having a “savory” or “meaty” quality). I think this does the job (and this is where nuance comes into play as there is more than one way to achieve umami ie soy, miso, kelp, mushroom, etc)

Pleasant savory flavor, easy to use, versatile. I will often use more savory spices, or some soy, and/or mushroom powder to boost the savory umami flavor. Umami doesnt always have to be salty. It just needs to expand the tastebuds to pick up on a slightly meaty essence. Hence why mushrooms and soy are often used. But some products are way overloaded with sodium. This has its fair share at 100 mg per 1/4 tsp serving, but it isn't going to push my intake over the edge.

Has a powder like consistency. Not at all granular. Think more like a mushroom powder.

Has a nice easy taste that works well sprinkled ON foods (potatoes! eggs, egg noodles, etc), or doled out into a recipe (meatballs, meatloaf, burgers, veggie burgers, roasts, seitan, gravy, etc). I recommend using it as BASE of flavor, then working up from there with other spices. But by all means, give this a try alone too.

I like it sprinkled into my sipping broths, where some need a little added oomph

title: I like their products, good quality, tastes as it should, nice surge of energy w/ each cup
text:
I think that is the stand out feature of the Host Defense products, they taste like they should. Coffee taste like coffee, cocoa tastes like cocoa, and matcha (for better or worse, haha) tastes like matcha. The addition of Lions Mane changes nothing. I find their stuff easy to drink and rather like them. Perhaps I stand alone on this, but that's where I am at.

I drink matcha daily, I consume mushroom supplements daily. I often combine the two. This product does it for me. I make according to directions, sometimes using a little more. I love matcha for its benefits, not so much for its taste. I usually add it to a smoothie, or I make a latte of the sorts using some hot water and cream, then add a little vanilla flavoring to tone down the matcha taste. This is all brands, and including this one. Though it is ever so more mellow than some matcha products. For that, it reminds me more of a ceremonial grade. I am thinking it is the addition of Lions Mane that mellows it out a bit. If need be, I could drink this plain.

Can save money by pricing out two different products, but I am not one to rate on price. I figure you can decide for yourself what your budget is for stuff like this. I have had blends like this before, and even just some matcha can come in at the price point this is per ounce. I assume this is culinary grade (so a tad pricey), but the matcha is at least sourced from Japan, and is certified organic. I really dont have any problems with the Host Defense MycoBrew products. I have had their [[ASIN:B09FQ1458D Instant coffee & mushroom blend]] , their [[ASIN:B09FQ13C1F hot cocoa with mushroom blend]], and now this matcha with mushroom blend. They've all be satisfactory, albeit on the higher end for pricing. Quality seems fine, everything dissolves well, and taste is as natural as can be. Even does a good job dissolving in cold water when shaken up.

BTW, their one pic in the product description shows an open container of brown powder. That must be their coffee, because this matcha is green, slightly olive drab but definitely green.

I'm actually having a cuppa of this matcha (hot water, half n half, [[ASIN:B08YB9TNDG no sugar vanilla syrup]], collagen powder) and actually am enjoying the taste and enjoying the nice low key energy coming over me. So at least I can also add that it is legit.

Not sure if its a repurchase, but its a possibility. If I traveled or worked in a regular office, I would have this tag along with me for on the go use.

title: soft natural vanilla that is perfect for non baking needs- smoothies, oats, frosting, etc
text: non alcohol option makes it nice for use in non baking preparations.But also fine for baking, cooking. I usually keep a few different styles on hand depending on my needs. Taste wise, it reminds me of vanilla bean paste, just a soft natural vanilla with no alcohol to cook off, or hope that it dissipates in whatever you put it in. But it does have glycerin, which blends in/disappears once in something. I like this for smoothies, oats, matcha, frosting. Stuff like that. I wont waste this in cookies or cakes. That I will use the ultra cheap alcohol based stuff.  Price is reasonable, but I dont rate on price.

title: Sweet w/ natural vanilla taste. Keto option has better taste over regular, inc MCT oil
text:
I much prefer the Keto Skinny Syrups over their regular skinny syrups. The sweeteners used are better tasting, and the actual flavors are better. BUT if you are brand new to Jordans Skinny Syrups, please know that they are not super flavorful. Many people love them, but I would prefer a stronger flavor across the board. Do yourself a favor, try one bottle first. If you like it, then feel free to stock up.

I find the flavors are stronger and come through much better with the Keto version over the regular skinny syrups. Those I find to be all sweetness and no flavor, always disappointing. So I have been making the switch. Hope they come out with more Keto versions. I also like the thicker texture- this is from the MCT oil. All around, even as a non Keto person, I much prefer this version over the regular. I give 5 stars because I can taste the vanilla, the vanilla tastes natural (all considered) and the price was good for 2 big bottles ($10-11 for TWO).

--SO, if you want a little more flavor and less sweetness, go with the KETO version (uses monk fruit & erythritol) .
--IF you prefer excess sweetness with little to no flavor go with their regular skinny syrup (sucralose).

I prefer to buy the syrups on Amazon because I can buy just what I want, rather than get suckered into multiple bottles for a shipping break. Prices fluctuate on Amazon, but I still prefer to buy it here. The website expects quite a bit to be spent before getting a shipping break (and coupons, sales dont help any--just makes you buy even more). Anyway, I appreciate being able to get it here when I want, as many or as little as I want.

title: pricey, but I like it. Made according to directions I can drink it black or w/ cream.
text:
I'm no stranger to mushroom supplements, instant coffee, or instant coffee plus mushroom blends.

I made this according to directions, and I found it to be tasty. It dissolved well, stayed mixed, and I didn't notice anything off. It didn't take long to drink it, but I didn't gulp it down either. When it is prepared as directed, it may or may not have enough of a coffee taste. I thought it was for the most part, fine as is, was actually kind of impressed--but I added just a little more and it was extra perfect. I'd drink it as my second cup of coffee, not my first or only.

It all dissolved well, and I drank it black. My next cup I added a little creamer. Again, I have had lots and lots and lots of stuff like this, so I kind of knew what to expect, and this was a little better than other formulas I have consumed. You may think differently.

As prepared, there is just 39 mg of caffeine. The other thing I do with stuff like this is to add it to my coffee (brewed or instant) for extra boost, or I add it to chocolate smoothies for a little extra kick of caffeine.

Ultimately for best price, buying a separate mushroom blend (single mushroom, or multi blend) and adding it to your coffee is the way to go. But who am I to judge how you spend your money? I think it is pricey for the amount. I like Mycobrew products but they are at the higher end for amount one gets. Even so, I dont rate on that. We can all see the price before purchase. I think everything I have had by Mycrobrew has had a good taste- nothing weird or off putting. Give their [[ASIN:B09FQ13C1F Hot Cocoa with Lions Mane]] for a chocolate treat.

Other coffee with mushrooms that I have liked (and has more coffee taste): [[ASIN:B08ZXJY5C3 EcoTaste Organic Mushroom Coffee]]

I also have enjoyed [[ASIN:B0964DP4TM Wundergrounds Brainchild Instant Mushroom coffee]]

anything by [[ASIN:B08RN3PCBW Apothekary The Littles variety pack]]

Add 1 rounded teaspoon to 6oz hot milk or water. Stir and enjoy!

Ingredients

title: taco seasoning flavor, large soft & chewy stick., easy to open, not my fave but good
text:
There is a lot of good going for this Baja brand of beef sticks. They are large and thick. Has an easy to open packet, low calorie, super low/no sugar, and while there is 390 mg of sodium, it isn't as crazy high as some. The texture is soft and chewy. Could use a little more snap, but overall I like it for a quick simple snack. The only down side to me is that there is an ever so slightly fatty vibe- more like biting into sausage.

Taste-wise? This definitely has a taco taste to me (street taco? I have no idea, but taco seasoning packet taste? yes). I love me some tacos, but as a beef stick flavor I dont care for it. I didnt know until I tried it. I'll work my way through the box, but likely not a repurchase.

I have also had their [[ASIN:B09NLBQ23L Traditional beef sticks]], and of the two, I like the "traditional" better. Though I find it a bit too plain tasting. Either will work in a pinch on the go, or paired with cheese. Nice hit of protein without a lot of anything else that is concerning. I dont love these, but I dont dislike them. Price is reasonable for the size of the stick. I would try other flavors. Hence my 4 stars

title: big beef sticks, soft & chewy, not too salty, but a bit plain tasting, fatty like sausage

title: perfectly good chewy wild rice, reasonably priced 5 lb bag for 100% wild rice
text:
Perfectly good wild rice. I have wild rice regularly (ish), and therefore is a pantry staple-- especially when I am trying to eat healthier, lol. More often I see it in stores mixed with other (real) rice, but when I get it on its own, I pick up a pack. Usually pricey when I can find it. So pricey.

This is just wild rice (really a grass), and the price point per ounce is really quite reasonable. Of course, this is more like bulk pricing, and a 5 lb bag will last a very long time. Thick pressure zip bag. Either keep it stored in this bag, or divide out into smaller bags or containers. Wild rice doesnt seem to ever go bad, but I am pretty liberal with best buy dates. Still, I will share some with my 70 something mom.

For those that dont know, wild rice is healthy, has an impressive nutritional profile, and has a great chewy texture. Pairs nicely with other textures- barley, any rice, even some pastas, vegetables, etc. But also works well on its own. Cook time takes awhile- plan for 45-60 minutes. It is "done" when the grass splits open. From there just adjust water and time depending on the texture you want.

Freezes well. Like, go ahead and make up a big batch, then freeze portions for quick lunch and dinner use.

No shortage of recipes using wild rice on the internet. Several can be found directly on their web page puremaitreya-dot-com

title: good flavor, dense, chewy. Not strong on whey protein taste
text:
This is the second Unite protein bar I have tried, and I like what I have had so far. This and the PB&J. Both are good. I like the other a little more than this, but the churro is pretty good too. The main thing is that it doesnt taste like a brick of whey protein. The ingredients are pretty good, nutritional profile is good, and it really hits the spot as a post workout or anytime snack. I like keeping stuff like this in my purse or car as you never know when you will need something to eat.

Dense, chewy, not too sweet. Can taste creamy almond, some cinnamon, and there are bits of something that add texture. Love that it is a woman owned company.

worth the try

title: surprisingly tasty- like a PB&J sandwich, good ingredients, good nutrition
text:
Gotta say, this is actually pretty good. It is always a toss up as to whether a protein bar will be any good. They always sound better than they are, always are pictured better than they are. Well I knew this wasn't going to look like a PB&J sandwich, but how would it taste? Interestingly, I can taste peanut butter and jelly.. very similarly tasting as though it were a sandwich. Not sure how they did that, but its pretty neat. It is a thick, dense chewy bar with bits of peanuts to break up the texture. I taste some sweetness like jelly/jam. And then of course peanut butter.

I like that it has a good amount of protein, fiber, and not too heavy in the whey protein taste. They did well with that. Not too sweet. I dont love it- but for a protein bar, I think it is pretty good. I have also tried their Churro bar, and of the two I prefer this one. Really like the simple ingredients, the nutritional profile, the freshness, and that it is a women owned company.

Ingredients:
Peanut Butter, Peanut, Iso-Malto-Oligosaccharide Syrup (from Tapioca), Whey Protein Concentrate, Organic Agave Syrup, Strawberry Fruit Bits (Apples, Strawbetter Juice Concentrate, Baobab, Sunflower Oil, Pectin, Natural Flavor, Red Beet Extract), Chicory Root Fiber, PEanut Flour, Dates, Organic Hemp Hearts, Natural Flavor, Sea Salt

title: gift worthy, lovely assortment, nice size, clear labels, nice presentation, glad I got it!
text:
Gift worthy set of spices. I received the box and didnt know what it was at first. I was like, OooooOooh who bought me something? it just has visual appeal. Comes wrapped in plastic film, so I expect the same if you were to purchase for someone else (or yourself). Once emptied, give the box to your kids to color, or give to your cat to sit in. Color it, and make it a fancy box for kitty.

Heavy box, packed with spices. Nice assortment. Much I already have, but I would love this as a gift, or for giving someone who is just starting out. Normally I would prefer a name brand, but there is enough info on the company that I felt comfortable giving it a try. Their web page is very easy to find.

I dig the labeling--clear to read, easy to see, and because of this I would reuse these containers. I like the small size of the containers. Nice for easy storage and for working with minimal space (campers, outdoor kitchens, apartments, dorms, small spaces, or for those that dont cook a lot or are learning). Can buy a bigger container to refill from, and keep the bigger containers in a different spot.

Twist off lid. No shaker. Pinch out, pour out, or use a measuring spoon.

5 stars because I am pleasantly surprised and overall impressed.

title: Canadian chocolate w/ nuanced tasting notes, nice little assortment. 12 pc per box, mixed
text:
12 individually wrapped candy hearts per box, 6 boxes. The boxes are cardboard, taped closed, and has a tuck away tab to keep closed once the tape is cut through. About 3 servings per container (assume 4 pieces make a serving), and provides a mix of white chocolate hearts, milk chocolate hearts, and dark chocolate hearts. All crisped.

Chocolate quality is fine. It is Canadian chocolate. I live at near the border, and it is known the taste and quality is different than American chocolate, even the same brand side by side. Friends and I would often go to Canada to buy chocolate (and lap dances as here to we didnt have dancing naked guys to go view stateside). So after getting our fill of one, we'd head to any store for our fill of another. Was always fun to make our declarations at the border.
Them: "Bringing anything back with you?..
Us: "memories! *big smile* and chocolate!" *bigger smile, holds up coffee crisp*

And so, this Valentines, I will pass out a few of these boxes to old friends as we fondly remember our old adventures looking for a good piece of.. chocolate. Borders are closed, or are at least not easy to cross, and most of us are middle aged and on diets (lol), so our um, adventures are on hiatus.

Anyway, the chocolate is pretty good to me. I cant quite describe the difference from most other chocolates, but there is nuance that you may or may not enjoy. But really, it is fine and I think most people would appreciate a cute container of num nums. SO much better than a box of mixed chocolate with weird fillings and truly cruddy chocolate from drugstore. BTW, check out their website for more info about the Jelina Chocolatier company. Not a dollar store brand. I would totally buy their white or milk chocolate bars. If they had orange chocolate I would love them forever *going to go look*

I really like the white chocolate, then the milk, followed lastly by the dark. I am not a fan of dark but this is at least creamy. Let the hearts melt on your tongue.

The boxes aren't fancy, just a simple heart shaped box.

title: crunchy but a tad oily, tasty salty garlic & parm flavor 3.5/4 stars
text:
A little oily, but packs a whole lot of flavor and crunch. Kettle chips, well., chips like this always pack more calories (and fat) per ounce than their other thinly sliced counterparts. These pack 220 calories per ounce.

I like the parm & garlic together. Salty taste, but doesn't appear to have too much sodium. I love chips for stuffing into my sandwiches, and these are a tasty addition. I also have enjoyed them alone. Somehow I have managed not to eat the whole container at once. While just being an 8 ounce container, it seems never ending. Mix of large pieces and smaller bits.

I cant figure out why, but I get some digestive distress. First time I had them I really did eat a lot, and then spent rest of evening not feeling well. I thought maybe it was something else I ate, but then the next two times I had some, I felt my insides churning again. I think these may be too fatty/oily for me-- even if the nutritional info seems within reason for kettle chips. All this could be just me, and I do tend to overeat. So I am likely eating too much of these at once (but when I do eat chips I tend to eat a lot, so I am not sure).

I liked the taste and crunch, I rather like the box container over the typical bag.

3.5 to 4 stars

title: delicious apricot juice
text:
Pomona is a quality brand, I've always been pleased with any of their juices. I had never actually had straight apricot juice, so this is a first. It tastes like.. apricot. It's good! Not too sweet, has a thick mouth feel yet there is no pulp. Kind of like how straight tomato juice is. Shake well! It is loaded with potassium (622 mg), who knew?!

Product of Georgia

title: Chai has pretty good chai flavor, ultra sweet as usual for the Skinny Syrups.
text:
I dont love Skinny Syrups- they tend to be way too sweet with little flavor. I could handle the sweetness if the flavor was as strong. This CHAI option is one of the best in my opinion as I can actually taste the flavoring--better balance. Still mega sweet, but I like the flavor. It works well in my smoothies and the occasional tea, especially chai tea. Yum.. I would like to see this come out in a Keto option. Not that I am Keto, but the flavoring tends to be better with their Keto options, and the sweeteners they use are different too. The regular skinny syrups use Sucralose. So while not exactly a 5 star product, it is one that I keep buying hence my 5 stars.

I had tried out a lot of their syrups. I had purchased several bottles (a wide assortment) at once on their website (they get you with shipping if you dont order a lot, and if you have a coupon or discount, you have to buy even more to hit the minimum for shipping, hence why I bought some on Amazon as I can buy one at a time as I want/need them). Please to see the bottles offered on Amazon. They cost more here, yet I prefer to buy one at a time as I need/want. Sometimes I go through a lot, sometimes it takes me awhile. Amazon helps me to get what I want without hassle.

title: VERY GOOD, pure, nothing else added, comes w/ scoop, glass bottle, shaker cap, or twist off
text:
A little bit goes a long way. There is nothing else added, this is pure monk fruit. The entire fruit is sweet, but the natural sugars in monk fruit are not the main compounds responsible for its sweetness. Monk fruit extract actually gets its intense sweetness from unique antioxidants called mogrosides, an inner part of the fruit. There are various mogrosides contained within, and the one used here is specifically mogroside V. "25%", which is a solid amount. It gives the greatest bang for the buck, and taste buds. A couple components in the monk fruit are sweeter, but there is less of it making it not as conducive to extracting.

There are no fillers, no other sweeteners, just monk fruit. MonkVee is a NY company. The actual product- thought it doesnt say, is going to be from China or Thailand, BECAUSE monk fruit is NATIVE to China and Thailand, nowhere else.

Because this is JUST monk fruit, and is a very concentrated source of sweetness, it is NOT a 1:1 swap for regular sugar. For that, you will need to buy a blend. A mere PINCH of this powder is equivalent to 1TBS of sugar. For that, baking might be tricky. But for coffee, other simple sweetening needs? YES.

Light beige super fine powder. No granules. Just powder that packs into the tiny long handled scoop that is included in the bottle. I appreciate this as it makes it much easier to portion some out into my coffee or whatever. I like it better than liquid versions.

Monk fruit sugar has been part of my pantry for many years now, before it became available in everything. Back then just the pure stuff would be found in specialty grocers. Most of the time now I keep a blend as it is easier for me to bake with. I like when products contain monk fruit because I know the taste is going to be better. Monk fruit does not have a lingering off taste that other natural (and artificial) sweeteners can have. By itself it has a lightly fruity taste, kind of like grapes. But this does not transfer to what it is mixed into.

This is pure monk fruit, dont need much, really best for coffee and applications like that.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. This contains 0.7 ounces (19.85 grams). It is a glass bottle with twist off lid and shaker cap combined. Also has a long handled mini scoop. It is a reasonable price within the normal range. I shopped around, and saw that at best I can buy a packet of nearly the same size for only $2 less. I will take this container and scoop any day over a pressure zip pack.

title: pleasantly mild matcha powder, not bitter. No problems
text:
Gentle tasting matcha- not bitter, not too green. It mixes well in hot water or hot milk. I usually make matcha lattes or add it to smoothies. I use a mixer when I make anything with matcha.

I love matcha, for the benefits, but not for the taste. So any time I find matcha powder that it more mild in taste, I am happier for it. This is pretty good. All told though, out of the dozens and dozens of matcha powder I have had over the past 15-20 years, I find most all of them to be just fine for my needs. From super cheap to super pricy. Yeh, the grade and region makes the difference, but the way I use it the nuances dont stand out enough to appreciate. I think those that also enjoy matcha as a hot tea will appreciate the gentle flavor of this. Definitely in the ceremonial spectrum.

I have no problems, concerns with it. Perfectly good matcha powder.

title: not overly sweet, good chocolate taste, makes a nice treat (60 cals, 6 grams sugar)
text:
I like it. The main reason I like it is that has a natural chocolate taste, isn't loaded with sugar, and the mushroom is hidden in the background yet has a decent amount. It really just tastes like hot chocolate to me, and not overly sweet. It dissolves well in hot water or hot milk (I used unsweetened almond milk). 60 cals per serving.. not too shabby!

I make small mugs of hot cocoa as any more than 6-8 ounces is just too much. So the serving size on this happens to be 6 ounces of liquid to one scoop, and that works for me. Need more? add more. Or supplement with some plain hot cocoa or whatever. I happen to have some chocolate collagen powder that pairs well with this. I could make my own blend easily enough, but this mix is quite nice. Not sure if it is a repurchase, but I like it and have no issues with it. I dont rate on price, sorry.

Cocoa, coconut sugar (6 grams), lions mane (800mg), fermented brown rice biomass, sea salt

title: gentle flavor, delicate vegetal notes, fresh aroma- good alone, as latte, etc
text:
1.4 ounce tin of mildly vegetal, overall mellow tasting matcha. It makes for a smooth tasting cup of plain matcha, or blends in well among other additions. I drink it primarily for the energy boost and the health benefits. I actually dont enjoy matcha much as a plain drink. The premium/ceremonial stuff is definitely easier on the tastebuds, and this Naoki matcha is just that. I can make a simple cup of hot matcha and add a little sweetener, cream. Works well in a latte, but I use 2-3 tsp of matcha powder for that (or 1-2 tsp of culinary). I can even add it to some hot cocoa when I want to totally mask the taste. I love adding it to smoothies, though usually I go with a cheaper culinary grade when I do that.

Beautiful green powder. The matcha is in a bag tucked into the tin. I poured mine into the tin. Contains 20 one teaspoon servings.

I see/taste nothing wrong with this matcha. Probably in my top 5 for ceremonial grade.

title: not too salty, not too hot, well balanced flavor
text:
I'm not well versed in Bloody Mary mixes. I just know that some are excruciatingly salty, and some have no flavor, or are watery. Some are hot, some are zingy, some are single note tomato boring. Pleased to report that this has a lovely tomato taste with well balanced salt and seasoning taste. Underlying hint of worchestershire. A kick of spice really makes this tasty. No zing/tart that I can tell.

I've enjoyed a little by itself too- just pleasing to me. It is on the thicker side, which makes the drink look and taste better- it doesnt get watered down. The bottle includes recipe for basic bloody mary (vodka) as well as others using tequila, rum, or beer.

It's good.

title: lovely assortment, mostly medium, 1 dark, 1 light, 3 flavored. Pretty good!
text:
Box of 10 bags of 10 capsules each. Keep the box for reference for what type of coffee each pack of capsules are. Primarily medium roast (including decaff) with a bag of light roast and a bag of dark roast. A few flavored varieties (caramel, vanilla, chocolate). I love dark coffee, and have been really enjoying the Nero most of all.

It is a really nice assortment, especially for workplace or household of different preferences.

Compatible with Nespresso Original line, or can easily be opened and placed in filter for pour over coffee (I do this for when I am on the go and dont have access to capsule brewers). It is just a foil top, and coffee is not super densely packed. I can tap out the coffee easily. I also do this for reviews so I can comment on how much coffee seems to be in a capsule. When it is loose, I just assume less that the densely packed options I have tried. I can tell it is less coffee in strength of taste. However, I have enjoyed what I have tried, and I would get this assortment again, or for someone else.

title: 1-2 pc for pop of minty freshness, not long lasting, but no less than similar brands
text:
Not too shabby for not being a plastic based gum. It provides some chew, but it isn't a long lasting chew stretchy chew-- the mouth feel is a little off. I am fine with that, because I dont like to chew gum for long anyway. I use it for quick breath freshening, and for use in long walks/hikes where the chewing action helps keep my mouth from feeling parched. Or nice way to make sure I stop eating after a meal.

Has a nice pop of minty flavor. One piece is fine for that. Similar in size to other pop out pieces. Use two pieces for bigger wad of gum. Love the box of multiple packs.

Kinda sticks to my implant, so I try to avoid chewing gum on that side. But just be me, or it might be the gum. Figured it was worth mentioning.

Uses about a gram of Xylitol per piece. While xylitol is good for teeth, and is used to make items sweet, be sure to keep this away from dogs as no amount of xylitol is safe for any sized dog. (most gums use xylitol these days).

Sweetened with xylitol and stevia. No aspartame!

title: organic powdered sugar, food based coloring, easy to make, lasts forever in fridge
text:
So far I have tried this red, the blue, and the yellow. I like the blue so far the best. Yellow has a slight off taste and has no vanilla taste (maybe I got a bad batch?), blue has a neutral vanilla taste that is very pleasing, and this red is somewhere between the two- I pick up hint of beet. Has a good flavor, but a little something else is there. I add a little extra vanilla and all is well. Looks lovely on white cake. I have enough for sugar cookies, which I will make as a Valentines day treat.

This is really just organic powdered sugar with food based coloring. I am prone to not feeling quite right after consuming artificial blues and reds. This gives me the option to have colorful frosting without using artificial dyes. The colors always turn out well, and this red "fruit punch" color is no different.

Easy to make-- same as other prefab kits and at home from scratch-- just add some liquid and some butter (or butter alternative). Use a hand mixer to get it nice and creamy, fluffy.

Priced similarly to other prefabs. If you dont care if you have food based dye or not, organic powdered sugar or not, then the most budget friendly option is a typical bag of powdered sugar and artificial dye.

Makes a generous amount, and leftover store really really well in the fridge. I have no problem taking a few spoonfuls out for use on a scone, muffin, or whatever else i have going on that can benefit from some frosting. It doesnt separate or flatten. Just looks and tastes as good as day one.

Now that I have tried a few, and for the most part enjoyed them all, I would buy from this company again.

title: worth the try- very good flavor, reminds me of crystal light, no weird tastes
text:
You know how energy drinks can have that "energy drink taste"? Kind of off putting, but the energy kick usually makes it worth it. This doesn't have that weird energy drink taste AND it provides a kick of energy from 80 mg of caffeine.

Taste wise, this dark cherry pomegranate reminds me a lot of the old crystal light raspberry ice circa 2005. So if you like that, then you will like this. This of course has the added benefit of including caffeine, electrolytes, and other energy supplements. It is sweetened with aspartame & maltodextrine.

Add one packet to 16.9 ounces of water, or use more water for milder flavor. Dissolves easily

I like that it isnt super loaded with caffeine, yet it is enough to feel like some cobwebs have been cleared out. Rather nice for a preworkout, during workout drink, or for anytime a little hydration with caffeine is desired. Come summer this might make for a neat cooling off popsicle. or caffeinated ice cubes.

I am stoked that i tried this as the taste is really nice, and I will be sure to toss some packets (or whole box) into my purse for on the go use (I have a physical labor job).

12 boxes of 6 packets each for total of 72 packets. Comes packaged in two trays of 6 boxes each.

title: delicate citrus essence, faintly sweet, adds dimension to vodka tonic. Gift worthy
text:
Very well packaged, nicely displayed. Would make a nice gift paired with a bottle of booze.

The small 6.7 ounce pull tab cans are ideal for use in cocktails, or even consumed alone over ice (I prefer to let the quinine breathe a little rather than drink direct). The addition of orange, tangerine and some sugar makes this the best tonic water I have ever had. Not sweet, just gentles the flavor profile.

Bubbles are crisp, and over all this is a very enjoyable "strong water". Makes for a more interesting vodka or gin tonic.

title: tangy, fragrant, dense bread w/ thick crust & moist spongey interior. Easy to make.
text:
Well, it tastes like sourdough, with onion and cheese. It has a tart aroma, which I find typical of this style of bread..because it is sourdough! Now add in some aromatic heavy hitters, and you have a fragrant tangy bread.

It comes with a packet of yeast inside the bag (thank you), and the directions are easy even though it does take some time. Once mixed, let it rest for 12-15 hours, then there are some directions thne let rest for another 1.5 hours, more directions. Bake. Eat. Overall simple, and I would make this again. I dont like complicated recipes or preparations, and this is very doable.

I just used my convection toaster oven and baked it on a flat sheet. I just left it in a ball. It baked up nicely, has a great crust, and the interior is spongy, moist. Looks like 'artisinal' bread. I am not entirely sure I made it right, but it turned out well enough to slice, add butter to, and have along side a hearty stewp (my version of thick soup). OH, I do remember thinking that I should have lowered the temp as the outside seemed to cook up very quickly. I ended up placing some tinfoil over top to keep it from further crunchification.

I dont know if I made it totally correctly, but it looked good, and tasted good.

Overall, I think you need to like strong flavors. This is sourdough, so it is tangy.. AND then the generous use onion and cheddar, which adds to the flavor profile. Many bread recipes I have used that call for onion, parm, any other cheese, even garlic will often not come through. So this taste profile is present.

title: my new favorite meatless burger! No fuss, good texture, neutral taste, great ingredients
text:
Happy to say, this "Mushroom With Meat-Like Texture" makes a good burger. Definitely a repurchase. I am not vegan or vegetarian, but I enjoy meatless burgers of all sorts. I have made various burgers from scratch, I have had my fair share over the years from the freezer section (boca/morningstar). I have tried some dry mixes. This is probably the best I have had as the texture is just right, and the taste is fairly neutral yet has a meaty vibe. AND the ingredients are so much better. No reliance on texturized soy, not loaded with sodium. Calories are on point, and I feel more filled up with this compared to others.

I love that it is packaged in four packets of basically two decent sized burgers. Two packets are wrapped together, so when you first open the box it looks like two packets.

Just add a little water (about 3 ounces) and some oil. Mix, let sit for a couple of minutes to hydrate. Then form into patties, and cook. I add a little oil to a skillet, then cook on medium low with lid on top. This made for a crispy exterior and tender interior. It is really simple, no fuss. I can see this being my go to when I want a healthier burger, mini meatloaf, or a few meatballs

Tastes good plain, tastes better with some salt. Beyond that the flavor modification possibilities are wide open.

Also love that it can be stored in my pantry, and for that I will most likely buy more soon.

title: neat flavor combo, low cal, low sugar, AND 5 grams of FIBER?! YUM!
text:
Interesting flavor profile, more of an acquired taste and best for those with open minded palates.

"It’s a type of Nimbu Pani - a refreshing beverage often made from a blend of lemon or lime, herbs, spices, cane sugar and water"

I was super curious how cumin would taste in a drink, and I am pleasantly surprised. I'm already a big fan of lime and basil. Neat combo. It almost reminds me of a ginger beer- sweet, savory, bright. Also, it includes ginger and mint. I like the flavor. What also impresses me is that it is relative low cal at just 50 cals for the whole can. AND 5 grams of fiber!! How is that? What a neat way to get in some fiber!

Sweetened with sugar and stevia. I wish it was less sweet. It is a tad too sweet for me, but it may be perfect for you. Definitely way less sugar than what is in a can of regular soda. I think it will taste more refreshing over ice in the summer. Has a light gentle fizz. Lovely color.

I'm so intrigued by this product that I am curious about other flavor option. I love loading up our extra fridge with a variety of canned drinks, and this brand seems to have some really interesting stuff.

title: salty tasty seasoning for use on anything, no oregano,
text:
SALTY! Not necessarily a bad thing depending on what you are using it in/on. I would say that it is Salty first, then a punch of garlic, followed by black pepper and turmeric equally, and more subtle. The aroma reminds me of some chicken broth bouillon I use. If you are new to Adobo, it may seem a little bland in some ways, but not far off at all from other versions. Makes it a tasty seasoning for just about anything.

While Adobo seasoning is typically comprised of salt, black pepper, turmeric, and garlic, there are variations out there that add in other stout spices for flavor or color. The stuff I normally buy has oregano. This does not. In some ways I like this version better as I am not always a fan of oregano. This is just what I listed, and the salt is very forward tasting, with garlic lingering, and everything else sort of settled in the background.

I like the small containers, that it is organic, NO MSG (unlike some Adobo blends). I have some [[ASIN:B09CQF7Z3K McCormick Organic Harissa]] that I like a lot, so I kind of expected to be wowed by this as well. It falls a little short for me, but I still like it.

I review this based on my experience of other adobo blends. BTW, there is no nutritional info anywhere, inc their website. Usually I like to know how much sodium is in something, alas no way to know.

title: fair price for 60 capsules, nice brewed or use as pour over, good taste
text:
A very smooth dark roast. I brew is as strong as can be, and this is borderline a little weak for me (I want my dark roasts to be chewy). But what I like about this is how smooth it is. It has an easy to drink, smooth taste, Creates a nice crema (tight froth) on top when used with espresso setting on nespresso maker. I have even opened up a couple of pods to make a pour over (no crema). The film on top is fibrous, so I use a knife to cut all around then peel back. Coffee is packed in tight, so I poke at the coffee to get it out. Then I tap it into a pour over filter. I prefer it brewed in nespresso but it makes a fine cup of coffee as a pour over too.

Of all the brands I have tried of dark roast capsules, this is probably the first one to be a smooth, bold dark roast. Most lean more medium and have a hint of tang (no dark roast should have tang). This is pretty good, no tang so definitely dark roast. Because of the smoothness, I can see even people who prefer medium roast to enjoy this. Again, those who like extra strong, bold super dark roast may find it a tad lacking, but not by much. Even so, I would buy this again.

title: really well done mix, nice balance of taste, lightly perfectly sweet, use milk for "latte"
text:
Nomad Chocolate did a really good job on this, and now I am intrigued to try their other products. WHY I like it is because it has a natural taste. The ingredients are simple (sugar, cocoa, instant coffee). As a "Mocha Latte", I like that it has a predominantly chocolate taste, and the coffee is settled quietly in the background. As much as I love chocolate, and as much as I love coffee, when the two are combined sometimes it just tastes "Off". Balance is key, and I cant make a good chocolate latte at home to save my life. I leave it to baristas, and now this prefab fabulous powder mix. Chocolate forward makes a good mocha, or mocha latte

They recommend using milk of choice. That is how you get the "latte", otherwise is just a "mocha". Fine either way. I happened to try it with just water to start as I happened to have had just boiled some water in a kettle. Totally delish.

Use a heaping tsp (or 2 level tsp) to 180 ml (6 ounces) liquid. There are directions to mix it with a portion of the heated milk, then top it with remainder of the heated milk. Keep in mind this is trying to prepare it like at a coffee shop. You do you, as it all works. Mix it all at same time with water, mix it all at same time with milk, uses as much powder or liquid as you want, to taste. Or follow directions to a t.

Be creative, make it an orange mocha latte by adding in orange oil, or peppermint mocha latte by adding in peppermint oil, etc.. top with some whipped cream.. mmm

Can even use it in baking, but I will keep it for making some good hot (r iced) cuppas. This is a repurchase for me, so 5 stars easily

title: good as an every day seasoning, salt forward, might want a grinder
text:
I couldnt quite pick up the flavor of black pepper and garlic, yet it didnt taste just like salt either. However, the predominant flavor is salty, just slightly toned down. I enjoyed it a lot to flavor some chicken. I think this would be delicious on beef, or any type of burger. If used as an every day seasoning, I woud consider adding it to a grinder as the salt is a little chunky.

I like BBB products, and this is another good one. I'd consider this one again

title: has become my go-to "skinny syrup" for flavoring everything
text:
I regularly use Hypothermias products. I have used several of their concentrates and ready to use products. While made for use in shaved ice, the syrups are versatile. I really like their sugar free options. Unlike a popular skinny syrup which uses sucralose, Hypothermias uses monk fruit and erythritol to sweetnen their sugar free syrups. I think it tastes better, is better on blood sugar, and the flavors are more robust. Pricing is similar. I feel like I found a cool little secret by using Hypthermias products in my coffee, smoothies, over ice cream, mixed with matcha green tea preparations. Add a few drops as an essence to water, or as the flavoring agent to "Italian sodas" or homemade soda waters. Awesome for skinny cocktails too

I love love love this pina colada. But I am partial to pineapple and coconut

title: pungent, robust garlic- exactly what garlic powder should taste like. Very good, cant go wrong!
text:
Tasty, robust garlic. Not exactly powder, more like super fine granules. Really tasty, pungent.. mmmm garlicky.

I am learning that it pays to pay for good garlic. I still like the cheap powder, but it tastes different than something that actually tastes like garlic. I love garlic, and this like having fresh chopped garlic without the hassle.

title: lovely instant espresso, creates a nice crema, tastes good to me, I would buy again
text:
I like instant coffee, and I really like instant espresso. It tastes as expected- no better no worse than other instant espresso. I like it more than many instant coffees. I would buy this again, so 5 stars.

I always have instant on hand for a quick, convenient cup of coffee (at home, on the go) and for adding to my smoothies and some desserts (ie chocolate cake, brownies, frostings). I use more than what the directions call for (1 rounded tsp to 6 ounces of water). I find that true of most instant espresso though. Typically I use 1 TBS to 8 ounces, then adjust accordingly as it is easy enough to add more water or add more instant coffee.

This instant espresso produces a lovely crema. The overall taste is mild and naturally sweet. It has a little of that instant taste to it, but it doesnt bother me. I like that it dissolved perfectly. I drink it black, or sometimes I add creamer and sweetener. Just depends what I am in the mood for. Will also dissolve in a cup of cold water when shaken well. Nice way to make a quick iced coffee.

title: easy batter, make adjustments for thicker/thinner pancakes, gently mix, dont over do it
text:
I use a little more liquid than what is called for. I find that there is always some variation among these pancake/waffle mixes- so I just know that I will use more or less liquid depending on how the batter mixes up. If it looks too thick, then simply add a few extra drops of water. DO NOT overmix. Overmixing will nearly always create a tougher/rubbery texture. It is easy to want to keep on stirring, but it really just needs to be incorporated gently.

I made pancakes. Ladled some batter into hot buttered skillet. Let it cook until light bubbles, and edges lift from pan. Then flip to finish off cooking. Taste and texture is good. Easy to have some additional mix-ins, such as vanilla, more sugar, fruit, nuts, choco chips whatever.

title: thick, creamy, semi neutral tasting vanilla, generous amount per packet
text:
Individual 100 gram packs provides 500 calories, and some robust meal replacement nutrition. Use less if caloric needs are less. One packet makes up quite a bit, so it would be easy to use 1/3 to 1/2 the packet. I use half a packet. When mixed with some non dairy milk, I find that it is very thick. Like a melted milkshake. And that is using half the packet and doubling the liquid.

I'd like to see more fiber. This is listed as having a mere 12mg. Usually fiber is listed in grams. Maybe this is mistake, because 12 mg is close to 0 in terms of relative amount. Their website shows 6 grams, which is better, but still could use more for a meal replacement. I'm still hungry after drinking this, and using the whole packet is too much for a single meal. So what I do is add some flax or chia, or I drink a glass of fiber supplement such as [[ASIN:B088SLR9QV Organic India Psyllium Husk Pre & Probiotic Fiber]]

The vanilla has a fair taste; slightly nutty. The sweetness level is pleasing. I dont love the overall flavor, but it is doable. While meant to be used as is, I think it would pair well with some other add ins- chia, fruit, peanut butter, etc. I may try adding some simple pumpkin pie spice, or cinnamon next time. That would be delish. OR unsweetened chocolate to boost magnesium levels (and taste).

Blend with ice to bring it to milkshake level consistency.

Sodium is high for a full packet (600 mg), but it has 700 mg of potassium to help balance it out. Has quite a bit of calcium (640 mg) and that is before adding any dairy/non dairy liquid.

Their website is loaded with info about the company, and all the products which influenced my desire to try this.

I like the individual packets for convenience, freshness, and for on the go use if need be. Best price comes from buying larger quantity, but it nice to see a 3 pack to be able to try it.

title: super tasty blend- hot, cool, salty. Use it on everything and in everything. Yum
text: Been awhile since I have had harissa seasoning. This is good- spicy, salty, great depth of flavor. Lends a spicy kick. This is a pack of six small 1 ounce (0.99) flip top shaker containers. It is one of those spices that just takes lots of different dishes up a level. Just add it to everything, even condiments. The spice level isnt uncomfortably fiery, it is more like a heated tingle. I find the whole blend to be super tasty. I like the smaller containers- enough to share or to stow away.

title: very smooth,  not super strong but makes good cup of coffee,
text: A very smooth dark roast. I brew is as strong as can be, and this is borderline a little weak for me (I want my dark roasts to be chewy). But what I like about this is how smooth it is. Creates a nice crema (tight froth) on top when used with espresso setting on nespresso maker. I have even opened up a couple of pods to make a pour over (no crema). Of all the brands I have tried of dark roast capsules, this is probably the first one to be a smooth, bold dark roast. Most lean more medium and have a hint of tang (no dark roast should have tang). This is pretty good. Because of the smoothness, I can see even people who prefer medium roast to enjoy this. Again, those who like extra strong, bold super dark roast may find it a tad lacking. Even so, I would buy this again.

title: hint of sweet, gentle matcha, light crispy wafer cubes. Lovely tea/coffee treats
text:
Taste is as anticipated- whisper sweet, hint of matcha, crispy. No cloying sweetness, has a mild lingering green tea taste. Basically a green tea milk cream layered with crispy wafers. These are cubes, and the delicate nature of the wafer lends to some excess crumble in the bag (not annhiliated cubes, but more from bits coming off the sides of each cube). The soft sided bag doesn't help, nor does scant shipping protections. It is a Korean product with nearly no English. You may have luck with a translator app. My experience with Osulloc products is that they are of quality.

100 gram bag contains 30 something wafer bites. 520 calories for the bag. Easy to eat the entire bag. Bag doesn't reseal, but does it need to? Just fold and use a clip. Or gobble them all up.

I dont rate on price.

title: initial odd taste, but it made me feel good, powered me up, low key steady energy
text:
Provides me low key energy without jitters. Powered through a major snow shoveling session without feeling drained. Electolytes kept me replenished as all that intense work had me sweating. Taste is ok, better after the first couple of sips. I felt good all around.

First sip made me shudder. Has some taste that I cant pinpoint that I find a little blegh. Yet, I value energy drinks for powering workouts and my motivation in general. So I kept sipping. Oddly, I found it tasted better with each sip. I couldnt tell you that it was blue raspberry if it wasn't labeled as such. Sweetness level is good, and most importantly the low key energy is noticeable. I drank the majority of a can before heading out to shovel the 2 feet of snow that fell the day before. There was a large area of my driveway that I needed to clear out, and I did so with ease. Gentle boost in energy, No waning energy, no jitters, no sleep issues.

Ingredients can be seen in one of the product pictures.

title: tasty, assorted blends for use on anything, Front label describes each. Gift worthy
text: I'm really not picky when it comes to seasoning. This is a nice little assortment, and I like the various spices that go into each blend. I like the look of the labels, the packaging (gift worthy), and that the front has a description of each blend. I see no reason not to use then on whatever you want. I particularly like any of these for use on seasoning potatoes or chicken-- stuff we have often and need ways to make it taste different. The seafood one is totally good on anything too. But I did use it when I made some salmon patties. Yum.

title: flavorful assortment for creating own unique blend, gift worthy, will need to grind
text:
Cool little kit. I see this more as a gift for others than something I would normally get for myself. Nicely packed, attractive box, has 5 spices of varying taste profiles, and a shaker bottle for use if/when creating your own blend. Just grab your grinder (or mortar and pestle) and get to it. Or use the individual blends.

--SPICY: coriander seeds, yellow mustard seeds, roasted cumin seeds, paprika flakes and all spice.
--SWEET & SMOKEY: smoked sea salt, brown sugar.
--HOT: chili flakes, paprika flakes.
--ZESTY: sea salt, lemon zest, anti-caking agent, lemon juice powder, citric acid.
--HERBY: rosemary, oregano, sage, thyme, bay leaves

title: kind of bland, but easy to drink. Best very cold
text:
Assorted flavors are good, although a bit bland. The flavors dont stand out, all have a tea taste with a hint of something. I couldnt describe any one of them. They remind me if anything of a bland gingerale. Not bad by any means, just not tasting like orange, or blackberry, or cucumber melon. That being said, I find them easy to drink. Best cold, does a fair job quenching my thirst as it is not too sweet, and I get a mild thrum of energy.

$2.50 per can is reasonable. I would consider these again- I never feel ill from drinking these.

title: Big G dropped the ball. Less than 2 ounces in this container, & very weak oregano
text:
Big G products are usually incredible. But this one is a bit of a miss. The weight is definitely off. I weighed the container, and just comes in at 2.25 ounces. So we can infer that it has less than 2 ounces of actual product. This is supposed to have 5.5 ounces, AND the label even says that. So it isnt a matter of being sent wrong one.. something on their end is messed up. Big production mistake somewhere along the line.

As for taste.., those expecting that extra green flavor may be disappointed. I happen to not love Oregano, but people in my house do. I actually like this because it is milder and more low key than the usual stuff I am used to. But even so, it isnt what anyone is going to expect despite my liking the more mild taste. Also? the leaves or whatever are more brownish yellow than green.

SO WEIRD.

Ok, edit to add... I just made a pizza & generously doused it with this. Never would I do that with other oregano. I barely tasted it.

I love Big G products, but sad to say this is not something I can recommend at this time

title: same nutrition all in convenient freeze dried powder. Great in my vanilla/banana smoothies
text: Just freeze dried pineapple powder. Taste just like pineapple. Very sweet and delicious. I love all things pineapple and my current use for this is as a smoothie flavoring agent. I have some protein or meal replacement powders that are blah, so I pick something to make it taste more appealing. I love adding this alone or with a frozen banana to a vanilla based powder. Mmmm yum!

title: blue is tasty, much better than their yellow. Makes generous amount, good coloring
text:
This Blue is better than their yellow. It is nice for those that want a food based coloring for their frosting, versus artificial, and want organic powdered sugar. Other than that, there is nothing exactly special about it--very similar to other prefab powder formulations (similarly priced too). You have to add your own liquid, butter, and depending on preference even flavoring. Buttercream is just butter (or butter alternative) and sugar, but nearly always has vanilla added in. Other prefabs have vanilla added in. This doesnt mention an vanilla, but I can taste it in this blue frosting (could not detect it in the yellow).

This makes a denim blue. They have other colors, and I have their golden yellow as well. The entire bag makes a generous amount. The directions are for making the whole bag as one big 1.5 cup batch. I would love to see a conversion for making a smaller quantity. However, after seeing how it is really just powdered sugar, I went ahead and made a smaller amount as I normally would if I was just grabbing my usual powdered sugar from the cupboard. That worked. I had already made a big batch of yellow for a spice cake, but didnt need the whole amount. Then when I made this blue, I made the whole amount, which I used on blueberry scones. It has a much better flavor than the yellow, and I didnt need to add anything to it. I can taste vanilla, and I dont detect anything else.
