The appeal to me is the food based coloring. Some colors from typical artificial food coloring make me feel off, so usually I just avoid foods of that nature--especially blue and some reds. But having a simple to make product that creates a vibrant food derived color, adds to my personal options. Again, this is really just sugar and coloring, but it works.

Pipes well, or just use a spatula.

title: no vanilla- be sure to add vanilla otherwise has slightly vague off taste,
text:
It's OK. It is nice for those that want a food based coloring for their frosting, versus artificial, and want organic powdered sugar. Other than that, there is nothing exactly special about it--very similar to other prefab powder formulations (similarly priced too). You have to add your own liquid, butter, and even flavoring. Buttercream is just butter (or butter alternative) and sugar, but nearly always has vanilla added in. Other prefabs have vanilla added in. This is plain, and you will likely want to add a little vanilla extract (or other) because there is a hint of some flavor that comes through. Not bad, but not pure.

This makes a golden yellow. They have other colors, and I have their blue as well. The entire bag makes a generous amount. The directions are for making the whole bag as one big 1.5 cup batch. I would love to see a conversion for making a smaller quantity. However, after seeing how it is really just powdered sugar, I went ahead and made a smaller amount as I normally would if I was just grabbing my usual powdered sugar from the cupboard.

The appeal to me is the food based coloring. Some colors from typical artificial food coloring make me feel off, so usually I just avoid foods of that nature. But having a simple to make product that creates a vibrant food derived color, adds to my personal options. Again, this is really just sugar and coloring, but it works.

Pipes well, or just use a spatula.

Overall.. I think it middle of road "OK", hence 3 stars. I like what they use for coloring, but dont like that there is no vanilla, and doesnt say so in description. The description doesnt say what exactly is in it. Why not? While ok without added vanilla, it has a vague off taste without it.

My review for the blue is same.

title: Milk chocolate is awesome, Dark chocolate is like liquid pudding, overall very good treat
text:
I regret nothing. Maybe because I have greatly cut back on sugar, but this is some seriously decadent tasting hot cocoa. It is quite tasty, and I would purchase this again. However, I will say that I like the Milk Chocolate more than the Dark Chocolate. The milk chocolate is as expected- sweet, chocolatey, does real nice with water or milk. Just so tasty, and enjoyable. Love it with whipped cream. The dark chocolate is oddly extra thick. Kind of reminds me of liquidy pudding. Still tastes good, but not as chocolaty as the milk chocolate. I will work through them all, but if/when I repurchase, I will go for the milk chocolate.

There is no nutritional information on the packet or the box. Not even directly on their website. There is a QR code that you can scan using your smartphone (and app) if you want to know specifics. I am not liking having to do that, at all. So for that, wouldnt give this as a gift, even though the boxing and packet make it look gift worthy.

Even so, I have been enjoying these a lot.

5, 10, 15 stars for the milk chocolate
3.5 stars for the dark chocolate

4 stars overall. Please list nutritional info somewhere other than just through a scan. BTW, nothing out of the ordinary in the ingredients. Very typical. Best maybe not to know if counting cals or sugar. But, I regret nothing ;)

title: fantastic crunchy snack, perfect level spice, loads of flavor, REALL GOOD
text:
Oh wow, these spicy sprouted almonds are SO GOOD. Perfect level of heat, loads of smoky paprika flavor, and the crunch level is awesome. These instantly became my favorite snack, and am already looking to purchase more. I didnt know I needed these Daily Crunch Sprouted Almonds in my life until my first bite. Now I am hooked. I also greatly appreciate that these aren't sweet. There is some monk fruit sweetener, but it lends to the Nashville Hot flavor profile, which is just delicious. Has heat that lingers but not hot or irritating.

Totally love.

title: gorgeous bag of garbanzo beans, slow cooked nicely, pantry must have
text:
Quality and taste is very good. No problems, issues, concerns. 5 stars. Not necessarily because it is better than other dried chickpeas, but because it is a good as anticipated. They look really good. Clean too.

I added a portion of the two pound bag into a slow cooker bean and split pea soup. Good stuff! I always keep dried beans tucked away into my pantry. Sometimes I can get this stuff cheaper in store, but more often I only find non organic, ok looking dried products. Online bean/legume tend to be pricier, hence why I font factor that into rating.

This robust pack of organic garbanzo beans are gorgeous. I like using the dried stuff for hot food preparations.

title: good taste, texture. Review is for Pumpkin Spice mix, & Panckake/waffle mix
text:
I have tried the PANCAKES & WAFFLES mix, as well as the PUMPKIN SPICE BAKING MIX. Both are very good. In short, I give the Pancakes 4 stars, and the Pumpkin cake 5 stars. I like them both enough to give an over 5 star rating. I can't review separately since they are both on this page. Hence why both are mentioned here.

PUMPKIN SPICE BAKING MIX: was very easy to make. Just add some egg and oil. I baked it in my large toaster oven using my 8"x10"2" oblong [[ASIN:B07YFFLM13 Wilton Non-Stick Diamond-Infused]] pan. Be mindful of baking time depending on oven size and pan size. My fully preheated small oven reduced baking time by nearly half. The cake turned out great. Moist, tasty. Just delicious to eat alone, but it would be extra fantastic with an icing or frosting. I had some whipped cream, which paired nicely. I love the taste and texture, and would buy this again. 5 stars

---------------------------
PANCAKE & WAFFLE MIX: 4 stars, very good though.

Pancakes turned out well. Had a fluffy texture, with a slightly chewy stretch that is often had in gluten free mixes. I like the overall taste and texture.

I followed directions for making 6 pancakes, which requires using 1 cup of mix. Yet 1/4 cup should yield about 2 pancakes. Math tells me then 1 cup should make closer to 8 pancakes. A one cup preparation actually yielded just four, 4" pancakes. SO basically one pancake per 1/4 cup preparation. These weren't big, wide, nor super thick. Since the batter didnt really pour, I figure it really needs more liquid. Then I would have gotten 6 pancakes, yet they would have been thinner. So trade off, I guess.

Nutrition panel says "includes 0 additional sugars". yet the ingredient list has cane sugar. That is an added sugar.

As for calories and other nutritional info, it is for the mix only. Numbers will vary depending on what else you use. For this mix, you will need an egg (or 2), some milk of choice, and oil of choice. I used almond milk, and coconut oil. Later, I had a few toppings on my plate to dunk my pancakes in (peanut butter, vegan butter, and medjool date syrup).

All tasty with good texture. Though, not all that filling to me. I think next time I make them, I will add in some protein powder and maybe some fiber, or use a topping or side to help fill up my belly. As is, too many calories for something that didnt put a dent in my hunger. On the plus side, I didnt feel weighed down either like i would with typical pancakes.

title: light mellow taste, dissolves well in hot water, nice addition to smoothies too
text:
It is matcha green tea powder (and also lists green tea extract). So I am not sure if there is an added green tea boost or no. It has a typical culinary matcha taste profile, though I think it is on the mild and mellow side, which makes it more palatable to me. It dissolves really well in hot water, and over all I find it easy to drink. Because it is so mild, I doubt I would want to use it in baking. But as a hot tea, or added into a smoothie- this is pretty good. Again, for me-- I like the extra mild taste. I drink matcha daily, have had all sorts of brands from different regions, and find them all similar. I like when the taste is mellow as I dont really care for the taste of matcha. But I love the benefits.

Comes well packaged- a bag within a bag, and has a wooden tea spoon too. 3.5 to 4 stars

title: You had me at CUP for CUP swap!  All around pleased with this quality brand
text:
I dont need gluten free, but I like using non white wheat flours for something different. I have a cupboard full of flours. Way easier for me to make something (especially gluten free) when the white flour alternative is something I can just swap out. I am sure there are some adjustments for some stuff, but the basic stuff- cookies, muffins, quick pizza crust, even bread and pancakes have all worked out well for me with this blend. I made small batches of stuff. Haven't tried cake yet- love me a simple cake.

So much better than all the separate components, which I have. Now that I am able to try out some pre done blends, this is so much better for me. Takes up less space, and definitely (for me) less waste (either from not using, or messing up the recipe/results). I am enthusiastic for this blend, and I see they have other blends too.

This brand, BakeGood quickly rose in ranks for quality, simplicity, and care. I am glad to see plenty of information on the product page and the labeling on the package. I appreciate the chocolate chip cookie recipe on the flour bag, and the biscuit drop recipe on the baking powder bag.

I see the baking powder as a bonus. I only use aluminum free, so this fits that need perfectly. I just went through my baking cupboard and tossed my old container of baking powder as it was nearly empty and likely was old enough to warrant the toss. Got this in its place, and it is working out fine as my replacement brand.

title: very good flavor, doesnt taste like a supplement, great cold or hot, plain or added to tea. YUM
text:
Really excellent tasting to me. I make use of elderberry supplements to provide additional support to my immune system. I dont use them every day, but I do make use of them 2-3x a week, or when I am feeling run down I will use them daily until feeling better. The directions on this happen to say the same thing. It is not meant to be a daily supplement forever more. Dont use more than one packet per day.

Very easy to mix into a glass of water (hot or cold) or into whatever else. When stirred into a glass of cold water I noticed a little left behind as I finished my glass. So I just added a splash of water, swirled, and drank it. I really like it warm, too. It just works so nicely on its own, but try it mixed in with tea- extra delicious!

It has really good flavor. It is incredibly pleasant tasting. Naturally sweet, doesnt taste like a supplement to me. I dont rate on price, but i do comment. Current "sale" price of $15.99/$1.33 each is fair. Closer to $1 would be better.

title: carame & pretzel has decent taste, good mouth feel- see/taste all components
text:
I have the Caramel Pretzel option. It is pretty good. My bar is set low as I have had some keto snacks that are really bad, and even some of the SlimFast snack bars aren't good (marshmallow cup is not good). This is one I would consider again. At least I can see the pretzel, and see and taste the caramel. Not too shabby.

I am not keto or diabetic, or looking to starve myself into weightloss, but I do want to have the occasional treat without wanting to eat the whole box. These snacks are the same size (maybe little heavier) than a reeces. Calories are on the low side (80 or less), and I am not going to be triggered to eat more because it isnt all that sweet.

title: tasty blend add loads of flavor, high versatile, gives a salty kick w/o sodium
text: Really good flavor  to me. It is one of those spice blends that can be used in and on nearly anything. Adds a good pop of flavor without any added sodium or heat. I have used it on potatoes, eggs, vegetables, on meat, and even sprinkled into a sipping broth for added flavor. Has a slight tangy kick that gives it a salty vibe. I have some of this portioned out into a smaller shaker jar as I like it enough to want to have easy access to it for use on everything.

title: covered 8 basic hot dogs, rolls no problem, bigger beef chunks, nice oniony/mustard taste
text:
I've only used one can so far of the eight. Some were dented, but not terribly so. All the cans were packed in a bag tucked into a box, so hopefully whomever packs this stuff will reconsider and use a box or bubble wrap instead. OK, back to the product:

I like chili dogs, and prefer no bean, so I often keep a few cans tucked away in my pantry for use when the time comes. Most brands are mediocre. I figured Hormel would have a better offering, and for the most part I think it does. If only because it didn't make me feel gross after eating a few hot dogs. Some chili dog sauce can be too rich or something. Like it seems like a good idea until I get to the last bite. Anway, I DO taste the mustard and onion in this. It isn't super pronounced, but compared to any other chili dog sauce, I can definitely taste it. If you want more pronounced flavor or texture, then add more onion and mustard, or skip this to use your usual sauce and add your toppings. Coney Island inspired, not a dupe. Take it for what it is.

I made up a package of 8 hot dogs. Basic dogs, basic rolls. I didn't think this would be enough, but it was, and I am generous. I even had a spoonful left over. I warmed it up on the stove. It goes from being semi solid to more of a soupy sauce. The chunks of beef are sizeable, which I appreciate- a lot of no bean chili dog sauces have almost no texture as the "meat" is chopped so tiny. These are chunks. But it doesn't look like much compared to the soupy sauce it sits in. Yet, in the end it was enough. Though I still think it could use a little more beef. Sauce is pretty good, not super strong in an one flavor, didnt make me feel ill, not too salty tasting, and I like it better than a few others I tend to buy. I think it has a good taste and texture as a base for further toppings (more mustard, more onion, some shredded cheese). It was only once I loaded up the hot dogs and rolls that I determined that this is just fine. The sauce pretty much stayed in place, and my husband and I ate it all up.

I really didn't mind it. It comes down to personal preference, right? I DO like it more than my usual random brands I find at the store, and I did taste the mustard & onion. If I have any issues with the other cans, I will be back to update. 4 stars because I liked it.

title: 3.75 stars. Dark leaning medium, sachets loaded with Arabica coffee, use 6-9oz water
text:
It doesn't say it here, but this is Arabica coffee, all sorts of additional info can be gleaned from their webpage.

Coffee taste is subjective, so take my thoughts on this as you wish. I have had the tea bag style coffee before- various brands, various roast levels, and found them all deplorable--and I am not even that picky when it comes to coffee, or brewing styles. I have preferences but I drink it all in any way I can get it. I didnt care for previous bag styes because no matter what I did, I could not get it to make a regular tasting cup of coffee. I'd have to use 2, 3, 4 bags. So, I gave up. I chose these tea bag style coffee pouches a try because I saw that it is styled for hotel use. I figured, this has gotta make an actual cup of coffee.

It does. I use 6-8 ounces of water for one large, fresh smelling sachet. I think I had done upwards of 10 ounces, but found I needed to steep longer. There aren't directions specific to amount of water to use. I do allow it to steep for several minutes as I like a strong cup of coffee. Rather it be too strong than too weak.

Taste: all the coffee in this listing says that it is a dark roast. There is no mention on the packets. Just gives the taste profile, which is nearly meaningless to me. I would say it is a dark leaning medium. Has a pretty smooth taste without any burts of tang or bitterness. The option I have is Guatemala. I actually enjoyed my coffee, though a more true dark roast would be welcome. I like my coffee extra dark, extra bold, and I drink it black. The only time I add creamer (save for something different to have) is when the coffee is too tangy, acidic, or bright (basically all light, most mediums). I was able to drink this black, but the ever so slight tang makes it a medium roast. I didnt have to use creamer, but I was tempted.

I do not rate on price. we can see the price before buying. We each have our own budgets, values, etc toward what we buy. If $12.95 for a pack of 5 looks good to you, then go for it. But I do comment. Personally, I do think it is a tad much. The current $3 off coupon brings it down to $2 per cup of coffee. Still a little much, and therefor likely not a repurchase... but I am not rating based on what I care to afford. For what it is worth, it is cheaper here than at their website.

There is a lot of coffee per sachet, so they aren't skimping. It is well packaged, smells fresh, tastes fresh. Actual resulting taste will vary on brew method, water temp, water amount, and personal opinion. Just need a mug and hot water. Fine for hotels, B&B's, guests, office, emergency supply etc. Could be used as a cold brew option (toss in a large travel tumbler, fill with cold water, enjoy the next day). Maybe as part of a coffee lovers gift.

I could go darker, stronger. Overall taste is good, makes for passable cup of coffee. Glad it gave me pep in my step as that is ultimately what I rate it on. Flavor and if I can feel it. 3.75 stars (but have to go with 4)

title: no odor, easy to prepare, no problems, I trust Skinny Pasta products
text:
I am a long time consumer of shirataki noodles of all shapes and sizes. There are a lot of brands available, and most are nearly the same. SO if you have never had shirataki (konjac root) noodles, then please know that they are not the same as traditional pasta. They all have a rubbery texture. If you are really desperate to reduce cals and carbs, these are worth the try. I find them enjoyable, especially in soups, simple veg/protein dishes, and Asian cuisine preparations. I have never cared for it prepared in Italian cuisine. It doesnt work for me. It is ok is used to cut into the traditional pasta (maybe like 50-50 of each). Taste is neutral, and while this brand has zero odor, many other brands do. If you find that any of them have an odor, just be sure to rinse well. Problem fixed.

So I bought this specific brand after trying their ultra magical [[ASIN:B08LW3T6XF Skinny Pasta cups of Soup]] . It somehow doesnt taste or feel like a shirataki product that is truly reduced in sodium (80 mg). It makes a lot, and hits the spot- fills my belly with very little calories, and feels glorious to consume on a cold winter day. I digress.. but I cant help but goosh my love for it. Pricy, but so good. So because it is so pricy, I figured maybe I could make my own cup of soup using their noodles. I wanted theirs because another brand I decided to try was absolutely terrible (I say they are nearly all the same, but occasionally a terribad one slips through. I do not recommend any version of ASIN:B07ZVDP46K shirataki noodles]] )).

Well, these dont quite fit what I am looking for, BUT they are very good as far as shirataki noodles go. I eat a bowl of them as I write this review. I emptied the packet into a strainer, gave them a good rinse, then placed them in a bowl of with boiled water. Then I drained, added low sodium broth powder, other seasonings, dehydrated vegetables. Let it sit, then have been eating it like a bowl of soup. All for like 25 calories! I may try their spaghetti shape to see if I can get this closer to their Skinny Pasta soup. But really, I will likely have to just buy more of their soup. Which is amazing. If they can make some shirtaki noodles that mimic what they use in their soup.. oh my.

In the mean time, this is pretty good.

title: melts just like regular marshmallows, more dense so more bang for buck, light taste
text:
Has a light, neutral flavor, not too sweet, and the texture is spot on. They are smallish flattish rectangles that very much remind me of when I make my own marshmallows, so I was not at all surprised or scared of the shape. Come on people, not all marshmallows are rounded. The size of one is about the equivalent of 6-8 small marshmallows. I had ripped one into several smaller pieces for use in my hot cocoa. I will say that these are more dense than regular marshmallows, and therefore provide more value than you think. Store bought tend to be more poofy and airy. These are denser (again reminds me of homemade).

Since they aren't as sweet, they dont pack as much flavor punch, but they are incredible for their ability to melt the exact same way as regular marshmallows.

I am super excited that these melt & blow up like any other marshmallow. I haven't tried them over a fire. I can make some healthier rice crispy (or whatever) marshmallow snacks now. I occasionally buy some healthier rice crispy treats, but they dont have that goey factor. ya know.. that mouth feel. Anyway, I would consider these again. I rarely feel like making my own marshmallows, so having something I can just buy is great.

I can't comment on the sweetener that is used or how it impacts the body, so do your own research if you have concerns. This listing includes nutritional information, just have to scout for it. Here it is for your convenience:

Nutritional Facts: Serving size 1 piece (7.5g),
Calories 15.3,
Fat 0g,
Sodium 0.05mg,
Carbohydrates 5.82g,
Sugars 0g, Sugar Alcohols 5.76g,
Protein 0.375g.

Ingredients: Water, sweeteners (maltitol, isomalt, maltitol syrup, lactitol) gelatine, natural colors and natural flavoring (vanilla).

title: Add to hot cocoa for extra antioxidants and boost of energy.
text:
Looks, smells, performs like nearly all culinary matcha I have ever used. Perfectly fine matcha to me. Has that green "vegetal" aroma, slightly earthy taste. It tastes as expected--like matcha. As much as I drink it, I have never liked the taste of matcha, but the benefits are undeniable. I love the antioxidants, the gentle, long lasting energy (I'm a die hard coffee drinker, but I give it to matcha--it provides better boost of energy), the reduced desire for sweets, etc. So I have been drinking it on and off for a couple of decades now. This past year I have made it part of my daily routine.

I rarely make it as a plain tea. I nearly always add it to a smoothie, or I make a tea of the sorts and add a bunch of other stuff to help mask the flavor of matcha. It doesn't help that I use 4x as much, or more (1-2 TBS versus 1-2 tsp). I have recently begun adding a little to a cup of hot cocoa, and that works really well. Ceremonial is often much more smooth and mellow tasting, but the cost difference usually inhibits me, so I just go with culinary such as this. For my needs, it works out very well. Also, culinary is definitely a better option for baked goods, ice cream, and adding to smoothies. Product of Japan.

title: Light tasty scone goes good with coffee
text: Pretty good mix. I need to cut back on sugar but still want snacks. These scones are pleasant and pretty easy to make. I like it with coffee.

title: water, soybeans, salt. Good addition to bring added saltiness, umami to broths
text: Good basic soybean paste. Water, soybeans, salt. Tastes as expected: mashed soybeans. The consistency reminds me of hot dog sauce. I dont know why it made me think of that, but it did/does. I have used soybean paste for adding a little salty umami flavor to broths, and I use this for that. Plenty of recipes that include this ingredient. It is a basic staple that adds a good depth of flavor.

title: reduced sugar compared to most milk teas, very creamy, lightly sweet, subtle flavor
text:
I like a few Enzo products, especially their plain matcha powder. Since I adore boba tea, I figured I would give their milk teas a try. I usually avoid the prefab milk teas because they are loaded with sugar. The Enzo varieties are greatly reduced in sugar by comparison.

The taste is creamy, lightly sweet, but it is a little light on the tea taste. But I often find that true of milk teas. I have tried it both warm and iced, and prepared as Boba/Bubble tea. I like it best as more of a creamer than a base. It has the typical orange color found in Thai tea. Can also be using in baking, and adding extra creaminess to smoothies.

1 Tablespoon per 2 ounces of liquid.

title: mellow mushroom powder that is nutritional addition to soups, stews, sipping broths
text: This is what I use to add to soups, sipping broths, and occasionally to my oats or smoothies. It is just dried mushroom formed into powder. I use powder extracts when I want more of a supplement, and I use mushroom powder like this when I simply want the nutritional benefit and mellow pleasing flavor. Works really well in hot food preparations.

title: mild lychee flavor, no mouth feel, fun to try but I prefer more flavor & texture
text:
Trippy! It was fun to try "bursting pearls" for my boba tea, but I think I will stick with the typical tapioca pearls. These have no texture or mouth feel. They simply just burst with even the most mild of pressure. They stand up to being in the glass of tea and ice, and hold up being sucked up through straw, but they instant burst in mouth. I never really even feel them. I miss that as I drank my "bubble tea". OOOh, maybe I will try it mixed with regular tapioca pearls.

I absolutely adore lychee. My go-to bubble/boba tea is non cream green tea sweetened with lychee syrup. This intrigued me because of that. The smell is distinctly lychee, but the taste is faint. I added a generous amount of the syrup that the pearls sit in to see if I can boost the taste. Nada. The flavor in the bursting pearls is also rather faint. I prefer [[ASIN:B0147N45ME Tea Zone Lychee syrup]] for my lychee green tea boba tea needs.

While it was a fun thing to try, it wont be a repurchase. If it had a stronger flavor, and/or if it had just a little more mouth feel, I would have enjoyed these a lot more. Overall, I think they are "OK"

Bottle says to refrigerate after opening.edit: my mistake, my brain saw words that made me assume to refrigerate after opening. There are no directions pertaining to that, but I refrigerated them & they seem fine. Use em up quickly.

title: significantly reduced sugar over other creamy milk teas, versatile
text:
I have had good experiences with Enzo products, so I was curious about this milk tea. I find that it is a very nice milk tea powder for boba tea. It is significantly reduced in sugar compared to other offerings. Use 1 heaping TBS per 2 ounces of water. It provides a super mellow, smooth matcha taste with creaminess and a little bit of sweetness. Hint of other green (veg? tea?). It's good. I might use it more as a flavor addition to my regular matcha- this will help tone it down

Has a fun bright green appearance- will stand out if used in baking.

It tastes good warm, but i prefer it iced with tapioca pearls (boba tea/bubble tea!). I have added extra cream and some lychee syrup to a couple of batches. I think I like it best made simply over loads of ice.

title: nice variety, pleasant looking packaging, definitely gift worthy
text:
Nice assortment of coffee. It has a good presentation which makes it gift worthy. As for taste, that is really up to the consumer. I bought this as a gift for a two person household, and they seem to like it. I would be told if it were cruddy. I think they, and most people would like trying something different.

Keep in mind that this is an assortment, with varying flavor notes, and the amount is for each bag to make a pot of coffee. Whether it does that is up to the maker of the coffee. Some people use very little coffee, some people use a lot. So make adjustments and you should be fine.

title: hard compressed disks might be challenge for some teeth, good flavor/texture otherwise
text: Good natural flavor- no weird off putting flavors. Just a compressed coconut "cookie" with vanilla flavor. Not too sweet. The small, hard disks may initially be hard to bite into, then once broke, through the pieces have a pleasant crunchy texture. Just might be a little hard for some people to get through that initial bite.

title: Deposited a toilet bowl full of noodles. Wet rubber bands.
text:
So yeh.. had noodles literally coming out my a$$. I have their angel hair and this regular spaghetti. The thinner angel hair is better in terms of taste and texture, but this spaghetti is extra rubbery with no noticeable ability to pick up other flavors. It just kind of sits in the dish. I had high hopes for this spaghetti noodle as it looks like my preferred [[ASIN:B08LW3T6XF Skinny Pasta noodle]] (but less expensive). I wanted to replicate their cup of soup by using cheaper noodles and my own broth. Well, never mind!!.. these are extra rubbery, hard to chew, and pick up little to no flavor in what it is being used in.

I have been eating shirataki noodles for well more than a decade, and have tried all sorts of brands and styles. This is pretty bad. Then the worst part was the next day using the toilet, and seeing a toilet bowl full of noodles. FFS! I had made a point to chew them well, and it was still hard to get them to be smaller pieces. Glad I did what I could because it would have been extra awful to have giant strands to contend with.

I didn't have any issue with their [[ASIN:B07SH5QF9X Angel Hair shirataki noodles]], so maybe give those a try. Still slightly rubbery but seems to pick up flavor better.

title: super fine powder, sweet for some applications, but not sweet enough for baking. YMMV
text:
Silky smooth "sugar", smaller, much finer granules than regular sugar or other 1:1 replacement sugar alternatives. So for that, I am not as fond of it for use in baking. Seems fine for coffee, tea, oat meal, and some baked goods that dont need much sugar (muffin). Good neutral flavor- not noticing any off flavors. But, as sweet as it is directly from bag, it doesnt translate the same level of sweetness to baked goods such as cookies, cakes (and may not be sweet enough for you in other applications). For that, I prefer [[ASIN: B07J1H2X2C monk fruit and erythritol blend]].

It is really a matter of preference, so this is strictly my take on it. 3.5 stars

title: lightly sweet, easy to drink, quick dissolve matcha
text:
Easy to drink matcha that dissolves well without too much fuss. Mellow, not bitter. Not too sweet, in fact I expected it to be sweeter than what it is. I really like that it doesnt contain a lot of sugar. Keeps it healthy.

I drink matcha daily. Hot, iced, mixed into smoothies. It is really good for me, and makes me feel good. I am not a fan of the flavor of matcha in general, so it is one of the few things that I need to add something to it to make it more palatable. A little cream and sweetener of some sort usually does it.

Love the long lasting low key energy vibe matcha provides. I am an avid coffee drinker (strong, dark), but the energy feel that matcha gives over coffee is significant. So I drink my morning coffee then switch to matcha. Loads of other benefits too.

I'll probably stick with my plain matcha, but I do think this is worth trying, especially if new to matcha drinking. Price is decent too!

title: 10 mg sodium per 2 Tbs serving (add to 1 cup water). Good veg & umami taste
text:
Ingredients: corn syrup solids, tomato, onion, garlic, yeast extract, carrot, basil, celery seed, parsley, spinach, turmeric, bay leaf.

Serving size: 2 TBS
Calories: 70
Fat: 0grams
Cholesterol: 0mg
SODIUM: 10 mg
Total Carb 14 grams
---Fiber 1g
---Total sugars 3 g
---includes 2 grams ADDED
Protein: 2grams
calcium 20mg
potassium 221 mg

Directions: Add 2 TBS broth powder to 1 cup boiling water. Simmer 1-2 minutes and serve

-------------------

Personally, I like it. I dont see a need for corn syrup as it contributes to the "added sugars". There is some naturally occurring sugar from the vegetables used. I think it has a very good taste-- vegetable with an umami taste (probably from yeast extract). Loads of green flecks from parsley, basil, spinach. I love that it is so low in sodium. I can drink it plain, or I can sprinkle a little of my [[ASIN:B000E6BRUW Redmond Real Sea Salt]] to give it the salty flavor I want but still keep it low in comparison to other broths and bouillons.

I acquired this early 12/2021, and it has a best by date of July 2023.

I like Frontier products, and really have no issue with this. I dont rate on price, but I do comment at times. There are 25 (2 tbs) servings, and at current price of $12.87, that makes it $0.51 per serving. That is about same price as another brand I use. So I think within reason for my budget and values.

What I do rate on is quality, my overall thoughts/experience, and how well the product matches up to the product description. So my 1 star deduction is really targeted toward the fact that the product listing does not include an easy to see ingredient list (it is there just look for it) and no nutritional panel for viewing. I took a big chance on this "LOW sodium" broth. But I wasnt sure what to expect. By labeling laws, anything labeled as "low sodium" cant have any more than 50 mg per serving. But how much a company considers a serving may change what is reasonable. Here, the 2 tbs serving size is meant to be used in 1 cup of water. That is reasonable. So I was willing to chance this, hoped it was following the labeling mandates, and used a reasonable serving. It totally fits that, since it is truly low sodium at just 10 mg (and is to be added into 1 cup of water). However, why not say this? It can only help them by helping others-- and is a very simple fix. Just type in the words, "10 mg per 2 tbs serving". Done.

title: tastes just like regular but w/o salt. Dissolves instantly for big mug of broth. Add salt if need be
text:
I see this brand in the store, but I rarely find the salt free version. Glad to be able to buy it online. I definitely enjoy a salty broth, but the amount of salt in most broths are astronomically high. I dont mind so much when I am making a big pot of soup, but if I want to just have a cup of broth a few times a day to warm me up, or fill a void, then I dont want the added salt making me super thirsty all day. So I figured I would buy a salt free bouillon and either drink it without adding anything to it, or adding my own salt if need be.

The flavor on these are good. Has that chicken (or beef) taste of the regular, but clearly no salt taste. I like it, though I usually sprinkle a little [[ASIN: B000E6BRUW Redmond Real Sea Salt]] in it. YUM. Totally hits the spot when I want a warm cup of something. Also helps fill my belly.

Love the powder packets.. makes it extra easy to make a big mug of broth whenever I want it. Dissolves instantly!

title: Nice addition to snack themed gifts baskets, movie night on the couch, portion control
text:
Nice big box of smaller packed Oreo cookies. Small packs help the cookies stay fresh!

I got this to add to a Snack themed gift. I know that when I buy Oreos (usually the Golden), it can take me awhile to go through the pack. Instead of being concerned with it going stale, I like the option of just grabbing a pack as I want them. ALSO helps in portion control. Because on the flip side, is me just eating the whole pack. For the person I bought this for, they are very self controlled in their eating habits. I know they enjoy Oreos, and so I figured they would enjoy the smaller stay fresh packs.

title: High quality brand, excellent balance of flavor, just like sugar, no weird aftertaste
text:
I like Better Body Foods, and have been using this brand on and off for many years. They have a few monk fruit blends available, two of which are not labeled organic, and this one that is. So if you didn't know, "organic" boosts the market value, hence the seemingly high price tag of $18 (or $1.12 per ounce). BUT, if you dont need organic, then select the [[ASIN:B07J1H2X2C Better Body Foods Monk fruit blend]] --same thing, just not "organic" to save several dollars ($8.41, or $0.53 per ounce), which is less than other quality brands I enjoy. Because of all this, I simply dont rate on price as we all have our own budgets, values, brand loyalties...and understanding.

So know at least that if you like this brand, and want to try this product, it is perfectly fine. I appreciate that it clearly spells out that it is a BLEND. Some brands are sneaky in their wording, so I greatly appreciate that they do not hide that this is a Monk Fruit AND Erythritol BLEND.

Nice balance of taste. I already think that Monk Fruit is a near identical match in taste and texture for sugar replacement. Add in a little Erythritol and it boosts the sweet level a little without being overpowering. No weird aftertaste, so by all means this is fantastic for baking.

I want some cookies and other sweet goodies, but I dont want the direct sugar hit. I have purchased various "keto" or diabetic snacks (I am neither, but both are low/no sugar options) and baking mixes. Some great, most mediocre. So I decided to try to just make my own stuff. I am starting off with simple recipes that I am simply swapping out the usual cane sugar for. Then eventually I will play around with the flours, to hopefully further reduce carbs. But the direct sugar? If I can get a good tasting snack/dessert by swapping out the sugar portion, then I consider that a win.

Using a 1:1 sugar alternative that actually tastes and performs like regular sugar is amazingly helpful. I like this blend, and have no problem recommending this product, or pretty much any other product in their line.

title: YUM! loads of dense, moist cake, w/chewy fruit in each bite, tender/non bitter nuts. Tin!
text:
Wonderful! Even people who hate fruitcake are likely to enjoy this! This is exactly what I want fruit cake to taste like. I knew a good fruit cake was out there! Here it is! I will buy this again, and am telling everyone I know about it. Mmmm I love it. AND it comes packed in an unmarked winter themed tin. (all nutritional info is on the package that the cake is sealed in). I really like this, and I will describe why. If you are like me, then you will appreciate this (and the cake).

A few years ago I got it in my head that I wanted to try a fruitcake-- everyone hates fruitcake! Maybe I won't. Alas, I didn't like what I tried-- and it was some popular specialty brand that fruit cake eaters rave over. Blegh (too much nut, too little fruit, almost zero cake). But then then I took it as a yearly holiday mission to find a fruitcake that I do like. I determined that I dont care for the spicy cakes that are primarily nut based with nearly no "cake", and usually not enough fruit. So I began looking for a cake based fruit cake that has a good balance of nuts and fruit mixed in.

This is basically what I am looking for!!! Loads of moist, not too sweet dense cake, with plenty of soft, sweet, chewy, non spicy fruit, and then has a mix of tender, non bitter pecans and walnuts layered on top, and lightly peppered within. EACH bite has a little of everything. The whole thing, bite per bite provides a pleasant mouth feel. Balanced in both taste and texture. It is just delightful, and I had trouble stopping once I started slicing off pieces for myself.

This is fruitcake for people who scoff at fruitcake, and for those looking for more "cake" in their fruit cake. The nuts are tender, and not overpowering. The fruit is chewy and sweet, with a more natural taste. Then the CAKE batter portion. Mmm WOW, so dense , moist, and rich. I would eat just that if they made it.

I know fruit cake is traditionally made with very little to no cake batter (boring!). Basically any that is there is to just hold the copious amount of nuts and scarce use of fruit together and soaked for long time in alcohol (rum?). But then over time as with any recipe new takes are made on it. Hence the wide variety available. I was getting to the point of wanting to try making my own "ideal" version, but I knew that trying to nail the dense rich cake would be a challenge (I'm not a baker, and have little patience). So its been kinda fun trying a cake or two every year to find one I really liked.

I do believe that found it with this Crave Island "fruit and nut dessert cake". I would get it again, and I do recommend it.

title: sweet, not cloying, lovely blue raspberry flavor. Versatile use in drinks and food
text:
I am familiar with Hypothermias products. I have used both the ready to use (sugar included) and the non sweetened flavor concentrates. The former is easier to use, but know that it contains loads of sugar. However, the overall flavor isn't cloying, and it is easy enough to reduce the recommended amount and not compromise taste. My review for this flavor is nearly identical to their other flavors, in that everything is the same save for the actual flavor. This is a ready to use syrup. I like Hypothermias products, and the ready to use is pretty good for home use as well as commercial use. I prefer their Black Cherry concentrate (unsweetened) as the cherry, or this blue raspberry taste is a little more robust, but this is pretty good too. Gotta love blue raspberry! Sweetened with sugar, not high fructose corn syrup, so seems to taste less cloying than others.

As mentioned, not just for shaved ice and slushies. Try it in smoothies, coffee, tea, pop, frosting, baking, as a regular syrup or added to other syrups and toppings for added flavor. I'll be trying this in a cherry scone recipe.

Good size. Comes well wrapped, and the cap is separate. They make big bottles, but no matter the size I have had, I find either option to be reasonably priced, especially when using for use in drinks-- way more affordable than a brand marketed for that purpose when the ingredients are very similar. I think sno cone syrup is a hidden gem in affordable drink syrups (ie, try it as a mixer, or as an "Italian soda" flavoring!)

title: excellent flavor, easy to drink, not for serious electrolyte replacement, but basic hydration
text:
Fantastic flavor, very easy to drink, not too sweet, no weird aftertaste. Just a pleasant carbonated drink. I grab a can of this whenever I am in the mood for some light fizz. It is just good.

But it falls short on whatever it is trying to be. Detox? Hydration? Energy? I wouldn't grab for this for any serious electrolyte replacement needs, but if it is a matter of drinking something versus not drinking something, then yes.. this will provide some hydration, and a little better than water in some cases.

Very tasty, super low cal, etc.. all good. But why not include a picture of this on their product page. I dont need to see several pictures of other people drinking it. I need to see what the can says so I can decide if I want to drink it. If I were shopping around for something of this nature, I likely would not have purchased it since I would not know what the nutrition panel says. But now that I have it, tried it, like it a lot.. I have to say, I would consider this again.

title: 3.5 stars. Thin angel hair good in Pho, Pad Thai, etc. Drain & rinse well
text:
Pretty good. One retail looking box with multiple packs of noodles. I had purchased a couple of different varieties because I wasn't sure which style I would like better (thicker spaghetti, or this angel hair). I primarily want to use it to bulk up some soup. It's cold weather now, and I keep having a craving for broth, and while I want to add something to it to bulk it up, I dont want to add carbs and cals. So here we are. I like shirataki noodles already, and I know it is often a matter of finding the right size style of noodle that makes or breaks the dish. As with any, drain and rinse the noodles well. I never use shirataki noodles as a spaghetti pasta replacement, usually I stick to other dishes just to bulk it up.

This kinda works for my quick noodle soup need, though I think these are better suited for pho or other Asian inspired dishes. I say this because the noodle reminds me more of a thin rice noodle. Slightly rubbery, but good. I think I will want to cook them more, or fry them a little for best taste and texture.

I haven't yet tried their [[ASIN:B07ZVDP46K spaghetti noodle]], which I want to use to replicate [[ASIN:B08LW3T6XF Skinny Pasta cup of soup]] but will do so and report back here when I am ready to write that review.

EDIT: Tried the other noodle. No go. While I have never had any issue digesting shirataki noodles, and was fine with this angel hair variety, the spaghetti ones I linked above basically um.. came out the other end whole. Gross. Also they were extra rubbery and didnt pick up other flavors. So basically boring, and weirdly chewy. 1 star for the spaghetti. 3.5 stars for this angel hair. I hemmed and hawed between a 3 star rating and 4 star since we cant do half stars. I went with 3, which means it is "just OK". I know I wont buy them again, but will use them up. (The spaghetti ones I wont use. Waste of money).

title: as close to a chocolate chip cookie bar as I have had in a long time
text:
The blonde brownies are surprisingly good, and super easy to make. Just need to add some butter, eggs, vanilla. They very much remind me of a cookie bar. Not a brownie. It nearly tastes like a regular cookie, but has that hint of something that is definitely reminiscent of a keto product. Though overall very good. Has a good crumble. Might be a tad to moist, oily, but flavor and mouthfeel is pretty good. The aroma reminds me of their [[ASIN:B08VN1RD9Y vanilla wafer cookies]] .

I am not at all keto, not even low carb. I am just looking to avoid/minimalize foods that trigger a life long issue with binge eating. Since sugar, in the form of treats seems to "spark my brain" to over consume (not just a piece of cake but the whole cake, not 1 donut, but 12, not a couple of cookies, but the whole batch, a frenzied driving need...), I am combating my problem by reducing sugary treats. It has been helping, a lot. No binge in 7 months. In 20+ years, I hadn't gone more than a few days. So this is huge, whatever I am doing. I can have a piece of this and not want the whole batch. It doesnt make my brain itchy to need to consume more. I still have a big appetite, and often over eat, but it isnt sweets, and it isnt a "binge". Not sure how to explain it.. but I feel much more in control.

And since I dont have a driving need for sugary treats, having Keto desserts on hand helps me to at least think I have something I can nosh on if need be (especially when husband comes home with donuts). I really know nothing much about the actual approved Keto sweeteners, so I can't comment on that.

I can only say that this is close to normal cookie taste I have had in awhile, and it still doesn't trigger my brain to dive in and binge. I have liked a wide assortment of Highkey products, and have been disgusted by some keto boxed cookies/cakes/muffin mixes.. so I am pleased that this is yet another amazing "keto" product by Highkey. And for $7.48, not terrible price. Thank you for not price gouging. For that, I will likeley buy more, and try their regular brownies sometime soon.

title: brilliant, tasty, easy way to have low carb hummus that indeed tastes like hummus!
text:
I bought these to make hummus, and hummus I did make! WOW--game changer. It tastes like regular hummus. Not "good for a hummus", but like, no one would know it wasn't made with garbanzo beans. Texture, weight, overall flavor is the same. Or at least nearly so.

I didnt follow a recipe-- just sort of winged it, and it all turned out well. It says to cook on stove, but I just poured kettle boiled water over about a half cup of these flakes, covered, and let sit for a bit. Then not sure whether to leave some water or not, I kept a little of the water and added the moistened flakes to my ninja single cup blender. It was looking like hummus! Then I added some [[ASIN:B08QH2M3YV delicious tahini]], salt, and fresh ground black pepper. Blended again. Taste? WOW, I could not tell difference between using lupini and using garbanzo. Add other flavors if so desired.

I had tried the flakes dry and wet, plain. They have an ever so gentle bitter taste-- in a good way. I found that this flavor would work great in making a hummus, and sure enough it worked well (I omitted my usual squeeze of lemon).

Since I had kept a little of the water, my hummus was a little runny. Instead of adding more flakes, I decided to add my trusty [[ASIN:B09B64FJ3X low carb, high fiber flour]] called Slimovina (another game changer in my life). This instantly thickened it up (it is my go to for adding body to soups and stews, and for making thicker sauces and gravies-- adds loads of nutrients but nearly no carbs. Can also be consumed as a hot cereal, or added to oats, grits.). So while I didnt set out to use the Slimovina, it was such a good/perfect addition that it might be my go-to mix. Just be mindful that Slimovina and Lupini products have A LOT of fiber.

Then I used these delicious (to me, some people find them bland) [[ASIN: B084WMWQR4 organic high fiber crackers]]. Again, watch the fiber, lol. But seriously.. my belly gets filled up!

I dont recall why I chose these particular flakes. Might have been price, might have been reviews, might have been random. I am just glad I did. I will buy again. This bag will last me awhile as the way made my hummus ended making quite a bit.

I knew I wanted to make hummus-- while I am not keto, I am watching (kinda) my calories and carbs. Ive been avoiding hummus because I tend to eat a lot, and even a small amount packs in calories and carbs. By switching to lupin, I am reducing a lot of the carbs. I have plain lupin flour on hand, but wasn't sure if it would work for making hummus, hence my looking for beans or flakes. The flakes are way quicker, easier, cheaper than the pre cooked beans. Un cooked beans would likely never get made by me. So I went with the flakes. Now I will have to try using this in other recipes. Cool beans. haha

title: comforting dissolvable ginger, sweetened. Nice hot or iced, plain or added to other drinks
text:
I like it!

I love ginger in all ways that I can get it. I particularly enjoy a hot (or iced) cup of ginger "tea". I prefer the dissolvable granules over tea bags (those are fine too, but I often just want instant), and despite watching my sugar intake, I actually prefer sweetened. Though I keep both sweetened and unsweetened on hand, and often use one of each when making a cozy mug of ginger "tea". Or added to Chai tea.

With all the pictures they have at least one could be the nutrition panel.

Each packet contains 70 calories. 0 fat, 0 cholesterol, 10 mg sodium, Total Carbs: 17 grams (13 grams of sugar, 11 of which is added). 240 mg potassium.

Ingredients: cane sugar, blend of ginger extract, maltodextrin.

For a small mug of tea, 1 sachet to 6 ounces of water. But since I usually have a larger cup 8-10 ounces, I usually use 2, hence my preference for using 1 sweetened, 1 unsweetened.

It is wonderfully comforting feeling, and just feels good in my gut. Not all that "spicy", yet it has a little ginger kick. I prefer a stronger kick, so this isn't as exciting to me but I am still very much enjoying it. I also enjoy mixing in a little matcha green tea powder for added antioxidant benefit.

title: best brewed with 6 oz water. Smooth taste, wonderful aroma, natural tasting coconut
text:
Wonderful, divine coconut aroma. Be mindful of how much water you use to brew this. By default, I brewed it with 10 ounces of water, but this product listing says to use 6 ounces. "To achieve optimal flavor our single serve pods should be brewed on the 6oz setting". I agree with that! It is otherwise watery. OR brew it along side another cup of coffee (so one of these at 6 ounces, then for me, a dark roast at 8-10 ounces- yum!).

Once I switched to small cup setting, the flavor was much more robust. Very smooth for a medium. A nice treat style coffee. I normally drink my coffee black, but the lovely fragrant coconut and matching taste begged for some additional cream. Creamy coconut.. mMMmMmm.

This would not be my daily drinking coffee, but it is nice for times I want something a little different, or to be able to offer something different to someone.

What I like is the natural flavor of it. I normally shy away from flavored coffees because the tastes are so off putting to me. I took a chance on this because I happen to like coconut in general, am familiar with The Coffee Beanery company, and was curious with their take on a coconut coffee. It's good.

JUST BREW WITH LITTLE WATER for best overall flavor.

title: smells good, dissolves easily, but falls way short on taste. Not bad, but not impressed
text:
As with any food or drink item, it comes down to personal taste. I drink matcha daily, and find most any of them to be good (enough). Curious to taste a melon infused ceremonial grade, I really didnt know what to expect. Here are my observations:

--I am not sure if it is ceremonial grade. I say this because.. I guess I am expecting it to be more difficult to whisk into cold water. As is, almost all matcha is tricky to dissolve even in hot water. I can stir this with a spoon. I mean, that's good for a cold drink, but it perplexes me in terms of what I know/experience with having consume ceremonial and culinary for 15+ years now. Anyway, consider it a positive that it stirs so easily into cold water.

--directions 2 tsp per 16 ounces cold water.

--Aroma is pleasant. Strong whiff of melon, grassy, fresh. Funny, that I had thought that, since those exact words are on the label.

--but that doesn't translate to taste. I can't exactly taste the melon. I think my nose is picking up on the smell in the glass but my taste buds dont actually taste it. Maybe a hint, at most. Thought maybe I just need to use more, but I did make it according to direction, and that is my observation on that.

--overall mild tasting, so in that it leans a little more toward "ceremonial"--but is has added flavor and dextrin, so I would use the term loosely.

In summary: I think it is "OK" which is middle of road 3 star rating. Wont me a repurchase at any price. I dont think it is bad, but it is really not a different, interesting enough exprerience to like it. If it had just a little more flavor, even a hint, I would be pleased. I ended up adding a berry blends powder to it. I dont want to have to "doctor it up". One thing to add it in to stuff to bury the taste, but another when it should have a flavor on its own to enjoy-- and it fall short, and needing help. I'll stick to plain ceremonial or culinary matcha.

Ah well, if it sounds good to you, go for it.

Ingredients
Premium Grade Matcha, Dextrin, Natural Flavor

title: very bland, minimal Chai spice taste. More like a sweet creamer. Use w/ chai tea bag for best taste
text: It is bland. I really can't tell that it has any "chai" spices. It is lightly sweet, and I think works better as a creamer than a base for a warm drink. I have added it to a chai tea bag with much better results. Serving size is 1 small scoop in 6 ounces of water. It tastes better doubled, which of course starts to pack on the calories. text: Love crispy oils.A little savory, a little sweet, a little heat. Makes the taste buds perk up. This Chinese chili crisp oil is within the range of expectation. title: mellow, mild, easy to drink culinary that leans more ceremonial. Durable tin. Pricy though!
text:
I like the smell and the taste of this "all purpose" matcha. The matcha is packed in a bag, tucked into a durable reusable tin container with twist off lid. Label has a basic latte recipe. Since I drink matcha daily, and try out a different brand frequently, I have a go to preparation for testing it out. I make a simple hot latte, but I always use more than typical amount (1-2 TBS vs 1-2 tsp).

It blended well with my hot water and cream. I am not a fan of plain matcha, so I added in some non sugar sweetener and a little vanilla. Some matcha powder will still taste much too strong and then I have to make modifications until it tastes right. I dont mind this, but it is much nicer when the matcha has a more mellow flavor (ceremonial will lean this way, but is often much more pricey). THIS culinary matcha is pretty smooth and mellow. Has a hint of that "green" flavor, but it really isnt bitter at all. It leans much closer to ceremonial, if you think of matcha on a spectrum. It even pairs well with hot cocoa, which has become my go to hot drink to warm me up on these cold pre winter days. Loads of antioxidants!

I dont rate on price (everyone has different budgets, values, needs), but I will comment. This is fantastically pricy for culinary matcha. $50 for 100 grams (3.5 ounces) is just over $14 per ounce. I have spent nearly that for ceremonial grade, but never for culinary. But I will say that this is a very pleasant (to me) tasting matcha, and it is more reminiscent to some ceremonials, and is way better than a lot of culinary varieties. It makes me curious about their actual ceremonial variety- how splendid that must be?!

I think this is quite good, and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it if the price works for you. Might make nice addition to a food/drink themed gift. The tin is also nice. Add in a whisk, and/or a frother, maybe a nice mug, cookies, etc.

I have been drinking matcha on and off for 15-20 years, and more so in the past couple as matcha has become readily available. Prices are all over, as is the quality. The quality, smell, and taste here is good. Yum Yum!

I see no reason not to give it full rating.

title: WHAT IS THIS SORCERY?!?! Amazingly good, like cup of soup dupe but even better (low sod)
text:
WOW WoW WOw! I am in love with this Skinny cup of soup. It is SO good. Let me list all the reasons why I am impressed and love this beyond measure.

--OK, so these noodles are perfect. SUCH a good mouth feel. Better than any noodle of any sort I have ever had in a soup, especially instant soup. Really good texture. More robust than raman, but not rubber band like a lot shirataki noodles (I wouldnt know it was shirataki/konjac). I already like shiritaki noodles of all sorts, but I still expected a mediocre taste and texture. This product blows my mind. Not only is it the best shiritaki product I have ever had (and I have had lots over the past 15 years), it is also an excellent "cup of soup" dupe.

--taste is just so good, so comforting, so very lovely on a freezing cold afternoon. Great alone, or as a snack. It isn't just good "for a skinny soup". It is simply really good (to me). I am a volume eater, and was looking for a good quick soup that wasn't packed with sodium. I found that with this.

-- JUST 80 mg sodium. HOW IS THAT POSSOBLE? This tastes like full salt. Is it truly, really this low in salt? I legit checked the package 3x to make sure I wasn't missing seeing a third number in there. VERY IMPRESSED. I swear I am skeptical.

-- And I CAN TASTE VEGETABLES!! Has an al dante vibe. Real veggies. Small flakes, but real none the less. I bit into a piece ofvegetable and recognized it as celery.

--I'm no vegan, not even vegetarian, but I am stoked that this does not contain animal products. It does not contain chicken.. yet tastes like chicken broth.

--FIBER! It has 7 grams of fiber. That's great!

--NO added sugar. 7 grams of carbs come strictly from the fiber, 2 grams of protein, 0.5 grams fat, 80 mg sodium, and just 70 calories..

--BEST YET?! IT IS FILLING! This is a pricy cup of soup, but it is generously sized. The noodles fill up nearly the whole cup. They did not skimp on noodles, veggies, or broth.

--super easy to make. The noodles are in their own bag. I am used to draining & rinsing shirataki noodles because of the odd/off flavor, but I did not notice any weird smell. So one cup I made by draining/rinsing bag first, the second time, I just dumped it into the cup. Either way is totally fine. Next, add the packets of dried vegetables and broth powder. Add boiling water. DONE! Now enjoy. If you want even more broth, pour this into a bigger bowl. Comes with a SPORK!

seriously.. WHAT IS THIS SORCERY???

Full rating for its amazingness. I dont rate on price (we all have different budgets, values, needs) and I do find it pricey at $5 a cup. I would eat this daily, and will somehow find a way to buy this regularly. Would be nice to see a subscribe and save option, or priced closer to $4, or maybe make it an 8 pack. I think price will deter some buyers. I happened to buy it on a whim (really wanted some healthy soup that didnt require me to always make from scratch). SO GLAD I DID, it is the best thing I have purchased (hence not scoffing too much at price). I will buy this again. Adding more to my cart right now!

PS. Says gluten free, and I imagine there is a classification for what can be considered gluten free. This says there is less than 20 ppm. Just like how something can still have fat but be considered low fat so long as it has less than a certain amount per serving (same goes for classifications for low sodium etc). So know what your threshold for gluten as this contains a hint of it.

title: mellow, lightly sweet, easy to drink-not harsh or bitter. Lovely as simple tea or latte
text:
Weird, I may be the odd one out, but I really like this matcha powder. Love the smell directly from packet. Taste is just as wonderful. I only taste this as Ceremonial Grade. I have been drinking matcha for a couple of decades now, go through A LOT of it, often culinary, sometimes ceremonial when I could find it. In the last ten years this stuff has exploded in availability, but it also brought quite a variation in quality and taste. Some ceremonial tastes more like culinary and occasionally a culinary is so smooth that it could nearly pass for ceremonial. Since I was so used to culinary (because of easier availability), that is what I got used to, and I pretty much just bought that. Well more recently I began dabbling back into ceremonial, and only a few out of a dozen or so have been what *I* consider ceremonial.

And so, my perception of this is that it definitely tastes like ceremonial. It is a product of Japan, so know that there are regional differences. It is SMOOTH, slightly sweet (naturally), mild/mellow, non bitter. A gentle, easy flavor that tastes good plain, or have added cream, sweetener. This is a pleasant matcha (to me). I find the culinary to be bitter, and extra green tasting,. I still drink it as I use it in smoothies and other drinks where the added ingredients mask the off putting flavor. This does not need that, at all and I wont waste it in a smoothie. I like this as tea, or matcha latte.

So ultimately it comes down to your own preference, and taste perception. I do not think that they are claiming ceremonial when its culinary.I DO think it is ceremonial. I've been drinking it daily with pleasure rather than just a healthy thing to do.

title: 3.5 stars (Saigon?) Cassia cinnamon sticks, thick & aromatic. Read on for difference in cinnamon
text:
There are different types of cinnamon available, typically classified as Ceylon (derived from the inner bark of the Cinnamomum verum tree) OR Cassia, so please know your cinnamon before ordering. It is unfortunate to see a product down rated for this misconception, yet it is also on the company to state the difference, and perhaps the expectation so the uniformed can be properly informed. Cinnamon is confusing, so please read on for more info.

If you are used to the smooth, tightly rolled, multi layered, highly fragrant cinnamon sticks most associated with baking, or added to cider, that would be CEYLON cinnamon (which this is not), and is considered the most safe (least amount of coumarin). When in its natural form, this is the kind most often found in stores. It is the kind that should be used most often because of its low coumarin content, but check this.. nearly all cinnamon powder we get in stores is NOT ceylon cinnamon, but a different, less "safe" variety referred to as CASSIA. It is harder to find powdered ceylon in stores, and unless it says ceylon, it is likely cassia. Ceylon is more pricy than Cassia. Unfortunate, since Ceylon is considered "true cinnamon" (AS A SIDE, those not used to powdered ceylon after a life time of powdered cassia will find that it doesnt taste as robust as cassia tends to have more oil).

There are a few types of CASSIA cinnamon, or rather there are a few regions of cinnamon that all get clumped in as Cassia. It is a single layer thick bark, that is always loosely rolled. It has a more questionable health profile due to its high coumarin content, and happens to be what we use nearly all the time in recipes. On the plus side, most recipes call for very little, and it would take a lot to reach upper limit consumption, so I dont worry myself over it unless you have issues that excess coumarin may affect (ie liver issues). But you do you. I keep both on hand, often use a mix, but I reach for precious Ceylon when baking, and when I want the added blood sugar reducing benefits, and sometimes top it off with Cassia (since cassia is the "cinnamon" we are more used to tasting). Ceylon is nice for adding to main dishes, lends an intriguing depth of spice, but is also good in baking. Just different. Actually, originally, ceylon is what should be used in baking as it applies to sweet goods, because of its blood sugar stabilizing effects. Shame the stores usually only carry Cassia.

So which is this? Well it doesn't expressly say it, but I deduce that since this is a product of Vietnam, the look of it, and the priced, that this is cassia. More specifically, Saigon Cassia. The look, smell, and performance is notable toward the cassia I am familiar with. SO buy this if you are looking for CASSIA CINNAMON, specifically SAIGON CASSIA (slightly different than original cassia, which originates from Indonesia, or China)!

Unlike ceylon, this cassia bark is thicker, more natural, peeled fresh in appearance. You will see little knots and other darer patches. The larger roll size is very typical. The smell is mild, the taste is sweet. Mildly spicy. Just depends on what it is used in. The aroma emanating from this bag reminds me of apples and cinnamon. I am surprised that is smells as fruity as it does. It is lovely.

HOWEVER, while I am confident on this being CASSIA, I am not absolutely sure which kind of cassia. Like I said, there are different sub types of cassia, and it is region specific, with different flavor profiles, and different coumarin content. It slightly resembles Chinese cassia too. So for that, I down rate because the product description and bag could be more.. descriptive. I am also familiar with this brand, and have found that the several spices I have had have been perfectly fine. This is the first time that I am left scratching my head a little.

I added a roll to my coffee, and it imparts a light cinnamon taste. It is the type of cinnamon stick that I would/will use in a simmer pot. If I was crafty, I would use these.. the look of them are more interesting than the smooth bark, tight thin rolls of Ceylon. Doubt I would go through the effort of grinding or shaving Cassia bark

I wrote this on the fly, didnt intend an essay. I just wanted to clear up some misconceptions when I saw people saying that this isnt the same as their typical name brand cinnamon stick. Accurate, because it is not the same type of cinnamon used. My apologies for any mistakes in my knowledge.

They include a way to contact them for more info (on the bag), but I would prefer to see more info on the bag. 3.5 to 4 stars. I am rating it on MY knowledge of cinnamon.

3-4 stars for use in drinks, though probably not baking
4-5 stars for crafting, simmering

title: effective energy booster, not my favorite flavor among their other varieties, still good
text:

This is the closest to being pleasant than I have ever had. Very sweet to me, and it kind of makes me thirsty.. but it POWERS ME UP, and that is my main interest. *GOAT SCREAM*

I've never met an energy drink that I would for sure buy again, and this one(particularly the Watermelon Fruit Punch) is a strong contender.

I am human, and may have overlooked something.., but so far so good. *GOAT SCREAM*

text:

Really quite small though. I would expect double the amount of cups for the price (not that I rate on price, but I do comment).

Taste was a tad light on apple and cinnamon, but it was still good. My next one may get an extra sprinkle of cinnamon. I like the ingredients save for the 15 grams of added sugar. It doesn't need that much sugar to taste good!

Other than that, I love how there is no preparation required. Just peel the film off, and place in microwave. Eat from the cup, or pop it out and eat from hand. Add a little whipped cream for added dessert like vibe.
