7 pictures of the front of the can, but not a single picture to the back of the can. Ya know, the spot that tells you what is in it? Please add this info.

I wont describe all that is in it, but this can has just 10 calories, 45mg sodium, 0 added sugar (2 carbs), and a host of vitamins, minerals, other supplements.

I think it tastes good, even at room temp. I have tried so many sports drinks and they all have an odd/off taste. This is the closest to being pleasant than I have ever had. Very sweet to me, and it kind of makes me thirsty.. but it POWERS ME UP, and that is my main interest. *GOAT SCREAM*

No jitters, no crash, just FUELED UP. It helped me work out extra long, extra hard with my first can. I drank half of it before starting, and consumed rest between sips of water. The great thing was that I went into my workout feeling really run down. I was like, ok.. even if I just get a solid 15 minutes in (down form my usual 45), I will at least have done something. Well, next thing I knew I finished my usual workout and wanted to keep going. I just felt.. GOOD. I went for a total of 121 minutes, a mix of boxing, squats, lunging, and arm/ab work. Ever play, Supernatural on the Oculus QUest VR? Great fitness game. I went at it for 2 hours, and if it werent for wanting to make sure I didnt injure myself, I could have kept going. I totally blame GOAT FUEL on that awesome workout.

I have two other varieties, Peach Pineapple and Tropical Berry. All similar, but this Watermelon Fruit punch is my favorite. Has the least weird taste. But I do like them all. Ive never met an energy drink that I would for sure buy again, and this one is a strong contender.

Drinking one as I write this, then I am off to clean the house. I'm giving it a generous 5 stars for the great way it makes me feel. If I learn anything else, or experience anything else, I will be back to update. I am human, and may have overlooked something.., but so far so good. *GOAT SCREAM*

title: Sweet and Spicy, a delightful treat. Really tasty. Add to a foodie gift basket!
text: Pack of two small jars, packed well. Would make nice addition to a foodie gift basket (give both, or part out into a couple of gift baskets---or keep one for self). It is sweet with a bite of spice. Very pleasant with butter on a plain bagel, or paired with cream cheese. I haven't gotten any further than that, and I may not need to. Though I imagine there are plenty of other pairings. Even tastes delicious off the spoon. Thinking it would be good slathered on a burger or chicken sandwich.

title: spicy, sweet, salty, soy forward. Watch out for sugar (9g per serving). Good flavor, bold taste
text:
I like Field Trip products. I have found them all to be tasty, fresh, and have a good mouth feel. The one aspect that I highlight in my reviews is that for a beef jerky, there is a goodly amount of added sugar. In this variety, it is 9 grams of added sugar per 1 ounce serving (11 total carbs per serving). 12 servings total.

This "Everything" spice is rather spicy,. It has a kick of heat. Not a building fire, but it is pretty warm. I think the taste of sweet, salty, smoky, and heat are the prevailing "flavors". I can pick up on some garlic, and sesame seeds. I wouldn't say I pick up on "everything bagel" seasonings immediately. I guess technically it is there. Soy aftertaste.

Texture wise, this is a softer jerky. Some pieces softer than others. Hits a range from a very tender level to firm and chewy, but still easy on teeth. Various sized pieces.

Good solid bag, pressure zip closure.

Like I said.. I like it, and I find it hard to stop eating it.. but as a discerning reviewer, I have to take note of some points that would deter me from making a purchase. Mainly:

--The nutrition profile being absent from the description. There is a small image, but I can not zero in on it enough to see what this product is comprised of (nutrition panel and ingredients).
--While I love the spice level, it is going to be a surprise for anyone expecting "everything bagel". This has those seasonings, but the overall sweet, salty, heat, and SOY are the predominant flavors.

3.5 stars. I like it much better than 3, so I am going with 4

title: spicy, overall flavor is better than canned stuff. Lovely with coconut milk added in
text: I like the overall taste. I find it hit or miss with prefab Indian marinades, sauces, curries. I am really not talented enough to make it taste as good as a restaurant, so I do rely on the prefab stuff. This is a tad spicier than what I normally go for. Pairing it with coconut milk, and having a side of rice or naan helps a lot. The tamarind flavor pops through, has a good level that I find quite enjoyable. Not sure if I would get this one again (spicy!) but I would consider other varieties from this brand. I think it tastes better than a lot of jarred stuff I have purchased.

title: lovely, comforting, creamy, lightly sweet. Nice alone, or paired w/ other mix-ins
text:
My first foray into multi grain tea powder, so I truly did not know what to expect. I am always game for trying new things and have a very open minded taste palate. This drink is delightful. Warm, comforting, and tasty, in a mild way. Use 3-6 ounces of water or milk, stir, drink.

It tastes nice plain, but I find great value in using it as a base for matcha powder, which I drink hot or cold, but always with other flavors to mask the taste a little.

Now that I think of it, if you add a little cinnamon, it kinda reminds me of an Horchata.

I dont know if this is ever made with another tea, but I find that it makes for a more filling cup of tea and adds some sweetness and creaminess.

It is nearly like a very watered down hot cereal, so I am sure to find other ways to use this if just drinking it plain doesnt seem suitable (quick mini soup base, add to oats, etc)

Not exactly for carb counters though- 17 grams of carbs, 5 grams added sugar in each packet. Not terrible, but this makes a small serving. No fiber. Has 2 grams protein, and 95 mg of sodium

title: tasty condiment, more on mild & tangy side; lovely with raman or egg dishes
text: Nice condiment for Asian dishes, or to spice up, brighten up nearly any other dish (love with eggs). Usually I add a spoonful to raman or other noodle dish. This can be eaten alone, but this particular style is to me best for complimenting a dish. Contains two, 30 calorie servings. Has a peel back top, so no need for can opener.

title: Just ground flax, highlighted with a little hint sweetness. Quite pleasant 4.5 stars
text:
I normally eat ground flax without any extras, but this has Yacon (natural sweetener) and Stevia. I was curious how it would taste- would it be too sweet, too "off"? I am familiar with both sweeteners, and yacon is delightful- very light, sometimes a hint of lychee, but in this it is just a hint of sweet. The stevia is surprisingly super light too. The overall taste of this flax is just pleasant. Not too sweet. Seriously impressed as so many sweetened items are way over done. Not this.. Just ground flax, highlighted with a little sweetness. It is extra nice added to yogurt, oats, smoothies. I would add this to a muffin or bread recipe.

Typical nutrition profile, loads of fiber. 25 grams per serving!

4.5 stars.
I would like to see a clear picture of the nutrition profile. Can zoom in on what they do provide.

title: lovely zip of non jittery energy
text: Japanese style matcha powder from Thailand. It is as good as most all other brands I have tried. I have been drinking matcha for many years, so I go through a lot. I always used more than double the usual amount. I add it to smoothies, or make cold or hot lattes. Since matcha itself does not taste good to me, I always use cream or non dairy milk, some sort of sweetener, and/or other flavors to help mask the taste. I have tried matcha at all price points, and I really dont notice a huge difference between them (save for maybe 1-2, where they really stood out in excellence). I am pleased with this, no issues. Slightly grassy, mild bitterness. But works well in everything I have used it in, and most importantly it gives me that lovely zip of non jittery energy that keeps me coming back for more.

title: goes with anything, great way to reduce cals & carbs, use alone or add in to real pasta for volume
text:
Well, it's not a substitute for Penne exactly since the noodles collapse, but it does provide a decent mouth feel. I like having various shapes on hand. I like how easy it is to prepare, and I love drastically cutting cals and carbs all while filling my belly. I have been using shirataki noodles for 15 years or so now. On and off. I like seeing it become more and more available in store and online. I dont get out to the stores as much these days, so I dont mind spending a little extra by purchasing it online.

Usually I am going through this stuff a lot when I want to cut carbs and calories. I am a volume eater, and so I work with it instead of fight it. Since shirataki is not the most amazing thing to me on its own, I usually use it to cut it into regular pasta, or to add volume to a vegetable dish. I use shirataki noodles so I can have the full volume I want, but some (or much) of the carbs and cals are reduced. I still get flavor of pasta, and mouth feel, but a whole lot less calories. Sometimes I eat this stuff on its own, just depends on what I am in the mood for. I also buy rice versions (with same approach--add it in with rice).

I always rinse my noodles really well before using it in some sort of preparation.

For this review, I made a quick lunch. I had made a simple "pasta" dish using just these noodles, mixed with some pumpkin puree, a splash of real coconut milk, and some seasonings. I'll make that again but will likely add in some vegetables and/or real pasta, maybe some chicken.

Good product, no issues. If you are brand new to Shirataki/konjac noodles, just know to rinse the noodles and that they have a texture that is slightly rubbery, and not like pasta at all. But its pleasant, and works with anything you put with it, and can really help a diet out. For those familiar, this is as expected, minus the ability to be an open noodle, like semolina penne pasta is.

title: nearly no excess liquid compared to big cans of salmon. Side by side, taste same. Loving this!
text:
5 ounce cans of Salmon, 1 can is 1 serving, which is great for portion control. It contains 350 mg of sodium, which is same as most tuna. Though more than some other canned salmon I buy. Still, doable for the fact that this is one serving. Perfect size to eat straight from can, make a sandwich, eat with crackers, or over salad, make patties, etc. More dry and firm, than total mush. Better than most tuna. Reminds me more of an albacore tuna in terms of texture.

No skin, no bones, no significant amount of water.

I like that there isn't a lot of liquid. Some large cans I buy have a slew of excess liquid, and I dont want to pay for water. With this StarKist Wild Pink Salmon, depending on what I am using this for, I dont even bother draining. I like that I am paying for flesh.

Tastes like salmon. I know some people have mentioned tuna. I took another can of salmon (the large cans, that typically have some skin and bones) and opened it up, and tasted them side by side. Tasted the same to me. I think the idea of it tasting like tuna is that it is in a tuna can, has small chunks like tuna, and of course is fishy.. Even I thought it was tuna like, then I decided to compare it side by side with other brands. All good.

These cans require a can opener. Price is good with subscribe and save. I am really pleased to have tried this, and it is now a pantry staple.

title: 100% Robusta beans (more caffeine than Arabica), Coffee that bites back! Jet FUEL!
text:
This has NOTHING added to it. It is labeled as such--100% Robusta bean. No mystery, no surprises. THAT's IT. 100% instant, freeze dried crystals that dissolve instantly in hot or cold liquid. Easy to open pack. Seems to be an even darker roast than some instant Robusta bean options. TRY this if you aren't afraid of something called high octane.

It isn't for people who dont like instant, who dont like bold, who dont like coffee that bites back.

Ok, so when it comes to "high octane coffee", companies basically mean that they are using ROBUSTA beans instead of the typical Arabica or Columbian bean. WHY? Because Robusta beans can have upwards of 25% more caffeine in them naturally. So why dont we all drink more of this? Because Robusta beans are also notoriously more off putting in taste. Some companies will add back a little Arabica, but then it reduces the so called caffeine boost. This instant Truck Stop Blend is on par with other 100% Robusta bean coffees I have had through the years. So if you have had Robusta beans before, then the taste will be familiar, perhaps leans a bit darker than some. If you never have had it then try to know what it is first (a different bean).. and know that it is not the same as your typical coffee, and it naturally has more caffeine in comparison.

IF you dont like the taste, then add it to a larger cup of your own coffee, or add it into a smoothie for added bit of pep.

For a milder version, I also like [[ASIN:B097S34NLK Slow Ride Instant Robusta]] less jet fuel tasting, more regular coffee tasting.

title: 40 count than includes single bites, tiny suckers, and mini size as part of the overall count.
text:
I have never rated on price, as we all have different budgets and needs, and values of time etc... but this is near scandalous. I think this is the one time that it is warranted--because what is received is not what arrived, and what is there is terribly deceiving toward the count in the box. It is not a matter of it being a totally bad product, or that I dont want to pay for something.. it is that it is disgustingly over priced, and not everything pictured is in it. $36 for 40 items (I might have 42). This includes tiny suckers (some of the sticks are broken), tiny single piece Now & Later, and single very small Sour Punch gummy sticks (HALF the length to what is shown). No Twizzlers at all. If it had been 40 full sized items plus the other small stuff added it? Ok, sure. Fun gift. Would consider again. But the tiny one bite items being used as part of the total count? Shameful.

I love the idea of a candy gift box. I thought that if this worked out, I would buy it for the office, or send some off to my younger family. Or just for myself, for fun. I'd buy it for the convenience (at any price) and simply enjoy it.. but the product does not match what is shown. I dont even go out to the stores, and this would be much easier for me to put together on my own for fraction of price and it would look better. The candy is just dumped in a box. No presentation for something that is marketed as a gift box of candy.

Also, only a few items have an expiration date. Others look like they were somehow rubbed off. What I have had so far, has been fine.

So if you like an assortment of candy that doesnt look like much, and may not all be there, and may be broken, and may or may not be fresh.. then go for it.

While I think it is better than 1 stars (2 stars), I definitely dont recommend it which brings it down to 1.

title: creamy, thick, delicious
text: thick, delightfully creamy, floral, sweet. Thicker than regular honey, can eat it off spoon or add it to teas or other foods. Really good stuff, and I see nothing wrong with this product. Manuka honey is lovely to keep on hand even for applying to face as a mask for a massive moisture surge (try on hands too!)

title: Great aesthetic appeal, loose tea w/ tapioca pearls, straws, & recipe cards. Lovely gift option!
text:
Lovely, good looking kit. Definitely gift worthy.

As a lover of Boba tea (aka bubble tea), I often make it myself. I cook the tapioca pearls, I make the tea, I make the simple syrup or buy specialty syrups. All very normal process, and boba tea lovers will likely already know how to make it. No special equipment required (unless you count a loose tea leaf strainer as special). SO I find this kit lovely. And this kit is inspired from their physical location/cafe (located in California)! They have lots of kits!

Sure I could just go buy the occasional cup of boba tea, but for me.. that is an excursion, also those places often use the prefab powder stuff. It is only very recently that some boba tea cafes have popped up in my area, and even "my area" is still at least a 30 minute drive (I live in rural area). Before that, I only got it when I was in a major city (like Toronto or NYC). Hence learning to make my own. Very easy.

I'd love this as a gift! It comes in a gift worthy package, and has a holiday look to it. I has a classy aesthetic to it. Very appealing. Brown box with black labeling. Inside packets of tea in predominantly black packing sits nestled on brown "grass". There are individually wrapped black boba tea straws. Even the description/recipe cards AND pack of tapioca pearls are color coordinated. Well done! I'd be proud to give this as a gift.

It comes with nice assortment of tea, and nice tapioca pearls (they never impart taste, just texture and visual interest). Even better if it would come with a few extra goodies. So, if you are considering this as a gift, I think it is fine by itself, or you can round it out with a few extra items. Since this is loose tea, a tea strainer might be nice. Some simple syrup OR any other flavored syrup. For example my most favorite Boba tea is Green (or black)Tea with Lychee. So I keep a big bottle of this [[ASIN:B0147N45ME Tea Zone Lychee syrup]]. Maybe a smaller bottle is available. But really any syrup is nice. If watching sugar intake grab a bottle of [[ASIN:B01LIM9DHY Jordon Skinny Syrups Pumpkin Trio]] and so on. Currently I am making a CHAI boba tea using this black tea, the pearls, and some chai syrup (or I do the pumpkin).

If you want to really boost the gift, add in a clear/see through cup. Half the joy of the drink is to be able to see the tapioca pearls :)

But I just want to say again, this product is fantastic as is.

title: taste strongly of sunflower seeds, lovely balance of sweet & salty. Very delicious, will buy again.
text:
The taste is fantastic. It is sunflower seed tasting forward, with a balanced level of sweetness and salt. I dont pick up on the chick pea, but that is such a subtle flavor in comparison to sunflower seed that that doesnt surprise me. Each packet has 3 grams of added sugar (from light brown sugar). I think it is reasonable considering that my occasional use of gummy supplements tend to have 3-5 grams of added sugar. I'd like to see an unsweetened option (no sweetener of any kind added) for times I dont want it to taste like dessert. But mmmm this is really good, and totally pleases my sweet tooth.

Easy to spread, nice directly from packet, or added to smoothie or over hot oats.

While the taste is phenomenal, the packet/delivery can use work. Be sure to knead the (easy to open) packet to mix everything well. Then squeeze it out onto food, or directly in mouth (makes for a very nice pre or post workout snack, or on the go in general). The spot of concern is in the remainder of packet-- unless I totally open the packet, I tend to leave some behind no matter how much I try to scrape it up. Temperature may have something to do with it, or maybe I haven't kneaded it enough. So if you can, have a knife or spatula on hand to dig out the last bits of the butter. Since it is recoverable, I will rate on my pure enjoyment of the taste of this chickpea butter. I know I will be buying this again.

title: unsweetened option, great ginger kick, dissolves easily, for lovers of ginger!
text:
YES! I love ginger, and I want it strong and spicy. This is so much better than a ginger tea bag. It is an instant concentrated ginger that quickly dissolved in hot water (havent tried it in cold). Is lovely on its own, or added to other tea. Add sweetener or not.

I am super stoked for this UNSWEETENED version. I have their [[ASIN:B07P1HYBSD instant Ginger and Honey]] version, and I love it--so comforting feeling/tasting. So with this unsweetened option, I use it along with a packet of the other, or on its own, or added to other tea (ginger or chai, usually). So many options.

This is the powder to get if you like that spicy kick of ginger

title: good fresh taste, NO added salt, packed with meat, barely anything to drain off
text:
NO SALT ADDED! I love this! This can has 20mg sodium, compared to my other brand that has 320 mg sodium per can. Huge difference. Now, the lack of salt is noticeable, but it just makes this tuna taste all the more clean and fresh.

I usually add in some mayo, so some salt is being added back in. I really love topping a green salad with tuna (and mayo) then adding some green olives. So yeh, plenty of salt there. Totally appreciate this not having added salt.

Much to my cats disappointment, this is packed with tuna with very little left over water. Many tuna brands are packed with water, to which my cats get to enjoy. This? I didn't bother draining it when I used it over a salad.

Small, robust flakes of meat. Really good smell and flavor to me. Looks good too. I like my tuna to taste like tuna. I have had some Albacore tuna that tasted more like chicken. If I wanted that, I would just buy canned chicken. This Sea Tale Albacore tuna is delightfully tuna tasting- as it should be.

Good stuff! Will buy again.

title: healthy herbal rooibos tea with added bits of herbs & fruit. Tasty selection. Love "Red" tea
text:
Subtle, delicate, cozy. Naturally sweet. Hot teas to curl up with on the couch and a book, or make it iced and sit outside to enjoy the sunset. These Carmien teas have a fresh, natural, pleasing taste. I have them in the variety pack that includes Tropical Burst, Floral Berry, and Citrus Chai. This pack uses RED Rooibos tea and other herbs and spices to create the flavor. (the other variety pack uses Green rooibos).

Rooibos tea is native to South Africa, where this product is from. Naturally decaffeinated, lightly naturally sweet, smooth, delicate, red. I have been drinking Rooibos for over 20 years, before it became readily available in the US. A friend of mine would travel to Africa, and always brings me back this lovely red tea. It is the tea that made me open to drinking tea on a regular basis- just a gentle, nourishing flavor. And so I have for many years, and I loved seeing it become readily available.

I am not normally into fruity or floral, but it works here. I think I like it best iced. I am a big fan of Chai, especially Chai rooibos, and this has the addition of some citrus bits. It is lovely. The hint of orange just goes so well with Chai. Has a bit of a holiday vibe to it.

This makes for a nice sampler. I think it would make a nice addition to a tea lovers gift basket.
I would consider this brand again, especially if I could choose one flavor at a time (I'll go through the Chai quicker than the other two).

title: another great Pinole oats option. I really like this one as a hot "dessert". Just so yum..
text:
I have yet to make it as an "overnight oats" preparation as I always make it hot. I just pour hot water from my electric kettle over it. I find that it cooks quickly, and it just makes my belly happy. I am a big fan of various oats and hot cereals, and this one does not disappoint.

I have tried this PB & Cocoa, their Banana & Cinnamon, and their Original. All good, all satisfying. I usually add in other goodies since I find hot cereals to not quite have enough oomph to keep my hunger at bay. But once loaded up with some additional goodies (like fruit, yogurt, nuts, collagen powder, protein powder, seeds, pumpkin puree, etc) then I am good for the day. This PB & Cocoa is rather nice even as a hot dessert. I have added in some additional peanut butter (or peanut butter powder), with a little whipped cream, or a little vanilla yogurt. Just lovely on chilly fall evening. But yeh, any are good to me, and easily a repurchase (especially as multi pack as it is a better bargain).

title: like a warm hug for my belly. Love the texture, taste
text: I make it hot, it cooks quickly, and it just makes my belly happy. I am a big fan of various oats and hot cereals, and this one does not disappoint. I have tried this orginal, their Banana & Cinnamon, and their PB & Cocoa. All good, all satisfying. I usually add in other goodies since I find hot cereals to not quite have enough oomph to keep my hunger at bay. title: 0.7 ounces. Nice sample size, travel size, or add to gift basket size. Robust matcha
text:
This matcha leans a little extra "green" tasting. I'll say it is robust, and definitely meets my expectations for culinary grade. I rarely notice the differences between all the matcha powder I have consumed over the years, so unless it is terrible, I always give it 4-5 star ratings. Since this has a more pronounced taste, I tend to add it to smoothies where the flavor is entirely masked. I love how matcha makes me feel, so no matter how it tastes I will consume it. Love the fog lifting effect, the non jittery thrum of energy, and all the other health benefits that this supports. I still drink a cup of coffee in the morning (I'm not a barbarian), but I do then switch to matcha. I dont love it, but I love what it does for me.

This size is nice for use on the go, for travel, office. Otherwise I tend to prefer larger quantities since I go through a lot. I use a lot more than the standard 1-2 tsp serving (usually I use 1-3 TBS) so this 0.7 ounce size is "cute".

I dont rate on price. Matcha is all over the place with pricing, both culinary and ceremonial, and regional difference. So you decide if it is a good price or not. For 6 bucks, I'd add this packet to a tea/caffeine themed food gift. Who doesnt love a thoughtful compilation of consumable products? This is a pleasant looking packet, and would tuck in nicely to a gift basket.

title: rich, tasty ghee with bits of truffle and truffle essence
text:
Smells like and tastes like Black Truffle to me! Gourmet Ghee Co. has several tasty offerings, and they have loads of info on their website if you want to dig further into who they are and what they are about.

This is a plastic container, 12 ounces. I think they used to sell jars, or maybe they still do (but in 9 ounce sizes). So I dont know if they are making a switch to all plastic?

I noticed the familiar, pungent aroma as soon as I peeled back the safety seal. Smells just like expected, and even the flavor is pretty darn good. Some ghee has a more buttery taste, and this one is overtaken by the truffle, which is a good thing. I love seeing the bits of truffle settled along the bottom. Delish as a dip for fresh bread, or to cook my eggs in. Haven't yet made a steak with it, but that is on the list.

Keep in mind that Ghee has a melting point of 76*F. When it is cooler than that, the ghee will be solid. It becomes softer (or becomes a liquid) the higher the temp. THAT is why some people may notice a more granular appearance. It likely has been warmed up (ambient temps) and cooled down a few times. It should not at all affect flavor or cooking.

The flavor to me is spot on. Truffle to me has a slight garlicky flavor to it and a slight earthy flavor. It is something special, and overall I find it pleasing.

Ingredients: pasture raised butter (milk), black truffle, truffle aroma

4.5 stars

title: add these to your holiday cookie plate. Delicious coconut spritz butter cookies!
text:
Mmmm yum. Reminds me of a holiday spritz cookie in both look, mouth feel, and to some degree taste. This has coconut as the main flavor (almond is often used in spritz cookies). It is a coconut shortbread, or butter cookie. It is delicious. I do not equate it at all on any level to biscotti. It melts in mouth, and is just delicious.

Light green (from pandan) with tan cooked edges. Looks homemade. Would make for a nice foodie gift, or set out for a holiday get together. I'm really pleased with these little cookies.

Ingredients: wheat flour. butter, vegetable oil, sugar, oil, egg, coconut powder, pandan flavoring, vanilla flavoring, polydextrose, exulsifier (e481 &471)

title: firm tasty beans, use them for front and center bean dishes, good mouthfeel
text:
Like an extra large navy bean. Similar in size and texture to a lima bean. A good hearty bean with pleasant mouthfeel. Give them loads of time to soak and cook, then add to whatever you want. I dont have specific recipes, but I like adding them to soups and "stewps" (extra thick soups). Nicre in dishes where you want the presence of beans to stand out, not disappear into background

Comes in a plastic tub with snap lid. I think these are excellent quality beans. If you cant find them in store (or dont want to go to the store), these are a perfectly good option. Also nice for simply tucking away into pantry.

title: Flavorful! Multi layered flavor-A good mix of Sweet, Tang, & Spicy. Glaze like- put on everything!!
text:
Kinda sweet, kinda tangy, and has a low key spicy finish. I tried it directly from the jar, and I found it surprisingly tasty. Multiple layers of flavor that also somehow all balance out. I really could keep eating it off the spoon. It has a light glaze vibe about it, yet it clings to proteins. Also had to try some with a sweet potato, and another time with some tempeh. I really imagine it would go well with anything.

For me the stand out feature is the balance of tastes, and the layers of taste. It isn't a single note BBQ sauce. I would totally get this for someone who likes BBQ sauce- perfect as an addition to a foodie gift basket. I dont rate on price, but I do comment. Single bottle is more than I have paid for a bottle of sauce. I would grab the 3 pack for a significant savings if I buy this again. Which I may, it really did/does (I still have some) impress me.

title: pantry staple for all sorts of cooking & baking needs, Lasts forever, delicate flavor
text:
I use rice syrup in recipes that I dont want the floral/fruity taste of honey to come through. This adds plenty of sweet flavor, that is mild tasting. Works great with proteins, and can also be used in sweet desserts. Nice in tea too, though for that I am more apt to grab the honey. Nice option to have on hand for vegan friends. Treat it like a regular sugar in terms of health.

I appreciate the squeeze bottle, so much better than the wide mouth jars I have purchased in the past (less/no mess!).

title: Been drinking FITNE nearly every day for 7 months, love their coffee, frequent repurchase
text:
FULL ingredient list is on back of package, down to percentages of each ingredient, which I included here. Would be good it they simply added a picture of the back of their box to show the ingredients.

Dissolves instantly, tastes delicious made as instructed (120 ml of water, or 4 ounces), or added to other coffee.

I have been drinking FITNE coffee products nearly every single day for at least 7 months now. I really like their coffee. I frequently repurchase, and I always try new stuff when it becomes available. Some I like better than others. This one is toward the top. I would buy this one again. I really also like their [[ASIN:B08WWFVQD1 white kidney bean extract]] variety. Couple bucks cheaper too.

Here is what it is. It is FUNCTIONAL (ie, it has added supplements, typically geared toward weight loss), and instant coffee, usually some creamer, and a sweetener. The preparation is to add it to 4 ounces of water. I have stretched it as much as 6 ounces for some, but it tasted too watery. I find that I can use 6 ounces with THIS variety, and it still tastes good. This is the most "coffee tasting coffee" of the bunch.

That being said, it doesn't have to be your only cup of coffee. I often have this as my 1st cup then have a regular cup of brewed coffee, or I start with a cup of regular coffee and enjoy this as my second cup. I enjoy the flavor, creaminess, and sweetness of this, yet I also really like plain black coffee, hence the two separate cups. Makes for a nice early afternoon "pick me up". Other crazy thing I do? I add a pack TO my coffee for a big cup of delicious coffee that has a little creamer and a little sweetener, along with the added benefit of (in this case) fiber, collagen, L-carnitine, and chromium.

Fiber is about 4grams, and since collagen and protein have a 1:1 ratio, the listed 1.5 grams of protein means that this has 1.5 grams of collagen.

title: neutral tasting, lightly sweet, dissolves well. More delicate in taste over Yacon syrup
text:
Very mild, delicate sweetener. I was expecting a more pronounced flavor more similar to that of Yacon syrup, which tastes mildly like lychee to me. This is more honey like in taste, yet much more toned down and without the floral notes. Overall I think it is lovely.

If you are used to stronger sweeteners, then this may initially taste bland, or not robust enough in sweetness. As you cut back on sugar or strong artificial (or even natural) sweeteners (looking at you, sucralose), then your taste buds will likely pick up on the nuances of this powdered yacon, and the sweetness will strengthen. If you really need a punch of flavor and still want to go the yacon route, try a yacon syrup. Only downside is that it has a more fruity-floral taste (like honey). This powder is more neutral tasting.

title: fresh crunchy slices of freeze dried goodness
text:
These are freeze dried, totally different than dehydrated. Totally different process, totally different end product. I keep an assortment of freeze dried products on hand as they have a long shelf life, and the fruit and vegetable options make for an awesome healthy crunchy snack. If you have never had freeze dried, then know that the finished product makes for a very light, very crispy texture. The usual flavor is toned down, and the natural sweetness is turned up a notch. No added anything. Just fruit slices. For me, taste is same as other freeze dried apples I have had. I suppose some nuances can be detected between apple varieties. Freeze dried is never dense, never chewy. Always easy on teeth. Almost more like compacted dust, in a good way.

Lovely to snack on as is, or use it as a salad topper, oatmeal topper, or as a "chip" to dip in some caramel.

If you are familiar with freeze dried food, then these are as expected. Tastes good, is well packaged. The bags are full of air and seem to keep the crisps from being accidentally smashed. I dont question the quality at all.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. I find it reasonable per bag. Usually I buy individual packs of same size for $1 at local store.

and I dont down rate for country of origin so long as it is listed in the product description. It is made clear in the product pic that it is a product of China. So if you see that, then it wont be any surprise.

I love that they have several other options available- love some freeze dried fruit snacks for low cal noshing on the go or on my couch.

title: Good all around EVOO with an extra punch of color and flavor.
text:
Nice balanced tasting olive oil. I love all sorts of olive oils, and am fortunate that I have an oil tasting store in my area. Because of this I have learned that not all olive oils are the same. I have different ones for different needs. What I like about this oil is that it is very smooth, with a hint of pepper. Has a nice mouth feel. It is light enough to use in nearly any application, yet has enough flavor to be used for dipping bread. I sometimes even take a swig, plain. Good all around EVOO with an extra punch of color and flavor.

My bottles are slightly dented. Doesn't affect taste, quality, or even overall look.

title: Hot with flavor. Very Nice flavor, plenty of heat
text: SPICY! To me anyway. Especially when I dipped my finger in to take a taste straight from the jar, haha. It is nice though. I thought maybe it had something else in it because it was more flavorful than expected for just red pepper.  I like it.

title: no added sugar, no carbs, high protein, good taste, easy on teeth
text:
I like both flavors. I appreciate that this is low cal and low carb. I rely on protein snacks to help take the edge off between meals, or when I am just in the need to chomp on something, but dont want a caloric hit. I keep bags of jerky in my snack basket hanging in the kitchen for this reason. I also appreciate that they include the nutritional info for one serving, and for the whole bag. There are only two servings per bag so doubling the stats would not pose a problem to figure out out, but still.. I like seeing stuff like that. That being said, I usually just grab a couple of pieces, so this is actually a multi serving bag for me.

Soft, chewy, dense. Fairly easy on teeth. Not too salty tasting, but it does have a lot of sodium (like all jerky does), yet potassium levels off set it a bit. No added sugar, no carbs. Just a natural taste and feel. I like it.

title: SWEETENED w/ stevia & monk fruit. Creamy, fairly bland, light natural cocoa taste.
text:
They use the search/traffic direction term "unsweetened" in the title headline description. Misleading! (for shame). So if that is what you are banking on, please know that this IS sweetened. It is sweetened with Stevia AND Monkfruit extract. When I see "unsweetened" I expect it to not have anything added that potentially sweetens it. If they mean that they dont add cane sugar (etc) then say, no sugar added, or sugar free. But unsweetened? that should mean- plain, nada. They do later include the term, "no sugar added". That part is accurate. (Doesn't use any of this terminology on the actual container). Still, downrate for that.

That being said, it isn't a super sweet milk. Good or bad depending on what you want from a chocolate flavored milk. I happen to despise chocolate cow milk (even as a kid), and I still thought it was worth trying it in a non dairy milk. I like hot cocoa, and chocolate smoothies, and some chocolate coffees, so I was curious how this would taste. It is It is fairly bland with a pop of natural cocoa taste. Lightly sweet. Rather pleasant straight from a cup. Creamy, slightly nutty, leans more toward an almond taste. I can totally drink it alone, or add it to smoothies. Definitely best cold. I am not for some nut milks in my coffee (coconut, cashew, oat yes. No on almond milk, and since this reminds me of that, I wont use this pecan milk in my coffee. You do you though).

Overall for a SHELF STABLE product (until opened), it is pretty good. I would get more use out of the Original flavor, so I may give that a try one of these days. But I do like this chocolate one. I like having some shelf stable tucked away in my pantry as I dont often get to the store.

INGREDIENTS:
Filtered Water, Pecan Butter, Cocoa Powder (Processed with Alkali), Natural Flavors, Calcium Carbonate, Tripotassium Citrate, Sunflower Lecithin, Organic Locust Bean Gum, Sea Salt, Gellan Gum, Monkfruit Extract Powder, Stevia Leaf Extract (Reb A). Contains: Tree Nuts (Pecan). This product has been processed on equipment that may process tree nuts, milk, and soy.

title: low collagen (3 grams) but it is a delightful, carbonated, non caffeine drink. Best COLD
text:
I tried their [[ASIN: B09DDFM2ZW variety pack]] which includes an assortment of caffeinated and non caffeinated options. I found that I was reaching for the non caffeinated options in the late afternoon and early evening. So much so that I knew that it would be a repurchase. When this came up as an option to try, I was pleased to see that I could keep my stock replenished with just non caffeinated options. These are pricey, but whatevs.. if you like it, go for it. I like it, I went for it.

Definitely best cold, and as I mentioned in [[ASIN: R27V0RVL092XQQ my review]] for the variety pack, the collagen content is really low (3 grams), but everything else is delightful.

As with the variety pack, and with this.. solid 4 stars

title: easy prep, very good taste & texture, has a comforting vibe to it. Great on cold mornings, evenings
text: I really like this, way more than anticipated. It has such a nice natural pleasing flavor, delicious texture, and a comforting vibe about it. Easy to make, cooks up quickly. I just added kettle boiled water over the cereal and it cooked thoroughly and quickly. I realllly enjoyed this.  However, the first time I had it, I noticed that it did not stick to my ribs, and I was in fact more hungry that I usually am after a period of time. So the next few times I had it, I added in some additional fiber and or fat. Whether it be a glop of peanut butter, or. a heaping spoonful of pumpkin puree, or yogurt, or additional nuts or granola, fruit etc. Basically I use this as the base to an "oats bowl". There are probably other things I can do with this, but right now it has been a nice warm brekky that I have been really enjoying. CRAVING, even. I'd even make a dessert out of it.

title: uplifting, non jittery low key energy, smooth taste- pretty good alone, or add your own flavors
text:
Easy to drink, easy to prepare, smooth, balanced taste. No funky taste. Worth the try!

I think it is pretty good. I dont even like the taste of matcha all that much, but I drink it every day for the benefits, how it makes me feel. So try them all, and they are nearly all the same to me. This "Matcha with Benefits" has additional mushroom powder, MCT, and vitamin d3, all of which I take on a regular basis. Often times I am making a smoothie or other supplement drink that incorporates a variety of mushroom extract powders and matcha (and other stuff).. so it seemed like something I should try.

Glad I did, because this is surprisingly smooth. Just a light, nearly bland flavor with a hint of matcha (good or bad depending on your taste buds). For that, I find it pleasant. Has a very balanced taste that I can actually drink alone. BUT, I usually add some additional goodies to it-- collagen, come liquid creamer or flavored liquid protein, sometimes I add in some sugar free coffee syrup (currently using Chai or pumpkin spice flavoring, because.. cool fall weather)-- and then it becomes an extra lovely mid day treat.

Provides that great low key strum of energy- non jittery, just awake and alive feeling.

This is a matcha to consider if you dont like matcha but want to drink it, and/ or dont know how to prepare it.

title: lovely strong ginger flavor, good balance of sweet, can taste honey, very easy to prepare
text:
I love LOVE ginger, and have been buying products of this ilk for several years. It simply isn't the same as using ginger tea bags where the ginger never seems to come through. ALSO this is an INSTANT drink. I dont want to mess with tea bags and jars of honey all the time. This is easy, convenient, tasty, and can use it anywhere, anytime.

This HOTTA Instant Ginger with Honey has a robust ginger flavor, and that is exactly what I want. This has some added honey and sugar, and the instant dissolving makes it super easy to use, and versatile. I can drink it alone, or add some matcha, or add it to other tea (especially CHAI), or any other drink (including club soda). Anything I want some honey and ginger in. It is easy to pack one in my purse for on the go use, or to enjoy at home. Very comforting. Just lovely.

I love the bite of ginger. That is really what I look for in these instant drinks. Does it it have the bite and heat of ginger? and this does. It has a good balance of sweet from sugar and honey. I definitely taste honey.

For a little less ginger, and a little more sweet, [[ASIN: B08Z85CNHV ginger crystals]] are a good option

Prepare each packet with 5 ounces of hot water (feel free to make adjustments)

Each packet provides 50 calories, zero fat, zero cholesterol, 5 mg sodium, 14 grams of total carbs (5 grams total sugar, 4 added), 0 protein.

Provides 35% DV of thiamine, robroflavin, and vitamin b6

Received Oct 2021
MFG Aug 11 2021
Best By date of Aug 11 2023

at $8.99 I will likely buy more.

title: non cloying, pleasantly sweet read to use cherry syrup, versatile use beyond shaved ice
text:
This is a ready to use syrup. I like Hypothermias products, and the ready to use is pretty good for home use as well as commercial use. I prefer their Black Cherry concentrate (unsweetened) as the cherry taste is a little more robust, but this is pretty good too. Sweetened with sugar, not high fructose corn syrup, so seems to taste less cloying than others.

As mentioned, not just for shaved ice and slushies. Try it in smoothies, coffee, tea, pop, frosting, baking, as a regular syrup or added to other syrups and toppings for added flavor. I'll be trying this in a cherry scone recipe.

It's a big gallon size. You may want to buy a pump for it depending on your use of it. I know they make smaller bottles too. I find either option to be reasonably priced, especially when using for use in drinks-- way more affordable than a brand marketed for that purpose when the ingredients are very similar.

title: really good flavor, texture makes them stick to teeth very unpleasantly
text:
I think the taste is good. I would buy these again if it weren't for the texture. Does a fair job of mimicking swedish fish. The downside to these is the texture. They stick terribly to teeth. Not a soft sticky where it just easily rinses away. This is the type of stickiness where I bite down, and my upper and lower teeth are stuck together!! Rather scary for a moment. Then once I can release my teeth from the gummy stronghold, I find that bits of gummy are caught all up in every crevice. Taking a sip of water does not loosen the bits. I need to hand pick them out, or allow my tongue work them out. And it isnt a quick thing.

I really want to eat these. It is disheartening as I otherwise like the flavor.

title: WOW. ultra smooth, delicate, not at all grassy or harsh. Hint of natural sweetness, SO VERY GOOD
text:
Outstanding!

NOT at all grassy. It is SO SMOOTH, and delicate. It is the best matcha I have had-- and I have been drinking matcha on and off for 15 years, with most of my consumption and purchases within the last two years. I have purchased and tried many brands of culinary and ceremonial, and I thought they were pretty much all the same (I figured some people just had better taste buds than I). I have pretty much rated them all the same so long as the product description and what I got lined up. The nuances not having significant enough impact on my taste buds that I cared what brand, what style, or what price point I went with. All the same to me. THIS STANDS OUT ABOVE THE REST. So if you can afford it, or are looking for a good brand to add to a tea themed gift basket, then I recommend this.

It is so smooth, gentle, and naturally sweet that I can actually drink it hot, plain. I otherwise dislike matcha, but love the benefits. This is divine! I dont have a matcha whisk as I usually just make a latte or smoothie with it. So I used my blender cup with 6 ounces of kettle boiled water and a heaping teaspoon of this powder. Lovely green, good foam, and just a very easy to drink taste. It doesn't bite back.

Still not one to just drink straight matcha, I then added it back to my blending cup, added some heavy cream and a little sweetener. WHat a delight! Even when I do this with all my other matcha brands, I can still taste that "special" matcha taste coming through (some variation but usually little grassy, little bitter, little "green"). But with THIS? It is so smooth, creamy, extra pleasant and easy to drink. I am so stoked to find a really good matcha. Price is way up there, so I would say this is what you want for actual cup of hot matcha. Or as a nice treat. This is all just my opinion, so take it for that.. but my impressions are authentic and I now understand the true difference between ceremonial and culinary. It seems like this is what ceremonial is supposed to taste like. Curious what others think.

I love the small tin it comes in. I will be holding onto it for reuse with other matcha. Nice for on the go.

title: firm dense bar, mild taste, easy to eat. Low level sweet
text:
I had ordered a box of French Toast flavor and instead received a box of [[ASIN: B09H3QTW9K Chocolate Peanut Butter]] flavor. SO my review here is for such. Given my favorable review for the PB, I imagine the French Toast would have been quite good. Ah well, so here are my observations of the PB variety:

Firm dense bar with mild chew. Pops of creaminess. Little bits of crunch. Noticeable chocolate and peanut butter taste with very mild sweetness and no off flavoring from proteins used. About as natural tasting as can be for a product of this ilk.

Ingredients and nutrition profile are pretty good.

I was kinda hoping for something that resembled the picture of a peanut butter cup on the packaging, but it's a long, flat, dense bar. Totally fine, but that image sure drew me in. The taste is surprisingly good. I have significantly reduced my sugar intake, so everything tastes almost too sweet to me, especially when formulas include non sugar sweeteners. This is refreshingly not all that sweet. Actually, those who are looking for or prefer extra sweet wont get that from this.

I dont think they are delicious, nor are they anything close to a peanut butter cup (probably a good thing), but it is a decent option for times I want a little something that isnt too sweet, or just something to fill the gap between meals. I'm not going to ever want to eat more than one.

Nice burst of fiber at 7 grams per bar. If new to chicory root fiber, be mindful that that ingredient can increase gassiness at first.

title: delicious, delicate wafer cracker is good alone, or holds up to soft cheese. "Buttery". YUM
text:
A delicate tasty crisp that can withstand a smear of gently applied soft cheese. Wonderful tasting on its own too--Actually I appreciate the taste of them even more when I consume them plain. The look of them reminds me of a wafer thin pizzella. Size wise, it is just a little larger than a slice of pepperoni (like the kind that come pre sliced in a shelf stable bag at any grocer), and just a hair thinner. Had I some dip, hummus, babaganoush, or other soft accoutrement, I would have dove into that with these. I just had some soft cheeses, so I used that (and some pepperoni). It all worked.

I think the taste and texture is outstanding. They somehow have a buttery taste with a hint of chick pea. They are not the typical hard, shiny rice cracker that is usually the standard gluten free offering. Easily some of the best crackers I have had. If I had my druthers, these would be just a little more robust, or maybe just a little thicker. Packaging is such that once opened, you will want to slide into another baggy to help keep it fresh. Though if putting out as a spread for a gathering, I am sure there will be no left overs anyway.

Serving size is 9 crackers, 70 calories, and because I find these very easy to eat alone, consuming the whole package could easily be done.

Ingredients: Chickpea Flour, Rice Flour, Potato Starch, Coconut Oil, Salt, Sunflower Lecithin

These are the original, and I see they have a slew of other flavor varieties, all of which pique my interest. I wouldn't hesitate to add these to a foodie themed gift, (gluten free or not).. they are just a unique, delightful wafer cracker.

title: versatile pantry staple- for quick gravies, adding flavor to soups, stews, sauces, even veggies
text:
Good product to have on hand. I was never into gravies as I only made them on the rare occasion I had a pan of drippings, but lately I have been craving gravy on everything. So I bought a few packets of gravy mix. Once those ran out, I looked for a bulk item. I find that these are a really good sized container for all my gravy needs. Easy to store. Easy to make. Tastes pretty good. I now keep brown gravy, mushroom gravy, and poultry gravy on hand. For mashed potatoes, french fries, stews, meats. I have even added a little to soups for added flavor and thickening, and even just a little to a pot of vegetables. Something about a hint of gravy coating really adds a ton of flavor.

Pantry staple for me!

title: delicious perfect texture can of dolmades
text:
I love love love Dolmades. These are so good. I am tickled that they can be purchased in large cans. I think this is more for restaurant or for larger gatherings on a platter. But my love of dolmades will allow me to work through these in no time. Price for this can is a little above some other offerings, but the quality is good to me. Also, it is a bargain compared to the smaller single cans I buy.

Yum yum yum-- tangy marinade, soft but still chewy leaves, perfect rice texture. I often eat these as a snack, or light lunch. Just always a delight to my taste buds.

title: lovely, neutral, non cloying sweet taste as expected from isomalt oligosaccharide syrup
text:
Probably the most attractive bottle of oligo rice syrup I have ever had. It was amusing to see this nice looking box with rope handle arrive. Big bottle, at 42 ounces. I usually only ever find tiny bottles, or jars. Amber colored. L Good thing this stuff lasts forever.

If you dont already know, it is a nice sweet syrup that is much less cloying than corn syrups or honey. It is not as sweet as sugar, so be mindful that you dont overcompensate by using more than necessary. I find that this syrup to be very easy to work into main dishes (especially proteins) and it suitable for baking or adding to beverages--just know that it has a neutral low key sweet taste.

Excellent quality, no issues.

title: Pleasant festive seasonal vibe, Lovely Chai variant, worth trying! gift worthy too!
text:
This holiday blend is a little different than my usual Chai tea in that it uses roasted green tea instead of black tea, and it adds in cocoa nibs. Chai formulas often differ, but for the most part they will still have that expected Chai taste profile. This has that, plus a little more.

INGREDIENTS: Hojicha roasted green tea from Japan, cacao nibs, cardamom, ginger root, cassia, black peppercorns, natural chocolate flavor, cloves, cardamom oil.

While I dont exactly consider myself a tea drinker, my wide assortment would have anyone thinking otherwise. When it comes to tea, I really like Chai. It appeals to me all fall and winter long- the colder temps just beg for a nice mug of it. I keep a selection of caffeinated and decaffeinated on hand depending on the time I want it. Sometimes I drink it black, sometimes I love the added taste that cream and a little sweetener adds to chai tea. THIS Steven Smith Teamaker Ho Ho Hoji Chai tea is quite pleasant.

I can tell that it isn't black tea as this just has a more mild, delicate base. Very smooth, gentle, pleasing. The roasted green tea is superb in this blend. Smells good. I can pick up on the notes of chocolate- it comes through in the finish. The other spices bring together the anticipated Chai taste. The one flavor marker that I do not pick up on is "stroopwafel" (caramel), and there is nothing in it that would highlight that flavor. Now, pair this with a side of stroopwafel? yes!

Lightly caffeinated, sol be mindful of when you drink it if you are at all sensitive.

I have tried it prepared three ways. I consumed it straight-- just two bags (I always use two bags of any tea I make, habit.. preference), I have tried it with just half n half, and I have enjoyed it with cream and a little sweetener. All good. The Chai flavor comes through on any option.

So overall I think it is worth the try. It is a quality tea, and I have no problem recommending it. In fact, I would also recommend as part of a tea themed gift. It is nicely packaged (attractive flip top card board box), individually wrapped and labeled sachets (they all have ingredients listed and how to prepare.. so this could be parted out/shared, or a combo of teas could be put together if you find other teas of interest).

As a Chai drinker, and as one impressed with this tea.. I looked to see if they had a black tea version, and they do [[ASIN:B00JGB6M9W Masala Chai #33]]

Quality, presentation, taste, and level of enjoyment warrants this a 5 star rating from me. If I had one spot of contention, it is the use of the descriptor "stroopwafel" as that connotes caramel which this does not achieve. I am really overall ok with that, but anyone latching onto that expectation may be disappointed. If we did half ratings, I would go with 4.5 stars. But I sure like it a whole lot more that 4 stars. So that is where we are at. Thanks for reading.

title: good price, taste, texture, smell. Easy to make, great w/ cream cheese frosting. NOT eggy
text:
One of the better Keto muffin mixes I have had. Actually I like this brand, as I have had other stuff by them. I have had some bad ones, so I am super stoked that this makes a decent muffin. The whole bag makes 12 small muffins. I am not entirely sure of the nutrition information factors in nutrition from the eggs and oil that you need to add or not. I am thinking not? Wish they made it more clear. For that, a star off rating.

The level of pumpkin spice is moderate. Easy enough to shake in some extra pumpkin spice if ya need it stronger (I do). I baked them in my [[ASIN:B09BYY97F3 silicone cup cake liners]], and the muffins released from the liners just fine.

Some keto muffins are eggy. These are not. They are moist but not "eggy" or spongy. I like that. That being said, I am tempted to reduce the egg further, or add in some flax or chia to offset the egg use and add more nutrition. I am not "keto", but I have greatly reduced my sugar intake, so many carbs are still (literally) on my plate.

Overall, I find the ingredients to be good, taste to be good, texture to be good, very easy to make, no weird extra ingredients needed, price to be good (not that I rate on that), and I will likely buy these again, especially since I want to make in a bread style next time. I highly recommend a keto cream cheese frosting- that takes these to a lovely dessert level., YUM

example of muffins I did not like (because of taste, texture, complexity... also, check out the price): [[ASIN:B099NR4W92 Yuck muffins]] (their cake was worse). Hence why I dont rate on price, as I personally think this LaKanto brand to be way more reasonable than some I have tried.

title: good flavor- gentle green with mild natural sweetness, lovely in hot or iced lattes & smoothies
text:
It's good. I was concerned after seeing a few pics that look extra watery. I went ahead and prepared it according to directions for a hot latte. I used a "heaping teaspoon" with 2 ounces of hot water. It stirred up pretty well. I dont have a whisk for matcha tea, so I usually run it through a hand mixer or in a blender cup. Looks deep green, creamy, lightly foamy. Has that mild green taste with natural hint of sweet. Tastes as expected. I then added about another two ounces of water for 4 ounces total (my heaping teaspoon was piled high). Still perfect. So I dont know what the user did to make a watery translucent preparation. I then proceeded with making it into an iced latte by adding a bunch of ice and topping it off heavily with unsweetened vanilla almond milk, for a 16 ounce cup of frothy cool deliciousness.

So yeh, good stuff. No issues.

title: firm dense bar, hint of sweet, good balance of chocolate & peanut butter taste, bits of crunch
text:
Firm dense bar with mild chew. Pops of creaminess. Little bits of crunch. Noticeable chocolate and peanut butter taste with very mild sweetness and no off flavoring from proteins used. About as natural tasting as can be for a product of this ilk.

Ingredients and nutrition profile are pretty good.

I was kinda hoping for something that resembled the picture of a peanut butter cup on the packaging, but it's a long, flat, dense bar. Totally fine, but that image sure drew me in. The taste is surprisingly good. I have significantly reduced my sugar intake, so everything tastes almost too sweet to me, especially when formulas include non sugar sweeteners. This is refreshingly not all that sweet. Actually, those who are looking for or prefer extra sweet wont get that from this.

I dont think they are delicious, nor are they anything close to a peanut butter cup (probably a good thing), but it is a decent option for times I want a little something that isnt too sweet, or just something to fill the gap between meals. I'm not going to ever want to eat more than one.

Nice burst of fiber at 7 grams per bar. If new to chicory root fiber, be mindful that that ingredient can increase gassiness at first.

title: chicory & dandelion make for a passible coffee swap, instant dissolve, good taste & mouth feel
text:
Lovely hot or cold. Dissolves instantly. Use more for a stronger coffee vibe, or use less for more of a tea like taste and mouth feel.

There are two varieties offered on this page, Chicory with Raspberry and Chicory with Dandelion. I have the latter. I am very familiar with coffee alternatives that use chicory and [[ASIN:B000SMN0DO dandelion]]. I like the taste of both, and I like the price on this Chicoraya brand a lot better. Chicory and Dandelion just work so well together as a coffee alternative. Dont expect a full swap, but it is so easy to drink that if it is passible when trying to reduce or eliminate caffeine while still maintaining the routine. I also like single ingredient [[ASIN:B09C4RNGSB Nucaf instant chicory]]

I usually prefer my coffee black, and this too tastes good "black". It also works really well as the base for creamer, coffee syrups, collagen powder, mushroom powder etc. I make some lovely afternoon and evening hot drinks. And I have also had it over ice.

I keep mornings for my real coffee.

title: good pantry addition, not the exact same as fresh but no surprises there. Has good uses
text:
It doesn't reconstitute to the same texture as fresh, but it works pretty well for use in recipes that are made better by sour cream (look at you mashed potatoes! Does fairly well in dips and as a Mexican food topper). Use less water, let set in fridge. If you use too much water or dont let it set then it will be runny and sad.

I aim to buy more to stock my longer term pantry with.

title: pleasant crunch, not sticky, easy on teeth, generous serving size, great w/ coffee or tea
text:
Small, pleasant tasting ginger cookie with a decent crunchy snap. Crunchy, not sticky. Not hard on the teeth. Pleasant tasting with good mouth feel. I would not know that these are gluten free. Small cookies, but there are 8 to a serving. Nice to grab one for a quick sweet tooth fix, or grab a handful and enjoy with some coffee or tea.

I know gluten-free can be tricky, and I think they pulled of a good product with this recipe. I dont rate on price (why choose to buy it or try it when the price is obvious). I do comment, and I know that gluten free products are often much pricier than their gluten laden counter part. Now add in it being more of a boutique product of a specific flavor.. and well ya got a price tag to go with it. If it looks good to you, I think it is worth the try. Might be nice to add to a foodie gift basket.

I rarely find a super strong ginger snap, at least not since the 80s. These definitely taste like ginger snap, but they aren't as intense as I would like (but none are). Since they are within the realm of reasonable expectation, and overall I find them quite enjoyable, and that I can afford $7 for a nice treat, I have no issue giving these a full 5 star rating.

title: very good taste, generous sizing, but expiry just a couple weeks away :(
text:
They include a picture of the nutrition facts. Take a look before purchase as it should not be a shock that it contains a goodly amount of added sugar. But to be fair, this is a huge block of Royal Chikki, and the serving size is huge. With seven servings, the serving size is generous.

If you dont know what this is, imagine a brittle. It is full of nuts (almonds, pistachios, cashews), and spices (saffron, lemon), ghee, and is held together by a sugary syrupy base. It is very good, and exactly as I expected it to taste. Sweet with a gentle lemon and cardamom finish

I am glad that the serving size is generous, as I am not prepared to budget in 500+ calories for a serving. Even breaking off a good sized piece will likely only be around 200 calories. Totally doable. Nice for when you want a little something sweet after dinner.

Unfortunately the manufacture date to the expiration date is just 6 months. I received this just a couple of weeks before the expiration date. I am sure it will be fine for awhile, but this needs to be figured out. Because of this it isnt gift worthy.

title: delicious flavor, multi purpose, excellent pantry staple. Try on ice cream, or in coffee!
text:
EXCELLENT taste. I am already a huge fan of medjool dates, and so this is right up my ally for taste and sweetness level. It isn't the first medjool date syrup I have tried, and it is all pretty much the same to me. Very good multi purpose sweetener/syrup.

It kind of reminds me of blackstrap molasses, but a little sweeter and milder. I could use these interchangeably. My first use of this was on low sugar vanilla ice cream. I knew then I was in love with it. I have tried it off the spoon, mixed in with coffee. I have used it on pancakes, and I will likely use it on waffles next time I make them. So this is a highly versatile item for me, and is likely a repurchase. YUM.

When I first tried medjool date syrup, I had no idea that it has a lower glycemic level. I usually avoid sugars and syrups, but this is giving me options I didnt even know I had. Sometimes I make real food desserts using pulverized medjool dates, and these medjool date syrups definitely save me loads of time and effort as I no longer need to use the food processer, or clean up. Big win for me all around.

I highly recommend giving it a try. Medjool date syrup instantly became a pantry staple

title: got a box of peanut butter cookies instead of chocolate chip. Very good, though!
text:
Well, I ordered a box of peanut butter cookies and a box of chocolate chip. I received two boxes of peanut butter cookies. I really liked those (5 stars), so not a problem for me. But I cant review these chocolate chip cookies. So I will just add what I had written for the other. Star reduction.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
I really like these. It really comes down to personal taste. I have tried so many Keto cookies and other desserts over the past year. I am not following a keto diet, but I have greatly reduced my sugar intake. I still gobble down pizza, pasta, & crackers but I have put the donuts, cookies, and cake down. I haven't had a taste for that, and I have reduced my weight by 45 lbs and counting. Sometimes I DO want a little something, and so that is where Keto desserts come in. I can eat a little or a lot, and it doesnt trigger my brain to need more of it, no frenzy ensues.

Some stuff is bad, some have been surprisingly excellent. I find these to be the latter. The peanut butter cookies just taste like peanut butter cookies to me. Crunchy, peanut-y, and not overly sweet. I dont even notice any particular kind of sweetener taste.

I really think they are good, and my empty bag is proof of it. I'll consider these again. I have added them to my list of keto desserts that I like and will definitely recommend to others.

1 serving (half the bag) is plenty for an after dinner snack, but I kept going and ate the whole thing. It wasn't just the taste, but the mouth feel. I usually prefer chewy, but the crunch on these were quite satisfying.

Comes well packaged- might make nice addition to a keto themed foodie gift basket.

title: nice peppermint flavor, great for drinks, better than a sugar free coffee syrup as its is minty
text:
Tasted straight from the bottle, it has a "natural" minty taste. This is not an extract, or a concentrate where one would expire if they tried it directly lol. This really reminds me more of an non alcoholic schnapps. Or a liquified mint candy. It will work well in hot cocoa, coffee, smoothies, frosting, other recipes where the amount of liquid wont disrupt the integrity of the texture. Also works good for those with a heavy hand (ever accidentally add too much peppermint extract to a cup of cocoa.. ugh!). Adding too much wont be an issue, but using too little might be. So I wouldn't use it as a 1:1 swap for extract. It's a big 7 ounce bottle so I automatically knew it wouldn't be extract level mint.

My use: in hot cocoa and choco peppermint smoothies. I tried sugar free syrups, but the mint is barely there and the sweetness level is way too much. I want the mint without having to deal with using an extract. This is a really good peppermint for this use. If I want added sweet then I have control over it.

5 stars because this is exactly what I was looking for and needed. I just added their Orange flavor to my cart because I love orange chocolate hot cocoa (and using orange extract is just as tricky).

PS:
Propylene glycol is a synthetic, colorless, odorless, tasteless, food safe liquid that belongs to the same chemical class as alcohol. It should not be confused with the toxic substance ethylene glycol (anti freeze).

title: fancy firm delicate sardines, beautiful tins, great for a foodie gift basket
text:
Sardine party! Party of one. These are DELICIOUS! I like sardines and really no one else I know likes them, so I set myself up a plate of fancy crackers and thin crust bread, and have a little party on my own. I need to do this more often because they are a fantastic snack. Even works well in place of or in addition to can of tuna if you are looking for a way to incorporate them more into your life.

I like most brands, but prefer the one that use smaller sardines. Those tend to be more pricy. I dont rate on price anyway, but I know the price range for sardines is easily anywhere from $1 to $7 per 3-4 ounce can. The kind I tend to buy are in the $3-4 range. This is above that, but I dont fault it. Sardines are regional too, so price can reflect that. As well as being "wild caught". I know that I will never eat a $1 can of sardines again (bumblebee- all mush--bleh).

I dont eat enough of them. I normally buy [[ASIN: B09BZQGX5D King Oscar]] or [[ASIN:B01FR2EPHE Season Brand]], but I will gladly try a more fancy brand on occasion. These fit that. They are good, are a smaller size, tin is packed, and they are flavored. I like any that are packed in oil best (seasoned or not). The tomato based ones aren't as exciting to me, but they are still good. ALL of these are good. I need more!

Since I have a couple of brands that are a bit less pricy, I am not sure if I would buy these again for me.

HOWEVER, the quality is fantastic, the flavors are good, wild caught, firm, small, and the tins are so nice to look at. I was proud of my little stack of sardines that I didnt want to open them! I would definitely consider these as part of a foodie gift basket.

title: sweet and spicy, great with proteins, yet works pretty well with starches and vegetables
text: A little more sweet than spicy, which I like. I like it paired best with proteins over vegetables or starches, but it is worth the try. I tried it on some plain bacon, and that was awesome. I was using the bacon in a sandwich and wanted to add a little extra something. This worked. My next try will be on some baked acorn squash.

title: lightly tangy, mildly spicy, gentle herbaceous flavors make for nice marinade
text: Creamy Malai & Herb is lightly tangy, lightly spicy, and lightly creamy. It does nicely as a marinade for chicken. I pick up on notes of ginger, lime, cardamom. Fenugreek is well balanced among the other spices. The overall formula creates a mild taste with a bit of tang and heat. I think those with more discerning taste buds will be better able to pick up on the nuances of flavor. It's lovely.

title: 3.5 stars  Very good flavor, lovey soft texture. Watch out for sugar load per serving
text:
Sweet, spicy tasty with a soft lightly chewy texture. Very easy on the teeth. A lot of added sugar, so be mindful if watching your sugar intake. Two, 1 ounce servings per bag. Very easy to eat it all at once.

Very tasty, wish it had less sugar.

title: loads of flavor with nice kick of heat
text:
Definitely has that Indian cuisine level of flavor. I know everyone has their own perception of what is "hot". I think both are hot, but not too intense. It has all the flavor with a kick of heat. Some "hot" ends up eliminating flavor which is useless to me. I like flavor. I can handle some heat. These are closer to the top end of what I can handle but I am very pleased that there is actual taste from spices coming through.

I think the red is hotter than the green, yet both are super tasty. Nice combo that I would buy again

title: nicely ground flax seeds, add to smoothies, use as egg replacer (binder) in recipes
text: Good sized amount in this jar. I keep it in fridge to help maintain freshness. Works well in my smoothies- adds a little nutrition and bulk, with no flavor. Nice to have on hand as an egg replacer in recipes. I am not vegan, but I prefer to keep eggs for eating rather than sacrificing for use as a binder. Flax is one of the items I keep on hand for that use in baking. Works well.

title: very easy to make, great addition to my pantry
text:
What was I thinking buying 6 lbs of gravy (*SMH*, lol). This will last me a long time, and I know it will stay fresh for a long time- there is nothing to go bad, and the container is durable with a good lid. The price is much more reasonable than small bottles or individual packs.

It can be used for so much beyond just gravy- use it to flavor up some roasts, add a little to soups, add to other dishes that benefit from flavor boost and some creaminess. And of course for use as a gravy. I sometimes like a little dish of gravy alongside some fries. I simply do not make enough meat to be able to make a fresh gravy every time I want it. Also, I dont have that ambition.

Anyway, I like it-- very easy to make, no fuss, really no effort. Tasty enough for all my gravy needs!

title: mild flavor, but nice trio of seasonal flavors
text:
Jeez, they aren't that bad. These Skinny Syrups use sucralose as the non sugar sweetener, so if you have digestive problems from certain types of sweeteners then know what you are buying before you purchase. Their KETO options use a different type of non sugar sweetener.

This trio is $15. I think that is a fair price for three 12.7 ounce bottles. AND free shipping from Amazon (w prime). When ordering from their website, you have to spend nearly $60 to get free shipping. Fine for big orders, but not when I want just a bottle or two. The pricing for the 24 ounce bottles are $7 on their website so that's $0.29 per ounce (not including shipping), and this is $0.39 an ounce. Very reasonable. Larger bottles can be purchased for increased savings per ounce.

TASTE? If you have used Jordon Skinny Syrups before, then you know how they tend to be more sweet than flavor. Particularly in the seasonal flavors. So pumpkin flavor is not strong, but it's good. Comes through stronger depending on what it is being used with (stronger with oats than coffee for example). I find their fruit flavors to be much more robust, so hopefully they can do a better job with pumpkin at some point. The KETO options are better still.

Although I would prefer a much stronger pumpkin flavor, I am still enamored with their syrups. I never used sweeteners in my coffee (just drink black), but I do enjoy all things pumpkin spice related, so I thought I would try out these syrups. I originally bought a big pack off their website, then decided to buy this smaller Trio as a part of a coffee themed gift.

It provides some flavor and sweetness that I normally wouldn't have. I have been able to make some pleasant hot beverages. I sometimes add a little extra pumpkin pie spice, but its nice that the flavor base is there with these syrups. I have been able to make some smoothies taste much more pleasant with the addition of these syrups. You know how it can be.. protein powders or meal replacement powders can just taste weird, add in some other supplements and ya got a big cup of meh. I add in a little of any of these syrups, and my taste buds are much happier.

Despite not having a strong flavor (any of these), I think the overall flavor is easy-- I do not taste a chemically taste. If I did I wouldnt bother with these syrups. But I keep buying them, so apparently I like them.

Overall, 4 stars.

title: lovely vanilla aroma, taste. Like sweetened extract. Use for visual effect
text:
This Madagascar Vanilla bean paste is nice for use in desserts where you want to be able to see the flecks of vanilla beans. Add it to homemade icecream, frappes, smoothies, custards, frostings. I use extract in batters. Each have their own purpose, and the ratio is the same.

texture: thicker than extract, more like runny syrup.

Keep in mind that this paste includes sugar (often used as a binder, adds sweetness). Not all do.

title: Rice Flour, New Mexico Chiles, Chili Powder, Cumin, Oregano, Turmeric
text:
For low FODMAP followers, this chili seasoning blends omits two of the greatest offenders: onion and garlic. Takes the guessing and worry from what's in it. So many blends incorporate these spices or they incorporate generic terminology that makes it a challenge to know what is truly in it.

So I think this is fine if you want to have a pre made blend, otherwise just using something from your spice cabinet should work if you know for sure what is in it.

This can certainly be a tasty blend for NON fodmap protocol followers. Chilis, cumin, oregano & turmeric make for a good addition to any taco, chili, popcorn, potato, veg topper, or added into a creamy base for a dip.

Rice Flour, New Mexico Chiles, Chili Powder, Cumin, Oregano, Turmeric

title: use for frothing, or just add into coffee.. but has slight off taste, doesnt lighten coffee
text:
I dont often froth my cream, but I tried it with this almond powder and it works well for that. Nice head of froth for an at home cappuccino.

As for use as a spoon in creamer, it works ok for that. Doesn't lighten my coffee much, adds a lot of almond flavor, and something else that isn't quite working for me in my coffee. So you must like that taste in order to like this.

bag says to store in fridge after use. I dont have the real estate for that, so I'm going to chance that it lasts well enough sitting in a cupboard.

3.5 stars. Overall I think it is "ok"

title: lovely tart and sweet taste, as good as all other brands I have had. Small bag will keep long time
text:
I like Golden Berries. I buy a bag every once in awhile. They last me a long time because they are not something I can eat a lot of at once. Usually just a small handful is the most I can handle. I like the pop of tart flavor with a sweet finish. I know that this food can be used in a variety of recipes, but just noshing on them straight from the bag is my preferred method.

They are as fresh and delicious as any other brand I have had. The difference here is that this is a small bag, that I actually find highly appealing since I dont go through much at once. Also a nice way to try them if you aren't sure if you'll like them. The pressure zipped bag seals well.

title: slightly bland but still tasty variety pack. Five 1 oz servings per bag
