text: Tasty mix, although the flavors aren't real noticeable. But I like them. Has a light crunch, easy on teeth. 5 servings per pack so be mindful of this if county calories as it is so easy to eat half the bag (or more).

title: Not clear calorie info! 278? 556? Heavy whey protein taste, ok texture. Choco is BAD BAD
text:
WTF. This is a tiny brownie. Each brownie is considered to have 2 servings. It says ON the packaging, 2 servings per package. Then it says, 50 gram serving. I weighed the browning in package, and it just reached 45 grams. SO WHICH IS IT? No matter the answer, given the confusion I would NOT recommend these. If they can't get the info straight, I just wont be able to trust the product.

So if it is "two servings" in a single pack, then DANG.. This isn't a big muffin. It is a 4 bite muffin, er "brownie". 4 bites. 556 calories!!! (278 per serving, 2 "servings" per package). NO ONE is breaking it in half and saving it for another day. I dont care how healthy it is, I am NOT eating 1/3 to 1/4 of a days calories in a few bites especially since it isn't all that good.

If they what they mean by "2 servings per container" is 2 packs are in this order, then that means the labeling is ridiculous, as it should never ever be labeled as such.

THEN, the fact that the product says per 50 gram serving, and the brownie actually only weighs 42-45 grams (they differ), then how does that affect the nutritional info. For those doing KETO, I am sure you want to know the specifics and accuracy. For anyone else just counting calories or sodium, that is a big deal too.

Anyway, so what is accurate?

If the calories for one pack (one brownie) is reaching 600 cals, then I would legit rather have a nutritionally void donut from a bakery for same calories or less. Or a King sized candy bar. At least I would enjoy it. That would be "worth" it as these are NOT even good. Overall I would rather do without, or try some other option. They have that weird tangy whey protein taste that is really off putting. Then add in that there is one small brownie and label it as TWO servings.. that ticks me off. Nearly 600 calories. GOOD GRIEF.

If it is "just" 278 per brownie, then it is more reasonable so long as all other info is accurate. But the taste of the chocolate is sour and horrible (and dry), the blondie is ok but still has weird smell and protein taste (and oily), and the red is best of all (I normally dislike red cakes) as it is bland, sweet, not too weird tasting, good mouth feel despite being a bit oily. Just not a good product no matter how i look at it.

Do better, Bett3r. At least make it known explicitly on the product page that each tiny muffin/brownie has 2 servings. ALSO? make this information more explicit on the packaging as well. These came loose in a shipping box, not a retail container. The wrapper is very hard to read. The spot that says TWO SERVINGS is faded out compared to other info. Sleazy.

Still interested? here are a few more observations:

I am reviewing the variety pack. There are:
--2 Chocolate. TERRIBAD. This is so bad. Just bad. Both taste and texture is horrifying. Dont.
--2 Red velvet. Best of the bunch. Actually quite good. Mild taste, lightly sweet. No weird flavor.
--2 Blondie. Not too shabby, but not exactly good either. Very bland. More similar to the Red velvet in that it has a pleasant moist texture, not too sweet, no strong intense weird taste-- but I can smell it. I took a bite of one, but wont finish it, and I will be tossing the other.

Chocolate is dry, the other two are oily.

I HATE WASTING FOOD. But here I am.

star rating in order as listed above 1, 4, 3 (more like 2.5)

I will keep the other red velvet cake flavor for when I feel like splurging, but the rest are not good enough in flavor, with the chocolate being HORRIBLE. Bad.. so bad..

Want something to satisfy the taste buds? At least these calories are tasty. Here are some of my go-to:

[[ASIN:B08WHWHCJ5 Gourmet Keto Snacks - Healthy Edible Cookie Dough]]
[[ASIN:B094TB7ZM9 EAT DIFFERENT Smart Cookies]]
[[ASIN:B091M8YBXT Kadabra Keto Chocolate Chip Cookies]]
[[ASIN:B08VN1RD9Y Highkey Vanilla Wafers]]
[[ASIN:B097Z4HNYK CRUNCHY keto peanut butter cookies]]

And these [[ASIN:B097HY7F6V Eat Me Guilt Free Cotton Candy Protein-Packed Brownie ]] , which I would have liked if it weren't so dry, but at least calories are in check, is a big portion, and if they make improvements, I would consider again. I gave those a 1 star, and I recommend it over these "brownies". Their whey protein doesnt taste as tangy and weird as this one. And I am not blowing my calorie allotment.

title: delicious mini cookies, coconut forward, be mindful of portion, nice texture, 4.5 stars
text:
A very good cookie. Serving size is just two small cookies. Not unreasonable, just really have to keep in mind what I am consuming. I have to portion out the two as I could easily eat half the bag or more. I usually buy the keto cookies where the nutrition lists the amount of calories for a serving size, or for the whole bag. And so when I brought this bag to my couch for an evening of noshing, I was glad I took a closer look at the serving size and calories. 2 cookies, 140 calories. There are 5 servings in the bag. I could easily eat a couple of servings. They really are small. But the ingredients are really good, the taste and texture is quite good (good as a cookie, not just a keto cookie), and is loaded with some good fat, fiber, and protein. So eat these when your sweet tooth can be satisfied with a small amount, and you want a quality product. Or you have a big calorie budget to work with. These are quite good!

Taste wise, you must like coconut (I do) as this is the most prominent flavor. I taste a hint of raspberry.
Mouth feel- they are neither crumbly or chewy. More like a slightly soft leaning shortbread. Thick but small cookies.

Overall very good. I had also bought a creamy keto dessert product that it is only now as I review this that I realize that the cookies and that cream is the same brand. So for something healthy, spectacularly sweet, and similar nutrition profile, check out [[ASIN:B08WHWHCJ5 Healthy Edible Cookie Dough]]. Will make your taste buds sing!

title: level up your snack game w/ sweet, delicious, creamy snack. Make taste buds sing!
text:
This is ridiculously good. Buy it, love it, you're welcome :)

It reminds me of coconut manna (coconut concentrate), which is thick, creamy, and naturally slightly sweet. If you like that, then you will so love this. You must like coconut as that flavor leans forward in this flavor profile. That being said, OMG this is delicious.

It is sweet, has a lovely creamy mouth feel, sparks happiness in my taste buds, and no odd off flavors despite incorporating protein powder. It is simply GOOD. Not just "good as far as Keto goes".. it is just GOOD. So flippin yummy. I also bought their [[ASIN:B094TB7ZM9 Smart Cookies]] (didnt realize it was same brand!), and thought those were fantastic.

As with any product that contains coconut products, it will get soft at room temp. So depending on what sort of texture you want- super creamy, or firmed up like cookie dough, or even hardened up so it has to melt in your mouth.. then either let it sit out in a warm environment, or toss it in the fridge.

I haven't come up with any clever ways to eat this. I absolutely been just eating it off the spoon. I make a point to get my spoonful, then put the jar away before consuming this sweet delight. I fear that I wont stop. It's healthy, but still loaded with calories. Delicious, sweet calories.

OH, it just occurred to me as I write this review that I am totally going to use this a a frosting for some keto snack cakes that I have (dry, blah, needs help).

This is called birthday cake flavor, and often that flavor is weird, but this is amazing. So good. So pricy though (but I dont rate on price.. you decide if it fits your budget or not). I did not expect to love this.

Ingredients: Blanched Almond Butter, Coconut Butter, Allulose, Soluble Tapioca Fiber, Coconut Oil, Pea Protein Isolate, Keto Sprinkles, Monk Fruit, Salt, vanilla

title: Perfectly fine matcha for a moderate price ($9.43 per ounce, not $19..99 an ounce). Lattes! coffee!
text:
They are confused. A 2.12 ounce packet for $19.99 makes it $9.43 per ounce, not $19.99 an ounce. If they change that, then maybe people would freak out less. This price is not out of the norm for matcha. However, there are various price points, so you look around and decide what is best for your budget. That being said,

All matcha powder tastes the same to me. It is one of the few things that I tend to buy based on price. I have purchased super cheap, and wildly expensive (because I can, and because I am curious), and it really comes down to what you need it for. Using it in smoothies, lattes, or other mixed ingredient drinks or foods? Then totally go for the cheap stuff. Using it as "ceremonial" tea, well then the nuances in flavor may be enough to warrant a more indulgent purchase. But even then, it may not matter.

This matcha is fine. It doesn't stand out above or below most I have tried. I think it is good. I like it in hot lattes, so for that I say it is more mild, smooth, and naturally sweet compared to some. I can even MIX IT WITH COFFEE and it still tastes good.. But really one must have discerning taste buds to really know and appreciate the difference. Or know and dislike the difference LOL

I do find that the benefit of matcha and how it makes me feel is something no price tag can compete with. I love the low key steady energy, the reduced cravings for all foods (especially sweets), the antioxidant load, and the reasonable price for such a multi tasking food product (no matter how pricey, it is still offering a lot of benefit for low amount).

The small packet size is nice for travel, for keeping at work, for adding to a food/drink themed gift, or for simply trying it.

My 4.5 stars (well, 5 star) rating is based on my perception of its quality in comparison to the dozens of brands I have tried over the years. I buy matcha frequently, and I find no issue with this. How good or bad it is is totally subjective. I may like it, you may not. I dont rate on price, but I have made my comment regarding that it is within a moderate price range. My packet did not come with an incentive for a free bag. Should I down rate because of that? LOL

title: Lychee flavor is spot on, overall has a slight bite (too much citric acid?), overall good
text:
Carbonated water with a light essence. It is not a sweetened drink in any capacity. Any mild sweetness is naturally occurring from the lychee puree, This contains just carbonated water, lychee puree, and citric acid. It has a bite, and it is a little stronger than other carbonated waters of this ilk, but the fruit flavor is stronger- so thats a win. I think the LYCHEE is spot on. They really nailed it with this flavor. I love lychee, and I am happy to taste natural lychee. If the slight bite from the citric acid could be reduced, then I think this would be a perfect drink.

I DO NOT rate on price (well, I rate on it when it is in the "rate feature" section, but not overall star rating). I may comment, but I see no point in rating based on it. I knew how much it was going into it, and it isn't beyond the range of similar drinks. I consider it a treat. Maybe I would buy more and more often if the price point was lower, but I wont down rate since I willingly saw how much it cost before purchase. $2.49 a can for something like this is something I would expect as a single can purchase in a store. I'd expect better price for a 12 pack.

title: crunchy perfection!! tasty, low cal, low carb, high fiber, no added sugar, good protein DELISH!
text:
Very satisfying. I happen to like "fiber cookies", and with these having the added bagel seasoning makes them a snack to look forward to. I LOVE these paired with some cream cheese, or other soft cheese. I buy those low cal [[ASIN: B07PJZDX7V soft cheese wedges]]. A great snack to have at the kitchen sink, or to snuggle on the couch with. I enjoy them plain, too. Or I add some tahini, or some hummus. Or as a vehickle for chicken, tuna, or egg salad. Lots of options.

SO GOOD. And yes, they definitely have the "everything bagel" seasoning on them.

Serving size is two crackers. Each cracker being the size of a playing card- but thicker. Crisp and crunchy, but easier on teeth than some wasa crackers.

I really like these, and will be getting more when time comes.

They are perfect to me.

title: balanced taste- little sweet, little chocolatey, shortbread texture, has slight coolness/erythritol
text:
Not bad. Not the best, but definitely not the worst. I have been working through them with ease, so that is promising.

I have purchased and tried so many brands of "keto" cookies. I am not following a specific diet, but I do aim to reduce my sugar consumption. I dont always need to eat cookies, but sometimes I want something sweet. I also keep stuff like this on hand to ward off temptation when my husband sits next to me with a box of fresh donuts (ugh). So yeh, I keep a variety of options on hand. Out of all I have ever tried, very few tastes great to e. But here are my favorites of the bunch:

--Tastes nearly like a home made, regular cookie: [[ASIN: B091M8YBXT Kadabra Chocolate Chip]],
--Nice for coconut lovers: [[ASIN: B08FP3M8DC Sweetwell Coconut]].
--Great natural vanilla taste: [[ASIN: B08VN1RD9Y Highkey Keto vanilla]]

These Lakanto cookies are decent. And they cost less (at $1.70 per ounce) than several brands I have tried. They taste better after I have had a couple, then they are more pleasant. WHile they are "sweetened with monk fruit" they are also sweetened with erythritol and has a hint of coolness with the first few bites. Smaller than a quarter, they have a shortbread texture, light chocolate chip taste, and not too overbearing in anything else. I have had some keto cookies where I just could not veg out on my couch and enjoy them. They worked better crushed over yogurt, smoothies, healthy ice cream.

These I can snack on. The nutritional info includes the amount of cals (etc) per serving, AND for the whole bag. I really appreciate that. There is no added sugar, and carbs are about where they typically are on a product like this. You decided if it fits onto your nutrient count. I like products like this because if I am really in the mood to nosh, I dont have to worry about exploding my calorie intake. I would normally eat at least 3 donuts in a sitting (easily 400 calories a donut-1200 calories, so matter what I ate all day I would ruin it after dinner with uncontrollable donut/cookie/cake consumption. Products like these keep me in check, even if I ate the whole bag-260 cals)

I do not rate on price because we all have different budgets and values surrounding where we put our money. I may comment on price, but I wont up rate or down rate based on that. The pricing on these are within the range of market norms. The three that I linked to cost more per ounce than this. And so, I aim to focus on quality, taste, and most importantly how well the product description and actual product line up. The hallmarks of making a decision.

title: naturally sweet, light caramel-vanilla-butterscotch taste, endless possibility. High nutrition!
text:
Has a berry aroma, but a caramel flavor. Butterscotch? vanilla? something along those lines. I totally dig it! Slightly sweet too! It DOES work well in coffee, oats, and smoothies. I am intrigued by the caramel vanilla taste. SO interesting, and I can see incorporating this into some low cal, low carb, high nutrition dessert options. It isn't super strong, but it is a nice flavor profile considering it is from a fruit. Bonus? loads of nutrients.

Next time I make [[ASIN: B07VVQ7XH4 ice cream]], I am going to add it into the recipe. I see a video posted for lucuma mousse, and that looks delish. So glad I tried this, it is highly likely a repurchase from me. Also, I have had other items from this brand, all have been top notch quality (which led me to try this).

title: "Thyme, basil, fennel, savory, Rosemary, lavender, and other spices." Fennel forward tasting
text:
For adding magic to a dish, I love this [[ASIN:B09394CFF7Herbs De Provence Seasoning]]. When it comes to Gramercy spices, I have not been as impressed as they make it sound like I should be. This blend is good, but extra heavy on the fennel. NOT all Herbs de Provence have fennel (one I linked to does not), and this has significant amount, so it easily makes the dish taste like licorice. As for lavender? It might be in there, but I do not see it (my preferred brand has noticeable bits).

The ingredient list is off putting. Thyme, basil, fennel, savory, Rosemary, lavender, and other spices.

What is "savory" as a listed spice, and why not list the "other spices". They do that with all their spices it seems.

While I typically use my favorite Herbs De Provence in just about anything (gives a little extra something- tends to be my secret ingredient), I find this blend to be best used in stews and hearty soups. They recommend using it with lentil soup, and I agree-- it seems to pair nicely with green lentils. Not bad with eggs. On point in a beef stew.

Overall-- OK, but not a repurchase. I have a brand I prefer, and this isnt it.

title: very mild blend, but perfectly tasty for oil & bread dip, white pizza, over potatoes, veggies
text:
As one greatly familiar with Za'atar, I immediately noticed how mild this blend is. I tried it directly off my finger, and found it quite pleasant but lacking that kick that I am familiar with with other brands. Not all za'atar spice blends include sumac, but this one does. It is all around MILD tasting.

I DO like it though. I prefer other brands for use directly in recipes, where the taste needs to be robust and have enough oomgh to come through, but I like this a lot for use mixed with oil for use with bread, pita, naan dip, or white pizza. I actually like this better than my other Zaa'tar for this purpose because of the more mild flavor. Holds up well as a quick coating for starchy potatoes and vegetables. Beyond that, I can't see using it recipes.

This blend contains salt (not overly done), and "other spices"-- why not just list them?

Try this if you like Za'atar but would like a more mild blend. This isn't going to be enough if you need the more pungent hit of thyme and sumace that other blends offer. But this mixed with olive oil then swipe some bread through it? yum!

3.5 stars

title: 3.5 stars. High fiber, protein per serving, but also high sodium. Is best baked. Light on lemon
text:
Love the fiber (5 grams per 2 TBS serving), protein (4 grams), and low carb (6 grams). But the sodium content is a bit stout for my preference (460 mg). Taste is light, breading texture is dense but light when baked in oven. It is heavier and darker when fried. I prefer baking.

Overall, I dont think it's bad, but that being said I don't love it. I am familiar with low carb breading and they do ok, it's just obviously not the same as regular bread crumbs--so, dont expect it to?. It works, it's ok. I know there are times I really want a breading but I dont want the carb load. I make sacrifices. I dont always want grilled chicken. Sometime I will have regular panko crumbs, and sometimes I further cut out some carbs by using alternatives. Options are good, and not everyone uses stuff like this for "keto", some people watch carbs and sugar for other health reasons. And so.. I think this is a fair alternative.

I have had their spent grain flours before, and find that I still need a little regular flour to make it work. But as a breading, it does what it needs to. I just dont think there is enough lemon pepper flavor, but you may think differently.

3.5 stars. Not sure if I like it enough for 4 stars. I will revise if I find I like it more and more.

title: like peanut butter and jelly, but tahini
text: I love love love tahini, but almost never pair it with sweet tastes. Having it combined with grape flavor reminds me of peanut butter and jelly. I've tried it off the spoon (sweet!), on crackers (ok!), but drizzled over ice cream, yogurt, or oatmeal has been good. Maybe I will try it as a dipping sauce for sliced apples, or other fruit. It isn't really my thing, but I see nothing wrong with the product. Ingredients: grape syrup, tahini

title: Works well in ADDITION to other flours. Egg replacer, add nutrition to everything
text:
It's very good, very fresh, and exactly as anticipated. It is finer than some brands of regular ground chia, but it is still highly textured. However, this works fine for the usual stuff- in bread recipes (as an add in, not as the base), for making chia crackers, for sprinkling on oats, yogurt, muffins. Add to smoothies, pancakes, home made fruit spreads, as a protein coating, add into meatballs, meatloaf, etc.

As with flax, chia can be used as a egg replacer in recipes. I dont recall exact ratio, but it is basically a some chia with some water, let sit (has some gelling properties), and then it can be used where eggs are called in. I will often do this not because I am vegan, but because I would rather not waste an egg in a recipe. Flax or chia (or a combo!) allow me to add nutrition to recipes and save some money I prefer to keep my eggs when possible as a food item.

I like the packaging. Pressure zipped durable paper bag.

title: creamy good flavor, use a mixer/blender/shaker for smooth milk, perfect for my daily smoothy
text:
Distributed from USA, but is a product of Russia. I dont have a problem with that, but that info needs to be clarified in the product listing otherwise looks like it says that country of origin is USA. That being said,

This big bag of oat milk powder is quite good. 3 TBS to 7-8 ounces warm water. I recommend using a mixer, blender, or shaker cup as trying to spoon mix it will only result in clumps. I find that my my [[ASIN:B0972S5VG7 Vortex smoothie blender bottle]] is perfect for this. Then I can just add in my protein powder and other supplements all at once. I have also made a larger amount and stored it in a mason jar. I give it a good swirl or shake before using it if it has been sitting for awhile.

Taste is good. Tastes as it should.. like oat milk. Nice creamy mouth feel. Works anywhere that you would normally use oat milk. I REALLY like having the powder. I should have been buying this well before now because it is really nice to have it on hand when I dont have pre made cartons on hand. I dont get to the store often and I go through a lot of non dairy milk for my daily smoothies. When I do go to the store I am usually picking up 3-4 large cartons. That takes up space in fridge. I have purchased shelf stable, but this bag takes up even less space. Anyway, it is a very helpful option.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. I find that this is priced better over other options at just over $9 per pound (even less when purchases in larger amounts).

title: Lifts the morning fog. Smooth, dark leaning medium, fine powder for espresso, nice black
text:
Smooth, robust medium roast. It is as bold in flavor as can be without being a dark roast. The slightly reddish color, and the wee hint of tang keeps it at the medium roast level. As someone who prefers dark roasts, this is very good for medium roast. SO I would say this is a dark leaning medium. Like, butted up right against dark. Knockin' on the door.

This is a brick of fine grind- very powder like. Perfect for espresso brewing, or pour overs. I haven't tried it in my regular brewer yet. I tend to go for my favorite [[ASIN: B08SBSSSJC POUR OVER]]

I drink my coffee black. Dark roasts never need anything, but lighter roasts usually need "help" through use of creamer, which can tone down bitter, grassy, green, bright notes. I find that this medium roast does not have any of those off putting notes, and I can drink this black just fine. As I drink it i feel the fog lift, and that makes me happy.

title: lovely aroma, strong flavor, must have spice for baking pantry
text:
Good, strong, fragrant cassia cinnamon. Can't go wrong with any Natruen spices. I have several, and have been pleased with them all. I happen to be getting low on cinnamon. My nearly empty container of Tones brand is the same size as this. It will surely last me a long time.

Sweet, pungent, spicy aroma taste and smell that makes cinnamon the delightful spice that it is. Currently fall season, so it is one of my go to spices for adding to coffee, smoothies, oat meal, yogurt. Trying to stay away from baking cookies, lol.. but maybe I can use it in a healthier dessert recipe.

The cap can be twisted entirely off, or the top can be twisted to either small sprinkle openings, larger shake opening, or a small measuring spoon/pour opening.

Acquired 09/2021 with Lot date of 02/2021. The expiry is 2 years from manufacture date.

title: healthy puffed quinoa for anyone, added flavors tone down quinoa taste, great snack
text:
I really like puffed quinoa. I use different shapes and sizes for a variety of snacking and food topping needs (yogurt, ice cream, salads, oat meal, or even as a cereal). Helps me get my nosh on without adding in sugar or too many calories. Each piece of this style is a good size for little and large fingers a like.

This variety pack tastes within the realm of what I am used to, but slightly more bland. Reminds me more of a cheerio than quinoa. That being said, you will need to like quinoa to like puffed quinoa. That simple. Quinoa has a slightly nutty, slightly bitter taste (in a good way) and having it in dried form doesn't change that. It tastes like quinoa but in dry puffed form.

I happen to like it a lot. That taste is toned down significantly with the addition of whatever flavor you ordered (I have the variety pack). I dont necessarily taste the added flavor (dragon fruit, sweet potato, or beet); really just a slightly sweet taste and a more bland quinoa taste (compared to plain puffed quinoa). Likely good for those demanding a more bland palate. It's good. I would rather that the nutritional info be just for one bag, or just two servings. This info is listed as having 4 servings per bag. Not bad, just more inconvenient. I normally dont eat/use more than 1/2-1 cup at a time anyway. It's one of those food products where a little goes a long way (good since I have a huge non stop appetite).

So yeh, overall likely best suited for kids, but is also perfectly fine for adults. I haven't decided if it is a repurchase or not. I do like the flavors, and I like the smaller bags. I also like that they offer a variety pack in a set of 3 (or 12) so one can try out a smaller portion before deciding. Nice touch.

Here are some of the puffed quinoa that I like: small balls of [[ASIN: B07WGJF8LW Plain Puffed Quinoa]], or large balls of [[ASIN: B07V2PFMBQ Yacon Sweetened Quinoa Puffs]], or this one by also by Awsum snacks that is similar in size and texture to the puffed quinoa I'm reviewing, [[ASIN: B0926V5SC9 Puffed Quinoa with Chia]]

title: another tasty Fitne product, good flavor, small serving size
text:
Functional hot cocoa! Natural chocolatey taste, easy to mix. Tasty treat. Small portion.

I am quite a fan of Fitne products. I am a regular buyer of their [[ASIN:B08WWFVQD1 Fitne 3 in 1 functional instant coffee packets]] , among others. All good. Despite my continual repurchase, I give them all a 4 star rating, including this cocoa because they all have directions to use just 4 ounces of water which is really a tease. With the coffee option, I find that those could use a little more coffee taste-- but I just add a packet to my regular coffee, which works out well. And it allows for a larger cup of coffee. So good! But with this, unless I am adding it to another cup of cocoa, or add in some unsweetened cocoa powder, the serving size is really small. Again, a tease. But oh so tasty!

When it comes to this cocoa, 4 ounces is exactly where I need it in order for it to taste right. I have tried 6 ounces, and it watered it down a lot. Even so, I really like it. It is easy to make, is super smooth, and has a good real chocolatey taste, lightly sweet, has added fiber (5 grams!), and my beloved white kidney bean extract (legit works for me, nice support supplement).

title: nutty, delicious. Thin, runny- and so tasty. Eat off spoon, squirt in mouth on the go!!
text:
ahhhh so good, so so good. I really like tahini of all viscosity- thin and runny, thick and sludgy. I find thin is easier to work with and has greater application, but thick has it's place too; just depends on what I am making. This Tavor tahini is more of a liquid, and it comes in a squirt bottle. It begs to be used on salads, as a dip, or even in hummus with no need for added oil. It is so perfectly tasty that I kept eating it off the spoon. It's nutty and bright, not bitter to me. I think it is lovely, and will enjoy every drop of it. So good, soo so good. Mmmm

Try it in a smoothie (I've been adding it to a pumpkin smoothie), or take it on the go-- just squirt in mouth for a tasty boost of fat and protein.

title: Low collagen (3 grams) per can, tasty assortment of flavors, mix of low (and no) caffeine
text:
I think these are pretty good. Nice fizz, intriguing assortment of ingredients, and the variety of flavors (includes some with caffeine, some without) is impressive. I would not buy these directly for the collagen. There really isn't much in each can, but it is a nice way to top off your other collagen supplements. Most collagen powders have 10-12 grams per serving. This in comparison is "3000 mg" (3 grams). I tend to see the lower amounts in boutique drinks and formulas. They highlight the collagen (and always list it in milligrams so it looks more impressive) but there is never very much compared to other basic products.

That being said, go for it. All the other "super herbs and antioxidants" make this a neat drink. No information beyond that though. The ingredients for each are listed among the product pictures. A little collagen is bonus. Low calorie, good taste (taste best cold from fridge or over ice), not overly sweet. I can taste a hint of something (not sure what, and I dont think it is the collagen) that is odd but not bad. I notice it with first sip, then it just disappears.

--As a collagen drink (based on amount of collagen)? 2 stars
--As a fun, tasty, fizzy, refreshing, assorted drink supplement? 5 stars
--Flavor variety? 5 stars
--Including a combo of lightly caffeinated and non caffeinated? 5 stars
--included info so I know how much "super herbs and antioxidants" are in each can? 1 star. Nothing (save for the vitamin C amount)

I dont rate on price. But at current price, these are $3.75 per can. Not terrible, but pushes the high end for me. I consider it as an occasional drink treat that I would find in a single can in a drugstore. As a multi pack, I would think it would be closer to $3 per can. The amount of collagen does not make up for it (I would need to drink 4 cans to equal my typical 1 scoop serving of any collagen peptide powder). Since we all have different budgets, this is the reason why I dont factor price into rating.

title: tasty as is, or makes a great base for other add ins (try pumpkin puree!)
text:
Tasty (but expensive) pasta. I made up both boxes at once, since these are just 7.5 ounces each (a regular sized box of pasta is 12-16 ounces). The pasta is made from white rice flour and quinoa flour. It cooks well and has excellent taste and texture. It very much reminds me of regular semolina pasta (in a good way). The flavor packet is quite tasty.

So basically boil the noodles, drain, add butter (or alternative), milk (or alternative), and seasoning packet. The flavor is robust, and salty, yet not over done. From here, you can eat as is, or modify it to your liking. Although I made it all at once, I made it 4 ways.

1. Just used butter alternative and reserved pasta water (I did not have compatible milk). This totally worked out well. "Butter" added depth of flavor and the pasta water thickened it and added a creamy texture.

2. In a side pan, I cooked up some onions, garlic, sliced baby portabella mushrooms, and sliced Brussels sprouts. Added in some salt and pepper, then tossed some with the pasta.

3. Because it is fall, and all things pumpkin are given a go in my house, I decided to add a generous amount of plain pumpkin puree to the pasta. This amped up the creamy factor, added a light seasonal flavor, and of course adds fiber and other nutrients. I added extra splash of the reserved pasta water. OMG this was so good. After that, I decided to just add all the side vegetables to the pot of pasta flavored with the packet, with the added pumpkin puree. So good.

4. Ricotta. I plated my pasta & veggies, then added a glop of whole milk ricotta cheese on top. So very good.

5.. One last thing.. I had also cooked up some chicken,. That would pair well with this. I didnt end up adding any to the pasta even though that was my intention. The vegetables I added and the ricotta cheese just made it perfect as is.

Ok, one last thought.. swap out milk for sour cream, and you have a more stroganoff flavor.

But if you want to just eat it plain, it is very good as is. I thought it was a tad salty, but when I looked at the nutritional info, it isnt terrible for a boxed item (340-470 mg per serving), but it could be less.

I dont rate on price, but I doubt this will be a repurchase at $8 per 7.5 ounce box. I think the price had been higher. It is good, and maybe I would consider it as part of a foodie gift basket, but not as a staple in my pantry. Maybe occasional treat.

4.5 stars (but better than 4 so I will hit 5 stars)

title: Easy to drink beet/mushroom/coffee blend. Mixes seamlessly w/ hot or cold liquid
text:
Beets, Mushrooms, Coffee. It's an instant drink that is hassle free, as it easily blends into hot or cold liquids. I have made it several ways over several days, and it has been easy to incorporate into my mornings. I already take mushroom supplements, and I have taken beet supplements on and off for years. "On" because it is good for high blood pressure (and performance, etc), "Off" because as much as I like beets, it can be hard to add into anything without the flavor taking over. SO, when it came to trying this, I was indeed skeptical.

First notice: beet taste is hidden. I dont think I could say that this has beets in it if I didnt know, ya know?
Aroma: slightly nutty. I can smell coffee. I can smell.. something else. Likely the confluence of all ingredients.

Taste: It tastes like coffee. Plus a little something in the background. It is within the range of normal for me. It's palatable. Lightly bitter if I use too much powder. I make a coffee smoothie of the sort every day, which includes mushroom powder. So now I use this instead.

--I have had a cup using 1.5 scoop of powder to 8 ounces of water.
--I have also simply added it to another cup of coffee (be mindful of caffeine content)
--I have used it in my hot or cold coffee "smoothies" where I have coffee, mushroom, collagen powder, super food creamer, protein powder or liquid protein drink. I add this in, and it totally disappears.

Either option is good. Although I have been drinking it daily, I am not sure if it is a repurchase. I think this product will appeal most to those who already like their products and are looking for additional support. Or are looking for all in one product. Great for travel, on the go, for pre/post workout.

ONLY CONCERN:
Info on bag is different than info on the product page, which is different than what is on their website.
On my bag there is no mention of how much beet or mushroom. On this page, it mentions an amount, but it also mentions other ingredients not listed on my package. Caffeine listed here and on my bag says 90 mg (but says 75 on webpage). So yeh, there is that. I will include a picture of my bag.

overall: 3.5-4 stars

title: gorgeous taste, amazing smell, whole peppercorn fresh ground is the best
text:
I love black pepper- whole peppercorns that need to be fresh ground. I avoid the pre-ground, powdered stuff, but they have that available on this page too if that is more your thing. Fresh ground though? that is pure bliss in terms of aroma and taste. Yum yum. Definitely a must have for nearly everything I eat. Same goes for my husband, so we end up going through a lot of pepper. A lot.

Thing is, I really can't tell the difference between brands. I Just buy what is available. Maybe if I had them side by side. Once in a great while I will get one that packs a little more heat, but otherwise they are all the same to me. Price on this is much more reasonable over some well known brand names.

That being said, this is good stuff. I have tried their white pepper too, and that is great. All fresh, vibrant, tasty, high quality, no issues.

title: very easy to make, just 1/3 c mix & 1/4c milk of choice. Sweet, needs nothing else
text:
I have the Almond & Chia option. The pancakes are very easy to make. Directions are super simple and accurate: Just stir together 1/3 cup mix, and 1/4c milk (non dairy works or a liquid protein drink such as [[ASIN: B003FDC2I2 Orgain Vanilla]] works too). That amount makes two small, reasonable sized pancakes. I prefer to cook them in a [[ASIN: B08TN2TF86 AEWHALE non stick skillet]] using the egg griddle option. Just makes for perfect thickness pancakes, evenly cooked.

They're good, really quite good. Nothing beats a white flour pancake, but I find these quite yummy. Great taste, texture. BUT they're sweet. The sugar comes from Jaggery which is an unrefined brown sugar, and it is second on the ingredient list--so yeh, it's notably sweet. I find it sweet enough to eat plain- no syrup or anything else needed, but I did try it with some low glycemic [[ASIN: B08LWTD5XN Yacon Syrup]] which was good. I can make up a couple of these pancakes and head out the door, eating by hand. I've even made them when I wanted a sweet-ish snack. They are pretty healthy overall.

I'm pleasantly pleased and impressed by this mix. Product description should not say "0 sugar". That is misleading. It does contain sugar. Star off rating for that.

title: creamy, robust natural pumpkin spice taste, I use 2 TBS per 12 ounce coffee
text:
I like it a lot. I am stoked that I can actually taste the pumpkin spice flavor, and my 5 stars is primarily based on that. My coffee tastes undoubtedly like Pumpkin Spice. YUM! Creamy, hint of sweet. Loads of spice!

As with the other Laird Alohoa OatMac superfood creamers, I find that I need double to the suggested amount. Their nutrition facts state that this has 8 ounce bag has 114 (3/4 tsp) servings, OR 32 (1TBS) servings. Their recommended amount is 1 TBS to 12 ounces of coffee. I will tell you that no matter what brand I use, and certainly this this brand too.. that I always need 2 full Tablespoons for 10-12 ounces of coffee. So for me, this halves the servings per container from 32 to 16. But that's my preference, you may be fine with 1tbs.

I tend to drink my coffee black--nothing added-- but I also enjoy a creamy coffee. Liquid creamer is more my style, but I do love a good powdered creamer if only because I dont have to store it in my fridge. I have liked all the Laird powder creamers I have tried (taste and healthy aspect). And since we have just landed in autumn season, that means pumpkin spice for me. So.. I REALLY like this. But I think I could grab one of their other varieties and sprinkle in pumpkin pie seasoning and it would work too.

Just be mindful that while it isnt exactly sweet, it does have 2 grams of added sugar per Tbs.

I find that it mixes just fine. I spoon some in, then stir until it dissolves.

As with their others, I give this 5 stars. If we could do half stars, I would do 4.5. I like it more than 4 stars for sure.

title: tasty, convenient, easy to use shiitake mushroom powder-for cooking & supplementing
text:
I go through a lot of mushroom powder. I find that it adds great depth of flavor to a variety of dishes, also it is healthy. I also take a variety of mushroom supplements, so I just try to get mushrooms anyway that I can as much as I can. When it comes to the powders labeled for cooking, I find that the price point is all over the place- likely depends on the mushrooms used. When it comes to flavor, shiitake is excellent.

I have been quite pleased with MicroIngredients products both in quality, taste, performance, and pricing. I will definitely keep on buying this Shiitake mushroom powder, as I find it is the prefect flavor for various culinary adventures, even basic ones like meatloaf and gravies. I find it easier to use than dried mushrooms, and definitely better priced and convenient over fresh. So yeh, this is a really good addition to my pantry (and smoothie cupboard).

title: aromatic, delicious. No problems!
text: Looks good, tastes good, smells good. Lovely addition to my variety of spices I keep on hand. Love all sorts of peppercorns. I keep a grinder of white, a grinder of black, and I have a grinder with a mix (sometimes I buy a mix, sometimes I make my own). I love white peppercorns added into a recipe more so than a finishing spice. Just such a unique flavor that is a must have in my pantry. Yum!

title: SO yummy for French fries, homemade chips, dips, rubs, baked potato, popped corn (& chili!)
text:
Mild, balanced chili seasoning--that tastes like prepared chili, not just the seasoning. Smells like chili seasoning. If there were a scratch and sniff sticker (I'm showing my age,lol) for chili, it would smell like this. It is a good seasoning for those who want a quick prep of chili flavor, or want something better tasting than what is usually offered in a pre mix packet. Also really nice (and my preference for using this) for adding a little chili flavor to something-- like popcorn, home made chips, french fries, baked potatoes, other vegetable fries (totally need to try this on turnip fries), or added to a creamy base as a dip. Perhaps as a rub? Or of course, as flavor base to a pot of chili. I think it would do well for making chili dog sauce, when you want the flavor but not necessarily the meat or beans (or heck, add in meat and beans).

Why are the actual ingredients not listed on this page?
Anyway, here is what this container contains:
INGREDIENTS:
Chili powder (chili peppers, cumin, salt, oregano, garlic), Salt, Masa Harina (corn flour), Cumin, Garlic, Onion, Red bell pepper

200 mg sodium per 1 tsp serving (50 servings per container). I'd prefer to see it listed as per TBS (especially since they provide a recipe that includes using 3 tablespoons, which is 9 tsp).

For my use, I will still put together my own seasonings to make flavor base for chili-- I can better control the salt. But, this is very tasty, and I am likely to buy it again for use as a topping for foods I want to have a chili flavor. It really does taste more like a prepared chili taste, if that makes sense. It's salty, but it is really tasty. I can dip my finger in and have a taste of it plain. If you do use for actual chili, then know that this is a middle of road level of spiciness. Not hot, but not bland. Definitely salty. Has a hint of sweet. Lovely meaty cumin flavor. I think you would do fine with this as is, or in addition to other seasonings. I like that it includes a simple recipe on the lid.

Acquired 09/2021 with expiration of 09/16/2022

4.5 stars (they should include the full ingredient list on the product page)

but such good flavor.. 5 stars. I would buy this again, and I would consider adding it to a food themed gift basket (I do a lot of consumable gifts for Christmas and other events-- who doesnt like to eat ? :) )

title: Added punch of flavor. More oomph. Great zesty peppercorn, smells so good
text:
Normally all black pepper is nearly the same to me. I buy it regularly because we add it to everything. EVERYTHING. Not pre ground powder, no no. Gotta have full peppercorn that requires grinding. That's an entirely different world of flavor and aroma.

My husband was the first the notice the extra bite of heat. I can say that this has a bit more punch than nearly all the other brands I have purchased. Not too far out there, just a little more oomph. Good stuff.

title: 4.5 stars, quality product. I use about double for cup of coffee, good taste, mixes easy
text:
The labeling includes info for 3/4 tsp (227 servings) as well as for 1 TBS (65 servings). You will likely use the latter, and if you do, then this is closer to 30-40 servings. But here is a quick run down for each:

--3/4 tsp has 10 calories, 0g fat, 0 mg cholesterol, 0 mg sodium, 1 gram carbs (0 fiber, 1 gram added sugar), 0g protein. 20 mg calcium

--1TBS has 30 calories, 1 g fat, 0 cholesterol, 5 mg sodium, 5 grams Carbs (0 fiber, 2 grams added sugar), 1g protein. 60mg calcium, 10 mg potassium

I needed closer to 2 servings for it to lighten up my coffee and make it taste cream. Admittedly I make very dark coffee. Even so, just be mindful if you are counting carbs or looking to reduce sugar. Although it does't have a lot.. you know how it can add up. My usual black coffee goes from having 0 sugar to 4 grams when I use this (as I use 2 Tbs). They do offer an unsweetened version (sans sugar, sans mushroom extract) [[ASIN:B0971V9JBS Unweetened Superfood Creamer]]

My coffee of choice is strong, dark, bold, black-- unsweetened, uncreamed. YET, once in awhile I go for something different. Or I get a little creative on my second cup of coffee after my initial preferred black cup. I happen to really like liquid oat creamer by [[ASIN:B086PJTNDK Oatsome]], and decided that this powdered oat creamer by Laird is worth the try. I... like it! I love that it doesnt take up any room in my fridge. I do find myself using more than the recommended amount in order to get that creamy taste. I use about 2 TBS for 10 ounces of coffee. Oops.

Anyway, I am also a huge fan of incorporating mushroom supplements into my coffee (hence my "creative" second cup of coffee, as I tend to use it to stuff a bunch of supplements in). This creamer doesnt say how much mushroom extract is in here, so I just consider it a bonus amount not as my sole means of ingesting mushroom extract. The addition of mushroom may also lend to why it doesn't lighten as much with a small amount of creamer. Not sure. I will be trying their [[ASIN: B09D44GJD6 Pumpkin Spice Creamer]] version soon (because, its fall and I must have all the pumpkin spice things) so I'll plan to add a note about my experience on that when the time comes.

It seems to blend just fine in with my coffee. I just spoon some in and stir. I dont notice clumps. I like the slight foam that forms (then goes away).

I think it is a quality product, tastes pretty good, and considering that it isnt actually cream-- I think it does pretty good job. Torn between 4 & 5 star rating. I am inclined to go 5 for the quality.4.5 if I could.

I do like this. It has piqued my interest on their other offerings.

title: lovely red lentils for curries, soups. Naturally soft nearly creamy texture. Yum!
text:
Big bag of red lentils. Red lentils vary in color, and it is simply a natural variation and not a matter of quality. They can range from yellowish gold to orange to actual red. These lean a little more golden once cooked. Red lentils are best for soups, stews, and dishes where the lentils just blend in, rather than stand out in terms of taste and texture. Think of creamy dishes, smooth dishes. Red lentils take on a more mashed texture. Great for creating a semi chunky semi smooth/creamy soup.

Red lentils just naturally cook up softer, hence why they are often the lentil of choice in curries, and thickening up soups. They move to the background. Use green or brown lentils when you want to maintain firmness and shape, as well as have a more pronounced taste and mouth texture. Good for dishes where the lentil is the star of the show.

Love me some lentils. I seem to not enough of them, and I am stoked to add this to my lentil collection. YUM

title: legit high quality ceremonial grade matcha from Japan. Stands out over others
text:
I go through a lot of matcha, both ceremonial grade and culinary grade. I usually find very little difference between the various brands I have tried. This is the first time that I could tell not only that it is indeed ceremonial grade, but that it just tastes all around better than most. I usually just drink my matcha added into smoothies, or mask it with more flavorful ingredients--so the acutal flavor isn't a big deal to me. But this one is nice because it isnt as green or bitter as most.. I almost never drink it hot, but I could drink this hot. I have made up a cup and it whisks kinda frothy. I still need sweetener and sometimes creamer, but this is just overall quite nice.

I just noticed the price. Ok, so if you are in the market for a high quality ceremonial grade matcha, this is legit. Matcha is all over the place in pricing, and since I find it nearly all the same it is one of the few products that I go for cheap, bargain pricing. But this one actually stood out to me over dozens of brands. A good one for those with discerning taste buds who are looking for a quality matcha experience. I am tickled that I finally noticed the difference.

title: tasty, not too salty, pleasant crunch, non greasy
text:
I really like these SALMON skins. I love salmon, salmon skin and I do not find these to be especially fishy tasting or smelling. Much more pleasant smelling than pork rinds/chicharrons. Healthier too. I am familiar with salmon skin snacks, and these are as expected. Light, crispy, non greasy. Good Fish has variety of flavors which I have tried. My favorite is this tasty chili lime flavor option. Yums! While the pieces are definitely crispy and crunchy, they also have a slight chew. Some more than others. I find them very easy to eat, and have been enjoying these a lot. Not oily or greasy--makes for a great snack directly from bag.

Anyway, if you like pork rinds and want to try something healthier, this may be a good option for you.

title: much prefer their instant version- better taste
text: I really like Molecule Instant coffee packets, I often use their Detox and Harmony blends. This Gamers blend is similar in some of the supplements it includes. I find their instant coffee to be pretty good and pairs well with my regular coffee. SO I had higher expectations for the nespresso pods--usually brewed is better, right?. I dont know.. I just didnt like this very much. While it has a dark roast taste, it is kind of weak. Lighter too. Had more watery taste. Might be better added to already brewed coffee (but then, that is what I like doing with their instant version).  I tried it in the nespresso machine, and I even gutted some pods to be brewed in a regular pot, and lastly tried it as a pour over. I just cant seem to make it work. However, I am a big fan of their instant so I will stick to that.

title: crispy, light, non greasy SALMON skins, various flavors, not too salty
text:
Crispy, light, non greasy SALMON skins. If you like pork rinds and stuff of that ilk, then this is pretty much in line with that. To me- someone who is familiar with salmon skins- this taste and texture is as anticipated. Has the crunch, and like any skin, will turn a little chewy the longer it is in mouth as it moistens. Various sized pieces, all crunchy but some more so than others. I rather like these, but I also like pork rinds. And I love love love salmon (and salmon skin). I like that I can grab a bag of these and have myself a relatively healthy snack. They are not greasy, and not overly salty. I dont even notice that much of a fish aroma.

This is a multi flavor pack, and I am glad I was able to try the 4 flavors. I like Chili Lime and Spicy BBQ about evenly, followed by Sea Salt, then Tart cranberry.

I dont rate on price because we all have different budgets, diets, interests. While maybe a little pricier than I can comfortably pay, I know salmon skins are pricy, and this falls within price range of fish skin snacks.

I'm happy with them, and I would consider these again. I acquired these September 2021, and these have an expiration date of January 2022.

title: I like it best for making pizza crust, and nut butter cookies
text:
I like this barely barley option over their high protein option. This contains just spent barely, and it is fairly easy to work it into recipes- breads, biscuits, muffins, even cookies. I find it takes me some trial and error to get the right taste and texture. They have some recipes on their website that include this flour. Many of their recipes use more than one flour, so I am not finding it to be a total 1:1 swap.. hence trial and error.

I like it best for pizza crust--love the added fiber boost. 25g per serving!

title: trial and error, but makes passible breads, treats
text:
INGREDIENTS: Spent grain flour, buckwheat flour, flaxseed meal, resistant corn starch, vital wheat gluten, psyllium husk powder (<--boosts fiber)

I find that their flours work best when combined with other flours. SO it isnt a direct 1:1 swap for a single flour. If you are aiming for waffles, pancakes, and muffins, I think their waffle & pancake mix might be a better fit. From what I have seen of their recipes, much of the dessert style ones use a combo of waffle mix and replacement flour. Would like to see more recipes specific to this flour, but there are some others on their website.

Yet, it kinda does work as is. I have used it to dredge proteins, and I have made a passible pizza crust, and even some biscuits. I think adding egg and/or oil helps. Play around with it. I like the high fiber and high protein component.

3.5 stars

title: portion control, convenient. Sweet, soft- great for Salads, Yogurt, Oats, Trail mix, Noshing
text:
Well packaged, super fresh. I have no problem with removing wrapper from comfort of my couch or on the go while driving. But maybe get it started if giving these to a kiddo.

Glad these are packaged in 1 ounce boxes (like a pack of raisins) because they are very good, and I would otherwise not stop eating them. The pieces are small- also similar to raisins or chopped dates, so very easy to pop in mouth, or sprinkle over yogurt, oatmeal, etc. Add to a trail mix. add to small batch muffins, pancakes etc. SALADS. Other dishes. Sometimes the added expense of single serve/convenience portions are actually money saving because the product will stay fresh longer over an open bag that doesnt get used up quickly.

Soft, moist, easy to eat. Has some added sugar (dextrose). I like dried apricots, and these have a better taste and mouth feel than some. I imagine it will come down to taste/texture preference. I see/taste nothing bad about these.

title: I prefer their instant version more
text:
I REALLY like Molecule instant coffees, including the detox one like this, but these pods fell short for me. I found that they taste a little weak. Like I can tell it is dark roast in flavor, but it brews light in color, and is watery tasting. Since I didn't like it in my nespresso brewer, I then tried it as a pour over by extracting the contents from the pod. That didnt change anything. AND? I had to double to check to make sure it wasn't decaff because I did not feel the usual uplift I normally get. I think I made 5 pods trying to get a good coffee taste and caffeine boost.

I think I will just continue with their instant packets. which I like plain or added to other coffee. [[ASIN:B08QGZT5G3 Molecule Detox Instant]]

title: very light mint finish, most noticeable in hot preparation; disappears in cold.
text:
I think the quality of this matcha is very good. Not bitter, not too "green" tasting. I have the option with mint, and it is very subtle. That can be good or bad depending on what you are looking for. If I wasn't looking for the mint flavor, I could easily just assume this was regular matcha. Yet, when I am looking for it, I notice the subtle minty finish. For greatest notice on the mint taste, it is best prepared as a hot tea, perhaps prepared a little stronger than the directions in order to pick up on the mint. I think those with discerning taste buds, those that enjoy the subtle nuances of a quality matcha will really like this.

Certainly works well in cold preparations too-- which is my go-to way of having matcha.

Comes packaged as a packet of matcha powder tucked into a pop top tin (I use a spoon or knife to pop it open).

title: works really well w/ other neutral flavors, in smoothies, creamy stuff. Great aroma
text:
I have a few Happy Home flavors which all have been good. I can add this to that list. The figured the strawberry might be a challenge to get a good natural flavor, but this is quite good. The aroma is deliciously strong. The strength of flavor depends on what it is being mixed into. Overall I would say it is a solid, middle of road strength. Adding it to a light neutral base will exemplify the strawberry flavor (think vanilla, or something creamy, frostings, cream cheese, home made whipped cream, ice cream, or something semi bland like pancakes, waffles, muffins). When I use it in a plain vanilla based smoothie, or when I make a smoothie with frozen strawberries, this flavoring really amps up the flavor profile.

I then tried it with something that can be hard to mask-- my iced matcha green tea lattes. I dont care for the flavor of matcha, but I drink it daily for its benefits. I usually add it to a stronger smoothie base. I decided to just use this Strawberry flavor with unsweetened vanilla almond milk, a little bit of Yacon syrup to add sweetness, and matcha powder. It really made a difference. I added a little of this liquid and it masked the matcha, though I couldnt tell it was strawberry. So I added more until I could taste it. I'm not sure how much I used, but it was a couple of generous splashes. So for stuff that has competing flavors, this may not come through unless using a lot. Even so, I'm impressed that it rose to the challenge.

Ingredients: Natural Flavors, Water, Alcohol, Propylene Glycol

title: pure stevia, no added ingredients, not a blend-- just stevia
text:
fine ground, yet slightly granular strong stevia. Dissolves well. Be mindful that a little goes a long way. I find most stevia tastes nearly the same, some being more mellow and other having a slight bitterness. This is a little more mellow, and it is just stevia. There is nothing added to it. So many stevia products are getting sneaky by adding in erythritol and only mentioning it in the ingredients, not elsewhere on package. Or there are other additions-- all to make the stevia taste a little less intense. I just want actual stevia. SO if you are used to one type of product, be sure to take a look at the ingredients because if you are used to one sort of taste, then the actual real deal may taste weird.

I like this

title: so versatile, has quickly become a pantry staple
text:
I didn't know tomato powder was a thing. I love tomatoes in all forms. I have it all. Canned, jarred, fresh, diced, pureed, sauces, pastes, stewed. Basically if it is tomato, I have it and now I can add powder to the list. Tomato powder is so versatile. It is now a staple in my pantry. I can make a quick ketchup, or bbq sauce, or dipping sauce, or pizza sauce, or sprinkle over eggs, pizza, vegetables, potatoes, add to rubs, into soups etc. Even make a healthy, super low sodium "V8". Endless possibilities. I really like it for a Hungarian style goulash I make that doesn't use tomato sauce, yet I always add a little paste to boost the flavor. I will be trying this in it asap.

I have used other Spice Village spices (love their paprika), and this seems perfectly fine. I have no other tomato powder experience to draw from, but I am quite pleased over this experience so far.

title: Fitne is part of my morning routine. Must have for me. Love the taste of all of them
text:
Love my Fitne coffee, been drinking it for a few months now pretty much every day. I have been consuming various Fitne coffee varieties. They are all similar in that they have instant coffee, some creamer, some non sugar sweetener, and then some variety of supplements-- usually focused on weight loss, and/or beauty.

I have not only tried a few varieties through testing, but also have repurchased them over and over.

I give them all 4 stars, but my repurchase history indicates that I should up it to 5 stars. I only keep it at 4 because the amount of water for a packet of functional coffee is just 4-5 ounces. I can stretch it as much as 6 ounces, but no further. The coffee taste is light, the sweetness can be robust, but overall all of them are very pleasant to me. I usually just add a packet to a cup off coffee. I nearly always just drank my coffee black until I began adding Fitne to my coffee. SO GOOD. I will then often add in some collagen powder and sometimes mushroom powder. My coffee is now a functional cup of awesomeness.

There is English on the package. It is mixed in, just look.

As for weight loss? I cant say for sure if my 40+ lb drop in weight can be attributed to this directly, but I do use it as a support as I sorta watch my eating (I only restrict desserts) and exercise more. I also use additonal supplements such as matcha green tea powder, white kidney bean extract, chromium picolinate, and saffron. Whether it is one thing, combo of things, or nothing.. I'be been quite pleased and impressed with my progress. If you happen to come across other reviews, I have never shied away from saying I am 305 lbs--always figure that height (5'11) and weight can help in various reviews. Well now I am 265, and keep on working at it. My Fitne coffee is a must have for me.

I like it a lot, it helps me start my day, seems to help keep me on track, and I simply like all the varieties I have tried (though I like the green bag and this one the most), and like I said.. it has been a regular repurchase for me.

If I still have the bag, I will take a picture of the backside. I normally dump all the packets into a larger container so I can just grab whatever I feel like each morning.

title: crunchy, naturally sweet. Snack on, or add to soups
text: Love freezed dried fruits and vegetables. The natural sweetness level is greatly increased, making for an interesting treat to snack on direct from bag. Yet can also be added to soups, etc for a "back to broccoli" taste. I have had their cauliflower and liked it enough to want to try some other varieties. Good stuff!

title: perfect for home made sweet bao
text: On the rare occasion I make home made bao buns, I always make a few sweet red bean buns (my weakness). I can buy red beans (adzuki) to prep myself and add sugar, or I can buy premade paste such as this. The latter is easier. Good price for a goodly amount of paste. I dont end up needing much, so even if I waste some, it wasn't too pricey. I'd definitely buy this again.

title: Yum. As simple and natural as can be. No added BS.
text:
I like it. I never make my own blends. Well, I used to, but then I found that I really prefer just buying a bag as desired. What I really like about this Evoke Muesli Morning Zen blend is that it just tastes as simple and natural as can be. No added BS. It is what I would make if I felt like constructing my own mix. It is just oats, raisins, almonds, cranberries, flax seeds, and pumpkin seeds. I like the ratio of oats to add-ins. Every bite seems to have a punch of tart sweetness and nuttiness. I have noshed on it plain, have had some with non dairy milk, have tried it on yogurt (love it on low sugar vanilla Greek yogurt), and have had it hot (with a spoonful of yogurt on top). I find it plenty sweet from the dried raisins and cranberries. Maybe I will try adding some to a muffin mix. I like it all, and I have zero issues with this brand or blend. Good stuff.

This is a generously sized bag. 2.5 lbs currently priced at $13.99. Seems reasonable to me. I dont rate on price because we all have our own budgets, etc.

title: Mr Tortilla for portion control, versatility, and taste. Can be frozen!
text:
I love Mr Tortilla. I am a regular consumer of their [[ASIN: B08C57H945 Mr Tortilla Whole Wheat Low Carb Tortillas]] and had yet to try a flavored version. They have several kinds. I am so pleased to have tried this savory spinach option. Oh my, these are such a treat. I love spinach tortillas for wrapping sandwiches, and these are even tastier than expected. Mind you, these are small at about 4.5", so you will be working small-- but once you get an idea of what to do with them, sky is the limit. I rely on Mr Tortilla for portion control. There is one brand that I can find in store, but they are always out. Then there is another grocer that has a store brand low carb tortilla, but its a drive. I buy a stack every time I go. But I love having an online option to buy. Also, because these are smaller (and the wheat ones I get are very low cal, low carb), I can even more so reduce my caloric intake all the while enjoying stuffing my belly. Mmmm food! These have double the calories and carbs than the ones I normally get by Mr Tortilla, but still.. just 35 calories 5 carbs each (versus 15, and 1g). Reasonable!

Here are some ways I personally create dishes with Mr Tortilla tortillas.

#1: Press a tortilla into a muffin pan, then bake. You now have perfect sized little taco bowls to fill up with whatever you want. I do this all the time. As a meal, as a snack. Try this!

#2 Mini quesadillas, but piled high. Just layer them up with other goodies, bake. Cut and enjoy

#3 Lightly fried with some sort of filling (doesnt have to be limited to Mexican cuisine inspired, can be savory or sweet). Love me some breakfast "tacos". I lightly steam or microwave to add softness, then add some filling. Fold over, then carefully do a light fry to them to add texture and close them up. Or not.

#4 Sloppy soft tacos. Do you ever just want to pick at an assortment of food? This is my go to item (especially the whole wheat tortillas) to simply sit my bum down on couch, with a tray of an assortment of fillers. I'll do cheese, some meats, some vegetables, refried beans, some sauces.. and then I just make up a little taco as I go. I dont socialize, but I imagine this would be a nice option for a small gathering.

#5 Cut in half, thirds, quarters.. then fried in oil to make fresh crunchy tortilla chips. Add salt while still hot!

#6 I like these spinach ones for use with chicken, or lunch meat, and some arugula. Quick tasty snack or light lunch. I will likely always keep a stack of these on hand now for this exact use. Can use them to wrap up some cheese and vegetables and olives, etc.

#7 I put a couple of the spinach ones in the toaster, and then added a little butter to have as a chewy side for some soup.

#8 Tostada, more or less. Lightly fry up or bake, then load with toppings.

This product listing doesnt show different ways to work with these tortillas but their whole wheat option does. [[ASIN: B08C57H945 Mr Tortilla Whole Wheat Low Carb Tortillas]]

It isn't just that they are good, but they have a good mouth feel. They are always well packaged. They are shelf stable until opened, then I put them in fridge. They do well in fridge, AND they freeze well (the whole wheat does for sure, I haven't had need yet to freeze these). So versatile.

title: robust flavor, sweet- exactly what is good for ice treats. Also works in other applications
text:
I like the Hypthermia brand of syrups. I have tried both unsweetened and sweetened varieties. I have tried other brands, and for the most part I think these brands are best for ice based treats. Yet, when it comes to this specific brand, I think it has much more versatile application. Unlike others, I find the taste to work well in club soda, added to iced tea, hot tea, and even as a flavoring for ice cream, or over foods. So, not all snow cone syrups are the same I have learned. Hypothermia is a brand I can say works for/on/in stuff beyond snow cones & shaved ice. But if that is all you are using it for-- very good. Strong, sweet, and taste will come through easily.

The Tigers Blood is tropical tasting. Berry forward with undertone of coconut. Well balanced I think.

title: best for ice treats, maybe for tea
text:
I like that it uses cane sugar- it has a sweet but not cloying taste, something that corn syrup creates. The flavor is about as expected. I think it is likely best for use in ice treats as the taste is more in line with that application. Just has that more commercial taste. The taste is just different than syrups I use for coffee, boba tea, etc. And it isnt as robust as other ice syrups (unsweetened or sweetened).

I do however like it for iced tea or making some of my hot teas taste better. I mixed it with some green tea, added additional matcha green tea powder, then added a splash of this to temper the semi bitter flavor of both teas.

I'll use it up, but Im sure it wont be a repurchase for my use.

But for those looking at it for ice treats? yes, totally has that taste.

title: for those that want a gentle, natural tasting drink w/o heavy sweetness or weirdness
text:
WOAH, I like this. You know how it is with protein powders, there is a built in cringe factor before taking that first sip. We buy powders not knowing how it is going to taste. Is it going to be the typical chalky, over sweetened, bland taste that needs help through adding in a bunch of other stuff, or is it going to be the mythical tasty magical elixir of awesomeness. Well, while it isn't the latter, it is a far reach from the former.

It is, to me, the most natural tasting concoction I have had in a long time. I always need to doctor up my protein or meal replacement drinks. This is a protein powder, but it has all sorts of added food ingredients that it really bumps up the nutritional profile. Not exactly a meal replacement drink, but if you're fasting this can provide enough of an edge to power through the day.

OK, so taste. This review is for the BANANA, but I am going to comment on the CHOCOLATE as well since I have both. And so both reviews will say pretty much the same. I love banana flavor in general. When it came to this.. I had high hopes but low expectations. lol. When I first opened the container, I took a whiff. I could not detect banana. I was sad. Ok, so I proceeded to fill my mixing cup with 8 ounces of unsweetened almond milk and 1 scoop of this powder (which was at bottom of tub). I made it basically according to directions. First time I try something I try to follow directions and then make adjustments as I go. The directions say water can be used. I mixed for 30 seconds. Then took a sip. I TASTED BANANA! YEAH!! Ok, already impressed. Next, the sweetness level. The sweetness level is very mild. It has stevia in it--and you know how companies can be-- they load that stuff in. So I am going to say that if you are used to the more heavily sweetened products, this will either be a super refreshing change, or it will be disappointing and you will want to add sugar. I am flippin' stoked that this has a lightly sweet taste. And that I can taste banana. And that overall all I am tasting is.. a mild, easy to consume plant based protein drink that does not assault the taste buds. It's.. gentle.

As for CHOCOLATE. Same idea, but instead of a natural banana taste, it has a pure cocoa taste. Because this too isnt that sweet, and the cocoa is like baking cocoa or raw cocao, it is a pure chocolate flavor. Usually I am ADDING unsweetened baking powder or raw cacao powder to make my so called chocolate protein drinks taste more like chocolate. THIS tastes like chocolate. Of course, there is never too much chocolate, so feel free to add more chocolate. Here too I tried it just with 8 ounces unsweetened almond milk and 1 scoop of powder.

I can drink them as is.. or if I were to "doctor them up", then I would likely add in some banana to the banana option as well as the chocolate option. Maybe add some instant coffee to the chocolate (with banana-- remember old star bucks vivanno? yeh, that's what I am going for). Then you know.. collagen powder, maybe some mushroom powder. Or I can just shake/mix/blend up a simple scoop with non dairy milk and be done. I'd say that this is for those that want a gentle, natural tasting drink w/o heavy sweetness or weirdness. I like it a lot for this reason. It quickly went to top of my list for drinks of this nature (i do have one brand I like that is super sweet that I use for masking harsher tastes such as greens and matcha).

BTW, both of the products I am using are in 16 ounce tubs of loose powder. 18 servings per container.

90 calories, 15 grams protein, 2 grams fiber (3 total sugar, 0 g added sugar, 6 gram carbs), 85 mg sodium, 0 cholesterol, 1 g fat (0 saturated, 0 trans). I'll include a pic of the label for more detailed nutritional info.

title: good matcha for cold preparations, very nice iced or in smoothies.
text: Reasonably priced matcha ($1.79 per ounce) that works just fine in my smoothies, or other shaken drinks. I often make hot or iced lattes, so I go through a lot. I really cant tell the difference between all the matcha tea powders I have tried over the years. Some are little brighter green, some darker, some more mild and sweet, some a tad more bitter. But all withing a tight range., More discerning taste buds will tell the difference, and likely more important for hot tea, ceremonial style preparation. But for me, and especially for cold prep or smoothie prep? All are good. This is good. Price would lead me to buy again.

title: Good! bland and chewy as it should be, little goes long way, eat hot or cold
text:
Nice change from my usual cellophane glass noodles (aka bean thread noodles, or Chinese vermicelli). The noodle threads are made from nearly any starch except for rice, plus water. This uses sweet potato starch. It doesn't impart much flavor itself, as to be expected. The noodles are really a vehicle for picking up the flavors of broths, sauces, spices, other food ingredients. Adds texture and visual interest to dishes. Once cooked, can be consumed hot or cold. Has a chewy texture. It is exactly as it should be.

Sometimes I find stuff like this in my local grocer, but usually I have to travel out to an Asian grocery store (I live in country, so it is a haul). So more often than not, I put in orders from Amazon. I no longer have any idea of what the cost is on some of this stuff, so I just buy what I think is reasonable. This is reasonable to me. $10 for 3 bunches of threads. Each bunch of threads make up a lot of noodles, and since it isnt a noodle you center the meal around, like spaghetti.. (is more of a texture additive), a little goes a long way.

title: Just puffed quinoa & yacon; great in yogurt bowls, over ice cream, cereals, noshing
text:
I love puffed Quinoa cereal. Of all the various brands I have tried, I am a fan of Wholefort, and this one is extra tasty to me. Quinoa cereals are usually JUST quinoa. So you really much love the taste of quinoa to appreciate these cereals. This particular variety adds in a little bit of Yacon (a low glycemic natural sweetener) I I already eat their plain puffed quinoa cereal. Funny, I normally dont have a bowl of it with milk, preferring to have it by the handful, in yogurt, or as an ice cream topper (low carb, low sugar commercial or home made ice cream). https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07WGJF8LW

What I like about this variation, is that the puffed pieces are a little bit bigger, making them much easier to just nosh on dry. And that hint of sweetness pairs well with the seedy taste of quinoa.

Now remember, this is made from Quinoa. It tastes like quinoa. I happen to love that, and I keep puffed quinoa in my snacking basket. These bags of cereal tend to last me quite some time- usually I grab 1/4 cup to 1 full cup at a time. Just depends on how snacky I am feeling. One of these days I am going to make marshmallow rice crispy treats.. er, puffed quinoa treats (make my own sugar free marshmallows, or buy low sugar marshmallows). I DO NOT rate on price, as we all have different budgets, values, needs. But I do comment. Since I cant gobble this down in one sitting, and I get several servings, and it helps keep my calories and added sugars in check.. I find a lot of value in it. If you think you will like it, then I recommend grabbing the 4 pack-- price is much better. Even so, current price of $15 makes it $1.87 per serving. If buy the 4 pack for $30, that brings it down to $0.94 per serving.

As for nutritional information. It does appear different on my bag than it does in product description, but the values are not different. They are not pulling a fast one. The info they provide in their product picture is for 45 gram serving. The serving size on the bag is for 30 grams (1 cup), and for 100 grams (bags has 255 grams, so they add in nutritional value for consumption of nearly half the bag too). I think we just have updated bags as what I have actually provides more information, and is more in line with a typical serving.

I already like the plain version (though smaller balls), and I really like this one, so this is a for sure repurchase once I get through my puffed quinoa stash.

YUM
INGREDIENTS: QUINOA & YACON (THAT'S IT!)

There are about eight, 1 cup servings in this bag.
110 calories,
.5 g fat (0 saturated)
0 mg cholesterol
50 mg sodium
Total Carbs: 24 grams
---4 grams fiber
