title: OK flavor, texture. Needs many extra ingredients, and time.
text:
I have the Protein Cake and these Keto Muffins. If you are doing a comparison, I think the muffins are better tasting than the cake, but are way more involved in terms of prep. If watching calories, carbs-- be mindful that the nutritional info is for each small muffin, and the cake info is for the entire cake.

I dont rate on price (we all have different budgets, needs), but I do comment. I have a huge budget, and $80 seems insane to me. I am well aware that products of this ilk tend to be pricy. I bake like this often. But when it comes to these, I would rather do without. The overall taste, prep time, and price per item just doesn't bring enough value to my life. That's $20 per box. Each box makes 6 standard smallish cupcakes. $3.33 per cup cake. Maybe 3-4 bites from each little muffin. Plus, there are several added ingredients that we need to add, some of which are wasted, and there is more time than usual involved to make these (beating egg whites into still peaks, etc). Nope. Not a repurchase from me. Plenty of recipes available. These dont lend a short cut.

On the plus side, the taste and texture is better than their Protein Cake (soggy, eggy pancake taste and texture, but at least very quick to make).

You will need several egg white, a couple of yolks, almond milk, vanilla extract, pumpkin puree or applesauce, as well as some butter "melted then cooled", a whisk beater/mixer to beat egg whites into stiff peaks, cupcake papers (or silicone ones). And patience. And ambition.

Taste and texture are "OK", and THAT is what my rating is based on. These are not as eggy as their cake, but still has that.. taste. Still a bit damp and dense. The butter comes through and helps to make it a little rich tasting. I use pumpkin puree, so I went ahead and added some pumpkin pie spice. I topped the muffins with some toasted hemp seeds for added crunch and flavor.

Results were ok. Mediocre. Better than their cake by far, but so involved from I normally care to get into. I will likely make up the next 3 boxes all at once. I am not doing "keto", but I do restrict my sugar intake, especially in form of desserts as I am trying to break a life long binge cycle. I can do various types of carbs without my brain firing up, but when it comes to dessert foods, I can undo many days worth of reasonable choices in a matter of minutes (I dont eat one donut, I eat a dozen, etc). Stuff like this normally helps me. I can maintain control. Was nice to try this out, but I wouldnt recommend them.
Of course, you may like them. Take close look at ingredients, what you need, and time needed. It might be just what your diet, life needs. Go for it. It just isnt for me.

title: eggy damp pancake texture, decent taste, plenty of sweetness, quick prep & cook
text:
You will need to add eggs, almond milk, vanilla extract, and apple sauce or pumpkin puree.

The "cake" is easy enough to make and bake. It is cooked in the micro wave. So if you are looking for a fairly quick, sweet treat that wont bust your calorie budget this might be for you. Each box comes with 2 "cake" mixes, and 2 glaze mixes.

The taste is not bad, but it is underwhelming. Tastes like an eggy, slightly soggy pancake, which is a bit of a turn off. I still ate it, but it didnt have a satisfying mouth feel. I may play around with the mix and see if I can get more loft and overall better texture. If I can, I will update this with what I did. I really do appreciate being able to make a quick sweet treat. I wonder if it would do better in an oven? It only makes a small portion- little more than a "cake in a mug".

Anyway... As is, I really could just make a pancake (using a keto mix, maybe adding in a scoop of protein powder and adding no sugar sweetener) and pretty much recreate this. I dont rate on price (we all have different budgets, needs), but DANG this is pricy for me so I doubt it will be a repurchase. $44 for 4 boxes (8 cakes), works out to $5.62 per mug cake. It just doesn't make sense, especially since several ingredients are still required.

If you use pumpkin puree, I recommend being very careful with measuring. My pumpkin puree seems extra wet, and I think it contributed to the extra soggy (but still cooked through) texture. Not sure. ALSO, since it will create a slight pumpkin taste, mind as well add a few shakes of some pumpkin spice.

Their MUFFIN mix has a much better texture (but it is way more involved in terms of preparation, and time). Also, $80. wowza
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B099NR4W92
[[ASIN:B099NR4W92 keto muffin mix]]

title: spicy with multiple levels of flavor, smells good, tastes good
text:
Oh smells so good. I take a whiff and my stomach growls. Makes me think of all sorts of lovely food I have had over the years and I know I wont be able to totally recreate it with this, but I can try. It is just such a fragrant mix, highlighting how much a spice blend can transform a food. Spicy but with loads of flavor- many levels of flavor. So good.

I have had a few spice blends from S-B Spices, and have been really pleased. I am a huge fan of their Herbs De Provence

title: crunchy, almost as hard as banana chips. Great flavors, just apples (& cinnamon or ginger)
text: You know how banana chips are hard and crunchy? That is how these are, but maybe just a little softer. So know that these are crunchy and may be too hard for some people. Small apple sticks, or slices. Kind of in between. You just have to want a more crunchy dried apple snack. That is all they are- dried apple, some plain, some with cinnamon, some with ginger. Nothing else.  I personally like the ginger best but I happen to love the bite that ginger has. They're all good (to me). I think I just expected longer, larger pieces. I chomp on these straight from bag, but I can see adding these in to some oatmeal or muffins-- I imagine they would moisten up, soften up some.

title: comes in a canister, smells good, tastes as good as matcha can get, great in hot/cold drinks
text:
Smooth, mild, mixes well into cold or hot drink preparations.

Perfectly good matcha to me. I go through a lot. I always use way more than the recommended amount. I like the steady energy it provides me, as well as the reduced need/desire for sweets, seems to reduce my appetite too. Add in the anti oxidant goodness, and it is a must have supplement in my life.

I rarely drink it hot, usually preferring a cold preparation instead. I have never been a fan of the taste of matcha green tea, but started drinking it maybe ten years ago. Something made me want it, and I remember scouring the Asian grocery stores for some of this allusive powdered green tea. This was before the ubiquity of internet shopping. So back then I only bought what I could get my hands on. It was from China. The two bags lasted me forever because I just didnt love the taste.. but the bags of powder seemed to stay fresh. When I eventually ran out, I decided to simply buy more of the same, this time having found them on Amazon. It was then that I learned that there are so many options and different price points, and from different regions. I have since purchased or tried many many many brands. What I have found, is that they all pretty much taste the same to me. Some are a little more mild, some are a little more bitter, some are ever so slightly sweet. But none of it really matters to me because so much of the flavor gets masked by other smoothie ingredients. However, the ones that are more mild & sweet are preferred as it is easier to mask the off putting flavor. I imagine if I drank it hot, with nothing else, then the nuances of flavor would be more noticeable, and therefore would be more picky about what I bought. Alas, I am good with whatever I have tried over the years.

Going back to this Panatea brand, I like the presentation and that it comes in a canister. Save for a few brands, most all come in packets, which I dump into a canister anyway. So this already being in a canister is thrilling to me lol
I like this matcha, and even think it smells kinda good. I think the price point is reasonable and competitive, which makes me consider buying it again when I need more.

title: lovely hot or over ice, on its own or added in with other flavors
text:
I love this instant chicory that I can nearly eat it by the spoonful. Ok, I stick my finger in and grab a taste. It is really quite pleasant. I have had chicory before- usually as part of a brewed blend, never instant. This is awesome. I find chicory to have the closest thing to a coffee taste. It is a nice way to have a quick iced or hot coffee like beverage without all the caffeine. Though, sometimes I do a half and half type drink- use some instant coffee and some of this, or I brew a full caffeine or half caffeine K-cup, then add this in.

Sometimes I add a little instant coffee to my chocolate creations and I think this could would for that too.

title: These are Unhulled WHOLE toasted hemp seeds- crunchy, salty, tasty. Versatile.
text:
The salted option is 100% as toasted hemp SEED should be.

Think about it. This is the whole seed-- which includes the shell. If you dont want the shell (and the ensuing pulpy crunch) then go with hemp HEARTS, which is the interior, without the shell. Complaining about the shell is comical to me when this is clearly an unhulled product.

And so, if you have had toasted hempseeds before, then I think you will find these salted ones tasty. I see there are various flavors, and mine if for the Himalayan Salt option. I find them to have an "easy on teeth" level of crunch (not hard, doesnt take much effort to bite down, nothing at all like pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds), salty like most toasted seeds (so be mindful if watching sodium intake). I may tongue some particles out from my teeth, but it isn't bad at all--and that sort of thing drives me crazy. I wouldnt eat these if they created a mess. These are fine. It is a seed, after all.

If you have never had toasted hemp seeds, do not get them confused with hemp hearts (softer, they are what are refered to as hulled hemp seeds). These toasted hemp seeds INCLUDE the woody outer shell. They are "unhulled". They are small. This style is always small bead like crunchy balls. These can be consumed alone, or sprinkled on salads, yogurt, or added to home made muffins, breads, etc. Sky is the limit.

It's not for everyone, that's for sure. But those complaining about the hull, these absolutely show that they are unhulled. Small, crunchy WHOLE HEMP SEEDS. Toasted. Salted. That's it.

When I eat these by plain, I find it hard to stop eating them. They have that addictive salty crunch.

title: tasty finishing salt
text: Very nice. Quality seems fantastic. I like the pressure zip bag that this gray Celtic/French salt comes in. Works well having some poured into my little salt bowl that sits out on my counter. It is the perfect salt to take a pinch of  to finish off a recipe/meal. Yum!

title: brown sugar is tasty, & can be used in coffee, blended w/ice, added to baked goods, icecream
text:
It's good. I have the Brown Sugar option, and this has a very pleasant brown sugar taste with a hint of tea. I normally use regular tea for the base of my Boba tea concoctions (my favorite is green tea with lychee syrup). I rarely do creamy, and never do powder premixes. I am not sure if it was a good idea for me to try this because it is really quite tasty--and I am trying to keep my sugar intake on the lower side. Just know that when using the full portion (4 tbs), there is 470 calories. 40 grams of added sugar, 50 grams of sugar, 85 grams carbohydrates. Also 340 mg of sodium. I find that I can easily halve that for a 16-20 ounce cup (loaded with ice). This isnt a drink mix you grab for as anything healthy. It is a treat and should be treated as such. Try it blended with ice for a frozen cappuccino sort of flavor. Add in a little instant coffee to boost the caffeine.

There is a spot in the product description where it says that it contains everything needed to make bubble tea. Basically what they mean is, sugar, tea, & cream. But for Boba tea (bubble tea) you will have to supply your own tapioca pearls. Using them or not using them does not change the taste of the drink, it is all about the added texture-- random chewy balls. Sometimes I use them when I am in the mood to cook up a batch.

Although there is some black tea in the mix, this could very easily be used as a creamer & sweetener combo for coffee. Also reminds me a bit of a horchata. Could be used as way to even out the flavor profile of a smoothie (just use sparingly). Could be added to baked goods, too. Or added to a batch of home made ice cream. It just has a really nice taste.

I think there are actually 20 servings per bag, if the 100 gram serving size is correct (based on weight of bag).

title: Works on everything, worth the try!!tasty flavor profile, need your own grinder (or theirs)
text:
FOR salt mills and grinders. This is for use in a grinder. You supply your own grinder. [[ASIN:B0179Q4Y9U This is the grinder I use]]

Nice herbal taste. Super light pink, almost gray salt chunks. Loads of pepper, rosemary. Also has garlic, thyme. It is an attractive compilation, and tasty too.

OR, use THEIR [[ASIN:B08HSL4XZJ salt grinder, which comes with this lovely salt]], then by this bottle to refill the grinder. I only discovered this when I came back to buy more. I just bought one of each.

Uprating to 5 stars, because I have come back for more. At some point it became my go to seasoning for EVERYTHING. Just has this balanced flavor with that little extra something that makes my meals stand out. Salty and herbally. Not too peppery. I love pepper, but am glad this is more in the background.

title: directed to use 5oz H20, but still makes weak (to me)coffee, even doubled up. Love the brewer though
text:
Use 150 ml (5 ounces) of water per packet. It is an interesting system for brewing. I have used the tea bag style, and this is hybrid between a bag and a pour over filter. The packet has two side crutches that is attached over side of a mug-- nearly any size as it stretches. I used on narrow mouth and very wide mouth no problem. Standard is likely easiest. Then tear off top of filter bag, and pour hot water slowly over top. Be mindful of how much water you use.

I think it makes for an OK cup of coffee. Cant say I really like it, but I can see the appeal for on the go. Got a hot water option at work? then these would be nice to keep stashed in a desk. Individually packaged, and easy to get into.

I used two packets for a 6-7 ounce cup off coffee. Still tasted weak. I used a second mug and poured the coffee through the grounds again to see if I can get a stronger cup. Not really. It is just blah to me, but I prefer strong coffee. I actually prefer actual instant powder coffee over the taste of this. But I think some will enjoy it. Light leaning medium, so it has a little acidity built in.

On the plus side, there was no problem using the brewer. The side arms are sturdy, and not a single one broke on me. The paper filter is sturdy as well. Be sure to pick it up by the arms when done brewing so as not to accidentally dump spent grounds in your cup. Anyway, I think the brew system is neat, and would be open to having a blank set to keep on hand for times I want a quick single cup of coffee. I tend to like pour over, just not THIS pour over coffee.

It's "OK", hence 3 stars

title: flavored w/ "milk" (a flavor similar to "birthday cake" flavoring), well packed, comes w/tool
text:
It's a nice treat. Just know that they are flavored macadamia nuts IN SHELL. Each shell has a split, which makes it easy to open them up WITH the included metal nut opener tool. Also, this is how there is a "milk" flavor--it has a noticeable sweet milk flavor. If you aren't familiar, it is the flavor that is usually associated with products that are labeled as "birthday cake" flavor (so snack cakes, cookies, ice cream, and now I guess nuts). Not bad, but I am not really one to enjoy milk flavor. I totally missed this in the description. It doesnt taste bad as it is on the lighter side, but it does reduce the flavor of natural macadamia. Adds unneeded sugar and salt.

Has that wonderful light crunch that is macadamia, though.

The packaging is really good. A bag within a bag. About the size of a bag of coffee. The outer bag has all the product info, and the metal tool. In that bag is then another bag, which contain the nuts.

It tastes fresh, BUT I did receive a bag with the date of 06/17/2021. I normally see this as an expiration date (so, about 3 months expired if so), or perhaps it is a manufacture date? Concerns me.

3 stars. I would like to see stronger reference to these being flavored. I wouldnt have gotten them.
Clarification on what that date indicates would be good too.

I'll eat these up. For what it is worth, I am liking them enough that it is hard to put a pause in eating them.

title: tastes like a real, fresh cookie. Chewy, has lovely mouth feel. Love chocochip, but churro good too
text:
Chewy, moist. I love their Chocolate Chip option, so I was curious for their snickerdoodle, well, Churro. It has the same great chewy texture. Truly the closest thing to a home baked cookie I have come across. Not just an excellent Keto cookie, but an excellent cookie period. I'm tempted to frost these with a low/no sugar frosting.

I am not following a particular diet so I dont have any restrictions, but I am reducing my sugar intake and it helps me to do so by choosing low carb, low sugar dessert options. I like that I can eat one of these and feel rather full. It is good enough to want to eat the whole bag, but the price keeps me from doing so. And, they are oddly filling.

I like how there is just enough sweetness. I dont find any off flavor. There have been so many keto cookies I have tried that have been abysmal. I am truly impressed with these. They are pleasant. I DO prefer the chocolate chip over the Churro., as they just have a little more flavor, but these are still excellent, especially if looking for that chewy mouth feel. I am impressed. I think I may make some unsweetened ice cream, or buy some low carb ice cream to make "ice cream sandwhich" with this cookie. It just seems to be missing something, but I think would be amazing with some frosting or used as holder for an ice cream sandwich.

Anyway, I recommend them. I think it is worth the try. They are pricy per cookie, but so far has been most real tasting cookie I have had.

title: strong concentrate, no added sweetener, highly versatile for drinks, foods. Great for soda.
text:
I love that this is totally unsweetened. You will have to add your own sugar or other sweetener. This is made for Italian ice, shaved ice--commercial, but it absolutely can be used at home for a multitude of purposes. I was curious how this would compare in taste to just using a cherry juice concentrate. Obviously one being naturally sweet, and one not. While the fruit juice concentrate offers more nutrition, there is benefit to using an artificial concentrate (intense flavor, little goes long way, super cheap, and zero sugar/sweetener of any kind). I can make an Italian Soda (carbonated water/club soda without watering it down with juice or juice concentrate. I do not need my drinks to be sweet, so this tastes fine without the additional sweetener. That wont be for everyone.. and when I do want it sweetened up I mix this concentrate with some sweetener, then add it to whatever.

Can be added to frosting, or home made ice cream, etc. I have yet to make it into a sweet syrup, but just adding in some sugar, agave, honey, corn syrup, etc.. makes for easy topping, dip.

They have lots of flavors, and if unsweetened isn't your thing, then know that they make some pre sweetened. This review is for the unsweetened. I just really like these unsweetened concentrate, then I can do what I want. I think this is the answer I was looking for. I like using drink syrups, but I dont want them loaded with sugar. I get the unsweetened, but sometimes I just want nothing added but the actual flavor. I can control the sweetness, or have no sweetness. I can sweeten or not sweeten depending on my mood.

Do you make your own pop? Any of these flavors could work for that, or even a few drops to make a water essence. I find this so much better than the wee tiny over priced bottles that are specifically marketed toward soda streams. This has been a cool find.

title: add 1 pack to 4 ounces water, or add to cup of coffee for added flavor & creaminess
text:
I consume Fitne coffee often. I have tried various options they have to offer, and there are a couple that I keep repurchasing. I have so far liked them all. It's instant coffee with added supplements. Usually focusing on weight loss and beauty. While I could use a boost in either of those categories, I really just like the flavor.

I prefer to drink my coffee black, but there is something kind of addictive about this stuff that I like adding it into my morning coffee. Or I add it into a cold coffee "smoothie" (more instant coffee, collagen, some protein powder, mushroom powder, etc). So I usually add it into a cup of brewed coffee, then drink it as is or pour it over ice. The amount in a packet is generous, but the amount of water that is directed to use is low-- just 4 ounces (250 ml). Not much, right? I have tried it just made with water as per directions, and while it tastes delicious I find that it can be stretched out to 6. Anymore, and it is really pushing it into a more watery drink. BUT if added to existing cup of coffee? perfect.

I like them all, but the white kidney bean functional coffee is my favorite, followed by this one.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08WWFVQD1/

I give them all 4 stars. I do keep repurchasing, but I keep it at 4 stars because the coffee flavor could be stronger, and I would prefer that it made a larger cup of coffee than just a mere 4 ounces.

But I love this stuff.

title: fresh, works well for seitan, nice resealable bag
text:
When I make seitan, I end up going through a lot of vital wheat gluten. For that, this package isn't as budget friendly as other options, but the quality is very and I have no issue with it. I like the resealable bag, particularly helpful for those who use it just in baking where a bag of this size will be good for several loaves of chewy bread, bagels, etc.

My latest batch of seitan was extra good this time around. I attribute it to this fresh bag of vital wheat gluten.

title: big size for decorating lots of goodies, made in USA. Yay!
text: Happy to find a large size squeeze bottle of icing from a US company. Rich hued green is lovely. I will be buying more for my icing needs. It's tasty!

title: if you have vintage teeth, this vintage candy may be too hard to crunch into
text:
This is one of those candies best for those who already know what it tastes like. It may be a hard sell for newbies. It's more vintage, but these candies are still around in specialty shops. Fun to see them offered in a big old bag here. I haven't had burnt peanuts in forever. It made me fondly think back on some other similar candies of my youth- boston baked beans is very similar except have a smooth outer shell rather than bumpy.

These are about what I expected. The crunchy outer coating is hard. Some are easier to bite into over others. Thinking this is something that was best left to my childhood as I find it not as appealing in my 40s. Funny, not funny, is that the spiky coatings remind me of the coronavirus. Odd how the past couple of years shaped my thinking.

5 pounds makes for a hefty bag. You will likely want to repackage these once open.

4 stars-- seems fresh, taste is on point for what it is, some pieces too thick/hard to bite through comfortably. Gift worthy, can be broken down and sorted into smaller bags for sharing

title: tastes best crumbled on low carb ice cream, just ok as a keto cookie
text:
As a cookie because you like cookies? the taste and texture is disappointing.
As a keto cookie compared against other Keto cookies? it is about right. But I have had better.

I ultimately think these would be nice crumbled over low carb ice cream, or blended into iced cream to make a low carb milkshake or "blizzard". Or over yogurt. Or even dipped in chocolate. I just dont care to nosh on these by themselves. Something is amiss.

There is an odd taste that I am trying to pin point. It is like it has a slightly creamy mouth feel- yet it is simply a moist dry cookie. I think I pick up on the palm oil or butter. The front loaded erythritol doesn't help as that just gives a little coolness with the scant cinnamon flavor. I think that is it.. all the components are there but the misfire on the taste buds. If this had less coolness, and a stronger cinnamon vanilla flavor, then it would come together better. I am not at all in fear of over eating these.

I have tried several brands, from super cheap to super pricy. I usually aim for chocolate chip and/or snickerdoodle. Some brands do both well, some fail on both, some have a mix--one is good, but the other not so much. I KNOW finding keto/low carb/low sugar desserts that hit the spot are greatly trial and error. When it comes to this sort of stuff, I dont necessarily think it is bad quality, I just think it isnt for my taste buds. This snickerdoodle option is simply not good to/for me.

3.5 stars-- boosting to 4 as I would consider another flavor option. Also, their mission is appreciated.

The brand that comes closest to truly tasting like a cookie that anyone would enjoy, are by Kadabra. Pricy, but everything about it tastes and feels like a cookie. Dangerously so--I almost prefer a cookie that doesnt taste great for fear of binging! :) I love their chocolate chip ones, and recently bought their Churro variety (basically, a snickerdoodle), and while I prefer the former, the Churro is pretty good. Fresh, chewy, sweet, not chemically (to me). Anyway, thought I would mention it in case you are still looking and want some direction
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B091M8YBXT/

title: intriguingly versatile, easy to use, nice option for dredging proteins
text:
Edit: I have purchased this 4x since trying it less than a year ago. It is my go-to for adding to my "quick soups", which is basically taking any left over vegetables, grains (or shiritaki noodles), left overs in general, then I add hot water and some bullion to make a broth and/or a scoop of [[ASIN:B09BBQ57SW bone broth superfoods protein powder]]. Finally I will add a scoop or two of this. It kind of just thickens up my broth, giving it more body and adds to filling my belly. I really love this stuff!! I haven't tried any of the other varieties as this Slimovina is working out so well for me. As soon as I open a current bag, I have been coming back to order another. Takes me awhile to go through a bag, but I use it often enough that I never want to be without it. Just wanted to pop in to say how much I use it. Thanks!

Nice alternative to wheat flour when used to dredge proteins. Get a little more nutrition and a lot less carbs. I haven't tried it plain like another reviewer has (that intrigues me now), but I have added it to juicy stuff to thicken it up into a sauce. It definitely works to add more body to some soups and stews. This product was entirely new to me, yet the ingredients are very familiar. I would have never thought that having them together could create something that would make some magic happen, haha. I like it! Welcome addition, and at $12.99 not a budget buster.

Ingredients: Almond Flour, Vegetable Fiber (from Non-GMO Whole Vegetables), Organic Psyllium Husk, Guar Fiber

title: tasty flavor profile, perfect for any chicken dish, works nice on potatoes too
text:
I like how the container clearly shows the nutritional information, as well as the list of ingredients. Take note that the serving size is 100 grams. This is a 680 gram container, so that is 6.8 servings. Unless significantly dousing your chicken with this stuff, I doubt you will use that much at once-- and therefor not take in much sodium, calories, etc. This Rotisserie Chicken seasoning also works nicely on potatoes.

I like the flavor profile. It has a little savory, a little sweet, and hint of citrus.

title: savory, robust, fine powder- excellent on poultry, gravies, stuffing
text:
I know the bottle says, "bringing together the classic flavors of sage, rosemary, thyme", but the ingredients just say, "spices". Does not spell out what is in this blend. That being said, if you're cool with that, then this is pretty tasty. It looks and smells like I would expect it to with those 3 herbs. All three are green, so this fine powder is also green.

Taste is very much something I would expect for a poultry blend. Think Thanksgiving dinner- turkey, gravy, stuffing. Has that savory, robust smell and flavor that makes chicken and turkey extra mouth watering. Can be used in marinade, in dry rub, wherever.. ya got license to do what you want with a dry spice.

title: very smooth, easy to drink. Best of the bunch so far for me. YUM!
text:
Nice, smooth taste. I really like this one. I usually pick up a bottle every time I am at the grocery store as a drink for the ride home. No matter the brand, there is always that harsh taste. I find this Kombucha to be very easy to drink, super smooth, and just enough sweetness. Lovely chilled direct from can, or poured over ice into a glass. Gentle fizz taste refreshing. I can see using this as a mixer.

Loving the tropical flavor. I'd stock up my extra fridge with various flavors--it really is that good (to me).

title: nice addition to home made muffins, pancakes, biscuits, etc
text: I like this for adding into prepared oatmeal, and for adding into muffin or pancake mix. I think I like it best for baking. I have added it to smoothies, which is fine, but adding it to baked goods is better for me. I make some low carb crusts, rolls, biscuits, and this is a nice flavor to add into the mix. Quality seems fine. I really see nothing bad to say about it.

title: fresh, clean, well packaged
text: It's good! Pereg has really good stuff. I have tried several items, and everything is always of perfect quality. Clean, fresh, tastes good. I even like the look of the packaging. I would consider this brand when putting together a food themed gift. I love buckwheat/wheatberries and I haven't had them in awhile (I dont always see it available in my local store), so it was a pleasure to have some= basically used in same manner as any other grain you can think of. Use a little less water for more chewy texture (and cook less time), or add more water, and cook longer for more soft texture.

title: dark, robust, strong full flavor, does not taste like some watery decaff. This is bold!
text:
well well well, this Cafe Aroma decaf coffee is quite good. Sometimes I can tell that a coffee is decaf, and sometimes the taste takes me by surprise and I have to double check that I grabbed defcaf and not regular. This is remarkably regular tasting. No way I could tell it is decaf.

This Cafe Aroma ground Espresso roast coffee is bold, dark, strong, and smooth. There is a slight bite of something I cant pin point, but it tastes good to me. I absolutely prefer dark roast coffee over all else, so finding a good dark roast decaf is a rare treat to come by. I sometimes switch to decaf when I want something coffee like in the afternoon. I usually drink my coffee black, sometimes with creamer, sometimes over ice. I like when a coffee can handle all that I do to it. This is dark and smooth enough to drink black, and it also holds up well to ice for a nice iced coffee drink. Once in awhile I will make my coffee "half caff" by using a combo of regular and decaf. I feel like I could add this into a less desirable coffee and it would make it taste better (like all the more acidic bright medium roasts that are too tangy for my taste).

I have a coffee maker than can do specialty drinks (ie "espresso"), but I have been using this simply with a pour over coffee brewer. I likely add more coffee than needed, but I figure I can add a splash of water to dilute if need be.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08SBSSSJC

Anyway.. side by side with a regular caffeine strong bold coffee, this totally stands up to the challenge of also being, strong, bold, smooth. My 5 star rating is based heavily on that. Any nuances in flavor likely come from brewing style. I just want to make sure that this was indeed a dark roast, and didnt taste like a watery decaff. I like it, and would consider it again. Currently priced at $5.49 for 8.81 ounces

title: 5 stars because it meets my needs for using in a cold blended/shaken drink/smoothie
text:
I do not have discerning tastes when it comes to matcha green tea powder. So long as it blends well enough to consume, and gives me that non jittery energy, I am happy. I go through a lot, and I usually just grab whatever looks good. I have purchased or tried at all price points (curiosity, and sometimes simply a matter of availability). But my first foray into using matcha powder was with a brand that was pennies per ounce, this was before massive online availability. I remember finding it in an Asian grocery store. So that was my experience for years until I eventually decided to try finding it online. I bought that brand here. Still cheap. BUT in the past few months the price has gone up 60%, no loner keeping it in the running for the mega bargain it was. This Micronutrients option now has that title for me. It works just fine for my smoothies. Any tangy green taste is masked once I blend it in with some flavorful protein powder or meal replacement powder. I tend to use a lot of matcha at a time. I think the serving size is 2 tsp? well, I tend to use 2-4 TBS. So no matter what brand I use, the taste can be a little harsh.

I never drink matcha hot. I dont doubt that the brand and quality makes a difference there. So for that, I cant comment. But if you are like me and just use matcha added into cold liquid.. this is really perfectly fine. I have tied so many brands and levels of "quality", and I cant really tell the difference. Not enough to seek out brands at higher price point. They simply all work for me. But for tea, yeh.. I imagine the nuances of taste are much more important.

I will probably buy this again. Nice big bag will last me a couple of months of daily use.

title: A blend. The ingredients are: Allulose, Erythritol, Inulin, Steviol Glycosides
text:
Sweet, has minimal cool feel (not like pure erthritol), and since it is a one to one swap for sugar in recipes, I find it all the more easy to work with. I used it in my blender to make powdered sugar. It works. I dont always have that experience with other sugar substitutes so for that reason, I would consider this again. I have drastically cut out sugar, and even sugar substitutes, but I know I will still have it on occasion. Of the two, I am better off with the sugar substitute. I wanted a sugar free frosting, and this "sugar" helped me out. I just wish they would call it a blend, rather than just call it allulose. There is no mention of the other stuff until you look directly at the ingredient list.

Ingredients: Allulose, Erythritol, Inulin, Steviol Glycosides

title: clean, tasty quinoa with added flavor bits. Fresh, high quality, nice presentation
text:
Quinoa with a bonus: added almond slices, berries, toasted coconut. Very clean quinoa as it is prewashed. Just cook it up like any other quinoa ie 2 cups water per 1 cup quinoa. There are approximately 2 cups in this container. Not likely a repurchase from me, but I find Pereg products to be of excellent quality. Never any issues. I think the packaging makes it look nice enough to be considered for use in a food themed gift or care package.

4.5 stars

title: smells good, tastes good. Lovely lemon flavor- I use a little more than some
text:
My bottle came with a plastic security seal around the cap, and the inside of the cap has a seal that likely had been attached to the bottle opening.

Smells good, tastes good. Flavor is lemony, as expected. I used maybe 1/8 tsp for 6ounces of water, and I could taste plenty of lemon. I have yet to bake with it, but I expect to use the same as I would if I was using vanilla. It is more mellow like that. Unlike other extracts such as peppermint where the amount used is usually very little.

title: love the canister- much nicer than spooning from packets. Works great in my cold shaken drinks
text:
Works for me. My standards are low for matcha as I never drink it hot, and I think for hot there are more nuances in taste to discern. But for cold? Nearly any brand works. I always drink it mixed as a cold drink. Often just shaken with non dairy milk and ice. Or, because I use entirely too much matcha at once, I will add in a flavored protein/meal replacement powder to help dilute the taste. Love the low thrum of energy I get, and how it somehow reduces my appetite, especially for sweet stuff. Some matcha is more pungent than others, and I find this one to be fairly mild (as evidenced by my not needing as much masking flavor). So yeh, it works for me.

This mixes well for me, no problems. I rather like the container. I usually end up trying/buying the kinds that come in packets then dump it into a canister. With this, I can just use directly from the can.

Price is mid range. I have purchased some really cheap stuff and have been pleased for my needs. I have purchased or been given to try much pricier. And this is really when I learned that it doesn't seem to matter what I use, it all seems to be the same for the manner I use it.

title: 4" round mini tortillas are tasty, chewy, and highly versatile. Yum!
text:
Lets clear the air. These burritos are mini sized at roughly 4.25" wide. Just a little larger than most hand palms. They are just 15 calories a piece, with 1 net carb, 2 grams of fiber, 1 gram protein. They taste good, and have a good chewy texture.

Get creative! sure you can make some super mini tacos, or you can stuff them into a muffin pan and make little toasted taco shells. Or layer them with filling and bake for mini quesadilla, or keep on layering for a towering quesadilla. Fill'em and lightly fry them. Cut them and fry them for quick chips. Or warm them up, and have an assortment of goodies to spoon in. Love doing that when I want everything, so I prepare little bowls of various fillings.. and I enjoy a buffet of the sorts from comfort of my couch.

Sure, I can buy larger burritos for low cal and low carb. I buy THESE for something different. Sometimes I want smaller portions, or a specific filling to wrap ratio. I sometimes simply like having a smaller vehicle for various fillings. It's my go to for making multiple small bites of deliciousness. When I want larger size, I use something different. It doesn't have to be either or.

title: Spicy low sodium, no sugar, high protein beefy spice blend. Works on/in anything!
text:
Try this if you are looking for a no sugar, low sodium, high protein seasoning. It is more of a spice blend than a biltong beef snack item, and that's fine by me. Just know what you're getting. I like this blend, but it sure is spicy. I grabbed a pinch full and popped it into my mouth--oof!. Loads of heat that nearly overpowers the beef. I sprinkled it generously over a basic salad, and I have tried it mixed in with cream cheese. My blend has a much finer texture than what is shown in the pictures. Less small strips and more of a powder- like course ground coffee? kind of a chunky powder. Very even throughout, anyway.

I like it. I really like that it isnt loaded with salt. It is a good way to add in some protein without needing a lot. Seems like it would pair with most food, and easy incorporate into anything. Thinking maybe bake it into some low carb biscuits? ooh, mmm--ok, I'm totally doing that later using my CarbQuick, and using their cheddar bisquit recipe
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07XP97V8T

title: Quality, freshness, performance, taste: 5 stars
text:
Quality is great- packaging looks good, lentils cook up as expected, taste great. Zero issues or concerns.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. I find beans, legumes, and some grains are tricky to buy online as they are almost always much pricier than what I find locally. But if you cant find what you want locally, and are finding it here, then you can decide what a good price is. Personally, I think these look better than some of the lentil offerings I see in my stores.

Quality, freshness, performance, taste: 5 stars

title: lovely lemony ginger flavor, mixes easily, gives a little energy kick, I'd buy again
text:
I like Kombucha but sometimes the flavor is a little off putting, or the vinegar bite is too strong, so I was curious how a powdered instant version would fare. My go to flavor is Lemon Ginger, so I figured if I were to try an instant version it would make sense to try a familiar flavor.

Directions say to add one packet to 14-16 ounces of still water or carbonated water. I currently do not have any carbonated, so I used filtered water. It mixes very easily, and has a pleasant taste. It isnt too sweet for me. I can taste lemon first with a light ginger finish. It is nice tasting and refreshing. Love loading my cup with ice and sipping on it. I actually like it better than most bottled Kombucha because it doesnt have any of that apple cider taste. If that is what draws you to Kombucha, then you will miss it here.

I would consider this again

title: little goes long way, sweet & maplely, not perfect swap but it does greatly reduce sugar load
text:
A little runny, but the taste is good. I dont do pancakes and such often, but when I do I tend to use a lot of syrup. The less viscous texture makes it go further than a thick syrup. Having something that still tastes pretty good and not be ruined by a lot of excess sugar is great to have on hand. I mean, there is never going to be an exact swap. Maybe cut in a little of your preferred syrup in with this? I like it better than some sugar free options I have tried off the shelf. A bit pricy for the amount, but I really dont rate on price. It was something I wanted to try and I knew what I was paying going into it.

Anyway, I think it is worth trying.

title: my review is for their "Whole Cacao Superfood Trail Mix"; big fresh pieces
text:
Hm, I think I am the only one so far that has received an entirely different product. So I will describe what I have and rate accordingly. Maybe they will be adding it onto this product page as an option soon?

I have the WHOLE CACAO SUPERFOOD TRAIL MIX, 16 ounce bag.

This is basically a large bag of Organic whole cashews, Organic 70% chocolate (organic cocoa mass, organic coconut sugar, organic cocoa butter), Brazil nuts, dried cacao fruit, organic dried coconut, organic goji berries, organic cacao beans.

Not really a "by the handful" mix as the pieces are whole, or just large. You'll probably eat one piece at a time, or carefully add pieces together to pop in mouth. It is easier to pour some into a small bowl or bag, and then pick out pieces as you go. It is a nice mix for noshing, especially if you have a need for something a little sweet. Serving size is just one ounce (16 servings total), 150 calories, 3 grams fiber, 3 grams protein, 9 grams fat (3.5 saturated), very low sodium (10 mg), and low sugar (2g added).

I think I am enjoying this more than I would granola. Totally different application, but this has been an enjoyable snack. Sometimes I toss in a medjool date or two for added chew and sweetness-- makes me feel like I am eating a candy bar, especially when paired with the Brazil nut.

It's good. Attractive bag. Has a cool look. I would buy this (and the granola) as part of a food themed gift for someone (who likes stuff like this, of course).

5 stars for quality, presentation, overall taste profile. I'd consider this again.

title: POWER blend has 200 mg of caffeine per can
text:
Not too shabby. First sip was a little blegh, then subsequent sips were smooth and bubby. I really can't discern much flavor. Maybe a hint of strawberry? I dont taste watermelon. Which makes sense because it doesnt contain anything that refers to watermelon, just strawberry juice. So then, why call it watermelon? hmm

--10 calories per can (the write up says 5 calories)
--Propriety blend 370 mg. As for caffeine content, it says right in the description (in a few spots) that it has 200 mg of caffeine, and to not exceed 2 cans per day. They list their other blends, and indicate the amount of caffeine (if any). Try the FOCUS, or ENERGY for LESS caffeine, or DEFEND, RESCUE, or DREAM for NO caffeine).

4 pack at current price of $12 makes them $3 per can
12 pack at price of $30.00 makes them $2.50 per can
24 pack at price of $50.00 makes them $2.08 per can

In store, there isn't much I can buy of this ilk below $3, but if I were thinking I would consume it often, I would spring for the larger pack. But if trying it for first time, then the small pack is likely best. I dont rate on price.

Ingredients: carbonated water, erythritol, strawberry juice concentrate, citric acid, stevia leaf extract, and monk fruit extract.

I think it is delightfully fizzy, has a very light, nearly bland flavor, and not too sweet. I like it a lot overall. The caffeine level is perfect. If it had more, then I would be concerned with the jitters. I always have a big cup of coffee in the morning, then later I usually want a pick me up- whether to power me through rest of day or a work out. I just like having something. And I prefer that something to be cold. Bonus if it is fizzy. Pop usually isnt enough to take care of the caffeinated need, but this TRU POWER workout blend gives me a little added pep without jitters. I could just make some iced coffee, or iced matcha, but sometimes I want something different.. so I keep an assortment of drinks in a spare fridge to grab when the mood hits. Since this is more of a neutral flavor, I find it very easy to drink, and refreshing. I would consider this again. Maybe even try another formula.

title: lightly sweet, mild tasting cabbage drink. I find it quite pleasant room temp or cold
text:
Awe, I like it but I knew what to expect. Ya'll know what cabbage tastes like right? and what it smells like? This is that. While it has a light natural honey taste, I can also taste the sweetness from cabbage that cabbage gets when slow cooked. Also has a mild cabbage smell. For some, that will be awful.. so yeh, I think you have to like cabbage and not mind the smell of cabbage to appreciate this. It's so mild tasting to me that I think it would be palatable for most people.

I think it is a nice, lightly sweet, mild tasting, very easy to drink cabbage juice. There is not much per packet, but one doesnt need a lot at once. The packet is sturdy and easy enough to open. I prefer to cut the tip off and pour into a small glass. I drink it room temperature or cold, doesnt make a difference to me.

All the packets come nestles in a durable branded box. Hefty! Funny.. my mailing bag arrived open. I half wonder if someone was planning to steal the contents but when saw it was a box of cabbage juice they decided against it. LOL. That being said, the box may come in handy for hiding stuff in the house, haha.

title: good natural vanilla flavor, takes a little more than expected but good overall
text: good natural vanilla flavor. Smooth tasting, and smells really good. I expected it to be stronger though. I used more than expected in making a drink that I wanted to have natural vanilla flavor. I figured a few drops, when I really needed to use a few long squirts. Once I eventually got it to the flavor level I needed, then I thought it was good. But I think I can get same effect from a bottle of vanilla syrup. Anyway, good overall. I am curious about their banana cream option, so I may go ahead and buy that. If I do, I will add my thoughts on it to this review.

title: just banana- nothing added, nothing taken away. Flavor develops when mixed, allowed to sit
text:
If you have never had banana powder before, do not expect it to be as strong as a fresh banana. If you are familiar with banana powder, then this has typical flavor and performance. LOVE banana powder and once I tried it I have been keeping a pack on hand. Usually I add it to smoothies, sometimes sprinkled on oatmeal or yogurt, and sometimes even by the spoonful. Can be used in baking, cooking, etc. Can even be used to set make up ("bake" your make up with banana powder is a thing, and THIS banana powder is pale yellow and fairly fine.. so give it a whirl).

ANY Banana powder is mild despite being only being a single source ingredient (banana!). I have tried a few brands now, at different price points, and they are so very close in taste. Have you ever had dehydrated banana slices? it is more like that. I started using banana powder about 6 months ago. I like using it to flavor up my more dull tasting protein drinks or meal replacement drinks. I usually buy vanilla, and sometimes there is barely any taste. Banana powder- a few scoops worth- is typically what I use. 1 scoop typically having 5-6 grams in weight, closely equating to the volume of a tablespoon. I'd say that maybe 3 scoops equal a banana. Just really depends on degree of strength of flavor you are looking for.

Nutritionally they are all the same, and even though you are not using a fresh banana the calories, carbs, and sugar add up. Like a fresh banana, it has some potassium, magnesium. Not all dried banana products will list the full nutritional profile as they dont have to, but it doesnt mean those nutrients dont exist. For macros, there is .6 mg of fiber per scoop. Ok, so it isnt metamucil, but that's not bad for such a small volume of whole food.

I will say this.. the flavor is more robust if allowed to sit a few minutes in liquid. So when I add it to my non dairy milk, or protein drink- the first immediate sip doesnt have much taste. I let it sit for 5 minutes, and the flavor just seems to come through much more robustly, also my drink is thickened up a little.

THIS Microsingredients brand has included a scoop.

I think this brand is really good. I like Rainforest Supply a little better:
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08Q7K7BWB

title: complex flavors, but too tangy & bright for what is typically darker roast
text:
I expected a darker, bolder, more rich tasting Sumatra. This is firmly planted in the medium roast flavor profile with a hint of tang that I usually prefer to avoid. For that, I didnt enjoy it all that much. But if you are one to prefer a brighter tasting medium roast, I think this will be perfectly fine. If you tend to prefer darker, bolder, smoother roasts- and typically taste that from your preferred Sumatra coffee, then this will be disappointing.

I do concede that the flavor is complex. I dont question the quality or freshness. It just isnt what I expected, and hoped for. Those with more discerning taste buds will pick up on the nuances of flavor as they describe: herbaceous, hint of grapefruit, mild smoke, etc. BUT, the end notes for me are too tangy, too bright, too bittter. NOT what my usual Sumatra coffee normally tastes like.

--quality/freshness 5 stars
--desctiption integrity: 4 stars
--overall taste as it applies to description & expectation: 2 stars
--Overall rating.. middle of road 3, which indicates that this is "OK".

title: really holds in moisture, helps keep food tender.
text:
Lupin, Cassava, Salt, & cornstarch, "spices" and natural flavors. I really like this. I am familiar with Lupin and Cassava flours, so was curious for its use as a "bread crumb". It is nice to have a low glycemic option. Lower carb, has a good amount of fiber, has some protein. It does have a bit of sodium in it, so watch out if you are keeping track (310 mg per 3 Tbs serving. BTW).

Note that this is their ITALIAN seasoning variety, they also have a PLAIN option (much like one would find for regular bread crumbs). I use the plain for breading chicken or fish, and use this seasoned for meatloaf and meatballs. Though sometimes I just use oatmeal. or a mix. I didnt think lupin & cassava flour to work as well as it does. But it does work. When used in meatloaf/meatballs, it does not need as much added moisture that regular bread crumbs or oatmeal needs. Overall I like using this, but I will still keep an assortment of regular bread crumbs on hand. It is just different.

Carrington Farms has been around for a long time. I used to buy a lot of stuff from this brand when it was readily available in membership stores and other chains. I have no problem or concerns with this product or company.

title: organic matcha from Japan, reasonable price, good quality, would buy again
text:
It's good. It is one of the few products I buy based on price as I find most matcha pretty much tastes the same to me as I use it primarily in smoothies. I think the more discerning taste buds among us would notice nuances among brands especially when using for hot tea. But I use a copious amount blended into usually a vanilla meal replacement powder or protein powder, and it all tastes the same. So much so that I dump each bag I get into a larger canister.

Currently $16.99 for this 3 ounce packet. Price wise, it is right in the zone of price per ounce I typically see. This is "organic" and a product of Japan, so it is a little more budget friendly when those two aspects are taken into consideration.

That being said, I am a long time consumer of NOW brand foods and supplements. This matcha is as good as anticipated from this brand, and I would have no problem getting this again. I get a great sense of well being, sustained energy, and reduced desire for sweets when I consume matcha (1/8- 1/4 cup in my smoothie), so it is a frequent purchase for me.

title: subtle flavor, plenty of heat
text: Spicy. Solid heat level. The flavor is subtle, so this is mostly used for kicking up the heat in dishes. The bag is generic looking with no specific info on the pepper, just that the company is in USA with peppers from China.  The peppers look good, and there are plenty to work with. DOes not take much to make a dish flaming hot. Good amount to work with when making spicy chili oils.

title: works as intended- extra firm, sets quickly, no taste, etc

title: super high sodium in flavored milk, otherwise good flavor, fun treat
text:
I love trying new stuff, so I am pleased to have had the opportunity to try this especially the plan powdered camel milk. Higher nutrition than cows milk, and easier on the digestive system; nice option for lactose intolerant folks. Please see the sodium content I listed below as it is outrageous.

The flavored options are pretty good. Turmeric being my favorite as I often make turmeric and ginger drinks. Chocolate and Strawberry are about even to me. Now, the thing that concerns me is the SODIUM content. At the time of this review, the listing does not include nutritional information. The box does not display this information, but there are cards inside the box that display this info. They also have this same info on their website (I wondered if the information on the card was a typo, or I misinterpreted what I saw).

The plain has a typical naturally occurring sodium content of 130.6 mg, which is 5.7% DV That's fine. It is the flavored options that blow me away, check it out:

--Turmeric & Ashwagandha : 447.8 mg which is 18.6% of DV
--Chocolate Bourban: 775.8 mg which is 32.3% of DV
--Strawberry 930.8 mg which is 38.7% of DV

WOW

So yeh, these were fun to try, and I would consider plain camel milk products in the future, but I will avoid the flavored packets. It is just too much for what it is. One thing to eat my sodium, but to drink it? hard pass.

Rating:
4 for flavors, nice variety, fair pricing, cute packaging
3 for combination of extraordinary amount of sodium AND not having the nutritional profile listed here

overall 3.5

title: soft, chewy, sweet, absolutely delightful. Too good.
text:
SHUT UP. These taste like actual, real, fresh cookies. I cant ever buy these again?! LOL. The cookies are moist, chewy, sweet, chocolatey, rich.. and natural, in that there is no off taste (to me). They dont taste like an "alternative". I've tried many keto cookies, or low carb/low sugar cookies, and while most have been good enough, these Kabadbra cookies are the closest to an actual cookie I have ever had. Get them away from me. haha!

I am both delighted by this and disappointed, haha. I rely on foods of this nature to taste just off enough that I dont want to eat the whole bag. But these are so flippin good, that I am not sure if I can be trusted around these. They are in an open bag, and the cookies aren't all that big-- AND and a whopping 130 calories per cookie, this is going to be a challenge. Calories aren't entirely my worry, it really is all about reducing sugar intake (not because I am doing "keto", but because I am trying to not load my body with sugar, and also keep cravings at bay). But even so, it is hard to just grab one, and calories do add up. They are moist enough to stick together, but I can pull each one (so far) apart.

I didnt intend to go on a diet, but I found myself suddenly disinterested in sweet foods (after supplementing with vitamin D3, drinking more Matcha). I have had a life long compulsion to binge on sweet food (packages of donuts, entire cakes, full containers of ice cream, bags of candy-- every single day, usually in the evening). Just one bite would spark my brain to dive in for more. In the past when I would diet, I would "take control" by not consuming foods of that nature-- because get this-- my regular food intake was always otherwise healthy and within normal portions. So if I "just" cut out the sweets, I am already drastically cutting calories. It would be a hard few weeks, but after awhile my brain would not be scratching for that sugar hit. But all it would take is just one donut, one piece of cake (no such thing as rationing), and my brain would light up and become ravenous for all the sugar. Then I'd spiral back into that sugar madness, gain weight back. Rinse and repeat several times through my life.

This time around, I just lost the taste for wanting sweet. I didnt even try. It just happened. I am shocked, and I aim to keep it going for as long as possible. I dont have a drive for sweet, but sometimes I want a little something. If I have a non sugar treat, I think my brain wont go nuts for it. I have dreams of eating cake, cookies, etc.. but no real drive for it in day to day life. 4.5 months so far!

That's my story. I like these-- too much. Worth the try if you are looking for a tasty cookie

title: like everything about it, except for the choking hazard level of dryness. Hard to swallow!
text:
Nearly flavorless, dry, and looks like a thick kitchen sponge. Solid blue green, no swirls of color at all.

The GOOD: good sized portion. Thick square, feels like I am eating a piece of cake. Has a light, pleasant flavor. Not overly flavored, hint of sweet. Low sodium, goodly amount of protein and fiber. Good initial mouth feel (bit down, has cake texture), pairs well (like your life depends on it) with coffee. Well packaged. 5 stars

The BAD: looks like a thick kitchen sponge, still has 8 grams of added sugar. Not something I would call a brownie. Cake yes, brownie no. 3 stars

The UGLY: Very dry. Well, it has a moist outer crust. Some may think it is oily. This part doesnt bother me at all. It is when I go to swallow that I am concerned that I wont be able to finish swallowing. I have never experienced that with anything. Bite after bite, I found this true. I needed water or a cup of coffee to be able to comfortably swallow. Not cool. 1 star

My rating is primarily on how dry it is. I CAN NOT swallow this without also taking a sip of coffee. It is a choking hazard. Maybe my pack is bad, but others mention it in their reviews too. It is not just dry, but choking hazard dry. I am not sure if I have ever had something like that before. If it werent for that, I would rate this much higher. I like the blandness of flavor, the overall size. I dont even mind the odd look to it. I am not that picky! I WANT to like this. I love how they have many options, but since this is my first time trying something from this brand, I am reticent to buy a different option. If this simply had just a little more moisture (or fat), then I dont think it would feel like it is getting stuck in my throat. And it is only for this reason that my rating is centered around. Come back at me if the formula changes to something I can swallow. I'll probably work through this box- carefully with a cup of coffee.

I dont mind the taste. The flavor is supposed to be cotton candy, and there is just a hint of that flavor, which I think I like over a strong flavor. The thickness and texture is much more reminiscent of a slice of cake. Definitely not a brownie. The single serving size is impressive. I immediately thought of how perfect this would be for my upcoming birthday. I am off sugar desserts, but will gladly still partake in a low/no sugar option. I could add in some frosting or whipped cream.. but the dryness keeps me from being excited about this. I DID try it with some whipped cream and blueberries, and it was a lot better.. I could swallow it-- but I shouldnt have to worry about choking.

If I could swallow it with ease, I'd give these 4 stars & buy more.

title: multi-purpose. Love it paired w/ starchy foods
text:
Nice tangy, spicy kick. Very reminiscent of Kimchi. Has similar ingredients. The first ingredient is "kimchi". Take a look at the ingredient list, and if something doesn't look good to you then move on.

Kimchi seasoning:
Kimchi: (Napa cabbage, radish, water, Red pepper, Salt, Onion, Garlic, Sugar, Yeast extract, Palm oil, Paprika for color, Ginger), Red pepper Powder, Sugar, Rice powder, Sea Salt, Hot pepper powder, Dried onion, Sesame seed, Dried garlic, Ginger powder, Yeast extract

The flavor is nuanced. It will depend what it is being used on as to whether what parts of the blend come through, especially the heat. There is some spice! I really like this doused on potatoes and other starches. Try it on sweet potatoes, on Udon noodles, or as a seasoning for baked turnip "fries". OMG. I have made a quick dip (mayo, or sour cream, or Greek yogurt, depending on my mood) and added this in. When I do that, the heat is reduced but the other flavors are amplified. Pleasant on broiled vegetables (Brussels sprouts, carrots).

I am going to maybe try it as a rub, or added in with bread crumbs. I am very pleased with this seasoning and it is highly likely a repurchase for me.

title: great mix of dehydrated veggies for use in any dish you want
text:
Just dehydrated vegetables. What you do with it is up to you. At this point I have tried several Ekofungi products, and have been impressed with them all. Even the packaging is attractive. I wouldn't hesitate to buy anything from them for myself, but also as a food themed gift. Grab a cute bag or box, stuff it will several options from this company, maybe add in a few other goodies, and you will have a great gift.

This consume blend is incredible. Will work in so many different dishes- lovely, easy way to add a vegetable boost of flavor and nutrition. It isnt an all inclusive mix for a specific dish- you will need to add your own spices, and you can use it in any dish you want.

title: wonderful blend, great versatility, pantry staple worthy
text: Love Ekofungi products. This blend is really nice. And I can see so many different ways to use it that it is likely to become a pantry staple. While I dont make risotto, I do make a soup-stew hybrid using any vegetables on hand along with a box of Orzo pasta. This works so nicely, and tastes so good.

title: so good on and in everything. Try it on ice cream!
text:
EXCELLENT taste. I am already a huge fan of medjool dates, and so this is right up my ally for taste and sweetness level. It kind of reminds me of blackstrap molasses, but a little sweeter and milder. I could use these interchangeably. My first use of this was on low sugar vanilla ice cream. I knew then I was in love with it. I have tried it off the spoon, mixed in with coffee. Will likely use it on pancakes or waffles next time I make them. So this is a highly versatile item for me, and is likely a repurchase. YUM.

I had no idea that this has a lower glycemic level. I usually avoid sugars and syrups, but this is giving me options I didnt even know I had. Sometimes I would make real food desserts using pulverized medjool dates, and this product will definitely save me loads of time as I no longer need to use the food processer. Big win for me all around.

title: large chewy berries, nothing added, tart with hint of sweet, versatile!
text: New to me! These are large, soft, chewy dried berries that are wonderfully tart with a hint of sweet. Unlike a lot of other dried berries, these have nothing else add to it. No added sugar, no added juice. Nothing to alter the flavor or reduce the tartness level. JUST dried "golden berries". I LOVE THAT. I have been noshing on these alone. I would consider tossing these into a salad, oatmeal, adding to muffins or scones.  I find the texture very appealing too. All said, I am impressed.

title: mediocre taste, performance. Has an off flavor- more reminiscent of typical energy drinks
text:
Taste is ok- It still has that hint of "energy drink" taste despite having good ingredients. I do like the carbonation as I am a big fan of fizz. Tastes best when consumed as cold as can be. Sugar is a bit much for my preference. Although not all that sweet, it has 11 grams of added sugar in small 8.4 ounce can. 80 mg caffeine... which I never feel. I can not tell when I have consumed this. Overall its ok, but wont be a repurchase for me. I dont rate on price, but I do comment. Doesnt do enough, there isnt enough in a pack to warrant this having a $3 per can price tag. If you like these, then the 24 pack has much better value, bringing price per can to more doable $1.67.

I think I was just expecting a non energy drink taste. Something with a more natural, pleasant taste. There is just something about it that is off putting. 3 stars for me. It's just "OK"

title: for the love of ginger. Fresh, robust, delicious!
text: I love ginger, and I often use ginger powder for baking, cooking, in smoothies and teas, and other concoctions. I have used various brands over the years, and I think this is the best I have tasted. Acquired in 07/2021, it has 3 year date on it. Comes in typical pressure zip bag. Kraft style, not Mylar. Not my favorite style, but it seems to keep everything I have that uses that style fresh (though mylar is usually even better). Sometimes as powder works its way up to the pressure zip zipper, it wont create a tight seal. I automatically rubberband my bags.

title: dense  loaf of mushroom bread w/ pumpkin seeds. Easy directions, includes everything. YUM
text:
Small, dense, hearty bread. Delicious direct from oven with a little butter, or slice of cheese, or dipped into fondue pot, or as a side with soup. I found it easy to make. The directions are clear, and they include conversions. It is in the directions, and you can also see it in the product description.

Now, the title of this says "pumpkin bread", and that designation brings to mind something entirely different. I think that could true of many folks taking a quick glance at this. In reading the directions, I could tell that it wasn't going to be what I typically think of as pumpkin bread (sweet, tastes like pumpkin). THIS is a more savory bread from mushroom powder and includes pumpkin seeds. The title should reflect that, which would also be more accurate as the bag only says "mushbread", they dont call it pumpkin bread. I downrate to 4 because of that. That being said,

I like it, and I would buy it again. I like Ekofungi products, and this bread has been a nice treat. I dont always eat bread, but when I do it is usually homemade. This includes everything, doesnt require much prep, and it turns out nicely.

title: mushroom powder is a must have 'secret ingredient' for wide variety of dishes. Always in my pantry!
text: Seems so simple of an ingredient, but mushroom powder adds a boost of flavor that is stronger and richer than using fresh mushrooms. I am a big fan of keeping a container of mushroom powder in with my spices, and this is a good brand to use. Excellent taste, adds that certain something to just about anything. Definitely a secret ingredient for those who ask :)  Ekofungi makes some fantastic blends, I recommend checking out more of their products.

title: super versatile rich coconut milk, lovely in various dishes and for making ice cream
text:
Great addition to my pantry. I use coconut milk often enough that it is often on my grocery list. I dont always find it at my local grocer, and I dont always remember to look, so finding it online at a reasonable price is nice.

I often use Thai Kitchen products, including coconut milk, so this is as expected in taste and quality. Love using it to add richness and depth to a variety of dishes, or simply for adding flavor to smoothies and oatmeal. But my most recent use is for making ice cream. I have a great little ice cream maker, and it helps me especially when I want to take control of the ingredients, especially sugar.

Budget friendly Ice cream Maker that I use (still love it lots):
https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B07VVQ7XH4/

title: FANTASTIC flavor. Simple ingredients (listed below), no Ace-k for those looking to avoid it
text:
I have the MANGO option, and it is AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS. Totally what I want for making Boba (bubble) tea. Also makes for an awesome ice cream topping. I have used it to add flavor to pitchers of iced tea. The flavor really comes through! This mango flavor just works so well with everything. YUM!! I'll maybe try other flavors. Please come add Lychee (my favorite for green tea boba tea)

Looks like the formulations are different. The Mango flavor does not contain acesulfame K (Ace-K). The ingredients as listed on the MANGO option can be seen in their product pics, but I will include them here for quick reference:

-Mango Juice (30%)
-Fructose Sugar
-Water
-DL-Malic Acid
-Mango Flavor
-Sodium Citrate
-Yellow #5, Yellow #6
-Potassium Sorbate

title: WEAK! Butter Rum & others have very little flavor. Smells great, but very weak taste
text:
In short: Butter Rum falls way short in flavor. I can smell it, but I cant taste it. Not even passable. Better off using a sugar free butter rum syrup, or extract w/ sweetener of choice.

I have had the opportunity to try 4 varieties of Stevia Sweet & Natural Premium liquid. The flavors I have are this Butter Rum, Pumpkin Spice, Gingerbread, and Root beer. My review is pretty much same for all.

They all smell fantastic. The scent permeates the bottle, and fills up the drawer I keep them in. They are all sweet (as expected), and easy to work with, but that is where the similarities stop. Somehow, while they all smell amazing, only the Pumpkin Spice has any real flavor. Even so, not sure if it is robust enough to suit my needs. Seems like I need to use a lot. Maybe I haven't tried them in the correct vehicle (maybe better in food then drink, etc), but I really cant taste any other than the Pumpkin Spice. I am sorely disappointed. I really wanted a good Butter Rum sweetener for use in coffee, baking, and ice cream making. BOO :(

I do not rate on price- you decide for yourself if you want to buy it or not, but I do comment. This pack of three was $38 for a pack of three at time of order. What equates to $12.66 per 1 ounce bottle for liquid sweetener prohibits me from buying this again. Says to use 5-8 drops, but that doesnt work for getting the flavor. Sweetness, yes. Flavor, no. It takes too much to get the flavor to come through all the while making whatever you have sweeter and sweeter. If it had stronger flavor, or some other wow factor, then I would reconsider. As of now, I would be better off to use an extract plus a packet of sweetener (or other liquid drops). OR a sugar free syrup. The flavor just isnt there enough for me.

That being said, I rate on quality and overall opinion of the product itself. This just has barely any taste. I can only tell it is Butter Rum because of the amazing smell. But once used in anything (currently have tried it with coffee and cream), I could not taste anything other than sweetness--though I can say that all of these are smooth. Nothing bitter, no off taste. If it just had more of the actual flavor, I would be so much happier. I dont need a bottle of plain liquid sweetener, I want a flavored sweetener! I if it were stronger, I would be pleased, but it falls short.

Refrigerate after opening. Acquired 07/2021 with expiration of 10/22
