title: sweet and floral, definitely leans more tea-like rather than coffee alternative-like
text:
As a tea, it's good. As a coffee alternative, it is a bit flat and watery. I have consumed coffee alternatives in the past, including options from Teccino that have been near coffee swaps, but this falls short. Has a light sweet taste, hint of floral. I like it as an iced beverage. Maybe in colder weather I will drink it to help warm myself up. Kinda was hoping though for a little more "coffee" taste. Usually chicory, dandelion, and carob are a sure thing for providing that coffee vibe. Maybe it is the addition of Tulsi. Mushroom should lend to more coffee taste too. Ah well, I tried and now I know.

I tried using less water, and tried doubling up the tea bags, but this is best for me consumed as an iced tea.

3.5 stars

title: fun name, great mix of fruit and seeds. 2 tbs serving provides 6 grams fiber
text:
8 servings per bag, serving size is 2 TBS. I usually use between 1 and 2 TBS to be sprinkled into my yogurt or oatmeal. Loaded with seeds and berries, it is nutritionally dense, and calorically dense as well (130 cals per 2 TBS serving). It has a bland taste, but it is a welcome addition to my yogurt or oatmeal bowls where I usually top it with fresh or dried fruit, granola, nuts, seeds, or whatever else looks good. Adds a nice dose of fiber (6 grams per serving). I likely wouldnt eat this as a bowl of cereal, but I can see maybe adding it into pancakes, or muffins.

Be sure to check your teeth for seeds after!

Acquired 07/2021 with Best By date of 11/2022

title: pretty tasty for a shelf stable convenience item, good hot or even cold
text:
I have the Mushroom Masala option. I eat the whole pouch. Not too shabby nutritional profile, and the ingredients look healthy. Has some fat, protein, fiber, and fairly low calories. High sodium is offset a little by the generous amount of potassium. Taste is decent. Could use a little more flavor. Certainly not restaurant level, or home cooked level.. but for what it is-- a shelf stable convenience item? Sure, I like it and will most likely buy it again. Try some other varieties too. Pairs excellent with rice. I have also eaten it with some naan, or pita bread, and even tortilla wraps. While I prefer it heated up, it does work in a pinch eaten room temperature, direct from bag with nothing else.

Nutritional info can be seen in their product pictures, last photo.

title: good depth of flavor, small non stabby chip, low level heat- doesnt build much
text:
Habanero flavor is tasty! They have a slight building heat, but definitely does not scorch the taste buds. There is just a lot of flavor- nuanced, subtle, multi layered, with a kick of heat. The smaller size chips make them easy to pop into mouth, yet just large enough to skim some dip. While I totally prefer a regular tortilla chip, these are welcome in my pantry anytime. Though for a whopping $7 a bag, likely not often.

Small 5 ounce bags, pack of two. All the chips looked good (not smashed up).

title: smooth, easy to drink, neutral tasting, less caffeine than coffee, works well added to coffee
text:
I prefer this mixed in with other coffee over drinking it as my coffee source. I really like this added into coffee. I regularly use mushroom supplements, and I always drink coffee, so I had to try this blend. I like it. I am happy that it has a smooth taste, but not exactly a coffee taste. It is kind of neutral. Makes it easy to blend in to other foods and drinks. Overall is good, and is very easy to drink.

There is something in the background that I cant quite figure out, but it isnt bad. I assume it is one of the mushrooms as each one has their own taste, and there are a few mushrooms here I dont think I have ever had. Doesnt stand out, just sort of plays on my tastebuds. Very interesting to me. Pleasant.

I have had other instant coffee mushroom blends, and this is the most smooth. Has a little less caffeine I guess than just coffee, so you will need to adjust for that, as well as for taste. I either stir this into my cup of coffee, or make a cup of instant using this and a packet of my own plain instant coffee (and sometimes more of one of my mushroom powders). Could also be added to a smoothie- especially chocolate. Mmm!

36 servings, give or take depending on how much you use. That is true of all the instant stuff as well as plain mushroom supplements.

title: very fresh, very moist, very sweet. Exactly how they should be.
text:
I prefer medjool dates WITH pits rather than without as they are much more likely to maintain their softness, freshness, delightful chewiness over ones without- which are more apt to dry out quicker. I am a long time consumer of medjool dates, so I kinda am specific on what I am looking for. These didnt say pitted, so I assumed they came with pits. Glad they do.

That being said, these taste as good as expected. I dont rate on price, but these are nearly double what I normally pay in store or online for one pound. Even so I wouldnt hesitate to buy these again, or try other products from this company. The freshness is on point.

My favorite use for them is to just eat them as is. I really love pairing them with a Brazil nut. I take the pit out, and slide a brazil nut or two inside, then eat it that way. Nearly tastes like a candy bar! There are some other natural snacks I make- maybe add in some coconut, nuts, chocolate, puffed cereal. Just sort of create sweet balls to nosh on.

Totally awesome processed into a paste for use in baking too.

Comes in a pressure zip bag. I clip the bag closed tightly to keep air out, and also because the pressure zip doesnt always catch fully.

title: what a flavor combo- garlicky w/ complex tasty heat, undertone of truffle
text:
Piquant, and very garlic forward with an underlying truffle taste. Must love truffle!.Hint of spice, loads of flavor. I love these Bougie BBQ seasoning blends. They are highly versatile, and make for great flavor on a wide host of dishes. Potatoes, pasta, eggs, chicken, and pork so far with this one. Ingredients are simple, straight forward, but complex in the taste they bring forward. I have three blends in my kitchen, and they are all good. Acquired 07/2021 with best by date of 09/2023

As with the others, the only thing I dislike is the cap. There is a generous amount of seasoning in these stout aluminum containers. The seasonings come bagged and stuffed inside. The cap is my only turn off. I like the container save for the fact that the lid comes off easily. It is otherwise a visually interesting design, and has a neat shaker top. Instead of being on top, the shaker or pour options are on the side. Seasoning is bagged for shipment, comes well packaged. Looks good, gift worthy. The cap/lid though troubles me. DO NOT GRAB IT BY THE LID, or it will just slide right off. It has happened to me, and fortunately I caught it before it totally fell off. When I reviewed a different spice blend, I mentioned this cap, but at the time I hadnt had one fall off yet. But now I can say that it has. I keep my spices in a drawer, so grabbing from the top is the norm. Or even picking up from the counter top. I hope it doesnt accidentally fall off while shaking spices out--that worries me most. OMG.

Even so, I would still buy these, and would still maybe consider them a gift.

title: delicious olives, great texture, fantastic in salads, or just noshing direct from jar
text:
My jars arrived fully intact and looking good. I immediately set out to try these olives. YUM!
Select "most recent reviews" in order to see reviews more relevant to your purchase, otherwise you are seeing older stuff that may have since resolved. The new reviews here are quite favorable, including mine. There is bound to be a dud in the batch or shipping, so hopefully you have a good experience, and if not, then the company rectifies it. I have had only good experience, and will consider buying these again.

This review is for both the GARLIC variety and the FETA variety, as I had purchased one of each. I eat a lot of olives. I find they really hit the spot when I need something to eat but dont want to commit to a meal. Or if it is getting close to meal time, and I need something to fend off the hunger for a bit. I'll eat 4-8 large olives and be satisfied. I love pretty much all olives, but I do particularly enjoy olives stuffed with garlic, feta, or blue cheese. Mmm! Also makes for lovely addition to salads.

As with ANY soft cheese stuffed olive, some of the guts are prone to come out. Doesnt matter where I have gotten them from, or what brand. Best to get a firm cheese, or other firm stuffing if you really need the guts to be fully packed.

title: Five, 50g (@1/2c) servings. Nutritional info listed below. GREAT ingredients, little bland
text:
Nutritional information included at end of review. Tis is a 250 gram box (8.8 ounces). There are five, 50 gram servings in a box, 202 calories per serving. I will include pics of what this amount looks like. Very typical amount for granola, and it equates to about 1/2 cup. I weighed it all out. $1.79 per serving at current price of $8.95. I dont rate on price, but I will comment that it is a little more than other offerings of similar composition. You will have to decide if it is worthwhile- we all have different budgets and needs.

Nice mix of ingredients, very good nutritional profile (see end of my review), and seems like a quality product. I have zero concerns with it. Small sized particles. Easy on the teeth. I like it, but I find both the texture and the taste a little bland. I really appreciate that it does not have a strong sweet taste. Just a hint. I would like to take a little more strawberry. Perhaps if I ate it hot. I have only been eating it mixed in with yogurt. By itself, I can pick up nuances of flavor. All very subtle. Your taste buds may very, haha.

Everything about it is rather neutral. Looks good though! I have been adding it to my yogurt bowls. If I were to bake some muffins I would be inclined to sprinkle this on top. I have no desire to eat this as a "milk and cereal" option, but I would consider adding it in with a cereal that I do eat like that (cheerios, etc), or sprinkled on top of oat meal. Dry is good too.

title: Robusta beans have more caffeine zing! Surprisingly excellent- smooth, tasty.
text:
I liked this instantly! I drink all sorts of coffee- from whole beans, ground, instant, hot, iced, cold brew, hot brewed, pour over, drip, Keurig, french press, Turkish, etc. Usually prefer super dark roasts, usually avoid light roasts. Prefer black coffee, but sometimes will use cream and sugar. Basically...If it has caffeine, I will drink it. I always keep instant on hand for emergencies, and because I rather like it. Sometimes it just hits the spot over other options. Also works great in smoothies, baking, and for a quick shaken iced coffee. So of course i had to try this. I rather expected it to be.. "OK". But it has a wow factor for me. I think it is the least "instant" tasting that I have had in awhile. Nothing is mentioned in the product description, and I only noticed it on the box after I had a couple of cups (was curious why it tasted so good, and in hindsight why I felt extra amped up). IT IS ROBUSTA coffee, not Arabica. Usually robusta has an off taste for me, but this is super smooth and tastes just right. Now it makes sense why I felt an extra zing, as robusta has more caffeine than other beans. Usually when robusta is used, it is make clear in the description as a selling point for extra caffeine.

Large coffee bits disintegrate quickly with hot or cold water. Directions say to use 8-10 ounces of water. I prefer it with 6 ounces of water, or to use a couple of packs for a full mug of coffee. BUT it isnt totally horrible using their ratio. Just work with it to determine best taste for you.

I normally drink my coffee black, but usually instant needs a little help with some cream (and sometimes sweetener). I think I am in love with this Slow Ride Instant Coffee because THIS is actually smooth and robust (and it is only a medium roast. I prefer dark!), and tastes great all by itself. YAY!!. It is very easy to drink. Quite enjoyable. I am getting an urge for another cup as I write this, so I think I will now go make another cup of coffee. I keep a well stocked coffee cabinet that includes Starbucks Via (all roast levels) as well as a few others. Pretty sure this Slow Ride Instant Coffee is my new go-to option. Really enjoying it.

That's my opinion on this, anyway. I am stoked to find such a good tasting instant. $20 for pack of 30. Nicely packaged. Would make a nice addition to a coffee themed gift.

title: Another reat functional FITNE coffee product. Makes for lovely dark cup of sweet coffee. Try ICED!
text:
To prepare, add 120 ml-- which is a mere 4 ounces--of hot water. Stir. Enjoy. I LOVE the taste. It has a good (to me) coffee taste, but a little more sweet than I normally go for. I dont taste much of anything else. But I am used to FITNE coffee products, and drink them almost daily. I love seeing the light froth that forms. I think this is crema, which can form on espresso or other strong coffee. "Crema is a flavorful, aromatic, reddish-brown froth that rests on top of a shot of espresso. It is formed when air bubbles combine with fine-ground coffee's soluble oils."

So, if prepared with just 4 ounces of water, it makes for a good strong cup of coffee. Add more water to suit taste. When I make it with just 4 ounces of water it reminds me more of Turkish coffee, or an espresso. Less of an instant coffee taste. Divine.

Lovely hot, but I love love love this over ice. I usually use 2 packets, OR I use 1 packet added to regular brewed coffee to give it a stronger coffee taste that would otherwise be watered down by the ice. It is delicious. When I drink this, I definitely feel that beautiful fog lift from caffeine. Sometimes I add a packet to hot brewed coffee just to add to the taste. Options!

These products aren't for everyone, but they are perfect for me. I have used various FITNE coffee products, and have been repurchasing their Instant 3 in 1 white kidney bean, l-lysine, b vitamin blend. https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08WWFVQD1
After my initial excellent experience, I have been trying anything and everything they come out with.
They have other nutrient "functional" blends such as one with collagen, and one that has apple extract. All taste like coffee, most all have non dairy creamer, all have sweetener. All have supplements. And all have been a delight to me. But Now that I have tried this black coffee, I would say this might be my favorite, or at least tied with the one I linked to.

Just an interesting selection of functional products to choose from with added supplements. This FITNE instant coffee option has the addition of Coenzyme Q10 & L Carnitine. Unlike the others which contain loads of added creamer, this one is pretty much just black coffee with added sweetener and supplements.

I'm just a big fan of Fitne, and was excited to try this black coffee version. I am greatly enjoying it and will now be buying more. Hence, 5 stars.

title: Everything blend is crunchy & tasty blend. Light on kelp taste.  Goes great with many dishes
text:
This review is for the Barnacle "Everything" seasoning (kelp, garlic, onion, sesame seed, salt, poppy seed)

Really good blend of "everything" seasonings. Garlic is most notable, followed by onion. Large flaky pieces- all add a nice crunch. Sesame and poppy seeds add a burst of flavor when they get chomped down on. Love the overall texture. Very much reminds me of "everything" bagel seasoning with the addition of kelp.

I have tried this plain, as well as mixed into dishes as the were cooking, and as a finishing seasoning before plating. To me, the kelp sits in the background. I love kelp, but it isn't something I want all the time. I figured if this was "kelp forward" then I would have limited (but still enjoyable) use. However, with this the kelp is very much in the background. I can taste it because I am looking for it, but no one in my house has commented on there being a kelp flavor. So, this is good or bad depending on what you are looking for. I think it is done well. I like how it imparts an umami taste without the fishy-seaweed taste that some kelp can have. Gain the benefit of kelp without it having to pair well Just the right amount of salt.

Comes in a short pot, twist off lid, with wide opening. Perfect for spooning out, or grabbing a pinch. BUT, a wide hole shaker would make it easier to use. Also, until further into the container (its packed to the brim), it is hard to shake to make sure it is well mixed. For all I know, all the kelp is at the bottom? And for those that say it is a strong kelp flavor might have it all on top? lol I have no idea. It looks mixed, but who knows.

Overall I like it a lot. 4.5 stars

title: Basil, Oregano, Thyme, Marjoram, Lavender, Rosemary//Lovely scent & flavor. Versatile use!
text:
This is one of those spice blends that is easy to grab for and use in pretty much everything. Listed in the "important information" portion of this product page, the ingredients are just: Basil, Oregano, Thyme, Marjoram, Lavender, Rosemary

So far I have used it on small potatoes, an assortment of vegetables, and as part of a "breakfast for dinner" where I make a hash of the sort using crumbled sausage, cut up white potatoes, cut up sweet potatoes, green peppers, red peppers, onion, kale, and mushrooms (all items I tend to keep on hand), then add a variety of seasonings. Likely awesome on pizza, pasta, etc.

Very pleased with this seasoning blend. Nice balance of flavor, with a little added something that exceeds my expectations.

title: perfectly fine bag of xanthan gum for all your binding, texture, thickening needs
text: I have had no problems with the quality of any of the "It's Just" products I have used over the past couple of years. Xanthan gum often comes up in recipes- particularly those centered around gluten free and/or low carb. When working with flour alternatives, there is a need for this ingredient to help the texture, and to encourage binding. It can also be used for thickening, stabilizing like one would use flour, cornstarch, or arrowroot powder (some are gluten free, some not, and some not keto friendly). Just know that it is gluten free and can be used as one would for thickening gravies, soups, etc. Also, keto friendly for those who follow that.

title: good size flakes, lovely cheesy/umami taste, fortified or those looking for B vitamins
text:
I have used many other brands of nutritional yeast (nooch) over the years. They are pretty much all the same. Some (But rarely) add salt or other flavoring, some have more of a powdered texture, some it is either a matter of being fortified with B vitamins or not at all. Which one you use is based on your needs and preferences. I dont need the added B, so I usually buy non fortified. All good either way. This is JUST nutritional yeast. Good sized flakes. NO added anything, well nothing besides B vitamins. THAT's IT. Nutritional Yeast can be purchased with or without added b vitamins (they have, or did have a non fortified offering which I got last year--yum). The latter is truly best for those that are low in these vitamins and otherwise dont get it from their diet (vegans).

I love nooch. I am not vegan, not even a vegetarian. I just love good food, good seasoning, and I love to eat. I always have a bag or three of nooch on hand. It is a great cheesy like seasoning. It is not actual cheese, nor does it fully taste like cheese. But it has an appealing cheesy-esque flavor. I'll usually sprinkle it on vegetables, or add it to meatball/meatloaf mix. But my main use is for making a quick "mac n cheese" using one of my favorite noodles and a copious amount of nooch. I'll sometimes add a little pasta water to it (thicken, make creamy), maybe a splash of olive oil, and other seasonings. Makes for a yummy quick lunch. Bentilla Zimmunity noodles: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DVCDPJ6

Good stuff, no issues, exactly what I expect and what I am used to. $12.99 at time of review is fair price for this 15 ounce pressure zipped bag of nooch.

title: perfectly good chip- thick, just enough salt & oil. Shipping/packaging= flat bag
text:
The chips are good. If I saw these in store, I wouldn't hesitate to grab them. They have the ripple shape of Lays, but aren't nearly as greasy and salty. These are more dry, perhaps more similar to Utz or Herr. Has enough oil and salt to be tasty, yet doesn't leave my hands greasy. Thick enough to handle a generous amount of dip. Good stuff. Perfectly good chip.

My disappointment comes in because the bag was flat when it arrived. Not much air. Came in a box with some air packs. I figured I would be opening up a bag of crushed chips, and indeed that was the case. Still enough large pieces to enjoy, but not enough full chips. I imagine it is strictly a matter of how it was handled and shipped. It would be better if these were offered as a case (or at least 2 or more) and packaged/shipped on its own so it maintains integrity of bag and contents. I am able to buy other chips and such like that from Amazon like that with no issue.

I do not rate overall on price (we all have our own budgets), but I sure will comment: I am floored over the nearly $10 price tag for a basic (albeit tasty) 9 ounce bag of chips. WOWZA! (will be reflected in the "rate features" portion).

title: balanced, smooth medium, robust but not bitter, likely appeal to wide range of tastes
text:
Pretty good bean. The bag of whole beans smell amazing when I open the bag. I much prefer dark roasts, but I am game for a well balanced medium, or dark learning medium. This is both. I can tell that it is a medium roast, but it has such a smooth flavor that the notes of the roast come through. It is overall pleasant and easy to drink. KI think this would satisfy a wide audience.

I find that it is pretty good black (I prefer black, especially with dark roasts, but any lighter roast tends to taste better with a little cream. Might be because it tempers any acid or bitterness), and it also holds up well to some cream. Tastes better hot rather than iced--some odd flavors come through to me

I dont rate on price as we all have different budgets and values. I love a good coffee and will pay nearly anything for it. I may not buy this again, but I would certainly recommend it or purchase it as part of a gift. I may give their decaff a try, and if they have a dark roast I would certainly likely enjoy that even more so.

title: one of my favorite foods, flavors. Excellent pack of seaweed sheets. YUM

title: like a concentrated honey taste, easy to use squirt liquid

title: love my Wylers lemonade- great as is, or add squirt of lemon for added tartness

title: just quinoa & chia- no added anything. Makes for a lovely crunchy snack as is
text:
I am loving this cereal as is, dry. I have been wanting to find a new snack, and it did not occur to me to try a cereal. This is a game changer for me. I wanted something unsweetened and unsalted. Just something to pop into my mouth and enjoy. Kind of like how people want popcorn (blegh). Now I have this. This works. I just have to portion it out, otherwise I could gobble the whole bag. Though considering some of the things I used to eat as snacks, it just has 600 calories for the whole bag. I could never actually eat it all in one sitting, but I like to look at things like that. It is a densely packed bag, very little left over spacing. Plan to use a chip clip or put into a zip lock bag or other container.

The nutty taste of quinoa and chia are evident. Likely less so when mixed in with milk, or yogurt. Not a cereal for those that prefer sweet. This is a lightly puffed, gently crunchy (doesnt hurt teeth), light tasting, almost neutral in flavor cereal. I really like it, and greatly appreciate the simplicity of it. Seriously: just quinoa and chia. YAY!

Sometimes I make my own marshmallows (unsweetened, or sugar controlled), and use it not only for use in hot cocoa etc, but also in homemade "rice crispy" treats. Instead of the rice cereal, I will use a natural, unsweetened puffed cereal or combo of cereals. I may add this in next time as the texture and taste would be pleasant to me to munch on.

title: delicious, light sweet ginger shavings. Tasty enough to snack on alone
text:
It is a lovely mild ginger that works well as a palate cleanser, for an additional pop of flavor in a multitude of dishes, or simply as a snack (sometimes I stand at fridge nibbling olives, pickles, ginger, etc). title: GREAT for homemade marshmallows (control sugar), & all other gelling needs, try in smoothies
text:
Gelatin dissolves in hot liquid, gels in cold. This is a good Gelatin that gels :) I prefer to buy brands that let me know what the origin of cows were used, and preferably grass fed (even though I am not sure if any can actually guarantee the latter). I dont rate on price, but this is perhaps the most expensive I have purchased for the size: 17.6 ounces for $25, $1.42 ounce.

That all being said, it seems perfectly fine. It works as expected. If you are using this strictly for health reasons, I recommend starting off low and slow and allow your gut to acclimate. Sometimes the sudden bump in protein and/or the fact that it isn't hydrolyzed peptides (already broken down into usable form) can trigger some digestive upset to start. Not everyone, but some. Sometimes I see mention of this in various collagen or gelatin products, and I know it is likely they started with too much, too often, too quickly. When used in recipes, it doesn't seem to have that effect. But yeh, gelatin is awesome for hair, skin, nails!

For thickening, say in a smoothie.. if you dont want to just add it in (it wont dissolve, but wont be too gritty), it can be prepped by add some powder to a small amount of hot water-- just enough to get it to dissolve, THEN add to your smoothie, which will then help thicken it, add a nice texture.

Been awhile since I have used a beef gelatin product. I was using stuff like this before hydrolyzed collagen became ubiquitous. Even though beef gelatin isn't broken down into peptides for quick, easy absorption, it still works really well for nutritional needs (especially hair nails), and is a very cheap option over hydrolyzed. The pro (or con) depending on what your needs are, is that it does not mix into cold liquid (does ok in smoothies); it needs hot (so coffee is good vehicle to mix it into, or soup). BUT, once cold, it sets into.. gelatin! Funny to have a cup of coffee flavored jello. Alas, it can be reheated and will turn back into liquid. Those days had been long gone as I have been using hydrolyzed products for many years now. BUT, I still have a need for gelatin in the kitchen, so I keep a small container on hand for that reason.

In cooking and baking, gelatin adds smoothness & creaminess in higher liquid volume foods (think mousse), and it is definitely used for solidifying liquids into a gel (ie like jello). You can make your own jello, gummies, MARSHMALLOWS!! (If you have never made your own marshmallows, or want to control the amount of sugar that goes into them, home made marshmallows are not complicated to make). Good for making a quick "jam/jelly", and so on,.

The beef gelatin is packed in a bag, packed in a box. No flavor that I can discern. I am super used to consuming stuff like this, so it could be that my taste buds aren't as sensitive to any flavors gelatin may impart anymore.

Toss up between 4 & 5 stars as I really see nothing wrong with it. You decide!
Made in China

title: good flavor spray for all sorts of food applications
text:
A truffle spray for use on anything, not at all limited to use on popcorn. All the aerosol and pump style butters and oils have calories even when it says zero. It isn't misleading if you know the rules of labeling. When used in applications such as this, if the amount (sprays, weight, size) per serving is less than X amount (ie, close to zero), then it can be considered zero calorie. But taken as a whole (ie entire contents, or other vastly large portion) then yes it accumulates into a more sizeable calorie distinction. So since I am not counting my sprays, or length of time, I just dont care.. I know I am not using the whole bottle. If I am using a lot, then I just assume I am using 1 serving of oil. But for the most part, I just spray away as I am using it to flavor my food and to enjoy it.

title: JUST fruit, nothing added, love dehydrated delicious fruit. Such a treat!
text:

So I would totally gobble up dried banana slices but almost always there is added oil and sugar. But NOT freeze dried bananas (or other fruit). It is JUST fruit. The freeze dried equivalent (all water has been removed) is 6 strawberries and 1 banana. And just 50 calories for the whole bag. I tend to just much on these fruit pieces direct from bag, but they are also great when added to yogurt, ice cream, or oatmeal. If they are in liquid long enough, they reconstitute a little. So plan accordingly.

An open bag is usually an empty bag for me, but sometimes I just pop out a few pieces and set the rest aside. Grab a little chip clip, baggy, piece of tape or whatever to keep bag closed.

I would buy these again. They taste like all other brands I have tried (and are from China, like all other brands I buy). I can get them (another brand) for half the price at a local dollar general, but not all those stores carry dehydrated fruit and I am not driving all over to find it. When I do, I only buy strawberry and banana so to find them here in a pack of 6 rocks my world.

PS, As with ANY freeze dried food, if it is super humid out, the food could be accidentally reconstituted. If its humid and you have an open pack, I think placing in fridge will protect it (or toss it in oatmeal and carry on!)

title: rich thick cracker that is easy on the teeth, taste good plain or w/ pungent flavors

title: Loads of nutrition, very mild taste, mixes well, beware licorice/Blood Pressure
text:
So many ingredients, I expected a terrible taste, or to overcompensate by being too sweet, or fake tasting. Most greens blends can be a little rough tasting. This is surprisingly.. OK! I initially tried this as is, as directed: 1 scoop to 10-12 ounces of water, shaken vigorously. I then took a sip, and was pleased that is had a light, neutral taste. Didn't make my taste buds sing, but didnt make my taste buds scream, either, haha! And for that I am happy with this product.

I find that it mixes well in with a vanilla meal replacement or protein powder. I tend to make a matcha smoothie, and I just added this powder in with it. Because the flavor of this is rather neutral, it just disappeared among everything else. Besides the impressive assortment of nutritional goodies, I think the main draw is that is isn't gross, that it is fairly neutral tasting, not too sweet, is palatable consumed by itself, or mixes in really well with other powders, juices, etc. Can be easily modified (want it more sweet? add your own sweetener, etc). Also mixes easily. No fuss.

I rely on smoothies, or supplements of this nature because there is only so much food I can eat, and only so much I can afford, and only so much I can find in my neck of the woods. I eat fresh, but I supplement greatly. When I am making use of powdered supplements like this, I can usually forgo my multi-vitamin capsules. Even with a well rounded diet, I use supplements to bridge the gap. Makes all the difference to me, so I look for stuff like SuperGreens72 to fortify my life. I like knowing that I am adding a wide variety of foods into my diet with this powder. While I kinda scoff at the price, I dont rate on it. I've purchased stuff for more per ounce. I think if it fits a need, and if it looks good to you then go for it.

Of all the ingredients, only one really stands out as something I would rather not be in there, and that is the licorice. It doesn't come through at all on taste, but it is something that anyone with high blood pressure should look out for. For some, it can exacerbate elevated blood pressure. It does this by reducing potassium, so make sure your electrolytes are in check (there is some potassium in this), and if you are about to take a reading make sure you haven't consumed "Glycyrrhiza glabra" (legit, real licorice).

Hefty, 1 lb pressure zip bag. I dont love the bag, but its doable. I find it easy to store in the fridge (which is what is recommended).

4.5 stars

title: fresh, tasty, onion goodness
text: We go through a lot of onion powder. We put it in and on everything. Good size, good brand, good stuff. We have it on regular re-order as we are pleased enough with it to not bother looking at other brands

title: pitcher = 64 ounces, add 2 packs to one pitcher. Good, but undertone of something odd
text:
Add two packs to a pitcher. What size is a pitcher? I have small pitchers, and large pitchers. The directions just say "add 2 packs to a pitcher and let brew for 20-24 hours". For clarification, they use 64 ounces as pitcher size, which is what I happened to use. I contacted them directly and was told this. So then, add more water or less water depending on your taste preference. Or use one pack to 32 ounces for a smaller batch.

2 packs added to 64 ounces of water (little less, maybe 60 ounces) and let sit to "brew" for 30 hours makes for a decent tasting cold brew. Not bitter (through cold brew never is). I have had better, but this is pretty good. I just find that it has a little off taste, not bad enough to not drink it, but off enough that I dont like it black (which is my preferred taste). Smells dark but tastes more medium? My next brew will use less water, perhaps that will make it taste better to me. If so I will be back to update.

Overall, I really like the convenience of it, and how there is no mess. The packs smell amazing.

title: super low calorie noodle, rinse thoroughly, then do what you want with it
text:
Just like an other shirataki noodle. Be sure to rinse the noodles well to remove any odd taste. After that, they will be nearly flavorless. I have been eating shirataki noodles (various styles) on and off for years. Such a cool way to have noodles and not have the calorie and carbohydrate hit. I like the skinny noodles the best, such as these capellini noodles. Shirataki noodles can be a little weird to work with as there is a slight rubbery texture, but they are worthwhile addition to a diet.

I find that I like these (and any shirataki noodle) best when mixed in with a little regular noodle. Provides a better mouth feel. Gives me more of the original experience so my brain and taste buds aren't wondering so much what happened, lol. I figure I am still getting my spaghetti, but not as much calories and carbs since I am cutting in with shirataki noodle. Even so, no matter how I have these noodles, I prefer it prepared in any way except for use with spaghetti sauce (ultimately no replacement for semolina), but prepared with anything else? yes! Love it with various oils, sauces, butters, seasonings, vegetables, and usually if I add a protein I go with chicken or shrimp. I tend to eat a lot, so if I can make substitutions, or bulk up my meals, then I do so. Shirataki noodles help with that. I think they are best for those that are dieting. I mean, at 10 calories per serving (20 calories total), it's a caloric bargain!

title: delicate Banh Hoi rice noodle sheets for use in light dishes & appetizers, not a soup noodle
text:
Delicate thin rice noodle sheets. For use in light dishes and appetizers. Cooks up quickly, easily. Do not let sit in broth or other liquid. It might work, but it isnt a soup noodle, and is really not priced for soup use. Try a different rice noodle for that. Nor is it a sticky noodle. This is a specially prepared rice noodle sheet for use in lightweight applications. The product picture includes a perfect depiction of how they are often used.

Add TO boiling water, let soften for 2 minutes, then drain and do a quick light rinse with cool water. Then take the intact sheets, and process with whatever flavorings you want. It is something that gets wrapped with something, or rolled and topped with a flavored oil & scallions, and/or is set next to a protein.

I found these easy to work with, and they were manageable, held up well, and I would buy these again. When you need a Bahn Hoi rice noodle, this is very good. If you just want rice noodles, then other styles are better. Bahn Hoi rice noodles are typically at a higher price point, so know what you are using this style for and buy accordiningly.

excellent quality, 5 stars

title: bright, tangy, floral-- very light leaning medium roast. Must like acidic bite
text:
Will you like it? You may, if you like light roasts, or light leaning medium roasts that have a bright, tangy flavor and acidic finish.

It's tangy. Is more reminiscent of a light toast. Acidic, bright, tangy, floral. Reminds me of a plain basic drive through dunkin donuts coffee where the coffee to me is pretty awful because of the tanginess. I grimace every time I take a sip. I drink my coffee black, and to make it palatable I have to add cream. I drank my first coffee black, and it was rough.

So while my preference is dark bold strong chewy coffee, I am also good with a medium, balanced coffee on occasion. I know medium roasts vary in taste and acidity. What I am looking for when I am testing for review is whether it lives up to its description or not. There isn't much information included here. They dont make the claim that it is balanced, or non acidic, so there isn't much to go on. SO all that I can really base this on are my tastebuds, and they dont care for this at all. Not at all enjoyable no matter what I do. You may love it though?

I dislike this enough to never drink it again past the one pot I made. I will use it up by adding it in with a darker roast, or I will just give it away. Oddly, the taste that I breath out after several sips has a decent coffee taste. It just doesnt taste good while actually sipping it. lol

title: vanilla has a slight tart fruit like taste, best loaded with ice. 130 calories per serving/meal
text:
$1.83 per serving isn't terrible but I can do better. There are 30 servings, and each serving is just 130 calories. I am not sure what it has to offer over other meal replacement drinks, or even some protein drinks. It has a good amount of protein and fiber per scoop, as well as an assortment of vitamins and minerals, as well as sweeteners that aren't supposed to trigger a spike in blood sugar. The "propriety blend" they call Lysulin is comprised of L-lysine, Vitamin C, and Zinc. Lysulin "works like a glucose sponge to remove glucose from the body before it becomes a problem". If you dont want the Lysulin as a meal replacement powder, it can be purcased separately as a powder, tablet, or chewable. This product has added benefit of being a meal replacement if trying to shed a few pounds (or in my case, save a few calories by drinking this before my main meal--helps fill me up so I eat less).

To prepare, the direction say to use 1 scoop and add to 8 ounces of water. There is your meal. 130 calories. The taste? Is odd. It isnt bad, and I find it palatable and almost pleasant, but it doesnt quite have a vanilla taste. It reminds me more of a light berry taste. I think because there is a slight tartness. I have made it with water and find that I need to add loads of ice to make it taste best. I have made it with unsweetened non dairy milk (adds 25-40 cals), and that tastes better. SO I guess this can be doctored up a bit to suit taste preference. But if you are absolutely using this with diabetes in mind, then be very careful with what you add to this. Regular milk is loaded with glucose spiking carbohydrates (over time it can increase resistance). Unsweetened non dairy milk such as almond milk is fine.

When I do load it with ice and make it with non dairy milk, then it is rather nice. I do not use this as a full meal replacement, but i have been having it just prior to sitting down to dinner. I tend to fast, and rarely eat breakfast. Sometimes I have lunch, and when I do it is either a light lunch or I have a big ole smoothie. I just dont have an appetite for most of the day, so it is normal for me to not eat. SO I suppose I could use this as part of my smoothie, but I really prefer it as a "pre dinner supplement" to help fill me up before diving into dinner. THAT HELPS. I was surprised and encourage by this. Not sure which component helped the most (likely fiber and protein, and then the volume of fluid), but I had made a light dinner and was feeling absolutely stuffed. so depending on what I am having for dinner, the pre loaded 130 calories may help reduce overall calories simply because I ate less at dinner.

BTW, I am not diabetic, but i have been labeled pre-diabetic. My A1C was borderline once, and while I have had totally normal readings that label is still on record. I figure it is something to keep an eye on anyway, and I am always looking for ways to help keep those numbers in the normal range. If this helps on some level then it may be worth keeping this in hand. I wish it had a better taste and was priced better (I dont rate on price, but this is kinda pricy for me for 30 servings at just 130 cals each, where as I can get other meal replacement powders and each serving is 240-280 calories, but i can easily use half and get 2x as many servings). I like that it is created with diabetics (and pre diabetics) in mind because that is ultimately how we should be eating to help keep our glucose in check.

Overall, 3.5 stars. Pushed to 4 since we cant do half ratings. I like it better than 3 because it is helping me.

title: natural mild flavored caramel, plenty sweet, works well with iced coffee drinks- YUM
text:
The sugar free syrups can be a toss up as to whether it is good or bad. Taking a chance, I am delighted that this tastes good to me--even directly from bottle. But my current addiction is to make a blended coffee drink such as a Dalgona, OR a more simple quick blended drink using instant coffee, non dairy milk, and this syrup. Tall plastic bottle may make it a challenge to store.

title: like packets of sugar (with ginger). Great for ginger lovers! Quite sweet. Mix hot or cold
text:
I think this is why I love the internet, being able to find foods and drinks from all around that aren't otherwise easily available from a local grocer. This ginger and honey powder indeed tastes like honey with some spicy ginger. It also has sugar, sucrose, and glucose--so it is sweet. But I like that I can actually taste the honey. And the strong ginger is most important to me.

When I made my first cup, and was heading back to my living room to sit down I had taken a sip and had a huge sneeze. I think that is my litmus test on the strength of ginger drinks. Can it make me sneeze? it is only with that first sip. I love ginger, and I want my ginger drinks to be strong. I could go even stronger with this but it is the best I have had of this ilk.

How I have had it:

1. small mug with hot water over one packet of this. Add as much water as you want, but if you want the strongest sweet and ginger flavor, then aim for 6 ounces water. Drink like a tea

2. glass mason jar loaded with ice, then either add a packet of this and cold water, or prepare it hot first then add over the ice. Again, adjust water amount based on preference.

3. I have made both hot tea and iced tea, and added in a packet of this for the ginger flavor and honey sweetness.

I could use less sweet, or just dried honey rather than the additional sweeteners. Love the ginger. It is nice to have after dinner when I want to finish with something sweet but dont want to have too many extra calories. Also the ginger helps settle the stomach.

I really like this being in easy to use packets (like a sugar packet, but a little larger). It makes it super convenient. I like that I can use it in cold water, which is nice for times I am on the go and want something interesting for my water bottle. 39 calories per packet.

title: baggy of meat cure makes for messy extraction from rest of seasoning mix
text:
I am not in love with this particular variety by Wyld Seasoning. Seems hit or miss for me. Some are amazing, and some are ok. But usually still ranks at least 4 stars. This one is a near miss. I will say that it is ok. 3 stars.

There isn't much flavor on this one, at least not in comparison to others I have had. It is notably salty tasting, with a spicy bite. I am just not picking up on anything else.

While it is cool that this includes a baggy of meat cure, it is rather messy. Maybe they could bag each separately (then I can keep seasoning & cure in baggies, and stuff back in container, or I can dump out seasoning back into container), or use some sort of divider, because I pulled out a bit of seasoning taking the baggy out. Think I was more disturbed by the mess than the loss.

Also, the interior seal wasn't attached. It is stuck up in the cap. Not a big deal if there was an outer seal (all the others I have purchased had an outer seal as well as the inner).

Just has a few things going against it that I would hesitate to buy another Wyld Seasoning summer sausage mix. As for their other seasonings offered around Amazon, mm yes.. good stuff. I am in love with their Campground seasoning mix. For a similar heat and salt taste, with a little more complexity, their Habanero & Mango seasoning mix is good too. No meat cure baggy to deal with.

title: My favorite Wyld Seasoning- smoky, sweet, salty, spicy. Use it on everything!!

I will update if I experience anything new. I am just half way through my bag (and am highly considering ordering more. so I guess I like it more than I though, ha). Solid 4 stars then

title: fresh, flavorful, smells great, balanced blend of spices: warm, sweet, floral, spicy, bright
text:
Garam Masala is a spice blend that is not comprised of a specific set and ratio of ingredients. each brand does their own thing, and even when you look up recipes to make your own blend, they are all different. What they do have in common is the taste profile: warm, spicy, a little floral, a hint of sweet for the more discerning taste buds. It adds a depth of flavor to cooking. Not a singular taste. Often many of the same ingredients, but there is always variation. So that being said, this Garam Masala spice blend contains:

--ground cloves
--cumin
--cardamom (black and green)
--star anise
--bay leaf
--coriander
--peppercorns (black and white)
--cinnamon

I have had some that also include red chili powder, as well as fennel. Some include Star Anise, some dont. I think this makes for a robust, flavorful, great smelling blend. I kind of anticipated a more clove like taste, but I think the balance of flavors is outstanding. I pick up on the cumin more than the clove.

All more that I can really say is that if a dish calls for Garam Masala, this is a perfectly good, budget friendly option. It certainly gives that dish that certain something. Overall I find it delightful and am happy to add it to my huge often used collection of spices and spice blends from all over. This is a big container, so unless you go through this spice blend a lot, I would maybe buy a smaller option, or find a smaller container to separate some into. Just depends on your storage for spices. I make dishes that require this seasoning, but I also try to find additional uses for it (flavoring home made crackers, chips, breads, rolls, crusts for savory items, popcorn, just about any bean or lentil dish, potato seasoning, meat seasoning, etc)

Product is sold by weight, not by volume. This container is 80% full, but weighed after emptying bottle, taring, then adding back in and weighed is 340 grams, as anticipated. T Label is on wide side of container. Lid is twist off, with the typical dual sided tabs, one for spoon measuring, one for shaking. Has a best before date printed on label under ingredient list for 02/2023 (I acquired this May 2021). I think that is pretty good!

title: good mouth feel, lovely sweet taste, hint of tart, cute packaging, gift worthy
text:
Candy, yum yum! Love the presentation and overall look. Name is cute too-- as a cat lover, Candy Kittens is adorable to me. I would be comfortable buying a box of this and giving as a gift to a gummy loving friend. Speaking of which, a friend and I swap "gummy" candy from various brands and regions of the world. This is soft, gummy candy. Not like the typical (Harbiro) gummy bears which are firm and rubbery (not a bad thing, I love all gummy style), and they have gummies that are just like this. Not all gummies are the same, nor are meant to be. This style is chewy but soft with added sugar coating. This style quickly became my favorite during one of our swaps. I find this style to have a better mouth feel, much more flavor, and more punctuated sweetness. Also, it allows for more nuance of flavor- not just a generic sweet, but also actual fruit flavor and sometimes a hint of tart. So I was excited to try these and since it is a multi pack, I can spare one to give to my friend. These are yum yum yum! Great gaming snack, work snack, curled up reading a book snack.

Since it is candy, I dont expect much from the ingredients. I always just figure high calories, high sugar. But this has the added bonus of being palm oil free, and using natural food based coloring, and actually included some fruit juice. Kind of an elevated feel as far as candy goes.

At 20 calories a pop, just be mindful. An open bag is an empty bag. So while there are 400 calories per bag, considering a donut has at least that, I will choose this when I am in the mood for some serious candy noshing. At least it will last me longer than a few bites :)

title: mild flavor, sweet & salty, versatile- dip, sauce, marinade, enhancer
text:

Sometimes I make chicken and just want something to dunk it in. I couldn't do that with regular teriyaki as it is almost always too concentrated and potent. Use this anywhere, for anything, anytime you want a mild tasting sweet and salty marinade, dip, sauce, flavor enhancer.

And yeh, be mindful that it is relatively high in calories, salt, and sugar.

Refrigerate after opening
