title: Good salt taste with HUGE sodium savings: 300 mg per tsp vs 2400 mg from regular table salt
text:
Definitely quite a sodium savings. This ZEA salt product has just 300 mg in 1 tsp (or 75mg per 1/4 tsp). Regular table salt has 2400 mg in 1 tsp (or 600 mg of sodium in 1/4 tsp). WOW!

I have tried a variety of reduced sodium products, and nothing quite tastes right. I still use the no-salt and low sodium options, but I nearly always find myself grabbing my regular salt instead. This is as close to salt as I have ever had (I use Redmond Real Salt).

The granules or flakes are a larger size, but they aren't too hard or crunchy. I tried this on plain chicken, and it was quite good I wanted to get a good idea of what this truly tastes like, as dipping my finger in it to try was not good, lol). It has a taste of the sea, but not in a seaweed or fishy way. I usually eat an avocado with salt, pepper, and turmeric every day, and I know this will be my go-to salt for that use. Just by making that swap, I am saving hundreds of mg of sodium. I know it wont be a 100% swap all the time, but I am pleased with this enough to incorporate it into my daily life.

I like the container- glass with a flip top cap. It is typical dual sided- so pour out side and a sprinkle/shake side. The shake side allows a lot to come out, so just be mindful of this when going to use it. The bottle is packaged in a retail box and includes a pamphlet of info tucked inside. Gift worthy for a food themed gift basket.

title: fine quality matcha best for hot tea and lattes, dont waste it on smoothies
text:
Quality tea. Smells good, has mild taste with hint of natural sweet. I drink matcha almost daily. I often buy cheap matcha for use in my smoothies, but for tea and lattes, I tend to go for a more ceremonial quality. The trick for making hot tea is to be very careful with how hot the water is. Too hot? you're going to get bitter tea. I tend to use too much matcha powder for hot tea. It really just needs a little bit. When I make smoothies or sometimes my iced lattes, I use a whole lot more. Given the price of this brand, I have to save it for hot tea, or simple lattes, or when I want a mild matcha for baking needs.

This is good matcha. No problems, concerns.

title: for baking, cooking, teas, and chewing
text: I like fennel seeds over powder because the taste is more pronounced. When I need powder, then I just run these through my grinder. I experiment with seasonings, so I dont have a specific need for fennel except for when the recipe calls for it. I do however use fennel as a quick little breath freshener (with health benefits). I find this to taste a little different than other small bags I have purchased. Not sure what makes it different. This bag seems fresh, and has a good flavor. Just a little more mild?

title: fine oat flour powder, smells good- fresh!
text: Perfect swap for wheat flour when needing to thicken soups, sauces, or make gravy. As for all other baking needs, just scout around the internet for recipes and ratios. It is not a 1:1 swap, but some wheat flour can be traded out for some oat flour. Oat flour can not be used to make oat milk (I was hoping) as all the fats etc have already been released. But it can be added into smoothies to boost fiber and protein. I like trying out various flours out of curiosity rather than a dietary need. This smelled very good upon opening, and the flour is silky smooth. Fine milled.

title: Jelectrolyte drink: excellent light natural flavor, really good ingredients, good texture/mouth feel
text:
Really good flavor! That comes from the variety of fruit juices used. I like that. I drank these at room temperature, so I dont if that affects the texture any. The gel is is a thick liquid. Not at all firm like jello- maybe the half way point after first making jello and waiting for it to firm up. This is more liquid with a fuller mouth feel. It is a pleasant take on electrolyte drinks. Jelectrolyte! :D

It is actually quite low in sodium for an electrolyte drink. They may use something different/better than other brands. I really love what I see in the ingredient list and their product description, so I may go ahead and try this on a heavy sweat day. I originally intended to just use this on my light need/light sweat days. I sometimes refrain from electrolyte drinks because of the mega sodium (save for intense sweat days, when sometimes it feels like a rebirth after becoming hydrated again lol). So my plan is to use this when I just want something more than water to replenish me, but dont want the heavy duty stuff. But I will give it a whirl the next time I am going to be involved in heavy labor.

Given the fantastic ingredients, I would just drink this daily for any reason, like a delightful daily supplement. However, the price is a bit prohibitive for me to use this daily, but I would consider buying this again. I dont rate on price, so go for it if your budget allows.

Tastes good, feels good. And as for the containers (that seem to be ubiquitous these days), I hold onto a few and use them for additional use:

1. portable cup. refill with water as a "cup" as needed.
2. fill with water and freeze. Use as ice pack on body, or freeze several for use in a cooler. Sometimes I just toss one in my purse if I have snacks in there and dont want to use a cooler. Then when melted I can drink it.

title: lightly sweet snack cookie hits the spot when the need to nibble comes on
text:
I have these and the Maria cookies. I didnt know what the difference was, so I figured I would try them both. These are just a little more sweet and have that short bread texture. The other reminds me of a non cream filled cookie-- like the backing of a cream filled cookie minus the cream. If that makes sense.

I really like both. I have been using them as my sweet nibble after dinner, or any time I would normally want a sweet treat. I had been devouring boxes of donuts on a near daily basis, so while these arent exactly that, they fit the need for my sweet tooth. The amount of calories I am not consuming by swapping in these is amazing.

Since i haven't been consuming too much excess sugar, I know my ability to taste sweet has increased. I know these are lightly sweet, but some may think they are bland. I really like the taste of these and will be ordering more.

As with the maria cookies, these are great alone, or could be crushed up to make a single serve mini pie, or as a topping for ice cream or yogurt, or some other creative mix.

title: lightly sweet, perfect for noshing, or eating instead of a box of donuts :P
text:
lightly sweet cookie that is perfect for noshing and not wanting to eat the whole box. If I want a sweeter version, then I go with their shortbread. Similar nutritional profile but that one is a little sweeter than this. I often have this as my "dessert" if I really need to nibble after dinner. Or I have some with my late morning coffee or tea. I was keeping and eating entire boxes of donuts in the house, so the fact that I can be satisfied with a few of these cookies, is a major improvement (and massive reduction in daily calories).

Great alone, but these would also work for making mini pie "crusts", and for easting along side some yogurt or ice cream with fruit.

title: large granule spice mix, great flavor, highly versatile, yum!
text:
They say to brush oil on the food you will be using this on if using it as a coating as the granules are on the large side. So the larger granules shouldnt be a surprise. Does great mixed into ground meat, or other ground mixes (I made a lentil "meat ball" recently as well as added some to regular meat balls). I love the texture it imparts. It reminds me of a couple of other well known & loved name brands I use for steak and chicken seasoning. I have added it to chicken salad, egg salad, and just a go to seasoning mix for whatever I have made lately.

It includes salt in the mix, so keep than in mind when incorporating it into recipes. Also has soybean oil which I could do without, but it is fine overall. I like the flavor profile. The large container will last me awhile, and I think the current price of $10 is fair.

title: good quality, lacks the peppery bite I was expecting. Bright, fruity, green- drizzle on salads
text: Fresh, fruity, and a little bitter in a green way. I expected a more peppery bite, but I fail to pick up on that at all. I always try a new olive oil by taking a swig from the bottle, and this was underwhelming to me in comparison to what I was expected from the product description. No peppery bite, not on the tongue, not at the back of the throat. But it does have a bright, fruity, tart taste that is appealing too. I have been drizzling it on my salads. One of these days I will dunk some good bread in it.

title: highly flavorful, versatile oil that has just enough spice, texture, and oil. Delicious!
text: Crunchy chili oil is a must have in my household. We dont use a lot of spicy hot, but we like the boost of flavor that oils like this contribute to a dish. I have used crunchier crunch oils, and more oily crunch oils. This is a good middle of the road chili crunch oil- plenty of oil, plenty of texture, just the right amount of heat. I tried this out as a flavor for baked drum sticks. I wanted to use this on chicken wings, but the price is crazy right now for that, so I grabbed some chicken drum sticks and got my fix that way, Mmm so many options with a spice like this. Could do without the msg, but I eat quite enough of this at once to worry. Such good oil.

title: great addition to my spicy peanut chicken and noodles quick dish. Fancies up my dinner game!
text: Chili Crisp is thick, crunchy, spicy, and tasty. I use it to add extra flavor and texture to my spicy peanut chicken  & noodles. Could do without the added msg. But mmm mmm mmm this is so good. Nice medium hot spice, lots of texture, great flavor. Put it on anything, or even nosh by the spoonful. If you want less texture and more oil, then be sure to select their Chili Oil option. Love that they have options!

title: fresh, smells so good, lots of broken but plenty of whole leaves
text:
A mixture of whole and broken. I dont mind this. A large container is just not going to stay as intact as the leaves carefully picked and placed in a small container. Or maybe higher volume would do better in a bag.

My small glass container contains 4 grams of whole leaf bay leaves. Usually goes for $5-7. THIS is 13x as much weight (57 grams) for $7.99. I just can't be upset over a few broken leaves (I thought about it, LOL). So definitely go with the smaller bottles if you absolutely need uniform looking leaves. If you dont mind a mix, then this will be perfectly fine.

I did notice a few spots here and there on some leaves, and some discoloration. I then took out my small glass container of organic leaves, and they pretty much looked the same. Just depended on which leaf I grabbed. I just hadn't really looked close at a bay leaf before.

This container smells amazing. Sniffing them side my side (this container and my other small glass container) the leaves smell the same, but the fact that there are so many in one spot, and the opening is bigger, this container just wafts a super fresh, lovely aroma that I hadnt really fully appreciated before.

While prior uses only had me adding 2-3 bay leaves, now I can gleefully add a half dozen to something and not worry about using up my stash too quickly.

Value= 5 stars (not that I rate on price, but I do comment, and I think this is good value)
Freshness= smells good, looks good. No question of freshness= 5 stars
Flavor= looks, smells, tastes like bay leaf, so 5 stars

broken leaves? yeh. Enough whole ones to still be a value purchase? yes. so overall I would go with 4.5 stars, but since we cant do that (and I do like this more than 4 stars), I am rating officially as 5 stars

title: fresh, good quality rice flour. Fine, light. Great for my sauces, soups, etc
text:
Nice fine flour for baking and thickening needs. I use it primarily for sauces and soups. I usually buy much smaller sized bags, so this huge 5 lb bag will last me awhile. I will portion out what I need as store rest in our extra fridge/freezer.

I think I will venture further with it and try out some recipes that call for rice flour. I know that it is not an even swap, but can be partially substituted for wheat flour, or combined with a bunch of other non wheat flours. Anyway, you know what to do with it if you are looking at this product. I imagine the main thing you want to know is if it is of quality and good freshness, and it is on both accounts. No problems, no concerns.

title: Iced tea enhancer! add fruity sweetness to a large cup of fresh brewed iced tea YUM
text:
I like my water plain, but I still have a use for this. Got a soda stream or enjoy buying bottles of club soda? Try this added in. I love carbonated water, and for that I like to have a little fruity essence. Sometimes I add a spoonful of a fruit juice concentrate (tart cherry, pomegranate, etc), or a and/or a squeeze of lemon, lime, or clementine.

Trying this Mandarin orange liquid water enhancer by Splenda adds options to my life. It has a decent orange flavor, but the sweetness from Splenda takes me a little getting used to. I dont love it for plain water, but I like it enough. It is for OTHER applications that I love it. I prefer it for carbonated water and for....iced tea!

I think I realized that I dont need sweet water. HOWEVER, it is perfect for my TEA. I dont always drink tea, but come summer I tend to have a hankering for it. I want it sweet, but not too sweet. I will use just about any tea bag I have (herbal/tisane, tea leaf), make it strong, then pour it over ice. Sometimes plain is good, but for some reason a little added sweetness hits the spot. I love orange, so adding a little orange flavor in my tea really ups my game. I imagine a lemon version would be great too. Anyway, so I am not using it as water enhancer but it is making for an awesome ICED TEA enhancer. YUM!

As expected, just try out different ratios of this to the liquid you are adding it too. Less for less sweet, more for more sweet, or less with more water, or more with less water. You get the idea.

Other fun application: add this to the water you use when making ice cubes.
Use it in making a quick slushy
Got a smoothie that could use some help in masking flavor of other supplements? add a little of this in
Yogurt, popsicles, banana soft serve ice cream with a hint of orange? orange creamsicles!

I've got summer on the brain :)

title: add to smoothies, mix into other foods, swap a little  in, or totally replace wheat flour
text:
This lupini flour has a mildly sweet scent, with a color and texture that reminds me of garbanzo bean flour. But unlike garbanzo bean flour this seems to blend in easier when I use it to for thickening needs. Anything i have used it in, including in smoothies, hasn't really imparted any flavor. It isn't at all bitter to me. Quite neutral tasting.

What got me interested in trying lupini flour is not for a specific dietary need, but the interesting nutritional profile. I love the high amount of fiber, protein, potassium (and less calories than many other flours), add in the fact that it has a lower carb load and I needed to give it a try.

I'm still on quite a learning curve for using this flour, but I know some white flour can be swapped out for some of this and even if nothing else changes in the recipe it should work. If a total swap is needed, then as with all the other non wheat flours, usually a little extra know how is needed (ie; using xantham gum, using other flours, etc).

I've used a couple brands of lupini flour, and they seem similar to me. This two pound bag is going to last me a long while.

title: add some to smoothies for boost in fiber and other nutrients
text:
Fresh!

I'm always down for trying new stuff. I hadn't yet had lupini flour until trying this brand and another, side by side. This flour has a mildly sweet scent, and anything i have used it in hasn't really imparted any flavor. I read that it is typically bitter? I didnt notice. I do use a wide variety of flours- like any and all of them- not so much for a health reason or needed restriction, but out of curiosity and a desire to learn how to cook and bake with items that aren't just wheat flour.

What intrigues me on this lupini flour is that it has a goodly amount of fiber, protein, potassium, and less calories than other flours. Lower carb load, too. I can always get behind the added nutrition and the better nutritional profile. I like when I can reduce some calories and carbohydrates.

I'm still on quite a learning curve for using this flour, but I know some white flour can be swapped out for some of this and even if nothing else changes in the recipe it should work. If a total swap is needed, then as with all the other non wheat flours, usually a little extra know how is needed (ie; using xantham gum, using other flours, etc).

I learned that this is a flour than can be eaten raw, and that it can be added to smoothies to bulk them up, to add fiber, etc. I have done this and this is how I know that this flour doesnt taste bitter-- at least not mixed in with what I have been using with it.

title: Lightly sweet & delicious mix of freeze dried banana, cashews, oats, perilla seeds (in own bag)
text:
This is good! I love it! The banana pieces are freeze dried, and so fresh tasting. Lots of cashew pieces. The oats are loose, not stuck into clumps. Has a sweet overall taste, but not cloying. They use unrefined sugar; appears to be 10g added sugar per serving. The perilla seeds come in their own little bag, which I think is great. Allows options that are much appreciated.

I can nosh on this alone, or add it to some yogurt, or ever to further top off some steel cut oats. Or best yet, add warm non dairy milk on top and allow the oats and bananas to reconstitute a bit. Oats become tender as do the banana pieces (because they had been freeze dried). YUM YUM.
But for the most part I eat it plain.
((check out their product page, and see recipes on what all to do with some of this granola!!))

Serving size is 38 grams, and there are about 5 servings in the bag

I dont rate on price, but will comment. For about 8 ounces in this bag, I think the price of $6.99 is fair.

I will buy again, and I will see what other options they have. The quality and overall taste has impressed me.

title: fresh coriander powder is bright and tasty. Pairs well w/ other spices, foods, even SMOOTHIES
text:
I use a variety of spices and have a well stocked daily spice drawer, as well as a robust over flow cupboard. This coriander is fresh, bright, and delicious smelling and tasting. I use it in whatever I can think to add it to. Usually chili, tacos, soups, and sometimes as a light seasoning for vegetables especially if I have another dish that has cumin or garam masala in it. They all pair well together.

Large container will last me quite awhile. I had been looking at health benefits of coriander, and am considering adding some to my smoothies.

While Coriander is from the seed of the cilantro plant, No worries on this tasting anything like cilantro leaf. Just totally different. Coriander is more cumin like in taste but brighter, more floral, less "meaty".

I'm pleased with this tall, large container of coriander. I do recommend. $9.99 at time of this review, is a good price of this size and quality.

title: fine powder dissolves well, perfect portion, very fresh, convenient on the go stick packets
text:
Quality product- has clean, fresh, pungent smell and flavor that can be expected from any "greens" product. Very fine powder (like Matcha). Nifty, easy to open, convenient packets fit a niche that you may be looking for: pre measured, long time freshness, and/or for use on the go or traveling. I have a bunch of different products of this ilk that I tuck in a big canister (an old coffee tub, actually) and then I can just select a "health stick" or two of choice.- then add to whatever concoction I am creating in the moment.

While I am not a big fan of plain green stuff, I will add a little vanilla protein powder to help mellow the flavor. I shake it together then drink up. Pretty good. But I have been thinking of other ways to use stuff like this, and I imagine it would pair well in soups, broths, salads, make a salad dressing, etc.. and that would likely be awesome. Of course as a simple tea, or added to water is good too if that is your thing. It mixes, dissolves well.

If you are used to (and enjoy) that special flavor that green matter imparts, then you will like this. I drink this type of stuff for added health benefit, so I am looking primarily for quality and this seems to have it. The quality of the product has piqued my interest in checking out their other Teazen offerings. So that says something.

Worth a try, anyway. Enjoy!

title: healthy clean flavor makes for comforting chicken & sweet rice soup
text:
I've made this before a few times, but it has been awhile and I did not have all the ingredients. When this came up as an option to test out I was stoked because this has everything I need to make this chicken soup. In prior times I purchased the individual ingredients. Let me tell you, that gets pricy to buy all the individual ingredients that dont get used often, and some of it is hard to find (I often traveled to get to an Asian grocer to buy small quantities or had to buy whatever I could find online, which was always in larger quantities). This is perfect. $10? take my money!

Ok, so here is a tip: you do NOT NEED to use a whole chicken or cornish hen. Use it if you have it and want to use it, but out of convenience, you can use bone in chicken parts or even boneless chicken. Maybe use your own bone broth. This is chicken soup with (sweet) rice, so it really isnt a complicated meal to make, or rather it doesnt need to be complicated. The instructions are on the bag (and say to use a whole chicken) but there are plenty of videos and blogs on how to make SAMGYETANG using any and all of those options. I recommend taking a quick peek at some before starting. Make adjustment to suit your flavor preference. I definitely add in salt, pepper, sometimes sprinkle in more ginger, garlic, sometimes some red pepper. Just depends on what I am feeling. Sometimes I add in a few more veggies. My main interest is in the base flavor profile, and the warming healthy clean flavor these ingredients provide.

title: tangy, slightly acidic, light leaning medium roast. Fresh & clean tasting, smelling
text: Clean, but slightly acidic flavor. A little bright for my preference. Well within realm of a medium roast. I think it leans a little light on the medium spectrum, and I prefer a more balanced medium, or a medium that leans dark (or better yet, a dark roast, haha). I know the perception of coffee taste is greatly subjective so while I dont love it as a medium roast, it does smell and taste fresh. I think you will like it if you like a slightly tangy medium roast. Comes in pressure zip bag.

title: Addictive! Taste, texture exactly as expected, but short on seeds/cranberries
text:
I'm quite familiar with this style of snack bar (from China, I only ever find them in Chinese grocers). I've been eating this style snack bar on and off for years. I love the taste and texture- it is unique and hard to describe adequately. I dont even know the proper name for them. Not even mentioned here? Just a puffed snack cake (but does not at all resemble rice crispy treats. The puffed rice is large, airy, and wet). When I hit up Asian grocery stores, I look for these sweet, soft, puffed rice snack cakes. Just a sweet treat that I like once in awhile. Super pricey here (I dont rate on price, but will comment), but it isnt often I am at a place that carries these. Oddly all brands are nearly all the same in flavor and texture, including this, so I can say that these are fine. This package of snack cakes is as expected, but I will add that they are NOT covered in seeds and fruit as shown in the product picture. Just looks lightly sprinkled on here and there. They are woefully deficient in seeds and cranberry. However overall texture and taste is exactly as it should be for a snack cake of this ilk. And I have yet to have had a bar of this ilk to be covered in seeds/fruit. What this is is actually in line with all the others I have ever tried, if that makes sense.

If you have never had these before, the bars are soft and moist, and have a faint wetness to it. Sugar soaked puffed rice. All soft. There is no crunch. But there is a pleasant dense bite down. Not much to chew as the bar compresses down easily with each bite. Yet oddly satisfying (to me). Nothing I would consider at all healthy, at 10 grams of added sugar per bar. Kind of addicting. The very first time I ever had one (15+ years ago), I had bought them on a whim, and thought they were weird. Then I kept eating one after the other, and decided I like them a lot. LOL. SO yeh, I they are oddly satisfying, and I think worth giving a try if you are open to new taste and texture. They are so light and airy that it would be easy to eat 2, 3, 4, or all 16 of them in one sitting. Dont ;)

Also, the product headline includes the word Vegan. The package does not. These are not vegan according to most standards- as these do contain eggs. I dont mind, but if you are banking on this for being vegan then ignore the headline and take a look at the ingredients instead.

They do best in a cool environment. I keep mine in the fridge to keep them firm and holding together. They wont be hard in the fridge, they will just be as they should- firm, holding together, have a solid mouth feel. When too warm, the sugar, etc becomes more loose and liquidy, making the puffed pieces not hold together as tightly. Trust me on this.

I hemmed and hawed over the rating. It would certainly be at least a 4. I cant do 4.5 but that is what I would have settled on. I like them more than a 4, so I am going to go ahead with 5. Overall based on my experience with this (and compared to all others) I'm overall quite pleased. I am tickled to be able to have a rare snack be shipped to my house.

title: excellent quality coffee, dark leaning medium is balanced and delicious
text:
Dark leaning medium roast tastes balanced, and smells great. I prefer dark roasts, but can enjoy a good medium roast when it isnt bitter or acidic. I knew this was going to lean a little dark when I opened the bag and saw the deep hued bean with a slight oily sheen. After I processed it in my grinder, the resulting grind was still a little dark (medium is usually much more red)-- so with my bias toward dark coffee, I was pleased to see this.

I brew my coffee in the Ninja Specialty Coffee Maker: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07PFLM2LK

I made a regular pot of coffee in my Ninja (half pot, classic brew) using 3 full scoops (about 6 Tbs) to 32 ounces of water. The taste on that was a slightly watered down medium taste to me. Very balanced, pretty smooth. But good black, and hot. It wasnt robust enough to go over ice as is. Must need stronger brew (more coffee to water ratio) for that. So then I decided to try another pot in my Ninja (half pot, RICH brew) using 4 full, rounded scoops (8-10 TBS) for 32 ounces of water and that made for a very rich, bold, but slightly bitter but still good tasting brew. It was good hot, AND over ice. My next pot will be to use same amount of coffee but use the classic brew option.

I can tell that this is a quality coffee. It made for a very satisfying cup of coffee, and I am included to buy this again (though I may try their actual dark roast since I love dark coffee most of all). I am never able to pick up on the subtle notes, but I do know whether I like the smell or not, the taste or not, and how well it does alone, or with add ins. I tend to drink my coffee black, but sometimes I add in creamer. Some coffee tastes watered down with creamer, and I want my coffee to still have a coffee tastes if I decide to mellow it out with creamer. This plays well with creamer.

title: roast it for added depth of flavor. Nutty, chocolatey, leans more coffee like than tea
text:
This is a good quality dandelion root tisane/herbal tea. The term tea is used liberally but this is technically a tisane (ie, non caffeinate herbal "tea"). This tisane tastes as anticipated: I open the bag, and it always smells nutty, chocolatey, with hints of hazelnut. I dont smell grassy or bitter, I just smell a pleasant, chocolately aroma. Green/grassy is more indicative of dandelion LEAF, this is dandelion ROOT (YUM!)

It leans more coffee like in is deep flavor than tea like, which tends to lean more bright. A mild herbal vibe to it. Kind of reminds me of a water down coffee. From there you can play around with it to see how best to consume it. I like to make it strong- real strong- and then add it over loads of ice. Great mid day treat without all the caffeine of other teas and coffee.

DO NOT USE boiling water, use water that is just under boil. Too hot water makes for bitter taste (I digress, but this is also true of green tea which is a true tea, but it uses delicate leaves that are easily scorched from boiling water). Let steep, strain, and drink. Or dont strain- the bits tend to stay at bottom of mug.

Sip this straight (again, has a deep nearly coffee like taste), with or without cream, sweetener. Hot or iced. OR can be mixed into a pot of coffee. Can just add straight from bag, or run some through the grinder (my preference). This can help reduce caffeine intake by swapping in some of this for some of your coffee.

Want added depth of flavor? try roasting some in the oven before grinding. OMG.. mmm

Try it straight from the bag too. It isn't something that is easy to munch on, but it has a nutty taste that is fun to try. Can grind it and sprinkle on oatmeal or on top of muffins if looking to add this in a variety of ways for health reasons.

If you look into coffee alternatives, dandelion root is often part of the mix. Usually chicory and a few others, too. I use DandyBlend on occasion, which is what introduced me to trying dandelion root "tea"
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000SMN0DO

title: well balanced, clean umami flavor, great ingredients, less sodium than many broths
text:
Nicely done seafood broth; has a clean flavor. It is about what I anticipated in terms of taste. I recommend taking a look at the ingredients on any option you are considering so you can mentally taste it, so to speak. This Seafood blend has: Shrimp, shrimp extract, katsuobushi (smoked skipjack tuna), Mussel, raw sugar, solar salt (evaporated sea salt), pollack, sea tangle extract (kelp), onion, garlic, potato starch.

So yeh, I think it has a pleasant seafood taste, and is well balanced- not too fishy, not too salty. It provides that wonderful umami taste that works so well with a variety of noodle dishes, or use in making a sauce or marinade. I had used this in flavoring chicken thighs (along with some soy, sesame oil, spices) for use with vegetable and udon noodle dish. I will definitely be using it next time I make pad thai.

I use it in place of or in addition to fish sauce for that depth of flavor, and something special, umami

I selected this for use as a seasoning/broth for use in a bigger recipe, not so much as a sipping broth- but for those that are interested in that, and like what they see in the ingredients then give it a try. I love that these packets of dry broth aren't saturated with sodium. I am very pleased with that.

Because of my favorable experience with this brand, I am now interested in their other offerings--the ingredients for the chicken, and especially the beef & mushroom sound fantastic to me. I am so pleased that I had the opportunity to try this brand.

no MSG, no Dextrin, and low(ish) salt content.

title: delicious mix of nuts and spices, balanced sweet taste, be mindful of portion size
text:
I have this in the Golden Chai option. It is delicious. Pecans, Cashews, Walnuts, Coconut chips, along with an assortment of chai spices and other flavorings. Ground flax also coats the nuts giving it a more robust mouth feel. It is really good NUT mix. No granola bits, but I do really like it and will be either snacking from bag, adding to my oats, or chopping it up fine then rolling my frozen Greek yogurt bar (yasso) in it. I Easy on the teeth.

There are 4 servings in the bag, so be mindful of how much you eat if calories are a concern. Would be very easy to consume whole bag in one sitting.

Love the flavor and the level of sweetness. It is not overdone, in my opinion, nor is the sweetness fake tasting. Really well balanced. I think they did a great job with this. Yum Yum

title: pretty tasting tea- so fresh. Excellent hot, iced, or used in bobba tea recipes. YUM
text:
I haven't had jasmine green tea in a long time. This has been a treat. Funny thing, I thought I selected matcha, so when this arrived I was momentarily confused. Then I saw that I ordered wrong. Not a bad mistake on my part! I love the occasional pot of tea. Loose leaf provides the most robust flavor. I love the hint of jasmine. I recommend trying it iced with a little sweetener. I have used it in making bobba tea (with tapioca balls, with or without cream, usually sweetened with a syrup or a little sugar, lots of ice).

The bag comes with a sealing tool/clip to help keep bag closed and fresh.

title: taco seasoning taste profile, light on chipotle and smoke, but overall good
text:
A spice blend that greatly reminds me of taco seasoning, but without the high sodium content. While I dont see cumin in the ingredient list, I do see "spices"-- not sure what that is supposed to mean. I do thik I tsate cumin though, and that is something in taco seasoning. But who knows. Here is the Ingredient list: Paprika, Brown Sugar, Salt, Sugar, Corn Starch, Garlic, Onion, Spices, Mustard, Rice Hull Concentrate, Chipotle Pepper, Natural Smoke Flavor

The chipotle and smoke flavor is not real strong. I like the overall flavor, and will likely use it in making tacos (I usually make my own seasoning, so this will make it extra easy. Then adjust to taste). Lots of other uses too, just figure on it having a taco seasoning taste profile.

title: spicy good flavor, excellent for hot chicken, makng spicy sauces
text:
I have had the spice blend made for lamb (but can be used on anything) and thought that was pretty spicy, then I tried this one for chicken, and the heat goes up a notch. I like the overall flavor of this blend a little better over the other. It works great on chicken. I took some chicken breasts, sliced them into tenders, coated them with panko and this for seasoning. WOO that made for a nice spicy plate of chicken to dunk in blue cheese dressing or whatever. Chicken wings are exploding in price, and I am not going to pay for hot wings. This doesnt replace that, but it is a nice way to get a hot chicken fix.

Also works nicely as a way to spice up some peanut sauce for spicy chicken with noodles and peanut sauce. Mmm mmm

title: spicy, moderate level heat- depends on what it is paired with. Use this with anything
text:
Spicy seasoning, add your own salt! I like that it is low sodium (15 mg per 1/4 tsp serving); I'd rather adjust for my own tastes and needs than to have it too high. I have a moderate heat level tolerance, and this seems about spot on- right in the middle of their pepper icon range. I think it depends what it is paired with.

Not all sure what the "spices" are as the first ingredient, but I know it also contains hot peppers/capsicum, garlic, onion and salt. Has a savory taste, as expected.

I never have lamb, it just never sits well with me (lamb burgers, lamb chops). I checked to see if this product had any recommendations for use beyond lamb, and sure enough it does say to use it on anything. Sold. I made some spicy beef and pork meatballs. Gave them some zing.

I dont think the overall flavor was robust enough for me to want to repurchase. I will keep on using it and trying it in different stuff. I like it so far, but not yet loving it.

title: OK. For full flavor, needs AT LEAST 3 bags per 16 OZ of water. Otherwise TERRIBAD brown water
text:
Ok, so I had the opportunity to try 2 options, a dark blend and this medium blend. I'd say they are about both equal to me in overall observation and experience. This is coffee as last resort. I LIKE instant coffee, and this isnt even instant. It is just kinda bad coffee. It tastes a little on the old side. Also it takes 3-4 bags to get any coffee flavor out from it (using 16-18 ounces water). So here is nearly same review as the other dark option (and I like the dark option a tiny bit better than this):

To make: 8oz hot water per bag, steep 3+ mins, toss out!!

In short, it takes 3 bags with 16 ounces of water to make a fair cup of coffee. Taste is smooth and mild, overall easy to drink. But use less than that ratio? woah, the Worst.Coffee.Ever. 
I drink nearly any coffee, brewed in any fashion. Give it to me ground, whole, instant. I was excited to try this. And now I am disappointed. The coffee absolutely tastes old when use with 1 bag per 8 ounce ratio. It reminds me of old coffee. The taste is too mild- definitely not bold enough for me (my preference is strong, bold, dark coffee). I had suspicion when I opened the bag. While it smelled good enough, it was a little weak smelling. And sure enough, it makes weak coffee at the 8oz water per 1 bag ratio. Did I use to much water? well..
NO INSTRUCTIONS. So yeh, I know it is a coffee in a tea bag, and could be figured out, but why not include instructions??  I assumed 8oz per bag (which is what the product description says, but there really should be a guideline ON the actual product. Yeesh), and decided to try it two ways, well 3 ways: 
1. My usual 16 ounces with 1 bag, and 2. the assumed 8z with 1 bag. Both made weak, old tasting, weird coffee. I initially tried the 3 minute steep, then I tried a 60 minute (yup, 60). No change. THEN 3. I decided to try THREE bags with 16 ounces of water. That changed everything. The taste went from ultra weak, undrinkable, unsatisfying old tasting brown water to a more smooth and significantly better tasting cup of coffee. Not bad at all. Had I not gone back and tried the 3 bags of coffee to 16 ounces, I would have left this review as simply being terribad. But I wanted to know if I could get this to a drinkable level. Now I know.. 3-4 bags for 16 ounces of coffee. I would definitely do 4 bags for a 20 cup. Which brings this bag to 4-5 servings max. Suppose that could be ok for travel, for quick cup of coffee at work with hot hot water, or a night out camping. 
Ultimately I am not going to use up 3-4 tea bags to make one mediocre cup of coffee on a regular basis. Just using the recommended 1 bag per 8 ounces doesnt work.  I had let it steep for a few minutes before trying, then I just left the bag in the cup for an hour hoping for more flavor to come through. NOTHING I did made it taste satisfactory. Not cool. HAD I NOT GONE BACK to try THREE bags for 16 ounces, I would have left it as a 1 star review, finding the 8 ounces per bag to make TERRIBAD, WEAK, BROWN WATER. So, play around with the ratio. A decent cup is attainable. Btw, 3 bags with 16 ounces of water didnt need much steep time (3 minutes), but I went ahead and left the bag in the cup. 
 I have plenty of k-cups, ground coffee, whole bean coffee, and an assortment of instant coffee that I 1000% prefer over this (even camping, or an emergency. But no, I'll use instant instead). Had this worked out, I would have bought more. I love the idea of coffee in a tea bag.

Giving this a GENEROUS 3 STARS... and only because I was eventually able to figure out a suitable ratio for mediocre coffee. WILL not be a repurchase, do not recommend

title: mild, lightly nutty, lightly sweet, very mellow; not at all bitter.
text:
5 stars: no issues or concerns on quality. Love the transparency of information, and the mini lesson on the product page. The matcha smells good, is a light fine powder, and makes decent hot tea, or blended into smoothies or other foods. Comes in typical pressure zip mylar bag.

I drink coffee, love my coffee, but consuming matcha lends to a more sustained caffeine feel with no jitters. So I drink a cup of beloved hot coffee, and since I usually dont eat breakfast, I will make a matcha latte mixed with non dairy milk and some protein powder or liquid. This provides some extra caffeine and allows me to fast longer. Also regular consumption of matcha decreases if not eliminates my need for sweets. I've always experienced that, and rely on matcha to keep me in control.

Overall.. kinda, no different than other brands I have purchased over the years. I have been drinking matcha on and off for 15 years or so. Unlike then, it is so easy to find now! I think I have only used culinary matcha powder, from super cheap to quite pricy. From various regions. This one is on the pricier side for me. I dont rate on price though- we all have different budgets, and some peoples taste buds are more discerning that others. I have to say, I really dont notice a difference.. especially when being added to a smoothie. I will say that I tend to use a lot of matcha at once and sometimes it takes extra preparation to mask some of the bitterness in many of the matcha I have. I dont need to do that with this. It stands out in that this does seem to have a little more mellow and sweet taste, even mildly nutty, and has a brighter green color than some, and I dont need as much extra stuff to mask it. It isn't bitter. So yeh, this is fantastic, but I find many brands to be really good. I have yet to meet one that I dont like.

title: Japanese matcha powder has light, mild, semi sweet taste- great for tea preparation
text:
Good quality matcha, no issues or concerns.

I drink matcha often, and purchase it regularly. It really doesn't matter if it is ceremonial grade or culinary grade. I have yet to meet one that didnt taste nearly identical. So most of my buying options have been based on pricing. Side by side is really the only way I can tell the difference. I can say that this Japanese matcha powder stands out in that it has a slight more mild, sweet taste over the many others I have used (typically culinary, usually Chinese, sometimes from Japan). For that, I would rather use this for making hot tea (ceremony) than to use it in other applications (culinary). But either is fine, for me.

I have been drinking it on and off for a couple of decades. It was more recently as I began seeing it used in commercial offerings (lattes, smoothies, and baked goods), that I decided to go from hot tea to making my own lattes at home, and adding it to smoothies. My go to preparation is to take a vanilla protein powder (or liquid) or vanilla nutritional powder and add a big scoop of matcha powder (likely way more than what is necessary). I add some ice, sometimes some collagen powder, add some non dairy milk (usually unsweetened vanilla almond, cashew, oat, or coconut) and shake it until it all blends together. I find by doing this that I am consuming it regularly. I do go through a lot through..

If you prefer to drink matcha as a tea, then this ceremonial grade is great. If your primary use is mixed into a smoothie, then the culinary is a more budget friendly option (which Nurticost also carries).
https://www.amazon.com/Nutricost-Organic-Matcha-Powder-Culinary/dp/B08MB7GF4X

title: Well packaged, high quality, potent smelling, robust tasting turmeric.
text:
Well packaged, high quality, potent smelling, robust tasting turmeric. The container has a twist off lid. The lid had a plastic ribbon seal, then once the lid was opened it had another seal. I needed scissors to get into both. Well done.

The aroma emanating from the tub is potent. It smells wonderful. I really like the smell and taste of turmeric, so taking a good whiff of this made me happy. I use it nearly daily for flavoring and for the health benefits. I use turmeric in my cooking, I sprinkle it on everything, and even add it to smoothies and hot drinks. It is just one of my favorite spices-- simply love the flavor. Having it in a big tub feels normal for me as I do make things that require more than a sprinkle or shake. This will live in my smoothie cupboard where I keep my protein powders and other add ins and supplements.

Funny, as someone else mentioned I too usually buy my turmeric in bulk, and I will plan to reuse this container to store the bagged turmeric. Though, I very well may just buy more of this brand. It is really good stuff! I truly never really notice a difference in taste or smell, but this reminds me of the times when I grate a a dried piece of turmeric. So fresh and robust. Good price too. Go for it!

title: perfectly good matcha green tea powder for use in smoothies, lattes, tea, baking, etc
text:
I have tried many matcha green tea powders from various regions. I have come to realize that it really doesnt matter which I get, they are pretty much the same to me. Any variance is rather insignificant. I pretty much buy based on size and price. I purchased three brands this last time around, and they all pretty much tasted same and performed the same. So yeh, I liked this, and would consider it again. Seems perfectly fine to me. The amount I go through, I am not willing to spend a lot.

I have used this in hot matcha as well as in cold. I tend to make the latter most of all. I like to add a generous amount of powder to a mason jar with lid (or a shaker cup, or blender cup) along with some vanilla protein powder or vanilla protein drink, sometimes some vanilla non dairy milk. Then I shake it like crazy to mix it all together. Lends to a gentle level of steady caffeine. No jitters.

title: budget friendly, perfectly good smelling, tasting matcha. Will buy again
text:
edit: From $10.36 to $16.36 ($1.86 per ounce) ?! Price has gone up 60% since my last purchase a few months back. For shame.
Micronutrients has a 1lb bag for $12.95 ($0.81 per ounce). The cheap stuff is perfect for smoothies.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08PY3Q8XS

There are so many options available now for Matcha. When I was first starting to drinking it some 10+ years ago, I didn't easily find it. I dont recall where I bought this brand, but it was the first kind I ever bought. I had 4 bags of this size, and I stored some in the freezer. I drank quite a bit of it then forgot about it- more of this in a second. Had since enjoyed some matcha on and off, but it was more recently that I really had a real hankering for it. I always drank it hot (like, ceremonial style), and it occurred to me to drink it cold... I had been seeing more and more "matcha lattes" and other matcha flavored drinks that one day I just decided to skip the hot water, and just add it into some non dairy milk, a scoop of vanilla protein powder, and an 1/8 cup of this matcha powder. Sometimes I blend it., but most often I use a shaker cup. Now it is is my go-to drink. I have 1 cup of coffee, then make up a goodly portion of cold matcha. It provides a caffeine boost without the jitters. I failed to realize I was using like 4x the amount, so I am trying to scale a bit. Funny thing is, is that my last bag of matcha which had not been opened yet had a severely expired expiration date. I didnt think I bought it that long ago, but I did. Not one to shy away from a date stamped on a bag of tea powder, I opened it up, took a sniff and found it smelled super fresh. Tasted as fresh as can be too. When I worked through this bag, I figured I better buy more soon. I did not expect to find it on Amazon, but I did and bought a bag, along with a few other brands. So many different opinions on all the different brands that I was curious about the differences.

Gottta say, this one continues to be perfectly fine. I will continue to buy it. There are some nuances among the brands I bought, but they are all fine in a nearly equal way. The price point of this makes it a budget friendly repurchase. It is a product of Thailand, and I find it to be a good product. If I learn otherwise, i will let you know. The expiration date on this one is for sometime in 2023, so figure couple years from now.

I find drinking green tea (matcha) daily has greatly extinguished my need for sweets

title: excellent balance of ginger, spice, sweetness, and other ingredients that lend to flavor
text:
I was skeptical on the use of three types of sugar/sweetener (Erytrithol, sugar, stevia), but it works really really well. I'm impressed. It is sweet but not cloying or disruptive. It provides a good balanced taste. I am greatly keen on the overall flavor. I LOVE gingerale, and can never seem to find anything that has that deep ginger bite. I have tried to make my own ginger sodas, and seem to always fail. I did not expect this to nearly hit the mark on what I want out of a ginger drink. It has a robust ginger flavor with a hint of spicy heat. I repeat, there is SPICE this is a spicy ginger. It is AWESOME. The carbonation has a small tight bubble feel to it. Between the flavor and the carbonation, I feel the flavor hit the back of my throat. I like it a lot.

Almost reminds me of a spicy ginger beer. I think the difference is that the sweetness on this is more dry. They really did a good job of balancing the sweetness on this. The other ingredients likely lend to the flavor profile, and I really like it. Has additional ingredients that put this into a supplement category, not just drink. I get no jitters from this. It is mellow energy. I can drink it more like a soda, or a mixer. The cans look like skinny guiness, and my husband thought I was day drinking. lol

Acetyl L-Carnetine HCL, Bacopa Monnieri extract, Tumeric root extract, N-Acetyl L-Tyrosine, Alpha GPC, Natural Caffeine, Green Tea Leaf Extract, L-Carnetine Tartrate, Citicoline, Guarana Extract, Maltodextrin, Acai Juice Powder, Acerola Cherry Extract, Carbonated Water, Erytrithol, Sugar, Inulin, Citric Acid, Stevia Leaf Extract, Capsicum

I do not rate based on price. We all have different budgets and have different threshold on what we are willing to pay. I am very pleased with this. It will be a treat rather than a daily go to because I do not have budget for it. But I wont down rate because of MY finances. I am just super pleased that this exceeded my expectations in terms of flavor. I'd consider it again, and I would recommend it.

title: robust smooth coffee w/ gentle, delicate note of fresh natural blueberry. No Jitters
text:
If you like artificial tasting flavored weak coffee, then this is not for you. :) This blows my mind how perfect tasting this Blueberry option is. I do not like blueberry coffee. Never have I liked it, so I never bother buying it. So why am I drinking this? Because, 6 months ago I tried their pumpkin offering. I am not into flavored coffee, but I am pretty basic and love all things pumpkin when the fall season starts. I had to try it as was so impressed as to how natural it tasted-- like actual pumpkin and not some artificial simulation of "pumpkin". It instantly became a must have, and I had since purchased from this brand. SO when a blueberry option came up, I nearly passed it over because.. ew, blueberry in coffee. But then I remembered my experience with the pumpkin, and thought it worthwhile to try it out. For science! er, for... free caffeine! :P

I put a cup in my brewer and walked away. When I came back into the kitchen, I was floored at how wonderful my kitchen smelled. I could SMELL FRESH BLUEBERRIES. Mildly confused because in the 42 seconds I was away I managed to forget I made a cup of coffee. What is this sorcery???

I drink my coffee black. Occasionally with cream. If I end up with a cup of coffee that doesnt taste good, then I have to add cream. When I try coffee out for the first time, I make sure to try it both ways so I can report how it tastes under both circumstances (sorry, I never add sugar).

BLACK: OH MY-- yum. Dark leaning medium, or medium leaning Dark roast is robust. Makes my tastebuds sing, and my brain cells perk up. The BLUEBERRY is subtle. Might be too subtle for some. Much of it has to do with the scent wafting from the cup, followed by the hint of berry taste in the cup. And what is there is very natural. Not artificial. Kind of what I would imagine as the difference between a basket full of fresh blueberries aroma vs an artificial "blueberry" scented body spray (not that I would ever wear something like that). I mean, it is just so well done that it brings a tear to my eye. So I will say it again.. it is a good robust coffee flavored coffee with a hint, a gentle, delicate note of fresh blueberry. If you prefer a more cloying, artificial blueberry taste, then this coffee (this brand) may not be for you.

WITH CREAM: this coffee holds up to cream. The coffee taste doesnt disappear. It is just more mellow. The blueberry gets further pushed to the background, and it really quite flippin' delightful. I never ever thought I would ever say that I like a blueberry flavored coffee. It doesn't compute. BUT once again, WAKE THE HELL UP coffee did it again. I am impressed. Also cool, is that they are located in my state of NY.

Another thing-- when I have tried "extra caffeinated" coffee, the coffee is degraded by a weird mix of arabica and robusta (which has more caffeine). Usually those are tolerable at best. I do not know what they do with this brand, but the coffee just tastes good to me. Smooth, easy to drink black or with cream, and it doesnt make me feel jittery.

here is my review for the pumpkin. I just reread it and I am amused at my fidelity of enthusiasm and description.
