title: perfect size for a couple batches of seitan (wheat meat). Great option for meatless mondays
text:
Seitan! On occasion, I make seitan- wheat meat. When I do, I go through a lot of vital wheat glutan. Usually I find small boxes at the grocery store which if fine if all I wanted it for is for bread making. But when it comes to making seitan steaks, sausages, and other "meat" dishes, I go through a lot- most recipes call for at least 1.5 cups. So this 20 ounce will provide a couple of recipes worth.

I'm not vegan, not even vegetarian, but I eat everything. I swear, seitan really hits the spot (if done right), and makes for an impressive "meatless monday" (or any day) option. Best mouthfeel, taste, and sight in terms of meat swap. Also a good option for meal prep options. If you cant get to the store, but have a hankering for something meaty-- whip up a batch of seitan! (practice makes perfect)

"It's Just" is a good brand. I have tried several items now, and they have all been of perfectly good quality.

The bag is a mylar style pressure zip bag.

$9.99 for 20 ounces is a fair price. If you go through a lot, then this is better priced than the tiny boxes offered in store. It isn't as good of a price as some of the much larger quantity options, but that makes sense since usually the greater the bulk, the better the price. BUT that is only helpful if you know you will be going through A LOT, So for me, this 20 ounce is good if I know I will be making a couple of batches of my seitan. If I knew I was going to make a lot more, then I may choose another options (2-4 lbs). I dont rate on price anyway, but I thought I would mention my thoughts.

title: big fresh bag of flour in pressure zip mylar bag
text:
"It's Just" is a good brand. They did a good job with including solid info on this package. The bag is a sturdy, pressure zip stay fresh mylar style bag. Easy to work with. Smells fresh, looks good- smooth and powdery.

Cassava flour is made from the yucca plant. Made from the entire root, it is more of a “whole food”. Once turned into a flour, it can be used as a 1:1 swap for wheat flour, or do a mix of flours depending on your needs. Might need to play around with it (and other ingredients) to get the right texture for what you are aiming to achieve. It doesn't provide same rise and loft ability of gluten flours, so keep that in mind when looking to make breads, doughs, etc. Just poke around online for recipes.

I had thought that this may be a good swap for me in terms of glucose control, but every time I read articles (including medical journals) the information varies greatly. I think much of the info ends up looking at tapioca flour rather than the whole food cassava flour (even the medical publications vary in what they use to determine glycemic index, etc). Very similar to tapioca flour, as it too is made from yucca plant, but the two are not the same thing. Tapioca is the bleached and extracted starch of the cassava root- so more processes and more starchy, nothing further to break down, and there for provides an easier glucose hit. But still.. I have decided that I will use the cassava flour in moderation (like anything else). It's been a nice addition to my pantry, especially if I am being cognizant of those that require gluten free fare.

title: slow cook to rehydrate, similar texture to boxed scalloped potatoes
text: Know that it takes awhile to rehydrate dried potatoes. Think of the potatoes contained in a box of scalloped potatoes- they are like that, but in small flat squares. End up in similar texture too. So no, not exactly like a fresh potato at all. But it is potato, and it is edible. Let it slow cook, or let it seep in water for several hours. Just give it time. Wish the packaging had this info. Also, would prefer a resealable bag, or perhaps a mylar style bag for freshness. Not a big deal if you will be using these up in a short while, but if you are buying to add to pantry for longer term storage then you may want a different container. Love stuff like this to have on hand when fresh isn't available. It isn't my go to, but I do always have dehydrated foods on hand.

title: satisfying level of sweetness, good taste & texture, hits the spot (pair w/yogurt/fruit/smoothie)
text:
I really like this. It hits the spot. Your experience may vary, but since I have a huge appetite, it isn't quite enough for me as a meal. I mean, I can eat it alone and feel fine, but I could easily eat more. Maybe its good that this is portion controlled. When I do need more, I bulk it out adding a glop of Greek yogurt on top, and then having a banana on the side. Or having a smoothie. Then it is perfect. Doesn't weigh me down. I eat this as a dessert too, as it has a satisfying level of sweetness. I love steel cut oats, and I love the granola add in-- very easy on my teeth.
Overall taste is very good to me.

Cooking it is a little weird. Ok, here it goes: take granola cup off (also serves as lid). Peel back the film over the cup that holds the steel cut oats. Looks disappointingly empty--but it does bulk out quite a bit once cooked. Add water to fill line. Where the eff is the fill line? It's on the outside- and just shows a little slash mark. It would be so much better to have a line on the inside. Ok, add the water (or milk). Put in microwave for 40s. Stir. Heat another 10-25s. Stir. Let sit. Add granola. OR you can add hot water and let sit for 5 minutes.

If on the go, just use the empty granola cup as the lid.

I really like this as the convenience item it is. I also like it as a dessert type item after a light dinner.

title: very rich luscious cream that instantly combats dry, parched skin. FOR DRY SKIN only
text:
Very rich cream that is definitely intended for those with dry, parched skin. Definitely not for those with reactive skin- it is rich. This formula is targeted toward those with mature skin; the age focus being in 60+ (I failed to see that when I ordered this). My dry 40+ skin lapped up this rich cream, and it was nice to have skin that didnt feel tight. For day or night, if you dont meet the age focus, then it may be best as a night cream. It very much reminds me of one. The cream has a pale pink color- reminds me of something I used to use or maybe sell back when I worked in a skin care store (merle norman), some 20+ years ago. Kinda also reminds of me of the old Oil of Olay night cream in terms of scent. I find it pleasant, but that is subjective.

They dont include ingredients here, nor on their website. Packaging is hard to read (small print on dark glossy box that has raised bumps/texture). I see some very rich ingredients to start such as lanolin, cholesterol, various oils, glycerin, shea butter. Variety of ceramides, ferments, flower extracts, and hyaluronic acid.

I have to say, it looks like a decent product, and feels like quality to the touch and how it feels on my skin. Typical 1.7 fluid ounce sizing. Little goes a long way. Pot style with easy to twist off lid. The size of the container is good for getting a handle on. Not so small to slip from hand, not so large that it is hard to grasp. The lid can double as a mirror.

I do not rate on price. No point for me. I have used much more expensive, and much less expensive stuff, with varying results. We all have different budgets, and mine is on the high side because I love skin care and it is a bit of a hobby of mine. But it comes down to what works for us. I think this may be worthwhile for those that are curious about this line, and have the budget for it. I mean, why not? :) . I see they have lots of other products. If they would include ingredient list, I would feel better about recommending.

But you know what, if I have an opportunity to try other products from this company, I absolutely will. I am intrigued, and my experience with this is favorable enough to want more. Early impression, but Im stoked to use this--it really helps my dry skin. Im pleased enough to go with 5 stars.

title: tasty, salty, ultra convenient noodle bowl. Add in some veg & protein to round it out
text:
Jjapaguri!! Chapaguri is simply a combination of two different Korean instant noodles “Spaghetti” and “Neoguri". Basically thicker and thinner noodles- so, more robust than what is found in typical dried raman squares. For fans of Parasite, this is what is referred to in the movie as "ram-don".

It is exactly as I expected- a dried raman noodle bowl. So yeh, expect the typical salty semi bland processed food flavor. It is a huge bowl, with lots of noodles. Excellent for a quick meal, even better if you can add in some fresh vegetables and protein. I think taste is good. A little spicy but not hot. I tend to "doctor up" stuff like this with extra pinch of garlic, black pepper, and sriracha.

I do not eat stuff like this regularly, but I do have a cupboard filled with foods like this. It makes for a great flavor, texture base for a larger dish (and then the salt isnt so scary), also is part of my food cache as I like to keep simple to make foods on hand in case of emergency. And yes, also is just fine on its own in a pinch for a quick lunch. I definitely recommend adding some vegetables and/or meat to it to round it out.

Price is about right- I find these in store for $3.50- 5.00 each.

5 stars. Its just exactly as anticipated and is good for what it is: processed, convenient, high sodium noodle bowl. Not exquisite flavor, but good flavor.

title: Gorgeous red peppers. 16 ounces makes for a giant bag- glorious!
text:
This 16 ounce bag provides A LOT of dried arbol chili peppers. I only dabble in heat, so this will last longer than what it rational for my use. I will be sharing this with a couple of friends. Got me thinking that it would be nice to bag up a couple handfuls and add it to a food themed gift. A bargain too. (Brilliant idea, precidedisarray!). Like others have mentioned, it is the whole pepper, including tops. The peppers are pliable, so not quite a super dried pepper (though this is what I have had in the past with other brands, of other peppers, so I am not sure what is normal anymore).

My first use in in soup. Today! I make soup often and look for different flavor profiles to literally spice things up. I decided to go with lots of vegetables, remains of a rotisserie chicken, a variety of spices, and a few of these peppers. I took out a handful (maybe 8-9 peppers) and placed them in a cup of hot broth to soften them up. Maybe about 10 minutes in this broth bath. Curious, I dipped my finger in this cup (maybe 1.5 cups) of broth and tasted it. WOWZA. That short bath released a whole lot of heat. So then I decided to not use 8-9 peppers, and decided to stick with three for a 10 quart pot of soup. I cut them up, discarded half of the seeds, and placed the peppers in with the remainder of soup. Definitely spiced it up! I tossed on one whole pepper for the fun of it. (I may regret it later. Soup is still cooking on low for a couple more hours as I write this).

I also had with some deviled eggs. I chopped up one small one from the broth bath, and added it into the deviled egg mixture. Oh boy, that was spicy. Definitely reminds me of cayenne, but with just a little more depth of flavor.

My next use will likely be with my "spicy peanut chicken noodles" (basically I make a peanut sauce and spice it up with sriracha, but I am going to hot it up with these peppers- then I add it to a thick noodle and piece of chicken (or firm tofu) and vegetables).

I would buy these again. If I ever get through this bag, haha

title: GOOD! Stevia with a HINT of natural, pleasant caramel. Mix into anything 1/8tsp=1 tsp sugar
text:
It is STEVIA plus CARAMEL flavor. THAT'S IT! Well, more specifically: organic inulin, organic caramel flavor, and organic stevia 97%. So if you like stevia, and you like a natural caramel, there are no surprises in taste. Dont dip your finger in it and expect to have it taste "good". Dont stick your nose in it. Just use it, and then decide. It's pretty good.

This is concentrated and intense. But add it to baking, add it to coffee and creamer, add it to oatmeal, etc.. then you get a bit of sweet and a hint of pleasant caramel. The caramel is the better of any I have tried (especially compared to liquid drops which tend to be yuck for me). THIS just tastes natural over artificial. IF ANYTHING, the taste of caramel is a tad weak compared to the level of sweet. Overall, very smooth, stirs seamlessly into my coffee. Nice option to have. It will take me forever to use this.
REMINDER: this is not a 1:1 swap. 1/8th of a teaspoon of this is equivalent to 1 teaspoon of sugar.

If a shaker container doesn't appeal to you, then they also offer packets (2 serving per packet, 200 servings total. This BOTTLE provides 200 servings too).
https://www.amazon.com/Delicioso-All-Natural-Substitute-Concentrated-100-Packets/dp/B08M15L5S5/

The container is about 5 inches tall. The powder takes up about a third of it. Does it need to be said that products are filled based on weight, not volume? Settling occurs. Sure this could easily be a 3 inch container, but I have no issue with it being 5"-- easier to see in my cupboard, and easy to shake. But a smaller bottle would be fine too. Either way, it does not mean we are getting less than the 1.6 ounces (45 grams).

Top has 3 options for dispensing, much like a salt shaker. Small holes, larger holes, and a wide slat.

I hemmed and hawed over the rating. The only negative is that the caramel could be a little stronger, but then I realized that I do taste it, it is just more subtle than a smack in the face. Side by side with other caramel laced stevia, this is the best of the bunch. So consider my rating to be 4.5 (but will hit the 5 stars since I think this is better than just 4). Hope that makes sense.

title: packets of instant coffee w/ broccoli & artichoke extract supplement. Good hot/cold
text:
Slim & Detox? I have no idea, and I am skeptical. I'm a sucker for coffee, so here I am. But it can't hurt to drink some coffee with broccoli and artichoke extract. Just cut open the packet, dump into a mug, add 8 ounces of hot water. Stir. Enjoy. I drink it black, or I drink it with some vanilla keto protein drink as a creamer.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08F4N1DL3/

20 packets for $20 make it $1 per cup of coffee

The coffee is instant. I like instant and it tastes like instant. Robust, leans dark. I dont pick up on anything else. If you dont want it hot, then add in some ice, or add it to a smoothie. Nice for on the go (works fine with hot tap water, or even cold), even if you are only looking for the coffee component only.

I'm giving an early impression rating of 4. I like the product, but way to early to tell if it has enough of anything to have a "slim and detox" effect. Will I know within 20 servings? Can I drink them all at once and be slim by days end? lol. There are no indications. I assume 1 packet per day. I see there are other offerings- instant coffee with supplements for immunity, for power, for men.. kind of neat take on a supplement. If you have money to blow and are curious.. go for it.

I'll be back to update if I learn anything new, or experience anything worth noting. I keep up with my reviews so I will be sure to add something by the end of May 2021.

title: light, easy crunch. Small puffed cracker, a little salty a little veggie
text:
Once again, Made Good is Mad Good. I love their products. These puffed crackers are easy to eat. I refrained from trying these for awhile because they arrived just as I got oral surgery. Kinda forgot that soft foods will be my life for awhile. But as I healed and began testing the chewing waters, I decided to get into a bag of these puffed crackers. They are easy on my teeth. While they are sturdy with a light crunch, they crunch down without being sharp or too hard. Small too- maybe size of a coin but puffed. Similarly sized to an oyster cracker.

Yummy taste. A little salty, a little veggie. Initially reminds me of a saltine, but the veggie flavor follows which makes this more of a light snack, than a basic cracker. Not super strong flavor, and that is what I was hoping for. Just something light and easy. Great alone as a snack directly from bag, or along with some soup. I see they have other flavors like cheddar or pizza.

I'd buy this again. I like stuff like this a lot

title: pleased with this powder creamer by Happy Belly
text:
I either drink my coffee black, or add the occasional liquid cream. I keep the powder variety on hand for options for other people, but I use it on occasion too. I am already familiar with, and have a favorable impression of a wide assortment of Happy Belly products, so I figured this would be a good quality too. It is!
Makes my coffee creamy, adds a creamy taste but no real discernable flavor. Works for what it is.

$1.99 for 16 ounces. Nice!

title: so versatile. Nice option to add to smoothies, oatmeal, yogurt, homemade ice cream etc
text:
Wish I knew about banana powder before now. I have purchased so many bunches of bananas to only have them go bad before I get around to them. Sometimes I peel them, slice them, and toss them in a freezer bag so I have them for a later date for baking and smoothies, but having a bag of powder adds to my options. Somestimes I will want the benefit of the actual fruit, and sometimes I more or less just want the flavor. I love banana! And so this awesome to have on hand. I recently added it into some homemade ice cream, and home made milk shake, some meal replacement smoothies (added it to a vanilla base), and I imagine the possibilities are endless.

Good banana flavor for banana lovers

title: convenient, tasty, versatile. I'd buy again!
text: It's gravy! I'm giving it 5 stars because it is exactly what I expected- good flavor, easy to make. Budget friendly too. I usually make my own from drippings or broth, but sometimes a quick packet makes it extra convenient. I've used a few Happy Belly gravy packets, and have enjoyed them all. I like the brand. Can also be used to flavor soup or chili base. For the past several days I have been pretty much just eating mashed potatoes for dinner. Had oral surgery, so soft foods is all I am on at the moment. I have options, but mashed potatoes seem to hit the spot. I didn't make up the whole packet at once as I usually do. I wasn't sure if I wanted gravy each time, so I just made a little. This worked out too, so in that sense I learned something new. I'd definitely buy this again.

title: bright, saturated colors. Neon? depends on how you mix, and what you add it to
text:
I'm pleased with this color assortment. Gel dyes seem more concentrated, so that is what I usually buy these days. I am not often in need of food coloring, but once in awhile I like to change things up when making a frosting. So my experience with these is just on that- frosting cookies, cupcakes, and cakes. Oh, and macarons. Colors are vibrant, bright. Really just performs as expected for gel food coloring. I like the long tip dispenser- feels easier to control what I am squirting out. My others have a flip cap and flat top. The long nozzle plus screw on cap also seem to lend to having a product that wont dry out, or accidentally open. I didn't think about that until now. So yeh, definitely pleased with this set by AGQ.

PS. The colors are bright and vibrant, but not exactly neon to me. I actually prefer the look of these colors as really all I wanted is a true, bright, color saturated dye. But when I think of Neon, I think of an off color- a neon green would be more chartreuse, and this is more of a vibrant kelly/grass green. The red is pretty red, yellow is bright yellow, etc. You can get the green to be more chartreuse by adding some yellow.

title: PHEW! I ordered on whim. So glad it isn't sweet. Just fizzy water w/ grapefruit/citrus
text:
I love carbonation. I love grapefruit. I do not like sweet drinks. So I am always wary when I go to grab a seltzer water as sometimes it has added sugar or sugar alternative. Yuck. I ordered this on a whim, and then was concerned that I may be getting a sweet drink. I failed to take a closer look. When it arrived and I saw no mention of added sugar or sugar alternative. Just carbonated water.. but then I noticed that there is orange juice and lemon juice. I figured I would be disappointed on some level- would it even taste like grapefruit?

First, is it not at all sweet, which is what I wanted. YAY! I just want plain carbonated water with a notable taste of grapefruit. The addition of orange juice and lemon juice sort sit in the background- really just rounds out the citrus taste without adding any sweetness or overpowering the grapefruit. Again, YAY

It has a good level of carbonation. I love my carbonation, so I can handle the higher levels. This is a more mellow amount, but still satisfies my need for the bubblies.

So, I am pleased, and would consider buying this brand again.

title: exactly what I was looking for: JUST carbonated water with natural ginger flavor
text:
I love ginger. I love carbonation. I wanted a simple carbonated water with ginger- JUST ginger. No sugar, no other flavors. This Langers Organic Flavored Sparkling Water, Ginger seemed to promise that, and it delivers.

I was worried that the ginger would be barely detectable, but I can taste the ginger. Phew! It is robust enough to feel like I have had a ginger drink. In the past I have mixed plain club soda or seltzer water with ginger juice concentrate from The Ginger People https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00HYJR9YK
But sometimes it watered down my fizz. So I am pleased that this Ginger flavored Sparkling water is tasty enough and needs no modification--unless I am feeling creative.

I will buy again.

title: robust, sweet, has thick truffle, and good whole hazelnut crunch
text:
A whole hazelnut in the center, surrounded my thick layer of truffle, then encased in a crispy chocolate shell. It has a robust, sweet taste with a mix of crunchy and smooth texture. I dont want to compare it directly to Ferrero Roche as I am not real familiar with it. But I did make a point to share it with people who are familiar with that candy as I was curious their thought on how similar it was, and how the overall taste is. They said that it is good, and reminds them of the other candy. Not the exact same-- this one has a little more substance to it. Overall both are good with no preference for one over the other.

I think that the chocolate is a bit different. Has a little more sweetness, and more robust taste. The other has a smoother, subtle taste. I really have no preference either. I think it really just comes down to trying it. This company isn't trying to be the other company. It just happens to offer one product that is in same shape as the other.

I think this brand has a stronger taste and more robust mouth feel. I am not a huge fan of truffle (that smooth ganache texture), and I think this has a little more of that going on.

Overall I think it is good. I like how there are a few different sizes to choose from. I have the option where it is two trays of 8 candies in a hard plastic container X2. Then both are tucked into a box. A nutrition into insert is included in bottom of each plastic box. This set up allowed me to share half of this package easily.

title: yummy easy to make gravy mix
text: Good flavor, easy to make. I dont often make gravy, but once in awhile it just takes a meal up a notch. Comfort food! Usually I am making it from meat juices, but having a packet to make up a quick gravy is really nice to have on hand. Maybe  I need to make a point to buy more. I know a packet of gravy can also serve as a seasoning, meat tenderizer, and even as a base to a thin sauce or soup. Lots of options. I made this though as per directions, and enjoyed myself a pork, mashed potato, and vegetable meal with side of gravy (originally intended to use a pork gravy packet, but was sent a Happy Belly pork rub instead-- which worked out well since I had a tenderloin ready for it). I have pretty much liked anything I have ever had by Happy Belly, an Amazon brand.

title: pork rub is great, other Happy Belly gravies & sauces are yummy
text: Well, hmm. I received a large packet of pork rub instead of gravy. The rub is fantastic, so it has been a pleasant mix up. I happen to have tried a couple of different Happy Belly gravy and sauce mixes which I liked a lot (Happy Belly usually does a good job with their products), so I imagine the pork gravy would have been just as good. I cant see the product page so I am not sure if I am only one or not that received pork rub instead of pork gravy.

title: SO GOOD!! I only drink super dark roasts, and this light is very smooth, very palatable
text:
I purchase Veteran Roasters coffee on occasion because it is amazing--it is a great quality coffee from a company with an excellent mission. "OUR MISSION: Veteran Roasters is dedicated to roasting great coffee to give homeless and unemployed veterans a place to work and regain their lives. They were on the ground for us, buy some grounds for them. VETERAN OWNED: Veteran Roasters is 100% veteran owned. We help veterans who struggle to truly return home. We hire homeless and unemployed veterans, provide skilled training along with a livable wage."

I always purchase the dark roast as I greatly prefer a strong, bold, cup of coffee. So when this option came up, I jumped on it but failed to see that it said light roast. I normally vehemently dislike light roasts. I tend to find them too green, too bright, too acidic, too bitter. Makes my brain pucker. I drink my coffee black, so overall taste profile is important. Well, first thing I noticed when this bag arrived is how amazing it smelled. The aroma wafts from the bag-- it is well vented. I normally dont even care for the aroma of light roasted coffee, but this had me sniffing on it repeatedly. Mmm.

When it came time to grind some beans, I noted the dry look, and attractive looking colors. Just extra picturesque. Definitely a light roast with its lack of oil sheen. I proceeded to grind what I needed for a half a pot of coffee. Reddish coffee, dry.. still smelling really good. I used my drip Ninja Specialty Coffee System to "classic" brew half a pot. I used about 4 of the Ninja scoops (approximately 8 TBS) with 30 ounces of water.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07PFLM2LK

WOW. This is undoubtedly the best "light roast" I have ever had. I normally really cant stomach it. I usually find it blegh. It is smooth, balanced, not at all bitter. It has a mild bright finish. I think those that prefer light roasts will enjoy the extra smooth easy taste. I also think that those that prefer medium will very much enjoy this, and may not exactly notice it being a light roast. It is a medium leaning light. As for those who prefer the darkest of dark roasts? Definitely try their dark roast option, BUT I think if offered this light roast at someones house, you would tolerate it well. It's impressive, really!! It definitely has the caffeine kick that only light roasts can truly offer.

While I prefer black, I did try it with cream. It stands up well to half and half being added in. Maintains a coffee taste and just further mellows out the overall taste.

Pressure zip bag

title: Very smooth, surprisingly extra good tasting strong robust coffee. Fine powder
text:
I always have instant coffee on hand. I use it in baking to amp up the taste of chocolate, or to add a special coffee flavor. I also drinking it willingly, lol. I make brewed coffee, pour over coffee, K-cups, and the occasional cold brew. And sometimes I just want instant coffee. It just hits the spot sometimes.. I had purchased this Nescafe Gold Espresso as I had just run out of my jar of regular Nescafe. I was looking for a dark roast option (which they have) but then saw the Espresso option. I was like.. hmm, I need to try this.

Love it! The coffee is a super fine powder, this is going to be even better in baked goods than the usual chunks of instant coffee. I can use it to sprinkle on top of stuff too. The fine powder makes it dissolve instantly. Works well blended into cold drinks, too.

As for a cup of coffee. OH YES. The directions say to use 1-2 tsp in 50 ml (1/3 cup) of water for a shot of espresso, or 1-2 tsp in 250 ml (1 cup) of water for an Americano. I tried 1 tsp in 50 ML and was impressed with the robust taste. Love the "crema" that forms on top. Lasts a short while then blends into cup.

TASTE is surprisingly smooth with a hint of sweet. It is just coffee- nothing added to it. It is not only good for an instant but it is pretty dang good as a coffee, period. It is robust and strong without being bitter. Definitely try it out following the directions, then work from there. There is no way I could sip that much instant in such little water with any other brand. Even this brand. But something about this espresso blend just works. I will buy it again.

Pictures are of just water poured onto coffee. Nothing added.

title: light leaning medium, floral-fruity, mild acidity, bright tasting
text:
I know how a coffee tastes completely comes down to preference. What I like about it, you may dislike. What turns me off about it, may be exactly what you are looking for. I'll do my best to at least explain it, so you can decide if it sounds good to you.

--7 ounce bag of whole coffee. Manufactured in August 2019, with best by date of August 2021. I acquired this in March of 2021. I'll finish it off well before this, but the date closing in had me concerned that I got a aging product. It smells and tastes fresh enough.
--A MEDIUM roast, that leans a little light. I can taste that slightly green, slightly floral/fruity, semi acidic tastes. It almost reminds me of a cup of coffee from a dunkin donuts store (which I dont like, at all). Just a wee bit bitter for me. But others love it, so you very well may like this if you enjoy that flavor profile.
--My personal preference is black, unsweetened coffee. Prefer very dark roasted oily coffee, but as a coffee lover I am inclined to drink all the coffee presented to me. I can handle a smooth, middle of road medium, or a dark leaning medium so long as it isnt bitter or too acidic. As a roast leans lighter, it takes on more of a green taste, bright taste, usually acid feel. THIS has that latter comment, just not as much tang as some. For that is is closer to being balanced tasting (bit not quite).
--In order to make this palatable for me, I have to add a copious amount of cream. Still tastes bright, but it isn't as acidic.

For me, it is not a preferred coffee and would not be a repurchase. Again, this is all based on MY preference. And all that I described may be exactly what you are looking for.

By the way, I use a Ninja Specialty Coffee Maker. I make half a pot (30 ounces) using 4 of their scoops (I think about 2 TBS per scoop?), on "classic" brew (regular amount of time for water to drip through), using filtered water.

title: very very good, very very sweet. Chewy mango, soft aloe, and super sugary
text:
Very good- excellent taste and texture. A mix of dried mango and dried aloe pieces. The dried aloe reminds me of dried pineapple in texture- soft light chew, and the mango is perfectly dried mango- dense, chewy. I can taste mango, but the aloe pieces are more like chewy wafers of sugar. I expected a stronger aloe taste, but it's faint. Maybe a good thing as aloe can be weird, but I could handle a stronger aloe taste to come through.

Downside? 1 bag has TWO servings. I eat the whole 2.1 ounce bag. That is 220 calories, which is fine but 50 grams of total sugar (18 grams of DDED sugar). I love dried fruit, but I treat it like candy. There is nothing else going for it. Even when no added sugar the sugar content is very high. So here, I can understand the naturally occurring sugar, but why add so much cane sugar? This isnt the only company who adds sugar to sweet dried fruit and call it "healthy".

Crazy thing? There are two other options-- and THIS is the one with the least amount of added & total sugar. I so want to try the aloe and ginger.. omg.. 70 grams sugar with 26 grams of added for the small bag. So sad!

Now, I dont need to have eaten all of it. So its totally on me that I just took a 50 grams of sugar hit, but yeesh. I legit have a container of cookies nearby, and 1 big chewy pepperridgefarm cookie has 12g of sugar, 7 added

so no, I would not say that this is a "It's a healthy snack alternative"
but is is so flipping yummy. LOVE the texture.

I am really keen on trying other options IF the added sugar content wasn't so astronomical. ALO, please take all this into consideration!

5 stars freshness, texture, even overall taste.
Massive added sugar: omg.. 1 star
BUT, since I failed to take a look at the nutritional information while making a selection, that is on me. 4 stars because it is really tasty and hits the spot

title: when weighed, 5 grams = 1 full TBS (1 tsp=2 grams). Sweet from sucralose, very natural vanilla
text:
The serving size states 30 calories for 1 tsp/ 5 grams. These do not equate/convert. I was suspicious of this as most creamers are 30 calories for 1 TBS. Now the conversion can be 1 tsp for 5 grams depending on what is being measured/weighed. To confirm my suspicion, I WEIGHED 5 grams of this creamer, and it indeed just filled my 1 TBS measuring spoon. I then measured out 1 teaspoon, and WEIGHED it on my food scale, and it came in at 2 grams. So go ahead and use a full tablespoon for 30 calories. Why? because then it comes to food, it is better to measure based on weight rather than volume.

I prefer this over other brands because the vanilla is more natural tasting. I definitely prefer this over other brand name sugar free versions as the taste is also pretty natural. I am super picky on flavored creamer, and often dont bother buying it because over and over again I am disappointed, but I do keep some on hand for company. I usually drink my coffee black, or will use real cream or half & half--but will try something different once in awhile. And I hope it tastes good. This tastes good to me. Love powdered form as it will keep much longer than liquid.

I have tried some flavored creamers and had to dump my coffee. So when I tried this, I expected it to taste off, and was worried that I would pouring my coffee out. But it doesn't taste off- all considered it is the best I have tried in a long time. I drank my whole cup! For the most part, it is just like all the others out there in terms of ingredients. Sweetened with sucralose, which is quite sweet. It doesnt lighten my coffee a lot (unless I use a lot, but then it is crazy sweet).

Mixes very well- no effort needed. Glad to have tried this, glad to have something good to offer company, and good for me. I think it is worth the try!

title: JUST fruit. Each packets=1 cup fruit. Great alone, in oatmeal, on salads, in trail mix
text:
WHAT TO KNOW:
--12 packs of dried fruit tucked in a box.
--Soft, triangular pieces of fruit leather. Approximately 15 pieces per packet (20g)

If I add in some nuts, crackers, or other nibbles, I have a tasty little snack. Hits the sweet tooth, especially when I want a gummy candy--without it being candy. I dotn rate on price- just on quality, experience, and how it met expectations. This is something i would consider again (already eyeballing another flavor option) and would recommend. All else is up to you.

YUM YUM.

title: plenty of pearls and straws to get your boba tea on
text: Loved this kit. Tapioca pearls cooked up perfectly for my boba tea needs. I appreciate the inclusion of wide straws for my drink. The amount of pearls have been plenty. I made countless drinks before finally running out. I would purchase again.

title: love the flavor combinations, chewy compressed fruit/ with texture
text:
I love "That's It" products. Truly, what is described on packets is all that is in it. That's it! The fruit is not quite formed into a leather, but it is firmly compressed. Leather is more of a masticated sludge dehydrated into a smooth chewy piece. This product is like taking dehydrated fruit, chopping it small, and compressing it tightly together. It stays all in one firm chewy piece, but there is texture from fruit bits. That gives it a better mouth feel to me.

Taste is a fresh as expected. Flavor is exactly as expected since there is nothing else added. Apples and Cinnamon taste like.. apples and cinnamon. Apple, Pear & Ginger is perfectly balanced. I can taste the sweetness from the fruit, then has a belly warming finish of ginger. Apple, Mango & Chili is awesome- sweet with a tinge of heat.

Excellent on the go, or at home when wanting something sweet but not wanting the calories or heaviness of a processed sugar laden food.

I had initially discovered That's It fruit bars a few years ago when I randomly purchased a lunch-able (or something like it, maybe another brand), and as part of the lunch kit, it had a fruit bar instead of the usual candy bar. I found it so delightful that I sought to buy just the fruit bar. So I have been eating those for awhile. When this "spice" option came up, I had to give it a try. These are great. The other thing I love? The box their products come in. Sturdy, simple design, even had a print of a bow on it. Makes it giftable.

title: syrup viscosity, floral-fruity taste (reminds me of lychee), raw, natural, low glycemic
text:
This was totally new to me. I was intrigued by the low glycemic index as I am trying..*trying*.. to cut back on sugar. This is a highly fluid, dark brown, natural sweetener made from the tuberous roots of the yacon plant. Leans a little more honey like with its floral fruity taste. Sweet but not sugar sweet. More like agave in sweetness level. If you are familiar with lychee fruit, it has a similar tasting note to me. I would liken this for use where you would honey, agave, maybe molasses (just not as bright, robust, nor as dense). I wouldn't use this in coffee (nor would I use Honey), but definitely pairs well with tea. Use it like a syrup--- pancakes, oatmeal, yogurt. I havent tried it in baking, but I am going to look into that. 5 stars as it seems like a quality product despite not having anything to compare it to. But I am pleased so far.

If I bought this again, I would prefer it in a squeeze bottle. Small 7 ounce jar is like opening a jar of something fluid and sticky. Be careful the first time opening it. Either way, I am pleased with this. Some may not like the taste, so I imagine that will determine a lot of reviews. I like the fact that it is a low glycemic sugar alternative that may help me cut down on sugar in some areas of life. If not that, then for the host of potential health benefits I have been reading about since trying this (better bone health, immunity, digestion, etc)

half the calories of sugar and a high concentration of indigestible inulin
1 tsp contains:
10 calories
3 grams carbs
2 grams sugars

more infoDrAxe
"Yacon root syrup contains a high percentage of fructooligosaccharides, which are prebiotics that pass through the upper part of the gastrointestinal tract and remain undigested. When fructooligosaccharides reach the colon undigested, they are then fermented by gut microflora, increasing bowel mass and promoting the growth of beneficial bacteria. For these reasons, yacon root syrup can be helpful when it comes to digestive issues, such as providing natural constipation relief and treating traveler’s diarrhea"

title: doesn't pack as much punch as actual salt, but pretty good dupe
text:
I'm glad there are sodium free options. Just using flavorful spices is not enough for my palate. I have tried "salt free" blends of spices and again not enough to quench that salt need. However, I still try to incorporate sodium free or lower salt options into my life. I am trying, anyway. I know lots of people in my life that swear by this Morton Sodium Free Salt Substitute. If I didn't like it I knew I could pass it on.

As expected, it doesn't quite pack the same punch as my usual Redmond real Salt has. I know my usual salt tastes a lot different than typical table salt, so perhaps I need to compare this substitute against regular white table salt instead. For that, they are closer in taste and tang. I have tried this in food prep and as a topper on cooked food. I shaked the amount I usually use and found I couldnt quite taste it. I added more, and could just detect the tang.

Overall I prefer my usual Real Salt, but when it comes to table salt vs this sodium free stuff, I think it is about the same. Table salt being a little more bitey.

Ultimately, if sodium needs to be reduced or totally cut out, then please give this a try. Its fine. It isnt salt, but it will give you a little of that salt vibe as well as still providing the ritual of using salt if you are the type to shake it on no matter how much salt may already be in something.

title: like any other flavored instant oatmeal: sweet, quick, a little gummy. Hits the spot!
text:
Perfect dupe for name brand equivalent. I'm not rating it based on how healthy or unhealthy I think it is. If you have purchased flavored instant oatmeal packets in the past- name brand or generic- then you know they are pretty much all the same- oats, sugar, added vitamins/minerals. I imagine the more discerning among us may note some fine differences, but for me I am not picky when it comes to flavored oatmeal.

You will know to expect an easy to make, sweet tasting, slightly gummy instant oat meal. Happy Belly has created an equivalent. It is exactly as expected, and I have been enjoying it as much as any other brand or generic of the same idea. As with all the others, I tend to use two packets, or I use one packet and add in some plain oatmeal (or if I want to beef it up, use steel cut as my based then add this in for flavor).

I dont do anything fancy. I dump two in a small bowl. Add a healthy amount of water. Put in microwave for a minute or so, then eat it. Or boil water separately then pour on top, stir, eat. Sometimes this type of breakfast (snack, or even as a dessert) just hits the spot.

What you get: 4 each of
--Cinnamon Spice,
--Maple Brown Sugar, and
--Apple Cinnamon.

title: delicious, robust china sourced garlic
text:
Product of China, Processed in USA. Not organic. Why buy it if this is not what you wanted. The reviews kill me. If you're belly aching that this garlic is from China, then read the description and take a look at the product pictures. It is so clearly shown it is laughable. Second, "what are the ingredients"? Garlic. It is granulated garlic. Single ingredient item here, folks. Guess what, unless garlic is specifically stated where it is from, you bet it is from China.

We go through a lot of garlic, so 24 ounces is a good size to keep on hand. Will likely do a subscribe and save order. We have tried many different Happy Belly seasonings, and figured the garlic should be just as tasty and fresh as we have come to expect from Amazon Brand, Happy Belly. This big tub of garlic meets our expectations.

This granulated garlic has a robust flavor. It is a very small granule. I wouldnt have noticed it being more granular than a powder, but it does have a little bit more texture when I spoon some out in comparison. It is all good. It blends right in/dissolves when mixed with other ingredients, or stays lightly granular when sprinkled on top of something. Excellent in everything. MMmm love garlic.

title: lovely meaty seasoning with hint of sweet. Add it to everything!
text:
Oh, very nice. Lightly sweet, lightly meaty- has that lovely umami taste. Add this powdered shiitake mushroom in just about anything. I usually keep an assortment of dried whole mushrooms on hand, but this is upping my cooking game. There is nothing I wouldnt add it to, really. I love adding it to broth, to meat juice to make a gravy/sauce, add in to eggs, soups, raman/udon/soba noddles. Just go with it. Try a little by itself so you get an idea of what it tastes like before adding it into anything-- but know that the magic is in adding it to something.

NO MSG, no added anything. Just powdered mushroom. DELICIOUS.

I also really appreciate the attractive packaging. Such a pretty label. *swoon*

title: dark leaning medium. Ultra smooth. Coffee tasting coffee. No acidity
text:
The best part of waking up is trying a new coffee in my cup. I may stand alone on this, but I am pleasantly surprised with how smooth and mellow this coffee is while still tasting solidly like coffee AND giving me a good caffeine buzz. Didn't expect to try a coffee from "WANTAI?!" * ....er, Taiwan. I use my Ninja coffee maker, use 4 scoops of coffee (that I grind in my Krupps grinder) using the scooper that comes with my machine . My scoop is double sided. Larger side holds 2TBS per scoop, and it is suggested to use 3-4 of the bigger end for making a half pot (30 ounces) of coffee. so I use about 7-8 TBS for half a pot of coffee. I brew is "classic" style (basic water flow, for typical pot of coffee).
My ninja: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07PFLM2LK

I usually drink my coffee black. I always drink it black for review, then do a cup with cream to see how it holds up.

For coffee roasts-- I prefer a strong dark, bold roast. I rarely go for medium roast unless it leans dark and has minimal acidity. The lighter it is, the more apt it is to be bitter and acidic it seems.

This? is a very dark medium, or lighter dark. It is an enjoyable (to me) cup of coffee that I would have thought anyone would like. It is coffee tasting coffee, if that makes sense. Nothing competes with it- no tang, no bitter, no biting acidity, not so dark that it scares people away, but bold enough to appeal to lovers of dark roasts. The whole beans smell amazing, and require an extra whiff after being fresh ground.

I immediately noticed now flipping SMOOTH and Balanced it is. ZERO bitterness or acidity. It tastes like.. coffee.
While I love this black, no cream no sugar. I tried a cup with half and half. Sometimes creamer can only save a bad coffee, but sometimes it can highlight the wonderful notes of a good coffee. In this case, it provides the latter. The cream just added a more rounded mouth feel and the coffee still maintained its "coffee" flavor. It didnt dilute.

I definitely felt like I had caffeine after drinking this. I had two small cups (trying to watch my caffeine intake) and felt alive.

The next time I made it I used the same amount of coffee and same amount of water, but brewed it on the "rich" setting of my brewer. This is a slower drip, which provides a slightly stronger brew. It definitely did that. I actually thought it too strong, so I will revert to making it "classic" strength going forward.

I havent tried it as a cold brew yet. Usually I use crappy coffee (anything I tried that I didnt love) as the cold brew process can take bitter coffee and make it smooth. This is already perfection for me, so I'll like it keep it for hot brewing methods.

The beans are dark, but not black and not too oily. They have a sheen. I think my assessment that this is a dark leaning medium seems accurate. Anyway, I am impressed. Glad to have 2 full pounds of coffee that I LIKe A LOT! Good for two years.

* In my overcaffienated state, I remembered an episode of 3s Comapny where Jack thought that the ceramic he broke was a pricy relic from.. Wan Tai (the tag was torn in half). So forever now I read Taiwan as Wan Tai. RIP John Ritter.

title: I need more tahini in my life. So delicious
text:
Delicious tahini- tastes the same as other organic tahini I have in my cupboard. I hadn't had any in awhile, and I forgot how good it is right off the spoon. I need more of this in my life!

I have the exact same jar as shown in their product pictures. The only ingredient is just organic ground toasted sesame seeds. The consistency is liquid, making it pourable. I have had consistencies that lean more thick as well as more liquid, such as with this. It all works for me, but I find the more liquid-like a little easier to work with as I tend to use it when I make dressings, hummus, baba ganouj, and in some baked desserts and breads. The liquid is easier for me to incorporate. I always stir the jar before use, but I have yet to find it separating out. It is currently winter with cool indoor temps.

title: must have spice for everything. Good packaging, great smell and flavor
text:
We go through so much fresh crushed black pepper that I am constantly refilling the pepper grinder. I always buy a large amount to get me though a few months. 16 ounces usually holds us for 3-4 months (varies). This 16 ounce pressure zip bag of peppercorns look and taste fresh. Love the aroma of black peppercorns, and the taste is a must have for nearly every dish. I grew up on fine ground pepper and pretty much never used it. Then about 10 years ago my husband introduced me to the wonder of freshly crushed black pepper. Sounds funny as it is such a basic spice, but there is a massive difference in taste between the two. So it is all crushed/course ground pepper all the time now. All. the. time. MMMmMMmMmmm

I'll likely buy this again. No complaints.

title: Full ingredient list and nutrition info provided below; sweet, fair electrolyte balance, easy mix
text:
With so many electrolyte drinks on the market, it comes down to selecting which one contains the ingredients that you need to feel best. They aren't all the same. The packets are great for on the go convenience, and they are a must have in a hot weather self care kit. I always keep a few packets on me when I am hiking or just on my person for emergency. Dehydration will run you down quickly, so being prepared with a simple powder and a bottle of water can make a huge difference. Definitely works better than water alone. That being said, I dont use these often. But I always have them on hand.

This formula contains an assortment of B vitamins. I have never tried one with synthetic B vitamins added to it. If you are sensitive to B vitamins (nausea) then keep that in mind when choosing this. I consumed this with food and didn't feel bad, but that may not be the case when out in a sweaty hike. I wont be tucking this away in my emergency kit as no one needs to be vomiting when they are already dehydrated. Casual daily use? sure.

Taste wise, I think it is ok. Sweet with a little citrus flavor. I tend to use more water than needed so it results in a hint of taste (I dont drink it as a "beverage" to enjoy), but for testing & review I tried it in the suggested 16 ounces of water. Btw, there is no mention of this on the package, I am going based on what is in product description. "can be diluted into 16 ounces of water'. It's.. ok. It is palatable. It is a bit on the sweet side as they added stevia on top of the cane sugar. I dont know why they put the term "keto" in the product description (it isn't mentioned on the product), but with 6 grams of sugar per packet (in an 8 g packet), be ware. Personally the actual real sugar used in the product is fine for me in an electrolyte drink as the primary components should be a balance in glucose, sodium, and potassium, which this has. But dont market it as keto so people searching for keto products see this. Grr.

Overall: 3.5 stars. But I'll rate it 4 as it does at have a fair balance of the primary electrolytes to be effective.

Unless I missed it, I do not know why there is no information on the ingredients. I typed out what I see on the bag:

title: lightly crunchy, lightly sweet. Great with coffee or tea
text:
I'm not keto but I am am *trying* to reduce my sugar intake. I can only do this if I have a tasty alternative. I have had the sweetwell meringues, which were surprisingly really good, so I figured I would start with their cookies in my exploration to find some sweet snacking options.

These hit the spot when I want to nosh. I like the coconut cookies with my black coffee. They have an initial salty taste to them, then it mellows out and I no longer notice it. Then it is just a light crunch (not hard on teeth), sweet, and coconut. I would consider these again, or maybe I will try another flavor variety. 3 pack, and I can't eat the whole bag at once, so thats good

Has fiber- chicory root- which can create some gas if you eat a lot in short time.

title: Chinese health food sensation? I'm game! First like a gem, then like a gummy bear post soaking
text:
Such a pretty food. The dried, hard gem looking peach resin nuggets are attractive to look at. The are not edible directly from bag. First they must be soaked. The soaking process can take a few hours to overnight. Just use room temp water, and the peach gems will soften, and greatly absorb the water. You will find soft, gummy bear like globs in place of the hard peach jewels. Might need to pick out some debris. BTW, if you want to move things along quicker, use warm water or look into stewing the gems, and then you should have softened pieces inside and hours time.

There are lots of recipes if you are feeling adventurous, or they can be consumed plain or mixed in with something simple like yogurt or oatmeal. They don't impart much taste, but they are an interesting food and medicinal item that is worth checking out. A small bag makes plenty! There is more than enough to try out several recipes.

title: excellent high quality bottle of black cumin seed, intense flavor but worth it for health benefits
text:
The most vile thing I have ever tasted. Perfect. lol. If you have ever had Black Seed Oil, then you know what to expect. If you haven't had it before and are considering it for all the health benefits- I say go for it, and brace yourself. It is wicked. It is even more intense than other brands I have tried, and I find this to be a good thing. It has a very fresh, concentrated taste. The taste is like raw thyme but with an extra bright punch of volatile intensity. So *maybe* it can be used in some foods, but really I just take it straight up. It is odd, and there is no masking it, so dont even bother. Just slug some off a spoon and chug some water or add it to some water and chug it all down quickly, then maybe have another sip of something. Welcome to the club.

But you know what? it is of excellent quality--best Ive had to date, and it works. I have relied on this for various things, and have always been impressed. It is one of the few things I make a point to keep around, and one of the few things that isn't directly medicine that I am willing to take. "black cumin seed oil.. the cure for all diseases except for death".

Now I'm off to take my daily dose *blegh*.

title: perfectly intense and fresh tasting cumin. After this there is nothing else
text:
MmMmmm intense cumin flavor. Not what I was expecting! I love this oil, and now I want to try other varieties. What a great way to get pure flavor of the spice I'm going for. Dry spices can be bland, and this takes it way up in flavor. Nothing but cumin extractives, sunflower oil, and datem (to prevent separation).

I love the savory, deep taste of cumin. I find it is an often overlooked spice. I am not vegan or vegetarian, but when I dabble in making those dishes I find the use of cumin brings forth a slightly meaty nuance. It is definitely my go-to spice for all things Mexican, and I am now using it forever more in homemade hummus.

Well packaged in shrink wrap- ensuring no in transit spillage, or tampering; as well as confidence in freshness and The bottle and sprayer are perfectly sized- not too big, and the sprayer has a good pull. Has not clogged up (that was a concern). ALL GOOD!

"Spray Gourmet is distinguished by a unique process of extracting resins and botanicals (that's the tasty part of the spice). We bottle these resins and botanicals in a suspension that's great for high-action cooking processes like grilling, tossing salads, cocktail-mixing, and more!.....Spray Gourmet has created a way to bring extracted spices in their purest and rawest form to your kitchen. That means you don’t need a lot of spice to get a lot of flavor. Each spray is equivalent to ¼ tsp or a pinch of spice"

title: go to peanut butter for on the go and for emergency preps/car kit
text: Super convenient peanut butter packs that last forever it seems in terms of freshness. I keep these on hand for convenience during my busy work day, for packing in hiking bag, and also for preps--especially in my car/truck kit. Sure we have loads of jars of peanut butter, but having a simple packet ready to go is great. I dont go through a lot of packets, so I am glad that these stay super fresh for a very very very long time. Just tear into the packet to get into it. Yum!

title: giant serving can be easily halved, best prepared like a milkshake, super sweet
text:
It is wickedly sweet when just mixed with water or non dairy milk using a shaker cup. So sweet it lingers for awhile after consuming. I do find that it is awesome when mixed with ice, a creamy oat milk, and ran through the blender. Then it tastes like a milkshake. Mm!

I like their fun addition of stuff. This has actual sprinkles that for the most part end up at bottom of cup. That's cool.

Birthday cake flavor is definitely reminiscent of a white vanilla cake with sweet icing. It is better tasting to me than some "birthday cake" flavoring. Usually I stay away from that as it is a "milk" flavor. Ever have milk cookies? It's an odd flavoring. Companies use it in ice cream and other confections they want to to call "birthday cake". This is first that made me think more of a liquified birthday cake. Not bad.

So if you like super sweet, then this is for you. I prefer it made into a milkshake. I have their Cookies N' Cream which I like a whole lot better if only because I can drink it shaken with milk or as a milkshake style.

The serving is huge (two giant scoops), and easily can be halved if you dont need/want that much.

title: huge serving size, customizable, good cookies n' cream taste
text:
This Cookies n Cream meal replacement shake is pretty good. It is sweet, so that may be good or bad depending on what you are looking for. I use water or non dairy milk with HALF the serving, and it turns out quite creamy. I go with half because overall I dont really need that much protein in one sitting (sometimes protein drinks hurt my stomach). So I use this as an in between meal (to stave off hungries), or as a sweet treat-- hits the spot as a milkshake.

I like the addition of cookie crumbs. It isnt strong, but it is just enough to make me feel like I had a little oreo style cookie. If you really want to boost the creamy factor to near level of a milk shake, then by all means use some ice or maybe some frozen milk or Greek yogurt. Use the full serving (two huge scoops) with less liquid. Mmmm

If just adding liquid, be sure to use a shaker cup. Stirring isnt enough

Unlike some other protein powders and meal replacement powders, the sodium level in one serving is pretty good. Not too crazy high.

Could be a little less sweet tasting. However this is much less sweet compared to their Birthday Cake option

title: deliciously sweet, like a light brown sugar
text: I love coconut sugar. It makes for a fantastic sugar alternative. It doesnt spike blood sugar levels like some other sugars and sugar free sweeteners can. It reminds me most of a light brown sugar-- sweet and dense. Not coconut flavored. Just a lovely rich taste. Excellent in baking and in coffee. Fresh tasting, fresh smelling. I would buy this brand of sugar again.

title: tasty- adds great umami to many recipes
text: Mmm I love dulse flakes. Adds a nice salty kick to eggs, potatoes, soups. I have to be mindful of how much I use as the naturally occurring iodine can be easily over consumed. A little goes a long way in flavor. Keep in fridge for sustained freshness.

title: Dark Roast Half Caff: robust, strong, delicious. K-cups brew fine, no issues whatsoever

title: chewy with a slight crispy crunch, excellent direct from bag
text:
With the mixed reviews, I was curious what I would get. My bag is not going to last long because I keep grabbing handfuls. Mine are a perfect texture of having a slight crispy crunch but with plenty of chew. Deliciously sweet. Hard to stop eating.

However, the crunch aspect really shouldn't be there. I think this is indicative of an old product or over dried product. Oddly, it makes me like them much more than my usual bag of extra soft (but tough) and chewy goji berries. They dont taste off. They actually are great tasting. I am a regular consumer of goji berries, and these have the typical sweet with slight tart undertone taste. The fact that these have a slight crunch makes them especially wonderful as a straight from the bag snack. I am reviewing this in Jan 2021, and it has an expiry date of 10/2021. SO I am not sure what the issue is. Or if it is even an issue? Wish I had better info for you. On my end, they are still totally edible. I've had other XLSeafood items, and have been impressed. I would buy these again.

title: Tastes like chewy ripe muskmelon, with hint of smoke. Perfectly chewy. Great quality YUM
text:
I would/will buy this again. It is just raw longan fruit sundried and lightly smoked. Non-GMO, no pesticides used, unsulphered. The overall quality is fantastic. Eat it directly out of bag, or use it in savory recipes, teas, desserts. I chomp on it from the bag, or have added it to granola or trail mix. Tastes like overripe honeydew or cantelope melon with a wee hint of smoke. So imagine chewy melon. Slightly naturally musky. Dry but chewy like a huge raisin. So good. Mmm.

The origin is China, as it should be since this is where it grows. This dried fruit can be an acquired taste, but this product is as expected. I am impressed with the consistency of texture, flavor, and size. I am very familiar with lychee fruit, and I know Longan fruit is part of the same family and even resemble each other-- but they are not the same. Lychee is a lighter, sweeter, mild taste. Longan has a deeper taste, sweet in an over ripe way. Both very good, just very different. "Fresh" lychee is easy for me to find, as well as canned, and occasionally dried. I have only ever had dried Lognan, have never seen the fresh fruit anywhere.

This XLSeafood dried Longan berries are addicting. Be mindful that they are naturally loaded with sugar and calories. On the plus side, they are also loaded with anti oxidants and other nutrition.

title: dark roast is strongly doused w/ cardamom-- loses coffee flavor
text:
Must love cardamom. I can give it 5 stars for quality, but in the taste category (and overall rating) I am giving it 4 stars. I know this is a preference thing, rather than a quality thing. So if you really like cardamom then go for it. I like cardamom, but this is rather strong. I taste that more than the coffee itself. If I could at least still taste the dark coffee, then I would like this a lot more. If you like strong cardamom then you will be pleased with this. If you want to try this anyway, know that the quality is quite good. I plan to add in some supplemental dark roast without cardamom to see if I can get a more balanced flavor. I never add cream or sugar to my coffee, and I find I need both to mellow out the cardamom.

I love a good cup of Turkish coffee. I have learned to look for dark roast, as many of the offerings available tend to default to a light, very green tasting roast. Anytime I have had it in an restaurant, it has always been dark roast, which is my preference for coffee anyway. The darker the better. Black. No sugar. No cream.

This small bag (in a box) of coffee is powdery as expected. Dark and rich smelling. I have the "with cardamom" option. Like I said.. the flavor is robust. I think I may cut in some fine ground dark coffee, or see if they offer a dark roast without it. I like it enough to finish it, but likely wont buy it again. Yet, I like the quality of the brand enough to want a non cardamom option.

I prepare it as it should. I use an Ibrik over a gas burner. I am not good at making it. My foaming skill is not as good as I want, but the coffee at least tastes pretty good. I love strong, bold flavor of Turkish coffee. I never water it down.

I really like that this company has so many offerings-- dark, medium, light roasts, some with cardamom, some without. I think I will try the French Roast so long as it doesnt have cardamom (or at least less of it). Otherwise will try another brand.

title: easy to drink, cozy afternoon pick me up, well balanced gentle flavors
text:
This is a very easy to consume turmeric milk drink. I have been drinking turmeric based drinks on and off for years. I find the experience delightful as well as healthy. I have made my own from scratch, I have purchased mixes, and this is yet another I can add to my list of mixes I enjoy. I normally dont include chocolate, but this is really well balanced in taste. A hint of spiciness, a hint of sweet. the mild raw taste of turmeric, and a chocolate undertone that when combined with warm milk (dairy or non dairy of choice) is just warming, comforting, and appeals to the senses.

As I drank this, I thought that this would be a good one for people who are new to turmeric drinks or who may not really care for them otherwise. This is just so light and balanced that as I said from the start.. is so easy to drink.

Can add more cocoa if you want to boost the chocolate taste. Can add more turmeric if you want, and so on. I have added collagen powder or protein powder on occasion. The drink is lovely mid-to-late afternoon as a pick me up, and as a cozy means to warm up on a chilly day.

If I dont drink this quickly, I make a point to stir it as I go otherwise some will settle to the bottom. To be fair, even my hot cocoa k cups and other hot cocoa mixes require this.

Ingredients:Cocoa (alkalized), dates, turmeric root, chocolate flavour, coconut, vanilla flavour, sea salt, cinnamon, cardamom, ashwagandha, black pepper.

title: perfect flavor, hard to put down, fresh & yummy. Definitely a repurchase
text: We love the Blue Diamond BOLD flavors varieties. The Wasabi & Soy is our favorite. I actually prefer to buy the package of smaller single serving packs but that hasn't been available lately. I bought these as a part of a snack pack gift for my husband, and they were good and fresh as expected. When the other becomes available we will likely go back to that. The big bag is too easy to keep on munching. SO GOOD.

title: fresh, chewy, sweet Fig Newtons anytime
text:
Love the big box of Fig Newtons. Fresh every time!
I occasionally pick up a single pack when I would be looking for something to nosh on when at a store. They give me that little bit of sweet without feeling like I ate a candy bar. Good mouth feel, rather filling. Hits the spot. But i haven't been going into stores but rarely this year, and I didn't even think to pick up a larger pack until I saw it while looking for other stuff in Prime Pantry. Price looked good, and I figured I would give it a whirl. Glad I did. I like having the individual packs on hand for whenever I want some Fig Newtons. I didn't want the packs where it is loose cookies. I would likely not get to them, or I would eat more than I wanted to use them up. The individual packs (seems to be 2 long cookies which is equivalent of 4 smaller loose cookies) are so much better for me.. can grab them as I want them and I know each package is fresh.

title: not watered down, tastes just like regular Dark Magic
text:
The best Decaff that I have ever had. I only started drinking decaff after my blood pressure started to go up, as well as I have found that I am much more sensitive to caffeine now that I am in my 40s. I usually have one cup of regular coffee, then I will switch to half caff or decaff. The main thing about the decaff coffee is that I usually find them to be watery tasting even if I try to make them strong. I was already a huge fan of Dark Magic, so when I saw that there was a decaff option I decided to try it out. You know what? This is amazing. It tastes just like the regular Dark Magic. So much so that I find myself double checking that I had grabbed the decaff option. It is dark, robust, strong.. has that deep wonderful flavor of a smooth dark roast. So if you like dark coffee and in particular Dark Magic, I highly recommend this. If you are a Dark Magic consumer, then you will be pleasantly floored by how much of a match this is. You too will be double checking to make sure you grabbed a decaff cup :)

I have since purchased larger quantities, but it was good for me to spend a little more but grab a smaller box to see if I like it or not.

I also occasionally like something hot on a winter afternoon, and this allows me to enjoy the ritual of making a cup of coffee without it effecting my sleep. Also nice t add a splash of Irish cream without the caffeine.

Now, if i could just find a half-caff kcup I like.

title: natural hazelnut flavor pairs really well with cream
text:
Good, natural flavored, medium roast hazelnut coffee from Amazon brand Happy Belly. Fairly balanced medium (leans a wee light). While I am not a huge fan of flavored coffee (or anything other than dark roasts), I do keep a couple of varieties on hand for my occasional guests. I kinda hate hazelnut in particular but the one family member we have over (these days, 2020) loves Hazelnut. They like this. They too note that it has a pleasantly light hazelnut flavor. And I can even have some since it is a much more natural hazelnut taste then some I have tried or smelled. I pretty much drink my coffee black, but I do prefer this with cream. Makes for a nice creamy natural tasting hazelnut coffee. Lovely with some cookies or biscotti.

Fresh!

title: stay fresh package, yummy vanilla sandwich cookie great w/ coffee, milk, tea..
text: I pretty much only like the Golden Oreos. Oddly I dont always see them in store or they are overpriced. When I saw them here in the Pantry, I added them right away. I dont have to try to find them in store. I dont eat them regularly, so sometimes I just buy them and tuck them away. I found that these stay fresh for a long time. Sometimes I just want a vanilla sandwich cookie (or 10), and knowing i have these already available to me is great.  Yum yum. Will be buying again.

title: fresh, fully intact, great for cheese & pepperoni snacking
text: These Ritz crackers arrived fully intact and with no broken crackers that I can tell. They taste as fresh as expected. I love keeping Ritz crackers on hand as they are awesome for loading up with cream cheese, hard cheese, peanut butter or whatever. The crackers have a really good taste, are easy to eat, and just come in handy for times I dont want to fix a hot meal. Love me some cheese, pepperoni and cracker meals :)

title: follow directions, cooks well, tastes good
text:
King Arthur is the gold standard for me in baked goods and ingredients. I think it helps that they are extremely helpful and knowledgeable. They can be contacted as needed, and I am always picking out recipes from their website, etc. I am not gluten free, but I am one of the few that have been intentionally buying some gluten free items for nearly 2 decades (because they taste/feel good; no dietary reason). Back then products were in a special section of the store if they even carried anything. I had become familiar with some things because of the rare few people that I knew at the time that had to eliminate gluten- so I ate what they ate. Oddly, I preferred the taste and texture of some stuff, and still do (brownies, breakfast stuff, crusts). Alas, over the years the gluten free revolution took hold and more and more products came out that resembled gluten products. I am only slightly disappointed, haha

Long way of saying that King Arthur does a great job creating gluten free products that have very similar taste and texture of a regular gluten item. If you dont care for the taste, then it likely isnt that it is gluten free. I had made these pancakes without issue (just follow directions!) but thought they tasted.. off. It was then that I realized I had the variety that is Gluten Free WITH Protein. I thought I had just Gluten Free. Now that I understand my taste buds can adjust. A boost of protein always tastes funny to me. You may not notice it at all or care, especially if you are used to it. One thing I can say is that the protein from Pea protein tastes much better than from whey or soy. So I'd say if you are interested in the gluten free WITH protein, then go for it. I was just surprised because I thought I ordered the other.

title: fresh, crisp, salty & light. Yum!
text: Fresh, budget friendly, arrived with box and all crackers intact. Tastes good-- light, crispy, salty-- just as I expect them to be. Great for soup, chili, or anything else. Or by itself.

title: great variety of full sized candy bars, perfect for Reese's fans
text: What a nice combo of treats for a Reese's fan. I bought this as a gift for my husband. I am sure I will find my way into this box too (been tempted every time I looked at them, so I had to wrap them up!). Great variety of full sized candy bars. I assume they are fresh, we'll find out soon enough. I will be back to state otherwise if they aren't.

title: crunchy, sweet snack that kinda reminds me of old boston baked beans candy
text:
Crunchy sweet snack. Chickpea and Jaggery/Gur Chana is a very sweet calorie laden snack, but it has a decent amount of protein and fiber as well as vitamins and minerals. I know that the chickpeas/chana used is a smaller version of the typical chickpea, easily about half the size. They have some crunch, some texture, some give, and have a sweet taste. Bite it in half and you will see a very small roasted "chickpea" coated in jaggery/sugar.

It isn't bad, but it doesn't quite taste like I expect. It actually reminds me more of a candy (like the old boston baked beans candy?). It is good, and I could nosh on a whole container as each container is just 3 ounces. This past week I was on the go a lot, and I had tossed it in my bag as a snack option. Really dont need much to take the edge off. But could easily eat the whole container if I were snacking on the couch or at my computer. No mess, no fuss, just you.

When it comes down to it, I rather like it and would consider it again.

title: good balance of sodium, potassium, & carbs; good flavor
text:
Need hydration? The Cure Hydration Mix is a very convenient to use packet of electrolytes that you just add to your water. I really like the Grapefuit flavor option, not that I need stuff like this to taste good. I dont use products like this that often, but it can sure make a world of a difference when working outside in hot weather or any other activity that depletes electrolytes. It is crazy how run down and off feeling one can experience, then drink some electrolytes and it is like the world is brighter and everything feels good again. That is when I know for sure i am dehydrated. And this is why I keep products like this around (and try to use them BEFORE I need them, but they work quickly even when used when they are needed). I buy tubs when I am using it daily (I do landscaping in summer), but also keep packets on hand for intermittent use, to top off during day, and for use in all my various 1st aid kits.

I always keep a couple of packets in my purse, especially extra in my 1st aid kit. Usually along with a packet of sugar or honey-- just in case. This doesn't contain cane sugar since it is marketed as "paleo friendly", but I am glad to see that it contains the necessary carbs to provide fuel and balance. Great ingredients- for that 5 stars

INGREDIENTS: Organic Coconut Water Powder, Organic Grapefruit Flavor, Orange Juice Powder, Non-GMO Citric Acid, Pink Himalayan Salt, Sodium Citrate, Organic Stevia Extract, Lemon Juice Powder, Beet Root Juice Powder, Monk Fruit Extract

title: Lipton wins out over generics, so tasty, versatile, and flavorful
text:
Very good, very fresh. Will not use generic brands again if I can help it after picking up a box of this onion soup. I added it in with a big pork loin that I threw in the slow cooker. This was the only seasoning I added. I was feeling famished the entire time it was cooking. Made for great au jus.

And of course for all the other reasons to have it on hand to use in a variety of recipes. It just an all around good flavor enhancer. I have used different generics and it had been awhile since I used Lipton. Really did make a difference for me, so this will be my main stay onion soup packet product.

title: chocolatey, creamy, great tweet "pick me up" or warm up, anytime
text:
Yummy hot cocoa. Seems to pack more cocoa in their cups than other name brands. More chocolatey and creamy. Have added them as a subscribe and save now that we have tried them. Yum!

We like Victor Allen products. My husband and I have been drinking more hot chocolate lately, not just because it is cold and dark and hot cocoa just tastes so good when chilled to the bone, but also as a replacement for coffee. I sometimes just want something more than my 1-2 cups of coffee, but dont necessarily want caffeine. I dont necessarily want half caff or caffeine free. Only occasionally am I a tea drinker. So I began havign a cup of hot cocoa in the afternoon, and it gives me that ritual of having something hot and also a sweet treat. My husband says his gut doesn't feel right if he keeps drinking coffee. I mentioned swapping to hot cocoa, and he has. And says it has saved his stomach.

I used to scoff at cocoa k-cups and just make some from a bag, but at some point I was introduced to cocoa k-cups and I find them super convenient and perfectly portioned (though I only use 6 ounces water to maintain chocolatey flavor. My husband uses 10 ounces). They are now a mainstay from fall through later winter. I still make my own hot chocolate, or take a pre mix from a bag.. but the k cups have been a very welcome addition. Yum!

title: fresh, thick, good dense chew- not too cripsy and flakey- just right, for me
text: Yum. I liked them too much. I gobbled them all down while watching tv. Thick enough to have a good mouth feel. Some are too light and crispy. These are just a little more dense. Fresh strawberry taste, sweet but not cloying. I really wish I didn't eat them all at once. lol.  So good though..

title: little sweet, a little tang (acidity), and a mellow finish, light leaning medium
text:
hmm, a medium roast made by blending light roasted beans and dark roasted beans together. That piqued my interest, but i have to say I was concerned that the brightness of light roasts would come through and possibly make for an acidic coffee. I prefer/love deep dark roasts but will drink a balanced or dark leaning medium. Even medium roasts can be too acidic and bitter- so I was definitely taking my chance on this. It's pretty good-- but not a repurchase.

My taste buds pick up a little sweet, a little tang (acidity), and a mellow finish. It leans a little light for what I consider to be a balanced medium profile, but it is still pretty good. Quality is not at all in question. I think it comes down to preference. So I say go for it if it at all sounds good to you.

title: excellent wakame- no issues or concerns. Yum!
text: Love Wakame. Holistic Bin has fresh tasting wakame flakes. You won't go wrong with this brand.  The bag is pressure zipped mylar, and it includes a little spoon.
