I have munched on it by itself, but usually add it to eggs, soups, and vegetables. Adds a lightly fishy salty taste. Go ahead and add it to anything you like. Yum yum!

title: tastes & feels like a puffed out freeze dried strawberry. Perfect texture and natural taste
text:
I am not keto, I am not even on a diet.. but I like to eat whats good and these are delicious. Of course reduced calories and sugar would be good for me to pay attention to. Anyway.. These are THE best meringue bites I have ever had. I didn't even know great meringue bites existed. I sometimes pick up a container as an occasional airy treat, but they aren't ever great. These are somehow way above and beyond all that I have ever had before.

Small, dense, but airy. Manages to have a little more mouth feel than other meringue bites I have had. So I feel like I am eating something. That makes for a better snacking experience. The other aspect that really impresses me is the flavor. I have this in Strawberry, and it tastes like.. well, a strawberry!! It has a very natural flavor. Reminds me of a freeze dried strawberry but puffed out. That is a pretty spot on description. So between the better mouthfeel and the super perfect strawberry taste, oh AND the fact that it isn't loaded with a sticky syrupy sugar flavor.. this is a pure joy to nosh on. Great for when I want to mindlessly pop snacks into my mouth...and I am not taking a huge hit with excess calories or sugar.

YUM.

Totally a repurchase.

title: does not perform as a creamer, clumps, but tastes great.
text:
The taste is very good. Prominent coconut flavor, more so than a liquid coconut milk. SO you must love coconut. It reminds me of when I blend coconut oil or manna into my coffee. So taste wise-- love it.

As a creamer? no. NO. It barely makes a dent in my coffee. Serving size of 1 tsp was a joke in my 10 ounces of dark coffee. It did not even lighten my coffee. I kept adding powder until I saw a change. I must have used 4 TABLESPOONS. Even then it was still dark, and it did not taste creamed up. Well, it tasted that way a little, but it tool A LOT. I am overall ok with that since I don't usually even use creamer. I just go black. But this is marketed as a creamer and it really doesn't do well as a creamer. I had to add A LOT to make it lighten up a little. Again, tasted good at least :)

Lastly, it takes a bit of effort to blend in. It does clump. I stirred in a little at a time, and it did not matter. Still clumpy. I have to smash bits apart with a fork. I would need to run it through a blender to really break it down. That being said, it might be a great addition to a smoothie!

The packaging is ok. Typical pressure zip mylar style bag. I find that these bags dont do well with powders as the powders get caught up in the pressure zip making it useless. So dont plan to use this, or if you do, wrap a rubber band around it or use a chip clip. Another container may be better.

I like that there is no sugar, nothing at all added to sweeten it. Thank you. I also like the quality of the company and the product in general. Just not at all as a creamer in specific.

But as for my coffee.. too much work, doesn't actually cream it. Love the taste through- fresh, natural. YUM!

title: Use this on everything, especially if you like a peppery kick
text: Yum! I have enjoyed all the Republic Craft products I have tried. I love trying different styles of sauces.  Not super thick, but not watery either. I like it as a dip, or as a coating. I haven't used it as a marinade but it could be used as such. I have drizzled it over a steak sandwich with success. It has a good flavor. Little spicy for me at times.. but that varies among taste buds :) I find this one good to keep on hand just because it is truly versatile. I recommend! (also grab a few different varieties as a gift- attractive bottles and great flavors. Be sure to add this one in!)

title: pair these with medjool dates for a quick energy boosting snack
text:
Excellent bag of brazil nuts. Perfect! YUM! I dont often find them in store, so I came here to see what I could find. I am quite pleased with this purchase and will certainly buy again. I love the crisp light crunch of a brazil nut. I have this thing where I take a medjool date, remove the pit, then slide in a brazil nut. Oh my, it is like having a piece of candy. The taste and texture is perfection. It takes care of my sweet tooth and it also gives me a little energy. The nuts come in a pressure zip bag. I keep some of each in air tight containers, and just grab a couple of each for whenever I need it. The rest I store in the fridge.

I buy these medjool dates: www.amazon.com/dp/B08BH6NBN8

title: basic saltine, ok overall, mostly all broken crackers
text:
Nah, they're ok. Taste fresh, has light crisp, salty taste. Side by side with another brand, I am not sure which is which. I'm going to stick to my $1-2 saltine crackers. I like saltines even though I don't eat them often. Usually I go for a more dynamic cracker with substance. But a classic saltine has its place, and I was curious if how these rated in comparison to other saltines.
These are good enough, but I'm not super impressed. They taste fine, so if it sounds good to you then please go for it. I have some disappointment with how 80% of my package is pretty much crumbs. I never have that issue with other saltines. This is one box with two plastic sleeves of saltines in plastic trays. The box wasn't banged up, so not sure why the crackers are all broken. I took pictures, and although many look intact, they really aren't. They fall apart as they get lifted out. Crumbs. At best I can dump them in soup or chili. Forget any other option. Not sure if it was a shipping issue or product issue. Either way, I'm not inclined to take a chance with a repurchase.

3 stars: they are "ok"

title: fresh, natural local bakery taste. Lightly sweet, great balance of lemon & ginger
text:
Fresh, natural taste that reminds me of something I would pick up at a local bakery. I am rather impressed. The lemon and ginger flavors are subtle but noticeable. A punch of tangy lemon with a bite of ginger. Lightly sweet, good crunch. Holds up well in coffee or tea. I am not much of a tea drinker but this flavor is especially awesome dunked in hot tea.

I also love their Cranberry variety. I do not like their almond variety at all (and almond is usually my go-to favorite).

The pieces come loose in a bag, two bags per box. I put my open bag in my own pressure zip baggie.

I recommend this variety of biscotti as well as their cranberry variety.
www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08776MGD3

title: lightly sweet, crunchy but with "give", very natural, artisinal taste
text:
I have tried three flavors of biscotti from Gusta. This Cranberry flavor is great, as well as their Ginger-Lemon. The Almond is terrible (no almond taste, tastes like cheese). The Biscotti with Cranberries is delightful. The two bite size is lightly sweet, has a hard crunch, but the moist cranberries provide a little more "give" than a typical hard biscotti. This variety by Gusta tastes fresh, natural, and not at all commercial. They taste like I picked them up from a local bakery. The bites are loose in a bag. The bag isn't resealable so plan to put them into a pressure zip baggie of your own. I have been enjoying this variety enough to want to repurchase. I do recommend the Cranberry and the Lemon-Ginger.

lemon ginger: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B087773XJ7

title: Almond is terribad- no almond taste; tastes cheesy. Other varieties are GREAT!
text:
I normally LOVE almond biscotti, and I will get to this particular variety momentarily. I enjoy a "breakfast cookie" with my morning coffee. Or occasionally when I drink tea. I have had the pleasure in trying three different varieties by Gusta. I found both the biscotti with cranberries and the lemon ginger to be wonderful. They have a fresh, natural taste that isn't too sweet nor does it taste commercial made. It has an artisanal taste. Tastes like something I could pick up from a local Italian bakery (and I actually think these are better than from my local bakery). The consistency is crunchy but has some give. It is really quite pleasing. The packaging is ok. These are bites (maybe two bites per piece), and they are loose in a bag with two bags in a box. Not resealable. I put mine in a large pressure zip bag. I like them enough to repurchase. They are tasty in a fresh, natural way. THEN came the almond biscotti-- usually my favorite. My GO TO flavor. I thought that if the cranberry and the lemon ginger were amazing, then the traditional almond should be out of this world. Um.. NO.

The almond has ZERO almond flavor. It taste more like cheese. It is very odd. I tried it over a few days thinking my taste buds were broken, but nothing has changed. These are awful. The kinda neat thing? they are individually wrapped. However, I think that lends to a lot of excess packaging for a small piece (again, 2 bites max). The flavor is indeed out of this world in that it is no where close in the flavor I was expecting. If it weren't for trying the other two flavors first, I would have never bothered with another Gusta product again. So, I am not sure what is up with the Almond biscotti. I definitely wont buy those again, and I am pretty sure I will not be consuming the remainder of the box. But I wanted to mention the other two varieties as they are quite delightful. I mean, I am impressed. I love the cranberry flavor for my coffee, and the ginger-lemon is fine for coffee but it really stands out with tea (I'm not a big tea drinker but come cold weather I enjoy it more). Chewy cranberries with the crunch of cookie. The lemon ginger is delicate and well balanced. I can taste the tang of lemon as well as the deep bite of ginger. Lovely! But the almond.. truly yuck. I do not recommend the almond. Go for the others.

Lemon Ginger: www.amazon.com/gp/product/B087773XJ7

Cranberries: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08776MGD3

title: easy to drink balanced medium, non acidic. Strong and mellow
text:
Caffe' Gusto Intenso Capsules medium roast with Intensity level of 9. It is produced a well balanced dark leaning medium flavor. I tend to drink my coffee black, unless the roast has acidity, then I need to tone that brightness down with some cream. This is a good one to drink black, yet it holds up to cream if so desired. Coffee is subjective, so all I can say is that I like it enough; no issues, concerns. Intensity level seems on par with other similarly designated levels. As one with a preference with super dark, bold, strong coffee, none of these are dark enough for me. But as an easy to drink medium? yes. Good stuff.

Btw, the coffee works well as a pour over. I always have kcups/capsules on me for coffee on the go. I do labor work, and I sometimes want a cup of coffee mid day. I usually have access to hot water but not always a specific brewer. Pour over is especially great with the LaVazza capsules because they are much wider & not as densly packed like a nespresso style capsule-- just easier to get the coffee out. These capsules are nearly just like a kcup, just much shorter--you'd have to stab a hole in bottom for it to work in keurig as the puncture pin wont reach it; otherwise will fit. I mention all this because sometimes we just need options. As a person on the go, I like to know what my opportunities and limitations are. Ignore all this if you happen to only have a Lavazzo machine and only every make coffee in it with these capsules. :)

title: Tasty, stay fresh packs of seasoning 18 boxes w/ 16 packets each. Salty/MSG
text:
Great prep item for apocalypse. Use it to spice all your dried grains, or as barter. Kidding.. kinda lol hey, 2020 isn't over yet. :P

I say this because each container has 16 packets. This order is for a box of 18. So 18 containers of 16 packets each. This will last awhile :) What I like it that the seasons will stay FRESH because of the packaging/packets.

Flavor is delicious, even though not as dynamic as I hoped for. I dont want to say it is bland.. just more single dimensional? My tastebuds pick up on salty, and some non-heat spice. It is really good though. Use it on anything. Know that it will give food a red/orange color. I love it sprinkled on potatoes (made in any fashion), over roasted vegetables (massage them in oil, grind some pepper over them, sprinkle on this seasoning.. mm), over chicken thighs.. etc. One of the things I did with it is to add half a packet to a big glop of mayo. It makes an awesome dip for french fries. YUM.

The flavoring is deep like cumin with a punch of salty taste. Coriander is made from seeds of cilantro plant, and does not at all taste like cilantro. Cilantro is the leaves. My husband hates cilantro and was concerned when he saw the term "culantro". I had to explain that it is coriander that is contained in this. Then he tried it directly from packet and concurred that there is no cilantro taste (*sigh*).

Just know that it is super salty tasting, has MSG, and contains food coloring.

I think it is a great staple, and I love the packets. It isn't a spice I use daily, nor would I use much at once, so knowing these will stay fresh for a very long time is great. Perfect portions. I love that something like this is available.

I would consider this again, and I would consider other offerings. Could make for a neat food themed gift.

title: fresh, bright, flavorful. Smells good, works well in variety of dishes.
text:
Since this is sun dried, I think it technically makes it Hungarian (aka American), while the more flavorful Spanish is slow toasted/roasted over a fire. But the labels often get mixed up. Basically, sun dried is considered less flavorful, much more mild, than others. However, it doesn't mean it lacks flavor. I find this to be lovely, fresh, mild, robust, lightly sweet paprika. Smells good, looks good, tastes great. My taste buds can pick up on paprika. I definitely find it more flavorful than the basic paprika I sometimes pick up. "Because our paprika is pure, you will feel the difference with a stronger more potent flavor". I do, I really do.

I keep a few different types of paprika in my large seasoning drawer. This is the type of paprika (basic, all purpose) I go through the most, where I tend to add it into everything I make, or as part of making my own seasoning blend. This company does offer a smoked paprika if that is more your style (which I need to buy!).

The seasoning comes in a mylar pressure zip bag. I will likely be transferring it to another container as I use it often enough to not want to bother with a bag. But if it just an occasional spice for you, then keeping it the bag is fine too. Should keep fresh for some time.

There was a time when I only thought paprika was a colorful addition to deviled eggs. Now I use it copiously in a variety of dishes. I especially love to use when making Hungarian goulash (i have a few different styles, and always use a lot of paprika YUM!).

title: Excellent as a breakfast cookie, pairs w/ coffee or tea, natural flavor, great crisp texture YUM!
text:
Breakfast cookies! I wouldn't have a hankering for one of these as a dessert, but it is my go-to snack when I am having a cup of coffee. They pair perfectly with coffee or tea, for me. They aren't too sweet, they are definitely hard and crunchy- reminds me of a biscotti, and the flavors are quite nice. Subtle, gentle, real flavors. I like them all.

I am usually not a fan of chocolate flavored stuff and even that one tastes really good to me- natural cocoa flavor. The "passion fruit and chia" is spot on to me. I did not expect those flavors to come through. I can even detect the texture that chia provides. I love love love the Orange variety as well as the Apple & Cinnamon- the last two remind me of a thick belvita. The lemon lime is impressive. I did not expect that to taste good. The lemon & lime are perfect tasting.

I think that is what stands out to me, the flavors are just so natural tasting. Nuanced, pleasant. The sweetness is just right- not cloying, but not bland. The crunch and crisp is fresh. While I aim to keep these as my coffee cookie, I could see grabbing one for on the go or just when I need to nosh a little. They aren't going to weigh me down or make me want to eat the whole box, nor will I get the sugar crash. They are dense, sizable cookies at just 100 calories per cookie (passion fruit & chia is 95 calories). Has a wee bit of protein and fiber, too.

I wonder if they make a ginger snap? That is what these remind me of in terms of overall texture/crunch.

24 count box, 5 flavors:
-4 orange
-5 passion fruit & chia
-5 chocolate
-5 lemon lime
-5 apple & cinnamon

I will get these again. I would prefer these over the biscotti I buy for my coffee/tea. If they made a gingersnap or almond, I will be extra in love. So yeh, I know we all have different taste preferences, and I try to describe as much as I can to give you an idea of what the experience will be like. I think you will like them if you like biscotti or other coffee cookies, or breakfast cookies. This is definitely a repurchase for me.

I've since purchased 3 more boxes.

title: loose, whole pieces, yummy alone, add in to other foods, or ground into a "breading"/coating
text:
I'm not keto, nor even low carb, but I appreciate foods that aren't full of junk. I'll save my added sugar for desserts. Don't need it in granola (not that that stops me, lol). This is a loose granola (no nuggets). has a cereal vibe to it. Maybe toss on top of yogurt. Or oatmeal, if you are not strictly keto. Works on salads too. Add it to healthy muffins, pancakes, cookies, etc. Run it through a food processor for use as a coating on chicken or vegetables.

Lightly sweet- has that cooling feel that erythritol gives food. Faint natural strawberry flavor from strawberries. There are a lot of nuts (big, full pieces), and other goodies. Here are the ingredients: Coconut Chips, Pecans, Almonds, Pumpkin Seeds, Sunflower Seeds, Unrefined Coconut Oil, Erythritol, Chicory Root Fiber, Coconut Milk, Strawberries, Cinnamon, French Sea Salt, Monk Fruit Extract

title: more nutty than vanilla tasting (to me )
text:
I'm not a fan of this flavoring. It made my coffee taste weird. A little more nutty than vanilla. I can't figure out if I used too much or too little. It could just be the Splenda. Oddly, I think it tastes better added to some real cream. I know that practically defeats the purpose, but when I do use cream, I tend to use a lot. I can use less by more or less mixing this in. For me, not terrible but not great. It wont be a repurchase for me. But you may like it!

I think it has some worthwhile benefit though:
-single portion
-doesn't need refrigeration
-nice option for guests
-might work out well in other beverages or foods
-definitely sweet
-lower calorie than other creamers
-cheap enough to give it a try. Tastebuds vary, so this is a matter of preference.

title: very natural tasting, minimally sweet, nice texture, and good overall taste
text:
Oddly good, and surprisingly natural tasting. It tastes better a few bites in, I think because my brain is looking for artificial flavor and either super salty or super sweet. This has none of that going on. It is balanced and rather delightful. Obviously we all have different preferences, so this may or may not be for you. All I can say is that these have the texture and light crunch of "cheese puffs" but have a natural peanut butter flavor with a hint of cocoa. Emphasis in on the peanut butter flavor. Not at all artificial tasting. Minimally sweet. Not addicting (as in, want to eat every bag in box), yet pleasant enough to enjoy the whole pouch. Good, generous serving size for adults or kiddos. Might intrigue your doggos too. Really great for on the go. A little fiber, a little fat, a little protein? Not a lot of calories or sodium? yes, please!

I didn't know what to expect, then I began to expect it to not be good.. then they came and I hoped for the best. I am really tickled that I find myself liking these Puffworks Dark Chocolate Organic Peanut Butter Puffs a lot.

title: minty fresh
text:
It's.. gum! Lots of white tablets in foil pop out sleeved packets.

Six total packs of peppermint (packaged in a set of 3, so there are 2 packages)
Six total packs of spearmint (packaged in a set of 3, so there are 2 packages)

Both are minty fresh. I prefer the peppermint, and my husband likes both.

I usually chew two pieces at a time, and it stays minty for quite awhile, I don't care to chew gum for long but some gum wears out before I do. This had plenty of time left on it.

title: keeps me full and steady, mild flavors, easy to make
text:
I have tried both Superfood Instant Oatmeal options. This has the addition of whey protein. I like them all equally- varieties and flavors. They all have a relatively mild flavor that could actually be stronger. However, I usually add in some other foods, so it blends together fine. Hint of sweet.

I have a big appetite, so as with the other I tend to make two packets (140 cals per packet) plus some cut up fruit, maybe additional nuts or seeds. If I go for one packet, then I am still adding fruit but also a side of something (English muffin with peanut butter, usually). No different than the typical instant (but not so awesomely healthy) flavored oatmeal packets.

Love the combo of ingredients. I like both flavors, though the apple one is rather faint in flavor. The maple has a little more flavor- still light though. My main draw is all the other ingredients, such as seeds, quinoa flakes, puffed amaranth. The addition of whey protein doesn't taste any different to me. Sometimes I can really taste whey protein in stuff and this one isn't noticeable to me. Maybe my tastebuds are broken?

What I really love is that both options seem to really stave off hunger and keeps me steady feeling. I don't always eat healthy (or I eat healthy part of day then lose it come dinner), so making a point to start my day off right and not feeling ravenous a few hours later is awesome. I like the overall taste, mouth feel, and ultimately how I feel. Good stuff. I am used to adding collagen powder to my oatmeal or coffee, so I would likely just buy their regular Superfood Oatmeal and continue to use my powder which of course has protein. I don't need to double up.
www.amazon.com/dp/B08FCXF3RJ

Just know that you will need scissors to get into these little plastic packets.

title: perfect light crunch, easy on teeth, great flavors, awesome as a stand alone snack
text:
Nana Joes granola is really good! Great noshing food. I find myself standing in the kitchen with a handful of granola whenever I am feeling snacky or peckish. Haven't tried it any other way as this is the way I like it. But maybe someday soon I will try it with yogurt, ice cream, or milk. Hmm, maybe as added texture in oatmeal. Maybe once I pick out all the larger clusters (it is natural for there to be various sized pieces) for my straight from bag snacking needs I will try it with other foods.

What I really like is that the granola isn't super hard. It more of a light, gentle crunch. Easy on the teeth. The addition of almond butter gives it a moist vibe despite being dry. Very interesting. The flavors are great too. ALL of them. It is lightly sweet and the flavors all come through. I follow no diet, have no restrictions, and dont even necessarily eat healthy, but I do like when healthy and yummy really come together. I can't decide which is my favorite, so I am glad this is a variety pack.

I'm already considering another purchase. Maybe even as a gift pack for someone for upcoming holiday.

title: thin but dense, very mild flavor, easy on teeth, holds up well to dips, pairing w/cheese
text:
I have a box of these Mary's Gone Crackers in the flavor, Chipotle. The flavor is very mild, and easy to work with. If you are hoping for a more pronounced flavor, these won't provide it. But they do have a nice, gentle flavor. There aren't many in a bag yet I can't eat many at once (despite having a huge appetite)--they are rather filling. The crackers are thin but dense. I can eat them plain or pair them with a soft cheese or hummus. They stand up well to dips. They have a snap, but are easy on the teeth. Can mash into the tops of teeth, so plan to pick some cracker out. They remind me of a thicker wheat thins (but ya know, gluten free). Pretty good overall.

My order was for a pack of six, and I received one box. Hopefully your order will be filled correctly. Better value with the multi pack.

title: lard for easy, consistent pie crusts; fat for other baking/cooking/frying needs
text:
Use this for baking, and really anything that can use some fat. This is lard with hydrogenated lard (don't be alarmed, fully hydrogenated products are fine, it when something says "partially hydrogenated" that you want to stay away from as it great increases artificial trans fat. Naturally occurring is ok too).

It is easy to work with. I like the flavor so much better than vegetable shortening. Veg shortening tends to taste waxy and plain to me. While this doesn't impart a strong flavor, there is a pleasant mouth feel that it provides that vegetable shortening just can't for me. It is even easier than using butter when it comes to crust making. Seems to take some guessing (and hoping haha) out of the mix. Less concern with temperature. I don't make enough crusts to have it down pat, so this gives me an edge. More consistency. Makes me want to make more pie crusts. I like the container. When I have purchased lard before , it has been in the sticks or blocks. I find this easier to work with and much easier to store. Just a preference for me.

I really like the South Chicago Packing products. Good quality products, Small company, Made in USA. I will more than likely purchase again. I know I have with their beef tallow products (which I just happen to use more of).

I use their "All Bake" beef tallow for other baking, cooking, frying needs.
https://www.amazon.com/South-Chicago-Packing-Shortening-Specialty/dp/B08GY5VFLX

and their Waygu beef tallow too (funny, I just realized that this is from same company--been buying it w/o realizing this)
www.amazon.com/South-Chicago-Packing-Paleo-friendly-Keto-friendly/dp/B0881XTCR3

Rating is 5 stars for quality of product.

Gift worthy too

title: high smoke point, great mouth feel, excellent for cast iron cooking & maintenance
text:
There isn't a real noticeable taste (good thing), it is more of a mouth feel thing. This doesn't feel waxy- it actually adds a decadent mouth feel. My primary use for this is in stove top cooking. I have this tub nearby at the ready for use in frying and other low or high stove top cooking needs. I have a gas stove and use cast iron pans, so fat is life. Nice for seasoning pans too. HIGH smoke point. Butter has much lower smoke point. So different fats/oils for different needs.

I much prefer this over vegetable shortening. I usually use butter when I bake as the waxy taste of vegetable shortening comes through. Butter also lends a depth of flavor. I CAN tell the difference. Beautiful looking cookies ruined by vegetable shortening. For shame. So, it was only recently that I have tried beef tallow in my baking. I still prefer butter for cookies (and most baking- butter is actually a cheap option per ounce, but takes up room in fridge, and not always a flavor I want in stove top cooking/frying), but beef tallow works wondrously in brownies, cakes, breads, and anywhere some fat in needed. Plays well with other spices. Shelf stable. Perfect texture direct from can.

The ingredients are Beef Tallow, HYDROGENATED beef tallow, soybean oil, little bit of BHT & citric acid to improve stability.
Don't freak out over the use of the term "hydrogenated"- that means that the fat is fully saturated. It is no cause for alarm/concern. It is when a product uses "partially hydrogenated" fats/oils that is disrupts the order of things and creates artificial trans fatty acids which we don't want a lot of. Small naturally occurring amounts (this has 1 gram per serving) is normal and ok. For those that are hep on vegetable shortening, even the cheapest kind usually doesn't have partially hydrogenated oils these days. So that's a good thing all around. But if you prefer tallow, this is a nice MADE IN USA from smaller company option.

Price wise? my last tub of beef tallow- for same size- was $5 more. So for tallow, it is competitively priced. Don't compare it to vegetable shortening. It's a whole different animal (haha!!). Really though.. everyone has their own budget

If you are into making pie crusts, they have a tallow & lard combo.
www.amazon.com/South-Chicago-Packing-Shortening-Specialty/dp/B08GYB84P1

Rating based on quality and over performance: 5 stars.

title: medium strength/intensity, medium, balanced flavor, mild acidity
text:
Edit/update: So, somehow I still had some of these capsules tucked away forgotten about. Came across them a full two years later and I was pleasantly surprised how fresh and robust they still tasted. I also want to add that they have a lot more flavor than some brands I have been using lately. I already had this at 5 stars, and so it remains. But I add glitter and exclamation marks as it was good then, and good now.
------------------------
This Solimo Espresso capsules for Nespresso Original Line makers makes a medium brew with a hint of acidity. It is mild. It is palatable to me, however I prefer a much darker, much stronger roast. Take note of the product picture where the strength/intensity is indicated at about the mid way point and is described as "mellow & balanced; full-bodied". I DID see that before I ordered and I was curious as to how much it lined up. I figure if I didn't like it, I could pass it off onto my husband who prefers medium roasts. So I hand it to Solimo for providing a super accurate description (despite my secretly hoping for a super dark, bold, chewy roast).

Size wise, it is within typical range of capsules I have purchased. The contents is the same: 1 full TBS. If you harvest this coffee for use in your Keurig (sometimes it just needs to be done, lol) then 1 capsule emptied into a reusable k-cup will comfortably brew a 6 ounce cup. Use 2 for 8, 10 ounces. (This would be typical amount for a regular brewer too-- 2 tbs per 8-10 ounces of water).

The foil on top is a tad softer, looser than I am used to. It was easy for me to poke into in order to take a closer look at the coffee and to measure the contents. I could tell from aroma that it was going to have a more medium roast flavor. Didn't effect brewing.

As with any coffee, it comes down to preference. Hence why there will always be such a range in review ratings. I appreciate the clear description, the coffee seems to be exactly as described, and while I normally don't RATE based on pricing, I am greatly appreciative of a much more budget friendly option- most are at least double, sometimes triple, or even quadruple this price. Clearly, go with what you like. Coffee, no matter the price is still an inexpensive life pleasure. At least with this option, it can be tried without having invested a lot.

Solid, basic coffee

title: impressive quality, awesomely sweet molasses taste. I'm impressed
text:
SO good. I am glad I had the opportunity to try this as I would never have otherwise done so. I ignored the "for Relieving Menstrual Period Pain" because although female, I never experience this. But further research into the use of something like this makes it interesting to me. I kept looking at the product and thought, "it's just brown sugar-- I'll try it". I have it in "natural flavor" option.

It is wonderful. It is small, dense squares of firm, moist dark brown sugar. It smells and tastes lightly of dark sweet molasses. The kind that has a deep, dark, nearly caramel flavor. It is quite good-- right up my ally in terms of taste and sweetness. You may think otherwise and may want to add it to something. I can eat it as it and really enjoy it.

I can bite into the cube, and it stays formed. The warmth of my lips lightly melts the top, but it stays solid. It definitely takes care of a sweet tooth. I can take a little nibble, or slowly consume the whole small square.

As firm and dense as it is, it melts down in a cup of coffee. It is delightful. I use blackstrap molasses in my coffee on occasion and this product reminds me of a solid version of the kind that I use.

I can attest that the product smells, and tastes of quality. The packaging is great- mylar lined pressure zip paper container.

I am impressed. Surprisingly impressed. Yay! 5 stars

title: a little bland, herby/savory flat undertone, nice noodles, 1200 mg sodium
text:
Not a full miss, but not a hit. I like the convenient, easy to make cup of slim egg noodles. While it is kind of herby and savory, the overall taste is slightly bland with hint of ashtray. Oddly, I thought it was ok enough as I can easily doctor it up with additional spices or other food additions (cheese crackers, yum!). When I tasted it I was initially impressed that it didn't taste salty, but when I looked at the label the amount in this cup is 1200 mg!!!!!!!!!!!!!! More than the cheapo "cup o'noodles"--and at least that tastes salty. Though, less than some cans of soup. I am surprised and disappointed because I expected this to be a little healthier all around. Really hoped for lower sodium. I love stock, and getting in all the collagen I can.

On the plus side: It is nice that is has a little fiber (2 grams), lots of protein (20 grams), low cholesterol (45mg), low sat fat (1 g), low calories (260), and no added sugar. So why so much salt? Again, it isn't like it tastes salty.

I don't often comment on price, but For $5.00 per cup, this needs to be better. I can otherwise take some cheapo cupO'noodles and stir in some collagen powder, and manage to take in less salt.

I like it enough to finish off my pack. I would consider it again if it reduced the salt, and maybe added in some additional flavor- it is really kind of flat and a little odd. Like the generous dousing of parsley as it adds some color. Otherwise, noodles are great, overall amount is good, and I feel ok eating it.

title: sparkling, lightly sweet, easy to drink Kombucha
text:
Very easy to drink Kombucha. Perfect 8.5 ounce size. Refreshing, light taste, lots of fizz. Delicious!

I like Kombucha, have been drinking it on and off for nearly 20 years. Let me tell you, the early stuff was rough. It was rare to find- definitely not mainstream. Some were so bad (like chunky vinegar) that I was turned off from it for many years. Then everyone seemed to love Kombucha and it gained popularity and seemed to be available everywhere. So a few years back I randomly bought a bottle at a local grocer (used to be specialty shops only), and I was amazed at how much better they tasted. Some brands are better than others, some are still a little too vinegary for me. But when I find one I like, I make a note of it. I REALLY LIKE this flavor and brand.

It is light, fizzy, and just the right amount. I love fizzy drinks, and this is so good. I really enjoy sparkling water, and this is like that in a good way. That it happens to be Kombucha is a huge bonus. Very smooth. Lightly sweet. Nice easy natural tasting flavoring. Light and refreshing. I love that it does not have to stored in the fridge. I keep some in the box and a few in the fridge. Best cold, but it tastes just fine at cool room temperature .

title: great flavor profile, thin marinade style bbq sauce; sweet/mild tang/mild heat
text:
I love barbeque sauce- all types and styles. I have my preferences, but I do like trying them all. It is just one of those really cool condiments that has such wide range of uses and flavors, that there is something for everyone and can be used with just about anything. Drizzle over meatloaf, chicken, use it as a marinade, as a flavor component in something, etc.. BBQ sauces range from super thin, to super thick, sweet, smokey, hot, tangy, etc...

Now this "Republic Craft Barbecue Bipartisan BBQ Sauce - The best of Carolina, Kansas and Texas BBQ" is a thin, easily pourable BBQ sauce that leans more marinade than thick dip. But use it for whatever you want! Slightly sweet, slightly tangy, and little bit of peppery heat. Not hot, but there is a little kick. I normally go for the thick, sweet sauces, and while this isn't that.. it is quite good. So much so that I've already put another in my cart as well as their mustard sriracha bbq sauce..

The attractive label, interesting name, and quality flavor profile makes it a contender as a gift.

title: lovely, fresh blueberry juice
text:
Feel like I am doing shots of blueberry juice. It isn't a concentrate, but it more concentrated than a juice that has some naturally occurring water. "Juiced using our refined method and filtered to reduce natural water content"

I have also tried their larger bottles that don't say "extract". Side by side, I can tell that this is more concentrated. It pours thicker into a glass. But not so thick it is syrupy. Tastes fresh, tastes like liquid blueberries.

Well packaged in a small cardboard box with cardboard holders/retainer to keep the 6 very small glass bottles secure. As with their larger 3 packs, I find that it could be given as a gift.

Personally, I would rather have a larger bottle than multiple small ones. But I do like that the smaller containers make it easy to have it on the go, or simply as a portioned out item. I wouldn't necessarily want more than 2.5 ounces at a time. It works nicely as a water add in, or addition to some club soda. But usually I just drink it straight. A little pricier than my usual blueberry concentrate, but less than some I have tried. Let your budget guide you.

My rating is based solely on freshness and taste. I think it is a fine product. No issue with taste, freshness, or quality.

title: tasty, crunchy, easy on teeth, reminds me of a tortilla chip texture, great ON sandwich
text:
I really like the Lundberg rice based snack products. They are (to me) a step above the typical rice based offerings. These Sante Fe BBQ chips have good flavor. A little smoky, a little sweet, a little kick-- but not spicy.

I wanted more substance than a potato chip but not as hard and crunchy as a typical shiny "rice chip". These provide a perfect mouth feel of crunchy chip, but are easy on the teeth. They really remind me more of a tortilla chip. This is great as I really wanted something with an easy snap. I love adding chips into/onto my sandwiches, burgers, and these chips were perfect on a turkey sandwich I made the other day. Added some extra flavor and texture. I managed to use less than normal because they have some substance compared to regular potato chips.

I have crumbled some on my soup, and even my salad. I have also just snacked on them plain.

My husband tried them and responded "those have good flavor". Pretty sure he had no idea they were a rice based chip. Normally he would only ever go for a tortilla chip or potato chip.

While I like rice crackers and other products on occasion, I really like that the Lundberg varieties dont exactly taste or feel like rice crackers/chips/cakes. If you are looking for a strictly shiny rice chip then know these are not that.

title: perfection: the rare super dark roast that tastes bold and strong from a K-cup
text:
YESssssssssssssssss!
This Dark Italian Roast is their darkest roast yet, and it is delicious. Must love dark coffee. I find this to be wonderfully bold, strong, intense, chewy. It is DARK. I can taste the bean. This is a solid cup of uber dark coffee. It is exactly the flavor & roast level that I love, and it happens to be something I RARELY find in a K-cup (bags of whole bean or ground yes, k-cups not as easily). When I do find one, I never forget it. THIS IS IT.

I should have known I was in for a treat when I first opened the bag and it had/has that glorious coffee aroma that just makes me go mMmMmMMmmm. Well, so does the coffee. I prefer my coffee black, but when the coffee roast is on the lighter side, it can taste more acidic or bitter, so I end up adding creamer to make it more palatable. The darker the brew the less acid by nature it is. Then when there is a dark brew that just has a real good strong coffee flavor, it needs nothing. Just black. This is gorgeous consumed black. My new favorite!

I brew it using 10 ounces of water. I know I can easily run it though the machine for another 6 or 8 ounces and it would still hold strong. But for that perfect dark brew, I go with 10 ounces. Oh my!

I love all sorts of coffee, and happily review just about any coffee. Love it when I encounter a brand or variety that I know I WILL buy again, and this has gone on my list.

If you are buying SF Bay, then you know that the filter is exposed and that the Kcups must be kept in the bag to stay fresh. That has always a turn off in terms of storage. I have to fit a bag in a drawer rather than use a kcup organizer (in drawer or on counter style). But, I am totally willing to overlook it for this particular Super Dark Italian Roast.

Yum! Cheers!

title: simple creamy coconut based creamer, is great frothed w/ milk foamer or shaken for froth
text:
Pleasant, natural coconut cream flavor comes through. I had their vanilla option recently, and this stands out to me as the coconut flavor comes through a bit more. I like it quite a bit more, actually. It tastes like I am using coconut cream but without all the calories, fat, etc. Not that I care, but I'd go ahead and drink up! Very low cal, very low fat, low sodium per 1 TBS serving. I imagine if you are Keto or something, then this is an approved item.

Shelf stable until opened. As with their vanilla variety, this does a great job being frothed up with a milk foamer, or even just with a generous shake of the bottle. It is pretty creamy, tasty, and works well in my coffee. I normally drink my coffee black, but lately the plant based creamers have been quite appealing. Especially because this can be foamed up.

Any particulates/sediment that come out from the bottle can be reduced by shaking the bottle thoroughly first (though first time wont work since there is no spare room.. but after that all good). If you have some in your cup, just stir. Or dont look. It tastes fine.

By the way, this is NOT a sweetened creamer. There is no sugar- no added sugar, no naturally occurring sugar. The light coconut cream taste is from watered down coconut cream with thickeners added back in to make for a creamier experience and mouth feel. Given the 1 gram of fat, I would not necessarily choose this for getting your coconut needs. Just use it/drink it because it tastes good, adds some mellow tastiness to coffee, and doesn't add a bunch of liquid calories, etc. Very simple. I like it.

A 1 tbs serving contains:
10 calories
1 gram saturated fat
0 cholesterol
15 mg sodium
0 protein
0 sugar

title: Zero added sugar, low cal, lightly creamy, nice tasting blend of Oats/Almonds/Coconut
text:
Love the "Oats n' Creme" variety. A great blend of Oats, Almonds, and Coconut make for a delicious creamer. If I concentrate I can make out each component. Usually almond milk/creamer is hideous to me in coffee, but in this blend it is perfectly fine.

This creamer is lightly creamy, pretty tasty, and I find I am using it nearly every day. I used to just drink my coffee black! But it has been a welcome addition. I love the shelf stable creamers. It is nice to be able to store them in the pantry and only need to refrigerate once open. I find I use more of this than I would a dairy creamer or a non dairy (but not plant based) creamer. So I am going through a container rather quickly. Your mileage may vary.

Worth trying, anyway!

title: smooth, medium-dark roast
text:
I prefer a dark roast, but find that I can enjoy a medium-dark roast. This definitely leans darker on the medium roast scale, or a little light on the dark roast scale. So that being said, the "level 8" intensity seems about right, and is indeed a "medium dark" roast. I appreciate the accuracy of roast level. Definitely helps in making choices.

I have had the Level 10 Onyx, and that distinction seemed appropriate for the resulting taste. Glad same holds true here with Level 8 Velvet.

I've always enjoyed Gevalia coffee. Remember when it was just a subscribe/catalog company? These pods are as fresh and densely packed as expected. Resulting coffee smells good, looks good, and tastes good. Smooth, not bitter or acidic, bold but a little more mellow than a dark bold roast. While I prefer the latter, I know that this is a medium-dark roast, and it is a GOOD medium-dark roast. I'm impressed with the Gevalia options thus far.

title: well balanced medium roast coffee, quite fresh
text:
I have been enjoying this bag of ground coffee. I also have the ground option, and they taste the same. The coffee is really fresh! It is a MEDIUM roast, pretty well centered in the medium roast spectrum. Some lean dark, some lean light, and this sits pretty much right in the middle. It is overall, well balanced. Some medium roasts can taste too acidic or bitter, and this is relatively mellow. Easy to drink!

I tend to prefer it with some sort of creamer despite my preference for black.

Overall, I consider it a decent coffee for anyone when there are various tasting preferences in the mix. For example I prefer very dark bold chewy roasts and my husband prefers lighter slightly acidic medium roasts or light roasts, yet we can both drink this. I will not be my regular go-to, but the quality, freshness, and middle of the road medium roast flavor profile has been a welcome addition.

--The Great Basic coffee is roasted is in small batches, hence that notable freshness.
--It is solidly in the middle of the roast spectrum (ie well balanced), and
--Is comprised of a dynamic blend of regional beans:
34% Colombia Excelso
33% Brazil Red Catuai
33% India Monsoon Malabar

title: well balanced MEDIUM roast BLEND, pleasant every day/everyone coffee
text:
I'm enjoying this bag of whole bean coffee. It is a MEDIUM roast, pretty well centered in the medium roast spectrum. It is overall, well balanced. Some medium roasts can taste too acidic or bitter, and this is relatively mellow.

Easy to drink, doesn't have a strong aroma but it does have a fresh taste. I tend to prefer it with some sort of creamer despite my preference for black.

Overall, I consider it a decent coffee for anyone when there are various tasting preferences in the mix. For example I prefer very dark bold chewy roasts and my husband prefers lighter slightly acidic medium roasts or light roasts, yet we can both drink this. I will not be my regular go-to, but the quality, freshness, and middle of the road medium roast flavor profile has been a welcome addition.

Coffee can be tricky to review as it ultimately comes down to personal preference. Just know that this is a medium roast- not light, not dark.. medium. And that this medium roast is fresh (made in small batches), is solidly in the middle of the roast spectrum (ie well balanced), and that it is a mix of regional beans:
34% Colombia Excelso
33% Brazil Red Catuai
33% India Monsoon Malabar

title: great coffee as expected: fresh, robust, bold, dark brew for specialty creations
text:
This review is for Gevalia Nespresso Compatible Capsules, Onyx Espresso Pods for Nespresso Original Line Brewer, 10 ct. Box (Pack of 6)

Smooth, bold, full bodied; great base for specialty drinks and (of course) consuming as is.

Easily my favorite dark roast offering for Nespresso Original Line brewe. I have always enjoyed Gevalia, and this level 10 is pretty robust. I like it for use in making specialty drinks where a strong dark coffee is the base (currently- pumpkin spice lattes are my thing). Gives some nice froth, and when brewed into a clear mug it just looks awesome.

Not often, but sometimes in lieu of using my Nespresso machine, I will scoop out the contents into another drip brewer for making larger cups and pots of coffee. 1 tbs per pod, so I end up using a few, but it works.

title: gift worthy delicious healthy juice selections. YUM!
text: Nicely packaged and would totally work as a nice "thinking of you" gift. I know I would love if someone bought me 100% pure organic juice of this caliber. I loved all of these. I didn't expect to drink a whole jar (8.2 ounces) at once, but I poured some over ice and sipped it through the day. The Blueberry & Maqui berry was my least favorite, but still quite good. It was also the least sweet and most neutral tasting.  It was the first one I tried. The other two bottles (blueberry, and blueberry AND cherry) I made myself drink a small amount over the course of a couple of days. No added sugars, no added junk juice, no nothing.. like they say, not even water. Very nice. I could get used to this :)

title: Woah, this is quite good. Watermelon balances out the Aloe & Coconut water
text:
How does this taste so good? WHAT IS THIS SORCERY? :)
-I drink coconut water but kinda hate it; but I drink it for the added hydration. Love everything else coconut though.
-Aloe Juice is fantastically disgusting to consume. There too, I don't need it to taste good as a supplement.
-Watermelon? yeh, I like watermelon, but in no way did I think adding this flavor to two heavy hitters of strong flavor could do anything helpful.
So I took a chance anyway. I drink the coconut water to help with hydration. I am on a diuretic, and I just like having a little added hydration. Also good for sweaty days, and any day I don't feel well. I'm sure there are other reasons I consume it, but don't recall. Overall wellness, I guess.

So this arrives. I decide to go for it directly from the box. Not refrigerating it first, no adding it to anything. I just dove right in.

What did I taste? watermelon.
THAT'S IT.
It has a hint of watermelon. No mistaking it is watermelon, but it is like someone just squeezed some watermelon juice into a container. If I concentrate I can pick up on each ingredient, but none of the weirdness they impart.

I AM IMPRESSED.

So this magic of mixing coconut water, aloe juice, and watermelon juice makes for a perfectly pleasant, EASY to drink (even at room temperature) concoction.

So I think this is quite good. Glad to have found a new option I can actually enjoy. I think you will like it too, and I recommend it.. just gotta like watermelon.

easy peasy.. 5 stars

title: well balanced medium, no acidity, lovely black or with cream
text:
A little flat on the aroma emanating from a freshly opened can, but the overall taste is quite good. I prefer dark roasts or a medium that leans dark, or at least a balanced medium. I find this to be a well balanced medium. I don't pick up on acidity or bitterness, seems well rounded. An easy to drink medium roast coffee that holds well on its own consumed black, or pairs nicely with a splash of cream. I can make a full pot and share it with my husband who tends to prefer medium, or lighter medium roasts. Nice to have options that work for both of us...and anyone that wants a nice cup of coffee. Pleasant to me.

Pack of four, 10 ounce cans helps to keep taste fresh over buying a large container of any coffee.

title: works excellently with a milk foamer/frother
text:
Very light in the vanilla taste. I'm not sure whether I like that or am disappointed in that. I sometimes find vanilla flavor to be too artificial tasting to be pleasant, and so I would rather not have it. This has a barely there vanilla taste but it is natural. So I would definitely rather have the latter. The coconut is natural tasting too. The creamer is thick and creamy. As with a lot of creamers, if you shake it really well you can get some foam to come out. When just poured into the coffee, expect to stir it a bit as there are some tiny fragments. I don't notice it texture-ally. I tend to see this in the shelf stable creamers.

As much as I love coconut and even vanilla, I am glad that this creamer has just a hint of flavor. When I do use creamer, I don't necessarily want the added flavor-- I just want it to tone down my coffee, add some silkiness. This works in that regard. If you want strong vanilla, or strong coconut, this won't be it.

However, It really steps up its game when used with a milk frother. I have frothed it warm, I have frothed it cold (warm is most delightful). I love making an espresso (or simply any cup of coffee), frothing a 1/4 or so of this creamer (just 10 cals per TBS), stirring in some pumpkin spice and brown coconut sugar, then topping with this frothy creamer. Now with those added ingredients, it lends a perfect hint of coconut, vanilla, and lots of creaminess. Foam is strong, and stays that way.

comes 6 in a pack. Shelf stable until open.

title: smooth dark leaning medium roast that still packs a caffeine punch (w/o jitters)
text:
I would/will definitely buy this canister of Happy Belly ground medium roast coffee with half the caffeine. It is half the caffeine of their "Special Roast". It has robust flavor without being acidic or bitter. I prefer dark roasts and this is a dark leaning medium roast. Well balanced for my tastes. Very easy to drink. Half the caffeine but truly still packs a punch.

I drink regular coffee, but usually only 1-2 cups. Some days I want to drink more, so I will switch to decaff (it's the ritual I still want through the day more than the caffeine). But using a half caff option is nice for days I definitely will be drinking a couple cups of coffee or more, and don't want to take in too much caffeine. I have had some half caff where it tastes fine, but I don't quite feel the kick of caffeine. This one I do. I had to double check my container!

I like that I can keep on drinking it and not feel jittery. I still cut myself off around noon, but I know I can have a little coffee beyond that time so long as it is half caff.

I want to point out again that this is a well balanced medium roast. I usually drink my dark roasts black, but have to use creamer on lighter roasts due to the acidity, bitterness, and brightness (yuck). This is so mellow and smooth with a pleasant depth of flavor that I can drink it black no problem. It is surprisingly extra good tasting to me. Writing about it makes me want another cup!

I tend to like Happy Belly products, an Amazon company, and this is another I can add to the list.

Best by 09/2022 (acquired 09/2020)
Roasted, packaged, ad shipped from USA.

title: Mild, gentle, semi sweet onion powder
text:
Good flavor. Fresh. Seems to be of quality. I know there are differences among brands, and nuances of flavor. Not all taste the same. This has a more mild, sweet onion flavor than some. I prefer a more robust, pungent flavor. This is good though, and I will gladly use it. Is lovely on burgers.

Texture: not quite a fine powder, not quite granular. Maybe more like a fine small flake?

Packaging: glass bottle with twist off cap & shaker holes.

Good product, no problems; just not my favorite. Not sure yet if it will be a repurchase. We go through a lot of onion powder so we'll see.

title: good bold basic coffee, easy to drink, lovely black or with cream
text:
Mmm! The past few mornings I have been enjoying this French Roast ground coffee by Happy Belly. It comes in a canister, something I rarely see anymore. Unless I missed it while digging around, you will need your own scoop.

I make half a pot using roughly 6 heaping table spoons with about 32 or so ounces of water. It has a robust flavor- I can tell I am drinking a decent cup of coffee. Not crazy amazing, nor fancy, but a good every day easy to drink bold coffee. I live for dark roasts, and this is pretty good for an already ground coffee. My coffee turns out very dark, can be comfortably consumed black, and withstands cream if you prefer. I like it black, but have also had it with cream.

Definitely powers my day! 4.5 stars

I've had Happy Belly products before and have always found them to be of good quality, and budget friendly.

title: lighter leaning medium, slight acidity, minor bite of bitter, has bright flavor like a donut shop
text:
I can definitely tell that this is a medium coffee. Reminds me of a few commercial donut shops regular coffee-- has a coffee flavor with a hint of acidity, minor bitter bite. Not my favorite roast as I prefer dark, but I can certainly taste test various roasts. It's too light and bright for me to drink black--the acidity and slight bitterness are a little much for me. I can drink dark roasts black and some mediums.. but this medium leans light But definitely not light), so to tame the bright taste I need a splash of cream to mellow it out. Not too shabby like that. Now my husband almost always drinks medium coffee and he likes this. He noted it is on the lighter end of the medium spectrum too. I know it isn't his favorite, so this won't be a replacement.. but it is good. I don't think it will be not liked by anyone. Just the nuances come down to personal preference.

The pods are exposed bottom. Must keep your pods in the bag they came in to maintain freshness. Coffee comes in a box with two bags of 15. Bags smell great when opened up.

title: easy to drink dark roast, not as strong/dark/bold as some. Good for most coffee drinkers
text:
I prefer dark brews, and while this is a dark brew it doesn't quite have enough of that chewy, bold taste that I look for in a dark roast. It is good though. Solid. It is a fair cup of dark coffee. Not bitter. Easy to drink black, or lightens up a lot with a little creamer. I find that it does best with just a simple 10 ounce brew. Some of my stronger bolder coffees can handle 14, 16 ounces. This really begins to taste like brown water when 14 ounces of water are used. So 10 it is for me (max 12). It's good, just not my favorite. A good one for those that like a solid coffee taste without the bitterness or acidity that lighter brews can impart. Yet not so bold and strong that it scares people off.

It's an open pod- much like SFB. My Keurig handles it fine. No issues thus far. The pods come in a box with two bags of 30. Since they aren't protected all around by plastic, be sure to keep the bag closed for maximum freshness.

title: chewy, sweet, versatile- YUM!
text:
I love medjool dates. I don't always see them in store, so I am pleased to be able to buy a big whopping 4.4 pound pack online. I've never been a fan of the term "nature's candy", but if out of all naturally sweet foods I have had, medjool dates fit that description. Soft, super sweet, chewy. It cures a need for something sweet.

Eat them alone (watch out for the pit), chop them up and sprinkle on oatmeal, or my favorite (and makes it taste like a candy bar): slide out the pit, and insert a roasted brazil nut. Mmmm! Maybe dip into some melted chocolate and let cool. Woah! Lots and lots of recipes for pulverizing these into a paste for use in making healthier desserts.

Keep in mind these are (naturally) sugary and still pack calories. But they also contains lots of other good nutrients.

I love that these come with seeds still inside. This helps keep them moist. I have found that if they ever do dry out, then I definitely relegate them for use in recipes. Usually added moisture from other ingredients makes it all work out.

This box, once opened is just a wide open tray of medjool dates. Since they are all for me, I went ahead and sorted them into smaller baggies, and tucked them back into the sturdy box they came in. Even better if you have glass containers. They will last a long while both in freshness and the amount-- one woman can only eat so many medjool dates. So dividing them into storage containers helps a lot. I think the best by date on mine is May 2021 (acquired Sept 2020).

title: Mix of bold, strong, Dark & Medium roasts. Great variety, I keep buying it
text:
Great sampler for those who prefer strong, dark(er), bold roasts. This is not a box entirely of "dark roast" as there are some medium roast options, but the medium selections do have a bold flavor, so they have earned their spot in this selection of "Keurig Bold Roast Coffee Collection Variety Pack". There are more dark roast than medium roast, if I recall correctly.

I have this on a subscribe/save order, so have had this selection multiple times so far. I find it a delightful mix to look forward to. I don't think there are any I don't like. But I certainly have my favorites.

It is also a nice way to sample different brands to see if anything new piques ones interest. I know I would not have normally have purchased KrispyKreme, but this has turned into not only my favorite of the bunch, but is in my favorite top 3 in all the land.

I recommend-- definitely worth the try :)

title: just Peachy. Easy to drink peach Oolong tea is loghtly sweet, not bitter
text:
The flavor of Peach Oolong is what I was hoping for. Indeed LIGHTLY sweet, in a delicate tea base. I often find black tea too harsh, and was pleased to see an Oolong option- which tends to have a gentle, easy taste. This is a combo of Oolong and Black, but the black barely makes an appearance in the flavor profile. You may or may not like this. I like that it is super well balanced and easy to drink. The peach is nice, the sweetness is just enough, and the tea flavor provides a pleasant but not overwhelming foundation.

Great option to have on hand when I just want something to drink, but dont want water or pop. Love having a fridge full of options, and this Peach Oolong by Honest has been a nice addition.

Organic Brewed Tea (Filtered water, fair-trade certified organic Oolong and Black Tea leaves), Fair-trade certified organic cane sugar, organic peach puree, organic agave syrup, natural flavors, malic acid, citric acid.

70 calories

title: good, strong and smooth cold brew, course gound, smells yummy
text:
One More Cup – Organic Cold Brew Coffee Grounds is a big 2 lbs bag of course ground coffee. This is a good medium dark roast. I often go for dark-dark, but this is really quite tasty. I just want my coffee flavor to come through, and this does. I love that I can get several cold brews out from this big bag of coarse ground coffee. I see that it mentions brewing it hot, too. If I want to go for a hot brew, I figured I could grind it a little more if need be from my auto drip, or make it in my French press. For fun, I did both, and yes it is a nice smooth coffee. I use around 1 tbs per 6 ounces of water for hot.

As for true cold brew, I do about a 1:4 ratio of coffee to water. I tend to err on side of more coffee versus less coffee since I want to make a strong concentrate (that can be watered down after) vs a weak cup of cold brown water (that can't be made stronger). Cold brew tends to be very smooth as it simply isn't as acidic as hot brewed coffee. Just keep in mind that this is a make ahead item, so give it 15-24 hours to "cold brew" before finished. Enjoy! I know I do.

title: fresh, quality coffee that seems a little too mild for a dark roast
text:
I find that I need more coffee than what I normally use to get a stronger taste. The bag states, 1 TBS per 6 ounces of water. That seems about right. I think many of my others brands say 1TBS per 8-10 ounces of water, and I initially just followed suit with this, but I found I had a boring cup of hot brown water. Once I upped the amount, the taste was much more pleasant. Even so, it is not my favorite. But it isn't bad! I think it is worth a try for the quality and freshness. Might be perfect for you or someone you want to gift to. I just prefer a more robust,bold dark roast and this seems quite mild. If you told me it was a medium roast that leans dark, I would buy into that description. But for a dark roast.. it seems too gentle. lol

I do think it is a quality bean, the bag smells and appears fresh. It does make for a very easy to drink cup of coffee. Not as bold as I like, but it is certainly smooth. I'll finish off this bag no problem, just not sure if I will buy again.

Thumbs up for being certified organic and fair trade certified.

title: Raw, Unrefined & Unfiltered- excellent, clean tasting oil for finishing, as a shot
text:
I love going to olive oil and vinegar tastings at a local merchant. I would make regular purchases but haven't been able to do so in 2020. I am very pleased to discover that the Papa Vince plain olive oil is amazing. I don't often have discerning tastes, but when it comes to olive oil I can taste and appreciate the nuances.

This is a beautiful oil. Raw, Unrefined & Unfiltered. I like to use it as a finishing oil, over salads, over roasted vegetables, as a dip for good Italian bread from my local Italian bakery, or- my most often way to consume it: as a shot. I love taking a big ole swig of quality olive oil. This has a smooth, buttery taste with a kick to the back of the throat peppery finish. Then it dissipates-- no lingering after taste.

It is very very nice, and I recommend it. It's pricey. Even more so than my other high quality brand.. but if this is in your budget or if you are looking for a nice gift for someone (this comes with a velour drawstring bag), it absolutely is a great product. I think they have same option sans bag for $1-2 less.

title: tasty, high quality oil oils and out of this world balsamic vinegar
text:
Papa Vince carries some fantastic olive oils. In the past (pre-covid), I would regularly go to a local olive oil merchant and do tastings of their selections before purchase. I have been running low on my olive oil and vinegar options, but haven't been able to go to my old place to purchase. I have been reticent to invest in anything new, other than a basic olive oil (and no, it is just not the same). I am happy to have the chance to try the Papa Vince olive oils because it has given me a new option for purchase. I find their "plain" olive oil to be exactly what I like for use in dipping, for salads, and for taking healthy "shots" of oil. This is soooo good., and I highly recommend it. I love the mild smooth buttery olive taste that follows up with a kick of pepper at the back of the throat, then dissipates. It is lovely. I really love it as a shot. Pricey but worth it.

The flavored ones are delicate. Lemon, Orange, Tangerine, Chili peppers. Very nice alone over a simple salad, or as part of a bigger recipe. Works nicely drizzled over roasted vegetables. I am so used to using plain olive oil, that it has been fun figuring out where these can fit in. I really like the chili pepper one a lot.

The Moscato Balsamic vinegar is a must have. There are very few that I have had in my life that really pack a lot of depth of flavor. This is instantly one of them. Excellent over anything you can think of. I like it drizzled over a pork tenderloin. Amazing on roasted Brussels sprouts. Of course salads and roasted vegetables are excellent applications.

I think all of it is of excellent quality. My go to is the plain as well as the balsamic. I will definitely be buying those again. The flavored is very nice, but I imagine those will take me longer to get through.

I love this for myself, and will likely continue with this brand. Love having found an excellent quality product. I think it would also make for a fantastic gift, especially if you can find a 6 spot wire basket or something for these to go in. They are attractive enough to keep out on display. I love seeing olive oils sitting out in a kitchen.

Bottles are well packaged and there is information inserts- including how to do your own tasting. Love that.

title: convenient packets soy sauce. Enjoy salty, umami flavor anytime
text:
"Why yes, I do need 500 packets of soy sauce" was my response when my husband saw this box sitting on the kitchen counter and asked about it. Then he claimed I was weird. Next time we need soy sauce, lets see how much my weirdness pays off.

It is a box packed to the brim of soy sauce packets. It's great! Super convenient and doesn't take up much room. We usually have a bottle of soy sauce in the cupboard. But, sometimes not. So then I go fishing around for random take out packets kicking around wherever condiment packets hang out. I never really thought of buying condiment packets before. It is like my mind was blown considering the impact of buying condiments in this travel friendly, portion controlled, easy to store format could have. Think of all the real estate I would get back from my fridge and lazy-susan cupboard if I bought some items in packets instead. Basically the rarely used or the regularly used but not enough at once type items (so hot sauces, wasabi, but not ketchup or mayo- we go through a lot of that). Acquiring a bunch of soy sauce packets is my gateway condiment packet buying experiment. It could be brilliant or it could be a bust. I don't think they actually go bad, do they?

Would make for an amusing gift for a college kid, or anyone who often makes use of soy sauce.

Flavor wise, it is about what I expect. Has that salty, umami thing going on. Have just used it on usual fare- rice, and some sushi.

No issues so far. Cant go wrong at $0.04 per packet.

title: Elevate your Italina cuisine night with delicious, fresh, quality products
text:
I have been enjoying the Papa Vince ITALIAN GOURMET GIFT BASKET, Mediterranean option. Priced separately, this is a good bargain. You get to try some delicious, naturally sweet sauce (2 bottles), a pound of fresh tasting pasta, a gorgeous balsamic glaze, and a smooth, buttery, peppery olive oil. This is real food, friends. Not quickly massed produced stuff. It has such a fine flavor, delicate even. There is nothing I haven't liked by Papa Vince. I personally can't afford it to sustain my pantry, but you bet it is on my list for those times I want to elevate my Italian cuisine. I will also be adding it to wish lists for when people want ideas on what to get me, hehe. I definitely think it makes for a great gift for.. anyone that likes food :)

I like that it is as fresh as can be, and that the pasta is low glycemic and definitely does not make me feel bogged down after. I tend to be sensitive to a lot of foods, and I am not rushing off to the bathroom with any of this. The sauce is so flippin good, I eat it by the spoonful. Actually, same thing with the olive oil. The sauce is thick, and naturally sweet. The sauce is in amber glass bottles with bottle cap that requires a bottle opening to get it off. While I am a big fan of onion and garlic, it is nice that this sauce only contains red cherry tomatoes, basil, extra virgin olive oil and salt. It can be used as is, or adjusted to your taste. Many people with food sensitivities refrain from onion and garlic (reminds me of FODMAP), so this sauce provides people with options.

The olive oil is divine. I love a peppery olive oil. It is really good tasting to me. I take swigs/shots on occasion direct from bottle. Starts off smooth and buttery then it finishes with that awesome pepper kick to the back of the throat. Mmm so good! Once in awhile I buy some fresh Italian bread from a well known local Italian bakery. It is glorious to take a plate and drizzle oil all over it then mop it up with the fresh bread- which I did with this. Add a few drops of the glaze to give it a little sweet bite.

Or take that glaze and drizzle it over salad (I had a bowl of sliced tomatoes). Another amaaaaaazing taste it to drizzle it over roasted vegetables. OMG.. right now all the fall vegetables are being harvested- and what an amazing time to roast some root vegetables, squash, Brussels sprouts in the oven. The balsamic glaze and a little olive oil, and maybe some salt and pepper make it quite a taste sensation.

I really appreciate all the information that came with the products, as well as what is listed on the product page. I even checked out the items individually (thinking about getting more sauce and pasta) and I gleaned even more info. I recommend giving this a try- for yourself or as a gift.

My rating of 5 is due to the great quality of each product in this Mediterranean set.

title: super smooth, very mild coffee, easy to drink, may not be punggent enough for some
text:
Very smooth, the most smooth and mild I have ever tasted. Zero acidity, zero bitterness. Just a silky smooth medium roast that is sure to please anyone. I tend to prefer darker roasts, and coffee with a bolder taste, but this mild flavor is about what I expect from the middle of the roast spectrum. It does very well consumed black (my preference) yet also stands up to some cream. If going for over ice, then definitely aim for using a greater amount of coffee.

Smells nice in bag, smells great once ground. I can smell hints of wood and something sweet. Taste wise, it is rather neutral. It is just so smooth that I don't pick up on the nuances of flavor.

I think the recommended brewing amount is 1 heaping TBS per 10 ounces of water when using a standard drip brew.

Very nice coffee especially if you are in need of low acidity due to sensitive stomach. It is indeed a gentle coffee.

title: delicious light flavor, lovely over ice, no need to add anything else, Yummy
text:
Mmm this is a nice tea. Naturally caffeine free. I have the flavor, Mandarin Mimosa. I'm not a big tea drinker, but I enjoy an herbal tea or tisane on occasion. I am partial to orange tea, so I was excited to try this. It is quite tasty, and needs nothing added. It already imparts a natural sweetness; it's lovely.

The weather is still warm, so I have been drinking it over ice. Very nice!

For hot tea, use 1 sachet for every 8 ounces
For iced tea, use 2 sachets for every 8 ounces.

I concur with doubling the sachets for iced tea. I use a 16 ounce mason jar and a couple of times I mindlessly just used 2 sachets (when it should be 4). I didn't correct it and drank it anyway over ice. It still tasted very nice, but when I tried it with 3-4 sachets, I liked the extra flavor much more. So double to get stronger flavor, or keep it single to get a hint or essence of flavor. I think the regular amount is good for hot tea-- though there too play around with it and see what strength of flavor you like best.

I really like the layers of flavor.

There are 48 sachets--12 in each lidded storage container. 4 storage cups total. Keep them all to yourself, or share.
$21.92 divided by 4, = $5.48 each cup of 12 sachets.
(I see some flavor options are a few pennies less)

Love this product! It may be my new go-to orange tea.

Apple pieces, mandarin orange peel, mangoe pieces, papaya pieces, pineapple pieces, licorice root, lemongrass, marigold

title: super convenient rice in a pinch, great prep item or on the go lunch item. Subtle flavor
text:
I like packets of rice for the convenience. I have been using products like this on and off for years. It is one of those items that are nice to have on hand for quick meal preparation. Just need to heat it up! Or could be consumed at room temp in a pinch. Cold rice? why not. So for me, it isn't an every day thing. Kind of a prep thing slash super convenience thing. It is what it is: flavored shelf stable rice that is already cooked but just needs to be heated up in the microwave (or consumed cold).

I have the Authentic Royal Ready To Heat Rice in the cilantro lime flavor. It is currently the priciest of the bunch. It has a subtle flavor- hint of cilantro, hint of tangy lime. Contains goodly amount of sodium but it doesn't make me feel thirsty like some boxed rice products. I don't think is missing anything, flavor wise. Seems to be just enough flavor without being over powering. I could go stronger, but I think it is a good balance overall. Makes me curious about the other flavor offering.

Easy to make: tear off top, place in microwave. Cook for 90 seconds. I imagine timing will vary based on individual microwaves. The contents of my pouch was piping hot and needed no extra time. Despite being hot, handling of the pouch required no pot holder. It has a touchable, cook exterior. So grab and go!

title: fresh taste, ranch flavor falls short, BUT great as anytime dressing/dip, contains eggs
text:
The Newman's Own Avocado Oil & Extra Virgin Olive Oil Dairy Free Ranch Dressing is as good as expected in terms of quality of ingredients and freshness in taste. I like it as a dressing or dip but it doesn't quite have that "ranch" taste. So I wont be reaching for this when I want ranch, but I will happily grab for it when I want a good, tasty salad topper. It is a good dressing though- and I may buy it again. Really can't go wrong with this brand, right?

It is creamy and thick, with a little punch of tangy flavor. I have used it over garden fresh tomatoes and hard boiled eggs. I'll be using it on my next sandwich as it is thick enough to spread with a knife. Adds a healthy zip of flavor.

By the way, this does contain egg yolks.

Ingredients:
Avocado Oil, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Water, Cage Free Egg Yolks (Cage Free Egg Yolks, Salt), Distilled Vinegar, Less Than 2% Of: Sea Salt, Lemon Juice Concentrate, Xanthan Gum, Garlic*, Onion*, Mustard Flour, Black Pepper, Parsley*, Dill*, Oregano*, Chives*, Spicy Brown Mustard (Distilled Vinegar, Water, Mustard Seed, Sea Salt, Turmeric, Spice). *Dried. Contains: Eggs

title: concentrated sweet non dairy creamer w/ subtle, natural vanilla taste
text:
Nestle Coffee mate Coffee Creamer, Dairy Free, Almond Milk Vanilla, Liquid Pump Bottle, 50.7 Ounce

It is made for businesses in mind. This may or may not be suitable to you depending on your preferences. So I will just describe it. The same aspect may be great for one person and terrible for another. Overall, I like it.

--The creamer (as most of these style creamers are) are shelf stable for 6 months, unopened. Once opened, the packing says it is good for 30 days. I'm comfortable with pushing it a couple extra weeks. Longer if I can fit it in my fridge. It has a well sealed container, and once the pump is placed, there is no taking it off. It locks.
"This product is best served at room temperature and should not be refrigerated as this can cause the product to harden. But not to worry, in case the pump clogs, you can simply run the pump under hot water to loosen the liquid. It can retain its irresistible flavor for 9 months at room-temperature, and once opened, keeps for 30 day"

--Tall bottle. More so once the pump is added on.

--Tamper proof. The pump locks on, so once on it isn't coming off. These bottles are really made for businesses but of course can be enjoyed at home.

--spot to jot down date of receiving, opening

--This is a CONCENTRATED product so it is on the thicker side. This "creamer" looks and tastes a lot like condensed milk. Sweet, thick, syrupy. Has a more tan coloring to it.

--It has a HINT of vanilla flavor. Very light, not strong, more natural than many vanilla flavorings. I like this.

--I couldn't tell it uses almond milk. I find of all the non dairy milks/creamers out there, usually almond milk tastes weird in my coffee. This tastes smooth, and non descript. Even those people who don't like almond milk likely won't have a problem with this. Could be a good one for the break room.

--It barely lightens my very dark coffee. I also made up a cup using regular Nestle Coffeemate Original unsweetened refrigerated creamer that I bought from the store. I used same amount (5 tsp), and it lightened it just a little more than this creamer does, but not by much. I guess my make my coffee thick too lol
