--I usually don't care for sweet coffee, but I don't mind it on occasion- especially for upcoming fall season where the flavored drinks just seem to be better when it is sweetened. Anyway, it took 5 servings to get it noticeably sweet, and it took about that much to lighten my coffee. That is 5, 1 pump (1 teaspoon) servings at 25 calories per pump (1 teaspoon) for an added 125 calories, 15 grams of sugar. I don't really care-- I drink, eat what I want.. but thought you may like to know that it seems to need more than 1 pump to make any real change to the coffee look or taste. I think I could get by on 3 tsp (1 TBS). Your tastebuds may vary.

--The other products- like the more liquid offerings are a 1 TBS serving (3 tsp = 1 TBS) serving, so my 5 tsp is not quite 2 TBS. BUT, this is considered a concentrated product. Just know it may take a little experimenting to find the sweet spot. ha

--I like the overall flavor., wish it creamed up my dark coffee more. Might be a nice option for uses beyond coffee and tea. Again, it reminds me of sweetened condensed milk (I suppose it is, just in a non dairy way!) and would maybe use it in a similar way. I could see drizzling it over ice cream, flavoring for a milkshake, yogurt, oatmeal, making a quick glaze or frosting, or even by the spoonful for those that enjoy a sugar boost.

--works well to add the sweetness and creaminess to an Irish coffee. Add your Irish whiskey of choice, and stir some of this in.

Not in love, but I like it enough.

title: Flavorful! a great spice blend for anything, not just for replacing salt
text:
Lots and lots of great flavor. I was attracted to this spice blend because of all the interesting, aromatic spices that are contained within it. I listed them below. I should use less salt, and I have an assortment of "no salt" or "low salt" blends, but sometimes I still need that bite that salt creates. However, I don't need as much when I have other flavors going on to excite my taste buds. So whether I use this alone or in combination with some salt, I simply tend to use less salt...and add lots of flavor!

This blend is for anyone, for use on anything. It stands out to me for its inclusion of cumin- which lends a depth of flavor that is wonderful for meats, legumes, potatoes, and rice. I mean, it can be used on anything.. I just happen to really like the flavor cumin imparts especially on those foods. Love the turmeric, too. Ok, love all of it!

Make adjustments-- add some salt, or sugar, or additional spices- make what you want of it. Like I said, it is great as a no salt option, but it is so much more than that, too. Enjoy!

Onion
Garlic
Turmeric
Paprika
Celery seed
Coriander
Basil
Oregano
Dill weed
Black pepper
Parsley
Thyme
Cayenne
Cumin

title: whole lot of delicious flavor packed into reusable pouches- ice packs, drink cup
text:
Organic Apple Mango Pineapple Banana is delicious. It is sweet with a hint of tang. It is hard to stop at just consuming one pouch. I buy stuff like this for my own use, as well as for use in treat puzzles for my dogs. I am not sure I will want to share this with them as this flavor combo is extra good tasting to me. I can eat it at room temp or from fridge. I like it straight from the pouch, or drizzled over yogurt, or oatmeal. I recommend the adults give it a try. It is a phenomenal yogurt topper. Ooh, or ice cream (haven't tried that yet, but I love vanilla ice cream and this would be nice on top). I like that I can toss one in my bag along with some other snacks, and can take off for the day knowing I have good tasting food to nosh on. This is a smooth thick puree, no chewing required. I like that I can slurp- no need for a spoon.

3.2 ounces in each. There isn't much in each pouch- couple of slurps and it's empty. I always add a splash of water to the empty pouch so I can consume whatever bit is still inside. I think this style of packaging should have more in it since I really doubt anyone would use less than one full pouch at a time, and I feel bad seeing the pouches build up. They are nice pouches! On the plus side, the pouches are quite durable. I use them to make ice packs. The spout is wide enough to easily put water inside. The twist cap goes on tight and seems leak proof. I even keep a clean one in my purse for on the go use as a way to get water from a sink when I am out and about. They aren't labeled for reuse, but I am reusing them as much as I can.

title: YUM! includess: Salt, Black Pepper, Sugar, Onion, Garlic, Celery Seed, & Lemon Oil YUM!
text:
I loved Big Gs "Sea Salt and Pepper", and their "Garlic and Pepper" so much that I was hoping for an equally really good Lemon Pepper seasoning. This is good! It has a punch of black pepper, the tart of lemon, and a interesting well balanced flavor profile from the addition of salt, garlic, celery seed, and sugar.

Ingredients: Salt, Black Pepper, Citric Acid, Sugar, Onion, Garlic, Celery Seed, Calcium Silicate, Lemon Oil

I tend to use lemon pepper seasoning on chicken, vegetables, and sometimes simple pasta and butter dishes. This is the first in awhile that I haven't wanted/needed to add additional lemon to the dish. It is quite good as is. Thank you!!

title: sprinkle it on everything, SO Much better than garlic salt- well balanced flavor
text:
A tasty, well balanced spice blend that isn't just a super salty "garlic salt". That is what I was kind of expecting, but actually I like this a whole lot more. Here is the ingredient list:

garlic, salt, spices, tricalcium phosphate (prevents caking).

The sea salt is in larger flakes. It has a subtle salty taste. I am so used to the fine salt mixed with garlic, that it is a rarely used item. Since acquiring this blend, it has been used several times. It is delicious to use on just about anything you want lightly salty tasting garlic flavoring on.

It IS great on everything. I also highly recommend their Garlic & Pepper spice mix- great flavor!

title: Garlic Pepper: garlic, salt, onion, black pepper, spices, white pepper, basil
text:
A tasty, well balanced spice blend that isn't just Garlic and Black Pepper. That is what I was expecting, but actually I like this more. Here is the ingredient list:
garlic, salt, onion, black pepper, spices, white pepper, basil, tricalcium phosphate (prevents caking).

It’s delicious, well balanced garlic pepper.I have grabbed it for everything so far: most recently-- to doctor up a store bought pizza, and as a flavoring for a pork tenderloin.

Definitely garlicky, has the kick of heat from garlic and pepper, but also has the other flavors to add depth and bite.

title: Keep the ritual! fresh, smells good, tastes good, has coffee mouth feel, great alternative!
text:
Surprisingly good and coffee-like. If someone made this for me, I would not know that it wasn't coffee at all. I tend to drink dark bold coffee, and while this isn't that.. it is quite coffee like. I have had various non-coffee products and I gave up on them. Most tasted more like a tea or something too bland to be satisfying.

When I first made this, I made it without having yet had any coffee. I made it like I would a pot of coffee (6 tbs for half pot.. not sure how many ounces of water I used), and I used the amount that I would typically use to make coffee, maybe a little less. I made it in my NinjaBrewer
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07PFLM2LK/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp

I couldn't taste fig, nor chickpea. I am not sure what I was tasting. It was mellow, smooth, dark, with a rich mouth feel. I put tried it over ice, I tried it black, and I tried it with vanilla macadamia creamer. Over ice, it watered down a little as expected. That reminded me more of an iced tea rather than coffee. Not bad, just not what I was going for. As for hot with creamer, the creamer barely touched it- the "coffee" stayed quite dark. I could taste more of the creamer than the "coffee". I typically drink my coffee black, and prefer this black too.

How does it taste so coffee like? and look like coffee? and brew like coffee? and feel like coffee in the mouth? How does it not taste entirely like figs? I'm in awe.

So I drank it all morning. I kinda forgot I wasn't drinking coffee. I was perking up naturally and without jitters. I think I felt a slump around 5-6 hours later. But wow, I was impressed that I didn't NEED my usual coffee.

Will I totally switch? No, definitely not.. I do love my actual coffee.

Would I buy it again? yes. There are some days I want the ritual of coffee without having the actual caffeine. I often will just make half caff, or decaff.. but this was a delightful change of pace. I was still feeling like I got some lift from it. Where is the energy coming from? So despite it saying that it can be consumed at night without disturbing sleep, I am reticent to drink it too late. Maybe I will try it sometime later in the day and see how it affects me. I think going forward, I will have a cup of regular coffee, then drink this rest of morning.

Could I have been fooled by this? sure! Maybe more discerning taste buds would pick up more flavor nuances than me. But if you are buying a non coffee product.. gotta say, you must be ok with it not being perfectly coffee-like. But this is quite close.

Do I recommend it? Yes!

I may try seeping it next time I make it.. see if I can use less, since I seemed to go through quite a bit in my first pot. It said it can be used in coffee pots! but is also says.. "Simply Steep, Strain, Serve And Sip".

title: moist (but dried) cranberries lightly sweetened with sugar, great for baking, noshing
text:
I'm not too choosy when it comes to selecting a bag of dried cranberries. They all seem about the same to me: dried cranberries, added white sugar, and lightly coated in sunflower oil (as a preservative, and to keep berries from sticking). Ultimately I prefer unsweetened (not even juice), but that is a rare find. So normally I grab whatever I find in the store, or whatever price seems best online. Because.. they really are nearly all the same. If sugar count seems to differ, then one must look at the serving size listed on bag. This 44 gram serving has 27 grams of sugar, where as another brand may be 71 grams pf sugar per serving, but their serving size is 100 grams, etc. Even so, this brand is about on par as others in that regard, or a little lower. BUT their pricing is rather high for a 1 lb bag compared to other offerings.

If none of that is a concern, then know that this is a a fresh tasting bag of moist (but dry) cranberries, lightly sweetened, and as delicious and versatile as expected. I am familiar with Country Spoon products and have always had a good experience with anything I have had.

title: Product of USA, lightly sweetened w/ apple juice, preserved w/ sunflower oil
text:
Good sized bag of dried blue berries. Nearly raisin in size. They are lightly sweetened with apple juice, and lightly coated with sunflower oil. Tasty dried blueberries, great for anything you want to add them to (or nosh by the handful). Yum yum!

No sugar added means- no.(white)SUGAR.added.
BUT, it does contain apple juice, which is sweet and contains naturally occurring sugar. Product description (and ingredient list) shows this.
Addition of sunflower oil is normal, as it is a natural preservative and also helps berries from sticking.

Both are very typical in "no sugar added" dried berry products.

Perfectly fine, fresh, and tasty product. I didn't realize it is the same company who makes some of the concentrated juices I buy for flavoring water or club soda with. Great!

title: makes my taste buds sing, awesome for vegan mac-n-cheese, and I am not vegan
text:
I love this pasta so much that I am already ordering more.

I really didn't know what to expect from this Bentilia Zimmunity "pasta". I have had some similar (ish) that were ok, some that were pretty bad. None that made me think/feel/taste like actual pasta. I did not expect to be totally enamored with this vegetable pasta, but I am. I cant get enough! I think it cooks up great- firm with similar texture to regular pasta. I have paid attention to how long it takes to cook on my gas stove, I just check the noodles and bite them to see if they are done enough for me.

Great taste, great mouth feel.

The noodles with nothing on it have a hint of spinach taste. The water it cooks in makes for great use in making a gravy, sauce, or for thickening up another sauce (much more significantly over regular pasta water). So if this interests you, then don't drain it using a colander, first pour the liquid into a storage container, then drain the rest. The liquid will thicken up on its own, and even firm up a lot in the fridge. I used it a couple times for other dishes. Haven't made a "gravy" with it yet, but it very well can be used for that.

The 8 ounce box has 4 servings, 170 calories. Cooked, makes a little more than 2 cups (see my pic). I have a huge appetite and am satisfied with eating the whole box. Ridiculous, but that is where I am at. If you have a normal healthy appetite, you can get away with less. If I had it with other vegetables or protein source, then I would not be able to eat the whole box. So maybe I will get on that. lol

I am not a vegan, I am not even vegetarian, but I appreciate plant based foods. I love all sorts of food- I love to eat- and this is right up my ally. When I was making my first box (I make whole box at a time- it is just 8 ounces) I was debating on what flavors to add. I figured I would go with simple additions such as butter, seasonings, and Parmesan cheese. Well then that changed to a vegan ghee (butter flavored coconut/avocado oil), seasonings, and topped with a generous dose of nutritional yeast. Sometimes a drizzle of hemp oil. I fell in love with that taste combo. Next thing I know I am adding a splash of the cooking water (now thickened up significantly) and more nutritional yeast to turn it into a creamy "mac and cheese" OMG.....OMG SO GOOD.

My fav so far:
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08C192Z5V/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp
https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B083FHHMYQ/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07VQXK517/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07NF9QC5R/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp

All of it together really made my taste buds sing. I have been craving this like crazy all week, and have made up 3 boxes so far over past 10 days. So yeh, I am buying more. Totally recommend it. One of the few products that make me wish I could give it bonus rating. Pricey, and don't care. I am able to make a good "mac n cheese" any time, and it makes me so happy to eat it.

title: solid, smooth coffee taste w/ hint of natural pumpkin
text:
PUMPKIN!
Yep, I have a weakness for Autumn and all things pumpkin. I embrace it, I am not ashamed of it. I just live-love-laugh it off (bahaha, couldn't help myself). I don't even like flavored coffee, and I don't even necessarily love pumpkin-- but I do love the change in weather from humid hot to cool and crisp, so I have a positive association with the flavors of the season. So.. GIVE ME ALL THE PUMPKIN THINGS.

This coffee is good! It is even good for those that don't like flavored coffee because it is so natural tasting (I actually taste natural pumpkin rather than simulated pumpkin). It is a darker roast, which my most favorite coffees tend to be dark, strong, bold roasts. I'd say it is as dark as a coffee can be when using an arabica and robusta mix. So not super dark, but a solid medium dark. Pretty smooth too.

Robusta beans can be tricky to work with-- use too much and the flavor suffers. That is where the extra caffeine comes from- robusta beans. I have had some "extra caffeine" brands and have been sorely disappointed in the flavor, or lack of. I am VERY PLEASED with this coffee. I can taste the coffee, I can taste a HINT of natural pumpkin, and I don't taste any off/odd flavoring from the robusta beans. A little extra caffeine is not hugely noticeable for me, but I will say it depends on the day. I don't feel weird or jittery.

I drink it black, but have tried it with cream. All good!

I have not consumed many of these--yet-- because the weather is still hot and humid, but the second it cools off I will be getting out all my fall flavors, buying bags of candy for all the trick or treaters we will never ever get (good), and decorations, hoodies, and "taking a stroll through the cemetery with a hot cup of pumpkin coffee while kicking leaves" . I have my plans. This coffee is part of it.

Oh, and I see that this company is in my state of NY. Neat!

title: Fun, fresh assortment, definitely spicy, lots of sour, not as much sweet
text:
What a mix! Seems like a really fun pack to give someone if they are into trying candies from a around the world, and are interested in a big pack of candies from Mexico. This assortment of candies come in a pressure zip bag individually wrapped in individual manufacturers packaging. Lots of color and fun sorting through these candies. The visual aspect is quite engaging.

Everything seems fresh and well packaged. All the candies I have tried so far have been intact and fresh.

For me, the candies have been fun to try, but many of the flavors and textures are really not for me. I was hoping for more nuance in flavors. I can have one on occasion, but not binge on them like I would some candy. I guess that can be a good thing, haha. It kind of feels like and tastes like the same candy over and over- many of flavor profiles are the same. HOT, SOUR, and a little sweet. I have really liked a couple, but the rest seem nearly the same to me. The emphasis seems to be on hot and sour. The sweetness or other flavors (like watermelon) just don't have a chance to come through. Yet on the Skwinkles was awesome. It likely all comes down to my own taste buds and preferences.

The positive experience has been in the trying something new, and it is neat to be able to try something I wouldn't otherwise find in NY.

title: ACV shots are exactly as they should be- not greatly watered down nor sweetened
text:
The real deal- it is ACV. It tastes like something I have made at home, but it is done for me and packaged to easily take it on the go. I have been drinking this straight from the bottle, but if I wanted a more mellow flavor, then adding it to ice cold water would do the trick.

I was pleasantly surprised to taste it and realize that it was indeed ACV, and not something super watered down, or pumped up with sugar or apple juice. It is as pleasant (or not pleasant, lol) as you would expect. And I thank RW Knudsen for keeping it real. No junk. Just that tang of ACV, followed by some heat from pepper, ginger, and cayenne. The turmeric is very light. I tend to use a heavy hand when I make similar concoctions. But it all goes together, and it tastes fresh and how it should.

Filtered water, organic apple cider vinegar, organic ginger juice, organic black pepper, organic turmeric powder and organic cayenne pepper

title: Versatile! Not just for Horchata drinks! Works so well with other drinks, foods, desserts
text:
It is for the most part what I think of when it comes to "Horchata". The base is sweet and creamy. Has a vanilla and very light cinnamon flavor. I think the cinnamon may be the aspect that could be off for some people-- all depends on what you have had in the past. For me, it is an occasional indulgence when out eating somewhere that might have it on the menu. So for at home.. I think this light creamy, vanilla and cinnamon flavor makes for a pleasant Horchata drink. Or Rum-chata. The base is quite sweet, so really no need to add anything to it. Maybe a little sprinkle of cinnamon for garnish. Give it some extra stirring or time to dissolve. Maybe run it through a blender to give it some froth.

Now while it is marketed for use in making Horchata, I have been using it in all sorts of ways!

--Coffee creamer, tea flavor- take a little extra oomph to stir it into coffee, but it eventually blends well and makes for a sweet creamy vanilla-cinnamon creamer. Or can stir some in with your plain creamer of choice, get it really well blended, then just pour into your coffee or tea. OR make a quick iced coffee using instant coffee, a mason jar, ice, "milk" of choice, and a couple spoonfuls of this to taste. Shake it all together, add a straw and enjoy.

--As a flavoring in oat meal, or steel cut oats. A little sweet, a little vanilla, a little cinnamon

--As a flavoring for HOMEMADE ice cream. Oh, this was my first thought when I was trying this out. I had been planning to make some vanilla ice cream in my Amazon Basics ice cream maker, and it occurred to me to add in this powder as part of the sugar component. I have to play around with it with future attempts to get the right ratio of flavor and sweetness, but it totally works. REALLY WELL.
https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B07VVQ7XH4/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp

--Now with fall upon us, that means fall flavors like pumpkin, chai, cinnamon.. and really this Horchata mix can be used along side these wonderful fall flavors. May use this as a base and blend in some pumpkin flavor (pumpkin coffee with this as a creamer? ooh!) or puree, or add a little added chai flavor to this, as well as a tea bag for chai tea with a twist. Or maybe some turmeric, ginger and this as the basic of the drink. So many options!

I ordered the pack of 6 and received the pack of six. One bag makes 27 twelve ounce servings (when using 2TBS per serving).

Kinda hemmed and hawed over the rating. My only issue with it is that it isn't a super instant easy blend. I mix in a little at a time and stir vigorously, so I do get it blended together. 4.5 stars if I could. However, the fact that I can use it in so many applications has boosted it to a 5. And everyone that has tried it has liked it.

title: salty, spicy (but not too hot), cheesy, well balanced mix of ingredients
text:
YUM!!!!
Mix of roasted and salted peanuts, together with almonds, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, hot and spicy nuts, nacho corn sticks, BBQ corn sticks, jalapeno cheddar sticks, and jalapeno pretzels. SO GOOD.

1st, these are fresh. My bag was acquired August 2020, it has a "best by" date of May 2021. Everything tastes fresh! EVERYTHING.

2nd, well balanced mix- no single item is over represented. BUT, I imagine that could very from batch to batch AND personal preference..

3rd. I WOULD buy these again. Pricey for a pub mix, but it is the only one so far that I really like. So maybe once in a great while I would treat myself to this. Definitely could make for a nice add on to a themed gift, or care package.

Truly, one of the few "pub mixes" that actually have a great balance of ingredients and textures that work together. I normally don't buy stuff like this for myself because I end up picking out just what I like (usually I eat all the sesame sticks). I normally don't care for a nut heavy mix, or too many boring pretzels (more on the pretzles used here later). I got this with my husband in mind because he tends to go for stuff like this (spicy, salty). But,... I really like it!

So I let him give it the first try. He had been eyeballing it for a few days, but it was when I made clear that "this bag is for you" (he had no idea where it came from, or that I was reviewing it for Vine), he immediately took off with them. A little while later, and with half the bag missing he came up to me and said, "these are really good. Have some".

So I did. And I agree. The flavor is spicy- flavorful- but not "HOT". I can tell there is some light heat, but most of the spice is that it is flavorful. Not just salty. It is delightful. It is indeed spicy. I expect a pub mix to be salty. Must grab a drink- grab a beer, and nosh on these. Portion some out or it would be real easy to eat all of these.

There are 17, 1/3 cup servings. 200 calories, 320 mg sodium. So try not to eat it all in one session.

Again, I find that it has a really good balance of ingredients. It isn't all nuts, or seeds or boring pretzels. I am not usually a fan of pretzels but these use those larger chunk pretzels (but small chunks in this mix) that have a lot of flavor and aren't too hard on the teeth despite usually being called a hard pretzel. I think the flavorings take the edge off. I actually find myself picking those out to eat, and could easily eat a bag of the just the pretzels they use in this. SO GOOD.

title: big ole box of generously flavored cinnamon coffee, medium roast, smooth
text:
Not much info on this product, and even less so on the packaging. You get a big box filled with loose K-cups. 96 of them! You must like cinnamon to really enjoy these.

Big box of medium roast coffee generously flavored with cinnamon. You may have a craving for cinnamon rolls after smelling this. Smooth and easy to drink. Big Texas flavor! I'm a dark roast/no flavoring type of gal, and this is (thankfully) pretty good! I have had it hot, over ice, black, and with cream. All good! Good enough to add it into my varied selections I have tucked away in a kitchen drawer.

I bet the more creative among us can come up with some neat creamer and/or food pairings.

This won't be my daily go-to coffee, but for a flavored coffee it is rather delightful. I appreciate the natural spicy taste. It doesn't have a weird off flavor that some favored coffees can have. Good thing, because 96 k-cups loose in a box is a whole lot of coffee. ha!

title: smells great in bag, fresh, is on lighter side of dark roast spectrum, slight acidity finish
text:
This bag of course ground dark roast coffee smells amazing. I love taking a whiff and savoring that coffee aroma.

I proceeded to prepare it as directed on bag 2:1 GRAMS of coffee to OUNCES of water, which ended up being about equivalent to 3/4 cup coarsely ground coffee to every four cups of cold water. Here it says 1:2 ratio of water to coffee, or whatever works for our own taste. I made it according to directions so I could determine future ratios.

Their ratio makes a standard cold brewed coffee. I doesn't need to be watered down, but it doesn't stand up well to melting ice cubes or creamers. I usually drink it black with lots of ice, and it didn't taste as special as I thought it would. I think my next batch will use more coffee or less water. I will need a higher coffee to water ratio to get a real cold brew concentrate. I like the overall strength of flavor, but it has a slight acidic-bitter edge. Usually what i make is much darker and smoother. By nature of the cold brew method, there should be no bite of acidity or bitterness. It is the one brew method where you can take an otherwise bad coffee and turn it into something good. I often use up old coffee or coffee I didn't care for hot in cold brew preparations.

As for "dark roast", it is on the lighter side of the dark roast spectrum. Leans a dark medium. The course ground is reddish in color. But, it does smell really good. Worth it to huff the bag, haha

A lot of this comes down to personal preference. You will get a fresh bag of course ground coffee, but if you are aiming for a deep dark roast this doesn't get there.

title: Citrus Ginger is lightly sweet, fizzy, base of barley malt, 70 mg caffeine
text:
I was supposed to receive Cherry Rhubarb, but instead received Citrus Ginger. So this review is for the Citrus Ginger (although it may be listed as Cherry Rhubarb).

I don't care for redbull/monster style energy drinks. They have a lot of off flavors that keep me from enjoying it. I will drink them if I just really need a boost yet don't want a hot coffee. So some of the newer generation of energy drinks have been paired down to fizzy water, flavoring, and some source of caffeine. THIS is what I am going for, and that is what THIS BRWD energy drink has going for it. Neither style is a wrong option, they are just different options. And so just know what you like and then look for it.

Unlike any of the energy drinks I have tried over the years this is the first to incorporate barley malt. "Barley is a natural grain rich in vitamins, anti-oxidants and protein necessary for recovery". The barley taste may be off putting to some.

The flavor? subtle, lightly sweet. "Only natural sugars from cane, barley and juice extracts are used".
Nice carbonation (MUST be carbonated, and I wasn't sure if this had fizz or not-- it does!). I can taste a foundation of barely malt with citrus top notes. The ginger is not as evident. I am a big fan of ginger, so I am a little disappointed that I can't quite pick up on that. Your taste buds may be different.

I like it super cold, over ice. Or even direct from can. Just depends on whether I am drinking it at home or on the go.

70 mg of caffeine from green coffee beans. No crazy boost of caffeine, but it just provide a gentle "pick me up". I like that there are no jitters or racing heart. This is what I need. Sometimes the other, older brands have way too much caffeine for me, so I aim to keep an energy drink at 100mg or less per can. This fits my needs.

Pretty basic ingredients: water, malt barley extract, cane sugar, lemon juice concentrate, natural flavors, caffeine

I'm not in love with this, but overall it is pretty good. I will enjoy the remainder of my cans before deciding whether to buy more. The $18 price is realistic, and keeping it around that price point may very well persuade me to keep some stocked in my drink fridge. Hopefully the correct flavor comes ;)

4/4.5 stars

title: outstanding! sweet, dessert like waffles w/ great mouth feel & are gluten free
text:
This makes for delicious waffles. Good thing they take some planning, because I could easily eat these any time.

Making the dough doesn't take long. I started off making the recipe for 9 waffles, then decided to go for the full 18 (so used 1 full bag). The items needed to make 9 waffles include using 3.5 cups of the waffle pre-mix, 1 stick of softened butter, 1 egg, 1 cup of hot water, and a packet of yeast (which is included!). Mix well. Then cover and let sit for 2-3 hours. There are then instructions to fold in some sugar pearls (included) and let sit for another 10-15 minutes. There are also instructions to divvy up the recipe by 9. (maybe this is when the 10-15 rest time comes in, I don't recall). I skipped the additional wait time and skipped dividing the dough. I went straight for the waffle maker, which make 4 square waffles at a time.
I had doubled all the ingredients so I could make "18" waffles. Using my waffle maker, we made 12 giant waffles.

OH MY. They turned out amazing. They were soft and cakey, but not spongy or dense. They had a great mouth feel. They got a nice sugary crust, and was so sweet that we did not use syrup. I usually use a lot of syrup with pancakes and waffles, and there was no way I wanted syrup with these. I ate one with some butter, and while it was good even that wasn't necessasry. They ate like almost like a cookie. When paired with bacon and eggs, all the sweet, salty and savory balanced each other out.

By the way, they are gluten free. I didn't even get this for that purpose. I'd recommend this to gluten free friends and family, but also for ANYONE.

So tasty!

We usually use a box mix where we just add water and pour it into the waffle maker. This is a dough. As it rises it becomes rather thick- spreadable but not pourable (hence being able to divide it into 9 balls). While the other is ok enough, these are really much much better. Basically what a Belgium waffle should really be like. If you wanted it less (or more!) sweet, the amount of sugar pearls can be adjusted to taste. I must say, I think the sweetness is what really makes it. Tastes like dessert. I think...forget the syrup and eat them plain (or with some butter) or even maybe try some jam or peanut butter spread onto it.

I must point out that the packaging is quite nice. The waffle mix is in a resealable bag that comes in another bag, Both have the instructions printed on it. The sugar pearls are in a resealable bag, and it happens to have a recipe for making waffles if you don't have the waffle mix on hand. The yeast packets are just basic packets. They are unlabeled, and really should/could be.

This kit came with 2 bags of waffle mix (I used one full bag to make the "18" waffles), and a portion of 1 of the 2 bags of sugar pearls. I used 2 out of the 4 yeast packets (since I doubled the recipe).

I really enjoyed this, and despite the time (was making it for dinner, so just needed to get it started 2-3 hours in advance) the prep time was short, as was the actual waffle making. And they were delicious.

title: tasty, nutty, fluffy couscous dupe
text:
I I don't have dietary restrictions, and so I selected this Shipetaukin Fonio for Couscous as I was curious to try something new. It sounded interesting and since I am a fan of all grains, I figured it would be pretty good. It is!

Cooks up like most grains- a 2:1 ratio of water to product. It is parcooked, and doesn't take long to cook on the stove. It cooks up fluffy and delicious-- just like couscous. I go through a lot of couscous and other grains in the cooler months- all the soups, stews, and other "bowls" I make. Really more of a cold weather food. Right now it is how, but I have used it as a base for a couple of "bowls" (scratch chicken fajita with this couscous and beans, and a spicy crumbled sausage with orzo, but added in this couscous for added texture, flavor, and protein).

If I keep loving it, then I may very well add this as a pantry staple. I really like the idea of a lower glycemic rating.

Fonio helps keep you feeling fuller longer with higher protein and a diabetic-friendly low glycemic index

title: best cold, great made into ice cubes, or used as base to various drinks, add to soups, etc
text:
I've never been one to actually enjoy a cup of coconut water- coconut everything else, yes.. but water.. oof. But I understand and appreciate the amazing hydration qualities it has. I keep shelf stable containers on hand for a myriad of reasons:
--add it to a smoothie
--add it to my water
--made ice cubes with it and add it to my water or other drinks
--use it as a base for refreshing drinks (club soda, coconut water, generous squeeze of lime, splash of pomegranate, or tart cherry, or blackberry concentrate)
--I rarely use it in cooking, but it could be added into something.

Coconut water doesn't have a coconut taste or smell. I can't describe it, but I have been drinking it long enough that it is a special taste that takes some getting used to. Not bad, just not Yum. For purpose of review I have primarily consumed this directly from bottle. This Coconut water by Rica is about what I expected, and I think it is perfectly fine. These are 11.2 ounce shelf stable containers.

Naturally a little sweet, there are 2 grams of added natural fruit sugar for 14 grams total, as well as some added potassium (619 mg 15% DV). Had 20 mg of sodium, and 70 calories. One 11.2 ounce bottle is one serving. Twist off cap. Definitely best COLD.

title: Half Caff- nice, dark roast to drink all day and not feel jittery
text:
Dark, smooth, bold roast with half the caffeine.

Most days I have one, but no more than two cups of coffee. I want more, but my blood pressure tells me otherwise. Sometimes I'll switch to decaff if I want to keep drinking cofffee (there is something to be said about the routine, not just a source of caffeine), but splitting the difference and being able to make a pot of coffee and drink what I want of it? yes!

This is full flavor, dark roasted half caff. I still get a caffeine kick but can drink more of it and not feel jittery or unwell. I appreciate the smooth, bold flavor, and it has been a good one for me to brew up especially when I am in the mood to drink coffee all day. I dont pick up on any hazelnut, which is good since I dont care for that flavor profile in my coffee. I just know that I like this, will continue to drink it, would recommend it, and very likely will buy again.

As with their other Coffeeland varieties, this is well packaged, the beans are fresh, smell great, and have a roasting date on the bag.

title: lightly sweet bubbly drink, refreshing and easy to drink
text:
I like it. I could drink it all day, but since it contains caffeine, I limit myself to one as I normally already had an actual cup of coffee to start my day. What I really like about it is its nearly neutral flavor. A hint of flavor and mild sweetness in a carbonated base. THIS is what I like, and this is what I go for in some of my drinks. So it is perfect for me.

I drink it cold direct from can, direct from the fridge. It is BUBBLY, which I love. I often drink plain club soda because I love carbonation so much. Sometimes I add in a splash of concentrated tart cherry juice or concentrated black berry juice.-- which adds a hint of flavor and not much sweetness. I don't care for sweet drinks, so that works for me. I normally don't care for "energy" drinks because they usually contain something that either makes it too sweet and/or too fake/weird tasting. I didn't know what to expect from this, so I was quite pleased when my first sip nearly reminded me of my club soda and black berry concentrate mix. LOVE IT.

To me, it tastes light and refreshing, a barely there taste with a barely there sweetness. I can taste a little undertone of something else- like a tea flavor (I assume it is the coffee fruit "fruity pulp of the coffee plant"). It just has carbonation with coffee fruit, cane sugar, blackberry juice concentrate, lemon juice concentrate, citric acid, caffeine. No, it does not taste at all like coffee.

Contains:
8% juice
100 mg of caffeine
45 calories in 1 can
12 grams sugar (5 added)

"Cold brewed from the fruit of the coffee plant — cascara is the naturally sweet, naturally caffeinated, nutrient-rich pulp that surrounds the coffee bean until harvest. The flavor profile is bright and bubbly, flavored with natural blackberry fruit juice."

title: strong, smooth, bold gorgeous dark roast w/ a valuable mission
text:
"OUR MISSION: Veteran Roasters is dedicated to roasting great coffee to give homeless and unemployed veterans a place to work and regain their lives. They were on the ground for us, buy some grounds for them. VETERAN OWNED: Veteran Roasters is 100% veteran owned. We help veterans who struggle to truly return home. We hire homeless and unemployed veterans, provide skilled training along with a livable wage."

I can appreciate this, and it makes the price a little easier to justify. Cheers!

I love dark roasts. I crave dark, bold, strong, meaty coffee. There is just something about a coffee that is as dark as the night. This Night Ops Dark Roast had me excited for my morning cups of coffee. I drink my coffee black. Sometimes I get a little desire for cream. This holds up well with the addition of cream. But if you can, please enjoy this black. Mmmm.

Kinda funny, I don't describe coffee well- the notes allude me. I tend to like the coffee or not. I have a bias toward dark coffee but can be objective when testing other roasts and regions. What makes me chuckle is that when I catch a whiff of the beans in the bag, I am reminded of the scent from an open can of beef stew or beef soup. Doesn't taste that way, just something I pick up on. So it manages to make me hungry as I grind the beans.

As a gorgeous, deep, strong, chewy, dark roast I will highly consider this again. I have been enjoying this a lot, and I am putting Veteran Roasters on my list for purchase toward upcoming holiday gift giving.

title: super fresh medium roast with robust flavor
text:
Fresh!!! (despite receiving it in August with an April roasting date)
Bag is packed tight- there is no air. Makes for some fresh whole beans ready to be ground.

A sticker on the bag lets me know when it was roasted. I like that.

This is a MEDIUM roast, that leans a little bold. Depending on how course or fine you grind you beans, can be stronger or more bitter. But with a little finagling it has a great overall flavor. Definitely has a presence. I usually enjoy a much darker roast, but since I know this is a medium roast I can say that it is exactly that. Medium roasts have quite a spectrum- can lean light,be centered, or lean dark. I think this one edges just a little toward dark. I can tell it is a medium roast.

Has rich flavor that can be consumed black, or holds up to ice and/or cream if you prefer.

I haven't tried it as a cold brew, but that is next on my list.

I would recommend this to those who enjoy a robust medium roast. I may not purchase this one again for me, but I would/will definitely purchase Coffeeland coffee again. I spy a dark roast that needs to be added to my cart :) Their product is fresh and well packaged. Love this!

title: refined coconut oil and avocado oil blend, liquid at room temp, buttery taste
text:
It's funny how this piqued my interest. It is new in that is labeled as a vegan "ghee", but Nutiva has had a very similar product out for many years that is just refined coconut oil with vegan butter flavor. This is nearly the same but with the addition of avocado oil. It isn't a slight. They are both really good, and about the same price per ounce. But its really more marketing.

This 29 fl ounce size is in a non-BPA plastic container.
USDA Organic ingredients, non-gmo verified.
Product of Phillipines and Mexico (coconuts and avocados, respectively)

I really like this stuff- either product, but I am really enjoying the refined coconut oil and avocado oil blend. The "vegan butter flavor" is a mystery. Probably same stuff in movie theater popcorn butter? Just kidding. Here is what Nutiva has to say,

"What is Organic Vegan Buttery Flavor? Our vegan buttery flavor in our Buttery Coconut Oil is made from pure certified organic non-GMO plants including sunflower, coconut, and mint. The buttery flavor does not contain any legumes, soy, corn, or corn derivatives. The product is free from peanut products, tree nuts, sesame seeds, dairy products, eggs, fish, shellfish, soy products, wheat, sulfites, and gluten. Our Buttery Coconut Oil also does not contain alliums (onions, garlic, leeks, chives, shallots)." So it doesn't explicitly say GHEE, but this is a very new product, and I imagine it is identical or nearly so.

Vegan Ghee Ingredients:
ORGANIC REFINED EXPELLER-PRESSED COCONUT OIL*
ORGANIC AVOCADO OIL,
ORGANIC VEGAN GHEE FLAVOR, (see above)
ORGANIC TURMERIC EXTRACT,
ORGANIC ANNATTO EXTRACT (FOR COLOR).

*Organic Refined Expeller-Pressed Coconut Oil. All the benefits of coconut oil, minus the coconut taste. This coconut oil is steam refined, no chemicals are used.

I concur with what others have mentioned.. it reminds me of popcorn butter. I think it is really quite good. It is as expected or better. It is shelf stable. Depending on the temp of your storage area as well as the texture you prefer for it to be in, it may be semi solid, or pure liquid. Coconut oil begins to soften at 76*F, so current summer temps leave it as a liquid when sitting out, but turns almost hard when set in the fridge. I say almost hard because this contains avocado oil, and it does not turn rock hard like plain coconut oil does when it is cold. It firms up just not as..hard. So it is still spreadable if placed in fridge. While this is pure liquid at room temp (76+), the other stuff buttery coconut oil is still a spreadable solid. So I am keeping mine in fridge as I like to spread it rather than use it as an oil right now.

I love that it can be used for anything. I am NOT vegan, I am not even vegetarian, I just eat... everything. I don't need to use real "ghee" (though I have some). Vegan ghee doesn't have same depth, but it is good as a replacement, or if you simply like stuff like this type of stuff (like me!). I find this to be more than adequate and it has the added benefit of being plant based and taste nice on toasted bagels. If I ate popcorn, this would be amazing on it. I do prefer it for cooking as I have other spreads I prefer to use for my toast, but this works too.

Tasty enough to eat off spoon, or blend into coffee.

It whips up a little it you run a hand held blender through it. Makes for nice frosting, or simply as a whipped "butter".

Acquired in August 2020, it has a "best before" date of January 2022. From my experience with their "coconut oil with buttery flavor", it doesn't go bad (I know this because I forgot I had/have an open jar tucked away that I forgot about until I tried this Ghee. I was like, I have had this before.. and sure enough it is very similar to their buttery coconut oil).

Good stuff. Enjoy!

title: a medium blend so smooth and balanced, it is a coffee for everyone
text:
Smooth with no hint of bitterness or acidity. A balanced, mild body. The initial sip is mellow and breathes out (and builds up) to an "even" coffee taste. It does well on its own (black) and can handle cream (still maintains flavor nuances). I have only consumed it hot, straight from the pot. I tend to prefer a dark, bold roast. I know this is a MEDIUM roast and am rating based on that. So I certainly enjoy a good medium roast so long as it isn't bright or bitter, or leans to light. I definitely like when it leans dark :) But this is so in the middle, it is an excellent example of what a medium roasted coffee can and should be. This is just a really nice coffee tasting coffee.

Has the fresh, rich aroma directly from bag. Mmm!

As a brew, it looks, smells, and tastes like the medium roast that it claims to be.

It is a coffee for everyone.

title: slightly off taste, very sweet, does go nicely with strong bold coffee
text:
I like them, but I don't love them. I like them well enough to eat them all up, maybe binge them.. but not enough to want to order more.

I like that:
--they are well packaged. There are two cookies in a mylar pack, 4 packs per box for 8 cookies
--they have a soft, gently chewy texture.
--definitely has a "birthday cake" taste. This is good or bad depending on your taste buds
--fresh; nothing stale about these.
--sweet if you like super sweet
--pairs extremely well with a bold, dark cup of coffee.
--I always bake with butter, so I am pleased to see actual butter listed

I don't like:
--"birthday cake" flavoring in cookies, ice cream etc can be kind of weird. This has that vanilla and "something else" flavor that I can't quite pin down.. but it is definitely reminiscent of anything that is worded as "birthday cake".
--not just a vanilla flavor (see above), not exactly what I would consider a "sugar cookie"-- if they were closer to that in taste, then I would be loving these.
--so soft that they nearly fall apart taking out of package. Since I am usually sitting at my desk with a cup of coffee when I eat these, I am not worried about pieces falling apart.
--I like sweet foods, I eat all sorts of stuff, and these are pretty much sweet first, then vanilla-esque, with a punch of "birthday cake" flavor.

Once I began eating them with a strong, bold, dark cup of coffee I could enjoy them a whole lot more. Definitely won't be my go-to dessert item, which is crazy because I love sweet sweet sugar cookies.

title: delicious chewy balls of happiness and joy, 1 serving veg per pouch
text:
MadeGood? More like MAD GOOD. These little bags of chewy granola are great. It is so hit or miss (more miss) for me when it comes to a granola that I actually enjoy eating. Often its "just there".

This is a 2 flavor variety pack, and the first flavor I tried was the Mixed Berry. This one is my favorite. I love the punch of sweetness and the soft but chewy texture. It speaks to me.

The chocolate chip is good too. As with the berry, it is natural tasting. They lean a little more dense but equally tasty and with a great mouth feel. I tend to prefer the fruit over the chocolate in general, but I have no issue with this flavor profile.

They are just little balls, about the size of a marble packed in a bag that is sure to keep these fresh for a long time. Easy to eat, just pop one in the mouth.

Good flavor, good texture, good amount of sweet, definitely natural tasting- tastes like something you could make at home. Not too much in a bag, yet just enough to feel satisfied. Great paired with some other healthy goodies. If you really wanted a crumble style, I imagine you could work these enough to sprinkle over yogurt.

Did you know they include vegetable extracts?
"A full serving of vegetables sneaks into every yummy individual package (yes, even the chocolate ones!). Six hidden veggie extracts harmonize with gluten-free oats and berry/chocolate pieces. "

free of the top allergens including nuts, gluten, and dairy.

title: lots of healthy fat, great as a supplement or for use in drizzling over foods
text:
Tastes like a liquid version of the hemp seeds I add to salad. Slightly nutty.

I find that I like to just take a small swig from the bottle, or use a spoon. I am not a total barbarian :)
I am the only one using it, and I want to make sure that I consuming this regularly. I considered cooking with it or drizzling it onto finished foods.. but have just been treating it like a supplement like I would with a bottle of fish oil.

"3:1 HEALTHY FAT RATIO – the organic hemp oil has the perfect 3:1 ratio of essential Omega 6 fatty acids to Omega 3 fatty acids and contains 6x more healthy fat than avocados, 40x more than coconut oil."

Seriously, if you want to use it as a supplement, it is easy so easy to take. It is very mild. I think among all my oils it it is is closes to an avocado oil. Not much in the way of flavor, hint of nuttiness. It is pleasant overall.

title: soft, chewy, dried apples & mango formed into shape of a bar
text:
It is JUST apples and mango (they have other varieties). "That's It" !!

Think of dried apples. If you have had them you know they are soft, chewy and taste like.. apples. Dried pieces of mango are nearly identical, usually a little firmer. More subtle taste. This is a combination of the two but formed into a thin rectangular chewy bar. A few bites and you are done. Not as thin as a fruit leather, but along that idea. You get a burst of sweetness without added sugar. Just 60 calories.

Dried mango has a subtle taste, so unless you have discerning taste buds you make not pick up on it. Apple dominates both in taste and it is first on the ingredient list (of just two ingredients- so I guess it could be 50/50 of each?). But I can taste the balance, and I am loving these so much.

It makes for a nice quick snack item. Or for those times you want a little something sweet but don't want to grab a donut. It often serves me well as part of a light lunch/breakfast on the go. I usually carry a few snack bars and this is just extra easy as it wont get smashed down or crumble. My go to food item on my way out the door as of late is my coffee, a a pack of Belvita, and one of these bars.

Lovely taste, lovely texture.. Makes my mouth happy.

It is boxed like a gift. There is an image of a big bow printed on the box.

title: fluffy, tasty seasoned "rice" with gentle flavoring and heat
text:
In short: a very easy, very quick to make fluffy, rice-esque side dish. It is tasty, it has a good mouth feel, and it eats well on its own or when paired with other foods and spices. I think it is worth trying. Way less sodium than many seasoned boxed rice/side dishes.

I eat everything and will try anything. I have no dietary restrictions, and just enjoy food of all sorts. I love flavor, texture, and anything that simply allows me to enjoy a meal.

I am LOVING this RightRice with Thai curry seasoning. The texture is perfect. The rice does not stick together, it is not at all gummy, it is fluffy and flavorful. I made it EXACTLY according to directions, and it came out PERFECTLY.

It has some very mild Thai flavoring, that could be amped up with additional seasoning, or simply consumed as is. If you are looking for a strong curry flavor profile, then you may not like it. It is just subtle. I do love curry and other Thai flavors, so I'm kind of in the middle on the seasoning. However, I really like the flavor as a rice seasoned with: garlic, chilipepper, parsley, turmeric, lemongrass, garlic oil. I can use it in soups, as side dish, as a main dish, I can add seasonings and complimentary sauces, or I can just eat it plain directly from pan.

There is some noticeable, building heat. I don't go for HOT, but I don't mind "WARM" spicy. This is more warm- doable for the non super spicy folks. It is flavorful enough to eat on its own if you just needed something quick and didn't have anything to add to it.

It is salty, but I like it. You may not. Less salty tasting than some pre-flavored boxed rices/side dishes. I imagine the plain has a lot less. This won't leave me dying of thirst. FOR REFERENCE, this has 390 mg of sodium per serving while boxed flavored rices(such as RiceA-Roni) have 750mg on up.

An entire bag makes a goodly amount of "rice". It contains 4, 1/3 cup dry servings. The directions include how to make an entire bag. I think the main aspect of this is making it correctly, and the directions are easy enough.

If making the whole bag (I do), then use 1 and 1/3 cups of water. Put water in a sauce pan, bring to a boil. Add contents of bag. Immediately take off heat and cover. Let sit for 12 minutes. Some back and fluff with a fork. Let sit for a couple more minutes. Light, fluffy, not sticky, non gummy, just nearly regular tasting rice dish. I would not think of it as a rice alternative (it does contain some rice).. the texture is very similar. I wouldn't know unless maybe I had them side by side. Dont really need to.

A lot of this is personal preference. I think it depends on what you are looking for and whether it meets your needs. I do think it is worth trying. Hard to imagine hating it outright. But who knows. I like it, I am considering another flavor.

$4 a bag- is that a lot? You decide. We all have different working budgets, so I rarely factor that into my rating.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
LENTIL FLOUR, CHICKPEA FLOUR, PEA FLOUR, RICE FLOUR, SUNFLOWER OIL, SEA SALT, SUGAR, VEGETABLE POWDERS (GARLIC, ONION), CHILI PEPPER, SPICES, PARSLEY, CITRIC ACID, MALIC ACID, TURMERIC EXTRACT (COLOR), SPICE EXTRACTIVES, LEMONGRASS EXTRACT, OIL OF GARLIC

Directions

Easy to cook in 12 minutes; To cook the entire pouch, add 1 & 1/3 cups of water to a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Add RightRice, return to a boil. Immediately remove from heat and cover. Let stand for 12 minutes. Fluff with a fork, let sit for 2-3 minutes and enjoy

title: raw, freeze dried black currant powder add antioxidants, fiber, and color to whatever you want
text:
I LOVE that this is made from WHOLE black currants- so that includes everything- skin, seeds, the fiber. All of it. NOTHING added to it. This is a whole food- raw and freeze dried-, and so you get all the benefits. While it is a powder, know that it won't fully dissolve, but if you wanted to stir some in water and drink it up quick, you can. Anything you can think of adding this to, you can. Sprinkle on something, stir into something, bake into something.. you get the idea. Even use it to color something with natural coloring.

--Black currants (Ribes nigrum) are HIGH IN antioxidants and vitamin C.
--6 oz (171 g) of organic black currant powder = 42.33 oz (1200 g) of fresh organic black currants.
--The pressure zip mylar bag is easy to open and close.
--each bag contains 21, 1 TBS servings
-- each 1 TBS serving contains 25 calories, 4 grams of fiber, 78 mg of Vitamin C, etc

Freeze dried whole currants make for a fresh and truly healthy food item to keep on hand. Because of the freshness that freeze drying imparts, and the extensive longevity (shelf life) of a freezed dried item, it would be great as part of an emergency supply kit, or just long term pantry item. You will get your vitamin C, and some tart/sweet taste, and beautiful color..

title: BEWARE: an open bag is an empty bag :)  cheesy, crunchy organic goodness YUM! YUM!
text:
This review is for the White Cheddar. I grabbed a bag and a drink then sat down at my computer to write some reviews. I thought, "maybe I should take a picture of these mini rice cakes", then next thing I know the bag is empty. I forgot to take a picture, and I didn't get much done. I think I just blanked out and gobbled these up.

So yeh, they are gooooood. Too good. If you like rice cakes, you'll like them, and if you aren't a fan of rice cakes, I bet you would like them. I think they are better than QuakerRiceCakes minis as this has a better crunch factor. The more you munch the more you can't stop. An open bag is an empty bag. If you need portion control by all means grab a little bowl, and save yourself from glutton. :)
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B084SVNHNC/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_dp

What makes them extra nice is that they are thin, so they are crunchy like popcorn (but chip shaped) rather than spongy like Styrofoam. I would still like them, but this texture is extra appealing. The salty, powdery cheddary flavor is just too good to put down. Just keep popping them in my mouth.. and like I said next thing i know the bag was empty.

Each bag is a good size-- like a chip bag you would grab off a store shelf. 5 ounces doesn't sound like much, but like chips, mini rice cakes aren't heavy. Plenty in a bag. And this is a set of 6..oh boy!

I'm pretty sure I shouldn't eat a whole bag at once. I'll try to restrain myself next time I open a bag.

I am already planning ahead and buying some more!

title: SO BAD. Smells & tastes like ACETONE- ie nail polish remover. Strong nasty
text:
Oh my.. this is sadly and almost comically terrible.

I have really open minded taste buds, I have tried things and thought whatever it was tasted ok where other people thought it was bad. Even if I think something doesn't taste great (some protein bars, protein powders, and some other supplements) I will still be able to gag them down. I'm a trooper.

There was one time I got a greens powder that had a hint of bile as a tasting note. But, I was able to power through it and make it work.

BUT THIS?

THIS IS the MOST WRETCHED thing I have ever tasted in my entire life. I am not being dramatic. WHAT IS THIS?
I dont see anything in the ingredient list that should create such an off taste and off scent.

It smells horrible, and it tastes just as bad. I tried. I tried again.. I. JUST. CAN'T.

I have had this one bar in a baggy, as I have tried it at different intervals over the past 2-3 days. Even tried "airing it out". texture seems nice, though. lol!

title: delicious, highly fragrant, appetite inducing scent, great product
text:
Of course this is Thai Hom Mali, that just means "Thai fragrant rice".. and jasmine rice is amazing. It is aromatic, and exquisite in flavor. If you have used Jasmine rice before, then you can expect a good quality rice at a fair price. If you are new to it, then be prepared to make this part of your staples.

While Jasmine rice is usually much pricier than a basic long grain rice, the flavor and scent is worth it. Especially if you are making anything with Thai flavors. There is such an amazing, rich, salivation inducing scent. Really takes a dish up a notch or so.

Seeds of Change is a really good brand. Occasionally I find some of their offerings in store or in warehouse club stores. Always good stuff. This is another really good product.

title: creamy with nice, super light/barely there vanilla flavor
text:
I eat what I eat and drink what I drink because I love food. I'm not vegan, keto, or anything but an inspired eater. I enjoy nut milks for drinking, baking, having over cereal. Not a fan of most of them for coffee as it always lends an odd flavor. For that I stick to heavy cream, half and half, oat milk, or go black. I make an exception for this Milkadamia Macadamia and Coconut creamer. It does impart a flavor, but it is subtle. I can tolerate it in my coffee. I tend to add a generous dose as I find it tastes better with more in it versus less (I most often drink my coffee black, so this is a big deal to add so much). Even the vanilla part of it is subtle. I happen to like that. IF you are looking for a strong vanilla (or other) flavor, this may not be what you are looking for.

By itself (I took a swig) it does taste like melted vanilla ice cream. Albeit light on the vanilla and no sugar.

Pricier than I normally go for, but macademia nuts are pricey. The formula is tasty, and I can see using it for a variety of uses. I like that it is shelf stable (until opened).

Pretty good overall. Definitely worth trying!

title: most excellent fat to add to kitchen pantry
text:
My new fat source for cooking, baking, searing, and whatever else I may need it for.

Shelf stable. In the current heat it is a glorious cream that melts beautifully over low heat and can withstand higher temps. I know if I stored it in the fridge it would firm up a lot. Silky smooth, neutral taste- though my dogs beg to differ. When I peeled off the protective wrapper, I didn't want any tallow that was clinging to the wrapper to be just thrown in the trash. So I made quick use of it as a hand lotion, and took a swipe down my legs. WELL, my dogs found me. LOL. So I think I will keep it strictly for my consumption.

By the way, it does a glorious job making home fries, and yes.. I took their recommendation to try it in a batch of brownies, and it was as decadent as I expected. Blows my mind that a simple switch from some oils (even butter in some applications) to this has made such a difference.

Throw out your vegetable oils. Use this. MMMmmmm.

I haven't done a lot with it, but I am so glad to have it in my pantry. As the heat dissipates I will be eager to cook, bake, etc again on a daily basis.

I'm already thinking ahead to christmas presents. Waygu tallow for everyone, haha!

title: super creamy, like whole milk but made from organic oats!
text:
I love this shelf stable Oatsome BARISTA non dairy creamer. I normally drink my coffee black, but sometimes I like a little cream (real cream, from cows). I will drink any non dairy product (almond, macadamia, cashew, coconut) as a "milk" but usually dont care for the taste of it in my coffee- always creates an odd/off flavor to me. I don't care for animal milk to just drink, but I do like it in my coffee (hence the half and half or heavy cream). I hadn't tried OAT MILK in my coffee, so I figured trying this Oatsome brand was a good time to do so.

IT. IS. AWESOME.

It is the most "cream" like of all that I have ever tried. It doesn't water my coffee down and even by itself it looks and has the mouth feel of creamy milk. A mere hint of something.. yet the taste is rather neutral, pleasant.

1 cup is considered a serving, so the nutritional stats are based on that. I just pour in whatever I want into my coffee. I have yet to sit down with it as a big ole cup of milk. Maybe when the weather cools and I am in the mood to bake some cookies. MMMmmm. or I could buy their regular oatsome milk as "milk", and it happens to have a few less calories.

I also like the Barista variety froths nicely. Sometimes I just shake the heck out of a container to get it to form foam, and sometimes I put a little into a cup and run my frother through it. Satisfying to look at, and satisfying to drink. YUM!

The fact that it is shelf stable (until opened, of course) means I can have a few bottles tucked away in the cupboard and not clogging up precious real estate in my fridge.

title: A bit of a dark flavor with the tang of salt and hint of heat
text:
Salt, brown sugar, cocoa, coffee, cayenne, and red pepper. (all organic)

It doesn't mention using this on chicken, but that is what I went with as that is what I had at the time. Next time I may add it to burgers or some cut of beef. I'll add that to my review when I do. As I was opening my bottle for the first time, I took a glance at the ingredients again. I pondered if it would make a nice spice to top off hot cocoa with (love cayenne and cocoa together), so I dipped my finger in the jar and then into my mouth. EGADS this stuff is SALTY. Ok, so we're not supposed to eat it plain, but I was trying to get a sense of the flavor profile. I should have paid more attention that salt is the first ingredient. That didnt stop me from generously dousing 2 boneless chicken breasts with this and then wrapping and placing in fridge until the next day.

Next day, I grilled these spice covered chicken breasts. They turned out really well- juicy and flavorful. BUT I couldn't tell you what flavors. It just tasted good.. and salty. Maybe I need more, or maybe beef or pork would pick up on the flavors. Maybe it isn't supposed to have an identifiable flavor. I could sense a little bit of heat, but not hot spicy.

I like it; I am not yet in love with it (I figure more trial and error is due). I know I can use this for some sort of flavor on my chicken, or whatever I go with. A bit of a dark flavor with the tang of salt, hint of heat. Interesting, and not anything I can really identify.

title: really good dark coffee, vague info on supplements, not sure if nearly enough
text:
Good coffee, but I think it would be better to just have a separate supplement so you know what you are getting.

I really like the flavor of this bold, smooth dark roast. It is delicious. I have thoroughly enjoyed every cup I have had. I don't taste anything else with it- no off flavors. I have had it black (my usual), and sometimes with a non dairy creamer. All good! I have consumed 1 (and sometimes 2) cups a day. I have one left.

Funny, I rather forgot that this was a supplement and every day this week I have been inordinately ravenous. Normally coffee staves off my appetite, and I don't think to eat. So rather surprising to me that I was feeling hungry earlier than normal and stronger than normal. No particular cravings, but crazy hungry. I am not usually THAT hungry. Coincidence that it happens to be when I started using this? Even if it were, I can definitely say that I have not experienced a reduction in cravings (and normally green tea leaf extract does that to me). Which makes me think there simply isn't enough supplement to be effective at 1-2 cups a day.

Other than a vague "45 mg of propriety herbal blend", I do not know how much of each component I am actually getting, nor are there instructions as to how much one should consume to be effective. In this instance, enjoy some (less expensive) coffee and take a separate supplement. This is too pricey, and too vague information/instruction to be something that I would recommend.

Middle of road 3 stars, as I think the coffee is really good, but the supplementation idea is bad. It is also super pricey for 10 k-cups (albeit really yummy coffee).

If I think of anything else, or if I have some additional revelation with the next (and last) cup of this coffee, I will be back to share.

title: make in mug for best mouth feel. super thin nearly crepe like texture, too thin SEE PICS!
text:
I'm not going to give these 1 star, as the convenience and on some level- the flavor gives it come merit.

However, these makes super thin, rubbery pancakes. So weird. If the could be just a little thicker, it would make for a better "mouth feel".

I made it THREE ways, following the three options on the packaging.

1. In a griddle. I added some butter, and then poured in enough to make 3-4" medallions. Despite the low temp (275*f) , the use of butter, and being in a non stick griddle, they wanted to glom onto the pan. They cook weird- there really is no fine crusting going on, or seeing the edges brown first. They just bubbled in center, yet wasn't flippable yet, and since they run so thin, there isn't much else for them to do. I could flip them and 3 of 4 held. But OH SO THIN.

2. In the microwave. Nearly same instruction, except use a dinner plate. I poured three, 3-4" medallions on the plate. Cooked in microwave according to directions 45 seconds. Mine needed 55 seconds. Microwaves vary. They turned out TERRIBAD this way. Maybe I needed to grease the plate first, but they stuck to it. It wasn't a matter of being underdone, or overdone.. they just fell apart. They are so thin!! The batter is too thin!!

3. Microwave in a mug. OK, this was kind of neat, and possibly redeemed this batter a little bit. Take a mug, fill it 1/3 of the way with the batter. Microwave 50-55 seconds (I used a small 8-10 ounce mug and it took 1min 20 seconds). The pancake managed to turn out a little "fluffy"-- well more spongey and a little rubbery, but at least there was enough mass to make it have a better mouth feel.

In ranking the method in how it turned out, I would go with #3, #1, and totally avoid #2.

Flavor wise? Not terrible. A bit sweet, didn't even need syrup. I think more fun could be had with the pancake in a mug option- use it as a base to make a dessert of the sort. Add some choco chips, or peanut butter powder, even protein powder.

Would I buy it again? No
Do I recommend it? No.. caveat- sending a care package to a college kid, need for convenience and the microwave mug option sounds appealing, maybe camping.. but really the mug option made best "pancake".

How could it be better? Somehow make the batter thicker or not spread out so thin. I wondered if working with a COLD BATTER would be better than a room temperature batter. Since there is no mention (that I noticed on bottle) about needing to go in fridge first, I just made it as is. It is a shelf stable product until opened, so I shouldn't HAVE to refrigerate it first. If that is the case, then it needs to be explicitly stated. I did put my bottle in the fridge after opening, but I haven't used it since. I will make a point to try making them again and I will come back to let you know if the pancakes cook up thicker (since the hypothesis is that the batter would pour out thicker, and not spread as quickly, possibly making a thicker, stable pancake). We'll see. Even if it turns out that way, my rating stays the same (because that info should be shared).

So in mean time, the end product is nearly as thin as a crepe. If you have egg rounds that get placed in a griddle, then maybe use that and fill it with this. I really dont know if that would work, but it really needs to be thicker. Maybe add in some extra baking soda? eh, I dont want to work that hard for a product that should make things easier.

Maybe you can make it work. This just isn't for me.

title: bright, zesty flavor plays well with any other spice; good one for beginners
text:
Yet another Sasinee seasoning that seriously whets my appetite. I love the gorgeous aromatic that is lime leaf powder, as well as the floral-citric flavor. A little piquant, a little lemony, a little limey, zesty, no heat, has a refreshing taste when used alone.

It is a fun spice to work with. It can add depth yet brighten things up. As a powder it mixes well into broths, creams, and curries. As a spice it is outstanding, but also has some health benefits.

My little packet of Kaffir Lime Leaf Powder arrived in tact and ready to go. It is in a pressure zip part mylar bag. Some spices and powders get caught up around the pressure zip area making it hard to get a good seal. My packet is still pretty new, so I haven't experienced that yet. But I imagine at some point I will put this in a container (reuse a glass spice container) or slip it into a ziplock baggy.

I have a premade wet spice blend for making green curries. Adding this into that flavor profile is AMAZING. It is one of those flavors that just add something special. If you are experimenting with new spices, this one is a great one to have on hand. It plays well with other spices, and like I mentioned it even does well on its own. A fun recipe to try is to roast some almonds (or cashews, or whatever) in the oven with a little oil, salt, and lime leaf powder. From there you could add in a little cumin to add depth and savory taste, or a little cayenne to give it heat (which pairs well with the tang of lime leaf), etc..

Lime leaf powder by nature of harvesting is pricey. This is about what I expect for a 2+ ounce size.

title: ORANGE CREAM is all but a dream- sadly NO flavor; just..MEH :(
text:
Where is the flavoring???? This review is for the ORANGE CREAM flavor by Zone Perfect.

I was so stoked to see this rarely seen flavor- usually it is vanilla or chocolate. Maybe an occasional berry. But ORANGE CREAM? never. I was looking forward to an ice cold creamy orange flavored protein shake. Immediately upon receiving these, I got out my mason jar, filled it with ice, and poured in the contents of one full 11 ounce container. Swirled it. Added a straw. It was a hot, humid day and I just got in from work. I needed a snack, and was really excited to take a swig. I expected it to be glorious. Orange cream should taste like the summer day it was.

*sigh*

*SIGH AGAIN*

If I didn't know what flavor it was supposed to be, I don't think I could figure it out. It is SO BLAND. Has a barely there indiscernible flavor. I like the smoothness, I like the creaminess, I like that it doesnt have a strong weird protein flavor.

BUT it doesn't really have ANY flavor, and certainly NOT orange cream.

TOTAL. LET. DOWN.

CLEARLY I am not a "giddy VineReviewer* yeesh, people have no clue. I dont care if money was directly spent or not (and we DO spend money), our reviews are as objective as others. Good and bad in all styles of reviewers.

EDIT to add, that I finally finished off this pack. It was never good. Just blah. WOuld have been so much better had it had actual orange creamsicle flavor.

It isn't gross, I can (and will) still drink this as is, I can drink it as a base for a smoothie, I can maybe even add it to my coffee, but it is not the taste experience I was anticipating. It did stave off my seemingly perpetual hunger. I want to give it 2 stars, but the serious lack of tasting like ORANGE CREAM is aggravating and unfair to those that may have been just as excited to enjoy this rarely seen flavor. If I could taste that flavor, I would have been "giddy". If I could taste the flavor, I would be keep it in stock.

I don't recommend it.
