title: dried galangal is a culinary game-changer. Lovely, easy, tummy growling delicious
text:
It never occurred to me to find DRIED Galangal (a ginger like root) for my Thai cooking needs. Usually for lack of galangal the next item to grab is ginger, either imparts a bit of spicy heat. But if you can get Galangal, please do so. I really love this in dry form. I always have some waste with fresh (despite putting ginger in freezer). I am totally sold on buying this forever more if it means I can just used a slice or two (or more) whenever I want to. YUM YUM!

Nice big thin slices in a pressure zip bag.

If you're looking to buy this, then you know what to do with it and how versatile it is. If you have a liquid based preparation, then this can just be tossed in. If it is a more dry preparation, then soften it up with a little hot water or broth. Add it to whatever you want. My picks are for use in simple broths, or any type of curry. Eat it if you grate it or slice it thin, use it for flavoring and toss it if you are adding it in for just flavor and/or visual use. I've tried to gnaw through big slices and it just doesn't work out, lol. But tiny slices (or grated) is fine. Once again, just like typical ginger.

I feel like a fancy cook with this.

Even writing this review has worked up an appetite.

title: mild, lightly figgy oil and balsamic vinegar combo- so many uses, yummy
text:
Oil and Balsamic Vinegar are two staples in my kitchen. This happens to be a mix of both, so be sure to shake that bottle vigorously prior to use.

The faint, but discernible fig flavor makes this multi purpose dressing great for salads, roasting vegetables, or anywhere you like using a savory balsamic vinegar. It is blended with non-gmo canola oil. It can be used alone or mixed in with another dressing. I had made chicken salad using the typical fare of mayonnaise as the creamy base. To give it a little punch of something extra, I stirred in a little bit of this fig balsamic vinegar. My next application was using it over salad, and then my favorite: drizzled copiously over roasted vegetables (carrots, onion, brussels sprouts, and mushrooms). My next venture will be to use it in an egg dish, perhaps a frittata. I've yet to use it as a marinade, but sure.. why not. Ooh my mushrooms are getting marinaded next time.

Seriously, if you love using balsamic vinegars, add this to your culinary options.

title: light, green, grassy flavor, Aquired taste, super fresh, LOVE the multiple small bags over 1 large
text:
It sure is an acquired taste, if you are new to Turkish brands of coffee (not just brewing style).

I want to say upfront that this is a light, maybe extra light roast. It is bright and grassy in flavor. It will throw you off if you have not had this level of roast in/for Turkish coffee. I have purchased other Turkish coffee brands before, and all that which I have tried smell and taste similar-- that odd green taste. What is that?I am so curious. I never see the roast level on Turkish brand coffee, so most of the time I buy whatever dark bean from whatever brand I like best and grind it to a powder (I have purchased grinders that can get this level of bean annihilation). That is the most important part is that it has a powder texture (think of a canister of baking cocoa)-- otherwise the coffee doesn't quite turn out for this style. End result needs to be thick and chewy :)

Otherwise, the freshness is great. I can greatly appreciate that this is a box of (10) 3.5 ounce bags of coffee. This keeps the coffee fresh, and allows you to enjoy is as you want if you happen to make it on rare occasions rather than daily. Brilliant! THANK YOU.
I tend to use too much rather than too little of ground coffee, I figure I can always water it down. My ibrik holds around 7 or 8 ounces of brewed coffee. I divvy up the contents between 2 small mugs, so I can enjoy the Turkish coffee making ritual and consumption. Sometimes I use cream, sugar, cardamom. Just depends on what I feel like. When served in a restuaruant, a small pot of water is also served along side the coffee so as to adjust the strength of taste. Normally all my other coffee consumption is black.

Does Turkish Munchies make a dark roast? I really love the box and bags. Also, the "fortune" telling is cute.

With my Ibrik for brewing, I followed the easy to read instruction card. I make Turkish coffee a few times a year, and always need a reminder on how much coffee to use, how to "brew" it. It is simple, but just takes patience and paying attention.

I much prefer dark coffee, so this brew isn't as delicious to me, but it doesn't mean its bad-- just know that it is a light roast. The powder is a light reddish brown, further showing the light roast. For me, a little cream mellows it out, takes down those green notes. Sometimes I add cardamom. MMMMmmmmMMmm

See my pics!

5 stars for quality product, great packaging, thoughtful clear instructions, adorable fortune telling card

title: cough drop sized candies in 3 fun flavors, amount of each will vary, not too strong/sweet
text:
Cheap little bag of hard candy with some neat flavors. Subtle flavoring- not too strong, not too sweet. Just a nice little something when you want something. The candy pieces are small but decent size to keep in mouth for a little while. Similar to size of a cough drop.

title: Collagen- great for convenience, ok for taste, creaminess, mouth feel, what are amounts??
text:
This review is for the unsweetened COLLAGEN creamer. Each 1/4 cup serving (4 TBS) provides:
-40 calories
-3.5 grams of fat (3.0 saturated)
-70 mg sodium
-1 gram carbohydrate (1 gram fiber, 0 sugar)
-2 grams of protein
127 mg calcium (10% dv)
183 mg potassium (4% dv)

There are 13 servings per container.

INGREDIENTS:
Cashew Milk (Water, Cashews), Coconut Cream (Coconut, Water), Grass-fed Collagen, MCT Oil (Medium Chain Triglycerides). *Contains 1.5% or less of Acacia Gum, Potassium Phosphate, Calcium Carbonate, Sunflower Lecithin, Sodium Citrate, Gellan Gum

I didn't see anywhere in the product description or the bottle how much MCT oil there is. According to PicNik, "There is roughly 1 TSP of MCT per 2oz serving. So roughly 16 tsp MCT oil per carton"
No idea how much collagen is in here.

Seems to be a decent product for a shelf stable item (until opened, then it needs to be refrigerated). I am not amazed by the taste or the lack of info about how much of the star ingredients are in it. If you are super keto or paleo and want the convenience of using a serving or two of this, then go for it. Overall, I think it's.. ok. Buy this for convenience. I likely wont use this again. It isn't terrible, it just isn't enough for me in terms of taste, mouth feel, and information (TELL PEOPLE how much MCT oil is in here in the description, as well as COLLAGEN powder)

There isn't much flavor or mouth feel when 1 full serving is added to 10 ounces of coffee. It doesn't add flavor (save for a hint of cow), but it also doesn't supremely water it down depending on roast level. Dark coffee is lightened up a bit and still imparts a coffee taste. Medium roast loses more of the coffee taste and takes on a hybrid creamer/coffee/cow flavor. Terrible in iced coffee. I find that it doesn't add that creaminess that actual creamer has- even though cashew milk is quite creamy and this contains gums that should provide a greater creamy mouth feel.

EDIT: while my opinion doesn't change on overall taste, I wanted to add that I have been adding it to my coffee after I shake the container A LOT. Crazy shaking! This makes it bubbly and frothy, which is amusing to see on my coffee. Looks fancy :)

When it comes to most applications, I tend to go non dairy (cashew, coconut, or almond) until it comes time to put creamer in a coffee. There I go black (sans coffee, sugar) or use real cream or half and half. Sometimes do the butter, coconut oil, collagen powder thing, if I want a "hot smoothie". I normally dont care for the taste that most nut milks impart in coffee. This is actually ok. I don't taste a radical change.

By itself- it is the collagen taste comes through- has that cow taste going on. I am glad it dissipates a bit once mixed into the coffee.

Acquired in July 2020, it has a best if used by date of October 7, 2020.

"keep refrigerated & use within 14 days after opening"

title: easy to drink medium roast that gives great flavor & energy w/ half the caffeine
text:
This review is for the Green Mountain Coffee HALF CAFF Keurig Single-Serve K Cup Pods, Medium Roast Coffee, 32 count

I'm not sure why the product description insists that this is hazelnut. It isn't. It is simply a well rounded medium roast with no additional flavoring.

It is quite good despite my preference for dark, bold varieties. I can drink this! I can even drink it without having first filled up on full caffeinated coffee. This is surprisingly energizing. Makes me want to find a half-caff in a dark roast, if that is possible. I had really cut down on my coffee/caffeine consumption, and at some point in day had switched to a decaff that is actually so good that I always double check to make sure it is decaff and not regular (i'm looking at you Green Mountain Dark Magic decaff). So this is nice too. Half the caffeine but can drink more if I want AND I can just go straight to drinking it in the morning as there is plenty of zip to be had by this brew.

It drinks well black, but occasionally I have added some creamer. My normal roast preference is dark, but this has a good flavor-- not tangy, not bitter, not acidic- just a mellow medium that is easy to drink, I think.

title: decent vanilla flavor, best cuper cold or in coffee, has that distinct whey protein taste
text:
I have the Iconic Kids Whey protein in Vanilla Vacay. The vanilla is pretty good. Best when it is super cold. Has that signature whey protein taste that kinda hits the taste buds at first, then mellows out. Not too sweet for me. Creamy.

I like it plain, directly from bottle or added into my coffee. I don't do creamer too often, but this is a nice way to boost my coffee. When I drink it plain, I am usually grabbing it on the run. Kinda nice to not have to get the blender out or the shaker bottle out. I have also had one prior to dinner, when I am hungry yet don't want to snack on anything. Just 80 calories staves off the hunger a bit longer. So it has its benefits to me, and adult.

8 grams protein

title: bag of medium roast ground coffee, not hazelnut
text:
The page needs to clean up the product description! This is for the Green Mountain HALF-CAFF medium roast ground coffee, 12 ounce bag. It is not hazelnut, it is not k-cups. The word "bagged" is in the description, and it is pictured as a bag.. so I figured I was getting a bag of coffee. BUT I wasn't totally confident. lol. I am actually really glad that it was NOT hazelnut as I prefer unflavored coffee.

5 stars for flavor, freshness, and the fact that I can drink A LOT more coffee and not have to be as concerned about the caffeine content. As a lover of dark roasts, I wasn't sure how this medium roast coffee would be. It is robust without being too tangy. Has a nice, strong coffee flavor but I brew it that way. "nutty and mellow" (but no, not a flavored coffee). It works well as an iced coffee. I just add more coffee and use less water. I drink it black with ice. Yum!

4 stars for being nearly a mystery item as to what would arrive.

title: robust medium roast that leans toward dark. Good coffee flavor plain or with cream
text:
This review is for VIVACE Medium Roast.

It makes for a robust brew. I would say it leas closer to the dark side of the roast spectrum. My preference is always dark roast, and occasionally I venture into medium roasts (and once in a great while, light). There seems to be quite a spectrum of flavor in the medium category. This is lively but not acidic. It tastes rich. I made it a little too strong in my NinjaCoffee Station, where I made a full pot where it recommends using 4-6 scoops of coffee. I did 5, and I think I would scale back to 4 next time. Made my mouth pucker a little- that probably is a touch of acidity that I picked up on. But, I added some creamer (normally I drink just black, no cream, no sugar) and it mellowed out.

Overall nice coffee flavor. I love trying new (to me) coffee, and this has been a pleasure to try. I imagine it will withstand being poured over ice which I will do next time I have it. While I probably won't order the Vivace medium roast again, I have put their Enzo dark roast in my cart. I figure if their medium roast is fairly bold, then their dark roast is probably gorgeous. Take my money! lol

title: smooth, rich, dark, bold, well balanced, easy to drink black/plain
text: Enzo dark roast is very smooth and balanced. It tastes great whether I brew it with 8 ounces, 10 ounces, or 14 ounces (8 +6) of water. I tend to go with a 10 ounce cup. While I drink my coffee black, I really don't think it needs anything anyway. It is a good one if you need a mellow flavor, but still want that dark taste. There is no bitterness, no tang, no off notes. I really don't taste any nuances either (I cant pick up on smoky, chocolate, or caramel--maybe my taste buds are out of service at the moment)-- just dark, smooth, gently bold & rich. It is a good, solid, well rounded coffee that I would certainly consider again. I love trying coffee, and there are only a few k-cups that taste really good to me. This is now on that list.

title: freeze dried freshness, lovely mild seaweed flavor
text:
This Numami brand of organic FREEZE DRIED seaweed is pretty great. Quite fresh and tasty. Wakame seaweed is a great addition to just about any dish. It is mellow in flavor; quite mild compared to some. Tastes like.. the sea? not exactly fishy, but something along that spectrum. Not strong to me. I like adding it to eggs, potatoes, vegetables, soups, sprinkled over avocados. Add it to broth and watch the seaweed flakes reconstitute! Love freeze dried for the amazing freshness and long shelf life. It provides a goodly amount of iodine per 1 teaspoon serving, so keep that in mind (could also make for a great prepper item if you are into that).

I could chomp on this stuff all day, but I limit to 1 serving, or less. Just a pinch. It has a light briny taste. Their Kombu seaweed flakes are significantly more briny (still super low sodium) and way higher in iodine (and smaller serving, even) and could work as a salt alternative (so long as you didnt use much as per the high iodine content).

One gram of seaweed flakes = 25 grams of fresh seaweed.
The fresh Atlantic Wakame is freeze dried after harvesting to preserve nutrients and remove 99% of water, giving you more seaweed and less water per gram.

Yum yum!

title: delicious, salty flavor yet very low sodium
text:
OMG I love this stuff. I have these Kombu flakes as well as the Wakambe, and I use them interchangeably and even my reviews will be quite similar. Very fresh, nice pieces, lovely food item. They are easy- too easy-- to eat. I LOVE seaweed, and I hadn't had any in awhile and was happy to be able to try these freeze dried variety.

The serving size is just HALF A TEASPOON, and I want to eat more than that. Great if you want this 1 ounce bag to last forever (140 servings).. but please keep to the serving since there is A LOT of iodine. I have had hypothyroidism since I was a kid, I take meds.. and am not really supposed to supplement with iodine but I do include foods anyway. In my 40s now..so give me seaweed!. I find it hard at times to limit.. especially since this stuff is SO GOOD. I could totally snack on it right from the bag.. Well.. maybe not so much the Kombu. There is very little sodium (10 mg per serving) but it packs a briny punch. But added to eggs, potatoes, vegetable, broth.. mmmm
Would be great as a salt alternative.

title: equal sweetness; swap same amount white sugar for this allulose baking blend
text:
Reviews for various products here, so just clarifying that I am reviewing the "Whole Earth Sweetener Co. Allulose Baking Blend, Granulated, Plant-Based Sugar Alternative, 12 Ounce

It is sweet like regular sugar. Allulose by itself is much less sweet than regular white cane sugar, as with Erythritol. These are the first two ingredients followed by Xanthan gum (thickener/stabilizer) and the other two sweeteners in this blend, Stevia EXTRACT and Monk fruit EXTRACT. The addition of these help bring the sweetness level up to that of cane sugar, hence the 1:1 swap out ability.

It is slightly more fine in texture, where as typical cane sugar is more granular. I wanted to see how well it does for a 1:1 ratio swap out by making standard chocolate chip cookies. I kept everything else the same, including the brown sugar. I really just wanted to see if I could tell a difference in taste or textures based solely on swapping out the white sugar for this Allulose Baking Blend.

I took one recipe and halved it. One bowl using white cane sugar, the other bowl using this Allulose blend. I always eat some raw dough, and it was a very close match. Had I not been tasting them side by side, I would not know the difference. Because I was.. there is a hint of difference, but I can't pin point exactly what. A slight extract type taste to it? The original/cane sugar based dough has a more deep sweet and the allulose blend is slightly lighter? Not off, just a less white sugar taste. I would say the same with the baked results. Had you handed me a chocolate chip cookie made with the Allulose baking blend, I would not know there was a different sugar being used. Side by side, bite for bite, the close resemblance makes this a good option for a 1:1 swap out. No need to use a different amount or to adjust anything else in recipe. 1 cup of regular white sugar has 773 calories. I do not know what your needs are for a sugar alternative, but I figured I would add that information in. Some people are fine with the fat and calories from butter (1 stick, or 1/2 cup is 800ish calories) but want to/need to reduce/eliminate the refined carbohydrates that is white sugar- for reasons beyond calories. Clearly MY cookies still used typical white flour and brown sugar (and a whole cup of butter) but I needed to be able to tell if the swap out for just the white sugar is noticeable. Obviously the more that is swapped out the greater the difference from an original recipe. But at least there are plenty of options out there!

**My review is to let you know that the swap from white cane sugar to Allulose baking blend was successful. All other reasoning for using it or not using it is entirely up to the individual and does not measure into my rating.**

What my rating IS based on:
The good:
--The product is well packaged in a press zip closure bag.
--easy 1:1 ratio swap. No need to adjust around it or for it.
--It works, it tastes fine.. again the nuance of flavor is rather minimal on my taste buds. YMMV
--I like it better than other baking blends I have tried where somehow the product tasted less sweet and less satisfying in flavor
The bad(ish):
--Pricey. However, I would expect to cost more than refined sugar. BUT,
--The contents is less than ONE pound, which yields 2.25 cups of sugar. So, you won't get much from this bag for most baking needs. If just wanting it for sweetening coffee, or similar, then it will last awhile. To be exact, there are 12 ounces, or 3/4 of a pound.

Other taste testing:
I don't drink my coffee with sugar, but I tried it for sake of review. It blends in with coffee, I would say even better than regular sugar. It just dissolves easily.

I tried it on some strawberries. There I prefer granulated sugar (on the rare occurrence that I am in the mood for an extra sweet strawberry)- but it is close. Again, side by side is more of a nuanced difference. Just having it without an immediate reference is negligible in difference.

The other matter worth noting is that there is no digestive upset. My gut is easily aggravated, and there was nothing after consuming several cookies (or any other time).

I have used other sugar alternative baking blends and of the few I have tried, this one takes the cake. haha.Even if I am not fully swapping out sugars, replacing some of it is sure to be helpful. I would consider buying this again, though would be better if offered in a larger volume.

"Allulose is a type of sweetener found in fruits such as figs and raisins, and helps make our blend very sugar-like when it comes to baking. Erythritol is a sugar alcohol found in fruits such as pears, melons and grapes. Both our allulose and erythritol are derived from corn, and while both ingredients are counted as carbohydrates in the nutrition table, neither impacts blood sugar significantly. The stevia & monk fruit extracts in our blend add sweetness to get the same 1:1 sweetness as sugar. We include xanthum gum in the blend to aid with texture, especially in gluten-free baking. And since it's zero sugar, zero calorie, and zero net carb, it is great for keto, paleo, and other low carb diets. Available in a 12-oz re-sealable pouch.Equal Sweeteners are suitable for people with diabetes. Replacing added sugar with zero calorie sweeteners can help individuals with diabetes manage their lifestyles while enjoying sweetened food and beverages."

title: Yummy, great little treat, pick me up, something sweet, easy, convenient
text:
Happy Belly Hot Cocoa Pods are as good as any others I have tried. Up until this past winter I was adamantly against hot cocoa k-cups given the price compared to just making my own with some hot water and powder. That and I usually like a super thick strong chocolate taste and made with hot milk. I know I know, K-cups are a matter of convenience (trust me, my monthly subscribe and save on coffee-and now cocoa-reflects how convenient k-cups are). Anyway, one day my husband brought me home some cocoa to try. I scoffed at it until the desire for a "little something" to drink struck me, and I decided to make a hot cocoa k-cup. I used a little mug and went for the 6 ounce serving. I didn't expect to like it, but I did. A lot. What a treat! And so quick, too! That then got me hooked on having to buy hot cocoa pods because that meant I could have a little treat anytime I wanted faster and easier than my more complicated hot cocoa making ritual. I still enjoy that, but 23 times out of 24 (ha) I just go with a k-cup. I can make it as I please, it is perfect for when I am all coffeed out and still want something hot to drink, or for when I want a little pick me up, or just a little sweetness. I almost always top it with whipped cream, and sometimes I add a healthy splash of peppermint schnapps for an added bonus. Or a candy cane.

While the Happy Belly hot cocoa pods compare themselves to Starbucks hot cocoa, I haven't had the Starbucks brand (even though I love Starbucks products). I do know from trying several Happy Belly products that their comparison is pretty spot on. But since I haven't had the Starbucks brands, I will say that I have had all sorts of Swiss Miss, Grove Square, and Cafe Escapes (and even some flavored ones like Junior Mints before switching to Schnapps!). They all pretty much taste the same to me. So I could/would select any based on price at this point. AND this Amazon brand, well.. the old Solimo is priced well at UNDER $10 for a 24 pack. I can't see the product description at this time, but I imagine the pricing will be similar. It is the same product after all.

The directions say to use 8 ounces of water, which is what I usually see. My husband uses 10 ounces, while I prefer a stronger 6 ounces. I have never run a plain water brew to clean off the needle after, but the box does suggest it.

I like these, and I would continue to use them no problem. Yum Yum!

text:
I use all sorts of different curry spices, and I rarely have a curry that I don't like. I love red curries, green curries, and yellow curries. This is a yellow curry. Yellow curry is considered a mild curry, although still flavorful. It tends to be bright, sometimes tangy yet bright spices are balanced with deeper, warming spices. Each curry blend is different, and there is no exactness to what goes into the blend. You have to try different ones to get what you like best, or learn about the individual spices to get an idea of what it will taste like (or buy a spice blend and modify it to your liking).

As far as spice blends go, this tastes good to me. I happen to love turmeric, and this leans more in that direction flavor wise.

When I use "yellow curry" spices, I tend to have a heavy hand. I go through A LOT at once, but I am usually making a lot of food at once. I generally use it mixed in with a little oil to release the smell and taste, then add in a can of coconut milk to make a delicious sauce for rice, chicken, and vegetables. Or lentils. MMMMmmmMmmm.

It can even me used as a dry rub, or as part of a marinade. That is the fun thing about spices- there is so much room for creativity (ooh, try it sprinkled on roasted potatoes massaged with olive oil, or strips of french fry shaped turnips- then bake in oven, omg.. yum), or add some to yogurt or sour cream for a quick dip, add some to broth of your choice to flavor enhance a soup, popcorn etc.

Anyway, I am happy to have been able to try the Happy Belly Curry. It does remind me of McCormicks, though possibly a little better (I have various curry spice brands, and I swear my McCormicks is a little darker than this, OR it has gotten old). This is so good. Seems to be a fair price for the size.

Coriander seed, turmeric, fenugreek, cumin, salt, ginger, mustard seed, anise, paprika, cassia oil

title: freeze dried chives look and taste perfectly like.. chives. Use less than what you would of fresh
text:
I have all sorts of spices in my collection, but I have never used dried chives. I usually just buy them fresh when I want them. These FREEZE-DRIED CHIVES may be my new go-to option when I want to use chives in a dish. They just look like cut up chive. Freeze dried.

And they taste like.. chives. YAY!

As with ANY dried spice, you need less of it to get same impact of fresh herbs. SO, use LESS of what you would normally use compared to what you would use when working with fresh. Rule of thumb:

"If you need to convert your recipe from fresh chives to dried chives use - 1 tablespoon fresh equals 1 teaspoon dried. If your recipe calls for fresh chive blades instead of tablespoons or teaspoons of chopped chives, use the ratio of 10 chive blades equals approximately 1 teaspoon of freeze-dried chives"

Usually chives will re-hydrate within the recipe or application you are using. BUT, If you need to rehydrate (usually for aesthetic purpose) then just add them to some water for 10-15 minutes. Drain.

I imagine these are neither better nor worse than other offerings, but I am pleased with the Happy Belly brand of seasonings.

title: decent multi purpose hexane free MCT/fractionated refined coconut oil
text:
MCT oil is Fractionated Coconut oil. It is refined and therefor flavorless. If you are new to this, then do not expect a coconut flavor. It can be consumed and/or used in DIY personal care, or as a carrier oil. Nice for drizzling over salads (need fat to make best use of vitamins and minerals), adding near end of cooking, or just at low temps. Can add to smoothies, coffee, or wherever you want to add in some medium chain triglycerides. Always popular with the keto crowd, this 32 ounce container of Organic, Hexane free MCT oil seems like most any other MCT oil offering.

Although this is an oil, please bear in mind that MCT oil from coconuts has a low smoke point, so you don't want to cook with it at higher temps (325*F). When an oil reaches their smoke point, it is degraded and prone to forming free radicals. Not what you want if better health is your aim. That is why MCT is best used in not cooking applications. Although this is refined and should have a higher smoke point, it all depends on the stability of its fatty acids, its free fatty acid content, as well as its purity. Refined vegetable oils have a higher smoke point due to their purity and low level of free fatty acids. MCT oil doesn't have a high level of free fatty acids, but its fats (medium-chain triglycerides) are not stable at high temperatures, hence recommendation to not cook with it, especially at high temps (325* & above). I would maybe go with super low temp- mid to late in the cooking process if at all. Baking is better, as internal temps tend to be in 150-190 range. Adding it to piping hot coffee is ok, since typical cup of coffee is 160*-185* F

MCT oil is digested in intestines. Start with small amount to see how your body handles it. Can work up to 2 TBS from just about everything I have read/remembered. Some people use more, but that is an individual thing and you will have to do your own research to determine what is best for you and your needs.

If adding it into coffee, while I do not mind the oiliness that is left on my lips (kinda nice in dry, cold weather), once way to byass that a little is pour oil and coffee (and whatever else) into a blender real quick. Just a few seconds seems to emulsify the the ingredients enough to take away the immediate oily texture. If you add in a pat of butter (essentially cream) you will have a semi frothy hot beverage. I love PlantationBrand blackstrap molasses added into the mix- a little sweet, adds a deep almost caramel flavor.

Price wise, seems on par with many. More than some, less than others. Bigger bottle, decent savings. No complaints.

text:

For best flavor, I brew on the smallest setting (6 ounces of water). If I just want a a small cup, then I leave it at that. If I want a larger cup, I don't do a greater amount of water, instead I just do a second k-cup and once again do another 6 ounces. I just find that the product gets watered down tasting and I prefer a strong chocolate flavor when having hot chocolate. Usually I prefer just buying a big pouch of hot cocoa mix, but this is awfully convenient when I just want a quick cup of something hot and sweet. I top it off with a generous dose of whipped cream.

I like it. I would consider a repurchase. The chocolate taste is decent. The peppermint could be stronger but I think this level is good for most people. I wouldn't but it for the reduced calorie option. That can go, lol. But yeh, overall it has been nice to grab a k-cup whenever the mood strikes.

text:

title: easy, consistent, delicious as is or modify to your liking. Makes a great base
text:
I love this Krusteaz Cinnamon Swirl Crumb Cake & Muffin mix. It is so easy to make, and the outcome is consistent every time I make it. I does really well being made in my convection toaster oven and I can follow the time and temp to a t, and it turns out perfectly.

title: good basic spice; great for homemade chai tea mix
text:

title: true coconut cream taste comes through on Toasted Coconut & Cashew option; smooth, bold
text:

Not a scorcher, thankfully. Heat with flavor. I don't normally go for hot, but you know how it can be, something labeled as hot doesn't have any heat. So I thought trying the HOT would be fun since I would either be able to say that I can handle the heat or I would say my mouth is on fire. I can tell you, it has a bit of a building heat and wowsa, my mouth was on fire a little when I ate it plain. Not bad- just more heat than I anticipated. I need to pair it with carbs for it to not totally set my mouth ablaze. It is a good hot, but not so intense that you can't taste the flavors. If you like mouth scalding hot, this isn't it. If you want some heat with some flavor.. this will do.

It is good quality. I LOVE the simple, real ingredients. Check them out: Water, Diced Tomatoes, Tomato Paste, Salt, Onions, White Distilled Vinegar, Green Bell Peppers, Natural Flavor, Coriander, Citric Acid, Cilantro, Cumin. Upon opening the sturdy plastic container, there is some liquid on top. If you shake the bottle, the chunks distribute pretty evenly. You can see the tomato chunks as well as bits of onion and green pepper. Flavor-wise, it has some heat and some tang.

Salsa comes in different tastes, textures, overall viscosity. I have had many brand and non brand names. I would liken this to a Pace brand style. HA- ok, so the product description also compares this to that brand. Well, I agree!

Anyway, it is good! I would totally buy this brand- maybe in a medium or mild. Because I am weak. lol

title: hearty, tasty flavor packed almonds- 260 cals, 8g protein, 23g fat
text:
As one of the Christmas gifts I came up with for my husband was to have a bunch of Sriracha flavored items.I found this multi pack of single serving Blue Diamond almonds with Bold Sriracha flavoring and figured it would make a great addition to my Sriracha themed gift. What I like about this particular item is that the single serve packaged help maintain freshness, especially if he (we) don't get to them for awhile. I also like the single serve packets to help with portion control. Now these are not their wee little 100 calorie packets that can be found (usually plain). These are a nice snack size- 260 calories, 8grams of protein, 23 grams of fat. When I am hungry or just have a snacking need, a packet of these is going to make me feel satisfied over a wee little 100 calorie packet. OR 400+ calorie donut which is just as easy to grab. So while we are both huge eaters, even if not for calorie control, at least we won't be eating a whole tub of flavored almonds in one sitting. We grab one of these packets and are satisfied. Speaking of which..

These are really good! Even though I bought these for my husband, I too have had to have a packet or two from the bunch. I have always found the BOLD flavor line from Blue Diamond to be really good. I especially love their wasabli, so going for some Sriracha flavor seemed a good option to try (err, give as a gift. haha). This Bold Sriracha is also really good- to my husband and I. I like that it packs a whole bunch of flavor. I don't find it to be too spicy., I am not a big fan of hot heat that builds and paralyzes my taste buds, yet I have always liked Sriracha as it is more about flavoring with some heat over just heat and little flavoring. I would say the flavoring on these is just flavorful and with very mild warmth of spice.

I'd buy these again- here, in store, whenever wherever. YUM!

title: lightly crunchy, perfect combinatioin of sweet and salty; so delicious
text:
YUM!!!!! Oh my, these are SO GOOD. I opened these immediately upon arrival. Boy, they really pleased my taste buds. They have that light crisp taste and feel that comes from roasting. The honey taste is light, and slightly sweet. Not cloying. An impressive balance between sweet, salty, and overall texture.

The pieces are small as they are chopped. The would be no doubt great on a salad, or used in baking. I had plans to make a nice cookie with these generously sprinkled on top, but I have not gotten that far. I just keep grabbing handfuls and eating it as is straight from the bag. I already plan to buy some more soon as the bag is quickly depleting. They are so yummy to me.

If I were to have a bag that seemed like it was going to be around awhile, I would store it in my fridge (as suggested) to help maintain freshness. This bag though is about empty- and I have only had it a few days.

title: smooth, dark, bold- no bitterness or tanginess; all wonderully robust dark flavor
text: I love strong, bold, smooth dark coffee. Double Diamond (and Dark Magic, Krispy-Cream1837) are my favorites for meeting this preference. I like that Double Diamond is strong and smooth made with the smallest water setting, as well as stands up to greater amounts of water without it tasting watered down. While I drink mine black 95% of the time, it does nicely with creamer. Never bitter, never tart; it is a true bold coffee. Love it (and the others mentioned).

title: chewy, dense, a little crunch yet soft. It takes awhile to consume.
text:
I usually carry around a snack bar or two in my purse. I often don't eat breakfast, just coffee, and so if I head out the door I like to make sure i have something on me just in case. Or for anytime if I am suddenly feeling a little too hungry for comfort. These energy bars contain caffeine (60-70mg), so depending on your level of caffeine sensitivity you will want to be mindful of how late you consume one of these. They are labeled as breakfast bars.

I have the Caramel Macchiato Clif energy bars. Initial taste is caramel, then it takes on a little of that protein bar taste, then in finishes with a coffee taste. Overall it does indeed remind me of a caramel macchiato drink. I definitely taste caramel, but it isn't overwhelming or too artificial in taste. I like the taste of coffee- well, more like I can taste coffee beans. It is sweet, and the added sugar is on the high side- 19 grams of added sugars. Since I am not chowing down on these like I would a box of donuts, the sugar doesn't turn me off, nor the calories. Overall mouthfeel and texture is pleasant. It is chewy, dense, a little crunch yet soft. It takes awhile to consume.

title: not sure what form the licorice flavoring is derived from
text:
Bought these as a gift. The recipient likes black licorice flavor, and they happen to like caramels so I thought this would make for a unique gift given the combination of flavoring and my having never seen this before (so likely neither would they). The gift went over well and they seem to like this candy. No comment on strength of licorice flavoring, or lack of it. They seemed pleased with it well enough.

From a reviewer standpoint, and one who looks for certain details in a product, I have to say that it is frustrating that the exact ingredients aren't listed, in this case- licorice. Is the flavoring from Licorice root (Glycyrrhiza glabra), or is it from the Anise plant? Usually confections are made with the latter, but it would be nice to know for sure. While the flavor profile is similar, there are nuances between the two. At this price point, I think it would be useful information to have. Also, given that it is a candy that some people may have the propensity to over eat, it is important to know which source the flavoring is from. Black licorice can be harmful in large quantities or even in smaller, but regular quantities (ie high blood pressure, and a host of other issues). Other licorice-like flavorings do not have same impact (ie; anise, fennel). So a few extra words of information on the packaging or even here in the product description could be helpful to some.

Ingredients: Corn Syrup, Sweetened Condensed Milk, Heavy Cream, Invert Sugar, Butter, Brown Sugar, Sugar, Natural Flavor, Sea Salt, Soy Lecithin

title: nice mix; a little something for everyone. Good solid flavor. Would repurchase
text:
Nice mix of coffees. A little bit of everything for everyone in the household. I prefer dark coffees, and their medium and dark coffees have good basic, strong coffee taste. Pleasing. I leave the light morning blend to my husband, as the lighter coffee is a little too light and bright for me. While the dark isn't as bold and chewy as some I have had, these are perfectly good coffees. I may start with a "preferred" k-cup, then have this as my second cup of the day. But even without my preferred, these are really quite good to me. I feel comfortable offering them up to guests, and I enjoy making myself 1-2 cups per day. As I am writing this I am thinking of making a cup. I know my husband has been drinking it too, and he remembered that we had gotten this before in a store, but couldn't remember where. Which is funny, because I had been thinking that, "there was this one time we got a box of coffee somewhere and it was really good".. but it had been awhile and I couldn't recall. Funny how it worked out that he remembered after seeing this coffee label. So yeh, We both have been enjoying this mix!

It is nice to be able to buy a whole bunch at once and not worry about being low too quickly. We do go through a lot and tend to order our coffee online. This will be a repurchase for sure. This is a box of loose packed K-cups, not individually boxed by type. I just keep them stored in this box, then dump out a bunch into a decorative kitchen basket. Since they are all good, I just grab one blindly. Surprise!

title: sweet and salty, lovely combination of flavors and textures; nice snack bar
text:
Tasty little treat. I wouldn't grab one of these if I wanted a "granola" bar, but as a snack bar- sure. I love the different layers of texture AND taste. I can taste the peanut butter, I can taste the peanuts, I can even distinguish the honey flavor. It has that sweet and salty thing going on. I love the bit of pretzel on top. When cold, the bar has a bit of crunch, when room temp or slightly warm, the mouth feel is different. It isn't soft exactly, but there is more "give" to the texture. I like it!

I don't want to chow down on these like an addiction, but I love them for in between meals (or as part of an on the go mini meal), or simply as something to squelch my sweet tooth. 180 calorie snack bar is better than 400+ calorie donut. Ok, so no comparison really, but if I can save a few cals here and there, great.

My two labs are my product models, so you will see them in my pics. They seemed interested despite not liking peanut butter. These aren't for them and I didn't share. But they are cute and they were at the camera when I was trying to take a picture.

title: 2 lb chewy M&Ms for a party of one. I am the party and I cant stop eating them.
text:
OMG, my belly is stuffed with these caramel M&Ms. These were waiting for me in my mailbox when I got home from work. Curious, I busted right into them. They are surprisingly good! AND it was hard to stop eating them. I did manage to put them aside long enough to have dinner, then I went right back to them. Oh boy, not sure if this is a good thing or a bad thing. And its a 2 lb bag! I have no plans to party with it. I intend to eat them all myself. :D

Normally I don't go out of my way to try other M&M flavors outside the classic plain or peanut. These have the expected candy shell, then the inside is a lightly chewy, mild caramel flavor. The caramel does not stick to the teeth!!!!
The caramel is so light, that it is almost like eating a chewy M&M. I can still taste the chocolate candy shell. It is an interesting combo.

I truly didn't know what to expect, and I am happy to report that the texture and flavor works well together, and the fact that the caramel doesn't stick to my teeth is greatly appreciated. Good mouth feel. I like them. Yum!

title: cracklin's are dense, crunchy, tasty, with good faty mouth feel. Pricey but quality product
text:
Big 7 ounce bag of fried pork snack. I have the Sea Salt Cracklins (dense, hard pieces). At $11.99, that is $1.71 per ounce. Quite pricier than some options. I don't eat them all the time, just once in awhile when I want a little salty crunch (and not have it be potato chips). I don't mind spending more for a quality product as an occasional snack, but for regular use the pricing is limiting to me. I dont often comment on price as our budgets vary, but this is one where it may not be my first choice given the price point.

I do like the background info on animal treatment. And I can confidently say that it is probably the best I have had in some time. Usually the ones I buy are the cheapies hanging in the store aisle- kinda bland- typical airy rinds. I have had some microwave varieties, but they are so salty. These are flavorful with a unique texture. Unique in that they aren't all hard, not all light and airy, and not all dry. Some are super hard and crunchy, some have a little more puffed skin so they are airy with lighter crunch. There is a wetness factor- rather a fatty mouth feel- that comes into play likely due to the fat left attached prior to frying--providing that "crisp and fatty textures" feel. They're good. I''d buy these for use to snack straight from bag, and reserve the cheapies for use in making "breading" for coating other meats.

Bag itself is attractive and fun to look at. If I were putting together a gift box/basket/crate, where some snacks like this would be appreciated.. I think this would be a real nice option to include.

title: Delicious!! but FYI--For NESPRESSO makers ONLY--NOT KEURIG; capsule not k-cup
text:
The second bullet point in the description states, "For use in all Keurig K-Cup Brewers". I could tell by the look of the CAPSULE that these were not K-cups, would not work in a KEURIG, and therefor could elicit disappointing purchases, or simply keep would-be customers from buying. Thought I would clear the matter up from the get-go.

So if you are looking for a really good coffee to use in your Nespresso machine, then these capsules are really good and strong. I have tried many I liked, some that were ok, and this one has shot to the top. It is just a gorgeous tasting coffee.

I find this to be a really good, strong, rich, bold, robust, deep roast. Wonderful simply black, or can handle a generous dose of cream. When I use a Nespresso machine, I like using the short pull most of the time. Sometimes a long pull waters down the coffee too much for my liking. However, THIS Cafe Bustelo Espresso Dark Roast coffee can handle extra water if one wishes, as the strong dark taste is maintained. It is delicious!

I don't always brew using a Nespresso machine. I sometimes dump the contents into a filter and do a pour over using the water from my electric kettle. Figured I'd add that in in case you are quirky like me.

title: bold, smooth, ultra fine grind, tasty black or with cream
text:
Bold, smooth. These capsules are for use in Nespresso machines. The pod is plastic with an aluminum top and bottom (for puncture). I have used it in machine (short is best for me), and I have used it in "pour over" coffee making by slicing open the top and tapping the coffee into a filter then pouring hot water over it. By doing this, I could take a look at the coffee itself. It is a beautiful, fine powder. Just what I want when making an espresso level cup of coffee.

I am also a fan of using coffee when baking chocolate cakes, cupcakes, brownies, and a few other confections. So I will be setting a box aside for that purpose. I just add either a whole pod or a half pod to my batter.

I like the overall taste. Easy to sip. Not bitter to me. Dark, smooth. Box says "Intensity level 11" (of 13)- seems about right. I would prefer even bolder and more intense, but this is good. I like it black, but it holds up well with creamer.

title: fresh, tasty, make nice addition to a themed gift
text:
Nice collection of quality spices. I tend to get into a rut when it comes to working with spices and it has been nice to have a fresh set to work with. I have a great assortment, but I always reach for the same ones. I have to say, I don't have marjoram in my spice drawer. Rosemary is always nice, and red pepper flakes are a must have. I guess I don't know Italian seasonings as I would not have expected this combo.

All three of these are ones I would not want a large amount of, so these small containers are perfect. They smell good, work nice with each other or separate. I think a pack of their spice series would make a nice inclusion in a themed gift. Doesn't hurt that there are a couple of included recipes.

The total amount of spice you are buying is 1.17 ounces for 13.28 (currently) which is 11.35 an ounce.
-Marjoram .2 ounce
-Rosemary .35 ounce
-Crushed Red Pepper .62 ounce

Quality is good, freshness is good, presentation is good. But you will have to determine if the price is right for you.

title: fresh, robust flavor; great mix of spices, fair priced, comes in mylar bag
text:
EDIT/UPDATE: I was just coming back to reorder when I decided to add that in to this review. I have purchased this several times since initially trying it in Oct 2019. It is now my go-to spice for potatoes (cut up, drizzled with oil, generous dusting of this spice, bake until done. YUM!). I had also purchased it as part of Christmas gifts. Especially nice for those I wasn't sure what to get. I bought one for a Keto friend and mentioned that it would be great on cauliflower- baked just like I mentioned for potatoes. Mmm I really do enjoy this spice mix.

I have the Svanetian salt, which is tasty. I do not know how much sale this contains, but it is delightfully salty tasting, in a good way. It is a small, 1.05 ounce mylar bag, which once opened you will either have to carefully find a way to close it up (I used a binder clip), or use another container. Although the mylar bag is not ideal, it does help keep the spices fresh until finally opened. I think the price is fair for the amount that we get and the blend of spices used; especially the more unique ones.

This blend is comprised of Coriander, Fenugreek blue, Dill, Garlic, Red Pepper, French Marigold, Salt.

It has tang, bite, and a savory under tone. I have only used it based on what I happened to be cooking. So I have used it on top of quinoa with vegetables, and some roasted potatoes. It is SO SO good on potatoes. I cut up several red potatoes, coat with olive oil, then generously douse the potatoes with this spice blend. Bake until soft. OH MY!. Perfect flavoring. While I want to try it in other applications, the potatoes just worked out so well that it has become my new dish to put into rotation. YUM!!!

I imagine it would be awesome with fish, chicken, other potato dishes. I may make a point to use in a soup or chowder next time. But, mmm potatoes.

It is aromatic with full flavor. Delicious!

title: zesty more than spicy, nice blend of herbs, love the crunch of spouted seeds, nice snack or topper
text:
I used to buy their pumpkin seeds all the time at the store, and I don't know why I stopped. It has been a while, for sure. I totally forgot about this brand until it came up as an option to try. I hadn't ever had their sunflower and pumpkin mix with spicy fiesta flavoring, so I had to know. It is fresh, crunchy and tasty as expected. The flavor is light, and kinda builds. Not spicy, more zesty. I love eating a few handfuls to curb my hunger, I love adding some into salads, or on smashed avocados. It is one of those foods I cant seem to want to eat a lot of at once, so a bag will last me awhile.

It is wildly pricey compared to the other options.

title: garlic ghee oil is delicious, dark attractive bottle, balanced flavor and mouth feel, YUM!
text:
This review is for the pourable Garlic flavored Ghee. I love garlic oil and I love using Ghee, so when I saw a garlic flavored Ghee come up, I knew I had to try it. I like that it is a combination of Ghee (from grass fed cows), Avocado Oil and Grapeseed oil. I normally don't use grapeseed oil, but I do have it among my oil collection. I use avocado oil often. So really a neat combo for me. In addition, I have a garlic oil that I love and was super curious how this would taste and perform. I love adding garlic flavoring to everything. MMmm

All that I like:
--I like that the combination makes it easy to pour from the bottle. The plain Ghee I have is in a jar and I always have to scoop it out. This is a nice change up. I wouldn't replace my ghee with this, but this is an awesome addition to my decorative caddy of oils that I pull from almost daily.

--Taste. It has a light buttery ghee, light garlic taste. It isn't as strong or pungent as my garlic oil. Honestly, that is good. My current garlic oil is so strong that it is easy to over power the dish. Sometimes it is bitter depending on the amount. This is smooth! I mean, I like the strong oil but this is easier to work with- more options for use. I kinda consider this more oil than clarified butter in terms of the texture, but it is working out well for all that I want it for. I should say it is balanced, overall- flavor wise, mouth feel, lool. I love that it is easily used for cooking or drizzling, hot foods or cold. LOVE IT. (yum over chicken, omg over steak!!!, lovely mixed in with mashed/smashed potatoes, nice flavor to cook eggs, etc)

--I think it would be nice as part of a gift for those that appreciate kitchen/culinary items.

--fair sized bottle, fair price. While it costs more than straight Ghee, and a lot more than grapeseed oil, it is a special mix with flavor, so I consider it about what to expect.

What I don't like:
--lol.. price if you have a heavy hand. I think I could go through a bottle every week or two, depending on what I am making.

Summary:
If I want just ghee, then I will get out my jar. If I want stronger garlic flavor then I will add some of my other garlic infused oil. Unlike my Avocado oil, I don't want to use this on a salad. As for grapeseed oil.. I don't use it often. But as a combo I like it. Unlike Ghee, the oils (especially grapeseed oil in my experience) goes rancid quickly--so plan to use this up sooner over later. However, I don't think that will be a problem for me. Also.. it is in a dark, attractive bottle, which helps.

This has been a fun, tasty addition to my kitchen and I am highly considering grabbing another bottle for myself, and am already thinking ahead to the holidays and host/hostess gifts.

Yum yum!

(ps, if they make Dill infused version, I am so buying a case, lol)

title: bright, tangy start with deeper finish, not as bold as I prefer, not an extra dark roast
text:
I am reviewing Timothy's Rainforest Espresso, Extra Dark. It has an interesting flavor profile. It is not what I would gravitate towards among all the other dark options. This is more like a bold medium, or a slightly more acidic dark. It starts with a bit of a tang and breathes out as a solid espresso roast flavor (the roast of the bean, not the beverage itself- no Kcup is creating an espresso experience). So this is lighter in taste that what I prefer. I prefer a deep, bold, strong dark, non acidic, no brightness. Labeled, "Extra Dark"- the bright tang with this throws me off. Which might be exactly what you like :) I'd say it reminds me of a stronger restaurant coffee.

I tend to drink two from Greenmountain: DarkMagic (Kcup or ground) and DoubleDiamond, for reference.

I have brewed it at different strengths- 8oz, 10oz, 16 oz, 20 oz. Forget the 20- it will indeed taste watered down using that much water. It seems to be well suited for 8 or 10 ounces; black or with cream. I tend to drink my coffee black, but I often try it with cream as well when I am reviewing. The coffee did remain fairly dark even with a generous addition of pure cream. So maybe it truly is "extra dark".

Overall I think most people who want a strong- but not "strong"- coffee will like this, especially if you are used to grabbing a coffee through a drive through or whatever is brewing at work. This has more oomph than some basic options. BUT if you are a connoisseur of truly dark, deep, bold thick-chewy coffee, this may not cut it. It will be like having a darker medium roast. (Again, I think the tang is throwing me off)

While tangy and bright, is smooth though, and that is important. It is a "fair" price- not on the high end, not on the low end. Solidly centered.

title: delicious, fresh container of Organic white, red, and black quinoa
text:
For whatever reason, the pricing on quinoa- whether it is organic, standard, white, tri-colored, red, etc.. is all over the place- including when staring at choices on a store shelf. I don't know what makes the difference and I find they are all the same, so usually I just buy the least expensive. Typically the smaller the package the greater the price per ounce. This is a 3 lb container and it comes in near or a little over what I normally get. The current range of prices I see are between .19-.59 per ounce. This comes in at .42 an ounce.

I can say that this is perfectly good quinoa. ZERO COMPLAINTS. BBF is a good, solid brand. I have had other items by Better Body Foods and have been pleased, so I am glad this follows suit. Sometimes I find their stuff in a membership/club store. I am a long time consumer of quinoa, even before anyone knew how to pronounce it, lol. Actually a seed rather than a grain, it is so versatile and a pleasant addition to the pantry. It is nutritionally packed with lots of protein, fiber, vitamins, minerals, etc. It has a light, slightly nutty, but almost neutral taste. There is no shortage of recipes to find. I usually keep it simple and add it to soups, chili, sometimes add it in with rice or lentils, makes for a neat taco "meat" alternative if you are into that, or as a base for some awesome meatless burgers (or less meat burgers by adding it with ground meat)-- or it can simply help stretch your food budget by filling out a food (such as adding it to taco meat, meat loaf, meatballs, or to chili, or anything else you want some added bulk and nutrition). I usually eat it as a hot food, but there are cold recipes too. I never eat it entirely plain. I use it like one would any other grain or grain like need- rice, millet, lentils, wheat berries/bulgar, freekeh, etc. A little bit goes a long way. It cooks up a lot and that's fine because it is great to use in coming days. Every time I make it I think to myself that I really need to make it more often.

I love the slight little pop of texture these have. It isn't crunchy, but there is a mouth feel that makes it extra yummy to me.

It is easy to cook: measure your amount, rinse/drain, add to water. Bring to boil, then reduce heat and cover pot. It is usually done within 15 minutes. I think I do a 2:1 ratio of water to quinoa.

One last thing.. I like the large hard plastic container with twist on lid. It will keep it fresh (and can be reused). I have had bags that come open over time, and I much prefer this closed container style. I will pay more for that.. so 5/5 stars

title: spicy, chewy, high sodium 750 mg
text:
Oof, that's some spice. I am a fan of Sriracha flavoring. This definitely has it, though it is at the upper limit of what I can comfortably handle. Not sure if like that much heat in a snack stick. I feel like I need to have something to go with it to take down the heat level. On the plus side, the heat level reduces my desire to eat. lol

Good: 13 g of protein. Texture is good- basically what to expect from a soft, chewy stick. Good size, easy to open, seems fresh. Travel friendly. If you like spicy, this is spicy

Bad- 750 mg of sodium. I know these foods tend to be loaded, but I was hoping that a seemingly healthier, higher end product would be more conscientious of the sodium levels. I've had similarly weighted ones with quite a bit less sodium.
Spicy- if you don't tolerate spicy well, this is not for you.

title: strong vanilla, solid medium roast, best with creamer for mellow pleasing natural flavor
text:
Never thought I would give a flavored coffee 5 stars. While I love almost anything vanilla, when it comes to flavored beans it usually doesn't translate well. Just because I don't care for something, I can give it an objective review- I know coffee well enough to know if it is worthwhile in terms of roast, flavor profile, etc. I decided to give this a try since I am already familiar with Victor Allen ground coffee andkcups. Usually budget friendly and a solid product.

Upon opening the bag, I got a huge whiff of vanilla. I kinda cringed. I set out to make a strong cup for use over ice (it's a hot muggy day). When done, I took a sip- blegh. I made it too strong. I added a splash of water, and it simmered down a bit. This gave me hope. I thought there was no way that I could drink this, but then it occurred to me to add creamer. See, I normally drink my coffee black. Only once in a great while do I add cream or sugar. For whatever reason, it dawned on me that a flavored coffee may actually benefit from cream. So I added a generous amount to my cup of iced coffee- and guess what? IT IS PERFECT. Now I could really test the coffee. I can taste the roast- medium I presume. The coffee flavor comes through with a strong but now gentle vanilla flavor. It is actually quite good. Really pleasant. I didn't care for it black, but it took on a whole new pleasing flavor by adding in some cream. I guess that makes sense- creamy vanilla. Maybe everyone else knows this already and I am just really late to the game, lol.

Anyway, it is no surprise that if a flavored coffee was going to be done well, it would be by Victor Allen.

title: Quite bold for a medium roast- love it. Smooth, balanced, robust
text:
This is a medium roast, and a bold one at that. I generally prefer dark roasts- I love strong, bold coffee. But when it comes to caffeine, I never turn down a cup of any roast or blend. So with enthusiasm I brewed up a large cup.

When I first opened the bag and took a whiff, I said out loud to no one- "oh gawd that smells good.. mmm". I can't quite depict the notes that I am smelling, but the bag says, brown sugar, roasted nuts, dark chocolate. Sounds good, smells good.. did it taste good?

YES.

I may have made my cup a little strong, but I intended it for over ice (hot, muggy day). I usually drink my coffee black, so I started sipping it that way. It definitely, solidly medium, but it has extra body with balance. The coffee flavor has presence. Robust, smooth, no bitterness. It handled ice well. I added to my coffee tasting test by adding a generous dose of creamer. While rounded out, the coffee flavor still came through- gorgeous, strong. I am nodding my head as I write this.. it is just a wonderful contender for coffee enjoyment. I have since learned that it is a Whole Foods Coffee using Latin American beans. I'd recommend it, and now I am curious of their other offerings. Good stuff!

title: not bad, kinda bland, definitely for end product finishing sauce and not for main flavor
text:
I found it pleasant, but a little bland for my taste. It has a very light lemon flavor with a touch of brightness from white wine, and the smooth, silky mouth feel of butter. Directly out of packet, it looks like yellow mayonnaise. Lemon-naise? Once heated, it melts down more like butter, albeit creamy, than a viscous sauce.

I included pics for visual on what it looks like out of packet.

I opted to try it with linguine, chicken, green beans. Since I wasn't sure how much I would need to take care of the amount I was cooking, I did a little side test with smaller amounts. I also tried it on the separate components. I liked it best with the chicken. It was more difficult to pick up on the flavor when applied to the vegetable or the pasta. It is so very light in taste, that I think it would be best as described- as a finishing sauce, and perhaps just on fish- where you want a tiny bit of flavor but nothing over powering. title: just because this doesn't show up in USDAorganic database doesn't mean it isn't legit.Read my review
text:
The very first review I see claims that because the product (nor company) show up in the USDA Integrity data base that means that the product is illegally labeled. *sigh*. A further glance at the USDA website Integrity Data base reads, "Did you search INTEGRITY for a certified organic business and didn’t see it listed? The next step is to ask the business claiming organic certification for the name of their USDA organic certifying agent. Then, contact the certifying agent (find them using USDA’s Organic Certifier Locator) to confirm certification and request a certificate. If the business is certified, the certificate must be available to the public from the certifier upon request. If the business appears to be falsely advertising as organic, please consider submitting a complaint with your evidence to USDA."

The information on Greenbow webbsite states that, "We source our Organic and NGMO bee products from all over the world such as South America, Asia, India, Africa, Brazil, and Canada."

SOooooo.. this tells me that since they don't use product based in USA (or use another USA based as mother company), but are selling in USA and want the USDA stamp, then they would have followed the steps outlined on USDA website (including utilizing an organic certifying agent- which GREENBOW has listed as certified by OCIA, which IS listed on USDA website as a legit certifier). Not wanting to leave anyone hanging, I contacted OCIA and asked for verification. The information has been forwarded to a certification director 08/2019. I may (or may not) hear from them over the next few days. While I am curious as to how this works, I am thinking that Greenbow would be taking a massive chance on lying about their product being certified USDA Organic AND listing their actual certifier. BUT, who knows.. and I just wanted to follow through as far as I could.. because someone decided that since they could not find the name in the USDA database then clearly it is a fraud. And that isn't necessarily the case.. as stated by the USDA website.

I have no bias, nor interest in this company. But I do get a fire lit under my butt when something like that is being written with no FOLLOW THROUGH. My aim is to be helpful. SO I am here to say that I am attempting to follow this through. If I do get contact with the desired information, I will let ya'll know. Lets see what we learn. Stay tuned!

EDIT!! I proceeded to contact OCIA, and the Director of Accreditation confirmed the legitimacy to me with this response, "OCIA does certify the bee pollen marketed under Greenbow. It is a private label, so another company actually produces the product but Greenbow is indicated on the label. Private label relationships are confidential, but I can confirm the product is certified by OCIA"

Also, there is a comment from GreenbowUS in that first review comment section which states, "you will not be able to find Greenbow in the USDA Integrity database because Greenbow is a brand name and our products are made by the parent company Y.S.Health Corp, a Certified Organic Manufacturer" Then proceeds to share webpage.

So, I think it is fine to go ahead and make your purchase if that bit was holding you back.

Now as to the review on the product iteself..

AS for this BEE POLLEN product? I like it. Its been years since I have purchased bee pollen, and recently I decided to buy some (I love superfoods and supplements of all sorts). I found this to be a reasonably priced, fresh container and have zero complaints thus far. I can't stand this stuff straight out of the jar, but I do like it sprinkled on my toast- especially if it has been slathered with peanut butter first. These are soft granules with very little mouth feel (not a crunchy item if you have never had bee pollen). They have a strong taste if consumed alone, yet have very little flavor once added into/onto something. Easy to use, and after I use up this jar, I will likely continue with it.

title: coconut oil NOT butter. Decent oil if that is what you are looking for
text:
The pictures show coconut butter, the product description headline says coconut oil. Coconut butter and coconut oil are not the same thing, and can not be used interchangeably. The label on my jar even says coconut butter but this is coconut OIL! I love coconut butter and I love coconut oil- but the wording, labeling, and actual product need to line up. And we should all be aware of this before purchase.

So I have coconut oil in a jar labeled coconut butter, and the product description and pictures say coconut butter but with a title that says coconut oil. If you order this, I guess expect to get coconut oil.

I even thought for maybe a moment I was getting it wrong, like it was "oil" by a company that calls their products Coconut Butter-- BUT, a little blurb on the label says to the word, and note the odd phrasing, "our coconut butter is sourced from fresh, the highest quality and grown without the use of pesticides or herbicides. Bottled in the USA". And, "this butter is food grade", and "Benefits of Coconut Butter" ....

It ISN'T BUTTER! It is oil (oil extracted from coconut meat), and not at all coconut butter (ground coconut flesh)

Just like Peanut butter is not peanut oil. If you want one but get the other, you will be sorely disappointed. Still usable and enjoyable for certain applications, but they are not interchangeable.

The remainder of the labels makes primarily skin and hair suggestions, and also says is food grade. Yet no food/nutrition label. Red flag for me.

If this were all labeled correctly, I would say that for the most part, what is not to love about cold pressed, unrefined, raw coconut OIL? Smells good, tastes good- basically exactly as expected from coconut OIL. Coconut oil is liquid at temps of 76 and above, begins to firm up or totally harden as temps decrease. Coconut butter (which this is NOT) is solid at room temp and just softens up at the temps rise. I use coconut oil to cook and bake with; not too often for use on my own skin or hair. Sometimes I give a little to my cats and dogs to enjoy. Priced a little high for me for 16 ounce container of coconut OIL. Funny, it would be about the right price if it were actually coconut butter. For the oil itself, I would give it at best 4 star rating. For all the confusion in terms of labeling and information, I have to drop it to 1 star. I think enough people could be confused to as to what to expect in their purchase that hopefully they will see this review and make a decision on what they are looking for (oil or butter). If the information is cleared up, or if I learn more, I will be back to update what I learn. I hoped this helped in one way or another. Take care :)

title: bold flavor, mixes easily with hot or cold, great for on the go or caffeine emergencies
text:
Starbucks has pretty good instant micro ground coffee. I like the strong taste of their French roast. It is pungent and bold. The coffee is ground super fine- it basically a soft, fine, powder. Doesn't look like much in a stick, but there is plenty to get a strong tasting cup of coffee. I have been enjoying it- on occasion- for years. I have found that it tastes the least like "instant coffee" and the most like a cup of coffee. I like super dark coffee, and I find their French roast is a good one. It isn't perfect, but it is a good one to have on hand. Great finding these online, as I am quite a distance from Starbucks these days. I find they are awesome to keep around for a multitude of reasons:

--Caffeine whenever you need it. On the trail, on the road, at your desk. If you have time, add it to really hot water. If you don't, just use super hot tap water. If you want it cold, go for it. Just a little extra time to dissolve. OR you can dissolve it in a little hot, then top it off with cold. I keep some in a mouse proof box in my truck for caffeine emergencies. I always have a couple in my purse. I am on the go but not always anywhere near a place to get coffee, so really these work in a pinch when I want the caffeine, or psychological comfort of a cup of coffee. Even just tepid tap water will dissolve this.

--At home. Once in a while I use it at home despite having other options. My husband pokes fun of me when I do because I have various coffee brewing systems, grinders, whole beans (always starbucks!), ground beans, etc.. and then I am standing there tearing open instant coffee packs. I don't know.. sometimes it is a taste I prefer in that moment.

--Baking a chocolate cake, brownies, or making a chocolate frosting? Coffee always boost that chocolate flavor and adds depth of flavor. A little instant coffee does the trick. This is a super fine powder, and will mix well in whatever you are baking.

--Amp up your yogurt or ice cream. Mix it in or just sprinkle it on top. YUM!!! If you like more granular coffee bits, then something like Tasters Choice would work (thats pretty good too, but more instant tasting).

--Adding it to a smoothy. I LOVE LOVE LOVE a chocolate based smoothy with a dose of coffee added to it. SO GOOD. Actually I think it was their Vivanno's back '08 or '09 that got me started on that. YUM.

--one more.. this is going to sound funny but maybe some of you will know what I mean. Have you ever been to a restaurant and had a cup of basically brown water? There is no taste to the coffee, and even the caffeine is questionable. It is usually breakfast I leave the house for, and so getting that early cup of coffee is necessary. This is where I grab an instant coffee packet and just stir it in. I don't do this often, but once in awhile I am grateful to have the added boost the Via provides. Then I can proceed to enjoy my meal.

Those are my uses for it :)

No complaints. Well, other than it is pricey. I go through enough to want quality, but not enough that it is a strain on budget. So I pretty much go with what I like, and that is the Starbucks Via.

If I think of anything else, good or bad, I will be sure to come back to update. I keep up with my reviews. I hope this helped. Take care :)

title: paying for pour spout container, excellent coconut oil
text:
I hadn't seen coconut oil in a pouch until now. I love Nutiva products, and have even had their coconut oil in a jar, so this has been neat to try. I've just used it at home, but I can see this being super handy and convenient on the go. I have enjoyed pouring it onto foods or into my coffee instead of spooning it out of a jar. The temps are hot and humid at the moment, so my oil is pure liquid sitting out. As with any unrefined coconut oil, it will stay liquid until 74 (76?) degrees Fahrenheit, then below that it begins to firm up (or if hard, begins to liquefy at 74/76*). SO, keep that in mind regarding where to keep it. If it does harden up, running the package under warm water will very quickly liquefy it. I confirmed this by placing a pouch in the fridge so it would harden up. For the most part though, pouring it out or squeezing it out will give you what you need from the container--it doesn't have to be liquid to get it out.

Of course, buying it in a jar is less expensive, but if you are looking for a neat, convenient packaging then the added expense may be worth it to you. The product is great, now you just need to determine if the pour-able container is what you want. I see the benefit of it if you are using it regularly and perhaps away from home.

Anyway, delicious coconut oil- cold pressed, unrefined- just the way I like it. Yum yum!

title: real cinnamon, health benefits, nice product
text:

title: this gelatin firms up, but can still be used for getting your collagen, more budget friendly option
text:
This gelatin is best for use in hot beverages or foods. or for making gelatin desserts, or for thickening up some dishes. I've used it to make marshmallows from scratch. That was fun! Basically, it is the type of gelatin that will firm up. So if you are deciding between this gelatin for your collagen needs and that of their more expensive collagen hydroslyate, know that this can be used in cold applications but it will need to be dissolved first in hot (otherwise it doesn't mix real well, but might be ok in smoothie or shaker bottle). Where as the other will never make something firm up and therefor can always be mixed in directly into cold.
Also keep in mind that it will eventually firm up as it cools down- so say if you mix it in with coffee, then as the coffee cools down it begins to firm up, and if it actually gets cold.. you will end up with coffee jello. It will all turn back to liquid once it is warmed up again, though.
