title: delicios, unrefined pink salt mined in USA
text: We've been using Redmond Real Salt for years, I think at least six years straight now. Once we switched from using basic white table salt, we have not been back. Provides a nice flavor and has a better nutrition profile than bleached stripped salt. Works in everything and on everything. No reason for us to use anything different.

title: light to medium roast, earthy, bright, tangy, rather smooth
text:
100% Costa Rican whole beans. I couldn't tell what type of roast this was going to be. Light, medium, dark? There is no indication of such important information. I see now that the product description says "earthy tones and high citrus notes", which in my experience depicts a light to medium roast. Would be helpful to just say so.

For my coffee consumption, I much prefer a dark, bold roast and rarely venture into the other side of the roast spectrum. But I went there with this bag of beans by Twin Peaks. It makes a bright, earthy, clean flavor profile. Slightly tangy but without the bitter or overly acidic flavor that light to medium roasts can take on. It could also be a matter of the wonderful brewer I use, so your experience might be different.

The finished brew can be mellowed out with a tiny splash of cream, or if you like the tangier taste then consume it straight from the pot. Once I realized this is a light to medium roast, I can say that I like it a lot more than I expected to, and it has successfully powered me through my day. I normally drink my coffee black with dark roasts. For me, this needed the splash of cream to knock the brightness down a bit. It worked though!

The whole beans look like a (not quite) medium roast. They are gorgeous to look at- dry, mottled, and fresh. The ground bean is a reddish clay color (see my pic). While I may not care for lighter roasts, I can say that the product looks, smells, and tastes of quality. I would be curious to try one of their darker roasts, so I can see how that compares to my preferred taste palette.

Price seems about average for 12oz of fresh, whole beans.

Hopefully they will change their product description to tell more about this roast, and less about their pour over product.

title: soft, dense protein bar tastes like an autum day
text:
What I like is that it doesn't taste like a commercial protein bar! A good one from Cliff, now I want to try other Whole Lotta bars. This is very natural tasting. It has great texture and taste. The bar is shaped into a loaf slice. It is dense, chewy, soft, and moist. Not crumbly. It is compact.

While small, it is something that can be nibbled at. I can eat a half dozen cookies in a couple of minutes. This is more of a take a bite, put it down. Go back to it, and consume over several minutes. I couldn't chow it down, which is good. I think it would work as a snack, super light meal, or as a hearty dessert. I plan to toss a couple in my purse for on the go energy.

The base of the bar is date pate. The other ingredients are pumpkin seeds, almonds, cashew butter, pea protein, sesame seeds, coconut, virgin coconut oil, sea salt, natural flavors, cinnamon, ground ginger, cloves, rosemary extract, nutmeg.

The spices remind me of fall. The warm spices are pleasing, cozy. I can taste the cashew butter, I can tell there are slightly crunchy bits of pumpkin seed and almond (and you can see them, too). The date paste gives it a light, slightly sweet taste, but not lingering or coy. This is really good, in my opinion.

I included some pics of the nutritional stats.

title: you had me at "high caffeine content"
text:
I'm a coffee drinker, not a tea drinker. Well, sometimes a tea drinker. I do have a cupboard full of tea and tea making equipment that would suggest otherwise. But coffee is my thing. What drew me to this tea is the assortment of interesting ingredients: black tea, lavender, bergamot oil, rose petals, marigolds, cornflowers.
I LOVE marigolds..to look at. I wonder what they taste like? That, and Tiesta "Victorian Earl Grey Energizer blend" tea had me at "high caffeine content" What you say, high caffeine? pour it in my mouth!

I made it according to direction for iced tea. 1.5 teaspoons per 8 oz water. Double for iced tea. Steep for 3-5 mins (50/25 servings per container). This is loose tea, so I pretty much filled up a tea ball and poured appropriately hot (195*f) water over it and let it steep. Probably too long, as I was finishing off my coffee and kinda forgot about it sitting there. So maybe I steeped it for 20 mins. Oops.

Btw, take a look at my pic with some of the dried tea-- gorgeous looking stuff!

I came back to it, and poured it over ice. My sniff test detected some floral notes, almost like a men's deodorant or cologne. Leans masculine, if that makes sense. My first sip made me shudder. Ahh, tea. I made it a tad too strong, but that can be fixed with a splash of water. I don't normally sweeten my drinks, but I added some coconut nectar to it, and took my cup back to my desk. Ok, now that has been sweetened up a little, and some of the ice has melted a bit, the tea has mellowed out. I can taste some black tea, but mostly the other more floral flavors with a lavender aftertaste. Overall taste is deep and astringent. It doesn't taste pretty and light, it has body and a little bit of a punch to it. These can be good or bad depending on what you are looking for. I can see myself switching to this after my morning cup of coffee, when I want to keep topping off my caffeine levels without having to turn to more coffee or soda. Personally, I will likely just drink it iced. Lots and lots of ice, and maybe sweetener. And maybe less steep time.

It is different.. unique. If you love trying all sorts of tea, this may be a good one. If you are more of a coffee drinker, but enjoy some tea on occasion, this one has the caffeine we all love. I'm not over the moon with it, but a solid 4-4.5 stars seems appropriate.

title: 2 pounds will last 2 life times. So worth it!
text:
I do not need two pounds of flaming hot cayenne pepper, but I bought that much anyway. All the cayenne pepper offered in the stores is typically no more than 30,000 HU (and costs a lot), and I wanted the 90,000 HU for the possible health benefits, as well as for a variety of recipes. I love making something I like to call, "flaming hot chocolate" (cayenne stirred into some hot chocolate)- great for blustery cold winter days.

This product comes in two, 1 pound freshness keeping Mylar bags. The expiration date is a few years out, but if concerned, I recommend that one bag is stored in the fridge or freezer immediately (or cool, dark place) if you are using it at home as a seasoning or as a supplement. It is just going to take a long while to get through each 1 pound bag. Then the bag you do open, maybe portion some out into a smaller container, and once again store the remainder in either a cool dark place, or fridge (or freezer). Just for ease of use, I portion out into a smaller container as it is just too much to be taking a tiny amount out of a big bag each time I want some pepper (also, exposing product to air over and over).

That being said, spices don't really expire. They might lose some flavor, but they don't go bad. They might lose some potency, but they don't go bad. So you're good. At 90,000 HU this will still be flippin' hot 7 years from now (I would know, I have not finished my 2 pounds of this cayenne pepper yet, bought in 2012!).

I love Frontier products, and appreciate that they offer so many spices in bulk, non irradiated.

title: smooth, robust coffeen bean taste
text:
"Bold 1937"
Mmm, I'm already on my second cup this morning. I LOVE a dark, bold cup of coffee. What I normally drink tends to be too strong for people. So while this isn't my all time favorite for that category, this is really good. I need to keep this stocked up, as it is just delightful.

This is for those that like a SMOOTH cup of dark coffee. I can taste the bean, and there aren't any off flavors. Just tastes pure and smooth. Robust with body, yet subtle enough for most coffee drinkers.

I drank my first cup black, as I usually drink it. Great!
I drank my second cup with cream, as I sometimes drink it. Oh wow.. Delicious!
My brewer offers 6, 8, or 10 oz. Both cups were brewed using 10oz of water.

I brewed a third, for taste testing purpose using 16 oz of water. (2 8oz)- I was curious how dilute a cup can be brewed before it loses flavor and tastes like brown water. I am pleased to say that it was still tasty after using 16 oz. This amount of water maintains a dark flavor, but *slightly* less robust. So go for that bigger cup, if you like!

title: robust, deep flavor
text: I don't care for too many of the K-cup coffee varieties out there. I really only like dark, strong, bold, full flavored coffee, and there are but a few that fit this taste profile. I liked the Jet Fuel. It is probably my third favorite after Green Mountain Double Diamond and Dark Magic. Definitely robust. I love the name- good stuff!

title: ceylon is mild, sweet, different than typical cinnamon (cassia)
text:
I like Frontier bulk organic products. I have been using them for years. I know the prices fluctuate on here, but I managed to get it a really good price. So, great price, quality, and quantity. I use a mix of ceylon and cassia cinnamon. The later is what is typically used in baking and what you get when you go to the store and pick up some cinnamon. I like adding the ceylon into my diet for the different taste and for some of the health benefits that are different from the Cassia variety.
A little bit lasts a long time, and since this is a 1lb package, I found it best to portion some out and store the rest in the fridge. Good stuff, I will buy again (eventually)

title: perfectly fine collagen product.
text:
I use collagen almost every day for the past several years. I like when I can purchase the kind that mixes easily into hot or cold beverages, which is referred to as hydrolyzed collagen. More and more companies are coming out with their version of collagen, so there are an increasing amount of choices available. I've used many, and for the most part they are all quite similar, if you are comparing collagen sources. This one has two types, 1 & 3, which is typically bovine sourced. The taste tends to be neutral, which is great for mixing seamlessly into other products. You can mix into your coffee, tea, smoothie, or even into foods like yogurt, soups, gravies, chili, etc. Some collagen mixtures have more than one type, which comes from multiple sources and will change the taste which can be more of a challenge to work with. This one is just an easy, typical collagen that will provide you with protein and amino acids, and a wonderful dose of collagen. So good for the body, skin, and nails. It is worth looking up the benefits of collagen and the different types.
I found that this one mixes just fine with my coffee or smoothie. I don't taste it, and there shouldn't be any real flavor but I am used to adding bovine type 1&3 collagen to my drinks, so I may have just gotten used to it. I have yet to experience lumps. I like it, and will happily use it all up and maybe get some more.

title: tasty, fiber & protein filled side or meal. High sodium though
text:
I've always enjoyed Zatarain's products. It is a brand that is special to me. I remember it was one of the first novel products I bought when I first moved out on my own at age 20. Now in my 40s, and although I tend to lean away from boxed foods I still buy something of theirs on occasion. I had not yet tried anything from the Garden District Kitchen collection. Eager to try out something entirely new, I was looking forward to this Roasted Garlic Adobo.

As always, the end result is yummy. I love garlic, black beans, rice. The other seasonings add a delicious depth of flavor, while not being overpowering. They do not skimp on black beans. I would say this is easily 50/50 black beans and rice!

I know to expect a lot of sodium in boxed/canned/convenience product, and this item definitely has a lot of sodium per serving. I don't know why there is always so much sodium in everything. Ugh! However, if you stick to one serving and are selective and careful about additional ingredients, and you aren't eating this every single day, then it can be manageable. If you have a big appetite, and decided to eat entire box, then be very careful of anything else you may eat in the day. (640 mg of sodium per serving, 2 servings per box.) If they could reduce the sodium a bit, that would be great!

On plus side, no sodium from MSG. Also, no artificial flavors or colors. Gluten free, too.

I happen to have a huge appetite. I tend to not eat, or not eat much during the day, and instead enjoy a hearty dinner. That is my preference. I made one box according to directions. It took all of ten minutes to make on stove top. Super easy! To round out the evening meal, I prepared some boneless chicken breasts (season with smokey chipotle seasoning) as well as a mix of plain vegetables to go with it. I dished out a serving each to my husband and I, leaving no leftovers. The amount in the serving isn't a lot- but it was great paired with other items. I loved scooping up bites of chicken, veg and this this mix into each bite. I liked not having a bunch of leftovers. If I were eating it with nothing else, I don't know if I could eat 2 servings, but I bet I would manage it. I am used to fiber filled foods, so I don't think that would be an issue. What I would likely do next time is to make it just like the picture on the box- add in some corn, avocado, onion, and maybe some sprouts. I love idea suggestions on boxes!

title: Non GMO, Non Irridated, Smokey, Little goes a long way
text:
Frontier products are great. One of my go-to brands.

Fantastic price compared to the typical store offerings.

I loved adding this to my collection. Nice blend to create a smokey taste without a ton of heat. Chipotle adds a little "extra something" to dishes. title: research supports benefits to using rosehips powder.
text:
I've used a variety of FRONTIER organics for many years. This is my first time buying rosehip powder, and I felt comfortable purchasing a bag from FRONTIER.

I bought it because I want to add foods, drinks and supplements that help reduce inflammation, are antioxident rich, and have some possible support in reducing blood pressure. Various literature, and even reviews have nodded toward using this for those reasons. I didn't want capsules, but those that are inclined could use this to fill their own.

I also use it because I use rosehip seed oil on my face and body. I like that it is gentle on my Rosacea, is moisturizing without being heavy, and is all around good for dry, sensitive, aging skin. So why not add those benefits into my body as well. The powder would also be good for topical application- such as a gentle exfoliant.

I use it by adding this to my smoothies every day, approximately 1 tablespoon 1x/day, and I have been consistent in doing so for about a month now. I don't discern a taste. The texture is a fine powder- not loose, but not at all clumpy or gritty. It blends in without even noticing it. I imagine it would be the same if i mixed it into tea. I don't expect any grittiness. I dare to say that it would mix with coffee, or oatmeal, if I wasn't having a smoothie.

So I am not opening and closing the same bag every day, I scooped out a 1 cup portion into a separate container. The remaining bag is closed up tight and stored in a cool, dark spot.

One area of concern is the bag it comes in. The original bag is a little thin, I think it should be packaged in a thicker mylar bag, or maybe a bag within a bag. A couple of spots where I was rolling and unrolling were looking like a hole could form. Maybe I am wrong, but it was something I noted. Since this is a big bulk bag, I wouldn't want the freshness to reduce. So when you receive it, be mindful of this and maybe wrap another bag around it (and take out what you need for a week or two, rather than dipping into bag daily).

The color of the product is spot on- orange-ish in color.

I'm about a month into my use of it, currently using 1 tbs a day. I have read mixed information on how much to use. I am a large individual, and think I could use more. WebMD has some interesting information on the benefits of using rosehips powder. They state that animal studies hint that a daily drink containing about 40 grams (about 3 TBS) of rosehip powder may also:

Lower blood sugar levels and help treat diabetes
Lower cholesterol
Lower blood pressure
Reverse obesity related to a high-fat diet
BUT, do more research into figuring out the amount that is best for you.

There is also an interesting study by NCBI, "The effectiveness of a standardized rose hip powder, containing seeds and shells of Rosa canina, on cell longevity, skin wrinkles, moisture, and elasticity" that might be of interest to you.

I have been making other changes in my life, so I am not sure yet how much this product is influencing how I am doing on its own- which I can say that I am feeling better- a little more pep in my step. I will keep track of my blood pressure, and will know more with my next set of lab work if there is anything to bee gleaned from that. I'm active with my reviews, so I will be back to edit as I learn anything new. Take care!

title: gives dish that umami flavor
text: Perfectly good fish sauce. Just three ingredients: anchovies, salt, and sugar (though I bet, water too.) This is a must have ingredient to bring out that special savory taste in dishes. Purchased in a pack of two, I am set for fish sauce for awhile. It is one of those things that aren't going to go bad, and you dont want to run out of if your local grocer doesn't stock it.

title: perfectly good rice noodle for Pad Thai
text:
Mmm, I love making Pad Thai. While I can often times find rice noodles at the grocery store, I don't always see this size. That, and when I do find them, I usually only pick up what I need and not enough to stock my pantry. This is because the noodles are often over priced, particularly the name brand ones, not many on the shelf, and not always are there other varieties to choose from.
I am familiar with and like Thai Kitchen, so I was happy to see a multi box offering. I loved having multiple boxes arrive at my door, knowing that I am set for rice noodles for a little while.
I cook them according to direction and they turn out well (bring water to boil, turn off, add noodles, cover and let sit for 8-10minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water). I always cook up the whole box as my husband and have huge appetites, and any leftovers are welcome and will be devoured.

title: tangy, warm, not quite enough umami or sweet
text:
In and of itself, I like the flavor. It doesn't quite have that Pad Thai taste by itself though. I find it useful as a base but I definitely find the need to add fish sauce, usually a splash of rice vinegar, and sometimes lime and/ or sriracha to boost the flavor (basically Pad Thai flavorings). This sauce is a little tangy and a little spicy (warm, but not hot heat level). It has a slightly runnier ketchup consistency.
While I have felt the need to add flavors to it to taste more like restaurant pad thai, I do like it just out of the bottle on rice noodles too.
Outside of Pad thai use, I had used it for flavoring in a spicy peanut noodle bowl. I just had some of this and that in my fridge to use up, which can be easily replicated. I had some already cooked up rice noodles, as well as scallion/green onion, chicken and some extra firm tofu. I crisped up the tofu in coconut oil (added salt, cracked black pepper, and turmeric). Then placed them on a plate. Then I tossed the already cooked left over rice noodles in the still slightly oily and seasoned pan. Scraped those around to pick up flavor. Cut in some scallion/green onion. Added in some already cooked chicken. I added a splash of fish sauce, seasoned rice vinegar, a squirt of sriracha, then a big squirt or two of this Pad Thai sauce. Then I opened up a can of coconut milk, added about 1/2 a can to the pan. Sprinkled in a generous amount of peanut powder. Mixed it all together, then plated. I added the tofu pieces on top (reminded me of egg in a Pad Thai dish).
SO I think I will keep looking for a prepared Pad Thai sauce that has the flavor profile I am looking for. It might not happen; I may just need to keep making my own. That being said, this isn't a bad sauce, it just isn't quite what I am looking for, and it can be used in other dishes.

title: mouth puckering tart, tangy, with essence of sweet
text:
If you are looking to purchase barberries, then you are likely buying them as a super healthy addition to your diet. If you haven't researched the healthy aspects to berberine (naturally occurring in Barberries) then I recommend you do so. I have pointed out some very specific things in regards to this product (especially in labeling). Please read.

-------Taste-size-texture: ------

-->If you haven't had them before, I will describe the taste. The dried berries are small, easily half the size smaller than a dried cranberry or dried grape (raisin). If you know what dried Goji berries look like, this is very similar in look and size. Slightly softer in texture. The taste could be likened to a dried cranberry, unsweetened, of course. Though unsweetened cranberries seem to rare to find in stores and some people might be thinking "craisins"- that it is not!. So, if you have had an unsweetened dried cranberry, it is a little more tangy and tart than that. I liken the tart factor closer to a Kumquat fruit. The initial taste is a bright tart experience (like the tart of citric acid), followed by a mellow berry (like a cranberry) taste, with a very softly sweet finish.

-->Do not rely on this to add much of a sweet factor to your dish, trail mix, or baking. Enjoy it as a healthy addition, for a bright tang to balance sweet (M&Ms, nuts, and barberries would be great!, or a chicken/walnut/blue cheese salad with these sprinkles on top, etc- use it to balance sweet and tangy, or sweet and savory, etc). The company included a small leaflet that contains a few recipes with direction to find more on their website (though there weren't any on their site, just a display for purchasing a different product of theirs).

-----Packaging and label (what's on it, what isn't)-----

--> Freshness packaging. The berries are contained in a zip bag that is part Mylar, part plastic. No specific information on type of plastic, but it should be assumed food grade. Keep zipped, and in cool storage location.

-->The bag states to "clean and rinse with water before use". I am surprised by this, as I've never seen this on a bag of dried fruit before. Outside of soaking for culinary purpose, typically, one would not want them wet, especially if being added to a dry recipe such as trail mix. I did clean and rinse my second handful (since I took note of the tiny print only after seeing someone mention it in a review here, so I took a look and sure enough it says that). I found a sifter (since all my strainers have holes much too large for these dried berries), did a quick rinse, then spread them out on a paper towel. They looked pretty clean, with only a little bit of some red color transferring from berry to paper towel. I dabbed them dry and ate them as is on the spot. If I were intending them for trail mix use, and did not want any additional moisture, then I would go through same process and dab a few more times. I don't think I care to have to "clean and rinse with water before use".

-->Zero nutrition facts on bag. Nothing on website. Most of the information on this particular product will be found directly on this Amazon page, but still nothing regarding nutrition facts. See other brands, or do a general search for nutrient information.

-->Does not state where it is sourced from, just where it is distributed from.

-->Label states, "wild harvested". Searching for clarification as to where this company grows and "wild harvests" their berries, but no additional information comes up. I may send them a message asking for clarification. If I do, and if I find out anything helpful, I will add it to this review.. However, hopefully they would add such information to their label, website, and product description here on Amazon.

In of itself, the berries seem fine. It is the lack of additional information (anywhere!!), that displeases me. Potential consumers like to have information, in redundancy. Adding the typical curiosities to a product write up is going to help a potential buyer to make a decision toward purchasing it. Lack of information (and other companies that do have such clarifications easily available), will likewise guide a potential buyer away from purchasing this one and instead buy another. I think barberries are a worthwhile addition to the diet, and all things considered, I would be inclined to purchase from a more transparent company. I try to write reviews that help potential buyers as well as the companies when considering my words. Just my two cents!

title: reduced sodium option
text: Tastes fine, tastes like regular salt  when tested off my finger. I put some in a shaker, and I find that I am more apt to use it in larger batch cooking (such as soups and chili) as opposed to a quick shake on meals. I bought my container back in August 2018, and now six months later it is still fresh. I like the composition; I really should put it to the forefront of my salt shaking needs. It has sodium, so it isn't for you if you need a no salt diet. It is nice way to reduce sodium intake and to be able to ingest a few additional minerals.

title: delicious and convenient
text: Wonderful container of ginger juice. I don't always want to buy fresh ginger, and even when I freeze it, I don't always want to mess with that. I like having ginger juice on hand to add a splash of flavor into my cooking. I have added it into water for added kick of flavor. It isn't spicy hot like biting down on fresh ginger can be, yet there is no mistaking that this is ginger juice. Shake it before you use it. Enjoy! Yum Yum!

title: Long term storage
text: I must say, I have not yet tried this product. I bought it on a whim during a lightning sale. I like having foods in long term storage, so I scooped this up knowing I likely wouldn't be using it any time soon. It has a shelf life of 10 years if left unopened. I think there are 72 servings.  I may use it at some point for every day use, but for now, it is packed in with some emergency food supplies.

title: super strong, dark, wonderful
text: I love Green Mountain Dark Magic, and had been buying that for years, and no other kind. Recently I decided to try Double Diamond. I didn't expect it to impress me, and definitely didn't expect to like it more than Dark Magic. Well, I do. Double Diamond is even darker, bolder, stronger, and tastier than Dark Magic. I like them both, but if I had to choose I'd go with Double Diamond. When I brew a K-cup, I always choose the 10oz and just drink it. With Double Diamond, I did that and while I was loving the super strong taste at that level, I decided to brew in another 6oz of water. It was still deliciously strong! So now I feel like I am getting more bang for my buck since I can make a bigger cup of coffee with one K-cup. I'd say the Double Diamond will make for an excellent iced coffee when the season calls for it. It won't water down too easily. YUM!!!

title: delicious Lychee flavor
text: It is sweet, thick, and super flavorful. It is exactly what I was looking for in a lychee flavored syrup. Although super sweet, it tastes strongly of natural lychee fruit. I am impressed. It is perfect for use in homemade green tea & lychee bubble tea. Delicious!

title: tasty combo
text: Ingredients: black pepper, red pepper, sugar and spices (including paprika). I like the taste of this blend. I use a lot of black pepper in my dishes, so this is a nice change in flavor. Although sugar is listed, I do not taste sweet. It must be a minimal amount. As for "spices", I would like to have that clarified. "spices (including paprika)"- like, what other spices? It isn't salty, so I will assume no msg, but who knows. What are the other spices? Is it a secret blend?  Doesn't stop me from buying it, but I am sure curious.

title: dark, bold, smooth
text: I like very few k-cups across all brands. Green Mountain Dark Magic and Green Mountain Double Diamond are the only two I really like. Both are dark, smooth, and bold. Been drinking both for years, with Dark Magic for the greatest amount of time.

title: unique tangy salt free blend YUM!
text: I bought this on a whim. I am not on a low sodium diet, but I enjoy trying out different spices and what not to reduce my use of the salt shaker.  The combination of spices used in this magical blend is wonderful. I don't know exactly what it is, but the taste is bright, tangy, and it seems like it is salty! It does what Mrs. Dash can not do, and that is to hit your taste buds in the salty spot all the while adding other subtle flavors. I LOVE adding it to smashed avocados on toast. Usually I dose it with Redmonds Real Salt, fresh ground black pepper, and turmeric, but I decided to just sprinkle this on instead. WOAH. It made me fall in love with the product. SO much so that occasionally I dip my finger in for a taste of it by itself. I have used it on sliced tomatoes, eggs, mashed potatoes, and grilled chicken. I am sure there are some limitations depending on the flavor profile you are going for.. but if you just want to add a pop of salty flavor without the actual salt, this might be a good contender for you.  I'm back to buy more as a gift!

title: Perfectly peppermint- sweet, firm, melts in mouth, lightly peppermint. Refreshing!
text: I've never had these outside of a restaurant setting, you know when there is a little dish of wrapped peppermint candies  at check out, or some are delivered with the bill.  They are sweet, firm yet melt in the mouth, and lightly peppermint. YUM! The effect is refreshing and often helps settle my belly. I wasn't looking for them in the store, but I came across an 18oz tub of them in the holiday aisle of candies. On a whim I decided to add it to my basket. I'm so glad I did, and at the price I found them for I will have to go back for more. However, even if I didn't find them again it is nice to know I can find them here on Amazon (albeit a bit more pricey). I just got home with these and as soon as I popped one in my mouth I went online to see where else I can find them. That is how enthusiastic I am about these little candies. My plan for this container is to toss a few in with other candies as part of gifts, have a bowl of these sitting out in my house for whenever, and I bet they would be wonderful additions to add to some holiday baking. I usually buy a pack of candy canes to stick in a cup of hot chocolate, but I am going to instead toss in a few of these. Though they might not be minty enough for that application they will certainly look good. I love that they are made in the USA, in North Carolina.

title: tastes too green for my preference. earthy and bright over deep and bold
text:
I bought it on recommendation from a friend. It is "ok". It might be great for you though!

I like the powder-like ultra fine grind. Exactly what is needed to make Turkish coffee. The resulting color is beautiful. I expect it to tasted deep, dark, and bold. However, it is rather "green" in taste. Someone mentioned that it tastes like "dirt". I can see that. It has an earthy, bright flavor.

It is smooth, there is no bitterness to it at all, but it doesn't have the deeper taste that I prefer and expect from my Turkish cup of coffee. I tried it with a regular amount of coffee, then the next batch I added a whole lot more. Each batch was similar in taste, in that it had no depth. Again, love love love the ultra fine grind, just not the "green' taste. By no means do I consider it a sub par product. It came fresh, looks like it should, just has a different taste than what I prefer.

title: Tastes so much like their regular coffee I had to look at the box again to make sure it is decaf.
text:
At any other time in my life, I scoffed at the thought of consuming decaf. I mean, why bother right? Isn't the sole purpose of coffee consumption based on the fact that it contains mood and energy elevating caffeine? Sure, until it is the caffeine that is the common denominator for some troubling symptoms. I know, I know, caffeine is not necessarily bad, and in fact can be very very good. However, some people are sensitive to it, or become sensitive, or becomes part of the problem. *sad face*

For me, for a few reasons, I needed to cut back. Thought that wouldn't be a problem, except that in recent years, I had actually learned to enjoy the taste of *good coffee*, and would actually miss the taste and ritual of making a cup-- even with other fine substitutions that I use (dandelion coffee and other alternatives are very good-- but they are really only that- alternatives).

So, I was accidentally given a box of Newmans Own decaf, which sat unopened for a year. I recently decided to try it. Having had their original (good, but a little light for my taste), I thought maybe it would be an adequate substitution. I was wrong, it really tasted more like water than coffee. On the plus, I found it works well as a carrier for an evening cup of coffee and Irish Cream. My next foray into decaf was when I tried a sip of Donut House, and was pleasantly surprised that it had a regular coffee smell with a stronger (yet still inadequate) coffee flavor over the Newmans Own. I would buy Donut House again as it is at least readily available at local stores.

Since I am a great fan of Dark Magic extra bold k-cups, and have preferred them time and time again over several dozen other brands of Kcups, I decided to check out the reviews for their decaff offering between here, the company website, and the Keurig website. When I saw reviews that stated that they loved the regular, and thought the decaff tasted like the regular, I had to order a box immediately.

I drink 1/2 to one Dark Magic regular cup of coffee most mornings. However, if I find am not sleeping as well, or blood pressure is going up, or just don't feel the desire for caffeine (over taxed adrenals?), yet I still want a cup of coffee, a good cup of decaff does the job. I found that good cup in "Dark Magic Extra Bold Decaf"; it really does taste amazingly like their caffeinated counterpart. Nothing about it tastes like "brown water". It tastes like regular coffee. But you have to like bold, biting coffee.

Seriously, it tastes so much like regular coffee that I really did go back to the box, and the cups to make sure it said decaf.

I will be ordering this brand again. And again..

title: Eat this off the spoon, add it to your coffee
text:
I never would have thought I would get excited over molasses. It was always one of things in the cupboard that rarely made an appearance on the counter unless it was needed for some gingerbread baking recipe. Funny, it was baking that led me to try it in other applications. I was working on creating a cookie that didn't require much white sugar, and took a chance at using some of the contents from the dust covered jar of molasses (another popular brand). It tasted great, so much so that it became my "secret ingredient". One day not long after, I had a craving for molasses. Weird, right? I tried a spoonful, but didn't really care for the taste by itself. I then added it to my coffee and found that it lent an intriguing flavor. After all the NON gingerbread baking with my new found ingredient, I didn't have much molasses from the initial jar left. I don't think I ever saw what an empty jar of molasses looked like.. ha. So when that was empty, I made purchase of this Plantation brand, which happened to be the only kind of molasses in the store I was in that time. It was less than $5 for 15 oz. I brought it home and tried a small spoonful. It just opened up my senses and something about it really appealed to me. It tasted real, like it was something I should be eating daily. I then added it to my coffee, and was amazed/delighted/stoked about how well it went with my coffee (which I drink very dark/bold, and now also primarily drink coffee alternatives--which I have reviewed); like it was made to go together: Coffee, Molasses and..Me! (I told you upfront that I was excited over this stuff.) With this newly discovered affinity towards molasses, I had to research to see if there were any benefits to consumption. Well, indeed there is. There is no shortage of good information by placing these words into a search engine: "blackstrap molasses benefits", and what blackstrap molasses is versus molasses.
So how is this brand different than the others? It has a natural, lightly sweet taste. The flavor profile is coffee/caramel-like. Not tangy nor robust, like many others (which is probably best for baking and BBQ sauces). It has a deep dark flavor that is highly appealing. Closer in taste to buckwheat honey. Try drizzling it over high quality vanilla ice cream, and you will pick up on the caramel notes. My primary application is to coffee/coffee alternatives. I have since tried (some offered on Amazon, in larger quantity) other brands of "blackstrap molasses". I assumed they would all have the dark flavor compared to regular molasses. Not necessarily true. Some taste too bright and tangy. Some are good, but not quite like this one. So if you haven't been consuming molasses and would like to start, just know that it might take some time and money finding one that is perfect for your taste preference. All the more I can say about this brand is that I have seen several bottles become empty these past few months. As a side, these nice glass bottles can be reused as cleaning/personal care product containers by using the spray mechanism from a plastic bottle. Just cut the straw part down some. Enjoy!

title: Bottoms Up! not "coffee", but not bad.
text:
I like dark, bold coffee. Just black, or sometimes with blackstrap molasses. Usually organic but not always. If making a pot, I would drink the equivalent of one to two "k-cups" per day. Compared to some, that isn't excessive coffee consumption. The motivation for my switch from coffee is: 1. I wasn't getting much of a "buzz", just jitters, sleep disturbances, and no real "benefit" as in previous years. 2. elevated blood pressure that may benefit from cutting back/quitting caffeine sources, primarily that found in coffee beans. 3. Overall health. Coffee can be "good" for you, or depending on other factors, can be "bad". To each their own. I'd like a break from substances that: overtax my adrenals, encourage stress response (getting hyped up on coffee then sitting at desk could be bad; getting hyped up on coffee then engaging in laborious yard work, can be good), and anything that promotes a more acidic body state over an alkaline one. Taking a holiday from coffee seemed like a wise choice. Simply switching to "decaf" coffee will not address this, as it still contains some caffeine, acid is high, and toxicants from the decaffeination process is concerning. If I incorporate coffee beans again, I can cut it with this product. So, since I believe that nothing should be eliminated without an "adaptive alternative", I set out to try a few different types of coffee replacements. I like tea, all kinds, and drink it daily. For me, it is not an adequate alternative for my coffee fix. I wrote another review for a dandelion product that I like very much, and will continue to buy at this point in time as it is quick to make due to it being instant, and is especially good as an iced drink. As for Teeccino, I will continue to drink this as well. Unlike some of the instant variations, this brews like coffee, so the morning ritual is still in place. Something about hot brewed beverage that can't easily be replaced. The color and thickness appears to be coffee-like. The mouth feel is coffee like, as well as the taste. The taste isn't like the coffee I used to drink, but it can pass for coffee--maybe an offbeat coffee. This product has "coffee flavor" from coffee beans as an ingredient, which helps. There is a slightly odd fruity flavor that reminds me of raisins. I don't dislike it, but I wouldn't want it to be any more pronounced. I like a strong, smooth taste, so I make a strong brew by using 1 tablespoon per one measuring cup of water (not to be confused with cups on a coffee pot). This is the suggested ratio for iced coffee. Since I have gotten into the habit of adding unsulphered Blackstrap molasses to my coffee, I have continued to do so with Teecchino. It lends a deeper note, and a darker flavor with a hint of sweet. Blackstrap molasses is a worthy addition to coffee; however, there is great variation between brands. Some are tangy or robust (best for baking, BBQ sauces), while the kind I prefer has an almost coffee/caramel-like taste (which I reviewed as well). It just goes so well with coffee, or non coffee. Or vanilla icecream. :)
I will continue to try other coffee alternatives, but if I don't get around to it for awhile, I am satisfied with my introduction to this one.

title: dark rich coffee it is not, but it is an admirable alternative.
text:
It was surprisingly easy to swap out my morning cup of strong, fresh brewed coffee for this semi watery instant blend. Hot or cold, I like my coffee strong, black, and unsweetened; whether it be from fresh ground beans brewed in a pot, a cup made from the Keurig machine, or a tantalizingly thick and strong liquid made using the Turkish coffee method, and occasionally the double cold brew method for iced coffee on extra hot days. Oh geez, just writing that makes me want to get grinding. Alright, so, good coffee is a joy. So then, why would I look for an alternative? Well, I was ruminating about how drinking it day in and day out has lost much of its potency for me. Whether it was one cup or several, it was all the same. So then it became simply about the taste and MINDLESS routine/ritual. Could I possibly drink something else to get me through the day, then on more mindful occasions, truly enjoy all the taste and effects of coffee--such as that beautiful rush of energy that seems to have subsided? Without much effort or willpower, I decreased daily intake and found myself fine with one cup of coffee per day, occasionally more when it was just there. That has been a fair way to go, but I became increasingly more curious about coffee alternatives. I also drink tea, but that is not an "alternative" to me, nor pop/soda, nor straight carob powder. A true adaptive alternative needs to be close to the item or behavior one is looking to replace. Therefore I began looking online for something "coffee-like". I decided on DandyBlend because the ingredients sounded promising in terms of taste and health. No particular event prompted me to make a switch, it was more like a variety of things. While there appears to be benefit to daily consumption of coffee, there seems to be more benefit to not drinking it every day. Are my adrenals being over taxed? Can my mildly elevated blood pressure benefit from reducing/eliminating caffeine? Perhaps I can find more natural energy and better sleep with eliminating coffee? *If* I were to get pregnant/breastfeed, wouldn't I have to give up coffee *gasp* (and a host of other things) for quite some time? Hence my purchase of 2 lbs for $28 (for you K-cup drinkers, the coffee price per pound is $25-$60!).
The granules very much remind me of "instant coffee". Actually, it smells like it, and somewhat tastes like it, too, which is not necessarily a bad thing. My taste buds think I am drinking coffee, or something so close to it, that I am not craving coffee beans. I am also liking the expedited means of getting this beverage prepared as it dissolves easily in hot or cold water. Scoop out weeks worth or so out of the bag and into a glass container. Store the remainder in a cool spot or the refrigerator to maintain freshness and eliminate clumping. Let me tell you how I feel: The first day, I decided not to have any coffee at all, just DandyBlend. I felt alright. The second day I had a bit of a headache and felt fatigued. I decided to add a splash (1/8c) of coffee to my DandyBlend to help alleviate any withdrawal symptoms. This is a good way to go- reduce systematically which will benefit physiologically and psychologically. I did the same the next, then just didn't bother after that. The transition was quick for me. It has been a week. I have felt fine, much in the same way as I did with drinking the coffee, yet the energy source seems more natural than contrived, if that helps. For preparation, I use hot or cold water, then I add a teaspoon (sometimes even tablespoon) of unsulphered blackstrap molasses (good health benefits and adds to the "coffee" taste). Since I have been making a large cup of iced DandyBlend, I seem to use a lot of the powder. I treat this like "coffee" and don't drink it past noon, however, that is a personal choice, and I doubt it would hinder good sleep later. Adjust according to your taste. For what it is worth, and mind you, it has only been a week, and I engage in other healthful behaviors, my blood pressure has been stable (and healthy) for day time readings. Night time is another story, but I really need to not take a reading during or just after a PvP warzone match in an online MMO-RPG that I play, ha! (You gamers will know what I mean)

text:
I bought two of the original flavor. Delicious seven layer cake but must be refrigerated or frozen immediately when you receive it. It says on the box to immediately freeze it.

I couldn’t wait to try it so I opened one of the packages carefully and saw that the icing was going to stick to the inner wax paper or whatever it is that it was wrapped in, so I (reluctantly) refrigerated one and froze the other the cake.

The next day I took the refrigerated cake out and carefully removed the wax paper. The cake looked great. None of the icing stuck to the paper.

After you refrigerate the cake, the next day you can slice it easily. I've never been good at cutting cake so my photo looks a little messy.

The cake was moist enough and sweet enough without being overly sweet or dry.

I understand why some people were disappointed. Maybe they opened the cake right away instead of freezing it or refrigerating it. I’ve had that experience from other companies before when I bought Babka that stuck to the tinfoil wrapping.

text:
Don't waste your money. Try to find REAL CHESTNUTS and roast them yourself. Here, they try to get them around Christmastime. As you can see from my other reviews, when I like something, I like it! I usually adhere to the motto: "If you can't say something good, don't say anything". This time is different.

I have gone through five of the six bags, trying them by heating them up with salt, without salt and even trying them cold to see if there was any way they would taste good. They are HORRIBLE!

They are NOT the hot roasted chestnuts my dad always bought little bags of for us every Christmas in New York, from the street vendors. Those were real and those were delicious. They had the right texture, also, not like these.

I'm not sure what these things are, but they are NOT CHESTNUTS. I'm a New Yorker who moved south only a few years ago. I know roasted chestnuts. These are disgusting. I'm giving up and throwing away the last bag. I'd be too embarrassed to give them to my friends.

The image I had in my mind when I heard the words "bone broth" was something similar to the homemade beef or chicken stock I have prepared from scratch in the past- we raise our own chickens and get beef from neighbors, and before I had a full-time job I used to make my own stock by boiling bones and chicken feet. It was time consuming but worth it- freaking delicious; I'd freeze portions to use in cooking other meals. So when I heard I could add bone broth to my diet for added protein, I was really looking forward to adding a convenient pre-made, easy to drink broth that was similar to my homemade stock.

What I didn't take into consideration was when I made my own, I also added my own seasonings & salt to satisfy my personal preferences. Which made it that much more enjoyable.

This product was apparently seasoned by someone who considers mayonnaise spicy, or someone who has no taste buds. On its own, it is suuuuper bland with a weird, semi-beefy aftertaste that lingers in the back of your throat, almost like it's hanging onto that dangly thing and refusing to budge. It also doesn't smell appetizing at all, even after heating. (Not that it smells *bad* but the smell is a lot like the taste....it almost smells like nothing, but there is a sliiight hint of a weird, almost iron-y odor to it that does absolutely nothing to enhance the appeal factor)

I prepared my first serving at work, and I was so put off by the whole taste sensation that I was not able to drink a full serving. Maybe it's because my expectations were totally prepared for something different, but it was quite off-putting after a few big sips. It occurred to me afterwards that it would probably be vastly improved with some salt and some other seasoning, but since I was at the office I didn't have any of that on hand.

I still have 3 boxes left at home and I'm not giving up yet. Once the unpleasant memory of the initial experience fades, I plan to give it another try, and this time experiment with some sea salt & maybe some sage or chili powder. If I can get it to resemble the taste of my homemade stock, or even taste more like plain ol' beef broth, then I will be able to add this to my menu :)

text:
[[VIDEOID:d22fb6a1106723ad83dae58a0ed36556]] Hotep family Turmeric is a perennial herbaceous plant that reaches up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in) tall. It has highly branched, yellow to orange, cylindrical, aromatic rhizomes.
The leaves are alternate and arranged in two rows. They are divided into leaf sheath, petiole, and leaf blade. From the leaf sheaths, a false stem is formed. The petiole is 50 to 115 cm (20–45 in) long. The simple leaf blades are usually 76 to 115 cm (30–45 in) long and rarely up to 230 cm (7 ft 7 in). They have a width of 38 to 45 cm (15 to 17+1⁄2 in) and are oblong to elliptical, narrowing at the tip.
Inflorescence, flower, and fruit

Turmeric flower

Wild turmeric, Australia
At the top of the inflorescence, stem bracts are present on which no flowers occur; these are white to green and sometimes tinged reddish-purple, and the upper ends are tapered.
The hermaphrodite flowers are zygomorphic and threefold. The three sepals are 0.8 to 1.2 cm (3⁄8 to 1⁄2 in) long, fused, and white, and have fluffy hairs; the three calyx teeth are unequal. The three bright-yellow petals are fused into a corolla tube up to 3 cm (1+1⁄4 in) long. The three corolla lobes have a length of 1.0 to 1.5 cm (3⁄8–5⁄8 in) and are triangular with soft-spiny upper ends. While the average corolla lobe is larger than the two lateral, only the median stamen of the inner circle is fertile. The dust bag is spurred at its base. All other stamens are converted to staminodes. The outer staminodes are shorter than the labellum. The labellum is yellowish, with a yellow ribbon in its center and it is obovate, with a length from 1.2 to 2.0 cm (1⁄2 to 3⁄4 in). Three carpels are under a constant, trilobed ovary adherent, which is sparsely hairy. The fruit capsule opens with three compartments.
In East Asia, the flowering time is usually in August. Terminally on the false stem is an inflorescence stem, 12 to 20 cm (4+1⁄2 to 8 in) long, containing many flowers. The bracts are light green and ovate to oblong with a blunt upper end with a length of 3 to 5 cm (1 to 2 in).

Turmeric powder is about 60–70% carbohydrates, 6–13% water, 6–8% protein, 5–10% fat, 3–7% dietary minerals, 3–7% essential oils, 2–7% dietary fiber, and 1–6% curcuminoids.[8]
Phytochemical components of turmeric include diarylheptanoids, a class including numerous curcuminoids, such as curcumin, demethoxycurcumin, and bisdemethoxycurcumin.[8][4] Curcumin constitutes up to 3.14% of assayed commercial samples of turmeric powder (the average was 1.51%); curry powder contains much less (an average of 0.29%).[22] Some 34 essential oils are present in turmeric, among which turmerone, germacrone, atlantone, and zingiberene are major constituents. . title: A short history of l Lifesavers.
text:
[[VIDEOID:85f6745123c6041526ebffb53f1d0399]] Hotep brothers and sisters and thank you for looking at my review of Life Savers an American brand of ring-shaped hard and soft candy. Its range of mints and fruit-flavored candies is known for its distinctive packaging, coming in paper-wrapped aluminum foil rolls.
Candy manufacturer Clarence Crane of Garrettsville, Ohio (father of the poet Hart Crane) invented the brand in 1912 as a "summer candy" that could withstand heat better than chocolate. The candy's name is since its shape resembles that of a traditional ring-style life preserver also known as a "life saver".
After registering the trademark, Crane sold the rights to his Pep-O-Mint peppermint candy to Edward John Noble for $2,900. Instead of using cardboard rolls, which were not very successful, Noble created tin-foil wrappers to keep the mints fresh. Noble founded the Life Savers and Candy Company in 1913 and significantly expanded the market for the product by installing Life Savers displays next to the cash registers of restaurants and grocery stores. He also encouraged the owners of the establishments to always give customers a nickel in their change to encourage sales of the 5¢ Life Savers. The slogan "Still only 5 cents" helped Life Savers to become a favorite treat for children with a tight allowance. Since then, many different flavors of Life Savers have been produced. The five-flavor roll first appeared in 1935.
A series of mergers and acquisitions by larger companies began in 1956. Life Savers is currently a property of Mars, Incorporated. In recent decades, the brand expanded to include Gummi Savers in 1992, Life Saver Minis in 1996, Creme Savers in 1998, and Life Saver Fusions in 2001. Discontinued varieties include Fruit Juicers, Holes, Life Saver Lollipops, and Squeezit.
Life Savers was first created in 1912 by Clarence Crane, a Garrettsville, Ohio, candy maker (and father of the famed poet Hart Crane). Clarence had switched from the maple sugar business to chocolates the year before, but found that they sold poorly in the summer, because air conditioning was rare, and they melted. He saw a machine pharmacies used to make pills that were round and wafer-shaped, and thought he'd use those to make mints, which at the time were made square (because they were pressed in sheets and then sliced into squares). The machinery could also punch a hole in the center, and Crane named the candy after its resulting life preserver shape.
In 1913, Crane sold the formula for his Life Savers candy to Edward Noble of Gouverneur, New York for $2,900. Noble started his own candy company and began producing and selling the mints known as Pep-O-Mint Life Savers. He also began to package the mints into rolls wrapped in tin foil to keep them from going stale. This process was done by hand until 1919 when machinery was developed by Edward Noble's brother, Robert Peckham Noble, to streamline the process.
In 1921, the company began to produce solid fruit drops. In 1925, technology improved to allow a hole in the center of the fruit candies. These were introduced as the "fruit drop with the hole" and came in Orange, Lemon and Lime, each of which were packaged in their own separate rolls. In contrast to the opaque white mints previously produced by the company, these new candies were crystal-like in appearance. These new flavors quickly became popular with the public. Four new flavors were quickly introduced, namely, anise, butter rum, cola and root beer, which were made in the clear fruit drop style. Other than butter rum, which remains in the brand's lineup of flavors, these did not prove to be as popular as the three original fruit drop flavors. In 1931, the Life Savers "Cough Drop" was introduced with menthol, but it was not successful. In 1931, rolls of pineapple and cherry fruit drops were also introduced. As the public response proved positive for these, a new variety of mint called Cryst-O-Mint, made in this same crystal-like style, was introduced in 1932. In 1935, the classic "Five Flavor" rolls were introduced, offering a selection of five different flavors (pineapple, lime, orange, cherry, and lemon) in each roll. This flavor lineup was unchanged for nearly 70 years, until 2003, when three of the flavors were replaced in the United States, making the rolls pineapple, cherry, raspberry, watermelon, and blackberry. However, orange was subsequently reintroduced .

• 1912: Crane's Peppermint Life Savers created by Clarence Crane in Garrettsville, Ohio.
• 1913: Edward Noble bought the Life Saver formula, renamed Pep-O-Mint Life Savers, and started Mint Products Company in New York City.
• 1921: The first fruit flavors were produced as solid candies.
• 1925: Technology improved to allow a hole in the center of the fruit candies.
• 1927: Cherry flavor is invented and added to regular flavors.
• 1935: The original Five Flavor roll of Life Savers debuted.
• 1956: Life Savers Limited merged with Beech-Nut.
• 1968: Beech-Nut Life Savers merged with Squibb.
• 1981: Nabisco Brands Inc. acquired Life Savers from the E.R. Squibb Corporation.
• 1987: Canadian Life Savers business acquired by Hershey Canada.
• 1992: Life Savers Gummies launches in three varieties: Grape, Five Flavor, and Mixed Berry.
• 1996: Canadian Life Savers business acquired by Beta Brands Limited.
• 2000: Kraft acquires Nabisco.
• 2001: Kraft acquires Canadian Life Savers business from Beta Brands.
• 2004: Life Savers business acquired by Wrigley's.
• 2008: Mars acquires Wrigley.

These Vanilla Sweet Crisps taste good. My problem with them is there were no chips in the bag. The only thing in the bag was crumbs like the bottom of a chip bag. Packaging should be better tested. If I bought these in the store I would take them back. I have been trying to determine what these crumbs might be good with.

The crisps are sweet and would probably be crips like crakers but with all the crumbs that was hard to determine. The package says there are 120 calories per 17 crisps I can't say if that is true or not. It would be hard to know if I had 17 crisps or not.

I will not be recommending these Vanilla Sweet Crisps to family and friends. If they perfect the packaging I would be willing to try them again. The flavor was very vanilla and I do like that.

title: I don't drink coffee often but I like this.
text:
This Torrefacto Premium Instant Coffee is perfect for me. I don't drink a lot of coffee so this instant gives me the right amount. I have only tried the vanilla and it is good.

The pack comes in three flavors Chocolate, Vanilla, and Cubano Silver. Each jar contains 8 ounces of coffee. The measurements are in metric but I used 1 heaping teaspoon.

I have recommended Torrefacto Premium Instant Coffee to family and friends.

title: Everything I tried was delicious and fresh.
text:
This Cappadocia Foreign Snacks Box is great. I love the variety in the box. Everything I tried I loved.

The box comes packed full of candy, cookies, and chips. Everything was fresh and the taste was wonderful. There is something in this box for just about anybody.

I have already recommended this Cappadocia Foreign Snacks Box to family and friends.

title: The flavors are wonderful.
text:
This s.a.l.t. sisters Grill Master Sample Kit is great. I used it on pork and chicken, both were delicious. When I opened the box I knew I was going to love it, it smelled wonderful.

The box comes in 10 flavors. Each flavor comes in a resealable plastic bag with the name of the seasoning on the individual bags. There is an enclosed card to let you know more about the individual seasonings and salts. It also comes with a recipe using each seasoning or salt.

I will be recommending this s.a.l.t. sisters Grill Master Sample Kit to family and friends.

title: Not what I am used to.
text:
This PREMIUM Korean Snack Box has a lot of snacks. I tried several bags of chips and some of the cookies. They are all fresh and crisp. They just do not appeal to my taste buds. The cookies are not as sweet as I am used to and the chips have flavors that just don't seem to go with chips. I will not go through all of the things I tried since it was most of everything in the box.

The box comes with several bags of chips, a sweet and sour rice cake, an orange drink, a small container of fruit jelly, an assortment of crackers and cookies. One of the things I tried was "Honey Butter Chip" I didn't like the first bite but I did eat two just to see if they would taste better. They did not.

I will not be recommending this PREMIUM Korean Snack Box to family and friends but I will tell them about it and if they want to try it I will give them the name and where I got it.

title: Not impressed - wasn't any different than any other food coloring.
text:
This Oil Based Food Coloring for Chocolate worked no different than any other food coloring. I used it in frosting and in white chocolate. I was not impressed.

The pack comes in 10 colors. It is an oil-based coloring that looks bright until it is mixed. To get the exact color on the bottle, a lot of coloring would have to be used.

I will not be recommending this Oil Based Food Coloring for Chocolate to family and friends.

title: Fun to use.
text:
These DOMISL Edible Markers were fun. My cake didn't look great but I did have fun. I think I should have put it in the refrigerator or freezer before drawing on it. There weren't any directions so I just played. I will be trying this again.

The set comes with 10 different colors of edible ink. There is a brush on one end and a blunt tip on the other. I used both tips and all of the colors. They worked okay but will probably work better on a cold frosting.

I will be recommending these DOMISL Edible Markers to family and friends.

title: Delicious!
text:
This Cerez Pazari Turkish Delight is absolutely delicious. My husband and I were a little skeptical, we usually are trying new things. We both took a little bite and then a few pieces.

This candy is a little chewy, not as much as caramel but chewy. It has good size pieces of nuts in the candy. Powdered sugar covers the candy that is cut into little squares.

I will be recommending this Cerez Pazari Turkish Delight to family and friends.

title: Good. Less salt than peanuts.
text:
These Original Wild Sprouted Pili Nuts are good. They have a good flavor and they are a little bit softer than peanuts. The salty part fills the salt craving for me.

These nuts are shaped similar to peanuts that have been halved. They are not as salty as peanuts so that is good for me since I am watching my sodium intake. I can't say these would be one of my favorites but they are good.

I will be recommending these Original Wild Sprouted Pili Nuts to family and friends.

title: These are delicious!
text:
These Keto Snacks Salty Parmesan Cheese Crisps are delicious. I wasn't too sure about them when I opened them but I was pleasantly surprised. If you have ever cooked with cheese, like grilled cheese and the cheese seeps into the pan and hardens a little that is what this tastes like. I love them.

The pack comes with three individually wrapped boxes. I opened the box and smelled them. They smelled wonderful. I love the taste, I can stop eating them!

I have already recommended these Keto Snacks Salty Parmesan Cheese Crisps to family and friends.

title: A delicious burst of flavor.
text:
These Angelic Bakehouse Pickled Onion Beet Snack Crisps have a great flavor. They are crispy and crunchy. I had a different idea of how they would taste, with the name I was thinking something sour. They are not. The taste is almost like a garlic rye chip. When I first bit into it the flavor burst in my mouth but before I finished chewing it the favor was gone and you are left with a dried bread taste.

The nutrition on the back is 120 calories for 14 crisps. If you are counting carbs you will have 17g. If you are counting fat grams they have 5g. If you need more protein, they have 4 grams. So, the nutrition is not to bad, except sodium which is 260 mg.

I will be recommending these Angelic Bakehouse Pickled Onion Beet Snack Crisps to family and friends.

title: I regret to say I will be tossing this out!
text: I was so excited to get to try this Plant Junkie Vegan, Plant-Based Avocado Oil Chipotle Lime Spread. My husband loves Chipotle anything. I like it too, but this was horrible.  Since I always give things a second try. I put it in the refrigerator to get it really cold but it was just as bad. I regret to say I will be tossing this out!

title: It literally made my husband sick.
text:
This bar smells delicious when you open the plastic pouch. I told my husband if it tastes as good as it smells it will be great. I was wrong. The first bite was tasty until I began to chew. The texture is horrible and the flavor gets worse the more you chew.

My husband ate his whole bar and was very sick a little while later. I would not recommend this EPIC Beef Sea Salt + Pepper Protein Bar to anyone.

title: Delicious
text: Chef-mate White Cheddar Cheese Sauce is delicious. I do not like all canned or jar cheese sauce but this one is a winner. I made shells and cheese and we loved it. I plan to make a dip of Chef-mate White Cheddar Cheese Sauce, diced tomatoes and green chilies, and sausage this weekend.

title: Delicious
text: I wasn't sure if I would like this or not because I do not like milkshakes and that is what it reminds me of. These Premier Protein Shakes with oats are delicious. I love the blueberries & cream. The flavor is more than I could have hoped for. I need more protein and this will be the perfect way to get that. I will be recommending this product to anyone that will listen!

title: No real flavor
text: When I opened the container the aroma was magnificent. I just had to try it right away. I did just as instructed and was so disappointed.  The aroma was still there but the flavor was not. I then decided to try it cold and see if I could make it stronger. The results were the same. No real flavor.

title: Delicious
text: I wasn't too sure about this product when I ordered it. I have been so disappointed in the past with this type of snack, but these ORCHARD VALLEY HARVEST Omega-3 Mix are absolutely delicious. I would recommend this to my family and friends.

title: Excellent Flavor and Texture
text: These are excellent gluten free snack bars. The flavor is very good and the bars are soft and easy to chew. The 8 grams of protein in each bar make them a good choice for training. I like to take one of these bars with me when I go for a run. They are easy to digest and give you a burst of energy. These bars are an effective, satisfying and healthy choice.

These gummies taste great and they are very useful for improving your overall health.

title: Good Flavor
text: I've never had golden milk before, but I really enjoyed this drink. It has a pleasant aftertaste of black pepper, but it's not overpowering. The bag zips closed to preserve freshness and it doesn't take up much shelf space. I mix a teaspoon of powder into a cup of warm almond milk. It makes for a drink that is pleasant to sip and smell. This golden milk powder is a convenient and enjoyable way to adopt a healthier lifestyle.

title: Great Selection of Candy
text: This product is an excellent bulk supply of candy. It is a good choice for Christmas, Halloween, parties, or just for having around the house. I like having a bowl of candy on my coffee table for visitors. This bulk supply is ideal because it offers a wide variety of flavors and is sure to contain everyone's favorite. This is a great product that will provide you with a terrific selection of tasty snacks.

title: Delicious Torte
text: This torte is absolutely delicious and it makes a thoughtful Christmas gift for friends and family. It has become a part of my family's holiday tradition.

title: Very Pleasant Flavor
text:
This is a very agreeable coffee with a pleasing flavor and a pleasant aroma. The bag can be opened by hand and does not require an unreasonable amount of force. You can grind the beans in a standard grinder for a medium roast coffee.

The flavor is very smooth with almost no bitterness. This is a pleasant coffee that does not have an overpowering flavor and is tasty alone or with added milk and/or sugar. I would get this coffee again. It's a good choice and pairs well with a standard breakfast.

title: Delicious Cookies
text:
This is a standard three pack of Oreo cookies. The size of each pack measures 10" X 6.5" so this is the same size pack you are familiar with from your local grocery store. The three flavors are original, double stuff, and golden cookies. The golden cookies have the same amount of white filling as the original cookies. I like these cookies for a quick boost of sugar after you go for a run or perform any other form of exercise. They are also always a hit with kids.

The packaging is very nice because it allows you to reseal the flap and keep the cookies fresh. These are the same great cookies you remember from childhood and it's nice to have a pack with all three flavors. They are perfect for snacking or dessert!

title: Delicious Apple Sauce
text: This sweetened apple sauce is perfect for kids. The flavor is much better than regular apple sauce without being overly sweet. The texture is smooth and without chunks which makes it perfect for very small children. This apple sauce makes a great, satisfying, and healthy snack which is ideal for both children and adults.

title: Good Soup
text: This is a standard can of cream of chicken soup that tastes good and has a pleasing texture. I like to use this as a base and add extra water, rice, and chicken for a hearty meal. Preparation is easy, you just pour the contents of the can into a pot and add water. Keep your stove on low to medium heat for best results. You don't need a can opener because it is a peel open tin can. It's good to have a couple cans of this in your pantry for a variety of cooking needs.

title: Delicious Coffee
text: This is some of the best coffee I've ever tasted. True to the label, it has the distinctive flavor of bourbon and vanilla. When you serve it with a little bit of cream, the result is something like a warm cup of Baileys Irish Cream. The package is relatively small, but the smooth flavor of this coffee is absolutely delicious. Whole beans help to preserve the flavor, so you need your own grinder to enjoy this package. Also included is a small bag of Peaberry coffee beans coated in semi-sweet chocolate. This coffee truly stands out as superior.

title: Good Flavor
text: This is a nice pack of coffee with a good, strong flavor. It is a rich, medium roast when taken black and with a bit of cream and sugar it provides a very pleasant taste. I practice intermittent fasting where I drink only coffee two days a week and this is a perfect choice for that. The packages are easy to reseal and they help keep the coffee tasting fresh. This is a good coffee to get you up and going in the morning.

title: Tasty and Easy to Make
text:
This 8 pack of convenient pancake mix is a great item for your pantry. We usually have pancakes once a week at my household and the kids love mixing and flipping the pancakes as they cook. This is a just add water mix, but you can also add an egg, or substitute milk for water if you want more protein in your pancakes. These pancakes have good flavor and the greater amount of protein helps sustain you throughout the morning.

I found that I needed to spray my griddle with cooking oil or butter between batches to keep the pancakes from sticking. It's nice to have extra boxes of pancake mix in the pantry for those days when you are late shopping and your growing kids need something to eat quick. These pancakes are tasty and easy to make.

title: Ideal Flavor and Texture
text: These are really good energy bars that are ideal for activities like running, cycling, cross-country skiing or any other endurance sport. The bars themselves look like a fancy pastry you'd get at a coffee shop. These bars are from the coffee collection and they have a subtle hint of the aftertaste you get when you eat a chocolate covered coffee bean. The bars have a soft texture that is easy to chew, and they have a pleasant taste without being overly sweet. This is a perfect mid-workout bar because they are easy on the stomach and provide plenty of fuel. These are some of the best tasting energy bars available and are perfect for coffee lovers.

title: Smooth and Agreeable Coffee
text: This is a delightful Italian coffee with a smooth flavor that has no bitter aftertaste. The grains are extremely fine and this is a good choice for either a drip or a press coffee maker. The package describes "floral and fruity notes" but I didn't detect anything that I would call sweet. Instead, I think this description reflects the coffee's mellow finish. This is a nice morning coffee because it is subtle with a good flavor. Anyone with a passion for coffee will enjoy this organic, premium blend.

title: Great Mint Flavor
text: I've always been a fan of Kit Kat and I like this new twist on an old favorite. The bars have a mint topping that is the same texture as a standard Kit Kat, combined with dark chocolate on the bottom. The wafer in the middle seemed to be the same as any other Kit Kat. The overall effect is very pleasant, and reminded me of a thin mint but with the additional crunch of the wafer. This is a good candy bar to eat by itself, or to use to adorn a bowl of peppermint ice cream. You could even break up the bar and use the individual sticks as stirring rods in an adult drink at a Christmas themed party. Everyone loves Kit Kat, and if you have a tray of these sitting out, people will be excited to try them.

title: Great Coffee
text: This product comes exactly as advertised. The bags of coffee that are provided are exactly the same size as any other coffee provider. It is ground coffee, and the bag has a folding tab so that you can reseal it after use and preserve the flavor. The flavor is very good, I always drink my coffee black and found this Colombian ground coffee to be rich without being excessively bitter. This is a great choice for a gift because who wants to run out of coffee? Recommended.

title: Great for Hydration
text: This stuff is addictive. I started drinking coconut water at the local Thai restaurant and I've developed a taste for it. Actually, it has about the same effect as an energy drink but I believe there are fewer calories in this than in something like a Gatorade. It's very tasty and great for quenching thirst. I only wish it was a bit cheaper.

text:

I like having these "flavor splash" bottles around because they keep me from "impulse eating."
