title: Be a barista hero
text:
I started really enjoying making my own pour-over coffee at home, but my wife missed the flavor shots you can pump at a coffee shop. This is so cool, it's pretty much the same vanilla syrup you can get at a big brand coffee shop, and it comes with its own pump to screw in! Bring the cafe experience home with you!
Now we really feel like our coffee at home is just as good if not better than going out for coffee (I say it's better!). Highly recommended, really good!

title: Super Kosher, alternative to "Tam Tam"
text:
Some background: The classic "Tam Tam" cracker is a staple snack, every strictly Kosher keeping individual in the USA should be familiar with it. Their everything flavor was one of my favorite foods as a kid, and every Jewish community I visited had it on their store shelves.
This new Kravy brand has their own take on it, with a somewhat more understandable name: These are made for dips, and calling it Dip Dip just makes a lot of obvious sense. (I believe the original name Tam Tam came from the Hebrew word Ta'am, for flavor, but I didn't know until someone pointed it out as an adult)
They are very tasty, the everything bagel style spices are perfect for using it with cheeses or dips, and the crunch doesn't disappoint either. I'm also a huge fan of seeing the ultra kosher certification on these available in Amazon. Kosher certification has different levels, with the strictest standards usually found in smaller pockets of the Hassidic population. But this product has the stamp of one of the highest standard certifications available. I'm not used to seeing it on products available through Amazon and it warms my heart to see now. Great product for your next Kiddush! (with herring of course!)

title: SUPER Kosher and tastes great!
text:
I got a 3 pack of the Pizza flavor to review, so I can't comment on the other flavors. However I can tell you that the Pizza ones I got are actually really tasty. They aren't very strong flavored, which I actually prefer. I was expecting a strong artificial saucy/spice flavor, but it is much more subtle. My family went through all three bags really quickly, so I guess they agree with me about that flavor! Don't expect to reseal the bag once opened, you will most likely finish it!
As a strictly kosher household, I actually really appreciate seeing brands like this available on Amazon. There are varying levels of kosher certification, and this brand has opted for some of the strictest and highest standard one there is. I don't require such a strict certification personally, but I love seeing it available on Amazon.

title: Turn any flavor syrup into a cafe-style pump!
text:
We've been loving DaVinci and Jordan's coffee flavor shots in our morning cup, but I've been using the bottle caps to measure. Not really ideal and sometimes kind of messy. I was looking around for a product like this and SO HAPPY we got to try one!
These look intimidating at first because they are taller than I expected, but they actually work perfectly- they turn my syrups into pump bottles like the café shops. It's not only more precise and less messy, it's actually fun! Very highly recommended!

title: Making your home a coffee shop
text:
This has become a staple in our household. My wife loves this in her coffee, the hazelnut flavor in particular. I may need to work out a subscribe and save deal to keep these in stock, last time we ran out I tried a local store brand and it just wasn't the same.

If you want to give your homemade coffee a flavor shot but avoid the calories, this is the good stuff.

title: Light, Airy and "Mezonos"
text:
This is a very light, crunchy and airy toast style snack, something more like large disc shaped salad crouton. The box comes with 3 cylinders of them, so for the price offered here you are actually getting 3 packages- I'm not sure why the listing doesn't show a picture of three, but you are in fact getting 3x of these. Paskez is a well brand in the Kosher food world, I'm actually not used to seeing it sold on Amazon so this is a pleasant surprise, and great for people who perhaps don't live near a kosher market to find them.
For religious folks concerned about this being "hamotzie", the package informs you that they are, in fact, "mezonos" (for those who know what that means).

I like them, they are great with dips or crumbling over salads. I'm surprised that for a whole grain snack that claims to healthy, it has 0 grams of fiber. But they seem more healthy than your average crouton for the same serving size, and are definitely lighter than things like Wasa bread. My kids are enjoying them as after school snacks with Nutella or cream cheese.

title: Good and relatively healthy coffee alternative
text:
I've had this flavor of Yogi tea before, so I knew what to expect in this case: A lot of individually wrapped caffeinated teabags! The flavor is not as harsh as other caffeine teas, and the added aroma of the other ingredients makes it a really pleasant alternative to coffee.
I can't comment on the accuracy of the health benefit claims, but I like it and definitely would recommend it.

title: So much more than Oatmeal
text:
To be honest, I was a bit unsure of what to expect with this product when I saw the ingredients. Things like quinoa, rye, etc offer very different flavors to oats, and I wasn't sure they would blend well together. But I'm happy to say it works, and quite well! My kids who tend to be pickier about their flavors even enjoy it, and as parents I like that it has more protein and fiber than your average oatmeal as well as a more adult flavor.
Really impressed with this product and I would recommend it!

title: Big ol' bag of gum!
text: I love classic Double Bubble gum, and this appears to be a wholesale-volume (think: Costco) sized bag of the stuff! It's the legitimate Double Bubble brand, each individually wrapped with the unmistakable label inside. Just repacked by a Cambie in a bulk sized pack. Very convenient especially for kids who can't get enough gum. The resealable bag is a nice touch compared to other bulk double bubble packs I've seen. Thumbs up.

title: A decent coffee for the money
text:
I'll be honest, coffee from Amazon is a gamble, usually. I've had some that was AMAZING one time, and then the same brand could be terrible the next time. I prefer local roasters because I know it is fresh as opposed to guessing how long this was in a warehouse shelf. I'm hard to please with my coffee, I guess. But this... was actually good, especially considering I don't even usually like Colombian coffee that much. I had a guest staying over who enjoys a medium roast like this so I figured it was worth a try in our pour over setup. I enjoyed it more than I expected to!

I still prefer local fresh coffee beans, but I have to admit, this seems like a really good amount of coffee for the asking price.

title: What's better than a tub of Nutella?
text:
Why, two tubs obviously! If you've never had Nutella before, what rock have you been hiding under? This stuff is GREAT and my kids are huge fans, especially since we have a peanut allergy in the house. My daughter used to feel bad that her friends could have peanut butter and fluff sandwiches, but no more! Nutella on bread is delicious (although admittedly, not exactly diet friendly!). And since it is hazelnut and chocolate, it doesn't irritate someone with peanut/legume allergies.
These containers will last us for a while, its a good value for an excellent product.

title: A GIANT can of awesomesauce!
text: What's better than a can of Heinz classic spaghetti sauce? how about a GIANT can of spaghetti sauce?! This is all the goodness that you expect from the ketchup and sauce behemoth that is Heinz, but on a massive scale. Seriously, if you're having a TON of family for a holiday, this is a lot easier and cost effective than many smaller cans. Shown is the giant can next to a regular sized can of baked beans for scale. Only those who are serious about their sauce should apply. Excellent product!

title: Good, but not as good as other flavors
text:
I'd say these deserve 3.5 starts, but I'm rounding up to 4. They are excellent for keto style diets, full of protein and low carb, just like real cheese... because it IS real cheese! These aren't cheese crackers or cheese puffs, they are actually dehydrated cheese! Real chedder so dehydrated, it no longer needs refrigeration and can actually CRUNCH in your mouth!
Here's the problem- while it has plenty of cheder sensations going down, in this dehydrated state it seems to lack some of the sodium flavor I associate with cheese. This brand also makes a spicy Pepper Jack flavor that has a real KICK, spicy and delicious. I tried that one first and LOVED it, however my kids found it too spicy for their taste. So I tried this next, thinking it would be a step down in kick. But it's almost like it stepped down TOO much, and just feels like it lacks flavor. My kids found it bland. So the first flavor was too much, and this one was too little. I actually opened a bag and poured it into a bowl and added some salt to experiment, and the flavor GREATLY improved! It's like, they were SO close to making a perfect snack, but just skimped a bit on the sodium to make it less flavorful. It's a shame because otherwise I really like this snack. I'll still eat it because it's a healthy diet friendly crunchy snack, but I can't help wishing they just added a tad more salt to bring out the flavors within. I still recommend the pepper jack, if you want bold flavor especially.

title: Pure cheese, and SPICY
text:
Ok, I'm going to admit this is not everyone's taste, my kids weren't really into the sharp spice of this flavor, but I really like the bite from it! The interesting thing about this snack is that it isn't cheese puffs or some other cheese flavored snack like I thought it was... no sir, this is actual DEHYDRATED CHEESE, removed of so much moisture it actually becomes crunchy balls that don't require refrigeration!
The good news is that it comes with all the concentrated goodness that cheese offers, specifically high amounts of protein and flavor. The bad news is that it comes with all the bad stuff too, like 13 grams of fat per serving. This is a great option if you're on a Keto style diet, but don't be like me and eat 3 bags in one sitting. You will regret it. But that flavor is just so addictive!

title: YUM.
text: Oh my goodness, my family loves this. This is a box of delicious portion-sized individual bags of... well I guess I'd call them cookies more than pop-tarts. They're using the name of the product you know, but they are similar only in as much as they are filled with something fruity inside a pastry/cookie outside. Basically a filled cookie. But no complaints here, they're really tasty! My kids take one in their lunch bag for school, and sometimes I'll sneak one at home too. Thankful that they are portion controlled so I don't overindulge.

title: Variety pack of name brand chocolate!
text: This is a very decent mix of various classic chocolate candies. Everything from M&Ms, Almond Joy, Kit Kat, Reeses, Twix, Snickers... the greats! It's been a while since I bought some of these individually, so having a multi-pack like this for me and my kids to enjoy is a real treat! The package came in a no-frills box, so thankfully nothing inside was damaged or melted or anything like that. It probably helps that I ordered this in the winter months, I wonder how it would do in the middle of the July. For now, I have only good things to say about it.

title: The candy is great, but not much of a mix
text:
I'll start with the good: There's some great candy varieties in here with plenty of shelf life left. My kids enjoyed picking through and finding some we haven't had in a while.
The not so good: Honestly, I love Snickers so I was happy to see so many in here. But if feels like almost half the bag is Snickers, as you can see in the picture. It sort of takes away from the "variety" feel when there's a largely dominant candy taking up a percentage of the bag.
The less good: Honestly, it's a really hard sell at nearly $20 per bag. I feel like if I went around Walmart and found candy bags (especially on sale), I could make a similar 2lb bag for significantly less. I guess the idea is that you're paying for the convenience of a variety bag, but again- the variety feels overshadowed by Snickers.

title: Making a classic kid friendly!
text:
Corn Flakes is a classic, but not necessarily a fan favorite with kids for breakfast. Sure, we can add tons of sugar and call it Frosted Flakes, but this is much better approach in my opinion. It's got some added sugar, but not the level that Frosted Flakes does.
However the touch of cinnamon gives it a decidedly more robust and mature flavor, one that both myself and my kids appreciate! Otherwise all the goodness of Corn Flakes is still to be found, and I like that it is still close enough to the original to warrant keeping the name and logo. So far my family is loving this, and I'll bet yours will too!

title: YUM
text:
Ok, I went into this with low expectations- I usually don't like gluten free foods very much, I don't like the taste, find them very heavy feeling and dense in my stomach, and generally notice them not all that healthy re: nutrition information. But I REALLY like this cereal. Like, REALLY like it.
It's sort of like a chocolate cheerios, however it tastes more "adult", like more of a natural cocoa flavor than a super sweetened mass produced sugary product. They somehow packed in a TON of protein, which is super cool, and it even has a respectable amount of fiber as well. This fits almost every diet rule I've been on. The only thing I don't particularly like about it is the high fat content, however that's something I'm used to seeing in gluten free foods. It doesn't feel particularly heavy when you eat it either.
They say this is for adults, and even have a tagline about you grew up, shouldn't your cereal... but I have to admit, I've got kids who seem to love it as much as I do! At least the box I got came in a multi-pack. I may have to hide the last boxes so I get some!

title: Ashwaghanda Forever! But suspicious claims to Kosher?
text:
Sorry about the title, I can't say Ashwaghanda out loud without making a Black Panther reference. As for this product, I like that it seems to be a fine powder that will dissolve easily and not add any detectible smell or consistency change to your drinks or smoothies. I've heard all kinds of claims about this stuff, and I'm not entirely sure if I can confirm or deny any of it concretely, however I will say this: It claims to be "kosher", but there is no symbol of the certifying agency on the package. As someone who keeps a kosher home, I'm well aware that there are different levels of kosher that are acceptable in different households, all depending on who certified it.
I've seen other products from Pomona that were certified, but claiming to be kosher without a certifying symbol on this one is fishy to me. I'm a little bit disappointed about that.

title: Some of the best coffee beans I've tried to date
text:
I'm a big fan of local roasted for freshness, but this has got to be one of the best whole bean coffee I've ever had, forget from a warehouse like Amazon, I think possibly in ever! I've been told good things about Yirgacheffe from friends who are coffee connoisseurs, and after being impressed with another style bean from this brand, I wanted to see what Rako has to offer.
Was not disappointed! This makes some seriously smooth and tasty coffee! Highly recommend it for your at-home pour over!

title: Good product, but not as good as their whole bean
text:
After loving some whole bean blends from this brand, I decided to try a ground bag for the convenience of not having to grind it up.
Well, I have to say, I personally would rather stick to their whole bean ones. This isn't bad, but it lost a lot of what I really loved about their whole bean options compared to local roasters. This bag tastes on par with other ground coffees that can be found in local stores, which is to say it is fine but nothing special. Decent coffee.

title: For those who prefer a lighter roast
text: I LOVE light roast coffee, but prefer the more controlled caffeine of a darker one. This coffee is some of the BEST medium I've ever had! It tastes light and smooth, low acidity and delicious with a spot of oat milk. I know, big coffee drinkers prefer black and dark roasts, but I served some to a guest without milk who agreed that was phenomenal coffee. Very impressed with this brand, I highly recommend it!

title: Excellent for strong coffee lovers
text:
This is a strong and bold flavor, which is indicative of the dark roast it claims to be. I actually really like the smell coming out of the bag, it's almost intoxicating! I'm still experimenting with different types of coffee since the pandemic to see what the wife and I prefer to brew at home. I've been sticking to mostly light and medium roasts, but I've been concerned about the high caffeine content and decided it was time to try some darker roasts.
I like the way I feel drinking this one (less jittery if I have more than one cup) and I really do enjoy the aroma, but it isn't quite as smooth as other coffees I've had lately. I'd definitely prefer this with milk and/or sugar rather just pure black. But if you like dark roasts, you'll probably love this. For the price, you get a very decent amount so I'd say this is a bargain!
I'm not sure why this is, but large coffee bags don't usually come re-sealable. I'm not sure why this is, but this brand is no exception. The large bag can be wrapped a little, but it doesn't have ziplock or foldable tabs or any of the things you usually find on smaller coffee bean packaging to keep it fresh. It appears to be par for the course, so I can't fault this brand for that, but I wish they made the large bags in resealable closures.

title: Excellent for parties!
text: These are wonderful bags for all kinds of things! My wife loves them for goodie bags at my kids' birthday parties, but they are classy enough to also be good for corporate swag bags or gifting. The quality is good, they seem thick enough to not tear or rip instantly, and I really like that you get a lot in the box at a time. This seems like a quality product for anyone who needs bags like this.

title: I love the BBQ spice!
text: I'll admit I was afraid to try this after seeing the negative reviews, but I think there must have just been a bad batch or something because the bag I received tastes great! I love bold BBQ/Chili flavored snacks like chips and nuts, and this mix hits the spot perfectly. There's a hint of heat, but its mild and not overpowering, just enough to add flavor without negative side effects. Nothing like the chemical bad flavor the negative reviewers are saying, so I can say at least the batches they are currently selling have fixed that issue. Delicious!

title: Kosher Pork?
text:
I was a little concerned about what goes into these because they make such a production about what it DOESN'T have in it. But as a Kosher diet keeper, I was intrigued. These are vegan snacks made out of mostly pea protein it seems- I tried another sample flavor and decided to try these too after finding the first ones pretty interesting.
I think the Nacho flavor might be my favorite, and it is pretty tasty to me. Some of my friends (and my wife) find it kind of gross, but I really like it, so 5 stars from me. Just keep in mind, different strokes for different folks, so it might be for everyone. I can't compare it to actual pork rinds as I have never eaten pork.

title: Kosher Pork Rinds?!
text: So, as a Kosher keeper, real pork rinds are off the table. But these aren't actually Pork- they are Vegan pea-protein salty snacks that just show a pig on the packaging. Do they taste like real Pork Rinds? I'd imagine not. I haven't had the real thing to compare. But these are a tasty salty snack that are surprisingly high in protein! I like the different flavors, I have to say my favorites are a toss up between spicy and nacho cheese. I let some friends taste-test as well, and it seems the jury is really divided: I enjoyed them as did my kids and neighbor, but my wife and a couple of other people really did not. So, I'm giving this 5 stars personally as I enjoy it but keep in mind it may be an acquired taste that not everyone is into. If you like puffed salty treats, then dig in!

title: Convenient and super sweet!
text: I really like the size of this container as well as the way you can measure it in squirts (rather than with a spoon or other utensil). This stuff is VERY sweet and concentrated, so you only need a small amount in your drink. That's why it can get away with such a small container for so many servings. Zero calories is great for all of us who need diet-friendly sweeteners, and I rather like the flavor of it. I'm not a fan of nutrasweet and would much rather have this any day of the week. A good product, I enjoy and recommend it!

title: I'm a believer.
text: I had heard a lot about Stevia before but dismissed it as just another sugar alternative. In my experience, you usually can't use them the same way as sugar as they don't behave the same way... but this somehow really looks feels and acts like fine confectionery sugar! And most importantly, it TASTES like it too! Color me impressed. I highly recommend trying this in your recipe as a more natural sugar substitute!

title: Great name brand alternative
text:
We have Quaker brand as well as local supermarket brand flavored instant oatmeal in our home. I'd put this product squarely in between them... it seems like a level over the store brand to bring it on par with name brand, but some discerning foodies can probably tell the difference. My kids are loving it, is a fun fast hot breakfast and tastes great while managing to stay pretty healthy.
Its a good value as a name brand alternative.

title: Spicy!
text: I like the combination of flavors and scents. It was a little spicier than I expected, but I'm not complaining- I love spicy! I love that I can use this as a go-to for certain meat and fish recipes when I'm feeling lazy and it tastes like I delicately measured spices to go with it.  It is also certified kosher and gluten free, things that are important in my household. I say it's worth a try!

title: A fan favorite
text:
Once in a while we get a sugary cereal as a treat for my kids, and Fruity Pebbles is one of their favorites. I really like the size of this box- a whopping 23 Ounces! The regular sized boxes last 2-3 days at most in my household (some of the kids request more than one bowl per day!), but this one has stuck around a while despite it being one of their favorites.
If you've never had Fruity Pebbles before, it is more-or-less a rice crispies style cereal with fruit flavors and colors added. Much like regular rice crispies, it is gluten free so that's a plus if you have a sensitivity or allergy to gluten.
This product is a good value for the money if you like sweet cereals.

title: Good for watching your sodium
text:
Low sodium diets are hard. As someone with acute hypertension, sauces are one of the biggest sodium bombs that are difficult to avoid. I like these because I can use them on pasta or in sandwiches without worrying that I'm adding too much salt for my diet. In something like cheese sauce or grilled sandwiches, the lower sodium is almost indiscernible. But make no mistake- on its own, it DOES taste low sodium. Someone who inst on a low salt diet probably won't like it unless mixed with other flavorful things. I tried it with a sauce for pasta and specifically added salt to my kids' bowls so they wouldn't complain, while I had the lower salt portion. I suppose the nice thing about this is that you can control how much sodium and add to each portion if you want less than the average sauce, but I do sort of wish they made up for the lack of salt with other spices (such as the way Ms. Dash lessens the salt-free blow to your taste buds).
Otherwise, this is a good healthy product that I intend to use more of. Thanks for making this a little easier for me, Happy Belly!

title: Mmm... Swiss chocolate!
text:
We love Toblerones! I got all excited about the size of these boxes when they arrived until I opened up one of the triangular tubes and found they weren't kidding about "tiny" in the description! These are individually wrapped chocolates that are grooved to break into three, yet the whole thing with packaging fits in your palm, like the sort of sized candy you'd give out for trick or treaters. This is great for portion control I suppose, but I'm spoiled by the standard sized Toblerones and found these almost comical at first.
That being said, they do fill up the cardboard tubes with plenty of these packages, and I like that my kids can each take one and it isn't that big of a deal. The taste is everything I expected it to be, classic Toblerone. To be honest, if they weren't tiny packages they'd probably be gone already by now.

title: All my favorite spices in one
text:
I love this, despite being called garlic pepper, it's actually salt and pepper and garlic and onions- basically all the starters I'd use for a basic spice in things like an omelette or fish. Its great, reach for one bottle, sprinkle as desired, lazy man seasoning is done.
Just today as I type this up, I took some leftover unseasoned rice and sprinkled this on it with some leftover meatballs- too easy. Now that I have it around I can't remember what I did without it.

title: LOVE IT!
text:
I've heard a lot about Allulose before, but I've never had the opportunity to try it so this was exciting for me. It's one of the newer sugar substitutes and claims to do all kind of miraculous things (boost fat loss, have zero or even positive effect on insulin levels, prevent fatty liver, etc). I can't say that I know if any of that is true, but I can say that I do enjoy it in drinks!
I made some smoothies and mixed drinks as well as used it for coffee sweetener, and it was pretty good in all of those things. I've heard people say that it has an aftertaste like most non-sugar sweeteners, but personally I didn't detect anything funky. I even tried some plain on a spoon, and it just tastes like someone made sugar into a syrup. Unlike other sweeteners which are more concentrated, this is more of a 1:1 ratio to sugar, so you'll need as many teaspoons of this as you do the real thing. That threw me off at first, as I put the amount I would normally use of other substitutes into the coffee, and it wasn't sweet enough until I added more.
I've also heard from others that Allulose sometimes gives people indigestion. I have a pretty sensitive stomach so that made me nervous at first. But after trying only little bits and feeling fine, I've added more and like I mentioned above, even drank some straight from a spoon and felt fine. Obviously, use in moderation if that's something you are concerned about. It definitely does NOT happen to everyone. Otherwise, I'm very happy with this product. Wish it was a little cheaper so I could use it more often- I've used almost the entire bottle already!

title: Flavor City! But not all Kosher...
text:
The smoked flavored pepper is INSANE, I love how it makes almost anything smell like it came off a smoker. The regular pepper and pink salt flavors are also great, authentic flavors for discerning foodies. However I can't comment on the White Summer Truffle flavor salt. My household keeps a strictly Kosher diet, and I was excited to see the OU certification on these bottles- on everything other than that one. I'm guessing since it is imported from France, the supplier couldn't be certified by the same organization, and therefore that one lacks the Kosher symbol. I did not know this before I got this set, so hopefully this information will be helpful for other strictly Kosher buyers to know ahead of time.
That smoked pepper, though... wow.

title: Confessions of a PB addict.
text:
I'm a PB fan. Peanut butter mixed with chocolate brownies? I'm sold. These are great little pick-me-ups to hold myself over until the next meal, while being portion controlled and delicious. Did I mention I love Peanut Butter?
They are a little messy however, as the PB is around the perimeter of the snack and tends to get on the packaging or your fingers. Best if you hold it by the brownie part when you eat. Otherwise, I'm a big fan.
In fact, writing this makes me want to go grab another one right now...

title: Delicious, but a little sweet
text: I like that this is organic and has nothing added to it. This is the sort of drink I'd want more of in my house. However, we found it a little too sweet to drink straight some of the time. We actually enjoyed it very much as an additive to seltzer water, either poured in half the glass or frozen as little strawberry flavored ice cubes! The bottles are also a good size and easily brought in a bag to work or out with you for the day. A little pricey, but not outrageous for an organic drink like this.

title: Great if you're a fan of this style sauce!
text: I've heard of European style sour sauce before, but this is the first time I've ever tried it. At first it seemed like an acquired taste I didn't have when I tried it straight, but then after using it on some meats for dinner I started really enjoying it. My kids no so much- they prefer the more sweet and less sour style sauces that they are used to. But this was definitely interesting and something I'm sure fans of sour sauce will enjoy.

title: We love Quinoa
text:
My wife makes really delicious Quinoa salads, so I was personally very excited to try this brand. I also personally liked that it is certified kosher, however the certification comes from an organization in Peru, which I was unfamiliar with and found interesting.
The bag it comes in is resealable, and very heavy duty. Usually if we buy Quinoa in a bag, the bag starts to leak and we find seeds everywhere, so I was concerned about it not coming in a jar. Thankfully, that isn't the case with this brand. The taste is exactly what we expected it to be, and I'm enjoying Quinoa salad for lunch! Three cheers for grocery shopping items that can come efficiently via Prime!

title: A Spicy Mayo inspired dipping sauce
text:
Let me start off by saying this stuff is pretty darned good. I enjoy some sharp heat in sauces to compliment my food, and this definitely has enough of that kick to be interesting. I'm also a fan of Hellmann's Mayonnaise (which in case you didn't know, is the same parent brand as Best Foods), so I shouldn't be surprised that I liked it.
But more than anything else, it tastes much like a fancy version of the spicy mayo you often find served with sushi. Come to think of it, more like spicy mayo meets salad dressing. We served it today with a fish course, and it went over very well. In fact, the 8 people at our table managed to mostly finish an entire bottle.
Unlike certain other dipping sauces, however, I didn't particularly like it with foods like french fries. That, at least to me, requires something sweeter and/or tomato based. But if you're looking for something with kick to go inside your burger, or perhaps to go with your fish or chicken, I really enjoyed it.

title: OM NOM NOM!
text:
Holy smokes, these are beyond delicious! The packaged arrived barely an hour or two ago, and I already had to hide it somewhere to prevent it from being finished in a single sitting. Seriously. It's half eaten already and my kids are begging for just one more.
More than just Carrot Cake, these have a distinct cheese-cake flavor to them with that wholesome carrot cake aftertaste. The cookie part has almost a graham quality to it, which makes each cookie taste like a mini carrot cheese pie in your mouth. The package says the flavoring is based on real cream cheese, so I guess that's how they do it. Amazing stuff- if you like carrot cake or even just cheese cake, you owe it to yourself to try these. Also? Don't look at the nutrition information. Trust me!
I'll be in the corner secretly finishing the box before my kids find me...

title: Sweet and Salty from Clif
text:
I'm a fan of sweet and salty combos (salted caramel, chocolate preztels, etc), so as far as Clif bars go, this was really exciting for me to try. I know some people aren't into that combo, but if you are, these are great!
The one thing I didn't like much was how crumbly they are. I usually grab things like this to go in the car, and I couldn't help making crumbs all over me and the the seat as I tried to drive with my other hand. Coming from other Clif products like their bites, I wasn't expecting that. But it doesn't take away from the flavor, which I thoroughly enjoyed.
Interestingly, I noticed some people mentioned that the Amazon bought ones weren't as good as store ones. I can't vouch for this since I've never bought this particular bar locally, but I can say that I enjoyed mine.

title: Clean and quality
text:
I'm not all that familiar with this brand, so I wasn't sure what to expect going into this. I know a lot of people prefer glass bottles (myself included), but the plastic bottles I received were surprisingly good. No adverse plastic flavor and no danger of shattering if you accidentally leave it in the freezer (been there with glass, not fun to clean up). I'd say it is comparable with other high end brands like Fiji.
Interesting to note that the bottles I received are also certified Kosher for Passover. Usually water does not need an additional certification for Passover use, but I suppose it shows the attention to detail this brand wants to offer.

title: ADDICTIVE!
text:
When I first opened this to try it, we got out some carrots to dip. Next thing we know, we're trying it on other things, rice cakes, marinading it into chicken, etc... until we realized that we went through nearly an entire bottle in one day!
It's sort of like the the kind of sauce that would go with hor d'oeuvres, but with a little more tangy barbecue style that makes it great as a marinade as well. It is not spicy, so if you're expecting something hot or heavy on the mustard flavor, this isn't it. But man, this is delicious! I'm glad this came in a multi-pack because we need to pace ourselves better for the next bottle.
Yes, it seems a little high on calories, but it is made with real sugar and not corn syrup, and it's kosher if that's something you're into. Very pleased with this product!

title: DELICIOUS!
text: I love almonds, but this takes something great and makes it even better! The chocolate and coconut go really well together, and it is dairy-free, kosher, and did I mention delicious? I wish the bag were bigger, I think we need to go back for more. Note: the cococut is a separate set of flakes in the bag, it isn't part of the almond flavoring. I didn't realize this at first and was picking out almonds with my fingers from the bag until my wife poured it into her hand and I saw the white flakes come out along with the nuts. I strongly recommend eating them together, otherwise you'll miss half the fun and end up with a bag of coconut flakes all by their lonesome on the bottom!

title: HEALTHY! -ish, at least
text:
Certified Organic, Vegan, Kosher, etc, what else could you want? Well, taste for one thing, but thankfully that isn't missing. These are really quite tasty, my picky eater kids loves them too.
But beware, just because it has natural ingredients doesn't make it guilt free to eat! The bars are natural and healthy but also high in sugar and fat. Those things are also healthy, but only in moderation obviously. One of my kids got excited that it was a "diet snack" they could eat as much of as they want, I had to explain that healthy doesn't necessarily mean that.
That being said, they're a great all natural snack in moderation to keep you from eating worse things between meals. The only thing I wish is that they didn't need the "may contain peanuts" parts. One of my kids has a peanut allergy so we were afraid to let her try it. But that is a reasonable expectation of a bar like this.

title: Grippin Grape is just OK as a flavor

I LOVE GoGo SqueeZ, probably as much or more than my kids. Not just because they happen to taste good and be good for you (all ingredients you can pronounce and recognize!), but because they also have no mess and no utensils required. But the Grippin' Grape flavor is a little bit meh.
The grape is a bit strong, and tastes like a concoction a kid might make in their cup if they had access to grape juice, apple sauce and a mashed sweet potato. One of my younger kids loves it, but the rest of us not so much. We prefer their other flavors like Apple, Peach, even Banana, etc. I was a little bit disappointed compared to their other flavors. Still, if your kids like it, its a good way to get some fruit and veggies in 'em! I would try one first in a small pack before jumping into a large multi pack like this and then regretting it. Taste buds vary so YMMV.

text:

title: For a hobbyist sausage maker these worked a treat
text:
I got myself a meat grinder because it was an idea I had and it was cheap enough to entertain. I've never made sausage before but after some research and some youtubes these were the casings I landed on.

I made an Italian pork sausage and a beef sausage with these. The casings were very easy to work with. I soaked them in warm water for 15 minutes to loosen them up and separate them. Then I carefully threaded a casing onto the outfeed tube on my meat grinder. It was slow going but that's because of me, the casing didn't care, they plumped up and autofed themselves off the outfeed tube as it reached max capacity and kept doing so until I was out of filling. It never tore, these casings are tough even though they are natural. Even when I twisted them into links the casings held strong. I was able to push and manipulate them in order to achieve consistent filling since my meat grinder outfeed wasn't what I'd call consistent.

I do believe I overstuffed them though because I did have a few burst when I cooked them in the skillet later on. I'm a novice and will put the blame on my skill, not the casing. Most were perfectly fine in and out of the pan and while the Italian pork sausage was delicious, my beef sausage were terrible. Again, my fault.

If you're looking to try your hand at sausage making or perhaps you're old hat at this I found these casings to be very forgiving and strong, easy to work with and made a fine product. Can't tell you what they tasted like but I think that's the point. They gave a good crisp snap when I cut into them, just the way they should.

Turns out, she isn't allergic or sensitive to it. But in the mean time, while testing the theory over the course of a month we had DELICIOUS food with the extra savory oomph of this MSG.

MSG isn't some secret poison that you should shun and fear. It's DELICIOUS and naturally occurring in many foods you already love for their umami flavor (tomatoes, seaweed, cheese). I'm not saying dump this stuff on like it's good for you, everything in moderation my dear chap, but if you want to kick up the flavor on some home cooking to elevate it to restaurant status, this is a good tool to keep in your home chef tool kit.

title: Not My Mother's Gooseberry Jam
text:
Frankly, I was disappointed in this jar of gooseberry preserve. My mother made gooseberry jam every summer. My father grew up on a farm and expected us to do our chores without complaint. We had translucent golden gooseberries and pale pink gooseberries. The plants were covered with thorns, so it was not fun to pick them.

My parents grew up in southern Georgia, but they moved north. I grew up about 20 miles north of New York City, along the Hudson River. It was an ideal climate, apparently, because we had bountiful crops of gooseberries, currents, red raspberries, black raspberries, blackberries and blueberries. We also had many fruit trees (apple, peach, plum).

I was looking for gooseberry jam for my older brother's 86th birthday, and I sent him a jar in memory of our mom. Hoping for a memory of our childhood, I was disappointed. The flavor is just not there. Also, potassium sorbate is used as a preservative. Of course, this gooseberry preserve is imported, but the shelf life should be a few years without the preservative.

title: Healthy Organic Ghee
text:
If you want to eat a good fat, here is a good substitute for butter. Ghee is clarified butter, and it is supposed to be very good for you. It is also great for cooking and does not easily burn. Ghee is also said to have medicinal properties as well. I have made ghee before with unsalted organic butter. Mine has a stronger taste. This brand is milder but nice. This was a bit pricey, but I thought I would give it a try. It is well worth the price.

Ghee contains vitamins A, D, E and K as well as Omega 3 and Omega 9. It is supposed to be good for digestion and elimination, as well as your skin, eyes and joints. This organic ghee is especially good, since the cows have been free-ranging in the pasture. The ghee contains many vital minerals and antioxidants as well as conjugated linoleic acid.

You can store this in your cupboard for a couple of months or so. Then it is a good idea to put it in the refrigerator. It is really handy to have a jar of ghee in your kitchen.

I made the first pack, opened the noodles and there was that off-putting odor, but it wasn't crazy strong. I rinsed them for the 15-20 seconds recommended (in the bag, after draining) and they were still very clumpy and I could see reside of the packing liquid.  I took them out of the bag, held them in my hand, and rinsed under running water for 45-60 seconds. They were much better at that point.  I made 10 oz of broth, but only poured 1/2 over the noodles. Next time I'll do maybe 6 oz and get a thicker broth (I'll still drink the broth, so no waste there).  I tried the beef and it has a lovely flavor, just a little spice. For the curry and chicken I made add meat to the meal so help bulk it up, as the portion size of the noodles is rather small. title: Traumatic arrival, but bouncing back slowly with some TLC
text:
I love this plant and when I moved into my new place a few weeks ago I decided it was time to gift myself with this new baby. I was so excited to open it and add it to the new home only to find the poor plant practically suffocating in the box. There was dirt everywhere and barely enough dirt to cover the roots that were completely removed from the nursery. A lot of leaves had shed and many began to brown. It seems that this plant has been through quite a ride with little protection. I just hope it’s as resilient to bounce back from it.

Update: after a day I noticed the leaves were beginning to yellow on the top and a few more from the bottom have fallen. The plant was unable to stand without the bamboo stick so I gave it a pick-me-up by wiping its leaves with warm water and paper towel, topped off the roots with some dirt (although it appears it needs to be replanted very soon), and gave it a good drink under a grow light. It appears it’s doing a lot better.

title: Remarkably good Decaf Tea! Value and Taste!
text:
I love strong black tea with a splash of Milk - usually blend my own selection of loose leaf teas (Assam, Orange Pekoe and darjeeling).
I had to switch to decaf and struggled to find one with flavor and strength.
Barry's Irish decaf tea is really tops but it works out very expensive for someone like me who drinks many cups during the day.
Fortunately I gave PG Decaf tips a try and purchased a special of 3 boxes of 70 bags which proves to be very economical.
I use 2 bags in a large mug and then let it steep for several minutes to get the full flavor and strength, but I am delighted with this 'Cuppa".
I microwave the mug with a little water first to get it really not, throw out the boiling water, add 2 tea bags followed by freshly boiled filtered water - then slip a cover over the mug to keep in the heat.
After several minutes,I just add a splash of full cream milk and Voila! Delicious!

text:
I really wanted to like this. The coffee is just ok tasting. I expected more I guess. It's not horrible by any means, and I like the story behind the product, but there is room for improvement with the first improvement needed is the pricing.

Pros:
Good story, women owned
Would be good for traveling

Cons:
Price- its expensive for the 6oz or so of coffee you get, if you paid full price on here you paid almost $3.00 for 6 oz cup of coffee. A full 8oz was too weak. I can get a grande, 16oz, cup of my fav latte at star bucks for around $6.00. Also, my walmart carries cooper cow classic for a few dollars cheaper than on here.
Consumer waste- everything comes individually packaged
Taste- just ok, small cup, not the same that I've had at Vietnamese places. I've found I like it better to let it drip, then take the coffee and run it thru the grounds again.
Coffee bag thing didn't stay sitting in the rim of any cup I tried. I had to hold it the whole time it was "dripping."

Buy a cheap French press or a clever coffee dripper, a canister of chicory coffee and some sweetened condensed milk and experiment until you get the cup you like.

title: If you have to drink decaf!

Good choice.

Learned something new today because of writing a review, who knew.

Anyways, so I found it interesting that they have these and I figured it would be an interesting snack. They claim they are slightly bitter but I actually found they are not that bitter at all. I have to say, I was more than unimpressed with the end result. The chocolate latte I got tasted ok, but wasn’t that impressive really. If you buy a box of chocolate milk powder, you can get a result as good if not better and it is significantly cheaper. You can get a huge box of powder for like $6 and get more than just 10 drinks out of that! And you don’t have to throw it in a blender either, mixing it with just a spoon is a pain and won’t really give you a nice mix, trust me I tried that too.

Just because this has maca in it, to me it is not worth it, not even close. Sad to say but this is a miss and way overpriced for what you are getting. Who wants to clean the blender after every time they make a chocolate latte? I sure don’t and yes I tried heating up the milk prior hoping this would then blend in easier with just a spoon but again no luck there either.
