The strawberry flavor is a link strawberries and cream snack, and the mint chocolate chip has little chocolate chips in them which is nice.

One thing we did notice was that each had varying levels of firmness. The minty ones are tougher, the churro ones are medium and the strawberry are softer.

They're a little grittier overall in comparison to a regular processed rice crispy, but the calories and sugar are lower so they are technically a bit "better" for you haha but yea just imagine a rice crispy trying to be healthier. They're pretty good for a light sweet treat though

title: Tasty
text:
This brand of Japanese seven spice tastes a bit different than the brand I'm used to (the brand you would see in a ramen restaurant or something), this brand is a bit more citrusy? But it's still very tasty.

Easy to throw on dishes to change it up and brighten the flavors. This is a very large bottle though so I would out some in a shaker and then put the rest in the freezer or something to preserve it and keep bugs from getting into it. (Small bugs/beetes love spice/chili flakes)

title: Great sampler set
text:
A nice set to try all the flavors.

At my local grocery store they only sell the regular so it's nice to try 3 other flavors.

One of the originals that I tried was chewy which was kind of off-putting? I don't remember it being as chewy so I'm not sure if I just got one that was a little off?

title: Nice value pack but difficult to seal
text:
Great value pack, but the bag is a bit if a hassle or reseal.

I like keeping this bag in my car for in the to but it's definitely difficult to properly seal while driving or on the go.

I also think these are a tad smaller than

title: Pretty good!
text:
This is my first time trying a powdered pb so I can't say I have much to compare this to.

I tried this in my protein shakes to change up the flavor and add a tiny bit more protein. In a shaker bottle, it did not blend very well and stayed pretty clumpy. I think in a blender it would probably smooth out a lot better. The clumpiness didn't bother me that much tbh since I shoot my drink back pretty quickly anyway.

I though the flavor was good, and definitely tasted "healthier" than a normal jiffy pb or something. And I mean that in a good way!

Of course it's a bit more expensive than regular pb but if you're watching your calories this would definitely help!

title: Small portion but very tasty.
text:
These little packets contain just a handful of piece of jerky. It is a snack pack so I get it, but it's a surprisingly small amount.

But this jerky is very tasty, and the texture is great, not too soft or chewy!

title: Really tasty!
text:
The presentation and texture of these remind me a lot of chocolate covered raisins, which I love. I think I read somewhere that the taste is supposed to mimic banana bread which is pretty accurate. They're sweet but don't taste artificial at all.

I wouldn't say these are necessarily "healthy" though since they are essentially a candy, and have 16g of sugar per serving. (2.5 servings in each little baggy). I usually have 1-2 pieces which is much less than a serving size to satisfy my occasionally sweet tooth.

The pieces are pretty decent size, as you can see in the pics. I'd definitely keep these around for when I have a random craving for something sweet, or perhaps a road trip or something since it comes in a nice resealable pouch.

I like these a lot and will probably try the other flavors, once I'm done with this bag. haha

title: Average taste, nothing spectacular but pretty good price.
text:
I'm not a very lucky coffee drinker so I thought the flavor of this was fine. My boyfriend who is a bit pickier said this is a very whatever tasting coffee.

It is a "morning blend" coffee so it's not surprising this coffee doesn't wow or blow minds. Lol

I tried it hot, making it in a French press, and also used it to make cold brew. It's ground a bit fine to make cold brew so it does leave residual coffee particles but it's not bad. I think I prefer it in the French press though.

The price is pretty comparable to bulk pricing so it's not bad at all.

I think this would work well at an office or breakrooms.

title: Nutty grainy taste, great mixed with quinoa. Packaging issues!
text:
I haven't tried using it alone because Im not sure I'll like the texture BUT Ive used this 50/50 with quinoa to give it a different grainier texture that I like a lot. Slight nutty grain flavor that's pretty tasty.

I received my bag with a hole in the side that leaked into the box it came in. Because the grains are so tiny they also leaked out of the box seams. This seems to have happened with other orders so I feel like that's something they should try to fix.

The price is definitely more expensive but this is a pretty niche organic product, and those things tend to be expensive for the trendiness...but if that's something you're okay with, then nothing wrong with giving this product a try!

Update: I had mended the bag previously because I received it damaged, (it was a very small hole on the side) but when I went to use it today it was leaking from the bottom somehow. I should've put it in a different container but kind of frustrating the resealable bag it comes with was damaged so easily.

title: Tastes like salsa Verde, comes with many broken smaller seeds
text:
This is the first go raw product I've tried, I was expecting something very different from it's spicy fiesta flavor.

I was assuming it would have a cumin/paprika/garlic/onion type of flavor but to me it tastes a lot like a dehydrated salsa Verde type of flavor. It's not really spicy at all either. It's kind of strange, I don't dislike it but I'm not sure if it's something I would purchase again for myself.

The seeds itself are pretty small and many come broken or split, so it's kind of a finer snack mix than you'd expect. Seems to have the potential to be a little messy.

I think it's an okay snack though, feels hearty and helps satisfy see hunger without feeling like you cheated with an unhealthy snack food.

title: Fruity, sweet tea that gives a nice caffeine kick
text:
I like it! A very smooth boost of caffeine that doesn't make me too jittery. Coffee tends to make me feel too wired and anxious so I think this is a lot more my speed.

The tea itself smells sweet and fruity upon opening. Makes a nice bright green tea. I drink it twice a day, it keeps me feeling alert and hasn't affected me sleep, even if I have a cup at 4 or 5 pm!

title: Heavy on the toasted garlic flavor
text:
I was seeing this spice blend all over YouTube randomly and thought I'd give it a try.

So far I've had it atop vegetables with a bit of olive oil before roasting them and it's pretty good. I would say the most notable flavors are toasted garlic and salt. There isn't much poppy seed and sesame doesn't have much of a flavor anyway. I like garlic so I didn't mind that that's really the main flavor component. The other bits do add interesting texture and a bit of crunch though.

I liked it but that being said, I'm not sure what else to use this for. It's not something I would use with meats so I guess it's more for vegetables and probably breads and dips.

title: Quality quinoa!
text:
I'm usually someone that likes to buy things in the bulk section, so that was where I was purchasing my quinoa.

However I will say, the Happy Andes brand quinoa does have a nicer flavor and mouth feel than the quinoa I've purchased myself, which was also not organic. I like making it with a bit of chicken stock and a bay leaf to add some more flavor. Nice and fluffy quinoa for healthy sides.

You get a lot of product in this bag, unless quinoa is one of your daily staples, I can see it lasting a very good amount of time. The bag is resealable to keep it fresh. The back comes with instructions along with information on the company and their mission.

Seems like a good company, making a good product. Would recommend.

title: Awesome, I use it for my cold brew
text:
Great little variety pack!

We're normally light roast drinkers but we also add a lot of creamer to our drinks so it can water down the coffee flavor a bit. Tried these out in the cold brew and I've really enjoyed them, Sumatra is probably my favorite.

Can't speak on the flavors made as a hot beverage, but as a cold drink, they were bold and flavorful but very smooth. These darker coffees also give off a much stronger coffee scent, if you like that smell. The price is pretty similar to store bought, and depending on how much coffee you drink, 3 bags may last you a while. I usually grind up about half a bags worth for our weekly brew, so this pack works great for us.

title: Convenient and tasty!!
text:
This stuff is awesome! I use knorr boullion cubes pretty often so I already knew I'd probably like this.

It is pretty concentrated so it can get salty quickly. I like salty so I'm okay with it but most people should use a light hand!

The liquid form of this product makes it even easier and convenient to use in soups, bases and rice. I even put a (very small) squirt of this with some frozen vegetables I was sauteeing and they ce out super tasty.

Even with regular use I think one bottle will last me a long time, so the price can be justified.

Definitely recommend if you're already a fan of knorr products!

title: Great for lovers of spiced cookies
text:
Carrot cake flavored Oreos, I don't think you'd be able to write that critical of a review even if you tried. Haha

They're tasty, I found the filling a bit too sweet, it's definitely sweeter than the normal filling.

The cookie part itself is really good. Tastes a lot like Ginger snaps.

I'd definitely give this a go if you like spiced cookies!

title: Smells like dry hay
text: I should've listened to the other reviewers on here. As soon as I opened the bag up the contents smelled very strongly of a grass/hay smell. I recently bought an organic green tea powder at the store and even though that wasn't the best quality either, this one made it seem far superior by comparison. This one is very bitter and has a very unpleasant taste. I'd definitely ask for a refund of this product.

title: Get it
text: Easy to use in French press, tastes great.

title: You’ll love or hate the taste
text: Absolutely no middle ground on these drinks in our house. Ordered the variety pack and my wife and daughters hated every single flavor, I liked some but honestly wouldn’t recommend them to anyone.

title: Variable bottle cap type LEAK and are unacceptable
text:
There’s two type bottle caps that you will get in Dasani water bottles. The good kind and the “I’m going to leak all over your stuff” kind.
The good kind is larger/longer and actually screws back on if you add a packet of drink mix.
The “leak all over your stuff” kind is a very short in height cap that does NOT are-seal well and any type of jostling or pressure blows the cap off and yeah… whatever the Dasani water bottle is carried in gets soaked with water or your drink mix.
Unfortunately, there’s no way to tell which on you’re going to receive so we’ve quit drinking and buying Dasani water delivered to our home. This is a real manufacturing quality issue and suffice it to say the manufacturer seems to ignore complaints from email and tweets.
Dasani gets a must avoid and do not recommend anyone to buy concerned about their things getting soaked from bottle leaks.

title: The bottle caps leak - BADLY
text: The bottle caps have gotten thinner and weaker (polite way of saying CHEAPER) in manufacturing over the years. If you add any type of powder mix to these bottles I’ve found you’re susceptible to having a spill in your car’s drink holder, your backpack, anywhere, these bottle caps are miserable and I’ve quit buying Ozarka due to this design flaw.

title: Wet
text: The raisins are too wet that they stuck together.

title: Too Soft and Not Chewy
text: Too soft, not chewy :(

title: Too Sweat
text: Average for the price. Everything is good except it's too sweet for me. I haven't had such sweet pizza before. The flavor is a disaster for my palates. For real, how did you make a pizza sweet like an icecream? Well the flavor is not for me but maybe someone particular will like that.

title: Tastes awwwwwesome！
text: Will buy again. It's become my favorite snack when stay up late for exams.

title: Professional strength. Good quality for your money.
text:
Professional strength. Super easy to work with.
Made mango and chocolate mousse birthday cake. My friend was over the moon for this cake.

title: Five Stars
text: great deal

title: Excellent quality
text: I really enjoy these walnuts. They are fresh and flavorful and large pieces. Good value.

title: All oil, no crisp.
text: This (leaky) jar is all oil and no crisp. It’s super expensive for what you get, but I’d be ok with that if I actually got chili CRISP and not just chili oil. The Lao Gan Ma is far better.

title: Good, fresh garlic powder.
text: Very nice garlic powder. The powder is fresh and not all clumped together.

title: Great for coffee or tea.
text: I love vanilla flavor, but I don’t really enjoy vanilla extract in my coffee or tea. There’s always that bit of harshness from the alcohol, which doesn’t boil off at the temp your coffee or tea is at when you add it. I really enjoy adding a pinch or two of this powder to my coffee along with the cinnamon that I also use. I also sometimes add a pinch to my matcha. If you’re used to the concentrated flavor of vanilla extract, obviously this won’t nearly be as intense. Extracts are always more intensely flavored than the original ingredient, that’s pretty much what they’re made for. I was a little surprised to read that review from someone that apparently didn’t know that. However, if you’re looking to add some subtle vanilla notes to beverages or baked goods, and especially if you like the idea of getting a whole food and not a processed extract, you’ll like this.

title: Very strong.
text: This powder smells very strongly and seems to be very fresh. I put a tiny amount into soups to give it a little bit of that pho flavor. I’m going to try adding some to coffee and tea as well. You don’t need much, this stuff is quite strong. This pouch will probably last me a decade.

title: Good stuff
text: I cannot stand the standard non-caloric sweeteners……aspartame, sucralose and stevia. I do like the sugar alcohols and monkfruit. I saw this and thought I’d give it a try. I do like it also. There’s a little tiny bit of an aftertaste, almost a bitterness, but it doesn’t bother me. So far I’ve used it in oatmeal and in making vinaigrette salad dressing, and I have experienced no upsets though I’ve only used a small amount.

title: Faux pho. Not very flavorful. Smelly packaging.
text: This is missing most of the flavors of pho that I really enjoy. Definitely no star anise flavor. No real beef flavor either. Worst of all, the can I got absolutely REEKS of incense. It smells like it was packed in a trunk full of incense for a decade. The smell is so bad that it gets on my hands every time I pick the can up. The soup is in a plastic bag inside the can so the smell hasn’t permeated it as much but I think I still taste it. Yuck. Get some regular bouillon/stock, add some onion powder, star anise, cilantro and lime and you’ll be closer to pho than this.

title: Just ok. No star anise. Doesn’t look like the picture.
text: This is the second of their seasonings that I’ve tried and I’ve been unimpressed by both. First of all, there is no star anise, which is the first flavor I think of when I think of Pho. I had to add some. I didn’t really taste most of the spices that are supposed to be in there. I basically got salt, citric acid, and a hint of cilantro. Also, the blend does not look like the picture. This was true of the other blend I got from them as well. The product image is of an attractive, chunky blend, but what you get is an olive drab powder with a few crystals and flakes. As these blends are fairly spendy, I won’t be rolling the dice on any more of them.

title: Great blend.
text: I use this blend on many vegetables and salad dishes. I just had a cold potato salad for lunch using this and it’s delicious. I cubed up two small-medium cold previously steamed red potatoes and put them in a bowl with 1 tablespoon Apple cider vinegar, about a half teaspoon of onion powder, a pinch of garlic powder and a generous sprinkle of this seasoning. Topped with a bit of chopped fresh cilantro. I did put a few drops of date syrup in to cut the tartness a bit. Anyway, it was delicious. The pepper is definitely prominent in this blend, so if you don’t like that, this isn’t a good choice.

title: If you don’t like artificial sweeteners you will not like this.
text: I really despise pretty much every artificial sweetener that I’ve ever tried. I use erythritol all the time however, and I like that very much. So when I saw this syrup with erythritol I was excited. It does not taste like erythritol, it tastes like every other artificial sweetener I’ve ever had. I had to throw it out.

title: Poorly sealed, so the powder was hard as a rock.
text: The jar wasn’t sealed correctly, so the powder solidified into a hockey puck inside the jar. Completely unusable.

title: Jury is still,out on these….
text: I’m not 100% convinced about the health claims of this product. However, they are beautiful. definitely look pretty in a vinaigrette or some thing like that. I would also mix them into orange marmalade for a color pop. I think I might look into if these would be edible sprouted. That might be interesting. Although, I have no idea if they’re viable. They may treat them so that they wouldn’t sprout.

title: I love Teechino, but not this flavor
text: I love Teechino and I love mango, but I didn’t love this. It’s a weird combo and one that does not work for me.

title: Love Teechino
text: I love Teechino products and these are no exception. I’m unsure if the health benefits are really all that, but since the teas still taste great I’m happy to drink them either way. If you’re trying to wean yourself off coffee, definitely check out the regular Teechino. The dark roast is wonderful.

title: Good, but sizing is inconsistent.
text: The turmeric smells and tastes very fresh. The only thing I don’t like about it is that the sizes of the pieces are very inconsistent. It goes from powder to larger chunks. I prefer the Pride of India product where the pieces are much more of a consistent size.

title: Good flavor
text: I’m taking these with me on a cruise so I can try to compensate at least a little for the overeating that inevitably happens.

title: Great bagel chips
text: These are great for dips and spreads, or crunching up and sprinkling over soups or salads. I like the fact that they are not completely saturated with salt. I thought that the garlic flavor was very good and not overdone. Some people apparently want a salt lick and garlic bomb out of their bagel chips, and if that’s what you’re looking for you may be disappointed. Mine did not taste stale and they weren’t all broken up.

title: Not a fan
text: I love Szechuan food and I love chili crisp that has these in it. I don’t love these. Maybe there’s some knack to cooking with these that I haven’t figured out but I just don’t care for the flavor these peppercorn impart.

title: Coarsely ground fresh powder
text: I put this stuff in capsules as I do not like the flavor at all. I know it’s authentic as I usually buy whole seeds and grind them myself and this smells and tastes the same. Don’t believe that one review that says it tastes like cumin. It doesn’t. It tastes like black cumin/nigella, and that is a very different thing.

title: Great teas. Love the Psychocandy
text: Nice assortment of unusual teas. I really enjoy all of these blends, though the one with the rose in it is my least fave. I wish they were a little stronger. I might grind them up a bit to try for better extraction.

title: Very good
text: I was a bit worried when I opened the bag. The tea is not cut or sifted, it’s whole leaves, flowers and twigs. Despite not looking like the linden tea I’m accustomed to, the flavor is great. I like to brew it with some fresh mint as well. Ambrosia.

title: Fresh, large seeds
text: I add cracked mustard seeds to all my cruciferous veggies to boost their anti-cancer properties. These are big seeds and they’re fresh and pungent.

title: Couldn’t use it
text: I just couldn’t get past knowing I was trying to put seaweed in a smoothie. It was a mental block and was my issue not the product.

title: I couldn’t stand the taste of this.
text: I couldn’t get past knowing what I was eating. That’s not the products fault, it’s mine.

title: Love this stuff
text: I love Teechino and I love cardamom. I don’t know if I love this mushroom as all I taste is the cardamom and teechino. This is probably a good thing.

title: Delicious
text: It’s shreds of delicious Vegan jerky. The texture is disconcertingly close to beef jerky. The wasabi flavor is subtle, it’s not going to clear your sinuses like wasabi peas will. But I really like it.

title: Fantastic. Tastes like Pho. Be wary of the licorice though.
text:
Update: I had to come back and edit this review because I am concerned about the licorice powder. I don’t know how much is in here, but I’m seeing a lot of people eating the whole bag in one day. I may or may not have been someone who did that same thing. However, licorice can be pretty dangerous in large quantities. People have actually died after eating too much black licorice. I wish they would either state how much is in there, or better yet use star anise to flavor it instead. I now limit myself to this only once a week. And I’m definitely not eating a whole bag of it anymore. There could be just a tiny amount and it’s OK, but I don’t know. I wish I did.
—————————————————+++++
The texture is actually disturbingly close to the softer forms of beef jerky. Enough so that I had to double check the ingredients because I was afraid I had bought the wrong thing. I love the flavor. It tastes exactly like beef pho. If you don’t like that flavor of star anise and licorice, you’re not going to like this. If you love pho, you are going to adore this. This stuff is amazing.

title: Strong chemical smell
text: I really wanted to try this, but when I opened the bag there was a strong chemical smell. I couldn’t bring myself to consume any of it after smelling that.

title: Excellent oatmeal.
text: This is really good oatmeal. I am happy to know that they don’t use round up on it, though I do wish it was fully organic. But, it would probably be twice the price then. Definitely far superior to plain old generic rolled oats.

title: Naturally dried bananas. Great snack. Also great in oatmeal.
text: These are naturally dehydrated bananas. If you’ve actually dried bananas yourself, you know that they’re not pretty and they’re not crisp. Those wonderful crispy banana chips you get some places are all fried and have preservatives or are dipped in something to keep them from browning before they’re fried. These are plain bananas with nothing added or fried or processed in any way other than being dehydrated. They are brown and chewy.  They are great to have on hand for camping or snacking or whatever. I’ve used some in oatmeal when I haven’t had fresh bananas in the house.

title: Great stuff.
text: Since it’s been close to a year since I’ve been to a Chinese restaurant, I was really craving some. I got this curry powder and whipped up a batch of Singapore Mei Fun. It came out great and really had the same flavor as the restaurant dish.

title: Delicious
text: I love this stuff. I haven’t had Nutella in years since it’s so unhealthy, but this tastes like what I remembered. Of course, this isn’t health food either, but it’s less unhealthy. Just be aware that maltitol can cause some stomach distress in some folks. So start slow and don’t eat a whole jar at once.

title: Great sweetener
text: I really like the taste of these packets. Very clean with no aftertaste. Just be aware that you need to be very careful if you have pets, as xylitol is very toxic to dogs. If I had dogs, I would actually only buy erythritol.

title: Really tasty flavoring.
text: This is pretty hot so I don’t use much, but it’s super tasty. I really enjoy it on rice, fish and eggs.

title: Looks nothing like the photo. Smells and tastes like poultry seasoning.
text: The product I received is a very fine green powder. Nothing at all like the chunky appealing looking picture. The packaging is cool, however it’s ill-suited for this type of spice blend. You get the blend in a plastic bag inside of a tin which has a magnetic base. There are holes in the side of the lid and a slot in the side of the can so in theory you could twist the lid and shake the can over whatever and dispense some herbs onto it. However, this fine powder is really going to just pour out the holes because they’re a decent size. Secondly, this blend supposedly has salt in it. Salt in a metal container is asking for trouble. Maybe if you live in Arizona you can get away with it, but here in Florida it’s going to be a rusty nasty mess inside there if you try to keep a salt blend in a metal tin. All that said, I don't think that what is in this tin is what is supposed to be in this tin. It smells like poultry seasoning. It tastes like add poultry seasoning. I didn't taste any salt I didn't taste any dill. I tossed it. I don't like poultry seasoning.

title: Great stuff
text: These onions are awesome. Really great to add to almost any recipe. As long as you give it enough time to reconstitute or cook. Also, I’ve made some great dips by toasting these in a dry pan then mixing with ranch and sour cream. Yummy.

title: Nice sauce alternative.
text: The roasted red pepper flavoring is not overwhelming. It’s a very nice, safe condiment. :-) Most people who don’t like spice will be OK with this.  I’ve been making salad dressing in the bowl by drizzling some of this on top of the salad and then drizzling balsamic vinegar. It makes a nice dressing. Also good on sandwiches.

title: Ok vinegar
text: This balsamic is ok. Nothing stood out about it. The flavor is ok, but mild enough that I had to use a lot more than I’m used to.

title: Ok. Too much oil for me.
text: The garlic crunch is pretty tasty. Unfortunately, the jar that I got was a lot more oil than it should’ve been. The company did refund me, but the next jar that we got wasn’t that much better.

title: Good bananas with nothing added
text: It seems to be so difficult to find dried bananas that are just bananas. They’ve either got oil or sugar or both added most of the time. These are just freeze dried bananas and they’re good. But they’re so expensive, and there seems to be a lot of settling, because the can just isn’t that full.

title: Don’t puff up in microwave
text: I’m used to the Sharwood‘s pappadum which puff up really nicely in the microwave. Thease don’t do that. Also, the flavor is not garlic. The flavor is hot pepper. It’s too spicy for me.

title: Great stuff
text: I love to sprinkle this on salads and veggies. It gives great flavor. I wish it wasn’t quite so expensive, and that the ziplock closure actually worked. In humid climes, that is an issue.

title: Fantastic
text: This is a nice assortment of dried fruit. The fruit is soft (for dried fruit) and flavorful. The pieces are very large, so if you want to use it in a fruitcake or in your morning oatmeal or something like that you’re going to have to chop them up. The first thing I pulled out of the bag was half of a dried pear and it was wonderful. My bag was sealed. The bags are Ziploc bags and then they have a fairly weak top seal. Which is so you can open them without having to slice off the entire top of the bag above the Ziploc. However, I could see with rough handling during shipping that it could come open. Mine was fine though. I would buy this again.

title: Mostly powder and super fine pieces
text: I had high hopes for these mushroom bits in soups and grain dishes. However, the package I got was almost half powder and super fine bits. I already have a lot of shiitake powder, and it costs a heck of a lot less. The mushroom pieces in the bag are ok, but I’m not at all happy that there’s so little of them and so much powder and tiny bits.

title: Pretty much only Special Dark in this assortment.
text: I was hoping for an even distribution of all three candies. However, the bag I received was almost entirely special dark miniatures, followed by a smaller amount of kitkats, and then just a scattering of Mounds. Worst of all, the candy had all melted at some point. It’s never fun to open a wrapper and get showered with shards of dark chocolate. But I was most annoyed at the overwhelming amount of Special Dark candies because I can get them in any store. This assortment was not worth over seven dollars a pound in any way, shape or form.

title: I love quinoa, and this is a great selection.
text: I love quinoa, and this is a great selection. This is a nice selection of three different kinds of quinoa in nice reusable square plastic jars. I really like this kind of plastic jar to put my bulk foods in after I’ve used the quinoa that came in it. The grains appear to be fresh and I have no complaints.

title: Love the coffee, hate the packaging.
text: These pods are probably the best tasting strong coffee K cups that I have ever had. They are really good. However, when you’re appealing to a demographic who wants a compostable K-cup, and then you wrap every pod in non-compostable or recyclable plastic, it’s pretty much a mixed message. Plus they take up an incredible amount of room since each one is packed in a plastic bubble. They’re not just plastic wrapped, I guess it’s packed in nitrogen. Which is awesome for freshness, but like I said they take up an incredible amount of room. If they’re going to do this, I would much prefer to see six or eight pods in each plastic pod.  But, like I said, if you like really strong coffee, these are the coffee pods for you.

title: Smells like mushrooms, tastes like sawdust.
text: I was excited to open this bag up and I was pleased by the mushroom odor that I smelled. Then I tasted it, and the disappointment was huge. It taste like sawdust. It doesn’t taste like mushrooms it doesn’t really taste like anything. And it leaves an unpleasant bitter aftertaste. I don’t know what this actually is, but I don’t believe it’s actually shiitake powder.

title: I love this stuff.
text: I used to eat a ton of rice until I started reading more about how much arsenic is in Rice these days. Unfortunately they are growing the rice in former cotton fields which are full of nasty pesticides. So, I’ve switched over to pearl couscous for a change from quinoa and other grains. I really love this. I make it in my instant pot and it comes out perfectly. Super easy and flavorful.

title: I like that they are recyclable, unlike K cups.
text: The pods are expensive, but at least they are recyclable. I love Nespresso coffee I just wish it was cheaper.

title: Smooth coffee
text: I got these for my mom who cannot have caffeine and doesn’t like super strong “burnt“ coffee. She seems to enjoy these quite a bit.

title: Delicious coffee. They need to work on getting the price down a bit.
text: After some time in Europe last spring, I came back to the US with a bad espresso coffee habit. The Nespresso machines do a great job. The only problem is that these pods are so expensive. But, for a treat, they hit the spot.

title: Good way to gradually cut coffee consumption.
text: I’m trying to cut down on my coffee consumption and I think this will help. I never used to like chicory coffee, but this seems OK to me. Of course right now I’m only putting a quarter teaspoon into my reusable K-cup along with my regular coffee. After a while I’m going to up it to a half a teaspoon and reduce the coffee. Hopefully eventually I’ll get to straight chicory. Teechino is another helpful product in my attempt to beat this addiction.

title: Ok flavored coffee.
text: I don't love these cups. They're a little too weak for my taste. However, I've had no issues with bad seals like many reviewers did. I also think they're somewhat overpriced right now.

title: Nice, mild flavored miso.
text: I use this as a salt replacement in cooking and I find it gives a nice depth of flavor.

title: Pretty misleading labeling. Tastes like xylitol.
text: I picked this up in the grocery store the other day.  I was aware by reading the ingredients that it was more erythritol than monk fruit, but I did not realize how much more until I tasted it.  Wow, it was like sticking an ice cube in my mouth. It must be almost 100% erythritol.  I’m hoping that at least it actually IS erythritol and not xylitol, which I think is cheaper.  I’m worried enough about that possibility that I’m not going to feed any treats or food made with this to a dog.  I’ve used both erythritol and xylitol in the past, and this taste way more like xylitol than erythritol.

title: Delicious cinnamon!
text: Great spicy cinnamon aroma and taste. Much better than the dollar store spices.

title: Yummy cacao
text: Great tasting cacao in a convenient bulk pack. I use it in oatmeal, and frozen banana ice cream. Great stuff.

title: I couldn’t tell it was decaf
text: It’s a very nice, mild cup of coffee. I like the lack of excess packaging and the economical price.

title: One of the few artificial sweeteners I will use
text: Generally I can always detect the bitterness of stevia, but in Truvia they’ve gotten the balance right. Unless I really go overboard, I can’t taste it. I’m a big erithrytol fan, I use it a lot for sweetening as it doesn’t have the cooling effect of xylitol, and I don’t have to worry about the dog getting some of it somehow. Great stuff

title: Great snacks. The cardamom flavor is subtle.
text: I actually wish the cardamom was more pronounced but I understand not everyone would love that. This is a nice snack that’s a little different. Really enjoyed these.

title: Heavy on the chili, light on the pineapple.
text: I was hoping more for a spicy teriyaki flavor but it's just hot. If you were put off by the "pineapple" don't be, I couldn't taste it at all. That said, it's good jerky.

title: Doesn't taste like much.
text: I'm sorry. I want to love this but I just don't. It doesn't taste like almond butter to me. It doesn't taste like anything, really. It's sad because I LOVE the powdered peanut butter and I was hoping for the same from this. But I'm just not getting it.

title: Great onion flavor.
text: This powder is fresh and strongly flavored. Great for adding to soups, rice, casseroles, eggs and more. Great stuff!!

title: I love this assortment.
text: Maple Sleigh is my favorite flavored coffee. The rest of the flavors I’ve tried so have not disappointed either. I get a decently strong cuppa using the medium button. Really like these.

title: Good pasta
text: The pasta has a nice nutty flavor and holds up well. Doesn’t fragment with somewhat aggressive mixing like some cheap pastas do. Good stuff.

title: Not to my taste
text: Didn’t work for me. I tried, I really did, but I just couldn’t drink this.

title: Not for me.
text: The product looks great, and seems like a great idea. I just did not care for the taste. I didn't get any chili or lime, just an unpleasant acidity. Bummer, because I had high hopes.

title: Yum!  Love this coffee
text: It tastes like maple and it's a nice cup of coffee. Would definitely buy again.  Hard to say much more than that.

title: Great coconut milk
text: I really love the concept of this. I use coconut milk in my coffee and love it. However. Amazon needs to work on the shipping of items like this. The box clearly says "This end up" and they of course laid it on its side in the shipping box. Three of the 6 containers were leaking by the time I got them.  The coconut milk in the undamaged ones was great.

title: Delicious. But not low calorie.
text: I really liked these wafels. I had stroopwafels in the Netherlands and they're awesome. I tried buying the in the packages here in the US and like most of our food, they were sickeningly sweet compared to the originals. These wafels are not too sweet. In fact, they're just right in that department for me. Unfortunately, instead of sugar, they went overboard on the oil. These are not low calorie by any stretch of the imagination at 130 calories per wafel. They're tasty as heck but I just wish they were less oily.

title: Did not care for the flavor
text: I wanted to love this, I really did. But the chai flavor is strange and bitter to me. It dissolved easily. I'm giving it three stars simply because my friend DID like it a lot. So between the two of us I'll average out to a 3.

title: Very pleasant mint tea.
text: I really like this ginger mint tea. It has enough of each flavor but not too much. I am a big fan of rooibos too so I found it to be a very nice blend.

title: Nice matcha blend
text: This is a nice matcha blend, not bitter at all. It has a very pretty green color.

title: Love Litehouse herbs
text: I've always loved Litehouse products and these are no exception. The only thing I don't like is that they don't come with an airtight seal. So storing them for long periods is problematic. I usually use them quickly enough that it's not an issue.

title: Really yummy spread in convenient packets.
text: I really like this spread. The vanilla flavor is very subtle, as is the sweetness.  I love the ingredients. One thing to be aware of is, be sure to knead the packet very well before opening. Do it as long as you think you need to, then do it some more. I didn’t do that on the first one and got a lot of separated oil. On the other hand, if you’re looking to reduce the fat content, you could opt to not knead it. However, the resulting nut butter is pretty dense. In any event if you don’t want to be hit over the head with sugar and vanilla you will like this spread. I’ll be buying more of this.

title: Great concept. I wish it was unsweetened, however.
text: I *really* wanted to love this. I love chai and I love the idea of medicinal mushrooms.  It smells fantastic. Unfortunately the stevia is too strong for me. I hate stevia and didn’t notice it as I had read the sweetener was palm sugar. I wish this was unsweetened so folks who want a sweet beverage can add the sweetener they want, and those who like unsweetened can be happy too.  After all, anyone who is health-savvy enough to drink something like this has definite ideas and preferences on sweeteners. I know I do. I’m giving it 4 stars because it’s a good product and it’s my own fault for not reading the ingredients. I was able to get the stevia taste down to a reasonable level by mixing one packet with 3 cups of coffee, which is what my big travel mug holds.

title: Great stuff. I’ve used it in salad dressings and ...
text: Great stuff. I’ve used it in salad dressings and to make a topping for my iced matcha lattes.  Google ‘cheese tea’ and you’ll see what I’m talking about. :-)  It sounds awful but is surprisingly good.  In any event, I don’t think you’re going to slather this on a bagel and fool anyone, but it is awesome in dips, dressings, baking, and so on. Great to have in the pantry.

title: Great stuff.
text: I love this stuff. The ginger is an awesome addition. It was love at first cup. I got this free to review it and to be honest, when I saw the price I thought it was crazy. I'd never had matcha before (outside of a few matcha lattes in coffee shops) and I didn't realize how much of a difference there was in quality between culinary and ceremonial grades. Once I tried this matcha I did what any sane person would do, went out and bought a few cheaper ones. I wasted more money on them than I would have spent on another tin of this. The others were not as beautiful of a green color and had bitterness that the Four Sigmatics did not. They are ok in smoothies and stuff but not for a pure matcha drink, in my opinion. I guess that's why they say "culinary".  I didn't buy any other ceremonial grade matcha as their prices are in line with this, considering they don't have the lions mane and ginger added. I taste no hint of any mushroom at all, by the way. I suspect that's why the ginger is there, to mask any taste of it. That's ok with me, I adore ginger. I will say, I don't use as much matcha as the package calls for. I'm happy with 3/4 teaspoon. Sometimes I add a little honey and coconut milk and it is to die for. Sometimes you do get what you pay for, and for me, this is one of those times.

title: Use as directed. That's the first and foremost thing ...
text: Use as directed. That's the first and foremost thing. Use in unoccupied spaces and air out welll before going in. I use this in my storage building because I don't want an insecticide film over everything. Be warned, it does have an odor though, and if you use it long term items in your storage will too.  It goes away. Eventually. But since the odor bothers me less than giant Florida palmetto bug roaches do, I'll continue to use it.

title: I found a green chile and lime salt in NM that I love but is hard to find and I hoped these ...
text: These salts just don't do that much for me. I found a green chile and lime salt in NM that I love but is hard to find and I hoped these would replace it, but they just don't compare. They have an overly artificial taste that I don't care for. The pickle salt is the best of the bunch in my opinion.

title: I had this on frites in the Netherlands and fell in love with it
text: Yum. Way overpriced but since I couldn't find in anywhere else, I gritted my teeth and paid the price. I had this on frites in the Netherlands and fell in love with it. Had I only known what a pain it would be to find here I'd have brought back a suitcase full.  It's sweet and curry flavored. I dip fried foods into it and I also use it on my roasted cauliflower. 1 Tablespoon mayo, 1 Tablespoon Ranch dressing, and a squirt of this. Rub/coat the florets of a whole head of cauliflower with the mix and roast it. Wow, is it good.

title: Super tasty and spicy
text: Super tasty and spicy. I really like mixing beer with this as it's a great way to have a honking huge drink, yet not really drink much. Especially if you serve it over ice.  Would make a great Bloody Mary too.

title: Great pepper, needs more info on the label.
text: I would give this 5 stars for flavor and spice, but I have to delete one or two for poor labeling. The label doesn't state what pepper or peppers are in this, if it's a blend or a single variety and most importantly, where it's sourced from. The Amazon description states "African Bird pepper" but that's not on the packaging anywhere. I would be happier if it said exactly what it is and where it was sourced on the bag. If you don't care about that stuff and just want some crazy hot pepper, it's awesome.

title: I love this soup base
text: I love this soup base. It's got great flavor and some dried onions for a little added something. It is absolutely wonderful for cooking rice and veggies in. Looking at the ingredients, it appears to be vegetarian, though not labeled as such. I think I'm going to fire up some black beans and brown rice cooked in this broth in the Instant Pot for a yummy lunch.

title: Fresh, large and flavorful.
text: These pods are large, fresh and really flavorful. I'm accustomed to putting 2 pods in my french press....when I did that with these pods it was actually too much of a good thing! These are so much larger and fresher that I now only use one.

title: Wonderful curry
text: This stuff is awesome. Richly colored, fragrant, just all around wonderful for those who love curry. The only real nit I have to pick is the packaging. The top comes off WAY too easily. If you happen to pick it up by the lid, a disaster could ensue. Plus, it's not really airtight enough. Still buy it, but just know you're going to want to put it in a glass jar.

title: Great rub with nice five spice flavor.
text: I love this stuff. If you're familiar with Chinese Five Spice powder, that is what this rub is based on.  I love five spice and this rub has just the right amount.  Sweet, savory and exotic, this rub is winner on salmon, shrimp & chicken. I've sprinkled it on french fries as well. I just wish they made this in the larger tub.

title: Decent flavored coffee. (Cinnamon)
text:
I used to love General Foods Int'l Coffees Cafe Vienna. Add some half & half & a little maple syrup & maybe a dash of vanilla and this takes me back to that place. It's not a heavy perfume-y flavor, and in fact it could be stronger for my taste. But I think it's a decent flavored cup. I would say if you find Green Mountain flavored k-cups to be a bit too much then you will enjoy these.

I don't know what the reviews saying the cups were weak or crushable received but mine are indistinguishable from any other K-cups. Oh, and in case you were wondering (as I was) it's real ground coffee, unlike some of those super cheap brands that put instant coffee in their K-cups.

title: Love these mushrooms!
text: Great stuff!  I love these.  They have great flavor and work well in the rice and soup dishes I use them for.  I love to put some of these in with the rice in my rice cooker.  They flavor the rice and reconstitute well in there.  Will be buying more.

title: If you love Pho you'll hate this.
text: It's just awful.  I took one taste and said, "Whaaaat????  Maybe I need to shake it up."  Shook it, took another taste, and poured it all down the sink.  I was sad as I love Pho but this stuff is terrible..

title: Ok, a little bland for me
text: I found this sauce to be a bit bland for me.  If I want jalapeno, I really want a kick.  The flavor wasn't stellar either.  The general consensus at the table was that it was just ok.

title: Seems to jam up the machine
text: Like many other reviewers said, it's instant coffee in a little plastic cup.  If I wanted instant coffee I'd save a ton of $$ and buy a jar, run a cup of hot water through the Keurig and plop in a spoonful.  And get better coffee.  But all that aside, something is weird about these, the second one I tried seemed to block up the machine and it quit brewing halfway through.  I won't try it again.

title: Good snack assortment.
text: I really loved the cashew crunch and the pretzel thins, they were great.  I don't like cheese straws but I'm told they were outstanding.  If someone were the kind of person who enjoyed creating gift baskets, this would be a nice, one-stop-shopping approach to getting goodies to fill a basket.

title: Can't tell it from "real" chicken buillon.
text: My Mom is a vegetarian and told me how great this stuff was.  I have come to take that with a grain of salt sometimes but in this case I was astonished.  She made chicken noodle soup using it, and after I ate two bowls of it I went to read the ingredients as I was sure it was chicken broth.  It's not.  Really awesome product.

title: Wow, this is great.
text: I have bought some of the jarred/canned cooking sauces and not been all that impressed.  I bought this a while back and it's been sitting in my pantry.  I finally got around to trying it and was blown away.  I used a pound of shrimp, a handful or two of cashews, and coconut milk instead of water.  Yummy!!!  I may try making a potato curry using a bag of those pre-diced-potatoes-with-onion (not sure if I can Simply say the brand name :-) that you find in the deli case at the supermarket.  I think that will be good too.  And more economical.

title: Look at the ingredients...
text: Many people drink green tea drinks thinking they're healthy and natural.  The first ingredient in this is sugar (fructose) and the second is non-dairy creamer. Green tea is all the way at the end of the list, third from the bottom.  It tastes good, but if you're looking for a healthy drink, this is not really it.

title: Great stuff

text:
I had ordered another "Virgin Coconut Oil" from the internet a few years back when I first heard of the health benefits. I couldn't stand it. There was a soapy undertaste that just made it unpalatable. I used it on my skin but couldn't ingest it. Then I bought some Spectrum coconut oil, but it was tasteless and odorless. Which is ok of course if you're just looking for a cooking oil. However I love coconut and feel the compounds that give the taste and smell are probably health-enhancing as well. I ordered this oil on the basis of the reviews and I love it. It has a light but very appealing coconut flavor and aroma and melts at the correct temperature, @ 76 degrees. If you have oil that is solid above that temperature it may be partially hydrogenated or otherwise adulterated. I am now eating one tablespoon per day and feel a difference in my energy level. I highly recommend this product if you are interested in trying coconut oil.

The product comes in a plastic jar. Nutiva adresses this on their site and states that they use "safe" plastic. I would prefer a glass container, but I guess that would increase the weight too much.

I also opted for the every-6-months subscription to save some money. It is my understanding that you can cancel the subscription before the next shipment with no penalty. However, I might be trying to get more sooner instead!

title: Magic buns???
text:
These buns were delicious. They held together well and didn't disintegrate under the pressure of my burgers and it's greasy rivers of flavor! YAY, you can stop reading here and go buy some.

But for those of you with developed minds... what kind of magic lives in these here buns? They don't mold. It wasn't some deliberate action on my part or anything. I wasn't in need of growing penicillin. If I had been, I wouldn't have been able to write this review. It didn't mold. Week two... three... a month??!!!!!!!! The rules of bread forbid one to keep month-old bread products and be willing to eat them. After that time, bread is supposed to challenge a garden for its source of greenery. It's supposed to lure pharmacists to your door begging for access to your medicinal ecosystem. But not this bread. I thought it was the potatoes but, potatoes come from the ground. I cannot understand it. To test my discovery, I made a bologna and cheese sammich and used a month-old bun ready to be over-taken by invisible spores of ick. However, it was tasty. I actually enjoyed it once I pulled my eyebrows down from the furrows of my long-gone hairline. There is magic, in these here buns. I have discovered magic!

title: What have I found here.......
text:
I ordered these for my best friend because he eats dill pickles like they cure some unimaginable secret ailment he is afflicted with. Surely he would rejoice in their mouth-busting flavor and declare me the greatest friend ever!!! Well, he does, but tempting strangers with the incredible experience of having my presence in their lives isn't why we are here.

He didn't like them and placed them on the kitchen table and walked away like the disgruntled bratty cat he resembles. I couldn't believe what I was hearing so I tried one.. then two... three... I lost count. I found them delicious. My problem was that this particular can of them appeared to have been placed through a blender. It was like dill pickle bread crumbs. I did what any sane human would... I licked my fingers to wet them in spit and dove in there to collect a coating of Dill Pickle Pringle crumbs. And I did it again. And I did it again. And in that fit of pleasure, I thought of something incredible.... a recipe. I would make a divine Greek chicken dish inspired by Dill Pickle Pringles, Tzatziki, and smoked Gouda... it was the highway that led to raising the bar of my awesomeness.

Forget my best friend and his snotty little judgment. What does he know?? I LOVE these divine chips. And I have a far more advanced palate for fine foods and sauces and spice... and flowers and style and fashion and colors and fabric and music and the arts and... wait.... you all don't want to know about me. You are here for the Pringles. I am not a Pringle. Perhaps a princess, but those are two different things.

I am Oper Winfret, and I like Dill Pringles!

title: The jury is in.
text: I am running late for a chemical peel so I will keep this short.  I ordered this thinking, "Less sugar means it's good for you".  Well, apparently seaweed, tofu, and kale are too.  I was having a bowl of ice cream and wanted some topping.  So I scooped my spoon into it and covered my ice cream with it.  It was something I had done many times before.  I had trained to do such things.  For years, whilst growing up, I would stop at the pantry, spoon in hand, and dive into the Nestle Quik to enjoy its wholesome deliciousness.  It had never let me down.  Well, I am not going to relive the time I mistook baking cocoa for cocoa powder, but something about this here sugar-free option took me there.  It wasn't that horrible, I have put it on my ice cream since.  But every time I reach for it, I have flashbacks of standing with a mouth full of baking cocoa and remember the kitchen countertops after I coughed it out.  I can still hear the lambs calling to this day... This is like the gluten-free option of Nesquick.  Have you ever eaten a gluten-free brownie that made you say "Oh, I could just eat the entire plate of them!???"

title: Let's talk Ketchup
text: I realize I risk insinuating presenting myself as a person who collects things in jars and hides them under my bed for having the time to talk ketchup, but I have moral obligations as a southern boy.  I was on a date and we stopped for some french fries before seeing a concert.  I needed some grease on my stomach in case the date went badly, I could just... drink myself through it.  Upon the arrival of my fried potato wedges, I grabbed what appeared to be ketchup, though I wasn't familiar with the brand.  I did find the little Monopoly character on it cute, so I threw caution to the wind.  I like Monopoly.  One thing is common amongst poor, okay, and wealthy southerners, we all use the same ketchup.  It's simply common knowledge... like breathing.  I squeezed some to the side of my fries and then dipped one of them into this thick concoction.  Let's just say, I have learned to carry a British accent and I now tell people I am from a distinguished village a few hours outside London.  This ketchup is so good.. soooooo good.  Like, go home to visit family and at the family barbecue, whilst sitting at the table letting the family see how fabulous I look, I pull my own ketchup out from my man bag and squeeze this heavenly creation upon my three-ply paper plate.  Momma screams and passes out, Poppa walks away in disdain... my younger cousins giggle from the kid's table at my gall.  Forget them.. forget them all, how dare these common people judge me!  I am from a distinguished village outside London.. and we use Sir Kensington's Ketchup!

title: Great Color, but Doesn't Last more than 20 minutes, and Requires Bright Lighting
text:
[[VIDEOID:8395340377a68c471f7b66aa826e4c2]] I ordered both this (Brew Glitter silver, left) and the Snowy River silver (right) to compare them. For that reason, this review will be very similar to the one I wrote for Snowy River. Although it's a tiny container, you really don't use much per drink.

I added roughly 1/8 of a teaspoon (I marked a 1/4 teaspoon at the halfway mark) of both to the bottom of the glass and then added one of my favorite drinks: Martini & Rossi Asti, which is a sweet Italian sparkling wine. This turned out to be a mistake, as they caused a great deal of bubbling. After the tests below, I added both to the control glass, and confirmed there was very little bubbling. In the future, I will add them after pouring the drink, and I definitely recommend you do the same.

I took pictures right after stirring, and then again 5 minutes later. I then did a taste test. After that, I also took a short video of me picking up and swirling both glasses.

Appearance-wise, I preferred the Brew Glitter. It was more silver, whereas the Snowy River seemed more white.

After the 5-minute mark, the Brew Glitter was still swirling around, while the Snowy River was relatively still.

However, this also meant that the Snowy River did not settle to the bottom of the glass even after 20 minutes, while the Brew Glitter did (not pictured, sorry, but you can tell that it has settled slightly in the video). For that reason, I'd recommend the Brew Glitter for people who drink relatively fast, but the Snowy River for people who drink more slowly.

Taste-wise, they had roughly the same effect: they made the Drink slightly sweeter, but with a sharper finish.

Both drinks require bright lighting to get the full effect. If your event will be in dim lighting, you probably won't think much of either.

As far as packaging goes, the Snowy River was much better. It came in a padded envelope with a professional advertising card. The Brew Glitter came in a plain white box filled with paper. It felt more like a mom-and-pop operation than a company. A sticker on the box or a postcard inside would improve this.

Personally, my preference is for the Brew Glitter. Although it settled after 20 minutes, I rarely take that long to finish a drink, and I preferred both the color and the swirling effect. However, you might have different preferences.

title: Durable, Don't Leak, a Great Value!
text:
I've had these since October, and I love them. I confess, I didn't buy them through Amazon, because I found them at the local grocery store. I was originally going to buy three, but I bought six "for when they break". But not one of them has broken in the 3.5 months I've had them. This is not because I'm gentle with them, either. I drop them all the time. But, so far, not a single crack. And no leaks, either. I am having some issues with the foam insert on one lid (I can't seem to get it clean), but that's easily replaced, so no worries there. As far as I can tell, even if you buy them through Amazon, these are the cheapest, most durable leak-proof glass water bottles on the market.

As for the water itself, I will admit that it was very good. But I moved to glass to get away from the waste associated with bottled water, so I won't be buying it again until I need to replace my bottles.

Nice rich well rounded flavor - I'm glad there are a bunch because these I actually like. Easy to use and they work well in my new handy dandy instant espresso machine.

title: Not my favorite

When they arrived, a group of us sat down to try them and everyone liked them - the next day there was only one left???? The taste was good, the texture was nice - and everyone wanted them. Very good for grab and go.

title: Ick! I hated this
text: I realize not everyone has the same tastes in coffee but I was hoping this would be a winner. ICK! It was just downright unpleasant. It smelled so good coming out of the brewer but the end product was NOT worth drinking in my opinion. If you like very strong coffee this might be for you but even though I like espresso and other dark roasts, this didn't have the same richness. I also tried the regular coffee from this brand and didn't care for it but that was at least drinkable. I couldn't get into this.  The several people that also tried it declined to have a second cup.

title: Not my fave
text: Eh...wasn't for me. I guess I'm a coffee snob but this tasted like regular diner coffee with an extra charge. I guess if you like really strong (but not dark roasted) coffee this would work for you. I do like rich dark roasts but this was just strong without the richness. May be fine for you but I won't be ordering it again. I am going to give it to my friends that are always complaining about the water that comes out of the coffee machine. Personally I think it will  make a better gift than anything I want to drink myself.

title: Needs some sugar (for me)
text: I'd really like to rate this 4.5 because I was surprised how tart it was. I'm used to fruity juices that are sweeter than this - however, I knew what I was ordering and this is THAT! Organic, cold pressed, etc. It's dark and rich looking and I plan to sweeten it a bit for me while all my health conscious friends can drink it the way they want. Tastes just like pomegranates but having only eaten them in the past, I did expect it to be sweeter.  Totally not a deal breaker - otherwise, everything is going for it. title: Decent chocolate flavor, no coffee taste
text: So I wasn't sure what to expect in a dark chocolate,mocha CLIF bar but seriously how bad could dark chocolate and mocha be? The bar was a bit dry but not too unpleasant and the flavor was decent. The coffee flavor is NOT noticeable -- it just makes the chocolate more intense. Overall a decent bar. I have members of my family who do NOT like coffee and they couldn't taste it, for me I would have enjoyed a second shot of espresso in the bar.

title: On the fence, tastes good but are the health benefits really there?
text: A friend of mine has been raving about all the benefits of Manuka Honey so when I saw this, I grabbed it. I wasn't sure what to expect at first. I got both the 15+ and the 20+ and overall I can't seem to tell much difference. I did prefer the 20 in the long run, but the costs of this was way more attractive. It's way better than grocery store honey which is so sweet you can't use more than a bit at a time. It did magically disappear and when it was gone, everyone was asking for more. I'm off to do some more research, I think it's very pricey. The people that generally use it seem to swear by it but I need to do some more research to find out if it's worth the bucks. It tastes fine, works like honey and isn't sicky sweet like the cheap stuff.

title: Good for you chocolate

I would have preferred it just as chocolate I believe but somehow the chocolate/peanut butter bars are mysteriously disappearing so someone likes it just fine. For what it is, it's pretty darn good. title: Lots of options, light to medium roast  K cups
text: There isn't anything wrong with these but there isn't anything notable. I generally prefer a darker roast and a more robust coffee so I'm probably not the best judge but I've been serving them to guests and they haven't complained and haven't left the cups empty so I assume I'm in the minority. There have also been repeat drinkers. There's a lot of coffee but it's just a box full and there isn't any separation between the three styles. They do have different colored labels so it's not difficult to find what you want. All in all, I'm not drinking it myself because it doesn't appeal to ME but it is being used without complaints. I'll give it 4 stars. If you are a medium/light roast person, this will probably be fine for you, if you prefer a dark roast, skip this one.

title: Ehhhh....Not great for me but might be okay for you.
text:
This was an okay cup of coffee. It wasn't horrible and it wasn't great. I admit to being something of a coffee snob and I generally grind my beans just before my coffee. This is pre-ground so for me that's a stroke against. I do realize that sometimes pre-ground works better, especially if there are a lot of drinkers so it may be a plus for someone else.

This is a rather mild coffee and I generally prefer a darker roast and a more robust flavor of coffee so this was a little light for me. It was still drinkable so I decided to serve it to some friends. None of them complained about the coffee and several went back for seconds.

If this is your coffee style, it's probably good. If you prefer more robust coffee, this won't be good. I'll serve it up to friends when I have a group over, but for me I'm going back to my hand ground beans.

However in the interest of scientific research (sounds better than pigged out) I have tried all the various types of chocolates available in this collection. The white chocolate wasn't as sicky sweet as the american version -- it was perfectly acceptabl
e and I didn't mind eating it at all.

The milk chocolate, the one I was most familiar with and I loved that one. (You'll notice I used the past tense--that one is GONE!). The Salted Carmel was a new flavor for me and it was wonderful. I even tested the dark chocolate and again, I wouldn't turn my nose up at it -- I'd still have to come back and determine that the Milk Chocolate was my favorite.

I live in FL and they arrived and were very soft.Of course I had to be sure they were safe to eat so I tried a piece. They were very soft and melty - good but messy. Then I put them in the fridge to set up. The next day, I had to try them again (science you know) and I found that right out of the fridge they didn't have as much flavor. They are now safely stored outside the fridge and are perfect.

It wasn't too overwhelming although it did taste a bit sweeter than the Chocolate/Chocolate. Great candy bowl filler. title: Excellent!
text: This is a nice smooth roast of coffee. No bitter aftertaste and smooth to the last drop. I bought some refillable K- ups and used my Keurig. Dark enough to be actual coffee. I generally prefer medium to dark roast but this wasn’t too mild. Almost “medium” roast in taste. Definitely yummy!

title: Good for you and they actually taste good too.
text: I wasn’t sure about these—ingredients were interesting but if you are reading this review you know that not all things that are good for you are worth eating. Still I’m up for a try. These arrived and they were pretty warm so I tossed them in the fridge but grabbed one to taste. Very acceptable flavor, great texture and pretty good. VERY filling. I easily split the bar and felt “full”. Later I tried another after they were chilled and I did prefer them chilled. They firm up a bit and I enjoyed them more than warm. I imagine room temp would work, but the first one I tried (warm) wasn’t  very appealing looking and felt a little mushy. I wouldn’t want to eat them as a full diet, although I think it’s hey have practically everything you need in them but they are tasty, filling and they do stay with you. Having to keep them chilled doesn’t make them overly convenient especially in the summer but it’s also not a deal breaker.

I've only used it on meat so far (beef and pork) and have been happy - now that I know what I have, I'll be expanding my use. I'm sure my veggies need this too!

This tastes rich and deep without any “decaf” taste—as good as any cup of coffee, but I can still sleep after drinking it. The K cup makes it easy and it’s also handy to have for guests.

title: Excellent pantry staple.
text: The portions aren’t large, about enough for 2 servings. I prefer Hollandaise on veggies but like Bernaise on beef. I had a sample of Bernaise. I followed the microwave instructions and heated it for 10 seconds at 50% power. It wasn’t quite warm enough so I put it back in for 5 seconds at full power and it was heated through. Poured over my grilled tenderloin (after taste testing) and it was perfectly decent. I’ve made Bernaise many times and although it’s not really “hard” it does take a few minutes and requires cleanup. This didn’t even get the cup I microwaved it in dirty and took less than 2 minutes. It’s tastes like Bernaise sauce. Winner in my book. Its definitely a pantry basic. I see that there are several other “flavors”. I expect I’ll skip the Hollandaise since I LOVE it and requires enough for drowning whatever it’s on. The others though look interesting and if they taste as comparable to the “real thing” as this one does they’ll be great to have around to dress up a meal.

I generally drink black coffee at home but a lot of times when I'm out and the coffee isn't "quite as good as at home" (coffee snob here) they are great to have as a backup. I don't need gluten free so I'm not necessarily the best market for them and I founds them OK but not fabulous. They were crispy, the picture on the package is the actual size of the cookies and they come nicely vacuum packed. The Double Chocolate was the best and the Chocolate Chip was okay but the Toasted Pecan although lower in sugar, was less enjoyable. HOWEVER, they weren't awful (and I've had some bad ones) and my Gluten-free friend who tried them was fairly pleased with them. If you need gluten free snacks and don't want to spend the time, these are worth getting. I did find them a bit better the next day and they were still crisp but I definitely needed something to drink with them - they are too dry to stand alone. I'd still recommend them - if you are looking for this type of product and I'll keep a box around for when needed (but I won't be sneaking into them...). I voluntarily reviewed a sample product.

title: Nice Ghee, Arrived Leaking All Over Bag
text:
We use ghee quite a bit to do Indian cooking but also generally speaking, especially if we can not get butter at the store and need to pinch hit.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a plastic bag which is sealed (thank God) and the jar is inside. Ours came with ghee leaking everywhere.

FLAVOR
This is a nice tasting ghee and is easy to cook with.

HOW TO USE
This does not generally have to be refrigerated but we will keep it there in hot weather. We just use as we do oil and butter. A little goes a long way. It is easy to over use this.

title: Nice Matcha, Bit Of Astringency But Still Good
text:
I am spoiled. I have some of the best matcha I have ever tasted. Everything pales in comparison. I try to be fair, however, so I am reviewing this based on overall matcha rating, not just my favorite.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a moistureproof envelope which can be sealed again with a zipper top.

COLOR
This matcha is a good bright green color as it should be.

FRAGRANCE
This smells fresh and nice.

BREWING
Just to clarify, we brewed this at 70 degrees centigrade which is around 162F. We tried it also at 75C which is higher temperature in F.

We warmed up the cup and chasen. We poured out the water, measured in the correct amount of matcha, strained, and then whipped it with the chasen until foamy.

FOAM
This did get a nice foam on it.

FLAVOR
The flavor was good. I would put it near the top of the ceremonial matchas I have tried so it was good. There was astringency or bitter twist at the end that was not too bad but it was there.

HOW DOES IT COMPARE TO MY FAVORITE?
My favorite matcha of all time is Encha. It is creamy, flavorful, easy to use, and there is no bitterness at the end at all- or at least it is minimal and well balanced. This was not quite as creamy and had a bit more twist of that bitter edge at the end.

OVERALL
If you want a decent ceremonial matcha, this is near the top of my list. Despite it not being able to match my favorite, if you like matcha, try this. (Matcha lattes with this are great, btw)

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a good matcha and performed well. It outshined some others that I have had in the ceremonial category.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I like this. It is a solid matcha. It just is not as good as my favorite. Don't let that stop you. It might very well be your favorite. It is a good one. Again, it does make exceptional matcha lattes.

title: So Far Makes A Great Substitute For Fresh Greens- Notes On HOW To Take This
text:
I like to keep barley green juice and wheatgrass juice powders on hand for winter because sometimes we get storms and fresh greens are either at a premium or we are unable to get any.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a wider based jar with a screw on cap. It is sealed with a plastic seal. There is a scoop inside.

HOW TO TAKE BARLEY GREEN JUICE
I have used barley green juice for most of my life. There are some important things you need to understand about this juice if you have never used it.

First, you need to drink it first thing in the morning on an empty stomach ALONE. If you don't there is an excellent chance you will have bad digestive issues. This is potent stuff so you have to go slow and be careful.

Secondly, you should start small and work up. If you have never used this before, I highly recommend you start with a quarter teaspoon at first and then gradually work up to the scoop that comes in the jar. That is the best way for your body to get used to this, not go into overwhelming detox mode. and make it a pleasant uplifting experience.

QUALITY
This barley green juice powder seems to be excellent quality. The color is great, the flavor excellent and it works well when taken.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you move slowly, take this alone (wait a half hour at least until eating or drinking anything else- hour better) this can be a big help to keep energy up and rebuild the body especially in winter months.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS so far. I am debating putting this into a glass jar (covered) to keep it from moisture even better than the plastic will. I found an old Japanese Barley Green juice powder jar that was very old a while back. It was in glass and sealed. It was just as fresh tasting as anything else I have used. I can not say that for plastic stored powders.

title: Great Aroma In Bag, Flavor Okay But Not Our Favorite Earl Grey
text:
My husband LOVES Earl Grey tea. When I saw this, I got it with him in mind.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a moisture resistant bag that is able to be resealed. You have to cut the top off to use it.

AROMA
The aroma of this is wonderful. When first opened, it is really strong.

HOW WE PREPARED THIS
We prepared this at both 208 and 200F. We used the proper amount per cup in the pot we made it in.

FLAVOR
Once brewed, that is where it started downhill. The flavor was okay, but it was not as nice as other Earl Grey that we have had. The tea itself has a bitter edge to it. It made this unpleasant to drink with the aftertaste.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is an okay tea, but not WOW. My husband will drink it, but he reaches for other Earl Grey teas before this one usually.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This is not the best tea we have had nor is it the worst. It is kind of in the middle. Without the bitter ending to it it would be pretty nice. The bitter taste at the end makes it not one that we want to reach for first. We tend to like Harney, English Tea Store, and Twinings better.

title: Green Tea With Light Lemon Ginger Flavor- Not Intense
text:

HOW THIS COMES

title: Where's The Blueberry?
text:
I am always on the lookout for natural products that allow me to have fresh taste when fresh fruits or vegetables might not be easy to get. This powder seemed perfect for summer.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a jar that is sealed with a vacuum seal. The jar is plastic so you will want to use up the powder within a few months of opening.

SCENT
I mention this because I smelled absolutely no blueberry scent. Is that a problem? I personally freeze dry blueberries and although the scent is not knock over powerful, it is there. This stuff has absolutely no blueberry scent at all.

FLAVOR
I put a teaspoon in a small glass of water and blended it well with a cordless blender. I got every bit of powder blended in. After letting it sit a few moments to absorb well, to my shock and disappointment, there was no blueberry flavor at all in this powder mixed in water. None.

I have freeze dried blueberries several times and when I put them back with water or eat them from the jar freeze dried, they have some blueberry flavor. This powder does not taste at all like blueberries.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I was hoping for a refreshing drink and blueberry supplement to add to mixers when I got this. What I got instead was tasteless purple powder.

MY RATING
ONE STAR. This has no blueberry flavor at all. It is frustrating as I expect at least SOME blueberry flavor from this. I have used the celery powder from this same company and it had flavor to it. This one I am not sure what happened here.

text:

You need to use this up within a year tops and keep it in a cool DRY place. Freeze dried stuff is prone to absorb humidity in the air, so keep that in mind.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fabulous way to supplement with fresh juice in those times when vegetables are not plentiful or easy to get and you just want something fresh to drink or eat.

title: ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC in Golden Milk
text:

PERFORMANCE
I made the best Golden Milk:
1/8 tsp cinnamon
1/4tsp turmeric
1/4 tsp or less of fresh grated ginger
1 cup milk (farm fresh, coconut, almond etc)
1Tbl honey (make a paste from the other spices)
1Tbl maple syrup
1/2 tsp vanilla extract.

Once I have made the spice paste, I stir in everything but the milk. I put milk in the frothing pot that I have and on the heated frothing setting I spin that around. It gets foamy and then I pour in another cup of farm fresh cows milk and froth that up with nothing added. I stir this all together in a very tall mug and enjoy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is very fresh turmeric. Making golden milk, it is absolutely fantastic. For other uses I see it as being excellent too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This stuff is worth it. It is really fantastic. I love how fresh it smells.

title: Pine Needle Tea Is Must Have For Lung Issues And Illness
text:
Have you ever had an illness that settles in the lungs and then just won't let go? I have used many remedies for illness that work, but once in a great while, there is something that hits hard. It will settle in the lungs and it seems like nothing will help it let go. That is where Pine Needle Tea comes in.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes with cut needles (still pretty big pieces) in a resealable bag. You can see the needles through the front window.

HOW I MAKE THIS
SIMPLE TEA
Take a teaspoon and a half of needles and put it in 8oz of boiling water. Let steep for about 15 minutes. Sweeten with honey and drink after straining.
SYRUP FOR ILLNESS
2 cups of water
1/8 c pine needles
Boil for 15 min or until half the water is gone. I often have more than half of the water gone. I mix the strained results with honey and keep it in the refrigerator. This will usually last through a winter and you can take it by the tablespoon like a medicinal syrup to help beat illness.

DOES IT WORK?
This does work. It is the same as other pine needle tea I have used and I even beat walking pneumonia once using it along with other supplementation when nothing else was working. I tried it out of desperation and was amazed at how quickly it worked. I am not saying it will work as well for you, I am only sharing my personal experience. It will help shorten colds and flu also.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are unable to collect pine needles this is a good alternative. The needles are dry and in a moisture proof bag so you can use at your leisure.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like having this handy as I was unable to collect pine needles the last couple of years like I usually do.

title: OMG It Is FABULOUS!
text:
