title: Felt like Royalty every time I made a new batch
text:
I Jjst recently discovered that I enjoy the scent and taste of Jasmine..

So I decided to intertwine my love for jasmine and dinking evening tea by purchasing this Jasmine tea. I was pleasantly surprised about how much I enjoyed it and how well the green tea went with the taste of Jasmine. The tea came in an elegant box and the tea bag itself was pretty appealing.

My only critique would be regarding the tea string which was weak and caused the paper at the end to slip into my tea a couple of times. Besides for that, this tea did the trick.

title: Great for milkshakes!
text:
Matcha is one of my favorite milkshake flavors so I love getting this specifically for that.
Still, it's a great ice cream option that's smooth in texture and taste.

title: Pleasant surprise!
text: These are hands down the best non-bakery store muffins I've ever had. The pumpkin flavor is fresh, the texture is soft, and the spice isn't overpowering. Will continue to buy!

title: Tasty
text: Very good option for sandwiches. A little "too sweet" for some people but I was fine with the flavor.

title: Very good!
text: Pleasantly surprised by how good this tasted! I haven't had luck with many coconut milk yogurts but this one tasted just like a cream dessert. Would definitely repurchase and recommend!

title: Better warm...
text: I wouldn't call these "beignets" but rather "US-style chocolate-filled donuts" because they are dense and huge! I didn't like them as is but they're pretty good when warmed up. VERY indulgent in terms of chocolate and hazelnut flavor so I can't see anyone eating more than one (or less, lol). Wouldn't rebuy for the home but would repurchase for a gathering.

title: Good...
text: Have no complaints about freshness and flavor but I do have a complaint about size. The slices were a little too thick for the kind of sandwich I wanted (Steak & Cheese) but other than that, I enjoyed them. Would buy again for a stir-fry.

title: Not good...
text: I like the convenience of these but this wasn't good. The "dumplings" were super doughy and the overall flavor tasted off. Would not buy again.

title: Great sauce!
text: Surprisingly well-balanced flavors. I was also a huge fan of how hearty the sauce is. Definitely will repurchase!

title: Pretty tasty...
text: Good carbonation and good apple flavor but flavor could be stronger. Not a fan of the high price so will buy when on sale again.

title: Meh
text: Really tasty ice cream but chocolate coating was too thick. I get the minis to avoid this situation but I guess the company thought the non-diary minis needed a thick shell. Obviously I disagree lol. Will repurchase if they change the coating though.

title: Tasty snack
text:
I'm a huge fan of these but I don't regularly buy them because of the price. I don't think these should be almost $2/each. I think if they are worried about money, just reduce the amount of spread in each container. There's currently too much for the amount of sticks so there's always leftovers.
Other than that, I'm a fan.

title: Not good
text: These are WAY too sweet and artificial tasting. My bf thought they were just "meh" but even he said he wouldn't eat them again because they were too decadent.

title: Better than Fruit Loops!
text:
I bought these because I had a craving for Fruit Loops but didn't want something as sweet. Pleasantly surprised by how these are exactly that - a less sweet version of Fruit Loops w/ an additional citrus kick.
Will buy again and definitely recommend!

title: Favorite oat milk so far!
text: Huge fan of the vanilla flavor and creamy consistency. Probably the first plant-based milk I've tasted where the vanilla flavor is actually noticeable!

title: No... no... no.
text: I didn't have high expectations for this bar so I wasn't disappointed BUT I wasn't pleased either. I've had vegan brownies before and this bar just tasted like straight figs. That isn't innately bad but it's not the promised flavor. Wouldn't repurchase and would only recommend to fig lovers.

title: Yummy!
text: I love this version of Simply's lemonade! It's rare to see affordable "fruit+lemonade" options with natural ingredients. My bf isn't a fan because he says it's too sweet so if you're not into sweet juices, I would recommend the original lemonade.

title: Better than starbursts!
text: I love Hi-Chews because they have a great texture and good flavors. The grape flavor doesn't taste like real grapes but it isn't overly sweet or artificial tasting either. It's a "grape juice" flavor and it's very tasty!

title: Really good but...
text: I really enjoyed this yogurt but I did have a major problem with the dried strawberry pieces. They're not dried berries but rather chunks of strawberry leather. I like fruit leather but it wasn't a pleasant texture in my yogurt. Wouldn't repurchase but would recommend to others who don't care about texture.

title: Good lunch option...
text: Got this for my bf and he said he enjoyed it. Wasn't overly salty or sweet and there was a fair amount of veggies and protein. Don't think I'll buy at full price but will definitely get more when they go back on sale.

title: Not bad but...
text: The yogurt's consistency was pleasant and I like having more non-dairy options BUT the mango flavor was highly artificial! I didn't hate it enough to not try 365's almond yogurt again but I definitely won't repurchase this flavor.

title: GROSS!
text: I'm not the biggest fan of artificial sweeteners. On the other hand, I'm a HUGE fan of tea and blood oranges so I gave this a try while it was on sale; HUGE mistake! All I could taste was the sweetener which had a horrible aftertaste. I could barely taste the tea and blood orange flavor. Will not repurchase!

title: Tasty fruit candy option!
text: I'm a huge fan of Hi-Chews and this pack was no exception! All the flavors (green apple, strawberry, and grape) tasted fresh and not too sweet. Definitely planning to buy more in the future!

title: Nice idea but...
text: I like having a non-dairy option for ice cream sandwiches but this one wasn't my cup of tea. The cookie was fine but the ice cream was bland and not creamy. I don't think this are horrible though... but I wouldn't repurchase.

title: Good intro...
text: This was the first oatmilk I tried (as an adult) and I was pleasantly surprised. I'm still not sure if it's for steaming purposes only but I enjoyed it as is. I used it with cold cereal, in teas, and added chocolate syrup to it. I also mixed it with almond milk on occasion which was nice. *shrugs*

title: Good rinds...
text: Epic's pork rinds were perfectly fried yet airy. I really liked the salt/pepper flavor but I took off a star because the pepper flavor was a tad overpowering.

title: Will not repurchase!
text: I'm a huge fan of sweet potato pie and natural ingredients so I jumped on these when they were on sale. Unfortunately mine came with extremely soggy "crust" and the filling had a bad aftertaste. Not a fan!

title: Not the same but...
text: I'm an '80s baby so I grew up with ChocoTaco! I remember the flavors and this version is only half right. The ice cream is the same but the chocolate is slightly less sweet (not a bad thing imo) and the shell is more flimsy (bad thing). I did enjoy the overall taste but I wish it was the same size and has the same shell from my childhood. Oh well, you get what you pay for lol.

title: OMG NO!
text: I was really hoping these would be good. The packaging looks great and the sausages, once cooked, look like the ones on the box. Unfortunately these were GROSS! They were dry yet mushy at the same time. The flavor is similar to paper with a slight undertone of forgettable spices. Basically, they are the worst vegetarian sausages I've ever had in my entire life! Will not buy again nor recommend.

title: Yum
text: Ordered these via Amazon Fresh but my order didn't arrive. Still, I know what these taste like because I buy them offline too and they're great imo. If you like the Xtreme Airheads Strips then you should like these because they are the same thing lol. And if you haven't had those before, they are basically flattened Sour Power Straws with a fruity flavor. Very good imo!

title: Great tea!
text: Huge fan of Taylors of Harrogate after tasting a sample via Prime Sample in 2016. Their Pure Sencha Green Tea is no exception - tastes fantastic! My bf and I both loved the flavor and the matcha powder wasn't overpowering. Would buy again and recommend.

title: YUCK
text: I was hoping for the best despite some of the reviews but it seems those people were right - this dish was gross. I cooked the package exactly as directed and the food came out bland with a weird aftertaste. Like something burnt but not...? It's a weird flavor to describe but not good. Would not recommend nor buy again!

title: YUCK!
text: I used to love these cookies when I was a kid but I think the company changed the recipe because these were horrible. I recently bought a pack in my Fresh order and instantly regretted it! The cookies are soft but the flavor is SOOOOO artificial. Would not buy again nor recommend!

title: My favorite (can) peas...
text: Del Monte has my favorite canned peas because they are sweet but not too sweet and aren't mushy. This can I bought with my Fresh order was no exception so I'm happy.

title: Corn...
text: Is it what it is lol. Mine arrived well within the expiration date and not dented so I'm happy.

title: Surprisingly good...
text: Although the Morningstar Farms Original Chik Patties do not taste exactly like a chicken patty, they do remind me of frozen chicken nuggets! With fresh veggies and condiments, this is a great option for a late-night junk food craving. For meat eaters like me, the closest thing comparable (imo) is a McDonald's chicken sandwich; hope this helps those wondering about the flavor!

title: I enjoyed the links
text: A little too salty to repurchase but other than that, I enjoyed the links. Great meaty flavor with a hint of smokey-ness.

title: I wouldn't buy it again but would recommend others to try it since everyone's palette isn't the ...
text: No complaints except it was less flavorful than I'm used to. Granted I know baby swiss lacks in the flavor department but this one was particularly bland. I wouldn't buy it again but would recommend others to try it since everyone's palette isn't the same. I also liked the price which upped my rating from a 2 to a 3.

title: And I enjoyed the smokey flavor
text:
I'm on the fence about these veggie burgers. On one hand, I do think they taste similar to red meat. And I enjoyed the smokey flavor. On the other hand, you have to cook these in a very specific way to not taste the weird texture they have. The texture, when not cooked a certain way, really took me out of the experience. It made me think of raw meat and I nearly threw up! Granted I am a omnivore, but I've never ate raw beef before so take the previous sentence with a grain of salt.

Not sure if I'll recommend but I think I'll try this again with vegan cheese and hope for the best. The flavor was good overall so I'm still open to it.

title: Five Stars
text: Huge fan of Goya's black beans. And yes, I can tell the difference between another brand's beans.

title: The filling is good but the crust is horrible
text: The filling is good but the crust is horrible. Not your typical flaky samosa crust. More like those crappy pizza roll crust. YUCK! Wouldn't buy again.

title: Another turkey I hated! Doesn't taste "cajun" but rather what people assume ...

title: Such a good deal! And I loved all the flavors excluding ...
text: I can't believe how cheap I got these for. Such a good deal! And I loved all the flavors excluding banana. I didn't try that one but my bf loved it!

title: Lots of broccoli unlike other broccoli cheddar soups I've had ...
text: Lots of broccoli unlike other broccoli cheddar soups I've had BUT lacking in flavor. Would buy again but only if on sale. I refuse to pay full price for a preheated soup I'll have to re-simmer with seasonings.

title: Randomly found these in Montreal and I'm happy to get them in the US
text: Randomly found these in Montreal and I'm happy to get them in the US. I love these! They smell like bad feet but have a great and natural cheese flavor. Plus they are very crunchy which makes them great for sandwiches.

title: This is my favorite applesauce. It's naturally sweet which means it's not ...
text: This is my favorite applesauce. It's naturally sweet which means it's not too sweet. Would recommend especially if you can find the larger size!

title: Surprisingly good popsicles! Taste very natural (although
text: Surprisingly good popsicles! Taste very natural (although, I'm unsure if they are) and good amount of sweetness. Wish I could get a pack in more than 4.

title: YUM

title: Absolutely hated this turkey
text: Absolutely hated this turkey. The peppercorn bits were way too big thus overpowering the taste of the meat. Wouldn't purchase again.

title: Wasn't gross but wasn't good. The peach flavor isn't artificial but this drink ...
text: Wasn't gross but wasn't good. The peach flavor isn't artificial but this drink isn't 100% juice like the brand implies. Wouldn't buy again but didn't hate it. Might be good for smoothies.

title: Delicious Green
text:
*in Oprah voice* I LOVE THIS TEA!

Taylors of Harrogate Green Tea with Jasmine has quickly become one of my favorite boxed teas. I received a box via Prime samples and have bought 3 boxes since then. I really love this stuff! The flavor feels light but tastes full. I'm not a fan of jasmine-flavored things but this tea has a sweet and light floral flavor I love. Also, I have a fondness for large mugs but only need 1 bag (at a 2min steep) for my 12oz mugs. Normally I need 2 so it's nice to save money. And speaking of which, this tea is SO AFFORDABLE! Right now it's less than $4 and Taylors' seem to always have a 20% off coupon on here. You can't beat that price especially for their quality! I digress. I'm so happy I found this tea and will continue to drink it unless they change it somehow.

title: Could've been better...

title: Disappointment!

title: Great green option...

title: I really like the tin but the flavor wasn't my cup of ...

We both agree is tastes like an energy drink but that's what it is so you can't fault it for that. I like the design but because neither of us would repurchase, I gave it an average rating.

title: "Pretty good"

title: Although this says "apple pie" it tasted more like peach to me
text: Although this says "apple pie" it tasted more like peach to me. My bf said the same thing and it wasn't until I took a double-take at my receipt did I realize it was supposed to taste like apple, not peach. For that, I wouldn't buy again.

title: Meh in a bag...

And although he's loca por coffee, I'm an occasional drinker who though this was just "meh." Not overly sweet, not strong (even for me), but I could distinguish the hazelnut.

title: Don't overhype if you're a childhood return!

The milk chocolate isn't as milky but overly sweet and the cookie has a weird grainy aftertaste. In short, these aren't horrible or even bad but they aren't great (or borderline good) either.

title: Didn't like but don't regret!
text: These were okay but I think fresh Mochi would be best (if available). Every flavor outside of the peanut butter one was kind of light (read: weak) but  it really depends on your flavor palette.

title: Delicious and not overly sweet! You also get a lot of bunnies in ...
text: Delicious and not overly sweet! You also get a lot of bunnies in this box which makes it (imo) an affordable snack.

title: A bit on the dry side but I love the taste especially when paired with Nutella
text: A bit on the dry side but I love the taste especially when paired with Nutella. Great breakfast for the on-the-go morning person (or lazy morning person lol).

title: Pleasant Surprise
text: I love ginger but I haven't found a ginger candy I like until now. These were just as strong as I thought they would be, which is why I normally hate ginger candy, but they are chewy like toffee so you can eat them piece by piece. Plus there's a nice balance of spice and sweetness.

title: I hate double-stuffed Oreos but my bf bought these so I ...
text: I hate double-stuffed Oreos but my bf bought these so I gave them a try. I like the vanilla/chocolate combo but the double-stuffing was too much. Hopefully we get this variety in a regular version.

title: Five Stars
text: Not as much juice in the center as I remember but still tasty!

title: Smooth and tasty!
text: I bought this for my boyfriend's birthday as a gift. He's a coffee fanatic so I wanted to get him a brand he's never tried. I picked this because it's organic and FT (fair trade) but didn't have high hopes since I never tasted this. Thankfully it all worked out because my boyfriend loved it! The first time he tried it, he thought he didn't brew it long enough because it was so smooth. He said it reminded him of tea but tasted like coffee. And now with each cup, he loves it more and more making it officially one of his favorites.

title: Delicious and fresh!!
text: Excellent quality. Will buy again.

text:
I tend to avoid writing reviews -- particularly when I have nothing of substance to add to what are already a significant number of positive reviews, which seems generally the case with my purchases.

I usually purchase either Twinings (easier to open packaging) or Bigelow (slightly stronger flavor) lemon/ginger tea in 100/120 unit orders - neither was available at a reasonable price when I last re-ordered mid-December 2020. So I was very curious to try Taylors. Sadly the experience was disappointing. Flavor was significantly weaker than either of the two competitors, but what was most vexing was the individual packaging - the scoring of the packet was faulty, frustrating attempts to open, leading to crude tears which often rips the tag; on at least one third of the tea bags I've attempted to use to date, the portions of the strings have been sewn _into_ the bag so that they are too short to be useful. While I don't know whether this is one unfortunate defective box of tea bags, I'm not prepared spend any more money to find out otherwise.

title: This is the best teabag Darjeeling tea I've found
text:
I'm admittedly fussy about my tea. I much prefer Darjeeling tea over others, and when I have time I prefer to make it with good loose leaf tea. But I'm not above using teabags for convenience to make a quick cup in the middle of a busy day. I hadn't found a good Darjeeling teabag until I stumbled upon these. I have tried many brands, including both the better-known ones (adequate but uninspiring), as well as specialty brands from small sellers (overpriced and very disappointing).

I find that this tea brews a very nice cup (I pour boiling water, steep for 5 minutes) that is much much better than any other teabag Darjeeling, including more expensive products. I won't say it's as good as loose leaf tea, but it certainly is quite pleasant and enjoyable, with very good flavor and taste. I can recommend it without hesitation.

title: Yes it's superior to the domestic (US) Rose's, but is it worth the price?
text:
I use a lot of lime juice cordial (aka sweetened lime juice) in my cocktails, including of course gin gimlets. So I bought this product on a whim, to try it out. I immediately noticed the subtle improvement in the lime fragrance, but it took a couple of sips before I was sure that there was a noticeable difference in the gimlet taste. There was, but it's rather subtle -- I don't know if I'd have really noticed if someone else had handed me the glass.

So overall I give the product a superior rating, it is really good. But I'm not quite convinced that it's worth the 50% price premium, especially for something I use a lot of. Your money, your choice.

title: This is an excellent coffee, surprisingly good in fact.
text:
I make my coffee rather strong, in a French press. I don't like coffee that's too acid or too bitter or too roasted. Also, I usually don't drink decaf, but partner-in-life wanted some to have caffeine-free but richly flavorful coffee in the afternoon or evening. So I went looking, and decided to try this one, based on the description.

Verdict: It's excellent. Even as strong as I make it, it has a lovely mellow chocolate-like body, with a lovely aroma that just prepares you for the pleasure of that first sip. And I find myself finishing the cup (actually a big mug), and wishing there was just a bit more left.

I can easily recommend it if you're looking for a nice decaf and your preferences align with well-rounded rather than strongly edgy. But I also recommend making it strong, you might be pleasantly surprised.

title: Meh.  Not convinced its Darjeeeling tea, and it's definitely not worth the premium price.
text:
I've been drinking Darjeeling tea for most of my life, and like to think I know what's good (and what's better). I was hopeful about this new product on Amazon, it all sounded great. And since these are tea bags, I wasn't expecting the moon, just a bit nicer than the competition (I'm comparing with Twinings here).

While the marketing is lovely, unfortunately the product is meh at best. It certainly doesn't have that special Darjeeling tea flavor that I'm so used to, and doesn't have any other redeeming flavors either. It's not even slightly better than Twinings, in fact, it's less flavorful if anything. I'm not even convinced it's real Darjeeling tea: if it is, it's the cheap stuff grown on the lower slopes. I'll pass, thanks.

For the price, I'd rather buy the Twinings when I want tea bags for the convenience. And when I want a nice cup of Darjeeling tea, I'll go to my tin of loose-leaf premium Darjeeling that still seems to be the only way you can get a really nice cup.

title: Delicious and nutritious dried cranberries
text:
Great product from well known and respected brand Ocean Spray. Have been buying it for years, always fresh, juicy, perfect combination of sweet and tart taste.
Great as a snack right out of the box or in various recipes. I personally use it every morning with my oatmeal for an extra serving of fiber and vitamin C plus it adds a very pleasant texture and jazzes it up a bit.
According to the manufacturer these cranberries have zero artificial flavors or preservatives, gluten and peanut free.
Also they been known to boost Immune System, Maintain Heart Health, Relax Muscle Cramps, Fortifies Bones, Combat Urinary Tract Infection (UTI), Help Cure Anemia.
Amazon offers best price plus of course convenience so I’ve got zero complaints and recommend this marvelous product to everyone.

title: Delicious English Black Currant Jam
text:
Was a bit hesitant to get it because of the high price for such small jar but it was well worth it! It’s very tasty, full of real black currant flavor, perfectly textured with lots of yummy berries, not too sweet or tangy, just right. It was a perfect breakfast companion to mini cheese danishes and English Lady Grey tea, I assume it would be amazing too with the toast, bagel or oatmeal.
Also it can be enjoyable right out of the jar or used for all kinds of sauces and pastry stuffings, very yummy and versatile product.
In my opinion it’s so much better than the version sold by the renown french brand BM.
Definitely recommend it to any black currant preserves lover!

title: Delicious sugar

Box arrived in good condition, spout on the side makes pouring out this sugar so much easier and powder wasn’t clumped, so no complaints and definitely recommend it to everyone.

title: Delicious
text:
Maybe its not the BEST tasting dulce de leche I have ever tried but its still is a very delicious tasting spread, made with wholesome ingredients, packed in an environmentally safe glass jar and made in Spain.
We got it only few days ago and already only a bit of this delightful caramel spread is left. It has light pleasant taste with notes of vanilla, perfectly sweet but not overbearing. You can bake with it, make it into a cream or just eat it straight out of the jar with coffee or tea. Perfect as a dessert or any time you would want a sweet and yummy treat. Definitely get it, price is a but high but considering its an imported product from Europe which gets delivered directly to the house, high price is understandable.

title: Delicious herbal tea!

I personally love to infuse it for 4-5 minutes then let it cool down a bit, then add some raw honey and voila my delectable tea is ready to be enjoyed any time day of night since it doesn’t contain any caffeine. If you’re a lover of citrusy flavored drinks or prefer your tea with a slice of lemon-try it and chances are you won’t be disappointed. Bigelow is great American tea producing company and their teas all are delicious and good quality 👍

title: Not great, not terrible. 5/5 Aroma, 2/5 Body.
text:
Let me start by saying that the cheap price of ~$3 USD for the tin is a large portion of the rating. I opened it and it smells like cheap liquid smoke and nothing else, which I wasn't used to for Lapsangs. Combine this smell with a spelling error on the tin and I was convinced i got a fake, but opted to brew it anyway. It brewed to the color featured in the photos, and tasted like a very mild version of the smell. If you don't like the scent of opening a bag of cheap extra-smoky flavored jerky in your nose, you probably wont like this. The flavor, when i can taste anything at all aside from the mild smoky flavor, is even more mild. I was kind of hoping for this tea to figuratively punch me in the mouth with smoke since it was so bold and smoky in the tin, but it didn't come close. Maybe mix this with another more full-bodied tea.

I've had better smoked teas for sure, but for the price, it's reminiscent enough for me. I loved smoked teas and this one isn't too terrible, but maybe not a good first choice for someone who is new to Lapsang Souchong.

title: Great Old Time Coffee Favorite...newly discovered
text:
I recently went back to coffee after a stint with drinking tea only. This time I wanted to change it up a bit and try fresh ground coffee at home with a french press. I fondly remember 8 o'clock coffee growing up and I thought I'd try the brand again with a french press and grinder. I bought a nice blade grinder and even nicer french press here on Amazon and a 2lb bag of medium roast whole been 8 o clock coffee. Wow...I have now re-discovered the joys of the morning rituals brewing coffee...the aromas...the taste. The coffee is 100% Arabica beans that are roasted and packaged here in the U.S. Same old time quality...added to a new world brewing method using the French Press. I highly recommend this coffee be used as a whole bean-at-home grind and with a good french press.

Best cup of coffee you ever tasted!!!

title: too expensive for what you get
text:
First, this chocolate syrup does not taste as well as the best sugar syrups.

But if you are looking at this product, it is because you must go sugar free, and in that category, it is relatively decent tasting.

The problem is that it is priced at almost 10 $ for a rather small bottle. At that price, it had better be the best chocolate syrup I have ever had in my life. It isn't.

Another defect is that before first use, you need to remove a plastic seal over the top of the bottle. Lots of products have that, both to ensure freshness as well as to prove it was not tampered with. (The industry term for this is a tamper safety seal?)

The problem with this syrup's bottle is that its seal is almost impossible to remove! The reason why is because it lacks large tabs that your fingers can readily grip. The tabs here were micro sized (< 1 mm?), my fingers could not get a grip, I eventually had to get a knife. I should not have to do this. The product engineer massively failed here. For this expensive of a product, it is inexcusable.

An intelligent design is that part of the tab juts out

title: very impressive, perfect for the tea lover in your life
text:
I drink a lot of tea, easily a few cups a day. I heard about this as one of Oprah's Favorite Things this year, so I was very happy to give the set a try. First, it arrives in a gorgeous black box perfect for gift-giving, if you're inclined to not keep it for yourself. Black is the theme here, as everything comes in black packaging. There's a silver strainer for using in a cup or tea pot, a black thermos (good for one cup of tea) which includes a tiny strainer inside, and two boxes of tea. Mine included a box of mint green tea and an herbal tea (After Eight), which has a chocolate flavor to it.

The tea is disc-shaped and comes in sealed pouches. You'll have to put them in bags or containers to keep them fresh after you open them, and I've been able to rebrew them once or twice. It says to use two discs if you brew a pot (I'm assuming a large pot), but they're fine for the travel thermos or a cup. I did have a little problem putting one in the thermos' strainer, just because it's a bit of a tight fit.

The thermos does a great job of retaining the tea's heat. Maybe too much of a great job! My nick is 'nekojita' for a reason (cat's tongue - someone who doesn't like eating or drinking things too hot). I've had to pour the tea out of the thermos into a cup to cool it down!

The set isn't cheap, but it's great quality. You definitely get what you pay for with this. I look forward to trying the other tea blends.

I like the squeezable bottle, and try to get it for my honey whenever possible. It makes portioning out honey so much easier. This honey is supposed to have a good amount of 'manuka' in it, meaning it'll be great for treating sore throats and ailments. It tastes good (I've tried a bit in teas) and came well-sealed. For the price, it's a good amount of honey. I wouldn't for baking, but will be doling it out once the sniffles start.

text: I'm an avid tea drinker, and lately I've been enjoying green, white and pu erh tea. I've several bricks of pu erh tea: aged, raw and ripe. title: Rich flavor for cold brew
text: I have been trying different coffees for cold-brewing lately. The Aiello Gourmet Coffee has a rich flavor when cold-brewed. The package is vacuum sealed for freshness. It is difficult to reseal afterwards if you only use a little at a time, but for cold-brewing I use about half a package to cold-brew 2 quarts of coffee, so it's not a big deal. It is a fine ground coffee, so you have to cut the quantity and time down a bit compared to a medium or coarse ground. It actually works out well, because I can set it up the night before, and 8-10 hrs later it is ready. I am enjoying the flavor and will definitely keep it in the rotation.

title: good for sardines
text: We're trying to get more fish/omega-3s into our diet so decided to give these sardines a try. They're sardines, so yes, a little smelly and strong-flavored. They come in a lot of oil, but they're moist and better than I expected (the husband agrees). We had trouble opening one can, but not others. It's easy to add fish to rice bowls or pasta with these cans in the house, and of course, the family cat heartily approves of them (once rinsed of oil).

title: strong peppermint green tea
text: Teafy produces quality tea, and this one isn't an exception. I like peppermint green tea, so had to try theirs. I will say that this is on the strong side (which isn't bad) so mind the measurement unless you like strong flavors. Or perhaps that was me. When I did a proper teaspoon, the flavor was perfect. Also, this blend fits better in tea ball diffuser (meaning mesh) than a teacup diffuser (usually porcelain or clay) which has larger holes.

title: pleasant oolong
text: I drink a lot of black and green tea and consider oolong somewhere in between. This is a really nice oolong to drink, milder than black but something different than green. It comes in a sealable bag and has large leaves which means you can put it in a pot or teacup with a diffuser that has larger holes than a tea ball diffuser. I brewed it for around five minutes had a very nice cup of oolong, and was able to rebrew it. This brand has yet to disappoint me.

title: tasty breakfast
text: This makes for a tasty breakfast; I really like the PB and cacao flavor. I make it with a mix of water and milk (more water), and for me, I have to let it sit another minute after cooking it for it to thicken up. I don't need to add additional sugar as it's fine as is. You can taste the peanut butter and cacao, but neither flavor is overpowering. It's something different and easy to make in the morning, and it does leave me feeling full.

title: Very tart
text: These are very tart; I don't mind because I like tart, but be aware of that. They're also very small. I was a bit surprised when the box came, and again when I opened it to reveal the tubes inside. These snacks are small tubes that are a bit gummy, so be aware there will be some sticking to the teeth. The flavor is definitely tart apples, with chia seeds mixed in (I got the apple chia flavor). I enjoy them and figure it's a little vitamin and fiber boost. However, the price for these does seem a bit high, maybe because of the quality of the ingredients. Be aware of that, and that these won't really fill you up. Also, they're made in Russia.

title: addicting
text: These crackers are addicting. Nice crunch and a hint of spice, they're savory and it would be easy to eat a bag of them in one sitting. Which isn't good since that's three servings. I've gotten others hooked on them. I thought these were one-serving bags, so you get a lot in this order.

title: lots of variety
text:
I like Bob's Red Mill products since they're quality and trustworthy, so I gave this variety box of peanut butter oat bars a try. They're a nice snack and help with the mid-day munchies, as well as not made with a bunch of fillers.
Of course, my favorite is the Peanut Butter & Chocolate bar, which has a nice chocolate flavor. I would gladly buy a box of these.
Next is the Peanut Butter & Honey, which isn't too sweet and lets the peanut butter flavor come through.
The Peanut Butter & Coconut surprised me, because I'm on the fence with coconut; sometimes I like it, sometimes I don't. It wasn't too strong of a flavor here and complimented the peanut butter. Not sure I'd get a whole box of it, but I didn't mind it at all in this box.
I ate the Peanut Butter & Jelly, but I'm on the fence about it. It's not bad, but it's not one I'd go out of my way to eat again.
I didn't like the Peanut Butter & Banana, but then again, I usually don't like anything with a banana flavor to it unless it's fresh-baked banana bread or an unripe banana. This one is on me.
The bars are easy to chew and decently moist. They vary in calories (surprisingly, the chocolate one has the least) and while they're not protein powerhouses, they're a decent snack.

title: delicious
text: These are a little pricy, but they're unroasted and unsalted cashew nuts. They're also very fresh and so delicious. I dislike salted nuts, so these are perfect. They're great if you want to add them to a recipe or roast and flavor them yourself, but I eat them straight out of the bag. They're a great snack and healthy.

title: good for baking
text: I used this lavender in a lavender tea bread and it turned out delicious. Also smells wonderful. You get a good amount for the money and the bag is resealable.

title: yummy and moist
text: These lemon and lavender macaroons are very yummy. They're also nice and moist, so they arrive fresh. The lemon flavor is strong but not overwhelming, and yes, they taste like almonds since that's the main ingredient. They're a bit different and vegetarian, and made from good ingredients. Something a little different, and they're not cheap, but the type of cookie you'd find in a bakery so think of the price that way. Two cookies are a 140 calorie serving, and I find that's usually enough since they're dense and flavorful. The bags are resealable to help keep them fresh.

title: good to have on hand
text: These are the type of things that are good to have on hand around the holidays; they taste good and most people enjoy chocolate and pretzels. Together, they're a snack people enjoy, so they're a nice gift or a good choice to take to a party or as a gift for a host. There's nothing amazing about these, just decent chocolate (milk and white) covering pretzels with sprinkles thrown in.

title: more to look at than to eat
text:
I've heard about these types of 'candy', and knew from a friend in Japan that these aren't given because of their flavor (warning, they don't really have any flavor). These candies are based on four famous jewels, and if you know anything about some Japanese traditions (such as their take on Valentine's Day), giving someone a jewel-like candy that doesn't have much of a taste would make sense. Especially since these don't cost so much in Japan.
However, they do cost a lot here in the US, so this definitely falls under a 'unique' gift category. It comes in a lovely display case (this one in a red box), and the seller takes care to ensure the candy arrives in great shape (that it remains crystal clear). If you want to give someone something I highly doubt they've received before, this might just be that gift.

title: Good tasting tea, semi-pretty flowers
text:
I must note that this blooming tea really should be brewed in a glass teapot, with enough room for the ball to open into a flower. Second, since it's white tea (with flavoring), you should be careful of the water temperature - it shouldn't reach boiling, but be around 180 F. Temperature and steeping time can affect its flavor.

That said, this tea has a good, fruity flavor with floral notes. It's not too strong, but it does have a nice taste. The flowers aren't as 'pretty' as other teas I've tried, and yes, bits do fall/break off. Not all of the tea 'balls' I've tried have opened all the way, either. If you're looking for the best presentation, this might not be the tea to try, but it does taste good.

title: perfect for this time of year
text: I love cinnamon, and I especially love cinnamon in mulled wine, spiced cider, and as a scent to make the house seem cozier. These sticks are a good bargain for the amount you get in the container and are usually around two inches or so in length (there was a piece of paper taped over the front to knock down the size of the sticks. I've had sticks that were more fragrant in the past, but are good and do a wonderful job of providing flavor and aroma, especially for the price.

title: great for snacks or gift giving
text: Individual, these chocolates are about four ounces each, which makes them perfect for snacks if you're keeping them for yourself. They come in a nice cardboard box with a handle, which is a good presentation for a gift (and easy to carry). It's a nice selection with dark chocolate caramels, milk chocolate-covered almonds (both flavored with sea salt), and milk chocolate-covered cherries, all individually wrapped. All of them taste delicious in my opinion, but others' tastes may vary. I like the variety of this set and that the chocolate is fair trade, as well as of good quality. All in all, a great item to have on hand this time of year.

title: gives a good flavor boost
text: I love a bit of spice, and this bag of chipotle powder definitely provides it. You get a lot of spice for the price, nice and fresh in a resealable pouch. I'd say it's medium to hot, as it provides a nice, smokey kick of flavor to whatever you put it in. It's definitely provided a good flavor boost to a few recipes.

title: the taste of fall
text: I love this tea so much, it's the taste of fall for me, though I could have it year-round. Definitely, my favorite pumpkin tea since it's a wonderful blend of spices, black tea, and 'pumpkin' flavor. I have it with a little milk and sugar to start my day.

title: nice selection of tea
text:
You get a really nice selection of black tea blends here, with a heart-shaped tea difuser. I will say that while I'm happy with this selection that I liked another one a bit better.
There was a nice scent with most of the tea blends, but nothing that really stood out with most of them. However, there is a wide variety here, between strong blends and fruity blends. My favorites tended to be the Comfort blend, Gratitude blend, and the Fog Cutter blend. Perhaps I'm influenced by liking stronger blends. I do like that here's a variety of blends here, including some that would make some good ice teas.
I did brew to the stronger time (five minutes). To each their own with tea, so I believe that some will really like these, since they do have a wide variety of blends.

title: not bad
text: For icing in a tube, this is not bad at all. It is a bit gritty, but it has good flavor and is 'stiff' enough to hold its shape, which helps in forming borders or whatever you want to design with the icing. You do need to knead the tube since it is so thick, and if you have any left over, you're to put the remaining icing in the fridge (it's good for up to two weeks). However, then it's REALLY stiff and impossible to get out of the tube unless you warm it up.

title: great for baking
text: This Rodelle cocoa powder worked wonderful in a batch of brownies, and will be used a lot for the upcoming holiday baking season (good thing it's good for over a year). This is unsweetened cocoa, which allows for a lot of flexibility in baking, and has a deep, rich flavor.

title: delicious
text: I love pumpkin. Really. So of course I love pumpkin spice lattes. Now I can have pumpkin spice coffe/lattes at home without having to pay a fortune. These coffee pods are delicious, and I've had no problem using them in my Keurig. I also like that they're recyclable. I'll definitely be stocking up on them, as pumpkin spice is not just for fall in my world.

title: wonderful variety pack of black tea
text:
Okay, I love tea. REALLY. I drink tea every day, and different types of tea. Black, green, white, pu'erh, you name it. So I was excited to try this variety pack from August Uncommon, especially since I've never heard of them before.
The teas come in black, resealable pouches and include a plastic spoon for measuring. They say they have about fifteen servings in each. They're marked with instructions and flavor 'notes', and I do like their branding, very nice.
Black Metallic - floral and smoky. Floral black tea with elderberry and violet tea notes. Wow, this really smells amazing. I think I liked this one the best since it was something different, had a bright taste and the florals really popped. Definitely a good blend to start the day.
Painted Dessert - bold and spicy. Crisp black tea with chili and chocolate. I thought I'd like this one the best, and I do like it, but it's my second favorite. I taste the chocolate more than I do the chili. It's good, and I bet it'll be better when the weather cools some more.
Low Country - rich and malty. Black tea with bourbon and burnt sugar notes. I hate to say that this is my 'least' favorite because it's still good. I wonder if my brother, the bourbon lover, would like it. It is strong, but it just...it lacks in flavor when compared to the other two. Like the other two, it smells AMAZING. It is something a bit different than a black tea, though.
All in all, I'll definitely order from this company and would like to try some of their other blends. I do get three brews from each serving, like they say, with plenty of flavor in the third brew.

title: Salt is fine, but the box was damaged
text: The salt is fine grain and is pretty standard. The clear plastic window on the box was not adhered to the box very well though, and a lot of salt spilled out from it during shipping.

title: a sweet surprise
text: I'll admit that I wasn't sure what to expect from these chips (or brand). But after trying their Churro Loco snacks, I want to try more of HA!s flavors. These are cinnamony goodness, yes they are, a nice, sweet treat packed with protein to satisfy your hunger. I like that they come in individual serving bags, which help with portion control, and they do a good job of giving you a treat that's not all sugar.

title: addictive
text: These chips are certainly snackable. I would keep a bag near my desk and grab them when I felt hungry, and had to stop myself after eating a handful. They have a good flavor to them, are crunchy, and you could use them to scoop dips and salsas. They're also a tad greasy, so despite being made (in part) from chickpeas, I wouldn't call them 'healthy'. They are gluten free, so there is that.

title: something different
text: I love yuzu, so finding this ponzu yuzu that's designed to remain fresh until you use all of it is wonderful. It's a refreshing bit of citrus in marinades and sauces, and well worth the price.

title: yummy
text: I use honey a lot in baking-in fact, I make a honey wheat oatmeal bread every week, among other things. This gave a wonderful flavor to the bread, as it did to a marinade and other recipes. The only complaint I have is that it doesn't come in a squeeze bottle (since I usually weigh things for recipes and it's easier to squeeze ingredients into the receptacle than to measure out). Excellent quality honey.

title: fuego indeed
text:
These are indeed spicy jerky sticks. I don't think they're overly spicy, but I do like spice. I also definitely had a lingering heat in my mouth from these and will have something to help cool it off. So be aware, these pack a punch.
That said, these are good. They are also not hard at all - I hate having jerky and then feel stuff stuck in my teeth afterwards. No problem here. Easy to chew and delicious. Great way to get some protein with nice flavor.

title: just vanilla
text: This is pure vanilla bean ground up: you can smell it as soon as you open the packet. It's really for adding vanilla flavor to drinks, smoothies and the like, and to some baking products, but not to replace vanilla extract (which has alcohol in it). I've tried this in teas and coffees, as well as some tea cakes, and it does give a boost of vanilla flavor.

title: wonderful for baking
text: This was recommended for a recipe, and the cakes turned out so delicious. Worked just as well for mochi, too. I look forward to using it in more recipes.

title: cuteness without the guilt
text: Supernatural's unicorn sprinkles allow you to pretty up your baking without any guilt or worries - it's low sugar, no additives for the color, and gluten-free, vegan, and soy-free. The sprinkles are cute with the stars and pastel colors, and don't taste like much (I don't really expect sprinkles to taste like much, to be honest). They're more expensive than other sprinkles, but then again, they come with less worries about any reactions, too.

title: creamy and nutty
text: I think of these bars as 'European' chocolate, they're very creamy and 'mild', quite delicious. They have whole hazelnuts in them, which is nice, though you may get a piece with a lot of nuts in it and a piece without any (not a bad thing considering that the chocolate is good). The bars are quite a treat and I find myself having a couple pieces here and there, easy to portion considering the whole nuts in them. If you love hazelnuts or know someone who does, I think you/they will enjoy these bars.

title: wonderful flavor
text: I'd never heard of pomegranate molasses before until I needed it for a recipe. Wow, it's a bright blast of flavor that I'm using a lot of now. This Cortas brand is living up to its reviews, and the price was good for four bottles. They arrived REALLY well packaged (it took a few minutes to get them unwrapped, in fact).

title: I wish this was available all year round
text: Though that would probably be a bad thing for my weight - this is just sooo good if you love pumpkin cheesecake. It's so creamy and delicious, not too heavy, and has graham cracker crust in it. I'll be waiting for it to come back in stock.

title: delicious
text: This is a delicious dark chocolate with cranberries and almonds. I've enjoyed this in the past, and miss the old packaging, but the chocolate inside is still the same. Great mix of tart cranberries with the dark chocolate and a bit of crunch from the almonds.

title: delicious
text: This is one of my favorite teas. I love the cinnamon flavor to it, a bit of extra warmth, and drink it all year round. The tea comes in individual packets which keeps it fresh (and makes it easier to take it with you), and the prices for the amount of teabags is good.

title: delicious chocolate
text: I used this in a cookie recipe as it was the powdered chocolate/cocoa recommended, and they turned out delicious (in fact, someone walked off with the tray of cookies when no one was looking). Will definitely purchase again.

title: perfect for sushi rice
text: I love this rice vinegar with my sushi rice, whether I make sushi or not. It gives it a nice flavor which accents a lot of dishes. It arrived in great condition.

title: gives a nice kick
text: Had a couple recipes that required this spice mix, and now end up throwing it in a lot of dishes (rice, meat, etc.). It's addictive and gives a nice kick to a meal, so having a bag this size is wonderful. Very good bargain, lot of flavor.

title: tasty lemon flavor
text: These do have a nice lemon flavor to them - I'll admit, I was torn between which flavor of these Biscolata Pia cookies to get, and went with the lemon ones since I adore lemon and it had good reviews. However, I think next time I'll try the chocolate flavors since I don't really like white chocolate. If you enjoy lemon AND white chocolate, you'll probably love these. They are soft and I like that they're not too big, and you get four containers which makes it a good price. It's a good snack, especially if you want to share them.

title: must have for some recipes
text: I couldn't get coconut milk from the stores around me that were delivering, so I figured I'd try it from Amazon. Goya has good coconut milk that tastes wonderful in the curries I make, and the cans arrived in great shape.

title: delicious
text: I bought this to make with a lemon cake and it's delicious. Gives the cake a wonderful flavor, so much so that I'm making it all the time now per the husband's request. Little goes a long way. Bottle arrived in good condition.

title: has a nice zest to it
text: This is  a 'creamy' Italian dressing even though it looks more like regular. It's nice and thick and has a zesty flavor to it, and is vegan and keto friendly. I guess it's nice that it's another way to get veggies in your diet. Because it is so thick, it works well as a dip.

title: beware - so addicting
text: Okay, maybe I could have lived without knowing about these cookies. Or at least, my waistline could have because these rare so delicious. I'm not usually the biggest chocolate chip fan, but the vanilla frosting drew me in. It's good that these aren't the biggest cookies, because they would do even more damage. One is enough to satisfy my sweet craving for a good while (though the husband can gobble two at a time very easily). They say it's best to eat them within twelve days upon arrival for freshness, and that's NOT a problem. The cookies are nice and soft, with lots of little chocolate chips and a good amount of frosting in the middle. It's going to be a challenge to hold back on ordering them.

title: just as good as the brand names
text: I used this to make a batch of risotto rice, and it was just as good as the Swanson low sodium chicken brother I usually use. There was enough for three and a half cups with half a cup left over, and it didn't taste any different than the other batches of risotto I made in the past. Can't check the price, but I would assume it's a little cheaper. Nice to have another alternative out there.

title: nice smoked paprika
text: I use paprika a lot, smoked and sweet - on a lot of dishes (those that call for it and those that don't). This might not be as strong as Penzey's, but it has a good flavor and is a value for its price. Came sealed and had more than enough time on the 'sell by' date.

title: tasty and easy to make
text:
I'll admit, I haven't made pancakes in a while, so I was happy to giveBob's Red Mill Homestyle Pancake Mix a try. I like that you just have to add water, so once you have the mix, no worries about other ingredients. I like that there's not a lot of weird things in the mix. I like the resealable bag.
I added the water, let it sit for a minute or two, and greased up a non-stick pan. Followed the instructions (dropped 1/4 a cup, let it bubble, flipped, gave it a minute or two) and these turned out tasty pancakes. Nice and simple. I don't like a lot of stuff on my pancakes, so a tiny bit of butter and some lemon curd and I was done. So tasty.

title: great red curry taste
text: I used this in a red curry recipe and I have to say, AMAZING. This is exactly like what I get when I eat out, so I'm soo happy right now. I'm also planning on making this A LOT. Just add some coconut milk, sweet chili sauce and ginger and there you go! I'm glad I read the reviews where I saw I can freeze this since it is a lot, and it does have a great kick of heat to it (I doubled it for one recipe, and next time I think I'll cut back to maybe one and a half). So yummy and I'll definitely re-order when my tub runs out!

title: great mix, fast delivery
text: I like that you can get the Nespresso Vertuoline capsules from Amazon for the same price and fast delivery with no extra charge. No, there's no savings here (these things never go on sale as far as I know) - you may get some 'freebies' like chocolates or biscuits from Nespresso if you order a lot of coffee at once, and free delivery if, again, you  meet a certain order amount. I don't have to worry about that with Amazon (at least with Amazon Prime). I like this Dark assortment variety pack because I've ordered all of these before, especially the espresso blends. All the flavors are very nice, have good flavor without being harsh. I love making my own lattes or coffee drinks with these.

title: brisk cup of coffee
text:
These Odacia pods are a nice, brisk cup of dark roast coffee - I like that I can brew one whenever I like (or a guest likes) without having to worry about making a pot or the coffee going stale, since I usually like espresso or smaller cups. This has a nice amount of caffeine and 'strength' to it without being too strong, and so does well with a little milk. It has a nice crema 'head' to it, as does the rest of the Vertuoline.
This is basically the same price as if ordering from Nespresso with two day shipping, which is great (no need to order a lot of coffee at once to get their free delivery). It would be nice if you could get the recycle bags through Amazon as well, but guess I'll just have to stock up whenever I do order from Nespresso or visit their store.

title: my own starbucks
text: Well, not exactly, but with these double espresso capsules, I can have a nice latte or espresso drink at home or take on the go for less money and fuss (no drive through, no busy parking lot, no wait). I love my Vertuo machine and that I can order from Amazon as well as from Nespresso. These Chiaro double espressos are a nice medium blend, a bit of a kick but not too much, and have a good flavor. I like to add heated milk to them (they produce a bit of their own foam), some cinnamon and a little beet sugar and maybe whipped cream now and then, and am good to go.

title: smooth green tea with mint
text: I like my green tea with a little flavor when I'm drinking this at work, and this is perfect - it's individually bagged, so I can throw it in a drawer or carry it around to meetings then have it whenever, and that also keeps it nice and fresh. The tea itself is smooth and tasteful with just a bit of mint, nothing too overpowering. It's a good quality of green tea.

title: aromatic and flavorful
text: I made some nut rolls and decided to give this Amazon brand spice a try. As soon as I opened it, you could smell the spice - very aromatic and fresh. I don't use much in the recipe which makes a LOT of nut rolls, but it definitely provided a lot of flavor in the nut mix. This is a good value for the spice, it's fresh and has a good 'sell by' date (though you should use it within a few months of opening), was well sealed and has a lid easy to remove though it has a shaker top.

title: okay if fresh isn't available
text: I love cilantro. LOVE IT. I much prefer fresh and if not, then a certain spice company where I can buy it in bags (I use it that much) since I do add it to a lot of things, especially when I cook rice. This Amazon brand isn't bad, it has a nice scent and the taste is all right. I like the big bottle (with a shaker lid) and it did arrive sealed. The date on the bottom states it's good for over a year, though really, once you open it, you should use it up within a few months.

title: addicted to this granola
text: This is my first in granola - I love this flavor, the mix of granola and chocolate and berries, and I feel better buying this brand than others.

title: delicious chocolate, could be more almonds
text: This is really good dark chocolate (so much that I have to fend off the partner from my stash), but I wish there were some more almonds in it - I specifically got this for chocolate AND almonds. That's my only complaint, though, as this is really tasty and I'm glad that it's fair trade chocolate.

title: tasty, but should have peanuts on bag
text: I noticed there's peanuts on the site but not on bag - there really should be peanuts on the bag because you do get a lot in it. Also, you get a good bit of white chocolate in it, too (I'm not so much a fan of it, but it does list it). As long as you expect a good mix of peanuts and white chocolate with your pecans, almonds and berries (goji and cranberries), you'll be all right. It's something a little different, a decent mix of sweet, salty and tart, and I like the resealable bag (that does work).

title: crunchy with a kick
text:
It seems to be popular these days to take legumes and make them into products you wouldn't suspect to find them in, such as pasta and chips. I have to say, I'm not complaining because usually they're tasty and healthier for you than wheat and potatoes, and these ORCHARD VALLEY HARVEST Chickpea Chips are a good example. Granted, they're still snacks, still fried (though in expeller pressed sunflower oil, whatever that means), but they're nice and crunchy, have a little kick to them from the chili lime flavoring, and have protein to help satisfy cravings as well. You get 3.5 servings per bag (around 25 chips, which while these are easy to eat, I've yet to have that many in a sitting), and the bag is resealable.
I find these enjoyable on their own, perfect to keep at work for when I need a bite, or at home with some hummus or another 'healthy' dip at hand.

title: if you like coffee....
text: You really have to like coffee with these CLIF energy bars - I mean, really. It's a lot like chewing espresso beans, albeit on the tasty side. You can tell there's coffee beans in these bars (organic Columbian beans at that), and the bars (I got the Caramel Macchiato flavor) are tasty. They're a bit chewy and a decent size, are over 200 calories and have 9 grams of protein (and a good bit of carbs), so they give you that shot of espresso and help a little with hunger. Not something I'd want to have all the time in place of coffee, but if you're on the go or doing activities, these would be good to help give you energy, especially since it's a twelve-pack.

title: in theory it would be a nice gift but....
text:
I really enjoy Tea Forte teas - they taste wonderful and they look so pretty. Yes, they're pricey, but I've always savored them and they do make nice gifts. With that in mind, I thought that this Jardin gift set would be perfect for a present - the box was lovely (and would do with just a gift bag and some tissue paper), the cup was such a lovely pink color, the little 'tea' tray was cute, as was the lid where you could let the little 'leaf' of each tea pyramid poke through the top. Even the tea selection is really good.
The problem? As you can see in the pictures, Tea Forte needs to do a much better job on the packing of these gift boxes. This came wrapped in a thin layer of bubble wrap and in a bigger box w/ some bubble/packaging, and still arrived damaged. Because the thin cardboard holding everything in place tore during shipping, the lid became cracked, which means you can't give away their supposed 'gift' set. I can keep this for myself (though the lid is useless), but if one is planning on getting this for a gift, one is definitely out of luck.

title: great in tea
text: I used to buy the rock sugar from Teavana stores, so been looking for a replacement. This works great in my tea, tastes just the same and is cheaper, so a win all around.

title: not too much of a kick
text: I do like having soup on hand for when things are busy or I just want a simple, easy dinner. This Campbell's Well Yes! Southwest-Style Chicken Tortilla Soup is nice in that it has a decent amount of protein and not too many calories (270 for the entire can), though you need to watch out for the sodium. It's quick (just heat up, stovetop or microwave) and has a fair amount of black beans in it so good fiber, and isn't too spicy (the husband was grateful for that). If you do like spice, you may need to add some seasonings to it, but easier to do that than take away. The flavor isn't bad - it's not homemade or what you'll get at a good restaurant, but we'll have no problem getting through the twelve cans and I'm interested in trying their other flavors.

title: a lot going on
text:
I was a bit surprised by these bars when they came in the sealed foil bags reserved for refrigerated items - and the packaging on the bars is a bit confusing itself. It seems these bars are best kept in the fridge/someplace cold, though they can last up to a week if not stored somewhere cold. I'm not sure I'd want to order these during the middle of the summer (just the foil bag, no cold pack) unless they do pack them w/ a cold pack.
That aside, they're not bad. I received the peanut butter flavor (with a tiny + mesquite), though it's not a strong peanut butter flavor in my opinion - too much going on here. Nutty? Yes, because there's SO MUCH in the bar - pumpkin seeds, hemp seeds, chia seeds and flax seeds. I didn't pick up too much on the chocolate flavor, though there's cacao nibs in there, too. It's a bit chewy, and you'll want to clean your teeth when you're done (all those seeds). There's also a fair amount of fat (27%) and calories (280 per bar) though the sugar and sodium isn't too bad.
But over $50 for 16 bars is a lot, especially when they're not the biggest bars nor are they shelf-stable that long. It's nice that they're non-GMO and the rest, but unless you've a strict diet, I think there's better bars out there on the market for a better price value. For the flavor and the fact that this was a decent snack that last me a few hours, I'll give it a good rating, but I am tempted to take off another star for the price and hassle of stocking it.

title: good unsweetened tea on its own or for mixed drinks
text:
I have to laugh a little about this being a 'true Southern tea', because from what I know about my time down South, Southern tea is sweet tea - my Southern sister-in-law (among others) is highly offended to have iced tea without any sugar. In fact, I do so love the debate that opens up between Southern friends and British friends over 'sweet tea'. I, however, tend to like my tea hot (and not too sweet), but now and then a nice iced tea is refreshing and then I don't want a lot of sugar in it. This Luzianne's unsweetened tea is very nice - it doesn't taste too artificial (it does have some preservatives on it), and it doesn't have any artificial sugar in it (which is a big no for me). It's brewed from real tea leaves, which does give it a good taste, and it's not too strong. It's great because you can add your sugar (or not, based on your preferences) and you can use it for various drink mixes since it's basically just tea (lemonade for an Arnold Palmer or even alcoholic drinks).
This arrived in good condition in a box, so no problems there. I would hope if you're paying for it, they would package it with better care.

title: good organic coffee
text: I'm not a coffee expert, but I do like some around the house for the occasional cup (and to get a jolt in me to help with headaches). This is great because it's ground, so don't have to fuss with that. I also like that it's organic. It's got a good flavor in my opinion, nothing too harsh, a nice 'breakfast' cup indeed. Not really catching all the flavor notes they cite, but it's tasty.

title: very addicting
text:
These seem a bit a little pricy (over four dollars for a bag) but they're really good. Also, they're better for you than most snacks out there (not saying they're really good for you, but better than most) with the protein and stuff. I can make a bag last a few days, my husband... not so much. They're crunchy and flavorful.
The aged cheddar is the hands down winner in the household - a definite cheese flavor without being too 'cheesy' or fake. Also, no radioactive orange color.
I like the Blazin' hot and he enjoyed it as well even though he's not the biggest 'heat' fan - it sneaks up on you and has more of a lingering impact. Though to me, it seems to have an odd umami taste to it.
The vegan ranch is pretty good, too. A little different than 'regular' ranch, but still good. Higher sodium content than the other two flavors, though.
All in all, I can definitely see ordering these again since they're better than a lot of other snacks out there and so tasty.

title: good flavor, not harsh
text: I'll admit that I'm not a coffee snob, but I find a cup a day helps to stave off headaches. So this bag is going to last a while, yes it will. I could smell it once I opened the package, and it smelled GOOD. Even better when opened - reminded me when I worked at a coffee house during university and they roasted their own beans. I use this in a french press and it's flavorful without being harsh/bitter. Very enjoyable.

title: really tasty
text: I enjoyed Pomona's pear juice, so I was willing to give strawberry juice a try even though I've never heard of it. I mean, I love strawberries, so why not? I have to say it's really, really good. I like that it's pure strawberry, just juice with nothing else in it, no sugar or additives, and that it's in a glass jar. You're definitely paying for that goodness, I will say, but when you think about it, it's about the same as a cup of fancy coffee these days and a heck of a lot better for you. A good way to get some fruit in you, a healthy way to get some fruit in you. I've had these cold from the fridge and right from the pantry, and it tastes fine either way.

title: addicted to this stuff
text: I'm addicted to this mayo - I use it more than the 'American' style, just prefer its flavor overall in sandwiches and a lot of dishes and recipes. I firmly believe once you have the Japanese version of egg salad you can never go back, and I've converted quite a few people to my way of thinking. This three pack is a life saver considering how fast I can go through these bottles, and that I can't always get to the few stores in the area that sell Kewpie mayo.

title: cheaper than starbucks
text: I do like my flavored coffee while at work to help me 'wake up', and these Forto energy drinks are a good find - I had the Vanilla latte, which is supposedly two cups of coffee. I like that you can have it cold or room temp so no worries about heat (I don't like things really hot), and there's no fake sugar in it (which I can't have). Since it's cold brewed, it's not harsh, so it's a smooth drink. The vanilla flavor isn't bad, I could definitely drink more of these though I think I'd like to try the chocolate now. You take off the lid, open the can, put the lid back on and there you go. It's cheaper than Starbucks and other than the whipped cream, I don't think you're missing much. I like that you can take these on the go with no worries.

title: love this tea
text: This has to be my favorite Harney and Sons tea, and they have some great flavors. The cinnamon flavor is strong but not overpowering, and the black tea robust. The silk teabag is one of the better way to brew with a bag in my opinion, and the metal tin keeps them fresh. I drink this all year round, but it's especially best in the cooler months.

title: nice selection of tea
text: This is a great selection of tea if you have tea lovers in your house, or for guests with different tastes - you have two black varieties (English Breakfast and Spiced Chai), a chamomile and green tea, and two fruit flavored herbals (lemon and orange) - that's three caffeine-free and three with caffeine. I think $5 per box is a little high, which is the only reason this isn't five stars, but other than that, it's a good variety pack and the flavors are nice. My favorites are the English Breakfast and Spiced Chai, but the others are nice, too (and will be great with cold season soon approaching).

title: in theory, this should be good
text:
I love Mexican food. I love spices and chocolate, and I've enjoyed the mole sauce I've tried in the past, though I can't say that I've tried Oaxaca Mole Sauce. I'm not an expert on Mexican food, though I've made some on my own based on recipes (probably not the most authentic, but I gave it a good try). So I was willing to try this mole sauce.
I wasn't daunted by the extremely general directions, though they did make me raise an eyebrow - melt SOME chocolate and add some sauce or water or oil or tomato (whatever you like!) and the powder mix then enjoy! I read the other reviews and knew not to use too much chocolate. I thought I had a handle on this.
Apparently, I didn't. I should have had some tomato paste on hand, in hindsight. I thought I didn't use too much chocolate, but it turned out so very bitter that I was left scrambling to tone it down as best I could. Didn't seem to work very well. Thought it would taste better on the shredded chicken, rice and refried beans I had for dinner, and it didn't work for any of them. In fact, it basically ruined the meal. I've some left over, so maybe I'll try again, but right now I've such a bad taste with this I'm not even tempted.

title: yummy treat
text: I love these snacks after having them in Japan and getting them whenever I find them in Asian grocery stores - they're a flaky wafer-like 'cookie' (so a bit of a mess to bite into) filled with chocolate (and hollow inside, they're not solid). Each one is individually wrapped and comes in a box, they were in good shape and delicious.

title: nice flavor for sushi
text: I think of this as an 'easy' way to flavor your rice - you can pick up some sushi vinegar and add it that way, or you can use this and not have to worry about adding too much. Personally, I do both, but sometimes this is just easier. You get three packs and one pack will flavor two cups of rice - put the cooked sushi rice in a bowl, sprinkle this on and mix together. Sometimes I use it when making sushi, sometimes I use this when I want flavored rice as a side with something else since it does give a tangy/acidic flavor (I like vinegary things).

title: nice and spicy
text: I've been looking for a spicy mayo similar to what they serve on sushi, and I think this is pretty close - I usually blend Kewpie mayo and sriracha sauce at home, but that turns out thin. This is nice and thick and oooh, what a kick! Very glad I found this, it's great on sandwiches and as a dip, and the next time they skimp on the spicy mayo for my take-out sushi order (or skip it entirely), I am prepared!

title: ehhh...
text:
Okay, I really like spicy foods. I'm not going to chow down in those insanely hot peppers or anything, but I do adore a bit of spice and heat in my meals. I always have sriracha on hand. I make my own spicy mayo with it. I liberally add cayenne and chili peppers to my meals. There's a theme here, see? So of course I'm going to try this 'spicy dipping sauce'.
And when I did? MAJOR disappointment. I'm sorry, but this is supposed to be 'spicy'? Did I receive a bad batch or something? Maybe the husband, who is not on the same level as me when it comes to spice/heat, will think it's 'spicy', but I am woefully, woefully disappointed. It's got a little flavor to it, but no heat.

title: not enough spice/heat
text: I was really hoping for more heat from this - I usually make a blend of Kewpie mayo and sriracha sauce, but wanted to see if I could find a mayo more like what they serve with sushi. This isn't it, and really, it's not 'hot' at all in my opinion. Not like I eat ghost peppers or anything, but no real kick. Not bad as a flavoring, but I won't be using this for anything I want a little heat on (so not really sure what, to be honest).

title: great in tea
text: I used to buy the beet sugar sold at Teavana, but with the stores closed, looked for an alternative to a way to sweeten my tea without using white sugar. This works just as well in my opinion, and is a good value. Will definitely be ordering again and hope they don't go anywhere!

title: tastes good
text: My husband uses a lot of olive oil when cooking his meat and vegetables, so I gave him this to try. It's a little different from the usual olive oils (first press, apparently), but it works well with the dishes and he's not complaining. Interesting that different presses will give a bit of a different flavor, but this is a good quality and that's what matters the most.

title: delicious
text: This pear juice does taste delicious (though my husband did find it to be very tart - hey, I like tart) - note that it does contain 1% lemon juice, so not entirely all pear, but it is sugar (well, additional sugar, barring that from the fruit) and additive free. I find it quite refreshing, but it is NOT cheap.

title: tasty yet pricy earl grey
text: I love earl grey tea, and Tiesta usually has good (if on the pricey side) teas. Their Victorian Earl Grey isn't an exception in that regard. There's lovely bits of flower petals in this blend (lavender, roses, marigolds and cornflowers), which enhance its aroma and give it a milder flavor - if I've any complaint (other than the price, which I don't mind paying for quality for the most part), is that the flowers seem to lessen the impact of the bergamot somewhat. For a tea marketed as 'awake', you don't get a strong jolt of the bergamot/citrus-based oil here, it's more from the black tea itself. So something a little more refined (probably hence the 'Victorian' part) and different, if you're in the mood for that. It comes in a nice, air-tight canister.

title: you really have to like coconut
text:
I figured I'd give these a try since cocount's not the first word here, but yep, it's definitely the strongest flavor. You get a lot of snack, 18 bags in a box, and there's a decent amount in each (1.5 ounces). But I don't see these are something that you can easily eat anywhere since they're not 'clusters' but a mix of coconut flakes (some large, some not), almond pieces, small bits of cherry and cocoa nibs, stuck together somewhat by a 'cocoa' glaze. So yes, there's a lot of small pieces that fall everywhere.
It's crunchy and again, definitely a predominant coconut flavor, followed by almond. I was hoping more for cherry and cocoa/chocolate, personally, considering they're the first two flavors mentioned. Nope. It's definitely crispy/crunchy, but not something I'll really enjoy for 18 bags or want to buy in bulk again.

title: regular cup of 'joe'
text: This is what is marked on the box - medium cup of coffee. Not too strong, not too 'bold', but a nice, medium cup of coffee for those times when you don't want anything too strong. Pretty good as is, nice aroma, like it for later in the day. Good price for the amount of pods.

title: nice bit of kick to these
text: I'm not always good about getting my protein in, and I don't always get out for lunch so jerky snacks like these are nice. I don't have a problem with the texture at all, in fact I prefer when I don't feel as if I'm about to lose a teeth on jerky sticks. I don't think it's 'mushy', but this is the jalapeno beef stick, which has actual bits of jalapeno peppers in it which you see when you bit into it. Not on a keto diet or anything, but do prefer to not have too much sodium or additives in my snacks if I can help it. These aren't cheap so they won't be a daily thing (the only negative about these jerky sticks, but then again, that is basically they're selling point so I won't take a star off for them). I'm now interested in the other flavors, especially since I don't eat beef too often.

title: chocolate with a little less guilt
text:
This is my first time trying Lily's Sweets, though I do buy other fair-trade chocolates - just not keto 'friendly' ones. The flavor is good in my opinion, the chocolate feels creamy in the mouth, nice and smooth, and melts well. I do like dark chocolate as well as milk chocolate, so I'm not finding it bitter at all. Every now and then I think I get a little stevia 'aftertaste', but just a hint - I don't tend to eat a whole bar of this, just a row or two at a time, so that might help. All in all, these are really good and I feel less guilty about indulging when they're low-carb and fair trade.
Though I did check the ingredients and noticed that 'erythritol' (a sugar alcohol?) came up before Stevia. So be aware that it's not just sweetened with that.

title: citrusy black tea
text: I've had Tiesta teas before, and they are a good quality tea, usually claiming some benefit ('energizer', probably because of the strength of the black tea in it as well as the citrus). It's got large pieces of said citrus (papaya and pineapple) and the flavor comes across well once you brew it, making me think that this would do well as an iced tea during the summer. I received the 4.5 ounce bag (resealable) and the tea has a good aroma and flavor, though it does seem a bit pricey.

title: good snack for the price
text: You definitely get a lot for the price here. I sorta want to take a star away because these are a little up there in the sugar (11g) and low in fiber (1g)... but they don't say they're energy bars or anything, just peanut granola bars. For what they are (snack bars), they're good. Definitely got that peanut taste, nice and chewy, bit of salt (not too much) - they're basically as advertised. Nice flavor, chewy as stated, good bits of peanuts in there, bit of sweet with a hint of salt to balance. Definitely nice to have on hand when you have a sweet craving or need a little something to get you to the next meal.

title: real vanilla beans
text: I must admit, I usually use Penzeys vanilla extract because I like making sure that my vanilla extract has real vanilla beans in it. This Grandma's Choice does use Madagascan vanilla beans in it, which is good. It also is 35% alcohol, like Penzeys, and the price is a little better. Maybe I'm just partial, but the scent seems smoother/less harsh w/ Penzeys, but when baking, it's pretty much equal. I feel it's a lot better than what you can buy in the store, and definitely better than any fake vanilla.

title: lot of variety, no decaf though
