text: Got the 'mega coffee sampler' and I will say that yes, lot of variety here - there were different coffee strengths (bold, really bold, 'light') and lots of flavors (pumpkin, mint, mocha, etc.). One thing it didn't have? No decaf at all, which was a disappointment when a guest wanted some decaf and I broke out this box. There were some 'lightly caffeinated', as mentioned, but no decaf. I guess it all depends on what box you get. Still, there's a lot to try here, including one 'mystery' cup.

title: nice salt, doesn't always grind well
text: I love pink Himalayan salt - I usually buy it to put into a salt grinder. So yes, eager to have salt grinders where I don't have to refill all of the time. I have to say that this is a little bit of a disappointment in that I opened these up (they were sealed well) and the first few times I used them, they ground up the salt well and it tasted great. But when I went to use it a couple of days later? I could barely get any salt out because it seemed 'stuck' in the grinder. It was in a cabinet away from the stove/moisture, so not sure what happened. I had to use the refillable salt grinder to add salt to a recipe, which was a letdown because I was hoping to use these disposable salt grinders for recipes where steam wouldn't affect the metal.

title: nice alternative to pasta
text:
This Wickedly Prime lentil pasta in marina and spice flavor is a great alternative to pasta - it's made with red lentils and I don't think it tastes that different. I've tried the chick pea pasta, and think this is a little easier to cook, to be honest - it doesn't 'foam up' as much when you add it to the boiling water. It cooks for about 8-9 minutes once the water reaches a boil, then you drain it (but don't rinse) and add some milk and butter to the pasta, along with the powder mix. There's dried tomatoes in with the pasta as well.
It's more of a spice mix than any heat to the pasta, but it tastes good and it's something a little different, not to mention this is rich in protein and lower in carbs than regular pasta. It's also gluten free, if that's a concern. I like that it's a break from carbs (a little less guilt) and so easy to make, a nice side for dinner.

title: a little pricey but so good
text: Okay, so this isn't cheap, but it's a lot healthier than nutella and it tastes really good. It has a little more of a nutty flavor as well, but then it's chocolate, hazelnut and almond - you still get a good, chocolate taste with this, you don't have to stir it  or put it in the fridge (you definitely want it to be room temp). It's nice and thick and great on crackers or bread/toast. I like that it doesn't taste sugary or oily, and the ingredients are simple.

title: amazing honey
text:
I love honey in tea and in some recipes while cooking, and this Beekeeper's Naturals Raw Honey flight came at the right time, as I'm fighting off a cold. There were four different honeys (Superfood Cacao, Sweet Clover, Wildflower and Buckwheat) in a box, nice size jars to have a taste of all of them and enough to last a little while/use in a recipe (not a really large jar since it's 4.4 oz, but bigger than some tiny sample sizes I've gotten in the past). It's a nice range from the lighter honeys (the clover and wildflower) to the darker (the cacao and buckwheat).

It's raw and sustainably sourced, so no worry about negative ingredients in the honey (a concern if it's not local a lot of times), and they taste great. My only problem is the packing could be better - they did come in a cute gift box and they try to put them in individual slots to hold the jars, but there was only a little bubblewrap on the very bottom and I guess from the box being thrown around in shipping, all the jars became loose in the box and one of them leaked a little honey. Can imagine that there might be more of a mess in warmer weather, and obviously you wouldn't want to gift the set in that condition.

title: lemon drink
text: This isn't really a tea unless you consider a hot beverage a 'tea' - it's a lemon concentrate that you add to hot water and is really great in the winter if you have a cold. It's resealable and you need to put it in the fridge after opening it, but you add a tablespoon or so to hot water and it's sweet enough to drink as is. Does a good job of soothing sore throats and helping coughs, but it also can be doctored up for a nice cold night.

title: good but pricey green tea
text: This is a nice gunpowder green tea - the leaves are large and rolled into a ball, which unfurl as you brew them (don't use boiling water, but a few degrees shy of the boiling point). The water's a little dark for green tea but the flavor isn't too strong, you get a nice flavor that isn't too overwhelming. If you want to try something with a little less punch than matcha, this is a good green tea to switch to now and then.

title: if  you like caramels
text: This is a very nice assortment/gift box of caramels (if a little pricey). You receive four bags/three flavors - sea salt, vanilla cream (two bags of these) and pecan, along with two small canisters (one of them that I received isn't the most airtight), in a cardboard box packed w/ paper confetti w/ a pretty wrapper on the outside. The caramels are flavorful and soft, so if you've someone who enjoys them, this would make a really nice gift.

title: small but a good snack
text: First off, these are small. You're not going to get something the size of what you expect to be a regular protein bar. They're short and thin. They're also very chewy and moist (some say oily), which I'll admit the later is a nice departure from chalky. I can't imagine two of these being a meal substitute, other than for a light breakfast or lunch. But they are filling for their size, especially the ones with chia in them (chocolate cherry bling). This is a nice variety pack, I have to say, and the flavors are good (not a fan of the maple, but considering the variety, that's to be expected). Yes, they have calories in them, but they aim for natural ingredients and protein and flavor. I think they do a good job, they're easy to pack in a bag or purse, and they support a good cause.

title: really nice flavored tea with benefits
text: This is a pleasantly flavored black tea with ginger, vanilla bean and cinnamon, as well as maca (a type of ginseng, I had to look it up). So yes, a little bit of spice but not overbearing, along the lines of a chai, almost, and really nice. I like to think I'm doing something good for myself by drinking this, considering the probiotics. Might be wishful thinking, but it tastes good and yes, it does help in the morning, but it's a bit of caffeine so....

title: matcha to go (sorta)
text: These are matcha 'satchets' (to go packets) in nice plastic canisters so you can take them with you, have at work or at home (though if that's the case, it's better to just have it in a can or packet and measure by the teaspoon). The packets don't tear very easily, which would be nice, but the contents are a nice, strong matcha (green tea powder) that requires a bit of blending for a brisk cup of green tea. The instructions are a bit off in that it says to boil water - you don't use boiled water for green tea, but around 170-180 F (below boiling) - add half the packet first and then whisk/stir, add more water and the rest of the packet. Or you can add these to smoothies or lattes, or anything else you want to give it a green tea flavor (even baked goods).

title: creamy and sweet honey dijon mustard
text: This is a sweet, creamy honey dijon mustard. Has a little tang to it as well. Goes great with cheese and on sandwiches, can imagine it works well in recipes where you add it for sauces or marinades because of its creaminess, but yes, there's definitely a good bit of honey flavor to it and I don't think it has too much of a mustard 'kick' to it. Nice flavor, though.

title: not herbal but a nice chai
text:
This is a black chai tea - there's 'herbal' on the label but I checked and rechecked, the first ingredient is black tea. I guess this is a line of herbal teas or something? But I've also gotten a green tea from them so... not sure. Anyway, yes, black chai tea. It has a lovely scent and what I enjoy about this is it's not peppery or harsh like some chai teas can be. It's also not the strongest, so if you want a chai tea that doesn't taste like a potpourri sachet has been crammed down your throat, this is a good one - there's the usual cinnamon, clove, etc. spice mix here. It comes with twenty tagless (no cords) bags in a box, which you have to tear apart as two are together.

Am a bit confused, though, about the caffeine in here - it says 'end the day' but it also says 'black tea' and nothing about it being decaffeinated, so some clarification on the caffeine amount would be good. I didn't feel as if I was missing out on my daily caffeine with this, so...

title: small little juice boxes
text: These Apple & Eve 'monster punch' juice boxes are mini fruit punch (4.23 oz) of apple juice, pear juice, cherry juice, pineapple juice, and orange juice mix with no added sugar - they're still 60 calories for a little box and 13 gr of sugar (no additional, just from the juice), but they taste good and they don't have too many ingredients other than the juice concentrate. They're meant for trick or treating/Halloween, so you can pass them out or for parties, but I've been bringing them to work for a little extra fruit kick/break from my water and tea hydration, and I imagine they'd be nice to pack in a lunch for the kids (or big kids) as well. They come complete with a straw, or you can just snipe an end off after unfolding the top a little and ensure you get everything out.

title: lovely green tea with peppermint
text: This is a lovely green tea with peppermint flavor, and a little matcha as well. You can smell the peppermint as soon as you open the sealed bag, and the bags are two each that you have to tear apart (my only complaint about the product, since I worry about ripping one of them). The tea has a wonderful flavor, a mix of the green tea leaves and matcha, and I enjoy it as is after letting it steep a couple of minutes. Nice way to start the day.

title: refreshing mint green tea
text: I loved the Teavana stores, the wonderful selection of teas.... Sad to see them go, but it's nice to know that one can still order some of their blends in sachets. These plastic containers contain 15 pyramid sachets of a green tea, spearmint, citrus blend (lemon verbena and lemongrass). I have to say, the predominant flavors are the green tea and mint, with just a hint of the citrus, but that's fine. It's perfect by itself, but feel free to add a little honey or sugar if that's your thing. There's a seal in the container, but a plastic lid that helps to keep the bags fresh after you open it.

title: not bad mac & cheese
text: This has an amusing box to it, I must say, and it makes you think this is healthier than it is. Yes, there's quinoa in it, but loose and mixed in with regular 'wheat' pasta. You boil the mix and luckily I have a strainer w/ small enough holes that I didn't lose much of the quinoa, then add some butter (more or less depending on how you want it to taste, I went with less and thought it was fine), milk and the white cheese powder mix). I didn't think it tasted bad as is, but added some extra ingredients to make a small meal out of it. It's a little better than some brands out there, non-GMO, and something a little different.

title: high protein milk drink
text:
So, had the husband try this with me, since he's a bit lactose intolerant. We both agreed that this (honey and oat) tasted a good bit like Ensure, but it was good and easy to drink down. It's nice that the bottles are small and easy to carry around, and it tastes good cold or room temperature. 12 grams of sugar is a little much, but then again, it seems that anything that tastes this good is going to have a bit of sugar and/or fat to it (5 grams fat). 15 grams protein does help to tide you over and it's an easy way to get the protein into your system.

Price is currently unavailable for this item.

title: something a little different
text:
Okay, to like this you have to like cashews - I happen to like cashews so that's a good thing. It's not quite like peanut butter because again, cashews.
The two ingredients in this is cashews and palm oil, and you have to knead the packet a bit before you tear it open to mix the two together. I'm all for 'natural' ingredients, though yes, this is a little on the oily side, and it is 210 calories per packet (it's good that this has portion control).
BUT, it's nice to have it in the packets for on the go - to take to work, to carry on you for travel or whatever. Have a few crackers or flatbread or whatever and it's good. It really has a nice 'fresh' cashew taste to it thanks to the two ingredients - again, if you like cashews, you'll like this.
It's just not something I'd have every day because of the calorie count, but it's good now and then, and it's great to have in a pinch. Also, something a little different than peanut butter.

title: very tasty
text: My husband, the cereal eater, was a bit dubious of this cereal considering the last time he ate Kashi it was a bit bland (in his opinion) and he tends to like things on the sweet side. Still, he 'took one for the team' and opened a box... and proceeded to have two bowls of this stuff. The verdict? 'Tastes a lot like cinnamon toast crunch'. Also, definitely won't be a problem going through the ten boxes that came in the package. This is really good for a 'healthy' cereal (though still 7g of sugar), and I can see kids willingly eating it. I will say that I was tempted to take off half a star because these boxes seem on the small/thin size to me, but the ounces are right up there and I know packaging has gone down in general. You might not get more than 4-5 bowls out of each one, considering how much was left after trying it for the review.

title: the 'no sugar' is aspartame
text: Okay, let me say that I like the flavor (raspberry lemonade) and this worked in a large bottle of water. Easy to use (tear open a packet and add, shake water). Easy to carry around. BUT, this contains aspartame, which I didn't know when I got this and I'm supposed to avoid because of migraines. Having one now and then to try these doesn't seem to trigger them, but I can't use these on a regular basis and no, sadly won't be buying these even though they do a good job of flavoring the water. So the review is I like them, if they didn't have all the fake sugar in them I'd buy them, and if you're fine with aspartame then you'll probably like this.

title: a decent breakfast alternative
text: I have to say that Carnation's Breakfast Essentials powdered drink mix is very tasty and a decent amount of protein while easy to mix - they suggest how to add it to skim milk or to add it to a smoothie (I just go w/ skim milk). You get four packs of  chocolate and three each of strawberry and vanilla which is a nice selection, and they're easy to take on the go since they're small and again, not too difficult to blend. They're vitamins and calcium as well as protein and low on fat (chocolate) if not fat free (hence why they suggest the skim milk). It's a nice break from the protein powders, I must say.

title: energy supplement on the go
text: These Cellucor C4 cans are great prework out drinks that you can take with your or have on hand before exercising to give you an extra boost. You don't have to worry about mixing anything or carrying powder and a shaker, just the can to pop open and drink. The flavor's not bad, and it provides you a caffeine jolt along with energy supplements without the sugar and carbs. I just wish it wasn't carbonated.

title: tasty multigrain breakfast
text:
So the Soulfull Project will donate a bowl of their cereal to a regional food bank for each one you buy. Nice. Their cereal? I tried the Brown Sugar Pecan Multigrain which does have a lot of multigrain in it (along with brown sugar, vanilla and salt, and not much else), and... it was good. I was surprised by how good it was, for 300 calories. It's got a bit of sweetness to it, not much but a little, and yes, GRAINY. You get a little grit and be careful of those chia seeds, but you know you're eating something healthy yet it's enjoyable. I'm not going to have a problem getting through this six-pack, trust me, and I'm interested in trying some of the other flavors.
Yes, it could be cheaper, but it's for a good cause and it's not that bad when you think of what you might be paying to pick up a bite to eat to go along with that fancy coffee.

title: something different in a good way
text: I'm always on the fence with licorice because I'm not the biggest fan if it's a really strong flavor. These Tara's licorice caramels? These are good - they're individually wrapped and they're not too big, and the caramel flavor blends well with the licorice, making sure that the latter doesn't come across as too strong, it's more of a secondary flavor/afternote. You do get the vanilla and butter with this, so caramel lovers will probably enjoy this as something different while licorice lovers won't be disappointed. All in all, it's something new and probably will keep me, a caramel lover, from eating the whole jar at once (not a bad thing at all). This definitely makes me want to try the brand's other caramel flavors since these come across as a quality snack for a good price.

title: easy food on the go
text: I tried the superberries bowl and it was all right. Not sure why the huge lid on this when you don't shake it or anything, and the spoon is very handy. I think it's better with less water than suggested, and have to wonder about all the sugar in this. It's a nice on the go breakfast or lunch, but there is that odd aftertaste and consistency as well as high calorie count for what should be granola and fruit, right? I could probably eat healthier with other protein bars and banana or an apple.

title: delicious and bright flavor
text: The first thing you notice when you open the very nice, airtight container is the HUGE orange slices in it, packed tight enough that you might have a little trouble digging in with your spoon. The orange is a predominant flavor, though it is tempered with the apple, pomegranate, hibiscus and other flavors, and the last two help to give it a reddish color. It's tangy and can be sipped without sugar, but a little rock sugar does 'gentle' it a little. It's good hot or cold so would make a great iced tea for the summer, but I'm drinking this while fighting off the remnants of a cold and can only wish that I'd gotten it sooner. It's definitely bright with flavor and, being herbal, can be sipped all day long.

title: decent gluten free cracker
text: These Wasa crackers are a little on the bland side if you eat them plain, but they do have a nice 'crunch' to them and are thick yet also are a little 'airy' - they aren't too hard and snap easy, if that makes sense. They go well with a cheese or spread, which is good, that's something that makes their blandness a good thing, and they're gluten free.

title: gourmet almonds
text: These are very nice 'gourmet' nuts with the skins removed - they are very large and mostly solid nuts, great for snacking, and the pink Himalayan salt gives them a little flavor without being overpowering. Though I'm always dusting my hands after trying these, it's a strong dusting that coats them. Obviously you have to watch the salt content with these because of it, but otherwise they're a good source of protein because of the almonds. They come in a resealable bag so a great way to take something to work or to carry on you for a mostly healthy snack, or to put out for snacking purposes/guests since these look nice.

title: good grain mix
text: The Near East Quinoa blend of quinoa and brown rice is a good way to get your grains without too much fuss. You can make it on the stove or in the microwave (I'd suggest the stovetop), with or without a little olive oil and salt or other seasonings you might want to add. It comes with two resealable bags, which you shake before you open up and scoop out the blend to make sure you get a good mix of both blends. It's a good idea to rinse if you can, there's a tiny bit of grit here (but not too much if you don't), and watch the cooking time (water absorption) to ensure that it doesn't evaporate too quickly so the rice and everything is nice and soft. I've been debating trying this in the rice cooker as a result, but I do like the blend as it's a good mix and something a little different.

title: not bad, but not the strongest flavor
text:
I usually use Torani vanilla flavor in my coffee drinks, but I decided to give this a try. First, wow, the price! Also, it recommends three pumps for your coffee, and more for other flavored drinks. I will say that there's not a lot that comes out with each pump (because I don't usually use that much flavored syrup due to calories), and let's be honest, you'd really use up the bottle quick that way. The flavor? It's not the strongest and I'm not getting the kick I'd associate with 'vanilla bean'. It's not bad, it is a nice vanilla flavor and it has sweetness as well (which you'd expect when it's a syrup and sugar is the first ingredient, with caramelized sugar for coloring). The pump is nice, too, though it took a lot of effort to get it to open.
It was nice to try this, but I think I'll stick with Torani.

title: easy to mix in drinks, no taste
text:
The ProNourish natural balance fiber is tasteless, plant-based fiber. You start with one scoop, which is about 15 calories, and it suggests you work your way up to about 6 scoops, but not at once (they say to bump up every three days or so). You can put it in cold or hot drinks, and drink it over six hours. The can should be used within four weeks of opening.

I've had this in plain cold water and in hot beverages, and it doesn't taste like anything. I think it dissolves better in hot liquid and have had it in coffee and tea, and it doesn't affect the taste (makes it a little cloudy, maybe, but no negative taste). I'm up to three scoops, and I can say that there's been a lot of gas, especially when I went up to the second scoop, which has gotten a little better after staying on the third scoop for a while... but I'm also not seeing any amazing benefits from this. No increased regularity or lack of bloating. So I don't know. It seems to work really well for others and yes, it's nice that it's plant based, no taste, and mixes well.

title: the nut flavor comes out in this one
text: This Cracked Nut Butter Unroasted Pecan Plus Almond Butter Dessert Spread arrived in a bubble wrap inside of an envelope, and I can't find any instructions if it should be put in the fridge once you open it (just that you need to stir it first before tasting). It's cookie dough flavor, but honestly? It tastes nutty - almond flavor at that. It's not bad, but if you want cookie dough flavor? I'm not getting it right now. Not at all. You can see from the ingredients that it's nuts and ghee (clarified butter) and enzymes and whey, for the most part, so it's not all bad, though there's a good amount of fat as well as protein, I think the main thing here is that it doesn't taste anything like it claims to be. It's not bad and it does give a nice flavor to shakes, just be aware that it's more nutty than anything.

title: makes a nice cold brew
text: So I don't have a drip coffee maker, but I did want to try cold brew. This seemed a great opportunity to do that. AmazonFresh's Go For The Bold made a really nice batch (or two) of cold brew coffee, I have to say - the grounds didn't give my filter any problems and after sitting in the fridge over night, it's strong but not harsh or bitter. The bag is resealable in that you can fold it down and there's tabs, but I prefer to put it in another bag just in case as I don't make coffee all that often. I'm sure this would work just find in a drip machine for a hot cup, too.

title: great for holiday baking
text: Really, what can you say about chopped walnuts? These are walnuts, they're chopped so that's one less thing you have to worry about when baking/cooking, they're fresh and it's a nice size bag so you should be able to go through it in a reasonable amount of time before they're no longer fresh, but there is a 'zipper'/seal so you can close it if you don't use them all up at once. They taste good and work great in baking recipes (cookies and breads).

title: very tasty, they're going fast
text: These are rather addictive and very tasty - being thin they're easy to eat and you don't think you're eating much, plus they're great for using in hummus and dips. They taste great and don't seem any different for being 'organic', which I'm sure is just some way that the flour was grown differently or treated differently, but appreciate that they seem a little better for me. But they did arrive in pieces for the most part (just makes it easier to fit into the mouth which doesn't help with the portion control), hence why not five stars.

title: it's different
text: Well, the good news is it isn't that bitter of a green tea, which I've had before. It blends well with smoothies and in my yogurt (I know, a little odd), or just when whisked in hot water. The chocolate... is something different. I'm on the fence if I like it, but I wanted to try something new. I may use this for a chocolate matcha recipe if I find one, something with enough sugar to mask the 'grassy' flavor, but yes, this needs a little 'mellowing'. Usually good matcha has an earthiness to it, but this is really strong.

title: very tasty and filling
text: These dark chocolate covered cherries are delicious. The small packs are handy and can be thrown in a bag, lunch, purse, what not and are one serving size of 230 calories, 120 which are fat, but you are getting dried fruit and chocolate. The cherries are nice and big, and I actually shared this with my husband, the trial bag. It's a good amount of a serving if you're craving something sweet or a dessert, but wasn't overbearingly sweet due to the dark chocolate. For about two dollars a pack, not too bad, considering non-GMO and no artificial ingredients.

title: very tasty, mix of nuts and candy
text: If you like peanut butter, you're really going to like this bag of 'trail mix', it does a good job of handling a craving for it and serving as a light snack - there's peanuts, candied peanuts, peanut butter chips, peanut butter m&m's and mini-peanut butter cups in there. Oh, and the peanut butter-covered pretzels, can't forget those! 190 calories per serving, and you want to watch that because it would be easy to sit down with the bag and not eat the whole thing, but have a few handfuls at the least. This would definitely be good to take to the movies and enjoy, something a little better than the candy bars you find there. Or mix it w/ a trail mix that's more fruit/nut heavy. Either way, it's delicious.

title: so now you can get olive oil on amazon
text: I used this in a couple of dishes and it tastes just as good as the last couple of olive oils I've bought from the store. Nice and clear, had a good taste that didn't overpower the food, I don't really know what to say about extra virgin olive oil. It worked well and I'll gladly use it again.

title: delicious oolong tea
text: This is a delicious flavored oolong tea. The mango isn't too strong, but it gives a nice fruit flavor to the tea, which I can enjoy brewed as is. It's not as strong as a black tea, and the rose petals help to mellow out the fruit flavor a little. I wasn't sure I'd enjoy this as much (since I usually stick to black or green teas), but I'm steadily going through the boxes.

title: perfect for baking/cooking, really saves time and effort
text: These Fisher chopped natural pecans are great for a recipe that called for them (a truffle recipe) and saved the time of having to chop them up (yes, it's not that hard to do, but again, when you're tired after working and just trying to get a recipe thrown together with minimal fuss, every saved step is appreciated). The nuts are nice and 'clean' in that there's minimum dust and no shells that I saw, they were nice and fresh and tasted delicious, and they come in a resealable bag (though best to keep in the fridge after opening). Plus, the great option of home delivery!!

title: great price savings
text: I like putting out 'treats' at work for people to enjoy, and this four pack bag set is a price savings compared to what I can find at the store (short of special sales). They arrived in great shape and I'll definitely reorder again in the future.

title: delicious granola
text: This is a delicious granola with dark chocolate chunks in it as well as fruit and not too many other ingredients. Since I can't find it in the grocery store, I like the large size of the bag here on Amazon and the price savings. It definitely livens up the yogurt in the morning.

title: great tasting almond flour
text: I tried this blanched almond flour in an Irish soda bread recipe and while it turned out delicious, it didn't rise much. I like the convenience of the flour and it has a good texture and taste, but will have to figure out how to work it into some recipes - it's really good in that it's gluten free (and peanut free), as well as high in protein, so if you want a paleo diet or want to cut carbs, this is an option. You just can't substitute it for wheat flour, though, and some almond flours work better for certain recipes, it seems. The flatness of the soda bread aside, everyone's eating it because it tastes great.

title: nice hazelnunt flavor, not too strong but it's there
text:
The husband adores hazelnut, so I figured these were a good thing to grab. These are two half candy bars in a single package (portion control?) which is nice, though you tend to think the bars are broken in shipment at first (at least the SO did).

The hazelnut is a little subtle upon first taste. I personally thought there was more nugget in these bars than usual, but I don't eat a lot of Snickers. The husband thought that there wasn't much of a difference at first, too... and then mentioned the hazelnut aftertaste... and then was all 'wow'.

If you're expecting a major hazelnut taste, I don't think you're going to get it. But these are nice and different, they have the chocolate and and the caramel and the nuts and yes, they do have the hazelnut in the nugget and a little bit more. Considering how the husband is going through these (I may have to hide the box), they're a hit. I do like that they have the smaller sizes... but maybe sealing the package between the two would be nice (in case you wanted to save the other half for later).

title: not overwhelmed by these
text: Okay, I hit a bakery that has a lot of gluten free stuff each week, so I think I have something to compare these to. Ginnybakes organic isn't bad, but their pistachio cranberry cookies were just... well, meh. The cookies don't look as packed with pistachios and cranberries as on the box (nowhere near as many cranberry pieces in each cookie), the taste was decent but nothing overwhelming, and to be honest? A bit hard and dry and I'm not sold on 70 calories PER COOKIE. It's not even that big of a cookie. I suppose if you don't have access to a gluten free bakery and are desperate for a treat these are an option, but while they don't taste bad, I'm not impressed.

title: great peanut taste
text: I've never had Fisher's peanut butter before, but I have to say, it has a great fresh peanut butter taste. I was definitely surprised by that. It was great in a PB&J sandwich, and it was delicious in a spicy peanut butter noodle dish I made (it incorporated into the sauce well and I didn't notice anything odd about the texture or the flavors. I look forward using all of the jars in the 12-pack, none of them will go to waste. If you like peanut butter, give this a try! It's a great value and so nice, to have it come to your door.

title: great pecans
text: These Fisher roased salted pecans are delicious and they are indeed 'mammoth' - you get a six pack of 4.5 large sized pecans in a supposedly resealable bag (the only reason this review is NOT five stars is because these bags are rarely resealable, I'm finding, so keep a baggie on hand). There's 4.5 servings per bag, and there's 110 mg of salt per serving, so these are lightly salted but not overly much (the salt is a light dusting). The pecans are fresh and tender, not dried out and it's rather difficult to stop at that one serving! It's nice that they come in a cardboard 'box'/display case to keep them stored in your pantry or cupboard. These are great to have on hand at work or anywhere else when you want a tasty, good for you snack.

title: delicious, just could use better packaging
text: These Fisher roased salted almonds are delicious - you get a six pack of 4.5 almonds in a supposedly resealable bag (the only reason this review is NOT five stars is because these bags are rarely resealable, I'm finding, so keep a baggie on hand). There's 4.5 servings per bag, and there's 110 mg of salt per serving, so these are lightly salted but not overly much (I'm not a big salt fan, these are good). The almonds are fresh and it's rather difficult to stop at that one serving! It's nice that they come in a cardboard 'box'/display case to keep them stored in your pantry or cupboard. These are great to have on hand at work or anywhere else when you want a tasty, good for you snack.

title: refreshing matcha tea with mint flavor
text:
I love matcha - I have it every day in some manner, I add it to smoothies or yogurts to get the health benefits, brew it in tea and even bake with it. It's not cheap to get a good grade for it, it's a finely ground green tea usually best gotten from Japan but there's good quality available elsewhere. So I was very interested to see that Lipton is making it available, especially in tea bags (usually you'll get a bag of it or individual 'sleeves' that you dump into water or scoop out).

Now for Lipton's match green tea and mint. You get a box of fifteen individually sealed triangular bags (they're on the small side). The packets keep the tea fresh until you use it, and you only brew for two minutes (best temp around 195, you don't want a full boil). This has a nice minty taste to me, not overbearing, but it's refreshing in the morning and the green tea taste is crisp. It's a decent grade of matcha, not too bitter, and I drink it without adding anything else. It's a great way to try matcha tea without the fuss (they also make it without any mint flavoring, if you prefer just green tea).

title: helps with the chocolate cravings
text:
I have to admit, I don't buy Nutella, but I've had it on a few things and thought this might make for a decent snack when the husband craves chocolate (and he really loves hazelnut), or wants to add a little something to the protein shakes. Right away, you note the chocolate taste - it's the predominant flavor. There is a hazelnut taste to the spread, but it's more chocolate than anything. And while this does go well on crackers or toast, it's rather runny, it's not as thick as it is pictured above. I'm hoping some time in the fridge will help. But hey, that helps with the shakes and all when it's not cooled off.

And while it has more protein than other brands, you're still getting a good bit of carbs with this. So I think of it as a bit of a treat, an indulgence, that's not TOO bad now and then but helps with the taste buds and is better than other options out there.

title: something different to eat while on the go
text:
Since I was traveling, I figured I'd get some of the Bumble Bee Snack on the Run! to try. Two flavors in fact, the Cheesy Tuna Melt and the Rosemary, Garlic and Sea Salt. First, these come in little boxes with a small can of tuna and a package of about eight tiny crackers. And a little plastic spoon so you can scoop out the tuna on the crackers.
I was worried because these went on my carry-on and came shipped in the mail, and there was a rattling sound. Figured the crackers were all mooshed up by then. Nope. Crackers in in fact all intact, no breakage (it was the spoon). Well, then on to the taste. I didn't get too much of a rosemary, garlic or sea salt taste from the one, it was more of a regular tuna salad, but it was good. Enough for a decent snack or a light lunch. And the Cheesy Tuna Melt was not too cheesy, just a little of a cheesy taste. I'd say there's enough in the can for a small sandwich (if you want to put it on bread and not the crackers) or again, a light lunch or a good snack. The crackers are buttery and pretty good, too.

All in all, these worked really well as something you can take with you on the go or have on hand for a snack. They were about 400 calories all together (over 200 for the tuna, over a hundred for the crackers), and a nice bit of protein at that because of the tuna. Not too much of a mess, either, since it was all contained. Definitely something to consider to keep around the office or to take while traveling.

title: not bad for teriyaki flavor, but contains MSG
text:
All right, these didn't taste too bad. It's teriyaki flavored, so a little sweet, not the strongest flavored. But it's 'beef and pork', and no ratio of what to what (though pork is the main ingredient). All I really taste is the teriyaki, to be honest. And there's no word on where that meat comes from, only that it's packaged in the USA (so obviously, the meat is NOT from the USA). Another concern is that this contains monosodium glutamate, so if you've a problem with MSG, you don't want to eat this.
The product comes in bite-sized pieces and has some definite chew to it, though not too much. Three ounces is three serving sizes. I didn't think it was overly sweet or salty (I'm not a big salt fan, but I do like sweet), but it is a bit high on the sodium for the daily amount. Honestly, there's other jerky snacks out there that I prefer for not having all the nitrates/fillers in them and that I know where the meat is sourced, so I'm not going to buy this. But yeah, I ate it, it wasn't bad for the taste.

title: sour snacks but a lot of sugar
text:
Okay, I enjoy Starburst chews and their jelly beans, and I really like sour things so I jumped on these. I will say that as sour treats go, these are enjoyable, they have a nice taste though nothing special. You have a resealable bag with cherry, blue raspberry (what is blue raspberry?), watermelon and strawberry - though honestly? not sure I can tell which is which. I was a bit surprised that for sour flavors and Starbursts, they didn't have lemon.
One thing to note is that these are basically pure sugar - 27 grams of sugar. They're gummy and coated in even more sugar. I don't know what you can use them for other than eating them out of the bag or maybe putting them on things as decoration, and to be perfectly honest, having a full serving (ten of these) made my stomach upset. It's a LOT of sugar.

title: tasty sauce, alternative to the sweet stuff
text: This is the first time I've tried any 'Stubbs' barbeque products, and I have to say it was pretty good. Then again, I do love a nice vinegar taste, and this 'mopping' sauce does have that, along with a pepper kick (you can see the black flakes in the sauce). It's a little thinner than most barbeque sauces, but my understanding is that mopping sauces are supposed to be a little thin so you can slap them on the cooking meat, like a basting sauce. I used this while baking some chicken and it turned out great. Like I said, a little sour, a little hot, and very good - not sweet like some barbeque sauces. Read some of the reviews and I want to try this in a crockpot next. Like the lower sugar in this recipe, and the price isn't bad for four bottles. Now I want to try some more of this line.

title: fun to make and delicious
text: Took a little while to arrive (came from overseas) but arrived in great condition. Followed a recipe I found online to make a huge pancake in a rice cooker and it was delicious (recipe on the package was in Japanese, but basically a packet of the hotcake mix, two eggs and a cup of milk.

title: Tastes great but not quite the same as their regular peanut butter
text:
OK, I love Skippy peanut butter, I even have two jars of it in the cupboards right now (regular and extra crunchy). So yeah, I grabbed the extra crunchy and did a taste test with the Natural with Honey Super Crunchy. And what I noticed? The Honey one was a little sweeter but still very good. I could have easily continued to eat it with crackers but had to stop myself (didn't want to ruin my appetite before dinner). Yes, this will definitely be put to good use.

I also noticed that the Honey jar says it's a 'peanut butter SPREAD', which is a bit odd, where the regular is 'peanut butter'. Don't know if it's because the Honey version is made with palm oil or not. Also, the Honey version is higher in sugar (carbs - nine versus six!), calories (extra twenty per serving) and lower in protein, which makes me think that's why it's a spread - more filler than peanuts to it. However, this is lower in sodium if you're trying to watch your sodium intake.

So a good tasting peanut butter if a little sweet, but a little worrying for the palm oil and the 'spread' thing.

title: Very tasty, but yeah, not everyone is going to like these
text:
Okay, I have to admit that I like seaweed/nori. I can eat it dried/plain, and I definitely enjoy it with sushi in rolls and in other Asian dishes. That said, yes I loved these chips and could have gone through the whole bag (I was hungry). I had to force myself to stop and save room for dinner - it's a salty/sweet combination thanks to the cinnamon flavoring and the brown rice backing to the chips.

That said, my boyfriend, who is NOT a big sushi fan, did NOT like these chips. He tried one and then shoved the bag at me. Considering that he is traditionally the salt lover in the family... yeah. I think these are going to be an acquired taste, but for those who do like seaweed or are up to expand their taste buds, they're good.

However, they're not a health-food snack, not really. Best to stick to just rice cakes and dried seaweed since these do have other additives to help make them all nice and tasty, and are high in sodium (well, seaweed usually is a bit). They might not be fried but there is still some oil to them as well as sugar, salt and various other things. Still, for an occasional indulgence and something different, I like them. I just wish the bag was resealable or, barring that, easier to fold over to close.

title: fantastic four pack of black tea
text:
This is a really great collection of black tea - the leaves are large and fragrant, the flowers included in the flavored teas bright and flavorful. The Earl Grey de la Creme has a bit of sweetness to it without sugar thanks to the vanilla, while the English Breakfast and the Cosmopolitan are nice and robust, perfect to start the day. The Bombay Chai is especially pleasing, with the perfect balance of spices without being overbearing - it is indeed great with milk and honey (or even sugar). These tins are packed with tea and would make a perfect gift together or broken up.
I received this item in exchange for an honest review

title: very tasty and highly addicting!
text: This box of Cailler's milk chocolate selection was basically decimated upon arrival, hence the five star review. They came in a very nice box, well wrapped and with a clear expiration/best by date, and would make a nice gift with the lovely packaging. There's a helpful booklet to let you know which chocolate is which, and a nice mix of milk chocolates with hazelnut fillings (prominent in the box), cream filling, almond and caramel. The chocolate is very smooth and tasty, and it's easy to go through several of these pieces at once (especially if there's someone in the house who enjoys hazelnut).

title: a healthier alternative when you want something sweet
text: These Nature Valley Protein Soft Baked Granola Bites with Blueberry Almond flavor aren't bad. They're about three roundish mini 'muffin' shapes to a serving (180 calories, 60 from fat), and you're supposed to get about 5 servings per bag. They're mostly soft, a bit crumbly and there's a bit of crunch to them (probably from the almond), and they claim no artificial colors, flavors or high fructose corn syrup in them. Also, 9g whole grain and 7g protein per serving. They have 24g carbs, 11g of that sugar and only 1 from dietary fiber, and a decent amount of sodium. So they're better than some snacks out there and they do have an oatmeal taste to them (with a bit of blueberry, nothing too strong), so if you're looking for something to satisfy a sweet craving or to replace a muffin, these will do. You might want to have these with a cup of tea, coffee or milk, because the texture is a little weird, probably in an effort to keep them healthy (you'll need something to wash them down).

title: it should be a healthy snack, but there are better alternatives out there
text:
It's a bit difficult to figure out how to rate this review, to be honest. I was surprised how much I liked Rhythm Superfoods kale chips in Kool Ranch flavor- upon opening the bag I was able to snack on them with ease. They were a bit addicting, the flavor nice, the chips crunchy and I was able to forget that I was eating kale. I'm not even a huge ranch flavor fan but these were good. Reading the label, they SEEM healthy. Yes, there's the mention of cane sugar (no mention of how much), but the rest *seems* healthy - kale, sunflower seeds, tahini, carrot, sea salt (okay, that maybe not so much), etc.
But then you compare the nutrition facts to a pack of Doritos and... eh, it's not so convincing. More sodium. Same amount of calories. More protein. Certainly more cost per pack. I have to wonder if it's worth it when you can buy your own kale and roast it or bake it at home, or add it to a smoothie with much less cost or added sodium, fat, or sugar. Isn't that the point of eating healthy?

text:

There's also a plastic 'clamp' so you can reseal the bag after cutting it open.
The tea itself is a very smooth, flavorful green tea blend. After steeping it for a couple of minutes in water that's cooled a little below boiling (the lower setting on my water kettle), I had a cup of wonderfully scented green tea with a bit of jasmine flavor, nothing too overpowering.

title: very smooth lapsang blend
text:

A minor quibble, but just commenting that you will have to place the bag into another baggie or find a container for the tea. However, I don't really take off points for packaging for a product, I try to rate for the product itself. Another thing to note is that the instructions for the tea is in Chinese, so pay attention to the instructions on the site, if you're not familiar with how to properly brew this type of tea.
After receiving the tea, I set about making a pot - fortunately I have a hot water heater that keeps the water at a proper temperature for this type of tea, so I didn't have to worry about brewing the water to boiling and then letting it cool a little. I must say, this after measuring the right amount of tea into my pot and letting it steep for a couple of minutes, it was a refreshing cup of tea - no bitterness, but a bit of smokiness. Not too much, overall my impression is that it was a very smooth cup of tea, perfect 'as is', and I will definitely enjoy this bag and look forward to ordering more in the future. It's a great cup of tea to enjoy in the mornings or after meals, not too heavy and very refreshing.

title: great wrap for sushi lovers

As for the taste? I like that these rolls aren't as 'salty' as some other ones I've had, they allow for the flavors you put in the rolls to come through a little better. The sheets don't crumble too easily when you pull them out of the bag (I've had some crack and break when doing that) and have slight perforations in case you do want to size them down a little depending on what type of roll you're going to make (I had to make one roll smaller due to the amount of rice I had left over and it was easy to size down the roll this way). title: The Most Awful Expensive Tea I Ever Tasted

I took a chance on purchasing this tea of a product (because I usually buy what brands I know & like, in terms of food & drinks). I suffer from IBS and because this product said "organic" peppermint tea that is loose-leaf in a teabag, I figured to give this a try. It even looks like it would be medicinal and beneficial for me to drink for my health and digestive problems. Also, I believed the customer reviews on this tea product as well.

As a person that has been drinking tea for many years (since I was 14), this is by far the WORST tea I have ever had, for it's price nonetheless. That is the insulting part. Usually the more expensive a product is (especially tea), most likely the better quality and potency it will be. Well, it is not in this case. I can't believe I wasted my money on this brand. It doesn't even taste like peppermint AT ALL! I never put sugar in my tea either. Perhaps it may taste a bit better with some kind of sweetener involved but I highly doubt it, personally. Plus, the tea bag is a bit bigger than most tea bags should be. When you put hot water in the cup, it inflates like a pool toy, and STAYS inflated for quite a while.

Let's put it this way...this tea has made me feel sicker than what I already am. I wish I can ask for a refund, but I learned my lesson that I should stick to what I know is best for me. Harney & Sons tea is SO MUCH BETTER than this brand of tea. BUYER BEWARE!

title: Mild Flavored Nutty Drink
text:
Pls Keep In Mind This is my FIRST time drinking White Coffee:::: Observations::
(1)This does NOT taste like coffee
(2) the grounds are a bit course
(3) color of end result is not white, is translucent somewhat a light tan or discolored beige hue

My boss and a friend had raved about white coffee, so I wanted to try it. It was an adjustment for me. I put 4 cups water in automatic drip machine w/4 Tbs coffee. Hence taste wasn't suitable, just kind of hazlenutty but weak, no coffee flavor. Then I grinded the coffee grounds, thinking that would help and did same process. No difference in taste. SO I decided to combine with my FAV coffee, French Market (w/Chicory) 2 Tbs each and, added Stone Cold Sweet Creamer to taste AND it taste better. But then again I LOVE French Market/Chicory with anything ;o)

Overall, this white coffee is a mild flavored nutty drink (no acid or bad aftertaste). So if you like hazelnuts, this is your drink. Actually because of strength, don't even need to use a creamer.

UPDATE: Used it in percolator but still not overwhelmed. I think it's an acquired taste ;o)

title: Really flavorful Tea
text:
This is the 1st time that I’ve had this brand of tea and all of the flavors (except 1) were very flavorful and refreshing. There were some flavors that I’ve never heard of or thought sounded odd, but for me, they surprisingly turned out to be the more refreshing teas.

I really liked how each bag describes what level of caffeine it has, so that I could choose the best one to try, depending on the day. I liked how there were a lot of caffeine free to choose from, so I can drink that in the evening instead of a tea that’ll keep me awake at night.

I also like how the instructions had some character in it and used fun words, instead of just stating the instructions traditionally (that would’ve been fine, too).

I really enjoyed almost all of the flavors and I was honestly a little sad when I drunk the last bag, because it was fun for me to try the familiar and peculiar flavors. The price was really affordable for me and I would order this tea again or one flavor.

I would recommend this tea for someone that either wants to try a new brand and hasn’t had this brand yet (like I did) or wants to have a range of options to choose from depending on the time of day (especially at night, because there’s a fair amount of caffeine free teas).

title: Very Good
text: I'm a big fan of Terra Soul products. They are consistently fresh and reasonably priced. This cacao is the same. Really nice but I can't tell that much difference between this "supposed to be better" Chilean Cacao and the fair trade stuff in the bulk bins. But it is tasty. With just a dab of additional sweetener it's a good chacalate'.

title: Not Quite as Fresh as You'd Like
text: I've gotten this same flax at Wh.Foods and it's been the freshest seed I've ever had. By a mile! So impressed and grateful to have fresh food. But these two bags aren't much different than what you'd get in the bulk bins. And it's fine but I'll pick it up at WFds next time.

title: Best Ever!
text: This has got to be the freshest and tastiest dulce I've ever tried. Really a beautiful product. I'm needing to be salt free but tolerate the very low sodium in this very well. And I instantly felt better from adding just a small pinch to my food. It gave me a little endurance too. Hard to imagine from such a small amount. Absolutely delicious on rice!

title: Great Flavor!
text: Delicious tahini. Not bitter at all. Very fresh tasting. The only downside is that even though the sell by date is 6/22 and I received it 7/21....it had still separated enough to be real hard to stir back together. I just use it anyway either by spreading it as is on breads or using as is in salad dressings. Works fine. The flavor is worth it. ~ Thanks

title: Not Organic
text: Somehow I bought this without realizing it's not organic. Not willing to risk GMO corn or that it could be desiccated with Round-up. Other than that it's a fine product. Fed it to my pig's and they really liked it.

title: Like Molasses
text: I like this stuff. Tastes a lot like blackstrap molasses but not as bitter and a tad sweeter. It's unusual. The carob flavor is pretty mild. I can see why folks would like it. It's tasty on oatmeal. But for $18/ bottle I can see why you might not like it . But..it's good on oats and it's not sugar. That alone might be worth the cost.

title: Unusual Sweet
text: This is a pretty organically processed sugar. It's not as sweet as coconut sugar. And tastes slightly fermented. Not in a spoiled way, but as an attribute of the flowers it comes from. It's a personal preference whether you will like that or not.

title: A Clear View
text: I've only used a few brands of Matcha and wouldn't count myself as a connisuer, but I do like this tea. It's smooth and very soothing. The Matcha enervation is real clean, lasts all day and is very clear feeling. But, for me, I find less is more with Matcha. If I use too much, that smooth feeling will be more like the caffeine of green tea which does not inspire me. I prefer the clarity and this Match is very good at delivering a smooth clean matcha vibe. Very good for the price.

title: Mild Flavor
text: They send a pretty big can of oil for the money. I transferred mine to glass and put it in the fridge. What I love about this oil is that once cooled off, it becomes soft like butter and I can just spoon it out and control my proportions  much better than pouring. This is one of the few olive oils that comes with the pedigree of being free of pesticides and other contaminants. The reason I bought it. The flavor is mild but good and the oil seems fresh.

title: Toasted Almond Butter
text: Actually pretty decent Almond Butter. It's toasted and the grind is fairly grainy, but tasty. The oil was almost completely separated in the jar I received, but I could stir it all back together without much trouble. The jar is plastic which could drop this review to one star. Anyway...I'll hopefully survive or just not eat it because of that. I moved it into a glass jar and tucked it into the fridge while I decide if I want to risk ingesting more plastic....

title: Average Flavor
text: I grew up in California and used to pick up wild almonds from the valley around Winters near Davis. There's nothing finer than Wild Almonds that drop when ripe, split their husk and the Sun toasts them in the shell. They are wonderfully crisp with white flesh and a hint of yellow in the meat. Absolutely the tastiest almonds you'll ever eat! These are not that. I had high hopes and greatly applaud the growing efforts these folks are making. Getting food directly from the Earth is a feat all on it's own. And their almonds are good, but not that sweet or unusual for flavor, but good nonetheless. It's August now and I've received last years crop. They are still fresh enough to be more than acceptable. Some of the almonds have a sweet flavor, others are a bit bland....truth be told. I long for those days in the California Sun.

title: Delicious Tea!
text: A really brilliant tea. All the best fruits and hibiscus and not sweet or tart. Perfectly balanced. But sadly it also included "natural flavorings" and if you are a purist and don't want a chemical additive in your beautiful cup of tea, then this one won't do. Sadly I couldn't drink it only because of the additive.

title: Great Taste ~ Really Tannic
text: I love the flavor of this tea but after brewing for only a minute it gets more and more tannic by the second. For me that makes the tea unpalatable. Other'n that....tastes like biscuits and butter with a touch of honey.

title: Too Much Lemon Essence
text: This tea is to lemony. Especially since that flavor is derived from some essences. Tastes a bit fake. Tossing it out.

title: Just average quality
text: I was hoping this tea might be able to replace the Lord Grantham Tea from the Republic of Tea. It's a better price for lot's more bags but the tea is just so-so and gets real tannic real fast. So you can't steep it long enough to get the good ginger flavor. I had to reorder from the Republic to get a better cup.

title: Delightful
text: I've recently quit coffee for the last time. Truly!! And I very much enjoy this Matcha. It's world's apart from the boost of coffee. This is more like truly living and not being forced to do so. The color of the matcha powder is very bright green and seems quite fresh. I'm not a true conasouir. For now a 1/3 teaspoon is going into the blender with fruits and coconut water, but I love the effect. Gentile and true. Feels great!

title: Not that great
text: For a Kalamata olive...baby or no these are just bleh. They are greasy and overly salty and there isn't a good fresh kalamata flavor about them. What flavor is there his masked by the salt. Buyer beware these are of course non-returnable and non-refundable. Very disappointed. ~ Soo...since I've got 4lbs I tried them again. Not as bad after getting past the top of the jug. For the price they are pretty good.

title: Good Sesame
text: I don't really know the season to harvest these, but they seem quite fresh. The flavor is fairly mild for a raw unhulled sesame. I'm pretty happy with them. Toasted they would be very nice! I made a tahini butter with these straight out a the bag and added fresh Walnuts to give enough oil to get a spreadable blend. I use the Nutramilk butter maker and this is the best true tahini so far. ~ Thanks! ~ ;o)

title: Tasty
text: I like the mesquite powder. First time I ever tried it. It's slightly sweet, much less then carob powder but I think can be used similarly, in nut balls or baking. I didn't care for it so much in my coffee.

title: Really Great Sticky Rice
text: Very good rice. Says it's from Thailand. Fingers crossed that's true, as the Thai rice is supposed to be the cleanest. No or very low arsenic. Out of the bag there is not much aroma. To look at, I was not impressed, but cooked up some of the nicest purple rice I've ever had. Everything you want in a sticky rice. ~ Thanks ;o)

title: Nice Flavor
text: I really like the mildly sweet flavor of these. They stay fairly moist too after the bag is open. The sizes are mostly small but the quality seems really good. Clean for a berry.  Highly recommended if you like mulberries.

title: Great Consistancy
text: I love these oats. They are different then a regular gooey thick cut oatmeal. The flavor is mild and they cook real fast. Not gooey but rather light in texture and flavor. Digestability is excellent and they stayed with me longer then regular oats. Not as flavorful, but still real good!

title: Best Sunflowers Ever!
text: Every one of these seeds arrived in perfect condition. No chips. No yellow seeds. Quite perfect and great flavor. Freshest I've ever seen. ~ Thanks

title: Very Clean Goji's
text: Really nice Goji Berries. Moist upon first opening the container. Easy to eat out of hand, but then they hardened up overnite and aren't soft anymore. Still they soften real fast with soaking and since I prefer them cooked anyway, no problem.

title: Easy to Use
text: Very happy with this source of Kelp. Can't stand anything fish wise or from the ocean, but just a few short shakes and I have my recommended daily dose of Iodine without any fish flavor! To use Kelp as an iodine source one must be very careful not to exceed 1/16th of a teaspoon per day. It's real potent and you can overdose pretty easy. Given that...this bottle will last a very long time.

title: Excellent oil. Very delicate flavor and the oil is ...
text: Excellent oil. Very delicate flavor and the oil is light. Fresh as can be tho and quite delicious with foods that don't overwhelm it's understated bouquet.

title: Sure would make a great body oil tho if you didn't mind smelling like ...
text: The fragrance of this oil is amazingly nutty. Delicious smell really. As strong as peanuts only very unique. Personally I didn't care for the flavor. A little bitter and undistinct. Sure would make a great body oil tho if you didn't mind smelling like fresh roasted nutz.

title: Delicious Sweet
text: Good Golly is this stuff ever tasty! Wow. Quite delicious. I bought it to try in coffee to replace coco sugar and it works. I'm fussy about sugars in coffee. A pure demarcarus is ideal but I can't eat sugar like that anymore. This is great. Also good as a smoothie sweetener. And then it's pretty nice right off the spoon. Sticky as all get out. Worth it ~ ;o))

title: Best Salt I've Ever Had!
text: Wonderful salt. So tasty! Like you can just dive in and eat a bit without needing the potatoe chips underneath. ~ Very strengthening for the body. Delicious ;o))

title: Excellent Milder Flavor
text: Very tasty nut yeast. It's different then the bright yellow stuff. This is a mellow amber color and I really like the milder flavor. Plenty nutty, cheesy and tasty. The flavor complements instead of taking over the whole meal. Great with almost any savory. Thrilled to find a nut yeast without added supplements.

title: Dubious vitamins
text: I would give this 5 stars for taste and freshness, but I don't like the added vitamins. There's no listing of source and generally the add-ins are just synthetic quality. Goes against my grain.

title: Celtic Salt

title: Very Savory
text: This is the best Coconut Amino's. Thick and rich in flavor and substance. A little smoky tasting, in a good way. Very savory and quite delicious. I've tried others that are watered down. Not with this one. It's really good

title: Great Grains
text: These Oats are the freshest grains I've got in the pantry. Farmer direct grain is hard to find and these won't disappoint. Amazingly free of hulls. I toast them a bit before course milling them in the Komo grinder for a fantastic breakfast porridge. Upon first bite you'll recognize the higher nutrient profile and abundant life-force that is in this fresh grain. What you won't get is an overwhelming oatty flavor that will hold up over cinnamon and such. These Oats hardly taste like Oats at all. I get faint aromas of roses and sweet spices from them when toasting. It's nice. Makes great rice cooked separately or in stews. But the rich Oat flavor just isn't there. For me, they are still very tasty and the extra nutrition a great gift to ones health. Mixed with Einkorn, Emmer, Wild Lake Rice or Black Barley you will have all the flavor one could ever want. ~ 15#'s fills 3+ gallons

title: Title slightly deceiving
text: While I love these noodles, I was expecting more of a soup (ramen) and they're more like stir fry noodles. I followed the instructions and had just noodles in hot, thick sauce. Don't get me wrong, it's delicious, but it's not exactly what I was expecting.

title: An excellent breakfast item
text: These are delicious. I had never bought instant grits before, and I wasn't sure what to expect. I was very pleasantly surprised. These are easy to make and I really enjoy them on cold mornings.

title: A must-have sauce
text: This sauce is delicious! I put this in a lot of what I have cooked recently, it adds a nice kick without overpowering the flavor of the dish. This isn't available in my local grocery stores, and the price for 2 of these is very reasonable.

title: Great quality product
text: I was a little hesitant to buy this but I am so glad I did. I put this on so much more than I expected, it's delicious and was fresh on arrival. I'm always nervouse to buy food items online, especially something like this, but I was pleasantly surprised.

title: Tasty, sweet and savory Eel
text:
I rather like Eel, and wasn't sure what to expect when I ordered this. For those like myself who enjoy tinned fish, this is a little different than the usual fare. For one thing, it is preserved in eel sauce, which has - to an american - a teriyaki or a sweet and sour-like character. Surprisingly, this is not overbearing at all, it's actually quite well balanced, though I like to add just a little salt to taste. In consistency - it is dense and thick, almost like it has been half-frozen, or candied. This will doubtlessly put some people off, especially if you were expecting the yielding consistency of sardines or sprats, but this is closer to kipper.

I rather like it. I want to try some more traditional, western-hemisphere style eel, but this is a nice treat. The sauce really overpowers the eel flavor almost entirely, which if you are buying tinned eel for the eel might not be ideal. However, it is good for a snack and to add some variety to your cabinet, and I'm told it goes well with rice.

At this price, would recommend, if you feel like the above might be something you'd be interested in. It's worth a try, anyway, and I'll probably order another six-pack in the future.

title: Woody black tea
text:
I use two sachets in 32oz of freshly boiled water and steep for three minutes. This produces a surprisingly strong tea, but not an overpowering one. This differs from other black teas in that it has a woody aspect to its flavor, though you have to look for it a bit. It's something more typical of herbal teas, I think, but not unwelcome here. I find black tea to be a bit too acidic and this is no exception to that, as it can produce some nausea near the end of a brew, but a shorter steep mitigates this somewhat. I'm not sure how it stacks up against loose-leave or more expensive Oolongs, but having tried it, it may be worth it to me to seek some out.

If you haven't had Oolong before, I'd recommend trying it.

title: A companion for Lady Grey
text:
I don't have a tremendous liking of black teas, as I tend to find them too acidic, even at relatively short steeps. Earl Grey, for example, it a bit too much for me even when thin, but I rather like Lady Gray. Also, I'm working on cutting down my caffeine intake, and so have been looking to compliment my usual herbal tea cycle with some decaffeinated black and green tea.

Earl Greyer qualifies on both accounts. It is a brighter - that is, more aromatic, fruit - black tea similar to Lady Grey. I use 2x Satchets in 32oz of freshly boiled water, with 4 minute steep. This produces a pleasant tea, not too fruit or acidic, and does not cause any nausea. The number of sachets in the tube is 50, for $15, which I consider to be an appropriate price, and one I'd be willing to pay again in the future.

Altogether, the bergamot is forefront and has a natural character, and the decaffeination does not seem to have given the tea a chemical quality as is sometimes seen. I intend to order again in the future, and would recommend.

title: Mildly, but noticeably, sweetened muesli
text:
I like muesli, though I only get to eat it about once or twice I week. I specifically like it to be unsweetened, the same as I like my cereals, and will regularly add raw rolled oats to my mixes. Added fruit is fine, I just prefer not to have other sweeteners - refined or otherwise - in there.

This is as the label says - mildly sweet. You can tell, since the individual oat flakes have a slight hardness and faint shininess to them, and it definitely tastes sweeter, both dry and with milk. That said, it is quite mild, and when mixed with 1:2 with unsweetened muesli it comes out just as delicious.

Otherwise, the mix is generous and I particularly like the inclusion of pecans and sunflower seeds. As the value is also fairly good, I would recommend giving this a try, either to have alone or in a mix with other muesli.

title: Delicious fish skins
text:
The moment I laid eyes on these, I knew I'd like them, and indeed I do. A crispy/crunchy battered salmon skin - don't let the salted egg drive you off, these are delicious. I liked them so much I bought more for my father, who also liked them. A very authentic flavor - not too salty, not too greasy, not too rich. Now you don't get a huge amount in a bag, and you pay quite a bit for it relative to other salty bagged snacks, but it's definitely worth buying as a treat now and again. I fully intend to do so.

Would recommend.

title: Not bad, but inferior to the thick version
text:
I purchased the thick version of Stockans Oatcakes, and I liked them enough that I think I'll add them into my typical rotation. I've tried a couple other oatcakes since - Nairns, Walkers - and the Stockans Thick remain on top. As such, I wanted to try an alternative variant, to see how they stacked up.

In brief, I like them less. The thick version has more body of course, but the thin ones also seem a bit drier. They re more in line with the Walkers, which are still pretty good on their own. I think I'd want to add some sort of spread to these to make them more interesting, rather than have them straight.

So not bad so far as oatcakes go, but the Thick Stockans are preferable in every respect.

title: A novel, tasty treat
text:
I've never had edinburgh rock, and so I didn't know what to expect. I was thinking it would be like Candy Hearts, which I don't like at all, but this was quite different. For one thing, the cream of tartar give it a unique tart flavor - not sour, as you have with citrus, but a different sort of thing. The consistency is much softer than Candy Hearts, much more crumbly. The flavors are very mild - you can tell they have different flavors, but only just barely. They are sweet, but the sweetness is not dominating, especially in competition with the cream of tartar.

Glad I purchased it, it sounded interesting and it turns out it was. Most of the family liked it, having only a chunk or two at a time, and so I will be ordering it again, either this product or a similar one.

Would recommend trying at least once.

title: Taste like figs
text:
Not sure why - if I didn't know that these were apricots, I would have assumed they were figs, that is what they taste like. Like the figs in fig newtons. They are soft, easy to eat, not too sweet. They make good snacking fruit, and they go particularly well in muesli, since they are diced small. I don't know if I like the flavor - I suppose I might order these again, for their figish taste, but if I wanted the flavor of diced apricots I'd probably try a different brand.

Also, almost all of mine has some powdery white coating or surface on some of the bits. This didn't hurt the eating at all, they tasted fine, and they didn't smell off, and though it superficially resembles some sort of mold on closer inspection it looks like it's probably just a characteristic of the drying process.

If the above sounds interesting, would recommend. If you want apricot-tasting dried apricots, may try something else.

title: Tasty preserved fish, smokiness is mild but dominant nonetheless
text:
These sprats are tasty tinned fish, and the equal of high quality sardines. They are hardly bony at all, they don't have any of that mild bitterness you sometimes get with kippers, and the smokiness isn't overbearing. You get plenty of sprats in a jar, I'd estimate between 3 and 4 standard sardine tins worth.

Personally I like them, and I'd order them again, but I wouldn't want to make them my primary choice of sardines. The smokiness is pleasing but it is also the dominant flavor. In total, a single jar has about 600 calories, and some, but not too much, residual oil. I'd prefer olive oil but rapeseed/linseed oil is fine too, it just doesn't add much character. I don't know if you'd have to refrigerate these after opening - the jar doesn't say one way or the other - but I'd rather not risk it, and though I like tinned fish I definitely don't like it cold.

So I would recommend at least trying these, especially if you like tinned fish, and I'd like it if Belveder put out a spiced variant.

title: They are awful
text:
I have tried many things in my life, most of them purchased off Amazon, and these are terrible. It isn't just the chili-lime - I really like chili-lime mango slices - but the apple and the watermelon are truly unpalatable. Synthetic - worse than synthetic, the have a chemical profile, you can hardly taste the fruit they are supposed to represent. Only the mango is passable, and even there, just barely. They might take it to a 1.5, if such was an option, but instead I'm rounding down because the other two are just that awful. A rare occasion where I couldn't finish even the second bag of the watermelon, I ended up throwing the rest of the box into the fire.

Terrible. Do not recommend.

title: A bit sweet for dried blueberries, but decent for snacking or baking
text:
I purchased these to add to muesli, and for snacking in general, and they are better suited for the former than the latter. They do have a decent, natural blueberry flavor, but the copious amounts of extra sugar really compete with it. As such, if you have something relatively bland, like unsweetened muesli, these add a lot to it, but if you are just snacking on them, you get an unremarkable blueberry experience. They are very soft and chewy, to easy to eat, and if you have a handful or two with each snacking session this bag will last a good three weeks or so.

I probably wouldn't buy this brand again, and try something with lower sugar, but it was worth trying once due to the great blueberry-to-dollar ratio. So would recommend in that respect.

title: Large, tart, sweetened cranberries
text:
I like dried cranberries, but usually the come in little bags, and I like to eat them a handful at a time, with three handfuls per snacking session. This is solution to my problem - even at my snacking rate, 2.2lb will last me three weeks or so. These are fairly large - between 1/4" and 1/2" - soft, juicy, tart, and a bit sweet.

Regarding that last point - almost all dry cranberries are sweetened, but these have an 26g of sugar - 22g of which is added - per 40g serving. Compare with Ocean Spray Craisins which have 29g of sugar for the same mount. So keep in mind that these 65% sugar. I generally prefer no added sugar to my dried fruit, but am still looking for cranberries which meet this requirement.

So they are at least as good as typical dried cranberries, and have a little less sugar than the mainstream brand. Would recommend for general snacking.

title: Not as good as Stockans, but tasty nonetheless
text:
I decided to try Stockans Oatcakes - the thick version - mostly out of curiosity, as they sounded like the sort of thing I would like. Indeed, I do like them, quite a bit, I've never had a biscuit/savory cake quite like them. Only possible critique is that they are just on the verge of being a bit "oily" - not quite all the way there, but almost.Now I intend to try several other kinds of oatcake, and this was the first.

The Stockans are a bit richer, a bit softer, and a bit heavier than these Nairns, which are more like a heavy cracker. These are good too, but they are a bit drier and less flavorful. As such, while I can have the Stockans on their own, these are better with a spread of some kind - preferably something with some moisture to it. A pack of these would make a decent breakfast, if paired with coffee or tea.

You get pretty good value for your money with these, despite the premium you pay compared to typical crackers. Worth trying, at least.

So I would recommend these, if you like wheat or oat crackers, as they are more substantial than your usual offerings and better able to take and accompany a spread. However, if you specifically want oat cakes, the Stockans Thick Oatcakes (ASIN: B00KX9QEE4) are the better way to go.

title: Well-suited for arancini
text:
I purchased this to make arancini for New Years, and it came out quite well. I cooked it briefly in olive oil and apple cider vinegar (no white wine on hand), then sauted it with chicken stock until fully cooked, adding a egg at the end to help it keep its shape. The risotto was good, appropriately sized, reasonably flavorful, so far as I could tell. Quite happy with the results.

Will order again when I make arancini the next time.

title: Rich, satisfying oat cakes
text:
Well I'm a fan. I've never had oat cakes before, but they sounded like just the sort of thing I'd like, and indeed they are. These are quarter-disks of compact-but-crumbly oat cakes which readily break apart and are easy to eat. There are six packs of eight cakes, with each cake being a little under 1/4" thick. One or two cakes is enough for a snack.

I quite like these. They are neither sweet nor salty, and they have a robust oat flavor to them. Direct comparisons are tricky, but it's something like the flavor of the crust of of an oat flour bread, if that makes sense. In terms of consistency, they are fairly soft and very slightly gritty - the closest comparison would be to a dense graham cracker crust. There is a hint of oil to the cake as well, though it comes through less as a flavor and more as a binder.

So I eat them as they are, and they have become a breakfast and late-night staple for me. I haven't tried them baked, toasted, heated, or with any other condiments yet, but I will shortly. I will definitely be ordering these and/or other variants again in the future.

Strong recommendation. If you've never had them before, I'd definitely give them a go.

title: Nice presentation, but that's about it
text:
So they are almonds covered in a chocolate-like coating, dressed up to look like olives. The presentation is so-so - basically they are just coated in a olive-great confection with a dab of red on the end. That's the only reason to buy these - otherwise, they are sub-par chocolate-covered almonds. If you want chocolate covered almonds specifically, I'd look elsewhere for a higher-quality coating. One thing I will say, these are much softer than your typical chocolate-covered almond, the coating being less dense than typical tempered chocolate, so it has that going for it.
