If you like the concept, as I did, go ahead and buy them, the presentation is neat. Otherwise, I'd give them a miss.

title: Well I like these crumbly oat-flake-bricks
text:
For the uninitiated, Oatbix are small bricks - roughly 3"x1.5"x.5" - of compacted oat flakes. They are very dry, and yield readily - you can crumble one into bits in your hand with little effort. You can eat them directly - I like to - and they resemble a much softer form of shredded wheat, but most people would find them too dry for this I think. Instead, you put 1-3 bricks into a bowl, add some milk, then break them up for consumption.

I like Weetabix, and now I like Oatbix as well. If you like Weetabix, you will find the Oatbix a bit more oaty, naturally, and a bit more bland as a result. I like the oat flavor quite a bit, so this is right up my alley - in particular, it's like getting the oat flavor of oatmeal/rolled oats but in a softer, more digestible form. Personally, I prefer to not let it soak for for long - I find it gets a bit too porridge like then - but instead gently crumble up a couple bricks, pour the milk on, and eat it immediately while it still has some body.

If you haven't tried any *bix, you might want to go for Weetabix first, as they have a bit more flavor to them, but these are also good. If you like wheat or bran cereal or cold oatmeal but find it a bit hard to chew through, this is a great alternative. In any case, it's worth giving a try. I've bought it before, and will likely do so again.

Would recommend.

title: Inoffensive, but unimpressed
text:
I'm not a tremendous fan of chai, nor of rooibos, so I suppose it isn't surprising that this isn't my cup of tea (haHA). Nevertheless of had other chai and rooibos teas which had a more sophisticated flavor profile, I found this to be a bit one-note, with the chai dominating. Not particularly relaxing or warming. It's possible that this tea would be better with a little milk and sugar - I generally take my tea straight and chai isn't well suited for that.

So it a meh for me, but if you like chai or milky tea maybe it will be different for you.

title: Creamy nougat with some substance, but so-so flavor
text:
I wasn't overly impressed with this nougat, which I found as a result of a thread online. It wasn't poor quality by any means, the chocolate was creamy and the nougat soft, but stable - you can bite into it but there's little to chew. No complaint about the consistency - it's the flavor, which I found to be unremarkable, maybe a little synthetic. More to the point, it isn't the flavor I usually associate with nougat here in the US - maybe Croatian nougat is different.

You do get quite a bit in a box, and presentation is on point. However, I don't think I'll be ordering this variety again.

title: Lovely color, unimpressive flavor
text:
The color is beautiful; the turmeric gives is a lovely golden-orange hue. The sachets will give everything they touch a golden-orange hue, if you aren't careful, or even if you are, as turmeric tends to do. Beyond that, I found the flavor unremarkable. The ginger is milder than most ginger teas, and I didn't feel like the turmeric added much to the flavor profile. I am drinking it right now, as I write this review, in white work pants, which I don't recommend for the task. The turmeric has a pleasant odor, but little flavor of interest.

As for digestive or calming effects, I've detected none. Drinking it now, I am experiencing about typical levels of indigestion/existential crisis.

So maybe give it a go if you think you'll like the turmeric/ginger blend, but otherwise, I'd give it a pass.

title: Not a very strong mango flavor
text:
I can't say I'm too disappointed, since I knew I was buying candied fruit, but this has relatively little mango flavor to it. Yupik's cubed papaya was most more flavorful - the sugar-sweetness dominates this one. I find that if I mix it is with Museli, it does help give a tropical essence to my breakfast, but only to a limited degree. I prefer my dried fruit unsweetened anyway, so this isn't all that surprising.

However, I purchased these for my mother to have in her breakfast cereal, and she seems to like them more than I do, not minding the additional sweetness. The fruit is very soft, very easy to eat or to add to dishes or baked good, so I imagine you could get a lot of use out of it in that regard.

So if you don't mind the sweetness or the milder mango flavor, would recommend. Otherwise would not.

title: Like maple sugar candy without the maple flavor
text:
That's what this reminds me of, maple sugar candy - the crystallized variety I mean. This is a little stiffer and a little less grainy that that sort of confection, it's like halfway between crystallized maple sugar candy and fudge. In terms of flavor, there's also a background butteriness which is toffee-like in character, but quite mild. If you've ever had soft toffee, this has many of the same characteristics.

I personally wasn't a tremendous fan, but the rest of the family really enjoyed them. I did like how the flavor was something novel, that becomes more and more rare as you get older.

It's sweet, but if you've never had it, I recommend giving it a try. It is well-worth the price for what you get.

title: They're cranberries alright
text:
Not much to say about these - they're dried cranberries. The addition of the juice does indeed make them softer and, you know, juicier than the more typical varieties, and even though the juice is unsweetened it still adds sweetness to the cranberries, if that's your thing.

So they are slightly sweeter, substantially juicier cranberries. I'd recommend them for snacking, but probably not for baking, since you do lose some of that characteristic tartness that you have in the unfortified varieties.

title: They're quite like raisins
text:
I purchased these because they sounded intriguing. I didn't expect to like them, but it's rare to come across something where I've never had anything quite like it before, so I gave it a go.

Somewhat disappointingly, there is very little olive flavor. Maybe at the tail end of it at best, but really these taste a great deal like raisins. They are a little less sweet, and a little less tart than raisins tend to be. I think I'm so used to olives being brined that I just assumed these would be to - but they are not, and probably for the best. They are best described as "sweet, but not fruity".

They are definitely less soft, though quite chewable, and they are also more astringent than I would have anticipated. You can't quite have a handful of these like you can a handful of raisins or other dried fruit, you only want maybe a half-dozen at a time. I'd say these are a little less fibrous, but not by much.

So they are neat. I recommend ordering some to try, or maybe to have out during a party or the holidays as a conversation starter. They are inoffensive enough to be safe for most palates.

Would recommend.

title: Just as satisfying as I remember
text:
I first had these when I was living in Ireland many years ago, and so I thought it was time to try them again.

For the uninitiated, these are small bricks or blocks of compressed wheat flakes, about 3"x1.5"x.5" or so. They are mostly wheat - dry and light with no additional sweetness. to them. You can eat one directly, which I don't recommend trying more than once, or you can put a couple in a bowl and pour some milk over them, crushing them up afterward with a spoon. They soften immediately, but still retain a little bit of their fiber and body. So they aren't crispy or dense like many wheat flakes tend to be in milk, and they aren't "goopy" like porridge. Basically, if you like wheat-type cereal but have trouble chewing or working through denser options, this is a good alternative.

Neato, in my opinion. I still like them, I usually have two or three of these in a bowl and they are satisfying enough. Not as filling as museli or oatmeal, but pretty nice anyway. A box would last me about three weeks, since I don't have them every day, and I'll probably order some again in the future.

Would recommend.

title: Spongy, spicy tofu snack
text:
I don't think this is for me, to be honest. The spicy is too spicy for me to enjoy, being about the heat of sriracha sauce. The snack itself is tofu-like; eating them straight from the package wasn't particularly satisfying, but they were different than other snacks I've tried in the past. Spongy, soft, surprisingly chewy, not all that filling.

Not for me, but if the above sounds interesting, maybe give them a try.

title: Remarkably appealing for a paleo mix
text:
I purchased this mostly as an additive to other museli, since I didn't think that it would be, on its own, compatible with my usually preparation of milk-in-bowl. However, it is actually quite good - the coconut goes far in adding bulk and fiber to the mix. That said, I will be using it mostly as an additive - it will stretch much further that way, and I am not on a paleo diet myself, quite the opposite really. It makes an excellent additive to other museii or granola mixes, if added with restraint.

Generally speaking, I would recommend this one, mostly for snacking or supplementing, but also on its own, if that's the sort of thing you are looking for.

title: Maybe a bit too seedy on its own
text:
I have recently discovered museli and am exploring the various types and kinds. Off all the Bob's Red Mill varieties, I like the New European Gluten Free the best. This one, a bit less so - it doesn't really absorb the milk all that well, with most of the ingredients being fairly impermeable. Now this is no major issue for me, because I just mixed it with rolled oats and some other grains, and it makes a great supplement to other museli, cereal, or granola. However, judged entirely on its own, I would say that if you are looking for a complete museli you should look elsewhere.

However, if a fruit/seed heavy mix is what you are looking for instead, would recommend.

title: Unremarkable or snacking, but good for mixing
text:
I was unimpressed by this mix for snacking - I'm not a fan of the addition of goji berries, they are a bit hard and bitter in comparison with the rest of the mix. This works well if you add it to Museli, granola, cereal, or trail mix, and would probably go well in baked good, but for snacking it is underwhelming.

Quantity is okay, freshness likewise. If you want to try a novel mix without needing to buy all the ingredients separately, then I recommend it. Otherwise, I'd just buy the four or five berries you want and make up your own mix instead.

title: Great value, but a bit too sweet for me
text:
Personally, I always try to buy my dried fruit without additional sugar. Fruit has sugar enough already, it doesn't need any more. However, I recognize that many people particularly enjoy the sugar-coated cubes, and so I purchased this for the family, particularly so my mother could try adding some to her Museli or breakfast cereal.

Personally, they are too sweet. I think these would be great without the added sugar, but with the extra they are one step off of candied. The papaya flavor is still quite good though, still quite natural, and the texture is quite consistent, having only a little fiber to it. It does go well in cereal and museli, and imparts a strong tropical influence to it, which is quite nice. I like it better as an accent than as a snack.

So I would say - not a very natural variety of dried papaya, but still quite tasty. You get a decent amount for what you pay, and a bag will likely last you a couple weeks to a month at normal levels of consumption

If you like sweetened dried fruit, would recommend.

title: Fairly good, though I prefer the pretzel
text:
These are decent - like all Combos, you get a decent amount of snack per bag, better than most alternatives, and they have a nice balance of crunch on the outside and soft on the inside. The cheddar filling isn't exactly natural, but it has a sharp, cheez wiz-like flavor profile to it. The cracker is fairly mild, which is why I recommend the pretzel shell instead - it better accompanies the filling and covers up some if its shortcomings.

That said, if you aren't a huge fan of pretzel, then these are a good choice. I prefer the cheddar Combos to the Pizza, as I find the latter to have too much of a tomato-paste overtone to be really satisfying.

title: My favorite of the original combos
text:
I like these best, of all the original Combos flavors. The pizza are okay, a little artificial, but the pretzel and the cheddar complement each other well. The ingredients are both highly processed, so don't expect a natural snack here, but they are both suitably pretzel-like and cheddar-like to strike the right notes. Crunchy on the outside and softish on the inside. Each packet is quite generous and provides just enough for a snack - much more for your money than the equivalent snack bag of chips.

If you are looking to try Combos, this is a good place to start. Probably the best balanced of the basic flavors. Would recommend.

title: Suitable on their own, better with other ingredients
text:
I purchased these as I am always looking for new options for entrees. They are interesting. You can't eat them on their own, either dry or cooked, they have almost no flavor. I soak them for about 10m, gently dry them out, then throw them in a saute pan with some salt and oil until they brown up in 10-15m or so. They end up tasting like whatever you cook them with, but are reminiscent of tempeh. The texture is vaguely chicken-like but more spongy/less fibrous. Not very filling, compared to most carbs, but I think it would compliment sauteed vegetables well in a way which is a bit more natural than most tofu.

Pricewise, too expensive. I might pay half this price for soy curls, especially considering what they are, but I wouldn't buy them again at this price point. Happy to do so to try them out, but not as part of my regular grocery list.

Would recommend trying, at least.

title: Decent standard golden raisins
text:
I purchased these because I thought I was buying jumbo raisins, which I prefer, but they ended up being pretty good anyway. The smaller raisins tend to be sweeter, but they go better in baked goods and museli. Some prefer them for snacking as well, whereas I prefer their jumbo counterparts on account of the reduced sweetness.

Anyway, these are soft and juicy, and a couple handfuls makes a nice snack. Would recommend.

title: Juicy, soft jumbo raisins
text:
I prefer jumbo raisins to their smaller alternatives, because they are typically less sweet and more filling. These are no exceptions - they are everything jumbo raisins should be, such that a single handful is plenty for the occasional snack. They do not have added sugar, nor any oil that I detected. I purchased them alongside regular golden raisins so as to check the size, and these are much, much larger, 4x as big I would say.

They are well-packed in their sack, but this is of minimal consequence, and so it loses no star from me. The price is quite good for five pounds, I don't mind paying it since this bag will last a month at least. Better suited for snacking than baking, on account of their size, but usable for most recipes anyway.

Would recommend, and will probably be ordering again.

title: Chocolate with an minty shell
text:
I bought these after someone mentioned it was their favorite European candy. It sounded good - a thin minty shell wrapped around good chocolate - so I figured I'd give it a try. Personally, I could go either way on them - I'd prefer the shell was slightly thinner so I could chew it right up and get both textures and flavors at once. However, if you let it sit in the mouth for a bit, it gets to that state in about 90 seconds, so not a deal breaker. The mint is decent quality, about a standard sugary peppermint. The chocolate is reasonable quality, better than most common American confections. All in all its an interesting treat.

While I am so-so on it, the rest of the family likes it quite a lot and have about finished off the bag already. Whereas I probably won't order it again for myself, I will be ordering it again for them, and possible a couple members of the extended family these holidays

So would recommend trying at least once, they deserve that much.

title: They're just like I remember, sans the red tip
text:
I purchased these on an whim, as the subject had come up in a recent conversation and I wanted to try them again, to see if they tasted just like I remembered. They do indeed - they have the same mildly mint-like flavor, chalky consistency, coarse texture, and satisfying snap that they did twenty years ago. They aren't anything too special, sure, and by the third package I was finished with the concept, but everyone I handed a pack to was happy to get it, all remembering bygone days two, four, six decades past.

Only complaint is that they don't have the little red tip, so you may have to tax your imagination a bit if you want to play at puffing up. Nevertheless, would recommend.

title: Dense and delicious
text:
I like cereal, but I do not like anything overly sweet - I prefer my wheat flakes and bran sticks and rice hexagons and, you know, oat toroids and the like. I had only ever heard of Museli second-hand, until I received a small bag of it as part of a granola sampler a few months ago. I basically forgot about it until autumn, when I started getting a hankering for something natural and harvesty.

This is good, it's quite good in fact. I'd never considered eating rolled oats with milk before, usually I"d only go with boiling water, but this was very nice. It has a wide variety of flavors and textures, a mild sweetness, and it is quite filling and fibrous. Some may find it a bit too heavy on the oats - my mother, who has started trying to incorporate museli into her diet, mixes this with something like Total to make it more cereal-like. I think the proportion is fine myself - so fine that I actually add more oats into it.

So if you like cereal, or want something substantial, I'd recommend this Familia Swiss Muesli. You get a respectable amount of muesli for what you pay, and its good quality to boot. While I'm still working my way through various brands of muesli, I'll probably be ordering this again.

title: Tart, soft, flavorful
text:
I purchased these after reading the word "fruit roll snacks". I was hoping for traditional fruit leather, or a natural version of fruit by the foot - soft, fibrous, naturally sweet, that sort of thing. These are different. They are quite tart, and have a fairly natural fruit flavor to them, they are soft and consistent all the way through - they don't have the bite of western fruit snacks. I would say that they are made from a fruit puree - if you flatten one out you can see that it is mostly translucent.

I would say that they are interesting. They have enough flavor that two or three is more than enough for a snack for me. For a fruit roll snack I'd prefer something with a bit more body, but these are nice on their own. For family and friends, the consensus is that they are too tart/sour to really enjoy, and so I will likely be finishing the bag myself.

Probably worth trying at least once, especially for how much you get in the bag, but I don't think I'll order them again myself.

title: Soft, tasty, but a little pricey
text:
I liked these bars - I had one per day with lunch for for a few weeks, and they were just sweet and rick enough to cap off the meal. All three flavors are distinct, though the vanilla least-so, and the ingredients seem to be of a high quality. Strong sesame taste, of course, an appropriately dry. They have a nice presentation as well, and are reasonably generous with the pistachio and cocoa nibs.

That said, these are fairly pricey so long as halva/tahini/sesame bars go, as much as 3x the price depending on where you source them. So if you like halva bars and already have ones you enjoy, these probably won' t impress you.

However, if you want to mix up your usual rotation and try tahini bars for the first time, in convenient 100 calorie packages, I'd recommend these, they are quite nice.

title: Tart, chewy fruit leather bites
text:
I rather like these - they are small individually wrapped chews - about 3/4" x 1/2* (slightly smaller than Caramel Creams) seemingly made from a translucent, richly-colored reduced fruit puree.

In terms of consistency, these are chewy, but not in the way that sticks to your teeth, at least not substantially, so they aren't fatiguing to eat. They do not have the pulp, grain, or fiber of more traditional fruit leather, these have a soft toffee-like smoothness to them. You can easily squeeze one between your fingers, for example, and it will flatten out and remain that way.

The flavor is natural, much more so than most fruit snacks, but both sweeter and much more tart. While there are multiple flavors in the bag, I didn't note any to have a distinct character that set it apart from the others, though there is some small difference between them.

It is fairly popular in the household, but most people have commented on the tartness and find it off-putting. It is strong enough that I only need about two for a snack, but for others it is too intense.

Personally, I would recommend giving these a try. They aren't quite the fruit leather bites I was expecting, but they are pretty good and something that most people probably haven't tried before.

title: Decent, natural tasting fruit rolls, if consumed as intended
text:
I purchased these because I wanted to try some fruit leather, and this seemed like a decent way to get some. They come two rolls to a pack, and in three flavors, mango, raspberry, and strawberry; naturally, you eight packages total, and as each has two rolls, there are forty-eight rolls in the box.

The rolls have a very natural flavor and consistency, exactly what you would expect from this sort of snack. Very soft, hardly chewy at all, the strips easily cleave apart and have a mildly pulpy/grainy consistency, as appropriate for this kind of snack. I, as an adult, found a single package a bit too light, so I usually had two packages per snacking session. I did learn that if you eat them the way they were intended, as a fruit roll, they last longer and are more satisfying. I you just pop one in your mouth, it goes down a bit quick.

I imagine that for kids, one pack would be enough. Each package comes with a little card, which might draw some interest, though I somewhat doubt it.

I don't think I'll buy them again myself - they were as expected, but nothing makes these stand out from other fruit leathers. However, other members of the family liked them, and some even showed sufficient restraint to only have one roll per session and put the other one away for later. So it is probably worth trying at least once.

Would recommend trying.

title: Not much of a pizza flavor, but decent snack otherwise
text:
I purchased these because I used to get them back in summer camp when I was a kid and remember them fondly. They are a bit different than I recall, but the experience is about the same.

They are salty on the outside with a mild pretzel flavor, they have a bit of crunch but are mostly crumbly and dry. The filling has a stiff, slightly grainy canned-cheez-whiz-like consistency, and I would say the flavor is most reminiscent of tomato paste, not much in the way of cheese even, much less basil. Basically you are getting an extraordinarily abbreviated pizza experiences from these, if that's what you are looking for.

However, they are easy to eat, and a single bag is actually pretty satisfying for a grown adult. So if you like the concept, but want to skip the pizza flavor, I'd recommend trying one of the other varieties. You aren't going to beat this deal, two boxes for $18, double the value of the usual offering, so if that's what you want stick with this one.

All in all, these aren't for me, and the family wasn't too interested in them either. Snacks rarely make it more than a week in our household and these are still hanging out two weeks later. So I think I'll distribute them to unsuspecting coworkers via the common room at work.

Wouldn't recommend.

title: More sweet than sour, mediums spice, fairly soft consistency
text:
I occasionally purchase some vegan jerky to add to my snack rotation. Usually it is far too expensive to justify it, especially given what it is made of, but this is a decent value for the money.

While Be Leaf has a shredded version of their jerky, which I prefer, these are "tenders" about the size of those found in typical beef jerky but somewhat softer and less fibrous. Chewy, but not enough to fatigue the jaw.

In terms of flavor, it's interesting. A little heat - by general snack food standards you could probably call this medium or hot, though if you like spice it's fairly mild, well below sriracha. It does not have too much of that "meat alternative" flavor you find in some plant jerky, but it is there. Not much of a sweet and sour flavor, more of a mildly sweet one.

I'd say this is worth trying at least once, it's a decent complement to other jerky. Would recommend.

title: Rich tablets of chocolate
text:
These are "neapolitans", or small, individually wrapped rectangles of chocolate, something like Andes mints. The quality of the chocolate is quite high, and these have ridges at the top which Bouchard claims is to increase surface area for the purposes of increasing the intensity of flavor. I don't know about that part - the texture is interesting though, and the little tablets have a nice, satisfying snap to them, having the characteristic rigidity of good chocolate. Definitely a higher class candy to put out for guests, at least. They are a bit small - I usually have two or three for a snack - but appropriately sized for what they are.

These are fairly dark, but not overly bitter; I am someone who will eat unsweetened baker's chocolate as a snack and find most milk chocolate overly sweet, and these were comfortably in the middle. Their milk chocolate counterparts, sold by Bouchard, are still very good, a creamy, rich milk chocolate that is also worth trying.

Per bag it is a bit pricey, but at 2lb you definitely get good value for your money, especially compared to many cheaper varieties of chocolate. Would recommend.

title: More enjoyable than expected
text:
I like my beef jerky, and occasionally go through a phase where I'll buy about $100 worth and snack on it exclusively for a couple weeks. I've tried numerous varieties over the years, and recently have been trying vegan jerkies to shake things up a bit. They are hit or miss, and almost always criminally overpriced for what you are getting, but some are quite good.

This is one of them. It is a soft, shredded jerky with a mildly spicy flavor, almost too easy to consume. You get decent value for your money, better than most plant jerkys offer, and it is savory and mildly spicy to make for a very respectable midday or late-night snack. Not greasy, not overly mushroomy. It has a bit of that fake-meat flavor common to vegan alternative products, but the Wasabi flavor covers this well. I am a big fan of the consistency - soft, chewy, lots of flavor from chewing.

All in all, I rather like this vegan jerky, it's probably one of my favorites I've tried thus far. I will probably be ordering it again, along with a couple other flavors from the same product line. If you like normal beef jerky and you want to vary up your rotation, or just want a savory snack, would recommend.

title: A classic confection, but not for me
text:
I purchased this on a whim - Amazon marketing got me - because I like fruity snacks and am a sucker for foreign treats. The licorice I'm familiar with is the Twizzlers variety - I'm not a fan anise, but the "red" peeling-away variety is okay, if a bit plasticy. I thought maybe authentic Italian licorice would be better.

It has a much more fruity fragrance to it, it smells delicious, a distinctly candy-strawberry experience. Flavor-wise it is underwhelming. Mildly sweet, mildly strawberry-like, but that's about it. It is stickier and more dense than Twizzler-type licorice by a fair margin, though this can be offset by slightly warming it in the microwave, only for five seconds or so. It's the sort of candy that gets stuck to the surface of your teeth.

Generally speaking, I wasn't a fan. I like softer, fruitier treats like fruit snacks or fruit leather more than this. However, when I shared some around, I found that this is the same kind of licorice my mother used to have when she was young. She had not had it for a long time, but reports it tastes just like she remembers. So that was an nice little surprise for the both of us.

So I don't think I'd recommend it if you like more modern, softer, candy with stronger, natural flavors, but if you want to experience the candy of yesteryear, give it a try.

title: Itty-bitty popcorn
text:
It really is just like that - itty bitty kernels of popcorn. All of them soft, no hard centers, with well-balanced saltiness. The avocado oil imparts a mild buttery flavor as well, or something like that. Nice for a snack - you'd think that with such small kernels you'd finish the bag in a couple sittings, but I liked taking a large spoonful now and again, so it lasted a couple weeks.

More of a novelty than something I'd buy regularly. However, I think this has a lot of potential as a baking ingredient and/or garnish, and may try mixing some into a batch of chocolate chip cookie dough, or layering on some blondies, to see how it affects the consistency. Might make interesting rice crispy treat as well.

Would recommend trying at least once, as it's pretty tasty.

title: Solid snacking fruit
text:
With no added sugar, these make a great fruit snack. They measure about 3" long and between 1"-2" wide, so about three are good enough for a snacking session. They have an even consistency - not too chewy, a bit fibrous but not overly so. Nice bite - easier than dried apples, for example - but easy to eat. Flavorwise - I found them not to have too strong of a pear flavor myself, it's mostly there in the aftertaste, but other members of the family feel otherwise.

I like that they have no added sugar, are easy to eat, and have enough in the package to last at least a week or two in the household. With the size they are, you can't really add them to a fruit mix, unless you dice them first, but that's not a problem for me.

Would recommend.

title: Sweet, bitter, sour, has it all
text:
I wanted to shake things up a bit and try something new, and this certainly qualifies. Golden Berries are chiefly tart, with a distinct underlying bitterness and background sweetness. The flavor, to me anyway, is comparable to dehydrated lemon slices with the seeds intact, or maybe like not-quite-ripe wild blueberries. They are quite moist - somewhat similar to unsweetened dried cranberries in that regard.

So they are neat. Tart enough that even a small handful is enough for a single snack. I bet they'd be quite tasty as part of a dried cranberry/blueberry/strawberry/raisin mix. The family is a little less positive, most find them too sour/bitter for what they are looking for from dried berries. I however like the variety.

Would definitely recommend trying at least once, I'll probably be ordering them again.

title: Excellent unsweetened dried pineapple
text:
I always look to purchase dried fruit with no added sugar, and this is just the ticket. The chunks are perfectly sized, they are fairly soft and chewy, and have a mild, natural pineapple flavor. By comparison, they are pretty close to a typical dehydrated apple, albeit a bit drier and more fibrous. Still sufficiently moist for snacking though.

Quality looks good - no issues with debris or foreign material in my bag.

Quite happy with this, and the family seems to enjoy it too. 2lb should last a week or two with constant snacking, since a handful is enough per session. Will probably be ordering this again in the future.

Would recommend.

title: Filling salty snack, a great complement to chips and the like
text:
These are a worthy addition to your snack cabinet. I wouldn't regard them as a healthy snack, exactly, but they are much more substantial and less oily than potato chips and various corn-based snack foods. You need less of them - a small handful is usually enough to satisfy. They have a small variety of flavors - the taste of the underlying vegetables do come through, albeit in a diminutive form.

In terms of texture/substance; they aren't so much "hard" as they are "stiff". This is to say, the toughest bits take more force to chew but they still break into blunt pieces, not sharp fragments. Most people shouldn't have an issue I think.

The quantity is great - since you don't need much per session, I imagine 2lb of these would last most people a month or more. In terms of value for money - it's slightly better than the typical $5/6oz ($.83/oz), being instead $25/32oz ($.78/oz), a savings of 7%.

Only improvement I can think of is to include a greater variety of vegetables in the mix.

All in all - would recommend, both if you like vegi chips or would like to try them.

title: Substantial texture, flavor like a cross between apricots and figs
text:
So I'm not a big fan of these, but it's mostly just a matter of taste. These are sweeter than the apricots I'm used to, specifically California sun-dried apricots, which tend to be tart. They are half-way between apricots and Turkish figs, in flavor. Now I don't particularly like figs, so obviously these aren't for me. But if you like figs but aren't in love with the texture, or find them a bit much, this may be a decent compromise.

Freshness and texture are both solid - nice and fibrous but not so consistent as the more traditional dried apricots can sometimes be. Two or three is sufficient for a single snack.

So I wouldn't buy them again, but would probably recommend trying once, if the above appeals to you.

title: Creamy milk chocolate with a snap
text:
After trying some of the Bouchard Belgian Dark Chocolate tablets, I wanted to try some of these for comparison. I would say they are very good, a great example of what creamy milk chocolate should be. You pay $30 for the bag, but it is 2lbs and the chocolate is first rate - so far above Hersheys that it barely qualifies as the same kind of product. They have just the right hardness to them - not too hard so as to crumble, not so soft as to be waxy. I keep the bag in the fridge and put out a handful of chocolates here and there. They are small enough that a couple are more than enough for a treat, either for breakfast, with lunch, or after dinner.

I'll probably order them again some day - these or the dark chocolate version. Would recommend.

title: Soft, chewy, substantive, great natural flavor
text:
I purchased these because they sounded tasty, and didn't have any extra sugar. They were exactly what I was looking for - a fibrous, substantive snack to have before leaving the house and after supper at night. You only need a couple to snack on, so the bag will last you a while. Makes a great complement to dried prunes or apricots - they aren't as sticky as the former nor tangy as the latter. The peach flavor is natural and thus a bit milder than some might be used to, but still very good. Price is a bit high, but probably worth it for what you get, you'd have trouble matching it without dehydrating them yourself.

I'll probably buy them again at some point. Would recommend.

title: Decent, a bit dense, might be better chopped than whole
text:
Flavor-wise, these are on point, they have a goji flavor and scent which is appealing enough. They are a little less sweet and a little more bitter than other kinds of dried berry - but not to the point they are unpleasant. I'm not a fan of the consistency, which is just a bit too dense for my liking, kind of densely chewy and fibrous.

I haven't tried yet, but these might be nice to chop up in a cuisinart and put in granola or mix with cereal, might make them a bit more consumable.

I don't intend on buying them again myself. If you want to try Goji berries, maybe start with a smaller quantity and get these if you decide you like them.

title: Natural orange flavor, but a bit sweet due to added sugar
text:
They are otherwise quite soft and moist and have a natural orange flavor about them, quite tasty. I knew these had the added sugar, before I bought them, so I'm not too surprised by that part of the flavor, and other people in the household seemed to feel like it improved the wedges, since otherwise they'd be a bit tangy. For my own part, I prefer not extra sugar added, but these are pretty tasty regardless.

Would recommend as a treat.

title: Tasty, reasonably soft dried mango
text:
These are mango strips, relative soft, and have a strong, natural mango flavor. Not quite as good as the a fresh mango but much more convenient as a snack. I purchased these because they had no added sugar, which is always my preference when it comes to dried fruit; these also lack sulfur, which makes them a little less soft than you often find in dried fruit, but they are certainly soft enough - right about at the level of dried apple slices, give or take.

Decent value, for mango anyway, I usually grab a small handful and a single bag will last me at least a week. I might not buy these very regularly, if I can get ordinary mango that is, but I will likely buy again. Would recommend.

title: Introduces some variety into the usual rotation
text:
These are interesting. They are chocolate disks with a grainy texture, given to it by the fact Taza stone-grinds their cacao beans. I rather like it - it isn't comprised of "hard" granules, its more like tiny crystals which give the whole chocolate disk a stiff, gritty bite. The flavors they include are quite good - none of them taste artificial, all of them have some complexity to to them. I rather liked the Vanilla, and the two Chili flavors also stick in mind - a bit of heat, but nothing intolerable.

The chocolate quality itself is very good - obviously so far about the usual Hershey fare that they barely occupy the same category. It's fairly dark - I like 80% plus dark myself and even will snack on baker's chocolate, so this is fine by me, but if you really stick to the milk chocolates this will be less sweet than you are used to.

All in all, would definitely recommend trying at least once, or giving to someone else to they can experience something new.

title: Worth trying, not subscribing
text:
I purchased this so my father and I could try some varieties of fish jerky. I found it to be interesting - I got out of the experience exactly what I wanted, all three jerkies had a unique character in terms of flavor and texture. A bit oily - and a bit firm - but it's not beef jerky, so some novelty is expected.

Not very much in the package. I know that premium jerkies all carry a premium price, but in this case there was maybe enough in each bag for two snacks each. If there was maybe double the jerky for the price, I'd consider it good value.

Anyway, if you want to try fish jerky, I'd recommend purchasing. Otherwise, it probably isn't worth the price.

title: Turns out this is not people-jerky
text:
I was happy to find what looked like salmon jerky-sticks for such a reasonable price, since I had never seen the like before. Unfortunately, this is for dogs and not people; fortunately I noticed this before actually eating one. Smelled delicious though.

So I gave brought them over to my buddy so his dogs could enjoy them instead, which turned out to be a good idea as one of them had just had a tooth extracted and could only have soft treats. He has two dogs, about 70lb apiece, and two sticks per dog was sufficient.

Both dogs loved them, so I suppose I have to recommend them as well.

title: Respectable prunes
text: I found these prunes to be respectable - moist, fibrous, and with no artificial sweetness. No pits, a couple pit fragments  but nothing concerning. Honestly, not distinguishable from store-bought prunes in most ways except value, you get more of these for your money than at many supermarkets. No complaints.

title: Great fruity snack for mornings and evenings
text:
I like to keep this bag on the shelf and grab a handful before I leave in the morning, and maybe before I head up for the night. They offer a diverse flavor and texture profile - soft, juicy, and maybe a bit sweet, especially the strawberries - which is a welcome break from the raisin/cranberry rotation. I like this mix of berries better than any individual ingredient by itself - dried blueberries and strawberries are a bit too sweet, dried cranberries a bit too tart, raisins a bit too familiar, but this strikes the perfect balance.

It's a bit pricey to buy all the time, but I recommend at least trying it once, and maybe adding it to your monthly grocery list.

title: Excellent biscuit cookie, for dipping or on their own
text:
I first tried digestives when I was living abroad in Ireland, and have always sought them since. While my favorites were the ones with the chocolate backing - which I recommend you try as well - these are a bit different.

Digestives are a sweet, crumbly biscuit cookie. They almost melt in the mouth, and don't survive more than two seconds when dipped in coffee or tea. They have a mildly sweet, slightly nutty flavor, something vaguely reminiscent of rose water. They are surprisingly satiating, and thus work well for a morning snack if you aren't the sort of person to do a full breakfast - two or three in the morning is enough to tide me over until lunch.

The tube size is generous, for what you get. The whole household likes them, and will grab one or two in the morning or at night. I don't know if they are actually healthier than typical cookies, but they certainly taste that way.

Would recommend - these and their chocolate-backed variants as well.

title: Delicious, crumbly biscuit cookie
text:
I first purchased digestives when I was living over seas in college - I had never had seen them before and could not believe how inexpensive they were - only 1 euro a tube, back then. When I came back to the states, I couldn't find them for years. Now I am happy to have had them again, this time the dark chocolate versions in addition to the milk chocolate - and they are just as delicious as I remember. The whole house likes them.

For the uninitiated, digestives are a sweet, crumbly biscuit cookie. They almost melt in the mouth, and don't survive more than two seconds when dipped in coffee or tea. They have a mildly sweet, slightly nutty flavor. These have a thin layer of dark chocolate, which is itself of decent quality, quite creamy. It is rare that anyone eats only one in a sitting.

I would recommend these - there are no American cookies quite like them. Get the three pack - you'll need it.

title: Just as good as I remembered
text:
I first purchased these when I was living over seas in college - I had never had digestives before and could not believe how inexpensive they were - only 1 euro a tube, back then. When I came back to the states, I couldn't find them for years. Now I am happy to have had them again, and they are just as delicious as I remember. The whole house likes them.

For the uninitiated, digestives are a sweet, crumbly biscuit cookie. They almost melt in the mouth, and don't survive more than two seconds when dipped in coffee or tea. They have a mildly sweet, slightly nutty flavor. These have a thin layer of milk chocolate, which is itself of decent quality, quite creamy. It is rare that anyone eats only one in a sitting.

I would recommend these - there are no American cookies quite like them. Get the three pack - you'll need it.

title: Decent taste, but fairly tough to eat
text:
I liked the flavor, but it was totally dominated by the seasoning/flavoring and I couldn't get much of the pork. Not unexpected, BBQ has a domineering flavor profile, but it made this particular snack sort of one-note. My main complaint though is that I found it difficult to eat, sort of hard and chewy - not the sort of thing I like in my jerky. It also came in larger sheets rather than smaller pieces, so I had to tear it up - again, not a big issue, but not as convenient as more traditional jerky.

It's the first time I've had pork jerky , so obviously it's possible that this is just how it differs from beef jerky.

So I don't think I'd recommend it, unless the above complaints don't apply to you.

title: Not very garlicy
text:
I like garlic and I like almonds, and so when I saw these were garlic almonds I was all over that. Honestly I'm disappointed. They have a garlic flavor, sure, but it isn't like a garlic bread level of garlic, more like a garlic potato chip. Still a natural garlic flavor though - and it's really tricky to get the same level of garlicness in a packaged product as you do with fresh garlic.

Nonetheless, I don't think I'll be ordering again.

title: Exactly as expected, rich and flavorful
text:
I'm really enjoying this pistachio butter. It carries a strong but not overpowering pistachio flavor, it isn't too sweet or salty, and the flavor and smell of the oil does not interfere. In consistency, it is comparable to - but thinner than - sunflower seed butter, and less grainy. In color, it is tan with that characteristic pistachio-green tint.

I have had it on its own, on bread, and in a pistachio-butter and jelly sandwich, and it is great in all three contexts. The thinner consistency means that whatever you use it in comes out less sticky than the equivalent using peanut butter, and thus a bit lighter. I haven't tried it yet, but I bet it would go well in a smoothie or shake.

It has had a warm reception from all members of the household, so it seems to be a winner. I would recommend you try it, even if only to try or mix up the breakfast rotation a little.

title: Far superior to standard dried apricots
text:
Normally, I purchase standard supermarket dried apricots, but I find them to be a bit overly sweet and of a synthetic texture. They have a dense, gel-like consistency to them. I don't dislike them per se, but they aren't like other dried fruit like prunes or apples.

These are far better. They taste like you would expect an actual dried apricot to taste, a more fibrous texture, a bit tart, but a stronger apricot flavor. Moister and less sugary than typical apricots, while still being sweet.

I obviously prefer them. However, other members of the household are divided on the matter - I would say most prefer the flavor and texture of typical dried apricots, finding them sweeter and easier to chew. Despite this, these are definitely worth a try. I would recommend them, and will probably buy more in the future.

title: Great mix of fruit bits for snacking and mixing
text:
I rather liked this mix of fruit bits, a nice change-up from the usual raisin/cranberry variety, and saves me the trouble of buying several kinds of chopped dried fruit separately. A touch bitter and a bit dense here and there, but only in comparison with raisins. Some might find it dry in comparison with some sorts of dry fruit, but not excessively so. I'd use this more for snacking than mixing with granola or cereal, myself.

A bit expensive for what you get, but otherwise would recommend.

title: Pleasant, floral herbal tea
text:
Many herbal teas have very little character, but chamomile is well-known and quite popular for a reason. It has that welcome, natural sweetness as well as a rustic odor about it which is quite pleasant. I personally have tried taking it for its putative analgesic and soporific effects but did not experience either, even at double strength.

However, it is gentle and so good for drinking at any time of the day, and a a suitable replacement for coffee and teas for those who could do without the caffeine.

Would recommend.

P.S. my steep for this is just below boiling, about five minutes.

title: Great value, satisfying flavor
text:
I purchased these because prunes are so much more expensive at my local stores. These are quite good - sweet with a strong prune-like flavor, decent fiber, texture. However, when I first opened them, I found them to be a tiny bit "dense" - but after leaving them (at room temp, in their opened, then re-sealed package) for a few days, they softened up quite nicely and resembled the prunes I get at local stores.

If it matters, these do help with maintaining regularity in a way that is more natural than taking something like psyllium fiber, so long as you have them with other food and at regular intervals.

Would recommend.

title: Great for the money, flavor is pretty good
text:
I purchased these for breakfast and late-night snacking. They are the best price/pound I could find, and both I and the rest of the household are happy with them, economically speaking.

Flavorwise, they are good, but I little synthetic. I'm not sure why - it might just be that they aren't as fresh as some other dried apricots I've had, but there is a minor bitterness to them that competes with the sweetness. I suspect most people will be perfectly happy with the flavor of these, but I will try some other brands to see how they taste in comparison.

So if you want a lot of your money, and you aren't too picky or are using these in a recipe, would recommend. Really, I'd recommend trying these at least once. If you are looking for a fresher-tasting product, you may want to look elsewhere.

title: Milder than many yellow dock teas
text:
I've found that yellow dock tea tends to fall into one of two categories - strong/sharp, and mild/smooth. This tea falls into the latter - it is a milder yellow dock which still retains the greater part of its (non-acidic) bitterness, but it has an almost creamy smoothness which blunts the effect. If you have found other yellow dock teas to be appealing but still too aggressive, this might work for you.

Recommended water temp should be just below boiling, two to four minute steep.

title: Very salty, olive oil bitterness, a bit much for me
text:
So I really enjoy the dry-cure black olives I get at the local supermarket, but they typically have pits in them. I wanted to make snacking a bit easier, so I purchased these instead. I've occasionally found pitless olives of this kind in local stores, but it is hit-or-miss and when I do find them they tend to be expensive.

I find these to be a bit intense for me. They are very salty, which is okay, but they also have olive oil bitterness to them which makes them difficult to eat just by themselves. More so than the supermarket ones, anyway.

They do make a good ingredient, though - mixing with rice or other starches, toppings on pizza, that sort of thing. So if you want these for cooking, they'll probably work really well for that. Not so much for snacking.

So would recommend as ingredient, not for eating on their own.

title: Great for late-night snack after exercise
text:
Basically, I use an intermittent-fasting type schedule, but I still like to have a bit of protein after my daily exercise, which I usually attend to at night. I find these to be perfect for this task - a half-cup provides plenty of protein, it is filling enough that I don't feel like eating anything else, and it has a pleasant, mildly-salty flavor which is appealing. I think I prefer the Nuts.com edamame, because it is a little saltier, but these are just fine.

Would recommend.

title: Tasty animal cookies reminiscent of dizzy grizzlies
text:
These are a fairly unique cookie snack, it sort of took me by surprise. A shortbread like sugar cookie coated in a firm, but not hard, icing, and little nonpareils. Not overly sweet, as you might otherwise expect, and they have a nice little bite to them. Pink frosted ones have a mild red-food-coloring bitterness to them, but it is so faint that I hardly noticed it. I purchased them for the family, and they received a warm reception from everyone.

Really good quantity for the value, I usually have four cookies per snacking session and a single bag will last me days, good value for a couple bucks. In a family situation you might get a day and a half, but still, not bad.

For those who remember Dizzy Grizzlies cookies from the early 2000's, these taste remarkably like them. While those cookies were only iced on one side, and had a denser coating of nonpareils, I could identify the similarity in flavor at once, even though it had been fifteen years since I last had the Grizzlies.

Anyway, would recommend.

title: Delicious, moist, great for snacking
text:
These are the best golden raisins I've had - they are large, moist, and have a natural fruity flavor profile. Not overly sweet, not as dry as black raisins tend to be but still with a bit of bite and texture, they are almost like cross between dried apricots and dried prunes. They even have an appealing range of hues.

Not the least expensive golden raisins you can get, even at bulk, but definitely worth the price, I'll be buying more when mine run out. Would recommend.

title: Grassy, pleasent for digestive troubles
text:
This belongs to the "grassy" class of herbal teas, but it is stronger than typical. Chickweed is said to aid digestion and this is what I found - in terms of it being a mild diuretic. Good for gently getting things moving again without throwing the rest of the system out of wack.

Maybe keep it in the cupboard for that purpose? A single teabag in 8oz is enough to give the flavor without causing any other effects. Worthy tasting, if you've never had it, but I probably won't include it in my usual lineup.

title: Honestly, I can't taste it
text:
This falls into the broad class of herbal teas that are a bit grassy but have very little character of their own. Mullein tea I found to be too mild to be worth bothering with, even when using three tea bags in my 16oz thermos and steeping them indefinitely. No notable health benefits, nor drawbacks. Maybe it would be more appealing in the traditional 6oz of water?

I'd give it a pass.

title: Decent raiseis, not very juicy
text: These are decent raisins, as black raisins go anyway. Not very juicy, and not overly sweet, a bit firm. If you want raisins to use as an ingredient, these would work well, especially in a granola or trail mix. However, if you want to eat the directly, by the handful - then I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

title: Mild, earthy a bit peppery, great compliment to an herbal tea supply
text:
This was one of the many herbal teas I've purchased over the last few years. I like the odoriferous, peppery flavor, as it added a pleasant aroma without changing the character of the tea too much. Works best in conjunction with a different herbal tea, I'd recommend something floral.

Definitely worth a try.

title: Mild, nutty cookie
text:
I purchased these mostly out of curiosity, as I heard about them online. As an American, I've never seen them on shelves, but I've had plenty of cookies like them. They are a harder cookie, suitable for dipping in coffee or tea, but a bit dry and hard to eat on their own. Mildly sweet, coconut is the dominant flavor.

If you want a pleasant, mild cookie, I'd recommend it. Otherwise, you might find it a bit underwhelming.

title: Savory, but overpriced
text:
This is a savory jerky snack, to be sure, but it is - as typical - overpriced for what you get. With standard beef jerky it makes sense, since you start with a lot of meat and end up with fairly little jerky, but this is just a plant mash. I would definitely eat this quite a bit if it was maybe half or a quarter of what they are asking.

Flavorwise, it is savory, yes, but as you might expect you get more of the seasoning and the salt than you do of any actual plant flavor. I suppose it depends on what you are looking for - if something that is just a medium to carry the spices, then have at it.

I suppose I would recommend it to try once, but not to buy regularly.

title: Decent fruit snacks, nothing special
text:
I purchased these along with about a dozen other kinds of fruit snacks, from Amazon and other retailers around where I live. The Sunkist are middle-of-the-road; consistency firm, mildly fruity, fairly distinct flavors. If you are primarily looking for the dollar value, these are a good choice - you get a lot for what you pay, and for most buyers this will keep them in gummies for a good month or two. If you are a more discerning gummy connoisseur, then they come up a bit short. My favorites are the Mott's, which are the most fruity in my opinion, but numerous smaller brands - Solely, Yum Earth, Annie's - tend to do gummies a little better in terms of natural flavoring.

So if you just want some for the kids, a good buy. Otherwise, look to other varieties.

title: Odiferous, distinct herbal tea
text:
Many herbal teas are fairly mild and grassy, but this is a welcome departure. Sarsaparilla has a flavor that can be directly compared to root beer - think a milder, much less synthetic variant, it sort of tastes like root beer smells. I noticed no health benefits of it, and the odor hangs around in cups, such that it tended to flavor the coffee I poured into the same stainless-steel Yeti cup.

I rather like it myself - it is a great alternative to the mint tea if you want to add a little variety to your rotation.

Would recommend, even if you aren't a fan of root beer itself. It's worth a try.

title: Fruity, kind of interesting
text:
These are sort of neat - they have a slightly dusty coating, and a slightly grainy texture, but their flavor is surprisingly fruity. I'm an adult male, but one or two packets is enough to snack on. They don't have that much of a synthetic sweetness to them, which is a nice surprise.

A little harder, chewier, grainier than typical fruit snacks - these are more of a candy than they tend to be. however, they aren't like jelly beans or gum drops, they are more fruity and less sugary than that.

I might not get them often, but they are definitely worth getting once, just to try them out.

title: As fruit snacks go, they are middle of the road
text:
Not too much to say about these - they compare favorably with Welch's and Sunkist, but unfavorably with Mott's. The purely berry flavoring makes each snack less distinct, so if you were actually eating them one gummy at a time instead of shoving them all in your mouth and chewing while opening a second package, then you might have trouble telling one flavor from another. Most other snacks aren't that distinct either - Mott's being the exception. I find that these have a slightly synthetic smell - and thus flavor - about them which is mildly off-putting, but only when compared with other fruit snacks. In terms of consistency they are on the firmer side, but are still easy enough to eat.

However, these are generally pretty tasty and make a good addition to breakfast or lunch.. As an adult male, I typically eat two or three packages at a time, but for kids one would probably be enough.

If all you've had are Welch's or various themed snacks, I would recommend giving these a try for some variety. For my own part, I don't think I'd get these again over any other brand of fruit snack on the market.

title: About as average as they come
text:
Typical fruit snacks in every regard; if you want the generic fruit snack experience, this is it. That's not a knock - they are solid enough fruit snacks, they have a fruity flavor, a bit of bit to the consistency but not too much, you get plenty for your money, and each pack is crammed full of them. You won't be disappointed. However, I prefer Mott's, which in my opinion are fruitier and have a softer, texture, which lets you work out more of the flavor.

These are good snacks and some will prefer them to other brands, so they are worth trying, especially for how many you get. I'd recommend comparing them to other brands to see what you prefer.

title: It grows on you
text:
I myself and a fan of yellow dock root tea. In contrast to many herbal teas, it is quite strong, something I appreciate. It is also very bitter, but it lacks the acidity that you find in more traditional teas, and so I have never had it make me nauseous. If anything, it seems to settle my stomach, after the fashion of an aperitif.

If there are any positive health benefits, I have not noted them, nor did I expect to.

I generally take water from a hot water tap, drop the tea bag right into it, and let it steep indefinitely. My sister found this to be far to bitter to stomach, so you may want to start with a shorter steep, but I think it is fine like it is. I generally use one satchet in 20z of water, so it's diluted some.

This yellow dock root tea is a little weaker than the Buddah Tea equivalent - ASIN: B00QL8EKOC - and I think I prefer that one to this one, but they aren't really all that different.

It is an acquired taste, and many will find it far too bitter to enjoy, but I would recommend trying it at least once. I plan on buying it again.

title: About average as fruit snacks go
text:
These are about equivalent with the Welch's, Sunkist, or Black Forest gummies - albeit a little larger in size, and a bit more berry-like in flavor. In terms of texture they are firm but not difficult to chew. Their smell is a bit synthetic but it was only noticeable in direct comparison with other fruit snacks. I'm not a big fan of having a large bag instead of smaller ones, but that is entirely dependent on use case - the bag closed easily enough and stayed sealed. You get a decent value for your dollar, not as good as the larger brands but still worth the money you pay, in my opinion.

These gummies are a little larger than the others, and have a slightly different flavor which is natural enough. I 'd recommend giving them at least one try, if you are the sort of person who likes fruit gummies. I don't know if they are healthy or anything, but it's nice to grab a handful for a snack now and again on your way out the door in the morning or as a bookend for lunch.

Would recommend trying at least once.

title: A higher-quality gummy snack
text:
I tried these alongside a bunch of other gummy snacks from Amazon and the local supermarkets. These are a little different - a step above the Sunkist and Welch's. They have a slightly grainier texture - not by much, just a little - which makes them a little more candy-like than traditional fruit snacks. They aren't overly sweet though - the flavor is a bit more fruity than you usually get. There are fewer per package than standard snacks, and they don't stick together since they have a slight powdery coating that prevents that . Also, they come in the form of little bunny heads, for whatever that's worth to you .

I would place them below Mott's in flavor, but above Sunkist, Welch's, and Black Forest. Kids might like the design and novelty of them, but for me not worth the tradeoff in terms of dollar value. Worth trying once, I suppose.

title: The best fruit snacks
text: I have tried numerous kinds of fruit snacks, on Amazon and in the local markets, and these are the best ones. The flavor is the best, the texture is the best, they are number one. They are more fruity than other snacks. they are more chewy - most other are a bit firm, but these you can really masticate, release that flavor. they aren't too sweet or sugary either, and each gummy has a different, distinct flavor. Will order again, and would recommend.

title: Standard fruit gummies
text:
I like fruit gummies and I've tried quiet a few of them. I would rate these about average - the are fruit, they have some bite to them so they don't get stuck to your teeth, the flavors are pretty good - if you want fruit snacks, these will hit the spot. You can hardly hope to beat the value in terms of quantity, you get plenty of snacks and they all come in one big, sturdy box.

That said, I think that I prefer the flavor and consistency of the Motts. They are the most fruity and have the nicest texture. I would buy these again on a whim, but I'd prefer the other brand if I could get it.

title: Tik-tok trends aside, they're pretty good
text:
These are surprisingly tasty, all things considered. What you have here are little plastic fruits filled with a kind of jelly - it has a consistency very similar to traditional jello (that is, not knox blox, but the original stuff). The flavor is actually fairly natural - fruity, but not too sweet. The plastic container is, sadly, inedible.

You don't get much per fruit, but you get a decent number of fruits per mesh bag. I had to clip the ends of the fruit to suck the jelly out, though apparently you can just twist the end of instead.

It's a novelty, but worth trying out I think. I wouldn't pay much more than $10 or so for a bag, and outside of the odd gift for a kid, I don't think I'll be getting it again. But glad to have bought it this once, and would recommend giving it a try.

title: Excellent snack pies
text:
I ordered these mostly to see what they were all about - Brits online said that these were far superior to the Cherry cake from the same company. While I agree - these are the better of the two - both are excellent and worth trying if you haven't already. The crust on these is crumbly and flaky, the filling is fruity and doesn't have the powerful, synthetic sugariness you find in the boxed snack cakes sold in America. Everyone I shared these with agreed on this; they are surprisingly good. I wish they sold them over here in the US, to be honest, but I plan on ordering more to give out as gifts to my siblings.

Would recommend.

title: Excellent snack tarts
text:
I purchased these after hearing from Brits about their terrible taste, I had to experience it for myself. Maybe it's just the effect of the low expectations, but I believe these are the best boxes snack cakes I've every had. They are *surprisingly* good. The crust is crumbly and soft, the filling is sweet but not overly so, it doesn't have any of that synthetic sweetness that you find in American snack cakes, it is fruity and the icing is just the right consistency, and the cherry is really like a cherry - better than maraschinos even.

Seriously, they are about as good or better than the baked tarts you get from the supermarket bakery sections around here. If you are an American and haven't had the opportunity to try them, I would definitely recommend these and the Black-current Apple variant from the same company. Will likely order again as gifts for friends.

title: A fairly sweet garlic sauce which just wasn't for me
text:
I didn't like it myself, but I suspect I really am not the target audience for this. I found it very sweet and to have very little traditional garlic flavor. I tried to spread it on some toast and I didn't like it at all. Maybe it would work as a dipping sauce for vegetables, or as an ingredient in a hot dish of some kind.

From what I understand, roasted garlic tends to become sweet, so maybe that's just what this is supposed to be. If that doesn't bother you, then this is fairly smooth, quite thick ( a little thicker than your average store-bought hummus), and there's plenty of it. If you want something to make garlic bread, this isn't it.

title: Squid-Jerky
text:
Tasty, salty, fishy - and it endures through a good chew. Basically the seafood equivalent of beef jerky, though much softer. Fairly rich, so you don't need a lot of it, my little pouch lasted about two weeks of a a pinch or two a day. I would describe the flavor as a mix a salty and sweet.

Definitely worth trying at least once, at this price. I would like to try the smoked variety next, if I can find it.

title: Not too fiberous, not too salty
text:
These are pretty good. The major thing is that they aren't as fibrous as you typically see in American-style sunflower seeds. Still a few splinters, but not many. These are also much lower salt that American's might be used to. They are still tasty, but just not that salty. Might serve you to lightly spray them with a brine solution.

I'd recommend giving them a try.

title: A tasty, salty, snack
text:
Amazon finally got me with one of its at-the-shopping-cart recommendations. These sounded interesting enough to be worth trying, I like salty things, pickled things, beans, high-protein snacks and so forth, and I hadn't tried these before, so they seemed to be worth a try. Maybe fit a similar niche to olives in my diet.

I'd say they are pretty good, but nothing to write home about. The three flavors are distinct; I wasn't a massive fan of the Chili and Lime, and the Garlic & Rosemary wasn't a strong as I would have liked, but they were all satisfactory. Texture was sold, nice little bit to them but nothing excessive. I could see myself buying a jar of these now and again.

A decent late-night snack which is milder than pickles or olives tend to be, but decently filling. I'd probably need twice the amount of beans in each package as they put in them, maybe rounding out to an even 100 on the calories would do some good. They are presently over-priced for what you get, I payed ~$24 for a pack of eight. They are worth half that, maybe. These are a four-star item at $16 for the eight-pack.

Household-wise, opinions were less favorable. The flavors are a bit strong, and you have to like the pickling flavor. If you like that sort of thing, I'd recommend you try them, get the variety pack, and don't pay more than $20 for it. If you don't like that sort of thing, then I'd give it a miss.

title: An ideal fruit bar in everything but size
text:
I really like these fruit bars, they are probably the best I've ever tried. Great, natural fruit flavor - they taste like something you would get if you dehydrated your own fruit and pressed it into a bar yourself. Nice chew to it, great bite. Each flavor of bar is distinct and tastes like should, given its constituents. The bars are moist but not sticky and smell quite natural.

I would definitely give these a five-star rating if they were maybe twice as large as they are. I have to eat at least two and sometimes three bars to be satisfied - which is nice, because you can try different flavor combination, but also means you have three times the wrapping material to contend with. I would like to see a non mini- variety of these. As they are, the price is a bit high to buy them regularly, though not to give them a try.

Anyway, I will likely purchase these again, and would recommend them to anyone looking to get away from the typical hard/sticky fruit-and-nut bars or the more artificially sweetened Nutrigrain offerings. These are the real deal.

title: Tasty, tangy fruit stix
text:
These are a nice little snack. The packages are a little small for your average adult, I think, but probably good for kids. They come in little rectangular rods, about 1" x 1/2" x 1/4", about 12 to a bag. Even consistency, a gummy with bite to it, think fruit leather but without bit of fiber and the like. Tasty - and tangy. All three flavors were quite good - not only were they distinct, but they tasted fruity as well.

Not particularly filling, as a adult male I found I needed at least two packs to feel like I had snacked sufficiently, but a nice bit of variety. I don't' think I'd buy them again, but they're worth trying at least once. By comparison, I preferred the That's It! Mini fruit bars (ASIN: B07YTJFLGT), as they had more fiber and texture to them, but that is mostly due to personal preference.

However, if you haven't tried these yet, I'd say give them a go.

title: More of a strawberry candy than a strawberry minit
text:
I purchased these, the wintergreen, and peppermint flavors to try alongside each other. All use the cooling sugar as their sweetener, but these strawberry mints are really mints in name alone. They aren't bad though - I wouldn't mind seeing more candy like this, fruit flavored tablets I mean. But this particular flavor is very synthetic and quite pungent, I can easily smell it from outside the tin. I found it to be a bit too synthetic for my own tastes, so I'm giving away the rest of the tins from my box to family and friends.

If you want to try some, maybe pick up a single tin from a local store before committing to the whole box. Even if you like the other Altoid Arctic mints, these may not be for you.

title: Not really much of a fan
text:
I mean, they are okay. The 3D-shape is a novel one and the colors are quite good, but in terms of flavor and texture they aren't for me. Flavor-wise they have a fairly synthetic sweetness and a floral scent, they aren't particularly fruity at all. Texture-wise, they have quite a bit of bite to them and are quite chewy, but are also quite solid - they don't stick to your teeth, for example, but cleave into little chunks. They are much closer to a stiffer gummy bear than, say, packaged fruit snacks like Motts.

Unless you are hosting a party and want to give out neat-looking gummies, I would not recommend them. .

title: Fairly good, wholesome cereal, if a bit hard
text:
Best way of describing this is that it tastes exactly like you would expect. Whole, grainy, earthy, with plenty of fiber. Very mild sweetness, on par with wheat germ. Goes well with milk or without. I've gone through two boxes of the four I bought and am looking forward the the remaining two.

It is fairly hard, though, harder than most bran flakes. When eating it without milk, after a few handfuls my jaw was getting tired. With milk, it isn't quite as nice as standard bran flakes, due to the thickness of each flake, but it's a bit tastier.

Anyway, if you like bran flakes and that sort of healthful cereal, I'd recommend it.

title: An alternative to potato chips with some variety of flavoring
text:
I saw these on a British television show and wanted to try them for myself, and as they are not sold in America, I bought them here instead. Monster Munch is a neat snack - in texture they are sort of Funyun-like, a puffed corn snacks. Flavor-wise, the "Roast Beef" was of greatest interest to me, and I would say it tastes like packaged brown gravy or the "Roast Beef" Ramen seasoning. "Pickled Onion" is pretty much a milder form salt and vinegar. "Flamin' Hot" tastes like hot sauce with exactly all of the spiciness taken away.

The individual packages are - apparently - child-sized and so I needed two or three to accompany a meal, so the value isn't really there in terms of making this a regular purchase. However, if you have never tried it, I'd recommend giving it a go.

title: Malty ketchup
text:
As an American I have heard, now and again, of brown sauce through television and other media, and so I wanted to give it a taste. It is quite good! I like malt flavoring but malt vinegar makes things soggy, but this has no such an effect. I would describe the flavor a ketchup-iike, but malty and with a somewhat greater complexity. It tends to dominate whatever you put it on, so best for blander things like chicken, potatoes, and milder sorts of fried fish.

If you haven't tried brown sauce, I would recommend giving a go, it adds variety outside the typical ketchup/mustard/mayo/BBQ that you find in most households.

title: Delicious for snacking or mixing
text:
I have used this mostly for snacking - a nice heaping spoonful now and again for a treat - and as an additive to my soylent and protein shakes. I recommend it for both - especially snacking. It is a fairly fatty powder, as you might expect - dry, yes, but fatty, so you need to mix it very thoroughly in shakes, and clean whatever you used fairly well. However, it has a rich, authentic coconut flavor, not synthetic or artificial in the least.

Haven't tried it in baking yet, but looking forward to doing so.

Would recommend.

title: Tasty to snack on right out of the jar
text:
I'm an American, and have never encountered onions like this before. However, I heard tell of onions, a long time ago, that were so sweet you could eat them raw right out of the ground. So I've been looking for something like that ever since. These aren't quite that good - but you can eat them right out of the jar as a snack, so we are half-way there. The taste is "mildly oniony" - almost like a authentic version of how funions smell. Not acrid at all, and there were no tears, and no comments on onion breath after the fact. The liquid appears to be some sort of brine, I haven't tasted it directly yet.

I don't think I'd buy this regularly, but I would put these in the same category as pickles - a nice snack that you might eat straight, but would probably instead add as an ingredient to other dishes to enhance the range of flavors.. Maybe worth halving, battering, and frying, who knows.

Would recommend trying at least once.

title: So-so oat bars for a snack now and then
text:
There are okay, so far as oat bars go. Somewhat chewy, a little less so than your average Clif bar, but with a similar sweetness profile. They have a texture slightly reminiscent of rice crispy bars, a really dense one. More sweet than oaty, but the chocolate is okay. If you want a fairly generic snack-type oat bar that isn't quite as overbearing as the supermarket brands, this isn't a bad way to go.

If you want a real, substantial oat bar, go for Bobo's (ASIN: B015TLG85A). I've tried a few different ones over the last few months, and those seem to be the best. Rather mild flavor, relatively speaking, but probably twice as dense as these, with more substance to them.

title: Excellent breakfast bars
text:
These are the real deal, so far as oat bars go. I've tried several breakfast-type bars, protein bars, energy bars, and these are top-tier. They're large, fairly substantial, brick-like things that are more than enough to serve as a filling breakfast. Not too much sugar or sweetness, they have a very agreeable texture which isn't too crumbly or hard or chewy, very nice all around.

The flavor - I would say - is fairly mild. I regard this as being a good thing, especially compared to its sweet, salty, competitors. If I were to draw a comparison, consider the difference between natural peanut butter and something like Jif.. They both have their merits, but the natural stuff has a bit more substance to it, even if it is less salty and sweet.

Anyway, I'd recommend them. Not really a snack bar, nor a treat, much more like a breakfast bar that will leave you fairly full for a couple hours.

title: Good for cooking, not for seasoning
text:
These MSG crystals are fairly large - in the >1mm range - so they don't really dissolve well on cooked food. Great for cooking, and probably okay in hot soups/stews/sauces too, but if you want to use it like salt, then you are better off going with Accent or something similar, MSG in fine powdered form.

This stuff is okay in limited amounts, but treat it like salt or oil, use in moderation.

title: Lots o' Pez
text: It's a big bag of Pez, just like you'd expect. If you are an adult, you have an abundance of Pez you can snack on, I'd each two or three packs in a go. However, this is really great for kids, because it's probably more Pez than they've ever seen in one place. Like a pound of Pez is a lot for an adult, but for an eight year-old it's a bag bigger than their head. Gets a great response.

title: Eh, they're okay for a treat
text:
So they are okay, so far as snacky oatmeal bars go. While not as sugary as many supermarket brands, they have that kind of sweetness you often find in protein bars, which I personally don't find to be all that palatable.
