Texture is nice - they are soft, and crumble a bit but not tremendously. They aren't particularly chewy or sticky, so I like that part, very easy to eat. A kid will probably mash it up though, since it doesn't really keep its shape.

I ordered these maybe two months ago, and I still have about half in my cabinet, so I'm not exactly overeager to chow down on them. This seems to be the opinion of the rest of the household - if something good comes along, it usually is gone within a week. If you want a good oatmeal bar, I recommend Bobos - the Coconut Almond Chocolate Chip. There's a lot there, but it really feels like a substantial bar. These, in contrast, are more like a sweet snack than something I'd eat as breakfast.

title: Decent as fruit snacks go - though a bit sour
text:
These are decent fruit snacks. Not quite as good as the Motts, which have a very natural fruit flavor to them, these are more in the candy domain. Texture is quite nice - not too chewy, not too hard. You don't get many in a single package, I'd say maybe seven gummies or so, but they are largish in size. As an adult male, I liked to have two or three packages in a sitting.

The gel inside is slightly sour, reminiscent of Gushers.

I don't think I'll order these again, but I'd recommend giving them at least one try, it's worth the $6.

title: Bitter, but it grows on you
text:
The flavor of this herbal tea is particularly strong, especially if you steep it for 10m+. It is quite bitter, though not to a degree that it provokes nausea, it's a different sort of bitter. Rather unpleasant to drink to be honest, but I found it quickly grow on me over time such that now it is one of the teas I look forward to the most. Many herbals are very mild unless you use two or three teabags in a standard 16oz thermos, but not this one. It has a pleasant odor which offers a preview of the taste.

The color when ready is yellow, after the fashion of dandelions, though clear of course.

I would recommend at least giving it a try, it's interesting enough for that.

title: Great herbal tea with distinctive flavor
text: This is one of my favorite herbal teas. It isn't acidic, it isn't too strong but it is very flavorful. I would say that the taste reminds me a great deal of roasted peanuts - or just the "roasted" flavor. I haven't noticed any other effects of drinking it, it isn't particularly calming or good for digestion, it's just a nice drink to enjoy.

title: Decent dry-roasted hazelnuts
text:
As dry-roasted hazelnuts go, these are average. Average in a good way - a little better than you would find in most nut-mixes. I like how they get away from the oiliness of other preparation techniques, but unfortunately these aren't as salty as I typically like in my nuts - I'd prefer they were more like dry-roasted peanuts in terms of salinity. I also like my skins on my hazelnuts, but that is difficult to manage. \

Normally I'd give these three stars, but I think as hazelnuts go they deserve a solid four; good quality, decent price, well within expectations. Consistent quality throughout the bag. Would recommend for hazel-nut lovers and use in recipes - for snacking, look for something a little less healthy.

title: Decently tasty fruit rolls
text:
So they are fruit rolls - pretty good in terms of flavor, nice chewy texture. Better than Fruit By The Foot, which to me (an adult) tastes off if you have more than two or three rolls at once. I usually have a couple of these for a snack with my lunch.

Value-wise, you can hardly match it, naturally - not at your typical supermarket, anyway. I would definitely recommend picking up a box if you want something fruity to complement your usual fare or you have kids who you'd like to have a marginally healthy treat.

title: Sour, but a little insubstantial
text:
If you really want a candy that is very sour but not much else, this is a good choice. It doesn't have a lot of substance to it - compared to sour patch kids, for example, you taste very little gummy while eating one. This isn't necessarily good or bad - it just depends on what you are looking for. The hollow structure of the straw means that it isn't as chewy as other sour gummies.

Grape flavor is so-so. Nothing overly remarkable. I would really prefer a multi-flavor pack, rather than six grape.

Worth a try, but try to find a single package before going for the six pack. Personally, I'm not a fan though.

title: Passable fruit leather
text:
I've had fruit leather from many different makers, most of them very small-scale, private enterprises. They tend to be more fibrous, thinner, a little tougher, but also more flavorful. These Stretch Island snacks are okay; identifiable as fruit leather but nothing remarkable. Definitely has a natural taste - they aren't synthetic in the slightest - but they could be improved by making them more distinct, I found all the flavors to be quite similar to one another. Not all that filling. Might be good for kids, though - for adults, it's barely a mouthful and then its gone.

Worth trying out once, but I doubt I'll order any more of them.

title: A superabundance of gummy snacks
text:
Great deal, in terms of gummy snacks - a whole eighty packages for a mere $12 or so. You can't touch that with supermarket prices, you can't even get close. I bought this because everyone in the family devours the fruit snacks the moment I bring them home: not this time - this sucker has so many fruit snacks that they had to make it out of a heavier gauge cardboard. It's serious business.

Flavor-wise, Welch's is up there with Motts and the like. Good taste - fruity, not too sweet, soft consistency, easy to devour in a single handful. I usually bring a couple to work for a snack, good stuff. I'd recommend it for just about everyone.

They aren't premium top-shelf fruit snacks, but they are certainly good enough. Would recommend for high volume households.

title: Great to give as a formal gift
text:
I have given this twice for a gift and each time the recipient was quite happy with it. The chocolate is of a good grade and each truffle is relatively large and has a different flavor profile. The presentation is top notch - the box is well proportioned, thoughtfully designed and made of quality materials, the decoration on the truffles is really pleasing to the eye - it is a visually impressive gift.

If it is value in terms of chocolate by weight, this isn't the best choice of course. You can get more chocolates of the same quality for a lower price elsewhere. However, if you want a classy gift to send out for a birthday, anniversary, congratulations, I would recommend it. For example, I sent it to my Grandma as a thinking-of-you sort of thing, and to my friend as congratulations on their new baby. It isn't too much chocolate or too little, it's just fancy enough to elevate itself over standard supermarket box chocolates without getting pretentious.

title: Good source of coconut oil
text: I've ordered these a few times. Excellent for long-term energy while hiking or working long hours. You can swallow them whole or chew for a nice, very mildly sweet coconut flavor. I've purchased them about six times now and will probably continue to do so.

text: A nice, cool sweetener, gives mints and baked goods a refreshing, chilly mouthfeel. Neat.

title: An interesting novelty, but not much more than that
text:
They're alright. Crispy, flavorful, but not worth the price by any margin. I originally purchased them to grind up for the purpose of making homemade pixies stix. They served this purpose well enough, though there are alternate flavoring options which work better (the freeze-dried powder tends to absorb moisture and clump).

I would recommend trying them once, if your are interested in a somewhat novel flavor and texture, but not something I would buy again.

title: Delicate, mild spiciness in the aftertaste
text: I tested about twelve different honeys when making mead, and this was in my top three. Very light flavor, and when consumed alone, has a very mild spiciness about it. Good for fruit, cheese, biscuits, not too overt. I would recommend it.

title: Interesting, mildly waxy flavor (in a good way)
text: When making mead I tested about a dozen honeys, and avocado was an interesting one. Sort of waxy, an interesting complexity to it when consumed by itself. I gave a couple jars away this last Holiday season and people seemed to like it. Winter Park's variety is good - I recommend it.

title: Interesting, subtle notes
text: While making mead I tested a wide diversity of honeys - twelve in all - and sage honey was by my favorite. This has a very interesting character to it, either eaten raw or paired with cheeses or toast, it really is an interesting, subtle flavor. I even gave some away this last Christmas. This particular variety is very good; I would purchase it again, and recommend it to others.

title: Not like the old formula, disappointed.
text:
I have used this product for many years, and though expensive, I liked that it had no added maltodextrin, was easy to use, and had no aftertaste.
When I ran out of my last order I went back to the company I usually use to purchase this and they were out of business.
Amazon was the only place I could find the product with the Covid19 buying shortages.
The new Fiberfit product is supposed to be 2x the fiber and twice as sweet. It was a bit thicker than the old formula, I compared them side by side. But, if anything, the fiber cuts the sweetness. I found I had to use twice the quantity to get about the same sweetness of the old formula. Problem is, this "new" formula is sold in bottles HALF the size as the old bottle and more expensive. What a waste of money! I spent over $160 on 9 little bottles that I will go thru quickly. I hope Fiberfit is ready my review because I hope they will consider going back to the older, sweeter formula. Like they say, " If it aint broke..."

Just keep in mind that the number of blueberries they associate with a serving size is assuming the small size of wild blueberries, not the larger size berries we see at the market.

I started adding this to a mix of vitamin C and electrolytes I drink in the morning and it makes for a nice blueberry lemonade flavor. It mixes in fairly well, maybe with a bit of clumpiness at times (especially after a while when it probably starts to pick up some moisture from the environment as it sits on my shelf), but not too bad, and that is just stirring, not blending for a smoothie which would probably mix just fine. It does come with a dessicant packet inside. It also comes in a handy resealable "ziplock" style bag and it helps to make sure the bag is sealed tightly between uses, so make sure to get it out with a spoon -- if you pour it out of the bag it may cake onto the zipper part of the bag and prevent the bag from sealing properly.

I noticed some complaints about freshness, but I haven't had any issues. The last bag I bought had around 1.5 years remaining on its "best buy" date and seemed totally fresh to me. The first bag I bought I tasted the powder straight when I first got it, and it had a nice flavor, not stale or rancid at all. title: Seems like a decent sweetener
text:
This is the first allulose I've tried so I'm not sure if these comments are specific to this brand or allulose in general. The first thing I noticed is that when I opened the bag and smelled the contents, it had a very slight funky smell to it, I know this sounds bad, but it didn't really translate to the taste, fortunately. However, allulose is supposed to not be bitter, and when I tasted it straight I did notice a very minor bitter/odd aftertaste. My bitter sensitivity seems to be relatively high so maybe most people don't notice this. Once I started mixing it into things (mainly hot beverages like tea and coffee), I didn't notice any bitterness or aftertaste, so it really isn't a major problem. My only other criticism is it seems a bit more like a powder, than like crystalized table sugar. Not sure if the crystals are just too small or what is causing that perception.

It is supposed to be about 70% the sweetness of sugar, and it seems less than that to me. I feel like I have to use a large amount before I notice a significant sweetness effect, and I find it hard to gauge how much to use.
However, I haven't used table sugar in a long time, and I didn't do any direct measurements or comparisons, so I cannot say for sure how sweet it really is. For all I know, this could be a misconception on my part.

All in all, I can recommend allulose as a fairly good sugar substitute, at least for tea and coffee. It doesn't seem to impact the flavor of the drink and can add noticeable sweetness while supposedly not having any impact on blood sugar (and apparently some studies found it might even help the body process other carbohydrates better, in terms of blood sugar impact). I still like to use yacon syrup in some cases, where I want that added flavor it has, but when I want a flavorless sweetener I think I'll be using allulose.

It sat on my shelf for a few weeks while I finished up a Twinings US box, so I've been drinking it for maybe a week or 2 now. I definitely like it better than the US. version of this tea but I can't quite put my finger on what it is. Some reviews say they think it is stronger, which may be true, but Twinings (US) and other brands have extra strong bergamot versions of their Earl Grey and they still aren't as good as this one. The US and UK ones both list bergamot and natural flavors in their ingredients (without specifics on what those natural flavors are). The UK one also lists lemon, maybe that makes the difference, or maybe it is just the specific formula of natural flavors that they use for the UK version.

The bulk packaging inside a single foil bag is perhaps a bit less convenient (I just put it inside a ziplock for freshness), but it is better for the environment so I don't have a big issue with that. The re-closeable outer box (with little paper catches to hold it in place) has worked well for me so far. Easy to open, easy to close, and stays closed.

The only thing they could perhaps make better would be to use some kind of resealable bag instead of the basic foil bag, so I don't have to use one of my own (if you open it carefully a clip may also work. mine ripped a bit when opening so I can't really clip it until I use up more of the bags to get more slack).

title: Love these

They can go on just about anything that works well with crunch, I typically put them on veggies, salads, and pasta dishes (after cooking so they don't lose crunch spending time in the sauce).  They are definitely pricey, but I view them as somewhat of a "gourmet" product, so I don't necessarily feel they are overpriced.

My only con is that I prefer things that are naturally fermented without added vinegar, but those types of pickles are usually more expensive, harder to find, and typically require refrigeration making them less convenient to buy online.  Whereas these are easy/convenient to purchase, store in the pantry, etc.  They are fairly inexpensive, but the small amount per pack has to also be taken into consideration.  However, the price seems competitive for this type of product.

title: Easy to use

A box is obviously better for dealing with smells.  However, it is pricier and probably less environmentally friendly due to the packaging, so I have to take off a star for that.

text: I really like their plain garlic nuggets, which I rate at 5 stars.  Perhaps that is part of the problem.  I feel the ratio is off here, there is too much of the herbs and not enough of the nuggets.  The herbs have a slight bitterness, but also it just isn't enough garlic flavor and crunch.  Overall I prefer to use the plain garlic nuggets and add in my own seasonings to taste.  I tried this once but I'll probably stick to the plain ones from now on.

title: Tasty but expensive
text:
I really like these olives but prices have skyrocketed over the last 10 years or so. I used to buy them in bulk for around $7.00 per bag from the seller's main web site. I also don't like the fact that the seller, Natural Zing, charges more here than on their main website, and as far as I can tell does not sell the bulk boxes here (which qualifies for free shipping on their main website, so they maybe could make those qualify for "prime shipping" here). So we pay more per bag and pay extra in shipping. E.g. if I had an Amazon gift certificate and wanted to buy these here I'd have to pay more. I rarely buy them now anyway, as I'm just not sure they are worth this price... maybe occasionally as a special treat, e.g. if they have a sale going or something.

Flavor-wise they are a bit bitter and salty, but otherwise very tasty and make a great snack. Maybe there is a bit of an acquired taste, like coffee, which could account for the mixed reactions on taste, not sure. I keep the bags in the fridge after opening and they get chewy when chilled, which I also like.

title: My favorite yacon so far
text: I've tried a few brands of yacon and so far I like this one the best.  It seems to be "less processed" to me, in the sense that it is less sweet and has fuller flavor.  Some people may want sweeter and less flavorful to come closer to being just a pure sugar, but to me the highly concentrated sweetness makes me question the health benefits.  To me this is more of a "food" that has some sweetness rather than a pure sweetener like most of us are used to. Many of the popular brands I've tried were thinner and sweeter.  My best guess would be that this brand is closer to how it was processed and consumed prior to it becoming popular, whereas those other companies are processing it differently (refining it longer?) to make it appeal to a wider audience.  Note that in general yacon is not a true sugar substitute since it has a slight molasses-like flavor (though to me it is much less bitter and burnt-flavored than molasses, and I have strong bitter receptors so I cannot tolerate a lot of bitterness, e.g. I can't really eat/drink stevia unless it is very dilute).  Although I would think that yacon might work well in certain flavors of baked goods (I don't bake with it), it is generally not a sugar substitute.  I think some people who don't like yacon are expecting a flavorless sweetener (that is also miraculously healthy for them).  Also be careful when reading the nutritional info on the various brands because many use significantly different serving sizes so you have to do the math, you cannot just directly compare the quantities of nutrients.

title: Tasty and fun to eat

I like the consistency when biting into them -- a bit of crunch but with some give, the outer skin has a chewiness that appeals to me as well. I think some people who don't like them may be expecting a dry snack. These are slightly moist and fermented, which makes them sour (the chili flavor tastes a bit like pepper jack cheese to me, that's my favorite flavor). People looking for something similar to a potato chip may not find what they are looking for in these. But with these you don't have to worry about eating fry grease or accidentally over doing it and eating too many calories (since they have so few calories it doesn't really matter how many you eat). The main down-side is that they have to be refrigerated after opening, which reduces versatility. At work to avoid having to use the communal fridge I just pack a day's worth to have at my desk and don't leave any leftovers overnight.

In addition to eating them straight out of the bag, these work well on salads, on top of cooked veggies/grains, etc. If you put them on some hot food (after cooking) and they warm up a little bit, they still work well. It is a decent way to quickly add some interesting flavors protein to a dish.

title: This yeast does not like to be handled too much
text: Okay...........I've got to come back and redo this review.  I've been making bread regularly (from scratch) and thought this would be a good investment. The first 2 times using this yeast, my bread turned into a big solid lump..no rise.  Tried twice and same result.  I've read through the comments to see if there was any advice to help the dough to rise. I'm definitely not new to making bread (regular loaf of bread).  Soooo.........I tried something.  I kept the water only lukewarm, whipped in my 2 eggs (I like to add eggs to my bread), and started adding my flour.  I DID NOT work the dough very much.  I mean, I punched it down and kneaded it for less than 2 minutes.  Maybe even for just 1 minute.  I stuck in in my oiled loaf pan and put it in the oven at 200 degrees for 30 minutes to rise.  Then, I turned up the heat to 350 and cooked it for 35 minutes.  Turned out great!  I've done this twice now and this is what finally worked for me.

title: 4-6 cups of green tea a day---good for your heart
text: For years and years, health care fads come and go.  We are told to eat this and that and we will live better, or told it's products are AMAZING!!! Well........the one product that continually gets rave reviews again and again is green tea.  So I decided to drink at least 4-6 cups of green tea a day.  it's antioxident properties are amazing.  Research again and again shows that it helps in the prevention of cardiovascular (heart) disease.  It eliminates free radicals in the blood stream that put you at risk for many different diseases. Now, I'm' not a health nut but I do value my health.  I try to eat well 80% of the time and I exercise regularly and try to watch my stress.  But this tea has been an added to my menu and I abslutely LOVE it.  I have tried so many different green teas that I can't even begin to count the number and names. Good Earth always makes an amazing product in quality.  This tea is no exception.  I feel it has a slight tint of sweetness because of the lemongrass and it's not as bitter.  It's very smooth for a green tea.  It is light and refreshing and I feel reenergized.  I boil 6-8 cups of water on the stove every day in a pan and add 4-6 bags of this tea.  I let the tea bags sit in the water and steep for about 20 minutes.  This is what allows the valuable products of the green tea to be absorbed into the water. I may drink a cup of warm tea and that point, but I refrigerate the rest.  I put it in a couple of containers, let it cool on the counter and then put it in the fridge.  When I'm ready to drink it, I may add a little coffee creamer or splenda.  YUM!  It has become my new morning coffee.  I absolutely LOVE this tea.  Thank you, Good Earth.

text:

Anthony's Millet is hulled, organic and in a resealable bag! There are no cooking instructions on the bag. Millet is 1 cup millet to 2 cups water or broth, bring to boil then reduce and simmer 15-20 minutes. I use my rice cooker on the white rice setting which is 15 minutes. There are many uses for this ancient grain from breakfast ( made with brown sugar and butter and maple syrup, add some fruit) to lunch (saute some veggies and eat hot or chilled) dinner--add some blackened tuna or chicken with veggies and drizzle with oil . YUM.

My toddler (18 months) also likes millet. I scoop some out and let it cool, I then roll it into small balls and toss with mixed veggies. He can pick them up and eat them ( they look like a mini meatballs). This is a great addition to his nutrition. Fiber and protein. Millet also contains iron!

Use this grain and swap out quinoa with it, it can be used almost the same. Use chicken stock for even more flavor when cooking. I received this Millet discounted in exchange for my honest review. I love it, as does my family. It is easy to cook, it is healthy and it last a long time.

text: Everything about the marketing, and bags per box looked great at first. Until you realize each bag barely have tea on them. You will need 2 bags to get any flavor out of these. As commented by another reviewer, is like sipping hot water. My quest to find a good and honest tea supplier continues.

title: Going back to originals
text: Stale coffee

title: Inoffensive
text:
I’ve no evidence that it helps one get to sleep. However, expecting dried leaves to help one get to sleep when there is a pandemic raging is perhaps asking too much of Mother Nature.

“You can’t worry about things beyond your control.”
“Um, who is such a fool that they’d worry about things they can control? Control the things you can control! Worry is for the rest.”

And so, there it is. It’s inoffensive. A little callous. Calming, without actually being relaxing. I will never use it all.

title: Weird.
text: This is the oddest Earl Grey tea, ever.  Not actually bad, but by no means good.  It doesn’t so much have flavor as it has ethos.  Perhaps I am not quite English enough—not sufficiently morally affronted by flavour—to properly appreciate this particular brew.

title: Awesome!!
text: The very best soft pretzels ever!  A nice bite to the exterior and perfectly soft inside. Delicious!  And a great company, too—we had a shipping flub that wasn’t even their fault, but they made everything good anyway! Can’t recommend highly enough! Will definitely be a regular customer!

title: Second review, equally perfect product.
text: Delicious, as previously reviewed

title: My go-to comfort food.
text: Nothing better in this world than Nabisco premium saltines for a comfort food for me. So, so much better than the heavy baking-soda taste of other brands. Melt-in-you-mouth delicious! Try them crumbled into a glass of cold milk, too!

title: Delicious and Packed Well
text: Love these candies, and you should try them!

title: Delicious and a Great Price
text: So much better than the more-popular Spearmint! Delicious and refreshing.

title: Tea Needs to be Steeped, People
text: Meh, it was ok, but tea needs to be steeped in boiling water for at least three minutes in order to deliver the flavour notes and health benefits. You should never make tea in a Keurig, and I should have known better.

title: My Mother-in-Law Loves It
text: What can I say? I hate coffee, but my mother-in-law (or, as we used to call her before gay marriage was legalized, my "mother-out-law") loves it, and genuinely appreciates the Keurig convenience, given that she's the only coffee drinker in our home when she visits for Xmas.

title: Childhood Favourite
text: So delicious, and so much better--and, as candy goes, healthier--than the sugar free kind. Everybody loves these, even my hubby who hates watermelon. Very nice, and a good price.

title: Love these
text: A co-worker and friend from work introduced me these, and they are delicious. I find the history of them to be a little absurd (it's on the package). The idea that Japanese culture is too prissy to allow removing a chewed piece of gum from the mouth, but they're completely au fait about smacking your lips while you chew candy "like a cow chewing it's cud" is nothing short of laughable. That notwithstanding, it's a great candy, and a satisfying chew. I'm not a big fan of the grape flavour--too much Dimetapp Elixir decongestant as a child--but those who like that flavour say these are very nice. The mango are fantastic, the green apple and strawberry are great.

title: Best All-Year Candy
text: Nothing short of my favourite all-year candy. These were fresh and uniform in shape and flavour. Very nice for when the Necco company decided to jack its delivery fees through the roof.

title: Reviewed Elsewhere... This is the Best
text: Sleepytime tea is absolutely the best tea for relaxing or falling asleep for the night. Nothing better is available, including straight chamomile.

title: Best Tea for Relaxation
text: This is the best tea, bar none, for relaxation, and I am so happy to find it available for the Keurig device that my consumerist lifestyle requires I use. Truly aromatic and delicious, and far more efficacious than chamomile tea alone.

title: Interesting, nice, but strong
text: I have gradually come to find that my appreciation of Twining's green tea is diminishing. It has a good flavour--but other traditional green teas have a better traditional Japanese taste--but it has a strong, sometimes unpleasant, aftertaste, and a strong stomach sensation that leaves me feeling somewhat nauseated.

title: An Xmas Tradition
text: Although I am disappointed in the size of this tin--as recently as last year, I was able to get King Leo in a full two-pound red and silver tin, so this year, I had to buy two, at a higher expense--this candy will always remain am Xmas tradition in my workplace. We all love it, and it's simply the best. We recommend the sticks (this product) over the King Leo mints; there seems to be a subtle difference in overall flavour and texture, and this is nicer.

title: The Perfect Candy
text: It's as delicious as ever. It's as expensive as ever. Deal with it; it's worth it, and (probably...) so are you.

title: Incredible Seller
text: I can't say enough about these candies or the amazing seller that is making them available. Made in Britain, Ltd., and its owner, Mr. Sedan, provide a great selection of great goods at great prices, considering they're all imported from the UK. I not be more pleased.

title: Incomparably Delicious
text:
When I was very young, this was a candy which I could find in my grandmother's crystal candy dish, regardless of the time of year. Their smell and taste is an amazing memory trigger, taking me back to days of fresh cinnamon toast and a stereo phonograph player in a five foot by two by two foot console. These are perfection. You'll find imitations all over the place--AVOID AVOID AVOID. Spend a little more (not a lot more) and stick to the original Necco deliciousness.

One recommendation: If you're not a 9 year old child with a sweet tooth, you probably won't go through 84 ounces of sugary goodness before the candy's natural hydrophilic quality will have overpowered the original packaging, turning some of the candies into jawbreakers. Fear Not! Open the original packaging and store in a vacuum-popped tupperware container (or vacuum-sealed bag, if you've one of those contraptions) and all will be perfect.

title: Better than the Original?
text:
Truthfully, who can remember what the original M&M/Mars Marathon Bars tasted like--other than the universally accepted, "They were just amazing!" They were. Here in my native Southern California, they were also 15 inches long, not merely 8 inches as was sold throughout the rest of the United States.

Today, while M&M/Mars continues to ignore requests from their customers to bring the Marathon bar back to market--it's probably just as well, as they would undoubtedly replace sugar with revolting and dangerous high fructose corn syrup--Cadbury in the UK continues to manufacture the original Curly Wurly bars, which are at least as good as the original American candy. Deliciously, the Curly Wurly doesn't taste like so much of the rest of Cadbury's chocolate.

Additionally, considering that American candy bars are close to $1.00/ea in local stores now, this is one of the best bargains in candy today.

So yummy!

title: It's the Economy, Stupid
text: While the flavour of this green tea was enjoyable (as either hot or iced tea), its recent price increase is certainly not. Paying 74% more for this tea than one pays Amazon for the equivalent number of servings of Bigelow or Twinings green tea ($39.95 US vs $23.00 US) or 83 cents/cup rather than 48 cents/cup is not justified by the product's quality, perceived taste, or manufacturer reputation. I would not purchase this product again at its current price-point. Additionally, it appears the current retailer no longer supports the convenient Subscribe-and-Save option.

title: Great tea!
text: Fantastic taste. Will buy again.

title: Yummy and plentiful!
text: Super yummy! Everyone I shared with loved them. Will definitely order from this company again.

title: Net cost is more than Trivia packets
text:
I bought this thinking the product in the packets were the same size as Truvia or other Stevia packets. At a couple dollars less than Truvia I thought it would be a long term cost savings.
As it turns out, you get about half as much. 500 packets of Truvia weigh 2.2 pounds. 500 of these weigh 1.1 pounds. What I thought was saving a few dollars was actually costing almost double compared to Truvia packets.
This was an extremely disappointing purchase.

title: Good decaf tea
text: This is a good tasting tea but it sometimes arrives with the box crushed from shipping. These are large tea bags with no string or tag.

title: Tasty!
text: I really love this soup. It's flavorful and enough for two. Lots of artichoke flavor.

title: Grat price
text: The eggs are on the small size, but I prefer that. Two are perfect with toast and for a light meal. The price is great for 18 organic eggs.

title: NO!
text:
I bought a case of these and really regret it. They are hard but not crunchy and although there are a few halopenos included there is no heat and a really bland flavor. I had bought Embasa brand carrots before and really liked them. Unfortunately they are difficult to find.
Donating the La Costena to the food bank.

title: meh...
text:
I like the bread because it's a good size for sandwiches but unfortunately it's not very flavorful. Toasted and buttered, it comes up really bland.
I was buying TJ's gluten free bread which has a great flavor but the loafs are very small. I'd rather have the flavor than the larger size.

title: Kiitchen Basics has changed!
text: Years ago Kitchen Basic stock and broths had a litany of "Oh, no", ingredients. Thankfully, that has significantly changed. This is a great stock that is really dense and flavorful. It's organic, and there are still just a couple of "natural flavor" mystery ingredients, but for the most part it's really great.

title: Wonderful!
text: Great flavor and better since they started adding more spices. Mild hit of chili heat and totally addicting. Pricey, but it's a large bag.

title: Unadulterated...
text: Really nice flavorful almond milk without all the funky additives you find in most nut milks. That costs you more, but it's worth it.

title: Wonderful!
text:
I looked all over the web for cinnamon mints and found that most lack one thing; Cinnamon! 90% of the mints out there use chemicals to mimic the cinnamon flavor.
These mints by 365 are made with real cinnamon and they have a strong, delightful flavor. They are also reasonably priced.
Try some!

title: Great!
text: A very dense, flavorful soup. My partner loves it. I go for the chili with beef flavor. Both are excellent! 24 oz goes a long way...

title: Terrific for quick meal prep!
text:
I've used this for years and used to have to order it from the product site and pay shipping, so I'm really glad it's now available from Amazon. When I don't have time to chop garlic or don't have it on hand, this is a super substitute. It's great in a quick meatloaf along with dried onion and other dried herbs (I also add basil, marjoram and and oregano).
The garlic flavor is mellow and doesn't have the unpleasant pungent taste of the chopped garlic in a jar.

title: Amazing!
text:
Canned or bottled soups are notoriously bad and often have a twenty ingredient litany of the most odd ingredients. The Roa's soup are totally different. Great taste and not filled with junk ingredients. This sausage potato soup is really good. It's the only one I can eat due to having Celiac's disease, but my partner has tried two of the others and loved them.
He eats his with crusty bread and I eat mine with a toasted gluten free bagel from TJ's (wonderful)!
We wait for the $4.99 sale and stock-up!

title: Nice...
text:
I was really pleased with this nut milk. Pricey, but NO funky ingredients that you find in many of the other nut milks (gums and phosphates, etc.).
It has a mild flavor and I was hoping for a bit more cashew"punch", but it goes well in my hot tea. Best nut milk I've found so far.

title: Meh...
text: Not bad, but you have to put up with stirring it every time and the flavor isn't all that inspiring.

title: What???
text:
Contains sodium phosphate and powdered milk? For $6.99? And not organic?
There are better, less expensive choices...

title: Wonderful!!!
text:
I needed white pepper for two recipes I had found. I did a bit of research and found that white pepper tends to lose it's flavor over just 6 or so months. I decided to buy a small amount since I wouldn't be using much.
Imagine my surprise when this showed up and it was a very large bottle containing a great deal of pepper and with a grinder. Not just a small grinder but one that is about 2 1/4 inches across.
The upside is that both my partner and I have fallen head over heels for the taste of this pepper compared to the usual black pepper. This has so many more layers of flavor. It's sharp and sweet and mellows beautifully into any braised dish. It does best when added to a cooked recipe, but we've also put it in salad dressing. It's really great in steak and chop rubs.
We've only had it a few weeks and we've already used 1/4 of the very large amount in the jar.
I also want to add that the white pepper was very fresh. From the first grind you could quickly smell the sweet savory flavor in the air. It comes from the company that sells it and it took a couple of weeks to arrive. Well worth the wait.

title: Tastes great!
text:
I'm not much for bottled barbecue sauce. Most are overly sweet which hides some dubious ingredients. This sauce is the exception. My partners family sent a gift box for Christmas with different kinds of smoked meat and it include a bottle of Jack Stack. We decided to try it and were really pleased to find that it has a great full bodied, smoked, with just a bit of heat flavor.
I checked with four local stores, none carried it andI was happy to find I could get it on Amazon. Pricey but worth it.

title: What are the ingredients?
text: I was interested in this product but found that there is no complete list of the ingredients. The term "all natural" means nothing. It is not recognized and monitored like the term "organic", which has to meet certain strict standards. I'll be looking for a more honest representation of a different  similar product.

title: Wonderful!
text: I've had this in my cart for a long time but balked at the price. The price was suddenly reduced by nearly half. I bought two. It tastes amazing. Very lemony and rich. We ate the first bottle in two days. What a treat!

title: Cost!
text:
I started to order this, but nearly $12 for the product and then $8 to ship it makes it way beyond my reach. Nearly $20 for 16 oz of pickled vegetables!
Hope the price comes down...

title: Tasty
text: Really nice peanuts. Good flavor and fresh tasting. Spendy but worth it.

title: meh...
text: Not impressed. It is partly my fault because I was looking for lemon pepper and failed to see that salt is the first ingredient. It's really fairly salty. Not much pepper taste. Decent lemon taste. Can't use much because of the very high salt content even if it is Kosher salt.

title: Nice vinegar
text:
This is a really fine apple cider vinegar. It's made by a smaller family company. It has a higher acidic level than Bragg's and a much darker color. It's a bit more expensive but you can use less.
Great product. Great buy!

title: Amazing!
text: Really incredibly good toffee peanuts. Totally addicting! They use quality ingredients and they taste fresh and are really crunchy.

title: Tasty!
text: Really tasty, melt in your mouth peppermints. Just wish the peppermint flavor was a bit stronger...

title: Expensive!
text: I love these noodles and also the other types offered by Lotus foods. The price here is really high. I have found it for several dollars less on another site.

title: Taste great
text:
I really enjoy these chips! The flavor is great. Thick chips with just enough salt.
Unfortunately they are way overpriced. I get them as an occasional splurge.

title: Tasty!
text: These are way too good! I can finish off two of them in a sitting if I let myself. (:

title: Strong!
text: This granulated garlic is very potent. The flavor is great. It doesn't have that "off" smell some dried garlic products have. I was using garlic salt, but those products were often mostly salt. With this, I can gauge both the garlic and the salt. I definitely use more garlic!

title: Great flavor!
text: These are wonderful mints. Very strong cinnamon flavor. It would be better if the tins were a bit larger and held more product. These are spendy but mostly worth it!

title: Great!
text:
I really love these! Strong flavor, great chewiness. The individual packets are necessary but often difficult to open.
Still 5 stars!!!

title: Great to finally find it here.
text:
I've been using Bob's Red Mill gluten free products for a long time. I am unable to tolerate exposure to wheat so rice and corn flour are my go to for baking needs. I use a mixture of his gluten free corn meal and gluten free corn flour to coat fried chicken and fried cod, halibut, etc.
I also use both to make cast iron buttermilk cornbread. Everybody loves it!
I'm really please that his products are now on this site. I would find them occasionally in my local stores, but could never rely on that. Well made good tasting products!

title: Great bargain
text: We really go through these quickly in our house. Real peppermint flavor, not artificial. Candy has been fresh every time...

title: Great!
text:
I have used this cornmeal for several years. Unfortunately I can no longer find it in any local store and we have 7 different grocery stores within a ten minute radius of where we live.
This cornmeal has a medium grind, and I mix it with about a quarter amount of corn flour when I make cast iron pan corn bread. It's always a hit!

title: Tasty!
text:
Really flavorful, well made cookies. Very thin with a good amount of chips in them.
They are shipped in a box that has special packing around them. This made a difference because the cookies are very fragile. One of the boxes I ordered showed up partially crushed. 95% of the cookies were still whole.

title: Fun candy
text: These are great. Strong, hot flavor! Watch your teeth if you're like me and tend to try and chew hard candy...

title: Decent
text:
This is a really decent chai tea. I deleted my first review of this item because I found the tea too weak. I discovered that I wasn't brewing it properly and am now changing my opinion.
This is actually a very good chai tea. The trick is to brew it for at least 6 minutes and be sure the mug is pre-warmed and the water is very hot. I also gently press the bag up against the inside of the mug several times to get a bit more flavor out of the bag.
Enjoy!

title: Great cookie
text: Bought these for my partner. He says the Meyer's lemon flavor is mild and not overpowering. Thin and delicious.

title: Really good!
text: Great price. Great taste! Candy was fresh.

title: cheap price, cheap taste
text:
You get what you pay for. This "white" tea has a VERY green tea bitter end note.
I'm willing to pay more for the milder, sweet taste of true white tea.

title: Not bad
text: Tried this first and it was pretty good. Tried Monin hazelnut and it was better and less expensive. Plus, the Monin comes in a glass bottle; Joe's doesn't.

title: Fairly nice
text: At this price it can hardly be the best but it's pretty good. Large bags with a good amount of tea in them. Steep for a shorter amount of time and DON'T squeeze the bags out. That leaves a very bitter taste. I mix it with a better quality tea to make ice tea.

title: Five Stars
text: Nice texture and taste...

title: Don't waste your money
text: The product was beat to dust by the other items in the shipment.  I bought it as an add-on.  It's now 3 times the price.  It's only 4 oz.  Don't waste your money.

title: Just OK
text: Decent, but too garlic heavy. That tends to overwhelm the other flavors in it.

title: Five Stars
text: Very nice, well packed with few broken leaves. Lasts many months,

title: Better choices...
text:
Middling tea. Fairly bland. Nothing special.

I switched to Clipper organic decaf which is also sold on Amazon. It comes straight from England and takes longer to get here but has more tea in each bag and awesome flavor.

title: Tasty
text: Great taste and texture, but if you are sensitive to xanthan gum (as I am), beware of eating too many. Xanthan can have a laxative effect!

title: Four Stars
text: Good flavor. A bit bland, but doesn't have a lot of junk ingredients.

title: Too pricey
text: Very tasty but also very expensive. I now buy another brand.

title: I loved rice crackers (I spent a good deal of time ...
text:
Really tasty snack that is gluten free. I loved rice crackers (I spent a good deal of time in Japan in my younger years), but when I found out I couldn't eat gluten (diagnosed with Celiac Sprue) I had to give them up because they're made with soy sauce which contains wheat. These are made with gluten free soy sauce.

Now, I wish they would make a rice cracker wrapped in seaweed!!!

title: Tasty treat
text:
Love 'em!!! I order them as an occasional treat. They are very difficult to find in stores. The price is great.

They bring back childhood memories of picking out the chocolate ones from the variety rolls!

title: Nice!
text: Great snack. Doesn't blow up your blood sugar. A bit bland at first, but the more you chew it, the better it gets.

title: You might want to try something else...
text: It's OK, definitely on the mild side, but I have found better choices. The bags are round and not individually wrapped. If you want your tea fresh or don't drink it that often, the foil wrapped bags are a better choice.

title: Enjoyed them!
text:
Tasty. Not too sweet. Price is a bit high for what you get, but I'm ordering them again.

The ones I received were fresh and soft.

title: Tasty!
text: Love them! Great, medium strong ginger flavor and nice texture. The 1 l-lb bag is a great saving over their price in the small boxes in the stores.

title: Get it, but be aware...
text:
Really nice. That being said, they're on the chewy side and be very aware that they are "Wild Peppermint" drops. They taste like the peppermint I used to grow in my garden. A more dense and earthy flavor.

Don't expect a traditional, purified and standardized peppermint taste that you find in grocery store candy.

One star off because I prefer a crunchy peppermint!

title: Decent tea
text:
Great full-bodied taste. Very large bags compared to American brands.

I usually order organic tea on Amazon that thanks 20 days to arrive from England, so I ordered this when I ran short.

One star off for the company not making the organic leap :)

title: More cash, less class...
text: More expensive and you have 100 of them stuffed in a brown carton. I like the tea, but not the packaging. I poked around Amazon and found a better, less expensive choice.

title: NUTS
text: Nothing special, but there isn't much else to choose from. Wanted GMO free and organic, but there are few choices and the prices are sky high. Maybe the prices will come down on the organic when people want better peanuts.

title: Great Garlic!!!
text: Great garlic flavor. It's strong, so you need to use it sparingly until you get the flavor you want. A bit too much salt, but just a bit. Great price AND is organic!

title: Decent tea
text: A really nice tea, but not as strong as the Twining Irish Breakfast tea. I like my tea dark and rich. This is a good second choice. Both make great ice tea.

title: Good choice
text: Very tasty pink salt. Ground fine enough to use in a salt shaker. A more pale color that some of the other pink salts I've tried, but it still has the distinct flavor I look for.

title: Really nice decaf tea
text: Strong, rich tea flavor. It makes great ice tea.

title: Great flavor
text: Great to add to burgers. Very natural fresh tasting flavor.

title: Bad aftertaste
text: After looking at the other reviews, I feel way out of the mainstream on this tea. I found  the vanilla to be overpowering and  the tea had an odd chemical aftertaste. I used the get Numi's Vanilla tea here on Amazon, but they quit carrying it. It had a wonderful, natural vanilla flavor. I guess I'll just have to keep looking.

title: Three Stars
text: Fairly weak jasmine flavor. I've had it for a couple of months and only used 3 tea bags.

title: Three Stars
text: Really good flavor, but not that many leaves. 25% of them were really small or broken.

title: A good decaf tea
text: A good decaf tea, but there are others that have a more robust flavor and cost less. Twinning's Irish Breakfast decaf has a strong, true tea flavor and makes great ice tea. I order a package of six on Amazon for a good price.

title: There are better choice out there (and on Amazon)
text: It has a strong Chai flavor, but an odd, almost chemical aftertaste. There are better choice out there (and on Amazon).

title: I went to order this tea, but after checking ...
text:
I went to order this tea, but after checking on another tea companies product and finding it had artificial flavors, I decided to call Davidson's and ask them about this organic tea. It is organic, the tea bags are not bleached, BUT it is not made with any actual vanilla. They use a mixture of fruit concentrates and minerals to get the vanilla flavor.
I decided not to buy the tea. When it says vanilla, it should have vanilla in it...

title: OK
text: Decent product but it's over half almonds. I like almonds but they seem to be the "filler" nut. I'd like the product to have equal portions of the various nuts advertised on the label.

title: Great Stuff!
text:
It's ground to just the right size for a salt shaker and doesn't cake-up in the high humidity of the Pacific Northwest. The flavor is really nice. It doesn't have the bitter after taste of regular salt and some of the sea salt's.

I highly recommend it!

title: Great!
text: Good value for the money. The granulated onion has a nice mellow flavor, not bitter like another brand I tried. Great fro using on meat with garlic salt, paprika and ground pepper.

title: Mediocre
text:
Decent mint flavor, but Lindt uses artificial flavors in most of their chocolates. Their bars look big, but the chocolate is very thin.

They brand themselves as a premium chocolate (with a premium price), but no really well made chocolate contains artificial flavors. What ARE those flavors? Chemicals? It doesn't say "natural" artificial flavors.

Their chocolate is good for a quick grocery store grab, but there are better choices out there.

title: OK
text:
Really tasty, but it's a very small bottle. I season a lot of meat with onion powder, so the next time I ordered a bigger size of a different brand. If this were larger and the price was right, I'd order it again.

If you only use it occasionally, it's a good choice.

title: Mellow flavor
text:
Really nice tea. The vanilla isn't overpowering. I drink it with a bit of cream and sugar. Tasty!

A bit too pricey, but I order it occasionally.

title: Great goodie!
text:
I found these while shopping in a drug store and thought I'd give them a try. I loved them! One issue with doing that was freshness, as they're not a popular item and sit on the shelf longer.
I searched for them on Amazon and found them at a much better price, and so far they've always been fresh.

Update 8/2019: I still enjoy this chocolate bar but find that the price point on this site is considerably higher than at a specialty grocery store chain in my neighborhood. I can buy the bars one or two at a time and don't have to order 10.

title: VERY strong flavor
text: I bought this because it was organic and reasonably priced. I used it in a recipe for meatloaf I often make. Long story short, this thyme has a distinctly different flavor than the brand I had been using, and the flavor is not really very pleasant. It lent a bitter, strong taste to the meatloaf. I think I used too much and the VERY strong flavor drowned out the flavor of the other spices used. I won't be using it again because I expect thyme to lend a sweet, middle tone to recipes, not the harsh bitter taste of this thyme, organic or not. I'm going back to my old brand! If you decide to try it, use it very sparingly to begin with and increase the amount to your taste.

title: Not very smoky
text: It's fairly light and bland compared to other smoked paprika I've had. Good price but mediocre flavor. Try some of the others offered even if they're more expensive.

title: Bland!!!
text:
I hate to disagree with most of the other reviews, but this tea tastes flat, bland and a bit bitter. I've searched for a decent decaf tea and finely found three, two here on Amazon, and for less money than the Taylors. Bigelow Organic Breakfast Blend is the best. It has a rich, deep, aromatic flavor and goes well with a bit of sugar and milk or just plain. Higgins and Burke decaffinated Orange Pekoe is lighter in flavor than the Bigelow, but still offers deep amber richness. The third isn't sold on Amazon, but hopefully they'll add it as they carry the Peet's brand coffee. Peet's decaffinated English Breakfast loose tea is decent, too.
I use the Bigelow for single cup enjoyment and the Higgins and Burke for making ice tea.

title: Decent Decaf
text: This tea has a fairly strong and distinct flavor, unlike many of the other black decaf teas.  I use it to make ice tea.  For just drinking a cup, I use Bigelow's Organic Breakfast blend.  Really nice, aromatic, heavier flavor.  Amazon sells it, too.

title: The Real Deal
text: Great hickory flavor.  Used it to make pulled pork for 20 people.  It has a rich, natural flavor, no chemical aftertaste.  Made the pork with only Hawaiian sea salt (red), black pepper, a little onion, some garlic and the Colgin Liquid Smoke.  It was gone in less than 2 hours!

title: Favorite Tea!
text: Great flavor.

title: Purchased the French Roast with no regrets!
text: Its delicious and the price is unbeatable. :)

title: Its delicious.
text: No disappointments here.

title: I'm obsessed, I have to buy some more!
text: Flavor is amazing.

title: Great tea
text: This is one of the best teas I have had. I will continue to buy and drink this brand.  Smooth taste good price

title: Weak to no taste-would return if I could!
text: Not the same taste I knew from before. No taste or smell in this batch I received. Very weak tea even with multiple sachets used. Have to add milk and sugar to add some taste to make it drinkable. I kept hoping it would improve, but alas, remains tasting like mainly boiled water. Will never buy again. Freshpak is better.

title: Organic Freshness guaranteed
text: Great organic product. Flavour, freshness and quality ingredients with nothing added. . Love it!

title: Ok taste. Damaged box. Buy again and hope arrive undamaged.
text: Box was completely crushed inside (shipping box unharmed). Thankfully individually wrapped so no broken tea leaves. Taste ok, but could be stronger. Trying different brewing options. Yes, tea is good to taste, but prefer a little stronger (may just need to try loose tea version).

All 3 of these are probably in the 8-11 Nespresso intensity range, so if you don't like it strong, I suggest looking elsewhere.

I recommend trying this to get a sampler of the Caffitaly line. Compared to the Nespresso pods that came with my machine, these work better as there have been no duds, produce just as good, if not better espresso, and cost less.

Ethopia Single Origin Arabica Sidamo Heights
Rich, bright, floral, and a little bit winey. Nice change of pace. You can sense that this came from Ethiopia, but it barely scratches that itch and doesn't make me dance like Kaldi's goats. 6/10

Brazil Single Origin Arabica Alta Mogiana
Here we have the standout of all 3. Balanced deep roasted flavors that are bold enough for a latte & wonderful by itself. This is the best pod coffee I've ever had from any pod device. I'll be buying more of these. 8.5/10

The Formosa is the top sauce of the bunch. It has a delicious mustard base heat, great on grilled meat. Clancy's has a good sweet heat flavor, good for meats. It's similar to a honey Sriracha. The other two are good but more basic hot sauce. Lucky's is more for tacos and the Texas Pete is basic general hot sauce. While there's a definite kick to all of them, none are so hot that they stay in your mouth too long. Definitely a great gift idea!

title: Quality components and great customer service
text:
I do love my Stormio Nespresso coffee but I do not love the price per capsule for my Vertuoline Plus machine. Fortunately, I can purchase quality coffee beans, grind them, and create my own capsules that work well in the machine, but I also understand that great coffee is my ultimate goal and don't expect to have a flavorful cup with ample crema unless I start with the best beans. A couple of hints I can provide for using the Capmesso system is to keep a stash of prepared, clean empty capsules of your favorites because the bar codes let the machine know how to and how much to brew per cup. Next, be sure your capsule is clean, free of bits before you apply the seal. The brush helps you out here, but be sure the holder is also free of any coffee. If there is adhesive on the rim of your capsule, be sure to get it off using alcohol if necessary or you could damage your machine. Just as you would not use a bent Nespresso filled capsule, don't use one you fill yourself. Use the correct grind of beans, feel it when you empty out a used capsule and feel your coffee. Tamp it down gently but it does need room to expand when wet. Use the end of the brush to secure the seal to the inner top edge of the capsule and don't forget to stretch it as you can, avoiding wrinkles and finish off by also smoothing down the miniscule edge around the rim, feeling for any opening. I have yet to have one fail when brewed. Lastly, I have found that by ejecting the spent capsule immediately after it's brewed, then following it up by running the hot water through an empty capsule right away, everything stays nice and clean, preventing problems with the machine. (I do this with the Nespresso filled capsules as well.)

Initially, there was a problem with the kit I received, so I reached out to the email address on the box. To my surprise, I received a response within a few hours and all was made good. The product is impressive and so is the customer service. I'll definitely be repurchasing the seals.

text: I can eat steel cut oatmeal every day and be happy. I do not want anything added by the manufacturer as I like to select any flavoring or fruits as it's being prepared. The packaging is impressive, the top of each package tears easily and I can fill it with water to prepare in the microwave. I always add a little more than to the line measurement inside the bag. title: Unlike fresh tofu, shelf stable is a good alternative
text: Silken tofu is not fresh tofu or what most people see in the refrigerated section of a grocery store, big biz store or buckets in Asian markets. It is on the pantry shelf, unrefrigerated.  I keep it on hand for nights like this one when I want tofu but have none in the refrigerator. Understand that silken is just that, softer by nature than what many expect. Even the Extra Firm is not.  It's silken, not rigid.  It's great as a scramble, blended until smooth, or added to a base of your choice.  I go for curry types and have found that when I cut open the carton on the dotted lines, if I let the water drop into the sink and then simply let the entire "block" drop into the wok or pa, I can break it into pieces with my spatula as it heats.

I use avocado oil or olive oil to saute onions, add the kippers, then add a whisked egg to the mixture until just set,  With hot sauce and sliced tomatoes, I'm happy.

title: Perfection in a can but the actual can is not perfect
text: I purchased and prepared a single can of MA MADE marmalade, using a full 4 pounds of sugar and adding too much water because I used the line on the back of the can, not the correct measurement line that's on the SIDE of the can. The can arrived in a very dented condition and I did not even see a line on the side until I was taking the can to the recycling bin.  I could not understand why I had to cook it for so long and then why it ended up producing 10 pints of the final product. Be sure to look for the line on the side, not the back with the instructions and other information!  The marmalade is tasty, bitter, sweet, fresh, luscious, and I will purchase another can.  Even folks who did not like orange marmalade loved this, perhaps because my product is thinner in consistency, making it perfect for mixing in Greek yogurt.  It thickens in the refrigerator.  I used the water bath technique for just over 5 minutes to seal the jars and each was a success.

title: It's Orville
text: I don't have a large popcorn popper, just my stovetop Whirley Pop pot and a few months ago, I purchased a case of these packets just to feel like I was eating popcorn from a movie theater.  It's designed to be used in a 12 ounce capacity machine but that doesn't prohibit you from opening the 2 packets and transferring their contents to another airtight jar to dole out smaller portions for your stovetop popping needs.  Cut off the corner of the coconut oil and squeeze it into a jar, placing the last of it directly into the pot.  Cut a small clip off the corner of the popcorn section and allow the salt seasoning to gently fall into a small spice jar, shaking a little to get out as much as you can.  Lastly, cut more of the corner so you can have the popcorn fall into the jar you have ready for the kernels.  To prepare your popcorn, simply use the coconut oil blend with the popcorn kernels and salt seasoning and there you have it, a recipe for movie theater popcorn.  When you use up the contents of one, repeat the process with another pack.  The quality of the popcorn is like any other Orville popcorn.  The oil blend is rather good, not heavy.  The salt seasoning is fine in texture, so it's perfect for popcorn.  Each batch does have several of its large kernels which don't pop or even crack but a majority are great.  I do find that there are more hulls than my other brands, so I've deducted a star because I just don't want to be chewing popcorn hulls.

title: Is this how a bird feels?
text: The Almond Butter Dark Chocolate KIND Healthy Grains Bars are very tasty, a little sweet, crunchy and a little bit chewy, too after awhile.  There is not a lot of chocolate, but that's not terrible.  The assorted grains are crispy and hard enough that I want to bite down on them carefully so as to not chip a tooth.  This is the kind of a bar that I'll probably get tired of after eating them for several days, so I can't give them a five star review.

title: Garlic lovers unite
text:
The Maesri Fried Garlic is so crunchy and garlicky that we use it every day on so many things. It's very well done, so if you don't like that, you likely will not enjoy it. Think of the garlic on a garlic bagel after it's been toasted and you get the idea. This is a large plastic jar that is sealed in cellophane in addition to the inner seal.
Recently made a dip with this, cracked pepper and a touch of cumin in sour cream for a plain potato chip dip. Perfect on ramen even if you add nothing else.

title: Basic brown rice
text: I like this bag of brown rice and find that it cooks extremely well in my rice cooker after soaking for a few minutes and several rinses in clear water.  It's not a fancy rice and that's just fine.  There are not many broken kernels.

title: Single can of tasteless  "smoked" oysters
text: Like a lot of other customers, I purchased what was listed as 5 cans of Roland Foods Premium Naturally Smoked Medium Oysters in Oil, Wild Caught, 3 Oz Tins and I received a single can of the correct oysters in a plastic envelope.  Fortunately, I had saved a captured image of the listing, so I was able to receive a refund after emailing it to the person with whom I spoke on the phone.  I was happy to have kept that image!  When I opened the lonely can of oysters, I was relieved that the tab style pull lid opened properly and the oysters were nicely nestled in the oil.  I drained the oil and ended up with about 1/3 of the can empty.  I put the oysters on a salad and with the first taste, noted that there was a very, very light smoke flavor and an even lighter oyster taste.  To my distaste, a number of the oysters were so dry that they literally broke into pieces.  I would not purchase these oysters again due to their lack of flavor and dry texture.  My review does not take into account that only one can was received, as they are simply not a good product.

title: Tangy dressing
text: I don't usually purchase bottled shelf stable salad dressings but for some reason, maybe because it reminded me of the dressings my mother used to buy, I purchased a single bottle.  It's very tasty.  It wasn't easy to remove the seal or unscrew the cap, but I finally got it done and then after removing the safety seal and replacing the cap, I gave it a good shake and poured it onto our salad.  All it needed was freshly ground black pepper and the mediterranean styled salad was a great hit.  I'll purchase this again.

title: McCormick's brand of bright red crushed pepper
text: Drogheria & Alimentari Organic Crushed Red Pepper in this package is enough to last for over a year so I have filled a spice jar with some, shared some with a friend, and placed the remainder in a vacuum sealed bag for freezer storage.  This is so much better than the pepper I've replaced it with and I would indeed purchase it again.

title: Add to ice cream or cookie dough for a treat
text: I first purchased a smaller canister of the Planters Salted Caramel Peanuts and decided that it was time to order a larger bag which would last longer.  The coating is not overly salty or hard, actually more of a granular coating.  If I only eat a few, they are quite tasty but if I have one too many, I can't stand them.  A very strong artificial flavor overwhelms the peanuts.  Instead of eating these on their own, they are much better when used in cookie dough or mixed into a very rich vanilla ice cream.  I won't be buying them again.

title: Mild and Hot are both excellent
text:
I've been purchasing the S&B Golden Curry Sauce Mix in both the Mild and the Hot varieties and really like them both. Each box contains two blocks of the curry and I slice off a piece for a single meal for one or more for multiples.
I then place the remainder in a zip lock bag and store it in the refrigerator until next time. I'd first purchased and loved the packets of prepared curry and vegetables which impressed my family, and then ordered a few of these to keep on hand. Japanese curry is different than the more well known Indian type of curry and I find that they are aromatic and not as hot as I usually consume. To add some heat to these, I put a few shakes of House Foods Shichimi Pepper Mix on top.

title: Slimy, salty, sweet & sour awful
text: The kids gave me 10 of the packets back because they hated them so much that they were discarded.  I said I had to try them myself and I'd find a home for the remainder of the packets.  These are perhaps the worst oatmeal packets I've ever attempted to consume.  Visually, they are slimy, like some broken flattened oats were covered in a slimy light brown sauce.  The first spoonful was gagging, like salty mucous initially, followed immediately by a sour flavor that was nauseating.  There is sweetness but it is overwhelmed by the salty, sour mucous-like disgusting oatmeal and there is a hint of cinnamon that trails like me in a race.  I had to brush my teeth.  Awful oatmeal.

title: Too many are sketchy
text: I recently purchased this 4 pound bag of REESE'S Miniatures Gold Foils Milk Chocolate Peanut Butter Cups, a 4 pound bag of Hershey's milk chocolate kisses in the blue foil, and a 4 pound bag of the Hershey's milk chocolate with almond kisses in gold.  They arrived in two deliveries, this one was with the blue kisses.  Both bags of kisses are fine, look good and taste good.  These peanut butter cups are pretty good but not perfect.  Some are formed properly but most are misshapen.  They are sealed but some chocolate peeks out from the foil like the foil has worn away.  Most are not round, but have flattened sides.  Since the bag I received was sealed, I'm not concerned about contamination, it's just very sketchy, like they were not stored properly.  The paper cups are stuck to the chocolate and are tough to remove, so younger kids need a little help or they will eat the paper.  I will use some of these in cookies instead of the candy bags for which I purchased them, and it's disappointing to have spent extra for gold foil in the first place.  I won't be ordering them from the seller again.  Reese's peanut butter cups are usually very tasty and the mini sized candies are a good addition to goody bags but this particular order was pretty much a waste.

title: Excellent package of kisses
text: Just like the other Hershey's Chocolate Kisses I've purchased recently, these milk chocolate treats wrapped in a lovely pale blue aluminum wrap are going to be added to our Valentine's goody bags.  I've had fun preparing personalized round labels for each variety and know they will be enjoyed.

title: Convenient packs for travel and home
text: We use a lot of Cholula Original Hot Sauce, but want to limit the amount of space it takes up in the refrigerator.  Once a bottle is opened, it tends to lose its potency, so despite the disadvantage of the plastic packet waste, the sauce remains strong and flavorful for a very long time.  The box can be stored in the pantry with a week's supply in a jar or bag in the kitchen and no refrigerator space needs to be delegated to this Mexican sauce.  They are easy to open and don't require teeth, a knife, or scissors.  If you have fingers and a thumb, you can tear it gently on one end and squeeze the contents onto your food.  I never even thought about buying these before but after receiving other hot sauces from takeout, I investigated and found this option.  The box is imprinted with the date of manufacture and the best by date but I suspect that with proper cool storage, it will live much longer.

title: Not as hot as I'd expected
text: That's not a terrible thing because that means I can use more being that I now have two large bottles of Marie Sharps Beware Comatose Hot Sauce.  I first tasted it on a spoon with a glass of water and piece of bread on the side but I needed only the hot sauce and not the rescue attempts.  The color is a lovely orange and the viscosity is what I'd call in the midrange of hot sauces.  Because there are so many seeds, a shake is sometimes necessary to get it out of the bottle.  I've never been to Belize but read up on Ms. Sharp, an impressive woman, so I was happy to try her product.  Women owned businesses there need promotion and fortunately, this hot sauce is rather tasty.  I'd buy it again.

title: Nuts are the best in most chocolate confections
text: The only thing that would make these better would be dark chocolate instead of the milk chocolate.  I received a lovely bag of perfect Hershey's Kisses that look perfect, taste perfect, and bring pleasure to every person who receives them.  I printed stickers for the bottoms of these kisses and could barely contain myself because of the deliciously strong aroma of the chocolate that brings up so many memories.  It may not be a gourmet chocolate product, but it warms the heart like a good bowl of mac and cheese or tomato soup.

title: It's grown on me
text: I've seen a lot of the Cascadian Farm Organic cereals online and in my daughter's pantry, so I ordered a small box of the Graham Crunch Cereal.  The cereal looks good with its curved, thin shape, and because much of the sugar has fallen off of the cereal, I transferred the cereal without the loose sugar into a jar for preservation.  It's a little crunchy but won't break teeth and due to the texture, it softens quickly when chewed or milk is added.  If you like your cereal to become soggy in milk after five minutes, this is a good choice.  If not, eat it quickly or drop a couple of pieces onto a spoonful of milk and consume it that way.  Or you could put a couple in your mouth and then take a sip of milk and eliminate the spoon as well as the bowl.  I like it with slices of fresh bananas and have one with each bite of cereal.  It's not real sweet.

title: Look at the images
text: I wish I had.  I was so excited to see the larger 25 ounce tray that I simply ordered it because the price was so much better than smaller packages.  These were needed for a special project, so it was important that they not only taste good, but be good looking.  It's been years since I purchased the Bergen Marzipan and expected these to be perfect.  What I received was an opened package of marzipan pieces which resembled those in the images that so many other customers posted.  Because the thin cellophane wrapper was popped open, many of the marzipan fruits were loose inside the shipping box and each and every one of the pieces is hard as a rock.  Waste of merchandise, money and human power to get them from Amazon to my dumpster.

title: Use a larger bowl than you think you need and supervise younger kids
text:
I make a fantastic pasta and cheese and always have some vacuum sealed packages in my freezer for last minute dinners. But, I grew up on the blue boxes of Kraft Macaroni and Cheese, usually sharing a box with one of my sisters after school. I made it for my daughter for special occasions and she makes it for her kids as well even though she also makes a mean pasta and cheese. I have to add that we always add vegetables. For the past year, I've been purchasing assorted prepackaged mac and cheese options and I've learned what works for us and what does not work for us. I do not like the packages with a cheese sauce at all and my neighbors are happy for that because they accept them in the bags of food I share. I tried this box of 18 individual servings because they have less packaging, are prepared in the microwave and involve only a bowl, spoon and glass for measuring 2/3 cup of water. No cover for the bowl, nothing else added unless you want vegetables and I'd suggest adding them after the package is prepared.

First of all, the water boils violently, so use a bowl larger than you think you need. Watch it carefully the first time you prepare one so you can stop the microwave if necessary unless you don't mind losing some of the starchy water and having to clean the microwave interior. Secondly, the bowl will be HOT, so watch younger kids who might want to prepare these on their own. Those are my only warnings. After 3.5 minutes, the pasta is likely done, so remove the bowl, add the powdered cheese powder, stir, wait a minute, add what you want to add, eat. It is salty, my only real criticism. The look and taste is very similar to the blue boxes of Kraft Macaroni and Cheese and you have a single serving which prevents eating more than you really need or want to eat for a meal or heavier snack. The school aged and younger kids love these and they take up no space in the refrigerator, freezer, and require no reheating the next day. Just open another packet if you are so inclined and repeat. These are not the nutritious meals I like to prepare, serve or consume, but for their ease, taste, satisfaction, reduced packaging and cost, I think they are one of the best in this category.

title: Not too salty, fresh and tasty almond slices
text: Added to salads with fruit or vegetables, this is a versatile almond product that was thoroughly enjoyed.  I usually don't think of adding sliced almonds but am very glad to have purchased a single bag because it complements the sweetness of fruit like persimmons or dried berries.  I'll purchase again.

title: Versatile sauce awakens the taste buds
text: I don't purchase many pre-made pouches of food but was intrigued by the S&B Hot Curry Sauce with Vegetables because the emergency Indian pouches in my pantry lost their appeal.  After researching Japanese options, I settled on these and was prepared for curry that was labeled as Hot but was more of a Medium.  I personally found these to have heat to them but a more delicate heat than that in Indian curries.  I did not find them to be overly sweet as some reviewers reported.  Actually, I found this curry to be delicious and ordered another case to share with others because I like them so much.  When hungry but not feeling like whipping up a meal, simply place a pouch in a pot of boiling water for 3-5 minutes, prepare your protein of choice, cook some short grained rice, plate them up with vegetables of choice and enjoy a tasty meal that satisfies.  Because of the high, nearly 800mg content of sodium in a pouch, I serve a half pouch for a single meal per person.  I'd also like to comment on the package graphics which are much more beautiful than those displayed in this listing.  There's pretty shiny gold that makes it appealing to look at.

title: Yummy creamy versatile tofu
text: I generally prefer firm or extra firm tofu but love this silken soft Mori Nu for its storage capabilities, taste, texture and color.  It's my go to soft tofu.

title: Good quality, easy to store in a cupboard, easier to transport than cans
text: It's not my favorite tuna, but as a chunky albacore tuna, it's very good because there's not a lot of liquid to drain from the pouch.  I purchased it for a camping trip and it worked rather well, easy to open, fun to mix into a salad in the campsite, and enjoyed by the kids and adults who had it with soup and s'mores.  Hadn't taken tuna camping before this one and the larger sized pouch was just what was needed. My only criticism is that the fish is not in solid pieces as the advertising photo demonstrates.  Nevertheless, I'm going to order a case of these because they are not salty, are flavorful, and everyone likes them.

title: Sweet rhubarb for toast, pastry or a spoon
text: I received 1 jar, not 3 but I guess that's okay since the jar I received couldn't be eaten anyway. It was opened and leaking even though it was inside a box and not an envelope. I purchased some last year locally and liked it because I love the tartness and texture of rhubarb. The product could be much less sweet but I don't see many rhubarb jam options available these days.  Unfortunately, this jar I received did not contain the edible jam and I got rid of it. I reuse the Bonne Maman jars so at least I got something out of the disappointing order.  I would not order this jam due to the large number of problematic orders I've since read about.

title: Not as good as homemade but a salty backup if necessary
text: Whisps are made of parmesan cheese and parmesan cheese and parmesan cheese with nothing else added.  The bag unfortunately ships in a bag mailer, not even a protective one, so many of them are broken.  It's the cheese source of the Whisps that is a saltier parmesan than the ones I make from a higher quality cheese which results in adding less than a full portion onto a bowl of soup which has no salt added.  They soften in soup and become spongy as expected, so if you want them crisp on soup, add them one at a time.  I won't purchase them again from Amazon and likely won't purchase them again simply because the salt overpowers the cheese flavor.

title: Learned my lesson
