text: Pay attention to the pictures and reviews.  Pay attention to the pictures and reviews.  I'm writing this twice because I wish I'd paid attention to the customer pictures and reviews.  Pacific Foods Organic soups generally have too much salt for my household and when I can find the reduced sodium varieties, I pick them up in the local stores.  The Roasted Red Pepper & Tomato Soup has added depth to the standard Tomato Soup and I usually have one or two in the pantry for emergency provisions or additions to a meal.  It's creamy, flavorful, and lends itself to upgrading with herbs, spices, and vegetables or grains.  Unfortunately, I received a case of the cartons which resemble those in many of the pictures up above, so I have to add the soup to my local shopping list.  This case of soup contains cartons that are popped at the top seams next to the plastic screw cap.  The caps are all intact but the paper seams are open for air to enter and soup to exit.  They were not totally empty, so the pretty red soup all over both cardboard boxes was a pretty obvious clue that something was amiss.  On a positive note, all I had to do with these packs of soup is hold each one over the sink drain upside down and the soup flowed with ease.  That made the load lighter for me to carry empty cartons and cardboard out to the trash instead of lugging twenty-something pounds of spoiled soup.  Just a hint to help save your back should the same thing happens to you.

title: Spice of Life
text: We've gone through a lot of the Starkist individual tuna varieties in their own little cup with a spork hidden in the lid and thought we'd see how these compared since we're basically eating them at home these days and not taking them out for lunch breaks.  They pretty much taste the same, perhaps a little better, but that could be simply because there's no guilt involved in wasteful packaging.  With these, you rip off the top of the bag or cut if you can't get it torn, put it in a bowl or dish, on crackers or bread, or throw it on your prepared salad and you have a tasty protein that's a single serving.  I'd never had the smoked tuna, so getting the variety pack allowed me to see why my daughter is now ordering those as her preferred option for the little bowls.  I had it with some sweet relish, pickled ginger and fancy oat cake crackers, then finished it off with a fresh orange for a very quick lunch.  I'll buy the variety pack again because I like sticking my hand into the box and pulling out a surprise flavor.

title: Thin, crisp, sweet, the best of Pepperidge Farm
text: I find it interesting that this listing says, under the heading of Safety Information, "Do not purchase if bag is open or torn."  How do you know if it's open or torn until it arrives at the destination and the package is opened?  Oh well, I actually purchased these locally and the bag was perfectly intact, as were the cookies inside.  Ok, a couple were broken, but these are so thin and crisp that I was not surprised.  It doesn't matter, though, because the Pepperidge Farm Bordeaux Caramelized Crisp Cookies are delicious and attractive.  On their own, with a hot beverage or sniffer of Cognac, or placed atop a dish of ice cream, the cookies are one of the best that Pepperidge Farms offers.  Because I want to maintain the crispness and integrity of the caramelized sugar, I carefully put them in an airtight container instead of keeping them in the paper bag.  This also keeps them intact because I prefer having a perfectly formed cookie over bits of cookies even though they both taste great.  I sometimes sprinkle the broken bits on plain yogurt with nothing else added, thereby enjoying a sweet and sour protein serving.

title: I hate these because they are too good
text: I love crunchy things more than I love soft things.  Pretzels should be crunchy and sometimes, as I chew them, I get a pasty kick more than a crunchy kick from the chewed product.  Think about it, flour and water can make paste, as my sister and I did when we were kids.  We even made kites out of newspaper and flour/water paste.  They didn't really fly but we loved the activity.  Anyway, the Unique Pretzel Shells are outstanding because I have the crunch and I can use the ones that split into two as dipping instruments for cheesy stuff, mustard, or softened peanut butter.  (Or almond butter, cashew butter, sunflower butter, cottage cheese, crab dip, artichoke dip, spinach dip, hummus, baba ganoush, salsa, or ........)  Unlike most of the folks with whom I've shared these, I prefer less salt and would love to have an unsalted version of these.

title: Excellent taste, viscosity and freezes well
text: I normally do not purchase a six pack of size 10 cans of processed nacho cheese sauce but when I saw this Rosarita brand case at a great price, I jumped on it.  I mean, let's face it, we are going nowhere these days where we could even consider purchasing from a concession stand and we are eating things that we usually do not eat, just to experience some variety.  Being fans of potatoes in any shape, color or recipe, my first thought as I awaited the package arrival was immediately baking potatoes and topping them with the nacho cheese sauce as a baseline.  Nothing else, just the potatoes and sauce.  Yummy!  Then we added things like green onion tops, garbanzo beans. toasted nuts, candied jalapenos, potato chip crumbles, well you get the idea.  I froze 1/2 cup containers of this stuff in the freezer and then popped them directly in a ziplock bag to take up less space and prevent them from getting lost, so we could take one out and pop it in the microwave any time the urge hit.  They taste as fresh as when the can was first opened.  Because the can is so huge, I shared some with friends and as soon as I receive word that someone needs more, I'll open another can.  I personally love spices, so I doctor mine up with jalapeno peppers even though there is a hint of heat in this as is.  (I'm also repurposing the cans because they arrived in perfect shape and make cute cans for the kids when covered with fabric or contact paper.  Will be on the lookout for lids from other cans this size that are not as strong.)

title: Great color and aroma
text: I loved the orange color of this VERO GUSTO BY BARILLA Tomato & Basil Pasta Sauce as it simmered with the cooked Italian pasta in a saucepan.  The texture was creamy, aroma was delicious, and when I added freshly grated Italian Parmigiano-Reggiano Cheese to my plated portion, salivation was immediate.  As I ate it by the forkful, I thought of how I could taste the tomato, the olive oil and the basil, each individually.  There was not a hint of sweetness.  Unfortunately, within minutes of finishing the meal, my digestive system revolted, an experience that is unnatural for me.  This is quite a disappointment because I'd placed an order for the alternate assortment of three varieties which I intended to include in holiday gifts I'm assembling. Fortunately, I was able to cancel the order before it shipped.  The packaging was impressive, the reviews were stellar, and I'd had higher hopes for these more expensive jarred sauces.

title: Minty, lemony, not oily
text: I enjoy making stuffed grape leaves but I also enjoy finding them pre-made to enjoy at any time.  Galil Stuffed Grape Leaves are quite tasty and not overly spiced so they work well either out of the can or dressed up.  They tend to hold their form and the rice is not overly cooked or too firm.  Each time I try these, I am reminded with the first bite that mint really enhances them because that's the flavor which jumps at me first.

title: Ignore the graphic images
text: My biggest problem with Wonderful Pistachios is that each time I open a bag, I expect the actual pistachios to look like those in the images that cover the bag and I am disappointed to reveal smaller, less beautiful specimens.  Nevertheless, I purchase them from Amazon and I also purchase them from local stores because they entice me.  I recently purchased a couple of the 24 ounce bags from a local store and they were really fresh tasting, but my last few orders here were mot as good.  I transfer my nuts to a glass jar to keep them fresh and I'd recommend storing them in something other than the thin cellophane bag in which they are packaged.  There are always some pistachios that cannot easily be opened so I put them in another jar and when I'm desperate, pull out a little hammer to crack them open.  I'll continue purchasing Wonderful Pistachios because even the salted ones are not too salty and they are the most readily available.

title: Manufactured in Canada or Pennsylvania?
text: I received 3 perfectly wrapped and sealed jars of my favorite Honeycup Mustard and despite the time being 10am and having only a cup of coffee after awakening, i opened the first jar and had it with crackers and cheese.  My favorite condiment is mustard and this one has been satisfying me since the late 1970's when my friend Jane and I would drive to Sausalito, Napa or Sonoma from San Francisco, buy a jar with some carrots and a fresh baguette and go for our hike somewhere.  When we were hungry, we would stop and enjoy the scenery.  Then we would tear off a piece of bread and cheese, use the carrot to spread the mustard on top, and finally enjoy a chunk of carrot that was redipped into the mustard jar.  Despite this listing saying that it is a product of Canada, all three jars I received clearly state on the label, "Stone County Specialties Inc. 458 Fairview St. Tamaqua, PA 18252"  I've never examined my previous jars purchased locally so I don't know if this is manufactured in the US now or both countries.

title: Best peanut butter for baking purposes
text: My mom used to buy Skippy peanut butter but as an adult, I seldom do.  I prefer peanut butter that is peanuts and nothing more, but that does not work well for baking purposes.  Seriously, you need a peanut butter like Skippy to make the best peanut butter cookies.  You may ask why I purchased this humongous jar of Skippy if I use it only for baking and I will let you know that it was offered at a price that I could not pass by.  It has been separated into smaller jars and shared with others who want it for their sandwiches.  I've kept a couple of jars for myself and after preparing a double batch of cookie dough, store some individual unbaked cookies in the freezer for baking a few at a time in the toaster oven.

title: Seedy and creamy, not the thickest consistency
text: I'm a huge mustard fan and have been known to have carrots dipped in mustard or a mustard sandwich.  When the condiment has the seeds included, I enjoy it even more because of the added texture and visual.  Grey Poupon Country Dijon Mustard is one of the mildest grainy mustards and it's easier to spread than most others.  I would not call this a gourmet condiment, just a nice one to have.  It's especially good with cheese and cornichons, no cracker is required, just splatter some on top of the slice.

title: Feel good tea reminds me to Breathe
text: After reading about problems with torn paper teabags from other customers, I was a little hesitant to order a box of 6 packages of TAZO Calm Chamomile tea bags and am so happy that I decided to make the purchase.  What I received is an order in perfect condition and I've yet to encounter a problematic teabag.  As with any individually wrapped teabag, I open it very carefully, knowing that a teabag can be unintentionally ruined.  Mine have all looked like the pressed flow through pleated bags I purchased elsewhere and I will update this review if necessary.  What I really like about this chamomile blend is that the taste is exceptionally balanced and the color (thanks to turmeric) is appealing.  Bring the water to a full boil (212 degrees F) and let the 8 ounces of water take what it can from these herbs.  When I want more of a mint profile, I add a little peppermint, but generally find that this is exactly what I want on its own.  It's not a hot beverage I enjoy in the morning because I like my kick in the pants then, but in the hours after the sun has set, it's the hot tea I select.

title: Pleasure from a case of pasta
text: Buying packaged pasta from a store, especially now when I'm reluctant to enter one, I would eye the package that looked the most intact before placing it in my cart.  Some are unappealing, others are desirable but containing broken pieces, and others cause me to wonder if air has accessed the pasta.  For some reason, I find it so pleasing to receive a sealed case of pasta from Italy that when opened, reveals perfect packages of my favorite Fusilli Bucatini Corti No 108.  This one has a high protein, thin but secure packages which reveal the contents, and most importantly, pasta that become perfectly al dente at 7 minutes.  Most importantly, when used in mac and cheese, it can't be beat.  I also love the La Molisana website.

title: Forget this one
text: Why is this "specialty" baking soda sold in the same crummy plastic impenetrable bucket under an assortment of names from assorted states in the USA?  I ordered another brand and was sent this one, and after exploring both products, made this discovery.  They have the same bad instructions for removing the horrible container lid and virtually the same descriptions.  Questions are answered by the same manufacturer or distributer or whatever they are.  The bucket I received had a lid that was opened on one side and sealed on the other.  I don't know how long air had access to the bicarbonate of soda inside the bucket but I can't use this for all the purposes I intended (baking and cooking).  Getting the lid off of the bucket was a terrible task and remember that mine was already half opened.  As a consumer, I should not have to research a way to open this lid.  I would suggest that if instructions are indicated, include them on the product.  Being familiar with similar buckets, I knew what to do and was surprised to have received a product that had a defective "secure" seal.  The actual bright white product I have does have some clumps that quickly were remedied with the back of a clean spoon.  I find nothing special about this product that warrants the high cost.  It is bicarbonate of soda, pure and simple, just like the one most of us grew up on which is available online and in virtually every grocery store and big box store in the US.  I'll give it two stars because it is baking soda and take off three because of the price, marketing and terrible container.

title: Single tiny tab sweetens to my taste
text:
EDITED TO ADD: I've deducted a star because on several occasions, two tiny tabs dispensed into my cup. I now dispense it into my hand and then drop it into the cup. Also, I've encountered pieces of a tab which is frustrating.

ORIGINAL: I don't use Splenda very often, not as often as one of my sisters who uses them with every cup of coffee or tea, and when I use a paper packet, I only use a half in a cup of beverage. I twist the top, intending to use it later but sometimes, it ends up being discarded because I don't recall how old it is. In the days when I used to go out in public, like as recent as early 2020, I would inevitably end up either dumping an entire packet in the beverage or wasting half because I certainly would not bring it home. These little dissolvable tabs remind me of what my Mom used to used decades, actually a half century ago or more, and I was mesmerized by them because we were not allowed to have them ourselves as kids. Now I can have what I wanted as a kid! A package of these is wider and shorter, thicker than a single paper packet of Splenda and I now have one in my bag and one in the kitchen.

title: Such a versatile grain
text: I'm a new fan of Palouse Brand grains and am actually awaiting delivery now for an assortment of their legumes which I ordered directly from them.  Currently, I am using both the Hard Red Winter and the Hard Red Spring Wheat Berries and because I purchased the 25-pound bag, I am sharing them.  I've put some away in glass jars, some in vacuum-sealed bags, and keep a jar for current use.  When I grind the berries, I do it as needed and if I have extra, I store it in the refrigerator or freezer, depending on space in the freezer.  I cook these, grind them for denser breads and sprout them for the wheat grass.  As I write this, I have a huge batch of Pressure Cooker White Bean-Parmesan Soup Recipe from the New York Times.  It's amazing and this farro is my favorite to use in the recipe.  I do soak them for a couple of hours in advance but it's not necessary.

title: Must be fresh to be good
text: The bag I just received expired six months ago, bummer.  Normally, these are delicious if you like prunes and chocolate.  The chocolate works well with the fruit, not quite dark and not milk chocolate.  When fresh, the texture and taste make for a wonderful little desert with a nice cup of strong coffee.  When old, skip them.

title: Can't get enough
text: I purchased the Tiptree Lemon Curd in a six pack because not only do I love it, but I wanted to share it with others.  It's really one of those products that is better purchased locally I've found because I can check the color of the curd and be sure that there is no problem with the lid popping open prior to purchase.  The curd is my favorite and I eat it several times a week in yogurt, on or in baked goods, or simply on a spoon dipped into the jar as I pass the kitchen.  For a case, I prefer ordering directly from the source.

title: Rich, thick coffee
text: I really like the Medaglia D'Oro Italian Roast Espresso when prepared as iced coffee with a hint of dark sugar and a splash of milk.  It's not a refined bean, just a reliable coffee in an appealing can that screams, "Italy!"

title: Prefer the bottle for pouring but like the look of the can
text: I purchased my first 11 ounce bottle of Lyle's Golden Syrup in a local grocery store and then bought a 16 ounce can from Amazon to see if there is any difference in the product.  They are the same, it's just the packaging that differs.  I'm not a big fan of corn syrup and learned about Golden Syrup several years ago.  I love it.

title: Concentrated taste and texture is satisfying
text: Eight cookies in a small box does not sound like a lot but each of these Walkers Classic Shortbread Fingers is satisfying and I personally find that a single one hits the spot when enjoyed with a cup of tea.  For some reason, I prefer these with tea to coffee.  Very buttery, the texture has a tendency to fall into pieces, so I usually have it on a plate which catches any crumbs and I enjoy them when nobody is looking.  In the past, I've dipped these in dark chocolate but for the past few years, simplicity has ruled and they are enjoyed straight out of the box.

title: Tasty decaf
text: Illy coffee beans are consistently good and I'm a fan of their packaging system which is reusable.  The decaf coffee is quite tasty, not strong and not weak.  I prefer a more bold brew but find that since I prepare this usually in the afternoon or evening, its calmer flavor is quite good.  I keep my can in the refrigerator because our decaf can isn't consumed every day.

title: Fun to make, not so good to eat
text: The kids had some fun making these little "candies" but nobody liked how they tasted.  For once, I was happy to have purchased only a single box for them to share.

title: Single small box of 7 packets (total weight is 4.34 ounces
text: I placed two orders for these nuts which I had first received from a friend who purchased them locally and I liked them as offering a little more than just a tiny bag of salted nuts.  The price was great for what I thought was 12 packages of 7 individual packs of cashews, so I purchased two cartons to take to my local firefighters, knowing that they appreciate the other goodies I've given them over the past few months.  Unfortunately, I just received two single small boxes of 7 individual packs in an envelope which is bad, but worse than that is that they both expired in October, nearly two months ago.  Oh, yes, one more thing.  One is the jalapeno as ordered and the other is roasted and salted but both are expired nuts.  I'm rating these as a 2 because I liked them when they were fresh, are a small size  that fits in the pocket, and they are slightly spiced which is a good option for those on the go who want protein with more than salt added.  A misleading description and expired product, puts this on my do not purchase here list.  I wish I'd read the reviews before I placed the orders instead of after they were already shipped.

title: Stale crackers, most are split in two pieces and soft
text: I purchased and received a case of 150 individual sized packets of Zesta oyster crackers which, according to Kellogg's who handles questions for them, expired the month prior to my even ordering these.  Normally, they are tasty and not very salty, crisp to eat out of the lightweight bag as a snack or put onto soup or salad.  These were stale which is why I investigated the best by date which is in a code on the box.  There is no information on the bags regarding dating.  Most of the oyster crackers are split in two, soft, and quick to become glue when consumed.  I'm going to try toasting some in the oven to see if that improves the texture.  I don't know why these are labeled as "Large" oyster crackers because they are the same as what I've purchased locally.

title: For those with no self control......
text: I have a problem.  When I open a bag of Goldfish crackers, they call to me and I find myself grabbing a few every time I pass the bag on the counter.  With these small bags, I can enjoy the bag by myself all at once and feel no guilt.  My favorite is the rainbow option and I find the pretzels to be a little underwhelming.  This was surprising because I also usually love pretzels.  I guess I'm a purist who enjoys the cheesy flavor of Goldfish crackers and the hard crust of pretzels but isn't moved by the blending into a single product.

title: Bitty sizes for kids to enjoy
text: I sent a box of these little bits of cookies and crackers to a preschooler for his class after I confirmed that they did not have a peanut free zone established as had been enforced in his previous school.  Each bag was just the right amount of little treats and the only problem was that they were not the freshest.

title: Emergency sauce when time is of the essence
text: I don't usually purchase or use sauces because I love creating my own, but couldn't pass up buying a jar of this Spicy Madras Curry to have on hand for an emergency.  Well, I had no emergency, but I did have a couple of eggplants, a winter squash, and some cremini mushrooms on this gloomy day, so I turned them all into a really delicious meal that was so tasty that I was reluctant to share.  I gave the vegetables several minutes in a little bit of preheated avocado oil in a Dutch oven and added the jar of sauce, a russet potato and a little water, covered and cooked until the potato was tender to a fork touch.  Wanting to test the sauce's true colors, I added no salt or other spices before tasting.  This was delicious, especially after I added a tad of cardamom.  I added no salt because it's salty enough as is.  Being that I prefer hot and spicy foods, I found this sauce to have a little heat but I would not consider it as a truly spicy product.  Next time, I'd add cardamom to the protein or vegetables earlier as well as peppers and maybe finish off with a little wedge of lime for a sour kick.

title: Not as good as the boxes
text: When I was younger, I loved making the boxed Kraft Mac and Cheese (orange), usually adding frozen peas to the mac when it was nearly cooked.  My sisters and I could finish off a box as a snack in the afternoon, we never had it as a serious meal.  I don't know that Mom and Dad ever tasted it, but we sure enjoyed the fast, easy hot snack that was fun to pick at with a fork, often directly from the pot.  My family still enjoys the boxed Kraft mac and cheese, adding peas, broccoli, or kale, always finishing with garlic and pepper.  We've tried other boxed mac and cheese packages and none compares, even after decades of attempts.  Finding a pack of these Kraft Deluxe Easy Mac White Cheddar Macaroni and Cheese at an insanely good price, I purchased them for the kids because they like to receive individual sized servings of foods from me.  The last mac and cheese cups were not good at all, made by another manufacturer.  These are okay, not terrible, and they can be improved with condiments if you want to spend the time trying to improve bland and pasty mac and cheese that fills about 1/3 of the cup.  For an emergency, they are acceptable if you have a microwave, as a meal of mac and cheese, we all prefer the original blue boxes over these cups and would not purchase them again even at an insanely good price.

title: Light and tasty decaf chai tea blend
text: I like the Twinnings Decaf Chai teabags for a light afternoon tea with cookies.  There is no bitterness and the light blend of spices kicks up the decaf black tea a notch.  It is improved by a little milk and sweetener of choice.  I like heavier notes in my chai tea usually, but this blend works rather well for a decaf option.  Each bag is not very heavily filled, sealed inside a packet of its own, and they don't fall apart when steeped or pulled out of the cup.

title: Disappointing flavors
text: Small bags of potato chips help me out because I have no self control when it comes to chips in the house.  I can't tell you why, but the chips in these bags are small, curled, and despite having a best buy date that's a couple months in the future, they do not taste fresh.  The vinegar flavor is particularly stale and many of them are simply little bits.  It's almost as thought the oil is rancid but we can't quite figure out why these chips are simply off.  Cape Cod Potato Chips are usually really good but this particular box was not.

title: Pretty good to munch on
text: The kids enjoyed a box of the cereal, more as a munchy snack in a cup than as a cereal with milk meal.  Although they enjoyed the puffs, they do prefer others but I won't hold that against these.  If you like sweeter over savory in a puffy snack, this is a good option.

title: Gifting these with a jar of peanut butter
text: I was going to purchase some peanut butter filled crackers for our maintenance staff and then realized that by purchasing these family sized boxes, each containing 6 sleeves of crackers, I could get peanut butter and they enjoy having as many as they want.  I've been told that it's not unusual for them to have half a sleeve on a lunch break and they prefer this since they claim it's fresher.  I've also given them small packets of tuna and cheese if they want to up it a notch and it's been a great success.  I find that the current Ritz cracker formula produces a lighter, more flaky texture, so I personally don't feel weighted down after enjoying a portion.

title: Box of cracker sand
text: I first had these crackers when I worked at the Green Festival and went crazy purchasing them for a few years.  It's been a few since I've had them, so before buying a big box, ordered one of the 6.5 ounce size.  I received a box of cracker sand, not crackers.  There is not a single intact cracker in the 6.5 ounces of crumby mess.  Since there aren't as many seeds as I recall, I will be using these as a coating for sauteed protein I guess because they are not useful as a cracker.  I've transferred these into a mason jar and am keeping them in the refrigerator.

title: Pretty good
text: I received a single can of artichoke bottoms with a pull top lid, not 3 cans as described.  These are pretty good and very versatile in salads, marinades, sandwiches, or cooked in a hot skillet or saucepan.  Half the fun of eating artichokes, in my opinion, is peeling off the leaves to reach the bottom of the vegetable, and with these, you don't have to do a thing.  I wonder what they do with the longer stems from these artichokes, another part I really enjoy eating.  I'll bet that if you marinate these and marinate some hearts of palm, they would be very close in a blind taste test.

title: A bit crumbly at times
text: I purchased Walkers Shortbread Highland Oat Crackers, 9.9 Ounce Box in a six-pack and the carton arrived in perfect condition with a reasonably distant best by date imprinted on each box.  The crackers are a little more crumbly than I recall, but the taste is what I expected in an oat cracker of this style.  The texture is consistent, not varying from bite to bite or cracker to cracker, and like others, they really need an accompaniment and don't do well when eaten in their simple dry format.  A soft texture and/or sweet topping do very well with these and they can really be adorned without worry that they won't hold.  I personally don't weigh them down so their texture can be enjoyed without the topping.  I appreciate that these each contain 4 individually wrapped packets so they will stay fresher.  I also store the opened crackers in the refrigerator.

title: Tangy sauce is versatile
text: I'd forgotten about Pickapeppa Original Hot Sauce for decades.  In the mid-70's, a coworker of mine from New Orleans brought a bottle of the stuff and an 8 ounce block of Philadelphia Cream Cheese to a gathering at the beach, put the cheese on a paper plate, poured the sauce onto it and served it with a box of crackers.  I don't remember what kind of crackers but I think they were Wheat Thins because I can visualize the yellow box.  At the time, I thought it was the best thing I'd eaten that day and I purchased a bottle the next time I was at the grocery store.  I had not tasted this again until last week after I purchased a bottle from Amazon.  I know the sauce can be used for so many things, but I put some Nancy's Organic Cream Cheese on a spoon and covered it with Pickapeppa Original Hot Sauce, then slipped it into my mouth.  It was as good as I'd remembered, perhaps even better because I didn't have the cracker to interrupt the smoothness of this duo.  The next day, I put some on my breakfast egg and it was just as tasty.

title: Crispy and smooth when combined
text: I have not purchased Ritz crackers in many years and have never purchased cheese in a can.  A friend gave me some of his homemade mac and cheese with Ritz crackers on top and I felt the immediate need to buy a box.  I came across this package deal of crackers and a couple of cans of cheese and it was a no brainer during these unusual times.  It was interesting that the crackers expire three months sooner than the cheese, and since I had no frame of reference as to which would be consumed first, I figured that we could always use other crackers with the cheese.  Ritz crackers are crisp and buttery, fitting into the mouth as one entire bite if wanted or bitten in pieces if that works best for you.  Since the cans of cheese don't need to be refrigerated, we did not feel the need to eat it in one sitting.  I actually gave one away with a couple of the Ritz cracker sleeves so the kids could make their own cheese cracker sandwiches.  The consensus is that this is a winning package which will be a repurchase when the price is right.  I only wish the cheese did not taste as salty as it does.  It is fun to dispense and eat, especially for kids, but by no means takes the place of cheese not from a can.

title: Cute itty bitty treats
text: The kids like the cookies and crackers but they often want more than one bag.  Youngsters can go through the bag rather quickly, especially since they can pop one little treat in their mouth without having to bite anything, just chew them.  We're making them last longer by having them practice their counting.  Adults likely would find these lacking because they are only a single ounce in small bits.

title: Great spice blend
text:
I usually don't use spice blends which contain salt, especially when it's the first ingredient, but being a pepper and garlic lover, ordered a single can of Slap Ya Mama All Natural Cajun Seasoning from Louisiana Original Blend from Amazon. The blend is great and fresh tasting, however the paper canister was covered with stickers which obstructed almost everything on it. Additionally, the dispensing disk is not sitting properly, so it does not seal the freshness and I've had to transfer the blend into another spice jar. Next time, I'll purchase this locally I hope.

The peppery spice adds oomph to anything food on which I've used it. I'm not a fan of very salty foods, so I add none until after I've Slapped some of this stuff into the dish and tasted it first. It's wonderful as a simple popcorn seasoning, french fry enhancement, or just a tad on a bowl of cottage cheese. It's good as long as it's fresh.

title: Very salty for my taste
text: Being very curious about the SkinnyPop product line, I purchased a bag of the 100 calorie individual portioned bags in the White Cheddar variety for us and had one sent to the kids which I cancelled.  The bags are nice and small and the popcorn looks white and fluffy in the bag.  Well, I should say that about 75% looks white and fluffy and the remaining 25% are tiny broken pieces which exaggerate the salty taste because of the coating method, I guess.  There are also a number of unpopped kernels, so warn the kids.  They use rice flour and milk free cheddar flavoring with the salt and stuff.  Had I not known what flavor I purchased and read the bag to confirm I received what I ordered, I would have thought these are butter flavor, but that's not a terrible thing.  I have never purchased a larger bag of SkinnyPop popcorn, so I don't know if the high small piece proportion is normal or if this is just a characteristic of the smaller bags, but I'm not going to purchase these again.  I'm happy that I was able to cancel the second order before it shipped and kicked myself for ordering before I tasted them myself.  I was wondering why only one small bag was eaten in the month we've had them and now I know why.

title: Small white popcorn kernels do have hulls
text: The first batch of Snappy White Popcorn I made in my Whirley Pop produced a number of unpopped kernels.  The second batch was terrific after I'd determined that I needed to increase the flame.  Every one since then has been great and I've experienced a mere few kernels that could not be enjoyed.  These are not the large mushroom type popcorn kernels, but closer to the artisanal type of small kernels that tend to be more flavorful.  The pure white popcorn is attractive and it shows off any added seasonings very beautifully.  I like the screw top jar with a built in handle but have found I prefer freezing popcorn to enhance freshness and poppability, so I transfer some to an airtight bag for that purpose.  For me the only negative is that the small hulls often find their way to my gum line, so I have to keep a dental pick/flosser nearby.

title: Peanut Butter Spread's convenience becomes inconvenient
text: I ordered these enticing packets very quickly and did not read the ingredient list or the reviews and that is my own fault.  Had I read the reviews and looked at the customer photos, I would not have ordered.  I placed two orders for these, one as a gift and one for myself and both arrived in similar condition.  Both arrived in plastic envelopes with the boxes flattened and loose packets in the envelope.  One order contained the full amount of 10 and the other order contained 8 out of 10.  Especially in the current era, it's off-putting to receive opened food items in the mail because one does not know where it's been or who touched it before it reached your home.  The biggest disappointment, however, was expecting peanut butter and receiving a product with vivid printed labeling as, "Peanut Butter Spread."  I personally don't purchase peanut butter spread filled crackers and purchased these as a protein source for day hikes with the kids.  Unfortunately, the product does not taste good and it's unappealing to look at.  Sure, you can knead the packet first to combine the oil with the solids but tell that to a three year old who wants it right now and starts ripping it open, allowing the oil to squirt out all over him and his protective not much older brother.  You end up with two unhappy kids and you are irritated because you did not bring enough stuff to clean up oily people and clothes.  I would not purchase these again online or in my neighborhood grocery store because the packets' convenience turns out to be very inconvenient and the product does not taste good.

title: Sour gnocchi
text: We love potato gnocchi and because I really like the Cucina & Amore dried Cannelinni Beans so much, I took a chance and purchased their brand of potato gnocchi for dinner this week.  I prepared the package which is quite fresh as directed and served them as I usually do, with olive oil, freshly shredded parmesan cheese and ground pepper.  This time, I prepared a fresh cabbage which was delicious, but when served together, everyone reacted the same.  This is by far the worst tasting gnocchi.  It looks lovely, little pillows of what should be potato forward flavors, but that is not the case.  It was reluctantly eaten and will not be purchased again.

title: Salty and Oily
text: I will not purchase Santa Cruz peanut butter again.  I was prepared that it might be more oily than I like, but I was able to stir it for several minutes to obtain a creamy, homogenous consistency which I suspected would become more firm in the refrigerator.  It did.  The peanuts are of a light roast and there was not a speck of solid peanut in the mixture.  Where this lost it for everyone who tried it was in the salty taste which even overpowered the taste of the peanuts.  This is definitely a more expensive peanut butter so I expected much more peanut flavor than what's in the glass jar.

title: Sweet and milky
text: There are no live cultures in this product and no reference whatsoever to cultures at all other than it being made of, "Cultured Reduced Fat Milk" as the first ingredient.  I love the GoGo fruit and vegetable products but this one is not worth the purchase.  Thankfully, I only purchased a package of 4 pouches because each of the 4 people who consumed one after refrigeration said they would have rather had a pouch of milk.  I would have rated these as a 2 but everyone else thought they were a 1, so the majority ruled. They were made in France.

title: Salt flavor, not banana
text: I find the texture of the purely elizabeth Grain-Free & Gluten-Free Granola, Banana Nut Butter to be appealing and nothing else is good.  There is no taste whatsoever of banana but an overpowering taste of salt. I had to reread the ingredients because I thought that I'd made a mistake.  There is a good texture, it responds to chewing very well, but the only taste I get is salt.  The granola looks excellent when put in the bowl and that's about it for a positive.  I will never purchase this again and would not serve it to family, friends or guests.  It's simply not good.

title: Enough to share if you dare, size is ideal for many culinary needs
text: A serving is 1/4 a cup, 28 grams, or an ounce of the contents.  Each of the eight packages contains 2.5 ounces, two and a half servings of delicious mildly salted shelled pistachio nuts, so the box houses 20 servings if you get technical.  You can buy them in individual servings, shelled or with shells to make it easy, but I purchased this box of nuts because I sometimes need 1/4 cup for a recipe.  A single bag is great to have on hand when you have the urge to assemble a trail mix concoction using residuals, and by opening the sealed bag, you up the chances of having great tasting pistachios in your mix.  My only complaint about the Wonderful Pistachios products that is consistent across the line is that the images in the packaging graphics look nothing like what it is inside the package.  For me, the effect is negative because I experience disappointment with the visual.  Fortunately, they taste good on most occasions.

title: Stir constantly for perfect pudding
text: It's been decades since I purchased a box of pudding mix.  I've only purchased the JELL-O brand, so this, of course, is the one I selected for purchase last week.  You see, I had a half-gallon of whole milk in the refrigerator and I needed to use it for something other than yogurt.  Now I read the label in the photos and missed the artificial flavoring text because I was drawn to the more prominent text below which boasts a few positive characteristics.  Since I had six cartons, it was either give them away or try a package to see how artificial it tasted.  The first package made a soft and creamy, very flavorful treat of four 1/2 servings of pudding.  I've since discovered a number of recipes that rely on this butterscotch pudding which I'll create next for the kids.  This pudding should be retailing for about a buck and change tops each four-serving package and I would pay no more.

title: Taste is relative, this is lower shelf to mine
text: I recently purchased a box of 20 organic peppermint tea bags by this brand which I found disappointing but I wanted to give them another chance since I did enjoy some Taylors teas years ago.  I wanted to try a different breakfast tea and after reading many reviews, decided to purchase a box of 50 Taylors of Harrogate Scottish Breakfast teabags.  Malty, bold, rich is what many said, so as a lover of malty Scotch Whiskys, I thought this would be right up my alley.  I was wrong and in a big way.  It's not a terrible tea, it is just not what I would describe as a bold or malty beverage.  It steeps as a dark brown beverage, however, after steeping for 4 minutes, 4 1/2 minutes, or 5 minutes, each cup is rather benign.  There is no discernible malt and it is far from bold.  In fact, to my surprise, I personally detect a stronger sour taste than anything else and there is only a minimal aroma from the tea. The tannins are not excessive, and since I'm not a fan of high level tannins, that's just fine.  What I do not like is the lack of flavor.  The box I received has a best by date of about a year and a half from now, so this is not an old box of tea.  As with other boxes of Taylors teas, these are a pair of square paper teabags that are perforated at the center and can be easily pulled apart for single teabag use.  The box is very lightweight, crushable with minimal effort (as during the fulfillment process) and it's sealed in lightweight cellophane.  The bags are not wrapped and they are compostable.

title: My order was a bad batch but the tuna is usually wonderful
text: We have been enjoying Ortiz Bonito Del Norte Tuna In Olive OIl for a few years, purchasing it locally.  I recently purchased a case of 12 cans and they were simply not good.  They were mushy, not the firm white flesh of tuna which we'd enjoyed on salads or with white beans and red onions.  I've deducted a star from what would have otherwise been a five-star product review had the case I received been up to par, but there is clearly something wrong with this particular case.  Each can looked beautiful with no dents or leakage, it's just the product that was inside the can that was not good.  I found no best by or production date anywhere on either the cans or the carton, so perhaps this was just a case that had been stored improperly or was sold out of date.  Nevertheless, I will continue to purchase this usually delicious tuna locally because it is better than most, having a light flavor, light color, packed in a clear, flavorful olive oil with a hint of salt.  Atop of a salad, it usually looks beautiful and tastes even better, especially when I include the olive oil in a dressing.  This is not a tuna I mix with mayo.

title: Far from gourmet but they hit the spot
text: I purchased several of these to distribute to folks who need a pick me up without a lot of unhealthy additives.  Too many cookies I've purchased arrived in crumbled condition, but these all arrived intact and for some strange reason, each box was shipped in its own envelope.  In this time of distancing, I'm not baking for folks as I used to do but I want them to have a little something sweet that is free of human hands touching the food.  Each package has four relatively small sandwich cookies that take the edge off of a hungry person and I can't tell you how quickly the boxes I purchased disappeared.  They are a pick me up for the person delivering your next package, and this little kindness doesn't break the bank.  I was told that these are preferred to the little packages of nuts because the saltiness brought on thirst more quickly than these cookies.

title: I'm an adult and love GoGo squeeZ
text: I've been purchasing a lot of the GoGo squeeZ products and have been willing to share.  From this one, the most simple applesauce to the blastZ with cherries, I now always have them on hand in the refrigerator, freezer and pantry.  Let's say you have fasted for bloodwork and don't want to carry something heavy with you to the lab for sustenance as soon as you can eat or drink, these are perfect because you can even slip it underneath your mask and drink/eat it the second as that blood is drawn and you don't have to wait until you get into your car to enjoy the applesauce.  The only problem with these is that people will ask you if you have one for them.  They are also great to remove from the freezer, squish with your warm hands after a few minutes, and you have a fruit slush.  I love them.

title: Crunchy tidbits are not hot at all and have minimal spice
text: If I did not know I purchased gluten-free pretzel bits, I would have no idea that these morsels are free of wheat.  They are firm, covered in flavorings, and delightfully, not spicy enough to warrant a warning.  I purchased a case to share with a friend with celiac disease and was assigned the task of tasting them first to assure that they would not be too spicy.  They are not.  Every person who has had a bag thus far is quite impressed.  I already liked Snyder's of Hanover wheat pretzels, so it is a pleasant surprise to see that they also produce enjoyable gluten-free pretzels.  These do have a substantial amount of sodium in the seasoning, so this is a consideration for those who need to reduce sodium intake.  There isn't a way to remove the salt as one might do with salted pretzels where you can rub it off of the surface area.

title: Finely ground organic nonGMO cardamom
text: The quality of the ground cardamom removed from the manufacturer's bottle is good but I won't purchase it again.  There is no identification of the source of the product but there is a clearly visible best by date.  The jar was so sticky from the Amazon labels but it wasn't an issue since I had to put the spice in an empty Penzey's jar since the cap was cracked.  There is a safety seal preventing tampering or spillage even with a cracked flip-top lid.  Of note also is that the holes in the lid are very large, so with finely ground contents, it's not easy to disperse just a tad.  By transferring the cardamom to another spice jar, I've remedied all the problems.  It tastes like cardamom, smells like cardamom, and feels like finely ground cardamom when touched with the fingers.  I usually grind my seeds from pods but was interested in the organic option of a uniformly ground spice and find McCormick to be a readily available, reliable source for spices and herbs.

title: Excellent water cracker option
text: I purchased a case of these for my nephew who loves water crackers, but by the time they arrived, he had already purchased some of the more major brand crackers.  No problem, though, cause we love crackers in this household and this being sesame made them even more desirable.  They are not as expensive as that major brand and about the same as TJ's crackers, and most grocery chains sell their own version of water crackers for a couple of bucks or more per box.  I'm happy to report that these are really, really good crackers even though I'd rather they had a few more sesame seeds.  They are not at all salty, are neither hard nor crumbly, and they hold your toppings without cracking.  Yes, some of them in the box are broken in two, but that seems to happen to any water cracker box I've ever opened and I've opened a lot during my time as a food demo person in another time.  I'd buy these again and would not hesitate to serve them to people I care about.

title: Each can was worst than the last
text: I've now made my final purchase of The Peanut Shop of Williamsburg products.  In this trio, each opened can was worse than the one before.  These are really terrible, and some ended up in the trash rather than refrigerator where they were saved for alternative uses than simply out of the can.  The box of three certainly looks good, it's the contents that are lousy.

title: Must LOVE Old Bay Seasoning
text: We opened the bag of chips in Baltimore and all thought these were way overkill with the Old Bay Seasoning.  Fortunately, we had our cold locally brewed craft IPA's opened and ready to join the party.  The first chip hit was a heavy celery seed at the tip of the tongue, followed by a slight sourness, ending with a peppery stun that lingered after the chips had embarked upon the digestive adventure.  The potatoes are thinly sliced, had an oil that was more than enough to allow for the seasoning powder to adhere to the chips.  Some were so thickly coated that they could not be eaten.  I have not yet but can imagine using these chips as the seasoning in fish cakes, most obviously using crab, bypassing a breading product like crackers, panko, oats or bread, and completely eliminating any Old Bay Seasoning or any of its components.  Other than that, these chips are far from the top of my potato chip loves but not at the bottom either.  This flavor has not enticed me to try any of the other Herr's varieties because they were a disappointment at a high price point choice for a potato-based snack food.

title: Bland, tasteless, yucky, made it to the trash
text: When I have peanuts that are not the best, I try to come up with alternative uses in the kitchen so as to not waste them.  I did not purchase the large can of these nuts, but rather a trio of The Peanut Shop of Williamsburg peanuts in three different pepper varieties.  The habanero variety was very salty and peppery hot, but not wonderful, so I turned it into a Thai inspired paste by grinding them and replacing the peanut butter and Thai pepper with these.  I covered Tempeh in the paste and the finished product was quite good.  These jalapeno nuts, on the other hand, were soft, tasteless, had virtually no heat to them, and they made it to the trash can, something I rarely do with any food.  I was surprised to note that the interior of the can was weird, having the coating buckled and even separating from the can.  I would not recommend purchasing these nuts at any cost.

title: Terrible, terrible Milanos are crummy, literally & figuratively
text:
UPDATE: The double milk chocolate Milanos arrived and the box looked perfect. The bags looked perfect. The best by date was nearly two months away. We opened the first bag and the cookies looked terrible. The color is pale, texture is soft, nearly mushy, chocolate may be double but it is dry and tasteless with bits scattered in the paper cups and foil-lined bag. I recently purchased a 3 pack of the Mint Milanos and figured that even in bits and pieces, they were ok mixed in ice cream and gave them a 3-star review. If these two types of Milanos are representative of the current Milano cookies, they are off of my purchase list and I would recommend them for nothing. They are terrible. My original review follows which was a sarcastic suggestion of seeing the positive in bits and pieces of cookies, assuming that what I received was not representative of all Milanos:

The Pepperidge Farm Milano Mint Cookies are darn tasty and I'm happy to have purchased the packages of 3 bags of 15 cookies each (that's not 8 servings if the serving is listed as 2 cookies) because since they are all (yes, all) are in pieces, they must have no calories, no fat, no sugar, no sodium and I guess, no nutritional value. But, you don't have to bite most of them because they slip right into even the smallest of mouths and you don't even really need teeth so if my dog could have chocolate without becoming gravely ill, even the toothless sweetie pie could have a cookie part. You know, the minty flavor in the chocolate sort of makes these cookie parts like having a cookie and feeling like you've just brushed your teeth, too. In reality, though, the cookies do indeed have calories, fat, sugar and sodium even though they aren't in the form I assume they entered the bags, and you did not brush your teeth after eating one of these, it just has a minty flavor. They are lighter in texture than traditional Milano cookies, so perhaps that's why the don't survive the transportation leg of their marketing journey. Because they are light, they are very good and even if they are not fully shaped and formed Milano cookies out of the bag, they can easily be mixed into ice cream instead of dunking one into a cup of coffee, tea, or hot cocoa.

title: Order from illy authorized seller
text: After I placed my order, I read some of the reviews and checked out some of the images showing dented cans of the illy Classico roast coffee cans I'd just ordered.  I'll admit that I worried about receiving old coffee, dented cans, 5 cans instead of 6, and even more awful things than what customers claimed in their reviews.  I'm happy to report that I received perfect cans in a perfect illy box that was inside a newfangled Amazon box, and judging from the one can pulled from the middle of the box, coffee that tastes and performs exactly as I expected.  I've purchased several types if illy coffee, both ground and in bean form and decided that for my purposes which include assorted methods of preparation and limited refrigerator space, a case of 6 cans of beans was the way to go.  I grind my beans for each use and store the opened container in the refrigerator to preserve its freshness and I also repurpose these emptied cans for a multitude of uses.  As with my Nespresso capsules, I want the coffee to be fresh, sealed and have had no oxygen touch the coffee until I use the capsule or open the can.

title: Such good basic black tea
text: I would not order the Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Gold, 160 Teabags again because it arrived days late and in terrible condition.  Now, this would not be such a big deal, but checking the other photos from customers, I see that this is not a one of a kind situation.  The actual tea bags are a very good, very popular black tea that is flavorful and drinkable either hot or iced, with or without added sweeteners, lemon or milk.  There is no waste because the bags are packaged in two bag increments without string, tab or wrapper.  Unfortunately, the box I received was smashed, open, and I cannot read the best by or lot production information on the box because it is so crumpled at exactly that spot.  I will purchase this in smaller amounts in my local grocery store because this is simply a waste of good tea and paper.

title: Nasty nuts
text: These are not like The Peanut Shop of Williamsburg Handcooked Virginia Peanuts which I've purchased in the past since I first had them in Williamsburg after moving to the state.  They are not "super extra-large" and they are chalky.  I loved blistered peanuts and these are simply not good.  Unfortunately, I purchased 2 of the colonial-style drum style, expecting the tins to be imprinted with the drum, not just have a partially glued on label with a graphic of a drum which also has Amazon stickers defacing what remains of the drum image.  This is on both cans, not just one.  The sticker is rather large on the can which is rather small and it cannot be removed, so the tin cannot be effectively washed after emptied or the "colonial style drum" will be rendered into pieces of paper hanging onto a simple metal can.  If at least the peanuts tasted good, I could write this off as a disappointment in the package, but since the peanuts are even worse than the container, it's a double whammy squared since I purchased 2 cans as gifts for little drummers who love peanuts.

title: Happy kids and then some
text: I sent this assortment as a gift and it was very well received.  Because I just learned that some others have received assortments that are not the OREO, CHIPS AHOY! & Nutter Butter Cookie Variety Pack, Family Size, 3 Packs which I ordered, I asked the recipient and have received confirmation that this order was delivered containing the assortment as described.  I personally have not had a Chips Ahoy cookie in many years, but these are the store-bought manufactured cookies that my mother always purchased, so I know them quite well.  Oreos were a favorite of all of my sisters, but I preferred the chips ahoy.  They also liked the icing on cupcakes while I ate the cake.  I ate only the egg yolk and they savored the white of hard-boiled eggs.  I convinced my younger sister to trade her crispy chicken skin for my skinned chicken legs.  I've gotten off track here, sorry.  I sent these cookies as a gift because the recipients love Nutter Butter cookies which I have never tasted.  This assortment was more interesting than sending them a single bag of cookies and since they are a family of five, the cookies will all be enjoyed even if they are in bits and pieces.  They have not yet opened the Chips Ahoy which, according to other reviewers may arrive broken, so I alerted them of that possibility and suggested that they enjoy them in a bowl with milk just as they eat cereal if that's the case with their shipment.  The cookies are well known and top-selling cookies by the Nabisco division of Mondelez International.

title: Blueberries?
text:
For the texture of this mix, the Bunnery Natural Foods Pancake and Waffle Mix, Wild Blueberry, 18-Ounce Package
has earned five stars and for everything else, it's zilch. A package produced thirteen large pancakes and about half had a single blueberry and half did not. Since I was making pancakes and not waffles and utilizing my decades of pancake making experience, I knew to add a little more milk to achieve the proper consistency. Some pancakes had rancid sunflower seeds but most had good tasting sunflower seeds. The millet added a delicious taste and crunch to an otherwise unremarkable product. The price is very high. I sent a message to the company two weeks ago regarding the lack of blueberries as I wondered if the bag I received was a fluke by using their website form option and have heard nothing back.

title: Robust?
text: I regrettably purchased two bottles of Crown Maple Syrup with Robust Flavor Bourbon Barrel Aged LTD Edition 25 FL OZ.  One was for my household and the other was a gift sent to my favorite person and her family.  I never saw it at Costco, but was persuaded by the numerous raving reviews with mention of it being sold and disappearing from Costco shelves, repeat purchasers, and the appealing company website.  Yes, it is delivered in a thick cardboard box, nice and secure in the exterior Amazon box.  Yes, the bottle resembles a top-shelf bottle of bourbon or whiskey with a sealed plastic stopper and classic bottle label.  True, the glass is thick and heavy, worthy of positioning at eye level so it's clearly visible when the refrigerator door is opened (refrigerate after opening) and easy to grab when you're ready to mix into a cocktail, include in a recipe, or use as a syrup for pancakes, waffles or French toast.  What I regret about the purchases is that the syrup is very thin in viscosity, not much thicker than bourbon itself, perhaps a shade darker, and it's not robust.  I find it to be rather bland, having only a hint of maple flavor.  It does, however, have the distinct bourbon essence from its storage in used wood bourbon barrels and that is a tasty enhancement.  This does not compensate for the initial visual impression of the bottle/box being greater than the overall taste of the maple syrup.  I'm reviewing only the bottle we received and not the one which I had sent as a gift.  Being that they both were purchased within two minutes of each other and were sent from the same location, I can only assume that they were from the same batch.  The only difference was that mine traveled across the country in a UPS truck for several days and the other was sent in an airplane and traveled only for a day.  I expect bourbon barrel-aged maple syrup to be more expensive due to the aging process and the packaging costs for this final product are high quality, but sorry, for the price of this maple syrup I received, I have to give it an average rating.

title: Bitter ketchup likely due to storage
text: Since I was a young person, Heinz Tomato Ketchup was the ketchup of choice in our family.  Now I must confess that I am more a mustard fan and user than a ketchup or mayonnaise loving person, so a single bottle usually lasts a long time unless I'm making barbeque sauce out of it.  I made this purchase because it's Heinz, it had no added sugar, it was offered at a very good price and I intended to share with my family members and friends who are also avoiding high fructose corn syrup and had already tried this product.  The case of 6 looked perfect upon arrival but the first bottle ketchup did not taste good.  The consistency was runny and the flavor was bitter.  I removed the seal on a second bottle and the ketchup tasted the same.  I then made contact with Kraft Foods, the manufacturer of Heinz products, and they responded very quickly.  Because of the communicative customer service representative, I'm rating this as an average product and once I purchase it in a brick and mortar store, should I find it to be a better product, I'll up the rating.  I'll still keep purchasing the Hot and Spicy Heinz Ketchup because it's so tasty that I often use in place of hot sauce and that says a lot.

title: Pasta looks good and tastes better
text: Fusilli pasta is good but Ferrara Long Fusilli pasta is great.  It's thick and when coated with a sauce, becomes slurpy.  I was going to make mac and cheese this week but received this case of 12 pounds of pasta so decided to make a sauce instead and hold off on the mac and cheese until next week.  This is a great decision because I discovered that since this holds a sauce so well, it's going to be used in a cheesy baked dish which will delight many.  Truth be told, I purchased this pasta because of its appearance, not because I'd eaten it before or had a specific recipe in mind.  After preparing the first pound which makes a lot, I have ideas like adding shellfish on top of a tomato-based sauce, the aforementioned pasta and cheese, a simple homemade pesto coating, just to mention a few.  I cooked this for 11 minutes and found that to be a good time for enjoying freshly cooked as well as when reheated.  Picky kids who only want pasta, butter, and cheese will likely really enjoy the curly, thick spaghetti-like pasta that they can twirl on a fork and get a really full mouthful to fill their belly.  The creative souls can even braid it for fun if it's been coated with oil first (yes, I tried) and then it really is fun to eat.  This pasta definitely needs something tasty to bring out its purpose as a vehicle for sauce.  Eating it on its own is not my personal cup of tea, but you may like that.  Due to its density, it can be very filling, so I serve it in smaller portions.  Oh yes, don't forget the parmesan!

title: Crisp smoky chips of joy
text: I've been eating more chips in the past couple of months than probably my entire life.  The reason is that once I open a bag, I have difficulty not hearing it call my name to have just one or two more until the bag is empty and in the trash.  I've been purchasing the one-ounce bags in assorted varieties by numerous manufacturers and these Kettle Brand Potato Chips have won my heart.  I purchased a case of the 1.5-ounce bags and am sincerely trying to split it into two servings but if I'm not successful, I've only eaten an ounce and a half.  Now, these are very smoky, slightly sweet and salty, but mostly smoky, so I'm more than happy.  I've not experienced unsealed bags or bags of crushed potato chips, but then I have not yet gone through each bag in this first case.  I'd say that these chips run second only to Tyrrell's Hand Cooked English Crisps which I first had several years ago.  Actually, I think I like this better because the flavoring is not as intense.

title: Small container
text: I sent this as a gift and unfortunately, the recipients received a single small bin of the YumEarth tasty lollipops instead of the five containers of 6 ounces each which were purchased.  It was packaged in a huge box which I was told was quite funny.  I've been purchasing the YumEarth lollipops for more than a decade because they are so tasty and easy to slip into a pocket or bag and always have them on hand to enjoy and share but this is not the way I'd recommend purchasing them.  Alternatively, I'd recommend purchasing the 5-pound assortment bag to get all of the flavors, keep them in an airtight container, and use a smaller container for a couple dozen at a time.  You could even have the kids decorate one that's easy to open.  If you don't need that many lollipops, they are also available in smaller sized bags of around 3 ounces, I believe, so you can get a half dozen of those and keep them fresh until you replenish your candy jar or jug.  I'm attaching a photo of what was received so you can see what flavors are included as of today.  By the way, YumEarth hard candies are also excellent, especially the peppermint variety.

title: Crisp, crunchy and they don't crumble
text: I was concerned that these gluten-free crackers might be soft or crumble when snapped into bite-sized pieces and found them to be as excellent as the Wasa crispbreads with grains that I've been eating for many years.  These are so light but not airy.  I enjoy crispness so I tend to break a piece off and eat it with an accompanying protein and/or fat.  At 50 calories each, I could actually consume an entire packet of 3 but limit myself if possible.  There's space in the box because these are not quite as thick as the Wasa crispbreads with grains, so don't be surprised.  I'm loving these, especially with the lightly toasted sesame seeds on top.

title: Strong taste of Stevia
text:
Prior to ordering this large resealable bag of Blue Diamond Oven Roasted Dark Chocolate Almonds, I read the ingredient list and was aware that one of the last ingredients is Stevia. The Blue Diamond has the following ingredients list: ALMONDS, SUGAR, COCOA POWDER (PROCESSED WITH ALKALI), CORN MALTODEXTRIN, NATURAL FLAVOR, SEA SALT, REBIANA (STEVIA EXTRACT).

I love Blue Diamond Almonds but I don't love these. They are fresh, tasty, flavorful roasted almonds as the base, but because the Stevia is a stronger taste than the cocoa coating, there is an unappealing taste that outweighs the almonds and the chocolate. If you've ever had a prepared package of sugar-free hot chocolate or coffee, you know what I'm talking about. This is not even a good option for those who are on a sugar-free diet for health reasons or simply by choice because sugar is listed as the second ingredient and precedes cocoa powder. I thought they would have a bittersweet cocoa flavor and actually wondered why refined Stevia was included when I read the list, but I'm not a chemist or food scientist, so I ordered the nuts, assuming it was to reduce the sugar calories. Unfortunately, the Stevia taste is more forward, middle, and end in the taste profile of these nuts, overpowering the cocoa and they are a disappointment. Nevertheless, they are Blue Diamond almonds and the actual nuts are firm and the thin shell of coating has a good texture. I just don't like the lingering unnatural taste of the added sweetener.

title: Goldfish crackers are still the best, rainbow colors taste earthier
text: I couldn't pass up an Amazon deal on the Rainbow colors six-pack even though I knew their best by date is 3 weeks from the date of purchase.  Because I share these bags with others, I know they will be consumed before the 23rd of August.  What I did not like, however, is that the manufacturer's box which simply had a mailing label and some other stickers plastered on had obviously been bitten into by something that was able to perforate a chunk out of the cardboard and the outer paper lining of one of the bags. (I suspect it was a machine and not an animal.)  Since the interior bag was still sealed,  the Goldfish were not harmed, and I decided to open that torn bag immediately and began counting from 1 to 55 as I put each one into my mouth, and then I stopped because that is a single serving and I didn't want to overeat.  Because I could easily count out another 55 rainbow-colored goldfish when I next notice the bag on my countertop today, perhaps I should write the date in a Sharpie on the paper bag and mark it again after each helping.  I may be imagining it, but these Goldfish have less salt and oil than the extra cheesy Goldfish which I usually buy.  I like this variety even more because, unlike M&M's, I probably will be able to identify the color with my eyes closed if I stop inhaling the 55.  Oh yeah, the kids love these, too.

title: Not as exciting as I recall from decades past
text: It's been quite a while since I purchased Constant Comment, having been a huge fan decades ago when the strings were attached by little staples and each teabag came inside its own packet.  This package of 40 contains 10 sealed paper envelopes which each hold 4 flat teabags.  A 7" string has a paper tab attached and there is nothing other than the pressure sealed paper bag and tea blend which has more clove in it than I remember.  I personally need to steep this longer than the suggested 2 minutes and find that it tastes better with a minimal amount of Italian raw orange blossom honey to enhance the hint of orange rind in the blend.  It's still a tasty tea.

title: Macaroni texture is good, that's about it
text: First of all, some of the 12 cups I received had plastic seals which were separated from the plastic cups, so the white powder coating the macaroni spilled all over and around the 6 packages of 2 cups each, coating interior of the Annie's box.  Maybe it occurred during transit, maybe it occurred while in the Amazon facility, but wherever it occurred, we didn't get to consume those cups.  I did salvage the cheese packets which are separate but included in each cup.  These are simpler than pie to prepare and they take only about 2 minutes in the microwave, a few seconds to stir in the cheese powder, and an additional minute or two to meld together into a single serving of gluten-free mac and cheese made by a company of which I am a fan.  Unfortunately, the solid texture of the pasta doesn't make up for the rather bland taste of the finished product.  It's not salty, so that's a good thing in my opinion, but it really does need additions to turn this into an enjoyable and nutritious meal.  Adding precooked vegetables like broccoli, peas or carrots will be an improvement that most kids can get into, especially if they are cut into small pieces or interesting shapes.  Shredded carrots can be snuck in and will contribute a sweetness for those who shy away from vegetables.  There is plenty of space in the cup since the water fill line is about halfway down from the top and the pasta doesn't swell much when cooked.  I'm glad we tried these but I will not be repurchasing.  All parts of the packaging are recyclable, just separate the paper from the plastic cups and rinse the cups.

title: Can become clumpy so shake it and use it daily
text: It's true that garlic is as good as ten mothers, thank you Les Blank.  This is finely granulated garlic as opposed to powdered garlic which seems to be more common in kitchens in the USA.  Mixed with a small amount of dried parsley and oil, the McCormick California Style Garlic Powder With Parsley Coarse Grind Blend is an excellent product that can simply be sprinkled into scrambled eggs in the skillet or blended into softened butter for easy peasy garlic bread.  Adding parmesan cheese takes it a step even higher.  You can add paprika for color, more parsley for color, and more.  Put some in a small bottle, add herbs and/or spices, and create your own blend.  The 24-ounce size is a great foundation for home kitchens as well as commercial applications, and since it's available here, I say go for it.

title: Large sardines are plain as can be
text: I personally really like sardines but I do not want to have them for every meal.  My dog, on the other hand, adores them and would select them before just about any other food except perhaps TJ's frozen French green beans, her favorite.  I often find sardines have either been overly salted or are drowning in oil in the can, both weaknesses which are not problems with these sardines.  They are great as the protein addition to pasta, salads, spreads, antipasti, or simply eaten out of the can on a slice of bread or cracker.  If you're a dog, following a trick seems to be the most appreciated method of consumption.

title: Planters does peanuts best, other nuts are simply ok
text: I am very curious as to how this can of mixed nuts compares to the Planters Deluxe Mixed Nuts because these are simply average.  The peanuts which are overwhelmingly the majority of the 56 ounces are good, as can be expected by Planters peanuts, but the other nuts are average at best.  Unfortunately, some are rancid despite having a lengthy best by date imprinted on the can.  Freshly opened with the heavy foil seal peeled back only halfway on our gently shaken can, we were surprised to note that there was no visibly heavy salt coating the nuts.  Following the initial taste, came a brief disappointment, but as with any nut in this house, we ate them anyway.  (Double entendre intended.)  Some of the nuts were soft in texture and the mix, in general, benefitted from the peanuts, so perhaps that is why Planters includes very close to 50% in the mix.  I purchased this giant can at a very good price but will not repurchase them even if they are on sale again.  There are simply too many other great nuts available and it's quite easy to put together a mix in a recycled can or jar.  I store all nuts in the refrigerator to preserve freshness and remind us that they exist. (Double entendre NOT intended.)

title: Simply top shelf
text: Luxardo Maraschino Cherries are available locally and I purchase a jar or two when I find them on sale.  In other words, I don't always have them in my jarred cherry arsenal.  I find them to be the absolute best for flavor and texture in a cocktail or atop a bowl of freshly churned ice cream.  The syrup is also a pleasant addition to plain yogurt or a glass of seltzer.  I also find the label to be attractive as it always makes me smile.  I don't know why, it just makes me happy to see a jar of these even when it's on the shelf in a store.

title: Creamy honey is light and flavorful
text: I grew up in Florida and my mother typically purchased orange blossom honey.  At that time, clover honey was the most popular but we had orange blossom honey.  Rigoni di Asiago Mielbio Organic Italian Raw and Creamy Orange Blossom Honey is the only creamy honey I purchase other than local honey and since I've purchased the company's other products, gave this one a chance.  It is so light and tasty that even as a person who does not love honey, I find myself taking a little spoonful to my tongue as I'm passing the jar in the kitchen.  It's great on toast, pancakes or waffles, apple slices with a bit of peanut or almond butter, in a cup of hot water with lemon wedges, in oatmeal or yogurt, or on a slice of lightly sweetened bundt cake that has been heated.  I use larger jars of honey for my baking and cooking, leaving this one for daily use.

title: Wish I'd only bought one can
text: I purchased two cans of The Peanut Shop of Williamsburg Banana Fruit & Nut Snack Mix 10 oz. Tins, one for me and another as a gift.  While The Peanut Shop of Williamsburg typically produces tasty peanuts, this snack mix leaves much to be desired.  Both cans contained two slices of banana and a single almond in addition to a large amount of very, very hard sugar-based crusting which can break a tooth if you bite down thinking that it's a thin shell surrounding an interior peanut.  We found the first can so unappealing that I did not present the second one as a gift.  Despite having an expiration date of twelve months from the date the mix was consumed, some of the nuts tasted a bit off, not spoiled, just not tasty.  I'll continue purchasing the company peanuts but will not purchase and cannot recommend this product.

title: Tasty broth, chunky vegetables, excellent instant ramen
text: I purchased the Veggie variety at a very reasonable price and am quite impressed.  Fortunately, I read the nutritional information prior to having it for lunch, so I realized that the sodium content is way too high, even when I eat the 1/2 package.  You see, this is a 2 serving package.  This is labeled as "Mild" but be advised that although being made in the USA, the style is Korean which is spicier than the Japanese ramen.  The noodles are long, wrapped into a circular form, and are some of the best packaged I've had in an instant type package.  For the first package, I did use the entire granulated spice packet and it makes a very tasty broth, enhanced by the vegetables and fried egg I added.  I have many ideas for using the broth packet, so it won't be wasted.  I will be checking on the price fluctuations for this product because right now, it's much higher than I'd pay in normal times.  The vegan instant soup is likely too spicy for young children who are accustomed to eating the chicken flavored ramen which are so popular in the USA.

title: A little heavy syrup is good in seltzer water
text: I grew up eating canned plums from Eastern Europe, so each time I open one of these cans, I think of Dad who loved them.  There is a permanent spot in my refrigerator for one of these and after I remove the pop-top to enjoy two or three, the rest are stored in a glass jar.  Initially, my intent was to bake a plum cake as Mom did, but I have yet to use these in any baking and have been eating them on a daily basis.  They are much better than prunes,  if you get my drift, and the heavy syrup is excellent in a glass of freshly made seltzer water.  It is very, very sweet, so I only use a little and keep the rest in a separate jar after the plums are gone.  I had planned to freeze some in ice cube trays but have not done that either.  I also have yet to cook it down to turn it into a glaze, but you never know.

title: Chopped leaves
text: The single can (yes, not 4 as advertised) looks just like the images and it is really nice because of an inner cap that should help preserve freshness.  Unfortunately, the first steep of 2 teaspoons of leaves in an 8 ounce cup with nearly boiled fresh water is average and the second steep, even with an additional 2 minutes of brew time, is like flavored water.
