title: Aromatic, full of flavor
text: He likes the Thai style chicken soup a lot but was disappointed that it was considered as two servings since the box appeared so small.  The box is quick to open, no tools are required, and he insists on having both cups of soup for dinner with a little salad.  The flavors are blended well, chicken does not taste like rubber, and he likes that this is a new offering from Amazon.  If I ate chicken, this is the one I would have dipped into because it smells good.  My concern, as with most packaged soups, is that the sodium is higher than in homemade soups, and since he ate the entire box in one sitting, he hit a sodium max.  Because a box of the Wickedly Prime soup can be stored in a cupboard or pantry, this is one to consider having on hand for cold days or those when you just don't feel like cooking. The six pack allows him to have some in the pantry and the office for days when he has pinky the microwave and no time.

title: Weak flavor, cinnamon is the high note
text: As much as I like the first Wickedly Prime tisane I tried, I dislike this rooibos chai.  The overwhelming flavor is cinnamon, the first ingredient on the list of spices.  This one is not a pleasant blend for my tastes and not one I'll pull out of the box.  Like the other, this is in a non-biodegradable yet pretty sheer bag, each is sealed in a heavy cellophane bag, so they will remain fresh and not leak the tea if you carry one for travels.  I may combine this tea with another to still enjoy the spices.

title: Layered flavors in a creamy soup
text: Flavorful, creamy, perhaps the most complex packaged soup I've tried, this was perfect for a quick, hot lunch on a day I was not feeling great.  It awakens the taste buds by being aromatic, ginger and curry coming forward as the apple tames a butternut squash.  The coconut flavor completes the soup that is now on my list of pantry staples.  The small box serving for two is quick to open, just fold the top flat, tear the top at the perforation and squeeze to pour out the soup from one corner.

title: It is all that
text: Yes, it really is a delicious tisane blend.  Each lovely bag is sealed in a thick celo sealed bag that's easy to tear open and the bags are of the non-recyclable type that look pretty, but it tastes really good and makes a nice strong brew in 5 minutes.  It's not as sour as some hibiscus blends I've tried and there is an appealing end note of mint that actually cleanses the mouth.  To top it off, the color is lovely.  It's good hot or cold and this is a great "tea" for days you're not feeling that great.

title: Cheaper and less complex than Nespresso but the best compatible
text: I've tried several compatible capsules for my Nespresso machine and have been disappointed with most. They simply don't compare with the Nespresso capsules in content or construction. They may work fine, but the coffees lack taste, depth, body, and they don't seem to extract the midst from the coffee. I am happy with the Gourmesso capsules, for they work better and the coffee tastes better. I have been using these as the second cup, usually starting off with a Nespresso coffee and having one of these a short time later. The cost is less, flavor is still good despite a lack of depth or complexity, and with my second cup, I've already gone through enjoy in the crema from the first so I don't miss the reduced crema dim these. As a note, there is always more dripped into the reservoir when I use these.

title: Hooray for virtuallly no residue of flavoring on the fingers
text: Although I prefer my peanuts to be in glass rather than plastic jars, what's inside this jar of FISHER Honey Dry Roast Peanuts made it worth removing the seal underneath the screwtop.  Not salty, not sweet, there is just a light coating which does not remain on the fingers, but stays on the peanuts.  They are crisp, flavorful, and quiet impressive.

title: Tasty and fresh, majority is halves.
text: Fisher Chef's Natural Walnuts get 5 stars for being non GMO certified and for being mostly halves of the nuts and not too many small pieces. They seem to be expensive, though, for non-Organic walnut halves.  I bake a lot and have an ample supply of walnuts, pecans and almonds at the very least in the pantry and freezer. Seriously, I must go through a pound or two a week. I recently opened another brand's sealed and "fresh" bag of walnuts that were rancid, so I will never buy that brand again. These, on the other hand, were delicious straight out of the bag. I'm using these nuts in their out of the bag unchopped form and will use my other favorite bag for recipes requiring smaller pieces. These are especially tasty when baked and bitten into while warm, as the flavors and oils come forward. They are also excellent when spiced as a snack with cocktails! I prefer pecans over walnuts, but I tend to look for quality nuts at a reasonable price and would repurchase these if the price was right.

title: Stronger than Dwayne Johnson
text: I've enjoyed Mentos mints on occasion for decades but had never tried their chewing gum until ordering on a whim a box of 6 tubs of the FreshMint flavor.  Since I recalled that the blue mento mints were peppermint, I figured that the blue tubs would also be peppermint.  These pieces are shaped similarly to the mints, and their initial hit of flavor is a whammy of a delicious minty reward with each chew.  The texture softens over chewing time yet the flavor keeps producing pleasure and juiciness, making the mouth feel cleansed.  I swear that chewing a piece of this cleans my teeth, but I have no definite proof, just a tactile sensation in the mouth.  I have put a couple of the pieces in a little reusable container to take with me because I don't want to leave the tub in the car.  The package I received is nice and fresh with a best by date of more than 2 1/2 years from now and since I don't like to waste, I'll be removing the plastic surrounding each tub, washing them, and using them for little jewelry making bits and pieces.  The plastic containers are structurally sound and the lids are securely attached.  When you're ready to open a canister, just remove the lock ring from around the base of the flip top lid and you're good to go.  I like being able to open and close this with a single hand.

title: Create smaller jars of personal blends
text: This is a pretty good organic ground cumin that's fragrant, ground uniformly and tastes like many others I've used. I'm not sure of the country of origin as it's not listed on the labels, but it is organic. I usually purchase my spices and dried herbs at Penzeys in smaller amounts but have received some directly from India to try.  I find this large plastic jar with large holes for shaking to be cumbersome for use at home, so I'm using it in smaller jars in a preblended form so that I don't have to grab am assortment of spices I regularly use for more spontaneous seasoning.  It's a mild cumin that lemme itself well to blending.

title: Not a bad cayenne pepper powder
text: This is a lot of cayenne powder for cooking or household use, so this organic pepper by Amazon is a great option if you need a pound plus of powder. The jar I received has a best by date of about a year and a half from now, so it's not a great consideration if you need it simply on occasion. Spices and herbs lose their potency, especially when not stored properly, something else to consider. This jar was sealed underneath the plastic shaker lid which has large dispensing holes. The color is vibrant and the flavor is quite good. For creating spice/herb blends to share, this is a really good component to include.

title: Mild and uniformly ground
text: This is a pretty good organic ground cumin. It's fragrant, ground uniformly and tastes like many others I've used. The plastic jars are made of a thin plastic and they have a tendency to squish, threatening their usability. I had to pour my cumin into a glass jar, but that's not a major issue since I'm using this up pretty quickly in preparing spice blends. I'm not sure of the cost for this product since it's new, so I can't comment on the value. Regardless, I like this for blending purposes. It's a mild cumin.

title: Store well to maintain flavor
text: If you need a lot of cayenne powder for cooking, this organic pepper by Amazon is a great option. title: Crispy and Creamy, one can satisfy
text: To my surprise, I discovered that the Arnott's Tim Tam biscuits are distributed in the US by Pepperidge Farm. I don't purchase cookies often but do have a hard time walking by Pepperidge Farm cookies in the market without being tempted. Like my favorite Milanos, these chocolate biscuits have the taste and texture which can accompany coffee, tea or milk. We have been enjoying our first package refrigerated because they hold up better when cold if they are dipped in a hot beverage and they are especially good when eaten with a scoop of quality vanilla ice cream. A package contains 11 cookies and a serving is computed as 2 cookies. The first ingredient is sugar and they contain palm oil, two things that normally stop me in my tracks, yet I was quite curious to try these Australian biscuits. To compensate for the not so good for us ingredients, we consume a single biscuit as a serving and account for the 95 calories and saturated fat in our total daily intake. These are sweet and chocolaty, crispy and creamy, the coating makes them special. I'd like to try the caramel variety next.

title: Gritty, thick style of chip
text: Amazon's Wickedly Prime Organic Tortilla Chips are of the gritty corn style, made basically of ground corn, oil and sea salt. Their hook is that they are organic, non GMO, and competitively priced. They ate also available solely through Amazon,so currently must be shipped to most customers. The package I received was intact, cushioned by air pillows in a large box, but as you know of you purchase items online, you can't always predict how they are sent. In a pantry box, I'd be concerned with heavier items crushing these as I experienced with another chip product in the past. If you intend to use these for shipping, you want whole chips so that's a consideration. The chips aren't overly salted and really hold up well for shipping because of their firm texture. These are not of the light, thin chip style. We especially enjoyed them by placing a layer on a flat plate, covering with shredded cheese, salsa and avocado, then microwaving the plate for about 30 seconds. It's also good with added black beans. There are 13 settings in the bag and we have tried to maintain the portion control. Unsuccessfully.

title: Ginger is more sour than hot
text: If you have had the green tea with match teabags from Costco, you get the idea behind this new line of teas from Lipton. Each of the 15 bags is sealed within a huge plastic pouch, making them a good option for travel. They weigh practically nothing and you can even slip one into your billfold. The tea is in a paper pouch with a cotton strong and paper tag for hanging around a cup or mug handle for brewing. Steep for 2 minutes, being sure to tap in any matcha powder from the bottom of the bag, then drink your tea. The green tea flavor prevails, followed by a hint of matcha and a slighter hint of ginger. If I did not know what I was drinking, I'd guess it contained lemon and not ginger. There  is no sourcing information, just a reference to Japanese matcha, and it was distributed in the USA.  The tea is okay but not good enough for me to want to drink or repurchase.

title: Flavorful enjoyment
text: I like the plain variety of Wickedly Prime cocoa truffle spread, but I love this one. Yes, they are sweet, but they are not intended as a main food source, merely an occasional confection to be consumed in moderation. For those who lack self control, this may be problematic because the flavor and texture are comforting and simulating at the same time. I love salty caramel and good  dark chocolate. A small spoonful of this won't kill me and it's delicious with plain Greek yogurt and some added vanilla. I'll repurchase this.

title: Single or double jars, the spread is good
text: Amazon's introduction of Wickedly Prime products is a very smart move, particularly since these chocolate and nut spreads are very popular. I've tried this variety in addition to the caramel and salt type which I like even better. Both have a substantial amount of sugar but the chocolate definitely comes through and they are reasonably priced. Of note is that this can be purchased in a single jar or double jar with the cost being the same per jar. If you do have Prime shipping then it's not necessary to purchase two jars at the same time unless you go through it faster than the shipping would take for reorder or if the product is on sale. I would say this is as good as any of the others I have recently tried and I have tried many. When baking cupcakes on a whim, I find that it's not necessary to make icing but instead put a little dab of this spread on top and everyone is happy. It's also good straight from the jar on small amounts.

title: Tasty in small amounts
text: There are so many chocolate and nut spreads available now that it's difficult to determine which one to try. I say try them all and choose what best suits your own taste buds, budget and fits into your nutritional needs. Amazon has introduced the Wickedly Prime brand and I think they are pretty good when compared side-by-side with others. Yes, they have a high sugar content, but I personally don't eat a lot at one time, so it fits into my motto of moderation. This variety is good but not as good as the caramel which I think is excellent. I would definitely purchase the brand again.

title: No additives and it's organic
text: This is my favorite coconut milk. I recently purchased a couple cans of a different company from an Asian market in my neighborhood and was so dissatisfied that I purchased a case of these so that I won't need to run to the store next time. It's organic and contains none of the crummy additives found in others.

title: Packaging is the attraction, small bars are as expected
text:
Kit Kat bars are tasty no matter what size. I would purchase this largest Kit Kat Box available as a novelty and would continue purchasing them in a bag for regular consumption. You're paying a premium for the packaging so if that's important then this is a really great option, however, if you are only into it for the candy, then there are better options available. The packaging looks like an enormous KitKat bar which is very clever and if you carefully remove the outer cellophane, you can reuse it to continue a gift. The interior cardboard box resembles a huge chocolate Kit Kat bar of the milk chocolate variety and by carefully opening one end to access the tasty little morsels, you can refill it with whatever you choose. Imagine refilling the cardboard box with Hershey Kisses and resealing it in the outer cellophane wrapper, then presenting it to your favorite person on Valentine's Day.

Trying to figure out how many would be in this box was rather confusing since it is advertised as 1.5 ounce bars equaling two pounds of chocolate. The nutrition facts state that a serving size is three 2-piece bars at 42 grams so I guess each bar is about a half an ounce which is nice for conserving your calories, fat, carbs and sugar intake. I personally really like this since I can be satisfied by having just one little snack bar. The others in my home tend to usually consume 3 or more at a time. The box I received is nice and fresh, with a best before date of 9 months from now and the box contained around 60 small bars, so it's less than the true 22 servings. We are very happy with this package because we are fond of the chocolate and wafer combination and still prefer the original milk chocolate rather than the dark or white chocolate options.

title: Small organic black peppercorns from?
text: This pound sized bottle of organic black peppercorns was packed in the USA but there is no reference to the type of peppercorns or where they were grown. Maybe I'm spoiled, but I like this information. There is a best by date on the plastic jar of more than a year from now, but it took me a minute to find it. The peppercorns are nice and dry, small, black, and they taste good. I do use several pepper grinders, each with a different type or blend, and these are is a Vic Firth wood manual grinder for everyday use. It's also a peppercorn I will use on pickling because it's much more affordable than what I purchase from Penzeys.

title: Saltier, many more Brazil nuts
text: We liked the single large bag of Happy Belly mixed nuts and decided to order this pack of 2 one pound bags. To my surprise, the best by date is about a year earlier, these have more salt and a gazillion more Brazil nuts which are the heaviest and least desirable in my household. Maybe this was an early batch which had been tweaked, maybe not. These are barely okay and had I not enjoyed the previous bag and expected the same quality and mix, these would be even more disappointing.  Won't order again.

title: More halves than pieces in my first bag
text: I am loving Happy Belly nuts of all sorts and was happy to purchase the California Walnuts, just in time for baking all sorts of goodies.  The bag of steam pasteurized mainly halves is in a bag which is shaped differently than the others I've received.  This one is in a broader bag which protects the  nuts more and allows for visualizing them even before opening the seal.  The expiry date on the bag I received today is June 30, 2017, and I've learned to really pay attention to those dates on walnuts due to the high chance of them becoming rancid, particularly when they are untoasted and unsalted.  I used what I needed today and placed the remainder in the freezer.  I purchased these using a gift card and they do not show up as an Amazon Verified Purchase, however I definitely purchased them from Amazon.

title: Have a small dish of vanilla ice cream if you want more sweetness
text: Marlo's Bakeshop manufactures biscotti in San Francisco. I first tried the pumpkin pie chocolate variety and did not like them at all, but find that the chocolate espresso variety is more tasty. Both are individually wrapped, 5 to a package at over a dollar for each biscotti. They are uniformly sized, however many did break into 2 or 3 pieces during shopping. This is important if you need the cookies intact for presentation purposes or become irritated when dunking smaller pieces intro your beverage. The texture is more airy than most biscotti yet they remain crisp until liquid is added and they don't become mushy. The flavor of these is pretty good with the addition of espresso complementing the chocolate. I don't dunk these in tea, very strong coffee is much better. They are not overly sweet and are enhanced by a strong coffee accompaniment.

title: Refrigerate after opening a bag
text: It's interesting that an attribute of this Japanese short grain polished white rice is that it is packaged for, "portion control," when each of the four bags contains 9 servings. I don't follow that logic. Anyway, it is perfectly sealed and contains 4 one pound sealed bags. The exterior bag has the date of harvesting, date of packaging and best by date. There are no directions or recipes on the bags in English,  but since I regularly purchase Japanese  rice from a market within walking distance of my home, I'm familiar with preparing it in my rice cooker. I first gently wash the rice in several refreshes of cool water, gently agitating it each time with my fingers. This particular rice had nothing floating, just the starchy residue, and no broken grains. I strained it after each wash until the water was clear, around 4 times. I then soaked the rice for 20 minutes in fresh water at a ratio of about 1:1 and let the rice cooker do the work for 20 minutes. Some cookers want to keep cooking, but that makes it too mushy for my liking. Letting the rice rest for about 10 minutes finishes it off and I then serve it from the bowl. I also often add a tiny bit of sea salt with the water, depending on the meal. This rice is also excellent in sushi,  I don't rinse it as much because I want it a bit stickier. This is a very, very white rice which has a little natural sweetness.

title: Refrigerate to maintain freshness
text: Sometimes I'll see nuts which are labeled as, "Reduced Sodium, " or something along those lines. I usually purchase unsalted nuts but do really like a hint of sea salt, and this Happy Belly nut mix is indeed to my liking. I've had their almonds, cashews and delectable deluxe mix, each is high quality and in my experience, they have all been fresh. My household agreed that these are the brand of nuts we will continue to purchase because of their quality and price. This mixed bag contains a lot of peanuts; actually only half of the bag is an assortment of other more expensive nuts and you can look at the Amazon provided details for the percentages. My bag appears to match the description and since we do like peanuts, we like this mix. I keep all our nuts in the refrigerator or freezer to help prevent spoilage, with a small mason jar filled for daily consumption. For a few dollars more, I prefer the deluxe mixed nuts, but do love these, too, when I crave or need peanuts. We are a very nut loving family but are aware that we must use moderation with the high fat food even though they are high in protein.

title: More, please
text: Fresh, delicious and affordable, we love the Happy Belly by Amazon Deluxe Mixed Nuts. You can get a version with peanuts which I imagine would be good as well, but what strikes me about these is that although salted, the sodium is minimal, just the way I personally like nuts. Ideal with a cocktail, they have been a hit around here and I only hope this bag survives until our dinner party a week from today because they are so darn good. Fortunately for me, the few Brazil nuts have my name on them because they are not high value nut in this household. Check out the description which gives a percentage of the included nut mix.

title: Mix a little into your plain nut butters
text: My preference is a dark chocolate in any shape or form, but I will not turn down a lighter variety, especially when nuts are a part of the confection.  Rivaling another well known variety, the Peanut Butter & Co. spread has less sugar, but still contains enough to give me a sugar rush.  I've tried this version as well as the dark chocolate variety of the Chocmeister Hazelnut spreads and definitely prefer the darker taste which contains basically the same ingredients.  This one has hazelnuts after the first cane sugar ingredient whereas the darker spread has cocoa butter before the hazelnuts.  Neither is as nutty as a simple nut spread, but for a little hit of chocolate, these are pretty good options.  Since each tablespoon contains 100 calories, I personally limit myself to a tablespoon max but others here are not as conscientious as I in reducing the sugar intake.  A tablespoon is definitely satisfying.  Since this is more flowing in texture, it works well as a little injection into vanilla cupcakes for a chocolate surprise.  I've also added a little of this into a simple nut butter to reduce the sugar content while getting the pleasures of the chocolate and hazelnuts.

title: Less sugar than many but still sweet
text: The dark chocolate variety of the Peanut Butter & Co. spread is darker in color than the milk chocolate variety, but the ingredients appear to be the same with one exception in the ordering on the label.  This has cocoa powder after the sugar whereas the lighter version has the hazelnuts after the sugar.  Their nutritional value are approximately the same, it's just up to you to determine whether you want a darker chocolate or not.  Although these supposedly contain less sugar than others, I still would prefer less sugar.  I have no problem with any of the ingredients, just prefer bitter to sweet and I find that the nuts tend to be inherently sweet.  Like the company's straight nut butters, this is gluten free.  It's pretty tasty, but at 100 calories per tablespoon, I am light handed when consuming this spread.

title: Smooth and creamy, stir with a sturdy tool to blend the oils
text: I like the Bestie nut butters which are distributed by Peanut Butter & Co. from NYC.  As with any nut butter, I first rotate the jars from right side up to upside down a few times to do a preliminary mix, but then stir with a wooden spoon to blend the oils with the nuts.  Each of these three small jars is creamy, contains a small amount of sea salt, and the cashew butter also contains additional oil.  They are all gluten free, but the almonds and cashews may have spread into each other during the production.  The plastic jars have an opening that is the same diameter as the jar, so accessing the butters is easier than in some other jars.  Each jar was well sealed.  At over ten a jar for these, I'm not a huge fan, considering other options which I really like.  It is faster to open one of these jars, though, than preparing a batch in my high performance blender, and the texture of each is consistent in these jars.

title: Not bad, cups contain ample amount for a serving
text:
I received a single small package containing five of the Peanut Butter & Co Dark Chocolate Dreams Dipping Cups, so I cannot comment on the full package of this listing or how it looks upon receipt. I expect that the full 45 ounces of product would travel better than the 7.5 ounces, so this review is only for the taste and consistency of the product, not a box of the little cups.

Peanut Butter & Co was a well know establishment in NYC for peanut butter lovers, however they have closed the doors and moved into an expanded venture of nut based edibles. We know that chocolate nutty spread options are increasing in the marketplace, and I was happy to try these to see how they compare with some of the others I've tried. The small cups are suitable for travel, and if you can handle the ingredients, they are a good option for day trips or journeys. They are well emulsified, so dipping into the cups is pretty good without much breakage of the dipper. Tastewise, it is pretty good, sweeter than I like but not too sweet to eat. These would have been a good item to hand out for Halloween because of the portability.

title: Tasty and crunchy fresh California almonds
text: If you like drier, less salty California almonds roasted a little more than others but not burned or overdone, you will likely enjoy these which are an Amazon product, only available from Amazon.  I really enjoy their crunchy texture, relatively nonexistent oiliness and mere hint of salt. The resealable bag is heavyweight, stands upright and may be emptied faster than you think if you like them as much as my household does, so be advised that they are available in a 3 pound bag. I have made a great batch of dark chocolate almond bark with these almonds.

title: No heavy sodium threat from these lightly salted nuts
text: I was not a big fan of the new Amazon brand of coffees, but I absolutely love the line of nuts.  The fancy cashews are in a thick and secure resealable bag that actually does reseal and it even can be stood on the counter for measuring or scooping.  At nearly 3 pounds of cashews, the bag I received has a best by date of May 2017, so I'm not rushed to push these nuts on everyone.  I keep mine refrigerated just to assure they don't go rancid.  Like the roasted and salted almonds, these cashews have a hint of salt, not a heavy concentration, largely due to the minimal amount of all that is used to prepare them for sale.  Cashews are a little oilier than almonds, so these are less crunchy than the almonds.  I've been buying smaller bags of raw cashew pieces from Trader Joe's recently, a way to prevent myself from eating too many at a time, but these are so darn good that I will be purchasing these large delicious nuts when the bag is nearly consumed.  If you want your cashews salty, you will have to add your own to the bag.

title: Neither oily nor salty, the crunchy almonds are just my style
text: If you like oily and salty almonds, it is likely that you will hate these.  I personally prefer either raw or dry roasted unsalted almonds and thought that I would mix these in with my Kirkland raw almonds for snacking and making almond butter, and I still intend to do that because of the qualities of these nuts with an expiration date of May 2017.  They are dry in texture and have only a hint of salt.  There is no visible oil on the exterior which is likely why the salt does not adhere to the nuts.  I like crispy things, so the crunch in these almonds really pleases me and I will be ordering when this bag is nearly empty.  I must order before they are gone or definitely will suffer from withdrawal.

title: Not too mushy when soaked in milk or water
text: We've recently tried the Evoke Athletic Fuel variety as well as the classic Swiss variety of muesli and prefer this one to the first because of the added cashew and pepitas.  Unfortunately, this one contains many raisins and since I personally prefer nuts and grains to dried fruits (specifically raisins), I've had to add oatmeal to both blends to reduce some of the sweetness from the fruit.  In its defense, the muesli is organic and the company seems to be solid, but for this price, I guess I expected more.  I have seen it on the shelves in a local large chain grocery store at a price substantially less than this bag is currently listed for, so I'd probably purchase locally if I want to replenish after the bag is emptied.  I've been eating muesli for decades and have consumed it hot, cold and in baked goods.  I've made my own blend and have recently been purchasing three blends from other manufacturers.  This one offers higher protein, and I've found that my preference is to have this one with cold milk.  I let it soak for a couple of minutes because I enjoy the softer base consistency accented by the nuts and raisins.  It does not get a mushy as some others.

title: Resealable bag is fresh, sweet blend of dried fruits, nuts and grains
text: Because of the raisins, dried cranberries AND dates, I find the Evoke classic muesli to be sweeter than I personally care for, so I've added some more oat flakes and nuts to the blend.  Yes, I could have simply removed some of the the dried fruits but I chose to dilute the muesli, so to speak.  I like this, but honestly find it to be not better than some others I typically consume which cost a fraction of the cost of the Evoke brand.  True, it is organic and the company seems to be doing the things we like to see, but it's just not one that I would seek out unless I happened to see it on the shelf in a local store at a more affordable price.  Muesli is versatile, can be extended as I've done, can be served hot or cold, with milk of choice or water, can be added to yogurt or ice cream, and can be included in baked goods.  I've been eating it for decades and would rate this as above average for no added sugar or oils in addition to the fruits and nuts, and for the organic nature of the sources.  I'm sure that if I preferred dried fruits more than nuts and grains, I'd love this, but since that's not case, I've had to improvise.

title: Thinner consistency than I'd expected
text:
I prefer the darkest, most bitter chocolates. Hazelnuts are a favorite, but I love nearly all nuts if they are fresh. Sugar seldom entices me, but watch out if a bag of savory snacks is opened in the house.

The nutiva organic hazelnut spread surprised me because the 13 ounce jar is smaller than I imagined it would be. The information on the label appealed to me because the product is organic, non GMO, gluten-free, vegan, and it contains 12 grams of sugar in 2 tablespoons which is more than I will use at a time. The calories in that serving aré 210 with 15 grams of fat. It has no cholesterol. In this spread that contains 40% less sugar than the leading brand which we all know is Nutella, the first ingredient is cane sugar. I'm surprised to read that this may contain traces of milk solids which to me says it would not be vegan, but what do I know? I again was surprised when I opened the jar of classic organic hazelnut spread with cocoa and after prying off the seal, discovered a very thin product which I tried to stir with a very fancy spoon. There was nothing solid at the bottom of the jar, it was all the same thin consistency which reminded me of Hershey's syrup from years ago. I coated the spoon and tasted this product only to discover that I love it. It is not overly sweet and the cocoa comes through clearly with a very strong hazelnut aftertaste. There are no synthetic additives in this fair trade certified product of the United States. It is recommended that this not be refrigerated even after opening the jar which makes it much easier to keep in an office setting inside a desk drawer for quick access. I think it's that good.

title: Slow air drying
text:
Semolina Artisanal Pasta is okay pasta. Having it travel across country being knocked around in transit resulted in some breakage of the pasta as well as the way too thin cello bag being busted open, exposing the rigatoni to live loosely in the shipping box instead of the cellophane. The rigatoni was made of organic USA grown semolina flour and water with nothing else added, so the gluten from the flour basically holds this dried pasta together when it is cooked.

The story of how this company originated is interesting and I wish the owner a lot of success. Her manufacturing involves slow drying the pasta but otherwise there is nothing extraordinary about it despite the organic semolina flour being sourced from the United States. The dies used for extruding these pastas are bronze in the old Italian tradition which ultimately makes for a rougher textured product.

Because the rigatoni is a larger tube, I decided to prepare it in a large pot, draining it after only six minutes from the boiling salted water. I then baked it in the oven with cheese, roasted cauliflower florets, a little pinot grigio, some red pepper flakes and olive oil. I added some of the reserved pasta cooking water which created some steam for the covered casserole since I only used about 1/4 cup of the wine for flavor. The rigatoni nearly held its shape since it was neither initially overcooked, nor weighed down by a heavy sauce. I specifically wanted to retain the tubular structure of this pasta and it almost worked. The shape did not last, however when reheated, and was visually unappealing when served. The taste of the pasta was nothing short of ordinary and the bite was simply average. If you live in LA and want to support the business, it may be okay but otherwise, it's not worth the cost.

title: Addictive sweet and hot sauce
text: I did not purchase Lingham's Hot Sauce through Amazon, but first found it at a dollar store. Hot sauces are a weakness for me,  followed by a lifelong love for mustards as is evidenced by nearly an entire shelf in the refrigerator. This is the first bottled hot sauce from Malaysia that I tried and, perhaps due to the first of 4 ingredients being sugar, I am addicted to the condiment. This is a thick, orange colored sauce that first surprised me with its sweetness. It is not what I was expecting and after the initial shock, I was hooked. The heat from chili peppers comes a moment after the sweetness and despite not being a great fan of sweet and sour sauce, I like the sweet and hot of this one. I've used it daily and must acknowledge that when my last bottle is empty, I will have to purchase more, regardless of the cost. I have used it on all sorts of foods including a very simple salad with a little bit of additional olive oil. That's when I knew I was hooked.

title: Light green tea from India, bitterness grows
text: The TEABOX Selim Hill Spring Green tea from India was cut leaves and to my surprise, more stems than I like in a tea.  The brew was rather light in complexity, not unusual for Indian green teas.  I received a number of small samples of assorted teas and found this one to be average for the price, but not exceptional due to the weakness of the brew which becomes bitter and astringent minutes after a brew.

title: Simple tea
text: I recently received a number of TEABOX sample tea products and have tried four as of today.  This is the one that is simply okay, not great and not one I would seek out again.  The Indian company is impressive and when shipped from them, the package is definitely fresh and presented nicely.  Their website describes the business and the photos are enticing.  This particular tea is more tannic than other breakfast teas, yet the flavors are father simple.

title: Mushy, stems not attached, and very sweet
text: I purchased three jars of the CherryMan cherries with stems at a local store and will be returning the two unopened jars because they are far inferior to the Tillen Farms cherries I was seeking at the time of purchase. These are mushy, very sweet, and a majority of the stems were free floating in the jar, not attached to the cherries. This was a disappointment because the label provides very enticing information which led me to think that they would also taste good.

title: Teff really is a supergrain
text: I know that Kashi is working hard on their brand and I respect their adding Chia seeds to some granola bars almost as much as I like their using teff, an underutilized gluten free whole grain in these crackers. There is no wheat in these, so if you are expecting something like flavored Wheat Thins, this will disappoint. We really like how they taste as an accompaniment to hot legume meals, just would like more spiciness as opposed to the existing lemon notes. Since not a single cracker was intact in our box, we had to sprinkle the small thin flavorful pieces into the bowls filled with lentils, then topped them off with yogurt, cucumber and a little berbere spice blend.

title: The best non-Nespresso capsules I've tried for my Inissia
text: I was contacted by someone at Jones Brother Coffee Company to try their Nespresso style capsules and selected the Noir Ristretto option because of the description.  I've personally consumed ten of the box of fifty and although the coffee is not as complex as the Nespresso Ristretto, it is the best compatible non-Nespresso coffee I have tried.  The actual capsules also performed by far better than any other generic options I've tried.  I'm using an Inissia and have encountered no problems at all with these capsules.  The coffee produces an ample crema, however it dissipates faster than the Nespresso Ristretto.  With each of the ten capsules I tried, I prepared both, side by side, and this occurred with each an every cup.  These were all consumed black, prepared in the same model Nespresso glass espresso cup, and because of the consistency in brewing and taste, I would rate these capsules as excellent.  I'll admit that since the price for these is currently not much different than the Nespresso capsules, these will not likely become my go to capsules, particularly since I cannot return the spent capsules for recycling as I do with the Nespresso products.  They are, however, arabico bean coffee is definitely the best generic capsules which I will keep an eye out for price reductions.

title: Don't be ridiculous
text:
So you know how quickly you can enjoy a package of these Annie's Shells and Cheese, but do you really want to spend over $5 for a single box of these things? Yes, they satisfy your quest for comfort food that is not quite the Kraft macaroni and cheese box, but for this amount of money, I think you would be better off finding a package of more than one of these boxes.

The shells are nicely formed and cook in only a few minutes. All you have to do is add some milk and if you like butter to complete the preparation. I personally add other spices and often add additional frozen vegetables in the same water in which I am boiling the pasta if I have only 15 minutes before serving a meal. The cheese product in this does not use animal rennet, so although it is not vegan, for those who eat no meat, it can work. The sauce is not creamy, but it tastes good if you add no salt.

title: Vermicelli cooks quickly
text: You can usually find Barilla pasta on sale in major grocery chains right next to the Barilla sauces and it is usually available at the big box stores in packages of 6. It can't get much more convenient than ordering from Amazon, especially when a coupon is offered, then it shows up at your door and you don't need to stand in line. This particular variety, the thin spaghetti, is what I call vermicelli and it looks beautiful when served on my Spode Vermicelli pattern plates. It is thinner than a traditional spaghetti so it cooks faster and if you use a lot of boiling water to allow movement as it cooks in the pot, you can have delicious pasta ready to be sauced in about five minutes. Since it's not as thin as angel hair, you have a decreased risk of overcooking the pasta. I sometimes break some of these strands before cooking, crisp them in a little olive oil, then add them to my cooking spiced rice, following the example of the rice-a-roni packages I would make in my early teens. It's also going when simply broken and added to broth since the small pieces cook very quickly.  I often cook till al dente, rinse, let it cool for a couple of minutes, then put it in a gallon sized plastic bag. Pour in a little olive oil and roasted garlic which I usually have on hand, squish the bag gently, then refrigerate. For a meal or a snack, you just put some on a plate and add shredded parmesan cheese, cover and microwave for a minute or so. I prefer to heat it on the stove in more olive oil so that it gets nice and crusty, but kids tend to want it fast. I personally prefer my spaghetti thin like this or opt for a thicker linguini. Barilla quality is really good and it is consistent.

title: Classic pasta for sauce
text: The ingredients are the same in the Barilla penne as the Academia Barilla penne pasta, but I prefer the Academia Barilla because it has a better bite than this blue box, made in the USA pasta.  This is labelled as non GMO, yet the other Italian made using bronze dies pasta is not. They are not greatly different, both are a really good penne that holds up well to sauces. This one takes an additional minute to cook and I always rinse mine after cooking.  If it is going to be reheated,  I definitely undercook it or it will become mushy.

title: Texture suitable for sauces
text: I came upon the Academia Barilla pastas at a local store for a buck each and stocked up because they are so fresh and tasty when cooked. We eat a lot of pasta and have found this to be a little different than the blue box Barilla pasta,  likely die to the bronze dies which make the texture a little rougher.  It adds to the bite of al dente pasta. It's a bargain at a dollar, led so at this current selling price.

title: You can't go wrong with this sampler
text: You cannot go wrong with this cookie sampler from Amazon. The Box I received included every single item that has been referred to in previous reviews which I relied on before making my purchase. I am almost embarrassed to admit that the first little package I ate was the Oreos. With this sampler you're able to try an assortment you might not otherwise try and for me, the Belvita was the winner which I had never had before. To top off the tasty treats, I now have money to spend on buying more cookies.

title: Tasty, nutty, crispy, good tasting snack
text:
These bars are quite the surprise, much more tasty than I'd anticipated. They are peanutty, crunchy, dark chocolatey, a little sweet and a little salty. They look good and arrived perfectly intact despite the high temperature these days. The box I received has a best by date of just over a year from now and these taste really fresh. These are snack bars, not meals, and they fit nicely on a bag or purse for travel. I used to love kind bars, then found them too heavy to enjoy. These are light and less sweet for me.

Made in Canada, the ingredients are:
Roasted Peanuts*, Semi-Sweet Chocolate (Unsweetened Chocolate, Sugar, Cocoa Butter, Soy Lecithin, Natural Vanilla Extract), Agave Syrup*, Soy Crisp (Isolated Soy Protein, Tapioca Starch, Salt), Brown Rice Syrup* Redskin Peanuts*, Roasted Soybeans, Peanut Flavor*, Sunflower Oil Blend (Sunflower Oil, Antioxidants (Mixed Tocopherols, Rosemary Extract), Cashew Butter, Almond Butter, Sea Salt, Agar

*Organic

I can't help but wonder about the "Peanut Flavor" but can be comforted knowing that it is organic.

title: Important security for a celiac
text: He is a celiac,  so the slightest amount of gluten can be life threatening. For everyone else, I use organic oats in baking and overnight refrigerator protein smoothies, but his must be gluten free.  He loves oatmeal cookies I bake using these Quaker gluten free quick cooking oats with Namaste gluten free flour blend and added home dried raisins or cherries. Sometimes, I add gluten free chocolate chips or bananas, but he does not care for the nuts everybody else loves. I've been using these oats for him since I first found them in a local market earlier this year.  I had read about Quaker Oats showing a commitment to providing gluten free products and liked what I read. Since he doesn't care about products being organic, this offers oats which may cost a little more without going over his budget.  He always complains about the high cost of his gluten free food yet insists on having bread, cookies, crackers or chips with every meal and snack.

title: Celiacs can now enjoy the same taste and texture
text: He loves these individual packages of gluten free oatmeal not because it tastes so great but because with celiac disease,  the risk of eating anything that contains gluten is a life threatening experience. I personally prefer others oats, always unflavored and unsweetened, and I tend to select organically grown grains of any kind.  He only cares about the lack of gluten and would eat cardboard if it had carbs. This gets 5 stars because Quaker has been working really hard on producing oats using techniques that are successful in removing stray grains.  I also like that they need not waste a batch that tests as containing gluten, but can use it combined with their regular oat products. Other manufacturers may not be able to do this.  This is very much the same as the regular Quaker oats packages and for those who cannot tolerate gluten, it is worth the increased cost of manufacturing.

title: Purchasing more for a friend with celiac disease
text: I'm more of savory craver than one who loves sweets, so these crackers are my preferred choice for snacking.  I purchased this large box containing 2 bags elsewhere and have been touting their taste and texture ever since eating them. They are not overly salty,  are not too hard so as to break a tooth,  need nothing added for enjoyment, contain seeds for enhanced texture,  and I'm returning for more. The sweet potatoes add a sweetness to these light yet crunchy corn based gluten free crackers.

title: Freshness is the key
text: Frosted Flakes are crispy and sweet when the box is freshly opened but they do lose something after they are exposed to air.  This large box never made it the stale point, though, because we found ourselves snacking on them straight out of the box because they were so darn fresh.  In milk, they do soften and the sugar coating sweetens the milk, making this a breakfast cereal that goes well with a cup of black coffee.

title: Huge bundle
text: The Gourmesso capsules work without a problem in my Nespresso machine. I have tried these in both the Espresso and Lungo modes and never had a delay in flow or difficulty in the capsule removal after brewing the coffee. Whereas I did not like the flavored varieties of this brand, some of this particular bundle were fine and provide an opportunity to try them out. With all the varieties, there is likely something that you find agreeable.  None of the Gourmesso coffees were good when brewed as a Lungo, so keep that in mind if you like your coffee robust and with a substantial crema.  Of this bundle, the Ristretto was very good, as was the Tarrazu Forte. Both were nicely balanced, had a crema that remained for the first sips of the coffee, and in the Espresso mode, they were fine. The weakest in flavor was the Ethiopian which was surprising because it was the darkest of the bunch when brewed. These varieties are worth considering for a more affordable option than the Nespresso capsules, but they are not of their quality in coffee.  Even friends who are not picky about their coffee noted the differences after having a Nespresso coffee first.  I was provided samples for evaluation.

title: Some are okay, others are not good at all
text: The Gourmesso capsules work without a problem in my Nespresso machine. I have tried these in both the Espresso and Lungo modes and never had a delay in flow or difficulty in the capsule removal after brewing the coffee. Whereas I did not like the flavored varieties of this brand, some of the unflavored varieties were fine. Of this bundle, the Ristretto was very good, as was the Tarrazu Forte. Both were nicely balanced, had a crema that remained for the first sips of the coffee, and in the Espresso mode, they were fine. The weakest in flavor was the Ethiopian which was surprising because it was the darkest of the bunch when brewed.  The decaf was like colored water and I would not recommend them, stick to the Nespresso brand for robust options These varieties are worth considering for a more affordable option than the Nespresso capsules in their huge bundle, but they are not of their quality in coffee. I was provided samples for evaluation.

title: Opportunity to try a more affordable option of okay coffee
text: The Gourmesso capsules work without a problem in my Nespresso machine. I have tried these in both the Espresso and Lungo modes and never had a delay in flow or difficulty in the capsule removal after brewing the coffee. Whereas I did not like the flavored varieties of this brand, some of this particular bundle were fine and provide an opportunity to try them out. Of this bundle, the Ristretto was very good, as was the Tarrazu Forte. Both were nicely balanced, had a crema that remained for the first sips of the coffee, and in the Espresso mode, they were fine. The weakest in flavor was the Ethiopian which was surprising because it was the darkest of the bunch when brewed. The Messico was rather benign, but more complex than the Ethiopian.  These varieties are worth considering for a more affordable option than the Nespresso capsules, but they are not of their quality in coffee. I was provided samples for evaluation.

title: Try the other Gourmesso varieties
text:
The Gourmesso capsules work without a problem in my Nespresso machine. I have tried these in both the Espresso and Lungo modes and never had a delay in flow or difficulty in the capsule removal after brewing the coffee. The individual sleeves I received were in the 2 per single foil packet older package, but I understand that now they are sold in a labeled packet inside the sleeve, similar to what Nespresso does with their capsules.

Unfortunately, I do not like any of the flavored offerings, with the Soffio Mandorla eing the worst of all. I had to dump that cup because it was so bitter. The crema in all of these was minimal and whatever did initially flow dissipated in a few seconds, even before bringing the cup to the lip. Each person who tried these had a similar reaction, with the Soffio Vaniglia as the only one being acceptable because the vanilla was deeply hidden underneath the bitter and weak coffee. We liked some of the other Gourmesso coffee capsules, but the flavored varieties will be used only when we are out of others to drink. A sample was provided for evaluation.

title: Top of an undesirable list
text: There are few crispy snacks I do not like at all and these seaweed crisps are near the top of that list.  They look good,  thin sheets with a lovely green color on one side,  perfect to hold and place in the mouth.  I ate two and passed the bag to the next taster who did not care for them but did not hate them.  Down the line,  all agreed that this single bag was enough and we were grateful to have received only one.  The first bite is pleasant,  good crunch and seaweed taste but then the unappealing characteristics took over,  culminating with a strange aftertaste.  Perhaps this was cinnamon?  None of would purchase these.

title: Excellent for those who like fruit and nuts but not raisins
text: We have recently tried several of the Cailler Swiss chocolates and this variety is one of our favorites. I am reminded of Muesli without the oats covered in a dark chocolate, but perhaps that is simply because it is also a Swiss product which I love. Loaded with almonds,  hazelnuts and sweetened blueberries,  the bar breaks into small pieces so it can comfortably be shared or saved for later. A small piece is delicious with a cup of coffee and small serving of vanilla ice cream.  The sweetest component is the blueberries and all flavors are balanced in the multitextural confection.

title: Typical European milk chocolate bar
text: Most milk chocolate bars made in Europe contain sweetened condensed milk. This tends to produce a sweeter chocolate product,  almost like a white chocolate.  The Cailler milk chocolate is a traditional confection that is creamy and very much liked by children because of the rather benign flavor which is more milky. The bar is good,  particularly for those who prefer a milder chocolate.  It is more expensive than other Nestles products,  so I personally won't be buying these for kids,  but for adults who love the European style of milk chocolate,  this was well received. It seems that there is currently  a greater interest in the USA for milk chocolates and this is worth a taste.

title: Creamy, dreamy dark chocolate
text: Dark chocolates are appreciated in this household, loved much more than milk chocolates.  CAILLER L'Ecorce 70% was a new product for us and it has been received with rave reviews.  This particular product offering is for three bars which are perfectly placed inside a protective cardboard box, contained inside a secure home for travel from Switzerland to Amazon to the consumer.  The box, as well as the chocolate bar packaging each are imprinted with a date of manufacture and best by date which is a year later.  What I just received was manufactured in August and there is no way the last bar will still be around beyond the end of the week.  The chocolate tastes fresh, looks dreamy, tastes creamy, not as bitter as many others in the 70% arena, and is delicious.  The package is like a sturdy cardstock, designed to look good and protect the contained chocolate bar.  The chocolate is excellent with a nice glass or port or a small espresso.  It is also good on its own, straight out of the package.

title: Delectable creamy nutty morsels with assorted tastes and textures
text: I think it took longer to access the chocolates from this layered packaging than to select a chocolate to try.  The fresh Swiss CAILLER signature selection arrived in perfect condition, visually appealing and securely contained in an outer cardboard box in which the small box of chocolates is presented.  The chocolates look just like the vendor images on this site, and the small morsels which amount to a bite or two each, are lovely and assorted.  The strap adorning the box contains a small brochure which describes each chocolate and an image for each.  The box does not have a traditional lid as do most boxes of chocolates, it just slips into the sleeve if you do not eat or serve all the chocolates at once.  The box contains a date, and mine was very fresh.  I usually prefer the darkest chocolates, but must confess that I found these milk chocolates to be addictive.  The chocolate itself is creamy, smooth, and delectable.  The fillings which I was able to taste were also of a high quality, but I prefer nuts, so this box of pralines is indeed my personal preference.  I did not see it labeled as a nut selection, so I was thrilled to see the little brochure labeling this as a praline collection.  I'd like to welcome CAILLER to the US and will do what I can to consume more.

title: Keep these out of my home please
text: I hate the Sunshine Cheez-It Original crackers because I have no control after opening a box.  There is another cracker like this by a different manufacturer that I also like, but they don't spark that desire to consume the entire box as this product does.  This isn't as salty but the cheesiness abounds.

title: Suitable size sauce can
text: What I especially like about the Hunt's Tomato Sauce is the size of this 15 ounce can.  It is just enough with none left over for most recipes I prepare and there is nothing extra added to destroy the flavor of the simple tomato.

title: Richer flavor from the fire roasting
text: Let's say you keep a can or two of canned tomatoes in the pantry for that emergency where you need to add them to a concoction you've come up with.  If your can is the Hunt's Fire Roasted Diced Tomatoes, you will be very happy to have experienced that emergency.  I was.

title: Minimal tannins in aromatic, delicate green tea
text: Green tea is very popular now and some are just becoming introduced.  I have been drinking green tea for many years and have found some to be great while others are barely drinkable.  Elitea offered me a sample for evaluation of their wild green tea grown in the Jiangxi Province of China and it is excellent tea at a good value.  Over a half pound is packaged in plastic and enclosed in a simple, yet attractive paper bag that is also sealed.  The leaves are not cut, so when brewed, the beautiful dried leaves unfurl, leaving you with wide moist green tea leaves.  The steeped liquor is a lovely yellow color and the aroma of the tea awakens the senses.  I've been using this for preparing sun tea outside, then chilling the tea and drinking it from the refrigerator.  I usually use ice in my iced tea, but I don't want to interfere with the delicate flavor of this tea.  I'm impressed.

title: Nearly as good as fresh lime juice but with a longer life expectancy in diminutive bottle
text: I was at a local market today and purchased 7 limes for a single dollar.  I squeezed them and put the juice into an ice cube tray for freezing.  For times when I do hot have fresh limes or frozen lime juice, the small bottle of RealLime juice is a perfect standby that takes up little space in the refrigerator.  I'm not thrilled with the preservatives, but understand the convenience outweighs the minor chemicals.

title: Perfectly sized for a full refrigerator
text: I'm not thrilled with preservatives but appreciate having this small bottle ready in the refrigerator at a moment's notice.  I much prefer this smaller size to the larger bottles more frequently seen in the shops I visit.

title: High fiber, just two ingredients in delicious half pound+ ¨cake¨
text: Not as fantastic as what I buy in high end cheese shops which includes almonds, and at a cost savings with the ease of having it delivered to the door, the Nature's Wild & Raw sun dried unsulphured figs and walnuts cake is delicious and I'm happy it is available from Amazon.  Made of just the figs and walnuts, it is loaded with the fig seeds that I love and it is sweeter than I usually want, but tempered by the walnuts.  Because it is naturally high in sugar, I eat small slices at a time so as to not overdo it, but be prepared to be tempted to eat the entire cake.  This is a product of Turkey, the source of some of my favorite figs.

title: Milder blend holds its own
text:
Unlike other breakfast teas, this blend by Capital Teas is very mild, low on tannins, fairly bland, and became more aromatic when consumed over ice. I added no milk but finally did drop in a bit of sugar which also helped develop the blend. The color was beautiful when brewed and produced the best cup for me when steeped with 195 degree filtered water for four minutes. I used more of the leaves than I usually do with others. The package I received was intact and the various leaves could actually be differentiated, with a majority being larger. It is a nice organic tea that can hold up despite a weaker impression than other breakfast blends.

I live about four miles from a Capital Teas store, often patronize the restaurant right next door. Like a larger chain in many malls, the store offers samples to entice patrons, and like that other chain, the demo teas lean to sweetened lighter blends.

title: When lightened and sweetened, it becomes a good black tea for consuming regularly
text: First thing, store these teabags in something other than the lightweight paper box in which they are sold.  That out of the way, Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Tea is a suitable bag for brewing once, not twice.  Product is a deeply colored, non-astringent brew that lends itself to enhancement with milk and sweetener of choice.  It is not complex, not aromatic, simply a nicely prepared tea bag which makes a fine base.  I do not care for this tea iced and I prefer it with a biscuit or toast.

title: Good leaves and buds
text: Dechunxian knows how to package their products.  Fortunately for us consumers, what is inside is as nice as the packaging.  Having tried their jasmine flowers, I suspected that the Jasmine Tea would be equally as nice and it is.  It is delightfully fragrant and not overpowering as some blends tend to be.  I steep mine for a maximum of about three minutes and also like to consume it throughout the day from a pot as a tall refreshing glass of iced tea.  I add nothing to it, but that is my preference.  You may like to sweeten it up for yourself.  A sample tin of the tea was provided for review.

title: Good option for organic turmeric powder in a small size
text: Seems like everyone is into turmeric these days.  You can buy it by the ounce, pound or capsule.  I like this particular organic turmeric powder but think it is currently overpriced.  It is securely packaged in a sealed plastic jar with a dispensing cap and screw top and since the powder is vibrant in color and I want it to stay that way, I have transferred mine into a glass jar and keep it in a cabinet.  The powder tastes very good and blends well with other spices for assorted curry blends.  There are currently a number of organic turmeric powders available and this one is fine.  Vedica Organics provided a sample for review at an extremely reduced cost.

title: Good to have on hand for emergecies
text: I rarely buy canned broth, but took a chance on a can of the Swanson Vegetable Broth.  Using it as the liquid base for a vegetable and shirataki noodle soup, it worked fine once I added about a pint of heirloom tiny tomatoes.  Because it contains quite a bit of sodium, I added no salt at all and the finished product was definitely salty enough.  I don't care for this as much as other carton packaged vegetable broth products, but am happy I tried it and will keep a can in the pantry for emergencies.

title: Beautiful and aromatic respectful product
text: You are not only purchasing about an ounce of tea flowers with this Dechunxian Jasmine buds, but you also receive a pretty pink square tin, a packet of sugar and a pink plastic clip for sealing your sealed foil bag of flowers.  It is worthy of a respectable gifting, and I am happy that I was offered a sample for review. There is nothing other than the flowers, so I am very happy. I combine these with green or yellow tea leaves and enjoy a delicious brew, sometimes adding a piece of vanilla bean.  The flowers can be used in assorted infusions as well because they apear to be quite fresh.  The package has a best by date which is over a year from right now. I'm very impressed and will be trying the chrysanthemum in the future.

title: Throughout the years, the confection has always been desirable and perfectly presentable
text: Chocolate products are a very personal preference and the Reber Mozart Kugel pieces have been a favorite in this household for many years.  We have returned from Europe with these and purchased them here in the USA.  I actually have a decorative tin which has been empty for a very long time and it still makes me salivate.  I recently purchased a small pack of 8 pieces for my daughter on the occasion of her birthday and of all the gifts she received, this is the one that she seemed to enjoy the most.  We had fun talking about our memories relating to the Kugel and she even allowed us to share them.  They are really unlike other chocolate truffle type products because of their beautiful foil wrappers and intricate layering of textures and tastes.  Looking at an unwrapped confection, unless you have already experienced them, the first bite is a very pleasant surprise.  The only problem with these is that once you have one, you are likely to forever be a fan and will have a hard time passing them by when seeing them in a store.

title: Sweeter, less crunchy, salt free
text: Terra sweet potato chips are tasty, a bit sweet, a little oily and not at all salty. For my taste, they would benefit from being a little more well done. Without added salt, a firmer crunch could better satisfy the snack craving.

title: Melting and molding these to perfection
text: I have been making chocolates lately, having some fun especially with chocolate lollipops and never thought I would actually purchase a white chocolate product, let alone consume it.  To my delight and surprise, the Lindt Chocolate Piccoli Blancor was offered at an incredible price and I wanted to make some teddy bears for a baby shower, so I gambled on a purchase.  They tempered perfectly and molded just as I wanted, so I have now purchased two other varieties of the Lindt Couverture dark chocolate products.

title: Skip these
text: We recently tried three varieties of the Planters peanuts in a can and this was by far the worst of the three.  Having a cocoa coating that remains on the fingers like the fake orange colored stuff on cheesy snack foods, it is not even worthy of licking off.  This is the only can we could not even finish and the cans are very small.  We washed off the coating and still did not care for them.

title: Best of the low sodium varieties
text: I like to keep a few cups of Dr. McDougall's prepared soups on hand for emergencies and the vegan split pea is probably the best of the lower sodium varieties.  It tastes a little smoky, has a good texture, and doesn't take forever to prepare, so it can be consumed in about 5 minutes.  I prefer this to any of the varieties which include pasta that tends to remain like cardboard.

title: Everyone wants a loaf of bread
text: For breads of an kind using whole wheat flour, King Arthur flour is as good as any freshly milled wheat as I've used.  Because any unrefined ground grain tends to spoil more quickly, I keep it stored in glass jars in the refrigerator and remove it to return to room temperature before using.  I've purchased other types that just do not have the texture the King Arthur flour provides.

title: Prime solid albacore tuna in a can
text: Bumble Bee has been the preferred tuna in our household for years, but I had not tired the albacore in a gold can until ordering it with a Prime Pantry package.  My goodness, this is good tuna and since we eat a vegetarian based diet with seafood a couple times a week, we want the fish to be good.  This is solid, tasty, not offensive or stinky, and it makes a delicious salad for sandwiches or simple addition to a vegetable, pasta or grain salad.  This is now a staple in our pantry.

title: Rinsing really helps prepare these large peanuts for cooking
text:
Royal Oak provides large raw peanuts in the Shell packaged in a bright yellow net bag with a black drawstring. Each bag weighs 2.5 pounds, has a lot date and best by date so you have an idea of when they will become stale. Raw peanuts taste very different than boiled or roasted peanuts, but don't be confused and think that since these are in a shell they would be cookef. They are not cooked and for him sn consumption, really should be.

Boiling the peanuts gives you a soft product and roasting them firms them to a crunchy peanut. Since they keep cooking after removed from the heat source, it's best to stop just before you think they are done. Rinsing them well before c [king helps remove the debris and dit that is in the bag. My first bags were a gift and I will be purchasing.

title: Artificially flavored yet they taste good and have a nice loose coating
text: The peanuts in the tin do not look like the peanuts on the package label, but I won't hold that against them because they certainly taste good.  This small can supposedly contains six servings, but I expect them to be eaten in less since they are so tasty.  The caramel is very sweet, but balanced by the saltiness and since the peanuts are small, there is a lot of the granular coating on each.  The cans I received all have  most peanuts split in half, but that just means more of the coating gets consumed.  They are not as good as my own homemade peanut treats, but they are certainly good in a pinch.  Just peel off the aluminum lid and we can dig in.

title: Refrigerate after opening and use within two weeks, very sweet creamer
text: I am not sure if the Coffee-mate French Vanilla Liquid creamer in the refrigerate after opening option is manufactured with a short best by date, but the two bottles I just received are only good for a little over a month.  Being relatively new to the Coffee-mate products, I have tried the concentrated versions of non-refrigerated French vanilla creamers and expected this one to be similar.  Instead, this is much more liquid, very much sweeter, and lacking in the strong vanilla flavor.  With one bottle in the refrigerator now and the second in the pantry for use in the next couple of weeks, I doubt that I will repurchase the product.  Had I tried this one first, it is likely that I never would have taken a gamble on the others which I do like.

title: Labels colors match the berries but not enough information provided
text:
We personally like the taste of goji berries, appreciate the no added sugar, enjoy their tartness, color and shape. We make tea from the berries but prefer to eat them raw. We do not eat goji berries unless they have been grown organically. When offered the Morning Pep berries for review, it seemed like a good thing, so I accepted. Packaged in a thick plastic bag that can stand up on a counter top, the bag is resealable if you cut off the top rather than tear it. I tend to put my berries in a glass jar because I don't trust people to reseal the bag after taking some. The first thing that made me uneasy with this particular product was there is no country of origin listed, just many statements like organic, pesticide-free, non-gmo, kosher, gluten-free. In very teensy tiny print is a label that says PACKAGED IN USA. Another says the berries will keep up to 12 months when stored properly.

No date of manufacturing, location, best by date is on the bag or label. This is a major concern, so despite these tasting like dried goji berries and even including some bitty stems, regardless of these being uniform in shape and size, I'm disappointed. As a consumer, I do not want to research a product or company to get information, but expect clear labeling on consumables. Other than this problem, the berries taste as good as most and they look good.

title: Smaller size package assists in restraint
text: The simplest Walkers Shortbread Pure Butter Shortbread Fingers in a 5.3 ounce box is ideal for portion control because unlike a larger box, a couple can be eaten and the rest can be saved for another treat or even shared.  Dipped in a cup of tea or coffee, the cookie is firm until it meets moisture, and the flavor is pure butter and flour.  In the past, I purchased larger boxes and tins, but have found that this small size works best in our household and with the incredibly reasonable price now, it is easy to share them.

title: Consistently tasty, firm and fabulous
text: It seems like anchovies are one of those foods that people either love or hate.  Unlike everyone else in my family, I love them and can devour an entire can at one sitting unless I control myself.  I prefer the CROWN PRINCE flat anchovies to others because they are easier for me to remove and transfer to another little container since it is usually just me eating them.  Anchovies in a jar tend to be more of a problem and I break them apart while trying to remove them.  With these anchovies, the taste is always delicious, the texture is always firm and not mushy, and my preference is olive oil to others.  I can reduce the sodium in the foods I eat, but I just love anchovies on a salad, pizza, baked potato, or simply on a cracker, so I compensate by basically eliminating the sodium I consume on days when I know I'll be eating these little fish.

title: Light flour produces tasty cakes
text: My mother used Swans Down cake flour so I have a strong memory of the box of bleached flour and didn't think that I could find a healthier alternative.  Fortunately,  King Arthur has come to the rescue and I now create perfect light cakes without losing so much of  the wheat's nutritional value. The texture is just what is needed and the taste is good.

title: Cheese subscription leaves much to be desired
text:
1. All the cheeses I received in 2 shipments were undersized, weighing between 6 and 7 ounces, not the 8 ounces which is a half pound. This adds up to revenue for the company and less product for the consumers.

2. Each cheese is wrapped in a lightweight wax paper that is folded and closed with a piece of paper tape which needs to be replaced as soon as possible because this does not protect the cheese from environmental factors which include the moisture from the ice pack's condensation.

3. The quality of cheeses is mediocre at best, most of the six I've received as of today are carried either by our local grocery store or Costco for a fraction of the price for a 6-7 ounce wedge. The assortments are not gourmet quality. There are no ingredients listed.

4. Customer service consists of a call center who can do nothing without consulting a supervisor.

If you want cheese and cannot obtain it locally, perhaps this subscription will work better for you. If you have cheese available or are considering gifting this to someone who likes diversity in their cheeses, I would not get this. Taste wise, it is limited and the presentation is not impressive. Remember that the recipient must be available to retrieve the package after delivery or it will spoil, particularly in hot weather.

title: Good color, flavor and texture
text: We consume raw cacao powder on a daily basis, sometimes it's in baked goods and others it is in raw foods.  In my experience, there has not been a major difference between most, but every once in awhile I find one that I prefer.  This particular organic cacao powder is one of the better varieties I've tried and I like that the cacao is from small sustainable farms.  I like to know from where products are sourced and with this one, it states only South America.  The resealable bag is not the most sturdy or secure, so I have transferred the cacao powder to glass jars to retain freshness.  This is the cacao powder I will be using when I prepare a vegan chocolate cake later this week.  A sample was provided for review.

title: Keep one in your bag and don't worry about it melting in summer heat
text: A few years ago, I started purchasing KIND bars from Amazon, then picked them up when I found them on sale in local stores.  Favorites have been those with dark chocolate and nuts, sea salt, and the coconut almond.  I recently discovered a new favorite which is unlike any other I've tried.  The [[ASIN:B00JA9LDH6 STRONG & KIND Roasted Jalapeno, 1.6 Ounce, 12 Count]] were in a basket at the checkout counter at my local Trader Joe's for a buck a piece, so I took a chance and purchased one.  Now right off the bat, I will say that not everyone will like these.  They are savory and since everyone in my household is a savory snack snackster, these are a huge hit and I purchased another dozen bars.  Roasted jalapeno is also known as chipotle, so the smoky heat combined with the minimally sweet nut and protein based bar just pops.  If you like the [[ASIN:B008YCDBGG Texas Pepper Works Candy-Krisp Jalapenos]] offered on Amazon (and stacked in my pantry), chances are that you'll also like these high protein bars.  I always carry a KIND bar in my bag and find that with no chocolate, I don't have a gooey mess if it's kept in a hot environment.

title: Even better than Rodelle vanilla extract, this will not disappoint
text:
For recipes requiring Dutch processed cocoa, I have found the Rodelle Gourmet Baking Cocoa to be outstanding in flavor and packaging. Yes, as I go through the 1.54 pound brown plastic tub with the screw top, I do find myself wondering why I don't transfer the powder to a smaller container, but I am so accustomed to reaching for the tub I identify from years of history and learned to keep it in a cool closet instead of kitchen cupboard.

The product does not routinely clump and always produces terrific baked goods. For many recipes, I ad a bit of instant espresso powder which brings out the richness of the chocolate. My go to chocolate brownies are variations of Alice Medrich's standard recipe which is available from various sources online. For chocolate baked goods, I always trust her.

title: Cream changer in this household
text:
I never, and I mean never ever, used Coffee-mate products, always preferring skim milk or almond milk in my coffee beverages and Chai. Amazingly, I received [[ASIN:B000YUOY30 Coffee-mate Coffee Creamer, French Vanilla Pump Bottle]] for review with a [[ASIN:B00HPN25C6 Nescafe Alegria 510 Barista Coffee Machine]] and I, along with everyone in this household am absolutely loving the flavor and foaminess of the creamer when used with or without the machine.

I personally enjoy a pump and a half in my cappuccino and add cinnamon to the foam. It is also delicious in Chai, with or without additional sweetener. I prefer my beverages less sweet, so this is an ideal product to use instead of milk and sweetener. Because it is shelf stable and will easily last for 30 days, this creamer which is lactose free, gluten free and Kosher can be used by nearly everyone I know except those who cannot have sugar products. This size is huge and the pump is designed to stay on when it's locked into place, but I have retained the cap so that I can pry off the pump when it no longer can access the stuff on the bottom of the bottle. I anticipate that will occur because the tube on the pump assembly is curved and I don't think it reaches the bottom of the bottle.

Being that I do not like flavored coffees at all yet really enjoy this creamer in small amounts, one can deduce that the flavoring is not overwhelming.
