Using this alone or halved with skim milk in my cappuccino, I'm in coffee heaven. This size is ideal for an office setting or home situation where several pumps are consumed on a daily basis. It should not be refrigerated or it will harden and become unable to dispense.

Little hint -- write the date the bottle is opened on the bottle, a Sharpie works best.

title: Not very sweet and especially tasty when warm
text:
Wanting to try the [[ASIN:B000EDDSES Bob's Red Mill Cereal Muesli, 4 - 18-Ounce Bags]] and not being prepared to purchase four bags, I recently picked up a single bag at a large store. I first made sure it was fresh and plopped down about four dollars for a single bag.

Opening the bag, my first thought was that the muesli was going to be too sweet for my liking because of the numerous bits of dried fruit. The first time I prepared breakfast with this, I took the residual heated and frothed skim milk from my coffee preparation and poured it into a small bowl of Bob's. I added nothing else and let it rest for about ten minutes. Oh my goodness, my first impression was so wrong it's not funny. The only sweetness came from the fruit, but the strong notes came from the chewy grains and crunchy nuts and seeds.

This muesli is more textured than the Familia brand I'd been eating for many years and I'm now a convert. Hooray for Amazon subscriptions.

title: Do you want instant or non-instant?
text: Most of the dry milk powders you'll find in the grocery store are instant, so you mix it quickly in water to achieve a reconstituted glass of milk.  I prefer the non-instant version like [[ASIN:B0001AVTD6 Non-Instant Non Fat Milk Powder, 1lb.]] for use in yogurt making and bread baking.  If I've run out of non-fat milk for coffee, I can mix it in warm water with a whisk, then use my milk frother to create the foam I want.  If I wanted this for making a glass of milk for drinking, I'd probably go with the instant because it is faster to just give it a shake or stir.  My intent with this package is to use some of it for making hot cacao mix using [[ASIN:B00HES9CMS Viva Labs Organic Cacao Powder: Raw and Non-GMO, 1lb Bag]] and [[ASIN:B009324C0U Nutiva Organic Sugar, Coconut, 1 Pound (Pack of 3)]].  Mix it in hot water, add a little homemade vanilla extract, stick in the milk frother and enjoy the cold weather.  I store my milk powder in a glass jar with the expiration date on the label I attach to the lid.

title: To my delight, my yeasted breads are greatly improved by using this flour
text:
Bob's Red Mill products are among those I frequently purchase, but I'd never tried [[ASIN:B004VLVPRG Bob's Red Mill Unbl White Flour, 24-Ounce (Pack of 4)]] until recently. I specifically purchased this for bread baking because I've been increasingly dissatisfied with the sacks of unbleached white flour from local grocery stores. Having 24 ounce packages was enticing because I would not have to store opened packages.

This flour is not on my regular deliveries because it is a product I don't want to think about. Knowing how good it performs, tastes, and stores in my pantry, it is a new staple that will need replenishment. The breads I've baked are tastier and more responsive to the yeast. This was quite surprising because the previous flour I used was not old and produces fine cookies and quickbreads, yet the Bob's Red Mill definitely produces better loaves of yeasted breads. The box I received was very fresh, manufactured only a couple months ago.

I keep an opened bag in a glass jar stored in the refrigerator. Incidentally, I have also sealed the bag using my [[ASIN:B00FXI5GDK FoodSaver V4880 Fully Automatic Vacuum Sealing System Bonus: Handheld Sealer, FreshSaver Container, Wine Stopper]].

title: True lemon in a portable bottle
text: When I tried my first taste of [[ASIN:B001Z2TTMM True Lemon 2.85 Ounce]], I knew instantly that this was going to be a staple in my household.  Think of the times you need a little lemon but either the one you have is not very good or you do not have a lemon at all.  Sprinkle a bit (and I mean a bit because it's concentrated) and you're good to go.  This is not a liquid, it's small crystallized lemon juice particles and it's tart and tasty.  I've even put some in a glass of ice water or evening beverage and even made a small batch of my own lemon herb pepper.  I purchased this because I could not find the small lemon juice from Italy bottle I used to get in my local market.  Very pleased to have met TRUE lemon.

title: Life span is a couple years after opening if it's kept cool and dry
text:
To my surprise, the package of [[ASIN:B005KR0MZG Red Star Active Dry Yeast, 2 Pound Pouch]] I just purchased at Costco for around four and a half dollars (the price has gone up lately) was made in Mexico. Regardless, the yeast is just as good as the last pouch I purchased, so I am not complaining. By keeping the yeast in a vacuum sealed bag in the freezer, I keep a 4 ounce brown glass jar that had contained yeast filled with this in the refrigerator and allow what I need to reach room temperature prior to baking. If I know I'll be using for several baking sessions, I'll leave the small jar on the counter top. Keep the yeast dry and cool to maintain the lively yeast. If I am ever concerned about yeast that doesn't appear to be active, I proof it. If it is still active, I then take into account the amount of yeast, water and sugar, using the proofed mixture in my recipe.

I've purchased bread machine yeast in the past but find that by adding a little piece of ascorbic acid powder which I've ground from a tablet in a small ceramic mortar and pestle to this yeast, I can achieve the same results. (I also often use all purpose flour with a little added vital wheat gluten instead of bread flour with great results.) The Red Star yeast works wonderfully provided it's active, fresh, and is used in the correct environment. If you are a beginning baker using yeast and you have been purchasing the small packets at the grocery store, this is a smart way to go. Even if you only use half of the yeast in the next two years which is about the truly active lifespan of the yeast after opening a fresh pouch, you have come out ahead. Just keep it dry, cool and if you can, vacuum sealed for protection.

title: If you need horchata in a can
text: It was fortunate for us that we received a can of [[ASIN:B00JD9ATUU Arriba Horchata Original Energy Drink, 11 Ounce (Pack of 12)]] for review and not an entire case because it was not appreciated in this household.  Cinnamon was the best part of the milk and sugar beverage, as it was much more sweet than anything any of us tends to consume.  There was no fighting over who got the last of the can poured in their little cup.  We did not hate it, we just did not like this horchata.

title: Sweet as sugar
text: I always have maple syrup in the pantry as well as honey and molasses.  Various sugars line a shelf, each used for baking purposes.  No pancake syrup has been purchased by me or my family and I remember the sweetness of Aunt Jemima syrup from my childhood.  Being curious about the [[ASIN:B00JSVK4WQ Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Pancake Syrup, Original, 20 Ounce (Pack of 6)]], I accepted a single bottle from Amazon for review.  It looks like the syrup from my youth or on the table at IHOP, and it tastes very similar, too.  This is not maple syrup and it's not honey, but it is made of only three things, Organic Invert Sugar Cane Syrup, Natural Flavor, Organic Caramel Color.  Nothing more, nothing less.  It pours like a pancake syrup usually pours, a little thicker than maple syrup, but thinner than honey which isn't a syrup.  It is dark in color and is bottled in a comfortably round plastic bottle with a nice pour top.  There is a protective seal which must be removed prior to using.  I'm going to try some in the next batch of honey sesame candies I'm making tomorrow because I think it will work well.  Of course, six bottles of this is a lot, so I'd recommend being sure you like it before ordering 120 ounces.

title: Delicious vinegar
text: Fortunately, a local store had two bottles of Champagne Vinegar - 16.9 Fl Oz at an incredible price, so I purchased them both.  At well under ten dollars each (really well under), and knowing the bottles were fresh, it was clear that I was getting a bargain.  Now if the product is not good, it's not worth anything, but in the case of this vinegar, I'm here on Amazon looking to replace the two bottles I've nearly depleted.  This is very delicate vinegar that is perfect for dressings or a simple slight pour atop a briefly oiled salad.  It is a 6% vinegar that contains sulfites, as do most vinegars.  This was produced in France and was distributed by a company in MA in the USA.  At this point, I'm going to look locally or try to find an affordable replacement for this light and refreshing vinegar that holds up on it's own.  I've even used it on strawberries instead of my usual balsamic.  My rating is for the vinegar, totally disregarding the exorbitant price posted as of today for this bottle of vinegar.

title: Mix with other peppercorns or use solo for their delicate flavor
text: White peppercorns usually contain peppercorns which are not white and I have no problem with that as long as I can pick them out in cases where I absolutely need only white peppercorns.  The Indus Organic Malabar White Peppercorns come in a comfortable plastic jar with a pretty lid, and before I refill my designated white peppercorn grinder, I go through them by hand.  I do not regularly see organic peppercorns, so this makes me happy, especially when they are fresh.  My previous supply was not organic, but was more uniform than these, from Penzeys spices.  I like these better.

title: I love surprises, especially when they taste good
text: I've recently purchased a number of nutiva products on Amazon and have had a good experience with each of them, so when I saw the coconut flour in a 4 pound bag at my local C-store, I purchased it last week.  The quality is as good as any nutiva product and I now feel like their biggest fan.  After baking chocolate chip cookies using the flour, I have a new recipe for my gluten free friends to enjoy.  I like it better than rice flours and my friend loves the cookies.  He cannot believe they were made with no grains at all and wants the recipe.  I feel obligated to note that I am a lover of coconut, so I may be biased.

title: Grainy texture makes my mouth and tastebuds happy
text: My only complaint with Ak-Mak Sesame Crackers is that I sometime misread the packaging and see it as ok-mok.  Any way I read it, the crackers are a staple in this household and have been for years.  I have seen these priced from $1.29 a box to over $3.00, and think that they are worth every penny because the ingredients are very simple, the crackers are very thin and textured with sesame seeds, and they are a great holder for whatever we place on them.  I'll admit to occasionally simply eating them plain because I want to enjoy the unadulterated whole grain taste.  I also like that the package is attractive and contributes little waste to the environment.  If you dislike whole wheat, stay away from these crackers.  If you like whole wheat as much as I, I'd like to introduce you to these thin crackers if you haven't already met.

title: Packaged in two sealed bags, so it stays fresher for longer
text:
I love Fiber One Bran Cereal and have eaten it for many years. Recently, I purchased another brand of high fiber cereal which resembles this General Mills cereal, but it is not the same. I'll admit that the box I purchased this past weekend was from a brick and mortar store and the cost was half of the current price (big store sale) and it's mot an item I think of purchasing from Amazon as a single box item. Regardless, because of the way this cereal is packaged inside the box leads me to believe that it would be a good product for shipping survival. Years ago, a box of this cereal contained a single bag and I needed to put it in a Tupperware container to remain fresh. It is now marketed in two packages rather than one in a single box, so I can put the single sleeve inside a glass jar after opening it and consuming the first serving. That is smart packaging.

The cereal is quite tasty in my opinion because it is not sweet, has a crunchy texture of a shape that I find appealing, and it is fantastic when served with warm milk and either fresh or dried fruit. It is a wonderful way to use my frothed milk after skimming the frothiest part into my cup of coffee in the morning. The cereal then becomes softer, so when I used the heated milk, I tend to use dried fruit instead of fresh fruit. Fiber One is also delicious in yogurt or even on ice cream instead of fattier nuts. I have used the cereal in baking with excellent results. My recommendation is to not limit yourself to consuming the cereal simply with cold milk. I will also remind you that this is very high in fiber, so beware if you grab it out of the box and lose track of how much you're consuming. You can have too much of a good thing, as you will likely discover the next day.

title: Superfood, it's not, but it is a tasty brown sugar made from coconut sources
text: As coconut sugars go, the Nutiva Organic Sugar, Coconut, 1 Pound (Pack of 3) is a good way to go if you need three pounds.  I question the labeling as ¨Organic Superfood¨ because I do not consider any sugar to be a superfood, but in moderation, if you are going to use sugar, this is one to consider.  The color of the sugar is brown, the texture is moist and fine.  It doesn't clump as quickly as brown sugar, but I haven't had an opened bag around long enough for that to occur.  Each pound is in a sturdy resealable bag and there's an interesting recipe on the back of the bag which I intend to try.  If this is your first experience with coconut sugar, don't be misled by the very white packaging and expect the product to be white like the coconut flesh represented on the package.  This is a whole other product which has a very caramel like, rich texture that lends itself to rich uses.

title: Consistently tasty and fresh
text: I'm very fond of Hemp Hearts and often simply eat them as a snack.  You can now find them in grocery stores as well as department stores which also sell packaged food products and the web is supplied with assorted recipes for hemp hearts or seeds from a gazillion sources.  Manitoba is the company that sold me my first hemp hearts and I tend to continue purchasing them because I'm so satisfied.  They are clean, fresh, sealed well, and so tasty that I rarely purchase sunflower seeds anymore because I tend to use this in their place.  Amazon offered these at a great price when I recently purchased them and I see that they are now even cheaper.  A one pound bag works best in my household and I have yet to have them turn rancid.

title: Creamy and mild, sauce heavy
text: I generally like Swad products and purchase them locally at an Indian market. Paneer Mahani is one of their Micro Curry heat it up products which I keep on hand for culinary emergencies.  This one is tomato based with cheese, cream, cashews, oil and spices. It's more creamy than others and less oily. I use it as a basis for a meal with vegetables added because I don't love creamy meals. The paneer in this one is squishy,  not a favorite, and the sauce is not at all spicy. It's okay but not a favorite Swad meal.

title: 10 boxes weigh in at just over 3 pounds of crackers or 80 servings
text: The texture of Wasa Crisp 'n Light 7 Grain Crackers is crunchy yet not hard.  They are sort of puffy flat sheets of grains which can be eaten plain or with toppings.  My favorite right now is with homemade rhubarb ginger preserves and a little cheese.  They are as tasty with a simple nut butter atop.  Have hummus and out of pita bread?  These work wonderfully and you can even spread the dip onto the cracker instead of dipping the cracker.  Tummy a little upset?  Dip these into a cup of tea for instant soothing.  This type of Wasa crackers are not available at all markets, so being offered a package of 10 from Amazon may be the way to go if you need this many boxes.  Each box contains about 8 servings of 3 crackers each.  They are made in Germany

title: For those who really like Organic Chia seeds, these are reliable
text: I've read about problems with Chia seeds over the past few months and am happy to report that the Nutiva Organic Chia Seeds in the 32 ounce package I received is fresh, looks like and tastes like organic chia seeds, and this bag contains Organic Chia Seeds grown in Bolivia.  I see that the price now is higher than when I purchased a few days ago, so I assume that this is one of those products which price fluctuates greatly depending on how much is sold.  For your chia needs, this brand is reliable and the product tastes as it should.  The only problem I had was that the line on the resealable bag designating where to cut was too high on the bag, so I needed to cut it twice in order to open the bag.  I've vacuum sealed mine in smaller packages, labeled them with number of bags and the date, and have them stored in a cool, dry closet.

title: Flakes you want to apply to food before serving
text: It has interested me for many years that in a society where we know sodium contributes to health issues, our supply of assorted gourmet salts is increasing.  In all honesty, for average cooking as in salting water or soups, I grab the old standby of Kosher salt,  For applications where the salt is added after the preparation, I often add Maldon Sea Salt Flakes from the UK.  My arsenal includes salts from all over the world, but there is something about this one that is my favorite when chocolate items are finished off with salt.  Caramels made with salt really pop when the Maldon is used.  I've had Maldon sea salt flakes in my cabinet for many years and doubt that I'll ever be without it.  It's that good.

title: Richer, creamier, it's a mature option for Nutella
text: Rigoni Di Asiago Nocciolata Hazelnut Cocoa spread is simply too good.  Fans of Nutella are in for a treat with this organic creamy spread that needs no refrigeration.  After you try it,  you'll find that it won't last long on your shelf. I first discovered this in a local grocery store and was drawn to the jar. Since the store was closing out the product,  I also bought a jar for my daughter.  We concur that this makes Nutella seem like an overly sweet version which is more geared to kids. This spread is good for adults and parents who care about providing quality more nutritious foods for the family.  I've made pocket pies with this as the filling, even combining it with raspberry preserves. I used a jar as the filling in a layer cake instead of icing. I've had it in yogurt and straight out of the jar when a chocolate fix was necessary.  This is a good product and my next project is using it in a Bundt cake.

title: For easy and sweet Matcha beverage, it's good
text: I personally love Matcha tea, whether it's prepared in a traditional tea ceremony or in a greet tea frap.  Rishi Tea Sweet Matcha is available in a small 4.4 ounce package and the Amazon price is currently less than we paid when in Florida at WF.  The ingredients are simple, Japanese Matcha and sugar, so you add the powder to your choice of milk.  Some of these mixes include assorted ingredients but this one does not.  My daughter likes this brand but I find it a little too sweet for my taste.  To give you an idea, she  loves Thai iced tea which I usually find to be too sweet, and if I order a green tea frap, I get it unsweetened.  After returning home, I picked up another brand of sweet Matcha powder and it tasted terrible, very unlike the Rishi brand.  That one was trashed and I purchased another box of this for my daughter to have on hand at her office.  It's worth a try if you like yours sweet and easy to make.

title: So tasty and addictive and now I have 4!
text: I purchased a jar of Texas Pepper Works Krisp Candy Jalapenos several months ago and was instantly hooked with a then new condiment.  I loved them so much that I purchased another jar for my daughter.  When offered a box of four for a review, I jumped on the offer, thinking that now I won't have to be stingy when offering them as a martini garnish.  I use these in cooking, add them to sandwiches or simple baked potatoes, snack out of the jar, but my favorite thus far is to place a little bit of the thick and sweet syrup in the bottom of a chilled martini glass, then pour in a freshly shaken vodka and ice (don't bother with the dry vermouth around here) and finish with three jalapeno slices.  I've also tried this in a Manhattan, but that doesn't thrill me.  If you like hot jalapenos and you are not opposed to sweet and syrupy, I cannot recommend these more.  I've yet to have a person not love them and I've served many.

title: Syrupy sweet and hot creates a good condiment
text: Texas Pepper Works Candy-Krisp Jalapeños are hot in flavor and sweet like candy.  We've eaten them out of the jar, in sandwiches, on a salad, on a baked potato, and in a vodka cocktail, and each time they have been enjoyed.  If you are a fan of jalapeños and like pepper jelly, you will likely like this product which has a texture that is more similar to an unchopped sweet relish than a crisp pepper.  The peppers are great in tunafish salad and the syrup was interesting in soda water.  I'd prefer that these be less sweet, but in general, I really like this condiment.

title: The best canned organic pumpkin available without a question
text:
Farmers Market Organic Pumpkin is by far our favorite available in the marketplace. Having previously purchased the [[ASIN:B00A8FH3UM Farmer's Market Organic Pumpkin Puree, 15 Ounce (Pack of 12)]] which is packaged in paper, I was reluctant to get this variety in cans, but chose a case due to the cost difference. To my delight, the cans are produced with a BPA free liner, they are labeled as Non GMO, and the pumpkin is as terrific in not better. The case I received has an expiration date of 19 months from today, so I know the cans are fresh. Being shipped in frustration free packaging, the carton was sturdy, secure, and was easy to open with all cans intact and perfectly labeled. The cans are easy to open if you have a can opener. Because I give my Shih Tzu a spoonful of pumpkin each morning for digestive issues, I typically remove the pumpkin from a can and freeze a portion so that it remains fresh until the first refrigerated container has been consumed. When using the pumpkin for baking or cooking where the entire 15 ounces are used, I eliminate this step and just use the pumpkin straight from the can. If ever the pumpkin appears to have separated with liquid floating as occurred with some previous packages I'd purchased, I simply stir it before using and find the pumpkin still to be excellent.
PS I find that the frozen containers definitely separate, however once they are stirred, they become more appealing. The dog loves it stirred or not, she doesn't differentiate and licks the plate any way it's presented.

title: Outrageously delicious and then some
text:
I was fortunate enough to win a contest for which I received an assortment of Wild Hibiscus products. Being the unselfish person I am, I shared the first several flowers of my [[ASIN:B004YL02LI Hibiscus Flower In Rose Syrup - 12.3 ounce unit - 15 Flowers Per Jar]] with friends as I'd seen them served when I was in San Francisco a few months ago. I placed a flower in the bottom of a fluted glass (faceted crystal), spooned on a bit of the rose syrup, then added a wonderful dry champagne. Visually, this cocktail is extremely appealing, as the bubbles drift from the flower to the top of the beverage. The syrup remains a lovely deep burgundy in color at the base of the glass with the flower hovering directly above, barely touching the syrup. The champagne turns pink as the glass is held and sipped. The flavor is outstanding, with a hint of rose essence. After the champagne is consumed, the tart flower is like a reward for emptying the glass. My first jar was fully consumed in this fashion despite my intentions of using the flowers in other recipes. I must buy more and am thrilled to see them available on Amazon.

PS these are equally as delicious in sparkling water or ginger ale and I'll bet they also work in tonic water.

title: Daily digestive dose for the dog
text: Although I love the packaging for the Farmer's Market Organic Pumpkin Puree, I'm going to purchase the product in cans next.  I use the pumpkin as a supplement for my Shih Tzu with a sensitive stomach and she loves this particular brand more than any other.  Because it's now offered at a lower cost in the cans, I'll be repurchasing that option.  In my experience, the pumpkin is as similar as can be, a little more chunky than other name brands which may or may not be organic.  Since I use only a spoonful every morning, I package the pumpkin in 3 small containers, freezing 2 and using one.  This way, the pumpkin remains in good condition and little Zhaba gets excited when she sees me remove the container from the refrigerator (or freezer).  With a small container in the freezer on most days, I'm also happy to have a little to add to a recipe when the urge hits and nothing is wasted.

title: Fresh, bright, tasty and in a secure bottle
text: I don't use as much turmeric root as some others, so the Frontier Herb Ground Turmeric Root in a 1.92 Ounce bottle is perfect.  Its fresh, ground finely and uniformly, bright in color, and I like the bottle as well as the cap.  I'll be ordering again when this bottle is empty, but I'll also reuse the bottle instead of recycling it.

title: Beans are moist and uniformly around 6 inches each
text:
The half pound bag of vanilla beans I received from Spicy World are not graded and the company has yet to respond to an email I sent a week ago. Spicy World is a wholesale distributor of goods from India, Britain and Africa. I did not find these beans listed on their website, but I did see a number of items I've enjoyed and others I would like to try. There are a couple pictures of vanilla beans on the Spices page. Nevertheless, as I said, they have not responded to my questions about these beans.

The beans are very fresh, dark and moist, containing much of the caviar. There is no reference on the packaging, just a label that says, "Gourmet Bourbon Vanilla Beans," and an outer bag that says, "Spicy World Vanilla Beans Madagascar Bourbon." Another assumption I'm making is that these were indeed grown in Madagascar and not from Madagascar, grown in India and processed using the Bourbon method. India is producing quality vanilla beans now so I am not confident in the source of these beans. The bag I received contains over fifty beans, each uniformly measuring just around 6 inches. They are aromatic and I expect them to last a long time, protected in a vacuum sealed bag and stored in a dark closet. They are sold in a sealed bag encased inside a zip lock bag. I've taken out what I needed, put a few inside a sealed test tube for later use, then prepared the remaining beans for storage. If I hear back from Spicy World, I'll update this review and likely change this to a five star review.

title: Belgian pearl sugar is not Swedish pearl sugar so be sure you get what you really want
text: For Liege waffles, you need Belgian pearl sugar, chunks which resemble irregular pieces of white sugar cubes.  These are more compressed than traditional sugar cubes and they melt inside the waffles but still remain a bit crunchy.  This is not the Swedish pearl sugar which is often used atop cookies and baked goods, but rather larger chunks that will melt when encased in dough and cooked.  The pearl white color lets us know that this is a refined sugar product and the package lets us know it originates in Belgium.  Yum.  A half pound box is worth a try if you're on the fence and since there aren't many options available in the US, [[ASIN:B0079KZV5S Lars' Own Belgian Pearl Sugar, 8 Ounce]] takes the cake.  I have noted that the price fluctuates on this site.

title: Grits cook quickly, are creamy
text: We've been enjoying corn grits milled at a local facility but they require soaking, repeated rinsing, and more than a half hour to cook.  They are very tasty, but do take preparation and time.  We just tried the [[ASIN:B004VLVN78 Bob's Red Mill Organic Corn Grits/Polenta, 24-Ounce (Pack of 4)]] and are hooked.  Requiring no preparation other than the boiling of water and no more time than five minutes in the water, these grits offer the texture we love, particularly when finely shredded cheese and chipotle peppers are added.  A single cup of dried corn makes four servings and we enjoyed them so much that we've yet to even cook an egg to accompany the grits.  We are, however, already planning our supper of shrimp and grits for next week.  There's no need to be from the South to enjoy this hearty household staple.

title: Perfect test for smoke alarm but lousy as a food item
text:
Three pop up bags of popcorn are included in this little box and all you need is a microwave, smoke alarm, mask, fan, bowl in which to put your popped popcorn, and water in which to drop the clumped together kernels that are sizzling when the popped bag is opened. If you're prone to burns, I'd also recommend ice cubes and a salve for your skin.

Each of the three bags we popped did the same thing, so either we received a bum batch, have a microwave that doesn't agree with the bags, or the stuff is lousy. We followed the directions exactly, entering 2 minutes into the microwave timer, then stood directly in front of the microwave as it popped. The pops sounded right, but after a minute and a half, the smell of burning popcorn seeped seeped from the appliance and we decided to not wait for the popping sound to be reduced to every second or two as directed by the instructions. Less than two minutes had passed when we opened the bag/s and we found the process or removing the top strip to be pretty simple. We grabbed the paper corner and pulled the cellophane off halfway across the bag, turned the bag and did it again from the other side, meeting at the middle to allow a lift off. The top was easily removed but we were overpowered by the nasty scent of burning corn and oil. With the first bag, we were naive about what was needed, so we were unprepared, thinking we'd be ready to eat the snack right out of the paper bag with no problem. Thinking like MacGyver, we quickly grabbed the first vessel nearby, a pot, and poured in the popped corn. Smoke poured out from the center of the kernels, and we dug out clumps of sizzling and stinky still burning corn. Immediately, we threw them into the sink and turned on the faucet, stopping the smoke. Unfortunately, we felt the need to try it again with a second bag. We had the same occurrence with the second bag, but we were prepared with a bowl in which to pour the popcorn. Since the place was already stinky, we popped the third bag to complete our experience, but we stopped popping after a minute in order to taste some of the popcorn before it had a chance to become affected by the smoke which we knew would develop inside the bag if we let it continue popping.

We then had three samples of popcorn and a stinky home and all concurred that the popcorn was not good even in it's smoke-free state. It was salty and oily. We were happy that we had not wasted any of our Penzey's spice blends to spruce up the popcorn. We offered no popcorn to the dog and the kernels we spilled on the floor remained there without offering temptation. Even at our cost of free for this box of [[ASIN:B00DF0KXYK Orville Redenbacher's Gourmet Naturals Popcorn, Classic Butter and Sea Salt, 3 Count]], the popcorn is not good, a surprise for an Orville product.

title: King Oscar is a King in this household not to be confused with another Prince of sardines
text:
In my opinion, these are the best canned sardines available and since sardines are very healthy, they are always available in my pantry. I sometimes mix them with mustard or hot sauce, occasionally just pour the can atop a salad and add some balsamic vinegar, use them instead of other fats on a baked potato, have a tasty sandwich on crusty bread with sliced onion, or just eat them out of the can. I do recommend, however, being thoughtful of others if you take these to work because the smell isn't always well received. Be sure to rinse the can and put it in something like a plastic bag or newspaper if using a community trash can.

After my first taste of King Oscar Sardines in Extra Virgin Olive Oil, I stopped even considering others. The tiny size makes them perfect to pop in the mouth and I have a little snap seal plastic container that fits the can perfectly if I eat only the top layer of the two. I'm particular about my sardines after craving them while in Spain prior to knowing I was pregnant years ago. I like these much better than the larger sardines of that time. If you like your sardines in sauces, I would also recommend adding a condiment of your choice directly to the can if you're so inclined. They are packed in Poland.

title: Contains wheat, these are not gluten free
text:
If not for the mislabeling in the description, the [[ASIN:B00DUQNFVC Werther's Original Baking Caramel, 9 Ounce]] would rate 4 stars from me, but after giving my friend with celiac disease gluten free brownies that I'd made with these and reading the back label stating, "ALLERGY INFORMATION: CONTAINS MILK, SOYBEANS AND WHEAT", I had egg on my face and had stop him from eating the brownies.

The caramels are indeed easy to unwrap and are ready for melting and using in your baked goods, ice cream recipes or dipped apples. As good as [[ASIN:B00A64NOPI Werther's Hard Candy, Original, 9 Ounce]], they are a very decent caramel flavor and texture which melts quickly in the microwave or in a double boiler. We enjoyed this bag in the gluten green brownies I'd prepared, but I'll again say that if one has celiac disease, don't eat these caramels. A single bag is more expensive than I believe they are worth, but I see that Amazon offers a multiple bag option at a better cost per bag. These aren't as expensive as the Williams Sonoma caramel apple kit that was available for Halloween, though, and I like them better.

title: Great vinegar but watch the price
text: I purchased the [[ASIN:B00117YTBC Omega Nutrition Certified Organic Apple Cider Vinegar, 12-Ounces]] and love it, but preparing to order it again, I see that the price has doubled.  It's a good quality organic vinegar for consumption or external application, but at nearly ten dollars now, I'm going to investigate other options.  For a price of around half of this, I'll give the product five stars, but at today's price, I'd suggest either waiting or checking elsewhere.  I also really like the bottle in which the vinegar is packaged because it's protected from light and the screw top seals well.

title: What's not to like?
text: I first tasted the [[ASIN:B004IS56Y0 Medora Snacks Popcorners Popped Corn Chips, Kettle, 1.1-Ounce (Pack of 40)]] on a JetBlue flight and I was hooked.  Truth be told, I salivate as soon as I'm seated on their airplanes at the thought that a basket including these savory and a little sweet snacks will be passing through the aisle and I will be eating a bag while the plane soars.  When my Dad flew up here to visit with one of my sisters, he had a bag and loved them as well.  A few weeks ago, I sent him a case of these, knowing that he would share them with my sister, brother in law, and my nieces and they would all enjoy them as much as we do.  I've since also purchased some for this household to enjoy and share.  The portion is perfect for a snack that won't wreak havoc on the human system and they can be enjoyed at any time, with or without accompaniment.  It's not necessary to be in flight to appreciate their crunchy, lightweight triangles that are just the right thickness to be nibbled if you have the will power to not pop the entire chip into your mouth.  This is still my favorite flavor, but I've been enjoying the white cheddar variety as well.  The plain salt aren't my favorites, but they are a part of the pack of 24 that's available at one Costco about 40 miles from home, the location where I purchased three cases this week.

title: Perhaps the boxes I purchased were "off"
text: I'll state right off the bat that I purchased four boxes of the Barefoot Contessa 29-oz. Chocolate Cupcake with Chocolate Frosting from a store other than Amazon and I baked a box today.  The cupcakes became a flat bunch of what looks like a cake, not cupcakes, overflowing into a single glob and the chocolate chunks for the frosting did not melt, but retained a granular consistency.  I spoke with a rep at Stonewall Kitchens, the company that used to sell this product, and learned that they no longer carry it.  The Best By date on the batch I purchased is over a month from now and I wonder if this might have something to do with the problem.  The only reason I've given this product three stars instead of one is because the chunks of flat "cupcakes" spread with a dollop of granular frosting are still moist, sweet, chocolatey and tasty.  We may have no cupcakes, but we do have a baked treat that will be picked at and enjoyed.  I can imagine that if the cupcakes puffed properly and remained in a domed form and the chocolate chunks for the frosting melted well, this would be an outstanding box of mix.  Should I find that another box of this mix works differently in a few days when I bake again, I'll update this review.

title: Campbell's trying new market and packaging
text: I received a single pouch of the [[ASIN:B0096RP84Q Campbell's Go Soup, Spicy Chorizo & Pulled Chicken with Black Beans, 14-Ounce Microwavable Pouch]] as a free with purchase offer and gave it to a friend who likes chorizo, chicken and black beans.  According to the consumer of the product, it was "okay" and he will absolutely not purchase the soup.  He said that free is the right price for him, but the soup is salty and not very appealing.  I can give it a three star review for the price at free, but in paying the three dollars +/- at which it is currently being sold, the review would be reduced to a lone star.

title: Delicious and aromatic Assam black tea
text: My pantry includes a huge assortment of teas, many of them of the loose black variety.  The tin I usually grab is filled with tea from the [[ASIN:B003MPJAOW Jivraj 9 CTC Leaf Tea (454 g, 1 lb)]] box because it produces a tasty and full bodied tea that is great either hot or iced.  I typically brew for three minutes, then remove the strainer and rebrew the plumped leaves later in the day for a reduced caffeine afternoon pick me up.  This tea from India is even better when sweetened a little and I often add steamed milk and spices to make an impromptu chai.  Because of the cut of the leaves, I've found this one pound box produces much more tea than other pounds of tea.  Friends from India prepare this tea by placing water, milk and tea leaves in a pot on the stove, then they sweeten and strain it into a cup.  They also add spices to create their favorite chai.  This is the only Jivraj tea I've tried, but I'm now interested in tasting their green tea.

title: Makes delicious brownies for lovers of bittersweet chocolate
text: I've been purchasing the [[ASIN:B001E5E0Y2 Navitas Naturals Cacao Powder, Organic, 16-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 2)]] for years and made a discovery I'd like to share.  When out of cocoa powder, I needed to bake a batch of Alice Medrich's Best Cocoa Brownies for an event and was short on time.  Remembering the cacao powder in the cupboard, I took a chance and was rewarded with a batch of brownies that drew more compliments than ever before, and I'm always praised for the brownies I bake.  They were especially bittersweet and didn't require the addition of espresso powder which I often add to chocolate baked recipes.  The ultra fudgy brownies were great with nuts, without nuts, and in the fresh batch I baked yesterday, I brought out the chocolate flavor the best so far with the addition of rehydrated cherries, cranberries and chopped figs.  I'd recommend thinking out of the box with this cacao powder and although it may lose some of the nutritional benefits with cooking, it sure does produce great baked goods if you are willing to taste your batter, adjust as necessary, and take a chance.  The above mentioned recipe was a perfect use because the cacao powder is cooked with butter and sugar initially and that's used instead of the typical chocolate chunks in brownie recipes.  Oh yes, in all recipes, I also added some chocolate chips -- found the extra bitter chips weren't as good as the semi-sweet because of the natural bitterness of the cacao powder.

title: Love the almond surprises the most but for young ones can be dangerous
text:
I've loved [[ASIN:B0015Q94NM Familia Swiss Muesli Cereal, No Added Sugar, 32-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)]] for years and haven't found it often in markets. Most offer the [[ASIN:B0015Q8VAE Familia Swiss Muesli Cereal, Original Recipe, 32-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)]] or more often, the [[ASIN:B00487HD5Q Familia Swiss Muesli, Original Recipe, 12 Ounce (Pack of 6)]], but I prefer receiving my sugars via fruit. Although I usually eat this cereal with skim milk, I have recently enjoyed it straight out of the package. It isn't easy because of the texture, but I sometimes just can't resist sneaking a taste or two. With warmed milk, the cereal is even better, and I've found that by using the extra milk I've frothed in the morning to wet my cereal, I have a perfect breakfast. Allowing the cereal to soak in the heated milk makes a softer muesli, but it still retains the chewy texture of the flattened grains.

My favorite reward when eating this cereal is finding a nice whole almond. This should be taken into consideration when feeding it to very young children who may not have fully developed their teeth yet. Finding these is rare, but this could be a choking hazard when a soft and smoother Swiss muesli is expected.

title: Price varies for these tasty Stash Tea blends which are offered year round
text:
When I first ordered the [[ASIN:B0046KMEYK Stash Tea Company Holiday Teas Gift Set with Festive Holiday Lid]], I was impressed at six boxes for less than eight dollars in a "Festive Holiday" package. Years ago I loved the [[ASIN:B000CQIDHE Stash Premium Licorice Spice Herbal Tea, Tea Bags, 20-Count Boxes (Pack of 6)]], but I had not had it in some time. It is not included in this seasonal package which contains a nice variety of teas which offers enough to suit most tastes. The price today is nearly twenty dollars which I believe is too high.

The lightweight cardboard package is sealed in cellophane and no scent escapes until the package is opened. The holiday lid opens like a book's cover, revealing six attractive silver box sides with white names and descriptions in English and French. By removing a tea box, you will discover the front and rear bright images are all reflective of the Christmas season. The blends include one herbal, one decaf black, one white, one black, one green, and one black and green. Each is blended and packed in Portland, Oregon, USA with other natural ingredients and each is really good. There is no excessive packaging and all is recyclable or compostable. The date on my carton is 03/12/2015, which is nearly two years from now. It's a five star offering, but I liked it better when it was sold at a lower price. I will repurchase when these boxes are empty.

title: Hits the spot
text: I have not had chicken or chicken soup for decades and I am not a usual consumer of dehydrated soup packages like this one. On a whim, I purchased the Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Vegan Chicken Flavor Noodle Soup, Light Sodium and I sure am glad.  There are times when we are under the weather and unable to eat regularly for one reason or another and these cups of soup are ideal to have on hand for those occasions. Having just eaten one for lunch, I first noticed the scent of pepper when I opened the package. I added boiling water, replaced the cover, then placed a dish on top of the paper cup while the soup steeped for a full six minutes. It looked good and tasted even better. There was no overwhelming saltiness and although I cannot attest to whether or not it tastes like chicken soup, I like it. The only thing I am not crazy about are the textures of the dehydrated carrots and corn which took much longer to soften. That being said, I will keep this product in the pantry for quick pick me ups and times of illness.

title: Yet another Kind bar he liked
text: If you try a Kind bar, it's easy to see why they are sold at your local higher end chain coffee shop. They taste good but have too much stuff that is not very good for you.  The peanut butter dark chocolate protein bar was included as a free sample in a coffee order I placed for my dad. He said it is tasty and quite filling, almost as good as the dark chocolate sea salt nut bars I'd been sending. The peanut butter is a good texture but this product isn't healthy enough to go on the reorder list.

title: Amazon to the rescue once again
text: My father became distressed when his instant cappuccino became unavailable at his local store. Upon checking Amazon's offerings of instant cappuccino in the French Vanilla variety, I thought this particular one resembled the canister he has been drinking for a few years on a daily basis. Lo and behold, the [[ASIN:B001EO5XPS Victorian Inn Instant Cappuccino, French Vanilla, 32-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 3)]] is the same and he is in ecstacy once again. He puts 3 spoons full into a cup, pours in boiling water, stirs, then reads the newspaper while enjoying his morning beverage. He likes the creaminess, sweetness, the vanilla flavoring, and the hint of coffee. I personally like a really strong coffee, but knowing that he is a happy man once again with his morning ritual,  I've got this on subscribe and save so he will always receive his delicious morning beverage.  I'm a happy person knowing that he is enjoying his beverage of choice and not having to settle for another.

title: Too tasty and full of Vitamin C (joking)
text: I've been purchasing [[ASIN:B000HDK0DC YummyEarth Organic Lollipops, Assorted Flavors, 5-Pound Bag]] for several years and have them on subscribe and save for my Dad who eats three every night while reading.  I've never met a person who didn't like one when offered.  I have to report that the [[ASIN:B00C25LNWA Yummy Earth 50 Bulk Snack Packs, 50 Count]] are equally as good in a soft gummy sort of way.  Each little package contains a daily supply of Vitamin C and with the exception of sugar, they are free of the stuff you likely don't want.  My friend who has celiac disease ordered a box of these after I gave him one to sample.  They are made in France and packaged in Mexico by a company from New Jersey.  Each of the four flavors is shaped differently, so you know what you're getting when you pop one into your mouth.  I try to suck on them and let them dissolve very, very slowly, but inevitably end up chewing the treats.  They do not stick in my dental work, so that's an advantage.  Labeled as Yum Earth, I wondered if it was a take off on Yummy Earth, but it is the same company, just a different name for the product.  These are goooooood.

title: Move over sunflower seeds
text: High in protein and tasty to boot, we've been enjoying [[ASIN:B001M1EQ60 Manitoba Harvest Shelled Hemp Hearts, 8-Ounce Bags (Pack of 2)]] since first receiving a sample last year.  They are part of a daily morning smoothie and they are thrown atop salads, too.  I was surprised to see a display of these in a local big box store a couple weeks ago and know it's becoming more readily available in my area.  If you haven't tried them yet, I recommend picking up a small bag at first because they aren't cheap and they don't last forever.  It is also important to keep these refrigerated because seeds or hemp hearts lose their nutritional value and they can go rancid.  We love these.

title: Tastes like licorice to me
text: I finally figured it out.  [[ASIN:B003WO0I6C SweetLeaf Sweetener (70-Count Packets), 2.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3)]], which is a very good deal here, tastes like licorice.  As I first tried to write a review a couple weeks ago, all I could think of was a bitter taste, but today it came to the forefront of my palate loud and clear.  If you're a licorice lover, you'll likely love this alternative to sugar, Splenda or whatever you usually put into your coffee, tea or foods.  I, personally find the SweetLeaf to be a tad bitter and it doesn't always dissolve in my iced tea.  A single packet gives a sweeter impression than Splenda, so I use less and often combine both.  I appreciate the herbal source but do find that I alternate among an assortment of sweeteners, depending upon my preference.  All in all, if you're a user, I do recommend purchasing here because I've found that it's a much better deal than in the local markets around here.

title: Don't leave home without one
text: Friends say that I am the one person they would want to be stuck with in an elevator.  It's not because of my charming personality, it's because of the little bag I always carry with essentials.  Think smaller than the bag you are allowed when passing through security at an airport and you've got my mini survival kit.  I always have with me one of the [[ASIN:B002BFXI56 TABASCO brand Pepper Sauce "6-pack Miniatures" 1/8oz.]].  I've tried the [[ASIN:B0025UBVXI Tabasco Pepper Sauce, 0.11-Ounce Single Serve Packages (Pack of 200)]] but found that they can do in a pinch but they don't have the kick of the bottled sauce.  Additionally, the little bottles hold more and if I don't use it all, I can always reseal the bottle.  These are not cheap and you may find them in a local store as I do, but if  you like your food "heated" and don't want to take a chance that the bottle in your local diner has been licked by a two year old or is stale, these minis are the way to go.  I've discovered that 99% of the time I've used my mini has been on eggs because most restaurants currently offer hot sauce condiments.  I have found that bars always have the sauce and haven't needed to pull out my own to spice up a cocktail.  They are also good to have on hand if you're dining at a friend's, want hot sauce and they have none.  I don't suggest doing this unless it's a close friend who won't be insulted and I would always ask before pulling out my own condiment in a private setting.  These are also cute to attach to a culinary gift as a decoration.

title: Full of grains, little salt and not overly sweet
text: After reviewing a Quaker instant "whole grain" oatmeal and finding it terrible, I thought it would be nice to review a product I've been eating for awhile now that is very good and available on Amazon.  The [[ASIN:B004MNEOYY Better Oats Abundance all Natural Multi-Grain Hot Cereal ~ Apples & Cinnamon Flavor ~ 5 Pouches per 7.4 oz Box (Pack of 3 Boxes)]] takes up less space in the cabinet and is extremely easy to carry in a purse or bag.  The individual package is marked with a water level, so it's easy and quick to add the contents into your extra large bowl (it really boils while heating!), fill the bag with cold water and add to the grains, stir, and then microwave.  It's possible to cook this on the stovetop, but I'd recommend other products if you're going that route to save the added expense of these little packages.  After two minutes, you'll have a fully bubbly bowl of expanded full of grains cereal that will satisfy your tastebuds and chewing needs.  It has more texture than traditional oatmeal, close to but not equal to a steel cut oatmeal.  Full of grains and some dried fruit, this weighs in at 160 calories, 90 mg of sodium, 9 grams sugar, 5 grams of protein and 3 grams of fiber.  This is just an overview.  Because I really don't like much in my cereals either hot or cold, I'm going to try the Better Oats Bare variety that I've just learned about.  This truly is better than oats and contains much more chewy grains and flax.

title: Real Medley of sweetness and "flavor"
text:
The packaging is curious of the [[ASIN:B007N04AF6 Quaker Real Medleys Apple Walnut Oatmeal +, (Pack of 12)]]. Remove the lid, remove the well secured seal, do not remove the sleeve from the plastic container. Add boiling water to the interior line which is just above halfway, cover and let rest for three minutes. OR add water to the same line, DO NOT cover, and microwave for less than a minute, then let rest for a minute before eating. Don't forget to stir after adding water in either technique. I used the boiling water method.

My first taste was shocking. I got a major hit of sweet and an unidentifiable flavor that was unappealing and downright offputting. I tried again and liked the texture but couldn't tolerate the sweetness and nauseating flavor. Next spoonful was sticky, gluey, and I decided to forfeit the remaining 290 calories and 22 grams of sugars. I picked out the two pieces of walnut and discarded the container and 90% of the product. I am very happy that I received only one package and will neither purchase nor recommend this product. I am disappointed in Quaker for creating a product that is marketed as a healthy option. Yes, multigrains are nutritionally better than refined grains, but all things must be considered and this was a huge disappointment. Two stars are earned only because for those who really must have sugars, at least they can get some fiber with their easy to prepare oatmeal.

title: Good macaroni product by reliable company
text: Made in the USA, the [[ASIN:B003EXXPWA Barilla Mezze Penne, 16-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)]] is another semolina pasta product that lives up to the Barilla name.  The sharp angle at which the pasta is cut provides a perfect shape for scooping sauces or serving as a cold pasta salad with larger chunks of delights.  Barilla is often available on sale in stores for around a dollar per one pound box, but this shape isn't always on the shelves.  It's nice to have it offered by Amazon in a package of four boxes.  I like this smaller penne size and find that it holds up very well when cooked.  I do use salt in the boiling water and coat the cooked pasta with a little olive oil to keep the pieces from sticking together as they sometimes do.  I also tend to include a little of the cooking water in my sauces.

title: Spicy and so aromatic
text: I see why [[ASIN:B0000TGTGU Tandoori Indian Grilling Paste - award winning spicy classic. 1 jar]] is award winning!  Mix it with some yogurt and you're ready to go.  No need to blend your spices or do much more.  I use it to create a very quick and delicious meal of Quorn naked cutlets by simply coating them and pan frying in a non-stick pan.  A delicious "crust" forms and I add green beans, okra, or whatever I have on hand, then serve it atop quinoa or rice.  Having an arsenal of herbs an spices on hand, I always keep this in the fridge for those last minute meals or cravings for some hot and fragrant.

title: Not the best when in hot environment but still tasty
text: I received the package of [[ASIN:B007PE7ANY KIND Nuts & Spices, Dark Chocolate Nuts & Sea Salt, 12-Count Bars]] in the early evening, so it had been sitting in the shipper's truck all day in the heat.  Unfortunately, when I opened the package, each bar was soft because the chocolate was melted and sticking to the wrapper.  Regardless, when brought back to a temperature closer to the 80 degree range, I eagerly tore open a cellophane package and carefully peeled it back to try my first KIND bar.  With the first bite, I was impressed by the great flavor of fresh nuts and simple dark chocolate, even after exposed to the environmental heat.  On the second bite, I was hit with the sea salt, making me think about how smart it is to add sea salt instead of using salted nuts which I sometimes do when making chocolate covered nuts.  That creates an inconsistent salt burst which I find appealing.  At the small size of 1.4 ounces, it's loaded with fiber from the nuts and chicory root fiber, with relatively little sugars.  I personally would seldom consider eating one of these as a meal, but would have it as a filling food when needed in times where a meal could not be obtained.  I would supplement this and would not rely on this alone for nutrition!  Without further information on what else is included in the diet, I don't understand how the "Yale-Griffin Prevention Research Center indicates that eating 2 KIND bars each day helps maintain your weight through low glycemic, deliciously satisfying, nutritionally rich ingredients that will keep you fuller longer."  I think that 400 calories of intake per day is too much for any snack item.  With that being said, I now carry one of these bars with me instead of another grain type bar for the times when I absolutely need something to eat or desire a chocolate fix.  When I have these, I no longer carry a little bag of nuts either.  Because I haven't yet purchased bars which haven't been heated, I can only say that those I've received are not visually appealing and require eating directly from the cellophane because the bits of chocolate fall away.  Despite that flaw, these are a great snack item that I will be purchasing and will try other varieties as well.  I would like to see these offered at a better value when purchased in a box rather than the current cost at about eighteen dollars for a pound box of twelve bars.

title: Saucy and hot for a moment or two
text: I purchased several assorted jars of Mrs. Renfro's Salsa products and will review them as we go through the jars.  The first one we've opened is [[ASIN:B004LG2AW0 Mrs. Renfro's Habanero Salsa Hot -- 16 oz]] and it's better than average but not knock your socks off jarred salsa.  Initially, the sauce was very thin in consistency, but after refrigeration, it thickened a bit.  Nevertheless, this is definitely not home-made fresh type salsa, it is a jarred and prepared in large batch salsa product.  At the cost of a couple dollars at the store, we were not dissatisfied, but I wouldn't pay more for this.  There are a few mushy tomato chunks in the product, so it's not totally smooth.  The heat is intense but lasts only briefly, so if you're looking for lingering heat, I'd recommend another salsa.  For a quick jolt of habanero, this is very good and worthy of a four star review.  I'll compare it to the other Mrs. Renfro salsa products as they are tasted.

title: Not Best of Walkers
text: The [[ASIN:B005V9ZB8Q Walkers Shortbread Dark Chocolate, Ginger Royals, 4.4-Ounce (Pack of 4)]] arrived in time for dessert so I was very excited to immediately open the package and break out the cookies to serve with vanilla ice cream.  The chocolate had clearly been melted at some point, with a muted color, irregular coating, sticking to the packaging.  These cookies were very unsuccessful and a great disappointment. My Dad loved the two types of Walkers shortbread cookies I brought to him, the [[ASIN:B001EPQ18K Walkers Shortbread Lemon Thins, 4.2-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)]] and [[ASIN:B001GCVLVI Walkers Shortbread Assorted, 8.8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)]], so these were much anticipated for a dark chocolate and ginger lover.  They were absolutely lousy and ended up in the trash.  The cookies were extremely chewy, sticking to the teeth, but I'm not sure if this is the nature of the cookies or simply the batch we received.  We opened each box, finding all cookies in the same condition -- messed up chocolate sticking to the package, cookies overtly sticky.  If I can find these in a b&m store, I'll update, but won't order online again. Trader Joe's triple ginger cookies have a better texture and taste so we'll have a piece of dark chocolate with those for the desired combination. I may try dipping those cookies in melted bittersweet chocolate, leaving an edge free for easy holding.

title: Who needs barbecue potato chips?
text: The [[ASIN:B000VZSYCK Tyrrell's Hand Fried Potato Chips, Sweet Chilli & Pepper, 5.29-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)]] is my favorite of the four varieties I've had.  That's not to say I won't grab a bag of [[ASIN:B000VZU3C4 Tyrrell's Hand Fried Potato Chips, Lightly Sea Salted, 5.29-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)]] just as fast, or the Mature Cheddar variety and even the Sea Salt and Cider Vinegar.  Really, they are all good!  Thinly sliced of potatoes that are grown within 25 miles of where they are turned into potato chips, each bag is imprinted with the potato variety and location where grown, so those who are interested in those details can be happy.  Since they are shipped to the states from England, I am not really impressed by the manufacturers proximity to the farms.  What does impress me is the flavor of each distinctive variety, the really light salt on the slightly salted variety, the spiciness to the sweet chilli flavor, and I love the pictures on the bags.  They hold up well after the bag is opened and don't deteriorate as quickly as other potato chips.  I've combined the slightly salted with the other flavors to cut down on the sodium and alleviate some of the snacking guilt.  My main criticism is that some of the chips have been blemished and others have been a very oily, but for the most part, these are top notch potato chips if you don't eat too many at once when the oil becomes overwhelming.

title: Best chips around for protein and iron
text: 31 chips in a serving and I have to count them out or I'll eat the entire bag and have all 4 servings at once!  This is an outstanding product that only suffers from having more sodium than I usually consume.  Regardless, the light, crisp, dippable, scoopable, stuffable snacks are now the favorites of my family and friends.  When I find a product that I like, I tend to give it as gifts so that others can enjoy my discoveries.  [[ASIN:B004D693CS Simply 7 Lentil Chips, Sea Salt, 4-Ounce (Pack of12)]] is my personal favorite variety, seconded by the [[ASIN:B004D6044O Simply 7 Lentil Chips, Creamy Dill, 4-Ounce (Pack of12)]].  I'm not sold yet on the [[ASIN:B004D67K78 Simply 7 Lentil Chips, Bruschetta, 4-Ounce (Pack of12)]] variety, but many of my friends prefer the Italian seasonings.  The chips remind me of mini pappadams.  These are so simple to slip into the mouth and kids adore them, too.  If you're looking for a new healthier savory snack, I don't think you can go wrong with these.  It's amazing just how tasty lentils can be!

title: Subtle passion fruit flavor in economical tea
text: If you can pick up the [[ASIN:B0028W3O56 Roland Kwong Sang Tea, Passion Fruit, 2.5-Ounce Tins (Pack of 6)]] when it's at a low price, I absolutely recommend its purchase.  I've consumed several of the Roland teas from Hong Kong and this one seems to have at least a little flavor of the applicable fruit or spice.  I sense the sweet aroma every time I open the can.  I'm not a fan of overly sweet flavorings and usually do not select any fruity teas, but this one is perfect for my taste with a subtle almost lychee aroma, requiring no sweetening additions.  The tannins are not overwhelming and it stands up well in the cup.  It makes a lovely iced tea (my favorite now), so summer screams out for this variety.  At the low cost of around a dollar (or less at the time of this writing), I'm going to pick up more for friends enjoyment.  Although it's a pain to remove the stickers from the tins, I also reuse the Roland tins for  other purposes and save some bucks on storage containers for kitchen, office, art, sewing and shop supplies.

title: Not limited to hot beverage
text: The Prince of Peace Instant Ginger Honey Crystals originally didn't impress me because the first ingredient was cane sugar, followed by honey and then ginger.  Because we don't drink many sweet beverages, the 70 calories and 17 sugar grams seemed outrageous.  We also were not thrilled with the biblical proverbs imprinted on the packaging.  After opening the first pouch, however, our family was hooked on the spicy sweet crystals.  Each pouch contains 12 grams of ginger and it is very, very spicy, just what we like around here.  We empty a packet into a little jar and always have some accessible in the kitchen.  I use a little binder clip on a packet in my bag when traveling, so I can slip a few crystals on my tongue even when there's no water available.  I add this to white or green tea, mix it in my chai and add no other sweetener, sprinkle it on yogurt, fruit and fiber cereal in the morning, and even have used it to tone down an overly spicy seafood stew I made last week.  I don't know how, but throwing in about a half teaspoon worked a miracle.  The hot beverage is great when we're nauseous or just feeling less than perfect, and when chilled, is a perfect complement to one of those clear beverages we may drink for relaxation.  If you like ginger, think about taking a break from the ginger chews/candy and try these little delectable crystals instead.

title: Addictive Oolong that doesn't break the bank
text: Prince of Peace has hit it out of the ballpark with this economical organic Fujian Oolong tea in unbleached bags.  This is consumed throughout the day in my home and we are not in the least bit jittery as often happens with the semi-fermented type of tea that nears black in its caffeine content.  Amazon offers the best price so far and we highly recommend the Prince of Peace Organic Oolong in the 100 count box!

title: Economical and Delicious
text: I've been drinking white teas for years and was thrilled to find the Prince of Peach Organic White Peony teabags on Amazon.  My local store only carries the smaller box of this particular Prince of Peace tea, and since we drink it daily, Amazon will be our go to source from now on.  The tea is not the prized Silver Needle, but for an organic tea in an unbleached bag with little packaging waste that is all compostable, it's a no brainer.  I brew it at a lower temperature, usually filtering the boiled fresh water over an ice cube as its being poured onto the teabag/s.  I highly recommend this white tea!

title: Toasty, tasty, flavorful and fragrant
text:
The [[ASIN:B0046LCK5M Roland Curry Sesame Seeds, 3.53-Ounce (Pack of 6)]] are yummy! As a lover of curry, I was unsure as to how flavorful these would be and I was thrilled to discover that they are delicious and very fresh. After checking the production code, I've discovered that the first batch I received was manufactured exactly one year ago, so they are good for some time. Each bottle is sealed in plastic and a freshness seal is under the screw top.

The ingredient list is: sesame seeds, natural curry powder, salt, seasonings, sugar, spices. The flavor is not a hot curry, but a sweeter version, so I tend to add garlic and pepper to mine. For milder curry loving individuals, this might be perfect with no further addition. I use it on rices, pastas, vegetables, in dips, combined with yogurt and lemon juice as a coating for searing fish, and on POPCORN!! The smaller size bottle is ideal so that I do not get heavy handed and the two part screw off cap is great for shaking, pouring or scooping out with a measuring spoon. (I typically only remove the top section for pouring.) I actually use the curry sesame seeds instead of salt much of the time and have ground them into a delicious paste. I must try other varieties some day, but for now, I'm satisfied with this flavor and recommend them to curry lovers.

title: Such a slight spiced clove fragrance
text: The [[ASIN:B0046LFBY4 Roland Ginger Tea/Canisters, 2.5000-Ounce (Pack of 8)]] had no scent or taste of ginger whatsoever, so I had high hopes that the [[ASIN:B0046LF8HY Roland Spiced Clove Tea/Tins, 2.5000-Ounce (Pack of 8)]] would compensate and I could create a blend of chai using both teas from Hong Kong.  Oh well, at least I can get a whiff of cloves with this batch, but I will need to use a lot of other spices to make a delectable chai.  If you're looking for a strong clove tea, look elsewhere.  Should you want some cute tins for gift giving and the flavor isn't a great issue, perhaps these will work for you.  In creating my gift bags, I'll include both tins of teas with some fresh spices.  My purchases of Roland teas are now complete and I would not recommend them.  They really could be marked simply as black tea leaves with a slight floral hint.  I expect that after the tins are opened, it's only a matter of days before they all taste the same.

title: Perfect with tea, coffee, milk, port or scotch whiskey
text:
Today is 12/2/11. My order of Walkers Shortbread Assorted, 8.8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) arrived yesterday and the BEST BEFORE date is END MAR 2013. Perfect! Plenty of time to share and consume these delectable treats from Scotland, the producer of my favorite whiskeys. Although the Amazon description states that this package includes, "Shortbread in five distinct shapes," the cookies are actually in three shapes. Included in each box are 4 rounds, 6 triangles, and 8 of the traditional fingers, totaling 18 cookies. They are fresh, golden, attractive to the eye and satisfying to the tastebuds. It's quite interesting that the boxes list the ingredients in many languages, but English is not included. They are made of wheat flour, butter (33%), sugar and salt. Walkers shortbread makes a gift that would likely be appreciated by any person who enjoys buttery confections that are slightly sweet who is not allergic to milk, wheat, gluten or nuts, is not vegan and has either teeth or rigid gums for chewing. The biscuits which are about 1/2 inch thick soften when wet, so a full set of teeth is not required.

When in a crunch for entertaining purposes, I've dipped the shortbread halfway into microwave melted bittersweet chocolate and then into chopped toasted pecans. There's no need to limit yourself to a plain shortbread when you can create a desert worthy of oohs and aahs in a matter of minutes. We love Walkers shortbread and are pleased to have purchased them from Amazon in a box of 6 packages.

title: Impressive gift basket, but not as weighty as described
text: I'm not sure why, but I imagined that I would need to assemble this gift basket upon arrival.  To my delight, it arrived protected by a sturdy box which was inside a larger amazon box.  This was fortunate because the large box was delivered a bit crushed.  When I opened the box for presentation at our Thanksgiving dinner, it took no time at all to remove the plastic covering that was wrapped around the entire filled basket.  Didn't even need to remove the ribbon, simply pulled the plastic away from underneath.  If you imagine the Wine.com photo, but subtract about 1/2 of the height, you have an idea of the true size.  Another helpful visualization is to know that the jar of Napa mustard (one of my favorites) is the size of a small jam/jelly/honey/syrup jars you might receive from a hotel room service.  We found the basket itself to be attractive and a keeper, but it will not be used for heavy objects since it's lightweight and the hinges are not strong.  It will be great for a light produce display at the farmers market.  Resting upon shredded brown paper with crumbled brown paper at the base are the food items which are almost all from California and in green packaging.  The Angelina's cookies are packed in Indonesia but distributed from California.  The complementary green and gold ribbon (as pictured) make for a very attractive presentation which is far nicer than many I've seen.  The assortment of sweet and savory is well balanced and there's something to please most people.  A college student would probably love to receive this package.  The most ample sized of the dozen items are the Ghiradelli squares, can of peanuts, Biscotti and Sonoma Jacks cheese wedges.  All in all, we really like this gift basket but feel that the price of nearly seventy dollars is a bit high for the small sizes.  At fifty dollars or less including delivery, this would be a fantastic gift basket which would be a no brainer for presentation, quality and value.

title: 1 out of 8 did not like these
text: I've purchased 4 boxes of Bobo's Oat Bars in the Chocolate variety from Amazon in the past month.  An acquaintance had told me how delicious they were, so I took a chance and purchased my first box before I embarked on a trip, planning to take some along for the journey.  Unfortunately for my wallet, every person but one to whom I gave a bar loved these, so I sent some a box to enjoy.  Prior to my first purchase, I did not realize these are soft, sort of brownie like in texture, a little sweet in a molasses sort of way (no molasses in the recipe, though), crumbly, and with two servings in a single bar.  Fortunately, I placed a bar in a small resealable plastic bag for the airplane trip, so I was able to break off a little piece any time I felt hungry.  That bag was a saving grace because when a bar was gone, I replaced it with another and you won't believe how often I pulled out that little bag.  I ordered the first box as a gift after I put a little bite into my father's mouth while he was busy enjoying himself at a slot machine and I realized that he needed to keep these on hand for him and Mom to have on the days they go out.  For those who have few teeth, these are edible because of the soft texture, yet they provide an enjoyable flavor.  Hiker's took these along for a day trip, not worrying about the double serving per package, happily eating the entire bar.  As they put it, they felt like they had a brownie along for the trek, much more enjoyable than other bars they'd taken in the past.  One sister has enjoyed these on days when she's been unable to break for lunch at work, having them with coffee or tea and some deep breaths.  Without eggs, butter or flour, they are terrific, even though Earth Balance has never been my favorite flavor.  I'll admit that I was expecting a firmer bar with visible chocolate chips, but after the surprise of a crumbly moist baked good with a not very sweet cocoa flavor, I was hooked.  I will gladly try the other varieties when I can find them for a lower cost than over two dollars per bar.  A retail value of about thirty dollars is too high for a dozen bars, so I've deducted a star from this review.  The one friend who did not love her Bobo's Oat Bar thought it tasted like cardboard and she claimed to have forced it down at work.  She loves the SOYJOY bars which I do not care for, so I guess the world is balanced.

title: Healthful quality fiber every day
text: I add flax seeds to foods regularly and have been enjoying oat bran for years.  Bob's Red Mill Organic Oat Bran Hot Cereal is my preferred brand, so it's great to find it offered at Amazon.  Known to add fiber and help reduce cholesterol levels, having this every day in one form or another is beneficial and can be very tasty, too.  The package contains a great muffin recipe and the Bob's Red Mill website offers additional recipes.  I'm currently reading the Dukan Diet book and see that one of the requirements for that program is to consume a tablespoon and a half of oat bran on a daily basis which sounds good to me.  He provides a little recipe for an oat bran pancake which I'll try.  I imagine that with the publication of this book in the USA, the interest in this product will skyrocket and that's a good thing.  Oat bran makes a great addition to bread doughs as well and you might even consider it in your next home made pizza.  This is much more than a hot cereal.

title: Nice on ice with fresh mint or spices
text: I drink a lot of tea these days and when the weather is hot, consume iced tea constantly throughout the day.  Being very sensitive to caffeine, I find that my yummy black and green teas raise my blood pressure and keep me awake often for much longer than I'd like.  Herbal teas are fantastic and I enjoy them immensely, but for a low cost decaf common orange pekoe/black tea option, I brew the Lipton Decaffeinated Black Tea, using usually 3 bags in a pot of boiled water.  Since I have a seemingly perpetual supply of mint, I add a spring to the glass with a Splenda and I'm set.  For a simple chai, I add an assortment of cardamom, pepper, nutmeg, cinnamon and ginger, depending upon my mood and I top it off with skim milk.  The 48 count boxes are attractive to me because they don't take up much space after the box is opened and I don't need to put the bags in anything other than the lightweight original box.  I also enjoy sharing with neighbors and find the box to be a perfect size as opposed to larger boxes which I might not be so inclined to share.  When Amazon offers these on sale, you can't beat the cost for reliable and simple tea in bags.  It may not be the finest tea in the world, but it is well worth the cost for an adequate tea.

title: Morocco's quality couscous
text: Couscous is finally a very popular alternative to rice, pasta and potatoes in the USA, but most of the couscous is not produced in Morocco.  My first taste of couscous was years ago in Paris and the Dari brand is the most similar to what I tasted first in 1975.  You do not need a couscous pot for this product, but you certainly can prepare the traditional meal by separating individual semolina grains into light, fluffy particles by rubbing it between the hands if you so desire.  With neither the inclination nor time, you can prepare it as simply as you'd like by using a microwave, boiling water and a few fluffs with a fork.  Dari produces semolina, barley and corn couscous at this time and I'm looking forward to trying the barley which is currently available on Amazon.

title: Outstanding suckers we always have on hand
text:
We always have the YummyEarth Organic Lollipops on hand and order them in the 5 pound bags. I adore them, always carry them in my bag, and enjoy sharing them. Kids loved these for Halloween, too! I had handed these out to my Dad's doctor's office staff when I was visiting a couple months ago and they all went crazy over these lollipops. Since that time, Dad been bringing some from his large bag to the office every week or so. When he asked for more this weekend I was surprised because his Subscribe and Save delivery wasn't scheduled for some time. Turns out he wanted to get more for the doctor's office for the holidays. I came up with a great solution -- order this 30 ounce container for the office. Everyone is happy and the container can be refilled from the 5 pound bag!

Every flavor is delicious and a little on the tart side. They are not exceptionally sweet, just hit the spot. Several fit into even the smallest bag for easy retrieval and they are great conversation starters if you've given one to an individual who has never tasted one. I personally eat very little candy, but I enjoy these immensely.

title: Not really a buzz, but has a nice flavor
text: I gave a box of the Coffee People Santa's Buzz K-Cup for Keurig Brewers, 24-Count K-Cups to a friend who has been drinking assorted Green Mountain blends since she purchased her Keurig brewer over a year ago.  Ironically, I was there when the package arrived, so I was able to try the first brewed cup.
